items.story: Grant went down early in Thursday's win over the Warriors, and he's now dealing with a strained left calf that could cost him multiple contests. With Cameron Boozer (ankle) also sidelined, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper are both worthy of streaming consideration in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Grant won't return to Thursday's game against the Warriors due to a left calf injury. He'll finish with three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) across five minutes.
items.story: Grant limped to the locker room in the second quarter and was ruled out for the remainder of the contest shortly thereafter. If he's forced to miss additional time, Kris Murray and Olivier-Maxence Prosper would be candidates for increased minutes. Grant's next chance to play will come Saturday at Minnesota.

items.headline: Grant went to the locker room during the second quarter of Thursday's game against Golden State due to an undisclosed injury, Drew Hill of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Grant is presumably dealing with some type of lower body injury after limping to the locker room, but the team has yet to issue an update. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Grant (head) is off the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Grant missed Saturday's game due to a head injury, but he will be available Monday. Over his last five appearances, he has averaged 14.8 points, 1.8 assists and 1.4 rebounds in 22.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grant (head) is out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Grant will miss the second leg of Memphis' back-to-back set due to a head injury. His absence should open up more opportunities for GG Jackson, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper.

items.headline: Grant (head) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Grant could be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a head injury. If the veteran forward is unable to suit up, Kris Murray and GG Jackson would likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Grant finished with 22 points (7-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), one rebound and one assist across 26 minutes in Friday's 142-111 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Grant led Memphis in scoring despite coming off the bench, delivering 22 points on just 10 field-goal attempts. The veteran forward was particularly efficient from beyond the arc and at the charity stripe, though he contributed little outside the scoring column. His 26 minutes in the lopsided victory are encouraging, but his fantasy value remains heavily dependent on scoring and three-point production.

items.headline: Grant provided 10 points (4-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt) and two assists in 22 minutes during Friday's 128-97 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Grant continues to play a limited role off the bench for his new team, leaving him well outside the top 200 in standard leagues. Through nine appearances, he has averaged just 9.7 points, 1.0 blocks and 1.6 three-pointers in 24.1 minutes per game. At this point, it's clear that Memphis is not prioritizing him, making him a non-factor outside of deep leagues.

items.headline: Grant had 11 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one block in 24 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Grant provided efficient scoring in his reserve role, connecting on half of his field-goal attempts while knocking down two triples. He has scored in double figures in three of his last four appearances, but his limited playing time and modest shot volume continue to restrict his fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Grant supplied 13 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and one block in 23 minutes during Monday's 110-105 victory over Utah.
items.story: The veteran forward paced the second unit in scoring Monday. In spite of the reserve role, Grant should continue to play meaningful minutes on a regular basis to begin the campaign for the rebuilding Grizzlies.

items.headline: Grant finished Wednesday's 123-103 win over the Jazz with 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one block in 24 minutes.
items.story: The veteran forward led the second unit in scoring Wednesday. Despite the bench role, Grant should play significant minutes on a consistent basis to begin the year for the rebuilding Grizzlies.

items.headline: Grant (rest) is off the injury report for Wednesday's season opener against the Jazz.
items.story: The veteran forward had sat out the end of the preseason for maintenance purposes. Grant is expected to open the season in a significant role off the bench in his debut campaign for the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Grant won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Hornets due to soreness, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Grant is dealing with "general soreness," so he will sit out the Grizzlies' final preseason contest. He'll likely be ready to go on Opening Night against the Jazz.

items.headline: Grant finished with 10 points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 14 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over Atlanta.
items.story: Grant came off the bench behind Jaylen Wells but was efficient during his limited run. The two appear to be the primary candidates for Memphis' starting small forward job, though Grant should have a significant role regardless of whether he starts.

items.headline: Grant appears to be among the Grizzlies' candidates for a starting role entering the preseason, Damichael Cole of The Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Memphis experimented with Grant in several lineup combinations during training camp, including extended work alongside GG Jackson. Grant's ability to switch defensively, attack the basket and space the floor gives coach Tuomas Iisalo flexibility, though it's unclear whether the veteran will ultimately start or operate as one of the Grizzlies' primary options off the bench.

items.headline: The Grizzlies are trading Ja Morant (elbow) to the Trail Blazers for Grant and Kris Murray on Monday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Trade speculation had surrounded Morant's name for several months, and Memphis is finally pulling the trigger on a deal. The Grizzlies took Cameron Boozer with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, but Grant still has a chance to start at small forward with his new team in 2026-27. Last regular season, Grant averaged 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.4 three-pointers in 29.7 minutes per game across 57 appearances.

items.headline: Grant supplied 12 points (2-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-8 FT), one rebound, one assist and two steals in 17 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to San Antonio in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grant's 12 points were enough to earn the second-highest total on the team amid anemic performances from the first unit. The Trail Blazers will now look to the offseason, and one of the biggest hurdles for team improvement is Grant's terrible contract. Grant has one year left of a five-year, $160M deal, a price that's almost unheard of for a guy who spent half of the season with the second unit. Grant certainly adds value to the team, but his contract limits the moves they can make while he is still on the payroll.

items.headline: Grant produced 17 points (6-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block over 33 minutes during Sunday's 114-93 loss to San Antonio in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grant comfortably led the second unit in scoring, but it wasn't enough as the Trail Blazers dropped to a 3-1 series deficit. Grant has had a tough series overall, however, as he's averaging 10.0 points and 2.0 rebounds while shooting 35.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Grant accumulated five points (1-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound and one steal across 20 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 win over San Antonio in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Portland was able to pull off the upset victory Tuesday, but Grant didn't play a significant part. The veteran forward has logged 20 minutes or fewer in each of his last three games since returning from an extended absence with a calf strain, and it remains to be seen if he'll see his workload increase at any point this series.

items.headline: Grant (calf) closed Tuesday's 114-110 Play-In Tournament victory over the Suns with 16 points (5-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one block across 19 minutes.
items.story: Grant returned to action after missing the previous seven games due to a right calf strain. Though he came off the bench and his minutes capped, Grant's impact didn't go unnoticed, as he connected on a couple of late three-pointers to help the Trail Blazers rally back to eventually secure the seventh seed in the Western Conference. Assuming he didn't suffer any setbacks, Grant should see an uptick in playing time when Portland faces San Antonio on Sunday in Game 1 of its first-round playoff series.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is available for Tuesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Suns, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Grant will shed his questionable tag and return from a seven-game stint on the sidelines due to a right calf strain to close out the regular season. The veteran forward's return will leave fewer minutes available for reserve players such as Kris Murray and Matisse Thybulle.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is listed as questionable for Tuesday's Play-In Game  against the Suns.
items.story: Grant holds a questionable tag after missing the final seven games of the regular season due to a right calf strain. Averaging 18.6 points across 57 regular-season contests, the veteran wing would provide a welcome scoring boost as the Trail Blazers look to secure the No. 7 seed with a win over the Suns. Grant has started each of his past 24 appearances, though it's possible he comes off the bench (if active) with the team rolling out a starting five of Scoot Henderson, Jrue Holiday, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is out for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Kings.
items.story: A calf issue will cause Grant to miss his seventh game in a row to close out the regular season. It remains to be seen if he'll be available for the Play-In Tournament.

items.headline: Grant (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Grant will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right calf strain and is without a clear timetable for a return to action. The veteran forward's next chance to play will come in Sunday's regular-season finale against the Kings.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Grant will miss his fifth consecutive game Wednesday night. As a result, he will have two more chances to suit up before the start of the Play-In Tournament. With Grant out again, Scoot Henderson will presumably remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is listed as out for Monday's game in Denver.
items.story: Grant will miss his fourth consecutive contest because of a strained right calf. With four games remaining on the Blazers' regular-season schedule, the team is running out of time to get Grant back on the floor. While he remains sidelined, Scoot Henderson is expected to stay in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Grant (calf) won't play in Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Grant will miss another game as a result of a calf strain. While he is on the shelf, Scoot Henderson is expected to remain with the first unit after starting the last two contests.

items.headline: Grant won't play in Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Grant will miss a second consecutive contest, and his next opportunity to suit up will be Thursday versus the visiting Pelicans. With the veteran forward out again, Scoot Henderson may find himself back in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Grant (calf) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Grant picked up a right calf injury in Friday's game against Dallas, and the issue is officially being labeled as a strain. Grant's absence could mean more minutes for Sidy Cissoko and Matisse Thybulle. Grant's next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Grant won't return to Friday's game against the Mavericks due to a right calf injury. He'll finish with 19 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 9-12 FT), four rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 29 minutes.
items.story: Grant finished the third quarter but won't return for the remainder of the contest due to the calf injury. The veteran forward's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game against Washington.

items.headline: Grant notched 18 points (7-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt), two rebounds and one block over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 130-99 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Making his return from a two-game absence due to a foot injury, Grant was his usual dangerous self from long distance. The veteran forward has drained multiple three-pointers in nine of his 11 appearances in March, averaging 17.5 points, 3.4 boards, 2.8 threes, 1.8 assists and 1.1 steals on the month while shooting 40.8 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Grant (foot) will play Wednesday versus the Bucks, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Grant is back after a two-game stint on the sidelines, which will likely result in fewer minutes for Sidy Cissoko. Grant is averaging 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.4 triples per game this season.

items.headline: Grant (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Grant may miss a third straight game due to left foot soreness, which would leave more minutes available for guys like Sidy Cissoko and Kris Murray. Over his last five outings, Grant has averaged 15.0 points, 3.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grant (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Grant will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to left foot soreness, and his next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Milwaukee. With the veteran forward sidelined, Sidy Cissoko, Matisse Thybulle and Kris Murray are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Grant (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nuggets, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Grant will not play Sunday due to left foot soreness, which will be his first missed game since Jan. 18. His next chance to play will be in the second leg of the Trail Blazers' back-to-back set against the Nets on Monday. Sidy Cissoko and Kris Murray figure to be the top candidates to fill in for Grant in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Edey had eight points (3-3 FG, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist and one block over 23 minutes during Monday's 117-111 win over Charlotte.
items.story: Edey bounced back on the glass after collecting just four rebounds across his previous two appearances. He's averaging 12.5 points and 6.3 rebounds over his last four games, though his playing time remains limited to roughly 20-25 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Edey (hip) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Saturday's game versus Minnesota.
items.story: Edey didn't suit up for Thursday's 126-98 win over the Warriors, though he will be back on the floor Saturday against the Timberwolves. Edey's return likely would have sent Taylor Hendricks to the bench. However, with Cameron Boozer (ankle) and Jerami Grant (calf) ruled out, Hendricks has a chance to remain with the first five.

items.headline: Edey (hip) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Edey is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back. If healthy, Isaiah Stewart (illness) would draw the spot start at center in all likelihood.

items.headline: Edey finished with 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two steals in 21 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 124-121 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Edey followed Monday's 23-point double-double with just two rebounds, as six fouls limited his effectiveness. He's played between 20 and 23 minutes in each of his last five appearances, restricting his ceiling despite efficient interior scoring. His rebounding and blocking upside remains attractive, but inconsistent production limits his reliability.

items.headline: Edey provided 23 points (10-15 FG, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and one block across 21 minutes during Monday's 136-120 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Edey finally came through for fantasy managers, recording just his second double-double of the season, including a season-high 23 points. Although the playing time continues to be a source of frustration, the production was a welcome sight. The Grizzlies will next face the Cavaliers on Wednesday, where Edey will look to continue building on what has been a modest start to the season.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Edey missed the previous two games due to a left ankle injury, but the Grizzlies' big man will return to the lineup versus Washington. Isaiah Stewart has been ruled out due to an illness, leaving Quinten Post as Edey's top backup for the road tilt.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against Washington.
items.story: Edey is in danger of missing a third straight matchup as he works back from a left ankle injury. The team should have another update on his availability as tip-off approaches.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is listed as out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: It will be a second consecutive absence for Edey. His next opportunity to get back on the floor will come Monday in Washington. In the meantime, Isaiah Stewart is in line to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Edey sat out Memphis' game Friday due to an ankle injury, and he is now at risk of missing both legs of this back-to-back set. With Quinten Post (concussion) already having been ruled out, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks remain the likely candidates to pick up extra minutes if Edey doesn't play.

items.headline: Edey won't play in Friday's game against the Pelicans due to left ankle injury management.
items.story: Edey will get the night off after appearing in eight straight games for the Grizzlies. Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks are next in line for minutes at center considering both Edey and Quinten Post (concussion) are listed out for Friday.

items.headline: Edey recorded eight points (2-3 FG, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, one assist and one block over 23 minutes during Monday's 118-102 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Edey continues to be a source of frustration rather than production, playing limited minutes on a nightly basis despite starting every game thus far. Coming off a significant injury last season, it appears as though Memphis is taking an ultra-cautious approach, restricting Edey to no more than about 24 minutes per game. Through nine appearances, he is averaging just 8.2 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.3 blocks, barely making him a top-140 player during that time.

items.headline: Edey delivered 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-5 FT), 13 rebounds, an assist and two blocks across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Edey delivered his first double-double of the season while providing two blocks despite playing just 25 minutes. His efficient shooting and strong rebounding helped compensate for limited offensive opportunities. Edey's fantasy value remains anchored by rebounds, field-goal percentage and rim protection, although his modest playing time and scoring figures can restrict his overall ceiling. He's averaging just 7.4 points, 8.1 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game.

items.headline: Edey provided six points (2-6 FG, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 19 minutes before fouling out of Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Edey was limited to no more than 20 minutes for the third straight game, providing endless headaches for fantasy managers. It's clear that Memphis is taking a cautious approach when it comes to ramping Edey up, while foul trouble has also been an ongoing concern. He is currently well outside the top-100 players through six games, averaging 6.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in just 20.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Edey produced four points (0-2 FG, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 21 minutes during Monday's 110-105 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Edey was back in the rotation after missing Sunday's game due to injury management. While it was great to see him back on the floor, early foul trouble limited him to just 21 minutes. It continues what has been a rough start to the season, both in terms of production and minutes played. With that said, Memphis is well within its rights to play it safe, given that Edey is coming off a relatively significant foot injury. He remains a clear hold, although managers may have to expect plenty of ups and downs, at least for the first month of the season.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is off the injury report for Monday's game versus Utah.
items.story: This was the expectation after Edey sat out the first part of this back-to-back set for maintenance reasons. The Grizzlies appear to be easing the big man into a full workload after he missed the start of training camp due to ankle and elbow surgeries, as Edey has yet to transcend 22 minutes in either of his first two regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Edey has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Sacramento due to left ankle injury management.
items.story: Edey will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set. With the big man unavailable, Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Edey posted eight points (4-6 FG, 0-1 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes during Friday's 111-108 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: The third-year center came up one bucket short of his first double-double of the season. Edey saw his workload managed for a second straight game after playing only 11 regular-season games in 2025-26 due to ankle surgery, but he's still averaging 9.5 boards a game even when limited to minutes in the low 20s. Once the Grizzlies begin to let him loose, the 24-year-old should start dominating the glass again.

items.headline: Edey posted six points (3-5 FG), nine rebounds and two blocks across 21 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Edey grabbed three offensive rebounds and protected the rim effectively despite playing just 21 minutes in his first regular-season appearance following two left ankle surgeries earlier this year. Memphis has emphasized managing the center's workload carefully, which could limit his immediate fantasy ceiling. Nevertheless, his rebounding and shot-blocking production in relatively modest minutes illustrates the value he can provide as his conditioning improves.

items.headline: Memphis exercised Edey's team option Tuesday.
items.story: Edey is now officially under team control until at least 2028-29. The third-year big man is healthy this fall and set for a big role at center for the rebuilding Grizzlies.

items.headline: Edey logged 10 points (3-5 FG, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block over 21 minutes in Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Edey scored 10 points in his second straight game, and his minutes gradually climbed during the preseason. The third-year center appears to be trending toward a full regular-season workload, a promising sign for Memphis fans who have waited a while to see his full potential.

items.headline: Edey tallied 10 points (3-3 FG, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, two steals and one block over 16 minutes in Friday's 104-100 preseason win over the Bulls.
items.story: Edey also committed three turnovers without handing out a single dime in his limited floor time, and ball security has been a bit of an issue for him. Though it's just an 11-game sample, Edey averaged 2.4 turnovers in 25.8 minutes per game last season. Still, he's an elite rebounder and shot blocker, so if he can stay healthy, Edey could easily be a top-60 player.

items.headline: Edey will play in Friday's preseason game against the Bulls and is expected to see an uptick in minutes, Rob Fischer of FanDuel Sports Network Southeast reports.
items.story: Edey made his 2026 preseason debut in Wednesday's loss to Orlando, posting two points, four rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block in 10 minutes. He underwent surgeries on his left elbow and ankle in March, and the big man will likely continue ramping up his workload ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) will play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Magic, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Although he'll play limited minutes Wednesday, it appears Edey has made swift progress in his recovery from elbow and ankle surgeries after the Grizzlies initially had Opening Night as the big man's target for a return. He's in the starting lineup, and fantasy managers should feel a bit better about drafting Edey at his ADP now that he's healthy.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) completed a full on-court workout Monday but won't play in the Grizzlies' preseason game against the Hawks, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: As expected, Edey will be held out of the Grizzlies' preseason opener, and it's not yet clear whether he'll play at all during the preseason. However, the big man is trending toward suiting up for Opening Night after undergoing surgeries on his left elbow and ankle in March.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) is not in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against the Hawks, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Edey is not expected to play in Monday's exhibition, and it's unclear if he'll suit up at all for the preseason. However, he is expected to be ready for the start of the regular season. Edey was active at training camp, participating in all practices and 5-on-5 work, and he's reportedly moving around exceptionally well following ankle surgery in March.

items.headline: Edey (ankle) remains on track for Opening Night, per Drew Hill of The Daily Memphian.
items.story: The Grizzlies continue to evaluate Edey throughout training camp, and they believe he's trending in the right direction. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on his recovery from elbow and ankle surgeries.

items.headline: General manager Zach Kleiman said Monday that Edey (ankle/elbow) has been cleared for on-court activity and is on pace to suit up for Memphis' regular-season opener against the Jazz on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Edey still hasn't been ruled out for the preseason, so there's a chance he will see some run ahead of the regular-season opener. The big man underwent surgeries on his left elbow and ankle in March, though he's trending in the right direction ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. The Purdue product appeared in only 11 regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.9 blocks, 1.1 assists and 0.6 steals in 25.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Edey's (ankle, elbow) role becomes more intriguing following Memphis' addition of Cameron Boozer with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The young center has shown encouraging development during his first two seasons and still projects to receive significant frontcourt minutes. However, Memphis now possesses additional depth in the frontcourt, creating some uncertainty regarding lineup combinations. Injuries have limited Edey to 66 regular-season appearances through two years, so his health is a far bigger concern.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced that Edey (ankle) underwent a procedure Tuesday to address lingering discomfort in his left elbow.
items.story: Since he's already been in rehab mode and was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing surgery March 3 to address ongoing discomfort and bone stress in his left ankle, Edey opted to get his aching elbow taken care of with another procedure. Edey is expected to make a full recovery from both the ankle surgery and elbow procedure prior to the start of training camp. Before being shut down in mid-December due to the ankle issue, Edey looked to be in line for a second-year breakout, as he had converted at a 63.3 percent clip from the field and posted averages of 13.6 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.9 blocks, 1.1 assists and 0.6 steals in 25.8 minutes per game over his 11 appearances. The Grizzlies view the 7-foot-3 big man as a key building block and will plan for him to settle back in as their starting center in 2026-27 so long as he's able to stay healthy.

items.headline: Edey underwent surgery Tuesday to resolve discomfort and bone stress in his left ankle, and he'll miss the rest of the 2025-26 season.
items.story: Memphis announced Sunday that Edey would require surgery, but he wasn't officially ruled out for the rest of the season until after going under the knife Tuesday. The club expects the big man to make a full recovery ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced Sunday that Edey is without a timetable for a return and will undergo surgery to address lingering discomfort and talar bone stress in his left ankle.
items.story: Edey underwent surgery on the same ankle last June and hasn't played since Dec. 7 due to the ongoing injury. Memphis is expected to provide a clearer timeline for the big man's return to action following his surgery, though it wouldn't be shocking to see the 22-36 Grizzlies shut him down for the remainder of the season. On a more positive note, the 2024 first-rounder is expected to make a full recovery.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced Wednesday that Edey continues to recover from a stress reaction in his left ankle and will maintain his current plan of offloading and rehabilitation before being re-evaluated in six weeks.
items.story: After Edey initially sustained the injury Dec. 11, the Grizzlies relayed that the second-year center would be shut down for at least four weeks before being re-evaluated. Despite having spent the past month rehabbing the injury, Edey seemingly hasn't taken any major steps forward in his recovery and will now need another six weeks to let his ankle heal up. As a result of this latest update, Edey appears unlikely to be ready to return to game action until at least early March, making it tough to justify rostering him in most redraft formats. With Brandon Clarke (calf) also facing a long-term absence, Jock Landale should continue to hold down the fort as the Grizzlies' starting center.

items.headline: Head coach Tuomas Iisalo said Sunday that Edey (ankle) will travel with the Grizzlies for Thursday's game against the Magic in Berlin, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Edey is set to miss his 15th straight game Sunday as he recovers from a stress reaction in his left foot. However, he's traveling with the team to Europe and could return against Orlando on Thursday or in next Sunday's rematch against the Magic in London. Iisalo also relayed that an update on the big man's progress is expected soon. If he remains on the shelf, Jock Landale will likely continue to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Gobert accumulated seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Gobert started to turn things around Saturday, blocking at least three shots for just the second time this season. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

items.headline: Gobert posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

items.headline: Gobert finished with 18 points (5-10 FG, 8-14 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 32 minutes during Monday's 106-98 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Gobert left points on the table at the charity stripe, though he still erupted for a season-high mark in points while finishing as Minnesota's second-leading scorer. The big man also led all players in rebounds, securing his third double-double of the campaign. He's grabbed double-digit boards in six of his seven outings this month, during which he's averaged 9.1 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 blocks in 28.9 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Gobert ended Sunday's 115-100 victory over Utah with 10 points (4-4 FG, 2-4 FT), 15 rebounds and two assists over 31 minutes.
items.story: Gobert controlled the glass, grabbing a game-high 15 rebounds while converting all four of his field-goal attempts. The veteran center recorded his double-double despite failing to register a steal or block, limiting his overall fantasy production. Gobert remains a dependable source of rebounds and field-goal percentage, with his defensive contributions typically providing additional upside.

items.headline: Gobert ended Wednesday's 117-107 victory over the Rockets with eight points (3-7 FG, 2-6 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, four blocks and one steal over 33 minutes.
items.story: Gobert blocked a season-high four shots, rewarding fantasy managers who stuck with him. It's been a somewhat underwhelming start to the season for the veteran center on both ends of the floor. Through eight games, he is averaging 7.5 points, 11.9 rebounds and 1.0 blocks, shooting 42.6 percent from the field and 42.6 percent from the line.

items.headline: Gobert (back) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Gobert didn't play in Saturday's 121-111 loss to the Spurs due to a back issue. However, he will be back on the floor Monday versus the Kings. With Gobert available, Joan Beringer, who started against San Antonio, is projected to head back to the bench.

items.headline: Gobert (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
items.story: Gobert will miss his first game of the season Saturday, which could result in Joan Beringer getting the start. Trey Lyles could also see a bump in minutes. For now, Gobert should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Milwaukee.

items.headline: Gobert (back) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game at San Antonio.
items.story: Gobert is a late addition to the injury report, so his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's 8:00 p.m. ET tipoff. Joan Beringer would likely be the top candidate to enter the Timberwolves' starting lineup if Gobert is not cleared to play in the second leg of the team's back-to-back set.

items.headline: Gobert amassed nine points (4-7 FG, 1-3 FT), 13 rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Friday's 127-101 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Gobert continues to struggle on offense, as this was the fifth time in six games that he scored in single digits, but he grabbed at least 13 rebounds for the fourth time in that span. Gobert has just three blocks this season, averaging 0.5 per game, so he's not the elite rim protector he once was. While he's not expected to lose his starting role, Gobert has showing signs of a decline, and he's no longer the automatic starter he was in past seasons. His offensive woes are too big to overlook, and he doesn't  do much in other categories outside of rebounds.

items.headline: Gobert produced one point (0-4 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 119-114 loss to Golden State.
items.story: The veteran big man failed to capitalize on the extra opportunity left behind by Anthony Edwards (knee), who is set to miss multiple weeks. Even so, Gobert should find himself being more involved in the Minnesota offense for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Gobert registered five points (0-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-8 FT), 20 rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block across 36 minutes in Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Gobert dominated the glass en route to a season-high 20 rebounds, including eight offensive boards, but his horrendous shooting performance prevented him from delivering a massive stat line. Gobert's elite rebounding should continue and provides a strong fantasy foundation, but his limited scoring and occasional free-throw struggles remain significant drawbacks in certain formats. He's failed to score in double digits in three of his first four appearances, a major downgrade for a player who has averaged double-digit points in each of his last 10 seasons.

items.headline: Gobert registered five points (0-2 FG, 5-8 FT), 15 rebounds and one assist in 33 minutes during Wednesday's 131-106 win over the Heat.
items.story: Gobert attempted only two shots on a night when Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball combined for 66 points on 46 attempts. However, Gobert led all players in rebounds and posted a game-best plus-29 in his 33 minutes. Offense has never been Gobert's strong suit, but as the defensive anchor for Minnesota, he'll contribute heavily to boards and, on most nights, blocks and steals.

items.headline: Gobert (rest) is expected to be available for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Gobert was one of many Timberwolves regulars who sat out the preseason finale, though the big man should be available Wednesday. He averaged 5.8 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.9 minutes per game across four appearances this preseason.

items.headline: Gobert (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the Bulls, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network reports.
items.story: Gobert, Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu are all resting for the final exhibition. Gobert should be good to go for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.

items.headline: Gobert finished with eight points (3-4 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Gobert converted three of his four attempts from the field but was unusually quiet on the glass, collecting just four rebounds while failing to register a block. Minnesota struggled to contain Detroit's interior attack, though Gobert's established role as the team's defensive anchor should remain secure entering the regular season.

items.headline: Gobert (rest) is in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against the Knicks.
items.story: After resting Saturday, Gobert will return to the starting lineup at Madison Square Garden. In two preseason games, the veteran center is averaging 6.5 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 17.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gobert (rest) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Gobert and several other prominent Timberwolves players will be idle for Saturday's exhibition contest. The veteran center's next chance to play is Monday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Gobert registered six points (3-4 FG) and seven rebounds across 17 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: Gobert handled his customary starting role at center and did exactly what was expected during his limited preseason workload, converting three of four attempts around the basket and grabbing a team-high seven rebounds among Minnesota's starters. The veteran center didn't record a block, but his fantasy appeal has long been driven primarily by elite rebounding, field-goal percentage and rim protection. With Minnesota changing several pieces around him this offseason, Gobert remains the established anchor of the team's frontcourt. His playing time in the preseason might be limited, but that's only because he's set to open the regular season as a key piece in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Gobert continues to work on expanding his offensive game, including participating in three-point drills with his teammates, Andrew Dukowitz of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
items.story: Gobert said shooting was an area of emphasis during the offseason and noted that competing with teammates in drills has helped make taking jumpers feel more natural in game-like situations. While it's unclear whether three-pointers will become a meaningful part of his offensive role, Gobert has worked on his perimeter shooting in previous offseasons as well.

items.headline: Gobert sat out France's 84-69 win over Sweden in Sunday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Gobert did suit up for France's victory over Slovenia on Thursday, so Sunday appeared to be a maintenance-related absence. The veteran center is getting ready for his fifth season with the Timberwolves in 2026-27, and it's plausible that Minnesota will rely even more on Gobert now that big man Naz Reid has been sent to Charlotte in exchange for star point guard LaMelo Ball. Gobert has averaged a double-double and at least one block while shooting no lower than 62 percent from the field in 10 consecutive seasons.

items.headline: Gobert should benefit from sharing the floor with one of the league's best passers in LaMelo Ball, according to Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports.
items.story: Minnesota's lack of a traditional point guard had occasionally limited Gobert's offensive opportunities, and Ball's pick-and-roll ability could help maximize the veteran center's efficiency. However, the departures of Naz Reid and Julius Randle may place additional frontcourt responsibilities on Gobert entering his age-34 season, as Jaden McDaniels is now expected to start at power forward.

items.headline: Gobert registered zero points (0-4 FG) and three rebounds over 22 minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to the Spurs in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Gobert struggled mightily during Friday's loss, failing to score for the first time this postseason while playing just 22 minutes. It was a disappointing end to the 2025-26 campaign for Gobert, who finished the regular season averaging 10.9 points, 11.5 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.6 blocks over 31.3 minutes per game. The veteran center is slated to make $36.5 million in 2026-27, though it's possible the Timberwolves reshape the roster around Anthony Edwards this offseason by moving Gobert, per Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic.

items.headline: Gobert logged four points (1-4 FG, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two steals and one block across 23 minutes during Tuesday's 126-97 loss to San Antonio in Game 5 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: After scoring in double figures in back-to-back games, Gobert struggled offensively Tuesday and played a series-low 23 minutes. The veteran center also failed to make much of an impact on the glass, matching his season low in rebounds across the regular season and playoffs. The Timberwolves will likely need the big man to bounce back in Game 6 on Friday if they hope to keep their season alive.

items.headline: Maluach provided 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds over 21 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 win over Sacramento.
items.story: After initially being a popular breakout candidate in fantasy circles amid Mark Williams' (shoulder) absence, Maluach has found himself stuck in a dead-even timeshare at center with Oso Ighodaro in the early going. Maluach has been only a deep-league option since Ighodaro took over as the starter, with the former averaging 7.9 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 17.8 minutes per game over his last eight appearances.

items.headline: Maluach closed with 11 points (4-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds and three assists over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 133-110 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Maluach was efficient off the bench, though five personal fouls and a lack of defensive stats capped his overall line. He has come off the bench since Oso Ighodaro moved into the starting lineup last week, but the two continue to split center minutes in what is shaping up to be a timeshare. That limits Maluach's ceiling for now, but he has more upside than Ighodaro and is worth holding in deeper leagues, particularly for those seeking traditional big-man numbers.

items.headline: Maluach closed with eight points (4-6 FG), six rebounds, two assists and two steals across 22 minutes during Thursday's 117-104 win over Orlando.
items.story: Maluach made the most of his opportunities, shooting efficiently while tying for the team lead in steals. The young center logged nearly as much playing time as starter Oso Ighodaro, who finished with just two points and five rebounds in 24 minutes. Maluach's encouraging performance could help him earn additional opportunities, though his reserve role limits his immediate fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Maluach isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Maluach has witnessed his workload decrease over his last three matchups, as he's averaged 15.3 minutes per game after logging 23.7 minutes per contest in his first three showings of the new campaign. He'll be deployed off the bench for the first time this season Thursday, making way for Oso Ighodaro to enter the starting five.

items.headline: Maluach registered five points (2-3 FG, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one block and one steal over 13 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Maluach started at center but played sparingly, with Oso Ighodaro receiving 24 minutes off the bench and finishing with 14 points. The rookie made the most of his limited offensive opportunities and contributed a pair of defensive statistics, but his playing time remains a significant obstacle to consistent fantasy production.

items.headline: Maluach posted 12 points (5-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 26 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Maluach delivered a solid performance in his third start of the season, reaching double figures in scoring while contributing on the glass and defensively. However, the young center also committed four turnovers and four personal fouls. With Mark Williams (shoulder) sidelined and Oso Ighodaro (oblique) still out, Maluach should continue receiving significant opportunities in Phoenix's frontcourt, making him an intriguing fantasy option for managers seeking rebounds and blocks.

items.headline: Maluach logged nine points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), nine rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 28 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Maluach fell just short of a double-double while also adding three combined steals and blocks. With Oso Ighodaro (oblique) sidelined, Maluach is basically the last man standing when it comes to center minutes. Seen as a potential breakout candidate this season, it's clear that the path forward is going to be a bumpy one. With that said, there is certainly enough upside to warrant holding in most leagues, particularly for those needing traditional big-man numbers.

items.headline: Maluach will start in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Trail Blazers, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Maluach will start over Oso Ighodaro on Opening Night, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges. Maluach can rack up the boards and defensive stats when given the minutes, so getting the starting nod in the regular-season opener is great for his fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Maluach finished with seven points (2-4 FG, 3-4 FT), 12 rebounds, one steal and one block over 24 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason loss to Utah.
items.story: Maluach had another subpar scoring effort, though he recorded a block for the third consecutive game while securing his second double-digit rebounding performance of the preseason. With Mark Williams (shoulder) sidelined indefinitely, Maluach will come off the bench behind Oso Ighodaro, at least to begin the 2026-27 campaign. The 20-year-old could also start if Ighodaro gets injured or doesn't play well.

items.headline: Maluach closed with 10 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 23 minutes during Saturday's 102-98 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Maluach moved into the starting lineup in place of Oso Ighodaro, who shifted back to the bench. The move worked wonders for Maluach, allowing him to put up what was easily his best game of the preseason. With Mark Williams (shoulder) sidelined indefinitely, both Maluach and Ighodaro have a chance to carve out meaningful roles. Even if he does come off the bench, it appears as though Maluach is the player fantasy managers will want to be targeting in drafts, likely in the 100 range.

items.headline: Maluach will be in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Spurs, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Oso Ighodaro started Phoenix's first two preseason games, but now Maluach will have an opportunity to make a case for himself as a starter. Joining him in the first unit for Saturday's exhibition will be Jalen Green, Luke Kennard, Dillon Brooks and Ryan Dunn.

items.headline: Maluach closed with six points (3-5 FG, 0-3 FT, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one block in 17 minutes during Monday's 109-107 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Maluach came off the bench in the preseason opener, perhaps a sign of what's to come once the regular season gets underway. While he did log more minutes than Oso Ighodaro, Maluach's production left a lot to be desired, particularly on the offensive end. Of the two players, Maluach likely has more upside when considering him with a late-round pick. However, managers should temper their expectations, at least until we have a decent sample size of what he is capable of during competitive NBA basketball.

items.headline: The Suns exercised the team's third-year option for 2027-28 on Maluach on Thursday.
items.story: This was a no-brainer decision after Maluach was selected in the first round last year. The second-year big man could be primed to take on a significantly larger role in Phoenix's frontcourt, which has a major void due to Mark Williams' offseason shoulder injury, and the camp battle between Maluach and Oso Ighodaro for the top center spot could stretch all the way up until the end of the preseason.

items.headline: Maluach earned significant praise from Devin Booker on Monday for the progress he's made during the offseason, Shane Young of the Suns' official site reports.
items.story: "I'd say he's taken the biggest leap of anyone I've seen this summer," Booker said of the second-year center. Maluach averaged just 8.9 minutes across 46 regular-season appearances as a rookie, but he followed that limited role with an impressive showing at Summer League. Booker's strong praise provides another encouraging sign that Maluach could be ready to take on a substantially larger role in Phoenix's frontcourt, which has a major void due to Mark Williams' offseason shoulder injury.

items.headline: The door is open for Maluach to start at center for the Suns in the wake of Mark Williams' offseason shoulder surgery, Bobby Marks of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The 2025 first-rounder is coming off a promising Summer League run, averaging 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 53.2 percent from the floor over four appearances. Williams is expected to miss around five months, so the runway with Phoenix's top spot at center could be a long one. Maluach does have Oso Ighodaro to overcome for the role, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on what projects to be a fierce camp competition.

items.headline: Maluach is set to battle with Oso Ighodaro for the top backup role at center behind Mark Williams during training camp.
items.story: The 19-year-old big man put forth a dominant Summer League run, averaging 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 53.2 percent from the field over four appearances. Ighodaro is the early favorite to handle the No. 2 center minutes behind Williams, though a strong showing at camp could force the Suns to give Maluach more consideration.

items.headline: The Suns are shutting down Maluach (rest) for the rest of the Las Vegas Summer League, per John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM.
items.story: Maluach put together an encouraging Las Vegas Summer League run, scoring at least 15 points in four appearances while registering three double-doubles as well. The 2025 first-rounder is next set to battle with Oso Ighodaro for the top backup role at center behind Mark Williams during training camp.

items.headline: Maluach tallied 23 points (8-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-9 FT), 15 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 100-88 Summer League win over the Pistons.
items.story: Maluach led his team with 23 points and pulled down a game-high 15 rebounds as part of a winning effort. The second-year center has impressed throughout the Las Vegas Summer League, scoring at least 15 points in all four appearances while recording a double-double in three straight contests. The Duke product played sparingly at the NBA level during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 3.0 points and 2.9 rebounds in 8.9 minutes across 46 regular-season appearances (one start).

items.headline: Maluach finished with 21 points (5-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks across 27 minutes in Monday's 95-88 Summer League win over the Bucks.
items.story: Maluach had another dominant performance Monday, recording his third double-double in as many games. The 2025 No. 10 overall pick out of Duke appeared in 46 regular-season games for the Suns during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 3.0 points, 2.9 rebounds, 0.1 assists, 0.7 blocks and 0.1 steals over 8.9 minutes. Maluach is still young, so he has more work to do to develop his game. However, with Mark Williams having trouble staying healthy over the years, it wouldn't be surprising to see Maluach make some starts in 2026-27. Even if he doesn't, it's still reasonable to believe he will be more productive than he was during his inaugural season.

items.headline: Maluach recorded 15 points (5-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 15 rebounds, one assist and one steal over 28 minutes during the Suns' 81-75 Summer League loss to the Pelicans on Sunday.
items.story: It was the second double-double in as many Summer League games for Maluach, who hauled in 15 of the Suns' 41 rebounds while finishing as the team's second-leading scorer behind Darius Brown (18 points). Maluach was a first-round pick of the Suns in the 2025 NBA Draft but averaged just 8.9 minutes per game in his rookie season. He figures to enter training camp competing with Oso Ighodaro for backup minutes at center behind Mark Williams (foot).

items.headline: Maluach finished with 19 points (7-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 11 rebounds, two steals and one block across 26 minutes in Friday's 81-79 Summer League win over Portland.
items.story: Maluach had a 19-point, 11-rebound double-double to begin his time in Las Vegas. He was efficient from deep, though he had trouble taking care of the ball and committed a game-high seven turnovers. The 2025 No. 10 overall pick appeared in 46 regular-season games for Phoenix during the 2025-26 campaign, finishing with averages of 3.0 points, 2.9 rebounds, 0.1 assists, 0.7 blocks and 0.1 steals over 8.9 minutes. Maluach is currently listed behind Mark Williams and Oso Ighodaro on the depth chart, but he will likely need to clean up some things before earning consistent minutes for the Suns in 2026-27.

items.headline: Maluach chipped in two points (1-1 FG) and two rebounds across five minutes during Monday's 131-122 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder struggled to earn consistent playing time in 2025-26, finishing with averages of 3.0 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 8.9 minutes per tilt across 46 regular-season games. Barring the Suns losing Mark Williams (foot) in restricted free agency, Maluach might have a hard time cracking Phoenix's Opening Night rotation in 2026-27 with Oso Ighodaro also in the picture.

items.headline: Maluach closed with zero points (0-2 FG) and three rebounds in 15 minutes during Sunday's 119-84 loss to the Thunder in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Maluach played a handful of extra minutes, as Phoenix was never really in the game against Oklahoma City. With Mark Williams (foot) still sidelined, the Suns' center depth is going to be tested. Based on what we saw in Game 1, there is a chance this series could be over sooner rather than later.

items.headline: Maluach contributed 18 points (8-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt), 14 rebounds, two blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Sunday's 135-103 win over the Thunder.
items.story: With Mark Williams (foot) inactive, Maluach saw extended playing time and made an impact in the interior, recording his first career double-double at the NBA level. It's been a quiet, developmental rookie campaign for the No. 10 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, as he'll close the regular season averaging 3.0 points and 2.9 rebounds in 8.9 minutes across 46 appearances with the Suns.

items.headline: Maluach is not in the Suns' starting lineup against the Lakers on Friday.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder made his first NBA start against the Mavericks on Wednesday, when he played 30 minutes and finished with four points, 14 rebounds and three blocks in a 112-107 win. Maluach will revert to a bench role Friday due to the return of Mark Williams, and the former will be competing with Oso Ighodaro for playing time.

items.headline: Maluach provided four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), 14 rebounds and three blocks across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 112-107 win over Dallas.
items.story: Making his first NBA start, the rookie center didn't make much of an impression on offense, but the 19-year-old set a new career high in boards while swatting multiple shots for the fifth time in his last seven games. Maluach's minutes of late have largely depended on the availability of Mark Williams (foot), and with the Suns having locked up the seventh seed in the Western Conference and the top spot in the Play-In Tournament, the team may elect to shut Williams down for the final two games of the regular season and give Maluach a longer look.

items.headline: Maluach will start Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: With Mark Williams (foot) sidelined, Maluach will get the starting nod for the first time in his NBA career. The rookie first-rounder has averaged 4.0 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks in 11.0 minutes per game across his last 10 appearances, though he'll likely see increased minutes Wednesday.

items.headline: Maluach accumulated seven points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 17 minutes during Sunday's 120-98 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Until Mark Williams (foot) is cleared to make his return to the floor, Maluach has a clear path to the No. 2 center gig behind Oso Ighodaro but is struggling for fantasy relevance. Across his past five appearances, Maluach has averaged 3.4 points, 3.8 rebounds and 0.4 blocks in 14.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Santos will start in Thursday's game versus Memphis.
items.story: Santos has come off the bench in each of the Warriors' last four games but is back in the starting lineup against the Grizzlies. The 24-year-old has started six times during the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 6.7 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists over 20.8 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Santos supplied 12 points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds and two assists across 19 minutes in Monday's 115-94 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Santos generated most of his scoring at the free-throw line, making seven of eight attempts despite connecting on just two field goals. His seven rebounds were also encouraging considering his limited playing time, but the 18-minute workload makes it difficult to expect consistent production. Even with Stephen Curry (oblique) unavailable, Golden State has several players competing for reserve minutes, and Santos will likely need a more substantial role before becoming a reliable fantasy contributor.

items.headline: Santos (ankle) is available for Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Santos will shed a questionable tag due to right ankle inflammation and suit up for Monday's road tilt. After starting six of his first eight appearances this season, the forward came off the bench in Golden State's previous two games and will likely operate as a reserve in New Orleans. Overall, Santos is averaging 5.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 18.6 minutes per contest across 10 appearances (six starts).

items.headline: Santos is questionable for Monday's game against New Orleans due to right ankle inflammation.
items.story: Santos appears to have put a lingering knee injury behind him, but he's now experiencing an issue with his right ankle. He'll presumably test the injury in shootaround and pregame to determine whether he can suit up for Monday's game.

items.headline: Santos won't start Wednesday's game against Houston.
items.story: Al Horford will replace Santos in the first unit Wednesday. The 24-year-old forward is averaging 6.1 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.1 minutes per showing across eight regular-season appearances (six starts).

items.headline: Santos (knee) will play Monday against the Pelicans.
items.story: As expected, Santos will suit up Monday after initially being added to the injury report as probable. He logged 12 minutes Saturday against Orlando in his first game back since Nov. 1, and while the Warriors will continue to keep a close eye on his workload, he's expected to see more run during Monday's clash, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle.

items.headline: Santos (knee) is listed as probable for Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Santos' knee issue isn't anything new, so he'll be on the floor Monday, barring a setback. The 24-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026-27, averaging 6.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 18.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Santos (knee) is active for Saturday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Santos missed Golden State's previous two contests due to a lingering knee issue, but he's ready to suit up after practicing Friday. His return will likely push Will Richard back to the bench, although Santos could be under a minutes restriction in his return.

items.headline: Santos (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game versus Orlando, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: Santos is feeling better, having participated in Friday's practice. Will Richard would likely retreat back to the bench if Santos is able to suit up Saturday.

items.headline: Santos (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Heat.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope supplied 20 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals across 23 minutes off the bench during Friday's 128-121 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Returning from a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue, Caldwell-Pope set a new season scoring high in a very efficient performance. The veteran wing is finding his rhythm with the second unit, scoring in double digits in six of his last seven games and averaging 12.4 points, 2.9 assists, 2.1 boards, 2.0 threes and 1.0 steals in 21.1 minutes, while shooting 50.9 percent from the floor and 48.3 percent from long range.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope (hamstring) is available for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope has been cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a right hamstring injury, which means fewer minutes will be available for the likes of Cam Spencer and GG Jackson. Caldwell-Pope averaged 9.2 points, 3.7 assists, 2.2 rebounds, 1.4 threes and 1.1 steals over 20.5 minutes per game in December.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope (hamstring) is probable for Friday against the Lakers.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope was initially considered questionable for this contest, but he's on track to play. With this news, GG Jackson and Cam Spencer could be a little less involved for the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope injured his right hamstring during the Grizzlies' loss to the Wizards on Sunday, which prevented him from playing against the 76ers on Tuesday. He's averaged 21.8 minutes per game this season, so his return would mean fewer minutes to go around for Cam Spencer and GG Jackson.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope is out for Tuesday's game against the 76ers due to right hamstring soreness.
items.story: The veteran swingman left Sunday's game against the Wizards with the issue, and he'll need at least one contest to recover. His absence should keep GG Jackson in the Memphis rotation, while both Jaylen Wells and Cedric Coward should also help pick up the slack.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope (hamstring) did not return after exiting Sunday's game against the Wizards in the second quarter.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope left Sunday's game with right hamstring soreness and was considered doubtful to return. He wound up missing the rest of the contest. He logged four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one block across 11 minutes before exiting. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against Philadelphia.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Wizards due to right hamstring soreness.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope left Sunday's game in the second quarter and is unlikely to return due to a hamstring injury. Cam Spencer will likely see more minutes with Caldwell-Pope out of the lineup.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope had 16 points (5-6 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists and three rebounds over 21 minutes during Monday's 119-103 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: With Memphis remaining shorthanded, Caldwell-Pope logged 20-plus minutes for a sixth straight game and made the most of the opportunity. The veteran guard delivered a team- and season-high-tying 16 points on extremely efficient shooting from beyond the arc. His five triples marked a season high, which is a positive sign considering he had shot just 33.3 percent from downtown on 3.4 attempts per game in 28 outings before Monday's contest.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope ended with 11 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, five assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Saturday's 130-122 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: The Grizzlies were short-handed with only nine players, so Caldwell-Pope had an enhanced role in the loss. The veteran logged a double-digit scoring total for the 12th time this season, but his secondary numbers were slightly below his usual totals. Caldwell-Pope entered Saturday's game averaging 7.6 points, 3.3 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 0.8 steals across 27 games.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope closed Monday's 121-103 victory over the Clippers with four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 23 minutes.
items.story: While Caldwell-Pope did not take many shots Monday, he contributed in other ways, dishing out six assists, grabbing a season-high seven rebounds and tacking on two steals. Caldwell-Pope figures to retain a sizable role off the bench, though his production has failed to impress during his first season in Memphis.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope notched 16 points (5-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Sunday's 119-96 win over Portland.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope has been stuck in a brutal slump to begin the season, but he finally showed some signs of life Sunday. The 16 points were a season high, a welcome sign as the veteran swingman looks to find his footing during his first year with Memphis. Caldwell-Pope is averaging 8.3 points, 2.8 assists, 1.6 rebounds and 1.8 three-pointers in 20.1 minutes per game over his last eight contests, shooting 51.9 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Caldwell-Pope contributed eight points (2-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and three assists across 21 minutes during Monday's 125-115 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Caldwell-Pope continues to do very little for his new team, having recently shifted to a bench role even though the backcourt is paper-thin right now. Through 18 appearances, the veteran is averaging just 7.5 points and 3.2 assists in 22.9 minutes per game. His days of being a fantasy-relevant player are well behind him, it would seem.

items.headline: James finished with 23 points (8-13 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds and three assists in 30 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
items.story: James pieced together an efficient scoring line and led the Sixers with 23 points, though it wasn't enough to help Philly secure a sixth consecutive victory. He was particularly sharp from beyond the arc, which is a welcome sight considering he was hitting at a clip of 21.7 percent from deep in his first 13 games of the 2026-27 campaign entering Monday. James has put up 20-plus points in three straight appearances and continues to produce across the board, averaging 5.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.0 steals over this brief stretch.

items.headline: James contributed 21 points (9-14 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, six assists, one block and three steals over 35 minutes during Saturday's 132-129 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: The Sixers fielded a very balanced offense on the afternoon, with all five starters plus two bench players scoring at least 12 points, and James' 21 was second only to Joel Embiid's 26. James has topped 20 points in back-to-back games and three times in his last five appearances, a stretch in which the 41-year-old slam-dunk Hall of Famer is averaging 18.2 points, 6.6 assists, 5.8 boards, 0.8 steals and 0.8 threes in 32.2 minutes.

items.headline: James provided 22 points (8-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and six assists over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic.
items.story: James took on additional offensive responsibility with Tyrese Maxey (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) sidelined, helping Philadelphia overcome a 17-point deficit. The veteran forward has scored at least 20 points in two of his last four appearances while continuing to provide reliable playmaking. His fantasy upside could increase if Maxey and Brown remain unavailable, though James' workload will likely continue to be monitored throughout the season.

items.headline: James (back) is available for Wednesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: The future Hall of Famer is off the injury report after sitting out Monday in Brooklyn, which was the back end of a back-to-back set. With Jaylen Brown nursing a strained hamstring, James should take on additional ball-handling duties.

items.headline: James (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nets.
items.story: As expected, James won't play in the second half of Philly's back-to-back set after finishing Sunday's 131-124 victory over Indiana with 15 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and one block across 33 minutes. The veteran superstar has yet to play in both halves of a back-to-back set this season, and that trend is unlikely to change. Dean Wade and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased roles in James' absence.

items.headline: James finished Sunday's 131-124 victory over Indiana with 15 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and one block across 33 minutes.
items.story: The 11 assists were a season high for the future Hall of Famer, who returned Sunday from a one-game respite. James continues to produce at a high level in his age-42 campaign, averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.2 steals per contest in 11 games this season.

items.headline: James (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: James sat out Thursday's game against Toronto with a back injury, but he's been cleared to return to the court Sunday. The future Hall of Famer has averaged 13.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 31.6 minutes across five games since the beginning of November.

items.headline: James (back) is out for Thursday's game against Toronto.
items.story: The future Hall of Famer is getting Thursday night off for maintenace purposes. Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown should do the heavy lifting offensively, while Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope should soak up extra minutes for the 76ers.

items.headline: James (back) remains questionable for Thursday's game against the Raptors, but he participated in the team's morning shootaround, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: James and Joel Embiid (foot) are both trending in the right direction after drawing questionable tags, but their availability has yet to be determined. Even if James is cleared to play Thursday, the lingering back issue is something to monitor. The veteran superstar played a season-low 29 minutes in Tuesday's loss to Boston, and the 76ers have a Sunday-Monday back-to-back set coming up.

items.headline: James (back) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Raptors, Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: The 76ers are considering giving the future Hall of Famer the night off Thursday. Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope would soak up more playing time in the frontcourt if James ends up sitting out.

items.headline: James provided 11 points (4-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and five assists over 29 minutes during Tuesday's 123-101 loss to Boston.
items.story: James struggled with his perimeter shooting, connecting on just one of six three-point attempts, but his eight rebounds and five assists provided useful secondary production. His limited scoring and absence of defensive stats have restricted his fantasy ceiling this season, especially as he's been operating more as a playmaker and less as a scorer in a star-studded 76ers lineup. James continues to offer multi-category value through rebounding and playmaking, though his efficiency and workload remain key factors in his fantasy outlook. He has surpassed the 15-point mark in just one of his last five appearances, averaging 13.8 points, 7.4 rebounds and 6.0 assists per game in that stretch.

items.headline: James supplied 22 points (8-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Sunday's 127-121 win over Chicago.
items.story: After putting up a season-low eight points and three assists in his return to Cleveland on Friday, the future Hall of Famer wasted no time getting back on track Sunday. The 22 points were a season high for James, who's off to a strong start in his 76ers career with averages of 15.6 points, 7.1 rebounds, 6.7 assists and 1.4 steals per game in nine appearances.

items.headline: Ighodaro produced seven points (3-5 FG, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals in 30 minutes during Monday's 123-119 overtime win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Ighodaro recorded a season-high four combined steals-plus-blocks, continuing to provide fantasy managers with serviceable production on that end of the floor. However, the same cannot be said for the rest of his game, making him more of a streaming option rather than a must-roster asset. In seven games over the past two weeks, he has averaged 2.0 combined steals-plus-blocks along with 5.3 points and 5.4 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Ighodaro closed with two points (1-2 FG, 0-2 FT), three rebounds, seven assists and one block in 32 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Ighodaro matched a season high in assists and played his most minutes of the year so far. The Suns seem to have an open competition ongoing between Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach for their top center spot, and the two big men should continue to jockey for playing time going forward.

items.headline: Ighodaro supplied two points (1-2 FG, 0-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block across 24 minutes during Thursday's 117-104 win over the Magic.
items.story: Ighodaro moved into the starting lineup for the first time this season, supplanting Khaman Maluach, who moved to the bench. Despite the promotion, Ighodaro had arguably his worst performance of the season. In five appearances, he is averaging 7.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.0 blocks in 21.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Ighodaro will start Thursday's game against the Magic.
items.story: After coming off the bench in his first four appearances of the campaign, the 24-year-old will get the starting nod over Khaman Maluach on Thursday. Ighodaro is averaging 8.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.0 blocks across 20.8 minutes per contest so far this season.

items.headline: Ighodaro chipped in 14 points (6-6 FG, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one block over 24 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Ighodaro provided an efficient scoring punch off the bench, making all eight of his shots. He also played 11 more minutes than starting center Khaman Maluach, continuing to command a meaningful role in Phoenix's frontcourt. However, Ighodaro's modest rebounding production and limited defensive contributions make him a difficult fantasy option to trust consistently.

items.headline: Ighodaro (oblique) is available for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Ighodaro was injured on Opening Night and missed the Suns' next two regular-season contests. He is now cleared to suit up versus Denver, potentially resulting in less work for Khaman Maluach. However, Ighodaro will operate under an unspecified minutes restriction, per John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM.

items.headline: Ighodaro (oblique) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Denver.
