items.story: Dunn was an extremely late addition to the injury report, which isn't a positive sign ahead of tipoff at 11:00 p.m. ET. If the second-year forward is ultimately ruled out, Rasheer Fleming would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Dunn closed with 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals across 27 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 120-98 win over the Raptors.
items.story: The second-year forward made an impact at the defensive end, with his four combined steals and blocks being his best effort at that end of the court since Jan. 27. Dunn has played at least 20 minutes in three straight games as Phoenix deals with injuries to its frontcourt, averaging 9.7 points, 6.3 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.7 threes in 23.3 minutes over that span.

items.headline: Dunn recorded 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 108-105 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Dunn had his best night in quite some time, recording double-digit scoring for the first time in his past 10 games, while also adding a pair of defensive stats. While this was certainly an encouraging performance, his recent lack of production cannot be overlooked. In 14 games over the past month, he has been barely a top-300 player, averaging 5.0 points and 4.5 rebounds in 19.3 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Dunn (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Friday's 122-115 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Dunn had been seeing his playing time trend down recently, but Friday marked the first time all season that the second-year forward failed to see any action for non-injury reasons. Though he's regarded as a versatile defender, Dunn's perimeter shooting hasn't developed as the Suns had hoped, as he's converting on just 32.6 percent of his three-point attempts on the season. Now that the Suns are at full strength on the wing and at forward sans Dillon Brooks (hand), Dunn looks like he could find himself outside of the rotation more often than not while head coach Jordan Ott prioritizes Grayson Allen, Haywood Highsmith and Rasheer Fleming in the second unit.

items.headline: Dunn won't start against the Kings on Tuesday.
items.story: With Devin Booker (hip) back in action following a four-game absence, Dunn will retreat to the second unit. Over eight outings off the bench in February, the second-year forward averaged 4.1 points and 3.1 rebounds across 15.9 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Dunn will start Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Dunn will make his first start since Nov. 21 due to Dillon Brooks (hand) being out of the lineup. Dunn has seen at least 20 minutes in each of his last three appearances, averaging 2.3 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 22.0 minutes per game over that stretch.

items.headline: Dunn registered nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and four steals in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 106-102 victory over the Nets.
items.story: The four steals were one short of a season high for Dunn, whose 21 minutes were also his most since Jan. 7. Dunn hasn't scored in double figures since Nov. 16 and has seen single-digit minutes in two of his last four games, so he's not doing enough to warrant much attention in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Dunn recorded three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 17 minutes during Monday's 126-117 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Dunn continues to play a secondary role off the bench, having logged fewer than 20 minutes in six straight games. Even when he has been afforded starter-level minutes, Dunn has been unable to produce at a standard league level. In his current role, he holds very little value outside of deeper formats.

items.headline: Dunn logged seven points (3-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and one steal over 12 minutes during Friday's 112-107 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Dunn logged a season-low 12 minutes, though he was productive during his limited run. He led the second unit in assists, dishing out at least three dimes for the first time since Dec. 20. Dunn hasn't scored in double figures since Nov. 16 and doesn't offer much fantasy value outside of some solid performances on the glass. Still, he had totaled only two rebounds in his past two games entering Friday's tilt. If and when the team returns to full strength, the second-year forward could struggle to earn significant burn on a nightly basis.

items.headline: Dunn chipped in five points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and one rebound in 16 minutes during Monday's 100-97 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Dunn failed to produce anything of note, another in a string of underwhelming performances. After opening the season as a starter, Dunn has since shifted to a bench role, averaging 5.3 points and 4.9 rebounds in 19.9 minutes per game over his last 11 appearances.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is available for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Dunn will return from a two-game absence due to a right knee injury, which will likely leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Rasheer Fleming, Isaiah Livers and Jordan Goodwin. Dunn has averaged 5.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.2 minutes per game across nine outings during December.

items.headline: Dunn is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers due to a right knee contusion.
items.story: Dunn is in jeopardy of missing his third straight outing due to the right knee injury he sustained in Friday's win over the Pelicans. If the second-year forward remains sidelined, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time. Across nine appearances in December, Dunn has averaged 5.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.2 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Dunn is out for Monday's game against the Wizards due to right knee soreness.
items.story: The forward will be trying to end a two-game absence during Wednesday's contest against the Cavaliers. Dunn's absence solidifies Royce O'Neale's streaming value in all fantasy leagues Monday, with Grayson Allen (knee) and Jalen Green (hamstring) out.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Dunn could miss a second straight game due to right knee soreness. If he is unable to play, Jordan Goodwin and Rasheer Fleming could see increased roles.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is out for Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Dunn is dealing with right knee soreness and won't suit up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. His next chance to play will come against the Wizards on Monday.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Dunn is dealing with right knee soreness following Friday's win over New Orleans and is in jeopardy of missing Saturday's rematch. If the second-year forward is unable to suit up, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is available to return to Friday's game against the Pelicans, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Dunn exited to the locker room in the second quarter due to a right knee issue but is available to return for the second half. He posted three points, three rebounds and one assist across seven minutes in the first half before heading to the tunnel.

items.headline: Dunn exited to the locker room after sustaining an apparent right knee injury in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Pelicans, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Dunn grabbed at his right knee and limped to the locker room with 9:52 remaining in the second quarter. If the second-year forward is unable to return, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time for the remainder of the game.

items.headline: Dunn supplied seven points (2-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal over 20 minutes during Saturday's 119-116 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Dunn continues to provide very little outside of defensive stats, scoring single digits for the ninth straight game. During that time, he has averaged just 4.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 19.7 minutes per game. At this stage, he should be viewed as nothing more than a defensive streaming option.

items.headline: Dunn amassed two points (1-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt), eight rebounds and four assists across 24 minutes during Monday's 108-105 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Dunn hasn't been much of a scoring factor since returning from a wrist injury that sidelined him for five games, averaging 4.0 points on shooting just 31.3 percent from the field in his last three appearances. However, he has been a force defensively, averaging 6.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in that span, and he will likely remain with the second unit in the foreseeable future despite starting 11 games this season.

items.headline: Pritchard will start in Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) sidelined for the front end of a back-to-back, Pritchard will start for the first time in 2026-27. The 28-year-old started 50 regular-season games during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 16.9 points, 4.3 rebounds and 5.3 assists in 32.8 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Pritchard had 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound and two assists over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 105-101 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Pritchard has scored at least 14 points in four of his last five appearances, with 15 triples during that stretch. However, his assists have fluctuated considerably, and he's contributed little defensively. His perimeter shooting remains his primary fantasy asset, while Boston's crowded rotation limits his overall ceiling.

items.headline: Pritchard racked up 21 points (7-16 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds and five assists in 32 minutes during Monday's 115-105 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Pritchard had his most productive game since late October, a welcome relief for fantasy managers. While it was good to see him doing what he does best, Pritchard remains outside the top 100 this season, averaging 13.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.4 three-pointers in 27.0 minutes per game. Assuming Boston remains relatively healthy, expect to see Pritchard flirting with top-100 value ROS.

items.headline: Pritchard finished Wednesday's 98-93 win over the Raptors with 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one assist and one rebound over 31 minutes.
items.story: The Celtics' offense looked sluggish on the second leg of a back-to-back set, not to mention that they were without Paul George (illness) for Wednesday's contest. Pritchard wasn't the most efficient from the field, but he led the Celtics' bench in scoring and finished third on the team in points behind Jayson Tatum (24) and Derrick White (19). Pritchard has scored in double digits in each of his last five games, and over that span he has connected on 43.8 percent of his three-point attempts on 6.4 3PA/G while averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 assists and 3.8 rebounds over 26.3 minutes.

items.headline: Pritchard finished Tuesday's 123-101 win over Philadelphia with 18 points (7-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and one steal in 30 minutes.
items.story: Pritchard delivered an efficient all-around performance off the bench, connecting on four three-pointers while adding solid rebounding and playmaking production. His consistent involvement in Boston's backcourt continues to support his fantasy appeal. He's scored in double digits in a season-long four consecutive games, averaging 13.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game over that stretch.

items.headline: Pritchard tallied 12 points (4-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and a steal across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Pritchard made all four of his field goals from beyond the arc to snap an 0-for-12 drought from three in his previous three contests. Inconsistency has been Pritchard's biggest issue so far. He has failed to score more than 12 points in four straight games, but he's also surpassed the 25-point mark twice already. At the end of the day, while his ability to produce across multiple categories remains encouraging, Pritchard's fantasy outlook still depends on his perimeter shooting as his primary source of production.

items.headline: Pritchard (eye) is available for Friday's game against the Hornets, Zack Cox of the Boston Heraldreports.
items.story: Pritchard will shed his questionable tag ahead of this contest after leaving Wednesday's game early. As of Friday afternoon, there's been no mention of restrictions or any limitations health-wise for the veteran point guard.

items.headline: Pritchard (eye) is questionable for Friday against Charlotte, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Pritchard is day-to-day after leaving Wednesday's win over the Bucks early. Meanwhile, Jayson Tatum (rest) has been cleared to return. Guys like Baylor Scheierman and Mike Conley could see more run if Pritchard is unable to give it a go.

items.headline: Pritchard exited Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks and did not return due to a right eye abrasion, finishing with 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-2 FT), five assists and one rebound across 18 minutes.
items.story: Pritchard was deemed questionable to return but never checked back in. He can be considered questionable for Friday's game at Charlotte, and if he's forced to miss time, Baylor Scheierman and Mike Conley would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Pritchard is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against the Bucks due to a right eye abrasion.
items.story: Pritchard logged just over 18 minutes before heading to the locker room with the eye injury. If he's unable to return in the final quarter, Baylor Scheierman would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Pritchard (shoulder) is available for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Pritchard will shed his questionable tag due to a right shoulder contusion and keep his record of perfect attendance this season alive. The 28-year-old guard has been inconsistent on the offensive end through seven regular-season games, averaging 13.4 points, 3.4 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 27.9 minutes per contest. He could see increased burn Wednesday in the absence of Jayson Tatum (rest).

items.headline: Pritchard is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee due to a right shoulder contusion, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Pritchard's status is uncertain after he struggled in Monday's loss to Houston, finishing with four points on 0-for-7 shooting across 30 minutes. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also questionable and Devin Carter (illness) ruled out, Boston could be shorthanded Wednesday. Pritchard's availability should become clearer closer to tip-off.

items.headline: Pritchard finished Monday's 109-93 loss to the Rockets with four points (0-7 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 30 minutes.
items.story: Pritchard couldn't buy a basket, missing all seven of his field-goal attempts while finishing with a team-worst minus-17 rating. Despite the shooting struggles, he logged 30 minutes off the bench with Paul George (rest) unavailable, suggesting his role remains secure. Pritchard should have opportunities to bounce back, but his offensive inconsistency has been frustrating for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard had 30 points (9-17 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 9-9 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 125-111 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Pritchard scored 20 of his game-high 30 points in the first half, which was a big reason why the Celtics entered the break with a 29-point lead. He did his scoring from all over the floor, and his nine made free throws were a career high. Pritchard's scoring production has been inconsistent over the first five games of the regular season, but he's the offensive spark plug that the Celtics rely on, especially when one of Jayson Tatum and Paul George is not on the floor.

items.headline: Pritchard registered 28 points (10-16 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, four assists and two steals across 22 minutes during Monday's 134-99 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Pritchard caught fire from beyond the arc, connecting on seven three-pointers while leading Boston in scoring despite coming off the bench. The veteran guard was particularly effective during the third quarter, helping the Celtics pull away in a lopsided victory. Pritchard's explosive shooting ability gives him considerable fantasy upside, though his production could fluctuate depending on his playing time.

items.headline: Pritchard finished with 17 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds and one assist in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Pritchard matched Derrick White for Boston's second-highest scoring total despite the former coming off the bench. The guard generated much of his offense at the charity stripe, converting seven of eight attempts while committing zero turnovers. His 28-minute workload suggests he'll remain a significant part of the Celtics' backcourt rotation, although his limited playmaking in the opener was less encouraging for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Pritchard didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia but is on track to be on the floor when the Celtics begin the 2026-27 campaign versus the Pistons. The 2020 No. 26 overall pick is coming off his best season in 2025-26, averaging 17.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists across 32.4 minutes per contest in 79 regular-season games, including 50 starts. With Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia, there is room for Pritchard to take over as the No. 3 offensive option behind Paul George and Jayson Tatum, giving him more than enough upside for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Pritchard and the rest of Boston's regulars won't be available for the final exhibition but should be good to go for the regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday. Pritchard provided seven points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 assists and three rebounds over 29 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over Charlotte.

items.headline: Pritchard provided seven points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 assists and three rebounds over 29 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: The 28-year-old guard had trouble getting his own shot to fall, but he led the Celtics in assists on the night while tying Jayson Tatum for the team lead in minutes. Pritchard posted better numbers last season than he did in 2024-25, when he won the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year award, averaging a career-best 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 boards, along with 2.7 threes in 32.4 minutes over 79 regular-season games, and he should be the engine of the second unit once again in 2026-27.

items.headline: Pritchard signed a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with the Celtics on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Pritchard's extension includes a mutual option for the 2029-30 campaign. The 28-year-old guard is coming off the best statistical year of his career, averaging 17.0 points, 5.2 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 0.7 steals across 32.4 minutes per game in 79 regular-season appearances (50 starts). Regardless of whether the 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year starts, he figures to play a sizable role for the Jaylen Brown-less Celtics.

items.headline: Pritchard posted 25 points (7-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), seven assists and four rebounds over 24 minutes during Saturday's 144-106 preseason win over the 76ers.
items.story: Pritchard helped the Celtics race out to a commanding lead in the second quarter with 11 points, nine of which came on three triples. The seventh-year point guard has been the Celtics' offensive spark plug the last few seasons, and he operated in a starting role for most of last year during Jayson Tatum's absence. Pritchard is expected to revert to a rotational role now that Tatum is back, but with Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia and Paul George in Boston, Pritchard could be the Celtics' second offensive option on most nights.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) said he'll play in Saturday's preseason game against the 76ers, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Most of Boston's regular players rested during the preseason opener, including Pritchard, but the veteran point guard will make his debut Saturday. He's coming off a career-best season during which he averaged 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds across 79 regular-season games (50 starts).

items.headline: Pritchard (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: This appears to be a scheduled rest day for Pritchard, as the Celtics are sitting a number of their regular rotation players. He'll have an opportunity to suit up for Saturday's exhibition against the 76ers.

items.headline: Pritchard said Monday that he's focused on making incremental improvements across the board rather than dramatically changing his game heading into the 2026-27 season, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: The veteran guard mentioned becoming more efficient while improving his production as a scorer, facilitator, rebounder and defender. Pritchard is coming off a career year in which he averaged 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds across 79 regular-season appearances, and he should be an even more important piece of Boston's backcourt this season with Jaylen Brown out of the picture.

items.headline: Pritchard could benefit from additional offensive opportunities after Boston dealt Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia, John Schuhmann of NBA.com reports.
items.story: Although Paul George is expected to step into a starting role, Brown's departure creates extra ball-handling and scoring chances throughout the rotation, potentially allowing Pritchard to build on last season's breakout campaign. Increased minutes in three-guard lineups could help preserve his fantasy relevance despite George's arrival.

items.headline: Head coach Steve Kerr said Monday that Williams (hamstring) is on track to return Wednesday against the Kings, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Williams hasn't played since Nov. 9 due to a left hamstring strain, though he could return to action as soon as Wednesday. The Warriors will provide an update on his status by Tuesday night, and if the 27-year-old is cleared to return, there would be fewer minutes available for guys like Gary Payton, LJ Cryer and Will Richard.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Williams recently progressed to on-court work, but he will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game. His next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Kings.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated Saturday.
items.story: Williams sustained a left hamstring strain in the Nov. 9 win over New Orleans, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Boston. LJ Cryer will likely continue seeing increased burn in Williams' stead.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com.
items.story: Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backcourt.

items.headline: Williams has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against the Pelicans due to a left hamstring injury, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports. He'll finish with four points (2-3 FG) in two minutes.
items.story: Williams didn't see much action Monday before going down with a hamstring injury. He dealt with a left quadriceps contusion earlier in November and has evidently picked up a hamstring issue on the same leg. Williams is scheduled to undergo an MRI and can be considered day-to-day until further notice, though head coach Steve Kerr didn't seem optimistic.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) isn't listed on the injury report for Thursday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Williams missed Monday's win over Phoenix due to a left quad contusion, though he participated in Wednesday's practice and will return to action Thursday. Through seven regular-season appearances (one start), he's averaging 11.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.0 steals in 17.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quad contusion. His next chance to play will come Thursday against Miami. Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see a bump in minutes in Williams' stead.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams is dealing with a left quadriceps contusion and could sit out the back end of this back-to-back set. If the 26-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see increased burn.

items.headline: Williams ended with 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 25 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The 26-year-old guard played more than 20 minutes for the second time in seven games so far this season, and both times the extra run has come while Stephen Curry (rest) wasn't in the lineup. In those two contests (one start), Williams has averaged 18.5 points, 4.0 assists, 3.0 boards, 2.0 threes and 1.0 steals in 24.5 minutes, giving him some DFS appeal the next time Curry gets a night off.

items.headline: Williams tallied 11 points (4-11 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and an assist across 14 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Williams reached double figures despite playing fewer than 15 minutes, demonstrating an aggressive offensive approach with 11 field-goal attempts. His reserve role remains the main obstacle to consistent production, but he could be a decent waiver pickup if he gets an expanded role. Williams has scored in double digits in three of his five appearances this season despite shooting 34.1 percent from the floor and 33.3 percent from deep.

items.headline: Williams will come off the bench Monday night against Denver, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Williams will rotate back to the bench with Stephen Curry returning from a rest day Saturday. Williams has totaled 18 points in 27 minutes over his first two games off the bench this season.

items.headline: Williams (back) is available for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Williams was deemed probable Sunday due to left lower-back soreness, but he's been cleared to play and should see minutes off the bench in the Warriors' backcourt. He started against Phoenix on Saturday in a game where the Warriors rested several starters and posted 20 points with five assists, so he's likely to see a relatively voluminous role with the second unit.

items.headline: Williams is probable for Monday's game against the Nuggets due to left lower back soreness.
items.story: The back issue seems to be new for Williams, but he is expected to play through it Monday. Williams got a spot start Saturday against the Suns due to Golden State resting many players, and he made the most of the opportunity, recording 20 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 8-11 FT), five assists, three rebounds and two steals in 24 minutes.

items.headline: Williams accumulated 20 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 8-11 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals over 24 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Suns.
items.story: With Golden State opting to rest a number of players, Williams was inserted into the starting lineup for the first time this season. He certainly made the most of his opportunity, finishing as one of three Warriors players to score at least 20 points. While this is likely just a one-off, it is worth keeping an eye on Williams' role moving forward. Should Golden State's trajectory continue downward, there is a scenario in which Williams could see more run later in the season.

items.headline: Williams will start Saturday's game against Phoenix, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: With Stephen Curry (rest) out, Williams will draw his first regular-season start with the Warriors. Through two regular-season games, he's averaging 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 steals in 13.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Williams ended with 14 points (3-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-7 FT), four rebounds, three assists and three steals over 18 minutes during Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Williams led the team in steals Wednesday and paced the second unit in scoring. It's hard to gauge how the Warriors will divvy up the minutes in more competitive games, but it looks like Williams will be a regular member of the rotation off the bench.

items.headline: Williams closed Saturday's 111-106 preseason win over the Kings with 19 points (7-8 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one assist and one steal across 17 minutes.
items.story: After starting Wednesday's loss to Portland, Williams shifted to the second unit Saturday. He still torched the nets off the bench and finished as Golden State's second-leading scorer behind Yaxel Lendeborg (23 points). Williams has scored in double figures in all four of the Warriors' preseason outings thus far, and he's making a strong case for additional minutes to open the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Williams will come off the bench in Saturday's preseason game against the Kings.
items.story: Stephen Curry is back and starting after skipping Wednesday's exhibition, so Williams will return to a reserve role. However, with Curry set to play just the first half of Saturday's exhibition, Williams should still see quality minutes.

items.headline: Williams played 18 minutes in Wednesday's preseason loss to the Trail Blazers, scoring 17 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT) while adding four assists, three rebounds and one steal.
items.story: Golden State rested most of its key rotation players, leaving Williams as one of the more experienced members of the starting five, and the 26-year-old guard stepped up with an efficient performance. The former Maverick is expected to be a consistent part of the second unit after signing a one-year deal with the Warriors in August.

items.headline: Williams will start in Wednesday's exhibition against the Trail Blazers, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Warriors are resting nine players for Wednesday's exhibition, so Williams could see major minutes in a starting role. Joining him in the first unit for Wednesday's game will be Will Richard, Malevy Leons, Dalen Terry and Charles Bassey.

items.headline: Williams posted 10 points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, an assist and a steal across 18 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Williams hopes to catch on with the Warriors after three seasons with the Mavericks, and although his speed and playmaking are unquestioned, he's buried on the depth chart and unlikely to make an impact. One possible advantage is Stephen Curry's advancing age, which could give him extra possessions in back-to-backs, but Williams is far from fantasy-relevant at this point.

items.headline: Williams has made an early impression on the Warriors with his speed and ability to put pressure on opposing defenses, Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Williams recorded 11 points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal in 16 minutes during Sunday's preseason loss to the Clippers. Coach Steve Kerr has called Williams the fastest player he's coached with Golden State, and his ability to attack in transition and off high pick-and-rolls could give the Warriors a dimension they've lacked in recent seasons.

items.headline: Williams has been impressive during training camp, with head coach Steve Kerr praising his speed and ability as a "defensive pest," Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Kerr called Williams the "fastest guy we've ever had," and he's seemingly made a positive impression with the Warriors thus far after signing a one-year deal with the club in late August. The 26-year-old guard was productive for the Mavericks in 2025-26, averaging 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals across 22.2 minutes per contest in 66 regular-season outings (15 starts). He'll likely fight to carve out a rotational role and figures to compete for playing time with the likes of De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton and Will Richard.

items.headline: Williams signed a one-year, $2.6 million deal with the Warriors on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Williams is coming off a successful campaign with the Mavericks. Across 66 regular-season appearances, he averaged 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.5 three-pointers. Minutes won't be easy to come by in Golden State, however, so he's likely going to be an emergency depth option.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is unavailable for Sunday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Williams will now miss a fourth consecutive contest, marking the end of a career-best 2025-26 campaign. Without the 26-year-old, extra minutes will presumably be absorbed by Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson. Williams started 15 of his 66 appearances, averaging 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 22.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful to play Sunday versus Chicago.
items.story: Williams is set to sit out his fourth consecutive game Sunday. Check back for official word on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Williams (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: As expected due to his doubtful tag, Williams will miss his third consecutive contest while continuing to battle an illness. With Williams sidelined and Klay Thompson also out with an illness, the Mavericks' depth will be severely tested on Friday. Ryan Nembhard, AJ Johnson, and John Poulakidas should all see increased opportunities.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is listed as doubtful for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Williams is still under the weather and is expected to miss his third straight game Friday. If the 26-year-old guard is ruled out, there would be more minutes available for Ryan Nembhard and John Poulakidas.

items.headline: Williams (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Friday in San Antonio. With the 26-year-old point guard out, Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams didn't play Tuesday against the Clippers, and barring a miracle, he's likely to sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set Wednesday as well. With Williams expected to be out, Ryan Nembhard should be in line to see more minutes in the backcourt.

items.headline: Williams (illness) won't play Tuesday versus the Clippers, Farbod Esnaashari of SI.com reports.
items.story: With Williams unavailable, Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson will have a chance to get back into the rotation. For now, Williams should be considered questionable for Wednesday's game in Phoenix.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Williams was previously listed as questionable, but it appears he will miss the front end of this back-to-back set. His absence could open things up for Ryan Nembhard in the backcourt.

items.headline: Williams is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Clippers due to illness.
items.story: Williams put up 13 points in 25 minutes Sunday against the Lakers but is in danger of sitting Tuesday after popping up on the injury report. The Mavericks should have a better idea of his status closer to game time.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Williams was a late addition to the injury report with the probable tag, but now we have official confirmation that he'll be out there. Over the past three games, Williams has delivered averages of 18.7 points, 4.7 assists and 1.7 steals per contest.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Williams recently popped up on the injury report because of an illness. However, the probable designation suggests he is expected to suit up versus Los Angeles. If the 26-year-old suffers a setback and can't play, Ryan Nembhard will likely see more minutes from off the bench.

items.headline: Williams ended with 23 points (7-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-11 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two steals across 26 minutes during Friday's 138-127 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Williams reached the 20-point mark for the first time since Jan. 24, and this was his best scoring output since he delivered 26 points in a loss to the Warriors on Christmas Day. Williams has been very productive off the bench and has scored in double digits in 11 of his last 12 outings with the second unit, a stretch in which he's averaging 12.8 points, 2.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game.

items.headline: Williams accumulated 15 points (4-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and two steals over 28 minutes during Monday's 124-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Williams has been a steady contributor off the bench for the Mavericks, and he's scored in double digits in all but one of his 17 appearances since the All-Star break. The bench role limits his upside a bit, but Williams can fill the stat sheet every time he steps on the hardwood, so he's a valuable option to target in most formats if he's available.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) supplied 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six assists and two rebounds across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 142-135 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Williams made his return to action after missing the previous three games due to a concussion. Though head coach Jason Kidd has been reluctant to use Williams as a full-time starter, the fifth-year guard still looks poised to remain a regular part of the rotation as the season winds down. While his production of late has been adequate, Williams doesn't necessarily need to be viewed as a must-roster player. Since moving back to a bench role March 6, Williams has averaged 10.9 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds, 0.8 blocks, 0.6 three-pointers and 0.5 steals in 19.1 minutes per contest while shooting 47.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) is available for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets, Brad Townsend of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Williams will return from a three-game absence due to a concussion. His return could spell fewer minutes for Ryan Nembhard and Klay Thompson.

items.headline: Grimes recorded nine points (1-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and one block across 30 minutes during Monday's 109-94 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Grimes has shot just 3-for-15 from the field over his last two appearances, but he's totaled 15 assists while averaging 32.5 minutes. His expanded playmaking responsibilities provide fantasy value despite the recent shooting struggles.

items.headline: Grimes logged 13 points (2-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds and seven assists in 35 minutes during Friday's 106-104 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Grimes struggled from the field three days after his career-high 47-point outburst, but he delivered when it counted. His step-back three-pointer with 57 seconds left off a pass from Matisse Thybulle put the Lakers ahead for good. He also excelled at the free-throw line. With Austin Reaves (heel) out, Grimes has taken on a much bigger role and has responded with the best stretch of his career.

items.headline: Grimes ended with 20 points (8-20 FG, 4-10 3Pt), seven rebounds and four assists over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 loss to Utah.
items.story: Grimes followed Tuesday's career-high 47-point explosion against Charlotte with another 20-point performance, giving him three consecutive contests in which he's reached the 20-point threshold. His 20 field-goal attempts Wednesday were particularly encouraging, suggesting the Lakers remain comfortable giving him a substantial offensive role while Austin Reaves (heel) is sidelined. Although he couldn't replicate Tuesday's exceptional scoring display, Grimes also added seven rebounds and four assists, showing his recent value isn't entirely dependent on perimeter shooting. His expanded opportunities could continue until Los Angeles returns to full strength.

items.headline: Grimes closed with 47 points (16-24 FG, 10-14 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, three assists and one steal across 42 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets.
items.story: Grimes erupted for a career high. He did most of his damage in a scorching fourth quarter, capped by a game-tying three-pointer in the closing seconds of regulation. His 10 made threes tied Kobe Bryant for the most by a Laker in a regular-season game. With Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined, Grimes has stepped up in a big way and has put together back-to-back standout performances.

items.headline: Grimes will start in Sunday's game versus the Suns, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined, Grimes will start Sunday. In two starts during the 2026-27 campaign, the 26-year-old is averaging 17.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.5 steals over 35.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games due to a right finger splint, but he's going to give it a go versus Phoenix. With Austin Reaves (heel) ruled out and Collin Sexton (eye) questionable, Grimes could step into the starting lineup. We'll have to wait for confirmation from LA prior to tipoff, but either way, he should see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
items.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Grimes didn't play Monday in Atlanta after scoring 12 points in 32 minutes as a starter in Detroit on Sunday. However, it appears that absence wasn't simply due to rest during the second night of a back-to-back set, as Grimes will now miss a second straight game after previously being listed as questionable. In his absence, Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr could remain involved with the second unit.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game in Milwaukee.
items.story: Grimes injured his finger in Sunday's game against Detroit and didn't suit up for the 124-114 win over Atlanta on Monday. With Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves (illness) both available, Grimes is expected to head back to the bench. However, another absence could still mean more minutes for Sandro Mamukelashvili, Ziaire Williams and Collin Sexton.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) is out for Monday's game against Atlanta, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com.
items.story: Grimes sustained a sprained right finger Sunday in Detroit, so he's sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. With Austin Reaves (illness) questionable to play, Collin Sexton could be thrust into a larger role in the backcourt.

items.headline: Grimes (finger) did not return to Sunday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Grimes went back to the locker room in the fourth quarter due to an apparent finger injury and was unable to return. He should be considered questionable at best for Monday's game against the Hawks.

items.headline: Grimes went back to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Pistons, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Grimes exited for the locker room in the fourth quarter, accompanied by medical staff. If he is unable to return, Collin Sexton could see extra minutes.

items.headline: Grimes will start Sunday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) sidelined for this contest, Grimes will enter the starting lineup for the second time this season. Grimes' only start came in the 103-87 win over the Clippers on Oct. 28, with the former 76er finishing with 23 points, three rebounds, five assists and four steals across 38 minutes.

items.headline: Grimes contributed seven points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds and four assists in 23 minutes during Monday's 138-117 win over the Heat.
items.story: It's been a rather disappointing start to the year for Grimes, who had been penciled in as a starter for the Lakers during the preseason but has since watched Matisse Thybulle win the job. Grimes has scored in double digits just once in his past six appearances, averaging only 8.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 26.3 minutes per game for the season.

items.headline: Grimes won't start Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Luka Doncic (back) is in the lineup following a one-game absence, pushing Grimes to the second unit. In four appearances off the bench this season, he's averaging 7.0 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grimes finished Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers with 23 points (7-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-11 FT), five assists, four steals and three rebounds across 38 minutes.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) unavailable for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Grimes got the starting nod for the first time this season. The 26-year-old shooting guard led the Lakers in minutes en route to team- and season-high marks in points, assists and steals. He's now scored in double figures in three of the Lakers' five regular-season games thus far.

items.headline: Grimes will start Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) sidelined, Grimes will get the starting nod for the first time this season. Through four regular-season outings, he's averaging 7.0 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 24.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Grimes provided three points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and one assist in 20 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 win over Utah.
items.story: After scoring in double figures in each of the Lakers' first two contests to begin 2026-27, Grimes deferred to Collin Sexton, who finished with 13 points in 20 minutes off the bench. The 26-year-old is averaging 8.7 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists in 26.0 minutes a night to begin his tenure in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Grimes will come off the bench in Friday's game against Denver, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Grimes is projected to start at small forward to open the season. He will come off the bench Friday in the final preseason game before the Opening Night meeting with the Warriors on Wednesday.

items.headline: Grimes supplied nine points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), six assists, one steal and one block across 26 minutes in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Grimes stayed in the starting lineup and did more as a distributor, posting a preseason-high six assists, though his three turnovers were part of a 29-turnover night for the Lakers. He has started all four exhibitions and appears set to open the season alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves.

items.headline: Grimes supplied 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two steals in 29 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Grimes reached double figures for the third straight preseason game, though six turnovers took some shine off his night. He's started all three exhibitions after signing a four-year, $60 million deal, and it's looking increasingly likely that coach JJ Redick will roll with him as one of the starting wings alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler.

items.headline: Spencer had 24 points (5-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 11-11 FT), one rebound and five assists over 21 minutes during Monday's 117-111 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Spencer continues to thrive as a reserve, averaging 16.0 points, 7.4 assists and 27.4 minutes over his last five appearances. His efficient perimeter shooting and consistent playmaking have strengthened his fantasy appeal despite his fluctuating role while Memphis deals with numerous injuries.

items.headline: Spencer recorded nine points (4-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, five assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Despite the return of Ty Jerome from a hip injury, Spencer maintained a sizeable role, playing at least 30 minutes for the fourth time in the past five games. Those in standard leagues should check the waiver wire, just in case Spencer was dropped. While he could certainly end up trending in that direction, this performance should provide some hope when it comes to his ROS value. With that said, Cameron Boozer was also out due to an ankle injury, while Javon Small was sidelined due to personal reasons.

items.headline: Spencer is not listed in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Spencer started in the Grizzlies' last four games, but since Ty Jerome (hip) is cleared to suit up, the 26-year-old will return to the bench. However, with Cameron Boozer (ankle), Jerami Grant (calf), GG Jackson (foot), Scotty Pippen (back) and Javon Small (personal) sidelined, Spencer should remain heavily involved as a reserve.

items.headline: Spencer posted nine points (3-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, 11 assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Spencer followed Wednesday's season-high 26 points with a career-best 11 assists, demonstrating his ability to impact games without relying on scoring. He's recorded at least seven assists in four straight appearances, reflecting increased ball-handling responsibilities. His expanded playmaking role makes him an appealing fantasy option while Memphis remains shorthanded.

items.headline: Spencer had 26 points (9-11 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one rebound, seven assists and one block over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Since entering the starting lineup with Ty Jerome (hip) sidelined, Spencer has put in averages of 18.3 points, 8.0 assists and 3.0 triples per contest on 61.3 percent shooting from the field and 88.9 percent at the line. As long as Jerome is out, Spencer should provide elite fantasy value.

items.headline: Spencer finished with 17 points (6-10 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, eight assists and two steals across 34 minutes in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (hip) ruled out, Spencer drew the start for the second time this season. He played well, ending the night with a season high in points. The 26-year-old also had another efficient performance and has now shot at least 50.0 percent from deep in 12 of his 13 appearances during the 2026-27 campaign. If Jerome can't get back on the floor Monday in Washington, Spencer will presumably stay with the first five, potentially resulting in another above-average showing.

items.headline: Spencer will start in Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (hip) out Saturday, Spencer will start against the Nets. The 26-year-old has started just once during the 2026-27 campaign, finishing with 10 points, five rebounds and 13 assists over 25 minutes in the 136-105 win over Sacramento on Oct. 31.

items.headline: Spencer provided 15 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-118 loss to Denver.
items.story: Spencer had already overtaken Scotty Pippen (back) before the latter went down with an injury, and the former continues to supply deep-league fantasy appeal at point guard. Over his past six appearances, Spencer has averaged 9.8 points, 6.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 three-pointers while shooting a scorching 50.0 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Spencer recorded seven points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 107-103 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Spencer made his presence felt as a facilitator, leading both teams with nine assists while adding six rebounds in an efficient performance off the bench. He committed just two turnovers and continues to provide Memphis with a reliable secondary playmaking option. Although his scoring output remains modest, Spencer's passing production gives him some appeal in deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Spencer won't start Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Ty Jerome (back) is back in the lineup, sending Spencer to the second unit. The sharpshooter has averaged 8.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 0.8 steals while shooting 58.8 percent from downtown across 18.0 minutes per game in five appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Spencer closed Saturday's 136-105 victory over the Kings with 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt), five rebounds, 13 assists and one steal in 25 minutes.
items.story: Spencer made his first start of the regular season Saturday due to the absence of Ty Jerome (back). Spencer answered the call by tying a career high in assists en route to his first double-double of the season and seventh of his three-year NBA career. He would likely revert to a bench role against the Pelicans on Monday if Jerome is cleared to return.

items.headline: Spencer is in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Kings on Saturday.
items.story: Spencer has come off the bench in each of the first five games of the regular season, but he'll get his first start of the 2026-27 campaign Saturday due to the absence of Ty Jerome (back). Spencer is averaging 8.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.0 threes and 0.8 steals over 18.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer produced eight points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 23 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 win over Portland.
items.story: Spencer registered season highs in both boards and dimes Thursday, leading the second unit in the latter category. Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal believes Spencer has leapfrogged Scotty Pippen in the backcourt rotation hierarchy, so Spencer's stock in fantasy looks to be very much on the rise.

items.headline: Spencer posted 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 16 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 win over Sacramento.
items.story: With Ty Jerome taking the league by storm in the early going, Spencer is falling behind in the race for minutes at point guard. Spencer should continue battling with Scotty Pippen for backup playing time.

items.headline: Spencer tallied 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 19 minutes in Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Spencer was perfect from three-point range off the bench, posting his best scoring night of the preseason. The third-year guard started 20 games for Memphis last season, but he's expected to begin the 2026-27 campaign in the second unit behind Cedric Coward.

items.headline: Spencer finished with eight points (2-3 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 14 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over Atlanta.
items.story: Spencer came off the bench and shared the floor with Scotty Pippen for a portion of the contest, continuing an experiment Memphis utilized during training camp. Spencer is among several players competing for starting and rotation opportunities and offers valuable shooting after hitting 44.8 percent of his threes during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Spencer is in the mix for a spot in the Grizzlies' starting five to begin the 2026-27 season, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen are competing for the starting point guard job with Ja Morant now in Portland, though there's also a battle for starting spots on the wings in Memphis. Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant and Jaylen Wells are all competing with Spencer for a role in the first unit. The 26-year-old shot an impressive 44.8 percent from beyond the arc in 2025-26, averaging 11.1 points and 2.0 triples per game across 72 regular-season games (20 starts). Spencer also averaged 5.6 assists per tilt and could operate as a secondary playmaker in the Grizzlies' starting five. Regardless, he should continue seeing a sizable role for a rebuilding Memphis squad.

items.headline: Spencer (back) should have a significant role next season after the Grizzlies traded Ja Morant to the Trail Blazers this offseason.
items.story: Memphis has a three-way competition brewing for No. 1 point guard duties ahead of training camp, featuring Scotty Pippen (toe), Ty Jerome (ankle) and Spencer. Even if he fails to seize a starting position to open the year, Spencer is far more likely than D'Angelo Russell to play meaningful minutes in the backcourt off the bench for the rebuilding Grizzlies. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (finger) also agreed to a buyout with Memphis on Saturday, further improving Spencer's chances of claiming a big role with the second unit.

items.headline: Spencer (back) will not play in Sunday's season finale against the Rockets.
items.story: Spencer will end his campaign with three consecutive absences. Overall, it was a breakout season for the second-year pro, who set career highs essentially across the board. In his 23.8 minutes per game, Spencer averaged 11.1 points, 5.6 assists and 2.5 rebounds.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is listed as out ahead of Friday's game in Utah.
items.story: Spencer has missed three of the Grizzlies' last four games. At this point, it would be surprising to see him suit up for the season finale versus the Rockets on Sunday. With Walter Clayton (hip) and Javon Small (thigh) both questionable, Jahmai Mashack and Adama Bal may be the featured options out of the backcourt.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Spencer continues to deal with lower-back soreness and will miss his third game this month. His next chance to play will come Friday in Utah. In the meantime, Lucas Williamson, Adama Bal and Rayan Rupert are candidates for increased playing time for the injury-riddled Grizzlies.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is available for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Spencer is suiting up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Over his last nine appearances (three starts), Spencer has averaged 9.8 points, 5.7 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 23.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game in Milwaukee.
items.story: Spencer is in danger of missing his second straight game, which could result in major minutes for Adama Bal. Check back for official word on Spencer's status closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Spencer is out for Friday's game against the Raptors due to low back soreness.
items.story: Spencer has put together two straight solid performances, but he'll be forced to the sidelines Friday after picking up a back injury. Jahmai Mashack and Walter Clayton could pick up increased minutes as a result of Spencer's absence.

items.headline: Spencer will start Monday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Spencer didn't play in Saturday's 125-124 win over the Bulls. However, he will suit up Monday and make his first start since March 13. In 17 starts this season, the 2024 No. 53 overall pick has averaged 11.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 8.4 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.7 steals across 29.1 minutes.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's matchup with the Suns.
items.story: Spencer is set to return from a one-game absence, and he should see quality minutes with Ty Jerome (ankle) out and Javon Small (back) not expected to play. Spencer has handed out a total of 17 dimes over his past two appearances, while committing just two turnovers.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: As expected, Spencer will miss Saturday's contest due to lower-back soreness, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against Phoenix. The Grizzlies will be extremely shorthanded against Chicago, so Rayan Rupert, Jahmai Mashack (ankle/nose) and DeJon Jarreau will likely see increased minutes.

items.headline: Spencer (ankle) is doubtful for Saturday's game against Chicago.
items.story: The Grizzlies might be running with a skeleton crew Saturday. With Walter Clayton (ankle) questionable and Ty Jerome (ankle) out, Javon Small may be running things in the backcourt to begin the contest. DeJon Jarreau and Rayan Rupert might also need to get more involved off the bench.

items.headline: Spencer accumulated 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), three rebounds, 10 assists, one block and three steals over 29 minutes during Friday's 119-109 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Spencer missed all six of his shot attempts during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, but he scored efficiently in this one and got some extra minutes with Ty Jerome (ankle) missing another game. As long as Jerome is sidelined, Spencer should be a reliable source of dimes.

items.headline: Spencer (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Spencer was held out of Monday's loss to Atlanta due to back soreness, though he's set to return to action Wednesday. Over his last five appearances (one start), the second-year guard has averaged 10.0 points, 4.2 assists, 1.8 three-pointers, 1.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals across 23.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is out for Monday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Spencer has officially been downgraded to out due to back soreness. The Grizzlies will be awfully thin in the backcourt Monday with Spencer, Cedric Coward (personal), Javon Small (back) and Jahmai Mashack (ankle) all unavailable. It'll presumably be up to Rayan Rupert, DeJon Jarreau and Walter Clayton to pick up the slack.

items.headline: Spencer is doubtful for Monday's game in Atlanta due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: It looks like Spencer will be joining Ja Morant (elbow) and Jahmai Mashack (ankle) on the inactive list for Monday's game, which should result in more minutes for Walter Clayton and Javon Small. Check back for official confirmation on Spencer's status closer to Monday's tipoff.

items.headline: Spencer is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Spencer started Friday against the Pistons and poured in an efficient 19 points but will revert to a reserve role Monday as the Grizzlies are slated to start Walter Clayton, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Rayan Rupert and Olivier-Maxence Prosper. Spencer has come off the bench in 46 of his 63 appearances this season, averaging 11.5 points, 4.4 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 22.2 minutes per contest as a reserve.

items.headline: Spencer will start against Detroit on Friday.
items.story: With Jaylen Wells (shoulder) out, Spencer will step into the starting lineup for the third time since the All-Star break. As a starter this season (16 games), the sharpshooter has averaged 10.8 points, 8.6 assists and 3.8 rebounds across 28.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is available for Friday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Spencer is no longer on the injury report after missing the front end of this back-to-back set. Spencer may be hard to trust in fantasy hoops, given Memphis' volatile rotations and injury reports, but Walter Clayton (ankle) is doubtful Friday, Scotty Pippen (toe) is done for the season, and it's unclear when or if Ja Morant (elbow) will suit up again, opening the door for Spencer to see decent minutes as a resreve against Detroit.

items.headline: Hopkins notched 18 points (6-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds, an assist and two steals across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 128-109 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Hopkins delivered the best scoring performance of his young career, taking advantage of extra frontcourt minutes after DeMar DeRozan was a late scratch due to lower-back spasms. Hopkins' efficient shooting and two steals boosted his fantasy line, but this was just the second time he's topped 25 minutes, so it's unclear whether the workload will stick. Hopkins remains a speculative option until he earns more consistent playing time.

items.headline: Hopkins won't start Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: The rookie forward started the last two games in Cameron Johnson's (ankle) absence, though it'll be Trevon Brazile who replaces Johnson in the first unit Wednesday. Hopkins is still likely to see meaningful burn with the Nuggets shorthanded.

items.headline: Hopkins had 13 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes during Monday's 134-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Hopkins delivered an efficient scoring performance in his starting role, reaching double figures for Denver while committing zero turnovers. However, the forward offered little production outside the scoring column and finished without a steal or block. Hopkins' substantial playing time is encouraging, but he'll need to contribute more consistently across multiple categories to establish reliable fantasy value.

items.headline: Hopkins will start Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: With Cameron Johnson (ankle) sidelined, Hopkins will draw his first career start. The rookie second-rounder has logged just two minutes over one appearance so far this season.

items.headline: Hopkins signed a two-way contract with Denver on Wednesday.
items.story: Hopkins was the No. 49 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. With this transaction, he will be allowed to develop at his own pace with a lot of reps in the G League.

items.headline: Hopkins (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Raptors, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Hopkins will sit out the Nuggets' Summer League finale. Over four Las Vegas Summer League appearances, he averaged 18.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.5 steals and 0.8 blocks in 25.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hopkins finished with 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Thursday's 108-101 loss to Portland.
items.story: Hopkins shot the basketball with efficiency Thursday and tied Trevon Brazile for the team lead in rebounds. He's provided solid production for the Nuggets lately, scoring in double figures while racking up seven or more boards in each of his last three Summer League appearances.

items.headline: Hopkins notched 14 points (6-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Hopkins continues to play well in Las Vegas, reaching double figures in scoring while doing a nice job on the glass. The second-round pick is an intriguing prospect, but it'll be tough for him to carve out a rotation role while Cameron Johnson and Aaron Gordon remain healthy.

items.headline: Hopkins produced 16 points (6-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 101-82 Summer League win over Minnesota.
items.story: Hopkins came up empty from beyond the arc but was otherwise excellent in Denver's lopsided victory. Of his seven rebounds, three came on the offensive glass. After pouring in 24 points Friday, the second-round rookie is off to an encouraging start in the Las Vegas Summer League.

items.headline: Hopkins totaled 24 points (9-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), four rebounds, three steals and two blocks over 26 minutes during Friday's 97-86 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Rockets.
items.story: The 2026 second-round pick led the Nuggets' Summer League squad in scoring, and he racked up five stocks in just 26 minutes of play. Hopkins will look to keep rolling Saturday versus the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Hopkins was selected by the Nuggets with the No. 49 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Hopkins made stops at Kentucky and Providence before spending his final collegiate year at St. John's. He appeared in 37 regular-season games for the Red Storm in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 0.3 blocks and 1.1 steals while shooting 36.3 percent from deep across 28.8 minutes. The 24-year-old is a capable scorer and defender, though his limited athleticism might limit his growth as a professional, at least early in his career. The Nuggets are still a championship-caliber club, considering the team is made up of veterans Nikola Jokic, Aaron Gordon and Jamal Murray, among others. As a result, unless Hopkins exceeds expectations throughout Summer League and training camp, he may not see consistent playing time in 2026-27. Still, with Gordon, Murray and Cameron Johnson known for having issues staying off the injury report, Hopkins' services might be needed at some point.

items.headline: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again, and Charania also noted Thursday that Curry is expected to miss close to one month.

items.headline: Steve Kerr told reporters Wednesday that Curry said he tweaked something in his abdominal area and "had never done it before." Kerr added that the concern level is high, but they will await the MRI results, Kelly Iko of Yahoo Sports reports.
items.story: For now, Curry should be considered highly questionable for Friday's game in San Antonio. De'Anthony Melton started the second half for him after he left Wednesday's game, so Melton will likely get the starting nod if Curry can't play Friday. Brandin Podziemski and Yaxel Lendeborg should also see plenty of offensive opportunities if Curry misses time.

items.headline: Curry won't return to Wednesday's game against the Rockets due to right abdominal soreness, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports. He'll finish with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) across six minutes.
items.story: Curry was seen grabbing at his right side multiple times before heading back to the locker room in the opening quarter. The superstar floor general's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game at San Antonio. With Curry sidelined, LJ Cryer and De'Anthony Melton are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Curry (hip/oblique) exited Wednesday's game against the Rockets, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Curry sank a three-point shot in the first quarter. However, he was in obvious discomfort after the landing and was visibly upset. The multi-time MVP left the court and went straight to the locker room, and he should be considered questionable to return.

items.headline: Curry ended Monday's 138-87 victory over New Orleans with 25 points (6-10 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 9-9 FT), five rebounds and two assists across 21 minutes.
items.story: Curry didn't need much time to make an impact, scoring 25 points before sitting out most of the second half due to the blowout nature of the contest. He was perfect at the free-throw line again, and he's shooting 98.7 percent from the stripe this season. Curry remains one of the league's most efficient high-volume scorers at age 38, and his minutes should return to normal in more competitive games.

items.headline: Curry popped off for 41 points (13-19 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 10-10 FT), six rebounds and six assists over 36 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over Orlando.
items.story: This was Curry's second 40-plus-point performance of the season, and through his first eight games, he has more total points (250) than minutes played (237). This was also Curry's 16th 40-plus-point performance since turning 35, putting him ahead of LeBron James for the most such games in NBA history. He'll look to keep his foot on the gas pedal Monday against the Pelicans.

items.headline: Curry tallied 29 points (9-19 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 5-5 FT), one rebound, four assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 win over Miami.
items.story: Curry enjoyed a strong night from beyond the arc, where he scored 18 of his 29 points. He also led the Warriors in scoring despite staying under the 30-minute threshold. The sharpshooter narrowly missed his fourth consecutive showing with 30-plus points, which is a mark he likely would've hit if not for a lopsided score down the stretch. Even so, Curry continues to put up strong showings as both a scorer and playmaker in the early going of the 2026-27 campaign, as he is now averaging 29.9 points, 4.4 assists and 4.7 made treys through seven games.

items.headline: Curry posted 34 points (9-21 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 11-12 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Golden State's 116-113 win over Phoenix on Monday.
items.story: Curry dazzled in his return from a one-game absence, as the 38-year-old got the night off in the Warriors' first night of a back-to-back on Sunday. He finished as the team leader in minutes while tallying game-high figures in scoring and three-pointers, helping Golden State earn a fifth straight victory after starting the season 0-3. The Warriors only play two more games this week, so Curry will likely suit up for the remaining tilts, both of which are at home.

items.headline: Curry (rest) is available Monday against the Suns.
items.story: After getting a planned maintenance day Sunday for the first leg of this back-to-back set, Curry is ready to roll. Looking ahead, Golden State's next back-to-back set begins Nov. 18.

items.headline: Curry (rest) won't play Sunday against the Clippers, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Curry will receive a maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Suns. De'Anthony Melton could draw the start sans Curry, and Brandin Podziemski will be more involved in the offense.

items.headline: Curry recorded 31 points (11-23 FG, 8-14 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 31 minutes during Friday's 112-95 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Curry passed Dominique Wilkins for 18th place on the NBA's all-time scoring list during the fourth quarter. With Jimmy Butler III (knee) and Moses Moody (knee) sidelined, the Warriors are leaning on Curry even more than usual, and they'll host the Clippers on Sunday.

items.headline: Curry contributed 44 points (11-27 FG, 6-16 3Pt, 16-16 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and two steals across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: After shooting a perfect 8-for-8 from the field for 24 points in his last time out, Curry was far more aggressive hunting his shot Wednesday. Although he didn't deliver his most efficient performance from the floor, the superstar guard got to the charity stripe often and scored his most points since Dec. 14, 2025. He contributed in other areas as well, tying for the team lead in rebounds. Curry also tied for second on the Warriors in assists and tallied multiple steals for the third time across four regular-season appearances thus far.

items.headline: Lendeborg posted 12 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds and three assists in 34 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Lendeborg supplied useful rebounding production from the starting lineup, collecting five offensive boards in a game where second-chance opportunities proved valuable. His shooting efficiency was less impressive, though, as he ended with more field-goal attempts (13) than points scored (12). Even with a down game in scoring, Lendeborg's substantial playing time and ability to contribute on the glass offer encouraging signs for his fantasy outlook. His expanded role makes him valuable across all formats and one of the top rookies in this class.

items.headline: Lendeborg produced 11 points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds, seven assists, one steal and two blocks in 33 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Lendeborg struggled to find his shooting touch from the field, but that didn't stop him from contributing elsewhere. He showcased his ability to facilitate Thursday, resulting in a new career high in assists, and he accounted for two of Golden State's seven swats on the night. Lendeborg continues to piece together a strong month, averaging 19.6 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.0 blocks through 10 November appearances.

items.headline: Lendeborg accumulated 13 points (6-18 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 loss to Dallas.
items.story: The rookie is being leaned on more heavily with Stephen Curry (abdomen) on the shelf, and Lendeborg may not be ready to shoulder that kind of responsibility.
