Over four games since Curry was sidelined, the 11th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is shooting just 34.2 percent from the floor and 19.0 percent from three-point range while attempting 18.3 field goals a contest, up from 13.7 in the 11 games prior. Lendeborg is still putting up solid volume stats without Curry in the lineup, however, averaging 17.3 points, 7.5 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.3 steals, 1.0 threes and 0.8 blocks during that four-game stretch.

items.headline: Lendeborg posted 28 points (9-23 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 8-8 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks across 33 minutes during Monday's 115-94 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Lendeborg delivered a stat-stuffing performance in the loss, but his efficiency, or lack thereof, left a lot to be desired for fantasy managers. Over his last two outings, the 11th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is 10-for-36 (27.8 percent) from the field and 2-for-11 (18.2 percent) from behind the arc. Lendeborg was also a game-worst minus-30 in his 33 minutes, but the Warriors are likely to continue leaning on the rookie for as long as Stephen Curry (oblique) remains on the shelf.

items.headline: Lendeborg amassed 25 points (9-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), 10 rebounds and two steals over 36 minutes in Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: This was Lendeborg's third straight 20-plus-point performance and the third double-double of his career. The rookie ranks inside the top-50 of all players on the season with averages of 21.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.4 triples, 1.1 steals and 0.7 swats per contest on 51.8 percent shooting from the field and 74.3 percent at the line.

items.headline: Lendeborg totaled 23 points (8-10 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Monday's 138-87 win over New Orleans.
items.story: Lendeborg was nearly flawless from the field, hitting all four of his three-point attempts. He also filled the box score in just 27 minutes. The rookie continues to look like the Warriors' No. 2 option behind Stephen Curry, and his all-around production should keep him in standard lineups. The lopsided score kept Lendeborg's minutes in check, but he still did plenty even in limited action.

items.headline: Lendeborg notched 23 points (9-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
items.story: Lendeborg combined efficient scoring with strong rebounding and rim protection, delivering one of his most complete performances of the season and ending just two boards shy of a double-double. His six turnovers were a drawback, but the 37-minute workload demonstrated Golden State's willingness to rely on him in competitive situations. His versatile statistical profile offers considerable fantasy upside as his role continues to develop, and he remains one of the most productive rookies in this year's class. He's averaging 21.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and a combined 1.8 steals-plus-blocks in his first 10 appearances of the season.

items.headline: Lendeborg contributed 17 points (6-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), eight rebounds, six assists, one block and three steals in 30 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 win over Miami.
items.story: Lendeborg continues to play at a high level for the Warriors, posting a third straight game with at least 15 points, a mark he's reached in seven of his nine appearances so far. Lendeborg should continue to operate as the Warriors' No. 2 option on offense behind Stephen Curry, and he's quickly rising up the Rookie of the Year rankings.

items.headline: Lendeborg logged 16 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Monday's 116-113 win over the Suns.
items.story: Lendeborg followed Sunday's career-high 37-point performance with another productive outing, overcoming a difficult shooting night by getting to the free-throw line nine times. The rookie also contributed across multiple categories and played a key role in Golden State's comeback, including a late block on Jalen Green. Lendeborg's expanding offensive responsibilities make him an intriguing fantasy option.

items.headline: Lendeborg tallied 37 points (13-19 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six assists, four rebounds and one steal over 34 minutes in a 124-112 win over the Clippers on Sunday.
items.story: Lendeborg scored 24 of his game-high 37 points between the second and third quarters of Sunday's game, and he picked up the scoring responsibilities in the absence of Stephen Curry (rest). Sunday was Lendeborg's second game of 30-plus points, and he has scored at least 26 points in four of his last five outings. In that five-game span, he has averaged 25.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 3.2 threes over 32.0 minutes per contest. The rookie 11th-overall pick has given the Warriors exactly what they need on offense, especially in the absence of Jimmy Butler (knee), who is not expected to make his 2026-27 debut until the new calendar year.

items.headline: Lendeborg posted 26 points (11-20 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Lendeborg has surpassed even the most optimistic expectations early in the season, scoring at least 25 points in three straight games. His 20 field-goal attempts and 35-minute workload were particularly encouraging, highlighting his growing role in Golden State's offense as the No. 2 option behind Stephen Curry, who scored 44 points in this win. Lendeborg's scoring and rebounding potential give him considerable fantasy upside, and he's averaging a robust 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and a combined 1.6 steals-plus-blocks in his first five appearances.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is available for Wednesday's game in Minnesota, as expected.
items.story: The rookie was able to get through shootaround and his pregame routine without issue, and there's been no discussion of any minutes limitations, so make sure you've got him active. Lendeborg is averaging 21.8 points, 9.3 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 2.3 triples, 1.0 steals and 0.5 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is trending toward playing Wednesday against the Timberwolves, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Lendeborg went through shootaround without issue and is currently going through his pregame routine, so we should have official confirmation on his status shortly. With Lendeborg expected to play, Georges Niang loses his streaming appeal.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) went through Wednesday's morning shootaround, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: The standout rookie remains officially listed as questionable for Wednesday's tilt versus Minnesota. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: The rookie standout is in danger of missing his first game of the season Wednesday with foot soreness. With the Warriors already short on forward options, Georges Niang could be thrust into an expanded role if Lendeborg cannot play.

items.headline: Lendeborg totaled 31 points (9-19 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 12-13 FT), 12 rebounds, six assists and one block in 31 minutes during Monday's 134-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Lendeborg put together the best final line of his young NBA career, propelling Golden State to a comfortable victory. The rookie forward has shown promise as a scorer, especially over his last two games, racking up 57 total points over this short stretch. Coach Steve Kerr noted after the game that he was particularly impressed with Lendeborg's performance in the win. "Basically, in all the critical moments of the game, we put the ball in his hands. And for a rookie to be that advanced already, it's extremely rare," said Kerr, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle.

items.headline: Henderson finished Monday's 128-111 victory over the 76ers with 17 points (6-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 26 minutes.
items.story: Henderson bounced back from a three-point outing Saturday, providing Portland with an offensive spark off the bench. He's scored at least 17 points in two of his last three appearances, though inconsistent shooting and competition for backcourt minutes limit his fantasy reliability.

items.headline: Henderson finished Thursday's 124-114 win over the Bucks with 27 points (8-12 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 6-7 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 35 minutes.
items.story: Henderson erupted after scoring just 19 combined points across his previous two games, when he shot 0-for-9 from deep. Injuries to Ja Morant (hamstring) and Deni Avdija (foot) have created additional opportunities, but Thursday's exceptional shooting efficiency appears difficult to sustain. Henderson's expanded workload warrants monitoring.

items.headline: Henderson closed Tuesday's 106-105 loss to Minnesota with nine points (4-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, one assist, one block and one steal in 21 minutes.
items.story: Henderson continues to struggle with his efficiency, shooting just 30.2 percent from the field over his last five appearances while averaging 9.2 points. The third-year guard has maintained a relatively steady role of approximately 22 minutes per game, but his limited assists and rebounding production have restricted his fantasy value. He remains a low-upside option in most standard formats despite Portland's depleted backcourt.

items.headline: Henderson is not listed in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Henderson started the previous five games for Portland due to Ja Morant (hamstring) being sidelined, but the former will slide back to the bench Tuesday. Henderson is averaging 8.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.7 steals in 22.3 minutes across nine outings in 2026-27.

items.headline: Henderson notched 13 points (4-10 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Henderson struggled from beyond the arc, missing all five of his three-point attempts, but his five made free throws helped him reach double figures, and he also found a way to leave his mark in each of the five statistical categories. Henderson's inconsistent shooting and modest workload continue to restrict his fantasy reliability, making him a difficult option to trust outside deeper leagues. Since moving to the starting lineup Oct. 31, he's averaged just 9.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 25.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Henderson chipped in nine points (1-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-8 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 victory over Phoenix.
items.story: That makes it three consecutive starts for Henderson, who's filling in for the injured Ja Morant (hamstring) in the interim. Henderson has yet to see a steady rise in productivity, so fantasy managers in most leagues should continue taking a wait-and-see approach despite the promotion to the first unit.

items.headline: Henderson finished with 14 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three steals over 31 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Aside from his four turnovers, Henderson played well in his first start of the season, providing a scoring punch for Portland while doing a nice job of disrupting passing lanes. Ja Morant (hamstring) will miss at least the next four weeks, so Henderson should be locked in as a starter for Portland. He's someone to consider grabbing off the waiver wire.

items.headline: Henderson will move into the starting lineup for Saturday's game in Utah, Trail Blazers' reporter Sean Highkin reports.
items.story: Henderson is replacing the injured Ja Morant (hamstring) in the first unit, so it'll be interesting to see how he fares with the increased opportunity. Per 36 minutes this season, Henderson is averaging 14.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Henderson (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Henderson will shed his questionable tag due to left ankle soreness and suit up in Los Angeles. The fourth-year guard is averaging 9.5 points in 20.0 minutes per tilt through two regular-season games.

items.headline: Henderson is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers due to left ankle soreness.
items.story: Henderson is evidently dealing with some soreness following Friday's matchup in Sacramento. The Blazers should have a better idea of his availability after watching him go through shootaround and warmups ahead of Tuesday's tipoff.

items.headline: Henderson provided 15 points (7-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 19 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 124-83 victory over the Suns.
items.story: While all five Portland starters scored in double digits during the rout, Henderson was the only member of the second unit to deliver 10-plus points. The fourth-year guard is firmly behind Damian Lillard and Ja Morant on the backcourt depth chart to begin the season and is working off the bench with Jrue Holiday, but after a strong training camp and preseason, Henderson could be poised to thrive in that role.

items.headline: Henderson logged 17 points (7-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two assists, one rebound, one steal and one block over 19 minutes during Portland's 128-118 preseason loss to Golden STate.
items.story: Henderson had a poor night from beyond the arc, but he was accurate enough on other parts of the floor to finish as the Trail Blazers' third-leading scorer behind Damian Lillard (23 points) and Ja Morant (19 points). Lillard and Morant are projected to be the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt for the 2026-27 season, with Henderson and veteran Jrue Holiday (rest) coming off the bench.

items.headline: Henderson will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale against the Warriors, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Ja Morant will replace Henderson in the first unit for Friday's final exhibition game. As a reserve this preseason, Henderson is averaging 10.5 points, 3.0 assists and 2.5 triples per contest.

items.headline: Henderson supplied nine points (3-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists and one rebound in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Portland wanted to take a look at Ja Morant out of the second unit, giving Henderson the chance to start Tuesday. It's hard to envision a player of Morant's caliber coming off the bench once the games begin to count, but this at least appears to be a fluid backcourt situation.

items.headline: Henderson will start Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Henderson will step into the starting five for the first time this preseason. He'll be joined in the first unit by Damian Lillard, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan.

items.headline: Henderson recorded 14 points (4-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three assists and two steals across 16 minutes off the bench in Monday's 119-66 preseason win over the London Lions.
items.story: Henderson was particularly effective from beyond the arc, knocking down four of his five attempts while tying Toumani Camara for the team lead in scoring. The 22-year-old guard also contributed defensively with two steals and committed just one turnover. His perimeter shooting was an encouraging development, though Portland's crowded backcourt could make consistent playing time difficult to secure. Damian Lillard was rested Monday.

items.headline: Henderson finished with nine points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block over 17 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Although most of the attention is on Ja Morant and Damian Lillard in Portland's revamped backcourt, Henderson should continue to play a prominent role off the bench this season. Henderson averaged a career-high 14.2 points despite playing a career-low 24.9 minutes per game last regular season.

items.headline: Henderson is in jeopardy of moving back to a bench role after Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade this offseason.
items.story: Henderson closed the 2025-26 campaign as a starter after missing the first half of the season with a torn hamstring. Not only do the Trail Blazers now have Morant in the mix, but Damian Lillard (Achilles) is also a candidate to jump into the starting lineup in his 2026-27 return to the floor. Until Portland makes its backcourt plans a bit clearer, Henderson is a difficult player to rank from a fantasy perspective ahead of the new year.

items.headline: Henderson finished Tuesday's 114-95 loss to San Antonio in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with five points (2-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and two rebounds over 17 minutes.
items.story: After a strong start to the series, Henderson scored a total of five points on 2-for-13 shooting in the final two games. Injuries derailed his third NBA season, limiting him to 30 regular-season appearances with averages of 14.2 points, 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.9 three-pointers in 24.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Henderson chipped in zero points (0-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 114-93 loss to the Spurs in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Henderson couldn't hit the side of a barn, missing all seven of his shot attempts as the Trail Blazers fell behind 3-1 in the series. The forgettable performance was in stark contrast to the first three games of the series for Henderson, as he averaged 23.3 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals while shooting 56.5 percent, including 52.2 percent from behind the arc. Given that body of work, Henderson should have a solid chance of bouncing back in a potential elimination scenario for Portland in Game 5.

items.headline: Henderson produced 21 points (8-18 FG, 5-10 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 36 minutes during Friday's 120-108 loss to San Antonio in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: It was another impressive performance from long range for Henderson, who has come out firing for the Blazers in the series. items.story: Henderson turned in an efficient performance en route to a game- and season-best 31 points across the regular season and playoffs. Additionally, the 22-year-old point guard became the youngest Trail Blazers player to score at least 30 points in the playoffs. He also knocked down a game-high five triples and is shooting 7-for-13 from beyond the arc through two first-round matchups. He'll look to remain productive in Friday's Game 3 in Portland as the Trail Blazers aim to take a 2-1 series lead.

items.headline: Henderson racked up 18 points (7-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Sunday's 111-98 loss to the Spurs in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Making his ninth straight start, the third-year guard was second on the Trail Blazers in scoring behind Deni Avdija's 30 points. items.story: The Trail Blazers employed a smaller lineup amid Jerami Grant's (calf) absence, running Henderson alongside Jrue Holiday in the backcourt for a second consecutive game. The move has reaped significant benefits with two convincing victories. Shaedon Sharpe's (calf) extended absence has opened a window for Henderson to show his potential after fading into the woodwork for most of the season behind Holiday. The team will likely ride with this successful scheme until Grant returns.

Although he struggled at the free-throw line, the rookie guard demonstrated his willingness to shoot from distance and avoided committing a turnover. Sharp will look to build on the performance as he competes for a spot in Sacramento's regular-season backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Sharp faces increased competition for playing time after the Kings signed Ben Simmons to a one-year deal Friday.
items.story: Although Russell Westbrook is out of the picture now, Ben Simmons will return to The Association and figures to see a steady role in the Kings' rotation thanks to his defensive versatility and playmaking. Along with fellow rookie Alex Karaban, Sharp isn't guaranteed a meaningful role to begin his professional career. However, the No. 45 overall pick out of Houston could see increasingly steady minutes as the season progresses, depending on whether the Kings trade some of their veterans.

items.headline: Sharp tallied 16 points (5-12 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three assists, two rebounds, three steals and one block over 30 minutes during the Kings' 92-90 Summer League win over the Hornets on Friday.
items.story: Sharp scored 13 of his team-high 16 points in the first half, with the rookie second-rounder being one of six Kings players to score in double digits in Friday's victory. He also made his mark defensively with three steals, an area of his game that has really stood out so far in the Summer League. Zach LaVine (hand), Malik Monk (personal) and Nique Clifford (rest) are all ahead of Sharp on the Kings' depth chart, but Sharp could earn himself a consistent role in the rotation with a strong summer, training camp and preseason.

items.headline: Sharp racked up 23 points (7-12 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four steals and one block over 23 minutes during Tuesday's 115-83 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Nets.
items.story: It was the Sharp and Darius Acuff Show on Tuesday, as the rookie duo combined for 49 of Sacramento's 83 points. Sharp caught fire from deep, knocking down a game-high six three-pointers, and he was a disruptive force on the defensive end, finishing with six stocks. However, with little offensive support from the rest of the roster, the Kings were blown out for the second straight game in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Sharp (undisclosed) supplied 21 points (4-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four steals and two rebounds across 26 minutes in Thursday's 91-85 Summer League win over the Clippers.
items.story: Sharp was held out of Monday's California Classic win over the Bucks but returned to action in the Kings' Las Vegas Summer League opener. The 2026 second-rounder led all players in scoring while coming off the bench Thursday. Additionally, he tied the game-high mark in steals.

items.headline: Sharp (undisclosed) won't play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: After playing in Saturday's win over the Nets and Sunday's win over Warriors Blue, Sharp will be held out of the Kings' final California Classic contest. His next chance to play will come in Sacramento's Las Vegas Summer League opener against the Clippers on Thursday.

items.headline: Sharp recorded 18 points (5-15 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block in 29 minutes during Sunday's 91-85 win over the Warriors Blue at the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Sharp put together a solid all-around performance Sunday, matching team highs in points and rebounds. Through two Summer League games, Sharp is averaging 15.5 points on just 30.8 percent shooting from the floor. While struggling with efficiency on the offensive end, Sharp has shined defensively, averaging 2.0 steals and 1.0 blocks per game.

items.headline: The Kings selected Sharp with the No. 45 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: After spending his entire four-year college career at Houston, Sharp will head to Sacramento and try to carve out a meaningful role. The Kings are amid a rebuild, and depending on their offseason moves, the 22-year-old guard could crack the rotation. Over 37 starts for the Cougars in 2025-26, he averaged 15.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.2 steals in 29.4 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Monday that Thiero (knee) has participated in live action, and the hope is that he'll be available by the end of the week, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Thiero has yet to make his season debut while recovering from a left knee injury, though he's trending in the right direction. However, the second-year forward isn't expected to play a meaningful role once healthy.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Thiero has yet to appear in the regular season and can be considered week-to-week. Even when he's healthy, Thiero isn't expected to play a key role for the Lakers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Thiero has yet to appear in a regular-season game due to a left knee injury that he picked up during preseason action in early October. His next chance to play is Sunday against the Raptors, but it's unclear when the second-year pro will be cleared to make his 2026-27 debut.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Thiero will miss his fifth consecutive outing to begin the 2026-27 campaign with swelling in his left knee. His next chance to suit up will come against the Warriors on Friday in the first Emirates NBA Cup matchup.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
items.story: Thiero continues to miss time due to swelling in his left knee. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Utah, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Thiero will miss a third straight game due to a left knee effusion. His next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Thiero will miss a second straight game, and the young forward has yet to make his debut in 2026-27. His next chance will come against the Jazz on Sunday, but even if he gets the green light, he's not expected to have a sizable role in the rotation.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Thiero (knee), who is out for Wednesday's game against Golden State, will begin ramping up soon and can be considered day-to-day moving forward, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Thiero won't play in Wednesday's regular-season opener due to swelling in his left knee. The second-year forward has yet to begin ramping up, so he can be considered highly questionable for Friday's game against the Clippers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Thiero will miss Wednesday's regular-season opener due to swelling in his left knee. His next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) didn't practice Tuesday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Thiero missed Los Angeles' final two preseason outings and also sat out Monday's practice with an undisclosed injury. The Lakers will release their injury report for Wednesday's regular-season opener against Golden State by Tuesday night, but for now, the 22-year-old can be considered questionable.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) didn't practice Monday, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: Thiero is trending in the wrong direction for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors. The Lakers continues to give him maintenance for an undisclosed issue.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) is out for Friday's preseason finale versus the Nuggets, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Thiero will miss the Lakers' final two exhibition games for "maintenance." It's unclear if he'll be good to go for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) is being managed for "maintenance," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: Thiero's practice reps are limited by an undisclosed issue. His status is uncertain for Friday's preseason finale against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) is out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Thiero is among several Lakers players who have been ruled out, though the team hasn't specified the reason for his absence. Coach JJ Redick indicated that the young forward remains day-to-day, leaving open the possibility of a return for Friday's preseason finale against Denver.

items.headline: Thiero tallied seven points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT) and four rebounds across 17 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: After an encouraging Summer League campaign, coach JJ Redick intends to give the 6-foot-8 Arkansas product every opportunity to be a key support piece for the Lakers this season. Unlike other spots in LA's rotation, Thiero's position is a bit more wide open, with Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Jarred Vanderbilt all competing for time. Although he shouldn't be considered a viable fantasy option right now, Thiero has the potential to be a bigger contributor.

items.headline: Thiero is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Lakers are playing on the second leg of a back-to-back preseason set, so there's no reason to play most of their starters. Thiero is vying for a spot in the frontcourt rotation, so he'll aim to make the most of this opportunity.

items.headline: Thiero finished Saturday's 92-88 Summer League loss to Golden State with 18 points (6-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes.
items.story: It was an efficient performance from Thiero, who made all nine of his shots between the field and the charity stripe while leading the Lakers in points, rebounds and steals. It was Thiero's first double-double of the Summer League and his most points in a game since July 10 against the Thunder (20). The 2025 second-rounder averaged just 6.0 minutes per game across 25 regular-season games in his rookie year, but he'll have the opportunity to earn a larger, more consistent role for himself in training camp and in the preseason.

items.headline: Thiero posted 15 points (4-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes in Saturday's 91-70 Summer League win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Behind a 34-point outburst from Arthur Kaluma, Thiero finished as the Lakers' second-leading scorer in the blowout win. He has now scored in double figures in four consecutive outings dating back to the California Classic Summer League. After averaging 1.9 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6.0 minutes per contest across 25 regular-season appearances as a rookie, the second-year wing will look to carve out a larger role during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Thiero (wrist) finished with 20 points (8-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-5 FT), four rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 96-84 Summer League win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Thiero had been battling a wrist injury heading into this contest. However, not only did he suit up and get the start, but he also finished with a game-high 20 points. The 2025 No. 36 overall pick averaged 1.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.3 steals over 6.0 minutes in 25 regular-season appearances for the Lakers in 2025-26. If Thiero continues to play well during Summer League, he might be able to climb the depth chart heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Thiero (wrist) will start in Friday's Summer League game against Oklahoma City, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Thiero had been dealing with a wrist injury, but he'll get the start to open Los Angeles' Las Vegas stint. The 22-year-old appeared in 25 regular-season games for the Lakers in 2025-26, averaging 1.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.3 steals across 6.0 minutes.

items.headline: Thiero did not play in Monday's 88-84 California Classic Summer League win over the Spurs due to a right wrist injury, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Lakers' Summer League head coach Ty Abbott said he's hopeful that Thiero will be available for their first game in Las Vegas against the Thunder on Friday, so for now, he can be considered questionable for that one. The good news is that it doesn't sound like Thiero is dealing with anything too serious.

items.headline: Thiero recorded 13 points (3-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-7 FT), three rebounds, three steals and two assists in 28 minutes during Sunday's 93-91 double-overtime win over the Heat at the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Thiero put together a solid all-around performance Sunday despite struggling from the floor. He stood out defensively, logging a game-high three steals. Through two Summer League games, Thiero is averaging 11.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 steals and 2.0 assists in 24.5 minutes per contest. One area in which he has struggled thus far is efficiency, as he has shot just 31.6 percent from the field on 19 attempts.

items.headline: Thiero produced zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over three minutes during Monday's 115-110 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Los Angeles' second-round rookie was used sparingly by the Lakers in 2025-26, logging a total of 25 regular-season appearances for an average of 6.0 minutes per contest. Depending on how many changes the team makes this offseason, Thiero could be in a better spot to compete for minutes in 2026-27.

items.headline: Thiero was ejected from Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Rockets, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Thiero got tied up with Aaron Holiday late in the fourth quarter, leading to both of them getting ejected. He concludes the contest with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 FT). in six minutes.

items.headline: Thiero (face) returned to Tuesday's game against the Thunder with 7:54 remaining in the third quarter, per the broadcast.
items.story: Thiero took an elbow to the face in the second quarter and immediately headed back to the locker room. However, he was eventually cleared to return and will likely continue to play meaningful minutes the rest of the way for the banged-up Lakers.

items.headline: Thiero exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Tuesday's game against the Thunder due to an apparent facial injury, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Thiero caught an elbow to the face from Chet Holmgren and headed straight back to the locker room with a towel on his face. Thiero should be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Sunday.
items.story: Since their last game Thursday, the Lakers have lost Austin Reaves (oblique) and Luka Doncic (hamstring) to long-term injuries, and with Marcus Smart (ankle) joining them on the sideline for Sunday's game in Dallas, Thiero was summoned from the G League to provide reinforcement. Even if he's included in the rotation Sunday, Thiero likely won't be in store for enough minutes to make a meaningful fantasy impact.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is available for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Thiero will be available off the bench after three straight absences. He's not guaranteed any minutes, however.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Thiero will miss a third straight game due to a left knee injury. His absence doesn't figure to impact the rotation. His next chance to suit up comes Tuesday against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) won't play Friday versus the Nets.
items.story: Thiero will miss his second straight game due to the knee issue, but he's a negligible part of the rotation anyway. His next chance to suit up will come Monday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Thiero is not usually in the rotation for the Lakers, so his absence won't have many fantasy implications. He's made only four appearances since playing double-digit minutes against the Spurs on Feb. 10.

items.headline: Thiero is questionable for Wednesday's game against Indiana due to left knee soreness.
items.story: It's unclear as to when this injury popped up for Thiero, who logged two minutes Monday night against Detroit. He's appeared in three games for the Lakers in March, so even if he is cleared to play, he's unlikely to be much of a factor.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Sunday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Thiero and Kobe Bufkin were both inactive for Saturday's 105-104 win over the Magic, but the two will rejoin the Lakers ahead of their next game Monday in Detroit. Thiero hasn't typically been included in the rotation when the Lakers are at full strength, but he could be needed to handle some minutes if Rui Hachimura (calf) and Marcus Smart (ankle) -- both of whom are listed as questionable -- are unable to play Monday.

items.headline: The Lakers assigned Thiero to the G League's South Bay Lakers on Friday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Thiero continues to bounce back and forth between the G League and the NBA. The rookie forward has a much clearer path to consistent developmental reps with South Bay.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Saturday.
items.story: Thiero will be available off the bench for the Lakers' game Saturday against the Nuggets but isn't expected to be featured in the rotation. He suited up for the G League club Friday and played 31 minutes in South Bay's 125-106 win over the Iowa Wolves, finishing with 20 points (7-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block.

items.headline: Garland notched 26 points (10-21 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and eight assists in 34 minutes during Monday's 116-104 loss to Houston.
items.story: Garland led his team in scoring, three-pointers and assists, but it wasn't enough to stop the Clippers from dropping a fourth consecutive game. He's now scored 20 or more points in five of his last six outings, and he stepped up his playmaking after totaling seven dimes in his previous two contests. Garland was unable to make an impact on the defensive end, but he did limit his mistakes effectively, committing just a single turnover for the third time in his last four games.

items.headline: Garland ended with 23 points (8-17 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five assists, two steals and one block over 35 minutes in Thursday's 124-112 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: After shooting at least 40.0 percent from deep in the Clippers' last three contests, Garland wasn't nearly as efficient Thursday. The 26-year-old still managed to score at least 20 points for the fourth consecutive game, and he's also been more productive on the defensive end of late. Garland is having an All-Star-caliber 2026-27 campaign, and he's now averaging 21.3 points, 2.2 rebounds and 6.8 assists across 33.1 minutes per outing in 14 regular-season appearances. With Brandon Ingram (Achilles) and Bradley Beal (knee) expected to return at some point, it's unknown if Garland will be able to maintain that same level of production.

items.headline: Garland produced 20 points (5-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Garland never found a rhythm as the Clippers were run out of their own building. Tuesday's outing cooled off a hot stretch for the point guard, who is averaging 21.3 points and 6.9 assists this season. With Bradley Beal (knee) and Brandon Ingram (Achilles) yet to take the floor, Garland is carrying a heavy load for a Los Angeles team that has fallen to 4-9.

items.headline: Garland produced 27 points (10-18 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and one steal in 35 minutes during Sunday's 113-105 win over Charlotte.
items.story: Garland led LA in scoring for the fourth time in five games, as he's poured in 24 or more points on four occasions over the same stretch. The silky-smooth guard has also dished out six or more assists in all seven outings in November, helping him compile averages of 19.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 7.5 assists and 2.2 three-pointers in 33.5 minutes a night. The Clippers have won two in a row and three of the last four games, and Garland's play has been at the center of it.

items.headline: Garland notched 24 points (8-17 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, seven assists and one block in 37 minutes during Friday's 113-112 victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Garland made the biggest play of the night, giving the Clippers the lead for good on a three-point play with 50 seconds left. Los Angeles has now won two of its last three after a 1-7 start. Up next is a home date with Charlotte on Sunday.

items.headline: Garland supplied 13 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and six assists in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 133-110 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Garland struggled from beyond the arc and committed four turnovers, and his playing time was limited due to the lopsided nature of the contest. The performance comes on the heels of a 24-point, 10-assist effort against the Pelicans on Sunday, so there's no reason for concern. Garland remains the focal point of the Clippers' offense and should continue to provide solid value in points, assists and threes, though his efficiency could fluctuate from night to night.

items.headline: Garland produced 24 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 9-12 FT), 10 assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: The double-double was the second of the season for Garland, as he produced 20 or more points for the fifth time in nine games to begin his first full season as a Clipper. The veteran guard still needs to prove he can stay healthy after missing significant time in 2023-24 and 2025-26, but so far in the current campaign he's averaging 21.2 points, 7.0 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.4 boards.

items.headline: Garland finished with 26 points (10-14 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and seven assists in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime loss to Miami.
items.story: Garland bounced back from a 5-of-14 shooting night against Toronto on Monday, leading the Clippers in scoring and tying Rui Hachimura for the team lead in assists. However, turnovers remain a concern for Garland. He committed six Wednesday after giving the ball away seven times Monday. That will cost him in nine-category leagues, but his scoring and playmaking still make him a solid fantasy starter.

items.headline: Garland ended with 16 points (5-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and eight assists in 36 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Garland led the Clippers in assists but struggled with his efficiency, committing seven turnovers while shooting just 35.7 percent from the field. He also failed to record a steal or block and finished with a team-worst minus-16 rating. The substantial workload and playmaking opportunities remain encouraging, though his turnovers significantly diminished his fantasy production.

items.headline: Garland notched 24 points (10-22 FG, 4-8 3Pt), five assists, two rebounds and one steal across 31 minutes in Friday's 127-101 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Garland turned in an efficient performance and tied for the game-high mark in scoring, reaching the 20-point mark for the third time across five regular-season appearances. He also matched his season high in three-pointers made after shooting 3-for-11 from downtown in his previous two contests. Additionally, the star point guard finished second on the team in assists and has dished out at least five dimes in four straight games.

items.headline: Garland racked up 16 points (7-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt), four rebounds and 11 assists across 36 minutes during Sunday's 108-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Garland led the Clippers in scoring and recorded his first double-double of the season, though he struggled from beyond the arc and committed six turnovers against Oklahoma City's aggressive defense. With Brandon Ingram (Achilles) and Max Strus (foot) sidelined, Garland continues to handle substantial offensive responsibilities, giving him a strong opportunity to produce points and assists despite his early-season efficiency issues.

items.headline: Garland amassed 26 points (9-19 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six assists and one steal across 37 minutes during Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Garland had another strong scoring night, leading the Clippers with 26 points after dropping 30 in the opener, but his nine turnovers weren't encouraging. With Bradley Beal (knee), Brandon Ingram (heel) and Max Strus (foot) all sidelined, the offense runs through Garland as the Clippers start a rebuilding season. Next up is a tough road test at Oklahoma City on Sunday.

items.headline: Garland accumulated 30 points (11-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-8 FT), one rebound, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 victory over the Kings.
items.story: The 26-year-old thrived as the focal point of the Clippers' offense in the absence of Bradley Beal (knee) and Brandon Ingram (Achilles), leading all scorers on the night in an efficient performance. Garland could be headed for career-high shot volume until his big-name teammates get healthy, giving him a chance to reach the 20 points per game plateau for the fourth time.

items.headline: Garland supplied 14 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, seven assists and a steal over 23 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Garland tied for the game lead in assists, though he committed four turnovers during the victory. Los Angeles acquired Garland from Cleveland in February in a deal for James Harden. Garland was dealing with a toe injury at the time of the trade, which limited his availability and production throughout the 2025-26 campaign. His healthy start this fall is an encouraging sign for a Clippers squad scrambling to fill the production void left by Kawhi Leonard.

items.headline: Garland recorded 11 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and four assists across 19 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Garland struggled to find his shooting rhythm, but he contributed as a facilitator, leading the Clippers' starters with four assists while committing just one turnover. The veteran guard played fewer than 20 minutes as Los Angeles distributed playing time throughout its roster, but fantasy managers shouldn't be worried about the limited playing time. He's penciled in as the starting floor general ahead of the regular-season opener against the Kings on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Garland recorded 15 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six assists and three rebounds in 15 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Garland was extremely efficient in his brief appearance, accounting for 15 points on only four field-goal attempts while committing just one turnover. The veteran guard is coming off a 2025-26 regular season in which he averaged 18.8 points and 6.7 assists per game, and he remains firmly entrenched as one of the Clippers' primary offensive initiators.

items.headline: Garland will start in Sunday's preseason opener against the Warriors, but he will only play the first half of the game, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Garland is headed into his first full season in Los Angeles with expectations he'll shoulder a heavy load offensively now that Kawhi Leonard is in Toronto. The veteran guard was limited to 45 total regular-season games in the 2025-26 campaign while splitting his time between the Cavaliers and Clippers, but Garland is healthy entering the new campaign.

items.headline: Head coach Ty Lue has been very impressed with Garland's offseason, per Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com.
items.story: Lue also notes he'll push Garland when needed, so it sounds like the Clippers are planning to give the star guard all the usage he can handle amid Brandon Ingram's (Achilles) absence. Provided he stays healthy after playing a career-low 45 regular-season games last year, Garland has the upside for a career campaign with a rebuilding Los Angeles team.

items.headline: Garland could face more competition for ballhandling duties at point guard after the Clippers drafted Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Garland came off the bench just twice for the Clippers last year, and that was likely done to ease him back into action due to nagging toe injuries. It's hard to envision the star guard seeing a noticeable decline in playing time due to the addition of Wagler, and Los Angeles must believe the two guards will mesh well alongside one another in the long run. If Wagler starts at shooting guard right away, his presence could help alleviate some of the ballhandling duties on Garland's plate.

items.headline: Garland finished with 21 points (8-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 31 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Garland battled foul trouble all night, eventually fouling out in the dying minutes. Although his numbers were fine, he never really found any rhythm, ultimately contributing to what was a devastating loss. With that said, his end to the season was certainly a positive one, positioning him to play a major role next season. In six games over the final two weeks, he averaged 17.0 points, 30. rebounds, 5.7 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.7 three-pointers.

items.headline: Garland racked up 16 points (5-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and three steals over 41 minutes during Friday's 116-97 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Garland rejoined the first unit after sitting out Wednesday's game against the Thunder. Garland has averaged 20.2 points, 6.4 assists and 2.4 rebounds since joining the Clippers. While his point total suffered, Garland exceeded his usual production in the secondary categories. For the Clippers to achieve maximum success, Garland needs to get closer to Kawhi Leonard's production, and a few of his lines have shown the potential to get there.

items.headline: Garland (toe) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's game against the Trail Blazers, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Garland was held out of Wednesday's matchup against Oklahoma City due to left toe injury management, but he's been given the green light to return Friday. He's averaging 16.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.0 steals through three April appearances.

items.headline: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
items.story: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. He was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Edwards will undergo arthroscopic right knee surgery and is expected to miss up to two months, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: This is a tough blow after a torrid start to the season for Edwards, and it looks like we might not see him again until 2027. Ayo Dosunmu will likely be elevated to a starting role while Edwards is sidelined, while LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga will see a bump in usage. There will also be more minutes available for Terrence Shannon, Bones Hyland and Cody Williams.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Edwards has been playing through knee pain this season, but it hasn't impacted his numbers, as he's already had two 40-plus-point performances. However, it's possible he could get hit with a maintenance day against the 1-3 Warriors. If Edwards is out, Ayo Dosunmu would have a chance to start, and there would be more minutes available for Terrence Shannon and Bones Hyland.

items.headline: Edwards totaled 47 points (19-34 FG, 5-15 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks in 41 minutes during Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: The Timberwolves weren't sure Edwards was going to suit up Monday, as the team was pondering a maintenance day for the star guard, but he was given the green light to play and put on a show. He turned in a game-high 47 points and reached the 40-point threshold for the second time through four games to open the new campaign. However, it wasn't quite enough to carry Minnesota to a victory, with Donovan Mitchell leading the charge for Cleveland to spoil Edwards' big night.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is available for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The Timberwolves were considering a maintenance day for the superstar guard, but Edwards is suiting up for the second end of this back-to-back set. He should be able to handle a normal workload Monday, barring any setbacks.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Minnesota is considering giving the superstar guard the night off for the second half of this back-to-back set. Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon would both have added fantasy appeal if Edwards sits out Monday.

items.headline: Edwards produced 15 points (5-23 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 115-93 victory over Orlando.
items.story: After a red-hot opening game, Edwards came crashing back to earth Friday with a highly inefficient shooting performance. While it wasn't his night offensively, he did manage to record a game-high four steals, salvaging what was an otherwise underwhelming effort. The fact Minnesota easily accounted for Orlando despite Edwards' struggles bodes well for the season ahead. As for Edwards, he will look to get back on track in a matchup against the Raptors on Sunday.

items.headline: Edwards ended with 45 points (16-29 FG, 9-17 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 victory over Miami.
items.story: Edwards was dominant Wednesday, setting a new franchise Opening Night scoring record to lead the Timberwolves to a victory to begin the 2026-27 campaign. The 2020 No. 1 overall pick averaged a career-best 28.8 points along with 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 steals over 35.0 minutes per contest in 2025-26. However, he appeared in only 61 games, marking the first season of his career with fewer than 72 appearances. Edwards has MVP potential, and while he'll face heavy competition for the award, he could at least be a finalist at the end of the year, assuming he stays healthy.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: The Timberwolves rested most of their projected regular-season rotation Wednesday, though Edwards should be back in action Wednesday. The star shooting guard appeared in four games this preseason, averaging 19.8 points, 2.3 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 0.8 steals across 22.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the Bulls, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network reports.
items.story: Edwards, Rudy Gobert, LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu all appear to be resting Friday. Edwards should be good to go for the regular-season opener against the Heat on Wednesday.

items.headline: Edwards ended with 20 points (5-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 9-9 FT), three assists and two steals over 28 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Edwards had trouble finding the net Wednesday. However, he has been known to have occasional shooting slumps throughout his career, so his performance against Detroit shouldn't be a cause for concern. The 2020 No. 1 overall pick had his best year in 2025-26, averaging 28.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 steals across 35.0 minutes, though he appeared in fewer than 72 regular-season games (61) for the first time since entering the NBA.

items.headline: Edwards closed with 26 points (8-16 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 25 minutes in Monday's 122-104 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Edwards returned from a one-game absence for rest purposes and looked fantastic, knocking down a game-high five triples en route to finishing as the game's leading scorer. The star guard has scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances, though Monday marked his heaviest workload yet, surpassing the 20-minute mark while also reaching 20-plus points for the first time.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason matchup with the Knicks.
items.story: Edwards is back after a one-game absence, but he'll likely still have his minutes limited, with this being the preseason. He's played well in his first two preseason games and looks comfortable sharing the floor with LaMelo Ball.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is not available for Saturday's preseason game against Miami.
items.story: Both Edwards and LaMelo Ball (rest) will get a breather Saturday while Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon form the Timberwolves' starting backcourt. In Edwards' last appearance against the Pacers on Wednesday, he finished with 19 points, one rebound and one assist over 20 minutes in a 123-112 loss. His next opportunity to play is Monday against New York.

items.headline: Edwards recorded 19 points (5-10 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound and one assist in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to Indiana.
items.story: Edwards was efficient from beyond the arc, connecting on four of five three-point attempts while playing limited minutes. The star guard continues to benefit from Minnesota's revamped offensive attack, with LaMelo Ball providing another playmaking option in the backcourt.

items.headline: da Silva racked up 12 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt) and two rebounds in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Da Silva has attempted just 13 shots over his last two games after averaging 15.7 across his previous three appearances. His improved efficiency hasn't offset the reduced offensive involvement, while limited defensive production further restricts his fantasy ceiling. Paolo Banchero's (ankle) eventual return could squeeze his opportunities further.

items.headline: Da Silva isn't starting Monday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Da Silva started Friday's game against Milwaukee due to Jalen Suggs coming off the bench in his return from a knee injury, but Suggs will return to the first unit for Monday's clash. Da Silva is averaging 15.8 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in his last five appearances as a reserve.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Jalen Suggs (knee) will come off the bench in his return to action, opening the door for da Silva to join the first unit in his return from a two-game absence due to a calf strain. Over his last five appearances (one start), the 25-year-old forward has averaged 15.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 31.8 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) is available for Friday's game against the Bucks, Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com reports.
items.story: After drawing a questionable tag and participating in Friday's morning shootaround, da Silva has been cleared to return from a two-game absence. Over his last five appearances (one start), the third-year forward has averaged 15.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 31.8 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) participated in the Magic's morning shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Da Silva has already missed multiple games due to the calf issue, but this is a step in the right direction. His participation in shootaround is a positive sign, but he'll still need to be cleared before Orlando can count on him for frontcourt minutes against the Bucks.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) is questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Da Silva is in danger of missing a third straight game with a left calf strain. Alex Morales, Goga Bitadze and Jase Richardson would continue to see more opportunities if da Silva is unable to go Friday night.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus the Jazz.
items.story: Da Silva will miss his second consecutive contest. With Orlando also down Paolo Banchero (ankle), Jalen Suggs (knee) and Jamal Cain (shoulder), head coach Sean Sweeney will shuffle things around, resulting in Alex Morales making his first career start. Goga Bitadze and Jase Richardson are in line for more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game at Utah.
items.story: Da Silva has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a left calf strain. The Magic could be extremely shorthanded in the frontcourt Wednesday, as Jamal Cain (shoulder) is also in danger of joining Paolo Banchero (ankle) on the inactive list.

items.headline: Da Silva (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Kings, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Da Silva was questionable to suit up due to a left calf strain, and he will indeed miss his first contest of the 2026-27 campaign with the ailment. Tuesday is the first night of a back-to-back set for Orlando, so the hope is that he'll be able to return for the road tilt against Utah on Wednesday. Jase Richardson, Jamal Cain and Jevon Carter should all see an uptick in minutes, but we'll have to wait for confirmation on who's replacing da Silva in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Da Silva is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Kings due to a left calf strain.
items.story: Da Silva was a late addition to the injury report, which is never a good sign, but the severity of the issue remains unclear. If he joins Jalen Suggs (knee) and Paolo Banchero (ankle) on the sidelines, Jase Richardson, Jamal Cain and Jevon Carter would be candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Da Silva posted 19 points (7-21 FG, 5-16 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and a steal across 39 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Da Silva had the green light to let it fly from beyond the arc, but his efficiency was poor. That's been a trend lately, as he's made just 34.8 percent of his three-pointers over his last four games in which he's logged at least 30 minutes. This was da Silva's first start of the season, but given that he approached the 20-point mark and pulled down seven rebounds -- his second-best output of the season in that category -- he could continue to see expanded playing time in a frontcourt without Paolo Banchero (ankle).

items.headline: Da Silva will start in Saturday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Da Silva will make his first start of the 2026-27 campaign Saturday. The 25-year-old started 34 regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 12.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists while shooting 38.2 percent from deep over 28.8 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Da Silva finished Thursday's 117-104 loss to the Suns with 18 points (6-15 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 30 minutes.
items.story: Da Silva finished as Orlando's second-leading scorer, connecting on four three-pointers while attempting a team-high 12 shots from beyond the arc. The third-year forward continues to see substantial playing time with Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, averaging 14.1 points across his first seven appearances this season. Although his contributions outside of scoring were limited Thursday, da Silva remains an appealing source of points and three-pointers while Banchero is unavailable.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with 23 points (9-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt), 10 rebounds and two assists across 35 minutes during Sunday's 108-97 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Following a quiet showing in Friday's 121-114 win over Toronto, da Silva erupted for his first double-double of the season Sunday. The 23 points and 10 rebounds were season highs for the 25-year-old, while the boards matched a career high he recorded back in January of 2025. Orlando will continue to rely on da Silva's production off the bench while Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) remain sidelined.

items.headline: Da Silva logged 20 points (8-10 FG, 4-5 3PT, 0-3 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 loss to Toronto.
items.story: The Magic struggled on both ends of the floor Wednesday, but da Silva managed to lead his team in scoring on only 10 field-goal attempts. He's connected on at least four three-pointers in three of the first four games of the regular season and has gone 14-for-31 (45.2 percent) from beyond the arc in that span. Da Silva's production floor will continue to be elevated for as long as Paolo Banchero (ankle) is on the shelf.

items.headline: Da Silva closed Sunday's 111-102 victory over the Knicks with 19 points (7-13 FG, 5-9 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one block over 27 minutes.
items.story: Anthony Black made his season debut Sunday, but Paolo Banchero is facing an extended absence with a high-ankle sprain and Jalen Suggs left Sunday's game early with a knee injury. Da Silva should remain worth streaming in most fantasy leagues as Orlando's sixth man for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Da Silva notched five points (2-9 FG, 1-7 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 29 minutes during Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: It wasn't a great outing for da Silva, as he was unable to replicate what he did during the season opener. His playing time remains solid, logging 29 minutes off the bench in this one. However, as a player whose overall value is built on points and threes, the off nights tend to hurt a little more. At this point, da Silva should be viewed as more of a stream-level player, as opposed to someone who needs to be rostered.

items.headline: The Magic have exercised da Silva's fourth-year rookie-scale team option, keeping him under contract through the 2027-28 season, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: The decision gives Orlando another year of control over the 2024 first-round pick, who has established himself as a versatile forward capable of spacing the floor. Da Silva will continue competing for minutes in a crowded Magic frontcourt, with his fantasy upside largely dependent on securing a consistent rotation role and increasing his offensive involvement.

items.headline: Da Silva recorded 18 points (7-14 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 0-0 FT), three rebounds, five assists and a steal across 20 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Da Silva provided an offensive spark off Orlando's bench, finishing third on the team in scoring while knocking down four three-pointers. The forward was particularly aggressive from beyond the arc, attempting 11 shots from deep and accounting for more than a third of the Magic's three-point attempts among reserves. His perimeter shooting could help him compete for consistent minutes in Orlando's regular-season rotation.

items.headline: Da Silva won't start Tuesday's preseason meeting with Cleveland.
items.story: Desmond Bane is back from his rest day, forcing da Silva back to the second unit. The 25-year-old forward is expected to play a meaningful role off the bench behind Paolo Banchero this season.

items.headline: Da Silva finished with 17 points (6-14 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals over 24 minutes in Sunday's 119-105 preseason loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Da Silva had another productive performance Sunday, with the 2024 No. 18 overall pick now having scored a combined 36 points in his first two preseason appearances. He averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 24.7 minutes in 77 regular-season games, including 34 starts, in 2025-26. While da Silva may not start as often during the 2026-27 campaign if Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner can stay healthy, he should continue to get his share of minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Sunday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: With Desmond Bane getting the night off for rest purposes, da Silva will join the first unit. Over 25 minutes in Wednesday's preseason-opening win over the Grizzlies, he provided 19 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal.

items.headline: Da Silva logged 19 points (6-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 122-118 preseason win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Da Silva wasn't very efficient from two-point range but put together a solid performance from beyond the arc en route to a game-high 19 points. The 25-year-old forward also tied for third on the team in rebounds. Da Silva averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals across 24.7 minutes per game in 2025-26, and he figures to serve as Paolo Banchero's primary backup this season.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with nine points (3-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Germany's 96-94 loss to Poland in Tuesday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Da Silva has been staying active this offseason ahead of his third NBA season. The Magic more or less maintained the same core from the 2025-26 campaign, positioning da Silva for a bench role at power forward behind Paolo Banchero to begin the year. Da Silva averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest over 77 regular-season games (34 starts) in 2025-26.

items.headline: Da Silva chipped in zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over eight minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to the Pistons in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Even with Franz Wagner (calf) and Jonathan Isaac (knee) sidelined, da Silva was phased out of the Orlando rotation at times during this series. It was still a positive 2025-26 campaign overall for the second-year forward, who averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per tilt over 77 regular-season games (34 starts).

items.headline: Da Silva posted 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt) and six rebounds over 23 minutes during Friday's 93-79 loss to the Pistons in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: After barely featuring for much of the first-round series, da Silva logged 23 minutes Friday, scoring double-digit points for the first time in the playoffs. Although the second-year forward had a solid outing, Orlando is going to need a lot more from its stars and role players alike if it hopes to put an end to Detroit's season in Game 7 on Sunday. Through six games, da Silva has averaged just 4.8 points and 3.3 rebounds in 16.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva racked up four points (2-2 FG) and two rebounds across 14 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 Play-In Game loss to the 76ers.
items.story: In what was another disappointing performance, da Silva offered very little on either end of the floor. Outside of a brief period in which he put himself firmly on the standard league radar, things haven't gone as planned in recent times. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, da Silva has been well outside the top-300 players in fantasy, averaging just 8.4 points and 3.6 rebounds in 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Da Silva will return to his regular bench role due to the return of Franz Wagner (ankle) to the first unit. In 40 appearances off the bench this season, da Silva is averaging 8.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists across 21.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: With Franz Wagner (ankle) unavailable for the second half of this back-to-back, da Silva will enter the starting five. As a starter this season (33 games), the second-year forward has averaged 12.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 28.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva supplied 19 points (6-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Friday's 138-127 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Paolo Banchero had a subpar showing after finishing with 10 points across 31 minutes Friday, but da Silva stepped up in a big way and finished tied for the third-most points on the Magic with Jalen Suggs -- only Wendell Carter (28 points) and Desmond Bane (27 points) outpaced them. The return of Franz Wagner means da Silva will head to the bench for the rest of the season, and while he can deliver solid fantasy production as long as he stays on the court, the reduced role will clearly have a toll on his fantasy value.

items.headline: Da Silva is not in the Magic's starting lineup against the Hawks on Wednesday, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
items.story: Da Silva has started 19 of the Magic's last 21 games (including 13 straight), and over that span, he has averaged 13.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 2.0 threes and 1.0 steals over 30.6 minutes. The second-year pro will retreat to the bench due to the return of Franz Wagner (ankle), but da Silva should continue to operate in a prominent role, especially if the former plays under a minutes restriction.

items.headline: Da Silva accumulated 18 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes during Thursday's 121-117 win over the Kings.
items.story: Da Silva continues to take advantage of several injuries in Orlando. He's been a solid source of fantasy value, posting averages of 14.1 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.8 three-pointers over his last 12 games.

items.headline: Da Silva contributed 21 points (9-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt), three rebounds, five assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Monday's 128-126 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After a number of underwhelming performances, da Silva managed to get things back on track, scoring at least 20 points for the first time in his past six appearances. Although he continues to start, da Silva has struggled to put up consistent numbers, ranking outside the top 110 over the past week. In four games during that time, he has averaged 12.5 points, 0.8 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, making him nothing more than a schedule-based streaming consideration.

items.headline: Da Silva notched 12 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across 21 minutes during Saturday's 105-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Da Silva continues play a significant role for the Magic amid the ongoing absence of Franz Wagner (ankle). He's started eight straight games, during which da Silva has averaged a serviceable 12.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 29.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with seven points (2-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 28 minutes during Monday's 124-112 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Despite continuing to play a sizeable role, da Silva was unable to maintain his recent production. In fact, this was arguably his worst performance in the past month, during which he has managed to put up top-40 value in standard leagues. In 14 appearances over that time, he has averaged 12.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 1.7 three-pointers. Despite this effort, he is worth holding for the time being, at least while Anthony Black (abdomen) and Franz Wagner (ankle) are sidelined.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way deal with Minnesota on Tuesday, per Sam Amico of HoopsWire.com.
items.story: The Timberwolves just waived Freeman on Saturday, but it didn't take long for the two sides to hash out a new contract. Freeman is likely to spend most of his time with the G League's Iowa Wolves.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) was waived by the Timberwolves on Saturday.
items.story: Freeman appeared in three preseason games for Minnesota, averaging 1.3 points and 1.3 rebounds over 5.7 minutes per contest. He does have experience at the NBA level beyond the preseason, so there's a chance he could earn a deep roster spot with a club at some point moving forward.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) won't play in Friday's preseason game against Chicago.
items.story: Freeman will miss another preseason contest due to a shoulder injury he sustained in Saturday's 125-124 win over Miami. It's unknown if he will be ready to suit up when the Timberwolves begin the regular season Wednesday versus the Heat.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) was unavailable for Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Freeman exited Saturday's contest against Miami due to a right shoulder injury and has since missed two consecutive games. The forward's final opportunity to suit up during the preseason will come Friday against Chicago.

items.headline: Freeman is out for Monday's preseason matchup with the Knicks due to a right shoulder injury.
items.story: Freeman exited Saturday's exhibition with a shoulder injury and will now miss Monday's preseason game. His next chance to get out there will come Wednesday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way contract with the Timberwolves on Thursday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Freeman was also on a two-way deal with Minnesota a season ago. He spent the majority of his time playing for the G League's Iowa Wolves, averaging 16.5 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.1 made threes in 39 games.

items.headline: The Timberwolves recalled Freeman from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Monday.
items.story: The move perhaps signals that Minnesota is bracing for Naz Reid (shoulder) to miss some time. Freeman is averaging 35.6 minutes per game over his last six G League games but hasn't yet made his Timberwolves debut.

items.headline: Minnesota recalled Freeman from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Tuesday.
