items.story: This transaction comes after he put up 26 points (10-13 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and a block across 27 minutes in Monday's 132-104 G League victory over the Westchester Knicks. With Jaden McDaniels (hip) slated to miss Tuesday's game, Freeman may have an opportunity to play, which would be his first NBA appearance of the season.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way contract with the Timberwolves on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: A second-round pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Freeman was limited to 22 regular-season appearances with the Pacers in 2024-25. He made a strong impression in the Summer League, however, averaging 16.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks.

items.headline: Freeman tallied 14 points (7-8 FG, 0-3 FT), 10 rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes in Friday's 113-104 Summer League win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Freeman closed out an impressive Summer League showing with another double-double on highly efficient shooting. While the big man is expected to spend significant time in the G League during the 2025-26 season, his strong summer performance -- combined with Myles Turner's departure and Isaiah Jackson's (Achilles) injury status -- could open the door for NBA minutes.

items.headline: Freeman registered 18 points (7-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and one block in 29 minutes during Thursday's 91-88 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: It was an efficient shooting performance by Freeman, who also turned in a double-double to help lead the Pacers to victory. The two-player is in a position to spend the majority of his time in 2025-26 in the G League. However, it's worth noting that Isaiah Jackson (Achilles) may not be ready for the start of the new year to help fill the void left behind by Myles Turner at center.

items.headline: Freeman tallied 17 points (6-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal across 27 minutes in Monday's 114-105 Summer League loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Freeman notched his second straight double-double Monday, this time finishing with 17 points. He appeared in 22 regular-season games (one start) for the Pacers in 2024-25, averaging 2.1 points and 1.4 rebounds across 8.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Freeman racked up 15 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, one steal and two blocks across 23 minutes during Saturday's Summer League 104-85 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Freeman missed only one field-goal attempt on his way to recording a double-double Saturday. The Akron product had an impressive bounce-back performance after finishing with only four points and three rebounds in Friday's game against the Magic.

items.headline: Freeman finished with four points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and three rebounds across 11 minutes during Friday's 129-115 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Freeman suited up for the first time in the past 32 games, albeit for a brief appearance. With the Pacers' playoff future now set, there is a chance Freeman could remain in the rotation for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers. Beyond that, he will likely spend the majority of his time spectating from the bench.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against Portland.
items.story: The two-way player has overcome an illness and will be available off Indiana's bench Tuesday. However, Freeman hasn't appeared for the Pacers since the Jan. 8 win over Chicago, so it's not a guarantee he'll see the court against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is out for Saturday's game versus the Hawks.
items.story: Freeman has been downgraded from questionable to out Saturday due to an illness. However, the rookie big man's absence won't impact Indiana's rotation, as he hasn't seen action at the NBA level since Jan. 8.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Freeman is currently battling through an illness, which has put his availability for Saturday's game in jeopardy. The rookie second-round pick last saw NBA regular-season action Jan. 8 against the Bulls.

items.headline: Freeman accumulated one rebound and one block over three minutes during Tuesday's 122-111 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Freeman barely saw the floor again Tuesday, having played more than 10 minutes only twice thus far. Despite dealing with a number of injuries, the Pacers have seen no reason to extend Freeman beyond a depth role. He has scored a total of just 20 points across 13 games, recording a season-high six points against the Rockets.

items.headline: Freeman is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Far from surprising here, but Freeman will return to his regular bench with the return of Myles Turner to the starting lineup. Freeman is averaging 9.9 minutes per game in seven outings (one start) this season, so he's not expected to see heavy minutes off the bench with both Turner and Pascal Siakam managing most of the frontcourt minutes.

items.headline: Freeman is in the Pacers' starting lineup for Monday's game against the Raptors, Scott Agness of FieldhouseFiles.com reports.
items.story: With Myles Turner (calf) sidelined and backup big men James Wiseman (Achilles) and Isaiah Jackson (Achilles) done for the year, Freeman will make his first career start Monday. Freeman, the Pacers' second-round selection in the 2024 NBA Draft, has seen sparse playing time this season, but he has a chance to earn a bigger spot in the rotation with a solid outing Monday.

items.headline: Freeman fouled out of Monday's preseason matchup against the Grizzlies with 3:59 remaining in the fourth quarter, Alex Golden of the 'Setting the Pace' podcast reports. Freeman produced six points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
items.story: Freeman was efficient while racking up seven rebounds, tying Myles Turner for the team high. Freeman injured his knee during Thursday's preseason win over the Cavaliers, though he was able to accumulate 24 minutes Monday, so the injury is likely already past him. The 24-year-old's next chance to suit up will come in the Pacers' final preseason game Thursday versus the Hornets.

items.headline: Freeman needed assistance walking to the locker room during Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers after suffering an apparent right knee injury, Tony East of SI.com reports.
items.story: Freeman couldn't bend his knee much on his way off the floor and likely headed to the locker room for further evaluation to determine the severity of the injury. Freeman finished the game with nine points (3-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, an assist and a block across 16 minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Freeman and the Pacers agreed on a two-way contract Thursday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Freeman, who spent five years at Akron, was the 50th overall pick in the 2024 Draft. It's not surprising that he was signed to a two-way contract. He'll spend the majority of the season in the G League getting developmental minutes.

items.headline: The Pacers selected Freeman with the No. 50 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Freeman spent five years at Akron before declaring for the NBA Draft. In 2023-24, he averaged 18.6 points, 12.9 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 1.6 assists in 35 games. While Freeman has shown impressive rebounding abilities for a 6-foot-7 forward, there is no obvious path for playing time right out of the gate.

items.headline: Kuminga contributed 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Monday's 142-116 win over the Nets.
items.story: Kuminga has scored in double figures in five straight appearances, averaging 15.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists during that stretch. His consistent starting role provides fantasy stability, though inconsistent perimeter shooting limits his upside.

items.headline: Kuminga totaled 23 points (7-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three blocks in 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Kuminga was held out of Tuesday's matchup against the Trail Blazers due to a shoulder injury, but he was cleared to suit up Thursday evening. He made it clear that the issue is no longer bothering him, as the 24-year-old led Minnesota in scoring while also chipping in on the defensive end. Kuminga recorded multiple swats for just the second time through 15 appearances this season.

items.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is available for Thursday's game against New York.
items.story: Kuminga sustained a right shoulder contusion in Monday's 106-98 loss to Portland and wasn't available for the rematch Tuesday. After carrying a questionable designation throughout the day, he has now been cleared to suit up for the meeting with the defending champs. The 24-year-old has appeared in 14 regular-season games for Minnesota in 2026-27, all of them starts, averaging 12.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting a career-best 39.3 percent from deep over 30.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Charlie Walton of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
items.story: After missing Tuesday's game against Portland, Kuminga now has a chance to return Thursday from a bruised shoulder. His status will affect Terrence Shannon's streaming appeal most prominently in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
items.story: Kuminga sustained a bruised shoulder during Monday's meeting with the Trail Blazers, and he's sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Terrence Shannon appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Kuminga in the starting lineup, while Trey Lyles and Bones Hyland will both have a chance to claim a larger role.

items.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 106-98 win over Portland and did not return, Andrew Dukowitz of ZoneCoverage.com reports. He closed with 13 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes.
items.story: Kuminga put together a productive performance before aggravating his right shoulder on a shot attempt, exiting at the 6:35 mark of the fourth quarter and not returning. The forward's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday in a rematch against Portland, though the quick turnaround makes his availability highly questionable pending further updates. Should Kuminga miss time, Terrence Shannon could see an increased workload.

items.headline: Kuminga closed Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans with 17 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-12 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
items.story: The 24-year-old forward has been one of the bigger beneficiaries of the shot volume that opened up when Anthony Edwards (knee) was shut down. Kuminga is averaging nearly three shots a game more without Edwards on the court, averaging 14.2 points, 6.0 boards, 3.3 assists, 2.2 threes and 1.9 combined blocks and steals in six games since the Minnesota superstar went for surgery. There could be more meat on the bone for Kuminga as well, as his 42.9 percent FG shooting over that stretch would be a career-low mark.

items.headline: Kuminga logged 16 points (5-10 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 117-107 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Kuminga chipped in across the board, continuing what has been a strong start to his career in Minnesota. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined for an extended period, Kuminga has been tasked with doing more on both ends of the floor, a role that seems to agree with him. Through nine appearances, he has averaged 12.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 2.1 three-pointers and 2.2 combined steals and blocks, good enough for top-90 value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Kuminga registered eight points (3-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds, three assists and four blocks in 33 minutes during Monday's 112-100 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Kuminga struggled to make an offensive impact but compensated with a season-high four blocks and his first double-digit rebounding performance of the campaign. The forward also connected on two triples, providing valuable production in multiple fantasy categories despite scoring in single digits. His defensive contributions were particularly encouraging, though his modest offensive involvement remains worth monitoring.

items.headline: Kuminga registered 20 points (7-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Kuminga stepped into a bigger offensive role with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, leading Minnesota in scoring while adding five assists without a turnover. His three triples and two steals added valuable fantasy production, making this one of his most balanced performances of the season. Kuminga could see increased scoring opportunities during Edwards' absence, which should raise his fantasy ceiling considerably.

items.headline: Kuminga notched 10 points (4-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 36 minutes in Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Kuminga recorded his first double-double of the season Monday and has been consistent to open the year, scoring in double digits in every game despite not attempting more than 10 shots in any of his four appearances. Sharing the floor with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball could continue to limit his scoring opportunities, but since Kuminga is putting up decent numbers in other categories like rebounds and steals, he's delivering solid upside. He's certainly making the most of his opportunity to play consistent starter-level minutes.

items.headline: Kuminga racked up 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 26 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Kuminga made the most of his limited shot attempts, knocking down three triples while committing no turnovers. The forward also contributed defensively and finished with a plus-23 rating in his 26 minutes. His efficiency was encouraging, though his fantasy ceiling will depend on whether he can establish a more substantial offensive role alongside Anthony Edwards.

items.headline: Kuminga finished with 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 0-0 FT), a rebound, three assists, four steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 win over the Heat.
items.story: Kuminga's regular-season debut with Minnesota featured limited rebounding but excellent defensive production, with his four steals showing how he can contribute in other areas, since he'll likely hold a secondary role in an offense monopolized by Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball. Kuminga's fantasy outlook will improve if he maintains this playing time and contributes more consistently in peripheral stats, since he's not expected to be a go-to scoring option anytime soon.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Kuminga joined several other regulars on the inactive list for Friday's preseason finale, but he should play Wednesday. The 24-year-old forward is ready to prove himself in a starting role with Minnesota after signing a two-year, $13 million deal in August.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Bulls, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: Kuminga will join several other key contributors on the inactive list in Minnesota's preseason finale. He should be able to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.

items.headline: Kuminga (soreness) recorded 16 points (5-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: After missing Minnesota's previous two exhibitions due to soreness, Kuminga showed little rust in his return, missing just one field-goal attempt while connecting twice from beyond the arc. His efficient performance and 22-minute workload were positive developments as he works toward being fully ready for the regular season.

items.headline: Kuminga (soreness) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Detroit.
items.story: Kuminga missed the previous two games due to general soreness but will return to the starting lineup Wednesday. The forward should see a fair amount of playing time in the first half, though his workload may be limited given the exhibition setting.

items.headline: Kuminga (general soreness) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: "[Kuminga] is dealing with a little bit of bumps and bruises that we're just being overly cautious with," said head coach Chris Finch when asked why Kuminga would miss Monday's exhibition. It sounds like there's a decent chance Kuminga will be able to get back out there for Wednesday's preseason meeting with the Pistons.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) is not available against the Heat on Saturday.
items.story: Kuminga played in each of the Timberwolves' first two preseason games but will observe Saturday's game from the bench in street clothes. His next chance to play is against the Knicks on Monday.

items.headline: Kuminga finished with two points (1-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt), three assists, one rebound and one steal in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Kuminga got the starting nod for the second straight game, another indication that he is likely to hold onto that spot when the season proper begins. Although he attempted the second-most shots behind Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels, Kuminga's fantasy flaws were on full display, managing to connect on just one shot from nine attempts. Assuming he is given the green light to start on opening night, Kuminga is worth a look late in drafts, remembering that if and when his shot isn't falling, he has very little to fall back on in terms of peripheral production.

items.headline: Kuminga contributed eight points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and two rebounds across 14 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: Kuminga started at power forward and scored Minnesota's first points of the game, finishing a drive off a feed from Ball. He didn't see much offensive volume after that, but he was efficient when called upon, making all four free throws and committing no turnovers. Kuminga's place in the starting five is particularly notable as Minnesota begins evaluating how its revamped frontcourt will fit together during the preseason, and it wouldn't be surprising if he opens the 2026-27 regular season in a starting role.

items.headline: Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with the Timberwolves on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Kuminga spent most of his career in Golden State before briefly suiting up for Atlanta during the 2025-26 campaign. In 294 career regular-season appearances, the 2021 No. 7 overall pick has averaged 12.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists across 22.1 minutes. He isn't the most efficient shooter from deep, but he will add more depth to a team that also acquired LaMelo Ball during the offseason. Kuminga might initially come off the bench, though that could change along the way.

items.headline: Coward racked up 16 points (6-15 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal in 30 minutes during Monday's 117-111 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: Coward continues to provide steady fantasy production, averaging 15.4 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 3.4 assists in 17 appearances. His consistent playing time and strong rebounding from the wing make him a valuable option across most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Coward finished with 23 points (8-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 3-5 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and four steals over 30 minutes in Saturday's 104-95 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Cameron Boozer (ankle) and Jerami Grant (calf) were unavailable for this contest. Despite Ty Jerome (hip) returning after missing the last four games, Coward tied his season high in points and steals. The 23-year-old did commit six turnovers Saturday. However, he has played well overall during the 2026-27 campaign and is now averaging 15.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.6 steals over 28.8 minutes per contest in 16 regular-season appearances. Coward has also shot an efficient 47.2 percent from deep and has drained at least four three-pointers in four of his previous five games.

items.headline: Coward logged 19 points (7-14 FG, 5-9 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Coward has hit 11 triples over his last three games, thriving as a perimeter threat while maintaining meaningful playmaking responsibilities. His versatile production provides a strong fantasy floor, although Thursday's blowout limited his minutes. He's becoming a dependable option across formats.

items.headline: Coward amassed 20 points (6-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 victory over Cleveland.
items.story: Coward was locked in from the jump, not missing a single shot through the first half of action, and he finished with a team-best plus-12 differential in the narrow win. Coward has been in a nice rhythm over the past three games, averaging 19.7 points, 7.7 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 3.3 triples, 1.7 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.0 turnovers per game on 58.8 percent shooting from the field and 75.0 percent at the line.

items.headline: Coward finished with 23 points (7-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks across 33 minutes in Saturday's 129-110 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (hip) and Zach Edey (ankle) both sidelined for this contest, Coward put the Grizzlies on his back by tying his season high in points to lead his team to their third win in the last four games. The 23-year-old still appears to have plenty of untapped potential, but he's shown signs of growth. In 12 regular-season appearances during the 2026-27 campaign, Coward is now averaging 13.8 points, 8.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.5 steals, all career highs, across 28.8 minutes per contest. He has also shot 43.5 percent from deep after draining only 33.8 percent of his attempts in 2025-26.

items.headline: Coward finished with 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds and four assists over 27 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: This was Coward's third double-double of the season and the 10th of his career. He's been a top-40 producer this season with averages of 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.3 triples and 1.5 steals per game.

items.headline: Coward tallied 23 points (8-19 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Coward was coming off back-to-back 10-point performances, but he was much more aggressive seeking out his own shot Wednesday and cracked the 20-point plateau for the first time this season. He'll look to keep his momentum going into Friday's meeting with the Thunder.

items.headline: Coward logged 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds and three assists over 31 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Coward fell just one rebound short of what would have been his third double-double of the season, although as a whole, this was a somewhat underwhelming performance. Despite some inconsistencies, Coward has cobbled together a strong start to the season, averaging 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.5 three-pointers, good enough for borderline top-50 value.

items.headline: Coward finished with 16 points (6-12 FG, 4-4 3Pt), 11 rebounds, three assists and one steal across 31 minutes during Monday's 110-105 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Coward recorded his second straight double-double, helping Memphis to its fourth straight victory to begin the season. After missing the second game of the campaign due to a wrist injury, Coward has put that behind him, playing some of the best basketball of his young career. In three appearances thus far, he has averaged 12.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.7 three-pointers, good enough for top-55 value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Coward delivered 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Coward recorded his first double-double of the season and posted another efficient performance while surpassing the 30-minute plateau for the first time in 2026-27. His efficient perimeter shooting also provided a boost. It's still early in the season, but Coward's consistent playing time and rebounding production are encouraging for fantasy managers, although his scoring opportunities could fluctuate alongside Memphis' other offensive options.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) is available for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Coward sat out Friday's 111-108 win over the Warriors with a left wrist sprain, but he's back in the starting lineup after a one-game absence. He started his lone appearance this season, tallying seven points, seven rebounds, two assists and a block in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) is questionable for Sunday's game in Sacramento.
items.story: Coward sat out Friday's 111-108 win over the Warriors due to the wrist issue, which resulted in GG Jackson drawing the start, and Jerami Grant saw a minor bump in minutes. It will likely be more of the same if Coward gets ruled out again.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Coward will miss Friday's contest due to a left wrist sprain, and his next chance to suit up will come Sunday against Sacramento. With the 23-year-old swingman sidelined, Jerami Grant, Scotty Pippen, Cam Spencer and GG Jackson are all candidates for a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Coward is doubtful for Friday's game against the Warriors due to a left wrist sprain.
items.story: Coward is expected to miss Friday's contest after posting seven points, seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 28 minutes in Wednesday's season-opening win over Utah. If he's ultimately ruled out, Jerami Grant, Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen would all be candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Coward chipped in seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Coward didn't need to shoulder much of the scoring load with Ty Jerome dominating offensively, but the second-year wing made an impact on the glass and finished with a plus-23 rating. His 28-minute workload suggests he'll remain an important part of Memphis' young rotation, though his scoring opportunities could fluctuate depending on the team's other offensive options.

items.headline: The Grizzlies exercised their third-year team option on Coward's contract Tuesday.
items.story: Coward is now officially under contract for the 2027-28 campaign after averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 25.8 minutes per game across 62 regular-season appearances (47 starts) in his rookie season. The 23-year-old swingman will likely begin the 2026-27 season in the Grizzlies' starting five when they host the Jazz on Wednesday.

items.headline: Coward amassed 13 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals in 26 minutes during Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Coward delivered his best preseason performance after failing to reach double figures in scoring in his previous three outings. An excellent fantasy breakout candidate, the second-year wing should be in Memphis' first unit when the regular season tips off.

items.headline: Coward recorded nine points (3-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal across 18 minutes in Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Coward drew the start and contributed across the board despite attempting only six shots. The wing's four assists were particularly encouraging, and he tied for second among Memphis players in both rebounds and assists. Coward has generated plenty of fantasy interest heading into the campaign, and his ability to contribute without requiring significant offensive volume gives him multiple avenues toward fantasy relevance. He's in the mix to open the 2026-27 regular season in a starting role, and a solid showing in preseason will boost his case to crack the first unit.

items.headline: Coward appears to be in the mix for a starting role entering the preseason, Damichael Cole of The Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Memphis experimented with several lineup combinations during training camp, with Coward, Jaylen Wells and Jerami Grant among the team's options on the wing. Coward and Wells have already logged significant minutes together, and the second-year wing's ability to fit alongside multiple backcourt combinations could help his chances of securing a prominent role.

items.headline: Coward finished with 19 points (6-10 FG, 5-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, four assists and a block in 27 minutes during Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League championship loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Coward continued his strong play at Summer League on Sunday, matching Cameron Boozer with a team-high 19 points on impressive efficiency. Coward excelled from beyond the arc, connecting on each of his five three-point attempts. The 22-year-old pro will look to take a step forward in his second season after an impressive rookie campaign in which he averaged 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 25.8 minutes per contest across 62 appearances.

items.headline: Coward racked up 28 points (9-19 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 28 minutes during Saturday's 101-90 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Rockets.
items.story: Coward was locked in on both ends of the floor, helping the Grizzlies punch their ticket to the Las Vegas Summer League Finals. He finished with a plus-10 rating and committed just one turnover in the convincing victory.

items.headline: Coward finished with 23 points (7-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 24 minutes in Thursday's 96-64 Summer League win over the Hawks.
items.story: Coward recorded a double-double in his first two appearances in the Las Vegas Summer League. Although he hasn't reached that mark since, he finished with 23 points Thursday, his highest-scoring performance during his time in Las Vegas. The 2025 No. 11 overall pick is coming off a quality 2025-26 campaign, averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists over 25.8 minutes in 62 regular-season appearances. As long as Coward can stay healthy, he is expected to build on his production from last season in 2026-27.

items.headline: Coward finished with 17 points (7-23 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 27 minutes in Monday's 96-88 Summer League loss to Dallas.
items.story: Coward recorded his second consecutive double-double Monday. However, he continued to struggle shooting the ball and has now gone 3-for-14 from deep in his two Las Vegas Summer League appearances. Turnovers have also been an issue, with the 22-year-old committing eight during that span. Coward is expected to play a prominent role for the Grizzlies during the 2026-27 campaign, so his performances in Las Vegas likely won't affect him one way or another. Memphis plays again Tuesday versus the Warriors, though it wouldn't be surprising if Coward sat out to rest.

items.headline: Coward finished with 17 points (5-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 97-96 Summer League victory over Chicago.
items.story: Coward appeared in 62 regular-season games as a rookie in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.4 blocks and 0.6 steals over 25.8 minutes per contest. Since he also played in the Salt Lake City Summer League, it's unclear how much more action he will see during his time in Las Vegas. However, even if the 22-year-old doesn't suit up again this summer, he's already expected to hold a prominent role for a Grizzlies team that no longer has Ja Morant on the roster.

items.headline: Coward (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Hawks, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Coward won't suit up for the Grizzlies' final game in Salt Lake City this summer. However, the 22-year-old swingman is expected to return when the Grizzlies open the Las Vegas Summer League against the Bulls on Friday.

items.headline: Hunter posted 30 points (12-16 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block across 37 minutes during Friday's 106-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter erupted for a season high, easily topping his previous best and knocking down nearly everything he threw up. His layup with under two minutes left tied the game, though the Kings couldn't hold on. It was a big bounce-back after a rough shooting night against Phoenix on Wednesday.

items.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as available for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter was listed as questionable ahead of this contest, but he will avoid his third absence of the 2026-27 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in 12 regular-season games, averaging 13.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists over 32.8 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter has been bothered by left hip soreness. While it kept him off the floor for Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, he returned for Wednesday's meeting with the Suns. If Hunter can't suit up Friday, it could mean more minutes for Leaky Black and Alex Karaban.

items.headline: Hunter (hip) is available for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Hunter is returning Wednesday from a one-game respite due to left hip soreness. It's unknown if Hunter will replace Keegan Murray in the starting lineup, but either way, his return is likely to shrink Murray's role a bit.

items.headline: Hunter (hip) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Suns, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter missed Sunday's 125-103 loss to Oklahoma City due to left hip soreness, and that same issue has earned him a questionable tag versus Phoenix. If he's unable to suit up, Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk will continue to get more burn.

items.headline: Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Hunter was added to the injury report close to tipoff, and he's since been downgraded to out. The Kings will be forced to play shorthanded Sunday, as Precious Achiuwa (ankle) and Zach LaVine (illness) are also unavailable. The absence of three starters should open up minutes for Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk.

items.headline: Hunter is questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder due to left hip soreness.
items.story: Hunter is a late addition to the injury report due to a hip injury. If he is unable to go, Malik Monk and Leaky Black could see extra minutes.

items.headline: Hunter supplied 24 points (7-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals in 42 minutes during Friday's 120-107 loss to Portland.
items.story: Hunter led Sacramento with 24 points and played a team-high 42 minutes. The veteran forward has become one of the few dependable scoring options for a Kings team searching for answers at 1-11. He'll keep getting heavy minutes, so his production should stay steady.

items.headline: Hunter chipped in 15 points (5-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 107-100 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Hunter was adequate during the loss, giving Sacramento reliable scoring from the wing. He's settled into a starting role and gets the job done without much fanfare. With Zach LaVine and Darius Acuff dominating the ball, Hunter will find his lines falling below his teammates fairly often.

items.headline: Hunter closed with 14 points (4-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 31 minutes during Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat.
items.story: The veteran forward missed the Kings' prior game Friday with an illness, but Hunter seemed his usual self Sunday. After a sluggish start to the season, he's scored at least 14 points in five of his last six contests, averaging 16.8 points, 4.3 boards, 2.3 threes and 1.3 assists in 34.5 minutes.

items.headline: Hunter (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Miami.
items.story: Hunter didn't play in Friday's 124-109 loss to the Spurs, marking his first absence of the season. He will return Sunday versus the Heat, likely meaning Leaky Black will head back to the bench.

items.headline: Hunter (illness) is listed as out for Friday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Hunter was listed as questionable but has now been ruled out for the first time this season. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday versus the Heat. With Hunter unavailable, Malik Monk might find his way into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Hunter is questionable for Friday against the Spurs due to an illness.
items.story: Hunter is a late addition to the injury report. If he doesn't suit up Friday, Malik Monk and Leaky Black should soak up more playing time for the Kings.

items.headline: Hunter recorded 14 points (4-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter played heavy minutes but couldn't build on Saturday's 19-point outing, offering little outside of scoring. He continues to see a starter's workload, but with modest peripheral production, he's mainly a points streamer in standard leagues.

items.headline: Hunter chipped in 19 points (8-18 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter scored 12 of his 19 points in the second quarter and finished Saturday as the Kings' second-leading scorer behind rookie seventh-overall pick Darius Acuff (38). Hunter failed to score in double digits in each of the first three games of the regular season, but over his last three outings, he has averaged 22.3 points per game on 52.3 percent shooting along with 4.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 3.7 threes and 0.7 steals over 34.0 minutes per contest. He'll continue to operate in an elevated role for as long as Keegan Murray (ankle) is out of action.

items.headline: Hunter logged 24 points (8-13 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Hunter finally found his footing, scoring a season-high 24 points, despite another loss. Prior to Tuesday, he had scored a total of 17 points across three games to open the campaign, an indication that this could be considered an outlier. While this was an encouraging shooting performance, fantasy managers certainly shouldn't overreact just yet.

items.headline: Hunter chipped in seven points (2-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter is off to a sluggish start to the new campaign. The forward has yet to score in double digits in any of his first three appearances, but he should be able to hang on to a starting role with the rebuilding Kings going forward.

items.headline: Hunter will start Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Ben Simmons is out for the season with a torn Achilles, opening the door for Hunter to step into the starting five. The 28-year-old appeared in only two games after being traded to Sacramento last season, and he averaged 13.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.7 steals across 26.1 minutes per contest in 45 regular-season games (25 starts) between the Kings and Cavaliers.

items.headline: Hunter (rest) is available to play in Friday's exhibition against the Spurs, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter missed Tuesday's preseason loss to Portland for maintenance, but he's been cleared for Sacramento's preseason finale. Hunter is averaging 3.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.3 turnovers per game this preseason.

items.headline: Hunter (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter will join several other regulars on the inactive list. His final chance to play in the preseason will come Friday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Hunter is not in the Kings' starting lineup against the Warriors on Saturday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter has started in each of the Kings' first two preseason games, but he'll come off the bench Saturday while Keegan Murray, Ben Simmons and Precious Achiuwa make up Sacramento's starting frontcourt. Hunter logged only three points over 13 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Lakers.

items.headline: Hunter finished with three points (3-3 FT) in 13 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason loss to Los Angeles.
items.story: Hunter started at small forward but didn't attempt a field goal during his limited action. The 28-year-old joined Sacramento late last season and appears positioned to open the 2026-27 campaign in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Kings general manager Scott Perry said Monday that Hunter is healthy ahead of training camp, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Hunter appeared in only two regular-season games for Sacramento following his midseason arrival before undergoing season-ending surgery in February to repair a retinal detachment in his left eye. His return to full health clears the way for Hunter to participate in camp and compete for a significant role on the wing in his first full season with the Kings.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) has a major competitor for usage after the Kings took Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Fantasy managers weren't quite able to get a clear idea about Hunter's role after his move to Sacramento, as the forward made just two appearances for the Kings before undergoing season-ending eye surgery. While Acuff is expected to play a big role and see plenty of ballhandling duties right away, Hunter could still move up the depth chart and benefit from a usage perspective if DeMar DeRozan (hamstring) winds up going elsewhere in 2026-27.

items.headline: Hunter is set to undergo season-ending eye surgery, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: Hunter managed to suit up for only two games for Sacramento before opting to undergo a season-ending procedure on his eye, but this likely won't be something that impacts his status for next year's training camp. He will end his 2025-26 campaign with averages of 13.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.7 triples in 26.1 minutes per game across 45 regular-season outings (25 starts) between Cleveland and Sacramento. With the 28-year-old forward sidelined, Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) has been ruled out for Saturday's game in San Antonio.
items.story: Saturday will mark Hunter's fifth consecutive game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Memphis. Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden will continue to pick up the slack in Hunter's absence.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Hunter is battling a left eye injury that cost him the final three games before the All-Star break and will keep him sidelined coming out of the pause. It's unclear how close he is to returning, but his absence will likely mean more opportunities for Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden. Hunter's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) will be reevaluated in about 10 days, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Hunter has been diagnosed with iritis after being hit in the eye during Friday's game against the Clippers, putting him out until after the All-Star break. Daeqwon Plowden and Nique Clifford are candidates for increased minutes with Hunter sidelined.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) will not play Saturday against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hunter picked up a left eye injury Friday against the Clippers and was unable to return to the contest. With Hunter sidelined, more minutes will be available for Daeqwon Plowden and Nique Clifford on the wings.

items.headline: Hunter won't return to Friday's game against the Clippers due to a left eye injury, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports. He'll finish with six points (1-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and one rebound across 25 minutes.
items.story: Hunter checked out of the contest with 2:06 left in the third quarter, and after a brief trip to the locker room, the Kings ruled him out for the remainder of the contest. The 28-year-old forward faces a short turnaround to recover from the eye injury, with the Kings returning to action Saturday versus the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Hunter produced nine points (3-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 26 minutes during Wednesday's 129-125 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter failed to impress during his Sacramento debut, continuing what had been a rough finish to his tenure in Cleveland. After the Cavaliers moved him to a bench role in mid-December, Hunter averaged 12.3 points (on 41.6 percent shooting from the field), 4.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 three-pointers and 0.7 steals in 23.4 minutes per game over a stretch of 20 contests before he was dealt to Sacramento. Hunter immediately moved into the starting five for the Kings and took on more minutes than he had been receiving with the Cavaliers, but he showed why his overall fantasy impact in category leagues remains limited when his shots aren't falling in. Though his value should rise with the move to Sacramento, Hunter still looks to be more of a streaming option for points, free-throw percentage and three-pointers in most 12-team leagues rather than a must-roster player.

items.headline: Hunter is in the Kings' starting lineup against the Grizzlies on Wednesday, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Wednesday will be Hunter's first look in a Kings uniform after he was acquired from the Cavaliers on Saturday. The veteran forward's insertion into the starting lineup will result in Precious Achiuwa moving to the bench.

items.headline: Hunter isn't listed on the injury report and is expected to make his debut with the Kings on Wednesday against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter didn't join the team in time to play in Sunday's game against Washington after being traded from the Cavs on Sturday, but he's expected to be on the court for Wednesday's clash. The Virginia product averaged 14.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 43 games this season with Cleveland.

items.headline: Hunter has yet to join the Kings and won't play in Sunday's game against the Wizards, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Hunter was traded from Cleveland to Sacramento on Saturday in a three-team deal involving the Bulls, and he will have to wait to make his Kings debut. Head coach Doug Christie said Sunday that the plan is for Hunter to practice with the team Tuesday and play against the Grizzlies on Wednesday, per Chris Biderman of The Sacramento Bee. Over 43 regular-season appearances with Cleveland in 2025-26, Hunter averaged 13.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Kings acquired Hunter on Saturday in a three-team deal involving the Cavaliers and Bulls, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After a couple weeks of speculation, Hunter will move on from the Cavaliers and will fill an obvious need at forward for Sacramento. As part of the deal, the Bulls will acquire Dario Saric and two second-round draft picks, while the Cavaliers will receive Dennis Schroder, Emanuel Miller and Keon Ellis. With the move to Sacramento, Hunter could see a bump in fantasy appeal with his new team after he had moved into a bench role with Cleveland in mid-December. Over his 43 appearances with Cleveland this season, Hunter averaged 13.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hunter recorded 17 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three steals over 23 minutes during Friday's 126-113 loss to the Suns.
items.story: It was a balanced scoring attack from the Cavaliers on Friday, and Hunter ended up leading the team in that category off the bench while tying a season high with three swipes. He has scored in double digits in each of his last two outings since returning from a knee injury, and he will end the month of January having averaged 12.3 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.4 threes over 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hunter (knee) posted 19 points (7-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 21 minutes Wednesday in the Cavaliers' 129-99 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter had been sidelined for the Cavaliers' previous two games due to right knee soreness, but he returned to action Wednesday and excelled as the team's go-to scoring option on the second unit. Prior to getting hurt, Hunter had been held under 20 minutes in his most recent two appearances, but the Cavaliers could call upon him to handle a larger role now that the team has a greater need for secondary scoring behind Donovan Mitchell while Evan Mobley (calf) and Darius Garland (toe) remain sidelined. Hunter could be in store for added usage in the short term as a result, but beyond potentially being a solid source of points, his production in other categories typically leaves much to be desired.

items.headline: Jenkins logged 11 points (4-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 38 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Jenkins has averaged 37 minutes over his last five games, but his scoring has declined in his last three appearances. Despite consistent playing time, his 11-for-42 shooting over that stretch limits his fantasy ceiling. His substantial workload maintains short-term appeal.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Friday's 105-102 loss to Toronto with 14 points (5-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals across 39 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins continues to receive substantial playing time despite cooling off considerably from his recent scoring surge. After producing three consecutive games with at least 21 points earlier this month, he has struggled to maintain that offensive momentum and has failed to reach the 20-point plateau in three of his previous four appearances. Still, Jenkins is averaging 18.2 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.8 steals per game since moving to the starting lineup Nov. 9. His combination of minutes, scoring potential and defensive activity keeps him relevant in deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Jenkins amassed 17 points (7-16 FG, 3-5 3Pt), four rebounds and nine assists over 36 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 win over New Orleans.
items.story: Jenkins was one of the top performers for the Pistons in this comfortable win and made the most of Cade Cunningham's (knee) absence, taking advantage of the expanded role as a playmaker to end just one assist shy of a double-double. This was Jenkins' fifth straight start, and he's performing well enough to lock down that role as long as he stays healthy, averaging 19.0 points, 4.4 rebounds and 5.4 assists per game in that span.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Tuesday's 105-93 win over the Spurs with 25 points (11-21 FG, 3-7 3Pt), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 38 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins finished second on the Pistons in scoring behind Cade Cunningham and buried a 25-footer in the final minute to seal the win. Jenkins bounced back nicely after a cold shooting night in Miami on Saturday. He has carved out a starting role with Isaiah Joe (hip) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) sidelined and is averaging 13.2 points.

items.headline: Jenkins had 21 points (6-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds and two steals in 42 minutes before fouling out of Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime victory over Washington.
items.story: Jenkins remained in the starting lineup, scoring at least 21 points for the third straight game. After a relatively strong start to the season, at least when compared to preseason expectations, Jenkins has seemingly assumed a starting role alongside Cade Cunningham. In three games over the past week, he has been a first-round player, averaging 24.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.3 steals and 4.3 three-pointers. Make sure he isn't available in your league.

items.headline: Jenkins notched 22 points (7-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and four steals over 36 minutes during Monday's 122-111 win over Washington.
items.story: Jenkins followed up his career-high 31 points off the bench Sunday by moving into the starting lineup and filling the stat sheet. His eight assists and four steals made for a strong fantasy line. With Isaiah Joe (hip) and Jalen Duren (hamstring) sidelined, Jenkins is worth a speculative add while he holds a starting role.

items.headline: Jenkins is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: The Pistons are shaking things up Monday, sending Paul Reed to the bench and moving Jenkins into the first unit. Over 20 career starts, Jenkins has averaged 17.2 points, 7.3 assists and 3.9 rebounds in 34.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jenkins contributed 31 points (9-17 FG, 8-15 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Jenkins caught fire from beyond the arc, drilling eight three-pointers while leading Detroit during his career-high scoring night. The guard provided a major offensive spark as Cade Cunningham struggled with his shot, finishing with 14 points on 6-for-15 shooting. Jenkins' 32-minute workload and prolific perimeter shooting make him worth monitoring in deeper fantasy leagues, although his long-term role remains uncertain.

items.headline: Jenkins ended Wednesday's 112-106 loss to the 76ers with five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and four assists in 21 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins struggled to establish an offensive rhythm, connecting on just two field goals while committing four turnovers. The reserve guard provided some playmaking but failed to record a steal or block, limiting his overall fantasy impact. With Cade Cunningham handling the bulk of Detroit's backcourt responsibilities, Jenkins remains a fringe option in deeper formats.

items.headline: Jenkins logged 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three assists, two rebounds and two steals across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 97-89 win over Charlotte.
items.story: With Ausar Thompson shedding his probable tag to suit up Wednesday, Jenkins came off the bench for a second straight game. The 25-year-old was productive, scoring in double figures for a fourth consecutive contest while bouncing back from a 1-for-6 shooting performance from downtown in the front end of this back-to-back set. He also tallied a season-high mark in steals.

items.headline: Jenkins is not listed in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Jenkins started in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers, finishing with 18 points, eight rebounds, six assists and one block across 38 minutes of action. With Ausar Thompson (ankle) back from a one-game layoff, Jenkins will return to the bench.

items.headline: Jenkins posted 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and a block across 38 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Jenkins capitalized on an expanded role with Ausar Thompson (ankle) sidelined, playing a team-high 38 minutes and contributing across several categories. His late three-pointer helped secure Detroit's victory, while his rebounding and playmaking added considerable fantasy value. However, his long-term outlook remains tied to the Pistons' injury situation, as a healthier rotation could reduce his opportunities moving forward.

items.headline: Jenkins will start Sunday's game against the 76ers, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jenkins gets the start due to Ausar Thompson (ankle) being out. Jenkins holds averages of 7.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 26.0 minutes per contest across two appearances this season.

items.headline: Jenkins posted three points (1-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists in 15 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 win over the Celtics.
items.story: Jenkins knocked down his lone three-point attempt in the second quarter but played a relatively minor role in Detroit's comeback from a 22-point deficit. The reserve guard committed one turnover and four fouls while receiving limited offensive opportunities. After averaging 9.3 points and 3.9 assists over 72 regular-season games last campaign, Jenkins will need a larger workload than Tuesday to replicate that production consistently.

items.headline: Jenkins finished with six points (2-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists, three rebounds and one block across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: After scoring 12 points in 18 minutes as a starter Saturday, Jenkins had a quieter scoring outing in a reserve role Wednesday. The St. John's product emerged as a key role player last season, averaging 9.3 points, 3.9 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 20.2 minutes across 72 regular-season appearances (19 starts). Heading into the 2026-27 campaign, Jenkins is positioned to serve as the primary backup to star point guard Cade Cunningham.

items.headline: Jenkins is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Wizards, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: The Pistons won't start Cade Cunningham in Saturday's preseason contest, meaning Jenkins will get the nod at point guard. The former St. John's standout is expected to operate as Cunningham's backup as long as he stays healthy, so he'll get the chance to run with the first-team offense in this game. He averaged 9.3 points and 3.9 assists per game across 72 contests (19 starts) in the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Jenkins finished with five points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four assists and two rebounds in 18 minutes during Monday's preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Jenkins helped Detroit erase a 19-point deficit and connected on a contested three-pointer to tie the game at the end of the third quarter. After emerging as a rotation contributor last season, the 24-year-old will look to secure consistent reserve minutes in a deeper Detroit backcourt.

items.headline: The Pistons exercised their 2026-27 team option for Jenkins on Monday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: This was basically a formality for the Pistons at $4 million. Jenkins was upgraded to a standard contract last season after a string of impressive performances. Across 72 regular-season games, he averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 assists and 2.3 rebounds on 40.8 percent shooting from the field, though he may face competition for backup backcourt minutes from rookie first-round pick Ebuka Okorie.

items.headline: Jenkins ended Sunday's 125-94 loss to Cleveland in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals with 17 points (4-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 7-8 FT), three rebounds and five assists in 34 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins was one of the best stories to come out of Detroit this season. He began the season on a two-way contract, but his stellar play quickly earned him a standard deal. He ended up with 72 regular-season appearances, averaging 9.3 points, 3.9 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 20.2 minutes per contest. He's expected back in Detroit, with the Pistons likely to pick up his team option.

items.headline: Jenkins closed with 19 points (8-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 41 minutes during Wednesday's 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Jenkins moved into the starting lineup, replacing Duncan Robinson, who was ruled out with a back injury. Jenkins made the most of his opportunity, scoring a postseason-high 19 points, adding three combined steals and blocks. In 12 postseason games, Jenkins has averaged 8.0 points, 2.8 assists and 0.9 three-pointers in 21.1 minutes per game. However, he has now scored double digits in four of the past six games, seeing elevated minutes on a consistent basis.

items.headline: Jenkins will start in Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against Cleveland, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: With Duncan Robinson (back) ruled out, Jenkins will start in Game 5. The 24-year-old started 19 times during the regular season, averaging 17.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 7.4 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.9 steals across 33.8 minutes in those appearances.

items.headline: Jenkins accumulated 14 points (6-14 FG, 2-5 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 26 minutes during Thursday's 107-97 win over the Cavaliers in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Despite continuing to come off the bench, Jenkins has now logged at least 26 minutes in three straight games, running with the closers in both games against the Cavaliers. Although Cleveland typically rolls with a double-big lineup, Jenkins has increased both his playing time and production, with Detroit seemingly taking the initiative when it comes to dictating the flow of the game.

items.headline: Jenkins totaled 12 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and four steals across 29 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 win over the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Jenkins logged at least 28 minutes for the second straight game, as Detroit opted to go with a smaller lineup in Game 1 against Cleveland. After a quiet start to the postseason, Jenkins has stepped up in the past two games, averaging 14.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 2.0 three-pointers. It appears that he has replaced Isaiah Stewart as the preferred first option off the bench, providing the team with another dynamic scoring option. With that said, should Cleveland's size advantage prove an issue in Game 2, we could see Stewart back in his traditional role, with Jenkins shifting to more of a depth role.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Sunday's 116-94 victory over the Magic in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 16 points (5-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one block over 29 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins had easily his best game of the postseason, scoring 16 points in 29 minutes and closing the game over Ausar Thompson. Although he has been a consistent part of the rotation, Jenkins has mostly served as a backup to Cade Cunningham. However, he played alongside Cunningham in Sunday's win, providing the team with an additional perimeter threat. Detroit will now face Cleveland in the second round in what figures to be another tight matchup.

items.headline: Jenkins won't start Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: With Cade Cunningham (chest) back in action, Jenkins will retreat to the second unit. Over his last eight appearances off the bench, the 24-year-old guard has averaged 6.3 points, 3.4 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 17.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Saturday's 116-93 victory over Philadelphia with 16 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-7 FT), four rebounds, 14 assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins continues to impress, recording his third double-double of the season. With Cade Cunningham (chest) still sidelined, Jenkins has certainly made the most of his opportunity. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged 19.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, 8.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers.

items.headline: Jenkins posted 26 points (9-19 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), five rebounds and eight assists across 37 minutes during Thursday's 113-108 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Jenkins continues to roll on the offensive end, as he led the Pistons in scoring on the way to a hard-fought victory. He's posted 20-plus points in back-to-back games and continues to put up strong numbers across the board while running with the first unit, which is where he'll remain until Cade Cunningham (chest) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Jenkins finished Tuesday's 127-116 win over the Raptors with 21 points (5-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 9-9 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one block over 37 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins attempted just nine shots from the field, but he still reached the 20-point threshold for the sixth time this season thanks to his work at the charity stripe, where he logged career highs in both made and attempted free throws. Jenkins saw his role off the Pistons' bench steadily increase as the season progressed, and he has thrived in a starting role while filling in for the injured Cade Cunningham (chest). Jenkins has started in each of the Pistons' last eight games, and over that span he has averaged 18.5 points, 6.9 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 2.1 threes over 36.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green ended Monday's 123-119 overtime win over the Pelicans with 25 points (9-17 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and two steals over 37 minutes.
items.story: Green has slowly started to turn things around after a lackluster start to the season, having scored in double figures in four straight games, culminating in Monday's season-high 25 points. In three appearances over the past week, he has been a borderline top-50 player, averaging 19.0 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.7 three-pointers during that span. Although his overall upside remains limited, he is playing well enough right now to be considered a worthwhile addition, even in standard leagues.

items.headline: Green posted 14 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds and three assists in 25 minutes during Friday's 111-101 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Green closed the door on Utah, throwing down a running dunk and converting the and-one in the final seconds to cap the win. Altbough his name is mentioned in trade talks, Green has given Phoenix reliable secondary scoring all trip, and he's averaging 12.4 points alongside Devin Booker in the backcourt.

items.headline: Green registered 18 points (6-14 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 win over Sacramento.
items.story: Green built on Monday's 16-point performance against Denver, and the expanded contributions outside scoring are particularly important for a player who has traditionally relied heavily on his offensive production. With Devin Booker and Dillon Brooks sharing most of the scoring responsibilities, Green's ability to contribute as a facilitator and rebounder could help stabilize his fantasy value even when his shot volume is relatively modest. He's now recorded 15-plus points in back-to-back games for the first time this season, and his last two performances are clear signs that he's trending in the right direction.

items.headline: Green finished with 16 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, three assists and three steals across 27 minutes in Monday's 117-105 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Green made the most of his 10 field-goal attempts and added three steals, giving him a well-rounded performance despite playing fewer than 30 minutes. Despite the workload, Green continues to have a disappointing season, but Monday's efficiency and defensive production were encouraging signs that Green can turn things around. This was his first game with more than 15 points since Nov. 7 -- he's done that just four times all season long.

items.headline: Green closed with 12 points (3-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and one steal across 21 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Green's first few weeks have been underwhelming, particularly for a player whose fantasy appeal has traditionally depended on scoring volume. He's producing a career-worst 11.8 points per game, and he's been limited to 12 points or fewer in each of his last three games and in four of his last five outings. There's still upside if his offensive responsibilities grow, but he's currently more of a speculative hold than a dependable fantasy starter, given his prolonged struggles.

items.headline: Green racked up 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 0-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes during Tuesday's 133-110 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Green shot efficiently from the field, but his playing time was capped at 21 minutes with Phoenix comfortably ahead for much of the second half. After missing nearly the entire 2025-26 campaign, Green has the scoring upside to make an impact in fantasy, but his lack of peripheral production limits his overall value. Assuming he returns to his usual workload in more competitive matchups, he should remain rostered in most formats as a points-and-threes asset.

items.headline: Green finished with 16 points (7-14 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, six assists and a steal across 34 minutes in Saturday's 102-99 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Green contributed effectively as a secondary playmaker, recording six assists while maintaining a substantial scoring role against his former team. However, four turnovers and limited perimeter production diminished his overall fantasy efficiency. His consistent playing time and offensive opportunities provide a strong floor, but the lack of consistency from a scoring perspective has hurt him so far. Green has failed to reach the 15-point mark in three of his last five appearances while averaging 11.4 points per game and 37.9 shooting from the field in that span.

items.headline: Green contributed 22 points (6-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 8-8 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The former Rocket set a new season scoring high while recording multiple blocks for a second straight game. Green is still struggling to find his rhythm, and through six contests to begin the season, he's averaging 12.8 points, 3.3 boards, 3.3 assists, 1.0 blocks and 1.0 threes in 29.0 minutes while posting career-low percentages -- 40.3 percent from the field, 68.4 percent from the free-throw line and 23.1 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Green logged 11 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-6 FT), eight rebounds, eight assists, two blocks and two steals across 36 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Green struggled with his efficiency, particularly at the charity stripe, but compensated with an impressive all-around performance. He led Phoenix with eight assists while matching Miles Bridges for the team lead in rebounds and contributing four defensive statistics. Green's substantial workload and versatility helped salvage his fantasy production despite the poor shooting.

items.headline: Green produced 20 points (8-13 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one block in 31 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Green led Phoenix in scoring while converting an efficient 61.5 percent of his field-goal attempts. The 24-year-old guard bounced back from a 12-point performance against Golden State on Saturday, reaching the 20-point mark for the second time in three games to begin the campaign. Green should remain one of Phoenix's primary scoring options alongside Devin Booker, giving him a solid fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Green registered 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one block in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 loss to Portland.
items.story: Green put together modest production in Wednesday's blowout defeat, which became lopsided early on. The 24-year-old guard endured an injury-ruined 2025-26 campaign, but he has a clean bill of health this year and should get on track before long.

items.headline: Green registered 18 points (6-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Green got off to a strong start and recorded 10 points in the first quarter alone, and he ultimately co-led Phoenix in scoring next to Dillon Brooks. The three steals were encouraging, and he's coming off averaging a career-best 1.1 swipes per game in the 2025-26 regular season, so there might be some upside in that regard. However, his fantasy value will mainly depend on what he does in the scoring column. He averaged 17.8 points per game across 32 regular-season appearances (27 starts) in 2025-26 in an injury-marred campaign. Green's scoring upside remains appealing for fantasy managers, particularly if he can maintain efficient perimeter shooting while contributing defensively during the regular season.

items.headline: Green (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Jazz, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Green was given the night off during Wednesday's loss to San Antonio. However, the 24-year-old guard will return to the lineup for the Suns' preseason finale.

items.headline: Green (rest) won't play Wednesday versus the Spurs, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Green was expected to sit this one out, so the latest update isn't surprising. His final chance to suit up before the start of the regular season will come Friday against Utah.

items.headline: Green did not participate in Wednesday's full morning shootaround and isn't expected to face San Antonio, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Green is among six Suns players expected to miss Wednesday's exhibition contest. The reason for his anticipated absence is likely maintenance-related, leaving Friday's preseason finale against Utah as his next potential opportunity to take the floor.

items.headline: Green recorded 18 points (7-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five assists, three rebounds and one steal in 29 minutes during Saturday's 102-98 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: With Devin Booker (rest) sidelined, Luke Kennard (20 points) and Green led the scoring attack for Phoenix. The 24-year-old swingman turned in an efficient shooting performance and tied for the team lead in assists. He's scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances in 2026 and has shot 14-for-28 from the field thus far.

items.headline: Green played 22 minutes in Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls, scoring 12 points (4-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT) while adding four rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block.
items.story: The former Rocket is heading into his second campaign with the Suns and is mainly hoping to stay healthy in 2026-27 after averaging 25.9 minutes over 32 regular-season games last season due to a hamstring issue. If Green can stay on the court, he should be one of Phoenix's primary offensive threats after topping 20.0 points per game in two of his last three seasons with Houston.

items.headline: Green totaled 11 points (3-6 FG, 4-6 FT, 1-4 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes during Monday's 109-107 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Green was one of three Suns players to score double digits, an encouraging sign given all the injury concerns he had last season. While this was obviously a very small sample size, Green looked energized on the offensive end, a positive sign for anyone considering him in drafts. As a result of basically missing the entire 2025-26 campaign, managers are showing caution when it comes to drafting him, typically targeting him well past pick 100. As a player who can routinely put up in excess of 20 points per game, Green makes for a highly valuable late-round target.

items.headline: Green said Monday that improving his playmaking and pace were major focuses during the offseason, with the guard working with Hall of Famer Steve Nash to develop those areas of his game, according to Suns reporter Ethan Kinney.
items.story: Green said Nash has helped him better understand how to read the floor and control the pace of a game, which could prove particularly useful with Phoenix looking to emphasize transition opportunities this season. Green averaged 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists across 32 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, and growth as a facilitator would add another dimension to his offensive profile.

items.headline: Green could experience a downtick in usage next season after the Suns acquired Miles Bridges from the Hornets this offseason.
items.story: Phoenix is welcoming in a new member of its starting lineup in 2026-27, with Bridges set to replace Royce O'Neale in that role. The Suns effectively replaced Grayson Allen with Luke Kennard, as both players profile similarly as three-point shooters, but Bridges poses a far greater risk to Green's usage than Kennard. Green still figures to slot in as the team's No. 2 scoring option behind Devin Booker, and the former will be looking to bounce back after averaging 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.2 three-pointers in 25.9 minutes per game over 32 regular-season appearances amidst an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Green racked up 23 points (10-25 FG, 1-10 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, four assists and four steals in 39 minutes during Monday's 131-122 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Green didn't have the best night shooting the ball, but he still put together an impressive stat line. Injuries derailed his first season in Phoenix, limiting him to 32 regular-season appearances. He posted averages of 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.2 three-pointers in 25.9 minutes per contest prior to the playoffs.
