items.headline: DeRozan (back) is active for Saturday's NBA Mexico City Game against the Pacers.
items.story: DeRozan missed Wednesday's 128-109 win over Toronto due to lower-back spasms, but the 37-year-old forward will suit up for the NBA's Mexico City Game against the Nuggets. The veteran's presence will likely mean less playing time for Alpha Diallo, Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile.

items.headline: DeRozan (back) is probable for Saturday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: The veteran forward is expected to end a one-game absence due to lower-back spasms Saturday. It's been a sluggish start to DeRozan's Nuggets tenure -- he's reached the 15-point threshold just one time over his first six appearances in 2026-27.

items.headline: DeRozan has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Raptors due to lower-back spasms.
items.story: DeRozan was a late scratch ahead of tipoff. With the veteran forward sidelined, Alpha Diallo, Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile are all candidates to see increased burn.

items.headline: DeRozan posted nine points (3-7 FG, 3-3 FT) and a rebound across 20 minutes in Monday's 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: DeRozan endured another subpar showing in what has been a disappointing start to the season for the veteran scorer. The lack of playing time has been an issue at the start of the season, as DeRozan has failed to reach the 25-minute mark in three of his last five appearances, including the last two. That reduction in playing time, as well as his limited role offensively, limits his fantasy upside considerably.

items.headline: DeRozan ended Monday's 134-114 loss to Golden State with 21 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 29 minutes.
items.story: DeRozan led Denver in scoring despite coming off the bench, reaching the 20-point mark for the first time this season. The veteran forward also knocked down two three-pointers and contributed three combined steals and blocks. Although his reserve role could limit his overall fantasy ceiling, DeRozan remains capable of providing consistent scoring production.

items.headline: DeRozan racked up 13 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-6 FT) and two rebounds across 28 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: DeRozan was relatively quiet in his Denver debut, despite ending as one of just three Nuggets to score double digits. He also turned the ball over five times during his 28 minutes on the court, capping off what was a disappointing performance. It appears as though DeRozan is going to be used as the team's sixth man, providing an offensive punch when Nikola Jokic is off the floor.

items.headline: DeRozan (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Lakers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: DeRozan received Wednesday night off but will return to action in Friday's preseason finale. He'll come off the bench while the Nuggets start Trevon Brazile in Aaron Gordon's (rest) stead.

items.headline: DeRozan (rest) won't play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers, Katy Winge of Altitude Sports reports.
items.story: The Nuggets' starters will all suit up versus Los Angeles, though the team will be without its top bench option. DeRozan has had a quiet preseason, averaging 4.7 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 10.2 minutes per contest. However, it's reasonable to assume he will be much more productive come the start of the regular season. DeRozan is expected to play in Friday's preseason finale against the Lakers.

items.headline: DeRozan recorded two points (0-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and two assists in nine minutes during Sunday's 133-128 preseason win over Chicago.
items.story: DeRozan struggled offensively in limited action, missing all four of his field-goal attempts while coming off the bench. The veteran forward has played fewer than 12 minutes in each of his three preseason appearances, suggesting Denver is managing his workload ahead of the regular season. His reduced preseason minutes shouldn't necessarily indicate a diminished regular-season role.

items.headline: DeRozan appears set to operate as the focal point of Denver's second unit this season, with head coach David Adelman planning to put the ball in the veteran forward's hands frequently, according to Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette.
items.story: The plan provides a strong indication that the Nuggets intend to keep their starting five intact while utilizing DeRozan as their primary offensive option off the bench. The 37-year-old has spent nearly his entire career as a starter, but his scoring and playmaking ability could give Denver a dependable offensive engine whenever Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray are off the floor.

items.headline: The Nuggets are signing DeRozan (hamstring) on Friday, per Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: The Nuggets may have lost Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers earlier this week, but they've quickly made a move to upgrade their roster. DeRozan, a six-time All-Star, should assume a significant role with Denver after averaging 18.4 points, 4.1 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 31.2 minutes per game across 77 regular-season appearances for the Kings in 2025-26. The veteran forward is in line for a usage decrease playing alongside Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, and it remains to be seen if he'll unseat either Christian Braun or Cameron Johnson for a starting position in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Kings waived DeRozan (hamstring) on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: With the Kings unable to find a suitable trade, the two sides will simply move on. With this news, DeRozan suddenly becomes one of the most intriguing free agents on the open market. In 2025-26, DeRozan averaged 18.4 points, 4.1 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 31.2 minutes per game across 77 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: DeRozan (hamstring) could be working with a new point guard in 2026-27 after Sacramento took Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: DeRozan's stay with Sacramento is certainly not guaranteed, though. The expectation is that the Kings will waive the veteran forward if they're unable to find a suitor in trade talks, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype. If DeRozan ends up sticking around with the Kings, he'll be trying to bounce back after averaging 18.4 points per game in 2024-25, his lowest total since 2012-13.

items.headline: DeRozan (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Portland.
items.story: DeRozan will end the season with a third consecutive absence due to a right hamstring injury. The veteran forward will finish the 2025-26 campaign having averaged fewer than 20 points per game for the first time since 2012-2013. He will end the season with averages of 18.4 points, 4.1 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 31.2 minutes per game across 77 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: DeRozan (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: DeRozan has been ruled out for a second straight contest while dealing with a right hamstring issue. He'll have a chance to return for Sacramento's regular-season finale against the Trail Blazers, though there's no reason to rush him back into action at this point.

items.headline: DeRozan is out for Tuesday's game against the Warriors due to right hamstring soreness.
items.story: It's set to be a rare absence for the star forward, who's sidelined for just the third time all year. With DeRozan out of action Tuesday, Daeqwon Plowden figures to jump into the starting lineup at small forward while veterans Malik Monk and Doug McDermott likely see an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: DeRozan is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Warriors due to right hamstring soreness.
items.story: DeRozan was held to 10 minutes Sunday against the Clippers in an ugly loss, and his availability is now in jeopardy for Tuesday's matchup. Sacramento should have another update on his status closer to tipoff after observing him go through shootaround and warmups.

items.headline: DeRozan ended Wednesday's 123-115 win over the Raptors with 28 points (7-18 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 12-12 FT), one rebound and four assists over 35 minutes.
items.story: DeRozan, who was returning from a one-game absence due to a hamstring problem, had an excellent performance against his former team, and he was particularly active at the charity stripe after draining all 12 of his attempts. The Kings don't have anything to play for in the final days of the regular season, but it's worth noting that DeRozan remains a reliable scoring option for Sacramento. He's averaging 19.6 points, 2.7 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game since the start of March.

items.headline: DeRozan (hamstring) will be available for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: DeRozan was held out of Sunday's game against Brooklyn, though it was mostly maintenance-related. The veteran is averaging 14.5 points, 5.5 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 turnovers in 28.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: DeRozan (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game in Brooklyn.
items.story: DeRozan had 22 points across 30 minutes in Saturday's 123-113 loss to Atlanta. However, the veteran won't be available versus Brooklyn due to hamstring soreness. With Malik Monk (shoulder) also out, among several others, Killian Hayes, DaQuan Jeffries, Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden should all receive more minutes, with two of those players potentially moving into the starting lineup.

items.headline: DeRozan finished Saturday's 123-113 loss to Atlanta with 22 points (9-18 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes.
items.story: Saturday marked the second game in a row that DeRozan led the Kings in scoring while connecting on 50.0 percent of his field-goal attempts. The veteran forward is averaging 18.5 points per game this season, which is his lowest mark since the 2012-13 season with the Raptors (18.1 points per game), though he's connecting on 49.5 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: DeRozan finished with 33 points (12-24 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 9-10 FT), six rebounds and 11 assists in 38 minutes during Thursday's 121-117 loss to the Magic.
items.story: DeRozan did his part on the offensive end and responded well after four consecutive sluggish performances as a scorer. He led Sacramento in the scoring department, and he also showcased his playmaking ability, resulting in his second double-double through 12 March outings.

items.headline: DeRozan provided seven points (3-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT), four rebounds and five assists in 29 minutes during Tuesday's 134-90 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: DeRozan was very underwhelming in this loss as the Kings dropped to 19-54 on the season. With nothing but lottery balls in play down the stretch, DeRozan could see his minutes and usage trend down.

items.headline: DeRozan closed Thursday's 139-118 loss to the 76ers with 13 points (6-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and five assists over 23 minutes.
items.story: DeRozan's playing time continues to occasionally fall victim to Sacramento's youth movement. The star forward's numbers are still solid overall despite some recent volatility, with DeRozan averaging 22.3 points, 5.2 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 30.0 minutes per tilt in his last six games.

items.headline: DeRozan recorded 41 points (11-21 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 18-21 FT), 11 assists, four rebounds and three steals in 38 minutes during Sunday's 116-111 win over the Jazz.
items.story: DeRozan continued his run of stellar play Sunday, posting season highs in points and assists. It was just the second time in DeRozan's career that he posted a 40-point double-double with assists. Surprisingly, Sunday's contest was the first double-double he has recorded all season. Over his last three games, DeRozan is averaging 35.7 points and 8.0 assists while shooting an absurd 68.4 percent from the floor.

items.headline: DeRozan generated 39 points (17-22 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block across 41 minutes of Wednesday's 117-109 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Charlotte had no answers for DeRozan defensively, as the veteran forward knocked down a ridiculous 80.9 percent of his attempts from inside the three-point arc. DeRozan's 39 points were a season high and his most since he dropped 42 on Feb. 10, 2025. It was a much-needed breakout game, as DeRozan had been averaging just 12.5 points, 4.0 assists and 2.3 rebounds while shooting 39 percent from the field over his last six appearances.

items.headline: DeRozan recorded 12 points (4-13 FG, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 114-109 win over Indiana.
items.story: Although there was no official announcement about a minute restriction, DeRozan returned to action and played only 24 minutes after a one-game absence. He connected on just four of his 13 shot attempts and appeared a step slow, which is likely due to lingering effects of his recent illness.

items.headline: DeRozan (illness) isn't listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: DeRozan was a late scratch ahead of Sunday's win over Chicago due to an illness, though he's set to return to action Tuesday. With the veteran forward returning to the lineup, Daeqwon Plowden will likely revert to a bench role. DeRozan has averaged 12.6 points, 4.6 assists and 2.2 rebounds in 26.4 minutes per game over his last five appearances.

items.headline: DeRozan has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus Chicago due to an illness.
items.story: This will be DeRozan's first missed game of the season, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Tuesday's game versus the Pacers. Russell Westbrook should see a sizable uptick in usage with DeRozan out, and there should be more minutes available for Daeqwon Plowden, Doug McDermott and Malik Monk.

items.headline: Risacher closed with 15 points (6-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Risacher was productive inside the arc and on the glass despite missing all five of his three-point attempts. His eight rebounds were particularly useful, giving him a respectable fantasy line. The third-year forward continues to offer complementary production in Dallas' rotation, but his limited playmaking and inconsistent outside shooting can restrict his value.  He seems to be trending in the right direction, scoring double-digit points in four of his last six appearances while averaging 12.3 points and 5.2 boards per game in that span.

items.headline: Risacher will start in Saturday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: With P.J. Washington (illness/shoulder) ruled out, Risacher will move into the starting lineup for the meeting with the Clippers. The 2024 No. 1 overall pick has started twice during the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 6.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.0 blocks and 1.0 steals over 25.0 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Risacher recorded 18 points (8-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and five rebounds in 26 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Risacher was a bright spot for Dallas in a blowout loss Sunday, leading the team in scoring while missing only one shot from the field. The third-year pro has not been able to string together multiple strong outings of late, logging four points, 22 points and five points, respectively, in the three games preceding Sunday's bout. Still, Risacher has posted his two highest-scoring totals of the season over the last three games, suggesting he is finding his footing.

items.headline: Risacher registered five points (2-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal over 14 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Fresh off a season-high 22 points in a loss to Minnesota, Risacher fell back to earth, turning in a mediocre performance. His fast start to the season is now a distant memory, as he's averaged just 6.9 points, 3.7 rebounds and 0.9 three-pointers in seven appearances over the past two weeks.

items.headline: Risacher tallied 22 points (9-14 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in 24 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Risacher saw more action than usual due to the Timberwolves jumping out to a large lead. He took full advantage of the opportunity by setting season highs in points and made threes. Risacher has struggled to consistently produce in his current bench role, though Thursday's showing could help convince the Dallas coaching staff that he's deserving of more minutes in the frontcourt going forward, especially as he's had his playing time dwindle since the start of November.

items.headline: Risacher is not listed in the starting lineup for Friday's game against Utah, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Max Christie (hip) unavailable for Wednesday's game in San Antonio, Risacher got the start. However, neither Christie nor Risacher will start Friday. Instead, Caleb Martin will roll with the first five.

items.headline: Risacher will start in Wednesday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Risacher will make his second start of the 2026-27 campaign Wednesday. The 21-year-old also started in the Mavericks' first meeting of the season with the Spurs on Oct. 24, finishing with 11 points, four rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks over 32 minutes.

items.headline: Risacher had zero points (0-3 FG, 0-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 115-100 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Risacher struggled to establish himself offensively, missing all three of his attempts from beyond the arc while finishing with a minus-19 rating. Dallas was missing several rotation players, including Santi Aldama (knee), but Risacher failed to capitalize on the available minutes. His inconsistent offensive involvement limits his fantasy appeal, even in an injury-depleted rotation.

items.headline: Risacher recorded 12 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals across 28 minutes off the bench during Friday's 116-111 win over the Rockets.
items.story: It's beginning to look like the Hawks may have given up on Risacher a bit too quickly. While the 21-year-old wing may never live up to his billing as the first overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, he's providing the Mavs with valuable depth so far, particularly on defense. Over the last five games (one start), Risacher is averaging 10.6 points, 6.0 boards, 2.0 blocks, 1.6 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.4 steals in 30.2 minutes.

items.headline: The Mavericks exercised their fourth-year team option on Risacher's contract Wednesday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: After being traded from Atlanta to Dallas this past offseason, Risacher is now officially under contract for the 2027-28 campaign. The 2024 No. 1 overall pick is averaging 8.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.0 steals, 2.0 blocks and 1.5 assists while shooting 30.8 percent from the field through four regular-season games (one start) with the Mavericks.

items.headline: Risacher won't start Monday's game against the Heat, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) back from a one-game absence, Risacher will slide to the second unit. The 2024 No. 1 overall pick is averaging 8.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.3 steals, 1.7 assists and 1.7 blocks in 30.3 minutes per game across three regular-season appearances (one start) thus far.

items.headline: Risacher finished Saturday's 122-16 loss to San Antonio with 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3PT, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 32 minutes.
items.story: Risacher and Naji Marshall were both moved into the Mavericks' starting five due to the absences of Kyrie Irving (rest) and Cooper Flagg (shoulder). Risacher scored two points or fewer in three of four quarters but did give the Mavericks a spark in the third with nine points. Flagg is expected to miss a few more games while recovering from a mild left shoulder sprain, so Risacher should continue to operate in an elevated role for as long as the former is sidelined.

items.headline: Risacher will be in the starting lineup for Saturday's matchup with the Spurs.
items.story: Kyrie Irving (rest) and Cooper Flagg (shoulder) are out, so Risacher will draw the start, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Max Christie, Naji Marshall, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford. Risacher has been struggling with his shot through the first two games of the year, converting just 33.3 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: Risacher (hip) is available for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Risacher was initially listed as questionable due to hip soreness, though he was eventually upgraded to probable before being cleared to play shortly thereafter. The 21-year-old figures to see significant minutes for the shorthanded Mavericks in the second leg of this back-to-back set, and he could step into the first unit if Max Christie (shin) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Risacher (hip) has been upgraded from questionable to probable ahead of Saturday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Risacher was initially tagged as questionable due to right hip soreness, but the third-year pro is trending in the right direction of Saturday's contest. Cooper Flagg (shoulder) has already been ruled out, and with Kyrie Irving (knee) now doubtful, Risacher and the other Mavericks role players are in line for more responsibilities against the Spurs.

items.headline: Risacher is questionable for Saturday's game against the Spurs due to right hip soreness.
items.story: A final call on Risacher's status will be made closer to Sunday's 8 p.m. ET tipoff. The Frenchman has seen considerable playing time off the bench in the early days of the season, logging at least 27 minutes in his two appearances and averaging 7.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 3.0 steals, 1.5 assists and 1.5 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Risacher ended Wednesday's 128-110 loss to Houston with four points (2-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and five steals over 27 minutes.
items.story: Risacher salvaged what was otherwise a disappointing performance, recording a career-high five steals. The jury is still out when it comes to Risacher's projected value. He will get an opportunity to turn things around in Dallas but will need to offer more on the offensive end should he wish to play a consistent role. Assuming the steals are more of an anomaly than a regular occurrence, he remains a stream-level player only at this point.

items.headline: Risacher won't start in Wednesday's game against Houston.
items.story: Risacher will move back to the bench to begin the 2026-27 campaign. However, with Santi Aldama (knee), Dereck Lively (foot) and Caleb Martin (thumb) unavailable, Risacher should be on the floor more than not on Opening Night.

items.headline: Risacher recorded 18 points (8-12 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds and four assists across 27 minutes in Friday's 135-111 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Risacher bounced back from a slow start, scoring 14 of his 18 points after halftime while making all six of his second-half field-goal attempts. His efficient shooting and four assists were encouraging signs as he continues adjusting to Dallas' offense. Risacher's role alongside Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving will be worth monitoring once the regular season begins, but based on his preseason performances, all signs point to him opening the regular season against the Rockets on Oct. 21 in a starting role.

items.headline: Risacher finished with 16 points (7-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block across 24 minutes in Sunday's 132-115 preseason win over the Rockets in China.
items.story: Risacher delivered a productive offensive showing, connecting on seven of his 13 field-goal attempts, and the young forward also chipped in defensively with a steal and a block, finishing with a plus-7 rating. His three turnovers were a minor blemish, but he otherwise displayed encouraging scoring versatility. Risacher's ability to contribute from the perimeter while providing secondary defensive production gives Dallas another wing option, as he looks to deliver a bounce-back year in 2026-27 after a subpar sophomore season in 2025-26. Risacher is competing for minutes on the wing, but this performance is certainly a step in the right direction.

items.headline: Risacher notched nine points (4-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Friday's 135-117 preseason loss to the Rockets.
items.story: With the Mavericks shorthanded, new head coach Dusty May started Risacher, Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Naji Marshall and rookie Morez Johnson during the preseason opener. After falling out of favor in Atlanta, the 2024 No. 1 overall pick is getting a fresh start in Dallas and making the most of his new opportunity. "I feel like we're going to be a good fit, especially on this team. We're going to play fast. We want to go," said Risacher. "We're going to play physical, and I feel like that's going to be a good fit. I like to play off-ball too, so I feel like just me being able to get to the right spot, get space, and finish those actions, that's going to be a big thing."

items.headline: Risacher is adjusting well to his new team and is looking forward to playing alongside Cooper Flagg, Grant Afseth of the Dallas Sports Journal reports.
items.story: Risacher has been adjusting well after being traded from the Hawks to the Mavericks in July, and he noted Thursday that he's confident his style will mesh well with Flagg. "I feel like we're going to be a good fit, especially in this team. We're going to play fast. We want to go," said Risacher. "We're going to play physical, and I feel like that's going to be a good fit. I like to play off-ball too, so I feel like just me being able to get to the right spot, get space, and finish those actions, that's going to be a big thing."

items.headline: Risacher was traded to the Mavericks on Sunday as part of a three-team deal that sent Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard (illness) to the Hawks and three second-round picks to the Thunder, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After being selected No. 1 overall in the 2024 NBA Draft, Risacher's tenure in Atlanta comes to an end as he'll head to Dallas. In 67 regular-season games (46 starts) with the Hawks during the 2025-26 campaign, the wing averaged 9.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 22.4 minutes per contest. Risacher still has much to prove heading into his third NBA season and will likely slot into a reserve role with the Mavericks, competing with the likes of Klay Thompson, Naji Marshall and Santi Aldama for playing time.

items.headline: The addition of Aaron Wiggins could further cut into Risacher's role during the 2026-27 season.
items.story: Risacher's minutes declined each month after January last season, and he was eventually demoted to the second unit after CJ McCollum solidified himself as a starter. Risacher was not a consistent part of the playoff rotation, and now he'll face even more competition for minutes following the arrival of Wiggins. The former No. 1 overall pick's long-term role with the franchise is murky at best.

items.headline: Risacher finished Thursday's 140-89 loss to New York in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with eight points (4-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and three rebounds across 16 minutes.
items.story: Though he saw his most playing time since the Hawks' regular-season finale April 12, Risacher didn't check into the game until the start of the second half, when Atlanta was already trailing by 47 points. The Game 6 loss brings an end to a disappointing second season for the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, who saw his numbers mostly hold steady across the board from his rookie campaign but saw a drop in usage from 21.6 percent to 17.7 percent while Atlanta fielded a more competitive roster. Risascher could re-enter the rotation to begin the 2026-27 season, but the Hawks are unlikely to count on him to fill a significant role.

items.headline: Risacher had zero points (0-3 FG) and four rebounds over two minutes during Saturday's 113-102 loss to New York in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Risacher barely saw the court, failing to score in three minutes. Despite his draft pedigree, Risacher has seemingly fallen out of favor in Atlanta, averaging just 15.7 minutes per game in 13 appearances over the past month. At this stage, it doesn't appear as though he will play any sort of meaningful role during the playoffs.

items.headline: Risacher won't start Saturday's Game 1 against the Knicks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Risacher got the starting nod in Atlanta's regular-season finale but will slide to the second unit for the start of the playoffs. The second-year forward averaged 7.9 points and 4.1 rebounds across 18.3 minutes per game in 21 regular-season appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Risacher will start Sunday's game against the Heat, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The Hawks successfully avoided the Play-In Tournament and will rest all of their starters during the regular-season finale, allowing Risacher to make his first start since Feb. 26. As a starter this season (45 games), Risacher has averaged 10.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Risacher (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Wednesday's 122-116 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Risacher's minutes had been trending down of late, but Wednesday marked the first time that he had failed to receive any playing time all season during a game in which he was active. Hawks head coach Quin Snyder inserted Corey Kispert into the rotation in place of the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, who hasn't displayed the sort of growth that Atlanta had been hoping for in Year 2. Risacher's 55.9 true shooting percentage is right in line with his mark from his rookie campaign (55.8 percent), but his usage rate has fallen from 21.6 percent in 2024-25 to 17.5 percent this season.

items.headline: Risacher provided three points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one steal across seven minutes during Monday's 108-105 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Risacher continues to play limited minutes off the bench, with fantasy managers forgiven for thinking he was out of the rotation altogether. In seven games over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 13.0 minutes per contest, putting up 5.6 points and 0.9 three-pointers.

items.headline: Risacher supplied two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one rebound in 13 minutes during Friday's 141-107 win over the Nets.
items.story: Despite its best efforts, Atlanta has been unable to develop Risacher to the point where he can be a meaningful contributor. While success has been a welcome theme for the Hawks in recent times, it has coincided with the fact that Risacher's role has reduced significantly. In 16 games over the past month, he has barely been a top-200 player, averaging 8.6 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 three-pointers in 18.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Risacher closed with six points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and two rebounds over 14 minutes during Friday's 109-102 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: After an encouraging three-game period during which Risacher averaged 14.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.3 three-pointers, things have regressed over the past two games. In that time, he has logged a total of 23 minutes, recording just eight points and five rebounds. Although he still has youth on his side, Risacher is certainly not looking like he will be an impactful NBA player.

items.headline: Risacher registered 17 points (5-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT) and two rebounds over 23 minutes during Saturday's 126-110 win over Golden State.
items.story: Risacher gave the Hawks a spark off the bench during Saturday's win, scoring 13 of his 17 points in the first half to finish tied with Nickeil Alexander-Walker as the team's third-leading scorer behind Dyson Daniels (28 points) and CJ McCollum (23 points). It's been an up-and-down season for Risacher, who was moved to a bench role following the All-Star break, though he's scored 33 points over his last two outings while going 11-for-14 from the field in that span (including 6-for-7 from three-point range).

items.headline: Risacher had 19 points (6-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 31 minutes during Thursday's 108-97 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: Risacher turned in his most productive performance in months, leading the second unit and recording his highest point total since a 25-point outburst against the Pelicans on Jan. 7. The No. 1 overall pick from 2024 dominated the glass with seven offensive rebounds and added a pair of blocks. While he has trended downward recently, averaging just 7.8 points on 38.5 percent shooting over his previous 12 contests, this breakout suggests he is beginning to find his footing in a reserve role. However, he'll likely see fewer minutes when Dyson Daniels (toe) is cleared to suit up.

items.headline: Bassey recorded 13 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals across 26 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Bassey finished one rebound shy of a double-double and missed just one of his seven field-goal attempts, but his contributions didn't end there. He also set season highs in assists and steals, making him one of Golden State's best players in this tight win. His long-term consistency will depend on maintaining a meaningful role in the Warriors' frontcourt rotation, though.

items.headline: Bassey ended with 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Bassey delivered his strongest performance of the season, capitalizing on increased minutes with his first double-double. He's started to establish a larger frontcourt role, combining efficient interior finishing with rebounding and rim protection. His limited offensive involvement caps his ceiling, but consistent minutes could make him a useful category-league streamer.

items.headline: Bassey recorded 10 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 FT), eight rebounds, one block and one steal over 22 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Getting his second start of the season, Bassey fell a couple of boards shy of his second double-double of 2026-27. The 26-year-old center has been taking on a bigger role than expected of late, seeing double-digit minutes in nine straight games (two starts) and averaging 17.4 minutes, 9.4 points, 6.4 boards and 1.0 blocks during that span while shooting 66.0 percent from the floor. With Kristaps Porzingis (illness) unavailable and both Al Horford (back) and Draymond Green (elbow) being far from iron men at this stage of their careers, Bassey should continue to be one of the players holding the Warriors' frontcourt together.

items.headline: Bassey will start Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Bassey will get the start due to Al Horford (back) being out. Bassey has averaged 8.5 points and 5.3 rebounds in 16.8 minutes per contest over his last four appearances.

items.headline: Bassey amassed 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and two assists across 20 minutes during Friday's 123-85 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Bassey was one of only two Warriors to score in double figures. The big man has struggled to earn consistent minutes behind Golden State's veteran frontcourt, but his energy around the rim stood out on a night when little else went right. Bassey could keep getting chances, as Kristaps Porzingis' (illness) abrupt departure has left a gap on the rotation.

items.headline: Bassey (toe) is available for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Bassey was listed as probable due to left toe soreness, and Bassey's availability is now confirmed. The big man is averaging 7.6 points and 5.7 rebounds per game in 10 appearances (one start) this season.

items.headline: Bassey is probable for Friday's game against the Spurs due to left toe soreness.
items.story: It's not clear as to when this injury popped up for Bassey, who missed the first two games of the season with a knee issue but has been otherwise healthy. Expect the team to confirm his availability for Friday as tipoff nears.

items.headline: Bassey closed Monday's 138-87 victory over the Pelicans with 12 points (6-8 FG), 10 rebounds, one assist and one block over 18 minutes.
items.story: Bassey was efficient around the rim and pulled down three offensive rebounds on his way to a double-double in just 18 minutes during a blowout win. He's back in a reserve role with Draymond Green healthy, and Bassey's minutes fluctuate depending on matchups, so he's best left for deeper leagues. Still, his per-minute rebounding is worth monitoring.

items.headline: Bassey recorded 19 points (7-10 FG, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds and one assist in 23 minutes during Monday's 116-113 win over the Suns.
items.story: Bassey delivered a career-best scoring performance and led Golden State in rebounds after Draymond Green was ejected early in the third quarter. The reserve big man capitalized on his increased playing time, collecting three offensive boards and providing an efficient interior scoring presence. His performance could earn him additional opportunities, although Green's availability will significantly influence Bassey's fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Bassey won't start in Monday's game against the Suns, John Dickinson of 95.7 The Game San Francisco reports.
items.story: Bassey got the start in place of Draymond Green (rest) during the first leg of Golden State's back-to-back Sunday, but he'll revert to the bench with the latter making his return to the lineup.

items.headline: Bassey is listed as the starting center for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Bassey will start in place of Draymond Green (rest), who will take the first night of Golden State's back-to-back set off. Bassey played nine minutes off the bench in Friday's 112-95 win over the Lakers, but he should earn a much larger role versus the Clippers and offers solid streaming appeal.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is available for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Bassey will play in his second consecutive contest after sitting out the first two outings of the season for Golden State. He posted 10 points (4-4 FG, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds and two blocks in just 13 minutes during Saturday's loss to Phoenix, and he should see limited minutes again with Draymond Green (back) returning to the lineup.

items.headline: Bassey is probable for Monday's game against the Nuggets due to right patellar tendinopathy.
items.story: Bassey has been dealing with a right knee issue for some time, but he is likely to make a second straight appearance. The big man played well during Saturday's loss to the Suns, logging 10 points (4-4 FG, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds and two blocks in just 13 minutes.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is available for Saturday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Bassey will return to action after missing the first two games of the regular season due to right patellar tendinopathy. The Warriors will be shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set, so the big man will likely see significant minutes.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Suns.
items.story: If Bassey is cleared to play, he would likely see meaningful playing time for the shorthanded Warriors. However, if Bassey and Draymond Green (back/rest), who is listed as doubtful, join Al Horford (back) on the inactive list, Graham Ike and Georges Niang would likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is out for Friday's game versus the Grizzlies.
items.story: The big man is dealing with right patellar tendinopathy and can be considered day-to-day. Even with Kristaps Porzingis (illness) out of action, Bassey is unlikely to play a significant role once healthy.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Bassey could miss a second straight game due to right patellar tendinopathy. However, the big man's potential absence wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is out for Wednesday's season opener versus the Lakers.
items.story: The big man is battling right patellar tendinopathy and can be deemed day-to-day. Even with Kristaps Porzingis on the mend with an undisclosed health issue, Bassey is unlikely to play a significant role once healthy.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's season opener versus the Lakers, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: Bassey missed practice Tuesday, placing him on the wrong side of the questionable marker. The big man is unlikely to play a significant role even with Kristaps Porzingis on the mend with an undisclosed medical issue.

items.headline: Bassey (knee) didn't practice Monday, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: The Warriors are treating Bassey as day-to-day with knee tendinitis. The big man can be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Lakers.

items.headline: Bassey registered eight points (3-5 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and three blocks across 27 minutes in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Starting in place of a resting Draymond Green, Bassey struggled against Walker Kessler early but dominated after halftime, finishing with a team-high 12 boards. Bassey's five turnovers are a concern, but he's making a strong case for backup center minutes behind Green and Kristaps Porzingis.

items.headline: Bassey will start Tuesday's preseason matchup against the Lakers with Draymond Green resting, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Bassey will get an opportunity with Golden State's first unit while Green sits out. The temporary lineup adjustment could provide Bassey with additional minutes and opportunities to contribute on the glass and defensively, though his role will change once Green returns.

items.headline: Bassey will come off the bench in Saturday's exhibition against the Kings.
items.story: Draymond Green (rest) is back and starting after skipping Wednesday's exhibition, so Bassey will shift back to a reserve role. As a member of the second unit this preseason, Bassey is averaging 8.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.5 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Bassey notched 13 points (6-6 FG, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist, three steals and three blocks over 24 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 preseason loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Bassey converted all six of his shot attempts and racked up six stocks in under 30 minutes. With Kristaps Porzingis (illness) out indefinitely, there could be a path to meaningful minutes for Bassey, so he's someone worth monitoring this preseason.

items.headline: Bassey will start in Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kristaps Porzingis (illness) remains out indefinitely, and both Draymond Green and Al Horford did not travel for Wednesday's exhibition, so Bassey will draw the start. He could see quality minutes with the Warriors resting nine players, and he's capable of racking up the boards when given the opportunity.

items.headline: Bassey finished with 12 points (6-10 FG, 0-2 FT), eight rebounds, two steals and one assist in 16 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Bassey made an immediate impact on the glass, grabbing six offensive rebounds while tying for the team lead in scoring. With Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) currently sidelined and Golden State potentially needing additional frontcourt depth, Bassey could make a case for rotation minutes with more performances like this.

items.headline: Bassey could see more playing time to begin the season if Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) isn't ready for Opening Night.
items.story: Bassey bounced around last season, appearing for the Warriors, 76ers, Grizzlies and Celtics, but he's looking to find a home in Golden State. Assuming Draymond Green starts at power forward, Bassey could challenge veteran Al Horford for the starting center job if Porzingis is out to start the year.

items.headline: Bassey agreed to a one-year deal with the Warriors on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bassey joined the Warriors for the end of the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 10.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.4 blocks in 20.2 minutes per game over five regular-season appearances with Golden State. He'll rejoin the club for 2026-27 and figures to provide center depth behind Kristaps Porzingis and Al Horford.

items.headline: Murray amassed 15 points (7-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 12 rebounds and one steal in 40 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 win over Boston.
items.story: Murray overcame another difficult night from beyond the arc to make the game's decisive play, grabbing an offensive rebound and scoring with five seconds remaining. His 12 rebounds helped compensate for the lack of perimeter production, and the fact that he's recorded at least 40 minutes in three of his last five games goes to show how much of a prominent role he has in the frontcourt. Murray has been struggling with his outside shot but has remained productive in his last seven games since returning from an ankle injury Nov. 8, averaging 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds and a combined 1.9 steals-plus-blocks per game despite shooting just 26.7 percent from three in that span.

items.headline: Murray amassed 12 points (6-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Murray has started three straight games, but his minutes have fluctuated between 21 and 40 during that stretch. He's attempted at least nine shots in five consecutive appearances, though inconsistent perimeter shooting and Sacramento's frequent blowout losses limit his ceiling. His defensive versatility offers some category-league appeal.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Murray was dealing with an illness that left him questionable to suit up versus OKC, but he's ready to rock and should reprise his starting role in Sacramento's frontcourt. He's averaging 10.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks in 28.2 minutes across five outings this season.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Murray didn't participate in Saturday's shootaround, so the questionable tag isn't a surprise. De'Andre Hunter and Dylan Cardwell could play a bigger role if Murray isn't available, especially since Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is also uncertain to suit up Sunday.

items.headline: Murray (illness) didn't participate in Saturday's practice, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Murray is dealing with an illness ahead of Sunday's home game against the Thunder. If he's unable to play, De'Andre Hunter and Dylan Cardwell would likely see increased burn, especially if Precious Achiuwa (ankle) remains out.

items.headline: Murray ended Friday's 120-107 loss to the Trail Blazers with 16 points (7-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and two steals across 40 minutes.
items.story: Murray put together a solid all-around line in his return to the starting lineup. He didn't force much offensively, but he was steady on both ends and didn't turn the ball over. Sacramento needs more nights like this from Murray if it's going to climb out of its early-season hole.

items.headline: Murray is in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Murray will return to the starting lineup after coming off the bench in Tuesday's loss to the Magic, when he tallied 11 points and two rebounds across 24 minutes. This will be Murray's first start since Oct. 23, but given that he's played between 23 and 28 minutes in each of his four appearances this season regardless of whether he starts or not, his role should remain steady.

items.headline: Murray (wrist) is available for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Murray is still dealing with lingering right wrist soreness following a recent extended absence, but he's fighting through the issue Tuesday. The sharpshooter opened the year as a starter but has fallen into a battle with Precious Achiuwa for the top spot at power forward.

items.headline: Murray is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic due to right wrist soreness.
items.story: Murray made his return to the court Sunday against Miami following a seven-game absence due to an ankle injury, and it now appears he's dealing with a wrist issue. The Kings will presumably monitor him closely during shootaround and warmups to determine if he can suit up Tuesday.

items.headline: Murray contributed 10 points (3-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, two assists, one block and two steals in 23 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat.
items.story: The 26-year-old missed the prior seven games with an ankle injury, and Murray got eased into the lineup Sunday on the second unit while Precious Achiuwa got another start at power forward. The duo could switch roles as soon as Tuesday in a home game against the Magic, but with Domantas Sabonis (knee) not 100 percent himself, there may be room for both Murray and Achiuwa in the frontcourt in the short term.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Murray last played in the 128-120 loss to Portland on Oct. 23. Since then, he's been on the shelf due to left ankle capsulitis. While Murray may come off the bench in his first game back, he will likely reclaim his spot in the starting lineup soon, resulting in Precious Achiuwa reverting to a reserve role.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Murray hasn't played since going down with an ankle injury on Oct. 25, so if he is cleared for Sunday's game, his minutes will likely be monitored. His return would likely push Precious Achiuwa back to the second unit.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-to-14 days, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
items.story: Murray has officially been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis, and he's set to miss at least the next 10 days. Precious Achiuwa has been starting in Murray's absence, and he should continue to see opportunities, as should De'Andre Hunter and Daeqwon Plowden.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: With Murray unavailable, Precious Achiuwa could get the start and De'Andre Hunter could get a bump in minutes. There will also be more opportunity for Daeqwon Plowden. Murray's next chance to play will come Tuesday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been downgraded to doubtful for Sunday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Murray was initially listed as questionable but is trending in the wrong direction ahead of Sunday's contest. In the likely event that he's ruled out, Precious Achiuwa, Alex Karaban and Daeqwon Plowden would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Murray is questionable to play Sunday against the Grizzlies due to left ankle capsulitis.
items.story: A final call on Murray's availability for Sunday will be made closer to Sunday's 9 p.m. ET tipoff. If he's not available to play, then Precious Achiuwa and potentially Alex Karaban could be in line to see more playing time at power forward.

items.headline: Murray notched 12 points (4-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 26 minutes during Friday's 128-120 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Murray rebounded from a two-point dud in the opener, reaching double figures and going 4-for-4 from the free-throw line. His three-point shot remains a concern, as he hasn't made a shot from deep this season. His starting role is still safe, but the winless Kings need him to right the ship soon.

items.headline: Murray ended with two points (1-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt), four rebounds and one steal over 28 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Murray showed signs of rust in his season debut, failing to convert any of his three-point attempts. The sharpshooter is locked into a starting role for the rebuilding Kings, and Murray should be a strong source of triples and defensive stats once he finds his shooting touch.

items.headline: Murray posted 10 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and four rebounds in 19 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Murray got into double figures in Tuesday's exhibition. The sharpshooter is locked into a significant role for the rebuilding Kings and should serve as a tertiary scoring option behind Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine this season.

items.headline: Murray (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Murray was sidelined for each of the Kings' first two preseason games, but the fifth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Saturday's contest. He was limited to only 23 regular-season games during the 2025-26 campaign, but he entered training camp fully recovered from a left ankle injury that required surgery in mid-May.

items.headline: Murray (undisclosed) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Lakers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Murray appears to be dealing with some kind of injury, though the team has yet to provide any additional details. He can continue to be considered day-to-day leading up to Saturday's exhibition against the Warriors.

items.headline: Murray (undisclosed) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Lakers, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: It's unclear why Murray is sitting out Sacramento's preseason opener, though his next chance to play in the preseason will come in Thursday's rematch against the Lakers. Precious Achiuwa, Dylan Cardwell and Alex Karaban are all candidates to see a bump in minutes due to Murray being sidelined.

items.headline: Murray is healthy entering training camp, Kings general manager Scott Perry said Monday, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Murray was limited to 23 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 while battling several injuries, most notably issues with his left ankle. He underwent an arthroscopic procedure in May to remove loose bodies from the ankle, but his healthy status entering camp indicates the issue shouldn't limit him as Sacramento begins preparations for the regular season.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is projected to start at power forward for the Kings in 2026-27, according to Kings beat writer Chris Watkins.
items.story: Watkins believes De'Andre Hunter will start at small forward next to Murray, with rookie Alex Karaban coming off the bench. Murray underwent an arthroscopic procedure to remove loose bodies in his left ankle back in May, though he's expected to be ready in time for training camp.

items.headline: Murray underwent an arthroscopic procedure to remove loose bodies in his left ankle Tuesday, per James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento.
items.story: Murray, who was held to a career-low 23 appearances in 2025-26, suffered multiple left ankle sprains during the season, and the hope is that the surgery will aid his recovery. The 25-year-old forward could be off the court for as many as eight weeks, but the expectation is that he'll be ready to go for the start of training camp in the fall.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) will be sidelined for the Kings' final game of the season Sunday against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Murray will end the season having not played since Feb. 25. The fourth-year forward couldn't get things going, struggling with injuries and appearing in just 23 games. He averaged 14.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.6 blocks and 1.0 steals in 34.5 minutes.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Murray hasn't taken the court since Feb. 25 after suffering a left ankle sprain. He'll have another chance to return Sunday in the regular-season finale against Portland, though his campaign is likely over considering Sacramento has nothing left to play for.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Murray will miss a 20th consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain, and it appears unlikely he'll return this season. His penultimate chance to suit up this season will come Friday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Murray will be sidelined for a 19th straight contest and remains without a target date to return.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Murray will miss an 18th consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain, though he was recently cleared to take contact in practice. He should be considered doubtful for Sunday's game against the Clippers.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Murray is taking contact in practice amid his recovery from an ankle sprain, but he isn't ready for game action. Considering the Kings are buried in the standings, the team is unlikely to be in a hurry to bring Murray back.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) is making good progress in his recovery and has been approved to participate in contact basketball activities, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Murray has battled a left ankle injury for most of the calendar year, and while he's making progress, each day that goes by lowers his chances of returning in 2025-26. The Kings sit at the bottom of the Western Conference standings, so there's little incentive to rush Murray back.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Re-evaluated doesn't mean Murray will return in two weeks, and with the Kings holding the worst record in the Western Conference, there's not much incentive for the fourth-year forward to rush back to the court. Precious Achiuwa has been the primary beneficiary in Murray's absence thus far.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Murray is set to miss an eighth consecutive game due to a left ankle sprain. His next chance to play is Sunday against the Jazz, though the Kings have not provided an injury update for the fourth-year pro. It's been a frustrating season for Murray, who has appeared in only 23 regular-season games due to multiple injuries.

items.headline: Murray will have his sprained left ankle re-evaluated by medical staff in two weeks, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: The injury is to the same ankle that caused Murray to miss 20 consecutive games from early January to post-All-Star break. The Kings will take a cautious approach with the fourth-year forward, who could be back in action in mid-March depending on how well he progresses in his recovery. Nique Clifford, Malik Monk and Daeqwon Plowden are all candidates for increased roles for as long as Murray is sidelined.

items.headline: Murray is out for Thursday's game against Dallas with a sprained left ankle.
items.story: Murray re-aggravated the injury during Wednesday's game against the Rockets, and he recently missed 20 games with the sprain. The sharpshooter can be considered day-to-day until the team offers an update on his status. His absence allows Daeqwon Plowden and Patrick Baldwin to play more minutes for the depleted Kings.

items.headline: Murray (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday's game against the Rockets, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Murray injured his left ankle -- the same ankle that cost him 20 games from Jan. 6 to Feb. 11 -- in the first quarter Wednesday and is unable to return. He'll end the contest with three points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound and one block across nine minutes. Look for Patrick Baldwin and Daeqwon Plowden to see more playing time for the rest of Wednesday's contest. Sacramento closes out a back-to-back set Thursday against Dallas.

items.headline: Murray sustained a left ankle injury during Wednesday's game against the Rockets and went back to the locker room, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Murray exited the game with 3:23 left in the first quarter after sustaining an apparent ankle injury. Wednesday's contest is Murray's fourth since a 20-game absence because of a sprained left ankle. Given Murray's injury history, expect the Kings to proceed with caution.

items.headline: Murray finished with 20 points (7-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 36 minutes during Saturday's 139-122 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Murray tied DeMar DeRozan for the Kings' highest scoring total. With Zach LaVine (finger) and Domantas Sabonis (knee) done for the season, there's tremendous pressure on Murray to carry a heavy load on both sides of the ball. While heavy usage should be expected nightly for Murray if he stays healthy, his lack of support may negatively affect his ability to post consistent totals down the stretch.

items.headline: Murray totaled 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists and one block in 32 minutes during Thursday's 131-94 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Seeing his first action since Jan. 4 after recovering from an ankle injury, Murray was dropped right back into the starting five and saw a full workload. With Domantas Sabonis (knee) set to miss the rest of the season, Murray will be the key figure for the Kings in their frontcourt. On the season, the fourth-year forward is averaging 14.6 points, 6.3 boards, 1.6 assists, 1.6 blocks, 1.4 threes and 1.1 steals over 20 games.

items.headline: Walsh will come off the bench in Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Sam Hauser will replace Walsh in the first unit for Saturday's game. As a reserve this season, Walsh is averaging 2.8 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.

items.headline: Walsh registered 11 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and one steal across 21 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Walsh helped set the tone for Boston's dominant opening quarter, combining with Derrick White for 19 of the Celtics' first 24 points. However, Walsh remains a secondary scoring option behind the Celtics' established stars, so his defensive contributions and perimeter shooting matter more to his fantasy outlook. He has scored in double digits in just two appearances this season, so it's hard to trust him outside of deep formats right now.

items.headline: Walsh is starting Sunday's game against Dallas, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: Walsh will enter the mix in place of Baylor Scheierman, who will be utilized off the bench during Sunday's clash. Walsh tallied eight points, two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 19 minutes during his last start Tuesday against Philly.

items.headline: Walsh is not listed in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against Toronto, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: After starting in Tuesday's 123-101 win over the 76ers, Walsh will head back to the bench Wednesday. However, with Paul George (illness) unavailable, Walsh should still get opportunities to produce as a reserve.

items.headline: Walsh will start Tuesday against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Joining Walsh in the first unit for Tuesday's game will be Derrick White, Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Neemias Queta. As a starter this season, Walsh is averaging 5.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 18.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh will start Friday against the Hornets, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Walsh will replace Hugo Gonzalez in the first unit for Friday's game. As a starter this season, Walsh is averaging 5.2 points and 4.0 rebounds in 17.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Walsh won't start Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Walsh was initially announced in the starting lineup, but the Celtics made a late switch, sending the fourth-year wing to the bench for the first time this season. Hugo Gonzalez will start in Walsh's place.

items.headline: Walsh delivered 15 points (5-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, an assist and a steal across 24 minutes in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime win over the Nets.
items.story: Despite playing just 24 minutes, Walsh set season highs in points and three-pointers made while matching his best rebounding output. Walsh has started every game for Boston this season, but with averages of 6.0 points and 4.5 rebounds per contest, his fantasy appeal shouldn't be very high outside of the deepest formats.

items.headline: Walsh recorded four points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and three steals over 18 minutes during Monday's 134-99 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Walsh struggled offensively but made an impact on the defensive end, matching his career high with three steals. The 22-year-old forward has started each of Boston's first three games this season, though his modest offensive role and limited playing time restrict his fantasy upside. Walsh remains a deeper-league option for managers seeking defensive contributions.

items.headline: Walsh had zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 13 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Walsh failed to score despite earning the start, logging just 13 minutes. Having Walsh as a starter was certainly a curious move, and first impressions were not good. Even if he is to remain with the opening five, Walsh is not someone fantasy managers need to pay too much attention to, outside of very deep leagues.

items.headline: Walsh is starting Tuesday's season opener against the Pistons, per Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston.
items.story: This was the expectation after Walsh worked with Boston's other members of the first unit throughout the preseason. He's getting the first crack as a starter in favor of Hugo Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman.

items.headline: Walsh finished Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over the Hornets with two points (0-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block across 17 minutes.
items.story: Walsh provided a muted impact on the offensive end in his limited burn Wednesday. The 22-year-old forward is a talented defender who still has room to grow offensively, and he is expected to open the season as a member of Boston's starting five, according to Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com. Across 25 regular-season starts in 2025-26, Walsh averaged 7.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.6 blocks in 22.7 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Walsh tallied 16 points (6-14 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, an assist and a block across 26 minutes in Thursday's 124-113 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Walsh joined Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Luka Garza as one of the four starters who crossed the 15-point threshold in this win for the Celtics, and he continues to make a strong case for a prominent role in the rotation with the start of the regular season around the corner. Although he finished with a minus-13 rating and committed five personal fouls, Walsh's aggressive offensive approach was encouraging as he looks to establish a larger role in Boston's wing rotation. He's in the mix for a bench role at either forward position.

items.headline: Walsh will start in Thursday's preseason game against Cleveland, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Walsh will get the start to begin the preseason. The 22-year-old is coming off his best campaign in 2025-26, and in 25 regular-season starts, he averaged 7.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 steals over 22.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh is learning from Paul George this offseason on how to expand his offensive game, per Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com.
items.story: After making a career-high 25 starts last regular season, Walsh is looking to take another step forward in 2026-27. He's in contention for a starting spot on the wing with Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Sam Hauser during training camp, which will remain a battle to monitor this fall.

items.headline: Walsh and the Celtics agreed to a three-year, $15 million extension Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Boston previously picked up Walsh's $2.4 million option for the 2026-27 season and now added three more years for their 2023 second-rounder. During the 2025-26 regular season, Walsh appeared in 68 games with averages of 5.4 points, 4.0 rebounds and 0.8 assists.

items.headline: The Celtics picked up their 2026-27 team option for Walsh on Monday, Adam Himmelsbach of The Boston Globe reports.
items.story: This is an expected move by the Celtics. Walsh appeared in 68 regular-season games in 2025-26, posting averages of 5.4 points and 4.0 rebounds in 17.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Walsh logged zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) across five minutes during Saturday's 109-100 loss to Philadelphia in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Despite the absence of Jayson Tatum (knee), Walsh didn't benefit. In fact, he logged a series-low five minutes while going without a point. Although the 2025-26 campaign didn't work out exactly as the team had hoped, Walsh at least saw his production improve, as he averaged a career-best 5.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.7 steals across 17.8 minutes in 68 regular-season appearances (25 starts). While Walsh should hold a stable role in the rotation for the Celtics next season, assuming he remains on the roster, he may have trouble being consistently productive as long as the starters stay healthy.

items.headline: Walsh isn't starting in Sunday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Walsh started in the Celtics' final three contests of the regular season, most recently finishing with nine points, eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 33 minutes in the 113-108 win over Orlando on April 12. However, with a healthy starting lineup for Boston versus Philadelphia, Walsh will head back to the bench, potentially seeing 10-15 minutes of work in Game 1.

items.headline: Walsh is starting Thursday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Walsh will take the place of Jaylen Brown, who is out Thursday due to left Achilles tendinitis. Walsh started a pair of games down the stretch but failed to score in double figures in either opportunity.

items.headline: Walsh is not in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Heat on Wednesday.
items.story: Walsh started each of the Celtics' last two games, but the third-year wing will revert to a bench role for Wednesday's contest. The Celtics will roll with a starting lineup of Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Sam Hauser, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta.

items.headline: Walsh will start in Sunday's game against Charlotte, according to Justin Turpin of WEEI.com.
items.story: The Celtics are down Jaylen Brown (Achilles) and Derrick White (knee), so head coach Joe Mazzulla will turn to Walsh to make his first start since New Year's Day. In 20 starts during the campaign, the 22-year-old is averaging 7.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.6 blocks and 1.1 steals across 21.5 minutes.

items.headline: Walsh recorded five points (2-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), three rebounds, three blocks and one assist across 27 minutes Friday in the Celtics' 109-102 win over the Hawks.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (Achilles) sitting out Friday, Walsh re-entered the rotation after going unused in each of the Celtics' last six games. Walsh fared well in his low-usage role, knocking down his lone perimeter shot while making his biggest impact at the defensive end. Despite seeing heavy minutes Friday, Walsh could drop back out of the rotation Sunday in Charlotte if Brown is cleared to return to action.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Walsh was sidelined for Friday's 120-100 win over the Mavericks due to an illness, but the third-year pro has recovered enough to return for Sunday's road tilt. His minutes were set to take a sizable hit due to the return of Jayson Tatum, but Walsh could still see some meaningful playing time for the next couple of weeks due to the absence of Nikola Vucevic (finger).

items.headline: Walsh (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Walsh is under the weather and will miss Friday's contest, but he'll look to progress enough in his recovery to be available for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers. Walsh's absence shouldn't impact the Celtics' rotation all that much, seeing as Jayson Tatum (Achilles) has been cleared to make his 2025-26 debut against Dallas.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is questionable for Friday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Walsh was a very late addition to the injury report. He's been averaging 13.0 minutes over his last seven appearances, and minutes will be hard to come by with Jayson Tatum (Achilles) targeting his debut against Dallas.

items.headline: Walsh ended with four points (2-2 FG, 0-1 FT) and three rebounds over 14 minutes during Wednesday's 103-84 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Walsh logged 14 minutes in the loss, most of which came during garbage time. While it has been a somewhat encouraging season for Walsh, his role in recent times has been less than ideal. In 12 games over the past month, he has seen just 13.8 minutes per game, putting up 4.2 points and 3.5 rebounds. At this point, he should not be rostered in any moderately competitive league.

items.headline: Walsh recorded 16 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and three steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-105 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Walsh had been quiet lately, but he turned in his first double-digit scoring night since Jan. 3. His versatility was on full display, and the large margin of victory helped him see additional run. Walsh can deliver when called upon, but his role hasn't been as consistent as it was at the start of the campaign.

items.headline: Walsh (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Celtics' 98-96 win over the Heat.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (hamstring/knee) and Sam Hauser (thumb) returning from one-game absences and with Nikola Vucevic making his Celtics debut, head coach Joe Mazzulla opted to remove Walsh from the rotation. Though defense is Walsh's calling card, his lack of productivity on the offensive end looks as though it cost him his spot in the second unit Friday. Since moving out of the starting five Jan. 3, Walsh has shot just 38.3 percent from the field and 25.8 percent from three-point range in 18 appearances. Walsh's move outside of the rotation may not necessarily be a permanent one, but even if he gets some minutes in the Celtics' next game Sunday versus the Knicks, he shouldn't be expected to deliver much fantasy value.

items.headline: Walsh logged zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over 10 minutes during Tuesday's 110-100 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Walsh went scoreless in the win, now serving as nothing more than a depth piece for the Celtics. Outside of a brief run earlier in the season, Walsh seems as though his time as a viable fantasy asset has come and gone. At this point, there is no reason to be holding him, even in deeper formats.

items.headline: Walsh ended with five points (1-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal over 16 minutes during Friday's 112-93 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Walsh was used sparingly again, playing fewer than 20 minutes for the seventh time in the past eight games. With Sam Hauser seemingly taking hold of the starting power forward position, Walsh has been relegated to a depth role. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 3.4 points and 2.5 rebounds in 14.5 minutes per game, leaving him well outside the top 300 in nine-category formats.

items.headline: Walsh ended with six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist and three steals across 26 minutes during Monday's 98-96 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Walsh logged 26 minutes in the loss, which is the most he has played in his past five games. After a stint in the starting lineup, Walsh has since been reduced to a limited role off the bench. In four games over the past week, Walsh has averaged just 1.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 16.0 minutes per game. Given the uncertainty in Boston, there is no reason to consider Walsh a pickup based on this effort.

items.headline: Walsh closed with 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), 13 rebounds, two assists and one block across 30 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 146-115 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Shifting to the second unit while Sam Hauser got a start at the four, Walsh produced his second double-double of the season, with the other coming Nov. 20 against the Cavaliers. Walsh's production has been on the decline in the starting five -- he'd failed to score in double digits, or pull down more than seven boards, in seven straight games -- but it's not yet clear if Saturday's effort will be enough for the third-year forward to regain his spot.

items.headline: Walsh is not in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Clippers on Saturday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Head coach Joe Mazulla will shake up the rotation Saturday, moving Walsh to the bench while Sam Hauser enters the starting five. Walsh has been a mainstay in the Celtics' starting lineup since Nov. 12, but over his last seven outings he has averaged just 4.0 points and 3.4 rebounds over 14.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh chipped in three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists in 19 minutes during Friday's 140-122 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Walsh returned from a one-game absence due to an Illness, slotting straight back into the starting lineup. The positives end there, however, as Walsh was unable to have any sort of tangible impact on the game.
