While it has been only two games, it appears as though Niederhauser may have moved ahead of Jackson in the battle for backup minutes behind Brook Lopez.

items.headline: Jackson closed Thursday's 124-112 loss to the Spurs with six points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), four rebounds, three steals, two assists and two blocks across nine minutes.
items.story: With Yanic Konan Niederhauser (foot) making his season debut, Jackson saw limited burn as the Clippers' third-string center. Niederhauser will likely require time to ramp up toward a more significant workload, though Jackson is still facing added competition for minutes moving forward.

The veteran big man has averaged 16.8 minutes over his last four contests, limiting his overall fantasy upside despite his efficient scoring and shot-blocking ability. He remains a viable blocks specialist in deeper category-based leagues.

He outscored starting center Brook Lopez 19-12 and played nearly four more minutes, providing the Clippers with an effective interior presence. Although Jackson failed to register a steal or block, his efficient scoring and rebounding make him worth monitoring in deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Jackson won't start Monday's game against the Raptors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.

He's averaging 8.6 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.2 blocks per game while shooting 60 percent from the floor, giving him enough floor, both in production and role, to be a worthy waiver pickup, particularly in category-based formats.

Jackson has scored in double digits in five of his last six games, but his reserve role compromises his fantasy appeal, even if he's making the most of the limited opportunities.

items.headline: Sabonis chipped in 15 points (5-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 17 rebounds, four assists and one block across 32 minutes before fouling out of Saturday's 97-96 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Sabonis remained a dominant presence on the glass, though his seven turnovers and the fact he fouled out diminished an otherwise productive performance. His combination of rebounding, efficient interior scoring and passing continues to provide a strong fantasy foundation. Saturday's relatively modest assist total also highlights how Sacramento's offensive responsibilities are being distributed, as Darius Acuff is now operating as the team's go-to playmaker. Sabonis has four double-doubles over his last five games and is turning things around after an inconsistent start to the season.

items.headline: Sabonis totaled 19 points (8-13 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 16 rebounds and one assist over 38 minutes during Friday's 106-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sabonis controlled the glass with a game-high rebound total and notched another double-double. He's averaging 13.4 rebounds this season and remains one of the league's most dominant rebounders, even on a team that has struggled to win. The veteran big man has been efficient around the basket, though Sacramento has struggled to capitalize on his production.

items.headline: Sabonis chipped in eight points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), 13 rebounds, eight assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Sabonis came within two points and two assists of a triple-double despite playing just 24 minutes, although his eight points represented a disappointing scoring total. The veteran's offensive opportunities were limited as Sacramento leaned heavily on Darius Acuff and Zach LaVine, but Sabonis' rebounding and playmaking remained productive. His relatively modest workload was also influenced by the lopsided score, and his ability to contribute in multiple categories should continue to support his fantasy value even when his scoring is limited. That said, Sabonis is averaging just 13.7 points per game and has scored 11 or fewer points in three of his last four appearances, so his scoring figures are undoubtedly trending in the wrong direction.

items.headline: Sabonis finished Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder with 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 13 rebounds and three assists in 29 minutes.
items.story: The veteran center's shot volume remains low as the Kings' offense re-focuses itself around rookie Darius Acuff. Sabonis has produced nine double-doubles in 12 games to begin the season, but over his last eight contests, he's averaging 11.8 points, 11.5 boards and 4.8 assists while attempting just 7.8 FGs a game, a drop of nearly four attempts a game from 2025-26.

items.headline: Sabonis ended with 21 points (9-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists over 35 minutes during Friday's 120-107 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Sabonis posted another double-double with 21 points and 12 rebounds, his usual efficient work in the paint. The big man remains the Kings' most reliable player even as losses keep piling up. He'll face a shorthanded frontcourt Sunday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Sabonis closed with zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two rebounds and five assists over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 107-100 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Sabonis was scoreless in his first game back from left knee soreness, and he posted a strange line for one of the league's most dependable big men. He still moved the ball well as a passer, but he didn't look like himself, and his minutes were limited. He'll have the advantage of a few days of rest before meeting Portland later in the week.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) is available for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Sabonis is returning from a one-game absence after being unavailable during Sunday's defeat to the Heat. With the star big man back in action, Dylan Cardwell is set to slide back to the bench Tuesday.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) is questionable to play in Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Sabonis missed Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat with left knee soreness, making it his first absence of the season through 10 games. Dylan Cardwell earned the start with Sabonis sidelined, so if the latter is forced to miss a second straight contest, the former would be the top candidate to start once again.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Sabonis was a late addition to the injury report due to left knee soreness and will be unavailable for Sunday's contest. Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa are candidates for increased playing time in his absence.

items.headline: Sabonis has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against Miami due to left knee soreness.
items.story: Sabonis was a late addition to the injury report and could miss his first game of the season. If the veteran center joins Maxime Raynaud (knee) on the inactive list, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Sabonis registered 17 points (8-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists over 31 minutes during Friday's 124-109 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Sabonis posted another efficient double-double, making eight of 12 shots and adding five assists, which ties him with Victor Wembanyama for third in the league in double-doubles. Four turnovers hurt, and Sacramento never seriously threatened after falling behind by 19 at the half. He's still one of the league's most reliable big men, but the Kings' 1-8 start caps his potential.

items.headline: Sabonis logged 16 points (5-10 FG, 6-9 FT), 17 rebounds, one assist and one steal in 35 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sabonis dominated the glass, pulling down six offensive rebounds among his 17 boards, after grabbing 14 against Memphis on Saturday. His playmaking was quiet, with just one assist, as Darius Acuff handled most of the facilitating duties. Regardless, Sabonis' rebounding alone keeps him among the elite fantasy centers.

items.headline: Sabonis racked up 11 points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 14 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 38 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: The Kings' shot distribution was dominated by rookie seventh-overall pick Darius Acuff (25 field-goal attempts) and De'Andre Hunter (18), but Sabonis still contributed offensively with a team-high eight assists. It was Sabonis' fourth double-double of the season, and he was two dimes shy from his second triple-double of the 2026-27 campaign. His 15.8 rebounds per game leads the NBA, and he is also averaging 16.0 points, 7.3 assists and 1.0 steals over what is currently a career-high 37.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sabonis finished with nine points (4-7 FG, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and a block across 40 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Sabonis has been absolutely dominant on the glass in the early stages of the season, grabbing at least 14 boards in each game and comfortably leading the NBA in that category at 16.2 per game. The other areas of his game weren't as dominant, however, as he attempted just seven shots while committing seven turnovers. Sabonis' rebounding and playmaking helped offset the single-digit scoring total, though the turnovers were costly for Sacramento. The star big man remains a strong fantasy contributor through his elite rebounding and passing, but his scoring volume can become a concern after back-to-back games with nine points.

items.headline: Sabonis supplied 20 points (10-16 FG), 14 rebounds and eight assists across 37 minutes in Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Sabonis turned in an efficient shooting performance Tuesday, reaching the 20-point mark for the second time in four regular-season games while finishing as Sacramento's third-leading scorer. The big man also paced all players in rebounds and assists, dishing out at least eight dimes for the third time this season. He's racked up three double-doubles and a triple-double thus far.

items.headline: Sabonis finished with 15 points (6-8 FG, 3-4 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists and two steals across 34 minutes in Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Sabonis followed his triple-double against Portland on Friday with another dominant rebounding performance, collecting at least 15 boards for a third straight game, and he easily leads the league out of the gate in rebounding at 17.3 per game. Sabonis remains a reliable source of rebounds and efficient scoring while also consistently filling the stat sheet. Through three games, he has two double-doubles and one triple-double while shooting an impressive -- yet unsustainable -- 80.8 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Sabonis totaled 27 points (10-13 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 19 rebounds, 10 assists and five turnovers across 39 minutes in Friday's 128-120 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Sabonis has been a monster through the first two games of the season, amassing 41 points, 37 rebounds and 18 assists while shooting 83.3 percent from the field and 90.9 percent at the stripe. After playing a career-low 19 games last season, Sabonis looks primed for a massive bounce-back year. Congrats if you snagged him with a top-30 selection on draft day.

items.headline: Sabonis had 14 points (5-5 FG, 4-4 FT), 18 rebounds, eight assists and one steal over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: The veteran big fell just short of a triple-double in the season opener, but he was one of only four Kings to even score in double digits on the night. Sabonis is likely to have trade rumors circling his head once again as part of a rebuilding roster, but as long as he remains in Sacramento he'll be one of the team's main options and should see more than enough usage to bounce back from a rough 2025-26 that saw him play just 19 regular-season games due to knee trouble.

items.headline: Sabonis tallied 14 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-10 FT), 10 rebounds and one assist over 30 minutes in Friday's 126-97 preseason loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Sabonis notched a double-double despite a dreadful night at the charity stripe. Sabonis has been on a long, bumpy road back to elite form, but getting a full 30-minute run in the preseason finale is an encouraging sign of his readiness after missing most of last season with a knee injury.

items.headline: Sabonis (undisclosed) is available for Friday's preseason finale against the Spurs, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Sabonis is back for the preseason finale after a three-game absence. He'll likely start Friday, which should push Precious Achiuwa back to the second unit.

items.headline: Sabonis (undisclosed) will not play in Tuesday's preseason matchup against Portland, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Sabonis joins several Sacramento regulars on the sidelines Tuesday, though no reason for his absence was provided. With both Sabonis and Maxime Raynaud (knee) unavailable, the Kings will need to rely on other frontcourt options against the Trail Blazers. Sabonis' next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against San Antonio.

items.headline: Sabonis (undisclosed) was a full participant during Monday's practice but remains questionable for Tuesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Sabonis has missed two straight games for undisclosed reasons, but it sounds like it's a minor issue. If the veteran big man doesn't suit up Tuesday, his final chance to play during the preseason will come Friday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Sabonis (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: This will be Sabonis' second straight missed preseason game, and the Kings have not yet listed an injury for him. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against Portland. Maxime Raynaud and Precious Achiuwa should see a boost with Sabonis unavailable.

items.headline: Sabonis (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason matchup with the Lakers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: After supplying four points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 10 minutes during Monday's preseason-opening loss to the Lakers, Sabonis will be held out of Thursday's contest for undisclosed reasons. The big man's next opportunity to suit up in the preseason will come Saturday against Golden State.

items.headline: Sabonis finished with four points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 10 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sabonis saw a light workload in Sacramento's preseason opener, playing exclusively during the first half. The veteran center hit his head in the opening minutes but showed no ill effects, though he committed five fouls in limited action. Sabonis remains one of the NBA's premier rebounders and distributors at his position after averaging a double-double during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Sabonis downplayed offseason trade rumors, per Sam Amico of HoopsWire.com.
items.story: Sabonis isn't an unrestricted free agent until the 2028-29 campaign, so the rebuilding Kings may not pull the trigger on a potential deal until the star big man builds his stock back up. He averaged 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game last year, all his lowest marks since 2018-19, before undergoing season-ending knee surgery in February.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) remains a trade candidate heading into the 2026-27 regular season, per Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento.
items.story: After sitting out for Lithuania during the FIBA World Cup qualifiers, Sabonis is ready for the start of Sacramento's training camp. The Kings could be preparing for a full-fledged rebuild after waiving veteran DeMar DeRozan over the summer, leaving Sabonis as a prime trade candidate. The star big man's market value isn't at its highest after he averaged 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game, all his lowest marks since 2018-19, before undergoing season-ending knee surgery in February. However, he's primed for as much usage as he can handle as long as he's with the Kings.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) did not participate in Lithuania's latest FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he turned his attention toward preparing for the 2026-27 NBA season.
items.story: Sabonis was limited to just 19 regular-season appearances for Sacramento last season due to injuries but remained productive when available, averaging 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 assists while shooting 54.3 percent from the field. The 30-year-old remains a major part of the Kings' frontcourt entering 2026-27 and should continue providing strong production in rebounds, assists and field-goal percentage.

items.headline: Sabonis (knee) has a new pick-and-roll partner after the Kings chose Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: With Russell Westbrook, an unrestricted free agent this offseason, seizing Sacramento's top spot at point guard a year ago, Sabonis saw a decrease in both usage and efficiency. The star big man averaged 15.8 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 29.7 minutes per tilt, all his lowest marks since 2018-19, before undergoing season-ending knee surgery. Sacramento appears ready to go in a different direction at the point, which could work to Sabonis' benefit in 2026-27.

items.headline: White amassed 14 points (6-21 FG, 2-12 3Pt), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: White endured an especially difficult shooting performance, converting just two of his 12 three-point attempts despite finishing with Boston's second-highest point total. His five assists helped soften the impact, but the absence of blocks and limited defensive production made this a disappointing outing for fantasy managers. White's ability to contribute across multiple categories remains valuable, although his efficiency was a significant drawback Sunday.

items.headline: White (shoulder) is not listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: White will return from a one-game absence due to a left AC joint sprain in his shoulder. Payton Pritchard and Hugo Gonzalez will return to the bench with White back in action.

items.headline: White (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: White drew the questionable tag for Saturday's game due to left AC joint sprain in his shoulder. The veteran guard will be in street clothes for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, but he could make his return Sunday against the Warriors. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also out, Payton Pritchard and Paul George will carry the workload for the Celtics, and there will be more opportunities for the likes of Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

items.headline: White (shoulder) is questionable to play in Saturday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: White is dealing with a left AC joint contusion, and the ailment could force him to miss his first outing of the season. Across 15 games in 2026-27, White is averaging 12.7 points, 3.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 1.1 steals, 0.7 blocks and 1.7 three-pointers in 29.9 minutes. If he's unable to play, Payton Pritchard may join the starting lineup, while Hugo Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman should see a bump in minutes off the bench.

items.headline: White had 12 points (5-16 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and one block over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 105-101 loss to Denver.
items.story: White recorded a season-high eight assists without committing a turnover, but his perimeter struggles continued. He's averaged 12.2 points, 4.4 assists and 1.8 triples over his last five games, shooting just 38.3 percent from the field. His playmaking and defensive versatility help offset inconsistent scoring in category leagues.

items.headline: White closed Sunday's 131-94 victory over Dallas with 16 points (6-11 FG, 4-9 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and two steals in 23 minutes.
items.story: White helped Boston establish early control, and the Celtics' enormous advantage let their starters rest for much of the second half. His 23 minutes reflected the one-sided score more than a change in his responsibilities, so fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about his reduced playing time, as he's logged fewer than 30 minutes in four of his last five appearances amid a dominant stretch for Boston. White continues to provide valuable three-point shooting and defensive production from the guard position, and Boston's six-game winning streak has given him plenty of opportunities to contribute without needing to carry the offense. White has also been trending in the right direction as a scorer, going 7-for-16 from deep in his last two games after a cold 8-for-27 stretch over five games between Nov. 2 and Nov. 10.

items.headline: White posted 19 points (7-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven assists, one rebound, four blocks and one steal over 38 minutes during the Celtics' 98-93 win over the Raptors on Wednesday.
items.story: White and the rest of the Celtics role players were tasked with larger workloads on the second game of a back-to-back set due to the absence of Paul George (illness). White answered the call by leading the Celtics with a season-high four blocks and finished second on the team in both points and assists behind Jayson Tatum (24 points and eight assists). It was a nice bounce-back performance from White after he put up only five points against the 76ers on Tuesday. The veteran guard is averaging 13.4 points, 4.9 assists, 2.4 rebounds, 1.9 threes, 1.1 blocks and 1.1 steals over 30.3 minutes per game in November.

items.headline: White posted 18 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and a steal across 25 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
items.story: White delivered an efficient performance despite limited playing time, connecting on a season-high four three-pointers and dishing out at least five assists for a second consecutive outing. His 25-minute cameo was his second-shortest outing of the season, but it came because of Boston's commanding advantage, so fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much. Despite the reduced workload, White maintained strong fantasy production, and his combination of perimeter shooting, playmaking and defensive contributions continues to provide a reliable foundation.

items.headline: White notched 24 points (7-18 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 9-9 FT), four rebounds, seven assists, a steal and two blocks across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks.
items.story: White overcame a difficult perimeter shooting performance by converting all nine free-throw attempts while adding seven assists and three combined defensive stats. His 35-minute workload and substantial offensive involvement were encouraging, particularly after a relatively quiet outing against Houston in his previous game. White's combination of playmaking, defensive production and scoring opportunities continues to support a dependable fantasy ceiling, and he should remain one of Boston's go-to players on offense, although a step or two below the likes of Jayson Tatum and Paul George.

items.headline: White registered 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two steals across 34 minutes in Sunday's 108-97 win over the Magic.
items.story: White has been underwhelming to start the season, and fantasy managers likely expected better numbers from the veteran combo guard. While White continues to see steady playing time above 30 minutes, reaching that mark in four of his six appearances, he has scored 15-plus points just twice. White's defensive activity and three-point shooting provide a useful foundation, but his scoring numbers are down compared to recent years. He's averaging just 11.8 points per game, and that would be his lowest mark since joining the Celtics in the 2021-22 season.

items.headline: White finished with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Friday's 125-111 win over the Bulls.
items.story: It was the second time in three games that White failed to score in double digits while attempting less than 10 field goals, but he did contribute defensively with two steals. White's production is streaky, and even with Jaylen Brown (knee) now in Philadelphia, the former is still serving in a complementary role to Jayson Tatum and Paul George, and even Payton Pritchard off the bench.

items.headline: White contributed 16 points (5-15 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds and seven assists across 33 minutes in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime win over the Nets.
items.story: White struggled from deep, making just one of seven three-point attempts, but his seven assists helped offset the inefficient scoring. His role as one of Boston's most important players is pretty much set in stone, but he needs to be more efficient with his outside shot to reach his fantasy ceiling. Through four games this season, White is averaging just 12.5 points per game while shooting 31.8 percent from deep, so there's definitely room for improvement.

items.headline: White (hip) is available for Tuesday's game against the Nets, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: As expected, the star guard is shedding a probable designation that was caused by a right hip issue. Although it's the second half of a back-to-back, White should be able to handle a normal workload as long as Tuesday's contest remains competitive.

items.headline: White (right hip) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: White is a little banged up from Monday's game against the Bulls in which he turned the ball over six times in 18 minutes. However, the veteran guard intends to play through the issue for the second leg of this back-to-back set.

items.headline: White chipped in five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals over 18 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over the Bulls.
items.story: White endured a quiet offensive outing, attempting just four shots while committing six turnovers. However, the veteran guard salvaged some fantasy value with three steals and a block despite playing only 18 minutes in the blowout. White's limited playing time was largely a product of the lopsided score, and he should remain a reliable contributor across multiple categories moving forward.

items.headline: White produced 17 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: White finished second on the Celtics in assists behind Jayson Tatum's 11 while knocking down three triples in an efficient shooting performance. The veteran guard committed four turnovers, but his substantial playing time and involvement as a secondary playmaker provide a solid foundation for his fantasy value alongside Tatum and Paul George.

items.headline: White (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's game against Detroit.
items.story: White didn't suit up for Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over the 76ers to rest but is expected to play versus the Pistons. The 32-year-old averaged a career-best 16.5 points along with 4.4 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.1 steals over 34.1 minutes in 77 regular-season games in 2025-26. White did have some trouble finding the net, especially from deep, though he reportedly worked on his shot during the offseason.

items.headline: White will not play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Most of Boston's regulars are getting the night off. White is expected to be in action for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Pistons.

items.headline: White played 20 minutes in Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over the Hornets, scoring 17 points (6-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and adding four steals, three rebounds and two assists.
items.story: Making his second appearance of the preseason, the veteran point guard finished second to Jayson Tatum in scoring for Boston while leading a defense that snatched 16 steals. White will be looking to improve his efficiency in 2026-27 after shooting a career-worst 39.4 percent from the field last season, along with a 32.7 percent mark from three-point range that was a steep decline from the prior three campaigns.

items.headline: White posted 15 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Saturday's 144-106 preseason win over the 76ers.
items.story: White finished behind Jayson Tatum, Payton Pritchard and Hugo Gonzalez in scoring. However, despite the 32-year-old's scoring contributions, he shot just 20.0 percent from deep, which isn't an encouraging sign after he shot a career-low 27.3 percent from downtown during the 2026 postseason. With Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia, White could see more offensive opportunities than ever in 2026-27, and since he worked on his shot during the offseason, his three-point issues might be behind him.

items.headline: White (rest) is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: White and other prominent Celtics players like Jayson Tatum (rest) and Paul George (rest) will be on the floor for Saturday's exhibition contest. It'll be White's first preseason game as he gears up for Boston's regular-season opener against Detroit on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

items.headline: White (rest) isn't in line to play Thursday against Cleveland, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: The Celtics appear to be resting their starters for this exhibition. Mike Conley is starting at point guard Thursday.

items.headline: White could see a slight uptick in offensive responsibility following Boston's acquisition of Paul George in exchange for Jaylen Brown and other assets, John Schuhmann of NBA.com reports.
items.story: George's ability to space the floor and operate off the ball should fit well alongside White. However, Brown's departure leaves significant shot-creation opportunities that White may be asked to fill. His versatile stat profile already gives him a high fantasy floor, and a modest increase in usage would further boost his value.

items.headline: White recorded 26 points (9-26 FG, 5-16 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists and three blocks in 45 minutes during Saturday's 109-100 loss to Philadelphia in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: White had easily his most productive game of the postseason, albeit in a losing effort. Despite continuing to struggle with his shot, he scored at least 20 points for the first time in the playoffs and for the first time since mid-March. Saturday's Game 7 loss brings down the curtain on a disappointing end to the season for the Celtics, who had a 3-1 series lead. Across 77 regular-season appearances, White averaged 16.5 points, 5.4 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 2.4 combined steals-plus-blocks in 34.1 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: White racked up six points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and three assists over 36 minutes during Tuesday's 113-97 loss to the 76ers in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: White continued what has been a rough playoff series, scoring just six points for the second straight game. While the Celtics still hold a 3-2 series lead, White's struggles couldn't have come at a worse time. He is averaging 8.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.4 three-pointers and 2.0 combined steals and blocks through five playoff games.

items.headline: White accumulated six points (2-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 33 minutes during Sunday's 128-96 victory over Philadelphia in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: White had a very low usage rate in this contest, but he was everywhere on the defensive end. The Celtics hold a commanding 3-1 series lead, and that's without White at his best. He's averaging 8.8 points on 30.8 percent shooting thus far over four playoff games.

items.headline: White contributed eight points (3-12 FG, 2-10 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 39 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the 76ers in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: White's lack of offensive precision continues to be an issue, as he scored no more than 12 points for the 10th time in his past 11 games. Despite putting up top-30 fantasy numbers this season, efficiency has been a major talking point. Through 79 total appearances, he has shot just 39.3 percent from the field, easily his worst fantasy category.

items.headline: White (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's Game 1 against the 76ers.
items.story: White was held out of Boston's regular-season finale due to a right knee contusion but will return for the start of the playoffs. The veteran guard averaged 10.6 points, 4.0 assists and 3.8 rebounds in 33.0 minutes per contest over his final 10 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: White (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Orlando, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: White isn't available for Sunday's contest, as expected. With Jaylen Brown (Achilles) also ruled out and  Payton Pritchard (foot) listed as doubtful, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Dalano Banton should see a big uptick in minutes in the backcourt, with a spot start likely for two of them.

items.headline: White (knee) is available for Friday's game against the Pelicans, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: As expected, White will shed his probable tag due to a right knee contusion and suit up in both halves of this back-to-back set. The veteran guard has been less involved on the offensive end of late, averaging 10.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 0.6 steals over the last five games. However, he has still been efficient over that stretch, during which he has shot 51.4 percent from the field and 45.8 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: White (knee) is probable for Friday's game against the Pelicans, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: White is expected to play through his knee issue for the second leg of this back-to-back set. With Jayson Tatum resting against New Orleans, White may see a bump in usage.

items.headline: Bridges notched 14 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 11 rebounds, five assists and three steals across 35 minutes during Monday's 123-119 overtime win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Bridges has averaged 15.0 points, 8.7 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.7 steals in 29.7 minutes over his last three appearances. His improved rebounding and versatile production have strengthened his fantasy value despite modest scoring.

items.headline: Bridges closed with 18 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 25 minutes during Friday's 111-101 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Bridges was efficient again and came close to a double-double.  The forward has quietly been one of Phoenix's most consistent players, averaging 14.6 points and 6.9 rebounds.

items.headline: Bridges produced 13 points (6-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 win over the Kings.
items.story: Bridges has played 29 minutes in consecutive games after averaging just 22.3 minutes over his previous three appearances. His five assists Wednesday matched his highest total since Nov. 7, while his defensive contributions strengthened an otherwise modest scoring line. Phoenix's balanced offense continues to limit his scoring ceiling.

items.headline: Bridges registered 16 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block across 29 minutes in Monday's 117-105 victory over Denver.
items.story: Bridges delivered a balanced performance without needing a particularly large offensive workload, as Phoenix had seven players score in double figures. His eight rebounds were especially useful, and the contributions in steals and blocks reinforced the versatility that has long been part of his fantasy appeal. He is sharing offensive opportunities with Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green, making Bridges' scoring dependent on the flow of each game. His defensive contributions help compensate when his shot volume is modest, though. This was also the first time that he surpassed the 15-point threshold since Nov. 5, snapping a run of five appearances with 14 or fewer points.

items.headline: Bridges produced seven points (3-9 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and two blocks across 26 minutes during Monday's 122-96 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Bridges' run of solid production came to a screeching halt as he scored a season-low seven points during this blowout. This game was over early, meaning the starters were limited during the second half. Poor performance aside, Bridges has had a strong start to his career in Phoenix. Through nine games, he has put up second-round value, averaging 15.8 points, 7.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.9 three-pointers in 31.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bridges amassed 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and two steals across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The former Hornet has quickly gotten comfortable in a Suns jersey. Bridges has scored at least 16 points in five straight games, averaging 19.2 points, 7.6 boards, 3.4 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.8 steals, draining multiple threes in each of those contests and shooting 38.2 percent from long distance.

items.headline: Bridges had 21 points (7-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and four steals over 35 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Bridges delivered one of his strongest all-around performances of the young season, finishing second on Phoenix in scoring while leading the team with four steals. He also connected on three triples and committed just one turnover, providing valuable production across multiple fantasy categories. Bridges continues to handle a substantial workload in the Suns' starting lineup.

items.headline: Bridges chipped in 24 points (10-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal in 37 minutes during Friday's 127-120 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Bridges led Phoenix in scoring and posted a double-double while adding three blocks. The forward has quickly become a key part of the Suns' frontcourt in his first season in Phoenix, and his production was even more important after Dillon Brooks was ejected in the third quarter. He'll try to help Phoenix bounce back Monday at Golden State.

items.headline: Bridges registered 17 points (7-17 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Bridges appears to be settling in nicely with his new team in Phoenix. The forward has watched his production across the board increase in each of his first three games, and Bridges hasn't looked to be hampered at all by a preseason ankle injury.

items.headline: Bridges amassed eight points (3-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: It was a quiet team debut for Bridges, who more or less went down with the ship Wednesday. The 28-year-old forward is expected to play a big role as one of Phoenix's secondary scoring options behind Devin Booker, and better days are ahead for Bridges.

items.headline: Bridges (ankle) will play in Friday's preseason game against the Jazz, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges will return to the lineup in Friday's preseason finale after missing two games with an ankle injury. The 28-year-old forward is gearing up for his first regular season with the Suns after averaging 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game across 77 regular-season starts with Charlotte in 2025-26.

items.headline: Bridges (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Spurs, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Bridges and the other veterans on the roster will sit this one out. His final opportunity to get on the floor before the start of the regular season will come Friday versus the Jazz.

items.headline: Bridges isn't expected to play Wednesday against the Spurs after missing Phoenix's full morning shootaround, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges appears headed for a night off alongside several other Suns regulars. Phoenix has one exhibition game remaining Friday against Utah, giving the forward another chance to get minutes before the regular season.

items.headline: Bridges (ankle) won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Spurs, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: While Bridges won't play Saturday, he was able to practice Friday, so he's trending in the right direction. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday in a preseason rematch with the Spurs.

items.headline: Head coach Jordan Ott said Friday that Bridges' (ankle) X-rays came back negative, and he participated in Friday's practice, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges exited Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls with a right ankle injury and did not return, though this news bodes well for his status ahead of the regular season. Ott added that the team will "be smart" with Bridges moving forward, so it wouldn't be surprising if he missed time during the preseason. The 28-year-old forward can be considered questionable for Saturday's exhibition against San Antonio until the Suns provide an update.

items.headline: Bridges exited Wednesday's 124-117 preseason loss to the Bulls with a right ankle injury and did not return, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges got tangled up fighting for a loose ball and tweaked his ankle, and while he initially tried to play through it, he retreated to the locker room a few possessions later. According to Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic, head coach Jordan Ott said after the game that he believes Bridges is "fine" and thinks there's a chance he could play in Saturday's exhibition against the Spurs.

items.headline: Bridges finished with eight points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 14 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Bridges started at power forward and scored Phoenix's first seven points before sitting out the second half with the rest of the starters. His ability to contribute as a scorer, rebounder and secondary playmaker should give him a significant role in Phoenix's revamped rotation.

items.headline: The Hornets traded Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Suns on Sunday in exchange for Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bridges should continue to start in Phoenix, but his usage will likely dip, as he'll be competing for touches with the likes of Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks. Bridges supplied averages of 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 triples per game this past season with the Hornets, but his offensive role might shrink some with the Suns.

items.headline: Bridges could take on additional offensive responsibilities after Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball, according to Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports.
items.story: The veteran forward remains one of the Hornets' most experienced scorers and playmakers, which may increase his importance as the team integrates younger players into larger roles. The addition of Naz Reid could push Bridges to small forward at times, and his long-term future could still depend on whether Charlotte pursues additional roster changes this offseason. Plus, he may lose out on some easy lobs that Ball was known for generating.

items.headline: Bridges ended Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic with 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 28 minutes.
items.story: Bridges propelled the Hornets to a 127-126 overtime victory over the Heat in Tuesday's Play-In Game, when he logged 28 points, nine rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 43 minutes, though he was unable to replicate that production in Friday's elimination loss. Bridges was productive to open the 2025-26 season, but his numbers dipped significantly following the All-Star break. Over his final 24 regular-season outings from Feb. 24 to April 12, he averaged 14.6 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.5 threes and 0.8 steals over 28.3 minutes per game. Part of that dip had to do with Bridges taking a back seat to the likes of LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller. Bridges is slated to earn $22.8 million in 2026-27, which is the final year he is under contract with Charlotte.

items.headline: Bridges finished with seven points (3-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and two assists over 24 minutes during Sunday's 110-96 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Bridges was mostly a non-factor in the win, limited to single digits for the first time in his past 10 games. Charlotte will host Miami in the first round of the Play-In Tournament, with the winner moving on to face the winner of Orlando and Philadelphia.

items.headline: Bridges posted 25 points (10-12 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and seven assists across 34 minutes during Sunday's 122-108 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Bridges and LaMelo Ball combined for 60 points in the win as the Hornets improved to 43-36 on the season. Bridges has been hot over his last eight games with 17.4 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 28.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bridges totaled 19 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and four steals across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Bridges posted a strong all-around line after failing to tally either a block or steal in four consecutive games. He shot the basketball with efficiency on the offensive end and set a new season high in steals. Bridges is averaging 15.3 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals over his last four appearances.

items.headline: Bridges notched 14 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and two assists over 29 minutes during Sunday's 114-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Bridges was Charlotte's leading scorer through the first half of action, but the Celtics held him to just four points over the second half. The 27-year-old forward has struggled to make much of an impact over the past four games, posting modest averages of 12.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists per contest.

items.headline: Bridges produced nine points (4-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds and four assists across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 134-90 win over the Kings.
items.story: This was a tame effort by Bridges' standards, with the Hornets utilizing a balanced attack Tuesday in the blowout win. Brandon Miller led all starters in minutes played (27), so Bridges' fantasy managers can write this off as an outlier.

items.headline: Hauser will start in Saturday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) won't play, so Hauser will get the start Saturday night. In Hauser's only start of the 2026-27 campaign, which was in the 109-102 win over Milwaukee on Nov. 4, he finished with 11 points and two rebounds across 30 minutes.

items.headline: Hauser contributed 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), one rebound and two assists in 25 minutes during Monday's 115-105 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Hauser connected on four three-pointers, matching his season-high with 12 points. It's been a relatively underwhelming season thus far for Hauser, serving as nothing more than a potential streaming option for anyone needing a boost in perimeter scoring. He has played more than 25 minutes only once in 14 games, an indication that nothing is likely to change, barring injuries to other players.

items.headline: Hauser ended Tuesday's 123-101 victory over Philadelphia with 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), five rebounds and two assists across 18 minutes.
items.story: The 12 points were a season-high output for Hauser, and this was the fifth time this season he's notched double-digit points. The 18-minute workload restricted his overall fantasy ceiling, but Hauser remains a specialist in three-point shooting, so he's better suited to be a waiver-wire pickup in category-based leagues rather than in standard formats.

items.headline: Hauser isn't starting Friday's game against Charlotte, per Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston.
items.story: Hauser is coming off the bench after making a spot start his last time out versus the Bucks. He'll be splitting the reserve wing minutes with Baylor Scheierman and Hugo Gonzalez on Friday.

items.headline: Hauser finished with 11 points (4-11 FG, 3-10 3Pt) and two rebounds across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Hauser continued operating primarily as a perimeter specialist, attempting 10 three-pointers while contributing little outside scoring. His 30-minute workload was encouraging, but the absence of assists and defensive stats will continue to limit his fantasy impact. Hauser remains useful for managers seeking three-point production, but he doesn't bring much more to the table.

items.headline: Hauser will start Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum (rest) sidelined, Hauser will get the starting nod for the first time this season. He's averaging 7.1 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 20.0 minutes per game over seven regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Hauser totaled two points (1-6 FG, 0-5 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 109-93 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Hauser failed to connect on any of his five three-point attempts as Boston struggled from long range, shooting just 28.6 percent as a team. The sharpshooter has a narrow fantasy profile built primarily around perimeter scoring, making outings like Monday's particularly damaging to his value.

items.headline: Hauser finished with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 20 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Hauser connected on three triples for the second time in three games to begin the season, providing efficient perimeter scoring off Boston's bench. However, he offered limited production outside of points and rebounds. His value remains concentrated in three-point shooting, making him more appealing in deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Hauser chipped in 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Hauser provided efficient perimeter scoring off Boston's bench, knocking down three of his five attempts from beyond the arc without committing a turnover. He finished with a plus-five rating despite the loss, though his 18-minute workload suggests his fantasy contributions will depend heavily on three-point shooting rather than consistent opportunities in other categories.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Hauser didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia, though that was the case with most of the team's core performers. The 28-year-old averaged 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists, all career highs, in 78 regular-season games, including 49 starts, during the 2025-26 campaign. Hauser could be in line for an even better season, especially if Paul George, Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Payton Pritchard miss time.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is not suiting up for Friday's preseason game against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Hauser and other prominent Celtics players, like Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Derrick White, will rest for Friday's preseason finale. The Celtics will open their regular season Tuesday against the Pistons, and Hauser is once again expected to operate in a rotational role off the bench, though he'll be competing against the likes of Jordan Walsh, Baylor Scheierman (rest), Hugo Gonzalez and Ron Harper for playing time.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is available for Saturday's preseason contest against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Hauser didn't play in the preseason win over the Cavaliers on Thursday, but he'll be able to log minutes off the bench in this contest. Hauser has a strong grip on a rotation spot, and a good showing in the preseason could boost his chances to earn consistent playing time once the regular season starts. He's projected to open the campaign as the backup small forward behind Paul George.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is out for Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics are resting several players ahead of this preseason game, and that includes Hauser, who's expected to have a sizable role in the rotation this season. His next chance to play will come against the 76ers on Saturday.

items.headline: Hauser's role could become more secure following Boston's offseason shakeup with the team swapping Jaylen Brown for Paul George and other assets, John Schuhmann of NBA.com reports.
items.story: While George is expected to absorb most of Brown's minutes, George's recent durability concerns may create additional opportunities for Hauser on the wing throughout the season. Hauser should continue to provide elite three-point shooting, with his fantasy value receiving a boost whenever George requires maintenance days or misses time.

items.headline: Hauser closed Saturday's 109-100 loss to the 76ers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist over 30 minutes.
items.story: The Celtics inexplicably brought Neemias Queta and Hauser off the bench in favor of Ron Harper and Luka Garza, but the experiment did not last long with Harper and Garza combining for 13 total minutes. Hauser closed the 2025-26 regular season with 78 appearances and averages of 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 three-pointers in 24.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser won't start Saturday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics will shake up their starting five in this do-or-die matchup, with Neemias Queta and Hauser both heading to the bench. The sharpshooter has scored six or fewer points in four of the last five games, shooting 34.6 percent from deep during that span.

items.headline: Hauser notched six points (2-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 22 minutes during Sunday's 128-96 win over the 76ers in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hauser continues to play a relatively modest role in this series. Through four games, he's shooting 38.5 percent from the field with averages of 7.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 23.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is not on the Celtics' injury report for Game 1 against the 76ers on Sunday.
items.story: Hauser managed a lingering back injury during the regular season and was sidelined for the Celtics' regular-season finale against the Magic on April 12, but the fifth-year sharpshooter will be available for Game 1 on Sunday. Hauser finished the 2025-26 regular season averaging 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 threes over 24.8 minutes per game, starting in 49 of 78 games.

items.headline: Hauser (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: As expected, Hauser will join several other Celtics players on the sidelines for Sunday's regular-season finale, but he should be available for the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs. He'll end the 2025-26 regular season averaging 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 threes over 24.8 minutes per game across 78 outings (49 starts). Hauser connected on 39.3 percent of his three-point attempts, which is the first time in his five-year NBA career that he did not shoot above the 40.0 percent mark. Boston will lean more heavily on Dalano Banton, Max Shulga, Jordan Walsh, Baylor Scheierman and Ron Harper against Orlando.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Magic, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: With the Celtics set to rest a lot of their regular rotation guys for Sunday's regular-season finale, there will be plenty of minutes and shots available for Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh. Check back for official confirmation on Hauser's status closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Hauser posted 24 points (8-13 FG, 8-12 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 28 minutes during Friday's 144-118 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Hauser stepped up in the absence of Jayson Tatum (Achilles), scoring a team-high 24 points. The sharpshooter is scorching the nets from deep ahead of the postseason, shooting 52.6 percent from deep in his last six games while averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 3.3 three-pointers per contest.

items.headline: Hauser (back) has been cleared to play in Friday's game against the Pelicans, per Jay King of The Athletic.
items.story: As expected, Hauser will push through his probable tag and suit up for the second leg of a back-to-back set despite lingering low-back spasms. With Jayson Tatum getting the night off to rest, Hauser could be in line for a slight uptick in usage and shot attempts.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is probable for Friday's game against the Pelicans, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum resting and Jaylen Brown (Achilles) considered questionable, Hauser could see a bump in touches against the Pelicans, making him worth a stream for managers in need of three-pointers. He's appeared in 27 straight games, averaging 9.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 26.0 minutes during that stretch.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is available for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: Hauser has appeared in 26 straight games (25 starts), and he could see increased usage Thursday due to Jaylen Brown (Achilles) being out. Derrick White (knee) and Neemias Queta (toe) are also questionable. Hauser is a candidate to rest Friday against the Pelicans, especially if he sees a major workload against New York.

items.headline: Hauser is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks due to low back spasms.
items.story: Hauser has been a key member of the Celtics' starting lineup because of his three-point shooting and floor spacing, so not having him would be a significant blow for Boston. Still, the questionable tag suggests a decision won't be made yet, and a final call on his status could be made closer to Wednesday's tipoff at 7:30 p.m. ET. If Hauser ends up being ruled out, Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman could see increased burn.

items.headline: Hauser ended Wednesday's 147-129 victory over the Heat with 23 points (9-11 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal over 29 minutes.
items.story: Hauser moved back into the starting lineup Wednesday and responded with one of his best games of the campaign. This was his third game with at least 23 points and his 11th game with at least five triples. This has the look of an outlier for fantasy hoops, however, as he's averaging 9.1 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.5 three-pointers across 73 appearances this season.

items.headline: Hauser will start Wednesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: After shifting to a bench role for Monday's matchup against the Hawks, Hauser will rejoin the first unit Wednesday. The sharpshooter has been in a slump recently, averaging just 5.4 points while shooting 30.3 percent from deep in his past eight games. Hauser will look to get back on track and provide his usual floor spacing alongside Jayson Tatum against Miami.

items.headline: Hauser isn't starting Monday's game against Atlanta, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics are electing to give Jordan Walsh an opportunity to start Monday, and Hauser will make the corresponding move to the bench. He's averaging 10.4 points and 3.8 rebounds in his last five appearances as a reserve, dating back to a stretch from Dec. 22 to Jan. 1.

items.headline: Hauser closed with nine points (3-9 FG, 3-8 3Pt) and five rebounds across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 119-109 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Hauser remains a streamer strictly for three-pointers in most fantasy leagues, though he's struggling to score at the moment. The sharpshooter has scored in single digits in five consecutive games, failing to knock down a single trey in three of them.

items.headline: Hauser logged two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Monday's 120-112 victory over Phoenix.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum healthy and gobbling up touches in this offense, Hauser's fantasy appeal is going to take a hit. Over his last seven appearances, he's averaging 8.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.4 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser provided 15 points (5-10 FG, 5-10 3Pt) and four rebounds over 24 minutes during Sunday's 109-98 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hauser caught fire from beyond the arc and appears to be a good fit alongside Jayson Tatum due to his floor spacing. Hauser won't have a big usage rate, but he will remain a solid three-point specialist in category formats.

items.headline: Hauser ended Monday's 108-81 victory over Milwaukee with 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 29 minutes.
items.story: Hauser continues to be a steady source of three-pointers in fantasy formats, but his upside is limited elsewhere. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 11.3 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.7 three-pointers in 27.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser closed with 16 points (6-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt), three rebounds and four assists in 29 minutes during Tuesday's 97-81 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Hauser took advantage of some extra touches due to Jaylen Brown being sidelined by a knee issue. Overall this season, Hauser is sitting just inside the top-200 players in standard nine-category formats with averages of 9.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.6 three-pointers in 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser ended Thursday's 121-110 win over Golden State with 16 points (6-10 FG, 4-5 3Pt), three rebounds and five assists over 28 minutes.
items.story: The fifth-year forward put together his best scoring effort since Jan. 23 with an efficient night from long distance. Hauser has drained multiple three-pointers in 17 of 19 appearances since moving into the starting five in early January, averaging 12.3 points, 4.1 boards, 3.3 threes, 1.8 assists and 1.1 combined steals and blocks in 28.3 minutes a game over that stretch.

items.headline: Hauser (back) will play Wednesday against the Bulls, according to Celtics reporter Bobby Manning.
items.story: Hauser will shake off his probable tag for this contest, setting him up to return from a one-game absence. With this news, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh could be less involved for the Celtics.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hauser is on track to return from a one-game absence. If he does get the green light, there will be fewer minutes available for guys like Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

items.headline: Hauser (back) will not play Sunday against the Knicks.
items.story: Hauser was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. With the sharpshooter out of the mix, the Celtics could allot more minutes to Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Hauser is in jeopardy of missing Sunday's contest due to lower-back spasms. If the sharpshooting forward is ultimately ruled out, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Hauser (thumb) is not listed on the injury report for Friday's matchup with the Heat, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: It looks like Hauser will be back in action Friday night following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which should result in fewer minutes for Hugo Gonzalez, Jordan Walsh and Ron Harper. Hauser is averaging 9.2 points and 2.6 triples per game this season.

items.headline: Hauser has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Rockets due to a right thumb strain, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Hauser out and Jaylen Brown (hamstring/knee) doubtful, the Celtics are expected to be shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh will likely see a significant bump in minutes, while Josh Minott may enter the rotation. Hauser's next opportunity to play will come Friday against Miami.

items.headline: Flagg amassed 28 points (8-17 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal across 31 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Flagg delivered the decisive moment for the Mavericks, converting two free throws with 3.7 seconds remaining after Utah erased a substantial fourth-quarter deficit. The second-year forward led the Mavericks in scoring and took an aggressive approach, drawing 10 free-throw attempts and making nine. His expanding offensive responsibilities continue to support his fantasy appeal, and while the five turnovers weren't ideal, fantasy managers can live with them given everything else he brings to the table. Flagg has surpassed the 20-point mark in six of his last nine games, averaging 24.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 2.3 combined steals-plus-blocks per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Flagg chipped in 33 points (11-15 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five rebounds, nine assists and four steals across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: This was Flagg's 10th career game with at least 30 points and five assists, and it was his fourth 30-plus performance of the season. The 19-year-old has gotten off to a hot start with averages of 24.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 6.4 assists, 1.4 triples, 2.0 steals and 0.7 swats per contest on 48.5 percent shooting from the field and 89.5 percent at the line, which has been good enough for top-eight value in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Flagg contributed 17 points (5-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Dallas fell behind 42-9 in the first quarter and never recovered, and the nature of the game conspired against Flagg's chances to make a big impact. The reigning Rookie of the Year has now endured three consecutive losses on the Mavericks' road trip, with Dallas losing those contests by a combined 86 points. His offensive responsibilities remain substantial in his second NBA season, but Sunday's inefficient performance illustrates how difficult it can be to maintain consistent production when the entire team struggles to generate quality looks. The numbers are telling, as Flagg is averaging just 15.7 points per game on 34.8 percent shooting during the current losing skid.

items.headline: Flagg chipped in 12 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and two steals over 27 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Flagg struggled to establish himself offensively, attempting only 12 shots as Dallas fell behind early and didn't recover. His seven rebounds and two steals helped preserve some fantasy value despite the modest scoring output, but fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about one bad game. Flagg has had some inconsistencies, but for the most part, his numbers have been excellent. He has surpassed the 20-point mark in seven of his 11 appearances, averaging 6.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.2 steals per contest.

items.headline: Flagg finished with 43 points (16-25 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-8 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block in 39 minutes during Monday's 125-122 win over Indiana.
items.story: Flagg delivered his best offensive showing of the 2026-27 season so far, beating his previous high of 33 points Oct. 30 against Houston. He also set a season high in rebounds and has now reached double-digit boards three times in 10 matchups. Flagg has now collected four straight double-doubles following Monday's victory.

items.headline: Flagg logged 25 points (8-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 12 assists, five rebounds and a steal in 28 minutes during Sunday's 130-93 win over the Nets.
items.story: Flagg was highly efficient in Sunday's blowout win, racking up 25 points on just 13 field-goal attempts. The second-year pro also impressed with his playmaking, dishing a career-high 12 assists. Flagg has recorded four double-doubles across nine appearances this season, two of which were point-assist double-doubles.

items.headline: Flagg registered 21 points (7-16 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and a block across 33 minutes in Friday's 112-100 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Flagg delivered an outstanding all-around performance, finishing three assists shy of a triple-double while helping Dallas take control in the third quarter. His three steals further enhanced an already impressive fantasy line, demonstrating his ability to contribute across multiple categories. Flagg's substantial playing time and versatile statistical production continue to establish him as a valuable fantasy asset with elite upside across all formats. Over his last five appearances, the second-year forward is averaging 23.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 1.4 steals per contest. He needs to improve on his three-point shooting, though, as he's made just 13 percent of his long-range attempts.

items.headline: Flagg notched 19 points (7-19 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 10 rebounds and five assists in 40 minutes during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: The double-double was the second of the season for Flagg, and his first involving rebounds. The second-year star is taking a step forward from his Rookie of the Year campaign, averaging 24.3 points, 6.3 boards, 6.3 assists, 2.1 steals, 1.0 threes and 0.9 blocks over seven games, and there's still plenty of room for growth in his skills. Flagg is shooting just 21.2 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Flagg ended Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings with 17 points (3-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 11-11 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals in 40 minutes.
items.story: With Kyrie Irving resting Monday, the Kings were able to devote most of their defensive attention to Flagg and hold the second-year superstar in check from the field. Flagg is still off to an excellent start overall, averaging 25.2 points, 6.5 assists and 5.7 rebounds per game so far this season.

items.headline: Flagg finished Friday's 116-111 win over the Rockets with 33 points (13-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 7-10 FT), nine rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block across 39 minutes.
items.story: Although he struggled from three-point range once again, Flagg turned in another productive all-around performance in Dallas' first NBA Cup game of the year. The star forward erupted for a season-high 33 points and was second on the Mavericks in scoring behind Kyrie Irving (35 points). Flagg also finished second on the team in rebounds and assists. He's posted at least 26 points, six assists and five rebounds in three consecutive contests, though he's shot just 20.0 percent from downtown during that span.

items.headline: Flagg finished with 26 points (10-23 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and eight assists across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 120-96 victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Flagg's phenomenal 2026-27 campaign continued Wednesday, with the 2025 No. 1 overall pick scoring over 20 points for the third time this season. He hasn't been consistent shooting the ball, and turnovers have also been somewhat of a concern. However, despite the struggles in those areas, Flagg is still putting up All-Star numbers, and at this rate, his name could be mentioned in MVP conversations throughout the year.

items.headline: Flagg finished Monday's 113-109 win over the Heat with 29 points (12-23 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 11 assists, six rebounds, five steals and two blocks across 40 minutes.
items.story: Flagg returned from a one-game absence due to a left shoulder sprain and stuffed the stat sheet. The star forward tied for the game-high scoring total in an efficient performance from inside the arc and dished out a career-high-tying 11 assists. He also logged a career-best five steals and has supplied at least three swipes in all three of his regular-season appearances thus far.

items.headline: Stewart chipped in 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and four rebounds in 21 minutes during Monday's 117-111 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Stewart continues operating in a limited frontcourt role, averaging 10.6 points and 3.3 rebounds this season. His modest playing time and limited defensive production make him difficult to trust in standard fantasy leagues, particularly with Zach Edey also commanding center minutes.

items.headline: Stewart accumulated eight points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Stewart returned from an illness but remained in a limited reserve role. He's played 20 or fewer minutes in four straight appearances, restricting his rebounding and defensive upside. Without more consistent playing time, his fantasy value remains matchup-dependent.

items.headline: Stewart won't start Thursday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Before missing the Grizzlies' last two games due to an illness, Stewart started his past two appearances while Zach Edey (ankle) was sidelined. Edey is out Thursday, but Taylor Hendricks will enter the first unit instead of Stewart.

items.story: Memphis is likely to check back in with Stewart closer to tipoff. The big man has a golden opportunity Thursday to start if available, with Zach Edey (ankle) already ruled out for the second half of this back-to-back.

items.headline: Stewart (illness) won't play Wednesday against the Cavs.
items.story: This will be Stewart's second straight game on the sidelines, which should lead to more minutes for Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post. Stewart's next chance to play will come Thursday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Stewart is out for Monday's game against the Wizards due to an illness.
items.story: The big man can be considered day-to-day ahead of Wednesday's meeting in Cleveland. A big workload could be in store for Zach Edey (ankle) if he's able to play for the Grizzlies on Monday.

items.headline: Stewart is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards due to an illness.

items.headline: Stewart chipped in 12 points (5-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and four blocks across 20 minutes during Friday's 142-111 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Stewart moved into the starting lineup, replacing Zach Edey (ankle), who was ruled out on the first night of a back-to-back. Stewart managed to block a season-high four shots, salvaging what was otherwise a mediocre performance. Assuming Edey returns for Saturday's game against Brooklyn, expect to see Stewart back on the bench, flirting with minutes in the low-20s.

items.headline: Stewart will start Friday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Stewart is getting a chance in the first unit due to Zach Edey (ankle) sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set. Stewart is set up to be a solid streaming option for this slate.

items.headline: Stewart (knee) is available for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Stewart was in danger of missing his third consecutive contest. However, that won't be the case. With Stewart back in the equation, GG Jackson and Taylor Hendricks will likely see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Stewart (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Nuggets.
items.story: Stewart has played well in his first season in Memphis, averaging a career-high 11.9 points while shooting 57.1 percent from downtown. He has missed the last two games due to a bone bruise in his right knee. If Stewart remains sidelined Wednesday, GG Jackson and Taylor Hendricks are candidates for more minutes.

items.headline: Stewart (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Stewart will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right knee bone bruise, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against Denver. With the big man sidelined, Quinten Post will likely see increased minutes.

items.headline: Stewart (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Stewart suffered a right knee bone bruise in Wednesday's loss to the Pacers and will hit the inactive list Friday. His next opportunity to play will come Monday at Toronto. Quinten Post figures to see increased burn for as long as Stewart is sidelined.

items.headline: Stewart (knee) exited Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers and did not return, finishing with six points (3-4 FG) and one rebound in 10 minutes.
items.story: Stewart was deemed doubtful to return and never checked back in. His next chance to suit up will come Friday against the Thunder. If the big man needs to miss time, Quinten Post would likely see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Stewart is doubtful to return to Wednesday's game against the Pacers due to a right knee injury.
items.story: It looks like Stewart will end his evening with six points (3-4 FG) and one rebound in 10 minutes off the bench. If he needs to miss additional time, Quinten Post would likely pick up most of his minutes, and Taylor Hendricks would have a chance to get into the rotation.

items.headline: Stewart recorded 24 points (8-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT) and four rebounds across 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 victory over Sacramento.
