Stewart has scored in double digits in three of his last four outings, and over that span he has averaged 14.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 0.8 blocks and 1.5 threes over 18.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart ended with 18 points (7-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one block across 16 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 victory over Portland.
items.story: Stewart dropped a season-high 18 points, although a lack of peripheral stats continues to be an issue. Having appeared in four games thus far, he has averaged just 9.8 points, 3.5 rebounds and 0.8 blocks in 17.5 minutes per game. Assuming Zach Edey's playing time continues to ramp up, there isn't much hope for Stewart being anything more than a situational streaming consideration.

items.headline: Stewart won't start Monday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: The big man will play in the second leg of this back-to-back set, though Zach Edey (ankle) will return to action and push Stewart to the bench. Stewart is averaging 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks across 19.5 minutes per contest in two regular-season appearances (one start) on the campaign.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is available for Monday's game at Utah.
items.story: Stewart will shed his questionable tag and suit up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Through two regular-season games (one start), he's averaging 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks across 19.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Jazz due to left ankle injury management.
items.story: Stewart may be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set after posting 13 points, five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and a steal across 22 minutes while starting in the absence of Zach Edey (injury management) during Sunday's win over Sacramento. If Stewart is ultimately ruled out, Quinten Post would likely see increased playing time behind Edey.

items.headline: Stewart accumulated 13 points (4-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Stewart got the start for the resting Zach Edey on Sunday, chipping in a full stat line. Stewart is in line to revert to the bench Monday in Utah.

items.story: Stewart is set to make his regular-season debut for the Grizzlies, and he should help back up Zach Edey and Cameron Boozer. With Stewart active, Quinten Post's minutes could dip.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Stewart wasn't able to go for Wednesday's opener against the Jazz due to an ankle injury suffered during the preseason, but he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Friday's clash. The Grizzlies will likely monitor him closely in shootaround and warmups to determine whether he can suit up Friday night.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Stewart has been battling an ankle injury he sustained in the preseason and won't suit up in Memphis' regular-season opener. His next opportunity to make his regular-season debut with his new club will come Friday at Golden State. In the meantime, Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is doubtful to play Wednesday against the Jazz.
items.story: Stewart is still recovering from an ankle injury he sustained during the preseason Oct. 5, and it looks like he'll miss Memphis' regular-season opener. With Stewart out of the lineup, Quinten Post should be more involved in the rotation.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced Friday that Stewart (ankle) will miss at least two weeks.
items.story: Stewart, who was traded from Detroit to Memphis over the summer, sustained a left ankle sprain in the team's preseason opener and is now likely to miss Opening Night. His absence opens the door for Quinten Post to move into the backup center role behind Zach Edey in the interim.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) didn't practice Friday, per Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site.
items.story: Stewart appears to be doubtful for Friday's preseason game in Chicago. He's recovering from a left ankle injury suffered in Memphis' preseason opener.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) didn't participate in Tuesday's practice and will not play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Magic, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Stewart is still being evaluated after sustaining a left ankle injury in Monday's preseason-opening win over the Hawks. The big man's next opportunity to play in the preseason will come against the Bulls on Friday.

items.headline: Stewart exited Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks in the first quarter and did not return due to a left ankle injury, finishing with one rebound in two minutes.
items.story: Stewart landed on an opposing player's foot and took a hard fall before limping back to the locker room. He was eventually deemed doubtful to return and never checked back in. The big man's next opportunity to play in the preseason will come Wednesday versus Orlando.

items.headline: Stewart is doubtful to return to Monday's preseason game against the Hawks due to a left ankle injury.
items.story: Stewart landed on an opposing player's foot in the opening quarter and limped to the locker room. If he doesn't return, he'll finish with a rebound in only two minutes of action.

items.headline: Stewart (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Monday's preseason game against the Hawks, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Stewart appeared to come down on an opposing player's foot and took a hard fall before limping to the locker room. If he's unable to check back in, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Taylor Hendricks could see increased playing time for the rest of the way.

items.headline: The Pistons traded Stewart to the Grizzlies on Wednesday in exchange for three second-round draft picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Stewart is coming off a strong 2025-26 campaign, especially on the defensive end, as he averaged 10.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 1.1 assists across 22.7 minutes per contest in 58 regular-season games (13 starts). The big man will likely command a significant role in the Memphis frontcourt, though he isn't guaranteed a starting spot and could begin the season operating off the bench behind Zach Edey (ankle/elbow) and Cameron Boozer.

items.headline: Stewart recorded three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 FT) across six minutes during Sunday's 125-94 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Stewart played a very minor role in Detroit's postseason run, averaging just 11.8 minutes per contest. He found more success in the regular season, posting averages of 10.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.6 blocks in 22.7 minutes across 58 appearances.

items.headline: Stewart racked up six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 13 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 win over the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: With Jalen Duren dominating the center minutes for the Pistons, Stewart continues to play a limited role this postseason. Stewart has averaged 4.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.6 blocks in 14.1 minutes per contest across eight games in the 2026 playoffs, shooting 55.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Stewart accumulated no counting stats across eight minutes during Friday's 93-79 victory over Orlando in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart played himself out of the rotation, logging just eight minutes in the first half. Paul Reed took his place in the second half, contributing to the come-from-behind victory. Although Stewart blocked a career-high eight shots in Game 4, it's been a relatively quiet series thus far. Through six games, he has averaged 4.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.2 blocks in 15.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart amassed eight points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and eight blocks across 17 minutes during Monday's 94-88 loss to the Magic in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart was a bright spot for the Pistons with a career-high eight swats in very limited action. With Detroit facing a 3-1 series deficit, Stewart made a strong case to be more involved going forward.

items.headline: Stewart closed with 10 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and two blocks over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 win over the Magic in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart's 16 minutes were eventful, as the big man didn't miss a shot while recording two blocks, though he also committed three turnovers. Turnovers aside, the 24-year-old was far more productive in Game 2 than in Game 1, when he totaled three points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal across 19 minutes. The numbers may fluctuate, but Stewart's role as a physical presence off the bench remains a key part of the Pistons' identity.

items.headline: Stewart supplied three points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal in 19 minutes during Sunday's 112-101 loss to the Magic in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart failed to have any sort of meaningful impact, continuing what has been an underwhelming few games. In fact, in four appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 8.0 points and 1.0 blocks in 15.7 minutes per game. Along with a number of his teammates, Stewart will need to be better should Detroit intend on going deep into the playoffs.

items.headline: Stewart chipped in eight points (3-3 FG, 2-2 FT) and one rebound over 11 minutes during Wednesday's 137-111 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Stewart logged 11 minutes in his return, back in action after missing 13 straight games due to a calf injury. Although he has proven to be a menace on the defensive end, Stewart's role remains limited, serving as the primary backup behind Jalen Duren. As for next season, he will likely be nothing more than a blocks specialist, providing managers with limited value off the waiver wire.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is available for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Stewart will shed his questionable tag and return from a 13-game absence due to a left calf strain. While he may operate under a minutes restriction in his first game back, the big man's return will leave fewer minutes available for Paul Reed.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: A left calf strain has held Stewart out for 13 consecutive contests, but the questionable designation gives him a real chance to return Wednesday. Stewart would likely face a minutes cap if he's upgraded to available, but he would still figure to push Paul Reed for playing time as the backup center behind Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is out for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Stewart was temporarily upgraded from out to doubtful earlier in the day Monday, but the team has now officially listed him as out, which will mark his 13th straight absence while on the mend from a left calf strain. The 24-year-old's next chance to take the court will come Wednesday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game versus Orlando.
items.story: The Pistons are upgrading Stewart from out to doubtful Monday, signaling that he's inching closer to returning from a left calf strain. Paul Reed should remain worth streaming in deep fantasy leagues for at least one more contest.

items.headline: Collins logged 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, one block and one steal in 22 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Collins has scored at least 18 points in two of his last three appearances, making eight three-pointers during that stretch. However, his 24-minute average over his last five games limits his rebounding opportunities and fantasy ceiling despite efficient perimeter shooting.

items.headline: Collins amassed three points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and one assist over 20 minutes during Friday's 105-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Collins struggled to make an offensive impact, attempting just four shots and failing to reach double figures for the second time over his last four appearances. His 20-minute workload was also concerning, especially considering that Paul Reed played 28 minutes off the bench. Collins has traditionally provided value through efficient scoring and rebounding, but his limited involvement Friday offered little for fantasy managers. With Detroit increasingly utilizing smaller lineups and Reed continuing to earn opportunities, Collins' playing time is worth monitoring, particularly if his offensive production doesn't improve. He's averaging 11.6 points per game in November.

items.headline: Collins registered 20 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: With Cade Cunningham (knee) unavailable, Collins saw some more shots falling his way, and he finished as Detroit's leading scorer in the win. This was just the third time this season Collins cracked the 20-point plateau, and he also dished out a couple of dimes after failing to do so in his previous three outings. Collins is providing late-round value on the year with averages of 11.1 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.4 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Collins provided 11 points (3-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, one block and one steal in 23 minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 victory over the Spurs.
items.story: Collins was efficient in limited action, bouncing back from a rough shooting night against the Heat.  With Jalen Duren (hamstring) sidelined, Collins should continue to see steady minutes in Detroit's frontcourt.

items.headline: Collins tallied 24 points (9-13 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 28 minutes during Monday's 122-111 win over Washington.
items.story: Collins recorded his second double-double of the season and hit multiple three-pointers for the third time in 10 outings. He also delivered three defensive stats for the second straight contest, a good sign for fantasy managers after Collins compiled just three steals-plus-blocks over his previous four showings combined.

items.headline: Collins closed Sunday's 121-116 loss to the Lakers with eight points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal in 32 minutes.
items.story: Collins struggled to make an impact offensively despite logging 32 minutes, attempting just seven shots while Detroit's reserves carried much of the scoring load. He salvaged some fantasy value with three combined steals and blocks, but his four rebounds were disappointing given Jalen Duren's absence. Collins' playing time remains encouraging, though his limited offensive involvement capped his production Sunday.

items.headline: Collins racked up four points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 124-91 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Collins scored no more than four points for the fourth straight game, continuing his rough start to the season. Despite seemingly landing in a favorable position this season, Collins has been largely underwhelming. In seven games, he has barely been a top-200 player, averaging 8.4 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.0 blocks and 1.0 three-pointers. At this stage, parting ways with him in standard formats is certainly a viable option.

items.headline: Collins posted four points (2-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and two rebounds across 18 minutes during Wednesday's 97-89 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Collins endured a rough shooting performance, missing all three attempts from beyond the arc while failing to contribute any assists or defensive statistics. The veteran forward also committed four personal fouls, which contributed to his limited playing time. His lack of production is concerning for fantasy managers, particularly if his minutes remain inconsistent.

items.headline: Collins registered 16 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds and two blocks across 34 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Collins followed his 23-point performance against Miami with his first double-double of the season, taking advantage of Jalen Duren's absence (hamstring) to play an expanded frontcourt role. Collins should remain productive, although his rebounding opportunities and minutes could decrease once Duren returns. That said, Collins is entrenched as the starting power forward and has done a good job of filling the void left by Tobias Harris (calf), who departed in the offseason to join the Spurs.

items.headline: Collins delivered 23 points (9-15 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 0-0 FT), seven rebounds and an assist across 29 minutes in Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat.
items.story: In a game where Cade Cunningham was limited to 16 points while Jalen Duren (thigh) and Ausar Thompson (undisclosed) left with injuries, Collins stepped up and led the Pistons in scoring. This was also a nice bounce-back effort for the veteran, as he had been limited to just six points in the season-opening win over the Celtics on Tuesday. Look for Collins to have a prominent offensive role for the Pistons as a shooter and floor stretcher.

items.headline: Collins closed Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics with six points (3-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 25 minutes.
items.story: Collins started for his new team, as expected, but certainly fell short of the mark when it comes to having a sizeable impact. The two combined steals and blocks were nice, but more is going to be expected from him, particularly on the offensive end. Despite the struggles, he remains a clear hold in all formats.

items.headline: Collins logged 12 points (4-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds and one steal over 22 minutes during Friday's 129-125 preseason win over the Raptors.
items.story: Collins co-led the Pistons in rebounds during Friday's preseason finale, and he ended off the first half nicely with eight points in the second quarter. Collins signed a three-year contract with the Pistons on July 1 to replace Tobias Harris, who is in San Antonio. Collins finished the 2025-26 regular season having averaged 13.6 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 0.9 steals over 27.1 minutes per game while connecting on 55.2 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: Collins finished with 11 points (4-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and two steals in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 128-106 preseason victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: The veteran power forward is replacing Tobias Harris (calf), who jumped ship for San Antonio over the summer, in the starting lineup during his debut campaign with the Pistons. items.story: Johnson battled through a tough shooting night, going 2-of-8 from deep, but came one rebound shy of a double-double. With Julian Strawther out until at least Thanksgiving, Johnson is the frontrunner to hold down a starting role at the wing.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is available for Friday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Johnson was deemed likely to play Friday, so it's not surprising to see him suit up after missing the last three games with an ankle sprain. The veteran forward hasn't played since the season-opening loss to the Warriors on Oct. 22, when he had five points in 11 minutes.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is expected to play in Friday's game against the Suns, per John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM.
items.story: Johnson appears to be primed to end a three-game absence with an ankle sprain. Less playing time should be available to Trevon Brazile and Bryce Hopkins on Friday.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: The fact that Johnson has been upgraded to questionable is a sign he's nearing a return, as he was added to the injury report as doubtful ahead of Wednesday's clash before being downgraded to out ahead of tipoff. He hasn't been able to take the floor since suffering a right ankle sprain Oct. 22 against the Thunder.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Johnson will miss his third consecutive game, so his next opportunity to suit up will come Friday in Phoenix. Without Johnson on the floor, Bryce Hopkins is expected to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is doubtful to face the Pelicans on Wednesday.
items.story: Johnson is on track to miss his third straight game Wednesday. Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile will continue to help pick up the slack in Johnson's absence.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Golden State.
items.story: As expected, Johnson will be shut down Monday while battling a right ankle sprain. Bryce Hopkins drew the start in Johnson's place Saturday and could have an opportunity to do so again Monday, though Trevon Brazile could also factor into the mix given a lack of depth at forward.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is doubtful to play Monday against the Warriors.
items.story: Johnson is on track to miss his second straight game Monday, which could result in another start for Bryce Hopkins and additional minutes for Trevon Brazile. With Johnson looking unlikely for Monday, it would be wise to bench him in weekly fantasy formats.

items.headline: Head coach David Aldeman said that Johnson is "day-to-day" due to his sprained right ankle, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
items.story: Johnson won't play Saturday against the Pelicans, but it sounds like the ankle sprain he's dealing with is relatively minor. For now, Johnson should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with the Warriors.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Johnson exited Thursday's season-opening loss to the Thunder with a right ankle sprain and will now be held out of Saturday's contest. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Warriors. DeMar DeRozan, Trevon Brazile and Alpha Diallo (wrist), who is listed as questionable, are candidates for increased playing time in Johnson's stead.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) didn't return to Thursday's game against Oklahoma City. He ended with five points (2-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 11 minutes.
items.story: Johnson was labeled questionable to return Thursday after suffering a right ankle sprain in the first half, but he failed to gain clearance to check back in. Alpha Diallo started the second half as a result and saw more opportunities in Johnson's absence. The 30-year-old Johnson can be considered questionable for Saturday's game against New Orleans until further notice.

items.headline: Johnson is questionable to return to Thursday's game against the Thunder due to a right ankle sprain, Katy Winge of Altitude Sports reports.
items.story: Johnson picked up the injury at some point during the first half. DeMar DeRozan and Alpha Diallo could see more opportunities if Johnson is unable to return.

items.headline: Johnson delivered 15 points (5-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two steals and an assist in 25 minutes during Sunday's 133-128 preseason win over the Bulls.
items.story: The veteran forward was locked in from downtown as the Nuggets' starting five all played at least 23 minutes in preparation for Opening Night. Johnson has never suited up for more than 66 regular-season games in a campaign, as injuries have plagued him since he was the 11th overall pick in the 2019 NBA Draft. However, he's been a valuable secondary scorer when healthy, averaging at least 12.2 points and 2.0 threes and shooting 39.0 percent or better from beyond the arc in each of the last five seasons.

items.headline: Johnson tallied 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt), a rebound and an assist across 15 minutes during Tuesday's 117-106 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Johnson is firmly entrenched as a starter for the Nuggets at the start of the season, despite the addition of veteran DeMar DeRozan, who will compete for time at Johnson's position. Staying on the court has been a consistent problem for Johnson, who has averaged just 56.3 games per season over the past three campaigns, and the organization hopes he can exceed his career-high watermark of 57 games.

items.headline: Johnson looks to be solidified as a starter for Denver in 2026-27 after Peyton Watson was dealt to Cleveland.
items.story: Johnson's debut season with Denver may have been a disappointment, but he still started all 54 of his regular-season appearances. The 12.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 0.7 steals and 2.0 three-pointers per game he averaged were his lowest since his days with the Suns, but Johnson did shoot a career-high 43.0 percent from deep last year and should continue to find plenty of open looks playing alongside Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray.

items.headline: Johnson notched 27 points (8-15 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 6-9 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block over 39 minutes during Thursday's 110-98 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson did everything he could to get Denver over the line, scoring a season-high 27 points, including five triples. While it ultimately wasn't enough, it does remind fantasy managers just what he can do on the basketball court. Strong performance aside, Johnson's season as a whole was serviceable, at best. In 60 appearances (including playoffs), he averaged 12.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.0 three-pointers in 30.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Johnson finished Monday's 125-113 win over Minnesota in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with 18 points (8-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and three steals over 36 minutes.
items.story: Johnson bounced back after tepid single-digit scoring totals in Games 3 and 4 against Minnesota. The trade for Johnson has been a net negative for the Nuggets. Michael Porter's impressive totals this season with the Nets probably generate some buyer's remorse within the organization, but Monday's result was more in line with what was expected from Johnson. Denver has fallen behind in this series due to a lack of production from the supporting cast, and the balanced outcome from Johnson and Spencer Jones produced the desired result.

items.headline: Johnson logged nine points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 27 minutes during Saturday's 112-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson's production has slowed in the first round, averaging only 10.0 points, 1.5 assists, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.8 steals over four games against the Timberwolves. Although Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray are propping up the team with stellar production, the two superstars need more help from the supporting cast. Right now, Johnson isn't holding up his end of the bargain. The Nuggets will face elimination Monday night, and the pressure will be on Johnson, Christian Braun and Aaron Gordon to deliver better results.

items.headline: Johnson produced six points (2-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 24 minutes during Thursday's 113-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson couldn't get anything going on the offensive end, although he was certainly not alone, as Denver was soundly beaten by Minnesota on the road. On the whole, it's been a mediocre season for Johnson, who is averaging just 12.1 points and 2.0 three-pointers in 57 total appearances.

items.headline: Johnson ended with 12 points (5-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt) and one assist across 33 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson logged 33 minutes in Game 1. While he managed to supply 12 points, he didn't contribute much to other statistical categories and struggled from beyond the arc. With a win by the Nuggets to open the series, Johnson will look to turn things around on the offensive end Monday night in Game 2.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is available for Game 1 against Minnesota on Saturday.
items.story: The Nuggets kept Johnson off the court for their final two regular-season games, but they'll have the forward back on the floor for the start of the playoffs. A midseason right knee bone bruise limited Johnson to just 54 appearances in his debut season with Denver, but he did average a solid 12.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.2 three-pointers per contest while shooting 43.1 percent from deep across his final 26 games.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Just like in Friday's win over the Thunder, Johnson will sit out this game due to rest purposes. The veteran forward, who averaged 12.2 points per game while shooting 43.0 percent from deep in 54 regular-season contests, should be ready to roll for the start of the playoffs next week.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Johnson will join fellow starters Christian Braun (ankle), Jamal Murray (shoulder) and Nikola Jokic (wrist) on the bench for Friday's contest. With Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Spencer Jones (hamstring) also ruled out, the Nuggets will turn to Tim Hardaway, Julian Strawther, Bruce Brown, Jalen Pickett and Tyus Jones to alleviate the load.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is questionable for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Johnson, along with Denver's other four starters, is carrying a questionable tag with the team contemplating some maintenance days. Bruce Brown, Tim Hardaway and Julian Strawther could see expanded roles if multiple players sit out for Denver.

items.headline: Johnson closed with 18 points (8-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 136-119 win over Memphis.
items.story: Johnson might have a secondary role in the Nuggets' offensive scheme, but there's no question the sharpshooting forward is making the most of his opportunities of late. He's scored at least 17 points in each of his last four games, and he'll continue to have tons of scoring touches as long as he stays. Over that four-game stretch, Johnson is making 45.5 percent of his threes on 5.5 attempts per contest.

items.headline: Johnson provided 17 points (6-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds and seven assists in 37 minutes during Monday's 137-132 overtime victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Although injuries and inconsistent totals have plagued Johnson's first season with the Nuggets, he's coming alive at the right time. Over the past 10 games, Johnson has remained steady, averaging 14.2 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.2 steals while maintaining a conversion rate of 52.1 percent during the span. Assuming he stays healthy, Johnson will prop up the wing position with fantasy-worthy numbers in the playoffs.

items.headline: Podziemski supplied 18 points (5-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds and two assists in 38 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 win over the Celtics.
items.story: Podziemski led Golden State in scoring and played a substantial role in snapping the team's five-game losing streak in a low-scoring contest where neither team reached 90 points. However, six turnovers and limited playmaking diminished an otherwise useful fantasy line. The heavy workload is encouraging, but his production remains stronger when he supplements perimeter scoring with his playmaking numbers. He should continue to see an expanded role on offense as long as Stephen Curry (abdomen) remains on the shelf. Podziemski has scored at least 15 points in three of his last four contests.

items.headline: Podziemski closed with 15 points (5-12 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 32 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Podziemski has missed all 10 three-point attempts over his last two games, undermining his scoring efficiency despite consistent shot volume. He's maintained roughly 30 minutes per game recently, but Golden State's struggling offense without Stephen Curry (abdomen) has limited his playmaking opportunities. His fantasy ceiling depends on rediscovering his perimeter touch.

items.headline: Podziemski accumulated 10 points (5-13 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three rebounds and four assists over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Podziemski has averaged 16.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.8 triples over his last five games. However, he's shot just 38.5 percent from the field during that stretch. His consistent offensive involvement provides fantasy appeal, though poor shooting and fluctuating minutes limit his reliability.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 15 points (3-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks across 30 minutes in Monday's 115-94 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Podziemski continues to have opportunities to take on more offensive responsibility due to Stephen Curry (oblique) being sidelined, but Monday's performance showed the limitations of that expanded role. Although he connected on three triples, Podziemski attempted just eight shots and committed five turnovers. He hasn't established himself as a consistent offensive solution in Curry's absence, but Podziemski's rebounding remains a useful complement to his scoring and playmaking.

items.headline: Podziemski had 22 points (7-15 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, four assists and two steals across 37 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Rockets.

The fourth-year guard could see his usage increase significantly with Stephen Curry (abdomen) slated to miss at least two weeks after an MRI revealed an abdominal tear.

items.headline: Podziemski totaled 25 points (10-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 26 minutes during Monday's 138-87 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Podziemski teamed up with Stephen Curry to account for 50 points on the way to a blowout victory. The 23-year-old guard has looked sharp from downtown over his last two matchups, hitting nine of 16 attempts. His 25-point showing is his best of the season thus far through nine appearances.

items.headline: Podziemski finished with 15 points (5-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, an assist, two steals and a block across 39 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
items.story: Podziemski delivered efficient perimeter shooting and valuable defensive production while playing a season-high 39 minutes, but with his workload sitting firmly at around 33 minutes per game, his role on offense is pretty much set in stone as a multi-category contributor who can hit threes. His scoring ceiling still depends on shot volume in Golden State's offense, but his contributions in other categories are a nice boost, even if they are inconsistent at times.

items.headline: Podziemski provided nine points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 32 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat.
items.story: Podziemski struggled to find his shooting touch but contributed in several other categories while logging the most minutes of any Golden State player. The fourth-year guard added two triples and a pair of defensive stats, helping compensate for his single-digit scoring output. His substantial workload and versatility provide a useful fantasy floor, though his offensive production remains inconsistent.

items.headline: Podziemski supplied 17 points (7-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and eight assists over 37 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 win over the Clippers.
items.story: The fourth-year guard set new season highs in boards and assists as he came within spitting distance of his first career triple-double. Podziemski has played only five of the Warriors' seven games so far due to back trouble, but he's been productive when on the court, averaging 16.4 points, 5.6 assists, 5.4 boards, 2.2 threes and 1.2 steals in 33.6 minutes. He is seeing a career-high shot volume, with 13.0 field-goal attempts and 6.4 three-point attempts per contest.

items.headline: Podziemski closed Friday's 112-95 win over the Lakers with 21 points (7-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals in 33 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski gave Golden State a strong secondary scoring option. The guard has taken on a bigger role in the starting lineup due to numerous long-term absences, and his all-around production was key to the comeback. He should keep seeing heavy minutes Sunday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Podziemski amassed 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Monday's 134-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski returned to the starting lineup after sitting out Saturday's contest against Phoenix, delivering an efficient performance while committing zero turnovers. The third-year guard also finished with a team-high plus-35 rating, contributing across multiple categories in Golden State's first victory of the campaign. His combination of rebounds, assists and three-point shooting should keep him relevant in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is no longer listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski didn't play Saturday against the Suns because of a back issue, but since the shooting guard isn't on the injury report, he should return to the starting lineup Monday. items.headline: Podziemski (back) told reporters Friday that he will not play in the second leg of the Warriors' back-to-back set Saturday against the Suns, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Podziemski missed the Warriors' regular-season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday due to back soreness, but he was cleared to play against the Grizzlies on Friday, when he played 33 minutes and finished with 18 points (7-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds, three steals and one block in a 111-108 loss. Stephen Curry (rest) is unlikely to play Saturday, so the Warriors' starting backcourt figures to be made up of some combination of De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard, Brandon Williams and Gary Payton. Podziemski's next chance to play is Monday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is good to go for Friday's game against the Grizzlies, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Podziemski is set to make his regular-season debut after sitting out Opening Night, which will shift De'Anthony Melton back to the second unit. Podziemski is expected to have a significant role in the Warriors' offense this season.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: The 23-year-old guard was previously listed as questionable, so he's trending in the right direction after missing Opening Night. If Podziemski is cleared to play, De'Anthony Melton would likely see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski will miss Wednesday's regular-season opener due to lower-back soreness, and his next chance to play will come Friday against Memphis. With the 23-year-old guard sidelined, De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton and Will Richard are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) was unable to practice Tuesday, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: It was reported on Monday that Podziemski will be listed as questionable for Wednesday's season opener, and Friedell confirmed that remains the case. If the Warriors opt to hold him out, the team could rely more on De'Anthony Melton.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Lakers, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.
items.story: The combo guard has had a back issue crop up and missed Monday's practice, leaving his status for the start of the year up in the air. If Podziemski cannot play, De'Anthony Melton appears to be the next man up on the depth chart at shooting guard.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 17 points (4-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes during Friday's 128-118 preseason win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Podziemski was quiet over the first two quarters of Friday's game before logging 10 points in the third to help the Warriors extend their lead. The fifth-year pro enters the 2026-27 with high expectations, which is reflected by the five-year, $110 million contract extension that he signed with the Warriors last Saturday. He could emerge as the No. 2 option on offense behind Stephen Curry, especially since Jimmy Butler (knee) is not expected to play until the start of the 2027 calendar year.

items.headline: Podziemski posted 17 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-5 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 26 minutes in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski tied for the team lead in scoring and hit a key fourth-quarter three-pointer set up by a Charles Bassey offensive rebound as Golden State erased a 13-point halftime deficit. After a slow preseason opener, Podziemski has scored 16 or more in two of his last three exhibitions and looks locked into a starting role next to Stephen Curry.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) is in the Warriors' starting lineup against the Kings on Saturday, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Podziemski sat out Wednesday's exhibition contest against the Trail Blazers, but the fourth-year pro will be on the court for Saturday's game. He's fresh off signing a five-year, $110 million contract extension that is fully guaranteed.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) and the Warriors agreed to a five-year, $110 million contract extension Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The deal is a fully guaranteed, rookie-scale contract extension that includes a mutual option for the 2031-32 season. Podziemski is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged career highs in points (13.8) and three-pointers (1.9) while starting in 43 of 82 regular-season games. Podziemski figures to start alongside Stephen Curry (rest) in the backcourt to open the 2026-27 season, though that could change once Jimmy Butler (knee) is cleared to return, which likely won't be until after the calendar flips to 2027.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) won't travel with the Warriors for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Podziemski is coming off a strong showing in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers, finishing with 16 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in 19 minutes. Golden State is resting several rotation players during the second half of a preseason back-to-back, and Podziemski should have another opportunity to suit up Saturday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Podziemski tallied 16 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block over 19 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski came out flat with seven points on 2-for-10 shooting in Golden State's preseason opener, but he found his footing against a Lakers team that was resting their stars. Podziemski was generating a lot of buzz at training camp, so it'll be interesting to see if he can keep it going  Wednesday in Portland.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded seven points (2-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 18 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Podziemski struggled from the field after earning a starting spot alongside Stephen Curry in Golden State's preseason opener. Despite the poor shooting performance, Podziemski appears positioned for a prominent role after a strong training camp, and coach Steve Kerr recently called him one of the Warriors' best players.

items.headline: Podziemski said at Warriors media day he wants to shoot more threes per game, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle.
items.story: Head coach Steve Kerr is in full support as well, offering Podziemski encouragement Wednesday to fire away from downtown. Podziemski opened last season as a part-time starter before moving into a full-time position with the first unit post-All-Star break, averaging 17.5 points, 6.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.0 steals in his final 27 regular-season games, and he could become a lethal threat from deep especially once Jimmy Butler (knee) and Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) are both in the mix.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 23 points (9-17 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 10 rebounds and one steal over 39 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game loss to the Suns.

With averages of 14.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.9 three-pointers, he is likely to remain on the radar heading into drafts next season.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 30 points (9-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 9-10 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 32 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Stephen Curry (ankle) returned to the starting five Friday, but it was Podziemski who led the way on offense for the Warriors as he paced all scorers on the night while setting a new career high. The third-year guard has dropped 20-plus points in seven of the last 10 games, averaging 21.1 points, 4.8 boards, 3.7 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.0 steals over that stretch as he heads into the regular-season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Podziemski produced 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across 24 minutes during Thursday's 119-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The 17 points tied Nate Williams for the team lead in the loss. Podziemski has scored in double digits in nine straight games as he tries to keep an injury-depleted Golden State roster afloat heading into the Play-In Tournament, averaging 20.1 points, 5.0 boards, 4.0 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.0 steals over that span while shooting 53.1 percent from the floor and 43.4 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Podziemski finished Tuesday's 110-105 win over Sacramento with 20 points (5-11 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal in 30 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard continues to roll. Podziemski has scored at least 14 points and drained multiple three-pointers in eight straight games, averaging 20.5 points, 5.5 boards, 4.4 assists, 2.8 threes and 1.1 steals over that stretch while shooting 54.1 percent from the floor and 45.8 percent from long distance.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Thursday's 118-111 loss to Cleveland with 25 points (9-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: This was one of Podziemski's best games of the season as he recorded his fourth game with at least 25 points, finishing one point shy of his season-best mark. He's been on a tear with 18.3 points, 5.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists over his last eight games, but Stephen Curry (knee) is targeting a return Sunday against Houston.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 23 points (8-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 32 minutes during Sunday's 116-93 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski matched Kristaps Porzingis with a team-high 23 points during the loss. While Podziemski has fared well in the starting role at point guard, the gap left by Stephen Curry (knee) is still quite noticeable. The team seems destined to finish at the bottom of the Play-In bracket without his contribution, but Podziemski has helped to keep the team above water. He's averaged 14.5 points, 6.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals since Curry's exit 21 games ago.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 22 points (6-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-8 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists and two steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 131-126 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Podziemski has reached the 20-point mark in three straight games, which marks his longest streak of the season doing so. With Jimmy Butler (knee) and Stephen Curry (knee) sidelined, Podziemski has been forced to embrace a bigger role on offense, but he's certainly thriving in that scenario. He's averaging 16.9 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 0.9 steals per game in 16 appearances since returning to the starting lineup on a regular basis Feb. 25.

items.headline: Podziemski notched 22 points (6-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), six rebounds and five assists across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 109-106 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Making his 15th straight start in place of Stephen Curry (knee), Podziemski scored 20-plus points for the second straight game and the sixth time in 13 March contests. On the month, the third-year guard is averaging 16.9 points, 6.1 boards, 4.0 assists, 2.3 threes and 0.9 steals in 33.5 minutes.

items.headline: Podziemski supplied 20 points (8-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 40 minutes during Monday's 137-131 overtime win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Podziemski bounced back with a solid total after struggling through a rough four-game stretch where he averaged only 10.0 points. The third-year pro has been indispensable during Stephen Curry's (knee) extended absence. Given the Warriors' playoff position with only 10 games remaining, Podziemski will continue to receive every opportunity to produce, with Curry's regular-season return becoming increasingly unlikely.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Wednesday's 120-99 loss to the Celtics with 10 points (1-8 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 7-10 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal in 28 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski couldn't get his shot to drop and finished with a minus-11 plus/minus rating in the blowout loss. The Warriors have now dropped six of their past seven games, and it'll be tough for them to right the ship Friday with a matchup against the 48-18 Pistons.

items.headline: Podziemski chipped in 25 points (8-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 7-9 FT), five rebounds, six assists and two steals across 37 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Podziemski was coming off a 25-point effort in Friday's loss to the Timberwolves, and he continues to put up excellent numbers since moving into a starting role. He has started the Warriors' last nine games dating back to Feb. 25, and he's averaging a robust line of 18.4 points, 6.9 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game over that stretch while shooting 38.5 percent from beyond the arc. As long as Stephen Curry (knee) remains sidelined, Podziemski should maintain elevated usage.

items.headline: Podziemski closed Friday's 127-117 loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds and two assists in 36 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard led the shorthanded Warriors in scoring, and the roster only got thinner as the night progressed with Al Horford (calf), Quinten Post (ankle) and Seth Curry (thigh) all heading to the locker room early. Podziemski has scored more than 20 points in three of the last six games, averaging 18.8 points, 7.0 boards, 3.8 assists, 3.3 threes and 1.0 steals in 35.7 minutes over that stretch, and it doesn't look like his workload or usage are going to be scaled back any time soon.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Monday's 119-116 loss to the Jazz with 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 0-4 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski has strung together four consecutive games with at least 14 points, and he's scored in double figures in 11 of his last 12 contests. The third-year guard should continue to handle extra usage in the absence of Stephen Curry (knee), averaging 16.5 points, 8.1 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.1 steals in 34.0 minutes per tilt in his last 12 games.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 26 points (10-18 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one assist over 40 minutes during the Warriors' 115-113 overtime win over the Rockets on Thursday.
items.story: Podziemski got off to a slow start to Wednesday's game but finished strong with 10 points in the third quarter and seven more in overtime to help the Warriors snap their two-game losing streak. His 26 points were a season high, and he was one rebound shy from recording his third double-double of the season. Podziemski has started in each of the Warriors' last four games and should remain a starter for as long as Stephen Curry (knee) is sidelined.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 22 points (9-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and three assists in 37 minutes during Monday's 114-101 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Podziemski posted a solid all-around line in the loss, but lackluster performances with the rest of the first unit weren't enough to turn the tide against the Clippers. He was one of only four Warriors to reach double digits in the contest, with only two other players scoring more than 10 points. Although Podziemski has been a great placeholder for Stephen Curry (knee), the team is in desperate need of more production.

items.headline: Gafford notched 10 points (5-8 FG), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Gafford has logged at least 24 minutes in three straight games after averaging 17.3 minutes over his previous three appearances. His improving workload strengthens his fantasy outlook, particularly for managers seeking efficient scoring, rebounds and blocks.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) is available for Sunday's game against Boston.
items.story: Gafford will manage to avoid an absence despite dealing with a shoulder stinger picked up during Saturday's loss to the Cavs. The big man is averaging 9.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.4 blocks over his last five showings.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) is probable to play in Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Gafford took an elbow to the shoulder during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland and eventually left and did not return to the contest. It's a good sign for Dallas that he's listed as probable, so all signs point to Gafford being in the lineup versus Boston.

items.headline: Gafford (face) won't return to Saturday's game against the Cavaliers, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Gafford took a shot by Thomas Bryant and exited the game after making two free throws earlier, but the center won't return. This means Morez Johnson and Santi Aldama should see more time in the frontcourt. Gafford ends the contest with 10 points (4-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and an assist across 17 minutes. His next chance to play will come Sunday against the Celtics on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Gafford (face) exited Saturday's game against the Cavaliers, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Gafford took a shot to the face from Thomas Bryant in the second half. He left the game, and after returning briefly to shoot his free throws, he exited again and went to the locker room. Gafford should be considered questionable to return, with Morez Johnson and Santi Aldama potentially in line to handle things in the middle.

items.headline: Gafford finished with 18 points (7-8 FG, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three blocks across 19 minutes in Sunday's 130-93 win over the Nets.
items.story: Gafford delivered outstanding efficiency around the basket while providing valuable rim protection, recording three blocks despite playing just 19 minutes. His limited workload remains a concern for consistent fantasy production, but his ability to accumulate points, rebounds and blocks offers considerable per-minute upside. Gafford remains particularly appealing in category formats emphasizing field-goal percentage and defensive stats, but the fact that he's logged fewer than 20 minutes in each of his last three appearances should be cause for concern.

items.headline: Gafford finished with 20 points (9-10 FG, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one steal and one block across 26 minutes in Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Gafford has been a scoring machine lately, averaging 19.0 points over his last two outings. The 20 points marked a season-high for the 28-year-old through seven games, and he's now grabbed seven or more boards in five straight contests. Gafford tied Walter Clayton for the team lead in scoring with Kyrie Irving (rest) out and Cooper Flagg finishing 3-for-19 from the field in 40 minutes of play. Gafford offers a reliable fantasy floor and will continue to work as the primary big with Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) both sidelined.

items.headline: Gafford amassed 18 points (6-7 FG, 6-9 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 29 minutes during Friday's 116-111 victory over the Rockets.
items.story: The 18 points were a season high for Gafford, who continues to operate without much backup in the paint as Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) remain sidelined. Gafford has recorded exactly two blocks in six straight games to begin the season, averaging 8.5 points, 7.0 boards, 2.5 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 23.3 minutes while shooting 70.0 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Gafford produced seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 120-96 victory over the Thunder.
items.story: The 11 boards led Dallas on the night, although Gafford didn't see enough offensive opportunities to produce his first double-double of the season. The 28-year-old center hasn't seen a significant increase in his workload to begin the season even with Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) still waiting to make their 2026-27 debuts. In 22.4 minutes over five games, Gafford is averaging 6.6 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 steals while shooting 65.2 percent from the floor. Wednesday's three-pointer was also the first of his career, and his second-ever attempt from beyond the arc. The other came in 2021-22, when he was playing for the Wizards.

items.headline: Gafford went to the locker room during the third quarter of Monday's game against the Heat due to an undisclosed injury, but he returned with 8:52 remaining in the period, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Gafford looked to take a knee to the body on a Giannis Antetokounmpo dunk, and the big man was spotted going into the locker room right after. However, Gafford was able to return later in the quarter after getting checked out.

items.headline: Gafford posted 12 points (6-9 FG), nine rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocks over 23 minutes during Saturday's 122-106 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Gafford scored eight of his 12 points in the first half and finished tied for the second-most points on the Mavericks behind rookie first-rounder Sergio de Larrea (21 points). Gafford's five combined blocks and steals were his most in a regular-season game since Feb. 5 of the 2025-26 campaign against San Antonio (seven), and he was one rebound shy from logging his first double-double of the season.

items.headline: Gafford totaled two points (0-1 FG, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 128-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Gafford didn't offer much on the offensive end in Dallas' season-opening loss. However, the big man recorded a game-high mark in blocks while chipping in a steal. He figures to operate as Dallas' starting center for now, though the eventual returns of Santi Aldama (knee) and Dereck Lively (foot) will likely eat into Gafford's playing time.

items.headline: Gafford (rest) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's preseason finale with the Hawks.
items.story: Gafford sat out Wednesday's exhibition for rest, but he'll be back in action for Friday's final exhibition before the regular season. Over 55 regular-season games (44 starts) in 2025-26, Gafford averaged 9.5 points, 6.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.3 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Gafford (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Pelicans, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: The big man is receiving a maintenance day Wednesday. His next chance to play comes Friday against the Hawks.

items.headline: Gafford produced seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), three rebounds and one steal in eight minutes during Friday's 135-117 preseason loss to the Rockets.
items.story: In an interesting move, new head coach Dusty May opted to start a small-ball lineup of Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Naji Marshall, Zaccharie Risacher and rookie Morez Johnson in the Mavericks' preseason opener, notably leaving Gafford to play off the bench. It's unclear if this trend will continue in the regular season, but with Dallas' frontcourt banged up, including a cloudy return timeline for Dereck Lively (foot), Gafford may need to play heavy minutes even if he operates off the bench.

items.headline: Gafford could have the green light to attempt occasional three-pointers this season, with head coach Dusty May encouraging the center to expand his offensive game, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: May said the Mavericks want Gafford to become more of a playmaking decision-maker on the perimeter and indicated that he'll be allowed to take rhythm threes as long as he earns those opportunities. Gafford has attempted just one three-pointer across his seven NBA regular seasons and has yet to make one, so any development of a perimeter shot would represent a significant change to his offensive profile. He averaged 9.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 21.7 minutes across 55 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. With Dereck Lively (knee) not cleared for the start of training camp, Gafford could be in line for major minutes out of the gate in 2026-27.

items.headline: Gafford will face increased competition for minutes during the 2026-27 season after Dallas selected Morez Johnson with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Gafford started 44 of the 55 games he appeared in last season, but there's a new head coach in Dallas, and the Mavericks just drafted one of his favorite prospects. With Dereck Lively expected to be back after recovering from foot surgery, Gafford will likely face stiff competition for frontcourt minutes during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Gafford (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bulls
items.story: Gafford will miss a fourth consecutive contest to end the season. The big man will finish the campaign with averages of 9.5 points, 6.9 rebounds, 1.3 blocks and 1.1 assists across 21.7 minutes per contest in 55 regular-season outings (44 starts). With Marvin Bagley (shoulder) and P.J. Washington (elbow) also ruled out, Moussa Cisse and Dwight Powell are expected to handle the center minutes.

items.headline: Gafford (rest) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Gafford missed the last three games, so it's not surprising to see his name on the injury report for the season finale. With P.J. Washington (elbow) and Marvin Bagley (shoulder) also doubtful, Moussa Cisse (two-way) could see more action, potentially entering the starting lineup for the second time this season.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: As expected after being listed as doubtful, Gafford will miss his third consecutive game due to a right shoulder impingement. With Gafford sidelined once again, Marvin Bagley is heavily favored to draw another start at center, while Dwight Powell should also continue to see rotational minutes behind him.

items.headline: Gafford is doubtful for Friday's game versus San Antonio.
items.story: The Mavericks expect Gafford to miss a third straight game due to a right shoulder impingement. Marvin Bagley should start at center Friday, making him a worthwhile streaming candidate in all fantasy leagues after posting at least 20 points and eight rebounds in three of his past four appearances.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Gafford will end up missing both halves of this back-to-back set due to a right shoulder impingement. Marvin Bagley and Dwight Powell are likely to handle the majority of the center minutes in Gafford's absence. His next chance to play will come Friday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Gafford is set to miss his second straight contest Wednesday. With Gafford expected to be sidelined, Dwight Powell, Marvin Bagley and Moussa Cisse are candidates to see increased run.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Gafford will miss the front end of this back-to-back due to a right shoulder impingement, and the big man faces a short turnaround if he hopes to play in Phoenix on Wednesday. Marvin Bagley will likely start in Gafford's stead, while Dwight Powell is expected to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Gafford is expected to miss Tuesday's contest with a right shoulder impingement. His absence could lead to a significant role at center for Marvin Bagley (shoulder), who is listed as questionable, with Dwight Powell in line to back him up. If Bagley is ruled out, Moussa Cisse would likely enter the rotation.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) won't return to Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Gafford injured his right shoulder early in the fourth quarter and immediately exited toward the locker room in obvious pain. He will finish Sunday's game with seven points (2-4 FG, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, two steals and two blocks in 20 minutes. The Mavericks will next play Tuesday versus the Clippers, and if Gafford can't suit up for that contest, Marvin Bagley should be considered the favorite to replace him in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Gafford (shoulder) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Gafford exited Tuesday's loss to Milwaukee in the second quarter due to a right shoulder stinger, though he's set to play Friday. Over 11 appearances in March, the big man averaged 15.1 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gafford has been ruled out for the remainder of Tuesday's game against Milwaukee due to a right shoulder stinger. He'll finish with seven points (2-6 FG, 3-6 FT), four rebounds and one block across 11 minutes.
items.story: Gafford looked to be in significant discomfort as he made his way to the locker room, and the team announced shortly thereafter that he'll be shut down for the rest of the night. Dwight Powell and Moussa Cisse should see an uptick in minutes in Gafford's absence.

items.headline: Philon produced five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 13 minutes during Sunday's 106-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: After going scoreless in four minutes during his NBA debut Saturday against Milwaukee, Philon saw an expanded role Sunday and scored his first regular-season points. The rookie guard knocked down his first NBA three-pointer and provided a modest spark off the bench. The 22nd overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft remains a developmental option for Philadelphia and holds limited fantasy appeal in his current role.

items.headline: Philon (coach's decision) didn't play during Tuesday's 106-100 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: There was some hope the rookie first-rounder would open the season as Tyrese Maxey's backup at point guard, but Anfernee Simons took on that role in the opener. Philon's fantasy value appears to be more pronounced in dynasty leagues.

items.headline: Philon logged 14 points (5-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), seven assists, two rebounds and one steal over 25 minutes during Saturday's 144-106 preseason loss to Boston.
items.story: Philon led the 76ers in both assists and three-pointers in Saturday's loss, and he finished tied with Jabari Walker as the team's second-leading scorer behind VJ Edgecombe (19 points). Philon was the 22nd overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, but the rookie's role this season is a bit muddied given the strength of Philadelphia's starting lineup and veteran role players like Anfernee Simons (undisclosed) and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (rest).

items.headline: Philon finished with six points (2-9 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists and two rebounds in 25 minutes during Monday's 120-97 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Philon struggled with his shot but didn't commit a turnover while receiving an extended look in Philadelphia's preseason opener. The rookie should continue to see opportunities during the preseason as the 76ers evaluate their backcourt depth.

items.headline: Philon faces plenty of competition for minutes and an uncertain role heading into his rookie campaign, per Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com.
items.story: Selected with the No. 22 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Philon will likely have to impress to take on a steady role after the 76ers added Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (finger) this offseason. Philon will need to prove he can be effective off the ball to see meaningful burn on a nightly basis during his rookie season, as the 76ers have plenty of ball-handlers ahead of him. The 20-year-old's off-ball movement and ability to hit catch-and-shoot threes could play a large part in his playing time, considering the Sixers also have Simons to handle the rock off the bench. Philon will also have to hold his own defensively to stay on the court. He earned All-SEC First Team honors with Alabama in 2025-26, averaging 22.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 50.1 percent from the field and 39.9 percent from beyond the arc in 30.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Philon (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Bucks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Philon will take a seat for the 76ers' Summer League finale. The rookie first-rounder scored at least 15 points in all four of his Las Vegas Summer League appearances, during which he averaged 18.5 points, 5.8 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 32.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Philon produced 15 points (7-24 FG, 1-13 3Pt), six rebounds, six assists and two steals over 37 minutes in Wednesday's 99-92 Summer League loss to the Magic.
items.story: Philon logged a heavy workload but struggled to find his shot, particularly from beyond the arc. Even so, the Alabama product made his presence felt elsewhere, leading the 76ers with six assists while matching teammate Amani Lyles for the team lead with six rebounds. Philon is averaging 18.5 points, 5.8 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals across four Summer League outings.

items.headline: Philon finished Tuesday's 90-64 Summer League loss to the Rockets with 17 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists, two rebounds, two steals and one block over 28 minutes.
items.story: Philon was one of the lone bright spots for the 76ers in Tuesday's blowout loss and led his team in both points in assists. He's averaged 19.7 points per game across three Summer League appearances, and he should provide the 76ers a solid scoring punch off the bench behind Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, with Anfernee Simons being Philon's top competition for playing time.

items.headline: Philon totaled 24 points (9-22 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six assists, three rebounds and one steal across 34 minutes in Saturday's 100-93 Summer League win over the Pacers in overtime.
items.story: Philon saw heavy usage and delivered with a team-high 24 points in the victory. He also led all players with six assists. Tyrese Maxey is entrenched as the 76ers' starting point guard, but Philon, the No. 22 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, figures to compete with Anfernee Simons for minutes off the bench in the backcourt.

items.headline: Philon finished with 18 points (6-19 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven assists, three rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes in Thursday's 101-93 Summer League win over the Pistons.
items.story: Philon struggled from inside the arc but knocked down a game-high-tying four triples while finishing as one of four Philadelphia players to score at least 18 points. The 22nd overall pick in this year's draft also dished out a game-high seven assists in his Summer League debut. The 20-year-old guard will likely have an opportunity to carve out a role off the 76ers' bench in 2026-27, though he'll have to compete for playing time with guys like Anfernee Simons and Dalen Terry behind a loaded starting backcourt.

items.headline: Irving had 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Irving scored all 16 of his points in the first half, making his contributions as a facilitator particularly important as Dallas nearly surrendered an 18-point fourth-quarter lead and ended up grinding out a win. His combination of perimeter shooting and playmaking remains valuable, though his scoring output was modest after looking dominant in the first half. Still, Irving has now scored at least 16 points in four straight games and in seven of his nine appearances this month.

items.headline: Irving supplied 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
items.story: After sitting out the second game of a weekend back-to-back set, Irving returned to action and delivered decent numbers. The veteran point guard has scored in double digits in all 12 of his games this season, and he's contributed at least five boards and five assists in three of his seven November contests, averaging 22.9 points, 4.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 threes and 1.4 steals.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Irving didn't play in Sunday's 131-94 loss to Boston, the second game of a back-to-back for the Mavericks. He will return Wednesday for the meeting with Golden State, likely resulting in Naji Marshall heading back to the bench.

items.headline: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland. He will, however, sit out the second leg of the back-to-back for Dallas, which will likely send Cooper Flagg's usage to the moon. Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Irving poured in a game-high 34 points in 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss to Cleveland, so there's a decent chance Dallas will give its star point guard the night off for the second leg of their back-to-back set. If he is indeed out, Cooper Flagg's usage would see a massive boost while Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton Jr. would figure to earn more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Irving ended with 34 points (11-25 FG, 7-16 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday's 127-117 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Irving finished with at least 30 points for the second time in his last three games. He also remained active defensively, recording a block for the second consecutive contest while garnering three steals for the second time in November. The 34-year-old veteran had a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign after missing last season while recovering from knee surgery. In 11 regular-season appearances, Irving is now averaging 22.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 39.8 percent from deep across 30.7 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Irving accumulated 10 points (4-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt), three rebounds, four assists and one block across 27 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Irving endured a disappointing scoring performance and attempted just 11 shots, but this was a game in which Dallas fell into an early hole and never recovered, which explains his 27-minute workload. Irving's established scoring ability remains valuable, so fantasy managers shouldn't overreact to just one bad game. He remains one of Dallas' go-to scoring and playmaking options behind Cooper Flagg, who also had a rough outing in this 39-point defeat.

items.headline: Irving delivered 35 points (11-18 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 6-7 FT) and four assists across 38 minutes in Monday's 125-122 win over the Pacers.
items.story: Irving produced an outstanding offensive performance, connecting on seven three-pointers while shooting efficiently from the field, but his production in other categories was subpar or nonexistent. His four assists show he's now a secondary playmaker behind Cooper Flagg, who notched six assists despite not being the default point guard. Still, Irving's elite shot-making continues to provide substantial fantasy upside, especially when his perimeter shooting reaches this level, but an uptick in assists or more consistent output in other categories would boost his fantasy profile considerably.

items.headline: Irving delivered 21 points (9-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal across 29 minutes in Sunday's 130-93 win over the Nets.
items.story: Irving produced an efficient scoring performance against his former team, helping Dallas establish a commanding lead before the fourth quarter. His limited workload reflected the lopsided result, not a diminished offensive role. Irving remains a dependable fantasy option even when he's operating as a secondary scorer and playmaker behind star second-year forward Cooper Flagg.

items.headline: Irving finished with 14 points (7-20 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 28 minutes in Friday's 112-100 win over the Jazz.
