items.story: Irving struggled offensively, shooting just 35 percent from the field while missing all four three-point attempts, but the three steals helped salvage some fantasy value. Irving's scoring and playmaking remain major fantasy assets, though his production can fluctuate when his perimeter shooting and assist numbers are limited. He's had more than five assists in just two of his seven appearances this season and has scored over 20 points just three times.

items.headline: Irving (illness) is available for Friday's game against Utah.
items.story: The Mavericks previously added Irving to the injury report as probable with an illness, so there was little doubt regarding his status. The star guard should be able to handle his typical workload Friday, provided he faces no in-game setbacks with the ailment.

items.headline: Irving (illness) is probable for Friday's game against Utah.
items.story: Irving presumably woke up Friday morning under the weather. The issue isn't expected to prevent the star guard from playing, and Irving is likely to go through pregame warmups before Dallas confirms his status.

items.headline: Irving registered 29 points (9-27 FG, 5-14 3Pt, 6-8 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: The 29 points led the Mavericks on the night, but it was a drop in the bucket compared to Victor Wembanyama's massive 52-point performance. Irving has produced 24 or more points in three of six appearances to begin the season, averaging 22.7 points, 4.8 assists, 4.0 boards, 3.5 threes and 1.2 steals in 29.8 minutes. However, he's also sat out two games for maintenance reasons on his surgically repaired left knee.

items.headline: Irving (knee) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Wednesday's meeting in Sacramento.
items.story: Irving skipped Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings for rest, but he'll get back out there for Wednesday's rematch in Sacramento. With Irving back in action, Marcus Sasser's minutes will likely dip.

items.headline: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Irving was initially listed as questionable before being downgraded to doubtful Monday afternoon, and he's since been ruled out. With the star floor general sidelined, Marcus Sasser and Walter Clayton are candidates for increased burn, while Cooper Flagg will likely see increased playmaking duties.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is now doubtful for Monday against the Kings.
items.story: The Mavericks originally listed Irving as questionable, but he's expected to miss his second game of the season. The team will be hoping he's ready to return Wednesday against San Antonio. Walter Clayton and Marcus Sasser could see extra run in Irving's expected absence.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is questionable to play Monday against the Kings.
items.story: Irving could miss his second contest of the season as he works his way back from an ACL tear in his left knee. He played a season-high 35 minutes during Friday's 116-111 win over Houston, so it's possible Dallas gives him some additional time to rest Monday. If that is indeed the case, Walter Clayton Jr. and Marcus Sasser are the top candidates to join the starting unit, while Cooper Flagg's usage would see a major boost.

items.headline: Irving closed Friday's 116-111 win over Houston with 35 points (12-19 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds and nine assists across 35 minutes.
items.story: The veteran point guard led all scorers on the night, combining for 68 points with Cooper Flagg as the Mavericks handed the Rockets their first loss. The 35 points were also a season high for Irving, as were the nine assists. He hasn't played more than 60 regular-season games in a campaign since 2018-19, but Irving's been mostly healthy to begin the current season and is averaging 21.4 points, 4.8 assists, 3.4 boards, 3.2 threes and 1.2 steals in 28.6 minutes over five contests while shooting 52.7 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is available for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Irving will shed his questionable tag due to left knee injury management and suit up for a second straight game. The veteran floor general is averaging 19.0 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.3 steals across 27.0 minutes per tilt through three regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Irving could receive a maintenance day Wednesday. If the star guard is sidelined, Marcus Sasser would likely handle an expanded role at point guard while Cooper Flagg takes on more usage.

items.headline: Irving tallied 18 points (7-17 FG, 2-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, six assists and two steals across 33 minutes in Monday's 113-109 win over the Heat.
items.story: Irving struggled from beyond the arc, but he made up for it with balanced production in other categories. Even as the veteran floor general cedes some playmaking responsibilities to Cooper Flagg, Irving still delivers. His ability to contribute across multiple categories helps maintain his fantasy value even when his shot isn't falling, so fantasy managers shouldn't read too much into his occasional shooting woes. He's still scored at least 15 points in each of his three appearances this season.

items.headline: Irving (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Irving sat out Saturday's loss to the Spurs in the second leg of a back-to-back set but is set to return to action Monday. The star point guard's return will leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Sergio de Larrea, Marcus Sasser and Walter Clayton, especially if Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is upgraded from questionable to available.

items.headline: Irving is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs due to left knee injury management, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Mavericks are taking a cautious approach with Irving since he's played only a few games since returning from the ACL injury he sustained in March 2025, so it's not surprising to see him sit for rest purposes. His next chance to play will come against the Heat on Monday, and in the meantime, Marcus Sasser is expected to replace him in the backcourt against the Spurs.

items.headline: Irving (knee) has been downgraded from questionable to doubtful ahead of Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: It looks like Irving will end up missing the second leg of the Mavericks' back-to-back set Saturday while managing a knee issue. Marcus Sasser figures to enter the starting lineup if Irving is indeed ruled out against San Antonio.

items.headline: Irving (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Irving may sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to left knee injury management. If the star floor general is held out of Saturday's contest, Marcus Sasser and Sergio de Larrea would be candidates for increased minutes. Naji Marshall could also see increased playmaking duties if Irving joins Cooper Flagg (shoulder) on the inactive list.

items.headline: Irving posted 24 points (8-15 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, three assists, one block and one steal over 25 minutes before fouling out of Friday's 121-105 win over Indiana.
items.story: Irving fouled out for the first time in his career, but he looked great while he was out there, finishing with a game-high 24 points and a plus-8 differential in the blowout win. Cooper Flagg exited Friday's game with a shoulder injury and is likely to miss Saturday's meeting with the Spurs, and it wouldn't be surprising to see the veteran point guard join the budding superstar on the sidelines for the second half of Dallas' back-to-back set, which will likely be the case moving forward as Irving continues to work his way back from an ACL tear.

items.headline: Irving (knee) will be on a minutes restriction in Friday's game against the Pacers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Irving will suit up for the front end of this back-to-back set, though he'll see limited playing time. As a result, Marcus Sasser could pick up a few extra minutes. Over 24 minutes in Wednesday's season-opening loss to Houston, Irving posted 15 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

items.headline: Irving registered 15 points (6-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 128-110 loss to Houston.
items.story: Irving got his first taste of regular-season action since tearing his ACL in March 2025. The star point guard wasn't very aggressive in hunting his shot, though he didn't miss an attempt from inside the arc and finished as Dallas' fourth-leading scorer. The 34-year-old also tied for third on the team in rebounds.

items.headline: Irving notched 18 points (6-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 1-4 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two steals across 25 minutes in Friday's 135-111 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Irving showcased his perimeter shooting ability, connecting on five of his seven attempts from beyond the arc, and he also thrived as a playmaker. Even though Irving was taking it slow in the preseason, as this was his first taste of competitive action since early 2025 due to a torn ACL, he looked better than anticipated. Irving didn't play in the fourth quarter as Dallas managed his workload, but he should be good to go for the regular-season opener against the Rockets on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Irving (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Hawks.
items.story: Irving didn't play in Wednesday's meeting with the Pelicans but will be back on the floor for the preseason finale. The 34-year-old most recently finished with 17 points, three assists and two rebounds over 21 minutes in a 131-115 preseason win over Houston on Sunday.

items.headline: Irving (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Pelicans, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Irving is sitting out this exhibition Wednesday. Friday's game against the Hawks marks his last chance for a tune-up.

items.headline: George (rest) isn't listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Wizards, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: George didn't suit up for Sunday's loss to the Warriors in the second leg of a back-to-back set, though he'll return to action Tuesday. The veteran forward has averaged 18.8 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.0 steals in 30.2 minutes per showing over his last five outings, and his return will leave fewer minutes available for guys like Jordan Walsh, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser.

items.headline: George (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser could all see increased burn. George will likely return for Tuesday's game at Washington.

items.headline: George finished Saturday's 97-96 loss to Sacramento with 19 points (6-21 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, one block and four steals over 37 minutes.
items.story: George struggled with his shot but made up for it with an excellent all-around statistical contribution, especially on defense. With Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) out, George embraced a bigger offensive role and attempted a team-high 21 shots. His five combined steals and blocks were especially valuable in category formats, showing he can stay productive even when his shooting efficiency suffers.

items.headline: George supplied 10 points (3-12 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist, one block and three steals across 23 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 105-101 loss to Denver.
items.story: The four combined steals and blocks were George's best showing since Nov. 4, when he racked up four pilfers against the Bucks. The veteran forward's offensive contributions have been erratic of late, and he's scored 10 points or fewer in three of his last six games, averaging 18.3 points, 5.3 boards, 3.3 threes, 2.2 assists and 1.5 steals during that stretch.

items.headline: George (illness) isn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against Dallas, Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.
items.story: George is set to return from a one-game absence due to an illness. With the veteran forward back in action, there will be fewer minutes available for the likes of Baylor Scheierman, Sam Hauser and Jordan Walsh. George has averaged 22.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.6 combined steals-plus-blocks in 29.6 minutes per tilt over his last five outings.

items.headline: George (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Toronto, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Mavericks. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Sam Hauser and Hugo Gonzalez are all candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: George tallied 36 points (14-22 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 123-101 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: George made his return to Philadelphia after being swapped for Jaylen Brown over the summer, as the former Sixer spent the previous two years there. George delivered masterfully with a game-high 36 points and six three-pointers, and he's now scored 25-plus points in three of his last four outings while shooting a scorching-hot 51.4 percent (18-for-35) from behind the arc over that stretch. Boston has now won four consecutive contests to improve to 9-2 on the season, and George's play certainly has a lot to do with that.

items.headline: George notched 27 points (11-18 FG, 5-10 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals across 28 minutes during Sunday's 117-97 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: George bounced back emphatically from Friday's eight-point performance, shooting 61.1 percent from the field while matching his season high with five made three-pointers. The veteran forward has now scored at least 25 points in two of his last three appearances, connecting on 12 triples during that stretch. Although his peripheral production was limited Sunday, George's scoring efficiency and three-point volume continue to bolster his fantasy value.

items.headline: George registered eight points (3-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, an assist, a steal and two blocks across 22 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
items.story: George struggled offensively, scoring a season-low eight points on 11 shots, but his defensive contributions helped salvage some fantasy value. His two blocks were particularly useful, but limited playing time and modest scoring output kept his overall production in check. George's ability to contribute defensive stats remains valuable, but his fantasy ceiling depends on improved shooting efficiency and consistent offensive involvement. George is in a battle with Derrick White to be the Celtics' No. 2 offensive option, as he's averaging 19.6 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.4 steals per contest.

items.headline: George produced 25 points (8-18 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 4-7 FT), three rebounds, five assists and four steals over 35 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks.
items.story: George committed a season-high six turnovers and uncharacteristically bricked three of his seven free-throw attempts, but he still delivered a quality stat line. He's been a top-20 player on the year with averages of 21.3 points, 5.6 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 3.4 triples and 2.6 steals per game on 46 percent shooting from the field and 80.8 percent at the line.

items.headline: George (rest) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: The star forward is good to go after sitting out Monday's loss in Houston. George is off to a fast start with his new team, having delivered at least 15 points in six straight games and seven dimes in three consecutive contests.

items.headline: George will be rested Monday against Houston.
items.story: There's no injury to report and this appears to be a planned maintenance day for the veteran. With George on the shelf, the Celtics will need guys like Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman to absorb more minutes.

items.headline: George posted 17 points (6-14 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists, two steals and two blocks across 33 minutes in Sunday's 108-97 win over the Magic.
items.story: George didn't have his best shooting performance, but fantasy managers will gladly overlook it, given his excellent multi-category output. His eight assists and four combined defensive stats helped offset a relatively modest scoring total, while his 33-minute workload reinforced his importance alongside Jayson Tatum. George's versatility continues to provide a strong fantasy foundation even when his shot isn't falling consistently. In six appearances this season, George has averaged 20.7 points, 6.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 2.3 steals per contest.

items.headline: George produced 18 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and three steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 125-111 win over Chicago.
items.story: George came out hot with eight points in the first quarter, and he ended the game a distant third on the Celtics in scoring behind Payton Pritchard (30 points) and Jayson Tatum (26 points). George also led the Celtics in assists, and Friday's game was the fourth time that the veteran forward has logged at least two steals. He has fit in seamlessly into head coach Joe Mazzulla's gameplan early on, and George is averaging 21.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 2.4 steals over 30.4 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: George registered 20 points (8-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 36 minutes in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime win over the Nets.
items.story: George delivered a well-rounded fantasy performance in a bounce-back effort after his 16-point output (5-14 FG) against the Bulls on Monday. His 36-minute workload and 16 field-goal attempts highlight his continued involvement in Boston's offense alongside Jayson Tatum. While his scoring may fluctuate, George's ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him a relatively stable fantasy floor. George has established himself as a reliable scoring weapon for Boston with at least 15 points in each of his four appearances so far.

items.headline: George amassed 16 points (5-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 25 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over the Bulls.
items.story: George struggled inside the arc but connected on three triples as Boston cruised to a comfortable victory. His playing time was limited by the lopsided score, and he committed four turnovers. The veteran forward has scored between 15 and 16 points in consecutive outings following his 38-point season opener.

items.headline: George had 15 points (6-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals across 34 minutes during Friday's 107-103 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: George came back to earth a bit after dropping 38 points in his season debut, but he still delivered a strong all-around performance Friday. The Celtics have their first back-to-back set of the season on tap for Monday against the Bulls and Tuesday versus the Nets, and it'll be interesting to see if the 36-year-old forward will play both ends after sitting out back-to-backs at times last year with the 76ers.

items.headline: George tallied 38 points (12-21 FG, 7-12 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, five steals and three assists across 31 minutes in Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: George turned in an efficient shooting performance, particularly from three-point range, en route to a game-high 38 points in his regular-season debut with the Celtics. The veteran forward provided a well-rounded stat line, leading all players in triples and steals while finishing as the Celtics' second-leading rebounder.

items.headline: George (rest) is expected to play Tuesday versus Detroit.
items.story: George didn't suit up for Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia to rest, though he is anticipated to be ready to go Tuesday versus the Pistons. The 36-year-old appeared in only 37 regular-season games for the 76ers in 2025-26, averaging 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.7 steals over 30.7 minutes per outing. Now paired with Jayson Tatum (rest), George still has All-Star upside, but he will need to figure out how to stay on the floor.

items.headline: George (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: George and the rest of Boston's regulars won't suit up for the final exhibition but should be good to go for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Pistons. George registered 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and five steals over 25 minutes during his Celtics debut against the 76ers last Saturday.

items.headline: George registered 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and five steals over 25 minutes during the Celtics' 144-106 preseason win over the 76ers on Saturday.
items.story: George didn't have the most efficient night offensively, but he demonstrated his defensive chops during Saturday's win, with four of his game-high five steals taking place in the first half. The veteran forward was the Celtics' return for Jaylen Brown in the offseason, and it'll be interesting to see how George and Jayson Tatum fit together early on in the 2026-27 season. George is expected to have his preseason reps limited before the Celtics' regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

items.headline: George (rest) is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: George will suit up in a Celtics uniform for the first time and face his former team in Saturday's exhibition contest. His playing time figures to be limited until the Celtics' regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

items.headline: George (rest) isn't in line to play Thursday versus Cleveland, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: The Celtics are holding several key contributors out of the starting lineup Thursday. Jordan Walsh is drawing the start at power forward.

items.headline: Head coach Joe Mazzulla praised George's experience Tuesday, per Justin Turpin of WEEI.com.
items.story: George has big shoes to fill in Boston this season, stepping into the role as one of Jayson Tatum's running mates following Jaylen Brown's exit. Staying on the court has been a major concern for George, who has made at least 70 regular-season appearances just once in his past seven seasons. However, he should push for mid-round fantasy value when healthy after averaging at least 16.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.5 steals per game in back-to-back years for the 76ers.

items.headline: Post (concussion) finished Monday's 136-120 win over Washington with five points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and three rebounds across nine minutes.
items.story: Post returned from a three-game absence due to a concussion, though he played a muted role even with Isaiah Stewart (illness) out. Post is now averaging 5.0 points and 2.2 rebounds in 12.4 minutes per tilt across nine regular-season games.

items.headline: Post (concussion) is available for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Post has passed each step of the league's concussion protocol ahead of Monday's action. The big man is slotting in as the clear backup center behind Zach Edey amid Isaiah Stewart's (illness) absence.

items.headline: Post (concussion) is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Post could miss a fourth consecutive game due to a concussion. Zach Edey (ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) have also been deemed questionable, so Taylor Hendricks could see an expanded role.

items.headline: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Saturday will mark Post's third straight missed game as he remains in the league's concussion protocol. His next chance to play will come Monday at Washington.

items.headline: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Post will miss a second straight game while in the league's concussion protocol, and his next opportunity to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn. With Zach Edey (left ankle injury management) sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set, Isaiah Stewart will likely get the starting nod, while Taylor Hendricks figures to see increased burn off the bench.

items.headline: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Post suffered a concussion during Monday's 118-102 win over the Raptors, and now he will have to clear a series of steps before he's allowed to return to the court. Taylor Hendricks will help pick up the slack while Post is sidelined.

items.headline: Post (head) didn't return to Monday's 118-102 win over the Raptors. He ended the night with one rebound in two minutes.
items.story: Post suffered a head injury shortly after checking in midway through the first quarter, and he was ultimately unable to gain clearance to return. He can be considered questionable for Wednesday's matchup against Denver until the team has more information to share.

items.headline: Post is doubtful to return to Monday's game against Toronto due to a head injury.
items.story: Post logged just two minutes and grabbed one rebound before exiting Monday's contest. Taylor Hendricks figures to see increased burn for as long as Post is sidelined.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Post has been cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. The big man is averaging 7.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 0.6 assists across 15.2 minutes per game through five regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Post is in danger of missing his third consecutive contest because of a right ankle sprain. If Post remains sidelined Wednesday versus the Pacers, Kris Murray should continue to see more minutes.

items.headline: Post (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Post is set for a second consecutive absence while tending to a right ankle sprain. His next chance to return will arrive Wednesday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is questionable to suit up for Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Post missed Saturday's 136-105 victory over Sacramento with a sprained right ankle, and he's now in jeopardy of missing a second straight contest with the injury. If he's unable to play, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks will split the backup center minutes.

items.headline: Post (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Post was listed as doubtful, and now we have official confirmation that he'll be on the inactive list Saturday night. His minutes will likely be divvied up amongst Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is doubtful for Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: A right ankle sprain is expected to cost Post at least one contest. Assuming he's eventually downgraded to out, more playing time should fall into the hands of Isaiah Stewart as the No. 2 center Saturday.

items.headline: Post (ankle) didn't return to Thursday's game against Portland. He recorded 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and four rebounds in seven minutes before exiting.
items.story: Post was off to a great start to Thursday's clash, and he may have had a significant opportunity to do damage in the second half if he hadn't tweaked his ankle, considering Zach Edey picked up four fouls before halftime. The severity of Post's injury isn't known at this time, and he can be considered day-to-day leading up to Saturday's game against Sacramento.

items.headline: Post is doubtful to return to Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers due to a right ankle injury.
items.story: Post appeared to step on an opposing player's foot and had to hobble off the court after the play. Zach Edey had four fouls in the first half, which likely means Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks will see more minutes down the stretch, assuming Post is unable to return.

items.headline: Post finished with seven points (3-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 17 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Despite the absence of the resting Zach Edey at center, Post didn't see a bump in playing time Sunday. Post appears to be stuck in the backup center role and could continue to struggle for fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Post won't start Wednesday's preseason game against the Magic.
items.story: Zach Edey (ankle) will return to action Wednesday, pushing Post to the second unit. The big man got the starting nod in Monday's preseason-opening win over Atlanta, contributing eight points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and four rebounds in 12 minutes.

items.headline: Post will start Monday's preseason game against the Hawks, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Zach Edey (ankle) isn't expected to play Monday, opening the door for Post to step into the starting five. The big man figures to compete with Isaiah Stewart for playing time behind Edey ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: The Warriors did not match the Grizzlies' three-year, $30 million offer sheet for Post on Tuesday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Post is now officially a member of the Grizzlies after spending the first two seasons of his career with the Warriors. The big man appeared in 67 regular-season games (35 starts) in 2025-26, averaging 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 17.3 minutes per contest. While he could carve out a more significant role with the rebuilding Grizzlies, Post will still likely have to compete for playing time with the likes of Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks behind Zach Edey (ankle).

items.headline: Post (foot) agreed to a three-year, $30 million contract with the Grizzlies on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Post is a restricted free agent, so the Warriors can still match this offer sheet. Including the Play-In Tournament, the big man missed the Warriors' final nine games of the 2025-26 campaign due to a right foot injury, and he finished the regular season with averages of 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.4 steals in 17.3 minutes per game across 67 outings (35 starts). Golden State has until 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday to match the Grizzlies' offer.

items.headline: Post (foot) averaged 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.4 steals in 17.3 minutes per game across 67 regular-season appearances (35 starts) in 2025-26.
items.story: Even as a member of the starting five, Post saw inconsistent playing time for the injury-plagued Warriors this season. The big man produced numbers similar to his rookie campaign but saw a dip in his three-point efficiency, shooting 33.6 percent from downtown. He still appeared in 25 more regular-season games than in 2024-25, though he missed the final seven outings of the regular season and both Play-In Tournament games due to a right foot injury. The 26-year-old's future in Golden State is uncertain, with the club holding a team option for 2026-27.

items.headline: Post (foot) is out for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Suns.
items.story: Post is in line for a ninth consecutive absence while on the mend from a right foot injury. If the Warriors are able to emerge victorious Friday, his next opportunity to take the court would arrive in Game 1 of the first round against Oklahoma City on Sunday.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Clippers.
items.story: Post will miss an eighth consecutive contest due to a right foot injury. However, his absence shouldn't affect the rotation with Kristaps Porzingis, Al Horford and Draymond Green all healthy.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Post will miss a seventh straight game due to a right foot injury, and his next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday during the Play-In Tournament. The big man will finish the regular season with averages of 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 17.3 minutes per showing across 67 outings (35 starts).

items.headline: The Warriors announced Saturday that Post (foot) will be re-evaluated next week.
items.story: Post is working his way back from right foot soreness, which has already cost him Golden State's past three contests. With Post and Al Horford (calf) both sidelined, the lion's share of the center minutes should fall onto Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green for the time being.

items.headline: Post is out for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Thursday will mark a second consecutive absence for Post, who left Sunday's loss to Denver early. Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green should share the center minutes for the Warriors versus Cleveland.

items.headline: Post has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Post departed Sunday's matchup against Denver due to right foot soreness, though it's worth noting that he's been ruled out Wednesday due to right foot injury management, so this appears to be a precautionary decision. Draymond Green and Omer Yurtseven should be in line for increased opportunities at center with Post, Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) all out.

items.headline: Post won't return to Sunday's game due to right foot soreness, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Post left the game in the second half and will not return. He saw limited action before exiting, totaling two rebounds and a steal in four minutes. The injury puts his status for Wednesday's game against the Spurs in question.

items.headline: Post exited Sunday's game against the Nuggets for the locker room due to an apparent right lower leg injury, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Post came into Sunday's contest dealing with a right foot issue, and it appeared as if he rolled his right ankle before exiting the game. He should be considered questionable at best to return until any further update is given.

items.headline: Post (foot) is available for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Post missed the last three games due to right foot injury management, but he will return to the lineup Sunday. In his last five games, he posted averages of 10.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 21.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Post (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Denver.
items.story: Post has missed three straight games due to right foot injury management, though the questionable tag is a step in the right direction. If Post is able to play, Omer Yurtseven and Malevy Leons could see fewer opportunities.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Post is slated for a third straight absence due to right foot injury management. Al Horford (calf) has also been downgraded to out Friday, which could once again open up more chances for Omer Yurtseven and Malevy Leons in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Post will miss a second consecutive contest due to right foot injury management. The 26-year-old big man's next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Wizards. With Al Horford (calf) also remaining out, Gui Santos and Malevy Leons are candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Post has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Mavericks due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Post has been working through a right foot issue as of late and will miss his fifth game since March 7, with his next chance to play being Wednesday against the Nets. He played 14 minutes in Saturday's loss to the Hawks, and those minutes should be absorbed by Kristaps Porzingis (back), the latter of whom is listed as probable for Monday's game.

items.headline: Post is part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Hawks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Post will start alongside Draymond Green in the frontcourt. In 34 starts this season, Post is averaging 9.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 20.6 minutes.

items.headline: Post (foot) is listed as available for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Post had been previously considered questionable due to a right foot issue. However, the second-year center has been given the green light to suit up Saturday. With Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (back) sidelined, Post and Draymond Green will handle most of the center duties.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Post didn't play in Friday's loss to Detroit because of a nagging foot issue. The Warriors are already down Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (back) for this one. On top of that, Draymond Green (back) is also carrying a questionable designation. If Post can suit up, he could be looking at more action versus Atlanta. However, if Post and Green join Horford and Porzingis on the shelf, the Dubs should rely mostly on Gui Santos and Omer Yurtseven to handle the bulk of the work underneath the basket.

items.headline: Post (foot) is out for Friday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Post will be sidelined for the first leg of this back-to-back set, joining Al Horford (calf) in street clothes. With this news, Omer Yurtseven could step into a larger role in the frontcourt behind Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Friday's game in Detroit.
items.story: Friday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so there's a chance that Post will get hit with a maintenance day. If he is forced to the sidelines, Omer Yurtseven could see an expanded role in the rotation.

items.headline: Post (foot) is available for Wednesday's game against Boston.
items.story: Post missed Monday's contest, but he'll be back in action for Wednesday's contest. With Al Horford (calf) sidelined, Post will look to mix in behind Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Post was unable to take the floor Monday against Golden State due to a right foot injury. However, he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Wednesday's clash, meaning he should at least have a chance to prove his health during shootaround and pregame warmups.

items.headline: Post (foot) won't play Monday against the Warriors.
items.story: Coach Steve Kerr mentioned in his pregame presser that Post was banged up after Sunday's game against the Knicks, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic, and the big man has since been downgraded to out. Look for Will Richard, Gary Payton and Malevy Leons to be candidates for an increase in playing time as a result.

items.headline: Post is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards due to right foot injury management.
items.story: After he posted a career-high 22 points (9-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt) and three blocks over 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks, the Warriors are thinking about holding Post out for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Draymond Green (back), who's expected to play Monday, and Kristaps Porzingis would be in line to share the center minutes if Post joins Al Horford (calf) on the sidelines.

items.headline: Post had 22 points (9-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and three blocks over 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With the Warriors extremely shorthanded, Post returned to the starting lineup Sunday after coming off the bench in Friday's loss to the Timberwolves. Even though he had the assignment of dealing with Karl-Anthony Towns, who posted a 17-point, 12-rebound double-double, Post still had a strong scoring line and delivered a new career-high mark in points while hitting the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. Post has scored in double digits in his last five starts. He could be a player worth keeping close tabs on, although his playing time will be tied to the availability of Draymond Green (back), Kristaps Porzingis (illness) and Al Horford (calf).

items.headline: Post will start Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Post enters the starting lineup due to Draymond Green (back), Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) being out of the lineup. In his last start, Post recorded 10 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal in 25 minutes. He will be supplemented by recent addition Omer Yurtseven at the five Sunday.

items.headline: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

items.headline: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Youngblood has been sidelined since Nov. 10 due to a right foot injury, with his latest designation identifying the heel as the affected area. The rookie guard had shown flashes of perimeter shooting before the injury, connecting on multiple three-pointers in three consecutive appearances. His next opportunity to return will come Saturday against the Knicks, though his limited role leaves him off the fantasy radar in most formats.

items.headline: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game at Minnesota.
items.story: Youngblood will miss a fourth consecutive contest with what the team is now calling a right heel bone bruise. His next opportunity to play will come Thursday in Milwaukee.

items.headline: Youngblood (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Youngblood will miss a third straight game due to a right foot bone bruise. His next opportunity to suit up comes Tuesday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Youngblood (foot) is out for Friday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Youngblood is in line for a second straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Monday in Minnesota.

items.headline: Youngblood has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to a right foot bruise.
items.story: Youngblood came down awkwardly following a fast-break layup attempt at the start of the fourth quarter during Tuesday's win over the Thunder and didn't return. He's recently carved out a role in Portland, averaging 14.8 minutes per game over the past five appearances, so in his absence, Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson are candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Youngblood supplied three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt) in seven minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Youngblood earned his first minutes of the 2026-27 campaign after battling an ankle injury. Portland's backcourt is already loaded with Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, but with Morant (hamstring) sidelined for an extended period, Youngblood could get some more run moving forward, although it shouldn't have much effect on the Blazers' rotation.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is available to play Saturday against the Jazz.
items.story: While Youngblood will be available for Saturday's game, that doesn't mean he'll get on the court. He's yet to log a single minute for Portland this season.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against Utah.
items.story: Youngblood has yet to make his 2026-27 regular-season debut due to a left ankle injury. However, his potential absence wouldn't affect the rotation.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle/two-way player) is out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: It's unclear at this time whether Youngblood is still dealing with an ankle injury, or if this decision is simply because he's on a two-way contract. Either way, he's yet to make his 2026-27 debut and will need to wait at least until Thursday against the Grizzlies to do so.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Youngblood will have to wait to make his 2026-27 season debut, and he'll miss a second consecutive game while dealing with left ankle soreness. His next chance to play will come against the Lakers on Tuesday, Nov. 27.

items.headline: Youngblood is out for Wednesday's regular-season opener against Phoenix due to left ankle soreness.
items.story: Youngblood missed Portland's final three preseason games due to left calf soreness, but now it's his left ankle that's giving him trouble. His next chance to play will come Friday in Sacramento.

items.headline: Youngblood (calf) won't play in Friday's preseason game versus the Warriors.
items.story: Youngblood will miss his third consecutive preseason contest due to lingering left calf soreness. It's unknown if he will be available for Opening Night versus Phoenix.

items.headline: Youngblood (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings.
items.story: Youngblood will miss his second exhibition game in as many days due to left calf soreness. His final chance to play again in the preseason will come Friday against Golden State.

items.headline: Youngblood is out for Monday's exhibition against the London Lions with left calf soreness.
items.story: The two-way player is sitting out the first half of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play is Tuesday versus the Kings.

items.headline: Youngblood finished Monday's 111-84 Summer League win over the Timberwolves with 20 points (5-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and three assists across 19 minutes.
items.story: After shooting just 1-for-8 from deep in Sunday's overtime loss to Orlando, Youngblood was efficient from three-point range Monday en route to a team-high 20 points. He's scored at least 14 points in back-to-back contests after posting just eight points on 3-of-13 shooting in Friday's loss to the Suns. The 24-year-old guard is signed to a two-way contract and figures to spend most of his time with the G League's Rip City Remix in 2026-27.

items.headline: Youngblood totaled 14 points (5-14 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 29 minutes during Sunday's 112-105 Las Vegas Summer League overtime loss to the Magic.
items.story: Youngblood had a tough time getting his shot to drop, but that was true for most of his teammates, with Portland converting just 36.9 percent of its field goal attempts in the seven-point loss. Youngblood is on a two-way deal with the Trail Blazers, so he's expected to spend most of the 2026-27 season in the G League.

items.headline: Portland signed Youngblood to a two-way contract Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Youngblood has been a standout player for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League. With this move, Youngblood is now likely to become a featured player for the Rip City Remix, but he may get some NBA looks with the Trail Blazers as well.

items.headline: Youngblood ended with five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 116-106 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Youngblood played double-digit minutes for the first time this season, called upon to do more after Oklahoma City ruled out a number of players earlier in the day. Given his season averages of just 2.0 points in 5.4 minutes, there is no need to make any roster moves in fantasy based on this effort.

items.headline: Youngblood closed with three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt), one rebound and one assist in 10 minutes during Wednesday's 138-89 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Youngblood continues to benefit from the fact that Oklahoma City is blowing opponents out on a regular basis. The majority of Youngblood's playing time has come during the final stretch of games, typically when the result has been decided. In 19 appearances, he has averaged 1.8 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Youngblood produced two points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across four minutes during Tuesday's 126-107 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The Thunder often blow out teams, allowing Youngblood and others to see a handful of minutes in garbage time. He's still pretty far off the fantasy radar, to be clear.

items.headline: Youngblood amassed three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt) over six minutes during Thursday's 141-135 double-overtime win over Indiana.
items.story: Youngblood didn't see any playing time during Tuesday's season-opening win over the Rockets in double overtime, but with the Thunder shorthanded Thursday, the two-way guard saw some action and scored his first NBA points. When Alex Caruso (concussion), Cason Wallace (knee), Isaiah Joe (knee) and Jalen Williams (wrist) return to action, Youngblood will likely be relegated to the G League.

items.headline: Youngblood signed a two-way contract with the Thunder on Saturday.
items.story: Youngblood played in six games for the Thunder during the preseason and averaged 11.0 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 20.7 minutes per game. He's likely to be a prominent player for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League to open the 2025-26 season.

items.headline: Youngblood ended with five points (1-7 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT) across 25 minutes in Tuesday's 116-112 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: After posting an efficient 25 points in Saturday's loss to Indiana, Youngblood came back down to earth Tuesday. The undrafted 23-year-old out of Alabama signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Thunder in June and may receive consideration for the team's final two-way spot ahead of the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Youngblood racked up 25 points (6-11 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 9-10 FT), five rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Saturday's 116-101 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Youngblood was efficient in the shooting department while leading the way for his squad with major minutes off the bench. He shot 54.5 percent from the field and 44.4 percent from beyond the arc in a performance that will likely get the attention of the coaching staff.

items.headline: Youngblood produced 20 points (7-11 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one turnover in 21 minutes of Sunday's 135-114 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: Youngblood, who went undrafted in 2025, was a standout player at Alabama. The Thunder scooped him up on an Exhibit 10 deal, and he went on to make a strong impression at the Summer League. He's expected to suit up for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League this season, but he's certainly making an impression on the coaching staff.

items.headline: Marshall ended Sunday's 131-94 loss to the Celtics with 13 points (4-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes.
items.story: With Kyrie Irving (knee) out, Marshall was one of Dallas' few reliable perimeter shooters, connecting on three of his five attempts from beyond the arc while the Mavericks struggled offensively. However, his limited playing time reduced his chances to contribute elsewhere. This was just Marshall's second start this season, and his limited role hurts his fantasy upside. He has played 25 minutes or fewer in five of his last six appearances, averaging 9.8 points, 2.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Marshall will start Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Marshall will draw his second start of the season due to the absence of Kyrie Irving (knee). Marshall's other start this year dates back to Oct. 24 against the Spurs, when he finished with 10 points, four rebounds, five assists and one steal across 21 minutes.

items.headline: Marshall notched 13 points (4-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, four assists and two steals across 23 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Marshall continues to be a dependable source of dimes as a facilitator off the bench for Dallas, making him worth considering in deeper fantasy leagues. For the season, the swingman has averaged 11.3 points, 4.4 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 24.6 minutes per contest through nine games.

items.headline: Marshall had 22 points (9-12 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 112-111 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: It was the best performance of the season for the veteran forward, as he set new highs in points, boards and made three-pointers while recording his first block of 2026-27. Marshall missed a few games due to an illness, but in five appearances (one start), he's averaged 13.6 points, 5.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.2 threes in 26.6 minutes while shooting 50.0 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is available for Friday's game against Houston.
items.story: Marshall initially drew a questionable tag before being upgraded to probable Friday afternoon, and he's since been cleared to play following a two-game absence. The 28-year-old forward is averaging 13.7 points, 5.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 27.7 minutes per contest in three regular-season games (one start). With Marshall back in action, Caleb Martin and Zaccharie Risacher could see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is probable for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Marshall is likely to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes will likely be available for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench.

items.headline: Marshall is questionable for Friday's game against the Rockets due to an illness.
items.story: Marshall has a chance to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes would be open for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench if Marshall is able to return.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) won't play in Wednesday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Marshall will now miss his second consecutive contest, meaning his next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against the Rockets. Without Marshall on the floor, Max Christie, Walter Clayton and Morez Johnson should each see a few extra minutes versus the Thunder.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is now doubtful for Wednesday against the Thunder.
items.story: Marshall was originally questionable, so he's trending in the wrong direction. With the Mavericks expected to hold him out, the team could rely more on Zaccharie Risacher.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Marshall is looking to return from an illness Wednesday. Zaccharie Risacher would likely play a larger role off the bench if Marshall remains sidelined.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Marshall is under the weather and will be held out of Monday's road game, and his next chance to suit up will come when the Mavericks host the Thunder on Wednesday. With the 28-year-old forward unavailable, Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser could see increased burn.

items.headline: Marshall posted 10 points (4-8 FG, 1-1 3PT, 1-3 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal over 21 minutes during Saturday's 122-106 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Marshall finished Saturday's game tied with both Walter Clayton and Marcus Sasser for the most assists on the Mavericks. It was Marshall's first start of the season, but he may move back to a bench role Monday against the Heat if Kyrie Irving (knee/rest) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Marshall will start Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: With Kyrie Irving (knee/rest) and Cooper Flagg (shoulder) sidelined in the second leg of this back-to-back set, Marshall will enter the starting five and figures to see increased playmaking duties. He's posted at least 15 points and six assists in back-to-back games to begin the regular season.

items.headline: Marshall finished with 15 points (7-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists and three steals across 33 minutes during Friday's 121-105 win over the Pacers.
items.story: With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) leaving the game in the second quarter, Marshall started the second half for the Mavericks and made the most of the increased opportunity. If Flagg can't play Saturday against the Spurs, Marshall would make for an intriguing streamer option in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Marshall notched 16 points (7-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 128-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Marshall wasn't very productive from three-point range but turned in a solid performance from inside the arc. He finished as the Mavericks' third-leading scorer while pacing the club in assists. After starting 47 of his 74 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, Marshall figures to operate as one of Dallas' first men off the bench this season.

items.headline: Marshall will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale against the Hawks.
items.story: Marshall started in Wednesday's exhibition loss to the Pelicans with Kyrie Irving (rest) unavailable, but Irving is back from his maintenance day. Marshall will be operating in a reserve role for the Mavs this season, so it'll be tough for him to find enough minutes to make an impact in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Marshall will start in Wednesday's preseason game against New Orleans, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Marshall will start for the second time this preseason. The 28-year-old started in 47 regular-season games during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 17.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.2 steals over 31.6 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Marshall tallied 16 points (7-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes during Friday's 135-117 preseason loss to Houston.
items.story: Marshall got to start for a shorthanded Mavericks team in their preseason opener, but that's expected to change once the regular season begins. Noah Weber of TheSmokingCuban.com believes Marshall's playmaking and finishing prowess could allow him to operate more as a point guard off the bench this year, so the forward should still handle a significant role as a member of the second unit.

items.headline: Marshall said during Media Day that improving his three-point shooting was a major focus during the offseason, Austin Veazey of SI.com reports.
items.story: The 28-year-old expressed confidence that the work will translate this season, saying that becoming a more consistent perimeter threat would make him "unstoppable." Marshall averaged a career-high 15.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals across 74 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 despite shooting just 29.1 percent from three. A significant improvement from beyond the arc would add another dimension to his offensive game after Dallas signed him to a three-year extension in August.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) signed a three-year, $52.2 million extension with the Mavericks on Sunday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Marshall signed a three-year pact with Dallas in July 2024 and is now set to remain with the team for the foreseeable future. The 28-year-old wing is coming off a career-best year in 2025-26, during which he averaged 15.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting 51.0 percent from the floor in 29.5 minutes per game across 74 regular-season appearances (47 starts).

items.headline: Marshall (hip) has more competition for playing time after the Mavericks chose Morez Johnson with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Marshall was one of the bigger fantasy beneficiaries of the various injuries to Dallas' frontcourt in 2025-26, averaging a career-high 15.2 points per game to go with 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals in 29.5 minutes per game over 74 regular-season appearances (47 starts). Dallas could lose Khris Middleton in unrestricted free agency this offseason, and Klay Thompson is also a rumored trade candidate, so Marshall still has a chance to battle with Max Christie for the top spot at shooting guard next year even though Johnson could create a crunch for minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Marshall won't play in Sunday's contest against Chicago, marking his third consecutive absence and the end of his 2025-26 campaign. Without him, Klay Thompson and Khris Middleton are in line to see more minutes while receiving additional scoring opportunities.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Bulls.
items.story: It appears as though Marshall will miss a third consecutive game while tending to a left hip contusion. If he's indeed ruled out for Sunday's game, he'll end the 2025-26 regular season averaging a career-high 15.2 points per game along with 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.8 threes over 29.5 minutes per game. Klay Thompson (rest), Khris Middleton and John Poulakidas should operate in elevated roles if Marshall is sidelined.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: As expected after entering the day with a doubtful tag, Marshall will sit out his second consecutive contest due to a left hip contusion he sustained during Tuesday's loss to the Clippers. With Marshall officially sidelined again, the Mavericks will likely lean on Khris Middleton and Tyler Smith to absorb the available minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) is doubtful for Friday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Marshall suffered a left hip injury during Tuesday's clash against the Clippers and was forced to sit out Wednesday's game as a result of the injury. It appears he'll need even more time to recover after being listed as doubtful for Friday, which would mean more playing time for Klay Thompson, Khris Middleton and Tyler Smith in the frontcourt. Expect another update on Marshall's status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Marshall (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Marshall injured his left hip during the Mavericks' 116-103 loss to the Clippers. The injury is severe enough for him to miss the second leg of Dallas' back-to-back set, and his next opportunity to play is Friday against San Antonio. With several Mavericks players missing Wednesday's contest, more minutes will be available for Ryan Nembhard, AJ Johnson, John Poulakidas and Khris Middleton.

items.headline: Marshall is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Suns with a left hip contusion.
items.story: Marshall left Tuesday's game early and was unable to return after logging 20 minutes. With Marshall expected to sit this contest out, the Mavericks may rely more on Khris Middleton, Tyler Smith and AJ Johnson.

items.headline: Marshall (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Tuesday's 116-103 loss to the Clippers and did not return, finishing with six points (3-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three steals and two rebounds across 20 minutes.
items.story: Marshall struggled on the offensive end Tuesday before taking a hard fall and limping to the locker room after attempting to contest a shot in the fourth quarter. It's unclear exactly what the 28-year-old forward is dealing with, though it wouldn't be surprising to see him appear on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game in Phoenix.

items.headline: Marshall (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Tuesday's game against the Clippers, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: While it's unclear exactly why he headed back to the locker room, Marshall contested a shot and took a hard fall before limping off the court. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Marshall recorded 13 points (5-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 32 minutes during Sunday's 134-128 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Even though Cooper Flagg stole the show with a 45-point performance, Marshall was efficient as a shooter and left his mark in other categories, posting at least two tallies in four of the five major categories. Marshall is ending the season on a strong note and has scored in double digits in five of his last six appearances, averaging 17.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Marshall was ejected in the fourth quarter of Friday's game against the Magic after being assessed two technical fouls, Kevin Gray Jr. of AllDLLS.com reports. He'll finish with nine points (3-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
items.story: Marshall was assessed his second technical foul with 10:40 remaining in the final quarter while on the bench, and his ejection came shortly after head coach Jason Kidd was tossed. The 28-year-old forward struggled in his return from a two-game absence due to an illness, and he'll aim to bounce back against the Lakers on Sunday.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is off the injury report for Friday's game versus Orlando.
items.story: Following a two-game absence due to an illness, Marshall is ready to take the floor for the Mavericks on Friday. The forward has averaged 20.9 points, 5.0 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 32.6 minutes per contest in his last seven games.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is out for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Marshall will end up missing both ends of this back-to-back set due to illness. Max Christie and Khris Middleton should both push for minutes in the 30s for the injury-plagued Mavericks on Tuesday.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Marshall was initially listed as probable before being downgraded to questionable Monday, and he's since been ruled out for the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Tuesday in Milwaukee. With Marshall sidelined, Klay Thompson, Khris Middleton and John Poulakidas are candidates to see an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is questionable for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Marshall was previously listed as probable, so he's trending in the wrong direction. If he's unable to give it a go, the Mavericks may need Klay Thompson and Khris Middleton to step up.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is listed as probable for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: It looks like Marshall will be able to play through the illness Monday, but his status won't be officially known until closer to the 8:30 p.m. ET tipoff. He has started each of the Mavericks' last 10 games, and over that span, he has averaged 18.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.1 threes and 1.3 steals over 30.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Marshall posted 19 points (7-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and five steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 100-93 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The five steals were a career high for Marshall, and he's scored at least 16 points in seven of the last eight games. During that stretch, the 28-year-old forward is averaging 20.4 points, 4.8 boards, 4.8 steals, 1.4 steals and 1.1 threes, and as long as he stays healthy he should retain a significant role in the rotation for the injury-depleted Mavs.

items.headline: Marshall finished with 28 points (11-23 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-7 FT), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 37 minutes during Saturday's 138-131 overtime loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Marshall struggled from deep, but he scored 19 of his team-high 28 points during the second half and overtime and was the only Mavericks player to score 20-plus points in Saturday's loss. The sixth-year pro has scored at least 25 points in three of his last four outings and has connected on 47.8 percent of his field-goal attempts over that span. Marshall is averaging a career-high 15.3 points per game this season along with 4.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 0.9 threes and 1.0 steals over 29.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Raynaud is expected to be re-evaluated soon, though he can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer an update on his status. Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa will likely continue seeing increased burn in Raynaud's absence.

items.headline: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Raynaud (knee) is expected to miss at least the first five or six games of the regular season, and potentially longer, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Raynaud is recovering from a right patellar subluxation and appears set to begin the campaign on the sidelines. The young center appeared in 74 games last season, helping anchor Sacramento's frontcourt while Domantas Sabonis battled injuries. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) also sidelined, the Kings will be especially dependent on Sabonis until their reserve centers return.

items.headline: Raynaud has been diagnosed with a right patellar subluxation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: Raynaud was taken back to the locker room in a wheelchair during Saturday's preseason loss to the Warriors, though he has seemingly avoided a serious injury. The big man will still begin the regular season on the inactive list, leaving additional minutes available for the likes of Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell (rest).

items.headline: Raynaud suffered a right knee injury during the second quarter of Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors and will not return, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Raynaud appeared to tweak his knee after bumping into Stephen Curry, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle. The injury was severe enough for Raynaud that he had to be taken off the floor and into the locker room in a wheelchair, and the Kings should have an update on the second-year center once he undergoes more tests on his knee. An extended absence would mean more minutes at center would be available for Dylan Cardwell (rest) and Precious Achiuwa.

items.headline: Raynaud is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Even though Domantas Sabonis (undisclosed) is out Saturday, Raynaud won't start, as Precious Achiuwa will get the nod at center. Raynaud has posted solid numbers in the preseason, tallying 25 points and 18 rebounds across two appearances, and he's expected to see steady minutes in the frontcourt, though he'll mainly operate as Sabonis' backup when the former is healthy.

items.headline: Raynaud totaled 13 points (5-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 24 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Raynaud turned in a strong final line, leading the Kings on the boards on the way to a double-double while also showcasing his ability to protect the rim. He entered the starting lineup Thursday after Domantas Sabonis (undisclosed) was ruled out, and the former took advantage of the opportunity. Raynaud is putting together a solid preseason, totaling 25 points and 18 rebounds across two appearances.

items.headline: Raynaud will start Thursday's preseason game against the Lakers, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: With Domantas Sabonis (undisclosed) out, Raynaud will step into the starting five. He'll be joined in the first unit by Darius Acuff, Zach LaVine, De'Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa.

items.headline: Raynaud recorded 12 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and two assists in 24 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Raynaud was one of Sacramento's first five players off the bench and grabbed three offensive rebounds, though he also committed five turnovers. The second-year big should continue to see plenty of opportunities during the preseason as the Kings evaluate their frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Raynaud registered 13 points (6-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and two rebounds in 18 minutes during France's 84-69 win over Sweden in Sunday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Raynaud made the most of his playing time Sunday, supplying an efficient 13 points. The 2025 second-rounder is preparing to compete with Dylan Cardwell for Sacramento's backup center role behind Domantas Sabonis during training camp in the fall.

items.headline: Raynaud enters his second NBA season after flashing intriguing offensive versatility during his rookie campaign.
items.story: The seven-footer can stretch the floor and facilitate from the frontcourt, giving Sacramento a unique developmental option. However, as long as Domantas Sabonis is in town, Raynaud will likely be competing for reserve minutes. Another year of development could help Raynaud carve out a consistent role in the Kings' rotation, and if he continues to impress, the Kings may be more willing to part ways with Sabonis.

items.headline: Raynaud (rest) is out for Friday's Summer League game against Charlotte, per Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140.
items.story: Raynaud is sitting out the Las Vegas Summer League finale Friday. The 2025 second-rounder is set to compete with Dylan Cardwell for backup center minutes behind Domantas Sabonis (knee) during training camp in the fall.

items.headline: Raynaud (rest) is out for Wednesday's Summer League game against Boston, per Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140.
items.story: Raynaud is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set after playing only 15 minutes Tuesday against Brooklyn. His next opportunity to suit up comes Friday against Charlotte.

items.headline: Raynaud produced 20 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Sunday's 104-85 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Raynaud dominated the glass and consistently created second-chance opportunities for the Kings, grabbing five of his rebounds on the offensive end. He's a double-double machine when given the minutes, but his upside will remain muted as long as Domantas Sabonis is healthy and in Sacramento.

items.headline: Raynaud (rest) is available for Sunday's Summer League game against the Wizards, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Raynaud is set to make his 2026 Summer League debut after sitting out Thursday's win over the Clippers. The 2025 second-rounder is coming off an impressive rookie campaign with Sacramento, averaging 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 26.5 minutes per game over 74 regular-season appearances (56 starts) in 2025-26.

items.headline: Raynaud (rest) is out for Thursday's Summer League game against the Clippers, per Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140.
items.story: The Kings are taking a cautious approach with the 2025 second-rounder's reps this summer. His next chance to play arrives Sunday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Raynaud provided 21 points (7-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 37 minutes during Sunday's 122-110 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Raynaud was one of the most productive rookies in the 2025-26 NBA season despite being a second-round pick, as the Stanford star grabbed a starting role once Domantas Sabonis (knee) was ruled out for the rest of the season and produced impressive numbers. Raynaud finished his first year in The Association with averages of 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.5 steals and 0.5 blocks per game while starting in 56 of his 74 regular-season appearances and logging 26.6 minutes per game. Raynaud also recorded 18 double-doubles and shot 57.1 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Raynaud finished with 23 points (9-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-5 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and one steal in 39 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over Golden State.
items.story: The rookie center just missed his 19th double-double as he's had a strong close to the campaign. Raynaud has scored in double digits in 11 of the last 12 games, averaging 18.8 points, 8.6 boards, 1.9 assists and 0.8 threes while shooting 57.2 percent from the floor and 43.5 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Raynaud notched 11 points (5-12 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 33 minutes during Sunday's 138-109 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: It was the 18th double-double of the season for Raynaud, who continues to be productive in a Kings frontcourt missing Domantas Sabonis (knee), Keegan Murray (ankle) and others. The rookie center's 15 boards represented his best showing on the glass since he pulled down 19 against the pelicans on Feb. 9, and he's scored in double digits in nine of the last 10 games, averaging 18.6 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.8 threes and 1.1 combined steals and blocks over that span while shooting 56.3 percent from the floor and 44.4 percent (8-from-18) from downtown.

items.headline: Raynaud had 28 points (11-14 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-7 FT), nine rebounds and four assists across 29 minutes during Friday's 117-113 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Raynaud's rookie efforts have transformed the future of the Kings' frontcourt. The center will likely headline a youth-based rebuild of the team. It wouldn't be surprising to see the Kings unload Domantas Sabonis to clear some cap room in the offseason, as Raynaud's stellar campaign may have made Sabonis expendable. Raynaud was one rebound shy of hitting his 18th double-double of the season during the win.
