items.headline: Booker is not playing in Saturday's preseason game against the Spurs due to rest, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Booker won't be an option for Saturday's game due to rest, as the Suns are managing his workload carefully with the start of the regular season right around the corner. Booker's next chance to play will come in the rematch against San Antonio on Wednesday.

items.headline: Booker scored 11 points (3-14 FG, 0-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT) and chipped in one assist over 23 minutes in Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The star guard couldn't get his shot to fall, but shaking off any summer rust is what the preseason is for. Booker heads into his 12th season with the Suns as the focal point of the offense and a reliable threat to average better than 25 points a game, but nagging injuries have been an issue for him in recent years. The 29-year-old has played 70 or more games only once in the last six seasons.

items.headline: Booker recorded 13 points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 16 minutes in Monday's 109-107 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Booker was limited to the first half of play in the Suns' first preseason game, but he looked good in his limited minutes and finished with a plus-18 differential. He did a nice job running the offense and was aggressive with his shot selection, so he looks all set up for another big season as the main man in Phoenix.

items.headline: Coach JJ Redick stated Monday that the team is optimistic Reaves (heel) will return for Friday's game against San Antonio, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Reaves has already been downgraded to out for Monday's clash against Utah, which will mark his fifth straight absence due to a bruised left heel. However, the sharpshooter managed to take part in a stay-ready game earlier in the day Monday and was moving well, per Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register. Reaves figures to be in line to take the court Friday as long as he continues to show progress throughout the week.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Jazz, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Reaves will miss a fifth consecutive game due to a bruised left heel. His next chance to suit up will come against the Spurs on Friday. Quentin Grimes should remain in the starting lineup versus Utah, while Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr are likely to see additional minutes off the Lakers' bench.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: The Lakers didn't do any live work Sunday, though this update is still encouraging. Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Reaves is expected to return in one of the Lakers' next two games. Quentin Grimes will likely continue seeing an expanded role for as long as Reaves is out.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Reaves (heel) to return for Monday's matchup with Utah or Friday's game in San Antonio, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
items.story: Reaves will miss his fourth straight game Friday, but it sounds like he'll be back next week. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton will continue to pick up the slack while Reaves is out, and Luka Doncic will see even more usage than usual.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Reaves suffered a heel injury during the 123-112 win over the Bucks on Nov. 11 and will now miss his fourth consecutive contest. It appears the 28-year-old is improving, so he should be considered day-to-day. While Reaves remains on the shelf, Quentin Grimes is expected to stay in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Reaves' (heel) pregame workout went "well," but he remains without an official timetable to return, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Given that Reaves' workout went "well" and the injury has been classified as a "heel bruise," we'd take the "no timetable" comment from Redick with a grain of salt. For now, Reaves should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Kings.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: The star guard was expected to test out his injured heel prior to the contest, but the Lakers don't quite think he's ready to return. With Reaves out for a third consecutive time, Quentin Grimes is primed for another start after going off for a career-high 47 points Tuesday.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) is out for Tuesday's game against the Hornets, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Reaves will miss a second consecutive matchup while tending to a bruised left heel. Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams should continue to see more minutes in Reaves' absence. His next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday against Utah.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Suns, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Reaves is dealing with a left heel bruise he sustained during Wednesday's 123-112 victory over Milwaukee, and he'll now miss his second contest of the season. Luka Doncic will carry the load on offense, while Collin Sexton, Jaden Hardy and Ziaire Williams should see a boost in minutes.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) didn't participate in Saturday's practice, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Reaves sustained a bruised left heel in Wednesday's win over Milwaukee and is considered day-to-day, though this update is not encouraging ahead of Sunday's game against Phoenix. If the 28-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes (finger) and Collin Sexton (head) would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Reaves (heel) won't undergo imaging and is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Suns, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: An official designation for Reaves' status will be given Saturday, according to Buha, and head coach JJ Redick also said Reaves has a bruise on his heel. The star guard is enjoying an excellent start to the season and is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game. If he's sidelined, expect Ziaire Williams to start in the backcourt alongside Luka Doncic.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said that X-rays on Reaves' left heel came back negative, but they won't have another update until he undergoes further imaging back in Los Angeles on Thursday, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Reaves hurt his heel coming down after a layup attempt, but the good news is that an Achilles injury has been ruled out. The Lakers are off until Sunday, but if Reaves needs to miss that game, Ziaire Williams would have a chance to start and Luka Doncic would be extremely busy on offense.

items.headline: Reaves will not return to Wednesday's game against the Bucks due to a left heel injury, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: The severity of Reaves' heel injury isn't currently clear, but the initial X-rays came back negative, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times. He's still set to undergo further testing Thursday. For now, Reaves can be considered questionable for Sunday's game in Phoenix, and if he needs to miss that one, Ziaire Williams would likely return to the starting lineup.

items.headline: Reaves exited Wednesday's game against the Bucks with an undisclosed injury, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Reaves came up lame after a drive to the hoop, subbed himself out of the game, and limped back to the locker room. For now, he should be considered questionable to return, and if he needs to miss time, that will open up minutes for Ziaire Williams and Collin Sexton.

items.headline: Reaves (illness) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: After sitting out Monday in Atlanta due to an illness, Reaves now appears on track to return to the Lakers' backcourt Wednesday. His clearance restores one of Los Angeles' top scoring and playmaking options after a brief absence and likely pushes Ziaire Williams back to the bench

items.headline: Reaves (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Atlanta, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Reaves was added to the injury report earlier in the day after being diagnosed with an illness, and he's since been downgraded to out. This will mark his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign, presumably opening up opportunities for Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr.

items.headline: Reaves is questionable for Monday's game against the Hawks due to an illness, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com.
items.story: The star guard is at risk of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set. Luka Doncic would dominate the usage for the Lakers if Reaves sits out, and Ziaire Williams would likely enter the starting lineup in this case.

items.headline: Reaves recorded 43 points (14-27 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 11-11 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 36 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Reaves was given the keys to the offense with Luka Doncic (back) sidelined, and he made the most of the opportunity, putting up a season-high 43 points. Sunday's contest marked Reaves' fifth career 40-point game. The 28-year-old pro is averaging 29.0 points, 3.8 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 36.3 minutes per game over his last four appearances.

items.headline: Reaves amassed 25 points (8-22 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, two assists and four steals across 38 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over Portland.
items.story: Reaves was Los Angeles' second-leading scorer, but it took him 22 shots to get there, and his outside shot was off all night. He made up for it with a perfect night at the free-throw line and a team-high four steals. On nights when Luka Doncic carries this much of the offense, Reaves doesn't need to be efficient for the Lakers to win, but they'll want a cleaner shooting night from him going forward.

items.headline: Reaves totaled 21 points (7-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds and four assists across 37 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Reaves was the Lakers' second scoring option behind Luka Doncic again and didn't commit a turnover in 37 minutes. Reaves has been productive to start the season, and his scoring floor alongside Doncic makes him a reliable fantasy starter across formats.

items.headline: Reaves ended Sunday's 131-125 victory over Toronto with 19 points (6-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and four assists in 39 minutes.
items.story: The 19 points were actually second on the Lakers for the night, as Luka Doncic put the team on his back with a massive 45-point performance. Reaves has been plenty productive on his own to begin the season, averaging 23.1 points, 5.1 assists, 3.4 boards, 2.3 threes and 1.0 steals in 36.0 minutes while shooting 52.0 percent from the floor and what would be a career-high 40.0 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Reaves chipped in 21 points (9-19 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 37 minutes during Friday's 112-95 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Reaves scored 21 points but had a rough night taking care of the ball, committing a game-high eight turnovers in the loss. The guard has been a reliable second option behind Doncic all season, but his struggles from deep and his giveaways were a big part of why Los Angeles couldn't stop Golden State's run. Look for him to bounce back quickly Sunday against Toronto.

items.headline: Reaves produced 16 points (6-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Without Luka Doncic (back) in the lineup, the Lakers went with a balanced approach on offense, and Reaves was one of four players in purple and gold to score 15 or more points. It was the first time this season the 28-year-old guard failed to deliver 20-plus, and through five games, Reaves is averaging 24.4 points, 5.4 assists, 3.4 boards, 2.6 threes and 1.2 steals while shooting what would be a career-best 56.9 percent from the floor and 48.1 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Reaves supplied 26 points (8-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 6-7 FT), four rebounds and seven assists across 39 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Reaves was a strong second option behind Luka Doncic, scoring 26 points efficiently and adding seven assists across a team-high 39 minutes. The guard has carried a heavy workload early in the season, and Los Angeles needs his secondary scoring and playmaking to take pressure off Doncic.

items.headline: Reaves finished with 29 points (7-12 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 11-13 FT), one rebound, four assists, two blocks and one steal across 36 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: The Lakers have gone 3-0 to begin the season, and Reaves has played a significant role in the hot start. He's churning out first-round value, averaging 26.7 points, 6.3 assists, 2.7 triples, 1.7 steals and 1.0 blocks per game on 63.9 percent shooting from the field and 89.7 percent at the stripe.

items.headline: Smith registered one point (0-1 FG, 1-4 FT) and four rebounds across six minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Smith struggled at the free-throw line and committed four fouls during his brief appearance. The 26-year-old big man was unable to establish much of a role despite Jalen Duren (ankle) being unavailable, with Paul Reed handling the bulk of Detroit's center minutes. Smith remains off the fantasy radar in standard leagues.

items.headline: Smith finished with six points (3-4 FG), six rebounds, two assists and one block in 10 minutes during Wednesday's 128-106 preseason victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Smith collected five defensive rebounds and converted three of his four shots, making a noticeable impact despite his brief appearance. The reserve big man also avoided committing a turnover, but he faces considerable competition for frontcourt minutes behind Detroit's established rotation players.

items.headline: The Pistons picked up their 2026-27 team option on Smith's contract Monday, per Keith Smith of Spotrac.com.
items.story: Smith brings the Pistons some depth at the center position behind Jalen Duren and Paul Reed. Smith appeared in just 15 regular-season contests a year ago, averaging 3.7 points and 3.3 rebounds in 9.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Smith provided four points (2-2 FG), two rebounds and one steal over five minutes during Sunday's 125-94 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Playing in his second NBA season, Smith was mostly reduced to G League appearances. With the Pistons, he appeared in just 15 regular-season contests with averages of 3.7 points and 3.3 rebounds in 9.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Smith signed a two-year contract with the Pistons on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Smith was previously on a two-way contract with Detroit. He's made a total of 13 NBA appearances, posting averages of 3.9 points, 3.5 rebounds, 0.9 assists and 0.5 blocks in 10.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Smith (knee) is available for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Smith will shed his questionable tag due to a right knee contusion and suit up Saturday. However, he isn't guaranteed to see meaningful minutes with Jalen Duren (suspension) back in the lineup.

items.headline: Smith is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Bulls due to a right knee contusion.
items.story: Smith may have sustained the injury during the Pistons' 126-111 win over the Knicks on Thursday, when he played 15 minutes and finished with three points, three rebounds and two assists. Even if he were cleared to play, Smith's minutes would likely take a significant dip, given that Jalen Duren will be available to play Saturday after serving a two-game suspension.

items.headline: Smith recorded up three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 15 minutes during Wednesday's 113-95 win over the Raptors.
items.story: With Jalen Duren and Isaiah Stewart both suspended, Smith entered the rotation as the backup to center Paul Reed, who entered the starting five in Duren's stead. The appearance was just Smith's sixth of the season with Detroit and his first at any level since Jan. 26, when he sustained a calf injury while playing for the G League's Motor City Cruise. Now healthy again, Smith should be part of the rotation for the Pistons' next game Feb. 19 versus the Knicks before Duren returns from his two-game ban Feb. 21 at Chicago.

items.headline: Smith (calf) isn't listed on the Pistons' injury report for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: The two-way center has made just five appearances for Detroit all season and hadn't seen action in the G League with the Motor City Cruise since Jan. 26 while he managed a calf issue, but he joined the Pistons for morning shootaround Wednesday and should be available to play in the club's final game before the All-Star break, per Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press. With Jalen Duren (two games) and Isaiah Stewart (seven games) receiving suspensions for their roles in a brawl that occurred in Monday's win over the Hornets, Paul Reed will likely step into a high-minute role as the Pistons' starting center, but Smith could be part of the rotation as Reed's backup until Duren is back in the fold.

items.headline: Smith accumulated nine points (1-7 FG, 7-8 FT), 14 rebounds, one assist, four blocks and one steal in 26 minutes during Saturday's 98-92 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Smith played just the sixth game of his career, dominating the glass with a career-high 14 rebounds while adding a career-high four blocks. Both Jalen Duren (ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) were sidelined, while Paul Reed was limited to just 22 minutes due to foul trouble. This allowed Smith to step into the largest role of his career, rewarding anyone who took a chance on him in deeper formats. While this was a great performance, it should be treated as nothing more than an outlier unless Duren and Stewart continue to miss time.

items.headline: Smith finished with six points (3-4 FG), seven rebounds, two assists and one block over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 124-113 victory over Chicago.
items.story: Smith played a season-high 16 minutes, moving into the rotation after it was earlier announced that Detroit would be without a number of its starters due to various injuries. This performance should not be viewed as anything other than an outlier, given he has not even been in the rotation for the majority of the season.

items.headline: Smith produced 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-7 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one block in 12 minutes of Monday's 128-112 preseason win over Memphis.
items.story: Jalen Duren was out with hamstring soreness, allowing Smith to absorb some backup center minutes behind Isaiah Stewart. Smith, who is on a two-way contract, is expected to spend a lot of time in the G League this season. To his credit, he certainly showed the coaching staff that he'll be ready if his name is called upon this season.

items.headline: Smith tallied 16 points (4-7 FG, 8-12 FT), six rebounds, three blocks and one assist over 26 minutes in Tuesday's 89-73 Summer League loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Smith came up short of securing his third double-double of Summer League play but still managed to post 16 points, largely fueled by frequent trips to the free-throw line. The center spent nearly all of the 2024-25 season in the G League but made one regular-season NBA appearance with the Pistons, logging 14 points and eight rebounds in 22 minutes against the Bucks on April 13.

items.headline: Smith racked up 15 points (4-7 FG, 7-8 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists and two blocks across 23 minutes during Sunday's 98-83 Summer League win against the Rockets.
items.story: Smith has recorded double-doubles in two straight games during the Las Vegas Summer League. The Mississippi State product continues to be a monster on the glass for Detroit, as he has racked up 23 boards across the last two games.

items.headline: Smith generated 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-7 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks over 26 minutes of Friday's 104-86 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: Smith's high-motor play style was on full display Friday, notching a double-double and accumulating three combined steals-plus-blocks in 26 minutes. Six of his 11 rebounds came on the offensive end, where he outmuscled New York's bigs for second-chance opportunities.

items.headline: Smith signed a two-way contract with the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, Jake Fischer of Yahoo Sports reports.
items.story: Smith has been a valuable commodity for Detroit's G League team, as he's averaged 17.7 points, 11.7 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.3 blocks per game through nine G League games this year. Obviously, the 24-year-old is not expected to replicate that output at the NBA level, but he'll provide the parent club with some upside and center depth.

items.headline: Williams isn't in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Jazz, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Williams will retreat to a bench role after being held to 12 total points in his previous two appearances as part of the starting lineup. Jake LaRavia is drawing the start at power forward as a result.

items.headline: Williams will start Wednesday against the Jazz, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Williams will replace Jake LaRavia in the first unit for Wednesday's game. As a starter this season, Williams is averaging 11.4 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.8 triples and 1.6 steals per contest.

items.headline: Williams closed with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal across 24 minutes before fouling out of Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets.
items.story: After opening the year as a starter, Williams is watching other members of the team gain a foothold in the first unit. Quentin Grimes erupted for a career-high 47 points Wednesday, while both Matisse Thybulle and Jake LaRavia have effectively been full-time starters for the Lakers in the early going.

items.headline: Williams will start Monday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: With Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (finger) sidelined, Williams will join the first unit for the first time since Oct. 27. In four starts this season, he's averaged 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals across 28.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Williams accumulated eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Williams gave the Lakers useful minutes off the bench, knocking down a pair of three-pointers and picking up two steals in his 20 minutes. The forward missed three straight games with soreness in his left foot, an issue going back to the preseason, before being cleared to return earlier in the week. The Lakers begin a back-to-back Sunday, so he could be held out for one of those games.

items.headline: Williams contributed 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over the Kings.
items.story: After beginning the year as a starter, Williams seems to be getting eased back into action following a recent absence. He'll continue competing with Jake LaRavia for the Lakers' fifth starting lineup position.

items.headline: Williams notched nine points (3-6 FG, 3-6 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 15 minutes during Monday's 138-117 win over the Heat.
items.story: Williams returned from a three-game absence due to a foot injury, but he operated off the bench for the first time this season and played limited minutes. Over his first four appearances, the sixth-year wing averaged 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals in 28.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Williams won't start Monday's game against the Heat, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Williams is returning from a three-game absence due to a foot injury, though he'll slide to the second unit for the first time this season. Jake LaRavia will draw a fourth consecutive start.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is good to go for Monday against the Heat.
items.story: After three straight absences, Williams is set to return to the rotation. In his absence, Jake LaRavia had made two consecutive starts on the wings.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is out for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Williams will now miss his third consecutive outing as he recovers from a left foot injury. Jake LaRavia is in line for a second straight start, while Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili should continue to see an uptick in minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raptors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Williams has missed the past two games for the Lakers, and with Sunday's game being the first of a back-to-back, he might need to spend one more game on the inactive list. If he's out again, Quentin Grimes will help fill his minutes.

items.headline: Williams has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left foot injury management, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
items.story: Williams will miss a second consecutive contest due to a left foot issue, and his next chance to play will come Sunday against Toronto. Quentin Grimes will likely continue to see increased playing time in Williams' absence.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is questionable for Friday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Williams started in each of the first four games of the regular season but was unable to play in Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers due to a foot injury. Jake LaRavia would likely remain in the Lakers' starting five if Williams is not cleared to play Friday.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Williams is sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jake LaRavia seem to be the most likely options to replace Williams in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Williams ended Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers with 11 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists and two steals in 29 minutes.
items.story: Williams made the most of his limited offensive opportunities, connecting on four of five field-goal attempts while adding four assists and two steals. The 25-year-old forward has started each of the Lakers' first four games, giving him a relatively stable role despite his modest scoring volume. His ability to contribute across multiple categories makes him worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Williams notched 14 points (5-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, one block and two steals over 31 minutes during Friday's 125-117 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Williams was efficient as a starter, hitting five of seven shots and finishing as one of six Lakers with at least 13 points. He has started both games since joining Los Angeles, and his minutes went up from the opener. Williams should hold on to the starting spot to help the Lakers on defense.

items.headline: Williams contributed nine points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds, four assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 127-105 win over the Warriors.
items.story: It was somewhat of a surprise to see Williams win the Opening Night starting gig over Quentin Grimes, who started four of Los Angeles' five preseason games. Although Williams should hold streaming appeal while working with the first unit, he figures to have a tenuous hold on the role.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is available and will start in Friday's preseason game versus the Nuggets, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Williams has been bothered by a foot contusion. However, he will get the green light to suit up and start in the preseason finale. The 25-year-old, who agreed to a deal with the Lakers in the offseason, averaged a career-high 10.2 points along with 2.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.4 steals over 22.9 minutes per contest in 56 regular-season games with the Nets in 2025-26. Williams should see some minutes throughout the 2026-27 campaign, though he will likely be off the floor more often than not.

items.headline: Williams (foot) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Williams has been dealing with a foot contusion recently, though he's trending in the right direction ahead of Friday's preseason finale against Denver. The 25-year-old swingman can be considered questionable for that contest until the Lakers provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Williams (foot) will not play in Tuesday's preseason matchup against Golden State, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Williams continues to deal with a foot contusion that has kept him out of recent preseason action. Coach JJ Redick indicated that the forward remains day-to-day, suggesting the injury isn't considered a long-term concern. Williams' next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against Denver in the Lakers' preseason finale.

items.headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Saturday that Williams is dealing with a foot contusion, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Williams has missed two straight preseason games due to the injury, which was previously labeled as general soreness. It's unclear when he'll be cleared to play, but it doesn't sound like he's practicing at full capacity yet.

items.headline: Williams won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Kings due to general soreness, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Williams was also held out for the second half of a preseason back-to-back Tuesday, and he'll take a seat again Thursday with coach JJ Redick indicating a number of Lakers are dealing with minor injuries, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com. Williams' next opportunity to return will arrive Tuesday against Golden State.

items.headline: Williams (rest) is out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: Williams will rest on the second leg of a preseason back-to-back set. His absence should open up minutes for Jarred Vanderbilt and Sandro Mamukelashvili.

items.headline: Williams finished with 13 points (4-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and three steals in 21 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Williams drew the start with Austin Reaves (ankle) and Collin Sexton (lower body) unavailable and made a strong impression on both ends of the floor. The 25-year-old is competing with Jake LaRavia and several other wings for a prominent role, and his combination of perimeter shooting and defense should help his case.

items.headline: Williams will start Monday's preseason game against the Kings, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: The Lakers will be without Austin Reaves (ankle) and Collin Sexton (lower body) Monday, and Jake LaRavia will come off the bench, paving the way for Williams to start. The 25-year-old is competing with LaRavia for a starting role this season, so Monday will serve as an important audition for Williams.

items.headline: Williams is expected to compete with Jake LaRavia for the final spot in the Lakers' starting five during training camp and the preseason, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Lakers would ideally like their fifth starter to provide positional versatility, rebounding and off-ball production alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Williams has the size to fit that profile, and his performance during camp and the preseason should determine whether he can separate himself from LaRavia and the other candidates.

items.headline: Williams (foot) and the Lakers agreed on a one-year contract Monday, per Dan Woike of The Athletic.
items.story: After spending the past two seasons with the Nets, Williams is joining the Lakers to help provide depth on the wing. The fifth-year swingman is likely to compete with Dalton Knecht, Jarred Vanderbilt and rookie first-rounder Cameron Carr (thumb) for reserve minutes during the 2026-27 campaign, so it remains to be seen how much fantasy relevance Williams will have.

items.headline: The Nets declined their $6.25 million team option on Williams' (foot) contract Sunday, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: While Williams could still re-sign with Brooklyn, he's set to enter unrestricted free agency after spending the past two seasons with the Nets. The 24-year-old wing missed the team's final five games in 2025-26 with a left foot issue, though he should be ready for training camp. Over 56 regular-season games (13 starts) last season, he averaged a career-high 10.2 points along with 2.4 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.1 assists in 22.9 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Williams (foot) will miss Sunday's regular-season finale against the Raptors, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Jalen Wilson and Trevon Scott should continue to get all the run they can handle Sunday, and Ochai Agbaji will have a chance to get into the rotation. Williams will end his age-24 season with averages of 10.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.5 triples and 1.4 steals per game.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: The Nets used just seven players Thursday for the front end of the back-to-back set, and they will again be extremely shorthanded Friday. Williams is not a lock to return for the season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Williams (foot) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Williams will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left foot issue, and he'll have just two more chances to suit up again this season. With the 24-year-old wing sidelined, Ochai Agbaji, Jalen Wilson and Malachi Smith are candidates to see an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Williams (foot) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Williams will miss a second consecutive contest. While he is sidelined, Drake Powell and Jalen Wilson are candidates to see more action versus the Bucks.

items.headline: Williams has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Wizards due to left foot soreness.
items.story: With Williams unavailable Sunday, there will be more opportunities for Ochai Agbaji, Chaney Johnson and Josh Minott. Williams' next chance to play will come Tuesday versus the Bucks.

items.headline: Williams won't start Friday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Terance Mann will return to the first unit, pushing Williams out of the starting five. The 24-year-old forward went unused off the bench in Sunday's win over Sacramento and isn't guaranteed meaningful burn if he's not starting. Still, he has averaged 14.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.6 steals over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Williams will start Tuesday's game against the Hornets, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: After going unused off the bench in Sunday's win over Sacramento, Williams will return to the first unit Tuesday. As a starter this season (12 games), the 24-year-old forward has averaged 13.3 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.4 steals and 1.1 assists in 24.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Williams (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Sunday in the Nets' 116-99 win over the Kings.
items.story: To open up playing time for every player on the 15-man roster and all three two-way players, head coach Jordi Fernandez has been shaking up his rotation from game to game over the last few weeks as the season winds down. Williams ended up being squeezed out Sunday, ending a stretch of eight consecutive appearances in which he had averaged 13.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.3 steals, 1.4 assists and 1.3 three-pointers in 22.6 minutes per game. While Williams will stick in the rotation more often than not over the Nets' final seven games, his unexpected absence Sunday illustrates the risk that he and all Brooklyn players will carry as streaming options down the stretch.

items.headline: Williams won't start in Sunday's game against the Kings, according to Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: Williams started in each of the Nets' last five contests, most recently amassing 16 points, two rebounds, two assists and three steals in Friday's 116-99 loss to the Lakers. However, the 24-year-old will head back to the bench Sunday, with Terance Mann returning to the starting lineup.

items.headline: Williams recorded 19 points (6-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), six steals, two assists and one rebound across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 109-106 loss to Golden State.
items.story: The 19 points led the Nets on the night, while the six steals were a career high for Williams. The fifth-year forward has started six of the last seven games, although he hasn't played more than 25 minutes in any of those contests. Over that stretch, Williams has averaged 13.0 points, 2.3 boards, 2.1 steals, 1.3 assists and 1.3 three-pointers while shooting 50.9 percent from the floor and 50 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Williams recorded 16 points (4-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 7-7 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 134-99 loss to Portland.

With Jalen Duren (hamstring) out, Reed has become a fixture in the rotation and is averaging 11.3 points and 7.8 rebounds.

items.headline: Reed had 13 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-6 FT), 11 rebounds and three assists in 38 minutes during Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime win over the Wizards.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench for the second straight game, Reed closed for the Pistons, recording his second double-double of the season, while also matching his season-high with 38 minutes. While his opportunity was helped by the fact that John Collins had some foul issues, Reed feels like someone who should continue to be rostered in most formats, at least until Jalen Duren returns from his hamstring injury.

items.headline: Reed will come off the bench Monday against Washington, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Reed averaged 12.1 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.3 steals in seven straight starts for the Pistons, but the team has elected to make a lineup change Monday. Daniss Jenkins will enter the first unit in Reed's place.

items.headline: Reed produced eight points (4-8 FG, 0-2 FT) and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Reed remained in the starting lineup due to Jalen Duren (hamstring) being unavailable, and the former made an impact on the offensive glass, collecting eight of his 10 rebounds on that end. However, Reed's playing time was limited to 20 minutes, and he failed to record a steal or block. The big man offers short-term rebounding upside while Duren is sidelined, but his modest workload limits his fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Reed racked up 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals across 28 minutes during Monday's 124-91 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Reed turned in another strong two-way performance, filling in for the injured Jalen Duren (hamstring). In four appearances over the past week, he has been a top-30 asset in nine-category leagues, averaging 15.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 0.8 three-pointers and 3.0 combined steals and blocks. The eventual return of Duren will certainly impact Reed's production. However, given how well the team has functioned with Reed as the starting center, there is a case to be made for him playing over John Collins, alongside Duren.

items.headline: Reed tallied 22 points (9-12 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block across 26 minutes in Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Reed continues to take advantage of the absence of Jalen Duren (hamstring), leading Detroit in scoring while narrowly missing his second double-double. Reed has at least 19 points and nine rebounds in two of his last three games, establishing himself as a valuable temporary fantasy option. However, his workload and production could decline significantly once Duren returns to the starting lineup.

items.headline: Reed will start Sunday's game against the 76ers, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Reed will enter the starting five due to Jalen Duren (hamstring) being out. Reed performed well during Friday's win over the Heat, logging 19 points and 11 rebounds in 26 minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Reed notched 19 points (8-11 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 11 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat.
items.story: Reed capitalized on Jalen Duren's early departure due to a right thigh injury, with the former recording a double-double while playing an expanded role off the bench. His efficient scoring and strong rebounding highlighted his ability to contribute when given substantial minutes. Reed could become an appealing short-term fantasy option if Duren misses additional time, although his role would likely diminish once Detroit's starting center returns. With Duren's status uncertain for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Reed could be in the line for a bigger role this weekend, though it'd be in a tough matchup.

items.headline: Reed accumulated six points (2-3 FG, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 17 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Reed turned in a serviceable performance, doing just enough to keep him in the discussion for standard fantasy leagues. Assuming he can play at least 17 minutes per game, he should be able to do just enough to hold value, particularly in big-friendly builds. Given that Javonte Green was shooting the lights out in this one, there is also a chance that Reed could see a little more court time on most nights, a fact that shouldn't be lost on fantasy managers.

items.headline: Reed supplied seven points (2-4 FG, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (reconditioning) back in action, Reed shifted to the bench after starting Detroit's first two preseason games. The big man failed to score in double figures after reaching that mark in each of his first two outings. However, he made an impact defensively with a game-high two blocks. Reed is in line to serve as Duren's primary backup during the regular season.

items.headline: Reed posted 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and two steals in Saturday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Reed was one of five Detroit players -- and one of three starters -- to score in double digits, and he finished second in both rebounds and steals. Reed made the most of the absence of Jalen Duren (rest), but when the latter is healthy, Reed will operate as his backup off the bench, limiting his fantasy upside considerably.

items.headline: Reed accumulated 10 points (2-6 FG, 6-6 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 21 minutes during Monday's 109-107 preseason victory over the Suns.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (rest) sitting out the preseason opener, Reed was elevated into the starting lineup. To no one's surprise, he made the most of his opportunity, contributing adequately on both ends of the floor. Although the recent re-signing of Duren does put a cap on what Reed might be able to do this season, the fact that Isaiah Stewart is no longer around can't be overlooked. Reed is slated to serve as the primary backup behind Duren, a role that Stewart filled last season. Assuming he can flirt with 20 minutes per game, Reed still makes sense as a sneaky late-round flier.

items.headline: Reed will start Monday's preseason game against the Suns, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (rest) out, Reed will enter the starting lineup in Detroit's preseason opener. The 27-year-old is expected to operate as the Pistons' primary backup behind Duren in 2026-27.

items.headline: Reed will be in line for increased playing time and is expected to operate as the Pistons' backup center in 2026-27, per Hunter Patterson of The Athletic.
items.story: The Pistons remain in contract talks with Jalen Duren, but assuming the restricted free agent returns for at least one more season, Reed should operate as Detroit's primary backup center. The club traded Isaiah Stewart to the Grizzlies in June, and all signs point toward Reed taking on an increased role. The 27-year-old center played double-digit minutes in 42 of his regular-season appearances (11 starts) in 2025-26, averaging 10.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals while shooting 62.6 percent from the field across 18.3 minutes per contest in those outings.

items.headline: The Pistons fully guaranteed Reed's $5.6 million contract for the 2026-27 season, Jake Fischer of BleacherReport.com reports.
items.story: This was essentially a formality for the Pistons after Reed put together a solid 2025-26 campaign. Across 65 regular-season contests, he shot 61.7 percent from the field for averages of 7.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.9 blocks and 0.9 steals in 13.9 minutes per contest. He's penciled in as the backup center ahead of the new campaign, assuming Jalen Duren ultimately re-signs.

items.headline: Reed ended Sunday's 125-94 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals with four points (2-5 FG), four rebounds and one assist across eight minutes.
items.story: Reed rarely saw big workloads for the Pistons and started just 11 regular-season games, but he was a very reliable reserve center. Across 65 regular-season contests, he shot 61.7 percent from the field for averages of 7.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.9 blocks and 0.9 steals in 13.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Reed ended with 17 points (7-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block over 16 minutes during Friday's 115-94 win over the Cavaliers in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Reed has been more active off the bench in the Pistons' last four games after being a non-factor for the majority of Detroit's postseason run. He has scored in double digits in each of his last four outings, averaging 13.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 0.8 blocks over 14.3 minutes during that span. Reed has supplanted Isaiah Stewart as the preferred big man off the bench behind starting center Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Reed logged 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Reed played the entire fourth quarter, as well as the overtime period, supplanting Jalen Duren, who once again struggled to have any sort of tangible impact. While Reed was able to provide the team with some much-needed energy, it was not enough as Detroit snatched defeat from the jaws of victory, falling to a 3-2 series deficit.

items.headline: Reed tallied 11 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 FT) and three rebounds over 10 minutes during the Pistons' 116-109 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals on Saturday.
items.story: Reed was a healthy DNP for the first two games of the series, but the veteran big man checked in during the third quarter of Saturday's game. He made an immediate impact off the bench, connecting on all of his shots from both the field and charity stripe, and his plus-11 point differential was second-best on the Pistons behind Ausar Thompson (plus-12). Given his solid play off the bench in Game 3, Reed should be part of Detroit's rotation for Game 4 on Monday.

items.headline: Reed had six points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and three blocks in 11 minutes during Friday's 93-79 victory over the Magic in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Reed moved back into the rotation, logging 11 minutes, the most he has played thus far in the playoffs. With Isaiah Stewart struggling to impact the game, Reed was thrown in, providing the team with his usual assortment of rebounds and defensive stats. The series is now tied at 3-3, with the two teams heading back to Detroit for Game 7.

items.headline: Reed (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Pistons' 94-88 loss to the Magic in Game 4 of the first-round playoff series.
items.story: After seeing action in each of the Pistons' final 20 games of the regular season, Reed has essentially fallen out of the rotation through Detroit's first four playoff contests while head coach J.B. Bickerstaff has leaned almost exclusively on Jalen Duren and Isaiah Stewart as the team's options at center. Reed has appeared in just two of the four games of the series, making a 45-second cameo in garbage time of a Game 2 win and then logging seven minutes in Game 3, when Duren contended with foul trouble.

items.headline: Reed will come off the bench for Game 1 of the Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Magic on Sunday, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: This is an expected development with Jalen Duren healthy again. Reed was sharp in a spot start for the regular-season finale with 26 points (11-11 FG, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, three steals and three blocks in 21 minutes.

items.headline: Reed recorded 26 points (11-11 FG, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, three steals and three blocks in 21 minutes during Sunday's 133-121 win over the Pacers.
items.story: Reed put together a flawless performance Sunday, logging a game-high 26 points without missing a shot or committing a turnover. On top of an impressive offensive display, Reed was productive on the defensive end, sending back three shots and collecting three steals. With Detroit now entering the playoffs, Reed's role figures to decrease, but he enters the postseason in outstanding form.

items.headline: Reed will start Sunday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (knee) out, Reed will get the starting nod in Detroit's regular-season finale. As a starter this season (10 games), the big man has averaged 14.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.9 blocks and 1.8 steals across 27.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Reed won't start Wednesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Reed got the start in Monday's 123-107 loss to Orlando, finishing with nine points, six rebounds, two assists and one block across 19 minutes. However, with Tobias Harris (knee) available, Reed will come off the bench.

items.headline: Reed is starting Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Reed will slide into the starting lineup Monday with Tobias Harris (knee) sidelined. Reed impressed in his last chance to start March 30 against the Thunder, when he finished with 21 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks in 34 minutes.

items.headline: Reed provided 10 points (4-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds, one block and two steals in 18 minutes during Saturday's 116-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Reed provided a solid boost off the bench Saturday, and he was far more involved across the board than in his previous showing, when he was held to four points and four rebounds in 16 minutes Thursday against Minnesota. The DePaul product has scored in double figures in four of his last five appearances and is averaging 11.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.6 blocks in 19.6 minutes during this stretch.

items.headline: Reed won't start Tuesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (knee) out, Reed got the start in Monday's 114-110 overtime loss to Oklahoma City, finishing with 21 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, four blocks and one steal. However, with Duren back in the lineup, Reed will return to the bench, likely limiting him to roughly 15-20 minutes of work.

items.headline: Reed finished with 21 points (7-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, four blocks and one steal across 34 minutes during Monday's 114-110 overtime loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Making his first start since Feb. 19 with Jalen Duren (knee) and Isaiah Stewart (calf) both unavailable, Reed delivered his third double-double of the season while scoring at least 20 points for the first time since Feb. 11. The 26-year-old center has chipped in double-digit points in five of the last eight games as he handles a bigger role in the frontcourt in Stewart's absence, averaging 12.1 points, 4.8 boards, 1.9 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.9 steals in just 18.5 minutes over that stretch while shooting 58.5 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Holiday closed with 18 points (7-13 FG, 4-5 3Pt), two rebounds, five assists and two steals across 28 minutes during Monday's 128-111 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Holiday continues to provide reliable production as Portland's sixth man, serving as a primary ball-handler for the second unit. His combination of perimeter shooting, playmaking and defensive contributions gives him solid fantasy value despite coming off the bench.

items.headline: Holiday registered 22 points (8-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, seven assists and four steals in 31 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Holiday delivered consecutive 20-point performances for the first time this season, adding a season-high four steals against his former team. With Deni Avdija (foot) sidelined, Holiday has assumed greater playmaking responsibility. His combination of assists, perimeter shooting and defensive production makes him a valuable category-league option while Portland remains shorthanded.

items.headline: Holiday tallied 23 points (7-19 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block over 31 minutes in Tuesday's 106-105 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Holiday was much more involved in the offense due to Deni Avdija (foot) being sidelined, finishing with a season-high 23 points and a team-high six dimes in the narrow loss. Holiday has been a top-100 player this season, averaging 13.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 2.5 triples and 1.0 blocks per game on 46.5 percent shooting from the field and 86.1 percent at the line.

items.headline: Holiday posted 19 points (5-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 118-108 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Although he hasn't entered the starting lineup, the veteran guard remains close to a must-roster fantasy player amid Ja Morant's (hamstring) absence. Over his past seven appearances, Holiday has averaged 14.1 points, 3.9 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 three-pointers per game while shooting a sizzling 52.5 percent from deep.

items.headline: Holiday closed Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers with 12 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and seven assists in 31 minutes.
items.story: Holiday was efficient off the bench and finished second on the Blazers in assists behind Deni Avdija. He's settled into a sixth-man role, running the second unit and closing some games, but his usage is spiking due to Ja Morant's (hamstring) absence.

items.headline: Holiday closed with 15 points (5-9 FG, 5-9 3Pt), four rebounds and one steal in 28 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 132-119 victory over the Suns.
items.story: The veteran guard set a new season high with the five made three-pointers. Holiday has scored in double digits in five of seven games to begin the season as the engine of Portland's second unit, averaging 13.4 points, 4.4 boards, 4.1 assists, 2.4 threes and 1.1 steals in 26.0 minutes while shooting 52.5 percent from the floor and 42.5 percent from long range.

items.headline: Holiday tallied 17 points (7-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt), eight rebounds, 10 assists and a steal across 29 minutes in Monday's 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Holiday delivered an excellent all-around performance off the bench, finishing just two rebounds shy of a triple-double. His 10 assists highlighted his importance as a facilitator, while efficient perimeter shooting further boosted his fantasy production. Holiday's ability to contribute across several categories provides considerable value, although his reserve role could lead to occasional fluctuations in playing time and overall production. He should be fine as long as his minutes hover around the 25-30 range.

items.headline: Holiday registered 22 points (8-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Holiday gave Portland a big lift off the bench. The veteran guard's scoring and defensive versatility have given the Blazers one of the league's deepest backcourts. His role should stay prominent with Shaedon Sharpe (knee) out.

items.headline: Holiday (hand) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Holiday sat out Friday's preseason finale due to right hand soreness, though he'll return to action in Wednesday's regular-season opener. The veteran guard appears likely to begin the season with the second unit, and he faces competition for playing time from Scoot Henderson and Vit Krejci.

items.headline: Holiday is out for Friday's preseason finale against the Warriors due to right hand soreness.
items.story: The 36-year-old veteran will skip Portland's final exhibition game with some soreness in his shooting hand, but this shouldn't be anything that impacts his status for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Suns. With Holiday unavailable, expect more minutes for Scoot Henderson and Vit Krejci.

items.headline: Holiday supplied 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-3 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Holiday's shot wasn't cooperating, but he still reached double figures. It will be a close call between Holiday and Ja Morant in deciding who will run alongside Damian Lillard in the first unit, but most expect Morant to edge out Holiday to start the season.

items.headline: Holiday won't start Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Holiday got the starting nod in Monday's blowout win over the London Lions, though he'll slide to the second unit in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan will start against Sacramento.

items.headline: Holiday finished with six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds and three assists across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: The veteran point guard got the start in place of the resting Damian Lillard on Monday. Holiday is expected to handle a reserve role once the regular season begins, but he could still push to play 30 minutes per game while Shaedon Sharpe (knee) is on the shelf.

items.headline: Holiday won't start Wednesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Holiday has been a full-time starter for most of his career, though he isn't guaranteed to begin the 2026-27 campaign in a starting role. The Trail Blazers will start Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan in their preseason opener.

items.headline: Holiday is expected to spend more time on the wing this season, per Ramona Shelburne of ESPN.com.
items.story: The veteran point guard averaged 16.3 points and 6.1 assists per game last year, his most since 2022-23 with the Bucks, but Holiday is likely to see fewer ballhandling responsibilities now that Ja Morant and Damian Lillard are manning the backcourt. Toumani Camara is the favorite to start at small forward for Portland, but Holiday is positioned for a very significant role off the bench and is worthy of a late-round fantasy pick. He should remain a major threat from deep after hitting a career-high 2.6 three-pointers per game in 2025-26.

items.headline: Holiday is in danger of handling a lesser role in 2026-27 after Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade this summer.
items.story: Additionally, it remains to be seen how the Trail Blazers will choose to deploy the returning Damian Lillard (Achilles) next year. Holiday is coming off a resurgent 2025-26 regular season, averaging 16.3 points, 6.1 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game in 53 appearances, so he at least appears to be the early favorite to start at shooting guard. Shaedon Sharpe and Scoot Henderson will also be battling for key roles, further making Holiday's fantasy forecast difficult to predict.

items.headline: Holiday supplied eight points (3-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and seven assists across 40 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Holiday couldn't find the bottom of the basket in the Game 5 loss. He made a decent contribution in secondary categories, but the backcourt combo of Holiday and Scoot Henderson was anemic in the scoring column. Holiday is still under contract with Portland for another year, so he's expected to return to the team and continue with the first unit. Over 53 regular-season games, Holiday averaged 16.3 points, 6.1 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals.

items.headline: Holiday notched 29 points (12-18 FG, 5-9 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and four steals in 41 minutes during Friday's 120-108 loss to San Antonio in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The veteran guard led the Blazers in scoring on the night, but it wasn't enough to pick up a win even with Victor Wembanyama (concussion) sidelined for the visitors. Holiday is averaging a whopping 38.7 minutes a game to begin the series, with the 35-year-old turning that workload into averages of 18.0 points, 8.3 assists, 5.0 boards, 2.7 threes and 2.0 steals per contest, and he'll likely be leaned on heavily again in Game 4 on Sunday.

items.headline: Holiday logged 16 points (6-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine assists, five rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 39 minutes in Tuesday's 106-103 Game 2 win over the Spurs in the first round of the playoffs.
items.story: The veteran guard struggled with efficiency in the win but still finished as Portland's second-leading scorer behind Scoot Henderson (31 points). Holiday has shot just 31.3 percent from the field through two first-round outings, though the 35-year-old led all players in assists Tuesday and has dished out 20 dimes in the series. He also tied the game-high mark in blocks in Game 2.

items.headline: Holiday posted nine points (4-15 FG, 1-7 3Pt), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Sunday's 111-98 loss to San Antonio in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: It's the second time in seven April contests that the veteran point guard has dished double-digit assists. Holiday's production has been inconsistent this month, and during that seven-game stretch, he's averaging 17.3 points, 6.9 assists, 5.6 boards and 2.9 threes while shooting just 38.3 percent from the floor and 31.7 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Holiday chipped in 23 points (8-18 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and one block in 33 minutes during Sunday's 122-110 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Holiday posted a strong stat line in the regular-season finale, and he's been one of the most consistent players for Portland all season long. The veteran floor general, who figures to play a big role for the Blazers in their postseason run as they'll attempt to get past the Play-In Tournament, averaged 16.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 6.1 assists per game in 53 appearances (51 starts) in the regular season. Those numbers are an upgrade compared to what he had done in his previous two seasons with the Celtics.

items.headline: Holiday chipped in 19 points (7-19 FG, 5-12 3Pt), six rebounds and 11 assists across 39 minutes during Monday's 137-132 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Although the team has adjusted the starting lineup to include Scoot Henderson in recent weeks, Holiday's numbers haven't suffered. He's averaged 21.8 points, 6.0 assists, and 4.5 rebounds since the recent adjustment, and it's a scenario that should stay in place as long as Shaedon Sharpe (calf) and Jerami Grant (calf) remain absent. Before Monday's loss, the new-look backcourt had generated three consecutive victories.

items.headline: Holiday ended with 27 points (10-22 FG, 7-15 3Pt), five rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Thursday's 118-106 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: The 27 points led all scorers on the night as Holiday continues to fill up the bucket from downtown. The veteran guard has drained at least three three-pointers in five straight games, averaging 20.8 points, 4.8 assists, 4.8 threes, 4.2 boards and 1.0 steals over that surge while shooting 49.0 percent (24-for-49) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Holiday totaled 30 points (10-21 FG, 7-15 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists and two steals in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 114-104 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Holiday took control on the offensive end and led the Blazers in scoring and made treys. He did so in an efficient manner by drilling 46.7 of his attempts from beyond the arc, and he fell one triple shy of tying his season high in three-point makes. Holiday isn't at the stage in his career where he's able to supply this type of pop on a nightly basis, but he still has a few elite performances in the tank.

items.headline: Holiday ended with 23 points (8-19 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 35 minutes during Friday's 100-93 loss to Dallas.
items.story: The 23 points led the Blazers on the night, as Holiday topped 20 points for the first time since March 13. The veteran point guard's usage has been a little inconsistent this month, but over his last 14 games he's drained multiple three-pointers nine times, averaging 16.2 points, 6.1 assists, 4.4 boards, 2.8 threes and 0.8 steals in March.

items.headline: Karaban was assigned to the G League's Stockton Kings on Thursday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: With Sacramento shuttling him back to Stockton after a recent recall, Karaban appears set for more developmental run outside the Kings' regular rotation. The rookie forward has seen limited NBA opportunities so far, so this move is unlikely to affect most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Sacramento recalled Karaban from the G League's Stockton Kings on Saturday.
items.story: Karaban has offered limited production across five appearances off the bench during his rookie season, so he may continue to provide depth following a short assignment to the G League team. The forward will need to make the most of any minutes he's given with the parent team, though he might continue to spend time with the Stockton affiliate, where he could see more consistent opportunities in the future.

items.headline: Karaban was assigned to the G League's Stockton Kings on Saturday, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Karaban hasn't made much of an impact with Sacramento, scoring just seven total points across five games, but he'll have more of an opportunity to perform and play meaningful minutes at the G League level.

items.headline: Karaban closed Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs with zero points (0-1 FG), one rebound and one assist across 11 minutes.
items.story: Karaban received his first meaningful rotation minutes of the season but failed to score on his lone field-goal attempt. The rookie forward entered the game during the first half as Sacramento searched for additional floor spacing, though he was unable to make much of an impact. Karaban remains outside the regular rotation and holds little fantasy value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Karaban finished with seven points (2-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Karaban made the most of his limited scoring opportunities, converting both attempts from beyond the arc while contributing in several other categories. The rookie forward also committed two turnovers but demonstrated the perimeter shooting ability that could help him compete for a reserve role in Sacramento. His regular-season fantasy appeal remains limited until he establishes consistent playing time.

items.headline: The Kings signed Ben Simmons to a one-year deal Friday, adding another bench option who will challenge Karaban for playing time.
items.story: Simmons will return to The Association after sitting out the 2025-26 campaign. With the three-time All-Star in the mix, Karaban faces increased competition for playing time off the bench. Karaban, the No. 29 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, could see increasingly steady minutes as the season progresses, though the UConn product isn't guaranteed a meaningful role early on, especially if Keegan Murray (ankle) is healthy to begin the campaign.

items.headline: Karaban finished Friday's 92-90 Summer League win over Charlotte with 14 points (6-12 FG, 2-8 3Pt), three assists and two rebounds over 35 minutes.
items.story: It was a bit of an inconsistent performance from Karaban, who scored seven points in both the first and third quarters but did not score in the other two frames. He still finished tied with Jonathan Mogbo as the Kings' second-leading scorer behind Emanuel Sharp (16 points). The Kings acquired Karaban from the Cavaliers after he was selected by Cleveland with the No. 29 pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, but the UConn product's playing time in his rookie season could be limited if he's behind De'Andre Hunter (eye) and Nique Clifford (rest) on the depth chart after the preseason.

items.headline: The Cavaliers selected Karaban with the No. 29 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Kings, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: The Cavaliers received the No. 34 overall pick and future second-round picks in the deal. The 23-year-old is a proven winner, helping the Huskies capture two NCAA championships. His athleticism is a concern, though his positive attributes make up for most of his shortcomings. It's unknown what the future holds for Sacramento's veterans, specifically, Domantas Sabonis (knee), De'Andre Hunter (eye) and DeMar DeRozan (hamstring). If those players aren't on the roster during the 2026-27 campaign, Karaban could see plenty of action. However, if they stay, it will be more difficult for Karaban to receive consistent minutes.
