The Trail Blazers have Damian Lillard (Achilles), Jrue Holiday, Shaedon Sharpe and Scoot Henderson in the backcourt already. Unless more moves are coming, it's a tricky spot to project Morant landing a major role right away.

items.headline: Avdija put up 31 points (12-19 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 2-5 FT), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five turnovers across 30 minutes in Monday's 128-111 win over the 76ers.
items.story: This was Avdija's second 30-plus-point performance of the season, and he helped the Trail Blazers end their six-game road trip on a high note with a win. Avdija has been flirting with top-75 value on the season with averages of 24.3 points, 6.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 2.3 triples, 1.0 steals, 0.5 blocks and 3.3 turnovers per contest.

items.headline: Avdija chipped in 20 points (7-13 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-7 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and two blocks over 36 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 loss to New York.
items.story: Avdija looked fresh in his return from a two-game absence and was one of the few Portland players who had his shot working in New York. However, with Damian Lillard, Sidy Cissoko, Toumani Camara and Scoot Henderson shooting a combined 11-for-42 from the floor and 5-for-26 from three-point range, the Trail Blazers weren't able to generate enough offense to pull out the win over the Knicks.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) is listed as available for Saturday's game versus the Knicks.
items.story: Avdija missed a couple of games due to a foot injury, but he will be back on the floor Saturday against New York. As a result, Jayson Kent will presumably return to the bench after starting the last two contests.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: The star point forward is looking to avoid an absence due to a bruised left foot extend to three games. Damian Lillard would do the heavy lifting offensively if Avdija is out, while Jayson Kent would be in line for a third consecutive start.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: A foot injury continues to bother Avdija, who will now miss his second consecutive contest. His next opportunity to get back on the court will come Saturday versus the Knicks. In the meantime, Jayson Kent could remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) is listed as questionable ahead of Thursday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Avdija missed his first game of the 2026-27 campaign Tuesday. If he stays on the shelf for a second consecutive contest, Jayson Kent is in line to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) won't play Tuesday versus Minnesota.
items.story: Avdija scored 27 points over 30 minutes in Monday's loss to the Timberwolves. However, he won't be on the floor for Tuesday's rematch. As a result, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday are candidates for more work, with one of those players expected to enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Avdija (foot) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: After playing 30 minutes during Monday's loss to Minnesota, the star point forward is in danger of missing the second half of this back-to-back set. Damian Lillard would do the heavy lifting offensively if Avdija sits out Tuesday, while either Jrue Holiday or Scoot Henderson would likely enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Avdija recorded 27 points (11-19 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 30 minutes during Monday's 106-98 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Avdija was ultra-efficient for the second consecutive outing, and he's now made 11 shots and three triples in back-to-back games. Over that same stretch, Avdija has shot a robust 22-for-32 (68.8 percent) from the field and 6-for-8 (75 percent) from long range while still chipping in across the board from a fantasy perspective. He's scored 24 or more points in four straight contests, pushing his average to 23.9 points to go along with 6.1 rebounds, 6.3 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 32.7 minutes across 13 regular-season outings.

items.headline: Avdija finished Friday's 120-107 win over the Kings with 34 points (11-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 9-9 FT), six rebounds, four assists and one block across 35 minutes.
items.story: Avdija was nearly perfect Friday, scoring 34 points on 11-of-13 shooting and going 9-for-9 at the line. With Ja Morant (hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe (knee) out, Portland is leaning heavily on Avdija, and he's delivered. The Blazers are 9-3 and 6-1 on the road, and Avdija is a big reason why. They'll need more of the same in back-to-back games at Minnesota on Monday and Tuesday.

items.headline: Avdija tallied 28 points (9-20 FG, 4-13 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, six assists, four steals and two blocks across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 118-108 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Avdija delivered an outstanding two-way performance, combining a team-high 28 points with six assists and six combined defensive stats. The star forward was coming off another impressive outing in the first leg of this back-to-back set against the Thunder, notching 24 points (8-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 34 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win. Avdija's substantial workload and versatile production continue to provide an excellent fantasy ceiling across multiple categories. He's scored at least 20 points in all but one of his last 10 games, averaging 23.5 points, 5.7 rebounds, 6.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Avdija recorded 24 points (8-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 34 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Avdija was the engine of the Portland offense, scoring well and creating for others. He's become one of the league's most well-rounded forwards and does a bit of everything for the Blazers. With so many key players out, Portland needs him to keep playing like this.

items.headline: Avdija finished with 15 points (5-13 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 24 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Avdija struggled to make a significant impact beyond scoring, finishing with just one assist while committing three turnovers. His 24-minute workload was also relatively modest, though that may have to do with how the game unfolded rather than an upcoming reduction in his role. Avdija should remain a key offensive player for the Trail Blazers, and this was just a down game in a matchup where Portland looked inferior on both ends of the court.

items.headline: Avdija racked up 22 points (6-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 9-14 FT), nine rebounds, 11 assists and two steals across 39 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Avdija came one rebound short of a triple-double, tied Damian Lillard for the team lead in scoring and finished with a game-high 11 assists. The downside was eight turnovers. He's still the hub of the Blazers' offense, and Portland's strong 6-2 start runs largely through him.

items.headline: Avdija ended with 21 points (7-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 6-9 FT), seven rebounds and 12 assists across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 win over Phoenix.
items.story: The 25-year-old forward came a few boards shy of his first triple-double of the season, and the sixth of his career. Avdija has scored more than 20 points in six straight games, a stretch in which he's averaging 24.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.8 rebounds and 1.7 threes, despite shooting just 29.4 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Avdija tallied 28 points (10-22 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 6-9 FT), three rebounds and five assists in 35 minutes during Monday's 118-110 victory over Denver.
items.story: The 28 points are a season-high figure for Avdija, who's now scored at least 23 in five consecutive games. The 25-year-old continued handling primary offensive responsibilities with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined, a trend that is likely to continue for as long as the first-year Blazer remains out. The only downside to Avdija's fantasy profile is his inefficiency at the free-throw line, as he's now missed three or more of his attempts in five straight regular-season outings.

items.headline: Avdija posted 24 points (6-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 10-13 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 win over Utah.
items.story: Avdija led all scorers on the afternoon as he dropped at least 23 points for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old forward is finding chemistry quickly with his new point guard Damian Lillard, and during that four-game stretch Avdija has averaged 24.3 points, 6.3 boards, 6.0 assists and 1.8 threes in 33.5 minutes.

items.headline: Avdija chipped in 24 points (8-16 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 8-12 FT), nine rebounds, seven assists and one block over 32 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 loss to Memphis.
items.story: The star forward is off to an excellent start this season, having produced at least 18 points, four rebounds and four assists in each of his first four appearances. Ja Morant's (hamstring) status is in limbo following Thursday's defeat, so Avdija may have to do the heavy lifting offensively if Morant needs to miss time.

items.headline: Avdija notched 23 points (8-15 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 3-7 FT), four rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Avdija tied Ja Morant for the team lead in scoring and nearly posted a double-double with nine assists, including a big three down the stretch. The forward has been the engine of Portland's 3-0 start, and with Shaedon Sharpe (knee) sidelined, the Blazers are leaning heavily on Avdija's playmaking.

items.headline: Avdija finished with 26 points (8-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 9-12 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and one steal across 39 minutes during Friday's 128-120 win over the Kings.
items.story: Avdija led Portland in scoring, adding six rebounds and six assists as the Trail Blazers moved to 2-0. He was a game-time decision with a right ankle injury before Wednesday's opener, but he logged a team-high 38 minutes Friday, so the ankle doesn't look like a lingering problem. Last season's breakout star remains the focal point of the offense even with Damian Lillard and Ja Morant now in the backcourt.

items.headline: Avdija closed Wednesday's 124-83 victory over Phoenix with 18 points (7-16 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals in 23 minutes.
items.story: Damian Lillard celebrated his return to Portland with a game-high 25 points, but Avdija was plenty productive as well, delivering the game's only double-double. The 25-year-old forward is coming off a career-best 2025-26 campaign that saw him score 24.2 points with 6.9 boards, 6.7 assists, 1.9 threes and 1.4 combined steals and blocks, and while the Blazers offense will now flow through the duo of Lillard and Ja Morant in the backcourt, it's encouraging that in Avdija's first game alongside them, his shot volume didn't take a big dip from the 16.1 FG attempts he averaged last season.

items.headline: Avdija (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Suns, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Avdija will shed his questionable tag due to right ankle soreness and suit up for Portland's regular-season opener. The star forward is coming off a career year in 2025-26, when he averaged 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists and 1.4 combined steals-plus-blocks in 33.3 minutes per game across 66 regular-season outings.

items.headline: Avdija is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Suns due to right ankle soreness.
items.story: It would be surprising if Avdija missed Wednesday's season opener at home due to ankle soreness, but we'll have a better idea on his status based on Avdija's activity level at shootaround. If he can't give it a go on Opening Night, Sidy Cissoko could start, and Ja Morant would likely see an uptick in usage.

items.headline: Lillard produced 18 points (4-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 9-9 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 29 minutes during Monday's 128-111 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Lillard has shot just 9-for-31 from the field over his last two appearances, but his perfect 13-for-13 showing at the free-throw line has helped offset the struggles. With Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined, Lillard should continue handling significant offensive responsibilities.

items.headline: Lillard amassed 15 points (5-16 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 33 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Lillard struggled to find his rhythm Saturday, opening the game with seven straight misses from beyond the arc. He finally found his touch late, drilling a three-pointer to tie the game with less than a minute remaining in regulation. However, despite erasing a 26-point deficit, the Trail Blazers couldn't complete the comeback and suffered their third loss in the past four games.

items.headline: Lillard finished with 33 points (10-18 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 8-9 FT) and six rebounds in 35 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Lillard delivered his first 30-point performance since March 2025, showcasing renewed scoring explosiveness against his former team. He's reached 25 points in three of his last four appearances, with 16 triples during that stretch. His scoring resurgence is encouraging, though fluctuating assists limit his fantasy consistency.

items.headline: Lillard tallied 33 points (10-18 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 8-9 FT) and six rebounds in 35 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 victory over Milwaukee.
items.story: Lillard failed to record an assist for the first time this season, but he made up for it by setting a new season high in scoring, beating his previous mark of 29 points Friday against Sacramento. The 36-year-old has been dialed in from deep of late, as he's converted on 10 of 23 attempts over his last two appearances. Lillard has poured in 20-plus points in three of his last four matchups.

items.headline: Lillard closed with 25 points (8-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Tuesday's 106-105 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: The veteran guard led Portland in scoring and caught fire from deep, a sharp turnaround after he struggled badly with his shot Monday. His driving layup in the closing seconds was blocked by Trey Lyles, and the Blazers couldn't convert on the putback. Lillard is averaging 19.7 points in his first season back since tearing his Achilles.

items.headline: Lillard chipped in nine points (2-15 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one block over 24 minutes during Monday's 106-98 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Lillard struggled mightily in the front end of this back-to-back set against Minnesota, finishing with a season-low-tying nine points. On a more positive note, the veteran guard still tied for the team lead in assists while committing zero turnovers. He's shot just 35.7 percent from the field in his last five games, during which he's averaged 18.6 points, 4.6 assists, 3.2 triples and 2.0 rebounds across 26.6 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Lillard posted 29 points (6-18 FG, 6-13 3Pt, 11-11 FT), two rebounds and six assists across 33 minutes during Friday's 120-107 win over the Kings.
items.story: The veteran added 29 points despite an inefficient night from inside the arc, making up for it by hitting six threes and going 11-for-11 at the charity stripe. With Ja Morant (hamstring) out, Lillard has excelled, getting the job done from beyond the arc and continuing to look like his old self. Portland has now won three straight to open its six-game road trip.

items.headline: Lillard finished with 18 points (5-14 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, three assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 118-108 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Lillard struggled from beyond the arc, making just two of 10 three-point attempts, but his perfect free-throw shooting helped him reach at least 18 points for the sixth time in his last seven appearances. Lillard's scoring and playmaking remain valuable, although his assist numbers have been trending in the wrong direction. He has dished out five or fewer assists in four of his last five outings. In that span, Lillard has averaged 20.4 points, 1.8 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game.

items.headline: Lillard ended Tuesday's 123-103 win over the Thunder with 25 points (8-15 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
items.story: Lillard took over after halftime, hitting three after three, capped by a logo shot at the end of the third that pretty much put the game away. He led Portland in scoring in limited minutes because the Blazers didn't need him late. He's looked a lot like his old self lately, which is great news for a Portland team that's missing Ja Morant (hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe (knee).

items.headline: Lillard delivered 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT) and seven assists across 20 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Lillard was efficient with his shot, but playing just 20 minutes limited his chances and ultimately snapped his streak of games with at least 20 points. The veteran guard's ability to generate assists and three-pointers remains valuable, and given that this was just the second time he played fewer than 30 minutes in a game this season, fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about a down game for Lillard, especially since this was the second leg of a back-to-back set against one of the top contending teams in the Western Conference.

items.headline: Lillard recorded 22 points (5-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), four assists and one steal in 37 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Lillard tied Deni Avdija for Portland's top scorer, mostly on the strength of four three-pointers and a perfect night at the line. The veteran guard re-signed with the Blazers in the summer of 2025 while recovering from a torn Achilles, and he looks like his old self in his first season back. He's Portland's best threat from deep and should continue to thrive in the team's revived offense.

items.headline: Lillard finished Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns with 25 points (9-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds and five assists over 33 minutes.
items.story: The 25 points led Portland on the night, as Donovan Clingan and Deni Avdija also delivered more than 20 points. Lillard has scored 20-plus in three straight games and five of seven to begin the season, averaging 20.1 points, 4.1 boards, 4.1 assists, 2.7 threes and 0.9 steals in his return to the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Lillard posted 20 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 9-10 FT), six rebounds, six assists and a steal across 30 minutes in Monday's 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Lillard made up for a quiet perimeter shooting night by making nine free throws and contributing across multiple categories. His six rebounds and six assists boosted his fantasy output, while the 30-minute workload gave him meaningful opportunities as both a scorer and playmaker. His ability to generate points at the foul line remains valuable when his outside shot isn't falling. Lillard hasn't shown any signs of rust and has scored at least 20 points in four of his first six outings this season.

items.headline: Lillard produced 22 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals over 27 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: The 36-year-old point guard bounced back from a quiet nine-point effort Thursday against the Grizzlies, as Lillard scored more than 20 points for the third time in five games to begin the season and drained multiple three-pointers for the fourth time. His return to Portland has gone as well as could have been hoped -- Lillard is averaging 19.2 points, 4.0 boards, 3.6 assists, 3.2 threes and 1.0 steals a contest, and the Blazers are 4-1 with him running the offense.

items.headline: Lillard registered 21 points (5-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 7-11 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Lillard came through when it mattered, hitting the clinching three with 43 seconds left. The 36-year-old has made a habit of big nights against the Lakers during his illustrious career, though he uncharacteristically missed four free throws. Portland is off to the franchise's second 3-0 start in the last 15 years, and Lillard's late-game shotmaking has been a big reason why.

items.headline: Lillard racked up 19 points (7-18 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals in 33 minutes during Friday's 128-120 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Lillard tied Toumani Camara for second on the team in scoring but cooled off from deep, making just two of his 10 three-point attempts after hitting six in the opener. The veteran guard missed all of last season while rehabbing a torn Achilles tendon after rejoining Portland, and his early workload has been encouraging. Lillard and the Blazers visit the Lakers on Tuesday.

items.headline: Lillard recorded 25 points (7-12 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 victory over the Suns.
items.story: In his first actual game action since being re-acquired by Portland last July, Lillard produced game highs in points and made three-pointers. He looked good alongside Ja Morant in the Blazers' new-look backcourt, and Lillard seemed fully recovered from the Achilles injury that cost him all of 2025-26. The 36-year-old guard had averaged at least 24.0 points, 7.0 assists, 4.0 boards and 3.0 threes in six straight seasons prior to the injury, and he seems more than capable of returning to that level of production.

items.headline: Green will return to the second unit for Friday's game against the Raptors, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Cade Cunningham (knee) is set to return, so Green will head back to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Green is averaging 6.0 points and 2.5 rebounds per game.

items.headline: Green racked up 18 points (7-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, one block and two steals in 35 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: Green moved to the starting lineup due to the absence of Cade Cunningham (knee) and made his presence felt, delivering his best scoring output since the season opener and notching a season-high mark in rebounds. Green should return to the bench if Cunningham is back Friday against the Raptors, and that should limit his upside considerably. He's averaging 6.0 points and 2.5 boards per game when coming off the bench this season.

items.headline: Green will enter the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Pelicans, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Green is getting the start with Cade Cunningham (knee) out, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson and John Collins. As a starter last season, Green averaged 12.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.0 triples, 2.0 steals and 1.2 blocks per game.

items.headline: Green finished Tuesday's 105-93 victory over the Spurs with six points (2-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT) and six rebounds over 23 minutes.
items.story: Green logged 23 minutes Tuesday, his highest total in six appearances, after playing 15 or fewer minutes in three straight games. The veteran wing has scored seven or fewer points in five consecutive contests, though his six rebounds Tuesday marked a season high. Despite the uptick in playing time, Green's limited offensive involvement continues to restrict his fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Green produced one point (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 15 minutes during Wednesday's 112-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Green attempted just one field goal and failed to record a defensive statistic, offering little fantasy production in his limited opportunity. He also committed three fouls while Detroit leaned heavily on its starting wings. With Ausar Thompson and Duncan Robinson occupying prominent roles, Green remains a low-usage reserve with minimal fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Green supplied three points (1-6 FG, 1-6 3Pt), one rebound and one block over 17 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Green struggled with his outside shot, missing five of his six three-point attempts. He has scored five or fewer points in three consecutive games, and his limited offensive involvement makes him difficult to trust in most fantasy formats. Green could continue receiving reserve minutes while Isaiah Joe (hip) is sidelined.

items.headline: Green dropped 19 points (5-10 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and four rebounds across 18 minutes in Detroit's season-opening 121-113 comeback victory over the Celtics on Tuesday.
items.story: The veteran forward scored all of his points in the second half to help the Pistons erase a 22-point deficit. Green fueled an 18-0 run and finished with a game-best plus-21 in his 18 minutes off the bench. He wasn't expected to be a major part of the rotation, but he's likely earned himself more opportunities moving forward.

items.headline: Green and the Pistons agreed to a one-year, $3.6 million deal Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Green played all 82 regular-season games for the Pistons in 2025-26, averaging 6.9 points and 2.8 rebounds in 17.6 minutes while shooting 38.1 percent from beyond the arc. He'll again provide the Pistons with some quality depth on the wings.

items.headline: Green (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Pistons' 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: After playing in all 82 games during the regular season as well as the Pistons' first 11 games of the playoffs, Green failed to see the court for the first time in the 2025-26 campaign during Game 5. Green's prospects for rejoining the Detroit rotation likely won't get any better moving forward, as the Pistons were without starting wing Duncan Robinson (back) for Game 5 but could get him back for Friday's Game 6.

items.headline: Green amassed two points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three blocks and one steal over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 victory over the Magic in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Green actually led the second unit in minutes played as the Pistons seem content to lean on the veteran. Meanwhile, Caris LeVert and Ronald Holland combined to see just 21 minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Green totaled 17 points (6-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and three steals across 27 minutes during Monday's 123-107 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Green rattled off his best performance in quite some time, playing an elevated role as Detroit went with an undersized lineup. While this was a great start to the week for anyone who grabbed Green, it's clear that his value is tied to the availability of others around him.

items.headline: Green provided two points (1-2 FG) and one rebound over six minutes during Saturday's 116-93 victory over Philadelphia.
items.story: Green logged just six minutes, the second time he has done so in the past two games. Despite having a couple of positive moments throughout the season, Green has been mostly a non-factor when it comes to fantasy. In 78 appearances, he has averaged just 6.8 points, 1.2 steals and 1.1 three-pointers, leaving him well outside the top 200 in standard formats.

items.headline: Green won't start Tuesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Green got the spot start in the front end of this back-to-back set, but he will retreat to the second unit Tuesday with Tobias Harris (hip) returning to the lineup. Green has averaged 6.4 points and 2.8 rebounds across 16.8 minutes per contest over his last five outings off the bench.

items.headline: Green finished with 19 points (6-12 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and two steals across 30 minutes during Monday's 114-110 overtime loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Making his first start since March 13, Green set a new career high in made three-pointers. The veteran forward has drained multiple treys in three straight games and five of the last 11, averaging 7.9 points, 2.5 boards, 1.7 threes, 1.3 steals and 0.9 assists in 16.3 minutes during that span.

items.headline: Green is starting Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Green is set for his second start of March while Duncan Robinson (hip) and Tobias Harris (hip) tend to their respective injuries. Green has struggled to produce off the bench, as he's averaging 5.6 points and 2.4 rebounds in his last eight outings, all as a reserve.

items.headline: Green (ankle) is available for Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: The veteran guard is available for the second part of this back-to-back set, shedding a probable tag. Over his last six appearances, Green has averaged 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 12.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green (ankle) is probable for Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: The veteran guard is likely to be available for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Over his last six contests, Green has averaged 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 12.5 minutes per game but could see an uptick in playing time if Tobias Harris (hip) sits out Thursday.

items.headline: Green (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Green popped up on Tuesday's injury report due to a left ankle sprain, but the veteran guard has been given the green to play against Atlanta on Wednesday. He has averaged 7.1 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.2 threes and 1.2 steals over 15.8 minutes across 13 games (one start) since March 1.

items.headline: Green (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Green is in danger of missing his first game of the season due to a left ankle sprain. If the veteran forward is ruled out, there would be more minutes available for guys like Kevin Huerter, Caris LeVert and Ronald Holland, especially if Marcus Sasser (hip) is downgraded from doubtful to out.

items.headline: Green finished Tuesday's 130-117 victory over Washington with three points (1-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and two rebounds in five minutes.
items.story: Green was a non-factor in the win, playing just five minutes off the bench. With Ausar Thompson now back in the lineup, Green's role is likely to be largely insignificant when it comes to fantasy production. At best, he can be utilized for streaming purposes for those who are desperate for steals.

items.headline: Green is not in the Pistons' starting lineup against the Raptors on Sunday.
items.story: Green started in Friday's win against the Grizzlies, finishing with six points, two assists, one rebound, three steals and one block over 21 minutes. The veteran wing will revert to a bench role Sunday due to the return of Tobias Harris (hip).

items.headline: Green supplied six points (2-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt), one rebound, two assists, one block and three steals in 21 minutes during Friday's 126-110 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Green moved into the starting lineup, replacing Tobias Harris, who was ruled out with a hip injury. As he has done for much of the season, Green made the most of his time on the floor, particularly on the defensive end, where he recorded three steals for the third straight game. Both Harris and Ausar Thompson (ankle) could return as soon as Sunday, meaning Green should be looked at for streaming purposes and nothing more.

items.headline: Green will start Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: With Tobias Harris (hip) unavailable for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Green will enter the starting five for the first time since Jan. 10. As a starter this season (four games), the veteran forward has averaged 12.0 points, 7.8 rebounds, 3.3 combined steals-plus-blocks and 1.5 assists in 35.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green totaled 17 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and three steals in 19 minutes during Thursday's 131-109 victory over Philadelphia.
items.story: Green has been a key player for the second unit in Detroit this season, but he's still a bit too volatile to trust outside of very deep fantasy formats when the team is close to full strength. Across 65 appearances, he holds averages of 7.0 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green produced six points (2-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 15 minutes during Sunday's 121-110 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Despite the absence of Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Caris LeVert (wrist), Green hasn't been able to claim a more prominent role. As a result, Green remains off the radar in most fantasy leagues, averaging only 5.2 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.6 steals in 15.2 minutes per contest in his last nine games while shooting 37.2 percent from the floor during this stretch.

items.headline: Green had two points (1-1 FG), three rebounds and one assist in 17 minutes during Saturday's 126-110 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Green continues to put up modest production, logging no more than 20 minutes for the 17th straight game. With the Pistons rolling out a relatively healthy lineup, Green's role is simply that of a depth piece. At best, fantasy managers could consider him for streaming purposes when in desperate need of steals.

items.headline: Green chipped in two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 17 minutes during Friday's 111-104 loss to Houston.
items.story: Green scored just two points, failing to reach double digits for the fifth time in the past six games. After a brief run of relevance earlier in the season, Green has seen his role regress in recent times. In that recent six-game span, he has averaged just 6.8 points and 1.5 steals in 17.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green is not in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: With Isaiah Stewart (illness) and Tobias Harris (hip) both back in the mix, Green is reverting back to usual role off the bench. Green has averaged 8.8 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.1 steals in 21.1 minutes per tilt across his last 14 games off the bench, so the door remains open for him to offer streaming value in the steals category.

items.headline: Green will start against the Clippers on Saturday.
items.story: With Isaiah Stewart (illness) and Tobias Harris (hip) unavailable, Green will get the starting nod against Los Angeles. In three starts so far this season, the 32-year-old swingman has averaged 13.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 steals in 35.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Green totaled 17 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and three steals over 29 minutes during Monday's 121-90 win over New York.
items.story: Green has now scored in double figures in three straight games and has played at least 24 minutes in those contests with Tobias Harris (hip) sidelined. The 32-year-old forward drilled a season-high four threes and collected three swipes in the blowout win over the Knicks. He's now totalled six games with at least three steals this season, the second most in the league by a bench player. Green should continue to see healthy playing time while Harris is out and could offer some streaming appeal in the short term.

items.headline: Green ended with 11 points (3-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Sunday's 114-110 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Tobias Harris (hip) is going to miss a couple of weeks, and Jalen Duren (ankle) is expected to miss at least one week as well. Ausar Thompson drew the start alongside Isaiah Stewart and Paul Reed in the frontcourt, but Green actually saw more minutes than Thompson. Green could offer some low-end streaming appeal for the next week or two.

items.headline: Green closed Tuesday's 128-106 victory over the Lakers with eight points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 31 minutes.
items.story: With Tobias Harris (hip) going down in the first quarter, Green logged his most minutes since Nov. 14. The 32-year-old forward struggled to find his rhythm from beyond the arc but was effective on the defensive end, chipping in a team-high two blocks. If Harris is forced to miss additional time, Green could step into a more prominent role.

items.headline: Green produced eight points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and three steals over 14 minutes during Monday's 112-105 win over the Celtics.
items.story: With the Pistons at full strength, Green has seen his minutes take a hit. Over his last five outings, the 32-year-old forward has averaged 7.8 points, 0.6 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.4 three-pointers in 14.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Huerter chipped in 20 points (7-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Friday's 105-102 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Huerter reached the 20-point mark for the second time in his last four appearances, and he's been putting up solid numbers lately with six double-digit scoring performances over his last seven outings. Huerter is enjoying a bigger role of late due to the injury of Duncan Robinson (quadriceps), and this was his third consecutive start. The veteran sharpshooter is averaging 13.3 points per game since moving to the first unit. His 36-minute workload was encouraging, especially with Detroit continuing to rely on his shooting to complement Cade Cunningham's playmaking. However, his contributions beyond scoring and three-pointers remain relatively modest, making him more appealing to managers chasing those categories than those seeking consistent all-around production.

items.headline: Huerter had 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), one rebound, seven assists, one block and one steal across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Huerter has logged at least 36 minutes in three consecutive games, signaling an expanded role in Detroit's rotation. His seven assists Wednesday helped compensate for another inefficient shooting performance. With Cade Cunningham (knee) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) sidelined, Huerter's playmaking opportunities could remain elevated, making him an intriguing short-term fantasy option.

items.headline: Huerter will start in Tuesday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: With Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) unavailable, Huerter will start for the first time this season. In 14 starts combined for Detroit and Chicago during the 2025-26 campaign, the 28-year-old averaged 12.7 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists over 27.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Huerter posted 20 points (9-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds, seven assists, a steal and three blocks across 38 minutes in Saturday's 137-117 loss to Miami.
items.story: Huerter played a season-high 38 minutes and delivered one of his most complete performances of the campaign, particularly after adding seven assists and three blocks to another strong scoring effort. Huerter will need to maintain a substantial role to become a dependable fantasy option, but there's no question he's trending up. He has scored in double digits in his last four games after not doing so in the first eight appearances of the season.

items.headline: Huerter recorded 24 points (9-14 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, five assists, five blocks and two steals in 35 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Huerter delivered an outstanding two-way performance off the bench. The veteran wing also knocked down four triples and played 35 minutes, easily surpassing his recent workload. With Isaiah Joe (hip) unavailable Sunday, Huerter capitalized on additional opportunities, though his defensive production is unlikely to be sustainable.

items.headline: Huerter supplied eight points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt) and two blocks over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 112-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Huerter connected on multiple three-pointers for the third consecutive game and surprisingly added two blocks, but he failed to register a rebound or assist. The veteran wing has settled into a relatively consistent bench role, logging between 19 and 24 minutes in each of his last four appearances. His perimeter shooting provides some value in deeper formats, though his limited contributions elsewhere make him a difficult option to trust in standard leagues.

items.headline: Huerter provided seven points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-2 FT), one rebound, one block and one steal across 16 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Huerter shot efficiently from the field but missed both of his free-throw attempts. The veteran wing played a limited role despite Isaiah Joe (hip) being unavailable, which doesn't bode well for his fantasy outlook once Detroit's backcourt returns to full strength. Huerter remains a fringe option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Huerter closed with three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists over 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Huerter struggled to find his shooting touch in his Pistons regular-season debut, connecting on just one of four attempts from beyond the arc. He played fewer minutes than fellow perimeter reserves Isaiah Joe and Javonte Green, the latter of whom erupted for 19 points. With Duncan Robinson also starting and hitting five triples, Huerter faces considerable competition for minutes and perimeter opportunities in Detroit's rotation.

items.headline: Huerter registered 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal in 18 minutes during Saturday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Wizards in overtime.
items.story: Huerter delivered an efficient performance from downtown and was one of five Detroit players to score in double figures. He also tied for second in the second unit in assists. The veteran swingman is expected to compete for playing time off the bench with Isaiah Joe and Javonte Green.

items.headline: Huerter said Monday that he's healthy entering training camp after undergoing surgery during the offseason to address a groin injury, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Huerter said the injury initially occurred during his time with Chicago before he aggravated it during Detroit's first-round playoff series against Orlando. He underwent a cleanup procedure after the Pistons' postseason run ended and has since returned to full health, putting him on track to participate in training camp without limitations.

items.headline: Huerter intends to sign a three-year, $27 million contract with the Pistons, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Monday.
items.story: Huerter was traded from Chicago to Detroit before last season's deadline. He appeared in 25 regular-season games (three starts) with the Pistons, during which he averaged 8.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.5 minutes per game. However, the Pistons added Isaiah Joe via trade this offseason, so Huerter will likely have to compete for minutes with Joe, Daniss Jenkins, Caris LeVert and Marcus Sasser.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is available for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter will shed his questionable tag due to a lingering left adductor strain and suit up in Sunday's do-or-die matchup. The 27-year-old swingman has appeared in just one game during the second round of the postseason, logging three minutes in Wednesday's Game 5 loss before aggravating the adductor injury.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter is on the injury report again as he continues to manage a left adductor strain that has kept him sidelined for the majority of the second round. While he was cleared to play in Game 5, he saw just three minutes of action off the bench and did not see the floor at all during Friday's Game 6 victory. Given the "all hands on deck" nature of a Game 7, the 27-year-old sharpshooter will likely be active, but he may not see the floor, as he has yet to log meaningful minutes since the first round.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is available for Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Friday.
items.story: Huerter's presence Friday helps put the Pistons at full strength for a win-or-go-home contest. The 27-year-old, who missed time earlier this series with a left adductor strain, logged just three minutes in Detroit's Game 5 loss because he aggravated the injury, per Jamal Collier of ESPN.com. Collier also noted that Huerter received an injection to gain clearance for Game 6, so the sharpshooter's workload could depend on his pain tolerance.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Friday, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: Huerter managed to make his first appearance of the series Wednesday after missing time with a left adductor strain, but he logged only three minutes and recorded one assist. It's unclear how much the 27-year-old will be able to contribute if he's ultimately given the green light to suit up.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) recorded one assist over three minutes off the bench Wednesday in the Pistons' 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Available to play for the first time since Game 4 of the Pistons' first-round playoff series versus the Magic, Huerter was a fringe member of head coach J.B. Bickerstaff's rotation. The veteran wing checked into the contest with 6:17 left in the first quarter and played a brief shift before heading back to the bench, where he remained for the rest of the game. Regardless of whether Duncan Robinson (back) plays in Friday's Game 6 after sitting out Wednesday, Huerter could find himself outside of Bickerstaff's rotation entirely.

items.headline: Huerter (thigh) is available for Wednesday's Game 5 matchup of the Eastern Conference Semifinals with Cleveland.
items.story: Duncan Robinson (back) is out, so Huerter should be in the rotation, although he may have his minutes monitored in his first game back. Huerter is averaging 1.5 points and 1.5 assists in 10.6 minutes per game this postseason.

items.headline: Huerter (thigh) participated in Wednesday's morning shootaround, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Huerter has missed the past seven games for Detroit, but he's listed as questionable ahead of Game 5. With this news, he's seemingly trending in the right direction with the series tied at two wins apiece.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter is in danger of missing an eighth straight game due to a left adductor strain. If the 27-year-old swingman remains sidelined, Daniss Jenkins will likely continue seeing increased playing time off the bench, especially if Caris LeVert (heel) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Huerter (thigh) is out for Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against Cleveland on Monday.
items.story: Huerter hasn't been able to take the court since April 27 while tending to a left thigh injury. His next chance to take the court will arrive in Game 5 on Wednesday.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is listed as questionable for Monday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter is in danger of missing a seventh consecutive contest due to a left adductor strain. If the 27-year-old swingman remains sidelined, Daniss Jenkins will likely continue seeing increased playing time off the bench.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is listed as out for Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals versus Cleveland.
items.story: Huerter will now miss a sixth consecutive contest. His next chance to return will be for Game 4 on Monday night. While Huerter remains on the shelf, Daniss Jenkins should see even more work from off the bench.

items.headline: Huerter (thigh) is doubtful for Saturday's Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter is expected to be sidelined for a sixth straight game Saturday. Daniss Jenkins is likely to continue to see an uptick in minutes for Detroit.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) has been ruled out for Thursday's Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter will miss a fifth consecutive game due to a left adductor strain. His next opportunity to suit up will come in Saturday's Game 3, and in the meantime, Daniss Jenkins should continue to see an elevated role off the bench.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Thursday's Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: The Pistons are bracing for Huerter to miss a fifth straight game due to a left adductor strain. The 27-year-old sharpshooter's expected absence should free up more playing time for Daniss Jenkins and Javonte Green on Thursday.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left adductor strain, and his next opportunity to play will come in Game 2 on Thursday. With the 27-year-old swingman sidelined, Daniss Jenkins and Javonte Green are candidates for increased minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Tuesday.
items.story: Huerter is trying to end a three-game absence with a left adductor strain Tuesday. If the sharpshooter is unable to suit up in Game 1, Javonte Green could see an uptick in playing time off the bench for the Pistons.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is listed as out for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Magic.
items.story: Huerter will now miss his third consecutive contest. As a result, Daniss Jenkins and Javonte Green are candidates for increased action, although it's possible head coach J.B. Bickerstaff continues to lean heavily on the starters.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is listed as questionable for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against Orlando.
items.story: Huerter played sporadically during the first four contests of this series before being ruled out altogether for Games 5 and 6. If Huerter misses a third consecutive game, Daniss Jenkins and Javonte Green could see additional action, although head coach J.B. Bickerstaff might continue to rely on the starters to absorb most of the minutes.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is out for Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs Friday against the Magic, per Hunter Patterson of The Athletic.
items.story: The Pistons won't have Huerter available for a second straight win-or-go-home contest, so the team will have to turn elsewhere to fill out the reserve minutes. Daniss Jenkins, Caris LeVert and Javonte Green are all candidates for increased playing time Friday.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs Friday against the Magic.
items.story: Huerter is in danger of missing a second consecutive must-win contest for the Pistons on Friday due to a left adductor strain. If the sharpshooter is ultimately downgraded to out, Caris LeVert would likely find himself getting more involved in the backcourt.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Magic.
items.story: Huerter will miss Wednesday's win-or-go-home matchup due to a left adductor strain. If the Pistons are able to stave off elimination, his next chance to play will come in Game 6 on Friday. With the 27-year-old swingman sidelined, Daniss Jenkins and Caris LeVert could see a slight bump in minutes.

items.headline: Huerter is questionable for Game 5 on Wednesday versus Orlando with a left adductor strain.
items.story: Huerter is in danger of missing Detroit's must-win contest Wednesday. If the sharpshooter cannot suit up, the likes of Daniss Jenkins, Caris LeVert and Javonte Green would all have an opportunity to step up.

items.headline: Huerter (hip) will play in Monday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against Orlando, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Huerter was tagged as questionable leading up to tipoff due to a hip issue, but the injury won't prevent him from suiting up Monday night. He's averaging 2.0 points, 1.3 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 13.0 minutes over his first three appearances of the series.

items.headline: Huerter (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Magic.
items.story: Huerter injured his left hip during Saturday's Game 3 loss to Orlando and was unable to return. Caris LeVert and Javonte Green would be in line for larger roles in Detroit's rotation if Huerter is unable to play in Game 4 on Monday.

items.headline: Huerter didn't return to Saturday's 113-105 loss to the Magic due to left hip soreness, finishing with zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five assists, one rebound and one steal in 15 minutes.
items.story: Huerter finished the third quarter but did not play in the fourth due to the left hip issue. The 27-year-old swingman's next opportunity to play will come in Monday's Game 4 in Orlando, where the Pistons will look to even the series.

items.headline: Huerter is questionable to return to Saturday's Game 3 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Magic due to left hip soreness.
items.story: Huerter finished the third quarter but is questionable to play in the fourth due to the hip issue. If he's unable to return, the swingman will finish with zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five assists, one rebound and one steal in 15 minutes.

items.headline: Huerter (illness) will play in Friday's game against the Hornets, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Huerter missed Wednesday's 137-111 win over Milwaukee due to an illness. However, after being upgraded to probable for this contest, the 27-year-old is now officially ready to go. In three meetings with the Hornets this season, Huerter has averaged 6.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.7 steals while shooting 33.3 percent from the field and 15.4 percent from deep across 22.7 minutes of action.

items.headline: Huerter (illness) is probable for Friday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Huerter is trending in the right direction after missing Wednesday's game against Milwaukee. Huerter is averaging 11.7 points, 3.8 assists, 3.7 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 2.0 three-pointers over his last six games.

items.headline: Doncic posted 28 points (8-24 FG, 3-14 3Pt, 9-10 FT), four rebounds, eight assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Monday's 109-94 win over Utah.
items.story: Doncic has cooled off after a torrid stretch, but he still managed to lead all players in scoring while tying teammate Quentin Grimes with a game-high eight dimes. Doncic's rebounding and shooting efficiency has plummeted in recent games, particularly from behind the arc. After scoring 32 or more points in 11 straight regular-season outings, he's now been below the 30-point threshold in three straight. Over that span, Doncic has still averaged 27.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 7.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 2.3 triples on 38.6 percent shooting and 20.0 percent from three-point range in 35.3 minutes.

items.headline: Doncic posted 25 points (9-18 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 36 minutes during Friday's 106-104 win over the Kings.
items.story: Doncic led the Lakers in scoring but had to work for it, with a handful of turnovers and a cool night from beyond the arc. Los Angeles bounced back after Wednesday's loss to Utah snapped its nine-game winning streak. Doncic is averaging 37.2 points, and he's carrying an even heavier load with Austin Reaves (heel) still sidelined.

items.headline: Doncic produced 29 points (10-28 FG, 2-12 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 37 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Doncic's streak of 11 consecutive 30-point performances came to an end as Los Angeles suffered its first defeat this month, ending the team's impressive nine-game winning run. His 2-for-12 showing from beyond the arc was particularly damaging, and he also committed nine turnovers while the Lakers shot a season-low 38.2 percent from the field. Despite the disappointing efficiency, Doncic remains the focal point of Los Angeles' offense and continues to generate enormous shot volume. Wednesday's outing was an unusual setback for a player who had been producing at an extraordinary scoring pace.

items.headline: Doncic recorded 36 points (13-34 FG, 5-16 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal over 42 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over Charlotte.
items.story: Doncic wasn't at his sharpest shooting the ball, but he made the plays that mattered. He set up both of Quentin Grimes' late baskets, including the game-tying three, and his fadeaway gave Los Angeles the lead for good in overtime. The superstar is averaging 39.0 points, and he's carrying an even heavier load with Austin Reaves (heel) out. The Lakers have now won nine straight and sit at 13-2.

items.headline: Doncic recorded 43 points (13-28 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 12-14 FT), nine assists, three rebounds and a steal in 35 minutes during Sunday's 131-123 win over the Suns.
items.story: Doncic got off to a blazing hot start Sunday, knocking down three three-pointers en route to 20 points in the first quarter. His dominant play continued past the first frame as he finished with five threes and a game-high 43 points. The star guard has now made at least five threes in 10 of 12 appearances this season and has recorded seven 40-plus-point performances.

items.headline: Doncic (ankle) won't be listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Suns, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: The Lakers have yet to release their official injury report, though Doncic won't be included after exiting Wednesday's win over Milwaukee with an ankle injury. The superstar point guard has been on a tear, averaging 41.6 points, 7.8 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 2.9 combined steals-plus-blocks in 36.3 minutes per game over his last nine appearances. He's scored at least 32 points in all nine of those outings.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Doncic (ankle) is "fine," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The superstar guard exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's win over the Bucks due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return. Doncic can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable marker until the Lakers release an official injury report at some point prior to Sunday's matchup in Phoenix.

items.headline: Doncic finished Wednesday's 123-112 win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-25 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 7-10 FT), five rebounds, five assists and three steals across 32 minutes. He exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Doncic didn't deliver his most efficient shooting effort, though he still led all players in scoring while knocking down a game-high-tying five triples. He has now reached the 30-point threshold in each of his last nine appearances. The superstar floor general also tied for the game-best mark in steals, logging multiple swipes for the fourth time over his last six outings. However, Doncic's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game at Phoenix, as he landed on Kyle Kuzma's foot and exited to the locker room Wednesday.

items.headline: Doncic contributed 32 points (11-22 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 7-7 FT), 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks across 39 minutes in Monday's 124-114 win over Atlanta.
items.story: Doncic returned from a one-game absence due to lower-back tightness and poured in 32 points on 22 shots in the absence of Austin Reaves (illness). Doncic led all players in points, assists and steals while tying the game high in blocks, and the superstar nearly recorded his first triple-double of the campaign. He's reached the 30-point mark in each of his last eight appearances and has posted at least five rebounds and five assists in all 10 of his regular-season games this season.

items.headline: Doncic (back) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Atlanta, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com.
items.story: After sitting out Sunday's matchup in Detroit, Doncic is good to go for the second half of this back-to-back set. The MVP candidate is on an absolute tear, having dropped at least 40 points in six of his last seven appearances.

items.headline: LaVine ended with 19 points (7-17 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 39 minutes during Friday's 106-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: LaVine was steady for most of the night, but his 29-foot pull-up three at the buzzer missed, and Sacramento lost another close one. The veteran guard has been efficient all season, averaging 21.0 points while shooting better than 50 percent from the field.

items.headline: LaVine registered 18 points (8-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 128-107 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: LaVine was efficient with his limited opportunities, connecting on eight of his 12 field-goal attempts, but Sacramento's offense increasingly revolves around Darius Acuff -- the rookie attempted 22 shots Wednesday compared to LaVine's 12. LaVine can still produce strong scoring performances, but his fantasy ceiling is lower than in previous weeks because he'll be the No. 2 option on offense behind Acuff. LaVine has failed to reach the 20-point mark in four of his last five appearances and is averaging just 19.1 points per game since the beginning of November, a downgrade compared to the 23.5 points per contest he averaged in October to open the campaign.

items.headline: LaVine (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: LaVine was under the weather and didn't play in Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. However, he will be back on the floor Wednesday, likely meaning Malik Monk will revert to his usual role as a reserve.

items.headline: LaVine is out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City due to illness, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
items.story: LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.

items.headline: LaVine tallied 31 points (10-16 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals over 33 minutes in Tuesday's 107-100 loss to the Magic.
items.story: LaVine briefly exited the game after rolling his right ankle, but he was able to return after getting checked out in the locker room and appeared to be fine, finishing with a team-high 31 points. He'll have a full two days to rest up before the Kings' next game Friday against Portland.

items.headline: LaVine notched 14 points (4-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 35 minutes during Friday's 124-109 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: LaVine struggled to get anything going, missing five of his six three-point attempts, but a perfect night at the free-throw line kept his scoring respectable. With Darius Acuff taking over more of the offense, the veteran's role and his name in trade talks will be worth watching as Sacramento's season slips away.

items.headline: LaVine recorded 21 points (6-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: LaVine was the Kings' second-leading scorer and chipped in a pair of blocks, but six turnovers dragged down his fantasy line. With Darius Acuff dominating the ball, LaVine has settled into more of a secondary scoring role. That makes him a points-and-threes contributor rather than a well-rounded fantasy option.

items.headline: LaVine (elbow) is available for Monday's game against the Mavericks, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine will shed the questionable tag ahead of Sacramento's matchup with Dallas. He is dealing with soreness in his right elbow after playing a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but he'll fight through the issue and reprise his starting role for the 0-6 Kings.

items.headline: LaVine (elbow) is questionable to play in Monday's game against Dallas.
items.story: LaVine played a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but it's unclear if that was due to the elbow soreness or the game being out of reach for the Kings. Either way, his status will bear monitoring ahead of Monday's clash with the Mavericks. If he's unable to play, Darius Acuff Jr.'s usage would skyrocket, while Malik Monk, Emanuel Sharp and Nique Clifford could all see increased opportunities in the backcourt.

items.headline: LaVine chipped in 11 points (4-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and one assist over 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Saturday was the first time this season that LaVine attempted less than 10 field goals, and his performance broke a five-game streak of 20-plus-point tallies. Part of that lack of production was due to him playing only one minute in the fourth quarter, when the game was well out of reach for the Kings. The veteran wing will finish the month of October having averaged 23.5 points, 3.2 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 2.5 threes over 34.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: LaVine tallied 21 points (7-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, five assists and three steals across 39 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: LaVine struggled with perimeter efficiency, connecting on just three of 10 attempts, but made up for it with five assists and three steals while going 4-for-7 from inside the arc. LaVine is off to an excellent start this season, scoring at least 20 points in every game and averaging 26.0 points per game. He's also shooting at an efficient rate, making 50 percent of his attempts and 35.7 percent of his three-pointers.

items.headline: LaVine supplied 22 points (7-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: LaVine delivered an efficient offensive performance, shooting 70.0 percent from the field while connecting on three triples. The veteran guard was one of three Sacramento players to score at least 20 points, joining De'Andre Hunter (24) and Domantas Sabonis (20). Despite LaVine's strong shooting, the Kings fell to 0-4 to begin the season.

items.headline: LaVine recorded 37 points (13-25 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five assists, two rebounds and two steals in 40 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: LaVine continued his run of strong play to begin the season, exploding for a game-high 37 points on solid efficiency. The 31-year-old pro has totaled at least 20 points and three three-pointers made in each of the team's first three games. He figures to maintain a high level of usage alongside rookie guard Darius Acuff this season.

items.headline: LaVine accumulated 22 points (6-15 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals in 39 minutes during Friday's 128-120 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: LaVine finished second on the team in scoring for the second straight game, though his outside shot was off. The veteran has led the Kings' perimeter attack early on, and he'll continue to play a lot of minutes as Sacramento searches for its first win. He'll next face the Grizzlies on Sunday.

items.headline: LaVine recorded 28 points (10-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds and four assists over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: The veteran guard had twice as many points as any other Sacramento starter, and only three of LaVine's teammates even scored in double digits in the rout. LaVine figures to see heavy usage on a roster lacking in established offensive options as long as he can stay healthy -- he played just 39 regular-season games in 2025-26 due to a hand injury that required surgery, but LaVine looks fully recovered to begin the current campaign.

items.headline: aVine generated 20 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 7-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Friday's 126-97 preseason loss to the Spurs.
items.story: LaVine led the Kings in scoring and posted his best preseason outing, nearly doubling his previous high of 11 points. The Kings went winless in the preseason, and they'll need LaVine's veteran production to get off to a good start against the Clippers in the season opener.

items.headline: LaVine (rest) will play in Friday's preseason game against San Antonio, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine didn't play in Tuesday's exhibition versus Portland. However, he will suit up for the Kings' final preseason game before Opening Night. The 31-year-old will be looking to bounce back during the 2026-27 campaign after averaging 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists over 31.4 minutes in just 39 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: LaVine (rest) will not play in Tuesday's preseason matchup against Portland, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine is among eight Kings players ruled out for Tuesday's contest. His next opportunity to play will come Friday against San Antonio in the preseason finale.

items.headline: LaVine posted 11 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt), two assists, one rebound and three steals in 23 minutes during Saturday's 111-106 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: LaVine didn't have the most productive offensive showing. However, the veteran shined defensively, finishing two steals behind Jonathan Mogbo, who had a game-high five. LaVine is coming off one of least productive seasons in recent memory, averaging 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists over 31.4 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games during the 2025-26 campaign. The 31-year-old has flashed All-Star upside in previous seasons, though it's unknown if those days are well behind him.

items.headline: LaVine finished with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT) and one rebound in 15 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: LaVine started at shooting guard but played only during the first half as Sacramento limited the workload of its veterans. The 31-year-old remains one of the Kings' primary scoring options after averaging 19.2 points during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: LaVine is healthy entering training camp, Kings general manager Scott Perry said Monday, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: LaVine underwent season-ending surgery in February to repair a torn tendon in his right fifth finger, an injury that limited him to 39 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. He averaged 19.2 points per game while shooting 47.9 percent from the field and 39.0 percent from three, and his healthy status entering camp puts him on track to resume a prominent role in Sacramento's backcourt.

items.headline: LaVine (hand) exercised his $49 million player option for 2026-27 on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: LaVine underwent season-ending surgery on his right hand before the 2025-26 All-Star break. He averaged 19.2 points in 39 regular-season games last season and was a two-time All-Star before being traded to the Kings in February of 2025. The Kings are listening to trade offers for LaVine and Domantas Sabonis (knee), but their hefty contracts are making things difficult. If LaVine stays in Sacramento, he would likely take a back seat as the Kings try to develop 2026 No. 7 overall pick Darius Acuff.

items.headline: LaVine (hand) is projected to have a new backcourt partner after the Kings selected Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: LaVine primarily worked alongside Russell Westbrook in 2024-25, the latter of whom is an unrestricted free agent this offseason. LaVine, on the other hand, has a player option worth over $48 million for 2026-27 and figures to exercise it after averaging 19.2 points per game over 39 regular-season appearances last year, his lowest output since 2017-18. Assuming he remains with the Kings, LaVine should have a good chance of having a bounce-back season.

items.headline: LaVine will undergo season-ending surgery on his right hand after the All-Star break, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: After missing Sacramento's final three outings before the All-Star break due to right finger soreness, LaVine is scheduled to undergo season-ending hand surgery. The veteran swingman will finish the 2025-26 season with averages of 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists while shooting 47.9 percent from the field and 39.0 percent from downtown across 31.4 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games (37 starts). He holds a $48.97 million player option for the 2026-27 campaign. With LaVine sidelined, Nique Clifford should continue to see an expanded role, while Malik Monk (illness) and Devin Carter are also candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: LaVine (finger) is out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: LaVine will miss a third straight game due to finger soreness. His next chance to play won't come until after the All-Star break, so he'll have over a week to rest and recover. In the meantime, look for Nique Clifford and Devin Carter to see more minutes.

items.headline: LaVine (finger) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: LaVine will be sidelined for a second consecutive game due to right finger soreness, and his last opportunity to suit up before the All-Star break is Wednesday against the Jazz. Nique Clifford and Devin Carter should see more minutes in LaVine's absence.

items.headline: Sexton closed Tuesday's 118-114 overtime victory over the Hornets with 10 points (3-12 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and three assists in 25 minutes.
items.story: Sexton struggled with his shot off the bench, but he calmly knocked down two free throws in overtime to pull Los Angeles within a point. He has been a reliable source of instant offense for the second unit all season, averaging 10.7 points.

items.headline: Sexton (head) is available for Sunday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Sexton will shed the questionable tag and suit up versus Phoenix. The veteran guard is averaging 10.3 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 2.6 assists in 17.8 minutes across 12 games this season.

items.headline: Sexton (head) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Suns, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Sexton was a full participant in Saturday's practice, and while the questionable tag indicates some caution, he's trending in the right direction and could be available Sunday. The veteran has been putting up solid numbers of late, scoring in double digits in all but one of his last five appearances and averaging 11.0 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game in that span.

items.headline: Sexton (head) was a full participant in Saturday's practice, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Sexton left Wednesday's game against Milwaukee early after bumping heads with Ryan Rollins and required stitches to close a cut on his forehead. However, Sexton escaped the incident without a concussion, and his ability to practice without restraint is a positive sign for his availability Sunday against the Suns.

items.headline: Sexton did not return to Wednesday's 123-112 win over the Bucks and required stitches to close a cut on his forehead, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Sexton knocked noggins with Ryan Rollins, but it sounds like he's avoided a concussion, so he should be able to get out there for Sunday's game in Phoenix. Austin Reaves (heel) also exited Wednesday's game, and if he needs to sit out Sunday, Sexton would have the chance for some extended minutes.

items.headline: Sexton went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against the Bucks after bumping heads with Ryan Rollins, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: There's a little over six minutes left in Wednesday's game and the Lakers are up by 20, so Sexton may be done for the night. Austin Reaves also exited Wednesday's game with an undisclosed injury, and if both these guys need to miss time, Ziaire Williams, Cameron Carr and Quentin Grimes (finger) would help pick up the slack.

items.headline: Sexton contributed 17 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 7-8 FT), two rebounds and two assists across 24 minutes during Sunday's 121-116 victory over the Pistons.
items.story: Sexton gave Los Angeles an efficient scoring boost off the bench, matching Ziaire Williams for the second-most points on the team behind Austin Reaves' 43. The veteran guard made seven of eight trips to the charity stripe, helping offset his lack of three-point production. Sexton remains a scoring-dependent fantasy option, though his offensive opportunities could increase when the Lakers are missing key backcourt contributors. Luka Doncic (back) sat this one out.

items.headline: Sexton ended Sunday's 131-125 victory over the Raptors with 14 points (6-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 19 minutes.
items.story: Sexton led the Lakers' reserves in scoring, making six of his 10 field-goal attempts in an efficient offensive showing. He remains a useful source of bench scoring, though his relatively limited playing time makes consistent fantasy production difficult to sustain.

items.headline: Sexton had 21 points (6-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds and two assists over 21 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers.
items.story: The 21 points were a season high for Sexton, who remained on the second unit even with Luka Doncic (back) held out of the lineup. Instead, Quentin Grimes moved into the starting five.
