Through four games this season, all off the bench, Sexton has averaged 12.0 points, 2.3 assists, 2.0 boards, 1.5 threes and 0.8 steals in 17.8 minutes.

items.headline: Sexton totaled nine points (4-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and four assists over 14 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Sexton has now made three straight appearances off the bench for the Lakers after missing the start of the year with a calf injury. His fantasy upside should remain capped while the team's backcourt is nearly fully healthy.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Sexton took a seat for Wednesday's 2026-27 season opener against the Warriors as a precaution, but he'll be ready to make his team debut Friday evening. He's expected to be utilized off the bench behind Luka Doncic and will be on a minutes restriction, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said that Sexton (calf) did not experience a setback, but the Lakers will sit him out of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors as a precaution, Daniel Starkland of Lakers Nation reports.
items.story: It sounds like Sexton is day-to-day, so for now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Clippers. Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili will help pick up the slack in Sexton's absence.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) won't play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors, per Khobi Price of The California Post.
items.story: Sexton isn't ready to make his Lakers debut Wednesday due to a calf strain. The veteran guard's absence should open the door to more playing time for Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.
items.story: Sexton did not play during the preseason due to a right soleus strain, but he was able to get through the Lakers' past two practices, so he's trending in the right direction. He'll likely have some minutes restrictions if he's cleared to play.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) fully practiced Monday, per Dan Woike of The Athletic.
items.story: Sexton missed the end of the preseason with a lower right leg injury, but he's trending in the right direction. His status remains uncertain for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against the Nuggets, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton will end up missing the entire preseason due to a lower right leg injury. However, head coach JJ Redick said the veteran guard is trending in the right direction ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) participated in Thursday's practice but didn't take part in any live action, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton is considered day-to-day with a lower-leg injury and didn't scrimmage Thursday. He can be viewed as questionable for Friday's preseason finale against Denver until the Lakers provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Sexton remains day-to-day with a lower-leg injury. His final chance to suit up in the preseason will come Friday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Saturday that Sexton is day-to-day due to a lower-leg injury, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton has missed multiple preseason games due to what was initially described as a lower-body injury, but Redick was more specific about the nature of Sexton's health concern Saturday. With two more exhibition games left on the schedule, the Lakers may keep Sexton sidelined until the team's regular-season opener against the Warriors on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Sexton (lower body) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against Sacramento, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Sexton has been battling a lower-body injury and will miss his third matchup of the preseason. However, the team isn't overly concerned at this point for what coach JJ Redick is deeming a minor injury for the 27-year-old guard, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com.

items.headline: Sexton (lower body) won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: It's unknown if Sexton will be available to play during the preseason, though his next opportunity to get on the floor will come Thursday against Sacramento. The 27-year-old ended the 2025-26 campaign with the Bulls, averaging 17.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals over 26.0 minutes per contest in 26 regular-season games.

items.headline: Sexton has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Kings due to a lower-body issue, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly what Sexton is dealing with, though he's considered day-to-day. His next chance to suit up in the preseason will come Tuesday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton agreed to a two-year, $19 million contract with the Lakers on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: LeBron James is leaving Los Angeles, and the Lakers are retooling via free agency. After re-signing Austin Reaves to a massive extension, the Lakers have signed Sexton, Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili, while pulling off a sign-and-trade for Walker Kessler. As things stand, Sexton appears set for a backup role behind Luka Doncic and Reaves in 2026-27.

items.headline: Sexton had 19 points (8-16 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 149-128 loss to Dallas.
items.story: Sexton played well in the final game, but it might be the last time we see Sexton in a Bulls uniform. Sexton is an unrestricted free agent and can shop around for a contract with another club. Given a depth chart that's deep at the guard position, the Bulls may not be compelled to give him a better offer.

items.headline: Sexton (finger/elbow) is available for Sunday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Sexton popped up on the injury report with a right finger injury and a left elbow contusion, though he'll shake off his probable tag and suit up in Chicago's regular-season finale. The 26-year-old guard has started four straight games for the shorthanded Bulls, during which he has averaged 18.0 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals in 30.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sexton (finger, elbow) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Although the Bulls aren't going to the postseason, Sexton is expected to suit up for Chicago's final contest of the 2025-26 campaign. He is coming off a 12-point effort in Friday's 127-103 loss to Orlando. However, Sexton has an excellent chance to turn it around against one of the worst teams in the NBA.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is listed as available for Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Sexton was in danger of missing this contest, but he is officially cleared to suit up. The 27-year-old is coming off one of his best performances of the 2025-26 campaign, finishing with 27 points, three rebounds, two assists and three steals across 34 minutes in Thursday's 119-108 win over Washington.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is probable for Friday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Sexton racked up 27 points (12-21 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals in 34 minutes during Thursday's 119-108 victory over Washington and will likely be available for the second half of Chicago's back-to-back set. With Josh Giddey (hamstring) still sidelined, Sexton should continue to start and see elevated usage.

items.headline: Sexton racked up 27 points (12-21 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals in 34 minutes during Thursday's 119-108 victory over Washington.
items.story: Sexton was one of three Chicago starters to finish with 20-plus points, as Tre Jones led the way with 31 points while Leonard Miller chipped in 26 points. This marks the first time Sexton has reached the 20-point threshold since March 30, and he looked much more comfortable on the offensive end after hitting on 37.2 percent of his tries from the field in his previous three matchups leading up to Thursday.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is available for Thursday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Sexton is expectedly shedding a probable designation Thursday with a right finger injury. The veteran guard is playing at a high level, averaging 19.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.8 steals in 27.6 minutes per contest over his last nine games.

items.headline: Sexton is probable for Thursday's game against the Wizards due to a right finger injury.
items.story: The probable tag suggests Sexton will suit up Thursday despite not being 100 percent healthy. He's averaging 18.8 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game over his last 10 appearances, and Thursday's matchup looks like a favorable one on paper against a lackluster Washington team.

items.headline: Sexton recorded 15 points (5-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, seven assists and four steals over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 129-98 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Sexton ripped away two steals within his first five minutes of play, and he finished with a season-high four swipes in the blowout win. He'll have another chance to take advantage of the Wizards' lackadaisical play in a rematch with Washington on Thursday.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is available for Tuesday's game versus the Wizards.
items.story: Josh Giddey (hamstring) is out, so Sexton should see quality minutes against the Wizards. Over his past six games, Sexton has averaged 20.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 3.3 triples and 1.3 steals per contest.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is listed as probable for Tuesday's game against Washington.
items.story: Sexton logged 31 minutes in Sunday's 120-110 loss to Phoenix, finishing with 18 points, nine rebounds, one assist and three steals. Assuming the 27-year-old can suit up, he could be more productive than usual against one of the worst defensive squads in the league, especially with teammates Josh Giddey (hamstring) and Matas Buzelis (illness) already ruled out.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) will play Sunday against Phoenix, Will Gottlieb of AllCHGO.com reports.
items.story: Sexton will be able to fight through a minor finger injury to suit for Sunday's tilt. He's been playing at a high level on the offensive end lately, averaging 21.0 points while converting at a clip of 52.2 percent from the field in his previous five appearances. With Josh Giddey (hamstring) sidelined, Sexton will slide back into the starting lineup and should retain increased usage.

items.headline: Sexton is probable to play Sunday against the Suns due to a right finger injury.
items.story: Sexton is dealing with a minor injury to a finger on his shooting hand, but it's not expected to keep him out of Sunday's game. Josh Giddey (hamstring) is questionable to play, and if he gets ruled out, that would open up minutes and a potential starting role for Sexton.

items.headline: Sexton registered 19 points (6-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes during Friday's 136-96 loss to New York.
items.story: Sexton returned to the bench with Josh Giddey (hamstring) back in the starting lineup, but he produced another strong showing as a scoring weapon for a Bulls team that's already out of playoff contention. Sexton has scored 15-plus points in seven consecutive games and is clearly ending the season on a strong note, showing he remains a very viable option ahead of hitting the open market in the summer.

items.headline: Hansen racked up two points (1-2 FG, 0-2 FT), one rebound and one assist over 12 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: The second-year center saw the floor due to Robert Williams' (rest) absence, though Hansen didn't make much of an impact. Through nine regular-season appearances, he's averaged 3.3 points and 2.6 rebounds in 9.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hansen accumulated six points (2-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 13 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 win over Utah.
items.story: Hansen earned a season-high 13 minutes with Donovan Clingan limited to just 15 minutes due to foul trouble against the Jazz. Hansen's playing time will continue to fluctuate between the Blazers and the Rip City Remix of the G League, and his opportunities should remain limited as long as Clingan and Robert Williams are both healthy.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers exercised their third-year team option on Hansen for the 2027-28 season, the team announced Thursday.
items.story: Portland's decision keeps the 2025 first-round pick under contract through the 2027-28 campaign. The 7-foot-1 center remains a developmental piece in the Trail Blazers' frontcourt, where Donovan Clingan currently occupies the starting role. The transaction has no immediate impact on Hansen's fantasy outlook, as his value will depend on his ability to carve out a consistent role in Portland's rotation.

items.headline: Hansen was assigned to the Rip City Remix on Wednesday, the Trail Blazers announced.
items.story: With Portland sending him to the G League, Hansen is set for additional developmental reps away from the NBA roster. The move suggests the center won't be part of the Trail Blazers' immediate rotation while he's with the Remix.

items.headline: Yang finished with 13 points (6-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four rebounds and four assists across 21 minutes off the bench in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: Yang delivered an efficient performance, converting six of his eight field-goal attempts while matching Deni Avdija for the second-most assists on the team. The second-year center also connected on his lone three-point attempt and played more minutes than any other Portland player. However, with Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams (rest) ahead of him in the frontcourt rotation, Yang may have difficulty carving out a substantial role during the regular season.

items.headline: Hansen registered 19 points (8-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block in 25 minutes during China's 89-87 win over Lebanon in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Hansen starred for China on Monday, leading the club in scoring and rebounding. Hansen, a 2025 first-rounder, is looking to carve out a more prominent role in his second season with Portland, but he'll likely need to overtake Robert Williams and Micah Potter for a rotation spot. With that in mind, Hansen's most likely pathway to steady playing time resides with the G League's Rip City Remix.

items.headline: Hansen recorded 15 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 20 minutes during China's 83-57 win over Qatar in Thursday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Hansen came off the bench but led China in both scoring and rebounding, continuing an encouraging offseason for the 21-year-old center. The 2025 first-round pick had a limited role as a rookie with Portland, averaging just 2.2 points and 1.5 rebounds per game during the regular season, but he'll have an opportunity to push for a larger role in his sophomore campaign.

items.headline: Hansen recorded nine points (3-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 24 minutes during Friday's 83-79 Summer League loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Hansen led the Blazers in rebounds and was one point shy from recording his second double-double over his last three Summer League games. The 2025 first-rounder is set to enter training camp battling with Robert Williams, Sidy Cissoko and Micah Potter for the backup center job behind Donovan Clingan for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Hansen finished with 13 points (6-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and four blocks across 26 minutes in Thursday's 108-101 Summer League victory over the Nuggets.
items.story: Hansen didn't have his most productive offensive showing Thursday, but he certainly got after it on the defensive end by finishing the evening with four blocks. The 21-year-old appeared in 43 regular-season games for the Trail Blazers in 2025-26, averaging 2.2 points and 1.5 rebounds over 7.0 minutes. Although Hansen's development is still a work in progress, it's reasonable to assume he will continue to improve throughout the 2026-27 campaign, especially if he gets more playing time.

items.headline: Hansen racked up 18 points (7-8 FG, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds and five assists across 21 minutes in Monday's 111-84 Summer League win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Hansen missed the front end of this back-to-back set with an illness but returned to action Monday. The big man turned in an extremely efficient performance and finished as Portland's second-leading scorer. He also grabbed a game-high 10 rebounds while leading the Trail Blazers in assists. Hansen has supplied at least nine boards and four dimes in both of his Las Vegas Summer League appearances.

items.headline: Hansen (illness) is available for Monday's Summer League game against Minnesota.
items.story: Hansen will return Monday, marking his second appearance of the Las Vegas Summer League. The 21-year-old last played in Friday's 81-79 loss to Phoenix, finishing with 12 points, nine rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes.

items.headline: Hansen (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Magic.
items.story: Hansen is under the weather and will miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's next chance to play will come Monday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Hansen finished Friday's 81-79 Summer League loss to the Suns with 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), nine rebounds and four assists over 26 minutes.
items.story: The second-year center led the Trail Blazers in rebounds, finishing one board shy of a double-double, while ending as the team's third-leading scorer behind DJ Steward (21 points) and Frankie Fidler (13 points). Hansen averaged just 7.0 minutes per game across 43 regular-season contests during the 2025-26 campaign, and he'll battle against Robert Williams for the backup center role behind Donovan Clingan for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Hansen is expected to play in the 2026 NBA Summer League, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Hansen will join Portland's Summer League squad after he is done playing for China in the FIBA World Cup qualifier. The 2025 No. 16 overall pick is coming off a quiet inaugural campaign during which he averaged 2.2 points, 1.5 rebounds, 0.5 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.1 steals across 7.0 minutes in 43 regular-season appearances. With the Trail Blazers in need of depth behind Donovan Clingan, Hansen will need to impress during Summer League and throughout training camp if he hopes to earn a meaningful role for the team in the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Hansen contributed zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) in one minute during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hansen's role with Portland was sparse during his rookie year, as he also made 14 G League appearances for the Rip City Remix. Overall, the 2025 first-rounder averaged 2.2 points, 1.5 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 7.0 minutes per contest over 43 regular-season games with the Trail Blazers. Robert Williams is an impending unrestricted free agent this summer, however, so Hansen could have an opportunity during training camp to claim the top backup center role behind Donovan Clingan.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen will rejoin the Trail Blazers after appearing in the Remix's last two contests and averaging 19.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks in 33.0 minutes. Unless Portland is without at least one of Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams for Sunday's game against Washington, Hansen isn't expected to be featured in the rotation.

items.headline: Portland assigned Hansen to the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: Hansen logged nine minutes at the NBA level Monday against Brooklyn, finishing with four points and three rebounds. He'll continue to see the bulk of his minutes with Rip City in the short term.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: The Trail Blazers will play the second leg of a back-to-back set Monday, so Hansen will be summoned to provide further depth in the frontcourt in the event Robert Williams (knee) is rested. Even if Williams ends up sitting out, Hansen won't be assured a spot in the Portland rotation, as interim head coach Tiago Splitter could turn to Sidy Cissoko to serve as a small-ball center when starter Donovan Clingan is off the court.

items.headline: Hansen played the final 48.9 seconds of Friday's 124-114 win over the Jazz, finishing with no statistics during his time on the court.
items.story: Recalled from the G League's Rip City Remix prior to Friday's contest, Hansen was unable to crack the Portland rotation while the game was competitive. Even though the Trail Blazers were without their top backup center in Robert Williams (knee) on Friday, interim head coach Tiago Splitter opted to run out small-ball lineups when starting center Donovan Clingan was off the court. Hansen looks like he'll continue to receive limited run at the NBA level for the rest of the season while he's yet to gain full trust of the coaching staff.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers assigned Hansen to the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: As such, Hansen won't be available for Tuesday's game against the Hornets. The rookie first-rounder has bounced back and forth between the G League and NBA this season, but he has not played double-digit minutes for Portland since Jan. 27 against Washington. In his last G League outing against the Valley Suns on Saturday, Hansen finished with 15 points (6-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal over 23 minutes.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen appeared in Rip City's wins over the Valley Suns on Friday and Saturday, totaling 36 points and 18 rebounds in those two outings. He hasn't logged double-digit minutes for the parent club since Jan. 27, a trend that is likely to continue Sunday versus the Pacers.

items.headline: Hansen (back) is available for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder will shed his questionable tag due to mid-back soreness and could see increased playing time Sunday due to Robert Williams (knee) being sidelined. Hansen appeared in eight outings in February, during which he averaged 1.8 points in 4.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Hansen is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Hawks due to mid-back soreness.
items.story: Hansen was able to play through the issue in Thursday's win over the Bulls, though he saw just two minutes of playing time. However, if he's cleared to play Sunday, Hansen would be in line for a larger role off the bench due to the absence of Robert Williams (knee).

items.headline: Hansen (back) is available for Thursday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hansen popped up on the Blazers' injury report Wednesday due to mid-back soreness, but the rookie first-rounder has been given the green light to play Thursday. Donovan Clingan (illness) won't play, so Hansen and Robert Williams are slated for elevated roles in Clingan's absence.

items.headline: Hansen is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Bulls due to mid-back soreness.
items.story: Hansen may have picked up the injury during his most recent appearance in the G League with the Rip City Remix on Sunday, when he posted 11 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 29 minutes in a 118-113 loss to the Santa Cruz Warriors. Robert Williams (foot) is also listed as questionable, so if both Williams and Hansen aren't available Thursday, Portland could turn to Sidy Cissoko or Jerami Grant to play center when starter Donovan Clingan is off the court.

items.headline: Hansen totaled no counting stats in four minutes during Friday's 127-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Hansen appeared during garbage time, continuing what has been a disappointing rookie season thus far. Although he has been able to see the court on most nights over the past month, his playing time remains largely underwhelming. In his last 12 appearances, he has averaged 2.1 points and 1.8 rebounds in 8.6 minutes per game. Outside of dynasty formats, he holds no fantasy value at this point.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: The rookie first-round pick should be available for the Trail Blazers' next game Thursday versus the Heat but is unlikely to be included in the rotation.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen will be available to play Saturday against the Lakers after being recalled. He last appeared for the Blazers on Tuesday, logging three points and two rebounds in 13 minutes.

items.headline: Hansen (coach's decision) didn't appear off the bench Thursday in the Trail Blazers' 117-101 win over the Hawks.
items.story: After making an appearance in the G League for the Rip City Remix on Wednesday and producing 22 points, seven rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 30 minutes in a 123-99 win over the Oklahoma City Blue, Hansen rejoined Portland ahead of its matchup with the Hawks. However, the rookie big man found himself outside of the rotation, as Portland went with Jerami Grant, Robert Williams and Duop Reath as its reserve big men before frontcourt starters Sidy Cissoko and Donovan Clingan. Hansen could have more G League assignments in his future if playing time remains hard to come by at the NBA level.

items.headline: Hansen collected 22 points (6-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 123-99 G League win over the Oklahoma City Blue.
items.story: Hansen led the Rip City Remix in points Wednesday to go with a full stat line. The rookie first-rounder is averaging 17.2 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 steals per game over six G League appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Hansen provided two points (0-1 FG, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 11 minutes during Saturday's 115-110 win over the Spurs.
items.story: Hansen played at least 10 minutes for the fourth time in the past five games, although his production has not followed suit. During that time, the rookie has averaged just 1.6 points and 2.0 rebounds, highlighting just how far he has to go before he becomes a viable NBA center.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: Hansen joined the Remix for Monday's 116-110 win over the Stockton Kings, recording 18 points (8-11 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 10 rebounds and four assists in 31 minutes. He hasn't seen the floor in each of Portland's last two games and isn't likely to play meaningful minutes unless there are injuries to multiple centers.

items.headline: Hansen was assigned to the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: Hansen has been splitting time between the Trail Blazers and the Remix all season. The Blazers got back Donovan Clingan (leg) and Robert Williams (illness) on Sunday.

items.headline: Hansen (face) is available for Sunday's game against the Warriors, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Hansen didn't play in Thursday's loss to the Pelicans due to a face injury, but the rookie first-rounder has been cleared to play Sunday. He started in his last outing, but he'll likely come off the bench due to the returns of Donovan Clingan (lower leg) and Robert Williams (illness).

items.headline: Hansen (face) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Hansen is in jeopardy of missing his second consecutive contest due to a facial contusion. However, if the rookie is cleared to play, he could see increased minutes if Donovan Clingan (lower leg) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Hansen (face) will not play Thursday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Portland is going to be very thin in the frontcourt Thursday with Donovan Clingan (leg) and Robert Williams (illness) both out as well. As a result, the team could lean on Duop Reath and Kris Murray.

items.headline: Camara racked up 18 points (6-11 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals in 37 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Camara scored all 18 points after halftime, rebounding from consecutive inefficient outings against Minnesota. His five combined steals and blocks showcased his defensive upside, while four triples added significant category value. With Deni Avdija (foot) sidelined, Camara's heavy workload strengthens his appeal in category leagues.

items.headline: Camara (soreness) has been cleared to play Thursday against Milwaukee.
items.story: Camara's availability was in question due to soreness, but he'll be able to play through the issue Thursday evening. He's averaging 10.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 steals over his last five appearances.

items.headline: Camara is questionable to play Thursday against the Bucks due to general soreness.
items.story: Camara is in danger of missing his first game of the season due to general soreness. If he's forced to the sidelines, his minutes will be divvied up amongst Sidy Cissoko and Jrue Holiday.

items.headline: Camara provided 10 points (4-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist and one steal in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 106-105 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Camara reached double figures but labored with his shot for a second straight night, and his layup attempt at the buzzer rimmed out. The forward was a reliable shooter early in the season but has cooled off in November. Portland needs his offense to come around to go along with his usual defensive work, especially during nights when Deni Avdija (foot) is sidelined.

items.headline: Camara contributed 14 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 36 minutes during Friday's 120-107 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Camara gave Portland a quiet but efficient 14 points in 36 minutes. He'll never be the Blazers' top option, but his defensive skill set makes him one of the team's most valuable role players. With Portland down two key guards, his minutes should stay high.

items.headline: Camara accumulated 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 30 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Camara was Portland's most efficient scorer Friday, hitting half of his three-point attempts while also doing the defensive work the Blazers count on. When he's making shots from the corner, Portland's starting lineup gets much harder to guard. He's a key piece of the rotation, and nights like this show why he's playing starter minutes.

items.headline: Camara posted 11 points (4-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-6 FT), four rebounds and two assists across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns.
items.story: Camara has now scored in double digits in six of his first seven appearances. He'll likely remain a low-end fantasy option, as Camara isn't handling additional usage in Ja Morant's (hamstring) absence.

items.headline: Camara ended Saturday's 112-90 victory over Utah with 14 points (4-9 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two steals in 31 minutes.
items.story: The fourth-year forward continues to fill up the bucket from long distance. Camara has drained at least three three-pointers in five straight games to open the season, averaging 15.2 points, 4.0 threes, 2.2 boards, 1.4 steals and 1.2 assists in 26.2 minutes and shooting a blistering 51.3 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Camara produced 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 26 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Camara scored double digits for the fourth straight game, adding four combined steals and blocks. He has been arguably Portland's most consistent performer, averaging 15.5 points, 1.3 steals, and 4.0 three-pointers in 25.0 minutes per game. He is currently shooting an impressive 61.1 percent from the field, well above what he has done throughout his career. Taking this into consideration, he could be viewed as a potential sell-high candidate.

items.headline: Camara closed with 12 points (4-5 FG, 4-5 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 victory over the Lakers.

The big man wasn't very efficient from the field, though he still led all players in scoring. He also paced all players in rebounds and finished second on the Celtics in blocks. Garza figures to serve as the Celtics' third-string center in 2026-27.

items.headline: Garza will start Thursday's preseason game against Cleveland, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: The Celtics are expected to rest several rotation players Thursday, opening the door for Garza to step into the first unit. The 27-year-old center will face an uphill battle for steady minutes during the regular season.

items.headline: Garza recorded 10 points (4-8 FG, 2-2 FT) and seven rebounds in 16 minutes during Bosnia and Herzegovina's 78-76 win over Italy in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 27-year-old is coming off a career-best 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged 8.1 points and 4.1 rebounds during the regular season for Boston. Garza remains under contract with the Celtics for 2026-27, but his limited defensive versatility and competition for frontcourt minutes could make it difficult for him to carve out a large enough role to provide consistent fantasy value.

items.headline: Garza produced zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one block in nine minutes during Saturday's 109-100 loss to the 76ers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Garza was elevated into the starting lineup, presumably to deal with the size of Joel Embiid. Although it may have made sense on the surface, Garza was simply no match for Embiid on either end of the floor and ended up playing just nine minutes. The Game 7 loss closes out what was an indifferent season for Garza. While he was mostly a part of the rotation, his role fluctuated and his playing time was typically reliant on the availability of either Neemias Queta or Nikola Vucevic. Across 69 regular-season appearances (six starts), Garza averaged 8.1 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 16.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Garza will start Saturday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against Philadelphia, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The 27-year-old center will get the starting nod over Neemias Queta in Saturday's do-or-die matchup. Garza started six games in the regular season, during which he averaged 12.3 points, 5.7 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 22.7 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Garza is not in the Celtics' lineup against the 76ers for Game 1 on Sunday.
items.story: Garza started in Boston's regular-season finale against Orlando on April 12, when he played 38 minutes and finished with 27 points, 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and three three-pointers in a 113-108 win. He will retreat to the bench for Sunday's contest and serve in a backup role behind Neemias Queta and Nikola Vucevic, though Garza may have a hard time finding some playing time given that rotations tend to shrink for the playoffs.

items.headline: Garza supplied 27 points (10-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal across 38 minutes during Sunday's 113-108 win over the Magic.
items.story: Garza was a force to be reckoned with, helping lift Boston to an impressive victory over Orlando. This performance puts a cherry on top of what has been a solid regular season for Garza, albeit as the second- or third-string center on most nights. With Neemias Queta (toe) and Nikola Vucevic (finger) both likely to return for the playoffs, Garza will almost certainly resume his role as a depth piece.

items.headline: Garza is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Magic on Sunday.
items.story: With Neemias Queta (toe) sidelined, Garza will be in Boston's starting five for the sixth time this season. Garza's last start took place March 30 against the Hawks, when he played 28 minutes and finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one block in a 112-102 loss.

items.headline: Garza had 14 points (6-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 16 minutes during Friday's 144-118 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: The Celtics held Neemias Queta to just 13 minutes Friday, which was likely done in an effort to preserve the standout big man ahead of the playoffs. Garza hadn't appeared in any of Boston's prior three games, which went hand-in-hand with the return of Nikola Vucevic, and Garza may move back out of the rotation once the postseason begins.

items.headline: Garza is not in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Heat on Wednesday.
items.story: Garza excelled in his spot start against the Hawks on Monday, when he played 28 minutes and finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in a 112-102 loss. He'll revert to his usual bench role for Wednesday's contest due to the return of Neemias Queta (thumb). Garza should continue to see meaningful minutes off the bench until Nikola Vucevic (finger) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Garza posted 20 points (8-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, one assist and one block over 28 minutes during Boston's 112-102 loss to Atlanta on Monday.
items.story: Garza made his fifth start of the season (and first since Feb. 8 against New York) due to the absence of Neemias Queta (thumb). Garza helped keep things close in the first half with 13 points (eight in the opening quarter) and finished as the Celtics' second-leading scorer behind Jaylen Brown (29 points). It was also Garza's second 20-plus-point game with Boston. He will likely revert to the bench for Wednesday's contest against the Heat, assuming Queta is cleared to return. Garza has averaged 17.7 minutes per game since March 1, with most of that time coinciding with the absence of Nikola Vucevic (finger).

items.headline: Garza is starting Monday's game against the Hawks, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Neemias Queta (thumb) has been ruled out for Monday's clash, which opens the door for Garza to make his fifth start of the 2025-26 campaign. His last start dates back to Feb. 8 against New York, when he recorded six points and three rebounds in 15 minutes.

items.headline: Garza provided 22 points (9-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-5 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal across 27 minutes during Friday's 117-112 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Garza was one of the most productive players for the Celtics in this tight win and ended up delivering a new season-high mark in scoring. Don't expect the big man to suddenly become a reliable scoring weapon for Boston, let alone a player you should target in fantasy ahead of the playoffs. This was likely a one-off performance for the big man, who has scored at least 15 points in just nine of his 60 appearances in 2025-26. Garza was averaging just 8.4 points and 3.4 rebounds per game in March before this 22-point explosion.

items.headline: Garza amassed 15 points (5-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one rebound and three assists in 15 minutes during Saturday's 111-100 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Garza was productive off the bench, scoring 15 points, falling just one point short of his season high. With Nikola Vucevic (finger) on the sideline, Garza has cemented himself as the primary backup behind Neemias Queta. While this was an encouraging performance, as a player outside the top 280 in seven games over the past two weeks, Garza's value is limited to deeper formats.

items.headline: Garza contributed 10 points (4-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), three rebounds, two blocks and one assist over 18 minutes during Friday's 120-100 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Garza saw at least 15 minutes of action for a third consecutive contest due to Nikola Vucevic suffering a fractured finger in the opening quarter. Garza turned in a solid outing on the offensive end, scoring in double figures for the first time since Feb. 4. He also chipped in at least two blocks for just the third time this season. Vucevic is expected to miss at least one month with the finger injury, so Garza is likely to operate as Neemias Queta's primary backup for the time being.

items.headline: Garza racked up seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds and one assist across 20 minutes during Monday's 108-81 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Garza saw meaningful minutes, with Neemias Queta given the night off for rest purposes. Although Garza had been trending up prior to the trade deadline, the acquisition of Nikola Vucevic put an end to any fantasy upside he might have had. For now, he should be looked at as nothing more than a schedule-based streaming consideration.

items.headline: Garza contributed three points (1-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and three rebounds in four minutes during Tuesday's 97-81 win over the Suns.
items.story: Garza continues to play third fiddle at center following the acquisition of Nikola Vucevic prior to the trade deadline, playing limited minutes behind both Vucevic and Neemias Queta. In four games over the past two weeks, Garza has averaged just 1.5 points and 1.0 rebounds in 3.6 minutes per contest, leaving him well off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Garza will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against the Bulls, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: Garza started the past three games for the Celtics, but head coach Joe Mazzulla will switch things up for Wednesday's match. As a reserve this season, Garza owns averages of 8.1 points and 4.4 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Garza is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Rockets on Wednesday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: With Nikola Vucevic (recently traded) yet to make his Celtics debut and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Sam Hauser (thumb) both sidelined, Garza will make his second start of the season Wednesday, when he'll form a frontcourt with Neemias Queta. Garza has logged double-digit points in three of his last four outings, and over that span he has averaged 10.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 threes and 0.8 steals over 18.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Garza registered 16 points (6-8 FG, 4-4 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 20 minutes during Tuesday's 110-100 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Garza connected on a season-high four three-pointers, helping the Celtics to a relatively comfortable win. While Garza has been able to carve out a somewhat consistent role as the backup center, Tuesday's acquisition of Nikola Vucevic from the Bulls could signal an end to that. Those holding Garza in deeper formats will want to keep a close eye on the rotation once Vucevic lands in Boston.

items.headline: Garza (illness) is available to play Wednesday against Atlanta, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Garza did not play Monday against the Trail Blazers due to this illness, but he will return after a one-game absence. With teammate Neemias Queta (illness) ruled out, Garza may have a chance at starting, but he will still likely split minutes with Amari Williams.

items.headline: Garza (illness) is questionable to play Wednesday versus the Hawks.
items.story: An illness forced Garza to the sidelines for Monday's win over Portland, but it might end up only being a one-game absence for the backup big man. If Garza returns Wednesday, Amari Williams will likely lose most of his minutes.

items.headline: Garza (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: Garza was added to the injury report as questionable earlier in the day due to an illness, and he'll ultimately be held out of Monday's clash. Neemias Queta and Amari Williams should see more playing time with Garza sidelined.

items.headline: Garza (illness) is questionable for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Garza was a late addition to the injury report, presumably after waking up under the weather. He's played a minor role in recent weeks with 17.3 minutes per contest over his last seven games. The Celtics could lean on some small-ball lineups if the center is unable to go.

items.headline: Garza finished Thursday's 119-114 win over the Heat with 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal over 28 minutes.
items.story: With Josh Minott (ankle) injured and tumbling down the depth chart, Garza is seizing a strong grip on the backup center gig behind Neemias Queta. Garza has averaged 9.8 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 21.9 minutes per contest in his last 13 games, shooting 64.9 percent from the field.

items.headline: Garza had 11 points (5-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and five rebounds over 19 minutes during Wednesday's 114-110 loss to Denver.
items.story: Garza has come to life to open January by scoring in double digits in three of his first four appearances of the month. He's averaging 21.8 minutes over this stretch. He should continue to see opportunities at center, as he appears to be close on the heels of Neemias Queta, who is averaging 23.8 minutes over this same four-game span.

items.headline: Robinson (illness) is out for Tuesday's game against Washington, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: With Robinson set to miss a third contest due to an illness, Boston will again be without one of its primary center options. His absence should continue to leave more frontcourt minutes available for Neemias Queta and Luka Garza on Tuesday, with the former being in line to see the lion's share of the playing time.

items.headline: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: Robinson will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to an illness. The big man's next opportunity to play will come Tuesday at Washington. Luka Garza will likely see increased minutes in Robinson's stead.

items.headline: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: Robinson is under the weather and will not play in the front end of Boston's back-to-back set, but he could be available for Sunday night's game against the Warriors. With Robinson sidelined, Luka Garza and Chris Cenac should both see a bump in minutes behind starting center Neemias Queta.

items.headline: Robinson went scoreless and didn't attempt a shot, but grabbed seven rebounds, added one assist and blocked three shots in 15 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Robinson made his presence felt defensively despite playing just 15 minutes, collecting three blocks and seven rebounds while Boston cruised to a comfortable win. His fantasy profile remains heavily dependent on rebounds, blocks and field-goal efficiency, as he rarely contributes meaningful scoring or playmaking. Sunday's workload was limited by the blowout, but his ability to produce defensive statistics in relatively few minutes remains useful for managers targeting those categories.

items.headline: Robinson delivered 12 points (6-6 FG, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block across 18 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Robinson produced exceptional defensive value in limited action and was efficient on offense, scoring in double digits for just the second time this season. While he's losing the battle for the Celtics' starting center spot to Neemias Queta, Robinson has excellent per-minute production. His rebounding, defensive production and field-goal efficiency make him intriguing in category formats, though his limited workload and free-throw struggles remain significant negatives.

items.headline: Robinson (illness) is available for Sunday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Robinson popped up on the injury report due to an illness. However, it won't keep him off the floor against Milwaukee. Robinson's presence will likely mean fewer minutes for Luka Garza.

items.headline: Robinson (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game versus Milwaukee, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Robinson isn't feeling well and may not be available against the Bucks, which would mark his second absence of the 2026-27 campaign. If Robinson can't suit up, it should mean more minutes for Luka Garza behind Neemias Queta.

items.headline: Robinson provided three points (1-8 FG, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 109-102 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: After opening the year as a starter, Robinson has now come off the bench in back-to-back games. Although he remains worth watching in fantasy leagues, it appears Neemias Queta is beginning to pull away with the team's top center spot.

items.headline: Robinson (thumb) returned to Monday's game against the Rockets with 5:47 remaining in the second quarter, per the broadcast.
items.story: Robinson headed back to the locker room in the first quarter with a left thumb sprain. He returned to the bench shortly thereafter and appears to be good to go for the remainder of the contest.

items.headline: Robinson (thumb) is probable to return to Monday's game against the Rockets, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Robinson exited Monday's contest in the first quarter with a left thumb sprain. However, the big man is expected to check back in.

items.headline: Robinson (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Monday's game against the Rockets, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly why Robinson headed back to the locker room, though he can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light. If he's unable to return, Luka Garza would likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) won't start Monday's game against the Rockets, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: After sitting out Sunday's 108-97 win over Orlando to rest, Robinson will play and come off the bench for the first time in 2026-27. Neemias Queta will get a second consecutive start, while Luka Garza will likely see his minutes reduced substantially.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) is not listed on the Celtics' injury report ahead of Monday's game against Houston.
items.story: Robinson's absence from the injury report suggests he'll be available Monday. His potential return would bolster Boston's frontcourt depth, though his minutes and role will be worth monitoring.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Robinson has been downgraded from questionable to out and will miss the first half of Boston's upcoming back-to-back set. He'll likely be able to suit up Monday in Houston.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) is questionable for Sunday's game in Orlando, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Robinson might get scheduled for a maintenance day. If he's forced to the sidelines, Neemias Queta would likely start, and Luka Garza could see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Robinson closed Tuesday's 125-124 overtime win over the Nets with seven points (3-4 FG, 1-4 FT), five rebounds and one steal over 25 minutes.
items.story: Robinson started at center but delivered a relatively quiet performance, collecting five rebounds without recording a blocked shot. He also struggled at the charity stripe, converting just one of four attempts. Robinson continues to share frontcourt minutes with Neemias Queta and Luka Garza, limiting his fantasy upside.

items.headline: Robinson accumulated four points (2-4 FG), four rebounds, two assists and one block across 22 minutes during Friday's 107-103 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Robinson twisted his ankle during his season debut Tuesday in Detroit, so it was encouraging to see him head into this contest without an injury designation. The 28-year-old won Boston's starting job at center in favor of Neemias Queta at training camp, but the two big men split the center minutes right down the middle Friday and could continue to do so going forward.

items.headline: Robinson posted four points (2-2 FG, 0-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Robinson was given the starting nod for the season opener, supplanting Neemias Queta. Despite the promotion, Robinson still played just 18 minutes, providing very little outside of his three combined steals and blocks. He briefly left the court after twisting his ankle but said after the game that it didn't impact his play and won't be an issue moving forward, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports. Luka Garza also featured in the rotation, logging eight minutes off the bench. Given that all three could spend time at the center spot, it's hard to know who should be prioritized in fantasy. For now, let's work under the assumption that Queta will play the most minutes, perhaps providing him with the safest floor.

items.headline: Robinson will open the season as the starting center Tuesday against Detroit, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Robinson was considered the favorite to start, and he officially wins the job for the season opener. He's had trouble staying healthy in the past, so it will be interesting to see how the minutes are divvied up between him and Neemias Queta.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) is expected to play Tuesday versus Detroit.
items.story: Mitchell got the night off in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia but is anticipated to suit up Tuesday against the Pistons to kick off the 2026-27 campaign. The 28-year-old, who signed with the Celtics during the offseason, spent his entire career with the Knicks since entering the NBA in 2018, averaging 7.5 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.7 blocks over 23.4 minutes per contest in 397 regular-season games, including 215 starts. Mitchell has had issues staying healthy, and he's also not the most consistent offensive contributor. However, he's as good as it gets as a rebounder and shot-blocker.

items.headline: Robinson (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Robinson and the rest of Boston's regulars won't play in the final exhibition but should be good to go for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Pistons. Robinson produced 12 points (5-5 FG, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, three blocks and an assist over 17 minutes in Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over the Hornets.

items.headline: Robinson produced 12 points (5-5 FG, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, three blocks and an assist over 17 minutes in Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: The longtime Knick got the start at center while Neemias Queta and Luka Garza both came off the bench, but it was Queta (24 minutes) who ended up seeing more court time on the night. How the Celtics split the center workload among the three will be a key storyline as the season begins, but Robinson likely won't see a heavy load as his new team tries to keep him healthy. Over 60 regular-season games in 2025-26 as part of New York's title run, the most he'd played since 2021-22, the 28-year-old averaged 5.7 points, 8.8 boards and 2.1 combined blocks and steals in 19.6 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Robinson (undisclosed) is starting in Saturday's preseason game against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Robinson missed the previous preseason contest due to an undisclosed injury, but the big man will get the nod and start Saturday against a depleted 76ers team. Robinson is expected to be the defensive anchor in the Celtics' lineup when the regular season starts, but given his injury history, his workload  should be monitored in the preseason.

items.headline: Robinson (undisclosed) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Robinson will join several other rotation players on the sidelines for Boston's preseason opener. The big man's next chance to play in the preseason will come Saturday against the 76ers.

items.headline: Robinson expressed confidence Monday that he's capable of handling a more consistent workload this season after focusing on his conditioning throughout the summer, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: "Definitely. I feel very confident in myself," Robinson said when asked whether he could play more minutes consistently. "I've been working on my body this whole summer. Figuring things out." Robinson averaged 5.7 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 19.6 minutes across 60 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. The big man has struggled at the free-throw line in his career, but he put in extensive work this offseason to improve that area of his game, per Zack Cox of the Boston Herald. Heading into training camp, Mitchell is expected to battle Neemias Queta for the starting center role.

items.headline: Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Wembanyama is dealing with lower-back tightness, leaving his status for Monday's road tilt up in the air. If he's unable to play, Luke Kornet would likely replace Wembanyama in the starting lineup, while Carter Bryant, Keldon Johnson and rookie Tarris Reed could all see a bump in minutes off the Spurs' bench.

items.headline: Wembanyama finished with 50 points (20-29 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 19 rebounds, one assist, four steals and five blocks across 32 minutes in Saturday's 114-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Wembanyama had his third career game with at least 50 points, tying David Robinson for the second-most in Spurs history. He also became the first player since 1973-74 to record at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game. The 2023 No. 1 overall pick is having another MVP-caliber year and is now averaging 29.9 points, 12.4 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 3.9 blocks, all career highs, along with 3.2 assists over 30.3 minutes per outing in 17 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Wembanyama finished Thursday's 124-112 win over the Clippers with 32 points (13-26 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 33 minutes.
items.story: Wembanyama was efficient from two-point range en route to a game-high scoring total, and he's supplied at least 25 points in three straight contests. The superstar big man also recorded his fourth consecutive double-double thanks to a game-best 11 boards. Wembanyama has been spectacular on both ends of the floor to start the season, and he's averaged 25.4 points, 12.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.8 blocks and 1.2 steals per contest over the last five games.

items.headline: Wembanyama racked up 25 points (11-23 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 18 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 34 minutes in Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Wembanyama dominated the glass, recording his 11th double-double of the season while ripping down a game-high 18 rebounds. He finished with a plus-6 differential, but his efforts weren't enough to prevent the Spurs' 12-game win streak from coming to an end. They'll look to get things back on track Thursday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Wembanyama posted 26 points (10-21 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, one steal and five blocks in 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 win over Utah.
items.story: Wembanyama put up a dominant showing at both ends of the floor after playing just 21 minutes in Friday's 123-85 victory against the Warriors. He tallied his second straight double-double while connecting on four triples for the third time this season, and he's now blocked five or more shots in three of his last four games. As long as the Spurs are in a competitive game, Wembanyama will play and continue racking up ridiculous stat lines.

items.headline: Wembanyama ended with 12 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 12 rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal in 21 minutes during Friday's 123-85 win over Golden State.
items.story: Wembanyama didn't need to do much Friday, and he still finished with another double-double in just 21 minutes as San Antonio blew the game open early. The outside shot wasn't falling, but he controlled the glass and found his teammates, including the alley-oop that gave Castle his career high. The Spurs led by 43 in the third quarter, so the big man got a light workload before Sunday's trip to Utah, which is a nice bonus during an 11-game winning streak.

items.headline: Wembanyama ended Wednesday's 124-119 victory over the Bulls with 32 points (13-18 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, five blocks and two steals over 32 minutes.
items.story: Wembanyama continued his torrid stretch, falling one rebound short of a double-double while racking up seven combined steals-plus-blocks. He has been nothing short of spectacular over the past week, highlighted by a 52-point, 24-rebound effort against Dallas and a 40-point, nine-block showing in Phoenix on Monday.

items.headline: Wembanyama produced 40 points (15-19 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 8-10 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists and nine blocks in 25 minutes during Monday's 122-96 win over the Suns.
items.story: Wembanyama was the definition of efficiency Monday, as he nearly recorded a triple-double despite being held to 25 minutes due to a comfortable margin for the Spurs. He needed only 19 attempts from the field to reach the 40-point threshold, a mark he's now hit or surpassed three times in his first 11 appearances of the 2026-27 campaign. Wembanyama also made his presence felt at the other end of the court by setting a season high in swats.

items.headline: Wembanyama posted 29 points (9-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-9 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Wembanyama delivered an outstanding offensive performance despite playing just 24 minutes, but he fell three rebounds shy of posting what would've been his fourth consecutive double-double. Wembanyama continues to offer elite per-minute and multi-category upside, and even if he posts subpar (for his standards) numbers in one category, he does enough in other areas to compensate in most games. The star big man is averaging 33.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 4.0 blocks per game over his last five contests.

items.headline: Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Leonard (knee) is doing individual on-court work and is progressing well, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: The Raptors are expected to provide another update on Leonard's status in about one week, though it's encouraging to see how he's progressed thus far. Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased playing time for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

items.headline: Leonard (knee) is continuing the reconditioning process, and another update will be provided in one week, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Leonard still in the rehab phase of his recovery from left knee swelling, there remains no indication of an imminent return to game action. The one-week update timeline suggests Toronto is continuing to monitor his progress before advancing to the next step, keeping his near-term availability uncertain.

items.headline: Leonard has completed treatment to reduce swelling in his left knee and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Leonard will now begin the next phase of his rehab, and while he'll be re-evaluated by Nov. 10, it's still unlikely we'll see him back on the floor until the end of November. Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to start while Leonard is sidelined, and it'll be Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett running the show on offense.

items.headline: Leonard (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least three to four weeks, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: The extended absence represents a significant setback for Leonard, who will be unavailable for the foreseeable future. His absence should create additional offensive opportunities for Toronto's remaining rotation players, with guys like RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Allen Graves seeing more usage. Ja'Kobe Walter has started the first two games in Leonard's absence, but that may be fluid depending on opponents and matchups. Leonard's recovery timeline will be worth monitoring, as the reported window represents a minimum absence rather than a firm return date.

items.headline: Leonard (knee) is expected to miss multiple weeks due to swelling in his left knee, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: An MRI revealed no structural damage, but the Raptors will take a cautious approach with Leonard's recovery following interruptions to his offseason preparation. The veteran forward was a late scratch for Sunday's loss to Minnesota and now faces an extended absence just two games into the 2026-27 campaign. Ja'Kobe Walter, who started in Leonard's place Sunday, figures to benefit from additional playing time, while RJ Barrett and Scottie Barnes could absorb more offensive responsibility. Rookie Allen Graves could also get more involved. An update on his progress can be expected in one week, when the Raptors re-evaluate him.

items.headline: Leonard is out for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves due to left knee swelling, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Leonard wasn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's game, and this late scratch is a huge blow for Toronto since Leonard is a key piece on both ends of the court for the Raptors. Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 3.5 steals per game in his first two appearances. With the star forward out, Allen Graves is expected to take his place in the starting lineup. Leonard is expected to undergo further testing Monday, and the Raptors will provide an update Tuesday, ahead of Wednesday's matchup against the Magic.

items.headline: Leonard ended Friday's 112-102 victory over the Wizards with 16 points (7-19 FG, 2-8 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist and three steals in 28 minutes.
items.story: Leonard made his impact felt defensively and finished one rebound shy of his first double-double of the season. However, his struggles from the floor continued Friday, and he saw his streak of 20-plus point games snapped at 58. Leonard has gone 12-for-36 (33.3 percent) from the field through the first two games of the regular season, but he's still wreaking havoc on the defensive side of the floor while building up on his conditioning. Leonard and Scottie Barnes will have their defensive prowess put to the test Sunday against Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball and the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Leonard finished with 23 points (5-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 11-11 FT), six rebounds, two assists, four steals and one block over 24 minutes in Wednesday's 135-92 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Leonard tied Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley for the game high in points. However, what set the 35-year-old apart from the rest were his contributions on the defensive side of the ball. Leonard averaged a career-best 27.9 points along with 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals over 32.1 minutes per game in 65 regular-season appearances with the Clippers in 2025-26. The 2011 No. 15 overall pick is certainly still considered an All-Star-caliber player, but he needs to stay healthy, which has been an issue throughout his career.

items.headline: Leonard (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bulls.
items.story: Leonard sat out Friday's preseason finale but figures to play when the Raptors open the regular season at home against Chicago. The star forward appeared in two games this preseason, averaging 13.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.0 steals in 19.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Leonard will be rested for Friday's preseason finale against the Pistons, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Leonard will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. His status ahead of an Opening Night matchup against the Bulls on Wednesday is not in doubt.

items.headline: Leonard recorded 21 points (6-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), five rebounds and two steals across 17 minutes in Tuesday's 148-98 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Leonard made an immediate impact in his preseason debut, leading Toronto in scoring despite playing just 17 minutes. The veteran forward was particularly effective from beyond the arc, knocking down four three-pointers while adding two steals. His efficient performance was an encouraging sign as he prepares for the regular season.

items.headline: Leonard (not injury related) will make his preseason debut Tuesday against the Knicks, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: After missing the first two preseason contests, Leonard has the green light for game action. The Raptors have brought him along slowly, and it's likely he will play a limited role in his first game back with the Raptors.

items.headline: Leonard (not injury related) won't suit up for Saturday's exhibition against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Leonard will miss a second straight preseason game while ramping up his workload following the offseason, but he's not dealing with an injury. His next chance to play in the preseason will come Tuesday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Leonard (not injury related) went through a full practice Monday, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: This was Leonard's first full practice since training camp opened. He's expected to be held out of his second straight preseason contest Saturday, but it seems safe to say he will be a full go by Opening Night.

items.headline: Leonard (not injury related) won't play in Saturday's preseason opener against Miami and is unlikely to suit up for next Saturday's preseason game against the Clippers, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Leonard is expected to miss both of Toronto's first two preseason games as part of his ramp-up plan. He'll have three more chances to suit up before the regular season if he's held out of next Saturday's contest.

items.headline: Leonard has yet to participate in contact drills and is unlikely to play in Toronto's preseason opener Saturday against Miami, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: The team has been content with a phased ramp-up for Leonard to start training camp, and while coach Darko Rajakovic stated Thursday that the team will consider playing the star forward Saturday, it seems more likely that he'll sit out. Toronto has also indicated that a load management plan has been developed for Leonard ahead of the 2026-27 campaign to keep him healthy over the course of the season, which is something he hasn't been able to accomplish in recent years.

items.headline: Head coach Darko Rajakovic hinted Monday that the Raptors will have a management plan for Leonard in 2026-27, per Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca.
items.story: Staying on the court has long been a major concern for Leonard, who didn't play in 2021-22 and hasn't made 70 regular-season appearances since 2016-17 with the Spurs. The focus for Toronto will be to keep the star forward healthy throughout the course of the year, which means Leonard could face sporadic absences. Although he carries plenty of risk in fantasy drafts because of that caveat, Leonard averaged a career-high 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game over 65 regular-season appearances for the Clippers last year.

items.headline: Leonard agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors on Tuesday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: The deal also has a player option for the 2028-29 season. After spending most of this past offseason in a holding pattern, Leonard is settling back in with Toronto for his second stint with the team following a six-year tenure with the Clippers that was tumultuous at times. The star forward is coming off one of the best campaigns of his illustrious career in 2025-26 with Los Angeles, during which he averaged 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game over 65 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Leonard and the Raptors have held advanced discussions and are nearing an agreement on a contract extension, Jake Fischer of The Stein Line reports.
items.story: Leonard is eligible to sign for up to two years and $126 million. An extension would solidify Leonard's long-term future in Toronto and remove any uncertainty surrounding his contract situation heading into the 2026-27 campaign. After his trade was recently completed, his fantasy outlook is much more straightforward heading into training camp.

items.headline: The Clippers and Raptors both agreed Monday to complete the trade sending Leonard to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Over two months after the deal was initially agreed upon, it will finally be processed following the NBA's investigation of salary-cap circumvention involving Leonard and the Clippers. The star forward is coming off one of the best seasons of his storied career in 2025-26 with Los Angeles, having averaged 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game over 65 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Dosunmu ended with 23 points (8-13 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes during Monday's 142-116 win over the Nets.
items.story: Dosunmu has scored at least 19 points in three of his last four appearances, shooting 30-for-55 (54.5 percent) from the field during that stretch. His consistent starting role and perimeter shooting provide solid fantasy value across most formats.

items.headline: Dosunmu contributed six points (2-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists and one steal in 32 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dosunmu cooled considerably after Tuesday's 30-point explosion, but his starting role remains secure with Anthony Edwards sidelined. Dosunmu's fluctuating shot volume creates scoring volatility, though consistent minutes preserve his short-term fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Dosunmu provided 30 points (11-19 FG, 7-11 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal across 39 minutes during Tuesday's 106-105 victory over Portland.
items.story: Dosunmu led his team in scoring for the second time in three games with a season-high 30 points and seven triples. He bounced back in a big way following an eight-point outing on 3-for-11 shooting in Monday's 106-98 win against the Blazers, helping Minnesota sweep the back-to-back series and improve to 7-1 over the last eight games. Dosunmu also led the Timberwolves in assists, with his final dime to Jaden McDaniels resulting in the game-winning bucket with 2.6 seconds remaining.

items.headline: Dosunmu notched 24 points (10-16 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds and three steals over 33 minutes in Saturday's 117-106 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Dosunmu was Minnesota's most effective scorer Saturday and reached the 20-point mark for the fourth time over his last five appearances. Dosunmu has benefited from a starting role while Anthony Edwards (knee) remains sidelined, and he's surpassed the 15-point mark in all but one of his nine starts this season. He should continue to see an expanded role offensively until further notice. Saturday's efficient shooting and three steals were encouraging, although his lack of assists limited what could have been an even stronger fantasy performance.

items.headline: Dosunmu produced 18 points (8-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 27 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 victory over Dallas.
items.story: Dosunmu capitalized on his scoring opportunities while making his presence felt at the other end. His consistent role on offense, with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, should continue to reflect an uptick in both his season-long numbers and usage rate. Dosunmu is averaging a career-high 18.1 points per game this season.

items.headline: Dosunmu logged 26 points (7-13 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 8-8 FT), four rebounds, two steals and an assist in 29 minutes during Sunday's 115-100 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Dosunmu continued his run of strong play Sunday, knocking down four of five three-point attempts en route to a team-high 26 points. The 26-year-old pro has shot an impressive 72.7 percent from three over his last two games. Over his last five appearances, Dosunmu holds averages of 23.8 points, 5.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 2.0 steals in 35.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dosunmu posted 26 points (8-14 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one block across 39 minutes during Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: The 26-year-old guard led all scorers on the night, as he continues to step up in the absence of Anthony Edwards (knee). In six games since moving into the starting five, Dosunmu is averaging 20.8 points, 5.7 boards, 4.5 assists, 2.2 threes and 1.7 steals while shooting 53.3 percent from the floor and 41.9 percent from beyond the arc. With Edwards not expected back from his surgery until late December, Dosunmu is poised for a lengthy run of elevated usage.

items.headline: Dosunmu closed Wednesday's 117-107 win over the Rockets with 21 points (10-20 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, six assists and two steals over 34 minutes.
