items.story: Johnson was initially listed as questionable but is now trending in the right direction ahead of tipoff. If he's cleared to suit up, the rookie would likely see increased playing time due to the Mavericks being extremely shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set.

items.headline: Johnson (shin) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Johnson is in jeopardy of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set due to right shin splints. If the rookie forward is unable to suit up, Naji Marshall, P.J. Washington and Tobi Lawal would be candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is not on the injury report for Friday's exhibition against the Hawks.
items.story: Johnson received a maintenance day and sat out Wednesday's exhibition, but he'll be back in action for the Mavs' final preseason game. This will be his second preseason appearance, and it will be interesting to see how much playing time he earns after logging just 12 minutes in his first preseason contest.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Pelicans, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder missed the start of training camp with leg soreness, so Dallas is taking a cautious approach. Johnson could return for Friday's preseason finale against the Hawks.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) won't play in Sunday's preseason game against the Rockets, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Johnson started at center during his Mavericks preseason debut, totaling four points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 12 minutes during Friday's 135-117 loss to the Rockets. The rookie has been dealing with a minor lower-leg injury during training camp, so the Mavericks will likely proceed with caution, but it appears he's slated for a major role right away.

items.headline: Johnson totaled four points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 12 minutes during Friday's 135-117 preseason loss to the Rockets.
items.story: With Dereck Lively (foot), Santi Aldama (knee) and P.J. Washington (ankle) all sidelined, Johnson started at center in a small-ball lineup with Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher, as Daniel Gafford operated off the bench. The rookie ended up playing only 12 minutes, but his limited action might've been precautionary, as he's been dealing with a minor lower-leg injury during training camp. While not an eye-popping box score, Johnson being thrust into the starting lineup during his first non-Summer League NBA action is encouraging for his short- and long-term fantasy value.

items.headline: Johnson (lower leg) is expected to play in Friday's preseason opener against Houston, per Brad Townsend of The Dallas Morning News.
items.story: Johnson has been limited at camp due to lower-leg soreness, but the issue shouldn't stop him from making his professional debut Friday. The rookie big man is competing with Santi Aldama for a key bench role for the Mavericks.

items.headline: Head coach Dusty May said Wednesday that Johnson has been limited in training camp due to lower-leg soreness, Ron Harrod Jr. of DLLS Sports reports.
items.story: The Mavericks have been managing Johnson's workload ahead of his rookie season, with May noting that the 20-year-old participated in every other live session Wednesday. Additionally, May said Monday that the power forward is getting close to practicing in full. Still, the Michigan product's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Dallas' preseason opener against the Rockets on Friday, Oct. 9.

items.headline: Johnson (undisclosed) has been limited during training camp thus far, though head coach Dusty May said Monday that he's working his way back and getting close to practicing in full, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: It's unclear what Johnson is dealing with, though the issue doesn't appear to be a long-term concern. Still, the 20-year-old's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Dallas' preseason opener against Houston on Friday, Oct. 9. The No. 9 overall pick in this year's draft, Johnson is fresh off winning a national championship at Michigan, where he averaged 13.1 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.7 steals in 25.1 minutes per game in 40 outings.

items.headline: Johnson enters his rookie campaign after Dallas selected him ninth overall in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The 6-foot-9 forward showcased his upside during Summer League, including a 27-point, eight-rebound performance against Golden State and a four-block outing against the Lakers. Dallas' crowded frontcourt may prevent Johnson from immediately seeing major minutes, but his rebounding, defensive versatility and athleticism make him one of the Mavericks' most intriguing long-term prospects.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) didn't play in Friday's 110-88 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: Johnson missed the Mavericks' final three Summer League outings with an illness but should be available for the start of training camp. The rookie first-rounder averaged 18.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.0 blocks, 2.5 steals and 1.5 assists across 30.3 minutes per contest in two Las Vegas Summer League appearances.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) didn't play in Thursday's 97-87 Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: The Mavericks held the rookie first-rounder out for a second straight game while he battles an illness. It's unclear if Dallas plans to give Johnson any further Summer League reps ahead of training camp.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) didn't play in Monday's 96-88 Summer League win over the Grizzlies but can be considered day-to-day moving forward, Ron Harrod Jr. of DLLS Sports reports.
items.story: Johnson is under the weather and was unable to suit up Monday after totaling 37 points, 13 rebounds, six blocks, five steals and three assists in Dallas' first two Las Vegas Summer League outings. His next chance to play will come against the Thunder on Thursday.

items.headline: Johnson closed with 10 points (4-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four blocks and two steals over 28 minutes in Saturday's 91-70 Summer League loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Johnson put up modest offensive numbers, though he stood out with a game-high four blocks to go along with two steals. The early returns on the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft have been encouraging, as his strong defensive showing Saturday came on the heels of a 27-point performance Thursday.

items.headline: Johnson produced 27 points (12-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and two blocks across 26 minutes in Thursday's 101-90 Summer League loss to Golden State.
items.story: Johnson turned in an efficient performance and stuffed the stat sheet in his Summer League debut, logging game-high marks in points and steals. The big man out of Michigan also led the Mavericks in rebounds and tied for the team lead in blocks. He figures to play a meaningful role off the bench to begin his rookie season.

items.headline: Johnson was selected by the Mavericks with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Johnson is a versatile defender and rim runner who posted averages of 13.1 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.1 blocks per game on 62/34/78 shooting splits during his sophomore season. His offense is a work in progress, and he's a bit undersized for the center position. However, his grit and commitment to winning should endear him to the Mavericks' coaching staff, specifically new head coach Dusty May, who led Johnson and the Wolverines to a national title in 2025-26. While the 20-year-old may not be an immediate threat to overthrow Dereck Lively (foot), P.J. Washington or Daniel Gafford for a starting job, assuming they remain on the roster, it could happen sooner than expected, especially if there are injuries.

items.headline: Wesley and the Clippers agreed to a 10-day contract Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Clippers were granted a hardship exception due to injuries. Wesley was with the Clippers for training camp but failed to make the roster ahead of Opening Night. He'll provide emergency depth in the short term.

items.headline: Wesley was waived by the Clippers on Saturday, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Wesley signed with the Clippers in September but won't make the team's initial regular-season roster. He's now set to explore other opportunities if he isn't claimed off waivers.

items.headline: Wesley signed a one-year deal with the Clippers on Sunday, Jake Fischer of BleacherReport.com reports.
items.story: Wesley spent the 2025-26 campaign with the Trail Blazers, where he struggled to carve out a significant role, averaging 4.8 points, 2.0 assists and 1.3 rebounds in a career-low 11.6 minutes across 31 regular-season appearances. Wesley figures to compete for a reserve role and provide backcourt depth for Los Angeles in 2026-27.

items.headline: Wesley produced no counting stats in one minute during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: After landing a one-year deal with the Trail Blazers last offseason, Wesley struggled to carve out much of a role in 2025-26. Over 31 regular-season outings, the fourth-year guard averaged 4.8 points, 2.0 assists and 1.3 rebounds in a career-low 11.6 minutes per game. Whether it be with Portland or elsewhere, Wesley figures to serve as backcourt depth again in 2026-27.

items.headline: Wesley finished with 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one block across 20 minutes during Sunday's 135-101 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Wesley continues to play a modest role off Portland's bench. Over his last five games, he's seeing 11.7 minutes per contest with 6.0 points and 1.8 assists on 47.8 percent shooting from the field. He's miles off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Wesley (foot) is available for Friday's game against Memphis, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Wesley will shed his questionable tag due to right foot injury management and suit up in his third straight outing following a 43-game absence as he recovered from foot surgery. It's worth noting Friday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, so the 22-year-old guard's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's rematch against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Wesley is questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies due to right foot injury management.
items.story: With a rematch with Memphis on tap for Saturday, Portland is considering giving Wesley a maintenance day following his recent multi-month absence. Scoot Henderson (hamstring) is set to make his season debut Friday, and Vit Krejci could be pushed into a more prominent role if Wesley is unavailable.

items.headline: Wesley (foot) logged five points (2-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four assists, three rebounds and one steal across 19 minutes during Sunday's 130-111 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Wesley made his first appearance since Oct. 31 following a lengthy recovery from right foot surgery. The Trail Blazers were missing Jrue Holiday (personal) on Sunday, and with Scoot Henderson (hamstring) closing in on his season debut, Wesley may have a tough time carving out a consistent role in the rotation.

items.headline: Wesley (foot) is available for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Wesley has not appeared in a game since Oct. 31 after undergoing foot surgery, but he will return to action Sunday. He figures to see a minimal role in his return, considering how much time he has missed.

items.headline: Wesley (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Wesley underwent surgery back on Nov. 8 and was given a timetable of 8-to-12 weeks. The Trail Blazers will be shorthanded Sunday, so Wesley could see a sizable role if he's given the green light to return.

items.headline: Wesley underwent a successful procedure to repair a fracture of the fifth metatarsal base in his right foot Wednesday, and he's expected to be sidelined for 8-to-12 weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: A fifth metatarsal fracture is a notoriously tough injury to recover from, and there's a high chance of experiencing a setback if brought back too soon, so it wouldn't be shocking to see Wesley's absence extend beyond this 12-week window. At minimum, he'll be out through the end of December, so he can safely remain on the waiver wire in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Wesley suffered a fifth metatarsal fracture in his right foot and will be sidelined indefinitely, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Wesley sustained the injury in Friday's win over Denver, during which he posted five points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two assists and two steals across 10 minutes. With the 22-year-old guard sidelined, Shaedon Sharpe (calf), Rayan Rupert and two-way player Caleb Love are candidates for a bump in minutes. Over six regular-season appearances, Wesley has averaged 6.0 points, 3.2 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 16.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wesley finished Sunday's 114-107 loss to the Clippers with six points (2-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two steals in 17 minutes.
items.story: Wesley hasn't been shooting the ball well through three games with a 33.3 percent mark from the field, but he's doing a solid job as the backup point guard behind Jrue Holiday. Wesley is averaging 5.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 2.0 steals in 17.3 minutes per contest, and he's likely to hold onto the role until Scoot Henderson (hamstring) gets the green light to return.

items.headline: Wesley tallied 13 points (5-6 FG, 3-3 FT, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, an assist and a steal across 19 minutes during Friday's 124-123 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Wesley agreed to a one-year deal with Portland after a circuitous trip through the waiver wire. Waived by the Wizards, Wesley will attempt to jumpstart his pro career after failing to catch on with the Spurs during a three-year stint. Wesley is unlikely to make a fantasy impact with many established players above him on the depth chart.

items.headline: Wesley and the Trail Blazers agreed to a one-year deal on Tuesday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Wesley, who was recently waived by the Wizards, was scooped up quickly by Portland. Wesley spent the past three seasons in San Antonio, where he accumulated career regular-season averages of 4.3 points, 2.4 assists and 1.2 rebounds on 40.9 percent shooting from the field. He'll be facing an uphill battle for playing time in Portland, however.

items.headline: The Spurs traded Wesley, Malaki Branham and a 2026 second-round pick to the Wizards for Kelly Olynyk (heel) on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Wesley is joining the Wizards after spending three seasons with the Spurs, most recently averaging 3.7 points, 2.0 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 11.8 minutes across 58 games during the 2024-25 campaign. The young guard joins a crowded backcourt that includes recent additions like veteran CJ McCollum and 2025 NBA Draft No. 6 overall pick Tre Johnson.

items.headline: Wesley finished with eight points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, four assists and two steals across 20 minutes during Sunday's 125-118 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Playing in his third NBA season, Wesley had yet another quiet campaign. Across 37 regular-season appearances, Wesley shot 43.5 percent from the field, 29.3 percent from beyond the arc and 62.3 percent from the line with 3.7 points, 1.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.3 three-pointers. He'll enter the final season of his contract in 2025-26, valued at $4.73 million.

items.headline: Wesley produced 15 points (5-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 victory over Denver.
items.story: Wesley joined Malaki Branham and Sandro Mamukelashvili in scoring double-digit points off San Antonio's bench in Wednesday's win. Wesley has become a consistent part of the Spurs' rotation, averaging 20.2 minutes per contest across his last 10 appearances. The 22-year-old guard has also been very efficient from beyond the arc over that span, converting 47.6 percent of his 2.1 three-point attempts per contest.

items.headline: Wesley accumulated five points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two steals across 27 minutes during Sunday's 148-106 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Wesley has been getting more opportunities with the Spurs, but his fantasy production has left a lot to be desired. Over his last eight games, Wesley has produced averages of 5.9 points, 2.3 assists, 1.8 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 0.9 three-pointers in 20.4 minutes.

items.headline: Wesley closed Monday's 125-109 loss to the Lakers with seven points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), three rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals in 22 minutes.
items.story: Wesley posted a solid all-around line in the loss, but lines like these have been few and far between -- he was coming off a scoreless outing in 10 minutes against the Pelicans on Saturday. The Spurs are 13th in the Western Conference and De'Aaron Fox (finger) is done for the season, so Wesley could find more opportunities down the stretch.

items.headline: Wesley finished with 10 points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals over 24 minutes during Friday's 145-134 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: The 2022 first-rounder logged his most minutes since the Dec. 13 win over Portland, and his 10 points were his most since way back on Nov. 26. Although it was rookie first-rounder Stephon Castle who stepped into the starting lineup, it would appear initially that Wesley is also one of the direct beneficiaries of the absence of De'Aaron Fox (finger) for the remainder of 2024-25. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on Wesley's role moving ahead.

items.headline: Wesley produced 11 points (4-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, four assists and two steals in 22 minutes during Tuesday's 128-115 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Wesley saw his largest workload of the season Tuesday and made the most of his minutes. However, the Spurs will be getting Devin Vassell (knee) back in action Wednesday, so Wesley will face an uphill battle for consistent minutes when the Spurs are close to full strength.

items.headline: Wesley ended Thursday's 118-105 victory over the Trail Blazers with 10 points (4-4 FG, 2-2 FT), one rebound, eight assists and two steals in 21 minutes.
items.story: With Jeremy Sochan (thumb), Devin Vassell (foot) and Tre Jones (ankle) sidelined and Malaki Branham (ankle) leaving the contest early, Wesley saw an increased role and made the most of it, recording season highs in points, assists, steals and minutes played. It was only the fourth time Wesley played double-digit minutes this season, and despite the solid performance, he'll likely remain in a limited role. Sochan is expected to miss multiple weeks, but Vassell has been cleared to make his season debut Saturday, while Jones and Branham could be back sooner than later.

items.headline: Wesley amassed five points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and one rebound in 13 minutes during Wednesday's 105-93 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Wesley logged a season high in minutes, a feat that is not that impressive given his previous high was 12. A portion of his playing time came at the back end of the game, once the result was decided. Even with the Spurs' guard depth a little thin, Wesley has been unable to carve out a meaningful role. Barring a significant shift in their rotations, Wesley is not someone who needs to be considered in standard formats.

items.headline: Wesley had his fourth-year team option picked up by the Spurs on Friday, Ty Jager of FanSided.com reports.
items.story: Wesley averaged 5.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 0.5 steals, 0.3 blocks and 0.4 triples across 17.0 minutes in the final 20 games of his sophomore season in San Antonio. Although his option was picked up, the guard will presumably have to earn a spot providing depth in the backcourt once the regular season tips off.

items.headline: Wesley had his fourth-year team option picked up by the Spurs on Friday, Ty Jager of FanSided.com reports.
items.story: Wesley averaged 5.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 0.5 steals, 0.3 blocks and 0.4 triples across 17.0 minutes in the final 20 games of his sophomore season in San Antonio. Although his option was picked up, the guard will presumably have to earn a spot providing depth in the backcourt once the regular season tips off.

items.headline: Wesley closed Sunday's 123-95 win over Detroit with 17 points (7-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, five assists and three steals across 30 minutes.
items.story: The 17 points were a career high for the second-year guard, while the boards and steals tied his previous highs. Wesley is still struggling to establish himself in the Spurs' backcourt rotation after being the 25th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, but he at least heads into the offseason with a bit of confidence.

items.headline: Wesley is starting Friday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: This marks Wesley's second start of the 2023-24 campaign, with his last dating back to Jan. 24 against the Thunder. He should get plenty of looks Friday due to the absence of Malaki Branham (concussion).

items.headline: Wesley ended with 12 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, three assists, one block and two steals over 19 minutes during Saturday's 131-106 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Wesley took advantage of the minutes he saw off the bench in a blowout loss, missing just one shot from the field and ending as one of the few bright spots on a Spurs team that looked overmatched on both ends of the court. Wesley should continue to see minutes off the bench in the final weeks of the regular season, and it wouldn't be surprising if he makes a start here or there.

items.headline: Wesley produced 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt), one rebound, three assists, one block and one steal in 17 minutes during Thursday's 131-129 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Wesley was efficient from the field and scored his most points since Jan. 24, which was much-needed for a Spurs squad playing without Victor Wembanyama (ankle). Wesley has played double-digit minutes in 23 of the Spurs' last 24 games, but he's averaging just 5.3 points, 3.3 assists and 1.3 rebounds in 16.7 minutes during that stretch.

items.headline: Powell will sign a deal with Turkish club Fenerbahce, according to NBA reporter Marc Stein.
items.story: After spending the past 12 years with Dallas, the veteran center was unable to make the roster this time around, with the team holding 15 guaranteed contracts. Powell holds career regular-season averages of 6.5 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.0 assists across 768 games.

items.headline: The Mavericks waived Powell on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: With NBA rosters due Monday evening, the Mavericks needed to trim their roster by one, and it's the veteran center who gets let go. With this news, Moussa Cisse is now penciled in as the third-string center.

items.headline: Powell re-signed with the Mavericks on Friday, Marc Stein of The Stein Line reports.
items.story: The 35-year-old is joining Dallas for training camp, and Stein adds that the team has not ruled out creating a spot for Powell on the regular-season roster despite currently carrying the maximum 15 standard contracts. Powell appeared in 63 games (12 starts) last regular season, averaging 3.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists.

items.headline: Powell will start Sunday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: With Marvin Bagley (shoulder) and Daniel Gafford (rest) out, Powell will get the starting nod in Sunday's season finale. As a starter this season (11 games), the veteran big man has averaged 5.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.4 steals in 24.6 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Powell (hip) is available for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Powell was initially tagged as questionable due to a hip injury, but the veteran big man has been given the green light to play Friday. He's averaged 17.8 minutes per game over his last eight outings (three starts) and should continue to serve in an elevated role due to the absence of Daniel Gafford (shoulder).

items.headline: Powell (hip) is questionable for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Like Marvin Bagley (shoulder), Powell was a late addition to the injury report. If one or both players end up sitting out, the Mavericks may need to rely heavily on Moussa Cisse.

items.headline: Powell won't start Wednesday's game against the Suns, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Powell got the starting nod during Tuesday's loss to the Clippers in place of the injured Daniel Gafford (shoulder), though it'll be Marvin Bagley who enters the first unit Wednesday. Powell has averaged 3.0 points and 4.5 rebounds across 17.5 minutes per tilt over his last four appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Powell is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's matchup with the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Powell is starting in place of Daniel Gafford (shoulder) on Tuesday. As a starter this season, Powell has averaged 5.5 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game.

items.headline: Powell isn't in the starting lineup for Monday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Powell started his squad's last two matchups but failed to do much with the opportunity. He'll return to a bench role Monday with Daniel Gafford set to return from a right shoulder sprain.

items.headline: Powell logged seven points (1-2 FG, 5-7 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 142-135 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Powell moved into the starting lineup, replacing Daniel Gafford, who was ruled out with a shoulder injury. Coming into Wednesday's game, Powell had accumulated two straight DNP-CDs, indicating that this game was likely an outlier.

items.headline: Powell is part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Powell had been out of the rotation for the last two games, but he'll jump into the first unit Wednesday in place of the injured Daniel Gafford (shoulder). Expect Powell to share center duties with Marvin Bagley.

items.headline: Powell ended Friday's 138-105 loss to Cleveland with 11 points (4-5 FG, 3-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and two steals in 21 minutes.
items.story: Powell had mostly been out of the rotation the past three games, but with Daniel Gafford taking a rest day and Marvin Bagley getting abused by Evan Mobley, Powell got some time to shine in the blowout loss. This was his third double-double of the season, but he'll likely return to being a fringe rotation player Sunday in Cleveland with Gafford expected back for that one.

items.headline: Powell will come off the bench during Sunday's game against the Raptors, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: The veteran center started Friday's game due to Daniel Gafford (ankle) and Marvin Bagley (neck) being out, but Powell will return to a bench role Sunday as both Gafford and Bagley are back in the lineup. In his last six games in a reserve role, Powell holds averages of 6.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 18.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Powell (calf) is available for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Powell found himself on the injury report ahead of Sunday's contest due to a calf issue, but he will be able to play through it. Powell started Friday's game due to Daniel Gafford (ankle) and Marvin Bagley (neck) being sidelined, but he saw just 15 minutes. Now, both Gafford and Bagley are returning to the lineup, which will likely reduce Powell's role.

items.headline: Powell is listed as probable for Sunday's game against the Raptors due to right calf tightness.
items.story: The calf issue is a new concern for Powell, though he's still likely to suit up Sunday. If Powell is cleared to play and Marvin Bagley (neck), who is listed as questionable, remains sidelined, the former would likely operate as Daniel Gafford's primary backup. Over four March appearances (one start), Powell has averaged 6.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.3 blocks in 20.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Powell will start against the Celtics on Friday, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: With Daniel Gafford (ankle) and Marvin Bagley (neck) unavailable, Powell will enter the starting five. As a starter this season (seven games), the veteran big man has averaged 6.0 points, 7.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.9 steals in 28.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Powell recorded 12 points (3-5 FG, 6-8 FT), four rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 117-90 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: With Marvin Bagley (neck) unavailable for a third straight game, Powell saw significant minutes off the bench once again. He led the second unit in points Tuesday, scoring in double figures for the second time over that three-game span. The veteran center is likely to continue seeing 20-plus minutes of action as Daniel Gafford's primary backup for as long as Bagley is sidelined.

items.headline: Powell logged nine points (4-5 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 21 minutes during Sunday's 100-87 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Powell made the most of his 21-minute cameo Sunday and finished just one point and one rebound away from posting a double-double. That said, Powell has played off the bench in his last 12 appearances but is averaging only 10.7 minutes per contest. Even if his last two outings are encouraging, he's not seeing the floor enough to be considered a reliable fantasy alternative even in the deepest formats.

items.headline: Powell recorded 13 points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 11 rebounds and one assist over 23 minutes off the bench during Friday's 124-105 loss to Memphis.
items.story: The veteran center produced his second double-double of the season, with the first coming Jan. 22 against the Warriors. Powell has struggled to get consistent court time even with Dereck Lively (foot) out for the season and Anthony Davis (finger) now in Washington. Friday's 23 minutes represented Powell's highest workload in February and just the third time in eight appearances this month he logged double-digit minutes.

items.headline: Powell won't start against the Timberwolves on Wednesday, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Daniel Gafford will return to the starting five Wednesday, pushing Powell to the second unit. The veteran big man has averaged 3.0 points and 6.0 rebounds in 16.0 minutes per game over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Powell logged 10 points (3-4 FG, 4-5 FT), 12 rebounds and one assist over 27 minutes during Dallas' 123-115 win over Golden State on Thursday.
items.story: Powell led the Mavericks in rebounds Thursday while recording his first double-double of the season (and first since Dec. 28, 2023). The veteran has started in five of the Mavericks' last six games, and he should remain in the starting lineup for as long as Daniel Gafford (ankle) is sidelined. Even when Gafford returns, Powell should have an elevated role off the bench in the absence of Anthony Davis (hand).

items.headline: Powell is in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Powell will be asked to join the starting five with the Mavs missing a good chunk of the starting frontcourt Thursday. He'll presumably tackle a heavier workload than usual with both Daniel Gafford (ankle) and P.J. Washington (ankle) out.

items.headline: Powell will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Powell made a spot start in place of Daniel Gafford, and he'll return to the bench Wednesday now that Gafford is healthy. Powell and Moussa Cisse should handle backup center duties against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Powell notched five points (2-2 FG, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds and three assists over 35 minutes during Monday's 113-105 win over the Nets.
items.story: Powell was elevated to the starting lineup due to the absences of Anthony Davis (finger) and Daniel Gafford (ankle). Powell ended up playing 35 minutes, his most in a game since Nov. 29 (another spot start). With Davis sidelined indefinitely and Gafford still questionable, Powell may be forced to start again Wednesday against Denver.

items.headline: Powell will start against the Nets on Monday, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Anthony Davis (finger) and Daniel Gafford (ankle) both sidelined, Powell will get the starting nod for the second time this season. During his lone start in a win over the Clippers on Nov. 29, the veteran center logged nine points, six steals, five rebounds, three assists and one block in 34 minutes.

items.headline: Powell (illness) is available for Thursday's game against the Warriors, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Powell has not played in the Mavericks' last four games, the last two of which were due to an illness. He's been cleared to play Christmas Day, though his return shouldn't impact any of the other players in Dallas' rotation.

items.headline: Powell (illness) is listed as probable for Thursday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Powell has not played in the Mavericks' last four games, though his last two absences were due to an illness. He's on track to be available for Christmas Day, though it's unclear whether he'll be in the Mavericks' rotation in Thursday's road game.

items.headline: Powell is out for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets with an illness, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning Newsreports.
items.story: Powell's next chance to return comes Thursday against the Warriors. Anthony Davis is set to play the majority of the center minutes Tuesday, while Daniel Gafford has the backup role all to himself.

items.headline: Powell is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets with an illness.
items.story: Powell is expected to be downgraded to out at some point prior to Tuesday's tipoff. He's been outside of the Dallas rotation for three consecutive games, so the center minutes are unlikely to be changed by his likely absence.

items.headline: Powell is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets with an illness.
items.story: The Mavericks are likely to see how Powell is feeling closer to tipoff before updating his status. The veteran big man has been out of the Dallas rotation for three straight games, so the center minutes are unlikely to be affected by his possible absence.

items.headline: Powell supplied seven points (2-4 FG, 3-6 FT) and nine rebounds across 24 minutes during Monday's 140-133 overtime loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Powell has been called to take on a larger role recently with the loss of Dereck Lively (foot) for the season, plus Anthony Davis (calf) was ruled out for Monday's game against the Jazz. In the three games where Powell has played at least 24 minutes, he's averaged 11.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.0 blocks.

items.headline: Powell won't start against the Nuggets on Monday.
items.story: The veteran big man got the starting nod in Saturday's win over the Clippers, though he'll retreat to the bench with Anthony Davis (calf) back in action. Powell will likely split time with Moussa Cisse behind Davis on Monday due to Daniel Gafford (ankle) and Dereck Lively (foot) being sidelined.

items.headline: Powell will start Saturday against the Clippers, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Anthony Davis (calf), Daniel Gafford (ankle) and Dereck Lively (foot) all sidelined, Powell will get the starting nod for the first time this season. The veteran big man has averaged just 4.7 minutes per game in his last three appearances and will likely split time with Moussa Cisse at center.

items.headline: Powell racked up no counting stats across three minutes during Saturday's 102-96 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Powell moved back into the rotation, albeit for a brief three-minute period. Despite multiple injuries to the frontcourt, Powell has been unable to carve out a consistent role, averaging 2.1 points and 2.0 rebounds in his first 13 appearances.

items.headline: Powell contributed 18 points (4-6 FG, 10-12 FT), six rebounds, one steal, two blocks and one turnover in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 107-105 victory over Indiana.
items.story: Powell collected a DNP-CD on Monday, but with Anthony Davis (leg) exiting Wednesday's game early, Powell was able to re-enter the rotation and started the second half. If Davis, Dereck Lively (knee) and Daniel Gafford (ankle) all need to miss Saturday's game in Detroit, Powell would likely get the starting nod as the last center standing in Dallas.

items.headline: Powell posted four points (2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two steals in nine minutes during Wednesday's 121-94 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Powell averaged 5.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in 14.4 minutes across four preseason games. With Daniel Gafford (ankle) banged up, Powell may be in store for elevated minutes behind Dereck Lively and Anthony Davis to begin the regular season.

items.headline: Powell will exercise his $4 million player option for the 2025-26 season, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: This isn't an unexpected decision by Powell, who averaged 2.1 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.0 assists over 55 regular-season appearances a season ago. He finds himself surrounded by competition in the frontcourt heading into the 2025-26 campaign and will need to battle with the likes of Kai Jones and Daniel Gafford to earn an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Powell had four points (1-2 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals over 21 minutes during Tuesday's 128-113 loss to New York.
items.story: Powell delivered another underwhelming performance, scoring single digits for the sixth straight game. In fact, to this point, he has scored double-digits only once all season, averaging 2.2 points and 2.3 rebounds in 10.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Powell won't start Sunday's game against the 76ers, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: With P.J. Washington back in the mix, Dallas will start Naji Marshall, Kessler Edwards and Washington in the frontcourt, sending Powell to a reserve role. Over his last 10 appearances (three starts), Powell has averaged 4.1 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 15.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Powell is in the starting lineup for Friday's game against Houston, Danielle Lerner of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.story: Powell will have a minutes restriction Friday, so his fantasy upside will remain limited despite the starting role. The veteran big man has averaged 4.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.5 blocks in 16.7 minutes over two games as a starter this season.

items.headline: Powell is still on a minutes restriction for Friday's game versus the Rockets, Brad Townsend of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Powell has suited up in each of Dallas' last nine outings after missing 16 straight contests due to a right hip strain. Considering Powell has averaged 14.4 minutes a game over that span, it seems reasonable to assume his playing time will continue to hover around 20 minutes.

items.headline: Knox signed a one-year deal with Unicaja Malaga in Spain on Thursday, per BasketNews.com.
items.story: Knox joined the Magic for training camp but didn't earn a spot on the Opening Night roster. He's now set to play overseas after spending the 2025-26 season in the G League.

items.headline: Knox recorded 11 points (3-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and six rebounds in 13 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason win over Memphis.
items.story: Knox provided a scoring boost off the bench while finishing as one of Orlando's more productive rebounders. The veteran forward will look to build on the performance as he competes for a spot on the roster.

items.headline: Knox agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the Magic on Wednesday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: The ninth overall pick in the 2018 Draft, Knox is set to compete for a spot on Orlando's regular-season roster during training camp. The 27-year-old forward appeared in 39 games with the G League's Windy City Bulls in 2025-26, averaging 21.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.2 combined steals-plus-blocks in 35.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Bulls signed Knox on Wednesday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Knox has bounced around the league quite a bit during his NBA career, having played for five different teams before landing in Chicago. This contract is likely a training camp deal, which means he could end up with the G League's Windy City Bulls for the 2025-26 campaign. The veteran journeyman played in 14 regular-season games with the Warriors last season, averaging 3.3 points and 1.2 rebounds per game, while shooting 50 percent from the floor and 26.7 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Knox ended with 14 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one block across 18 minutes during Wednesday's 131-116 loss to Houston in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Knox scored a season-high 14 points, making the most of a rare opportunity to play meaningful minutes. The Warriors were never really in the contest, with the coaching staff opting to rest their stars down the stretch. Golden State still leads the series 3-2 with Game 6 coming up at home on Friday.

items.headline: Knox agreed Saturday with the Knicks on a rest-of-season contract, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Knox will get an opportunity to prove his worth to the Warriors for the remainder of the 2024-25 campaign. The 25-year-old forward previously made seven appearances for Golden State earlier this season over the course of a pair of 10-day deals, averaging 4.0 points and 1.6 rebounds in 7.3 minutes per game while shooting 45.8 percent from the field.

items.headline: The Warriors intend to re-sign Knox to a second 10-day contract after his initial 10-day deal expires Saturday, Anthony Slater of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Knox has played in four games for the Warriors since signing his 10-day deal Feb. 19, averaging 5.8 points, 2.3 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 7.5 minutes per contest. All but one of those appearances has come at the tail end of blowouts, so Knox doesn't look as though he'll be in the mix for a rotation spot with the Warriors. in fact, playing time could be even more difficult to come by for Knox moving forward with Jonathan Kuminga (ankle) closing in on a return from a long-term absence.

items.headline: Knox and the Warriors agreed to a 10-day contract on Wednesday, ESPN's Ohm Youngmisuk reports.
items.story: Knox has been a standout with the Santa Cruz Warriors in the G League, averaging 21.6 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.5 three-pointers, 2.3 assists, 0.8 blocks and 0.7 steals while shooting 49.9 percent from the field across 28 appearances. Knox, along with the newly-signed Yuri Collins, are likely to provide Golden State with some emergency depth in the short term.

items.headline: The Warriors plan to sign Knox to a 10-day deal following the All-Star break, Anthony Slater of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Golden State will likely wait until shortly before Friday's game in Sacramento to make the signing official, so that the team can maximize Knox's 10 days with the team. The 25-year-old forward attended training camp with the Warriors on a one-year deal, but after failing to win a spot on the season-opening roster, he joined Golden State's G League affiliate, the Santa Cruz Warriors. Over his 28 appearances with Santa Cruz, Knox has averaged 21.6 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.5 three-pointers, 2.3 assists, 0.8 blocks and 0.7 steals while shooting 49.9 percent from the field and 39.1 percent from three-point range across 32.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: The Warriors waived Knox in October of 2024, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Knox was unable to obtain a regular-season roster spot after spending the preseason and training camp with Golden State. Knox will now likely join the Santa Cruz Warriors of the G League for the 2024-25 campaign.

items.headline: The Warriors waived Knox in October of 2024, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Knox was unable to obtain a regular-season roster spot after spending the preseason and training camp with Golden State. Knox will now likely join the Santa Cruz Warriors of the G League for the 2024-25 campaign.

items.headline: Knox and the Warriors agreed to a one-year deal Wednesday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Knox will join the Warriors for training camp, though he isn't guaranteed a final roster spot. In 306 career NBA games, Knox holds averages of 7.4 points and 2.9 rebounds while shooting 39.2 percent from the field.

items.headline: Knox produced seven points (3-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 0-4 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal across 19 minutes in Sunday's 92-68 win over the Lakers in the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Knox was previously thought to be out for the Summer League due to a strained calf. However, he returned for the Warriors' second game of the California Classic and was inefficient from the field off the bench. The 24-year-old averaged 7.2 points and 2.4 rebounds across 18.1 minutes in 31 games with Detroit before getting traded to, and eventually cut by, the Jazz.

items.headline: Knox is part of the Warriors' Summer League roster.
items.story: Knox started the 2023-24 campaign with Detroit but was traded to the Jazz in February and released shortly after, ending up with the Rip City Remix of the G League. The 2018 lottery pick will get a chance to prove he's worthy of a roster spot with Golden State this Summer.

items.headline: Knox was traded to the Jazz from the Pistons on Wednesday, James Edwards of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Pistons attached Knox to a 2024 second-round pick and the rights to Gabriele Procida in exchange for Simone Fontecchio. Knox had a little bit of success in Detroit with averages of 7.2 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers, but he failed to score in his last two outings. In Utah, Knox figures to fight for minutes at the end of the rotation behind Lauri Markkanen, John Collins, Kelly Olynyk and Ochai Agbaji.

items.headline: Knox is starting Friday against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Knox came off the bench in his last four appearances, but he'll rejoin the starting lineup Friday due to Mike Muscala (concussion) and Isaiah Stewart (ankle) being out. Over nine starts this year, Knox has averaged 9.1 points and 3.9 rebounds in 24.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Knox isn't in the starting five for Wednesday's game versus the Hornets, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Isaiah Stewart will replace Knox in the starting lineup Wednesday. Knox is averaging 11.0 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 21.6 minutes across his last five appearances coming off the bench.

items.headline: Knox is in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against Milwaukee, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Knox joins the first unit with Isaiah Stewart sidelined due to an ankle injury. Detroit opts for an offense-centric lineup, as he's flanked by Bojan Bogdanovic and Marvin Bagley in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Knox won't start Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Knox drew back-to-back starts with Bojan Bogdanovic sidelined, but the latter has been cleared to suit up, sending the former to the bench again. Over his last 12 appearances (five starts), Knox has averaged 10.8 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 23.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Knox racked up 19 points (7-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 35 minutes during Friday's 112-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Moving back into the starting lineup with Bojan Bogdanovic (calf) sidelined, Knox tied Alec Burks for the team lead in scoring. The 2018 lottery pick is on his fourth team in six seasons, but Knox is filling a hole in the Pistons' rotation well enough at the moment, averaging 11.3 points, 2.6 boards and 1.5 threes in 22.1 minutes per contest over the last 11 games.

items.headline: Knox will move into the starting lineup for Friday's game against Houston, Lachard Binkley of TheDreamShake.com reports.
items.story: Knox will be replacing Isaiah Livers in the first unit. Knox gave the Pistons a spark off the bench against the Spurs on Wednesday, scoring 12 points with four rebounds and a pair of three-pointers in 24 minutes.

items.headline: Knox accumulated 18 points (7-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, three assists, two blocks and one steal across 23 minutes during Friday's 113-109 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Detroit's rash of injuries has revived Knox's career a bit, although his stat lines are far from dependable. Detroit is Knox's sixth team in six years, and despite the state of Detroit's roster, he'll continue to be used as part of the second and third unit. Knox will have other opportunities to produce in the short term, but his fantasy value is limited.

items.headline: Knox will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Knox started three straight games for Detroit and averaged 11.3 points and 2.3 rebounds across 24.1 minutes. However, he'll be replaced by Isaiah Livers for Wednesday's tilt.

items.headline: Knox will start Thursday's game against Boston.
items.story: Isaiah Stewart is sitting out with a toe issue, but he's believed to be day-to-day. Knox already has two starts to his name this season, but he struggled in those with 8.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.0 three-pointers on 33.3 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Knox chipped in 14 points (5-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and one rebound across 24 minutes during Saturday's 126-115 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Knox stepped in and knocked down his shots coming off two consecutive DNP-CDs. The 24-year-old can't be relied on as anything more than a sporadic scoring sparkplug, but perhaps his workload will grow moving forward with Detroit reeling.

items.headline: Knox won't start Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: After a couple of standout games, Knox was rewarded with back-to-back starts. However, he failed to impress, and the Pistons' small-ball lineup didn't work out. Marvin Bagley is back with the first unit, but as long as Jalen Duren (ankle) is sidelined, Knox should carve out a sizable rotational role. Over his first four appearances of the season, Knox has averaged 11.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 27.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Knox supplied 11 points (5-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 31 minutes during Friday's 108-100 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (ankle) sidelined for a third straight game, Knox slid into the starting five for the Pistons and produced his first double-double in three games since rejoining the club last week. The 24-year-old forward has never lived up to his draft pedigree after being a lottery pick in 2018, but Knox is seeing big minutes right now in an injury-wracked Detroit frontcourt and has some short-term fantasy value.

items.headline: Knox will enter the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Cavaliers, James Edwards of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jalen Duren (ankle) is sitting out again Friday, but Marvin Bagley will go back to the second unit this time around. Knox has played well in his two appearances for the Pistons, averaging 15.0 points on 75.0 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Knox was practicing with the starters during the team's morning shootaround ahead of Friday's matchup versus the Cavaliers, Mike Curtis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Marvin Bagley (illness) is questionable for the contest but was participating in the shootaround, though he was operating with the backups. With the Pistons in the midst of a nine-game losing streak, it's possible coach Monty Williams will make a change to the starting lineup even if Bagley is cleared to suit up. If Knox is starting, Isaiah Stewart would presumably slide over to center in Bagley's stead.

items.headline: Knox recorded 18 points (7-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt) and three rebounds across 24 minutes in Sunday's 119-108 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Knox joined the Pistons on a one-year deal Wednesday after being cut by the Trail Blazers on Oct. 21. He made an immediate impact Sunday as the leading scorer on the team coming off the bench. Knox's role on the Pistons could grow if he continues to contribute positively off the bench, and he'll get his next opportunity Tuesday against the Hawks.

items.headline: Knox has agreed to a one-year deal with the Pistons, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Pistons are dealing with a slew of key injuries, so Knox may have a shot at some end-of-rotation minutes. He will be familiar with the Pistons as well after playing 42 games for them during the 2022-23 season. During those games, Knox averaged 5.6 points and 2.6 rebounds in 14.1 minutes.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers will waive Knox on Saturday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Knox was in contention for a spot on the Trail Blazers' opening night roster but ultimately lost out to Ish Wainright, whom Portland claimed off waivers Saturday. The Trail Blazers will retain Knox's G League rights if he clears waivers, but it's uncertain if the 24-year-old will report to the Rip City Remix or if he'll instead pursue work overseas.

items.headline: Knox signed a training camp contract with the Trail Blazers on Monday, Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com reports.
items.story: Knox appeared in 63 matchups between the Pistons and Trail Blazers last year and averaged 6.6 points and 2.8 rebounds in 15.1 minutes per game. After the team declined his team option in late June, he'll have an opportunity to compete for a roster spot during training camp this year.

items.headline: Knox (quadriceps) is available for Sunday's matchup against the Warriors.
items.story: Knox was listed as probable earlier Sunday, so his availability is unsurprising. Knox has taken advantage of playing more minutes down the stretch, averaging 14.2 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game over his last 10 appearances.

items.headline: Knox is probable to play Sunday against the Warriors due to a right quad contusion.
items.story: Knox is dealing with a bruised quad, but it doesn't sound like it'll be keeping him off the floor for Sunday's regular-season finale. He should start and see plenty of minutes for a Portland team that will likely have only eight guys available, and he's coming off a 30-point, 11-rebound performance, so he's an attractive target in daily fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Knox registered 30 points (10-15 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Saturday's 136-125 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Knox is one of the many Blazers players that has thrived with a more significant role, and after he was granted a start after a 24-point outing off the bench against the Spurs on Thursday, he didn't disappoint. Knox has scored 19 or more points in three of his last four appearances and is expected to have a sizable role in the season finale against the Warriors on Sunday.

items.headline: Knox will start Saturday's game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Knox has started only two of the past six games but has still crossed the 24-minute threshold in all of them. During this run, he's averaged 14.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 29.3 minutes.

items.headline: Knox logged 24 points (9-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 24 minutes during Thursday's 129-127 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Knox moved back to the bench after starting Portland's previous contest, but despite the demotion, he popped for a team- and season-high 24 points on efficient shooting. With Portland essentially shutting down its regulars, Knox has seen an increased role over the Trail Blazers' past nine games, averaging 12.4 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 25.8 minutes with 42/26/66 shooting splits during that stretch.

items.headline: Knox will not start Thursday at San Antonio.
items.story: Knox has been rotated in and out of the first unit over the last handful of games as the Trail Blazers continue to pack it in for the rest of the season. In his last two appearances with the reserves, Knox averaged 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.0 steals across 28.0 minutes.

items.headline: Jones closed with eight points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two steals over 27 minutes during Thursday's 124-112 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Jones has scored eight or fewer points in consecutive games, with his shot attempts declining sharply. His defensive contributions offer some fantasy value, but inconsistent offensive involvement limits his ceiling despite steady minutes.

items.headline: Jones closed with five points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-6 FT), one rebound, one assist and one block across 28 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Jones struggled offensively Tuesday, attempting just three shots after scoring in double figures in three consecutive appearances. Despite the setback, the veteran forward has maintained a consistent starting role, averaging nearly 27 minutes over his last four games. His contributions from beyond the arc and as a shot-blocker provide fantasy value, though his limited offensive opportunities can lead to inconsistent scoring.

items.headline: Jones totaled 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-7 3Pt), five rebounds, four blocks and one steal in 29 minutes during Friday's 113-112 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Jones was disruptive on both ends, knocking down four threes and blocking four shots. The forward's defense has always been his calling card, and when the outside shot falls, his fantasy value skyrockets.

items.headline: Jones closed Sunday's 139-123 win over the Pelicans with eight points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds and three assists over 29 minutes.
items.story: Jones has started each of his eight appearances so far this year, serving mostly as a defensive presence for the Clippers. However, his role could alter once Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is cleared to make his season debut.

items.headline: Jones ended Wednesday's 117-116 overtime loss to Miami with 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal across 37 minutes.
items.story: Jones returned to the starting lineup after missing Monday's game with a right knee injury he suffered Sunday. He handled a full workload and was a factor on the defensive end, finishing with four combined steals-plus-blocks. He's a useful source of defensive stats when healthy, though his limited offensive role caps his upside.

items.headline: Jones (knee) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Heat, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Jones will be back in action Wednesday following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which should result in Kobe Sanders returning to the second unit. Jones is averaging 11.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.2 triples and 1.2 steals per game this season.

items.headline: Jones (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Jones exited Sunday's loss to the Warriors and did not return due to a right knee injury. He's now listed on the injury report with right knee soreness, and the veteran forward's next chance to play will come Wednesday against Miami. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Jones (right knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Warriors, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Jones appeared to sustain the injury in the third quarter of Sunday's game, and he'll be sidelined for the rest of the contest. Gradey Dick and Kobe Sanders are both in line for minutes the rest of the way in the absence of Jones, who will finish with nine points (3-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds and one assist over 28 minutes.

items.headline: Jones amassed 15 points (6-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, two blocks and four steals across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The 15 points led the depleted Clippers' starting five on the night, while the steals and blocks were season highs for Jones. The veteran forward is seeing a little more usage than usual in the early going, and through four games, he's averaging 12.5 points, 5.3 boards, 2.5 threes, 1.8 assists and 1.8 steals while shooting 57.6 percent from the floor and a sizzling 55.6 percent (10-for-18) from long distance.

items.headline: Jones closed Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers with 16 points (6-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 35 minutes.
items.story: Jones tied Rui Hachimura for second on the team in scoring, with the former doubling his output from the opener while adding two steals. His defensive role keeps him on the floor amid the team's many absences, giving him more chances to contribute offensively while scorers like Bradley Beal (knee) and Brandon Ingram (heel) are out.

items.headline: Jones racked up eight points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal over 26 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 win over the Kings.
items.story: Jones put forth a productive Opening Night performance, contributing both defensively and as a playmaker. The door is open for Jones to handle more playing time until Brandon Ingram moves past an Achilles injury, but it's worth noting that Jones has typically been a low-usage player throughout the course of his career.

items.headline: Jones generated 14 points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, an assist and a steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Jones had his best preseason showing after scoring just 11 points across his first two appearances. He is valued more for his perimeter defense than his scoring, but efficient nights like this one help his case for a regular role at the wing, as well as a supporting role at the four spot.

items.headline: Jones will only suit up for the first half of Sunday's preseason game against the Warriors, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Jones will join Darius Garland, Max Strus, Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson in the first unit, though none of them will play in the second half. Jones started 45 of his 50 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, averaging 10.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.9 steals across 27.0 minutes per contest on the campaign.

items.headline: Max Strus gives the Clippers another veteran wing capable of occupying many of the same lineup slots as Jones.
items.story: While Jones offers considerably more defensive versatility and athleticism, Strus provides superior floor spacing and could be preferred in lineups that need additional shooting. The added competition makes Jones' minutes somewhat less secure and reinforces his status as a low-usage contributor whose fantasy value will generally come from defensive statistics rather than offensive volume.

items.headline: Jones could be in danger of moving into a reserve role in 2026-27 due to the selection of Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: If Wagler can win a starting job this offseason, it's likely that either Jones or Kris Dunn would be the odd man out of the first unit. The Clippers could move Dunn to small forward and Kawhi Leonard to power forward more often in small-ball lineups in this case, which would further jeopardize Jones' playing time. Jones started all but five of his 50 regular-season appearances a year ago, so he may at least open the new season in the first unit as the incumbent veteran.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) started the second half of Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors, per the broadcast.
items.story: Jones appeared to roll his right ankle in the second quarter before limping to the locker room. However, the ankle issue seemingly isn't serious enough to prevent him from playing in the second half of Wednesday's win-or-go-home matchup.

items.headline: Jones exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors due to an apparent right ankle injury, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Jones appeared to roll his right ankle and briefly stayed in the game before limping to the locker room. He should be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Jones ended with 11 points (4-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one block over 23 minutes during Tuesday's 116-103 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Jones and Brook Lopez combined for 21 rebounds in the win. The 10th-year pro bounced back to double-digit scoring totals after a three-game string of poor results. He's scored in double-digits only twice over the past eight games. The Clippers' frontcourt needs more nights like this from Jones to stay ahead of the pace in the playoff race.

items.headline: Jones ended with two points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and seven rebounds across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 119-94 victory over Toronto.
items.story: Despite his stable starting role, Jones doesn't tend to see enough usage to offer much fantasy appeal outside of deep settings. The forward has averaged 8.9 points, 4.3 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 29.7 minutes per tilt in his last seven games, shooting 46.2 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Jones closed Thursday's 105-99 loss to the Pelicans with 22 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-7 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
items.story: With Kawhi Leonard (ankle) sidelined for the second leg of a back-to-back set, Jones had to embrace a bigger role on offense, and he responded by tying his best scoring mark of the season. It's worth noting that Jones has had four of his five best scoring performances after the All-Star break. The 10-year veteran is averaging a career-best 11.1 points per game in 2025-26, but that number rises to 12.6 if only counting his performances after the break.

items.headline: Jones amassed 10 points (4-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block across 24 minutes during Monday's 119-115 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Jones has typically stepped up when Kawhi Leonard (ankle) is absent, but a poor shooting night thwarted that possibility. The support role for Leonard has fallen to Bennedict Mathurin with more frequency, although it was Jordan Miller's 22-point pop from the bench that absorbed a good chunk of Leonard's lost output Monday.

items.headline: Jones provided 10 points (4-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two steals over 34 minutes during Friday's 119-108 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Jones continues to produce on both ends of the floor, scoring in double digits for the eighth time in the past nine games. He has also recorded 15 combined steals and blocks in his past three games, flirting with top-20 value during that time. For now, Jones has to be added in all leagues, at least until John Collins (neck) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Jones (head) has been cleared to return to Monday's game against New York, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jones made a quick stop in the locker room after taking a blow to the head during the third quarter, but he was quickly given the green light to continue. He checked back into the game with 3:35 remaining in the third period.

items.headline: Jones went to the locker room during the third quarter of Monday's game against the Knicks due to an apparent head injury, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jones looked to take a blow to the head while finishing at the basket, and he exited the matchup at the next whistle. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Jones produced 12 points (4-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 34 minutes during Friday's 116-112 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Jones didn't have an efficient night from the field during Friday's loss, but he managed to reach double-digit points for the fourth time in his last five games while swatting two shots for the ninth time this season. Since the All-Star break, Jones has averaged 13.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 threes and 1.0 blocks over 31.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jones finished Thursday's 94-88 loss to the Timberwolves with 18 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-5 FT), one rebound, one assist, two blocks and one steal over 32 minutes.
items.story: The team didn't do enough to account for Kawhi Leonard's (ankle) absence, as the Clippers posted their second-lowest total of the season despite a decent line from Jones. Although the addition of Bennedict Mathurin has been significant, Jones has served well as a frequent fill-in for Leonard and will usually post viable totals when the All-Star is absent.

items.headline: Jones posted 22 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 34 minutes during Thursday's 115-114 win over Denver.
items.story: Although Bennedict Mathurin's 38-point result was the biggest headline for the Clippers, Jones proved to be a valuable piece of the puzzle as the team moves forward without James Harden's services. Kris Dunn lacks the necessary production to fill the scoring gap at point guard, so the Clippers will lean more on Jones and Mathurin while Kawhi Leonard takes the reins on offense. Jones is currently averaging a career-high 10.5 points per game this season, and that number could continue to rise due to the Clippers' needs on offense.

items.headline: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
items.story: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue to see increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

items.headline: Pippen (back) remains out for Wednesday's game against Denver, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: With Pippen set to miss another game, Memphis will continue to operate without one of its backcourt reserves. He has now been sidelined for six straight contests due to the back issue and can be considered week-to-week until Memphis offers an update on his recovery. Cam Spencer remains worth streaming in most fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Pippen (back) won't play in Monday's game versus the Raptors.
items.story: It will be a fifth consecutive absence for Pippen, who has been sidelined by back soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Denver. In the meantime, Cam Spencer is in line for more minutes.

items.headline: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Pippen is set for his fourth consecutive absence while dealing with a back issue. His next opportunity to return will arrive Monday in Toronto.

items.headline: Pippen (back) won't play Wednesday against the Pacers.
items.story: This will be Pippen's third straight game on the sidelines, which should continue resulting in more minutes for Cam Spencer. Pippen's next chance to play will come Friday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Pippen will miss a second consecutive contest due to lower-back soreness, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday against Indiana. Cam Spencer will likely see increased playing time off the bench with the 25-year-old sidelined.

items.headline: Pippen (back) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Pippen didn't suit up for Saturday's 136-105 win over the Kings. With Pippen in line to miss another game Monday, Cam Spencer will likely be on the floor more than usual behind Ty Jerome (back), who is not listed on the injury report for the meeting with New Orleans.

items.headline: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Pippen is working through a back injury and will end up missing his first game of the regular season. He is averaging 16.0 minutes per game off the bench, and that playing time will be absorbed by Cam Spencer, GG Jackson and Jerami Grant. Pippen's next opportunity to play is Monday against the Pelicans.

items.headline: Pippen (back) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Pippen has appeared in all five of the Grizzlies' regular-season games, though he's now in danger of missing Saturday's meeting with Sacramento. With Ty Jerome (back) also questionable, Pippen might find himself in the starting lineup. However, if neither of those players can suit up, Cam Spencer may get the start.

items.headline: Pippen recorded two points (1-1 FG) across 14 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Pippen's underwhelming start to the season continued Thursday, playing fewer than 15 minutes for the second straight game. Despite chatter heading into the season that he could battle Ty Jerome for the starting point guard position, it is clear that he is simply not in the discussion at the moment. Through five appearances, he has averaged just 6.4 points, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 16.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Pippen supplied nine points (2-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, five assists and three steals in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Pippen is playing the backup role at point guard to begin the year. Ty Jerome, who erupted for 45 points Wednesday, appears to have a strong hold on the top spot at the one for the time being.

items.headline: Pippen recorded 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists and one steal in 16 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Pippen came off the bench behind Ty Jerome, who started at point guard, but played well alongside Cam Spencer in the second unit. Pippen is considered Jerome's primary competition for the starting point guard job and should remain firmly in the rotation even if he begins the season as a reserve.

items.headline: Pippen is viewed as the biggest challenger to Ty Jerome for the starting point guard job, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: With Ja Morant out of the picture, Jerome has emerged as the most likely candidate to fill his shoes, though Pippen is also in the mix. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo called the 25-year-old guard an "easy fit" alongside other players thanks to his ballhandling, defense and ability to hit perimeter shots, and he figures to take on a sizable role regardless of whether he starts. Pippen appeared in just 10 regular-season games (six starts) in 2025-26 due to toe injuries, averaging 11.4 points, 4.7 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals in 21.2 minutes per contest. He shot just 31.3 percent from deep in that small sample last season, though he's a career 39.3 percent shooter from three-point range.

items.headline: Pippen is a full participant to begin training camp, Grizzlies president of basketball operations Zach Kleiman said, according to Memphis reporter Landon Speck.
items.story: Pippen continues to go through camp without any health-related restrictions, clearing the way for him to compete normally throughout the preseason. The guard's full participation is encouraging after he underwent a toe procedure back in March. As Memphis begins sorting out its backcourt rotation ahead of the regular season, Pippen's battle with Ty Jerome will be one to watch.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has a chance to begin the new year as Memphis' starting point guard after Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade with the Grizzlies earlier this offseason.
items.story: Pippen will have to gain clearance ahead of training camp after undergoing a toe procedure in March, but he certainly appears to be a winner of the team's offseason moves. Ty Jerome (ankle) poses a significant risk to Pippen's role, however, and the two guards figure to engage in a battle for the top role at the point this fall. Pippen is looking to bounce back following an injury-ruined 2025-26 campaign, during which he averaged 11.4 points, 4.7 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals in 21.2 minutes per game across 10 regular-season appearances (six starts).

items.headline: Pippen will miss the remainder of the 2025-26 season after undergoing a sesamoidectomy to address ongoing discomfort in his right big toe, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports Friday.
items.story: Pippen had no return timetable after his initial injury diagnosis, and the Grizzlies have no incentive to rush him back, so shutting him down isn't surprising. It's unclear what Pippen's offseason will look like, but he should be back to full strength by training camp next season. He missed the beginning of the campaign after undergoing surgery on his left big toe, so Pippen will finish his third year in Memphis with averages of 11.4 points, 4.7 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals across only 10 appearances (six starts). He's under contract for at least one more season before a club option in 2027-28.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced Thursday that Pippen will undergo a sesamoidectomy to address discomfort in his right big toe and is without a timeline for a return.
items.story: The guard is expected to make a full recovery from the procedure, and while a timeline for his return hasn't been established, the non-contending Grizzlies will most likely hold him out for the remainder of the season. Pippen has been limited to just 10 appearances so far in 2025-26, after his season debut was delayed while he recovered from a October surgery on the big toe on his left foot. His absence should help open up extra opportunities in the backcourt for rookies Walter Clayton (ankle) and Javon Small.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is out for Thursday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Pippen will miss a third straight game, including his second in a row due to an injury that the Grizzlies are labeling as right great toe sesamoiditis.
