Before making his season debut in early February, the 25-year-old guard had previously missed time to begin the campaign while recovering from surgery on the great toe on his left foot. While the fact that Pippen's latest absence isn't being attributed to his surgically repaired toe is a welcome sign, the Grizzlies haven't indicated when he might be ready to resume playing.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has been ruled out for Tuesday's against the 76ers.
items.story: Pippen had previously been sitting out one half of back-to-back sets due to left great toe injury management, but after missing Monday's 126-115 loss to the Nets, he'll now be sidelined for a second straight game due to soreness in the great toe on his other foot. With Ty Jerome (calf) and Cedric Coward (knee) returning to action following maintenance days Monday, Pippen's absence won't necessarily free up more minutes for other players.

items.headline: Pippen is out for Monday's game against the Nets due to right toe soreness.
items.story: As expected, the Grizzlies are downgrading Pippen from doubtful to out Monday. The expectation is that the guard will return to the lineup Tuesday, when Memphis takes on Philadelphia. Javon Small, Cam Spencer and Walter Clayton should each see plenty of playmaking opportunities for a Grizzlies team that has just eight active players Monday.

items.headline: Pippen is doubtful for Monday's game against the Nets due to right great toe soreness.
items.story: Pippen has played in seven of the team's last eight games, but he appears set to miss Monday's contest as he continues to nurse a toe injury. If he is officially ruled out, Javon Small, Cam Spencer and Walter Clayton could see expanded roles.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Saturday's meeting with the Clippers.
items.story: Pippen sat out the second leg of a back-to-back set Wednesday, but he'll be back in action Saturday evening, along with Ty Jerome (calf). With both Pippen and Jerome active, Walter Clayton, Jahmai Mashack and Javon Small will likely see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is out for Wednesday's game versus Portland.
items.story: Pippen will join Ty Jerome (calf) on the inactive list, so Cam Spencer, Javon Small and Walter Clayton figure to handle the point guard duties Wednesday evening. For now, Pippen can be considered questionable for Saturday's game against the Clippers.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against Portland.
items.story: The Grizzlies are expected to hold Pippen out of action for toe injury management. In his likely absence, Javon Small and Cam Spencer are in line to share the minutes at point guard Wednesday.

items.headline: Pippen provided 15 points (7-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals across 22 minutes during Friday's 124-105 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Getting the start in place of Ty Jerome (thigh), Pippen continued to be busy on defense while scoring in double digits for the fourth time in seven games (three starts) since making his season debut Feb. 6. Over that stretch, the fourth-year guard has averaged 11.3 points, 4.9 assists, 2.4 steals, 1.9 boards and 1.1 threes in 20.7 minutes.

items.headline: Pippen is in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Mavericks on Friday.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (thigh) sidelined, Pippen will make his second start in three games, joining Javon Small, Jaylen Wells, GG Jackson and Olivier-Maxence Prosper in the first unit. Pippen's last start was in a 123-114 loss to the Kings on Monday, when he posted six points, eight assists, two rebounds, five steals and seven turnovers over 22 minutes.

items.headline: Pippen isn't part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Pippen started Monday night and generated six points, two rebounds, eight assists and five steals over 22 minutes. He'll retreat to a reserve role Wednesday, as Javon Small will replace him in the first unit.

items.headline: Pippen is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Kings.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (illness) sidelined, Pippen will enter the starting five and make his second start of the season Monday. The Vanderbilt product didn't make his season debut until Feb. 6 due to a left toe injury and is averaging 12.5 points, 4.8 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.5 rebounds in 20.3 minutes per contest through four appearances.

items.headline: Pippen was ejected late in the fourth quarter of Saturday's loss to the Heat after engaging in a fight with Myron Gardner, Drew Hill of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: It seemed Pippen was the one who went straight at Gardner, so it wouldn't be surprising if he receives a fine or a suspension in the coming days. Pippen ended the game with 18 points (7-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block across 21 minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Pippen missed the front end of this back-to-back set due to left great toe injury management, though he's set to play Saturday. The 25-year-old guard has appeared in three outings (one start) this season after recovering from left great toe surgery he underwent in October. He's averaging 10.7 points, 4.3 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.0 rebounds in 20.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Pippen has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Jazz due to left great toe injury management.
items.story: Pippen will miss the front end of this back-to-back set but could return for Saturday's game against Miami. With the Grizzlies set to be extremely shorthanded in the backcourt, Cam Spencer, Jahmai Mashack and Javon Small should see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is off the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Pippen missed the second half of the team's back-to-back set Saturday as he returns to action following an extended absence due to a left great toe injury. He will return to the lineup Monday after recording 13 points, six assists, three rebounds and a steal in 22 minutes in his season debut Friday.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Portland.
items.story: Pippen made his regular-season debut in Friday's loss to the Trail Blazers but will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back due to left great toe injury management. His next opportunity to play will come Monday against Golden State. The Grizzlies are expected to be extremely shorthanded in the backcourt Saturday, leaving more minutes available for the likes of Javon Small, Walter Clayton, Jahmai Mashack and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) contributed 13 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six assists, three rebounds and one steal in 22 minutes during Friday's 135-115 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Finally cleared to make his season debut after recovering from October toe surgery, Pippen was plugged right into the starting five and delivered a strong performance, although his minutes were unsurprisingly limited. With Ja Morant (elbow) facing an uncertain timeline for a return, Pippen appears likely to split minutes at point guard with Ty Jerome (calf) in games where both players are available. Jerome sat out Friday's contest, but he'll likely return to action Saturday in Portland. Pippen, meanwhile, is likely to be rested for that game coming off the long-term absence.

items.headline: Pippen is in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Trail Blazers on Friday.
items.story: Pippen was given the green light to make his 2025-26 regular-season debut Friday after recovering from a procedure he underwent in October for a left big toe injury, and he'll be in the starting lineup due to the absence of Ty Jerome (calf). Pippen averaged 9.9 points, 4.4 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals over 21.3 minutes per game during the 2024-25 regular season.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is available for Friday's game against Portland.
items.story: After undergoing left big toe surgery in October, Pippen will make his regular-season debut in the first leg of this back-to-back set. It wouldn't be surprising to see him operate under a strict minutes restriction during his return. Over 79 regular-season appearances (21 starts) in 2024-25, Pippen averaged 9.9 points, 4.4 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 21.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is questionable for Friday's game in Portland.
items.story: This is the first time that Pippen has received the questionable tag this season, so it's possible he could be making his regular-season debut Friday night. He'll likely have some minutes restrictions in his first game back, but if Pippen is cleared, he'd be worth a look in deep leagues. Through 15 games in March last season, Pippen registered averages of 12.1 points, 5.3 assists, 1.5 triples and 2.1 steals per contest on 51/46/86 shooting splits.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Pippen has yet to make his 2025-26 regular-season debut while recovering from left big toe surgery that he underwent in October. The good news for the fourth-year pro was that he was initially listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game, rather than being outright ruled out, indicating that he is getting closer to a return. Pippen's next chance to play is Friday against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is listed doubtful for Wednesday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Wednesday marks the first time all season that Pippen hasn't immediately been listed as out in advance of a game, which signals that he's closing in on making his season debut. While there's a good chance he'll be ruled out prior to Wednesday's matchup, Pippen could have a realistic shot at debuting Friday in Portland. Ty Jerome has thrived as the Grizzlies' starting point guard in two games since making his season debut, but Pippen could be in line for a sizable role of his own out of the Memphis backcourt once healthy, at least until Memphis gets Ja Morant (elbow) back in action.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Pippen has yet to debut this season due to left big toe surgery, which he underwent in October. Pippen recently joined the Grizzlies' G League affiliate for practice, suggesting he may be approaching his return. His next chance to suit up comes Wednesday against the Kings.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Pippen has yet to make his season debut while recovering from left big toe surgery he underwent in October and will remain sidelined Saturday. However, the 25-year-old guard recently joined the Grizzlies' G League affiliate for practice and appears to be nearing a return to action. His next chance to play will come Monday against Minnesota, though he should be considered doubtful for that game until Memphis offers an update on his status.

items.headline: The Grizzlies recalled Pippen (toe) from the G League's Memphis Hustle on Wednesday.
items.story: Pippen was able to practice with the Hustle prior to being recalled, which puts him on track to make his season debut within the coming days. Memphis has an upcoming back-to-back set this weekend, playing Friday in New Orleans before heading home to face Minnesota on Saturday. Pippen can be considered doubtful for those contests until the Grizzlies release an injury report Thursday afternoon.

items.headline: Pippen (toe) is practicing with the G League's Memphis Hustle on Wednesday.
items.story: Pippen is on a brief assignment to get some extra reps during his recovery from toe surgery, and he'll be recalled following Wednesday's session. The guard has still not made his season debut, but Pippen is tracking toward doing so at some point in the near future and should be ready to go in early February if all goes well.

items.headline: Maxey contributed 22 points (7-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds and five assists across 35 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
items.story: Maxey has struggled from beyond the arc in his last two appearances, connecting on just two of 10 attempts. However, his substantial playing time and prominent offensive role continue to provide a strong fantasy foundation, even with Philadelphia's crowded rotation.

items.headline: Maxey produced 17 points (4-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-10 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one block in 36 minutes during Saturday's 132-129 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: After sitting out Wednesday's game with a minor foot issue, Maxey was back in action Saturday and saw his usual workload, although he did fail to score at least 20 points for the first time since Nov. 6. Through nine games in November, the All-Star guard is averaging 23.1 points, 6.7 assists, 2.7 boards, 2.4 threes and 0.8 steals.

items.headline: Maxey (foot) is available for Saturday's game against the Bucks, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: Maxey was deemed a game-time call for Saturday's game, and after the star guard went unscathed after warmups, he'll be back in the starting lineup. It remains to be seen if he'll have a minutes restriction, but having Maxey back in the mix is huge for the 76ers. He's averaging 26.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 5.8 assists per game this season.

items.headline: Maxey (foot) will be a true game-time decision for Saturday's game against the Bucks, head coach Nick Nurse told Ky Carlin of USA Today.
items.story: According to Nurse, Maxey will go through his usual pregame warm-ups to see if he can play. If he suits up, he could have a minutes restriction, as Nurse also said Maxey "isn't there yet." If Maxey doesn't play, Anfernee Simons would remain in the backcourt alongside VJ Edgecombe.

items.headline: Maxey (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Maxey sat out Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic, but he was a full participant at Friday's practice, so he's trending in the right direction. If Maxey is cleared to return, Anfernee Simons would likely head back to the second unit and VJ Edgecombe's usage rate would dip.

items.headline: Maxey (foot) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Maxey was held out of Wednesday's win over Orlando due to right foot soreness, though he's trending in the right direction ahead of Saturday's game against Milwaukee. The Sixers should provide an update on the star point guard's status by Friday night, and if he's cleared to return, Anfernee Simons and Labaron Philon would likely see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Maxey (foot) is out for Wednesday's game in Orlando, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Maxey will join Jaylen Brown (hamstring) on the inactive list for Wednesday's game, and it'll be Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope starting in their places. For now, Maxey should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Bucks.

items.headline: Maxey is questionable for Wednesday's game in Orlando due to right foot soreness, Gina Mizell of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: Maxey came out for his pregame routine and then quickly retreated to the locker room, where his injury status was updated, which is not a great sign. If Maxey misses Wednesday's game, VJ Edgecombe, LeBron James and Joel Embiid would see an uptick in usage, and there would be more minutes available for Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.

items.headline: Maxey closed Monday's 135-123 win over the Nets with 24 points (7-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), nine assists, one rebound and one steal across 35 minutes.
items.story: Maxey put up a season-low-tying 12 field-goal attempts but turned in an efficient outing and reached the 20-point mark for a fifth straight game. The star point guard also paced all players in assists, dishing out his most dimes since Nov. 2. Over his last five games, Maxey has averaged 25.8 points, 6.8 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 35.2 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Maxey finished with 27 points (9-19 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, six assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Sunday's 131-124 win over Indiana.
items.story: The star guard has now dropped at least 24 points in four consecutive games, accomplishing this feat in all but two of his first 14 appearances of the season. Maxey hasn't seen a noticeable dip in usage with the new-look 76ers, averaging 26.7 points, 5.6 assists, 3.4 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.6 three-pointers per game so far.

items.headline: Maxey provided 27 points (8-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 10-12 FT), two rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block across 35 minutes during Thursday's 123-112 win over Toronto.
items.story: Maxey continues to give fantasy managers efficient production in almost every statistical category. He led his team in scoring for the second straight outing while matching VJ Edgecombe for the team lead in assists with eight. Maxey excelled at getting to the free throw line too, setting a new season high in makes and attempts. He'll keep working as the primary scorer on most nights, and when LeBron James (back) is out of the lineup, Maxey can step in as an elite playmaker.

items.headline: Maxey tallied 24 points (8-12 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), one rebound and four assists across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 123-101 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Maxey led the Sixers in scoring for the eighth time in 12 outings, pouring in an efficient 24 points. He has now hit at least one three-pointer in every contest so far this season, and he's taking good care of the ball recently, averaging just 1.0 turnovers over his last four games. Maxey will continue to provide fantasy managers with contributions across the board for 9-3 Philadelphia.

items.headline: Maxey racked up 27 points (9-16 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds and seven assists across 36 minutes during Sunday's 127-121 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Maxey delivered another strong offensive performance, shooting efficiently from all three levels while leading Philadelphia with seven assists. The star guard also committed just one turnover despite handling significant playmaking responsibilities, and he connected on a key three-pointer late in the fourth quarter to help secure the victory. Maxey continues to provide elite scoring and assist production alongside a crowded group of offensive contributors.

items.headline: Maxey produced 19 points (5-16 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), one rebound and seven assists across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 112-106 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Maxey struggled inside the arc, converting just two of his nine two-point attempts, but his perimeter shooting and perfect night at the foul line helped offset the inefficiency. He also committed only one turnover while handing out seven assists. With Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown combining for 56 points, Maxey didn't need to carry the scoring load to help Philadelphia secure the win.

items.headline: Maxey amassed 26 points (10-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 assists, four rebounds, two steals and two blocks across 36 minutes in Monday's 126-107 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Although he struggled from three-point range, Maxey was nearly perfect from inside the arc. The star point guard led all players in scoring and assists, securing his first double-double of the season. He also turned in another productive performance on the defensive end and tallied multiple steals for a second straight game. Maxey has yet to score fewer than 26 points in a game this season and continues to make an impact on both ends of the floor.

items.headline: Maxey finished with 38 points (13-23 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 8-9 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals across 38 minutes in Saturday's 109-104 win over Charlotte.
items.story: With LeBron James (rest) and Joel Embiid (foot) sidelined for this contest, Maxey stepped up to lead Philadelphia to its sixth win of the 2026-27 campaign. The 25-year-old got off to a hot start, and while he cooled off in the second and third quarters, he got back on track in the fourth by scoring 15 of his 38 points to seal the deal. Maxey has played at an MVP level, averaging a career-best 29.6 points along with 4.1 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.7 steals over 37.6 minutes per outing in seven regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Maxey amassed 27 points (10-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-7 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 38 minutes in Friday's 98-93 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Maxey led the Sixers to a second victory in as many games against the Knicks this season, leading all players in scoring. The star point guard didn't have his best performance from the charity stripe, though he turned in an otherwise efficient shooting effort. He has yet to record fewer than 26 points and four assists in a game this season.

items.headline: Maxey finished Wednesday's 114-109 victory over the Pacers with 27 points (8-18 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 36 minutes.
items.story: Maxey took over down the stretch, scoring 17 points in the fourth quarter and knocking down two three-pointers in the final 90 seconds to help Philadelphia secure the comeback victory. The dynamic guard led the 76ers in scoring and continued to shoulder a significant offensive workload despite sharing the floor with several established stars. His combination of scoring volume, perimeter shooting and heavy minutes makes him a dependable fantasy option.

items.headline: Maxey logged 29 points (11-24 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 6-7 FT), five rebounds, four assists, three steals and a block in 33 minutes during Sunday's 106-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: It took a while for Maxey to get going Sunday, but he turned it on in the second half, scoring 23 of his 29 points. The star guard also made an impact defensively, posting a game-high three steals and adding a block. There was a moment of concern for Maxey when he and John Collins clashed heads and were slow to get up, but both appeared to recover shortly thereafter. Still, it's something to monitor ahead of Wednesday's game against the Pacers.

items.headline: Maxey contributed 26 points (9-22 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds and four assists across 36 minutes in Saturday's 127-116 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Maxey remained aggressive offensively, and this was the second straight game in which he attempted at least 20 shots from the field -- and he's yet to shoot under 19 in any game. His substantial shot volume reinforces his prominent role in Philadelphia's offense, but his lack of efficiency could be an issue, especially since he needs to stay effective to avoid ceding touches to Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid (rest) or LeBron James (back). The scoring efficiency is worth keeping close tabs on -- Maxey is averaging 28.7 points per game in his first three outings but is shooting a mere 32 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Vanderbilt provided four points (2-3 FG, 0-2 FT) and seven rebounds over 14 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets.
items.story: Vanderbilt made his presence felt on the glass, collecting six offensive rebounds despite playing fewer than 15 minutes. The veteran forward has remained a limited part of the Lakers' rotation, averaging approximately 12 minutes over his last five appearances. His rebounding ability offers occasional value in deeper leagues, but his minimal offensive involvement and restricted playing time limit his fantasy upside.

items.headline: Vanderbilt closed Sunday's 121-116 win over the Pistons with two points (1-1 FG, 0-1 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and one block across 14 minutes.
items.story: Vanderbilt was remarkably active on the glass despite playing fewer than 14 minutes, collecting eight defensive rebounds and two offensive boards. He also contributed three assists and a block, providing useful peripheral production despite attempting just one shot. His rebounding ability remains valuable, but inconsistent playing time makes him difficult to trust in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Vanderbilt produced zero points (0-1 FG), seven rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Vanderbilt made his season debut, bringing some defensive energy off the bench. Once Luka Doncic (back) and Ziaire Williams (foot) return to action, Vanderbilt is expected to fall back into obscurity.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (undisclosed) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.
items.story: Vanderbilt skipped the Lakers' preseason finale, but he'll be available for Opening Night. However, he's not guaranteed a spot in the rotation.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (undisclosed) isn't expected to play in Friday's preseason game against the Nuggets, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt was spotted in street clothes, though it's unknown why he isn't playing in the Lakers' preseason finale. His next chance to suit up will come in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Vanderbilt recorded four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 10 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over Sacramento.
items.story: Vanderbilt didn't take the floor until the fourth quarter, suggesting he's fighting for a roster spot. His fantasy arrow is pointing down ahead of the new season.

items.headline: Vanderbilt is among the candidates for the Lakers' final starting position, according to Jovan Buha of Buha's Block.
items.story: Vanderbilt's defensive versatility, size and rebounding make him a theoretical fit for what Los Angeles wants from the role, but Buha is skeptical that he'll win the competition after playing a modest role last season. Jake LaRavia and Ziaire Williams appear to have the inside track entering camp, so Vanderbilt may need a strong preseason to move up the pecking order.

items.headline: Vanderbilt should continue to provide defensive value after LeBron James' exit from the Lakers, Broderick Turner of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Despite James' absence, the arrivals of Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili give the Lakers additional options on the wing and in the frontcourt. While Vanderbilt's rebounding and defensive versatility remain valuable, increased competition for minutes could make it difficult for him to carve out a reliable fantasy role.

items.headline: Vanderbilt finished Monday's 115-110 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals with zero points (0-1 FG) and one rebound over three minutes.
items.story: After suffering a finger injury in Game 1, Vanderbilt made his second appearance of the series in Monday's Game 4. He played a very minor role for the Lakers in the regular season, posting averages of 4.4 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.8 steals in 17.4 minutes across 65 appearances.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (finger) is available for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt is back after a one-game absence, which could result in fewer minutes for Dalton Knecht and Jake LaRavia. Vanderbilt is averaging 3.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 12.1 minutes per game this postseason.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (finger) is questionable for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals versus the Thunder, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt missed Game 2 on Thursday after dislocating his right pinky finger in Tuesday's Game 1 loss, but there's a chance he could return for Game 3 on Saturday. If he's cleared to play, Dalton Knecht and Jake LaRavia's minutes could dip a bit.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (finger) has been ruled out for Thursday's Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Thunder.
items.story: Vanderbilt will miss Game 2 after exiting Tuesday's Game 1 loss in the second quarter due to a dislocated right finger. The forward is considered day-to-day, so a return for Saturday's Game 3 remains possible, though his absence could lead to increased opportunities off the bench for Jake LaRavia in the meantime.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (finger) is doubtful for Thursday's Western Conference Semifinals Game 2 against the Thunder, per Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com.
items.story: Vanderbilt suffered a dislocated right finger during the second quarter of Tuesday's Western Conference Semifinals Game 1 loss to the Thunder. With Vanderbilt expected to miss Game 2 on Thursday, Jake LaRavia is an option for an expanded role.

items.headline: Vanderbilt is day-to-day with a dislocated right finger, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: Vanderbilt suffered the injury during the second quarter of Tuesday's Western Conference Semifinals Game 1 loss to the Thunder. It sounds like he has a chance to play through the issue going forward, so Vanderbilt can be tentatively viewed as questionable for Game 2 on Thursday in Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Vanderbilt has been diagnosed with a full dislocation of his right pinky finger, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt exited Tuesday's Western Conference Semifinals Game 1 loss to the Thunder in the second quarter after hitting the backboard and injuring his finger. He was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game after exiting to the locker room and can be considered doubtful for Game 2 on Thursday until the Lakers offer an update on his status.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (finger) has been ruled out for the remainder of Tuesday's Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Thunder, Khobi Price of The California Post reports. He'll close with two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound across six minutes.
items.story: Vanderbilt exited to the locker room in the second quarter due to a right finger injury and will remain sidelined for the remainder of Tuesday's contest. The forward's playing time has decreased of late, so his absence shouldn't create major ripple effects in the Lakers' rotation, though Jake LaRavia could see a slightly larger role off the bench. More updates will likely follow, but for now, Vanderbilt should be considered questionable for Game 2 on Thursday.

items.headline: Vanderbilt exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Tuesday's Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Thunder due to an apparent right hand injury, Dan Woike of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt attempted to contest a dunk but ended up hitting his right hand on the backboard. He appeared to be in a considerable amount of pain while heading back to the locker room and can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Lakers' 98-78 win over the Rockets in Game 6 of the first-round playoff series.
items.story: Lakers head coach JJ Redick utilized an eight-man rotation while Friday's contest was still competitive, and Vanderbilt ended up losing hold of his spot on the second unit while Luke Kennard, Jake LaRavia and Jaxson Hayes operated as the team's main reserves. The Lakers could eventually get Luka Doncic (hamstring) back at some point during their Western Conference Semifinals series versus the Thunder, and Vanderbilt will face an even tougher path to regaining playing time once Los Angeles is at full strength. Before failing to get off the bench Friday, Vanderbilt had appeared in 11 straight games dating back to the regular season and averaged 4.3 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 14.3 minutes.

items.headline: Vanderbilt accumulated eight points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-1 FT), four rebounds and one steal across 14 minutes during Sunday's 115-96 loss to the Rockets in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: This was Vanderbilt's best game of the series as he logged at least 14 minutes for the fourth game in a row. Overall this series, he's averaging 15.3 minutes per contest with 4.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 0.5 steals.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (calf) is available for Sunday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Vanderbilt will shake off a questionable tag and should see increased playing time moving forward, as Austin Reaves (oblique) and Luka Doncic (hamstring) are out for at least a month, while Marcus Smart (ankle) also remains sidelined. Over his past 10 appearances, Vanderbilt has averaged 3.1 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 13.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Vanderbilt is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas due to right calf soreness, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt may want to test his calf while going through his pregame routine, so he could be headed for a game-time call Sunday. If he's ruled out, that could open up some minutes for Jake LaRavia and Maxi Kleber.

items.headline: Vanderbilt registered nine points (4-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and three steals over 12 minutes during Thursday's 139-96 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Vanderbilt has had a hard time staying in the Lakers' rotation, but he was able to make an appearance with Thursday's game getting out of hand early. Considering he didn't see the floor in Tuesday's win over Cleveland, Vanderbilt isn't a lock to see steady playing time during the final week of the regular season.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (coach's decision) didn't receive any playing time Monday in the Lakers' 100-92 win over the Rockets.
items.story: After a recent stretch in which he appeared in five straight games and averaged 12.0 minutes, Vanderbilt has now been left out of head coach JJ Redick's rotation for the past two contests. The Lakers seem content to lean on Jaxson Hayes and Rui Hachimura to fill out minutes in the frontcourt when starters LeBron James and Deandre Ayton are off the court.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Sunday's 128-104 win over the Kings.
items.story: Vanderbilt ended up dropping out of the rotation after he had appeared in each of the Lakers' last 35 games and averaged 4.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 0.9 steals in 18.8 minutes per contest during that stretch. The veteran big man had been trending down prior to his absence Sunday, playing no more than 12 minutes in any of his last five appearances while converting on just 36.4 percent of his field-goal attempts. Head coach JJ Redick went with Maxi Kleber (13 minutes) on the second unit in lieu of Vanderbilt in what could prove to be more than a one-time arrangement.

items.headline: Vanderbilt ended Saturday's 105-99 win over Golden State with 13 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 19 minutes.
items.story: Saturday marked Vanderbilt's fourth game this season with multiple threes. He also grabbed eight rebounds and forced some turnovers on defense. The Lakers rotation has fluctuated all season long, so a few more strong showings could lead to Vanderbilt's role expanding.

items.headline: Vanderbilt had seven points (3-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt), one rebound, two assists, one block and four steals across 22 minutes during Thursday's 112-104 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Vanderbilt was a bright spot on the defensive end for the Lakers on Thursday, recording a season-high four swipes and his eighth game with one steal and one block. Across 12 games in January, the 26-year-old forward is averaging 4.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.5 blocks in 21.1 minutes per contest

items.headline: Vanderbilt recorded six points (3-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and five rebounds across 15 minutes during Thursday's 135-117 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: With Rui Hachimura back in the mix, Vanderbilt's path to playing time is obstructed. At least for the time being, Vanderbilt is really going to struggle to keep his fantasy value afloat due to a minor role in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Vanderbilt won't start against the Bucks on Friday, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With LeBron James (foot/sciatica) back in the lineup following a one-game absence, Vanderbilt will slide to the second unit. Over his last 10 appearances off the bench, the 26-year-old forward has averaged 6.6 points and 6.0 rebounds in 23.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Vanderbilt is in the Lakers' starting lineup against the Spurs on Wednesday, Ryan Ward of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt will make his third start of the season Wednesday due to the absence of LeBron James (foot/sciatica). Across his prior two starts, Vanderbilt averaged 8.5 points, 10.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals over 27.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Vanderbilt posted seven points (3-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Tuesday's 111-103 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Vanderbilt gave the Lakers a huge lift off the bench on both ends of the court Tuesday, and that's been the case a lot recently. Over his last six outings, Vanderbilt has seen 24.6 minutes per night with 7.2 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.2 three-pointers on 60.7 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (leg) is available for Friday's game against the Grizzlies, Dan Woike of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Vanderbilt was initially listed as questionable for Friday's contest due to right leg soreness, though he was eventually upgraded to probable and has now been cleared to suit up. The 26-year-old forward has logged 20-plus minutes in six consecutive contests, averaging 6.7 points and 6.0 rebounds in 24.5 minutes per tilt during that stretch.

items.headline: Vanderbilt (leg) is probable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Right leg soreness is unlikely to stop Vanderbilt from playing Friday. The forward has averaged 6.7 points, 6.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 24.7 minutes per contest over his last six games, shooting 53.6 percent from the field.

items.headline: Vanderbilt is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies due to right leg soreness.
items.story: Vanderbilt is in jeopardy of missing Friday's contest after logging 20-plus minutes in six straight games. Maxi Kleber and Dalton Knecht would likely see their minutes increase if Vanderbilt doesn't play Friday. Vanderbilt is averaging 5.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists over 19.2 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Vanderbilt had five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and two steals over 22 minutes during Sunday's 125-101 win over the Kings.
items.story: Vanderbilt has stepped into a larger role lately, with the Lakers looking for a defensive spark. Over his last five outings, he's seen 24.2 minutes per contest with 6.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.4 three-pointers on 48.0 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Vanderbilt chipped in seven points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 11 rebounds and one assist over 25 minutes during Thursday's 143-135 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Although Jaxson Hayes slid into a starting role with Deandre Ayton (elbow) on the sidelines, Vanderbilt finished with the big rebound total. Hayes managed only three boards, while Vanderbilt and Luka Doncic led the rebound brigade with 11 each. Now in his third full season with the Lakers, Vanderbilt's production remains minimal, averaging just 17.6 minutes across 17 games.

items.headline: Vanderbilt chipped in seven points (2-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one block and two steals in 15 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 win over the Suns.
items.story: Vanderbilt played double-digit minutes for the first time since Nov. 14. After not seeing the floor in eight straight games, the defensive-minded forward has received minutes in two of the Lakers' past three games. With Austin Reaves (calf) sidelined for at least a week, coach JJ Redick might open up the rotation, which could bode well for Vanderbilt's playing time.

items.headline: Hardy logged two points (0-6 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists and one steal over nine minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers.
items.story: It took both Luka Doncic (back) and Ziaire Williams (foot) being sidelined to get Hardy into the mix, but he failed to make a case for more playing time in the future. Hardy figures to revert to emergency backcourt depth once Doncic and Williams return.

items.headline: Hardy registered 13 points (4-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals and an assist across 19 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: After coming over from Washington this past summer, Hardy is trying to make a case for a bench role with the Lakers. The combo guard looks to be quite lost in the shuffle, but Hardy could inch his way up the depth chart once Los Angeles begins to trim its roster.

items.headline: The Wizards traded Hardy and two second-round picks to the Lakers in exchange for Deandre Ayton on Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Hardy will get yet another fresh start, this time in Los Angeles. In 57 regular-season games, split between the Mavericks and Wizards in 2025-26, Hardy averaged 9.2 points and 1.0 assists in 15.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hardy closed Sunday's 130-117 loss to the Cavaliers with six points (2-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 0-2 FT), one rebound and three assists in 16 minutes.
items.story: Hardy opened the season without a stable role with Dallas, but his minutes picked up a bit with Washington. The combo guard averaged 12.6 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 20.4 minutes per tilt over 23 games for the Wizards. Hardy is under contract for the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Hardy (back) will be available for Friday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Hardy missed the past two games but will be available for the second-to-last game of the season. In 22 appearances with the Wizards, he's averaging 12.9 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 20.6 minutes.

items.headline: Hardy (back) is questionable for Friday's game against Miami.
items.story: Hardy remains day-to-day after missing the past two contests for Washington. He could see a sizable workload Friday if he gets the green light to play, given how shorthanded the Wizards will be against the Heat.

items.headline: Hardy (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hardy will be sidelined for his second straight contest. He was previously considered questionable, so he'll have a chance to return Friday against Miami.

items.headline: Hardy (back) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Hardy wasn't available in Tuesday's 129-98 loss to the Bulls. He's back on the injury report for Thursday's rematch. If Hardy can suit up versus Chicago, he may be needed in the starting lineup. However, if he doesn't get on the floor, Jamir Watkins and Bub Carrington may see more minutes.

items.headline: Hardy (back) is out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hardy was a late addition to the injury report with lower-back spasms and is ultimately unable to play Tuesday. With the fourth-year guard sidelined, more playing time is open to Bub Carrington and Sharife Cooper in the backcourt.

items.headline: Hardy (back) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hardy is a late addition to the injury report with lower-back spasms. If the fourth-year guard is ultimately downgraded to out, more playing time would be available to Bub Carrington and Sharife Cooper in the backcourt.

items.headline: Hardy racked up 19 points (7-15 FG, 5-10 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 25 minutes during Saturday's 152-136 loss to Miami.
items.story: Hardy had his three-point shot working throughout Saturday's clash, marking the third time in his last six games that he's torched the nets for five or more made treys. He was also involved on the defensive end by racking up at least one steal and one block for the first time since March 17. Hardy is averaging 16.2 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists over his last six matchups.

items.headline: Hardy (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Sunday in the Wizards' 123-88 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Though Washington ruled out seven players ahead of Sunday's contest, head coach Brian Keefe maintained a 10-man rotation, and Hardy ended up being the odd man out. Hardy had previously appeared in eight consecutive games, averaging 13.9 points, 3.4 three-pointers, 1.4 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 21.4 minutes per contest over that stretch. The fourth-year wing should have a good chance at re-entering the rotation Monday against the Lakers, though the Wizards aren't expected to provide any clarity prior to the game regarding whether Hardy will play.

items.headline: Hardy contributed 21 points (8-18 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 0-2 FT) and two rebounds across 27 minutes during Wednesday's 133-110 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Hardy scored at least 20 points for the second straight game, continuing to provide the Wizards with a consistent scoring punch off the bench. Over his last five appearances, Hardy has averaged 17.3 points and 4.2 three-pointers in 26.4 minutes, but he's offered little in other areas (1.4 assists, 0.4 steals, 0.2 blocks, 0-for-2 on free-throw attempts).

items.headline: Hardy logged 25 points (9-18 FG, 7-13 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes during Sunday's 145-113 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: This game was over in a hurry, so Hardy was able to take advantage of some garbage time. He's trending up over his last seven games, posting averages of 13.3 points, 1.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 3.0 three-pointers in 22.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hardy chipped in 16 points (6-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 32 minutes during Tuesday's 130-117 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Hardy logged 32 minutes, the most he has played since joining Washington. He ended the night scoring in double digits for the 11th time in 15 appearances as a Wizard. It's almost impossible to get a read on what the rotation is going to look like from one night to the next. At this point, managers should look at Hardy as a potential streaming consideration when in need of points and threes.

items.headline: Hardy provided 17 points (5-12 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound and one block over 23 minutes during Tuesday's 150-129 loss to Miami.
items.story: Hardy is carving out a decent role with the Wizards and should continue to battle with Sharife Cooper for backcourt reserve minutes. Hardy has scored in double figures in all but one of his 10 outings with Washington, averaging 12.8 points, 2.0 rebounds, 0.8 assists and 2.0 three-pointers in 19.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hardy ended with 18 points (7-13 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 126-109 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Hardy has been making the most of the bench role he's earned in Washington and has scored in double digits in each of his seven outings since being traded from the Mavericks to the Wizards just before the deadline. In seven games in Washington, Hardy is averaging 13.9 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.6 assists across 20.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hardy provided 14 points (6-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes during Monday's 123-118 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Hardy continues to provide the Wizards with an offensive punch off the bench, tallying double digits for the sixth straight appearance. While he has managed to flash some offensive upside, Hardy's peripheral production remains basically non-existent. In his six games as a Wizard, Hardy has recorded a total of 14 rebounds, three assists and three combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Hardy posted 11 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT) over 20 minutes during Saturday's 134-125 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Hardy scored in double figures for a fifth straight appearance, although his peripheral production remains basically nonexistent. In fact, in those five games since joining the Wizards, Hardy has recorded a total of just 11 rebounds, two assists and three combined steals-plus-blocks. At best, managers in deeper formats could consider streaming him in for points and threes.

items.headline: Hardy recorded 16 points (5-10 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one block in 22 minutes during Sunday's 129-112 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Hardy has scored in double figures and knocked down at least three triples in all three games for the Wizards since being acquired at the deadline. The 23-year-old guard's playing time could vary game to game as Washington's rotations have been difficult to predict in recent weeks.

items.headline: Hardy posted 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes during Wednesday's 138-113 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hardy, who made his Washington debut after being acquired from Dallas at the trade deadline, put together a strong showing in limited playing time off the bench. Player development is going to be a big focus for the Wizards after the All-Star break, so additional opportunities may arise for the 23-year-old guard.

items.headline: Hardy (rest) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hardy is available for the first time since being traded from Dallas to Washington, though it's unclear how large a role, if any, he'll play for his new team. Keep an eye out for an update on Kyshawn George (ankle) and Bilal Coulibaly (heel) closer to tipoff, as both are listed as questionable. If one, or both, are sidelined, Hardy could be tasked with a sizable role.

items.headline: Hardy (rest) will not play Sunday against Miami.
items.story: Hardy, who was traded from Dallas to Washington on Wednesday, has yet to be cleared to make his Wizards debut. It remains to be seen what type of role he will play with his new squad.

items.headline: Hardy (recently traded) is out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Wednesday's trade centered around Anthony Davis (finger) still isn't official, so Hardy is unable to make his Wizards debut. His next opportunity to do so arrives Sunday against the Heat.

items.headline: Hardy (trade pending) won't play Thursday in Detroit.
items.story: The trade sending Hardy to Washington has not yet been finalized, so Hardy won't be available for Thursday's game. He'll likely make his Wizards debut Saturday in Brooklyn.

items.headline: Hardy is being traded to the Wizards on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Anthony Davis (finger), D'Angelo Russell (illness) and Dante Exum (knee) will join Hardy in Washington, with Khris Middleton, AJ Johnson, Malaki Branham and Marvin Bagley heading to Dallas. The Mavericks also received two first-round picks and three second-round picks.
items.story: Hardy was an inconsistent part of the rotation in Dallas, but he could get some time to shine in D.C., so he's worth monitoring in deep leagues. He'll still be competing with Russell and Bub Carrington for minutes, and things could get complicated once Trae Young (knee) is cleared to play, so this is a wait-and-see situation in most fantasy leagues. Hardy can be considered doubtful for Thursday's game against the Pistons while the deal finalizes.

items.headline: Hardy is not in the Mavericks' starting lineup against the Jazz on Saturday, per Christian Clark of The Athletic.
items.story: Hardy has started in each of the Mavericks' last three games and averaged 13.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 3.0 threes over 25.0 minutes per game over that span. He'll retreat to the bench for Saturday's contest while Max Christie enters the Mavericks' starting five.

items.headline: Hardy is starting Monday's game against the Nets, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Hardy will draw just his second start of the season as the Mavericks have elected to shake up the first unit Monday. His last start dates back to Dec. 23 against Denver, when he finished with 10 points, two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Hardy is in the Mavericks' starting lineup against the Nuggets on Tuesday.
items.story: Hardy has been a healthy DNP in four of the Mavericks' last nine games, but the 2022 second-rounder will enter the starting lineup Tuesday for the first time this season due to the absence of P.J. Washington (foot). Hardy is averaging 5.7 points, 1.2 rebounds and 1.1 threes over 10.5 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Hardy notched four points (1-5 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 11 minutes during Monday's 119-113 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: It's worth mentioning that Brandon Williams sprained his right ankle Monday, making his status worth monitoring. If Williams can't give it a go, it's possible Hardy gets a longer look. Hardy has averaged just 8.3 minutes across his last seven appearances.

items.headline: Hardy supplied 17 points (4-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT) and three rebounds across 14 minutes during Monday's 120-96 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Hardy paced the Mavericks with a season-high 17 points, though it had little impact in an eventual blowout loss. The young guard's minutes have fluctuated throughout the year, as he's averaged 5.9 points in 10.9 minutes across 12 appearances. One factor that could help him secure a steadier role is his strong three-point shooting, as he's knocking down 45.5 percent of his attempts this season after hitting four from deep Monday.

items.headline: Hardy finished with zero points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and one rebound over 10 minutes during Wednesday's 101-99 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Hardy has not been a consistent figure in the Mavericks' rotation and barely sees the court as the third-string point guard behind D'Angelo Russell and Brandon Williams. Hardy has gone scoreless in two straight contests and will likely see very limited action moving forward.

items.headline: Hardy produced 11 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, one assist and two steals over 21 minutes during Monday's 101-94 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Hardy played at least 20 minutes for the first time this season, tallying a season-high 11 points. Dallas is struggling to find a winning formula at the moment, having won just one of its four games thus far. While Hardy can provide an offensive boost off the bench, he is largely unproven when it comes to putting up consistent numbers. There is no reason to make him a priority right now, but he is worth keeping an eye on moving forward.

items.headline: Hardy recorded 13 points (5-15 FG, 3-9 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and three turnovers in 18 minutes of Monday's 114-101 preseason win over the Jazz.
items.story: D'Angelo Russell was rested Monday, so the Mavericks opted to start Cooper Flagg at point guard. Hardy made the most of his limited run off the bench, but Ryan Nembhard, who is also vying for rotation minutes, played 26 minutes and had six points, 12 assists and five rebounds.

items.headline: Hardy produced 12 points (4-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 22 minutes of Monday's 106-89 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Mavericks coach Jason Kidd utilized 15 different players Monday, but it was Hardy who led the team in minutes played. Hardy is certainly not shy on the offensive end, and he seems determined to make his case for an early-season role in the absence of Kyrie Irving (knee).

items.headline: Hardy (ankle) is available for Friday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Hardy missed the Mavericks' last two games due to a right ankle sprain, but he's progressed enough in his recovery to play in Friday's interconference clash. Hardy averaged 12.1 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists over 18.8 minutes per game in his nine outings prior to his most recent injury.

items.headline: Hardy (ankle) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Hardy is in danger of missing his third straight outing due to a sprained right ankle. If the 22-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Max Christie and Brandon Williams are candidates for an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Hardy is out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers with a sprained right ankle.
items.story: Hardy will miss a second straight game Wednesday, and his next chance to return to play comes Friday against Toronto. The Mavericks have very little depth at point guard remaining at this stage of the season, leaving the team with Spencer Dinwiddie as their lone true floor general. Dinwiddie has been a hit-or-miss fantasy option, but he's averaged 16.4 points on 47.3 percent shooting from the field, 7.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 1.8 three-pointers in 33.9 minutes across his last 14 contests overall.

items.headline: Hardy (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Clippers, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: This is not surprising, as Hardy had to be helped off the court Friday after sustaining the injury late in the fourth quarter. His next chance to play will come against the Lakers on Wednesday, but it's unclear if the guard will be able to return to action before the end of the regular season.

items.headline: Hardy (leg) has been listed as doubtful for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Hardy is trending toward being sidelined for Saturday's matchup against the Clippers due to a sprained right ankle. If he's ultimately ruled out, Dallas will likely lean on Max Christie and Naji Marshall to pick up the slack off the bench in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Hardy (leg) registered 16 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, five assists and two steals in 29 minutes during Friday's 114-91 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Although Hardy began the day on the injury report, he logged 28 minutes with no adverse effects from his leg ailment. Spencer Dinwiddie's arrival has temporarily sidelined Hardy's aspirations to take over the lead role at point guard after the loss of Kyrie Irving (knee). However, he still plays a vital role on a depth chart that is thin in the backcourt.

items.headline: Hardy departed Friday's game against the Clippers in the latter stages of the fourth quarter due to an apparent leg injury, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Hardy had to be helped off the floor, and further tests will be needed to determine the severity of the injury. Hardy finished the game with 16 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, five assists and two steals across 29 minutes off the bench. He should be considered questionable for the second leg of the back-to-back set against the Clippers on Saturday. That said, his chances of playing should be very slim -- at best -- considering he had to be helped off the floor by his teammates and the medical staff.

items.headline: Hardy finished Thursday's 101-92 win over the Magic with 22 points (7-12 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT) and three rebounds over 20 minutes.
items.story: Hardy was one of several Dallas players who posted a solid line coming off the bench, and this 22-point output was his second-best output since the All-Star break. He's been on a solid run of play recently, scoring 15 or more points in three of his last five outings and averaging 13.0 points per game while shooting 52.2 percent from the floor in that span.

items.headline: Cain (shoulder) is available for Friday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Cain went through Friday's morning shootaround and is ready to go for game action. Now that Jalen Suggs (knee) is back in the lineup for the Magic, Cain's playing time could take a slight hit going forward.

items.headline: Cain (shoulder) participated in the Magic's morning shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: With Cain still carrying a questionable tag after shootaround and his availability still unsettled heading into Friday, his participation in morning practice is a step in the right direction. Cain is averaging 7.0 points on 19.5 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Cain (shoulder) is questionable for Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Cain was unable to go Wednesday against the Jazz due to a shoulder injury, but it appears as though he'll have a chance to return in time for Friday's clash. The team should have another update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Cain (shoulder) is out for Wednesday's game in Utah.
items.story: With Cain inactive, Alex Morales will draw the start, and there will be more minutes available for Jase Richardson. For now, Cain should be considered questionable for Friday's matchup with Milwaukee.

items.headline: Cain is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Jazz due to a left shoulder contusion.
items.story: With Tristan da Silva (calf) joining Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) on the sidelines, Cain started Tuesday against the Kings, posting five points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 20 minutes. Da Silva and Cain are questionable for the second night of a back-to-back set, so Jase Richardson and Jevon Carter could be candidates for increased roles if both questionable players are ruled out.

items.headline: Cain will start Tuesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: With Tristan da Silva (calf) joining Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) on the sidelines, Cain will enter the starting lineup for the second time this season. He posted 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 25 minutes during his first start Nov. 2.

items.headline: Cain registered five points (2-9 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT) and five rebounds in 25 minutes during Thursday's 117-104 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Cain struggled to find his shooting touch after scoring 10 points against Washington on Monday, missing five of his six attempts from beyond the arc. The 27-year-old has logged at least 24 minutes in consecutive games, benefiting from Orlando's depleted rotation with Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined. However, Cain's inconsistent scoring and limited contributions outside of rebounding make him a difficult fantasy option despite the increased playing time.

items.headline: Cain will come off the bench in Thursday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Cain drew a spot start Monday against Washington and took advantage by tacking on 10 points, three rebounds and one assist in 25 minutes. However, he'll return to a bench role due to Anthony Black returning from an ankle injury.

items.headline: Cain is starting Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Cain will step in for Anthony Black, who's sidelined Monday for rest purposes. Cain is averaging 8.0 points and 1.8 rebounds over his last four appearances.

items.headline: Cain amassed nine points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-5 FT), one rebound and two steals across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Cain made the most of his opportunities at the charity stripe, converting all five attempts while contributing a pair of steals. However, the reserve forward struggled from the field and offered little production elsewhere. His limited playing time makes him a difficult fantasy option outside of deeper leagues.

items.headline: Cain logged zero points (0-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt) over 14 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Cain received a modest opportunity off Orlando's bench but failed to make an impact, going scoreless without recording a rebound, assist, steal or block. He'll likely need to earn a larger role before becoming relevant outside the deepest fantasy formats.

items.headline: Cain posted 15 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), two rebounds and an assist across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 122-118 preseason win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: After a few late-season pops, Cain made a strong first impression this season with a great total off the bench. After spending most of last season on a two-way deal before converting to a standard contract in March, he's using the preseason to earn a spot in the regular rotation.

items.headline: The Magic exercised their 2026-27 team option for Cain on Monday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: This was a formality after Cain carved out a key role down the stretch of 2025-26, averaging 17.6 minutes during Orlando's playoff run. Look for him to compete for a rotation spot entering 2026-27 with momentum on his side.

items.headline: Cain notched five points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 24 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to Detroit in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: With both Franz Wagner (calf) and Jonathan Isaac (knee) sidelined, Cain was thrust into a significant role during the final stretch of Orlando's playoff run. Over 40 regular-season contests (one start), the fourth-year forward averaged 5.4 points, 2.0 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 12.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cain supplied five points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-7 FT), four rebounds and one assist in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 116-109 loss to the Pistons in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Cain was inserted into the starting lineup after Franz Wagner was ruled out due to a calf injury. However, despite the promotion, Cain was unable to elevate his production, continuing what has been a quiet series thus far. Through five games, he has averaged just 5.8 points and 3.2 rebounds.

items.headline: Cain will start Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons.
items.story: With Franz Wagner (calf) sidelined, Cain will draw his third career start. In his lone start during the 2025-26 regular season -- a loss to Cleveland on March 24 -- the 27-year-old forward posted 17 points, six rebounds and three assists across 32 minutes.

items.headline: Cain supplied eight points (4-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and nine rebounds in 24 minutes during Monday's 94-88 win over Detroit in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Cain had a strong showing off the bench and was all over the highlight reels for his monster slam over Jalen Duren. If Franz Wagner (calf) is forced to miss time, Cain looks like someone the Magic will lean on along with possibly Tristan da Silva.

items.headline: Cain totaled 20 points (9-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 25 minutes during Friday's 127-103 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Cain scored a season-high 20 points, albeit against an opponent that seemingly gave up before the game even started. Although Cain has been able to carve out a spot in the rotation, this performance should be viewed as more of an outlier, given that he had scored in single digits in the previous four games.

items.headline: Cain (calf) is available for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Cain exited Monday's win over the Pistons in the second quarter and did not return due to a left calf contusion. However, the 27-year-old forward will be back in action Wednesday. Over four appearances in April, he has averaged 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 21.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Cain (calf) is expected to play Wednesday against Minnesota, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Cain made it through shootaround and "should be good to go," according to coach Jamahl Mosley. Cain, who is listed as questionable, holds averages of 8.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.0 three-pointers in 19.6 minutes over his last seven outings.

items.headline: Cain is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota with a left calf contusion.
items.story: Cain left Monday's win over the Pistons in the second quarter with the injury and was unable to return. If his absence extends into Wednesday, Tristan da Silva could pick up a few extra minutes.

items.headline: Cain exited Monday's 123-107 win over the Pistons in the second quarter due to a left calf contusion and did not return, finishing with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 11 minutes.
items.story: Cain checked out with 8:29 remaining in the second quarter and never checked back in after being deemed doubtful to return. He can be considered questionable for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves until Orlando offers an update on his status.

items.headline: Cain is doubtful to return to Monday's game against the Pistons due to a left calf contusion, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
items.story: Cain logged just over 11 minutes before exiting due to the calf injury. If he's unable to return, he'll finish with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist.

items.headline: Cain totaled eight points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 21 minutes during Friday's 138-127 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Cain was coming off a strong 17-point showing Wednesday against the Hawks, but he was unable to replicate that type of offensive production Friday night. Still, he managed to contribute across the board, which included dishing out a season-high four assists. Cain is averaging 9.6 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists over his last five matchups, all off the bench.

items.headline: Cain isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Cain drew a spot start Tuesday against the Cavs and took full advantage, as he put up 17 points in 32 minutes. However, he'll retreat to his usual bench role Thursday with Jalen Suggs back from an illness.

items.headline: Cain finished Tuesday's 136-131 loss to the Cavaliers with 17 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds and three assists across 32 minutes.
items.story: Cain moved into the starting lineup, dropping a season-high 17 points, albeit in a losing effort. With both Jalen Suggs (illness) and Anthony Black (abdomen) sidelined yet again, Cain was given the starting nod for the first time this season, and certainly made the most of his opportunity. While we aren't running to add him, he is a name to watch, just in case this performance leads to an increased role moving forward.

items.headline: Cain is starting Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Cain will draw his first start of the season with both Jalen Suggs (illness) and Anthony Black (abdomen) sidelined for Tuesday's matchup. Cain has appeared in nine games off the bench in March and is averaging 6.4 points and 2.6 rebounds in 13.7 minutes.

items.headline: Cain agreed to a standard contract with the Magic on Friday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: After joining Orlando on a one-year, two-way deal in July, Cain has been upgraded to a standard contract and will be eligible to play in the postseason. The 27-year-old forward has averaged 3.5 points and 1.1 rebounds in 8.0 minutes per contest across 27 appearances this season. He has logged double-digit minutes in four straight games and could remain in the rotation in the short term while Franz Wagner (ankle), Anthony Black (abdomen) and Jonathan Isaac (knee) are sidelined.

items.headline: Cain provided two points (1-1 FG), three rebounds and one assist across 14 minutes during Monday's 124-112 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: After logging 19 minutes and producing 12 points, seven rebounds and one block in the Magic's previous game Saturday in Miami, Cain remained in the rotation for the second straight contest. The two-way player hasn't been a factor for the Magic for much of the season, but Cain appears to have at least temporarily gained the trust of head coach Jamahl Mosley. Cain could see his minor role in the rotation disappear once the likes of Anthony Black (abdomen) and Franz Wagner (ankle) return to action, however.

items.headline: Cain ended with one point (1-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across nine minutes during Tuesday's 144-103 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Cain remained in the rotation during the blowout win, logging minutes for the fourth time in the Magic's past five games. To this point, he has offered nothing in terms of tangible production, scoring a total of just eight points during that five-game span. He can safely be left on the waiver wire in all formats.

items.headline: The Magic signed Cain to a two-way contract Friday.
items.story: After not receiving a qualifying offer from the Pelicans, Cain became an unrestricted free agent, which ultimately led to him joining his new squad. He began his NBA career with the Heat before playing for New Orleans during the 2024-25 campaign. He's averaged 4.8 points and 2.1 rebounds while shooting 45.9 percent from the floor and 33.6 percent from beyond the arc across 81 regular-season games in three campaigns in the league.

items.headline: Cain posted 18 points (6-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 28 minutes during Sunday's 115-100 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Cain finished as New Orleans' second-leading scorer during Sunday's regular-season finale. The 26-year-old two-way player will be a restricted free agent during the offseason, and he finished the 2024-25 campaign with averages of 5.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.2 blocks across 13.6 minutes per game in 37 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Cain had 25 points (8-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 5-7 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and one steal in 35 minutes during Friday's 153-104 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Due to New Orleans dealing with a laundry list of injuries to end the 2024-25 season, Cain has begun to receive increased playing time. The 26-year-old forward recorded season highs in points (25) and minutes played (35) in Friday's blowout loss. For the first time this season, Cain has scored double-digit points in three straight outings.

items.headline: Cain recorded 20 points (6-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven rebounds and one steal in 27 minutes during Thursday's 136-111 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Cain erupted for a career-high 20 points in the loss, stepping up for a New Orleans team that was extremely shorthanded. The Pelicans could get some reinforcements back for the second leg of this back-to-back set, but Cain may have earned himself a longer look in the rotation in the final two games of the regular season.

items.headline: Cain logged 15 points (7-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt), three rebounds and two steals over 16 minutes during Tuesday's 119-114 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Cain emerged off the bench to provide instant offense, turning in 15 points in just 16 minutes of action. The 26-year-old has averaged 10.0 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 21.5 minutes across his past four games, and Cain could continue playing meaningful minutes from the second unit to close out a losing season for the Pelicans.

items.headline: Cain amassed 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and four steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 124-108 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: During his tenure with the Pelicans, Cain has been a non-factor, but he's one of a few developmental players who may see an extended run in the final week. After not catching on with the Heat, he's appeared in 32 games for New Orleans this season.

items.headline: Cain ended with five points (1-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across eight minutes during Saturday's 146-117 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Cain saw minutes for just the fourth time in the past 11 games, saddling up for eight minutes of garbage time. The Pelicans are focused on nothing but lottery balls, meaning Cain, along with a few others, could at least play a role down the stretch. With that said, it is unlikely to yield consistent production.

items.headline: Cain finished with three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt) in 10 minutes during Thursday's 124-116 win over the Suns.
items.story: Cain missed the Pelicans' final two games before the All-Star break due to an illness, but he was cleared to play when the team opened its second-half schedule Feb. 21 in Dallas. However, Cain didn't crack the rotation in that game or any of the Pelicans' subsequent two games before getting a chance to pick up some minutes Thursday. The Pelicans were without one of their key wings in Bruce Brown (rest), but with Brown expected back for the second leg of a back-to-back set Friday in Phoenix, Cain could move back out of the rotation.

items.headline: Cain (illness) is not on the injury report for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Cain is set to return following a two-game absence due to an illness. However, he hasn't been a regular member of the rotation even when healthy. The three-year forward has been limited to only 21 appearances off the bench this season while averaging 12.3 minutes per game, so his fantasy value is close to minimal.

items.headline: Cain (illness) is out for Thursday's game versus the Kings.
items.story: Cain will miss his second straight contest Thursday due to an illness. His next chance to suit up will come against Dallas on Feb. 21.

items.headline: Cain (illness) will not play against the Kings on Wednesday.
items.story: Cain has played a total of 24 minutes across two February appearances, so his absence won't carry many fantasy implications. His next chance to play comes Thursday in a rematch against the Kings.

items.headline: Cain (illness) is available to play Wednesday against Portland.
items.story: Cain will be returning from a one-game absence after missing Tuesday's game versus Minnesota. He hasn't seen the floor since Dec. 15, however, and he's not guaranteed any rotation minutes.

items.headline: Cain will not play Tuesday against Minnesota due to an illness.
items.story: Despite being healthy, Cain hasn't seen the floor for the Pelicans since Dec. 15, so his absence doesn't carry many fantasy implications. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against Portland.

items.headline: Braun racked up 21 points (8-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal in 38 minutes during Sunday's 151-145 overtime victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Braun has averaged 16.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.6 steals and 33.0 minutes over his last five games. His improved perimeter shooting and defensive production have strengthened his fantasy value, while consistent minutes provide a reliable floor.

items.headline: Braun contributed 19 points (7-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one block and four steals over 31 minutes during Friday's 133-124 victory over the Rockets.
