However, he'll now miss his 10th outing overall as he deals with soreness in his right knee. Prince's absence shouldn't have an impact on the rotation, and his next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus New Orleans.

items.headline: Prince supplied three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and two steals over seven minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Prince made his first appearance of the regular season after missing Detroit's previous three games. The veteran forward connected on one three-pointer and recorded two steals but failed to register a rebound or assist. His limited playing time suggests he will primarily serve as depth in Detroit's rotation, leaving him without meaningful fantasy value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Prince (personal) is available for Friday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Prince is back with the team after attending to a personal matter. The veteran forward is ready to make his Pistons debut, though his role is uncertain.

items.headline: Prince (personal) is listed as probable for Friday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Prince missed Tuesday's season-opening win over Boston while attending to a personal matter, though he's trending in the right direction for Friday's contest. The veteran forward isn't guaranteed to play a meaningful role when he returns to action.

items.headline: Prince (personal) is out for Tuesday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Prince was previously carrying a questionable tag and will now miss Opening Night. The veteran is expected to be an emergency depth option this season.

items.headline: Prince (personal) is questionable for Tuesday's season opening game against the Celtics.
items.story: Prince might not be able to join the Pistons while attending to a personal matter. The veteran forward may not play meaningful minutes even if he's available, though.

items.headline: The Bucks traded Prince and Gary Harris (groin) to the Pistons on Tuesday in exchange for Caris LeVert and two second-round picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Bucks have entered a rebuild after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Bobby Portis to Miami, so they'll send Harris and Prince to the Pistons to acquire LeVert and draft compensation. Prince spent the last two seasons with the Bucks, though he appeared in just 26 regular-season games (seven starts) in 2025-26, as he missed significant time after undergoing surgery to address a herniated disc in his neck Nov. 13. The veteran forward is a career 38.7 percent shooter from beyond the arc and figures to provide wing depth for Detroit.

items.headline: Prince exercised his $3.82 million player option Monday for the 2026-27 campaign, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Prince is set to return to Milwaukee and will serve as a veteran presence for the rebuilding club. The 32-year-old forward appeared in just 26 regular-season games (seven starts) last season, missing significant time after undergoing surgery to address a herniated disc in his neck Nov. 13. He averaged 9.2 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.8 assists while shooting 43.6 percent from beyond the arc in 23.5 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Prince amassed 14 points (5-14 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 32 minutes during Sunday's 126-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: A neck injury robbed Prince of a huge chunk of the season, limiting him to 26 regular-season contests. He averaged 23.5 minutes per game to go with 9.2 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.6 steals and 2.3 three-pointers on 45.0 percent shooting from the field. Prince holds a $3.82 million player option for 2026-27.

items.headline: Prince notched 16 points (6-15 FG, 4-12 3Pt), 11 rebounds, four assists and one block over 37 minutes during Tuesday's 96-90 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Prince needed 15 shots to score 16 points, but he continued his strong play and has surpassed the 15-point mark in three straight games, including in five of the Bucks' last seven. Prince is one of several role players who are benefiting from an uptick in playing time in the final days of the regular season. Over that aforementioned seven-game stretch, Prince is averaging 13.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game while shooting 44.2 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Prince will start Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: With Ryan Rollins (hip) joining an extensive list of Bucks players on the inactive list, Prince will get the starting nod in the front end of this back-to-back. The veteran forward has averaged 7.0 points and 3.3 rebounds in 21.7 minutes per contest across three starts this season.

items.headline: Prince amassed 18 points (7-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt), two assists, one block and one steal across 25 minutes off the bench during Friday's 133-101 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: With Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee), Kevin Porter (knee), Ryan Rollins (hip) and other Milwaukee players unavailable, Prince wound up being the leading scorer for the shorthanded squad as he tied his season high in points. The veteran wing has scored in double digits in three of his last five games, all with the second unit, and Prince is averaging 12.0 points, 3.4 boards, 3.2 assists, 2.8 threes and 0.8 steals in 28.0 minutes during that span.

items.headline: Prince (neck) is off the injury report for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: After sitting out Wednesday's loss to Houston, Prince is ready to roll for Friday. The veteran swingman has averaged 9.1 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 24.2 minutes per contest in his last nine games.

items.headline: Prince (neck) is out for Wednesday's game against Houston.
items.story: The veteran forward will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. With this news, AJ Green and Gary Trent are likely to see increased reps.

items.headline: Prince produced 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-7 3Pt), six rebounds, eight assists, one block and two steals over 38 minutes during Sunday's 127-113 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: It was easily Prince's finest effort since coming back from midseason neck surgery and perhaps of the entire season, as the 18 points and eight dimes were both season bests. The Bucks were missing each of Ryan Rollins (hip), Kevin Porter (knee), Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee), Bobby Portis (wrist) and Myles Turner (knee) on Sunday, so Prince's usage is going to take a hit once some of those names re-enter the fold.

items.headline: Prince will come off the bench for Wednesday's game in Portland.
items.story: AJ Green will replace Prince in the first unit for Wednesday's game. As a reserve this season, Prince owns averages of 5.8 points and 1.5 triples per contest.

items.headline: Prince contributed eight points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist over 22 minutes during Saturday's 108-105 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Prince was given the starting nod for just the second time this season, highlighting just how desperate things are in Milwaukee at the moment. Having played seven games since returning from injury, Prince has offered very little on paper. In 18.3 minutes per game during that time, he has averaged just 6.1 points and 1.6 three-pointers.

items.headline: Prince is part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Prince will make his second start of the season, stepping in to replace AJ Green. In his only appearance as a starter, Prince posted eight points, two rebounds and one assist across 23 minutes.

items.headline: Prince will come off the bench for Thursday's game in Utah.
items.story: Ousmane Dieng will replace Prince in the first unit for Thursday's game. As a reserve this season, Prince owns averages of 5.8 points and 1.4 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Prince will start Tuesday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: With Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) sidelined, Kyle Kuzma will start at power forward while Prince draws the start at small forward. The 31-year-old has appeared in four outings this month, during which he has averaged 5.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 16.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Prince notched 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 22 minutes during Sunday's 134-123 win over the Pacers.
items.story: This was a positive step for Prince as he continues to shake off the rust. He had been held scoreless in two of his previous three contests since returning to action March 10. If his minutes continue to trend up, Prince will soon find himself on the fantasy radar in deeper formats.

items.headline: Prince produced zero points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and three rebounds in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 129-114 loss to the Suns.
items.story: This was Prince's first action since he underwent surgery Nov. 13 to address a herniated disc in his neck, and he understandably had some rust. Prince does have a solid path to minutes in Milwaukee, making him worth monitoring in deeper leagues as he ramps up.

items.headline: Head coach Doc Rivers said Prince (neck) will be available for Tuesday's game against the Suns, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Prince underwent surgery Nov. 13 to address a herniated disc in his neck and hasn't played since Nov. 4. He's set to return Tuesday, though it wouldn't be surprising to see him operate on a strict minutes restriction following the extended absence. He'll likely compete with Kyle Kuzma and Gary Trent for playing time as he is eased back into action.

items.headline: Prince (neck) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Suns, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Bucks had previously hinted that Prince may not be able to return for the remainder of the 2025-26 season after undergoing surgery to repair a herniated disc in his neck. However, Prince's questionable tag for Tuesday says otherwise, as it appears he's excelled in his rehab and is nearing a return to game action. If the veteran forward is cleared to play Tuesday, expect Milwaukee to deploy him with caution off the bench after not playing since Nov. 4 against Toronto.

items.headline: The Bucks applied for a Disabled Player Exception for Prince earlier this month, indicating that they anticipate that he's "substantially more likely than not" to be unable to play through June 15, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Milwaukee labeled Prince as out indefinitely after he underwent surgery Nov. 13 to address a herniated disc in his neck. Approximately six weeks later, the Bucks haven't yet offered a more official timeline for Prince's return, but the team's decision to apply for a DPE implies that he's effectively being viewed as out for the season. Ultimately, an NBA-designated physician would need to concur with the Bucks' assessment that Prince is unlikely to return before June 15 in order for Milwaukee to be granted a DPE, which would enable the team to sign a player to a one-year deal worth about $1.7 million -- half of Prince's salary -- or less. Before being shut down after undergoing surgery, Prince had appeared in the Bucks' first eight games of the season and averaged 6.1 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers, 1.0 assists and 0.8 steals in 21.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Prince underwent surgery Thursday to repair the herniated disc in his neck and will remain out indefinitely.
items.story: The Bucks released an update Monday noting that the forward is in line for a significant absence, so this latest report doesn't provide much in terms of a timetable for his return. The team should release updates on Prince's status as he begins to clear hurdles in his rehab.

items.headline: Prince is expected to miss a "significant period of time" after he was diagnosed Monday with a herniated disc in his neck, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Before missing Milwaukee's last two games due to the injury, Prince had been a key bench player for the Bucks, averaging 6.1 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers and 1.0 assists in 21.0 minutes over his first eight appearances of the season. A clearer timeline for Prince's return should be established once he's able to resume on-court work, but he can be considered as week-to-week for now. His absence likely won't have many fantasy implications, though it could open up a few extra minutes for reserves such as Kyle Kuzma, Bobby Portis, Amir Coffey and Cole Anthony.

items.headline: Prince (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Rockets.
items.story: Sunday will mark Prince's second straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's game in Dallas. Prince's minutes will likely be divvied up amongst Kyle Kuzma, Bobby Portis and Amir Coffey.

items.headline: Prince (neck) will not play Friday against the Bulls.
items.story: Prince was unable to shed his questionable tag and will miss his first game of the campaign. With Prince sidelined, the Bucks could use a committee approach to soak up his minutes with guys like Kyle Kuzma, Cole Anthony and Amir Coffey getting some extra run.

items.headline: Prince is questionable for Friday's game against the Bulls due to a neck strain.
items.story: Prince is in jeopardy of missing his first game of the season. The veteran forward has played a strict reserve role so far, although Prince's absence would free up some extra minutes for Kyle Kuzma off the bench.

items.headline: Prince provided zero points (0-5 FG, 0-5 3Pt) and one assist across 21 minutes during Tuesday's 128-100 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Prince was unable to make any of his shot attempts, and the lone stat he recorded was an assist in 21 minutes of action. Tuesday marked Prince's first scoreless outing of the season, so hopefully he is able to get back on track Friday against the Bulls.

items.headline: Prince chipped in eight points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and one block in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 121-111 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Prince's low workloads could hold him back, but he's quietly off to a great start to the campaign. Through four games, he's on pace for 10th-round value in nine-category formats with averages of 7.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.3 steals, 0.5 blocks and 2.0 three-pointers on 57.9 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Prince scored three points (1-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and added three rebounds, three assists and a steal over 21 minutes in Friday's 122-116 win over Toronto.
items.story: Prince was unable to follow up Wednesday's performance, making just one field goal. His value is largely dependent on how efficient he is from the field, which does not deem him a consistent fantasy option at the moment.

items.headline: Prince finished Wednesday's 133-120 victory over the Wizards with 11 points (4-5 FG, 3-4 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one steal across 22 minutes.
items.story: Bucks head coach Doc Rivers is going to bring Prince off the bench this season, but he's likely to be a key member of the second unit with minutes in the low-to-mid 20s. Prince is typically a low-usage player who can chip in with some points, three-pointers, rebounds and steals, but his fantasy appeal is likely to be limited to very deep leagues in his new role.

items.headline: Prince agreed to a two-year, $7.1 million contract with Milwaukee on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Prince signed a one-year deal with the Bucks last offseason and started 73 of his 80 regular-season appearances, averaging 8.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 steals in 27.1 minutes while shooting a career-best 43.9 percent from beyond the arc. Milwaukee will retain the 31-year-old's services for at least one more season, as he'll have a player option for the 2026-27 season, per Charania. Prince should be one of the top players off the bench if he doesn't crack the starting five.

items.headline: Prince produced zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one block across four minutes during Tuesday's 119-118 overtime loss to the Pacers in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Prince was moved to the bench in Game 3 of this series and saw his role steadily decline in favor of Gary Trent. Prince was relied upon heavily across 80 regular-season games, averaging 8.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.8 three-pointers. The 31-year-old forward should have plenty of suitors once he hits free agency this offseason as a reliable role player.

items.headline: Prince is not in the starting lineup for Game 3 against the Pacers on Friday.
items.story: The Bucks are tweaking their lineup for Game 3 and Prince will move to the bench since Gary Trent will be promoted to the first unit. Prince registered six points (2-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four assists and two steals across 19 minutes during Tuesday's 123-115 loss to the Pacers in Game 2.

items.headline: Prince registered six points (2-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four assists and two steals across 19 minutes during Tuesday's 123-115 loss to the Pacers in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Prince has seen a reduced role through the opening two games of this series. He's averaging 19.5 minutes per contest with 3.0 points, 3.5 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers on a combined 2-of-5 shooting from the field. At Prince's expense, the Bucks have been relying heavily on Bobby Portis and Gary Trent in the second unit.

items.headline: Prince (knee) isn't listed on the Bucks' injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Pacers.
items.story: Prince missed the club's regular-season finale due to a knee injury, though he's slated to return to game action Saturday. The veteran forward has averaged 7.0 points, 3.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.4 steals across 27.8 minutes per game in his last five outings.

items.headline: Prince (knee), who missed Sunday's regular-season finale against Detroit, is expected to be available for Saturday's Game 1 against the Pacers.
items.story: Prince has played a key role for the Bucks this season and is expected to retain his starting spot in the backcourt next to Ryan Rollins due to Damian Lillard's (calf) ongoing absence. Across 80 appearances in the regular season, Prince averaged 8.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.8 three-pointers in 27.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Prince (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: As expected, Prince will be sidelined for Sunday's regular-season finale as he gets additional rest ahead of the Bucks' postseason run. Andre Jackson and Pat Connaughton should get extended run due to Prince's absence.

items.headline: Prince is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game versus the Pistons due to right knee patella tendinopathy.
items.story: Prince is expected to sit out Sunday's regular-season finale alongside many of Milwaukee's other regulars. If Prince is ultimately downgraded to out, Pat Connaughton and Andre Jackson should receive increased playing time.

items.headline: Carlson finished with six points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound across 14 minutes during Tuesday's 106-105 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Carlson has logged at least 14 minutes in consecutive games after averaging just 9.5 minutes over his previous four appearances. The reserve center has scored at least five points in three straight contests, but his limited rebounding production and crowded Portland frontcourt continue to restrict his fantasy upside. Carlson remains a low-priority option outside deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Carlson ended Monday's 106-98 loss to the Timberwolves with five points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 14 minutes.
items.story: Carlson saw the floor for a fifth straight outing, providing a boost on the glass while leading the second unit in rebounds. The big man has logged double-digit minutes in three of the last five games, averaging 3.2 points, 3.6 rebounds and 0.6 blocks in 10.4 minutes per tilt over that stretch.

items.headline: Carlson recorded two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 12 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Carlson saw his first minutes as a member of the Trail Blazers after missing the start of the season due to a concussion. With Robert Williams (knee) given the night off, Carlson assumed the role of backup behind Donovan Clingan, although he didn't offer much outside of his two blocked shots. Given that Williams could return as soon as Saturday against Utah, there is no reason to consider Carlson outside of very deep formats.

items.headline: Carlson (concussion) is available for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Carlson is available to make his regular-season debut with Portland after missing the team's first two regular-season games while in the league's concussion protocol. However, he isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

items.headline: Carlson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Carlson is trending in the right direction after missing Portland's first two regular-season games while in the league's concussion protocol. His potential return likely wouldn't impact the rotation.

items.headline: Carlson (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Carlson is still in the league's concussion protocol and will remain on the inactive list for a second consecutive contest to begin the regular season. The big man's next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Lakers.

items.headline: Carlson (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Carlson will miss the Trail Blazers' regular-season opener while in the league's concussion protocol. His next chance to make his regular-season debut with the club will come Friday in Sacramento.

items.headline: Carlson signed a one-year, $2.5 million contract with the Trail Blazers on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Carlson spent the first two years of his career in the Thunder organization, making four starts across 74 regular-season appearances. He averaged 5.8 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.6 blocks in 11.6 minutes per game in 2025-26, and he will add depth at the center position for Portland. He's not expected to be a major factor in most fantasy formats, however, as he'll probably compete with Yang Hansen and Sidy Cissoko for the third-string center role behind Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams.

items.headline: Carlson is not in the Thunder's starting lineup for Sunday's Game 1 of their Western Conference first-round series on Sunday, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
items.story: Carlson started in the Thunder's final two games of the regular season and averaged 24.5 points, 11.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 3.0 blocks and 1.0 steals over 39.5 minutes per game. He'll revert to the bench for the Thunder's playoff opener, and he's unlikely to see much playing time in the postseason outside of garbage time.

items.headline: Carlson totaled 26 points (10-20 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, five blocks, two steals and one assist over 42 minutes during Sunday's 135-103 loss to the Suns.
items.story: With Isaiah Hartenstein (calf) and Jaylin Williams (Achilles) inactive, Carlson started his second consecutive game and excelled, recording his second double-double in as many outings. It marked season-best totals for the Utah product in points, blocks and three-pointers made. He'll close the regular season averaging 5.8 points and 3.0 rebounds in 11.6 minutes across 42 appearances (four starts).

items.headline: Carlson supplied 23 points (8-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 12 rebounds, five assists and one block in 37 minutes during Friday's 127-107 loss to Denver.
items.story: Carlson moved into the starting lineup for the third time this season, recording his third career double-double. If we rewind almost 12 months to the day, Carlson amassed his first double-double, finding himself in basically an identical situation. With Oklahoma City once again guaranteed the top seed in the Western Conference, it wouldn't be surprising to see Carlson playing big minutes again during Sunday's season finale.

items.headline: Carlson will start in Friday's game against Denver, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
items.story: With Chet Holmgren (back), Isaiah Hartenstein (calf) and Jaylin Williams (Achilles) ruled out, Carlson will enter the starting lineup. In two starts this season, the 26-year-old has averaged 8.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.5 steals across 20.5 minutes of work.

items.headline: Carlson (back) recorded zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound while playing the final 1:50 of Monday's 123-103 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Carlson was cleared to play after missing the Thunder's previous 11 games due to a low back strain, but the second-year center wasn't part of the rotation while the contest was competitive. With the Thunder at full strength in the frontcourt, Carlson's opportunities are likely to be limited to garbage-time scenarios for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Carlson (back) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Monday's game in Philadelphia.
items.story: While Carlson will be available for Monday's game, so will the rest of the Thunder centers, so there are no guarantees he'll be able to find minutes in the rotation. In 35 appearances for the Thunder this season, the second-year center has averaged 4.9 points and 2.6 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Carlson (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Washington.
items.story: Carlson will miss an 11th consecutive contest due to a lower-back strain, and he remains without a clear timetable for a return. He can be considered doubtful for Monday's game against the 76ers until Oklahoma City provides an update on his status.

items.headline: Carlson (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Carlson will miss a 10th consecutive contest due to a back strain. The second-year big man appears to have no timetable for a return, but his next chance to play comes Saturday in Washington against the Wizards.

items.headline: Carlson (back) is out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Carlson will miss a ninth consecutive game due to a back strain. The second-year big man looks to be out indefinitely, but his next chance to play comes Wednesday against the Nets in Brooklyn.

items.headline: Carlson (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Carlson will miss an eighth consecutive game due to a back strain. He doesn't have a concrete date to return to action, but the big man has a minor role in the rotation, so his absence shouldn't affect many fantasy decisions. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Magic.

items.headline: Carlson (back) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Carlson has been ruled out for a seventh straight game due to a back strain. With Isaiah Hartenstein (calf) also out, look for Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams to aid Chet Holmgren at the center position. Carlson's next chance to play will come Sunday against Minnesota.

items.headline: Carlson (back) is out for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Carlson will be inactive for a sixth consecutive game as he nurses a back injury. His absence potentially leaves Jaylin Williams and Kenrich Williams as the only active players to play the five spot for Monday's contest, as Chet Holmgren (illness, questionable) and Isaiah Hartenstein (calf, out) could both be unavailable as well.

items.headline: Carlson (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: This will be the fifth consecutive game on the inactive list for Carlson, and it's not encouraging that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff. For now, he should be viewed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Carlson (back) remains out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Oklahoma City's third-string center will be sidelined for a fourth straight game. His next chance to play comes Saturday against Golden State.

items.headline: Carlson (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Carlson will miss a third consecutive game due to a lower-back strain that flared up and forced him to exit early against the Pistons on Feb. 25. The Utah product is averaging 10.7 minutes per contest across 35 appearances with the Thunder this season, so his absence shouldn't significantly impact the rotation. The center's next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Carlson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Mavericks due to a lower-back strain.
items.story: Carlson will miss a second consecutive contest after exiting Wednesday's loss to the Pistons due to lower-back soreness. The second-year center has struggled with back issues of late, as he also missed the final game before the All-Star break due to back spasms. His absence shouldn't cause any waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Carlson (back) is out for Friday's game against the Nuggets, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
items.story: Carlson exited Wednesday's game against Detroit due to low back soreness, and the issue is significant enough to keep him from taking the floor Friday. His next opportunity to play will arrive Sunday in Dallas.

items.headline: Carlson won't return to Wednesday's game against the Pistons due to low back soreness, Nick Crain of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Carlson tweaked his back during the first quarter and will end the game with four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists in four minutes. The second-year center previously missed the Thunder's final game before the All-Star break due to a similar injury, but he was available for each of Oklahoma City's first three contests of the second half.

items.headline: Carlson (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Carlson missed Oklahoma City's final game before the All-Star break due to lower-back spasms but is set to return Friday. The two-way player has appeared in just one game this month and isn't guaranteed to see the floor Friday.

items.headline: Carlson is out for Thursday's game against the Bucks due to lower-back spasms.
items.story: Carlson has eight days to rest up before the Feb. 20 matchup against the Nets. His absence should have a negligible impact on the Oklahoma City rotation Thursday, though.

items.headline: Carlson is not in the Thunder's starting lineup against the Heat on Sunday, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
items.story: Carlson drew the start Friday against the Grizzlies and finished with five points, one rebound, one block and one steal over 16 minutes in a 117-116 victory. He will revert to a bench role Sunday after Chet Holmgren (shin) was cleared to return.

items.headline: Carlson is in the Thunder's starting lineup against the Grizzlies on Friday, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
items.story: Carlson will draw the start Friday due to the absences of Chet Holmgren (lower leg), Isaiah Hartenstein (soleus) and Jaylin Williams (heel). It'll be Carlson's second start of the season, with his first taking place Dec. 22 against Memphis, when he logged 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists over 25 minutes.

items.headline: Carlson ended with 15 points (6-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and two steals in 22 minutes off the bench during Friday's 131-94 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: The Thunder gave their starters the fourth quarter off in the rout, allowing Carlson and other members of the second unit to get extra run. The 26-year-old center cashed in the opportunity and produced his first double-double of the season. Carlson has seen at least 20 minutes of court time in five of OKC's last 13 games, all in contests the defending champs won by 16 or more points, and in those appearances he's averaging 12.0 points, 6.6 boards, 2.0 threes and 1.6 assists.

items.headline: Carlson had 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one block in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 124-95 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Carlson saw some decent run at center in the absences of both Isaiah Hartenstein (calf) and Jaylin Williams (heel) on Wednesday. His role hinges largely upon the availability of Oklahoma City's key players, which will be something to monitor on the Thunder's injury report prior to Friday's clash in Golden State.

items.headline: Carlson produced one assist in two minutes during Tuesday's 130-110 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Carlson barely touched the floor Tuesday, with his role severely impacted by the return of both Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. While Carlson has shown some promise to begin his career, it appears as though he is a long way from being considered a viable fantasy asset outside of dynasty formats.

items.headline: Carlson won't start against the Spurs on Tuesday, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
items.story: With the Thunder's regular starting five back at full strength, Carlson will move back to the second unit. While he could see the floor due to Jaylin Williams (heel) remaining sidelined, Carlson is not guaranteed significant playing time.

items.headline: Carlson is starting Monday's game against the Grizzlies, Rylan Stiles of SI.com reports.
items.story: Carlson will get his first crack with the first unit due to the absences of Isaiah Hartenstein (calf), Chet Holmgren (illness) and Jaylin Williams (heel). Carlson is averaging 4.9 points and 2.3 rebounds in 10.3 minutes over 18 appearances this season but should be in store for more chances to make an impact Monday night.

items.headline: Carlson finished Sunday's 131-101 victory over Utah with 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds and one block across 24 minutes off the bench.
items.story: Two straight blowout wins, as well as the continued absence of Isaiah Hartenstein (calf), have allowed Carlson to play more than 20 minutes in back-to-back games for the first time this season, and he responded with a solid performance Sunday. The Thunder might be headed for a more competitive contest Wednesday against the Suns, but as long as Hartenstein remains sidelined, Carlson could have some appeal as a DFS punt play.

items.headline: Carlson supplied seven points (2-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 11 minutes during Monday's 126-109 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Carlson hasn't been utilized that much as Oklahoma City's third-string center. Across 10 regular-season appearances, he's averaging 3.2 points, 2.1 rebounds, 0.5 assists and 0.6 blocks in 8.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Carlson ended with 11 points (5-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt), five rebounds and one assist in 20 minutes during Sunday's 137-106 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Sunday marked Carlson's fourth time reaching double digits in scoring in his career, and the reason for his extended playing time was due to Chet Holmgren (back) being ruled out and Ousmane Dieng (calf) leaving the game early. If these respective injuries persist for Holmgren and Dieng, Carlson may find himself in a role as the backup big man to Isaiah Hartenstein and Jaylin Williams.

items.headline: Carlson (calf) contributed 17 points (4-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 6-8 FT) and nine rebounds across 24 minutes in Tuesday's 116-112 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: Carlson returned from a three-game absence and led the Thunder's second unit in scoring against Milwaukee. The big man also finished as the team's second-leading rebounder. Carlson is on a two-way contract and is likely to spend most of his time with the G League's Oklahoma City Blue in the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Carlson (calf) didn't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Pacers.
items.story: Carlson continues to nurse a calf injury, which has kept him sidelined during the preseason. The next opportunity for him to suit up will be Tuesday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Carlson (calf) didn't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Hornets.
items.story: Carlson has now missed back-to-back preseason matchups while tending to a right calf issue. His next chance to take the court will come Saturday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Carlson won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Mavericks due to right calf soreness, Rylan Stiles of SI.com reports.
items.story: Carlson will miss the second half of the club's back-to-back set due to the calf issue, and his next chance to play will come in Thursday's preseason game against the Hornets. The 26-year-old center posted seven points (3-8 FG, 1-6 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across 11 minutes in Monday's win over Charlotte.

items.headline: Carlson closed with 12 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two assists across 24 minutes in Saturday's 109-80 Summer League loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Carlson delivered a solid showing Thursday despite his team shooting just 31.8 percent from the field. He logged significant minutes throughout Summer League and re-signed with the Thunder on a two-way contract July 8.

items.headline: Shannon notched 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and five assists across 24 minutes during Monday's 142-116 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Shannon has scored in double figures in four straight appearances, averaging 13.5 points, 3.5 assists and 23.8 minutes during that stretch. His improving offensive consistency is encouraging, though his limited defensive contributions and reserve role restrict his standard-league appeal.

items.headline: Shannon chipped in 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Shannon scored in double digits for the fifth straight game, continuing to provide Minnesota with valuable offensive contributions off the bench. However, while the scoring has been serviceable, a lack of supporting stats shouldn't be overlooked. In his past five games, he has averaged just 3.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 three-pointers to go with his 17.0 points per game.

items.headline: Shannon had 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 21 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Shannon provided a spark off the bench Thursday, leading the second unit in points and assists. The third-year wing has scored in double figures in four consecutive contests, averaging 17.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 25.5 minutes per tilt during that time.

items.headline: Shannon totaled 12 points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound and four assists over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 106-105 win over Portland.
items.story: Shannon has scored in double figures in three consecutive appearances, averaging 20.0 points, 3.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists during that stretch. The third-year guard has averaged 27 minutes over those contests, establishing himself as a productive contributor in Minnesota's rotation. His increased offensive involvement gives him growing fantasy appeal, particularly while Anthony Edwards remains sidelined.

items.headline: Shannon collected 34 points (8-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 15-16 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal in 35 minutes during Monday's 106-98 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Shannon delivered the best scoring performance of his young NBA career Monday by getting to the free-throw line with ease. He scored 15 of his 34 points from the charity stripe and shot the basketball with efficiency from the field to help his club secure a victory. Shannon also did damage as a playmaker, leading the team with six assists. The 26-year old is unlikely to put together this type of line on a nightly basis, but he's scored in double figures in eight of 11 appearances so far this season and continues to show signs of improvement.

items.headline: Shannon recorded five points (1-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 18 minutes during Sunday's 115-100 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Shannon returned from a three-game absence with a hip injury, though he continues to struggle for consistency. He's been a pretty big disappointment overall since Anthony Edwards (knee) went down, logging 20 minutes or fewer in three straight appearances.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Shannon missed the last three games because of a hip injury, though he will return for the meeting with the Jazz. The 26-year-old has played well throughout the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 12.0 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists (all career highs) over 22.0 minutes per contest in seven regular-season appearances. With Shannon back on the floor, it could mean fewer minutes for Jaylen Clark, Cody Williams and Trey Lyles.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Shannon's absence will leave Minnesota a bit shorthanded on the wing. His limited role makes the absence unlikely to have a significant fantasy impact, though the Timberwolves could distribute his available minutes among their remaining perimeter players.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) is questionable for Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Shannon is in danger of missing a third straight game while tending to a bruised left hip. He'll presumably need to prove his health during shootaround and warmups to gain clearance to play Friday night.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) is out for Wednesday against the Rockets.
items.story: Shannon was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. He's having an excellent season off the bench for Minnesota, and his absence opens the door for players such as Bones Hyland, Isaiah Evans and Jaylen Clark.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game in Houston.
items.story: Shannon didn't play in Monday's 112-100 win over Milwaukee. The 26-year-old is having the best season of his career, averaging 12.0 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists over 22.0 minutes per contest, so being without him once again would be a tough blow for the Timberwolves. If Shannon misses his second consecutive game, Cody Williams, Trey Lyles and Jaylen Clark could each see more minutes.

items.headline: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Shannon will miss his first game of the season due to a left hip contusion, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against Houston. With the 26-year-old swingman joining Anthony Edwards (knee) on the inactive list, more minutes will be available for guys like Ayo Dosunmu, Isaiah Evans and Jaylen Clark.

items.headline: Shannon has a left hip contusion and is questionable to face the Bucks on Monday.
items.story: Shannon could join Anthony Edwards (knee) on the sidelines, potentially leaving Minnesota thin on the wing. His absence would create additional opportunities for the Timberwolves' remaining perimeter players such as Bones Hyland and Ayo Dosunmu.

items.headline: Shannon's contract option for next season has been exercised by Minnesota, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
items.story: This is an expected move after Minnesota drafted Shannon in the first round in 2024. Shannon is being forced into an expanded role in the absence of Anthony Edwards (knee).

items.headline: Shannon closed with 15 points (5-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Shannon made the most of what ended up being a blowout win, scoring double digits for the third straight game to begin the season. In three appearances, he has averaged 12.7 points and 2.3 three-pointers, providing Minnesota with worthwhile contributions. Anyone in deeper formats could do worse, given the fact that his role appears relatively secure.

items.headline: Shannon will come off the bench in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Shannon started in Minnesota's preseason finale with the main guys resting, but he'll shift to a reserve role Wednesday with the regular starters healthy. As a reserve last season, Shannon averaged 5.0 points in 11.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Shannon will start Friday's preseason meeting with the Bulls.
items.story: The Timberwolves will rest their usual starting five, opening the door for Shannon to enter the first unit. He'll be joined in the starting lineup by Zyon Pullin, Jaylen Clark, Cody Williams and Joan Beringer.

items.headline: Shannon (undisclosed) contributed five points (1-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 18 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Shannon returned from a one-game absence and saw significant minutes as a reserve but struggled to make much of an impact. After averaging 5.6 points and 1.1 rebounds in 12.5 minutes across 43 regular-season appearances last season, the wing will look to carve out a consistent role off the bench during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Shannon (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Knicks.
items.story: Shannon will be unavailable at Madison Square Garden after starting Saturday against the Heat. Across three preseason games, the wing is averaging 11.3 points, 3.3 assists and 2.7 rebounds in 18.5 minutes per contest. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Shannon recorded 19 points (8-16 FG, 3-6 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 22 minutes during Saturday's 125-124 preseason win over the Heat.
items.story: The Timberwolves rested their projected starting five and Ayo Dosunmu on Saturday, opening the door for Shannon to enter the first unit. The 26-year-old swingman delivered a productive performance, finishing as Minnesota's third-leading scorer while tying for second on the team in assists. He's in line for a steady role off the bench to begin the regular season.

items.headline: Shannon will start in Saturday's preseason game against the Heat.
items.story: Shannon is getting the start with Anthony Edwards (rest) taking the night off. In two starts last season, Shannon averaged 17.0 points and 4.0 assists per contest.

items.headline: Shannon faces additional competition for playing time following Minnesota's agreement with Jonathan Kuminga.
items.story: Shannon currently sits second behind Anthony Edwards at shooting guard while providing depth at both forward spots, but Kuminga's expected place in the starting five further crowds Minnesota's wing rotation. Shannon should still have an opportunity to earn a reserve role, though he'll be competing with Ayo Dosunmu, Jaylen Clark and others for minutes behind the starters.

items.headline: Shannon notched 21 points (8-15 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 22 minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to the Spurs in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Shannon shed a questionable tag due to a head contusion to suit up Friday, and he delivered a bounce-back performance after shooting 0-for-5 from the field in Tuesday's Game 5 loss. The second-year swingman finished as Minnesota's second-leading scorer while pacing the bench in points. The 25-year-old saw increased burn in the playoffs after Donte DiVincenzo ruptured his Achilles, and with the latter likely to miss most, if not all, of the 2026-27 campaign, Shannon could be in line for a more sizable role depending on what moves the Timberwolves make this summer. He averaged 5.6 points and 1.1 rebounds across 12.5 minutes per game in 43 regular-season outings (two starts), though Shannon certainly flashed his potential during the postseason.

items.headline: Shannon (head) is available for Friday's Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals versus San Antonio.
items.story: Shannon appeared on the injury report because of a head contusion. However, the injury won't keep him off the floor for Friday's must-win clash against the Spurs. The 25-year-old has averaged 8.6 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.0 assists across 25.0 minutes during this series. Shannon's presence will likely result in less opportunity for Mike Conley and Bones Hyland.

items.headline: Shannon (head) is questionable for Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Friday.
items.story: Shannon is a late addition to the injury report with a head contusion. Mike Conley would appear to be the primary beneficiary from a fantasy perspective if Shannon, who's logged at least 20 minutes in five of Minnesota's last six contests, is unable to play Friday.

items.headline: Shannon will come off the bench in Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Friday.
items.story: Anthony Edwards will replace Shannon in the first unit for Friday's game, and Shannon's minutes figure to dip with the demotion. In two games off the bench this postseason, Shannon has averaged 9.0 points and 1.5 three-pointers in 10.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Shannon finished Monday's 104-102 victory over the Spurs in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 16 points (5-13 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 35 minutes.
items.story: Shannon's emergence in Minnesota due to some key injuries has really helped the team remain on course. Through four postseason appearances, the guard is averaging an impressive 14.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers on 47.7 percent shooting after averaging just 5.6 points during the regular season.

items.headline: Shannon chipped in 24 points (9-20 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two steals across 35 minutes during Thursday's 110-98 victory over the Nuggets in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Shannon received just his third start of the season, filling in for Ayo Dosunmu, who was a late scratch due to a calf injury. Despite a lack of big-game experience, Shannon proved to be a real difference-maker, leading from the front alongside Jaden McDaniels. Minnesota will now face San Antonio in the second round of the playoffs. The availability of both Dosunmu and Anthony Edwards (knee) will likely determine whether Shannon continues to play a sizeable role.

items.headline: Shannon is in the starting lineup for Game 6 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Nuggets on Thursday.
items.story: Shannon is the next man up after Ayo Dosunmu (calf) was ruled out for Thursday's matchup. Shannon and Bones Hyland should be in for a sizable uptick in minutes with Dosunmu, Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) all unavailable for Game 6.

items.headline: Shannon (illness) is off the injury report for Game 4 on Saturday versus Denver.
items.story: Shannon wasn't available for Game 3 on Thursday due to an illness, but he's feeling better and ready to go for Game 4. That said, Shannon's presence is unlikely to affect Minnesota's rotation Saturday.

items.headline: Shannon (illness) is out for Game 3 against the Nuggets on Thursday.
items.story: Shannon and Jaylen Clark will both miss Thursday's matchup after falling ill. Neither player has taken the court through the first two games of the series, so their absences should have little impact.

items.headline: Shannon (illness) is questionable for Thursday's Game 3 versus Denver.
items.story: Shannon hasn't been part of Minnesota's playoff rotation through the opening two games. His potential absence shouldn't have an impact.

items.headline: Shannon won't start Saturday's Game 1 against the Nuggets.
items.story: Shannon got the starting nod in the regular-season finale, though he'll slide to the second unit Saturday. Over 41 regular-season appearances off the bench, he averaged 5.0 points and 1.0 rebounds in 11.6 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Shannon closed with 26 points (6-18 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 14-18 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal across 35 minutes during Sunday's 132-126 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: Shannon was inefficient from the field and failed to knock down a three-pointer, but he got to the charity stripe consistently and grinded his way to a team-best 26 points. Seeing heavy minutes of late, the 25-year-old has eclipsed the 20-point mark in each of the Timberwolves' past three games. He'll close the regular season averaging 5.6 points and 1.1 rebounds in 12.5 minutes across 43 appearances.

items.headline: Shannon will start Sunday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Shannon will make just his second start of the season due to the team resting the majority of their rotation players. Shannon has averaged an impressive 28.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 29.5 minutes per contest over his last two appearances.

items.headline: Shannon amassed 33 points (11-14 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds and five assists in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 132-120 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Shannon didn't start Wednesday, but he made his presence felt off the bench and led all Minnesota players in this loss while setting a new career-high scoring mark. This was just the seventh time Shannon scored in double digits this season, and even though one game won't be enough to experience a drastic uptick in his fantasy upside, don't be surprised if he has a bigger role offensively in the final two games of the regular season, especially if the Timberwolves continue to rest most of their starters.

items.headline: Poole provided 25 points (9-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 31 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Poole supplied a much-needed offensive spark for New Orleans, combining with Jeremiah Fears for 54 of the team's 91 points. Poole's scoring ability and three-point volume remain his clearest fantasy strengths, although his limited playmaking and defensive contributions make him more dependent on shooting efficiency than guards who regularly contribute across multiple categories. Poole has been making the most of his opportunities since returning to the rotation and is averaging 15.0 points per game over his last seven appearances off the bench, scoring in double digits six times and shooting 39.4 percent from three in that stretch.

items.headline: Poole finished Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons with 22 points (5-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 9-9 FT), one rebound, five assists and two steals in 30 minutes.
items.story: This was Poole's fourth consecutive game with five dimes, and he finished with a season high in points and three-pointers made. He's been heating up over this four-game stretch with averages of 15.0 points, 5.0 assists and 1.8 triples per contest.

items.headline: Poole finished Saturday's 116-108 loss to the Nuggets with 14 points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds and five assists in 24 minutes.
items.story: Poole scored at least 13 points for the third straight game, and he is seemingly now a consistent part of the rotation in New Orleans. While managers are well within their rights to be skeptical, Poole is all of a sudden back on the radar, even in standard leagues. With that said, his overall upside is limited, particularly if he is playing no more than about 25 minutes per night.

items.headline: Poole finished with 14 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), an assist and a block across 21 minutes in Wednesday's 145-111 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Poole made efficient use of his limited offensive opportunities, but his 21-minute workload and minimal secondary contributions limited his fantasy production. Poole's scoring ability provides occasional upside, but his inconsistent playing time and narrow statistical profile outside of the scoring column make him difficult to trust in standard formats.

items.headline: Poole posted seven points (1-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one block over 34 minutes during Monday's 138-87 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Poole logged a team-high 34 minutes but managed only five shot attempts and finished with a game-worst minus-47 rating. His heavy workload came largely in garbage time of a blowout. Without more offensive involvement, he's difficult to trust in fantasy lineups, especially when the Pelicans are back at full strength.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Poole was initially listed as probable due to left ankle tendinopathy, and he's since been cleared to play Wednesday. The veteran guard is averaging 6.0 points, 3.0 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 16.0 minutes per contest across four regular-season games.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Poole is expected to return from a three-game layoff for the meeting with the Jazz on Wednesday. The 27-year-old hasn't had a memorable 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 6.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals across 16.0 minutes per contest. If Poole is cleared for action, it would likely mean fewer minutes for Bryce McGowens and Trendon Watford.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Poole will miss his third consecutive contest due to a sprained left ankle. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus Utah. Bennedict Mathurin and Herbert Jones should continue to earn more run in Poole's absence.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Poole will miss a second straight game due to a sprained left ankle. His next chance to suit up will come Monday at Memphis. Bennedict Mathurin and Herbert Jones are candidates for increased playing time in Poole's absence.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Poole will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set after spraining his left ankle in Wednesday's loss to Denver. His next chance to play will come Saturday against Atlanta. In the meantime, Bennedict Mathurin and Herbert Jones are candidates for increased burn. With Dejounte Murray (personal) also out, AJ Johnson could enter the rotation.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) is now doubtful for Thursday against the Kings.
items.story: Poole appears likely to miss the second leg of this back-to-back set. The veteran left Wednesday's game against Denver after just seven minutes and failed to return. His absence could open things up a bit for Bennedict Mathurin.

items.headline: Poole (ankle) won't return to Wednesday's game against the Nuggets. He'll finish with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one steal over seven minutes.
items.story: Poole was on the injury report heading into the contest due to an illness. While he was able to suit up, he has since been ruled out due to an ankle injury suffered in the first half. The Pelicans play again Thursday versus the Kings, so Poole should at least be considered questionable.

items.headline: Poole (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Poole is cleared to play through an illness Wednesday. He's handling the backup point guard role behind Jeremiah Fears, averaging 7.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.7 minutes per game over three appearances so far.

items.headline: Poole (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Poole is under the weather but appears likely to suit up in the front end of this back-to-back set. Through three regular-season games, the veteran guard is averaging 7.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poole supplied six points (2-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt), three rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal over 22 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime loss to Denver.
items.story: Poole saw 22 minutes off the bench, continuing to play a modest role for the Pelicans. Through three games, he has averaged 7.3 points and 4.0 assists in 18.8 minutes per game. It appears as though he is going to be saddled to the bench a lot, making him a non-factor in standard fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Poole finished with 14 points (4-5 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one rebound and two assists in 13 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Poole delivered an efficient offensive performance, leading New Orleans in scoring despite playing just 13 minutes. The veteran guard connected on three of his four attempts from beyond the arc and should continue providing the Pelicans with perimeter scoring. His fantasy value will depend on his role within a backcourt that also features Dejounte Murray (rest) and Jeremiah Fears.

items.headline: Poole finished with nine points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound and one steal in 16 minutes during Tuesday's 116-110 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Poole came off the bench and didn't commit a turnover during his limited workload. The veteran guard should provide New Orleans with additional scoring and shooting in a reserve role this season.

items.headline: The Pelicans gave Poole another competitor for playing time with the signing of Bennedict Mathurin on Wednesday.
items.story: Poole was a massive disappointment from a fantasy perspective in 2025-26, averaging 13.4 points, 3.1 assists and 2.0 rebounds per game over 39 regular-season appearances while falling out of the rotation at times. He'll be battling with Jeremiah Fears for the backup point guard role behind Dejounte Murray at training camp, while the addition of Mathurin could make it difficult for Poole to see steady minutes at shooting guard off the bench.

items.headline: Poole provided New Orleans with an additional scoring threat initially during the 2025-26 campaign, but he would eventually fall out favor with the coaching staff.
items.story: Poole ended up making 39 regular-season appearances, shooting 37.2 percent from the field with 13.4 points, 3.1 assists and 2.0 rebounds. With Dejounte Murray (hand) expected to be back at full strength, Poole will face an uphill battle for playing time in 2026-27.

items.headline: Poole will come off the bench for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Jordan Hawkins will replace Poole in the first unit for Sunday's game, and it'll be interesting to see how many minutes Poole receives in the reserve role. In 31 games off the bench this season, Poole has averaged 12.0 points, 2.8 assists and 2.2 triples per contest.

items.headline: Poole closed Tuesday's 156-137 win over Utah with 34 points (12-23 FG, 7-16 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes.
items.story: Zion Williamson, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones were all active Tuesday, but none of them saw the floor. Poole, who has been used sparingly in recent weeks, may get an extended look in the final two games of the regular season as the Pelicans have nothing to play for.

items.headline: Poole will start Tuesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Poole will get the start for the first time in three months. In six starts during the campaign, the 26-year-old has averaged 18.0 points, 1.7 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.7 steals across 33.7 minutes.

items.headline: Poole notched four points (2-9 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), one rebound, two assists and two blocks in 18 minutes during Monday's 129-111 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Poole was back in the rotation for the first time in the past eight games, likely as a result of Dejounte Murray being ruled out due to illness. In what has been a frustrating season for Poole, this appearance is likely to be a cameo rather than what to expect moving forward. Barring a shift in the teams' direction, Poole seems destined to spend a lot more time on the bench.

items.headline: Poole (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Sunday in the Pelicans' 137-117 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: After being left out of the rotation for the Pelicans' final nine games before the All-Star break, Poole had resurfaced on New Orleans' second unit to begin the second half. He averaged 10.4 points, 3.6 assists and 3.0 assists over his last five appearances, but Poole had seen his playing time trend down over the Pelicans' previous two matchups, when he logged a combined 25 minutes. Though New Orleans was missing Zion Williamson (ankle) on Sunday, the returns of Trey Murphy (shoulder) and Dejounte Murray (reconditioning) were enough to bump Poole back out of the rotation. The 26-year-old guard's outlook for playing time will only worsen once Williamson is cleared to return to action.

items.headline: Poole contributed 23 points (8-15 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Saturday's 126-111 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Poole remained in the rotation Saturday, scoring 23 points in the process, the most he has scored since Dec 31. After being out of the rotation for nine straight games, he has now logged at least 24 minutes in two consecutive contests. It's hard to get an exact read on what is happening with the rotation, but assuming he continues to play a meaningful role, he could be worth a speculative pickup, specifically for those needing points and threes.

items.headline: Poole posted three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists across 25 minutes Friday in the Pelicans' 139-118 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: After going unused in each of the Pelicans' last nine games, Poole was dusted off and inserted into the rotation as New Orleans looked to add some more offensive firepower to the mix while Trey Murphy (shoulder) was sidelined. Despite seeing a healthy minutes total off the bench, Poole failed to deliver much of a spark. The Pelicans could get Murphy back for the second leg of their back-to-back set Saturday versus the 76ers, and Dejounte Murray (Achilles) is also drawing closer to his season debut, so Poole could find himself back outside of the rotation in short order.

items.headline: Poole (coach's decision) didn't appear off the bench Sunday in the Pelicans' 104-95 win over the Spurs.
items.story: After playing fewer than 20 minutes in three of his last five appearances, Poole saw his spot in the New Orleans rotation disappear entirely while the Pelicans welcomed Jose Alvarado (oblique) back from a nine-game absence. The Pelicans brought the 26-year-old in on an offseason deal with the hope that he would provide a scoring punch as a lead guard off the bench, and though he's averaging 14.5 points in just 25.4 minutes per game on the season, Poole has connected on just 37 percent of his attempts from the field and 33.6 percent of his attempts from three-point range. Poole is on New Orleans' books through next season at a hefty salary, so unless the Pelicans unload him ahead of the Feb. 5 trade deadline, he'll likely get another look in the rotation at some point down the road in spite of his struggles.

items.headline: Poole amassed 11 points (4-17 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 112-104 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Poole continues to struggle to maintain fantasy value with the last-place Pelicans. Over his last seven appearances, the combo guard has averaged just 11.3 points, 1.7 assists, 1.6 rebounds and 2.4 three-pointers in 20.2 minutes per game, though he's shooting 47.2 percent from deep during this span.

items.headline: Poole contributed 16 points (4-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's 122-116 loss to Denver.
items.story: The 26-year-old guard continues to light it up from long distance. Poole has drained four or more three-pointers in six of his last nine games (two starts), averaging 14.9 points, 3.3 threes, 3.0 assists and 1.2 boards in 24.3 minutes while shooting 43.5 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Poole ended with 21 points (7-11 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two assists and one steal in 23 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 128-118 loss to Orlando.
items.story: The 26-year-old guard has been seeing a wildly varying role in the Pelicans' backcourt of late. Poole has started two of the last eight games and played anywhere from 12 to 39 minutes during that stretch, failing to score a point at all in two of those contests while topping 20 points in four others. That volatility makes him a risky DFS option, but Poole is averaging 14.8 points, 3.3 threes, 3.1 assists and 1.3 boards in 24.9 minutes in that time, production which has some value in deeper season-long formats.

items.headline: Poole registered zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one assist across 12 minutes during Friday's 128-107 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Poole delivered another woeful performance, failing to score for the second time in the past three games. On the whole, Poole has been a disaster this season, both in terms of fantasy and reality. In 14 games over the past month, he has averaged 14.3 points, 3.4 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 25.4 minutes per game, barely making him a top 200 player in standard leagues. At this point, it appears as though a trade is the only way of salvaging his season.

items.headline: Poole won't start against the Wizards on Friday.
items.story: With Trey Murphy (back) returning from a one-game absence, Poole will slide back to the second unit. In 14 appearances off the bench this season, the 26-year-old guard has averaged 15.2 points, 3.2 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 25.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poole is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Hawks.
items.story: Poole is coming off a scoreless, 0-for-4 shooting performance, but he'll have an excellent chance to bounce back Wednesday night with Trey Murphy (back), Herbert Jones (ankle) and Jose Alvarado (oblique) all watching from the sidelines. Poole has been better as a starter this season, posting averages of 17.4 points, 4.6 assists and 2.8 triples per contest.

items.headline: Poole amassed zero points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one block over 18 minutes during Tuesday's 111-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Poole will want to forget about this dud quickly, as he finished scoreless for the first time this campaign. He's been in a shooting slump lately, hitting 35.0 percent from the field over his last seven games with 13.7 points, 4.0 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 2.3 three-pointers in 24.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poole notched eight points (3-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt), eight assists, two blocks, one rebound and one steal across 25 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 125-106 loss to the Heat.
items.story: With Trey Murphy back in the lineup following a one-game absence due to back soreness, Poole came off the bench after getting the spot start in Friday's loss to Portland. The 26-year-old guard struggled to find his rhythm from the field, finishing with just eight points after scoring at least 16 in each of his previous three appearances. However, Poole still led the Pelicans in assists, dishing out a game- and season-high eight dimes. Additionally, he set a new season high in blocks as well.

items.headline: Poole closed with 16 points (5-16 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 2-3 FT), one rebound and six assists over 30 minutes during Friday's 122-109 loss to Portland.
items.story: Poole made his fifth start of the regular season Friday and first since Nov. 4 due to the absences of several key starters, including Trey Murphy (back) and Saddiq Bey (hip). Poole wasn't the most efficient from the field, but he led the Pelicans with six assists and finished tied with Karlo Matkovic as the team's third-leading scorer behind Zion Williamson (35 points) and Jeremiah Fears (18 points). Across the 10 games since returning from an 18-game absence due to a left quadriceps strain, Poole has averaged 17.1 points, 3.4 assists, 2.1 rebounds, 2.4 threes and 1.0 steals over 36.4 minutes per game, though he's connected on just 27.6 percent of his three-point attempts over that span.

items.headline: Poole will start against the Trail Blazers on Friday.
items.story: The Pelicans will be without several key contributors Friday, giving Poole the chance to step into the starting five for the first time since Nov. 4. Over nine outings in December, the 26-year-old shooting guard averaged 17.2 points, 3.1 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 26.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poole ended with 26 points (6-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 10-10 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 134-118 loss to Chicago.
items.story: The team's unwillingness to move Poole back into the starting lineup is a bit of a head-scratcher. Coach James Borrego seems focused on developing Jeremiah Fears, and the staff may have concluded that Poole's second-unit contribution is more valuable. They may be right on that account, as Poole is certainly logging minutes like a starter. He posted his second consecutive 26-point total during the loss, and we'll get a better idea of how he's doing with his sore ankle during an upcoming back-to-back scenario next week.

items.headline: Poole ended with 26 points (7-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block over 26 minutes during Monday's 130-125 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Poole could find his way back into a starting role soon, as he's consistently outperforming Jeremiah Fears off the bench. Fears logged only 22 minutes in the defeat, and Poole was obviously more effective for the duration of the game. Aside from a poor performance against the Sixers, Poole has made a strong case for a first-unit gig since returning from injury, averaging 16.1 points, 3.3 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals over the last eight games.

items.headline: Poole logged 19 points (7-18 FG, 2-11 3Pt, 3-6 FT), five rebounds, six assists, one block and four steals across 31 minutes during Friday's 115-108 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Poole missed the Pelicans' previous game with a nagging ankle injury, but he played through any residual pain and posted a solid number with the second unit. Although Jeremiah Fears appears to have a solid grasp on the starting gig at point guard, Poole will continue to push the youngster for time. The job was Poole's to lose earlier in the season, and his ankle kept him from retaining the role. Once Poole is back to 100 percent, the tide may turn in New Orleans' backcourt.

items.headline: The Nets exercised Wolf's team option Thursday, per Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today.
items.story: This is an expected transaction for the 2025 first-rounder. The hope is that Wolf will eventually become a key rotation piece for the Nets as he continues to develop.

items.headline: The Nets recalled Wolf from the G League's Long Island Nets on Wednesday.
items.story: Wolf will rejoin Brooklyn following a brief stint with Long Island, though the move doesn't necessarily indicate an increased role in the NBA rotation. The second-year big man will look to earn additional playing time, but his immediate fantasy appeal remains limited without a consistent workload.

items.headline: Wolf had six points (2-4 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist over 15 minutes during Sunday's 136-109 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After not receiving any playing time in the Nets' first two games of the season, Wolf got some run with Brooklyn trailing by double digits for nearly the entire second half. With Noah Clowney, Chaney Johnson and Moritz Wagner occupying most of the frontcourt minutes in the second unit, it seems like Wolf will be the odd man out on most nights.

items.headline: Wolf (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: The second-year big man didn't receive an opportunity in Brooklyn's defeat on Opening Night. Wolf will need to carve out a more substantial role in the Nets' frontcourt before becoming relevant in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Wolf amassed nine points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 16 minutes during Thursday's 114-108 preseason win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Wolf came off the bench once again, a role that figures to stick come opening night. Both he and Moritz Wagner are likely to be battling for backup minutes behind Day'Ron Sharpe, although it would appear as though Wagner might have the inside track as the first big off the bench. With that said, neither has significant appeal in fantasy leagues, at least not to begin the season.

items.headline: Wolf finished with nine points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five assists and three rebounds in 15 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Wolf made the most of his limited playing time, with his five assists tying for the team lead. The second-year big showcased his versatility as a passer while connecting on his lone three-point attempt.

items.headline: Wolf (rest) is ticketed for a reserve role in 2026-27 after the Nets acquired Julius Randle from Minnesota earlier this offseason.
items.story: Wolf closed last season as a starter while the Nets gradually began shutting down most of their key players, but the 2025 first-rounder might even struggle for a significant Opening Night role in 2026-27. Not only did Brooklyn add Randle as its starting power forward, but the team also signed Moritz Wagner and drafted Joshua Jefferson to further upgrade the frontcourt.

items.headline: Wolf (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Wolf will sit out Brooklyn's Summer League finale for rest purposes. The 22-year-old big man will finish the Las Vegas Summer League with averages of 11.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks in 21.4 minutes per tilt across four outings.

items.headline: Wolf finished with 14 points (5-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 20 minutes in Tuesday's 115-83 Summer League win over Sacramento.
items.story: Wolf ended with only nine points in his first Las Vegas Summer League appearance. Since then, the 22-year-old has reached double figures in scoring in his last two Summer League games, though he's shot an inefficient 0-for-6 from deep during that span. Wolf, the 2025 No. 27 overall pick, finished his rookie year by averaging 8.9 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 0.6 blocks and 0.5 steals over 20.8 minutes in 57 regular-season games. He should see routine action in 2026-27, potentially making a few starts here and there when necessary.

items.headline: Wolf closed with 20 points (9-16 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 26 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Wolf showed out offensively, matching teammate Chaney Johnson with a game-high 20 points.
