Coming off a rookie campaign in which he averaged 8.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 20.8 minutes per contest across 57 regular-season appearances (15 starts), Wolf will look to use the Summer League to sharpen his game and push for a larger role during the 2026-27 season. That opportunity may be harder to come by, however, after the Nets added Julius Randle at power forward this offseason.

items.headline: Wolf (back) finished with nine points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block across 21 minutes in Friday's 91-65 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: It wasn't a great performance from Wolf, but it was still an encouraging showing considering he wasn't available for the California Classic because of a back issue. The 22-year-old appeared in 57 regular-season games during his rookie 2025-26 campaign, and he averaged 10.2 points, 2.3 assists, 6.3 rebounds, 0.8 blocks and 0.7 steals over 26.0 minutes in 15 starts. Looking ahead to next season, Julius Randle, who was acquired from Minnesota in June, has a firm grasp on the power forward position, while Day'Ron Sharpe is the favorite to start at center. However, Wolf should have an opportunity to see consistent playing time in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Wolf (back) is out for Monday's California Classic Summer League Game against the Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Wolf will miss a third straight Summer League game due to lower-back soreness. His next opportunity to play comes Friday against the Knicks in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Wolf (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Wolf is dealing with lower-back soreness and will miss a second consecutive Summer League contest. His next opportunity to play will come Monday against the Kings.

items.headline: Wolf didn't play in Saturday's 79-76 California Classic Summer League loss to the Kings due to lower-back soreness, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Coach Dutch Gaitley said the Nets want to be smart about Wolf's availability in Summer League, and his next chance to play will come Sunday against the Bucks. The big man missed Brooklyn's final 11 regular-season games due to an ankle sprain, finishing the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 8.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.2 assists across 20.8 minutes per contest in 57 regular-season games (15 starts).

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) is expected to open 2026-27 in a bench role after the Nets acquired Julius Randle ahead of Tuesday's draft.
items.story: While Brooklyn did lose Nic Claxton (finger) in the Randle trade, the expectation is that Day'Ron Sharpe is sliding into the top center position next year. Wolf, a 2025 first-rounder, should have a chance to battle for that role in the Las Vegas Summer League as well as during training camp, though Sharpe does possess a veteran's advantage. The Nets also landed Joshua Jefferson near the end of the first round of the 2026 NBA Draft, leaving Wolf to vie with the newcomer as well as Noah Clowney (ankle) for playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: The Nets announced Friday that Wolf (ankle) is being shut down for the rest of the season, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: With the Nets playing out the final string of a losing season, they're taking a cautious approach with the rookie first-rounder. Wolf showed promise at times in his first year, averaging 8.9 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 20.8 minutes per contest through 57 regular-season games (15 starts). With Wolf's campaign over, Noah Clowney, Josh Minott and Chaney Johnson should help pick up the slack at power forward.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) has no timetable for a return, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Wolf remains in a walking boot due to a sprained left ankle, and the rebuilding Nets are unlikely to be in much of a hurry to push the rookie first-rounder back into the fray. The likes of Ziaire Williams, Drake Powell and Josh Minott should continue to soak up more playing time going forward.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Wolf will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain and continues to be ruled out a day in advance of tipoff. The rookie first-rounder's next chance to play will come Friday against the Hawks. In the meantime, Josh Minott and Jalen Wilson (illness) are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) won't play in Sunday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: It will be Wolf's fourth consecutive absence. With the Nets going nowhere near the playoffs, the club will likely exercise caution with the rookie first-rounder. As far as Sunday's contest is concerned, Ziaire Williams should be considered a favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) won't play Friday versus the Lakers.
items.story: This will be Wolf's third consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's not encouraging that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff. For now, he should be considered doubtful for Sunday's matchup with Sacramento.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) won't play Wednesday against the Warriors, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Wolf picked up a left ankle injury during Sunday's matchup against Sacramento, and he hasn't been able to take the court since. His next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against the Lakers.

items.headline: Wolf (ankle) is out for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Wolf will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set after tweaking his ankle Sunday against the Kings.  Josh Minott, Chaney Johnson and E.J. Liddell are candidates to see increased minutes with Wolf on the shelf.

items.headline: Wolf sustained a left ankle injury in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Kings and will not return, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports. He'll finish with nine points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-2 FT) and four rebounds across 12 minutes.
items.story: Wolf turned his left ankle and limped off the court before being helped to the locker room. The rookie first-rounder faces a short turnaround if he hopes to play Monday in Portland, so he can be considered highly questionable for that one until Brooklyn provides an update on his status. If he's forced to miss time, Josh Minott, Chaney Johnson and E.J. Liddell would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Wolf closed with 15 points (4-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds and two assists across 26 minutes during Saturday's 104-97 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Wolf tied a season high with 10 boards during Saturday's game and finished as the Nets' leading scorer en route to the first double-double of his NBA career. The rookie first-rounder has started three of Brooklyn's last four games, but he'll likely come off the bench against the Trail Blazers on Monday if Nic Claxton (rest) and Michael Porter (ankle) are cleared to return.

items.headline: Wolf is starting Thursday's game against the Hawks, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Wolf will get the starting nod Thursday with Brooklyn missing both Nolan Traore (rest) and Michael Porter (ankle). Wolf fared well in his last start Monday against the Grizzlies, as he finished with 14 points, nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Wolf racked up 13 points (2-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-9 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 28 minutes during Tuesday's 138-100 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Wolf didn't have his best shooting performance, but making seven of his nine trips to the charity stripe allowed him to salvage his scoring output. The rookie out of Michigan also ended two boards shy of recording what would've been his first double-double since Jan. 11. Wolf has been trending in the right direction of late, scoring in double digits in six of his last eight games despite coming off the bench in all but one of those outings.

items.headline: Wolf won't start Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: With Michael Porter resting Monday, Wolf posted 14 points (5-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 28 minutes during a 126-115 victory over the Grizzlies. However, the rookie slides back to a bench role with the Nets' leading scorer returning Tuesday. Nonetheless, with Day'Ron Sharpe (thumb) and Ziaire Williams (illness) sidelined, Wolf should still see a solid role as a reserve.

items.headline: Wolf contributed 14 points (5-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 28 minutes during Monday's 126-115 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Wolf shifted into the starting lineup, replacing Michael Porter, who was given the night off for rest purposes. Wolf fell one rebound short of what would have been just the second double-double of his career, while also managing to add a pair of defensive stats. While this was an encouraging performance, it's hard to view him as anything more than a stream or stash guy, given the fact that his playing time is wildly unpredictable.

items.headline: Wolf will start Monday's game against the Grizzlies, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Wolf will enter the starting lineup with Michael Porter (rest) sidelined Monday. Wolf's last start dates back to Feb. 9 against the Bulls, when he finished with 13 points, six rebounds, two assists, two steals and three blocks in 26 minutes.

items.headline: Wolf finished Saturday's 107-105 victory over the Pistons with eight points (2-3 FG, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one block across 19 minutes.
items.story: Wolf logged fewer than 20 minutes for the second straight game, continuing what has been an unpredictable two-week stretch. In eight appearances during that time, he has averaged 10.1 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers, barely putting up top-180 value. Although it seems as though Wolf should be ascending, it appears as though the Nets' coaching staff has other ideas, at least for now.

items.headline: Wolf logged 23 points (7-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 6-8 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and two steals over 27 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 106-102 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: The 23 points were a new career high for the rookie forward. Wolf is still predictably showing some inconsistency, but he's scored in double digits in eight of the last 11 games (one start), averaging 12.5 points, 5.4 boards, 3.0 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.4 combined blocks and steals in 22.4 minutes over that stretch.

items.headline: Wolf logged 16 points (5-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 23 minutes during the Nets' 148-111 loss to the Celtics on Friday.
items.story: Wolf started out nicely with seven points in the first quarter. He was held scoreless in the second and third quarters, but with the Nets facing a blowout loss, the rookie first-rounder and other reserves saw increased burn in the fourth. Wolf tallied nine points in the final frame and finished as the Nets' second-leading scorer behind Michael Porter (18 points), and it was the fifth time this season that the former scored at least 15 points in a game.

items.headline: Wolf produced 14 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 22 minutes during Thursday's 126-110 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: This was an encouraging performance for Wolf off the bench, but his role has been too volatile in recent games to trust him in most fantasy formats. Over his last five games, he's averaging 21.0 minutes with 8.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.2 three-pointers.

items.headline: Wolf amassed 11 points (4-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-4 FT), six rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and one steal across 28 minutes during Thursday's 112-84 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Wolf posted an impressive box score during the defeat, showcasing his diverse skill set. As long as Nic Claxton (ankle) remains sidelined, Wolf has a clear path to increased usage. Day'Ron Sharpe started Thursday's game at center, but he played only 20 minutes and finished with four points (1-5 FG), five rebounds and three assists.

items.headline: Wolf will come off the bench for Wednesday's game versus the Pacers, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: While Wolf won't start, it's worth noting that Michael Porter (knee), Noah Clowney (ankle) and Nic Claxton (hip) are out, so Wolf still has the potential to play meaningful minutes while working in a reserve role Wednesday evening. Wolf has logged at least 20 minutes in each of his previous three outings and has recorded double-digit points in all of them.

items.headline: Wolf provided 13 points (5-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists, three blocks and two steals over 26 minutes during Monday's 123-115 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Wolf moved into the starting lineup, scoring in double digits for the third straight game. Although his role continues to fluctuate, his production over the past week has been relatively strong, averaging 12.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.5 three-pointers and 1.8 combined steals and blocks in four games during that time. While he is more of a stash than a must-roster player, he is doing enough to be held in certain formats at the moment.

items.headline: Wolf is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Bulls, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Wolf will step into the starting five for the eighth time this season, giving the Nets a bigger look alongside Noah Clowney and Nic Claxton in the frontcourt. In his first seven starts, Wolf averaged 10.3 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 28.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wolf racked up 16 points (7-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven rebounds and six assists over 20 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 127-113 victory over Washington.
items.story: The six assists were a career high for the 27th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, while the 16 points were Wolf's highest total since Dec. 12 against the Mavericks. The Michigan product remains inconsistent in the second unit, however -- Wolf has scored in double digits only four times in the last 11 games (three starts), averaging 8.7 points, 5.5 boards, 2.5 assists and 1.0 threes in 20.8 minutes a contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Wolf will be deployed off the bench Tuesday against the Lakers, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Wolf will retreat to a bench role following the return of Noah Clowney from a back injury. Wolf has struggled to produce off the bench of late, averaging 6.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in his last five appearances as a reserve.

items.headline: Wolf chipped in six points (2-9 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and one block across 29 minutes during Sunday's 130-77 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Wolf salvaged a rough shooting night with a big performance on the glass. The 27th overall pick in the 2025 Draft tied his career high in rebounds along with six points and four assists. Wolf missed all five of his tries from distance but still averages 1.1 makes from downtown on the year.

items.headline: Wolf will start Thursday versus the Nuggets, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Joining Wolf in the first unit for Thursday's game will be Nolan Traore, Terance Mann, Michael Porter and Nic Claxton. Through four starts this season, Wolf has posted averages of 11.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 triples and 1.3 steals per contest.

items.headline: Wolf produced 14 points (3-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 26 minutes during Sunday's 126-89 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Wolf struggled to find the bottom of the basket during the blowout loss, but his assists and rebounds salvaged his bottom line. Wolf is seeing extra time due to injuries for Noah Clowney (back) and Cam Thomas (knee). While both could return as early as Tuesday, Wolf should still log a healthy dose of minutes, especially if either of them receives a minute restriction.

items.headline: Wolf isn't starting Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: The Michigan product drew a spot start Sunday while Michael Porter got a regularly scheduled night off, but it'll be right back to the bench Monday night for Wolf with Porter back on the court. Wolf played well in his last appearance as a reserve Friday against the Bulls, ending with 13 points, four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 19 minutes.

items.headline: Wolf finished Sunday's 124-102 loss to Chicago with 14 points (6-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one block over 25 minutes.
items.story: With Michael Porter getting the night off for rest, Wolf drew the start for Brooklyn and put together a pretty solid outing. He's been getting more opportunities lately, and that makes him worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats. Over his last four games, he's averaging 8.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.0 steals, 1.0 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 19.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jordan won't start Thursday's game against the Kings.
items.story: After starting the last two games, the veteran big man will slide to the second unit in favor of Karlo Matkovic. Jordan has yet to make an appearance off the bench this season, as he didn't see the floor in New Orleans' first two games.

items.headline: Jordan finished with nine points (3-3 FG, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block across 20 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Jordan was inserted into the starting lineup after Yves Missi was ruled out with a knee injury. At this point in his career, Jordan is mostly a locker room guy, seeing the floor on rare occasions. New Orleans plays Denver again Wednesday, and Jordan could once again find himself in the rotation, assuming Missi is ruled out. If that is the case, Jordan could be utilized for streaming purposes.

items.headline: Jordan will start Saturday against the Nuggets.
items.story: Jordan has been out of the rotation through the first two games of the season, but with Yves Missi (knee) unavailable, he will draw the start against Denver's Nikola Jokic. Across seven starts last season, Jordan averaged 3.9 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.0 blocks per game.

items.headline: Jordan was a DNP-CD during Tuesday's 116-110 preseason win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Jordan was available but didn't see the floor despite New Orleans going deep into its bench. The veteran center is expected to provide depth behind Yves Missi and could have difficulty finding consistent playing time when the Pelicans are healthy.

items.headline: Jordan re-signed with the Pelicans on Tuesday, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: The terms of the agreement are not yet clear, but it figures to be a one-year contract for the veteran's minimum. The 37-year-old center, who's entering his 19th season in the NBA, offers the Pelicans leadership and a veteran presence for their young big men like Derik Queen, Yves Missi and Karlo Matkovic. Jordan made 16 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 for New Orleans, averaging 4.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 0.8 blocks in 16.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jordan won't start Friday's game against the Raptors, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Jordan got the starting nod in Thursday's loss to Detroit but will slide to the second unit in favor of Yves Missi on Friday. Jordan recorded six straight DNP-CDs before Thursday's contest, so the veteran big man isn't guaranteed to see the court Friday.

items.headline: Jordan is in the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup with the Pistons.
items.story: Dejounte Murray, Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey and Zion Williamson will join Jordan in the first unit for Thursday's game. In six starts this season, Jordan has posted averages of 3.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.0 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Jordan isn't in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Lakers, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Jordan will revert back to the bench with Zion Williamson returning to the hardwood Tuesday evening. Jordan struggled to see much playing time even when in the starting five, so he's unlikely to have much upside in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Jordan contributed three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and one steal in 13 minutes during Saturday's 115-105 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Jordan was given the starting nod for the fourth straight game, although his playing time tells a different story. Despite starting, he has logged no more than 13 minutes in each of the past two games, an indication that he could slide back out of the rotation, especially with Yves Missi returning from a calf strain. Even if Jordan can remain a nightly part of the rotation, his days of being a viable fantasy asset are now well behind him.

items.headline: Jordan amassed six points (2-3 FG, 2-4 FT), 15 rebounds and four blocks in 31 minutes during Saturday's 126-111 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: After not touching an NBA court since Oct 29, Jordan was thrust into the starting lineup Saturday. Not only did he log a season-high 31 minutes, but he rewarded anyone who took a chance on him by gobbling up a game-high 15 rebounds to go with four blocked shots. It's unlikely Jordan will put up these type of numbers consistently, but he appears to still have the ability to crash the boards and make an impact on defense.

items.headline: Jordan will start against the 76ers on Saturday.
items.story: The veteran center hasn't seen game action since Oct. 29 but will join the starting lineup in favor of Bryce McGowens on Saturday. Over two regular-season outings (one start) thus far, Jordan has averaged 4.5 points and 5.0 rebounds in 11.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jordan ended with two points (1-1 FG) and five rebounds over 12 minutes during Wednesday's 122-88 loss to Denver.
items.story: Jordan was given the starting nod, an indication of how desperate things are in New Orleans at the moment. The Pelicans have lost all four games to begin the season, the last two by significant margins. Despite starting, Jordan was a non-factor during his limited time on the floor. To be clear, he should not be starting for an NBA team, nor should he be on any fantasy rosters.

items.headline: Jordan is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game in Denver.
items.story: Jordon looked decent across 11 minutes in his regular-season debut Monday, but he'll draw a tough matchup against Nikola Jokic on Wednesday, so he's still not the most attractive target despite the starter designation. Joining him in the first unit will be Jeremiah Fears, Trey Murphy, Herbert Jones and Zion Williamson.

items.headline: Jordan posted seven points (3-4 FG, 1-2 FT) and five rebounds across 11 minutes during Monday's 122-90 loss to Boston.
items.story: The 37-year-old big man looked surprisingly spry out there, throwing down a thunderous jam for his first bucket, and he brought some much-needed size to a New Orleans team that was without Zion Williamson (foot) and Kevon Looney (knee). The Pelicans will fly to Denver for their next matchup with the Nuggets on Wednesday, and if Williamson is again sidelined for that one, Jordan should remain in the rotation.

items.headline: Jordan (recently signed) isn't listed on the Pelicans' injury report for Monday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Jordan signed a one-year deal with the Pelicans on Friday but didn't play in the team's loss to the Spurs that night. The veteran big man isn't guaranteed to see the floor against Boston, though he could enter the rotation if Yves Missi (ankle) and Karlo Matkovic (back) are ultimately ruled out.

items.headline: Head coach Willie Green said Jordan (recently signed) is unlikely to play in Friday's game against the Spurs, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jordan signed a one-year deal with the Pelicans on Friday and isn't expected to suit up against San Antonio. In the likely event the veteran big man joins Yves Missi (ankle), Kevon Looney (knee) and Karlo Matkovic (back) on the sideline, Derik Queen and Hunter Dickinson are expected to see increased minutes at center.

items.headline: Jordan signed a one-year, $3.6 million contract with the Pelicans on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: The Pelicans have had some tough injury luck in the frontcourt, so Jordan is being brought in to bolster the team's rebounding and interior defense. Yves Missi (ankle) and Karlo Matkovic (back) are both questionable to play Friday against the Spurs, while Kevon Looney (knee) is sidelined. That means Jordan could be thrown into action right away.

items.headline: Jordan finished the 2024-25 campaign with averages of 3.7 points, 5.1 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.3 steals across 12.3 minutes per game in 56 regular-season outings (five starts).
items.story: The veteran big man received inconsistent run as Nikola Jokic's backup this season. Jordan appeared in six of the Nuggets' seven games during their first-round series win over the Clippers but made only one appearance during the second round, logging just two minutes. The 36-year-old is set to become an unrestricted free agent this offseason, and he'll likely be tabbed for a role providing depth and serving as a veteran presence at this stage of his career.

items.headline: Jordan recorded one rebound across five minutes during Monday's 105-102 loss to the Clippers in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: After sitting out Game 1 for a coach's decision, Jordan was used sparingly in Game 2. The Nuggets are rolling with a tight rotation against the Clippers, and that's unlikely to change now that the teams are tied at one win apiece.

items.headline: Jordan won't start in Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Nikola Jokic (ankle) will return from a one-game absence Friday, pushing Jordan to the bench. The veteran big man has averaged only 6.7 minutes per game in his last three appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Jordan closed with 10 points (2-4 FG, 6-12 FT), 17 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 36 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: The veteran big man collected a game-high 17 boards in Nikola Jokic's (ankle) stead on Wednesday, matching a season high in rebounds to go with his third double-double of the campaign. Jordan doesn't always see the court when Jokic is available, but the former has filled in serviceably when the latter has been out of action. Through five starts in 2024-25, Jordan has averaged 8.6 points, 13.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.8 blocks in 30.4 minutes while shooting 69.6 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Jordan is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Spurs, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: Jordan is one of several players who will have the chance to handle an expanded role Wednesday, as head coach Michael Malone decided to rest all the usual starters. Jordan has made four starts this season, averaging 8.3 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and a combined 2.1 steals-plus-blocks per game in those four contests.

items.headline: Jordan is not in the Nuggets' starting lineup against the Bucks on Wednesday.
items.story: Jordan was in the Nuggets' starting five for the last two games, but he'll retreat to the bench Wednesday due to the return of Nikola Jokic (ankle). Across those two starts, Jordan averaged 10.5 points on 69.2 percent shooting, 16.0 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 1.0 steals over 34.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jordan totaled 10 points (4-6 FG, 2-5 FT), 17 rebounds, seven assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Monday's 129-119 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Jordan was surprisingly productive in the assist column Monday, setting a new season high in just his second March appearance. The veteran center has made a splash while filling in for Nikola Jokic (ankle), recording a double-double in back-to-back performances. Jordan can be considered a worthwhile streaming option until Jokic gets the green light to return.

items.headline: Jordan finished Sunday's 116-111 win over Houston with 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-3 FT), 15 rebounds, four assists and one steal over 38 minutes.
items.story: With Nikola Jokic (ankle) still sidelined, Jordan started at center Sunday, pushing Russell Westbrook to the second unit. According to coach Michael Malone, Jokic is unlikely to play in Monday's game against the Bulls, but he's expected back at some point during the team's five-game homestand. If Jordan remains in the starting lineup, he'll be worth a look as a streamer after his eruption Sunday night.

items.headline: Jordan will start in Sunday's game against the Rockets, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Aaron Gordon has been serving as the club's starting center due to Nikola Jokic (ankle) being sidelined, though Jordan will suit up for the first time since March 2, pushing Russell Westbrook to the bench. Jordan made two starts during January, accumulating 12 points, 17 rebounds, three blocks, three steals and two assists across 46 total minutes.

items.headline: Jordan chipped in two rebounds and one assist in four minutes during Saturday's 123-100 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Jordan barely saw the floor in the loss, playing fewer than 10 minutes for the first time in the past eight games. Although he is playing as the primary backup behind Nikola Jokic, his days of being a viable contributor are well behind him.

items.headline: Jordan totaled four points (2-5 FG), 11 rebounds, one assist and one block across 17 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 122-105 win over the Suns.
items.story: The veteran center got a bit of extended run in the fourth quarter as Nikola Jokic took a seat, and Jordan parlayed the opportunity into a season high in boards. The 36-year-old is actually third on the Nuggets' depth chart in the middle, however -- Zeke Nnaji played 21 minutes Saturday -- and Jordan hasn't seen 20-plus minutes in a game since making a spot start against the Rockets on Jan. 15, giving him very limited fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Bey finished with 21 points (8-17 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, three assists and one block across 37 minutes during Friday's 126-120 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Bey shook off a brutal shooting night against Detroit and was one of the Pelicans' most reliable scorers, especially from beyond the arc. He's been a bit up and down lately, but he's still averaging 16.5 points and remains a key part of the starting five.

items.headline: Bey logged 10 points (3-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and one steal across 42 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Bey's scoring dipped after posting 23 and 30 points in two of his previous three outings, but his expanded starting role continues to generate fantasy opportunities. He's logged at least 35 minutes in three of his last four games, providing enough volume to offset occasional shooting struggles.

items.headline: Bey finished with 23 points (8-15 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 33 minutes in Monday's 115-94 win over Golden State.
items.story: Bey led New Orleans in scoring and matched his season high with five three-pointers, providing the perimeter production the Pelicans needed to snap their six-game losing streak. This was his fifth game of the season with at least 20 points, and he remains a key contributor for the Pelicans regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench.

items.headline: Bey notched 30 points (11-20 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 10 rebounds and one block across 35 minutes in Friday's 142-111 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Bey made the most of his second start of the season by posting season-high marks in both points and rebounds while notching his first double-double of the campaign. Bey has been a bright spot for the Pelicans this season and has scored in double figures in all but two of his 13 appearances despite regularly coming off the bench.

items.headline: Bey will start Friday's game against the Grizzlies, Rod Walker of The Times-Picayune reports.
items.story: Bey will be making his second start in three games after coming off the bench in each of New Orleans' first 10 contests. He put up nine points and tallied four assists in 24 minutes during his first start of the season Monday at Golden State.

items.headline: Bey notched 15 points (5-11 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), a rebound and two assists across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 145-111 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Bey remains a useful player to roster in category-based formats if you're looking for a second-unit scorer. He's scored in double digits in all but one of his last eight games, averaging 16.1 points per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Bey won't start Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: With Zion Williamson (rest) back in action, Bey will retreat to the second unit. Over 10 appearances off the bench this season, he's averaged 16.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals in 26.9 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Bey will start Monday's game against the Warriors, Rod Walker of The Times-Picayune reports.
items.story: With Trey Murphy (knees) and Zion Williamson (rest) sidelined for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Bey will step into the starting lineup for the first time this season. The 27-year-old forward has logged at least 26 minutes in five straight games, averaging 19.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.4 steals across 29.6 minutes per contest during that span.

items.headline: Bey recorded 17 points (5-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one block over 31 minutes off the bench during Friday's 115-109 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: The veteran forward led the Pelicans' second unit in scoring, assists and made three-pointers in another productive effort. Bey has found another gear since Halloween, and over the last four games he's averaging 20.5 points, 5.0 boards, 2.3 assists, 2.0 threes and 1.5 steals in 30.5 minutes while shooting 53.6 percent from the floor and 40.0 percent from long range.

items.headline: Bey notched 22 points (9-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 120-113 overtime victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Bey provided an efficient scoring punch off the bench, shooting 64.3 percent from the field while finishing second on the team in points behind Zion Williamson. The forward also chipped in three assists and committed just one turnover. His scoring ability gives him some appeal in deeper formats, though his fantasy consistency will depend on maintaining a substantial role in New Orleans' rotation.

items.headline: Bey ended with 25 points (9-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), six rebounds, one assist and four steals across 26 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 win over Atlanta.
items.story: Bey played a key role in Saturday's win, with 21 of his game-high 25 points coming through the first three quarters. He finished with season highs in points, rebounds and steals, and it was his second game of the season with 20-plus points. However, Bey's production floor would take a hit if one or both of Dejounte Murray (personal) or Jordan Poole (ankle) were to return for Monday's road tilt against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Bey finished Thursday's 132-120 win over the Kings with 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 24 minutes.
items.story: Even with Dejounte Murray missing Thursday's game to celebrate the birth of his son, Bey watched Herbert Jones get the nod in the starting lineup and enjoy a season-best outing. Bey is still maintaining modest production in a reserve role, averaging 13.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 24.2 minutes per game over his first five appearances.

items.headline: Bey finished Friday's 120-119 loss to Utah with 20 points (8-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block over 22 minutes off the bench.
items.story: The Pelicans' second unit was productive overall, with three players scoring in double digits, but it was Bey who led the way for the unit. The journeyman forward is on his third team in six NBA seasons, but after starting 64 of 72 regular-season games for New Orleans in 2025-26 and averaging 31.2 minutes, Bey's looking at a reduced role off the bench to begin the current campaign.

items.headline: Bey ended with 13 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and five rebounds across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Jeremiah Fears got the first crack in the starting lineup Wednesday, but Bey had a decent showing off the bench in his own right. Yves Missi strengthened his hold as a starter with an impressive Opening Night performance, but Bey should remain in contention for a spot in the first unit on the wing throughout the course of the year.

items.headline: Bey logged 19 points (7-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and two steals over 17 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason win over the Wizards.
items.story: Bey exploded off the bench for a game-high 19 points after totaling just 21 points across his previous three preseason appearances. He posted a career-high 17.7 points per game last season, and New Orleans rewarded him with a three-year, $55.5 million extension in September. Bennedict Mathurin's arrival could cut into his time this season, but he'll still be a valuable piece of the offense.

items.headline: Bey is not listed in the starting lineup for Friday's preseason game against Washington.
items.story: Bey will come off the bench in the final preseason game for the Pelicans before the team kicks off the 2026-27 campaign versus the Pacers on Opening Night.

items.headline: Bey ended with four points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two steals and one rebound across 17 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Making his first start of the preseason, Bey struggled to make much of an impact outside of recording two steals. The 27-year-old is projected to serve as a top reserve on the wing during the 2026-27 campaign after averaging 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists across 72 regular-season games (64 starts) last season.

items.headline: Bey finished with 12 points (3-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and five rebounds in 17 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Bey provided a solid scoring contribution in limited action, connecting on two triples while converting all four of his free-throw attempts. The veteran forward will look to establish a consistent offensive role in New Orleans' crowded rotation, though his fantasy value will likely depend on his playing time and perimeter production.

items.headline: Bey will not start in Tuesday's preseason game against Oklahoma City, Andrew Lopez of Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Bey will come off the bench in the Pelicans' first preseason game. The veteran wing signed a three-year extension in September after averaging 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 31.2 minutes per contest in 72 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with New Orleans on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bey, who sat out the 2024-25 season after suffering a torn ACL, proved to the Pelicans that he's deserving of a raise. He averaged 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.1 made threes in 72 appearances during the 2025-26 season, and following this healthy extension, he'll presumably play a key role in the frontcourt heading into the new campaign, even with Bennedict Mathurin entering the mix.

items.headline: Bey tentatively projects as the Pelicans' starting small forward, but the addition of Bennedict Mathurin gives him a formidable threat for a starting job.
items.story: Mathurin was effectively a full-time starter for the Pacers before becoming the first man off the bench following his trade to the Clippers. Bey is coming off a career year, averaging a career-high 17.7 points per game while shooting 45.1 percent from the field in his first season with New Orleans (72 regular-season games), so the camp battle between Bey and Mathurin for a spot in the first unit should be one to monitor this fall.

items.headline: Bey (rest) will remain out for Sunday's game in Minnesota.
items.story: Bey will end up sitting out New Orleans' final three regular-season games for rest purposes, which should continue to lead to more minutes for Micah Peavy and Josh Oduro. Bey scored a career-high 17.7 points per game on 45.1 percent shooting from the field and 84.1 percent from the free-throw line in his first season with the Pelicans.

items.headline: Bey will be rested Friday against the Celtics.
items.story: This will be Bey's second straight maintenance day, which isn't a surprise since the team has nothing to play for. Bey could also be held out of the season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Bey is questionable for Friday's game versus Boston for rest purposes.
items.story: The Pelicans are considering holding Bey out Friday. If the forward is ultimately downgraded to out, Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Poole would likely see significant playing time for the shorthanded Pelicans.

items.headline: Head coach James Borrego said Bey will dress for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, but he doesn't expect him to play, Erin Summers of the Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Derik Queen figures to see heavy minutes Tuesday evening with both Bey and Zion Williamson not expected to touch the court, so Queen is on the radar as a potential target in daily fantasy leagues. Bey's next chance to play will come Friday in Boston.

items.headline: Bey produced 32 points (10-24 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 9-11 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two steals in 39 minutes during Sunday's 112-108 loss to the Magic.
items.story: For the fourth time this season, Bey recorded at least 32 points for the Pelicans. Across 72 games this season, he's averaging 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.9 steals and 2.1 three-pointers.

items.headline: Bey ended with 20 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal in 29 minutes during Friday's 117-113 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Although Bey struggled beyond the arc, he managed a productive evening elsewhere on the court. Bey's numbers have been somewhat volatile this season, but he's managed a serviceable floor over the past 10 games, averaging 19.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.9 assists over the span. His high-water mark of 42 points illustrates his massive scoring potential in the right scenario.

items.headline: Bey posted 18 points (7-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist and one block across 31 minutes during Sunday's 134-102 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Bey finished just three boards away from recording a double-double, and the five-year veteran continues to leave his mark offensively since he's regularly scoring more than 15 points. He's scored at least 17 points in eight games in a row, a stretch in which he's averaging 19.9 points per game while shooting 47.9 percent from the floor and an impressive, yet unsustainable, 52.9 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Bey notched 19 points (6-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one block in 30 minutes during Friday's 119-106 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Bey is riding a strong stretch of play, and this loss to the Raptors was the seventh straight game in which he scored at least 17 points. Over that prolific span, the forward is averaging 20.1 points per game while shooting 51.1 percent from three-point range. Bey should continue to be one of the Pelicans' go-to options on offense in the final weeks of the regular season as long as he remains available to play.

items.headline: Bey finished with 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 28 minutes during Tuesday's 121-116 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With this loss, the Pelicans no longer have a chance to make the postseason. With that in mind, it remains to be seen if that will affect Bey's usage and minutes for the final few weeks, though he's likely to remain heavily involved in the short term.

items.headline: Bey provided 20 points (6-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, six assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Thursday's 105-99 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Bey seems to have bounced back from the two subpar showings he had in the losses to Toronto and Houston on March 11 and March 13, respectively, and this was his third consecutive game with at least 20 points. Bey has reached the 20-point mark in five of his last eight games, averaging 18.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals per game in that prolific stretch.

items.headline: Bey finished with 25 points (10-21 FG, 5-10 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and two steals over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 124-109 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Bey has been a key part of New Orleans all season and has put together a solid fantasy campaign thus far. Through 63 games, he's on pace to return eighth-round value in nine-category formats with averages of 17.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Bey posted 23 points (8-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, three assists and one steal over 35 minutes during Monday's 129-111 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Bey got back on track, scoring double digits for the first time in his past three games. In what has been a breakout season for Bey, he had been in a minor slump of late. The production had been underwhelming, but it appears his role is secure, as he has played at least 29 minutes in all but one of his past 10 games. With New Orleans looking to win, despite its record, Bey remains a must-roster player across all formats.

items.headline: Mitchell posted 19 points (5-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, eight assists and two steals over 38 minutes during Tuesday's 115-109 victory over Utah.
items.story: Mitchell was Miami's second-leading scorer behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and also ran the offense, finishing as the Heat's top playmaker. He's settled in as a starting guard who can do a little of everything, and nights like Tuesday's are why Erik Spoelstra keeps him on the floor late. Miami opens a five-game homestand Friday against Cleveland.

items.headline: Mitchell closed Sunday's 114-108 win over Sacramento with 17 points (6-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-6 FT), three rebounds, 11 assists and one block over 40 minutes.
items.story: The double-double was the sixth of the season in 10 games for Mitchell, and the 28-year-old point guard has scored in double digits in all 10 of those contests. He's headed for a breakout campaign, averaging 16.2 points, 8.5 assists, 2.2 threes, 1.7 boards and 1.2 steals in 35.6 minutes while shooting 50.4 percent from the floor and 40.0 percent from long range.

items.headline: Mitchell amassed 22 points (9-18 FG, 4-9 3Pt), two rebounds, eight assists and one steal over 38 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Although Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo led the Heat's offense, Mitchell continues to thrive as a reliable third scoring option and primary facilitator. This 22-point output matched his previous season-high mark, and he's reached the 15-point plateau in six of his nine appearances. He's averaging career-high marks in points (16.1) and assists (8.2) per game so far.

items.headline: Mitchell closed with 11 points (5-13 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, 10 assists, one block and four steals in 43 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime win over the Clippers.
items.story: Mitchell's shot wasn't falling from deep, but he logged a team-high 43 minutes and made up for it with a double-double and five combined steals-plus-blocks. He's now scored in double figures in all eight appearances this season, and his playmaking has been a steady source of fantasy value. As long as he's seeing this kind of workload, he should be rostered in most formats.

items.headline: Mitchell closed Monday's 138-117 loss to the Lakers with 15 points (5-5 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven assists and one block across 29 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell continues to flourish in the early going, having scored in double digits in each of his first seven appearances while dishing out at least seven dimes in five of them. On the year, the point guard has averaged 16.0 points, 8.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 33.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mitchell closed Friday's 145-125 win over Indiana with 15 points (6-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt), six rebounds, 11 assists and one steal in 35 minutes.
items.story: The double-double was the fourth in six games for Mitchell, and the 28-year-old point guard has also recorded at least one steal in four straight contests. He's thriving as the facilitator for Giannis Antetokounmpo, averaging 16.2 points, 8.2 assists, 2.0 threes, 1.7 boards and 1.2 steals in 34.2 minutes to begin what's shaping up to be a career-best campaign.

items.headline: Mitchell ended Wednesday's 129-117 victory over the Hawks with 10 points (5-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt), one rebound, 10 assists and two steals in 34 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell was coming off back-to-back 20-plus-point performances while shooting 60 percent from the floor, but his scoring came back down to earth Wednesday evening. Still, he came through with the assists and steals and committed just two turnovers in his 34 minutes of floor time. He's gotten off to an impressive start this season, and he'll look to keep rolling Friday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 21 points (9-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two assists and three steals across 33 minutes in Monday's 113-109 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: It wouldn't be a stretch to say Mitchell has been the Heat's second-best player so far this season behind Giannis Antetokounmpo. He reached the 20-point threshold for a second straight contest, and while his two assists were a season-low mark, his three steals were a season high. He should remain a valuable backcourt contributor thanks to his scoring, playmaking and defense.

items.headline: Mitchell logged 22 points (8-13 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal across 37 minutes during Saturday's 115-110 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: While the Heat have gotten off to a rough 0-3 start, Mitchell has been a consistent bright spot for the club. Through three games, Mitchell is flirting with top-50 value behind averages of 17.0 points, 8.7 assists, 2.3 triples and 1.0 blocks per game on 51.4 percent shooting from the field and 80 percent at the charity stripe.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 18 points (6-14 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 3-5 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two blocks across 33 minutes in Friday's 128-111 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Mitchell followed his 11-assist season opener Wednesday with a more scoring-oriented performance, attempting nine three-pointers while maintaining a substantial workload. His five assists were a notable drop from Wednesday, but the two blocks helped offset it in fantasy formats that reward defensive metrics. Mitchell's consistent playing time is encouraging, although his value could fluctuate depending on whether he prioritizes scoring or playmaking alongside Miami's other offensive options. It's still early days in the season, but he's settling well as a complement to an offense driven by the frontcourt pairing of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

items.headline: Mitchell scored 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT) while adding 11 assists and a block across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Mitchell handled substantial playmaking responsibilities in Miami's season opener, finishing with a double-double despite attempting just eight shots. His 11 assists were encouraging, but five turnovers and limited defensive production somewhat diminished his fantasy output. Mitchell's value will depend heavily on his ability to sustain strong assist numbers, particularly given his relatively modest scoring upside -- at best, he's likely to operate as the Heat's No.4 option on offense behind Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and Andrew Wiggins.

items.headline: Mitchell tallied 13 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four assists, two rebounds and two steals in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 144-128 preseason win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Mitchell helped set the pace for Miami's offense while contributing on the defensive end. He did suffer a cut above his right eye, which required stitches, but he was able to return to the game. Mitchell's combination of playmaking and defensive activity should keep him firmly involved in the Heat's backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Mitchell (rest) is in line to play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Nets, Will Manso of Local 10 Miami reports.
items.story: The Heat plan to get most of their regular players some minutes Wednesday. Mitchell should get some burn in the first half of this exhibition.

items.headline: Mitchell (rest) won't suit up for Saturday's exhibition against the Timberwolves, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Heat will be resting their entire starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game, so expect ample minutes for guys like Ryan Conwell and Bez Mbeng. Mitchell should return for Wednesday's exhibition against the Nets.

items.headline: Mitchell recorded three points (1-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four assists, one rebound and one steal in 13 minutes during Saturday's 129-105 preseason win over the Raptors.
items.story: Mitchell drew the start at point guard alongside Klay Thompson, Andrew Wiggins, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, and the entire starting unit was limited to first-half action. The 28-year-old appears to have the inside track on the starting point guard job after averaging 9.3 points and 6.5 assists across 28.6 minutes per game during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Mitchell could be in line for a larger role after Miami traded Tyler Herro in the deal for Giannis Antetokounmpo, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sentinel reports.
items.story: With the Heat expected to lean on Mitchell as a primary backcourt facilitator, he'll have the opportunity to capitalize on the attention Antetokounmpo commands offensively. However, Mitchell's fantasy value will likely hinge on whether he can provide enough scoring to complement his defensive impact. Over 70 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, he averaged 9.3 points, 6.5 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals while shooting 49.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Mitchell amassed 28 points (12-24 FG, 4-9 3Pt), six assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block across 48 minutes in Tuesday's 127-126 overtime loss to the Hornets in the Play-In Tournament.
items.story: Mitchell turned in an efficient performance and led Miami in scoring, albeit in a season-ending loss. The 27-year-old point guard also paced the team in steals. The Baylor product delivered a productive campaign on both ends of the floor as a regular starter for Miami. Over 70 regular-season appearances (all starts), he averaged 9.3 points, 6.5 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals while shooting 49.0 percent from the field and 39.5 percent from downtown in 28.6 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Mitchell chipped in 12 points (5-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 26 minutes during Sunday's 143-117 victory over the Hawks.
items.story: Mitchell converted both of his three-point attempts, ripped away a steal and committed only one turnover in his 26 minutes of floor time. The 27-year-old point guard will end the season with averages of 9.3 points, 6.5 assists (career-high), 1.3 triples and 1.0 steals per game on 49/39/65 shooting splits.

items.headline: Mitchell (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Hawks.
items.story: Mitchell is set to return after a one-game absence, which will likely push Kasparas Jakucionis back to the second unit. Jahmir Young could drop from the rotation entirely with Mitchell active.

items.headline: Mitchell (shoulder) is listed as out for Friday's game against Washington.
items.story: Mitchell logged 37 minutes in Thursday's 128-114 loss to Toronto, finishing with 15 points, three rebounds and 11 assists. With Mitchell now ruled out for the second game of a back-to-back, Kasparas Jakucionis will likely enter the starting lineup and handle things at the point guard position against one of the worst defensive clubs in the league.

items.headline: Mitchell (shoulder) is questionable for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Mitchell may be held out for maintenance for the second leg of this back-to-back set. If Mitchell ends up sitting, the Heat could turn to rookie Kasparas Jakucionis.

items.headline: Mitchell recorded 15 points (7-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-4 FT), 11 assists and three rebounds over 37 minutes during the Heat's 128-114 loss to the Raptors on Thursday.
items.story: Mitchell dished six of his team-high 11 dimes in the third quarter to help the Heat cut their deficit to single digits, and he finished tied for the second-most points on the team behind Bam Adebayo (24). It was the ninth time this season that Mitchell recorded 10 or more assists in a game this season (and first since Feb. 3) en route to his fifth double-double of the 2025-26 campaign. He has averaged 14.3 points, 7.5 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 2.0 steals over 31.6 minutes per game since April 1.

items.headline: Mitchell notched 21 points (8-15 FG, 5-10 3Pt), two rebounds and seven assists in 40 minutes during Wednesday's 147-129 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: This was Mitchell's best scoring line of the season, beating his previous mark of 18 points set against the Knicks on Nov. 17. With 66 games played, Mitchell is on pace to finish just outside the top-150 players in nine-category formats with 9.2 points, 6.5 assists, 2.7 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 1.3 three-pointers.

items.headline: Mitchell had 12 points (5-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Sunday's 135-118 loss to Indiana.
items.story: This was a strong effort from Mitchell, but the Heat were unable to grab this win against the struggling Pacers and fell to 39-36 on the season. Mitchell is on pace to finish just outside the top-150 players in nine-category formats on a per-game basis with 9.0 points, 6.5 assists, 2.7 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 1.2 three-pointers.

items.headline: Mitchell ended Wednesday's 120-103 win over the Cavaliers with 11 points (4-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 32 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell saw another sizable workload in the win, although his usage was relatively low. Across his last 11 games, he's returning 11th-round value in nine-category formats with 10.0 points, 5.0 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 1.4 three-pointers.

items.headline: Mitchell accumulated 16 points (7-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt), three rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Thursday's 134-126 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Although Mitchell has lost out on some playmaking chances since Tyler Herro returned, the former is beginning to pick things up a bit in the scoring department. Mitchell has averaged 11.8 points, 5.0 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 27.0 minutes per tilt in his last five games, shooting 55.8 percent from the floor during this stretch.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Thursday's 112-105 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Mitchell got back on track from beyond the arc after going 0-for-5 in his previous two appearances. He enjoyed an efficient performance in the win, needing only nine attempts from the field to score in double figures. The Baylor product has scored in double digits in three of his last four outings and is averaging 5.3 assists and 5.3 rebounds over that span.

items.headline: Mitchell had 12 points (5-9 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 150-129 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Mitchell has shown the ability to stuff the stat sheet, but his fantasy upside has decreased a bit, even though he remains a regular starter for the Heat. Mitchell has scored in double digits in just three of his nine appearances since the All-Star break, but two of those have come in his last three games.

items.headline: Mitchell finished Friday's 128-120 victory over the Hornets with 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-4 3Pt), two rebounds and seven assists over 27 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell had been held to single digits in the scoring column in each of the past two games, but he got hot from three-point range Friday to break back into double figures. He also did a nice job making LaMelo Ball work for his buckets, holding Charlotte's star to 21 points on 7-for-22 shooting. The Heat will need a similar effort from Mitchell on Sunday against the Pistons if they hope to keep their four-game winning streak going.

items.headline: Mitchell (shoulder) is available for Tuesday's game against Brooklyn, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Mitchell was added to the injury report ahead of Tuesday's clash due to a bruised left shoulder, but it won't force him to miss any action. The Baylor product will look to begin March on a high note after averaging 8.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 5.7 assists over 10 February appearances.

items.headline: Mitchell is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Nets with a bruised left shoulder.
items.story: Mitchell participated in Monday's practice, which is an encouraging sign for his status. In the event that the point guard cannot suit up Tuesday, fantasy managers could turn to Pelle Larsson as a streamer in shallow leagues and Kasparas Jakucionis in deeper settings.

items.headline: Mitchell (shoulder) was able to practice Monday, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Mitchell suffered a left shoulder contusion in Saturday's win over the Rockets, and that's notable because he battled a left shoulder injury earlier this season. It sounds like he's day-to-day, and his status for Tuesday's game versus Brooklyn will be established Monday afternoon or evening when the team releases its injury report.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is available for Thursday's game against the 76ers, per Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald.
items.story: Mitchell is playing through an illness, and there's no indication he'll be limited in any way Thursday. Across his last eight appearances, the fifth-year point guard has averaged 8.9 points, 6.3 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.5 three-pointers in 27.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is questionable for Thursday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Mitchell was able to play through a questionable tag Tuesday against the Bucks, finishing with nine points, eight assists and six rebounds in 28 minutes. If he's unable to play Thursday, the Heat will likely lean on Kasparas Jakucionis and Dru Smith.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Mitchell will return from a one-game absence due to an illness. As a result, Kasparas Jakucionis is expected to retreat to the bench. Over seven February appearances, Mitchell has averaged 9.0 points, 6.0 assists and 2.1 rebounds in 27.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Mitchell was previously listed as questionable, but it appears likely that he will return from a one-game absence. With this news, the Heat won't have to rely on Kasparas Jakucionis and Dru Smith as much.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Bucks, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Mitchell remains day-to-day after missing Saturday's game against Memphis. If he's unable to play, the Heat will likely rely on rookie first-rounder Kasparas Jakucionis and Dru Smith.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is out for Saturday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Mitchell played through a head illness in Friday's win over the Hawks, but he won't be able to suit up in the second leg of this back-to-back set. His absence could lead to a spot start for rookie first-rounder Kasparas Jakucionis, while Dru Smith could see more minutes off the bench as well. Mitchell will aim to return to the hardwood when the Heat take on the Bucks on Tuesday. Feb. 24.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is listed as doubtful for Saturday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Mitchell was able to play through a head illness during the Heat's 128-97 win over the Hawks on Friday, when he logged seven points, seven assists, five rebounds, three blocks and one steal over 27 minutes. It appears the illness will prevent Mitchell from playing in the second leg of Miami's back-to-back set Saturday, and his absence will likely result in rookie first-rounder Kasparas Jakucionis being moved into the starting lineup against Memphis.

items.headline: Mitchell recorded seven points (3-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven assists, five rebounds, three blocks and one steal across 27 minutes during Friday's 128-97 victory over the Hawks.
items.story: Mitchell was a late addition to the injury report Friday due to an illness but was ultimately cleared to play in the front end of this back-to-back set. After averaging 4.3 assists per game over his previous three outings, the 27-year-old point guard dished out a team-high seven dimes against Atlanta. Additionally, he swatted multiple shots for the first time this season and set a career high in blocks. Mitchell isn't guaranteed to score in double figures on a nightly basis, though he typically offers value through his assist numbers. Aside from his three blocks Friday, the Baylor product hasn't recorded many defensive stats of late, and he has totaled just two steals over his last six appearances.

items.headline: Mitchell (illness) is in the starting lineup for Friday's game in Atlanta.
items.story: Mitchell is feeling a bit under the weather, but he'll power through and get out there for Friday's game. Joining him in the first unit will be Andrew Wiggins, Norman Powell, Pelle Larsson and Bam Adebayo.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner closed with six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Kalkbrenner has played fewer than 20 minutes in three consecutive games, averaging 4.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks during that stretch. The second-year center has taken a backseat to Moussa Diabate, who logged 38 minutes Tuesday, significantly limiting Kalkbrenner's opportunities. His shot-blocking ability provides some appeal in deeper category leagues, but his reduced playing time makes him difficult to trust.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner isn't starting Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Kalkbrenner started Charlotte's previous two games, but he'll return to his usual bench role Thursday due to Moussa Diabate returning from a quad injury. Kalkbrenner is averaging 4.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.0 blocks in his last four appearances as a reserve.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner racked up eight points (4-7 FG), 15 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal in 35 minutes during Monday's 124-112 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: It was a banner evening for the second-year big man, who recorded a career-high 15 rebounds and swatted a season-most three shots. Kalkbrenner functions as a strict reserve when Moussa Diabate (quadriceps) is healthy, but the former should retain enhanced fantasy appeal while the latter is injured.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner is starting Friday's game against Boston.
items.story: Kalkbrenner is getting a spot start at center for the injured Moussa Diabate (quadriceps) on Friday. He makes sense as a plug-and-play fantasy option in the short term.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner provided one point (1-2 FT), one rebound, one assist, one block and one steal in 13 minutes during Wednesday's 97-89 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Kalkbrenner played a limited role off the bench, attempting no field goals while contributing modest defensive production. Moussa Diabate handled the bulk of the minutes at center, logging 35 minutes compared to Kalkbrenner's 13. The second-year big man's restricted workload makes him difficult to trust in standard fantasy formats, though his shot-blocking ability could provide some value in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner ended with four points (2-3 FG), five rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 14 minutes during Wednesday's 110-103 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: Kalkbrenner lost the starting center job midway through last year, and his reserve position is carrying into the new campaign. The second-year big man is likely to struggle for fantasy viability as long as Moussa Diabate is dominating the center minutes.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner is in the Hornets' starting lineup for Friday's preseason game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Kalkbrenner will draw the start for Friday's preseason finale while Moussa Diabate (elbow) is sidelined. Across three preseason games, Kalkbrenner has averaged 4.3 points and 3.3 rebounds over 15.4 minutes per game. It's unclear what his role will look like for the 2026-27 season given the presence of both Diabate and rookie first-rounder Hannes Steinbach.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner finished with four points (2-2 FG) and five rebounds in 12 minutes during Sunday's 105-90 preseason win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Kalkbrenner continued what has been a modest preseason, doing very little to endear himself to fantasy managers. It appears as though Moussa Diabate will retain the starting center position heading into the regular season. This means Kalkbrenner is likely to be up against Hannes Steinbach for backup minutes, limiting his appeal across all formats. For those in deeper leagues, Kalkbrenner should be seen as a potential streaming option for blocks.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner said Monday that improving his physicality was his biggest developmental focus during the offseason, Owen O'Connor of SI.com reports.
items.story: Physicality was already an area in which Kalkbrenner made noticeable strides during his rookie campaign, particularly absorbing contact defensively and setting screens. The 7-foot-1 center averaged 7.6 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 21.4 minutes across 69 regular-season appearances last campaign, and further improvement in that area could help him earn additional playing time in Charlotte's frontcourt. His competition is much fiercer this season due to the additions of Hannes Steinbach, Naz Reid and Royce O'Neale.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner finished with 10 points (5-7 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 0-2 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and three blocks in 30 minutes during Thursday's 86-74 Summer League win over the Magic.
items.story: The second-year center was dominant defensively and controlled the paint throughout the contest, finishing one rebound shy of a double-double while showcasing the passing ability that Charlotte hopes will complement his elite rim protection. The problem with Kalkbrenner's fantasy appeal is that he has to compete with Hannes Steinbach and Moussa Diabate for minutes.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner could face increased competition for frontcourt minutes after Charlotte acquired Naz Reid as part of the LaMelo Ball trade, according to Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports.
items.story: The second-year center enters a rotation that already includes Reid, Moussa Diabate and other young big men competing for reserve roles, including 2026 lottery pick Hannes Steinbach. While Kalkbrenner's rim protection and interior defense should help him earn opportunities, his playing time could be volatile based on matchups. His long-term outlook remains promising, but consistent minutes may not be as straightforward as originally thought.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner produced two points (0-3 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block over 18 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Kalkbrenner had a muted impact on the offensive end during Friday's season-ending loss, failing to score in double figures for a 13th straight game. The rookie second-rounder began the 2025-26 campaign in a starting role but suffered a sprained left elbow in late December and lost his spot in the starting lineup when he returned Jan. 10. Kalkbrenner appeared in 69 regular-season appearances (31 starts), averaging 7.6 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.5 blocks, 0.8 assists and 0.5 steals while shooting 75.3 percent from the field in 21.4 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner produced nine points (4-4 FG, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 21 minutes during Sunday's 110-96 victory over New York.
items.story: Kalkbrenner continues to serve as the backup center, a role that has yielded very little in terms of viable fantasy production. In 15 games over the past month, he has averaged just 6.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 18.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner won't start in Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Kalkbrenner started in place of Moussa Diabate in Friday's 129-108 win over the Pacers. However, with Diabate returning from his one-game absence caused by an ankle injury, Kalkbrenner will head back to the bench.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner will start Friday's game against Indiana.
items.story: With Moussa Diabate (ankle) out, Kalkbrenner will enter the starting lineup for the first time since Feb. 22. As a starter this season (30 games), the rookie second-rounder has averaged 8.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 25.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner posted eight points (3-4 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one block over 18 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 win over the Nets.
items.story: Kalkbrenner continues to play a backup role, which, to this point has yielded very little in terms of fantasy production. In 14 appearances over the past month, he has barely been a top-200 player, averaging 6.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game. At best, he can be streamed for blocks when the schedule works in his favor.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner supplied 13 points (5-5 FG, 3-3 FT) and five rebounds in 24 minutes during Thursday's 130-111 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Kalkbrenner was perfect from both the field and the charity stripe, bringing his season field goal percentage to an impressive 74.6 percent. The rookie center saw 24 minutes of action, marking his highest playing time in a single game since he moved into the starting lineup for an injured Moussa Diabate back on Feb. 20. Kalkbrenner continues to provide steady interior depth for Charlotte, and over his last eight appearances, he is averaging 7.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.6 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (illness) is listed as available for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: The rookie center will return after a one-game absence and should reclaim his reserve role behind Moussa Diabate, likely pushing Xavier Tillman out of the rotation. Over his last eight appearances, Kalkbrenner has provided steady rim protection and efficiency, averaging 5.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks in 16.1 minutes per contest during that span.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (illness) is probable to play Saturday in San Antonio.
items.story: It looks like Kalkbrenner will be back in action Saturday following a one-game absence, which will likely result in Xavier Tillman dropping back out of the rotation. Kalkbrenner is averaging 8.0 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (illness) won't play in Wednesday's game against Sacramento, per the FanDuel Sports Network broadcast.
items.story: Kalkbrenner was a late addition to the injury report Wednesday evening before being cleared to play. However, the rookie center will wind up being unavailable for the contest due to illness. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Spurs. Moussa Diabate and Xavier Tillman will likely handle most of the center duties Wednesday.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (illness) is listed as available for Wednesday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Kalkbrenner was added to the injury report Wednesday evening due to an illness, but the rookie center has been upgraded to available for the contest. In his last eight appearances, Kalkbrenner is averaging 5.9 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.5 blocks over 16.1 minutes.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (illness) is now probable for Wednesday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Kalkbrenner is a late add to the injury report Wednesday, as the rookie big man is feeling under the weather. While he's still likely to play, fantasy managers should keep an eye on his status leading up to the 10:00pm ET tipoff.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner closed with 13 points (6-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 17 minutes during Tuesday's 103-101 win over Portland.
items.story: This was a strong showing for the rookie, but his workload again paled in comparison to Moussa Diabate. Until this position battle shifts towards Kalkbrenner, he's going to remain a deep-league fantasy option at best.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner totaled six points (3-4 FG), two rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 14 minutes during Wednesday's 118-89 win over the Celtics.
items.story: Kalkbrenner continues to play a limited role as the backup center, having logged fewer than 19 minutes in six straight games. Charlotte has won 16 of its past 19 games, with Moussa Diabate playing a huge part in the recent success. With Diabate seemingly locked in as the starter, Kalkbrenner should be viewed as nothing more than a blocks streamer.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner will move to the bench Tuesday against the Bulls.
items.story: This is an expected move with Moussa Diabate and Miles Bridges back from their suspensions. Kalkbrenner is likely to maintain a sizable role with the second unit, to be clear.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: A sprained left ankle won't stop Kalkbrenner from playing Tuesday, but the expectation is that the returning Moussa Diabate (suspension) is going to replace Kalkbrenner in the starting lineup.
