Kalkbrenner has started four consecutive games, averaging 8.8 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.8 blocks in 26.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner is probable for Tuesday's game against the Bulls with a sprained left ankle.
items.story: The rookie big man picked up the issue in Sunday's game against the Wizards, but it appears to be of minimal concern. Moussa Diabate is set to return from suspension Tuesday, which is likely to send Kalkbrenner to the bench. Kalkbrenner has started four straight games, averaging 8.8 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.8 blocks in 26.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner (ankle) is available to return to Sunday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Kalkbrenner sustained a left ankle sprain during the third quarter of Sunday's contest, but the team announced that he is available to return to the game. With the Hornets sporting a large lead, it remains to be seen whether he returns to action or not.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner went back to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Wizards with an apparent ankle injury, Roderick Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Kalkbrenner appeared to roll his ankle before heading to the locker room during the third quarter of Sunday's contest. If he is unable to return, PJ Hall and Xavier Tillman could see extra minutes.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner registered 12 points (5-7 FG, 2-2 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist and one block over 36 minutes during the Hornets' 118-113 loss to the Cavaliers on Friday.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder finished as the Hornets' leading rebounder (including a career-high nine offensive boards) en route to the third double-double of the season (and first since Nov. 3 against the Pelicans). Kalkbrenner has started in each of the Hornets' last three games and should serve in that role against the Wizards on Sunday, though he'll likely revert to a bench role against the Bulls on Tuesday since Moussa Diabate will have served his four-game suspension.

items.headline: Kalkbrenner is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Hawks.
items.story: Kalkbrenner is getting the start due to Moussa Diabate (suspension) being unavailable, and the former will be joined in the first unit by LaMelo Ball, Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams. Over 26 starts this season, Kalkbrenner has registered averages of 8.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game.

items.headline: Fears racked up 29 points (9-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 9-10 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two steals and five turnovers across 34 minutes in Saturday's 114-91 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: This was Fears' second straight 20-plus-point performance, and it was nice to see him chip in some defensive stats after he had failed to record any in his previous outings. However, he again struggled with turnovers, and over the past three games he's committed 13 total giveaways. That's coincided with three straight losses for the Pelicans, so he'll need to do a better job of valuing their possessions to give his team its best chance of snapping the three-game skid Monday versus Phoenix.

items.headline: Fears totaled 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one block over 38 minutes during Friday's 126-120 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Fears tied Zion Williamson for the team lead in scoring and tied his season high in minutes. The finish was rough: Jared McCain blocked his driving layup, and his three-point attempt to cut the deficit to one fell short. With Dejounte Murray (ankle) still sidelined, the second-year guard is running the offense full-time and averaging 15.6 points and 5.4 assists.

items.headline: Fears finished with 16 points (6-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Fears was unable to finish the game after fouling out, but the second-year floor general posted an impressive stat line that included two defensive contributions. Fears is locked in as the Pelicans' starting point guard more than ever after Dejounte Murray asked for a trade, and he's averaging 17.1 points, 5.2 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game since the beginning of November.

items.headline: Fears registered 19 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 10 rebounds and 10 assists across 29 minutes in Monday's 115-94 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Fears put together a memorable performance, recording the first triple-double of his young career in a winning effort. After scoring in single digits in the first two games of the campaign, the guard has reached double figures in 13 straight contests. Overall, Fears is averaging 15.5 points, 5.5 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals while starting all 15 games this season.

items.headline: Fears tallied 14 points (6-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four rebounds and five assists across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 145-111 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Fears delivered efficient scoring and solid playmaking despite New Orleans' lopsided defeat. His five assists were encouraging, but four turnovers and a lack of defensive stats reduced his overall fantasy value. Despite the Pelicans' struggles, Fears has posted solid numbers overall as a scoring threat -- he's posted double-digit points in each of his last 10 games while averaging 16.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Fears registered 25 points (10-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals across 29 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: The second-year guard set a new season scoring high as he delivered at least 20 points for the fourth time in the last six games. Fears has seemingly found his groove in his sophomore campaign, and over that six-game stretch the seventh overall pick in the 2025 Draft is averaging 20.3 points, 6.5 assists, 5.7 boards, 1.5 steals and 1.3 threes while shooting 52.7 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Fears finished with 24 points (9-16 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-7 FT), five rebounds, five assists and two steals over 36 minutes in Friday's 115-109 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Fears not only led his team in points Friday, but he also recorded a season high in scoring while hitting the 20-point mark for the third time in his last five appearances. He hasn't been consistent shooting the ball, and turnovers have also been an issue at times. However, the 20-year-old has played well overall, now averaging 15.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.1 steals across 28.9 minutes per contest in nine regular-season games.

items.headline: Fears contributed 12 points (5-17 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and seven assists over 38 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime victory over Memphis.
items.story: Fears logged a season-high 38 minutes, helping New Orleans to its third straight win. With Dejounte Murray sidelined once again due to personal reasons, Fears assumed the role of lead facilitator, recording at least seven assists for the third straight game. In four appearances over the past week, he has been a borderline top-80 player, averaging 12.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.9 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.3 three-pointers in 30.5 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Fears posted 20 points (9-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven assists, five rebounds and one steal over 31 minutes during the Pelicans' 121-99 win over the Hawks on Saturday.
items.story: Fears filled up the box score for a second consecutive game, leading the Pelicans in assists while finishing as the team's second-leading scorer behind Saddiq Bey (25 points). Fears struggled with his shot over his first four games of the 2026-27 regular season, but he's gone 18-for-28 (64.3 percent) from the field over his last two outings, including 4-for-7 from three-point range. The second-year pro is trending in the right direction and will have momentum on his side heading into Monday's road tilt against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Fears finished Thursday's 132-120 win over the Kings with 22 points (9-16 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-3 FT), 13 assists, eight rebounds, four blocks and two steals over 29 minutes.
items.story: Fears entered Thursday's game having connected on only 31.1 percent of his field-goal attempts (including 18.8 percent from three-point range) through his first four outings of the regular season. The second-year guard was more efficient against Sacramento. He scored 16 of his team-high 22 points across the second and third quarters, and his 13 assists were a career high. It was the first double-double of Fears' NBA career, and he was two boards shy from logging his first triple-double. His production floor could be lower against the Hawks on Saturday depending on the statuses of Jordan Poole (ankle) and Dejounte Murray (personal).

items.headline: Fears finished with 11 points (5-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and a steal across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Fears is enduring a rough start to the season, with this 11-point outing being his best scoring output of the campaign so far. Through four contests, the second-year floor general is averaging just 9.0 points per game while shooting a dismal 31.1 percent from the floor and 18.8 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Fears will start Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Fears got the starting nod in New Orleans' preseason finale and will remain in the first unit over Herbert Jones on Wednesday. Over 49 regular-season starts in his rookie season, Fears averaged 15.3 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.3 steals across 27.6 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: The Pelicans exercised the $8.27 million third-year team option on Fears' contract Tuesday, Terry Kimble of SI.com reports.
items.story: Fears is now on the books through the 2027-28 season. The young point guard had some impressive showings during his rookie season, but as long as he's operating in a reserve role behind a healthy Dejounte Murray, his upside will be limited in Year 2.

items.headline: Fears tallied 14 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, five assists and three steals in 22 minutes in Friday's 107-106 preseason win over the Wizards.
items.story: Fears tied for the team lead in steals and reached double figures in scoring for the fourth time in as many preseason games. The second-year guard averaged 13.3 points this exhibition season in a starting role. Dejounte Murray (toe) sat out Friday's finale, which gave Fears even more time with the ball in his hands.

items.headline: Fears chipped in 16 points (6-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five assists, three rebounds and three steals across 20 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Fears led New Orleans in points, assists and steals as the Pelicans held on for a narrow victory. The 20-year-old has scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances after averaging 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.2 steals across 82 regular-season games (49 starts) as a rookie in 2025-26. How Fears coexists with Dejounte Murray (toe) over a full campaign and how the point-guard duties are divided will be a storyline to monitor as the regular season approaches.

items.headline: Fears recorded 11 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 19 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Fears drew the start at point guard and delivered an efficient scoring performance, although he committed three turnovers. The second-year guard showed encouraging perimeter shooting and should remain in the mix for backcourt minutes, but competition from Dejounte Murray (rest) and Jordan Poole could limit his opportunities once the regular season begins.

items.headline: Fears is in the starting lineup for Thursday's preseason game against the Heat.
items.story: Fears is getting the nod at point guard as the Pelicans are changing their lineup again for this preseason contest. The former Oklahoma star is coming off a rookie season in which he averaged 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game across 82 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Fears finished with 12 points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 17 minutes during Tuesday's 116-110 preseason win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Fears provided an efficient scoring punch off the bench and committed only one turnover. The second-year guard should remain a significant part of New Orleans' backcourt rotation after showing considerable promise as a rookie.

items.headline: Fears is set to share the second unit with Bennedict Mathurin in 2026-27.
items.story: The Pelicans bolstered their bench with Wednesday's signing of Mathurin, who is expected to help lead New Orleans' second unit alongside Fears in the backcourt. Over 82 regular-season games in 2025-26, Fears averaged 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 25.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Fears enjoyed an outstanding rookie season, appearing in all 82 regular-season games while averaging 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.4 assists.
items.story: Fears capped the year by setting the franchise rookie scoring record with a 40-point performance and enters 2026-27 as one of New Orleans' most promising young guards. Even with Dejounte Murray expected back, Fears has positioned himself for a significant role in the Pelicans' backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Fears totaled 36 points (12-28 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 12-14 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block across 41 minutes during Sunday's 132-126 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Fears continued his strong scoring stretch to close the regular season, scoring exactly 36 points for the second straight game. His usage spiked over the past three contests, averaging 28.7 field-goal attempts after not reaching the 20-attempt mark in any prior game. The No. 7 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft will close his rookie campaign averaging 14.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.2 steals across 82 appearances (49 starts).

items.headline: Fears tallied 36 points (13-29 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 7-11 FT), six assists, three rebounds and three steals across 44 minutes in Friday's 144-118 loss to Boston.
items.story: After dropping a career-high 40 points in Tuesday's win over Utah, the rookie first-rounder turned in another impressive offensive showing Friday, though he was less efficient. Fears also led New Orleans in assists and steals and has tallied six dimes and three swipes in back-to-back outings. He'll likely continue to play a sizable role during Sunday's regular-season finale in Minnesota, as the Pelicans have little to play for at this point.

items.headline: Fears popped off for 40 points (17-29 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists and three steals over 38 minutes during Tuesday's 156-137 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Fears not only set a new career high in scoring, but he also established the Pelicans' single-game rookie scoring record in the blowout win. He became just the fifth rookie in the past decade to post a 40-5-5 line, and he only committed two turnovers in his 38 minutes of floor time.

items.headline: Fears recorded 19 points (4-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 9-11 FT), three rebounds, seven assists, one block and two steals over 37 minutes during Sunday's 112-108 loss to the Magic.
items.story: With Trey Murphy (ankle) and Dejounte Murray (hand) sidelined, Fears was able to play a featured role in the backcourt. Over his last seven games, he averaged 17.7 points, 4.4 assists, 3.1 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.1 three-pointers on 46.2 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Fears will start Sunday versus the Magic.
items.story: Fears is getting a spot start with Trey Murphy (ankle) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey, Zion Williamson and Yves Missi. As a starter this season, Fears has averaged 13.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.1 triples and 1.2 steals per contest.

items.headline: Fears amassed 28 points (10-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds and six assists in 37 minutes during Friday's 117-113 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Fears matched a 28-point effort that he also managed against the Kings a month ago. It took 11 more minutes on the court this time around, but he padded Friday's line with five more rebounds. The return of Dejounte Murray (Achilles) has cut into the rookie's production, but his proficiency at the off-guard position has offered additional opportunities. The Washington product has successfully fended off Jordan Poole on the depth chart, giving the Pelicans more flexibility to trade backcourt pieces in the offseason trade market.

items.headline: Fears contributed 21 points (7-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 26 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 118-106 loss to Portland.
items.story: The teenage rookie led the Pelicans in scoring as he continues to find some success from long range to close out the season. Over 16 games (one start) since the beginning of March, Fears has averaged 13.0 points, 3.3 assists, 2.4 boards, 1.6 threes and 0.8 steals in 21.9 minutes over that stretch while shooting 41.3 percent from beyond the arc, a big step up from the 32.4 percent mark he held heading into the All-Star break.

items.headline: Fears won't start in Sunday's game against Houston, according to Lachard Binkley of SI.com.
items.story: Dejounte Murray (hand) didn't suit up for Friday's 119-106 loss to Toronto. As a result, Fears entered the starting lineup, finishing with 10 points, four rebounds, three assists and one block across 27 minutes. However, with Murray cleared to return from his one-game absence, Fears will head back to the bench.

items.headline: Vassell finished with 10 points (2-7 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 26 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: Vassell struggled to find his shooting touch, but the Spurs didn't need him to deliver a big performance in a game where Victor Wembanyama's 50-point explosion carried San Antonio's offense. Vassell remains an important perimeter scoring option, though his fantasy production can fluctuate when the Spurs lean heavily on their other offensive weapons, as his role is mostly secondary. He has scored in double digits in his last three appearances, but he's also reached the 15-point plateau just four times all season long.

items.headline: Vassell provided 15 points (6-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals over 32 minutes during Thursday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Vassell's three steals were a welcome addition to a balanced performance. Even though he's a secondary scoring option, Vassell remains an important part of the Spurs' starting lineup, and his ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him ways to stay productive. Vassell has scored in double digits in five of his eight appearances since the beginning of November, but he's averaging just 10.9 points per game in that span while shooting 40.5 percent from the field and 30.3 percent from deep.

items.headline: Vassell provided 12 points (4-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Vassell had one of his better showings of late after struggling through a cold stretch in his previous two games. His outside shot has been inconsistent all season, and he is hitting just over 31 percent from deep. San Antonio leans on him as a two-way wing, and his perimeter defense keeps him on the floor even when his shot isn't falling.

items.headline: Vassell (groin) is available for Friday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Vassell has been cleared to suit up and should provide San Antonio with a reliable perimeter scoring option against the Warriors. Through 10 games, he's averaging 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists.

items.headline: Vassell is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left adductor tightness.
items.story: Vassell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence with the issue. Julian Champagnie would likely draw a third straight start at power forward for the Spurs on Friday if Vassell is unable to play.

items.headline: Vassell (adductor) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Bulls, Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio reports.
items.story: Wednesday marks a second consecutive absence for Vassell due to an adductor injury. His void in the starting lineup paves the way for Julian Champagnie to draw a second straight start on the wing for the Spurs.

items.headline: Vassell (groin) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Bulls, NBA reporter Matthew Tynan reports.
items.story: Vassell missed his first game of the season in Monday's 122-96 victory over the Suns. As a result, Julian Champagnie entered the starting lineup. If Vassell remains sidelined against the Bulls, Champagnie is expected to stay with the first five.

items.headline: Vassell (groin) is out for Monday's game against the Suns, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Vassell was unable to shake his questionable tag and will be considered day-to-day going forward. In his absence, the Spurs may lean more on Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson and Carter Bryant.

items.headline: Vassell is questionable for Monday's game against the Suns due to left adductor tightness.
items.story: Vassell could miss his first game this season. If he is unable to go, Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson and Carter Bryant could see extra minutes.

items.headline: Vassell registered 15 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals across 21 minutes in Saturday's 125-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Vassell made the most of his limited opportunities, combining efficient shooting with playmaking and defensive contributions. He remains a valuable source of perimeter scoring for the Spurs, but his fantasy ceiling depends on receiving a more substantial workload. Currently, he's a secondary scoring option behind the likes of Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle.

items.headline: Vassell produced 19 points (6-10 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 26 minutes during Friday's 124-109 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Vassell was red-hot from the outside, hitting five of his six three-point attempts and tying Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper for second on the team in scoring behind Victor Wembanyama. He came out firing early, knocking down three triples in the first quarter as San Antonio built a lead it never gave up.

items.headline: Vassell amassed 11 points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 25 minutes during Monday's 119-97 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Vassell finished in double figures but offered little additional production, failing to connect from beyond the arc for the first time in three games. San Antonio's balanced offensive attack limited his opportunities, with Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and Keldon Johnson all scoring more points. Vassell remains a regular starter, though his relatively modest usage and limited peripheral contributions can lead to underwhelming fantasy performances.

items.headline: Vassell racked up 21 points (8-18 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three steals in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime win over Utah.
items.story: Vassell overcame a slow start, scoring 17 of his 21 points after halftime to help San Antonio erase an 11-point deficit. Although he struggled from beyond the arc, the veteran wing contributed three steals while logging a season-high 38 minutes. His substantial playing time and scoring involvement remain encouraging for his fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Vassell supplied 14 points (5-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt), four rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 win over the Kings.
items.story: Vassell stuffed the stat sheet in just 24 minutes of action, as he finished with a team-high eight assists in the lopsided victory. He's now had at least six dimes in two consecutive games, showing improved playmaking chops for the 2-2 Spurs. With Tobias Harris (calf) still working towards his season debut, Vassell should continue operating as the starting power forward.

items.headline: Vassell provided seven points (2-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Vassell drew the start and played the fourth-most minutes for San Antonio, but he struggled to find his rhythm offensively. The veteran wing went scoreless from beyond the arc on three of his four attempts and failed to record a defensive statistic. With Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and De'Aaron Fox all playing prominent offensive roles, Vassell may face increased competition for shot attempts this season.

items.headline: Vassell tallied 12 points (5-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Vassell was back in action Wednesday after resting for each of the Spurs' last two exhibition games, and the seventh-year pro led the team in steals while finishing second in rebounds and fifth in scoring. Vassell's offensive ceiling figures to remain low while sharing the court with Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle and others, but that allowed Vassell to thrive in a complementary role during the Spurs' run to the NBA Finals last year. Friday's contest against the Kings is the Spurs' last preseason game before they kick off their regular season Tuesday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Vassell (rest) will play Wednesday against the Suns, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Vassell is back in action after missing the Spurs' last exhibition for maintenance reasons. He's starting in place of the injured Tobias Harris (calf) on Wednesday.

items.headline: Vassell (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against Utah, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News.
items.story: Vassell is joining the rest of San Antonio's usual starters on the sidelines Monday. His next chance to suit up arrives Wednesday against Phoenix.

items.headline: Vassell registered 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 18 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Vassell was efficient during his limited playing time. The veteran wing helped San Antonio build a commanding first-half advantage before the starters rested, and his combination of perimeter shooting and two-way production should remain an important part of the Spurs' rotation. Unless something dramatic happens in the Spurs' camp over the next two weeks, Vassell should open the 2026-27 regular season as San Antonio's starting small forward.

items.headline: Vassell has been working on getting downhill and finishing through contact ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, Cory Mose of KVUE News reports Saturday.
items.story: Vassell scored a career-high 53.4 percent of his points from beyond the arc in 2025-26, averaging 13.9 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 0.9 steals across 30.5 minutes per game in 67 regular-season appearances (65 starts). Just 42.8 percent of his shot attempts came from two-point range, marking a career low after he finished above 50.2 percent in each of his previous five seasons. Vassell may look to increase his two-point volume while applying more pressure at the rim as he continues playing a sizable role for a San Antonio squad aiming to get back to the NBA Finals.

items.headline: Vassell produced 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 39 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to New York in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Vassell turned in an efficient performance in Saturday's season-ending loss and finished as San Antonio's fourth-leading scorer. The 25-year-old swingman also supplied at least three combined steals-plus-blocks for the ninth time across 23 playoff appearances. Vassell started 65 of his 67 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, averaging 13.9 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 0.9 steals across 30.5 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Vassell contributed 14 points (4-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and one block in 38 minutes during Friday's 105-104 loss to New York in Game 2 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Vassell continues to play well on both ends of the floor, providing solid yet modest production. In 14 playoff appearances over the past month, he has averaged 12.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.5 three-pointers. Having lost both games at home, San Antonio will now head to New York for Games 3 and 4 looking to extend the series beyond four games.

items.headline: Vassell notched 22 points (7-14 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one block across 38 minutes during Wednesday's 122-113 loss to the Thunder in Game 2 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Vassell was one of three Spurs to eclipse 20 points, joining Victor Wembanyama (21) and Stephon Castle (25). Vassell has been solid through 13 postseason appearances, posting averages of 13.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 0.9 blocks and 1.2 steals.

items.headline: Vassell amassed 14 points (5-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals over 36 minutes during Monday's 104-102 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Vassell has been a steady contributor for the Spurs this postseason, scoring in double figures and posting at least one swat in all six games so far. The swingman has averaged 12.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.2 blocks in 34.2 minutes per contest during the 2026 playoffs.

items.headline: Vassell amassed 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 35 minutes during Sunday's 114-93 win over Portland in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The Spurs continue to rely heavily on their starters as they surged to a 3-1 series lead. Vassell has struggled a bit from beyond the arc, but he's averaging 13.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.5 steals through four postseason games.

items.headline: Vassell closed Tuesday's 106-103 Game 2 loss to the Trail Blazers with 16 points (6-16 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 12 rebounds, three steals, two assists and one block across 34 minutes.
items.story: Vassell struggled from three-point range but still finished as San Antonio's third-leading scorer. Including the regular season, the 25-year-old wing grabbed a season- and career-high 12 boards and recorded his second double-double on the campaign. He also tied the game-high mark in steals and has tallied two combined steals-plus-blocks in each of the first two games of this first-round series.

items.headline: Shead posted 13 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven assists, four rebounds and two steals over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 win over Orlando.
items.story: Shead's 13 points led all Raptors bench players Wednesday, and his seven dimes were tied with Immanuel Quickley for most on the team. It was Shead's first double-digit scoring effort of the season, and he'll continue to lead Toronto's second unit as the backup to Quickley.

items.headline: Shead (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener versus Chicago.
items.story: Shead sat out Friday's preseason finale but isn't dealing with an injury ahead of the regular-season opener. He's expected to operate as Immanuel Quickley's primary backup in 2026-27.

items.headline: Shead will not play in Friday's preseason finale against the Pistons, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Toronto's regulars are getting the night off to rest up before Wednesday's season opener against the Bulls. Shead is expected to play a backup point guard role to begin the campaign.

items.headline: Shead finished with four points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists, two steals, two blocks and one rebound in 21 minutes during Thursday's 122-120 preseason loss to New York.
items.story: Despite continued shooting woes, Shead got it done on the defensive end of the floor, racking up four combined steals and blocks. Although he managed to finally land a three-pointer, it would appear as though anyone considering Shead with a flier pick in drafts shouldn't be hoping for too much in terms of offensive output. At best, he could be utilized as a steals specialist, with some upside in assists.

items.headline: Shead registered 13 points (5-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two assists, one rebound and two steals in 19 minutes during Saturday's 114-106 preseason win over the Clippers.
items.story: Shead was more efficient than he was during the preseason opener, but he still failed to hit a three-pointer, making him 0-for-6 from behind the arc through two games. While Shead is slated for a backup role behind Immanuel Quickley, his defensive presence off the bench will be a key part of the Raptors' success this season.

items.headline: Shead finished Saturday's 129-105 preseason loss to the Heat with three points (1-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block in 28 minutes.
items.story: Shead struggled mightily with efficiency in Toronto's preseason opener, though he chipped in across the stat sheet. The 24-year-old point guard led all players in assists while tying for second on the Raptors in rebounds. Shead signed a three-year extension with Toronto on Thursday and figures to continue operating as Immanuel Quickley's primary backup.

items.headline: Shead and the Raptors agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Raptors have now secured their backup point guard through the 2029-30 season. Last regular season, Shead averaged 6.6 points, 5.4 assists and 1.7 rebounds in 22.6 minutes per game across 82 outings (12 starts). He's poised for a similar role in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Raptors exercised the $2.3 million team option on Shead on Thursday for the 2026-27 season, per Michael Scotto of USA Today.
items.story: Shead is all set to reprise his role as the primary backup point guard behind Immanuel Quickley (hamstring), though Ja'Kobe Walter is also in the mix to compete for reserve minutes. Last regular season, Shead averaged 6.6 points, 5.4 assists and 1.7 rebounds in 22.6 minutes per tilt across 82 games (12 starts).

items.headline: Shead logged 14 points (5-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and seven assists across 36 minutes during Sunday's 114-102 loss to Cleveland in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Shead scored at least 14 points for the second time in the past three games, albeit in a losing effort. With Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) missing 16 of the final 19 games across the playoffs and regular season, Shead was handed a starting role, at least periodically. In 13 appearances over the final month, including the postseason, he averaged 7.9 points, 5.1 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.5 three-pointers. Moving forward, it appears as though Shead will likely serve as a backup, providing deeper-league value for anyone needing assists.

items.headline: Shead will start Friday's Game 6 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Cavaliers, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Brandon Ingram (heel) won't play in Friday's do-or-die matchup, opening the door for Shead to enter the starting five. The second-year guard started Games 1 and 2, during which he averaged 10.0 points, 3.0 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals while shooting 43.8 percent from the field in 33.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Shead finished Wednesday's 125-120 loss to Cleveland in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 18 points (7-15 FG, 4-10 3Pt), one rebound, seven assists and two steals over 34 minutes.
items.story: Shead stepped into a larger role after Brandon Ingram was ruled out after just 11 minutes due to a heel injury. As he has done all season, Shead upped his production, providing the Raptors with a viable option off the bench. If Ingram is ruled out for Game 6, expect to see Shead playing a larger role once again, either as a starter or coming off the bench.

items.headline: Shead isn't in the starting lineup for Game 3 against Cleveland on Thursday, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Shead caught fire from beyond the arc in Game 1, but he was unable to replicate that same production in Game 2, as he was held to three points on 1-for-5 from deep. As a result, Ja'Kobe Walter will get the nod in the starting lineup Thursday, bumping Shead to a bench role.

items.headline: Shead totaled 17 points (6-11 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), one rebound and two assists over 28 minutes during Saturday's 126-113 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Getting the start to open the playoffs with Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) unavailable, Shead was locked in from long distance, and his five made three-pointers was more than he's produced in any regular-season game during his career to date. The 17 points also represented the second-year guard's best offensive output since Jan. 11, when he dropped 22 points on the Sixers. With Quickley's status uncertain for Game 2 on Monday, Shead could be in line for a significant role in the Raptors' backcourt once again.

items.headline: Shead is in the Raptors' starting lineup for Game 1 against the Cavaliers on Saturday.
items.story: Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Game 1, prompting the Raptors to move Shead into the starting lineup alongside Scottie Barnes, Brandon Ingram, RJ Barrett and Jakob Poeltl. Shead started 12 regular-season games, during which he averaged 11.5 points, 7.5 assists, 1.8 rebounds, 1.8 threes and 1.3 steals over 32.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Shead won't start Sunday's game against the Nets, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Immanuel Quickley (foot) back in the lineup, Shead will slide to the second unit. The second-year guard has averaged 7.3 points and 6.3 assists across 23.8 minutes per game in four appearances off the bench in April.

items.headline: Shead closed Friday's 112-95 loss to New York with five points (2-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and two assists in 27 minutes.
items.story: Shead drew the start for Friday's game due to the absence of Immanuel Quickley (foot/rest), though the former wasn't able to take advantage of his expanded role. Quickley is expected to be back in action for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Nets, which would result in Shead retreating to a bench role.

items.headline: Shead is in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Knicks on Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Immanuel Quickley (foot) is not available for Friday's contest, so Shead will make his 12th start of the season and the fifth in 11 games since March 23. Shead's last start took place April 1 against the Kings, when he played 37 minutes and finished with 16 points, seven assists, one rebound, two steals and one block in a 123-115 loss.

items.headline: Shead will come off the bench for Friday's game in Memphis.
items.story: Brandon Ingram (heel) is back and starting after a one-game absence, so Shead will retreat to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Shead owns averages of 5.7 points and 5.0 assists per game.

items.headline: Shead accumulated 16 points (5-9 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, seven assists, one block and two steals over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 123-115 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Shead got the start Wednesday, his fourth start over the Raptors' last six games, and he was active both as a scorer and playmaker. Considering that Immanuel Quickley is dealing with a foot injury, it wouldn't be shocking if Shead remains in the starting lineup, thus bolstering his fantasy upside. Shead is averaging 12.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 8.0 assists per game when deployed in a starting role this season.

items.headline: Shead will start in Wednesday's game against Sacramento, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Shead didn't start in Tuesday's 127-116 loss to the Detroit Pistons. However, Ja'Kobe Walter will head back to the bench Wednesday, allowing Shead to make his fourth start in the last six games. In 10 starts during the campaign, the 23-year-old has averaged 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, 8.1 assists, 0.1 blocks and 1.3 steals while shooting 40.9 percent from the field and 36.2 percent from downtown across 32.1 minutes.

items.headline: Shead will come off the bench Tuesday against the Pistons.
items.story: Shead drew a spot start Sunday against the Magic and delivered a double-double, but he'll move to a bench role Tuesday with Brandon Ingram returning to action. Shead has struggled as a reserve recently and has been held to single figures in 12 straight bench appearances.

items.headline: Shead will start Sunday versus the Magic.
items.story: Shead will be filling in for Brandon Ingram (heel), who was a late scratch for Sunday's game, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Ja'Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl. As a starter this season, Shead has averaged 11.7 points, 7.9 assists, 1.9 triples and 1.1 steals per contest.

items.headline: Shead will come off the bench for Friday's game versus the Pelicans, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Ja'Kobe Walter will replace Shead in the first unit for Friday's game. As a reserve this season, Shead has posted averages of 5.8 points, 4.8 assists and 1.3 turnovers per game.

items.headline: Shead chipped in seven points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and 14 assists over 29 minutes during Monday's 143-127 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Getting his first start since Jan. 21 with Immanuel Quickley (foot) unavailable, Shead set a new career high in assists. The second-year guard hasn't scored in double digits once in 11 March games, however, averaging 3.6 points, 5.0 assists and 1.7 boards in 21.1 minutes on the month, and he'll be tough to roster in most fantasy formats even if Quickley misses additional time.

items.headline: Shead will start Monday's game against the Jazz, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Immanuel Quickley (foot) out, Shead will draw his first start since Jan. 21. As a starter this season (seven games), the second-year point guard has averaged 12.9 points, 7.6 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 33.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Shead had two points (1-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and one block across 21 minutes during Sunday's 120-98 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: With Immanuel Quickley (foot) set to miss Monday's tilt versus the Jazz, Shead is a prime candidate to start at point guard. Shead has averaged 5.0 assists, 4.2 points and 1.5 rebounds in 21.8 minutes per tilt in his last six games, shooting a miserable 31.0 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Shead finished with nine points (3-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and three assists over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 122-111 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Shead continues to play a sizable role for the second unit, but his fantasy appeal remains limited to deeper formats. Over his last six games, he's averaging 4.0 points, 2.8 assists, 1.8 rebounds and 0.5 three-pointers in 19.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Shead logged 12 points (4-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, six assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Sunday's 122-94 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Despite being stuck in a reserve role, Shead has dished out at least four dimes in seven of his last eight games. The second-year guard's upside remains capped by a healthy Immanuel Quickley, with Shead averaging 5.1 points, 4.6 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 21.4 minutes per contest in his last eight games.

items.headline: Shead won't start against Portland on Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With RJ Barrett (ankle) back in the lineup, Shead will slide to the second unit. Over 39 appearances off the bench this season, the second-year guard has averaged 6.4 points, 5.3 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 20.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Shead produced 15 points (5-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, six assists and two steals over 33 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 victory over the Kings.
items.story: RJ Barrett (ankle) and Ja'Kobe Walter (hip) remain sidelined for Toronto, which is allowing Shead to handle a starting role in the backcourt alongside Immanuel Quickley. Shead has averaged 12.9 points, 7.6 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 33.9 minutes per tilt across seven games as a starter this season, so he should hold onto streaming appeal until either Barrett or Walter is back in the fold.

items.headline: Shead is in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Warriors on Tuesday.
items.story: Tuesday marks Shead's fifth start in six games as he'll join Immanuel Quickley in the backcourt while the Raptors opt to start Scottie Barnes at center due to the absences of Jakob Poeltl (back) and Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb). Since Jan. 3, Shead has averaged 9.1 points, 6.3 assists, 1.7 rebounds, 1.3 threes and 0.9 steals over 26.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Shead is not in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Lakers on Sunday, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Shead will retreat to the bench Sunday due to Immanuel Quickley (back) being cleared to return from a two-game absence. Shead has started in each of the Raptors' last four games, and over that span he averaged 11.8 points, 7.8 assists, 2.3 rebounds, 1.3 threes and 1.0 steals over 35.0 minutes per game, though he connected on just 35.0 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: Shead ended with 15 points (4-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, 13 assists and one steal across 39 minutes in Friday's 121-117 overtime loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Shead made his fourth straight start and delivered the most eye-catching line to date, logging his first double-double of the season. While the 23-year-old's scoring efficiency can fluctuate, his passing has stood out, as the guard is averaging 7.8 assists during this four-game starting run and 6.8 across eight January appearances. His playing time figures to scale back once Immanuel Quickley (back) returns, but Shead has shown he can effectively run the offense and facilitate when given the opportunity.

items.headline: Shead logged 22 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-8 FT), six assists and two rebounds over 37 minutes during Sunday's 116-115 overtime win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Shead made his second start of the season Sunday due to the absences of Brandon Ingram (thumb) and RJ Barrett (ankle). Shead made the most of his opportunity, finishing second on the Raptors in points and assists behind Scottie Barnes (31 points and seven assists). The Raptors and 76ers face each other Monday in a rematch, and Shead would likely remain in the starting five if Ingram and Barrett are unable to play.

items.headline: Shead will start Sunday versus the 76ers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Brandon Ingram (thumb) unavailable, Shead will draw the start and he'll be joined in the first unit by Immanuel Quickley, Ja'Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. In Shead's previous start this season, he finished with 18 points (6-15 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one turnover in 34 minutes, so he's on the radar as a potential streamer in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Shead accumulated four points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 97-96 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Shead wasn't able to find his rhythm offensively, but he continues to excel as a playmaker. Over his last seven games, he's shooting 37.5 percent from the field with averages of 7.7 points, 5.3 assists, 1.1 rebounds, 0.7 steals and 1.3 three-pointers in 22.0 minutes.

items.headline: Shead produced 19 points (8-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 0-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one block in 29 minutes during Monday's 107-106 win over Orlando.
items.story: In a game when Brandon Ingram, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley combined to score 34 points while going 14-for-46 from the field (30.4 percent), it was Shead who came to the rescue for the Raptors with a team-high 19 points off the bench, 12 of which came in the first half. It was a season high in points for Shead and just the third time he's scored in double digits. Since Dec. 2, he has averaged 8.3 points, 5.5 assists, 2.3 rebounds, 1.5 threes and 1.1 steals over 23.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Shead supplied eight points (3-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight assists and one steal across 29 minutes during Sunday's 141-127 overtime win over the Warriors.
items.story: Shead's playmaking continues to be solid, but the rest of his game leaves a lot to be desired in terms of fantasy hoops. Over his last seven appearances, he's shooting 32.7 percent from the field with averages of 6.6 points, 6.1 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.4 three-pointers in 22.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Shead is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Shead should see regular minutes off the bench in this game, but he'll move to the second unit due to Immanuel Quickley (illness) returning to the starting lineup. Shead is averaging 5.8 points, 1.8 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game when coming off the bench this season.

items.headline: Reid logged 12 points (4-19 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and one block over 39 minutes during the Hornets' 111-97 loss to the Hawks on Friday.
items.story: Reid recorded his second-straight double-double and sixth of the regular season, although he needed 20 field-goal attempts to reach double-digit points. It was arguably his worst shooting performance of the season, and the veteran big man is connecting on a season-low 38.8 percent of his field-goal attempts in 2026-27. For the month of November, Reid is averaging 18.5 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 2.5 threes and 1.0 steals over 32.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Reid ended Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers with 23 points (8-18 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals across 41 minutes.
items.story: Reid played a team-high 42 minutes and gave Charlotte a brief lead in overtime with a 29-foot three-pointer, but he couldn't convert on several looks in the final minutes. It was one of his more efficient outings in a season in which he's often had to force the issue on offense. The forward is averaging 17.2 points and 8.2 rebounds in his first season in Charlotte.

items.headline: Reid logged 16 points (6-18 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals in 34 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Reid's move into a prominent role with Charlotte has led to 17.3 points and 8.5 rebounds per game, making him a dependable fantasy option beyond his traditional scoring. His ability to stretch the floor is especially valuable for a big man, though shooting just 41.1 percent from the field has hurt his efficiency. The consistent workload gives him a relatively stable floor, and while the Hornets have been struggling, he remains one of the few reliable fantasy options on the roster on a steady basis.

items.headline: Reid registered 25 points (10-26 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 13 rebounds, four assists and two steals over 32 minutes during Monday's 124-112 win over Cleveland.
items.story: Reid took on a massive offensive load, attempting 26 shots with Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Brandon Miller (groin) and Dennis Schroder (hamstring) all sidelined. The efficiency wasn't there, but Reid's scoring, rebounding and four threes made for a strong fantasy line.

items.headline: Reid registered 14 points (6-17 FG, 2-5 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and two turnovers across 26 minutes in Friday's 119-80 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: The Hornets were dominated from start to finish, resulting in Reid watching most of the fourth quarter from the sidelines. He was the only Charlotte starter to reach double figures, but he didn't do it efficiently, converting just 35.3 percent of his shot attempts. Reid has been hit-or-miss this season, averaging 16.6 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 2.3 triples per game on 41.6 percent shooting from the field and 65.2 percent at the line. Those numbers have him ranked outside the top 150 in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Reid recorded 28 points (11-18 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block across 36 minutes in Wednesday's 114-104 loss to the Nets.
items.story: After averaging 11.5 points per contest on 32.6 percent shooting in his previous four outings, Reid delivered a major bounce-back performance Wednesday, albeit in a losing effort. The big man posted a game- and season-high scoring total and paced the Hornets in rebounds, finishing a rebound away from his fourth double-double of the season. Kon Knueppel made his season debut Wednesday, though he exited to the locker room in the first quarter and did not return due to left leg soreness. If Knueppel needs to miss additional time, Reid could continue seeing increased usage.

items.headline: Reid finished with 14 points (4-12 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block across 36 minutes in Saturday's 109-104 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Reid had difficulty getting most of his shots to fall in Friday's 95-79 loss to the Wizards. Things didn't get any better Saturday for the 27-year-old, who failed to sink any of his attempts from behind the arc. Still, despite some rough patches in his first year with the Hornets, including getting benched during the second half of Wednesday's meeting with the Pistons, Reid is averaging a career-best 15.9 points and 8.6 rebounds per contest. However, it's unclear if Reid will be able to remain as productive once Coby White (calf) and Kon Knueppel (hamstring) are cleared to get back on the floor.

items.headline: Reid recorded seven points (2-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and one block across 13 minutes in Wednesday's 97-89 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Head coach Charles Lee said postgame that Reid "didn't meet our standards in the first half," and he didn't step on the hardwood in the second half. Although he saw limited action, the big man still finished as the Hornets' third-leading rebounder. He scored 17-plus points in each of the first four games of the regular season, recording two double-doubles in that span.

items.headline: Reid finished with 18 points (8-22 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal across 29 minutes during Monday's 110-103 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Reid struggled offensively through three quarters before erupting for 16 points and seven rebounds in the final period to help Charlotte secure the victory. Despite the inefficient shooting performance, the big man delivered another strong showing on the glass and continues to play a prominent offensive role for the Hornets. His ability to contribute points, rebounds and three-pointers makes him a valuable fantasy option, and he did this despite being under the weather prior to the game.

items.headline: Reid (illness) is active for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Reid was listed as probable heading into Monday's contest against Washington after battling an illness over the weekend. He'll continue operating as the starting power forward for the 2-1 Hornets.

items.headline: Reid is listed as probable for Monday's game against Washington due to an illness, according to the NBA's official injury report.
items.story: Reid appears likely to suit up against the Wizards, though his availability will be confirmed closer to tipoff. Assuming he's cleared, the big man should continue handling his usual role in Charlotte's frontcourt.

items.headline: Reid notched 23 points (9-16 FG, 5-8 3Pt), nine rebounds and two blocks in 37 minutes during Saturday's 115-110 win over Miami.
items.story: Reid was phenomenal on the defensive end, helping hold Giannis Antetokounmpo to just 14 points on 4-for-11 shooting, and he delivered on offense as well. After a lackluster preseason, Reid has been rolling to start his 2026-27 campaign, churning out top-50 value with averages of 20.0 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 4.0 triples per game on 47.1 percent shooting.

items.headline: Reid recorded 17 points (7-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes in Friday's 128-81 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Reid did most of his damage in the first half, as he logged only seven minutes in the second half of this blowout loss. The big man was the only Hornets player to score more than 11 points, and he also finished third on the team in rebounds. He's totaled 37 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists through his first two regular-season games with the Hornets and will likely continue seeing increased usage for as long as Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) are unavailable.

items.headline: Reid finished with 20 points (8-18 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds and seven assists across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 110-103 win over the Nets.
items.story: Reid appeared in his first game for the Hornets on Wednesday, and it didn't take him long to make a positive impression by narrowly missing a triple-double. The 27-year-old spent his entire career in Minnesota before being traded to Charlotte in the offseason. In 483 regular-season games with the Timberwolves, he averaged 11.9 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.5 assists while shooting 37.1 percent from deep over 21.7 minutes per contest. Reid could be in line for his best campaign to date in 2026-27, and he might be even more productive than projected initially as long as Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (ankle) are sidelined.

items.headline: Reid posted 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Friday's 117-98 preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Reid reached double figures in scoring across four preseason games, averaging 13.3 points over the span. Charlotte acquired the veteran big man from Minnesota in the June trade that sent LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves, and he's expected to start at power forward for the regular season in a move that should benefit both teams.

items.headline: Reid finished with 12 points (4-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and three assists across 26 minutes in Wednesday's 114-93 preseason loss to Boston.
items.story: Reid led Charlotte with six rebounds but couldn't find his shooting touch, converting just four of 14 attempts while missing five shots from beyond the arc. The versatile big man started alongside Moussa Diabate and continued to see opportunities on the perimeter, though his offensive efficiency will be worth monitoring as he settles into his role with the Hornets.

items.headline: Reid ended with 13 points (3-9 FG, 6-7 FT, 1-5 3Pt) and four rebounds in 16 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: As expected, Reid slotted into the starting power-forward position vacated by Miles Bridges, who is now in Phoenix. Reid was one of three Hornets players to score in double digits, an encouraging sign for anyone thinking of drafting him. While he should be a relatively consistent source of points and rebounds, Reid may need to add another string to his bow should he hope to impress fantasy managers. At this point, Reid is a viable target in the middle rounds of drafts, with the possibility that he flirts with top-50 value if he can develop a more well-rounded game.

items.headline: The Timberwolves traded Reid, three first-round pick swaps, three second-round pick swaps and a 2033 unprotected first-round pick to the Hornets on Thursday in exchange for LaMelo Ball and Josh Green, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Minnesota has now moved on from Reid and Julius Randle this offseason, with the former heading to another crowded frontcourt. Reid has averaged at least 13 points and five assists while shooting 36 percent from three in each of his past two seasons. Currently, he's slated for another reserve role, but Miles Bridges has been in the rumor mill this offseason, so Charlotte may not be done making moves.

items.headline: Reid ended Friday's 139-109 loss to San Antonio in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 18 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds and one assist across 32 minutes.
items.story: Reid did his best to keep the Timberwolves' season alive Friday, with the veteran big man finishing as the team's third-leading scorer behind Anthony Edwards (24 points) and Terrence Shannon (21 points). Reid saw his numbers dip slightly in 2025-26 compared to the previous season, though he noted to reporters during Saturday's press conference that a right shoulder injury around the time of the All-Star break played a part in that, per Chris Hine of The Minnesota Star Tribune. Reid is entering the second year of a five-year, $125 million contract, and while he's come off the bench for most of his NBA career, he could operate in an expanded role in 2026-27 if the Timberwolves opt to trade one or both of Rudy Gobert and Julius Randle, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic posits.

items.headline: Reid ended with 15 points (6-12 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Sunday's 114-109 victory over San Antonio in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Reid injured his ankle early in the fourth quarter but returned to the contest. He was also involved in the game's pivotal news item, as he was on the receiving end of Victor Wembanyama's Flagrant 2 foul, which caused the MVP candidate's ejection. Reid avoided injury despite taking an elbow to the face and managed a solid line that came one rebound shy of a double-double. The series is now guaranteed to last at least two more games, and Reid's high floor will make him a solid DFS target for Game 5.

items.headline: Reid (ankle) returned to Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs, per the game broadcast.
items.story: Reid went down in a heap in the fourth quarter before limping to the locker room due to an apparent right ankle injury. Fortunately, he was able to return to the contest shortly thereafter.

items.headline: Reid went back to the locker room during Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals due to an apparent right ankle injury, Charlie Walton of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
items.story: Reid went down in pain early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest after getting rolled up on by Luke Kornet. With Reid out of the lineup, the starting five is likely to play the majority of the remaining minutes of Game 4.

items.headline: Reid closed Monday's 104-102 victory over San Antonio in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist and one block over 30 minutes.
items.story: Reid's numbers are down slightly in the postseason, which comes as a bit of a surprise with so many injuries on the team. Through seven games, he's averaging 11.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.9 assists on 47.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Barrett notched 12 points (5-16 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block across 31 minutes in Wednesday's 98-93 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Barrett struggled with efficiency in this low-scoring affair, though he still finished as one of six Raptors players to score in double figures. The veteran wing produced across the stat sheet, as he led the Raptors with a season-best seven assists and ended second on the team in rebounds. He also tied the game-high mark in steals, supplying multiple swipes for the second time this season.

items.headline: Barrett provided 27 points (9-21 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 9-11 FT), seven rebounds and four assists in 37 minutes during Friday's 121-107 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: With Scottie Barnes (groin) sidelined, Barrett stepped up and set a new season scoring high while tying for the game high with teammate Alijah Martin. Barrett has hit for at least 20 points in every game but one to begin the campaign, averaging 21.6 points, 6.1 boards, 3.9 assists and 1.6 threes in nine contests, and his usage and production could be a bit higher in the short term if Barnes misses any more time.

items.headline: Barrett posted 22 points (7-17 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), five rebounds and three assists across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 128-109 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Barrett reached the 20-point mark for the seventh time in eight games this season, reinforcing his status as one of Toronto's most consistent scoring options while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is out. Barrett's offensive volume remains encouraging, although his limited defensive production and modest playmaking restrict his fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Barrett closed with 26 points (10-19 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-8 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 37 minutes during Monday's 125-118 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Barrett delivered an efficient offensive performance, finishing one point behind Immanuel Quickley for the team lead in scoring. Barrett also contributed two blocks and posted a team-best plus-18 rating, helping Toronto overcome a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit. Barrett's substantial playing time and consistent scoring opportunities continue to provide a solid fantasy foundation.

items.headline: Barrett closed with 22 points (9-18 FG, 4-9 3Pt), 10 rebounds and five assists across 32 minutes during Sunday's 131-125 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The veteran wing scored 20-plus points for the fifth time in six games to begin the season, as the absence of Kawhi Leonard (knee) has resulted in a little more shot volume for Barrett. During those six contests, Barrett is averaging 19.8 points, 6.2 boards, 4.2 assists and 1.5 threes, but those scoring numbers are dragged down by what would be a career-low 29.0 percent shooting from beyond the arc. He already seems to be turning things around on that front. After going 1-for-11 from downtown in his first three games, Barrett is 8-for-20 (40.0 percent) in the last three contests.

items.headline: Barrett finished Wednesday's 129-99 win over the Magic with 25 points (9-18 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and one steal over 32 minutes.
items.story: Barrett helped the Raptors jump out to an early lead with 12 points in the first quarter before adding another nine in the second. His 25 points were second-most on Toronto behind Scottie Barnes' 28, and Barrett was one rebound shy from logging his first double-double of the season. The veteran forward has scored at least 20 points in each of the first four games of the regular season, and his offensive output will be needed more than ever by the Raptors given the extended absence of Kawhi Leonard (knee).

items.headline: Barrett notched 20 points (9-21 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-5 FT), two rebounds, two assists and three steals over 32 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: With Kawhi Leonard (knee) sidelined, Barrett finished as Toronto's second-leading scorer despite struggling with his efficiency, particularly from the free-throw line. The forward remained aggressive offensively, attempting a team-high 21 shots, while his three steals provided additional fantasy value. Barrett should continue handling a significant offensive role for the Raptors, though his inconsistent shooting remains a concern.

items.headline: Barrett recorded 23 points (9-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and one block over 34 minutes during Friday's 112-102 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Barrett was one of four Raptors players to haul in at least nine rebounds during Friday's game, and he finished as the team's second-leading scorer behind Scottie Barnes (28). Barrett has scored 20-plus points in each of the first two games of the regular season and figures to have a larger role offensively while Kawhi Leonard elevates his conditioning.

items.headline: Barrett closed Wednesday's 135-92 victory over Chicago with 20 points (8-14 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-7 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 26 minutes.
items.story: The new-look Raptors got off to a roaring start in 2026-27. Barrett was one of four starters to reach 20-plus points in the season opener, and although he was unable to connect on any of his three-point attempts, the Toronto native was still highly efficient from the field. He finished second on Toronto with a plus-34 rating in 26 minutes, and he'll aim to build upon the solid outing against the Wizards on Friday.

items.headline: Barrett (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against Chicago.
items.story: Barrett sat out Friday's preseason finale but should be back in the lineup when the Raptors host the Bulls. Across four preseason appearances in 2026, he averaged 18.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 0.5 steals in 23.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Barrett will rest for Friday's preseason finale against Detroit, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Pressreports.
items.story: The Raptors are resting their entire first unit and possibly some key reserves. Barrett is expected to be ready for an Opening Night matchup against the Hawks on Wednesday.

items.headline: Barrett recorded 21 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 7-10 FT), eight rebounds and four assists across 31 minutes in Thursday's 122-120 preseason loss to New York.
items.story: Barrett attacked the basket throughout the contest, earning 10 free-throw attempts while grabbing eight rebounds, including two on the offensive glass. He also connected on two three-pointers and finished as Toronto's second-leading scorer behind Scottie Barnes. Barrett has now scored at least 17 points in consecutive preseason appearances, highlighting his offensive involvement alongside Barnes and Kawhi Leonard.

items.headline: Barrett finished with 17 points (6-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three assists over 23 minutes in Tuesday's 148-98 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Barrett provided steady offense alongside Toronto's other starters, converting half of his field-goal attempts and getting to the free-throw line five times. His contributions helped the Raptors score 86 points in the first half, putting the game well out of reach before halftime.

items.headline: Barrett recorded 20 points (7-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 23 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason win over the Clippers.
items.story: Barrett's 20 points were a game high, and he finished with a ridiculous plus-21 differential in the win. He's not a great free-throw shooter, and he won't do much in the defensive categories, but Barrett should be a reliable source of points and triples as one of the key cogs in Toronto's offense this season.

items.headline: Barrett finished with 15 points (3-9 FG, 2-4 FT, 7-8 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 17 minutes in Saturday's 129-105 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Barrett was efficient from deep Saturday, and he managed to tie Tyreke Key with a game-high in scoring. The 26-year-old averaged 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists over 30.3 minutes per contest during the 2025-26 campaign. However, he appeared in less than 58 regular-season games for the third consecutive year. Regardless of what the future holds for Barrett, he will need to remain healthy. His three-point shooting also needs work, especially since he shot a career-high 40.1 percent from downtown in 2020-21, his second season in the NBA.

items.headline: Barrett wants to stay with the Raptors, per Sam Amico of HoopsWire.com.
items.story: Barrett is set for unrestricted free agency next summer following the expiration of his rookie contract extension, originally signed as a member of the Knicks in 2022. The 26-year-old swingman tends to be a better fantasy investment in points leagues. He's never shot at least 75 percent from the free-throw line and has averaged at least one steal just once in his career.

items.headline: Barrett did not participate in Canada's latest FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he gears up for the 2026-27 NBA season.
items.story: Barrett averaged 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 57 starts for Toronto during the 2025-26 regular season while shooting 49.1 percent from the field. The 26-year-old remains an important part of a Raptors offense that is expected to feature Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley. That collection of scoring options could limit Barrett's overall usage, but he should remain a steady source of points and rebounds in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Barrett amassed 23 points (9-25 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, six assists and three steals in 43 minutes during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett played a huge role during Toronto's seven-game playoff run, scoring at least 18 points in each contest. The star forward put together another productive campaign in 2025-26, averaging 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 30.3 minutes per contest over 57 regular-season games. With most of the Raptors' core players under contract for 2026-27, Barrett is likely to handle a similar role next year.

items.headline: Barrett produced 24 points (8-21 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 43 minutes during Friday's 112-110 overtime victory over the Cavaliers in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett landed a three-pointer with just 1.2 seconds remaining in overtime, sealing an emphatic victory at home. The shot was reminiscent of Kawhi Leonard's game-winner back in 2019, with the ball skying off the back of the rim before dropping into the basket. It continues what has been a strong series for Barrett, who's averaged 24.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.7 three-pointers thus far. Toronto will now head back to Cleveland for Game 7, where Barrett will look to lead his team into the second round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett tallied 25 points (9-19 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-9 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 125-120 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett was relatively efficient in this one, though he did struggle at the charity stripe. Still, the 25-year-old forward led the Raptors in scoring and has now reached the 20-point threshold in four of five first-round outings. He also recorded his first double-double of the season with a game- and season-best 12 rebounds. Barrett and the Raptors will aim to stave off elimination in Friday's Game 6 in Toronto, though they could be without Brandon Ingram, who left Wednesday's loss early due to right heel inflammation.

items.headline: Barrett finished Thursday's 126-104 victory over the Cavaliers in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 33 points (12-19 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-7 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals in 39 minutes.
items.story: Barrett showed up for the Raptors in a big way on the offensive end. He combined with Scottie Barnes for 66 points, though it was Barrett who drilled a team-high six triples. The 25-year-old's production on the offensive end proved to be one of the key difference makers in Game 3 to keep his squad's playoff hopes alive. Barrett is averaging 26.3 points while hitting at a clip of 64.4 percent from the field through the first three games of the first round.

items.headline: Barrett recorded 22 points (10-13 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and five assists over 38 minutes during Toronto's 115-105 Game 2 loss against the Cavaliers on Monday in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett was rebound shy from logging a double-double and had another efficient performance from the floor Monday, finishing as the Raptors' second-leading scorer behind Scottie Barnes (26 points). Barrett has gone 17-for-26 (65.4 percent) from the field over the first two games of the series, and the Raptors will need that efficiency in Game 3 on Thursday if the team wishes to avoid going down 3-0 in the series.

items.headline: Barrett logged 24 points (7-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 7-9 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal over 32 minutes during the Raptors' 126-113 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs Saturday.
items.story: Barrett was quiet in the first quarter with just two points, but he responded by scoring nine points in the second frame and 13 in the second half to lead the Raptors in scoring. He's carrying some momentum from the tail end of the regular season, when he averaged 21.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.4 threes in 31.5 minutes across his eight games prior to the start of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett chipped in 26 points (9-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-9 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes during Sunday's 136-101 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Barrett's status was up in the air earlier in the day, but he took the court and helped the Raptors clinch a playoff berth in the lopsided victory. The Raptors have made the playoffs despite a slew of injuries throughout the regular season. Barrett endured a whopping 25 games lost to injury, and the lengthy absences of Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Jakob Poeltl also posed challenges. Although Quickley left the game with a hamstring issue, Barrett and the rest of the first unit are healthy as they prepare to take on the Cavaliers in the first round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett (knee) is available for Sunday's game against the Nets, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barrett was unable to play against the Knicks on Friday due to right knee soreness, but he has been given the green light to suit up in Sunday's regular-season finale. In five outings since April 1, Barrett has averaged 19.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.4 threes and 0.8 blocks over 33.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Barrett (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Brooklyn, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barrett was ruled out shortly ahead of Friday's 112-95 loss to the Knicks, his former team.
