items.headline: Coach Erik Spoelstra stated after Monday's 128-110 win over Houston that the team held Adebayo (hip) out of the second half in an effort to be proactive, and the injury isn't expected to be a long-term issue, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: This is positive news for the star center, who didn't come out of the locker room to start the second half of Monday's clash. Miami will presumably re-evaluate Adebayo over the next few days to determine whether he'll be able to suit up for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee.

items.headline: Adebayo (hip) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against the Rockets, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports. He'll end with four points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), one rebound, two assists and two steals in 16 minutes.
items.story: Bobby Portis and Nick Richards will be asked to hold down the fort at center with Adebayo shut down for the night. He can be considered day-to-day moving forward until the team has another update to share.

items.headline: Adebayo is dealing with tightness in his right hip and is questionable to return to Monday's game versus Houston, Zachary Weinberger of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Adebayo played 16 minutes prior to his questionable designation, tallying four points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), one rebound, two assists and two steals. Bobby Portis should see more burn in the meantime.

items.headline: Adebayo recorded 20 points (5-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 9-13 FT), five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks across 36 minutes in Saturday's 137-117 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Adebayo couldn't replicate Friday's 37-point, 14-rebound performance against Cleveland, but his defensive contributions were outstanding. The five combined steals and blocks were especially valuable, and he's now scored at least 18 points in four of his last five outings. Playing alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo has created some competition for rebounds and interior touches, but Adebayo's versatility allows him to remain productive in multiple categories even when his scoring opportunities are reduced compared to last season. He's definitely trending in the right direction after a slow start to the campaign, averaging 23.1 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game in his last six outings.

items.headline: Adebayo amassed 37 points (13-19 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 9-10 FT), 14 rebounds and three assists across 38 minutes in Friday's 133-121 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: After scoring 11 points on 1-of-8 shooting from the field in his previous appearance, Adebayo bounced back with his best performance of the season. The star big man tied for the game-high mark in points, setting a new season high. He also led all players with a season-best 14 boards, recording his third double-double of the season.

items.headline: Adebayo racked up 11 points (1-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 9-12 FT), eight rebounds, four assists, two blocks and four steals across 37 minutes during Tuesday's 115-109 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Adebayo struggled to score from the field, but he still found ways to matter, mostly by getting to the line and anchoring the defense. His late block helped Miami hold off Utah's final push. He was also Miami's second-highest rebounder with eight boards.

items.headline: Adebayo finished Sunday's 114-108 win over the Kings with 18 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and three steals across 34 minutes.
items.story: The 29-year-old center had a bumpy beginning to the season as he adjusted to having Giannis Antetokounmpo in the lineup alongside him, but Adebayo is in a groove now. He's scored at least 16 points in six straight games, averaging 23.0 points, 9.2 boards, 3.0 assists and 2.2 steals over that span while shooting 59.8 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Adebayo supplied 18 points (7-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-7 FT), 10 rebounds, one block and one steal across 33 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Adebayo couldn't repeat the 35-point double-double he notched in the win over the Clippers on Wednesday, but he posted consecutive double-doubles for the first time this season. The big man is finding his footing after a slow start to the season and is growing more comfortable playing alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo. Over his last five outings, Adebayo is averaging 24.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.0 steals per game.

items.headline: Adebayo provided 35 points (14-20 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and one steal across 41 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Adebayo led all scorers and nearly doubled his 16.3-point average entering the night, shooting 70.0 percent from the field. He's been a model of consistency to start the season, and nights like this show his ceiling when Miami leans on him offensively.

items.headline: Adebayo recorded 16 points (5-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals in 31 minutes during Monday's 138-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The star big man has been a model of consistency early on, collecting at least seven rebounds, three assists and multiple steals in six of his first seven appearances. For the year, Adebayo has averaged 16.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.3 steals in 31.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Adebayo recorded 27 points (11-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-5 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 145-125 win over Indiana.
items.story: The 27 points were a season high for Adebayo, and for the second straight game he fell one board shy of his first double-double of 2026-27. The veteran center is beginning to find a groove alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo, hitting for at least 20 points in three of the last four games while averaging 19.8 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 2.3 steals and 0.8 blocks while shooting 50.9 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Adebayo provided 24 points (8-16 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 8-9 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals in 33 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 win over the Hawks.
items.story: This was a nice bounce-back performance for Adebayo following Monday's eight-point, 3-for-10 shooting effort, and he finished with a sterling plus-22 differential in the 12-point victory. He also became Miami's all-time leading rebounder, surpassing Udonis Haslem, who had held the mark since Nov. 21 of 2012.

items.headline: Queen ended Saturday's 114-91 loss to the Spurs with 15 points (7-16 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds and one steal over 35 minutes.
items.story: Queen has recorded just one steal or block in three of his last four games, but even if his defensive contributions have been lacking a bit of late, he'll remain valuable due to his activity on the glass and his scoring numbers. He's scored in double digits in five of his last six appearances (one start), averaging 12.0 points and 8.0 rebounds per game in that stretch. This was his fourth double-double of the season.

items.headline: Queen will start Saturday against the Spurs.
items.story: Queen will earn his first start of the season with Zion Williamson (thigh) out, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Jeremiah Fears, Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey and Yves Missi. Per 36 minutes this season, Queen is averaging 20.1 points, 10.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 three-pointers, 1.5 steals and 1.4 swats.

items.headline: Queen delivered 17 points (6-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds and one block across 20 minutes in Monday's 115-94 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Queen matched his career high with four three-pointers and recorded a double-double despite playing only 20 minutes. The second-year big man's shooting was particularly noteworthy for a frontcourt player, but his rebounding was just as encouraging. Yves Missi's return from a knee injury has added competition for minutes in New Orleans' frontcourt, and Queen came off the bench Monday, but he's making his presence felt. He has scored in double figures in 10 of his 15 appearances this season.

items.headline: Queen posted 16 points (4-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 8-10 FT), four rebounds and three blocks in 21 minutes during Monday's 138-87 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Queen was one of the few bright spots for New Orleans, leading the team in scoring and swatting three shots. He did much of his damage at the free-throw line. He continues to come off the bench despite Yves Missi's (knee) absence, which limits his ceiling, but Queen's scoring and shot-blocking keep him relevant in most formats.

items.headline: Queen contributed 20 points (8-21 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and one block across 27 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 120-113 overtime win over the Jazz.
items.story: Queen didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance but wasn't shy about hunting his shot en route to a season-high-tying scoring total. The second-year center also led the Pelicans in rebounds and assists, dishing out a season-high six dimes. He's scored 20 points in back-to-back outings and will likely continue seeing increased burn in Yves Missi's (knee) stead.

items.headline: Queen notched 20 points (7-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime victory over Memphis.
items.story: Queen continued to come off the bench, yet put together another intriguing performance. The fact that he has not been inserted into the starting lineup despite an injury to Yves Missi (knee) indicates that the coaching staff is not comfortable playing him for more than about 25 minutes on any given night. While this does limit his overall upside, he is doing more than enough in a bench role to be considered a must-roster player.

items.headline: Queen posted eight points (3-6 FG, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 win over Atlanta.
items.story: Queen finished Saturday's game as the Pelicans' second-leading bench scorer and finished second on the team in rebounds behind Karlo Matkovic (10). Although he's coming off the bench, Queen's averages early on in the 2026-27 season are similar to what he produced during his rookie campaign last year. The Maryland product is averaging 11.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals over 23.7 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Queen notched 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 12 rebounds, an assist and a block across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Queen delivered valuable rebounding production in a reserve role, reaching double digits in points for the fourth consecutive game while notching his second double-double of the campaign. Queen is averaging 12.5 points and 9.3 boards per game despite not starting in any of his four appearances this season, so he should remain a valuable fantasy contributor regardless of whether he starts or not. He's also been remarkably efficient.

items.headline: Queen closed Friday's 120-119 loss to Utah with 12 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals over 29 minutes.
items.story: Yves Missi needed assistance to the locker room after suffering a left knee injury during Friday's loss and did not return, which allowed Queen to flirt with 30 minutes. If Missi needs to miss time, Queen would likely be one of the primary beneficiaries, so he's an attractive speculative add in fantasy leagues. While earning 27.8 minutes per game as a starter last season, Queen averaged 13.4 points, 8.1 rebounds, 4.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks per contest on 49.8 percent shooting from the field and 78.5 percent at the stripe.

items.headline: Queen contributed 10 points (2-4 FG, 6-6 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and two steals over 18 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Queen recorded a double-double, delivering a solid line despite playing limited minutes off the bench. With Yves Missi having arguably the best game of his career as the starting center, it appears as though Queen is going to serve as the backup, at least for the foreseeable future. He remains a viable asset in standard fantasy leagues, with a view to increasing his value if his role also increases at some point.

items.headline: The Pelicans exercised their third-year team option on Queen's contract Tuesday, Terry Kimble of SI.com reports.
items.story: The No. 13 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft is now officially under contract for the 2027-28 season. The big man averaged 11.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.9 combined steals-plus-blocks across 25.0 minutes per tilt in 81 regular-season appearances (48 starts) in his rookie season. Queen is expected to compete for minutes with Yves Missi and Karlo Matkovic in 2026-27.

items.headline: Queen totaled six points (1-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and two steals across 19 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Queen struggled mightily from the field but was a force on the glass, hauling in a game-high 11 rebounds. The 21-year-old has grabbed at least eight rebounds in all three of his preseason appearances. With Zion Williamson and Yves Missi expected to occupy the starting frontcourt spots, health permitting, Queen will likely be relegated to the second unit. However, the Maryland product should still have a sizable role this year after averaging 11.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.0 steals across 81 regular-season games (48 starts) as a rookie in 2025-26.

items.headline: Queen scored 10 points (3-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-7 FT) while adding nine rebounds, three steals and an assist in 17 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: The 21-year-old center showed flashes of his upside as a rookie in 2025-26 after being the 13th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but Queen remains stuck on the second unit as long as Zion Williamson and Yves Missi remain healthy. More consistent minutes could still allow Queen to improve on the 11.7 points, 7.1 boards, 3.7 assists and 1.9 combined steals and blocks he averaged last season.

items.headline: Queen impressed during his rookie campaign despite missing time early in the season due to a wrist injury, flashing the versatile offensive skills that made him a lottery pick.
items.story: Queen posted several standout performances, including the first 30-point triple-double by a rookie center in NBA history. Queen should compete for an even larger frontcourt role in 2026-27 as one of New Orleans' top young building blocks.

items.headline: Queen went for 30 points (11-28 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-8 FT), 22 rebounds, four assists, one steal and a block in 41 minutes during Sunday's 132-126 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Queen was dominant on the glass Sunday, collecting a career-high 22 rebounds. The impressive rookie was also able to amass 30 points by being especially aggressive in hunting his shot. This was evident in the fact that he took 28 shots from the floor, blowing past his previous high of 18 attempts. Queen averaged 24.0 points, 18.3 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.7 steals in 39.0 minutes per contest over his last three appearances to close the season.

items.headline: Queen supplied 25 points (9-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 7-9 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and one steal in 39 minutes during Friday's 144-118 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: It was the 11th double-double of the season for Queen. After promoting him to a starting role earlier this year, the Pelicans somewhat curiously got away from the rookie first-rounder a bit following the All-Star break as it pertains to his playing time. Queen has made just four starts over his last 25 contests, averaging 9.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 22.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Queen recorded 17 points (6-9 FG, 5-6 FT), 12 rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and three steals over 37 minutes during Tuesday's 156-137 win over the Jazz.
items.story: With Zion Williamson, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones all sitting out despite being healthy, Queen entered the starting lineup and nearly put up a triple-double. The Pelicans have nothing on the line in the final two games of the regular season, so Queen may get another extended look or two.

items.headline: Queen is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's matchup with the Jazz.
items.story: Queen should get all the run he can handle with Yves Missi (hand) out and Zion Williamson and Saddiq Bey not expected to play. Additionally, Queen will make for an attractive target in daily leagues with a favorable matchup against Utah. As a starter this season, Queen owns averages of 12.7 points, 7.6 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.0 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Queen closed with 12 points (4-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, seven assists, one block and two steals in 28 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 118-106 loss to Portland.
items.story: The seven dimes represented Queen's best effort in that category since Feb. 4. The rookie center has scored in double digits in four straight games as his usage ticks back up, averaging 12.3 points, 7.0 boards, 2.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks over that span in 24.0 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Queen finished with 11 points (5-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal in 21 minutes during Thursday's 129-108 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Queen was one of the lone bright spots for the Pelicans in a blowout loss. He reached double digits in the scoring column after being held to nine points or fewer in three straight games, and he nabbed his first double-double since Jan. 16. Despite a solid night, consistent production has been tough to come by for the rookie, who has seen north of 20 minutes only five times in 13 March showings.

items.headline: Queen contributed 14 points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 9-9 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 124-109 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Queen continues to play a reduced role off the bench, but he made the most of his minutes Wednesday. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 18.6 minutes with 7.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.6 three-pointers.

items.headline: Queen amassed 13 points (5-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one block across 25 minutes during Sunday's 138-118 win over Washington.
items.story: Queen has been a volatile fantasy asset lately, but Sunday's game was a step in the right direction. Over his last eight outings, the rookie has seen 21.1 minutes per contest with 9.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 0.8 blocks on 39.7 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Queen totaled 19 points (6-13 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 29 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 137-117 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: The Pelicans' top two scorers on the night both came from the second unit, as Jeremiah Fears paced the team with a career-high 28 points. Queen hadn't scored more than eight points in any of the prior three games since shifting back to the bench, while DeAndre Jordan has done little since joining the starting five. Even with the Pelicans in full tank mode, it's not clear how long that arrangement might last.

items.headline: Queen won't start against the Warriors on Tuesday.
items.story: With Dejounte Murray starting in his return from a torn Achilles, the Pelicans will keep DeAndre Jordan in the starting five and deploy Queen off the bench for the first time since Nov. 14. The rookie first-rounder has averaged 12.4 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 2.2 combined steals-plus-blocks while shooting 56.4 percent from the field in 27.1 minutes per game across seven February appearances.

items.headline: Queen registered 18 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, two blocks and three steals across 28 minutes during Friday's 139-118 loss to Milwaukee.
items.story: The rookie center just missed recording his 11th double-double of the season, and Queen's five combined steals-plus-blocks was his highest total since the calendar flipped to 2026 -- he racked up five blocks and two steals against the Bulls on New Year's Eve. Queen is still prone to some inconsistency, but over the last eight games he's flashed an impressive collection of skills, averaging 13.5 points, 6.6 boards, 3.4 assists, 1.1 steals, 1.1 blocks and 0.9 threes while shooting 57.1 percent from the floor and 63.6 percent (7-for-11) from long distance during that span.

items.headline: Queen notched eight points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist, one block and three steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 120-94 win over the Kings.
items.story: With the Pelicans buried in the standings, the rookie first-rounder looks to be cemented as the team's top center from here on out. Queen has been prone to the occasional dud, but he's shown plenty of potential across the board in 2025-26. Over his last eight outings, Queen has averaged 11.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.9 blocks in 25.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Queen accumulated 16 points (5-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals over 31 minutes during Monday's 102-95 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: This was a terrific showing for the rookie as he continues to be a bright spot for the club. Although the Pelicans do not have their first-round pick this season, the team may end up being sellers at the trade deadline. If they unload a player or two, Queen could potentially see a bump in usage.

items.headline: Queen posted 22 points (8-12 FG, 6-7 FT), nine rebounds, seven assists and two blocks over 34 minutes during Friday's 114-106 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Queen snapped a four-game, single-digit scoring streak in Friday's win, and he did a much better job of asserting himself in the offense and taking advantage of matchups whenever he had a smaller defender on him. The Pelicans have now won three of their past four games, and they'll look to keep the good times rolling Saturday in Philadelphia.

items.headline: Queen accumulated four points (2-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist over 17 minutes during Sunday's 104-95 win over San Antonio.
items.story: It was one of Queen's worst performances of his rookie season, and he was soundly outplayed by Yves Missi. Queen's starting role appears to be safe for now, but he certainly has some competition. Over his last appearances, Queen has averaged 8.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 23.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Queen amassed 14 points (5-11 FG, 4-4 FT), 12 rebounds and three assists over 28 minutes during Friday's 127-119 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After finishing with just four points on 0-of-5 shooting in Wednesday's win over the Nets, Queen bounced back Friday. The rookie big man was one of six Pelicans players to score in double figures and has posted at least 10 points in four of his last five outings. Additionally, the Maryland product grabbed a game-best 12 boards, securing his fourth double-double in eight appearances this month. During that span, Queen has averaged 10.1 points, 9.9 rebounds and 5.5 assists across 27.1 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Queen finished with 10 points (5-10 FG), 13 rebounds and five assists across 29 minutes during Tuesday's 122-116 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: It was the ninth double-double of the season for Queen, seven of which have come in his last 14 games. Over that stretch, the rookie center is averaging 12.9 points, 9.6 boards, 4.9 assists, 1.4 blocks and 1.1 steals in 28.1 minutes. He continues to look like something of a steal himself as the 13th overall pick in the 2025 Draft.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (groin) won't play in Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
items.story: Antetokounmpo is dealing with a groin injury. He was initially listed as questionable, though he has since been ruled out, marking his first absence of the year. His next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday against Philadelphia. In the meantime, Bobby Portis and Andrew Wiggins are candidates to fill the void in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Antetokounmpo previously dealt with a wrist injury in November, and he's now working through a groin issue that puts his status for Sunday's game up in the air. He has yet to miss a game this season, but if he's not cleared to play against Oklahoma City, then Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis would be the top candidates to enter Miami's starting lineup.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo chipped in 27 points (7-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 13-16 FT), 14 rebounds, nine assists, one block and one steal across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Antetokounmpo nearly recorded a triple-double in his first matchup against his former team, helping Miami extend its winning streak to six games. The superstar forward has registered four consecutive double-doubles, averaging 29.5 points, 12.5 rebounds and 6.3 assists during that stretch while shooting an impressive 73.7 percent from the field. His elite efficiency and consistent contributions across multiple categories continue to make him one of fantasy basketball's most valuable players.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo supplied 27 points (7-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 13-16 FT), 14 rebounds, nine assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: This was Antetokounmpo's third straight double-double and his 12th of the season. When punting free throws, Antetokounmpo has been a top-five producer this season with averages of 28.2 points, 12.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.3 swats per contest on 60.2 percent shooting from the field and 64.5 percent at the line.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo chipped in 20 points (8-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 13 rebounds, six assists, three blocks and one steal across 29 minutes in Monday's 128-110 win over Houston.
items.story: Antetokounmpo paced the Heat in scoring while hauling in a game-high rebound total. Monday marked the superstar forward's 11th double-double of the campaign, with 10 of those coming over his past 11 tilts. Through 14 games in his first season in Miami, Antetokounmpo has dominated to the tune of 28.3 points, 12.5 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.3 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo delivered 34 points (13-17 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-9 FT), 14 rebounds, eight assists, a steal and three blocks across 31 minutes in Saturday's 137-117 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Antetokounmpo followed Friday's 37-point performance against Cleveland with another dominant outing, this time coming within two assists of a triple-double. He's scored at least 30 points in his last three appearances, and his partnership with Bam Adebayo is beginning to produce the results Miami envisioned. Antetokounmpo has notched 10 double-doubles over his last 11 appearances.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available to play in Saturday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Antetokounmpo has been dealing with a right wrist sprain recently, but it hasn't stopped him from suiting up, as he's yet to miss a game this season. Miami has won three consecutive contests, and Antetokounmpo will be looking to make it three straight outings with 30-plus points.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Antetokounmpo has been a mainstay on the injury report of late with a right wrist sprain, though he's expected to play in the second leg of this back-to-back set. The superstar forward is coming off a 37-point effort and has averaged 28.8 points, 12.3 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 2.1 combined steals-plus-blocks per game through six outings in November.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo recorded 37 points (15-20 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 6-11 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block over 31 minutes during Friday's 133-121 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo combined for 74 points against Cleveland, illustrating how dangerous Miami's frontcourt pairing can be when both players are clicking. The change of scenery hasn't altered Antetokounmpo's elite scoring and rebounding potential, although his free-throw shooting remains a familiar concern in category leagues. His ability to produce dominant numbers without requiring excessive minutes continues to make him one of fantasy basketball's premier options, even if this game snapped his run of double-doubles at eight contests. He's averaging 28.8 points, 12.3 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.3 blocks per game in his six appearances since the beginning of November.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Friday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The superstar forward is ready to suit up Friday despite dealing with a wrist sprain. Barring any setbacks, Antetokounmpo should be able to handle a normal workload and is looking to push his streak of double-doubles with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds up to nine games.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is probable for Friday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The superstar forward appears on track to suit up Friday despite dealing with a wrist sprain. Barring any setbacks, Antetokounmpo should be able to handle a normal workload and will be aiming to extend his streak of double-doubles with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds to nine games.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo racked up 30 points (12-21 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-9 FT), 11 rebounds and four assists over 31 minutes in Tuesday's 115-109 win over the Jazz.
items.story: This was Antetokounmpo's third 30-point, 10-rebound double-double of the year, and he's double-doubled in all but two games this season. The 31-year-old superstar has been playing well for Miami, averaging 27.7 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.9 stocks per game on 56.7 percent shooting from the field and 61.6 percent at the stripe.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Tuesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Antetokounmpo was initially listed as probable, though there was added concern regarding his availability after he was downgraded to questionable late Tuesday. However, the multi-time All-Star is good to go, avoiding his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Antetokounmpo was tagged as probable to play Tuesday, but he's now being downgraded to questionable versus Utah due to a right wrist sprain. Over his last seven games, Antetokounmpo has racked up double-doubles in every outing while recording two triple-doubles. If he can't play, Bam Adebayo, Davion Mitchell and Klay Thompson will carry the offensive burden for Miami, with Bobby Portis and Andrew Wiggins getting extra burn off the bench.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo is probable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz due to a right wrist sprain.
items.story: Antetokounmpo has found his way onto the injury report over Miami's last few matchups due to a wrist issue, but he's yet to miss any time. That trend looks like it will continue Tuesday in Utah.

items.headline: Antetokounmpo posted 29 points (14-23 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-7 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two steals over 34 minutes during Sunday's 114-108 victory over the Kings.
items.story: The 29 points led the Heat on the night. Antetokounmpo has scored 20-plus points in nine of his first 10 games with his new team, and he's recorded at least a double-double in seven straight contests, with two triple-doubles in the mix. During that seven-game stretch, the 31-year-old superstar is averaging 27.1 points, 14.9 boards, 6.3 assists, 1.4 blocks and 0.9 steals while shooting 56.4 percent from the floor.

items.headline: The Nets exercised Saraf's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
items.story: Brooklyn will retain Saraf for another season as the young guard continues his development. The decision reflects the organization's commitment to evaluating its recent draft investments, though it doesn't signal any immediate change in his playing time. Saraf will need to establish a consistent rotation role before becoming a reliable fantasy contributor.

items.headline: The Nets assigned Saraf to the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday.
items.story: Saraf will have an opportunity to receive more consistent playing time with Brooklyn's G League affiliate after seeing limited action early in the NBA season. The second-year guard faces considerable competition for backcourt minutes with the Nets and is unlikely to hold significant fantasy value unless his role expands.

items.headline: Saraf (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Brooklyn opted not to use Saraf in its season opener, leaving the young guard outside the initial backcourt rotation. His playing time could remain sporadic while the Nets evaluate their other perimeter options.

items.headline: Saraf finished with eight points (3-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists in 15 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: Saraf knocked down a pair of three-pointers and committed only one turnover during his limited run. The second-year guard is competing for minutes in a crowded Brooklyn backcourt and will look to build on an efficient preseason opener.

items.headline: Saraf (rest) is in line for a reserve role in 2026-27 after the Nets drafted Mikel Brown earlier this summer.
items.story: The 2025 first-rounder bookended his rookie campaign as a starter, but a bench role appears more likely to open this season now that Brown is in the fold and Egor Demin is healthy. Nolan Traore is recovering from offseason knee surgery but is expected to be ready for the start of training camp in the fall, so Saraf is set to battle with youngsters Traore and Drake Powell as well as veterans Keon Ellis and Terance Mann for playing time in the second unit.

items.headline: Saraf (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Saraf is healthy but will be sidelined for the Nets' Summer League finale for rest purposes. He'll close the summer averaging 10.0 points, 3.3 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 23.9 minutes per contest across six appearances between the California Classic and Las Vegas Summer League.

items.headline: Saraf finished with 15 points (4-14 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), one rebound, five assists and one block over 32 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Saraf didn't have his best showing Saturday. He shot an inefficient 4-for-14 from the field while failing to make any of his attempts from behind the arc. Saraf, the 2025 No. 26 overall pick, appeared in 44 regular-season games for the Nets as a rookie, averaging 7.5 points, 2.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.9 steals across 20.8 minutes. Several aspects of the 20-year-old's game need improvement, and while he could earn a larger role during the 2026-27 campaign, he will continue to face stiff competition for minutes.

items.headline: Saraf recorded 15 points (6-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt), seven assists, three rebounds and one steal in 27 minutes of Monday's 100-79 Summer League win over the Warriors Blue.
items.story: It's been a decent start to the offseason for Brooklyn's second-year guard. Through two games, he's averaging 12.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.5 three-pointers on 45.5 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Saraf (undisclosed) is available for Monday's California Classic Summer League game against Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Saraf sat out Sunday's win over the Bucks -- Brooklyn's second game of a back-to-back-to-back set -- due to undisclosed reasons. However, he'll return for the Nets' final California Classic contest. Across 27 minutes in Saturday's loss to Sacramento, the 20-year-old point guard posted 10 points, six rebounds, one assist and one block.

items.headline: Saraf (undisclosed) will be inactive for Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Saraf will be held out of the second leg of a back-to-back-to-back set, and his next chance to play will come Monday against the Warriors. Dion Brown should be able to enter the rotation Sunday with Saraf inactive.

items.headline: Saraf finished with 10 points (4-10 FG, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block across 27 minutes in Saturday's 79-76 California Classic Summer League loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Saraf had a slow start to his inaugural season in 2025-26. However, he had a strong finish to the campaign by averaging 14.0 points, 3.8 assists and 1.0 steals across five regular-season games in April. Saraf's production could improve in 2026-27, though he won't have an easy path to substantial playing time, especially with Egor Demin (foot) healthy and Nolan Traore looking for minutes. Additionally, the Nets added Louisville guard Mikel Brown using the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

items.headline: Saraf should have more competition for playing time in the backcourt after the Nets selected Mikel Brown with the No. 6 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Saraf, a 2025 first-round pick, opened his rookie season as a starter before becoming more of a part-time player, bouncing back and forth from the G League throughout the course of the year. It wasn't until the late stages of the regular season that Brooklyn handed him more of a featured role, as the team battled a litany of injuries down the stretch and needed healthy bodies to soak up extra minutes. Saraf could carve out a role as the top backup point guard in 2026-27, but the addition of Brown complicates his path to steady minutes.

items.headline: Saraf amassed 15 points (6-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, four assists and two steals over 26 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 136-101 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Saraf's rookie season officially came to an end Sunday. He spent lots of time in the G League as well, but he amassed 44 regular-season appearances at the NBA level. He didn't have much fantasy appeal until the very end of the campaign, finishing with averages of 7.5 points, 3.3 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 0.9 steals on 39.6 percent shooting in 20.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Saraf logged 19 points (8-16 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one block in 28 minutes during Thursday's 123-94 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: The Nets were without most of their roster for the front end of this back-to-back set, and only seven players saw the floor as a result. Although he's seen healthy workloads, Saraf is averaging just 11.8 points, 4.1 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 26.7 minutes per contest over his last 13 appearances.

items.headline: Saraf closed Tuesday's 96-90 win over Milwaukee with 19 points (5-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 9-10 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 36 minutes.
items.story: Saraf didn't have a good shooting performance Tuesday night but going 9-for-10 from the charity stripe salvaged his scoring output, and he complemented it with decent numbers in peripheral categories. Saraf has started just three times since the beginning of March, but he's been showing what he can do of late with an uptick in his playing time. He has scored in double digits in five of his last eight appearances, a stretch in which he's averaging 11.5 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game despite shooting just 40.2 percent from the floor and 18.8 percent from deep.

items.headline: Saraf will start Tuesday against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Saraf will start in his return from a one-game absence, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Malachi Smith, Drake Powell, E.J. Liddell and Trevon Scott. Across seven starts this season, Saraf has posted averages of 5.7 points, 3.9 assists, and 2.4 turnovers per game.

items.headline: Saraf (back) is available for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Saraf didn't play in Sunday's 121-115 win over the Wizards. However, he was listed as probable heading into the meeting with Milwaukee, and it's now confirmed that he will avoid a second consecutive absence. The rookie has had a quiet start to his NBA career, averaging 6.6 points, 1.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.8 steals while shooting 38.2 percent from the field and 21.6 percent from deep across 19.6 minutes in 40 appearances.

items.headline: Saraf (back) is probable for Tuesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Saraf was held out of Sunday's contest due to back soreness, but the issue should cost him only one game. Expect confirmation on his availability for Tuesday closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Saraf (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.

items.headline: Saraf (back tightness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Saraf was a late addition to the injury report, and the Nets may err on the side of caution. Nolan Traore and Tyson Etienne could see more minutes if Saraf is held out.

items.headline: Saraf amassed two points (1-4 FG), two rebounds and four assists across 25 minutes during Friday's 141-107 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Saraf continues to play through some recent struggles, turning in his third straight subpar performance. During that time, he has averaged just 5.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.3 assists, barely making him a top-400 player. With continued uncertainty regarding the Brooklyn rotation, Saraf is not someone who needs to be rostered outside very deep leagues.

items.headline: Saraf will come off the bench for Friday's game against the Lakers, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Nolan Traore will replace Saraf in the first unit for Friday's game. As a reserve this season, Saraf has averaged 6.8 points, 3.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game.

items.headline: Saraf closed with 14 points (5-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 109-106 loss to Golden State.

Saraf has scored in double digits in seven of his last eight games (two starts), averaging 12.3 points, 4.5 assists, 2.5 boards and 1.6 steals in 26.6 minutes during that span.

items.headline: Saraf is part of the first unit for Wednesday's game against the Warriors, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Saraf will make his seventh start of the campaign, filling in for Nolan Traore (rest).  Saraf has been playing well as of late, averaging 12.0 points, 4.1 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.6 steals across 25.9 minutes spanning his past seven outings.

items.headline: Saraf closed Sunday's 126-122 loss to the Kings with 22 points (10-20 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal in 29 minutes.
items.story: The 22 points were a season high for Saraf, who crossed the 20-point marker for the first time this season. With the Nets playing out the final weeks of a losing campaign, Brooklyn should continue getting an extended look at the rookie first-rounder. Over his last six contests, Saraf has averaged 12.3 points, 4.5 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 27.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Saraf (foot) is available to play Friday against the Knicks.
items.story: Saraf will shake off a probable tag for this contest. Over his last two appearances, he's averaging 13.5 points, 4.5 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 3.0 steals in 27.5 minutes per contest. Saraf should continue to play heavy minutes for a banged-up Nets squad.

items.headline: Saraf is probable for Friday's game against the Knicks with left foot soreness.
items.story: Saraf is likely to end a one-game absence with the injury. The rookie first-rounder is beginning to flash some of his potential, scoring at least 10 points and handing out at least four dimes in four consecutive appearances.

items.headline: Saraf (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.comreports.
items.story: Saraf was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. Nolan Traore, Drake Powell and Terance Mann could see a bit more run with Saraf out of the picture.

items.headline: Saraf is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to left foot soreness.
items.story: The questionable tag suggests that Saraf is day-to-day. Over his last eight contests, he's been more involved with averages of 7.9 points, 4.1 assists, 1.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 21.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Saraf contributed 15 points (5-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four assists and four steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 114-95 loss to Portland.
items.story: Saraf provided a spark off the bench, tallying 15 points while recording a game-high and season-best four steals. The guard has now scored in double figures in each of his past four games, a notable stretch considering he had reached the 10-point mark just four times across the rest of the campaign. With fellow rookie Egor Demin (foot) out for the year, Saraf should continue to see extended opportunities down the stretch of the regular season.

items.headline: Saraf (calf) is available to play Monday against Portland.
items.story: Saraf will shake off a questionable tag for this contest. In his most recent outing Saturday against the 76ers, the rookie put up 12 points, five assists, four rebounds and two steals across 31 minutes. With Brooklyn shorthanded, Saraf should see 20-plus minutes again.

items.headline: Saraf is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Portland due to a left calf contusion.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder likely picked up the injury during Saturday's game against the 76ers, when he played 31 minutes and finished with 12 points, five assists, four rebounds and two steals in a 104-97 loss. Tyson Etienne would see a significant bump in minutes if Saraf was ruled out for Monday's home contest.

items.headline: Saraf won't start Saturday's game against the 76ers, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: With Nolan Traore back in action, Saraf will slide to a reserve role. However, the rookie could still see plenty of action, given Michael Porter (ankle) and Drake Powell (knee) are out Saturday.

items.headline: Saraf will start Thursday's game against the Hawks, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Saraf will step into the starting lineup Thursday with Nolan Traore (rest) unavailable. This will mark Saraf's first start since Oct. 29, when he failed to score in 12 minutes against Atlanta.

items.headline: Saraf (back) is available to play Monday against Memphis.
items.story: Saraf will shake off a probable tag for this contest. Over his last five games, he's averaging 4.6 points and 2.4 rebounds in 14.6 minutes.

items.headline: Saraf (back) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Memphis.

items.headline: Brooklyn recalled Saraf from the G League's Long Island Nets on Friday, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: In a related move, the Nets assigned Drake Powell to Long Island, so the team could turn to Saraf to take Powell's spot in the rotation in Friday's game in Boston. Saraf hasn't made an appearance at the NBA level since the All-Star break, but he shined in his most recent G League outing Thursday in a 119-116 loss to the Grand Rapids Gold, finishing with 21 points (9-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three steals, two rebounds and two assists in 30 minutes.

items.headline: Saraf supplied 12 points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds and two assists over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 115-110 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After scoring three points on 1-of-6 shooting from the field in Monday's win over Chicago, Saraf bounced back on the offensive end Wednesday. The rookie first-rounder was one of six Brooklyn players to score in double figures, marking just the second time over his last 10 outings that he has reached double digits. Saraf has spent a considerable amount of time with the G League's Long Island Nets this season but has appeared in each of Brooklyn's last 10 games. With the club near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings, he may continue to see increased playing time as Brooklyn prioritizes its youth movement.

items.headline: The Nets will recall Saraf from the G League's Long Island Nets ahead of Sunday's game versus the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With both Cam Thomas (ankle) and Nolan Traore (illness) unavailable for Sunday's game, Saraf will be up with Brooklyn to bolster the team's depth in the backcourt, though he's not a lock to enter the rotation. The rookie first-round pick has made just 12 appearances for Brooklyn this season and is averaging 5.4 points and has a 2.8:1.9 assist-to-turnover ratio in 16.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Nets assigned Saraf (knee) to the G League's Long Island Nets on Saturday.
items.story: Saraf missed the parent club's past two games due to a left knee issue, and it's unclear if he'll play in Long Island's matchup against the Stockton Kings on Monday. Over 11 appearances in the G League, the rookie first-rounder has averaged 13.6 points, 4.4 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 25.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Saraf is out for Friday's game against the Clippers due to left knee soreness.
items.story: It'll be a second straight absence for Saraf, whose next chance to play comes Sunday against the Grizzlies. Fellow rookie Nolan Traore could see an uptick in playing time in the Brooklyn backcourt Friday.

items.headline: Saraf has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Magic due to left knee soreness.
items.story: Saraf was recalled from the G League by the Nets on Monday, but the rookie first-rounder will not be available for Wednesday's home tilt. He'll look to progress enough in his recovery to be available for Friday's game against the Clippers. He's bounced back and forth between the G League and NBA this season, averaging 5.4 points, 2.8 assists, 1.6 rebounds and 0.7 steals over 16.9 minutes per game in 12 regular-season outings (five starts) with the parent club.

items.headline: Brooklyn recalled Saraf from the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday.
items.story: It appears the rookie first-rounder is joining the parent team for Wednesday's game against the Magic. However, most of Saraf's development should continue to come in the G League this year.

items.headline: Saraf (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the 76ers, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: As expected, Saraf will overcome a probable tag due to a sprained right ankle. The rookie first-rounder has averaged 5.4 points, 2.8 assists and 1.6 rebounds in 16.9 minutes per contest through 12 regular-season games thus far.

items.headline: Saraf (ankle) is probable for Tuesday's game against the 76ers, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Saraf was recalled from the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday, and while he's dealing with a sprained right ankle, he's likely to be available for the parent club against Philadelphia. The rookie first-rounder has appeared in 12 regular-season NBA games (five starts) thus far, averaging 5.4 points and 2.8 assists in 16.9 minutes a night. However, he's coming off a 40-point (14-26 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT) explosion for Long Island on Monday afternoon.

items.headline: The Nets recalled Saraf from the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday.
items.story: After missing time recently due to an illness and heading to the G League, Saraf will return to Brooklyn ahead of Tuesday's matchup against the 76ers. The rookie first-rounder has appeared in 12 regular-season games (five starts) with the parent club, averaging 5.4 points and 2.8 assists in 16.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Saraf was assigned to the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday.
items.story: Saraf has been dealing with an illness that held him out of Brooklyn's last two games, and now he will spend some time with the Nets' G League affiliate, assuming he is healthy enough to play. In 12 NBA games this season, Saraf averages 5.4 points, 1.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.7 steals, 0.3 blocks and 0.8 threes across 16.8 minutes.

items.headline: Jones finished Friday's 126-120 loss to the Thunder with 14 points (4-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 33 minutes.
items.story: Jones turned in one of his better offensive showings of the season. He's been knocking down threes at a much better clip over the past week after a cold start. The veteran wing is valued mostly for his defense, but the outside shooting gives 5-12 New Orleans a needed boost.

items.headline: Jones had nine points (3-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt), one rebound, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Jones matched his season high with three triples, but his defensive production remains inconsistent. He's recorded multiple steals just twice in his last five games, while his rebounding has been particularly underwhelming. Despite a steady rotation role, his limited offensive involvement makes him difficult to trust outside deeper category leagues

items.headline: Jones ended with eight points (4-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Friday's 142-111 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Jones got the starting nod for the third straight game, matching a season high with 32 minutes. Although his role has increased over the past two weeks, his production has been far from ideal. In eight games during that span, he has averaged 8.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 three-pointers in 25.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jones will start Monday's game against the Warriors, Rod Walker of The Times-Picayune reports.
items.story: Jones will earn his fifth start of the 2026-27 campaign with Zion Williamson (rest) out Monday. Jones has averaged 9.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.5 minutes per tilt across four starts this season.

items.headline: Jones is not starting Friday against the Timberwolves,
items.story: Jones will return to the bench due to the return of Trey Murphy (knee). Jones is averaging just 6.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game this season while starting in four of his eight appearances.

items.headline: Jones amassed nine points (3-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Jones struggled to establish himself offensively but made all three of his field goals from beyond the arc. His defensive versatility remains his primary fantasy asset, though his limited scoring production and relatively modest workload capped his value Monday.

items.headline: Jones contributed 16 points (7-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, an assist and two steals across 32 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 win over the Kings.
items.story: Jones made his first start of the season due to the absence of Dejounte Murray (personal) and delivered efficient scoring inside the arc while adding two steals, reinforcing his value as a defensive specialist. Jones' fantasy appeal is strongest in category-based formats that reward defensive production, but his usual bench role limits his upside. Before Thursday, he averaged just 3.5 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals on 17.5 minutes per game off the bench.

items.headline: Jones will start Thursday's game against the Kings, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
items.story: With Dejounte Murray (personal) unavailable, Jones will get the starting nod for the first time this season. He has yet to play 20-plus minutes in a game and is averaging 3.5 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 17.5 minutes per contest across four regular-season outings.

items.headline: Jones supplied two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 16 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Jones continues to play a minimal role, having logged no more than 18 minutes in any game thus far this season. Once seen as a key piece for the Pelicans, it would appear as though he is now on the outside looking in when it comes to meaningful minutes. While he can be viewed as a steals specialist, the fact of the matter is that he is averaging only 0.7 steals per game to this point.

items.headline: Jones is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Pacers.
items.story: The Pelicans will go small for Wednesday's season opener, starting Dejounte Murray and Jeremiah Fears in the backcourt. Jones still should see quality minutes in the reserve role, but his upside will be limited.

items.headline: Jones chipped in seven points (3-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and one steal across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Though the expectation this offseason has been that Jones would start for the Pelicans, his role doesn't appear to be set in stone quite yet. Bennedict Mathurin remains a candidate for a spot in the first unit to begin the new season.

items.headline: Jones won't start Thursday's preseason game against the Heat.
items.story: Jones got the starting nod in the Pelicans' preseason-opening win over the Thunder on Tuesday, though he'll slide to the second unit Thursday. Bennedict Mathurin will enter the first unit in Jones' place.

items.headline: Jones is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's preseason game against the Thunder, Andrew Lopez of Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Jones will start on the wing, with Zion Williamson and Yves Missi as the frontcourt pairing. The former Alabama standout was limited to just 56 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 and averaged 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists while logging 28.4 minutes per game. If he stays healthy, he should be a lock in the starting unit.

items.headline: Jones continues to provide New Orleans with elite perimeter defense and positional versatility, making him one of the NBA's premier role players.
items.story: While Jones' offensive responsibilities remain modest, his ability to contribute steals, blocks and efficient complementary production keeps him fantasy relevant. His role as the Pelicans' top defensive wing should remain unchanged heading into 2026-27.

items.headline: Jones (rest) is out for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Jones will end the season on the sidelines for rest purposes, as the Pelicans will assess other players on the roster. Jones featured in 56 games for the Pelicans in the 2025-26 regular season, averaging 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.6 steals across 28.4 minutes per contest. He also shot 38.3 percent from the floor, and in almost every statistic, this was a step in the wrong direction compared to the 2024-25 campaign.

items.headline: Jones (rest) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Jones will sit out for a second straight contest as the Pelicans continue to give some other players a look in the rotation. It remains to be seen if Jones will suit up for the season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Jones (rest) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Jones may sit out the Pelicans' penultimate game of the season for rest purposes. His absence would open up additional playing time for Derik Queen, Micah Peavy and Jordan Hawkins.

items.headline: Head coach James Borrego said that Jones will be in uniform for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, but he doesn't expect him to play, Erin Summers of the Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Zion Williamson and Saddiq Bey are also expected to sit out Tuesday's game, which should result in big minutes for Derik Queen and Micah Peavy. It'll be interesting to see if Jones plays Friday in Boston.

items.headline: Jones recorded three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal across 13 minutes during Friday's 117-113 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: Jones saw his role reduced in a big way Friday, as the Pelicans elected to lean more heavily on their bench players such as Derik Queen (28 minutes) and Micah Peavy (32 minutes). New Orleans doesn't have much to play for after being eliminated from postseason contention, so it seems the club is aiming to develop younger talent down the stretch of the regular season. Still, Jones has continued to be part of the starting lineup, so unless the team reports otherwise, he figures to be a bigger part of the game plan heading into Sunday's tilt against the Magic.

items.headline: Jones racked up 11 points (4-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt), four assists and one block over 27 minutes during Thursday's 129-108 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Although the Pelicans were missing Trey Murphy (ankle), Jones managed just 11 points in the loss. He remains a low-end fantasy asset, posting averages of 10.3 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 rebounds, 1.6 steals and 2.0 three-pointers over his last eight games.

items.headline: Jones provided 11 points (4-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Thursday's 105-99 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The Pelicans appear to have a revolving door at the center position, and Jones' versatility should keep him cemented in the starting lineup going forward. Jones has averaged 10.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.2 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 31.2 minutes per tilt in his last five games, offering him some low-end fantasy appeal in nine-category setups.

items.headline: Jones notched 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 36 minutes during Wednesday's 122-111 win over Toronto.
items.story: Jones put together a solid line and was on fire from beyond the arc. Overall, he's been a hit-or-miss fantasy asset this season with averages of 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.4 three-pointers on 38.9 percent shooting.

items.headline: Jones totaled 14 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 31 minutes during Friday's 118-116 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Jones has scored in double figures in two straight games for the first time since mid-December. Since returning to action at the end of January, Jones' production has been modest; he's averaging 8.3 points, 3.6 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.6 steals while shooting 36.9 percent from the field.

items.headline: Jones notched two points (1-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and four steals over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 110-101 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Jones continues to struggle offensively, scoring in single digits for the fourth time in his past five outings. During this span, Jones has averaged 6.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 2.4 steals in 29.4 minutes per tilt while shooting a paltry 29.3 percent from the field.

items.headline: Jones produced five points (1-8 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists, one block and five steals in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 113-109 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Jones recorded at least five steals for the second time this season, and he snatched eight against Houston on Dec. 18. Jones has been a little underwhelming for the most part in recent weeks, however, as he's averaging 7.3 points, 3.4 assists, 3.1 rebounds, 1.9 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 30.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jones registered eight points (3-11 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 0-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists and one block across 30 minutes during Monday's 120-94 win over the Kings.
items.story: With Jordan Poole totally phased out of the New Orleans rotation, Jones seems to be locked in as the top shooting guard the rest of the way. Jones still appears to be knocking off some rust after missing extended time with an ankle sprain in January. Over his last nine outings, Jones has averaged 7.6 points, 3.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 29.5 minutes per game while shooting a poor 24.4 percent from deep.

items.headline: Jones accumulated 12 points (4-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 36 minutes during Monday's 102-95 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Jones cashed in a season-high four triples Monday after failing to eclipse more than one in a game since returning from his ankle injury. While he has not shot the ball well from beyond the arc recently, converting just 18.2 percent of his three-point attempts in the five games prior, Jones' performance Monday can be an encouraging sign that he may be getting back on track in terms of his efficiency.

items.headline: Jones notched nine points (3-12 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, five assists, two blocks and two steals across 27 minutes during Tuesday's 104-95 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Jones opened Tuesday's game with six straight misses and never found his footing offensively. The struggles were team-wide, as the Pelicans shot just 34-for-99 from the floor and 10-for-40 from three-point range against the Thunder's No. 1-rated defense. On the positive side, Jones contributed four stocks and five assists without a turnover and ended his evening with a plus-9 differential.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) finished with zero points (0-3 FG, 0-3 3Pt), five assists, two rebounds, two steals and two blocks across 25 minutes in Friday's 133-127 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: With Jones making his return from an eight-game absence due to a right ankle sprain, the Pelicans opted to include him as part of a starting unit that lacked a true point guard while Jeremiah Fears moved to the bench. Jones ended up taking on some extra playmaking responsibilities as a result and netted a season-high assist total, and his output in that category plus strong defensive numbers helped offset the lack of scoring production. Assuming his ankle presented no complications during Friday's contest, Jones could see his minutes pick up slightly in the Pelicans' next game Sunday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) is available for Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Jones will shake off his questionable tag and return from an eight-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. The 27-year-old forward has appeared in just one game since Dec. 23, so it wouldn't be surprising to see him operate under a minutes restriction. Still, his return will leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Micah Peavy, Bryce McGowens and Jordan Hawkins.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Jones has a chance to end a seven-game absence due to an ankle sprain. If the forward makes his return to the New Orleans lineup, fewer minutes would be available for Saddiq Bey and Yves Missi in the frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Jones, who has missed the past seven games for New Orleans, was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. He is getting closer to a return, however. His next chance to play comes Friday against Memphis.

items.headline: Jones is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pistons with a sprained right ankle.
items.story: Jones is trying to end a seven-game absence with the sprain. However, his potential absence would leave Saddiq Bey locked into significant minutes, while the door would stay open for Yves Missi to soak up more playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Jones hasn't taken the court since Jan. 6 due to a right ankle sprain. The team has yet to provide a clear timetable for his return, but his next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against Detroit.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Jones will miss a sixth straight matchup while tending to a right ankle sprain. His next chance at a return will arrive Sunday in Houston.

items.headline: Jones is out for Wednesday's game against the Nets due to a sprained right ankle.
items.story: Wednesday is marking a fifth consecutive absence for Jones, whose next chance to play arrives Friday in Indiana. Saddiq Bey is primed for a big workload against Brooklyn, with Jordan Hawkins also being a candidate for an expanded role off the bench.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Jones is set to miss his fourth straight game due to a right ankle sprain, and he has appeared in just one matchup since Dec. 23. With the 27-year-old forward on the shelf, Bryce McGowens and Micah Peavy are candidates for increased roles, especially if Saddiq Bey (hip) is downgraded from questionable to out. Jones' next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against the Nets.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Jones is set to miss a third consecutive game due to a sprained right ankle, which is the same injury that caused him to miss seven straight games prior to Jan. 6 against the Lakers. Bryce McGowens and Karlo Matkovic are the top candidates to start Sunday in Jones' absence. Jones' next opportunity to play is Tuesday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) will not play Friday against the Wizards, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
items.story: No surprise here, as Jones was previously listed as doubtful. Meanwhile, Trey Murphy (back, ankle) remains questionable. Guys like Jordan Poole, Bryce McGowens and Micah Peavy may see increased roles with Jones out of the mix.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Jones appears likely to miss his second straight game Friday. Meanwhile, Trey Murphy (ankle, back) is questionable for the Pelicans. With this news, the Pelicans may need players like Jordan Poole, Bryce McGowens and Micah Peavy to step up once again.

items.headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Jones has been downgraded from questionable to out because of a sore right ankle. The 27-year-old had missed seven straight games due to a sprained right ankle before returning for Tuesday's game against the Lakers. His next chance to play will come Friday at Washington.

items.headline: Jones is questionable for Wednesday's game in Atlanta due to right ankle soreness.
items.story: Pelicans' head coach James Borrego said after Tuesday's loss to the Lakers that Jones was in danger of sitting out Wednesday's game due to the ankle issue, and now he's officially being listed as questionable. With both Jones and Trey Murphy (back) uncertain for Wednesday's game, Jordan Poole could see a sizeable uptick in minutes in a potential starting role versus the Hawks.

items.headline: Clowney (illness) is available for Friday's game against Detroit, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Clowney popped up on the injury report due to an illness. However, he now has the green light to suit up for Friday's game versus the Pistons. The 22-year-old hasn't had a productive 2026-27 campaign, averaging 6.3 points and 4.0 rebounds over 21.5 minutes per contest in four regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Clowney (illness) was downgraded to questionable for Friday's game versus Detroit, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Clowney woke up under the weather and could be a game-time call Friday. He's played a modest role so far with 21.5 minutes per contest. If he's unable to play, the team could rely more on Josh Minott.

items.headline: Clowney amassed three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to Boston.
items.story: Clowney made his lone field-goal attempt but was otherwise quiet offensively, attempting just one shot despite playing 24 minutes. The 22-year-old forward contributed two blocks, matching his total from his previous three appearances combined. Clowney has averaged just 6.3 points and 4.0 rebounds through four games, limiting his fantasy appeal despite a relatively steady role in Brooklyn's rotation.

items.headline: Clowney logged nine points (3-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, an assist and a steal across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 110-103 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Clowney was perfect from the field but attempted only three shots, highlighting his limited offensive involvement in Brooklyn's season opener. Still, his nine points were the third-best mark on the team behind Julius Randle (33) and Michael Porter (26). His move to a reserve role after starting in 60 of his 66 appearances in 2025-26 also raises questions about his fantasy outlook, particularly with Randle and Porter occupying prominent frontcourt roles. Unless Clowney earns additional minutes or becomes more involved offensively, his production could remain inconsistent despite his ability to contribute off the bench.

items.headline: Clowney finished with 15 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four assists, three rebounds and one steal across 22 minutes off the bench in Monday's 131-122 preseason win over Washington.
items.story: Clowney provided an offensive spark for Brooklyn, converting four of his six three-point attempts while also contributing as a facilitator. The 22-year-old forward committed zero turnovers and was one of five Nets players to score at least 15 points. His perimeter shooting should help his case for a meaningful role in Brooklyn's frontcourt rotation, though the team has several options competing for minutes.

items.headline: Clowney is not in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against Washington.
items.story: Clowney will retreat to the bench after finishing with 11 points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT) across 20 minutes as a starter Thursday against Philadelphia. The young forward will cede his starting role to Michael Porter, who missed the previous contest due to wrist soreness.

items.headline: Clowney recorded 11 points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one rebound, one steal and one block in 20 minutes during Thursday's 114-108 preseason win over the 76ers.
items.story: Clowney moved into the starting lineup, replacing Michael Porter, who was out due to a wrist injury. Although Clowney ended as one of five Nets players to score double digits, the rest of his box score was a little empty. He is expected to play a bench role when the season gets underway, leaving him off the radar when it comes to standard fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Clowney is in the starting lineup for Thursday's preseason game against the 76ers, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Clowney is expected to be a bench option in the regular season, but he'll get the starting nod Thursday because Michael Porter (wrist) won't start. Clowney is coming off a career-best 2025-26 season, averaging 12.3 points per game in 66 regular-season appearances, including 60 starts.

items.headline: Clowney acknowledged Monday that his offensive role will shrink following the Nets' acquisition of Julius Randle, adding that he's focused on improving defensively in order to earn playing time, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Clowney started 60 of his 66 regular-season appearances last campaign, averaging 12.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 27.0 minutes per game. Randle's arrival is expected to push the 22-year-old into a reserve role and reduce his shot volume, making Clowney's ability to contribute defensively and on the glass increasingly important to securing consistent minutes in Brooklyn's frontcourt.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is likely to move into a reserve role after the Nets acquired Julius Randle prior to Tuesday's draft.
items.story: Clowney was basically a full-time starter a year ago, coming off the bench just six times across 66 regular-season appearances. Now that Brooklyn has Randle in the fold, however, Clowney figures to open the new campaign as the primary backup power forward. Furthermore, the Nets' selection of Joshua Jefferson near the end of the first round of the 2026 NBA Draft clouds Clowney's fantasy outlook heading into 2026-27.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) won't play Sunday in Toronto, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Clowney will end up skipping Brooklyn's final five regular-season games for left ankle injury management. Through 66 games during his 2025-26 campaign, Clowney registered career highs in points (12.3), rebounds (4.1), assists (1.6), triples (2.0) and steals (0.8).

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) won't be available for Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Clowney is set to miss a fourth straight game Friday, remaining on what is an extensive injury report for the Nets. E.J. Liddell and Trevon Scott should continue to be in line for more frontcourt minutes.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Clowney will miss a third straight game due to a left ankle issue, and his penultimate chance to suit up this season will come Friday in Milwaukee. With the 21-year-old forward unavailable, Chaney Johnson, Jalen Wilson and Ochai Agbaji are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Clowney didn't suit up for the 121-115 win over Washington. He will now miss a second consecutive contest, meaning he will have only three more chances to play before the end of the Nets' season. With Clowney out again, Chaney Johnson could find himself remaining in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against Washington.
items.story: Clowney was added to the team's injury report as questionable due to a left ankle issue, and he's since been downgraded to out. Expect Chaney Johnson and Jalen Wilson to see more opportunities in the frontcourt Sunday as a result.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game versus the Wizards.
items.story: If Clowney needs to skip Sunday's game, there will be more minutes available for Josh Minott and Jalen Wilson. Check back closer to Sunday's tipoff for official confirmation on Clowney's status.

items.headline: Clowney was ejected in the third quarter of Friday's game against the Hawks after being assessed two technical fouls, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports. He'll finish with 12 points (4-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 21 minutes.
