items.story: Clowney was handed a technical following a scuffle with an opposing player, and he earned his second after appearing to say something to an official. Josh Minott and Chaney Johnson are candidates to pick up the slack for the remainder of the contest.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is good to go for Friday against the Hawks.
items.story: Clowney is no longer on the injury report after previously carrying a probable tag. The forward is averaging 7.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 18.5 minutes per game over his last eight appearances.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is probable for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Clowney is battling left ankle soreness, but the issue isn't likely to stop him from playing Friday. The Nets have been reducing Clowney's workload, as the third-year forward has averaged 7.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 18.5 minutes per tilt over his last eight games.

items.headline: Clowney ended with five points (2-6 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Friday's 116-99 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The third-year forward returned to the court after a four-game absence due to a wrist injury, but Clowney didn't make much of an impact. The 24 minutes were his biggest workload since March 7, and through 10 games this month, he's averaging just 9.7 points, 3.9 boards, 1.5 assists and 1.4 threes in 22.4 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) is available for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Clowney is back after a four-game stint on the sidelines, which could shift Terance Mann back to the second unit. There will also be fewer minutes available for Ziaire Williams and Chaney Johnson with Clowney active.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) is probable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Clowney is on track to return from a four-game absence Friday, but he'll likely have some minutes restrictions in his first game back. If Clowney is cleared, there will be less minutes available for Terance Mann, Ziaire Williams and Chaney Johnson.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Clowney will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a right wrist sprain, and it's not an encouraging sign that he continues to be ruled out a day in advance of tipoff. With Michael Porter (hamstring) and Danny Wolf (ankle) also out, Ziaire Williams, Jalen Wilson and Josh Minott are candidates to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) won't play in Monday's game versus Portland, per C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News.
items.story: Monday is set to be a third consecutive absence for Clowney due to a sprained right wrist. Chaney Johnson, E.J. Liddell and Tyson Etienne could all find themselves being more involved for the depleted Nets on Monday.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) won't play Sunday in Sacramento, according to Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: Clowney suffered a sprained right wrist in Wednesday's loss to OKC, and he was subsequently ruled out for Friday's game against New York. His next chance to suit up will be Monday in Portland. Without Clowney in the rotation, Ziaire Williams, averaging 11.4 points, 2.6 boards, 0.6 assists and 2.0 steals in eight starts this year, will presumably remain with the first five.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist), who's out for Friday's game against the Knicks, is doubtful for Sunday's contest versus the Kings, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Clowney is having his right wrist sprain evaluated, which will likely cost him at least two games. In his absence, the door is open for the likes of Chaney Johnson, Ziaire Williams and Drake Powell to claim a more sizable role.

items.headline: Clowney (wrist) won't play Friday versus the Knicks.
items.story: Clowney injured his wrist during Wednesday's loss to the Thunder and will now sit out Friday's game, which should open up minutes for Danny Wolf, Chaney Johnson and Josh Minott. Clowney's next chance to play will come Sunday in Sacramento, but with that game being the first of a back-to-back, he should be considered highly questionable for that one.

items.headline: Clowney won't return to Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to a right wrist sprain. He'll finish with three points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and two rebounds across eight minutes.
items.story: Clowney logged just under eight minutes in the first quarter and won't play in the final three due to the wrist injury. Danny Wolf and Chaney Johnson are candidates to see increased burn while Clowney is sidelined. His next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Clowney (rest) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Clowney is set to return from a one-game absence for rest purposes. Though he appears to be locked into a starting role, Clowney has logged 20 minutes or fewer in four consecutive contests while scoring 10 points or fewer in each outing during this stretch.

items.headline: Clowney (rest) has been ruled out for Monday's matchup with the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Clowney only logged 19 minutes his last time out, and Monday's game does not come in a back-to-back set, so the 21-year-old getting popped with a maintenance day is a bit egregious. With Clowney unavailable, Danny Wolf should get all the run he can handle and Josh Minott will have the chance for some extended minutes.

items.headline: Clowney had 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist across 20 minutes during Thursday's 108-97 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Clowney remained in the starting lineup, but his playing time has seen a sharp decline over the last week as the Nets experiment with different rotations. Even as a member of the first unit, the 21-year-old big man has seen his usage scaled back. After an eight-game stretch where he became a focal point of the rotation, averaging 28.9 minutes per contest, he has averaged just 19.3 minutes over his last three games.

items.headline: Clowney finished with 17 points (6-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals over 34 minutes during Thursday's 126-110 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Michael Porter led the way in scoring for the Nets in this loss, but Clowney's impact was big on both ends of the court as well. The big man hasn't recorded a double-double since mid-January, but his uptick in the scoring column can't be overlooked. He has scored in double digits in all but one of his last seven contests, though he's cleared the 15-point plateau just three times in that span.

items.headline: Clowney had 17 points (4-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 8-9 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 27 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Clowney was efficient from the floor and has now scored in double digits in five of his last six appearances, averaging 12.8 points and 3.7 boards per game over that stretch. One aspect that can't go overlooked is how comfortable Clowney has looked shooting the three of late. Not only is he shooting 48.1 percent from deep over that six-game span, but he's also drained at least one three-pointer in 10 straight games. He's attempting a career-best 6.3 three-point attempts per game this season.

items.headline: Clowney recorded 22 points (6-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 6-10 FT), five rebounds, one block and one steal across 33 minutes during Tuesday's 123-114 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Clowney notched his eighth game of the season with at least 20 points, drilling four triples for the third time in the last six games. The 21-year-old forward's numbers through eight games in February closely resemble his season-long averages, with 12.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.1 threes, 1.0 assist and 0.8 steals over 26.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Clowney amassed 12 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist and two steals over 31 minutes during Sunday's 115-104 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Clowney continues to play a key role for Brooklyn, but his fantasy output has been modest. Over his last four games, he's seeing 26.3 minutes per contest with 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.8 steals and 2.3 three-pointers on 44.4 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is off the injury report for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Clowney missed Brooklyn's final contest before the All-Star break, but he's all set to play Thursday. One of Ziaire Williams or Terance Mann is likely heading to the bench. Over his last four appearances, Clowney has averaged 11.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 2.0 three-pointers in 24.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Clowney was previously upgraded to available for Wednesday's contest but was unable to get through pregame warmups. The 21-year-old forward's next opportunity to play will come against Cleveland on Feb. 19. Danny Wolf, Jalen Wilson and Ziaire Williams are candidates for increased playing time due to Clowney being sidelined.

items.headline: Clowney (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against Indiana, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Clowney was previously considered probable due to a sprained left ankle, so his availability doesn't come as much of a surprise. With Michael Porter (knee) and Nic Claxton (hip) sidelined Wednesday, Clowney could take on a larger role offensively.

items.headline: Clowney is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Indiana due to a left ankle sprain, Meghan Triplett of YES Network reports.
items.story: Clowney is likely to play through a sprained left ankle for Wednesday's contest. The power forward is coming off back-to-back quality games, having posted 18 and 22 points, respectively.

items.headline: Clowney amassed 18 points (5-10 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 27 minutes during Saturday's 127-113 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: It was Clowney's best scoring effort since Jan. 16, when he struck for 23 points against the Bulls. The third-year forward scored just six points total in his first two February games after returning from a lower-back issue, but Saturday's performance suggests he's nearly back to 100 percent.

items.headline: Clowney (back) tallied six points (3-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes Tuesday in the Nets' 125-109 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Clowney stepped back into a starting role Tuesday in his return from a five-game absence due to a lower back sprain, resulting in Terance Mann moving to the bench. The third-year forward struggled to make an impact during his time on the court and fell well short of his season-long average of 28.6 minutes per game, though he sat out the entire fourth quarter and likely would have played more had the Nets been more competitive. Expect Clowney's minutes to pick up in the Nets' next game Thursday in Orlando.

items.headline: Clowney (back) is good to go for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Clowney is all set to return from a five-game absence. Given the lengthy rehab stint, he may face restrictions in his first game back. With this news, Danny Wolf is likely to retreat to the bench.

items.headline: Clowney is probable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers with a lower-back sprain, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Clowney is set to finish a five-game absence with the injury. His expected presence figures to force Danny Wolf to play a bench role Tuesday. Over his last six appearances, Clowney has averaged 12.5 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 30.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Clowney (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Clowney's absence will extend to five games while he's dealing with a lower-back injury, and his next opportunity to play is Tuesday against the Pistons. Danny Wolf has started each of the Nets' last two games and could remain in the starting lineup for as long as Clowney is sidelined.

items.headline: Clowney (back) won't play Friday in Utah, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: This will be Clowney's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's unclear if he's made any progress with his back issue. Danny Wolf should get another start Friday evening, and he could see some more shots falling his way with Michael Porter (personal) also unavailable.

items.headline: Clowney (back) is out for Thursday's game in Denver, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Thursday will mark Clowney's third consecutive game on the inactive list, but perhaps he'll be able to get back out there for Friday's game in Utah. Danny Wolf and Jalen Wilson wil likely help pick up the slack while Clowney is out.

items.headline: Clowney (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Clowney is set to miss a second consecutive game due to lower-back soreness, and he'll aim to progress enough in his recovery to return Thursday against the Nuggets. Terance Mann could remain in the starting lineup for Tuesday's contest in Clowney's absence.

items.headline: Missi closed Saturday's 114-91 loss to the Spurs with nine points (3-8 FG, 3-6 FT), 14 rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: Missi made his biggest impact on the glass and on defense, collecting 14 rebounds while adding three combined steals and blocks. His limited offensive involvement and struggles at the free-throw line remain concerns for category-based fantasy formats, but his rebounding and defensive upside make him useful when he receives a substantial frontcourt workload. He hasn't scored in double digits in any of his five appearances since returning from a knee injury Nov.  14, averaging just 5.2 points but adding 9.8 rebounds and a combined 2.2 steals-plus-blocks per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Missi notched three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and four blocks over 22 minutes during Saturday's 116-108 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Missi returned to action after missing 11 straight games due to a knee injury. He was placed on a minutes restriction, limiting him to just 22 minutes of playing time. While the offensive output was sketchy at best, he did manage to block a season-high four shots while also flirting with double-digit rebounds. Assuming his playing time increases over the next few games, Missi is someone who should be rostered in all leagues, specifically by those needing rebounds and blocks.

items.headline: Missi (knee) will be available for Saturday's game against Denver, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
items.story: After missing 11 straight games due to a bone bruise in his left knee, Missi will officially return to the court Saturday. The 22-year-old center will be making his return under a minutes restriction, per Rod Walker of the Times-Picayune, though Missi will likely take on a heavier workload once he's gotten a few more games under his belt.

items.headline: Missi (knee) has been upgraded to probable for Saturday's game versus the Nuggets.
items.story: A bone bruise in Missi's left knee has kept him on the sidelines since Oct. 23, though he appears likely to end his 11-game stretch of absences Saturday.

items.headline: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Even though Missi has been trending in the right direction and was recently cleared to resume on-court activities, this game will come too soon for him. This means Missi will miss an 11th consecutive game while dealing with a left knee bone bruise. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Nuggets, and in the meantime, Karlo Matkovic figures to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Missi (knee) is listed as doubtful for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: According to Will Guillory of The Athletic, Missi was cleared to resume on-court activities Thursday. The doubtful tag is the big man's first since going down with a left knee bone bruise in late October, signaling he's at least inching closer toward returning to game action. Karlo Matkovic is in line for at least one more start at center for the Pelicans on Friday.

items.headline: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Missi has been sidelined since picking up a left knee bone bruise Oct. 23. He remains without a timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week moving forward.

items.headline: Missi (knee) won't play in Saturday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Missi sustained a bone bruise in his left knee during the 120-119 loss to Utah on Oct. 23. The 22-year-old hasn't played since, and considering he doesn't have a definitive return date, he should be considered week-to-week. Without Missi on the floor, DeAndre Jordan, Derik Queen and Karlo Matkovic could all see more action, though it appears none of them are a lock to take over the interim starting center job at the moment.

items.headline: Missi has been diagnosed with a left knee bone bruise and will miss an extended period of time, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Missi currently has no official timetable for his return, but he appears likely to miss significant time. Derik Queen could be elevated into a starting role while Missi is sidelined, so make sure the former is not floating around on your waiver wire. Missi doesn't offer enough upside to warrant holding onto in redraft fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Missi (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Missi exited Friday's loss to the Jazz with what the Pelicans are now calling a left knee bone bruise. His next chance to suit up will come in Wednesday's rematch against Denver. In the meantime, Derik Queen and Karlo Matkovic are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Missi won't return to Friday's game against the Jazz due to a left knee injury.
items.story: Missi needed to be helped to the locker room after colliding with Zion Williamson, and while we don't know the extent of this knee injury, getting ruled out so quickly is not encouraging. If he needs to miss time, Derik Queen and Herbert Jones would benefit.

items.headline: Missi was helped to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Jazz due to an apparent left leg injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Zion Williamson appeared to collide with Missi's leg, and the 22-year-old center required assistance getting back to the locker room. If he's unable to return, Derik Queen figures to see increased playing time the rest of the way.

items.headline: Missi ended with 13 points (5-6 FG, 3-4 FT), 14 rebounds, five assists, three blocks and two steals across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Missi made the most of his promotion to the starting lineup, turning in arguably the best performance of his young career. For anyone who took a chance on him at the end of drafts, now could be an ultimate sell-high opportunity. With that said, it does appear as though he is going to be the starting center moving forward. While managers shouldn't expect numbers like this on a nightly basis, he should be a solid source of rebounds and blocks.

items.headline: The Pelicans exercised their fourth-year team option on Missi's contract Tuesday, Terry Kimble of SI.com reports.
items.story: Missi is now under contract for the 2027-28 campaign. He's expected to open the 2026-27 campaign as the Pelicans' starting center after averaging 5.7 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.5 blocks and 1.3 assists in 19.7 minutes per game across 66 regular-season appearances (14 starts) last season.

items.headline: Missi amassed 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-5 FT) and nine rebounds across 19 minutes in Thursday's 128-118 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Missi turned in an efficient performance from the field and was one of six Pelicans players to score in double figures. He also tied for the game-high mark in rebounds. The big man is in line to open the regular season as New Orleans' starting center but may have to compete for additional playing time with the likes of Derik Queen and Karlo Matkovic.

items.headline: Missi will start in Tuesday's preseason game against the Thunder, Andrew Lopez of Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Joining Missi in the first unit for Tuesday's exhibition will be Dejounte Murray, Herbert Jones, Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson. Across 14 starts last season, Missi averaged 7.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.9 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Coach Jamahl Mosley stated during Thursday's media day that he's challenging Missi to contend for Defensive Player of the Year this season, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
items.story: Mosley notes that he's well aware of how talented Missi is on the defensive end, and he's looking for the third-year center to take yet another step forward as the 2026-27 season approaches. The big man saw his opportunities take a hit during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 19.7 minutes over 66 games after logging 26.8 minutes per game in 73 appearances during his rookie year. Missi is poised to open his third NBA season behind starting center Herbert Jones.

items.headline: Missi recorded 24 points (9-13 FG, 6-8 FT), nine rebounds, two steals and four blocks in 27 minutes during Cameroon's 78-62 win over Nigeria in Thursday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 22-year-old is coming off his second NBA season and will enter training camp battling for minutes in a crowded New Orleans frontcourt that also features Derik Queen and Karlo Matkovic. Missi's rebounding, rim protection and athleticism give him a clear path to maintaining a significant role, but the presence of Queen and Matkovic could prevent any substantial increase in playing time. His limited offensive range also caps his fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Missi (hand) continued to play a meaningful role in New Orleans' frontcourt during his second NBA season, averaging 5.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 66 regular-season appearances.
items.story: The 22-year-old remains one of the Pelicans' top young interior defenders, and New Orleans has reportedly rebuffed trade interest from multiple teams this offseason, underscoring how highly the organization values him. Although he'll continue competing for frontcourt minutes alongside Derik Queen and DeAndre Jordan, Missi should remain an important part of the center rotation entering 2026-27.

items.headline: Missi (hand) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Missi will miss a third consecutive game. With Zion Williamson (knee), Karlo Matkovic (back) and Herbert Jones (rest) also ruled out, Kevon Looney is in line to make his third consecutive start.

items.headline: Missi (hand) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Missi is slated to miss his second game in a row while on the mend from a right hand sprain. He'll have one more chance to take the floor this season Sunday in Minnesota.

items.headline: Missi (hand) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: The second-year big man will miss his first game since Feb. 26 due to a right hand sprain, and his penultimate chance to play again this season will come Friday in Boston. Zion Williamson, Herbert Jones and Saddiq Bey will all dress but are not expected to play, so Derik Queen, Hunter Dickinson and Josh Oduro are likely to see increased playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Missi has a right hand sprain and is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Missi was a late addition to the injury report which is usually not a great sign in fantasy hoops. He was coming off a strong performance with 18 points (8-9 FG, 2-4 FT), 13 rebounds, three assists and four blocks over 40 minutes during Sunday's 112-108 loss to Orlando. DeAndre Jordan and Derik Queen may see more minutes if Missi is held out.

items.headline: Missi amassed 18 points (8-9 FG, 2-4 FT), 13 rebounds, three assists and four blocks over 40 minutes during Sunday's 112-108 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Missi recorded his fifth double-double of the season in the loss Sunday. He's fared well in 14 starts this season, posting averages of 7.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.9 blocks on 60.6 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Missi is in the starting lineup for Friday's matchup with the Kings, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Joining Missi in the first unit for Friday's game will be Herbert Jones, Trey Murphy, Saddiq Bey and Zion Williamson. Across 12 starts this season, MIssi has averaged 6.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.9 swats per contest.

items.headline: Missi won't start Thursday's game against Portland.
items.story: With Trey Murphy (ankle) back in the lineup following a three-game absence, Missi will slide to the second unit. The big man has averaged 3.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.8 blocks across 20.2 minutes per game in his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Missi is in the starting lineup for Friday's matchup with the Raptors, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Missi will replace DeAndre Jordan in the starting lineup, and it'll be Jeremiah Fears, Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey and Zion Williamson joining him in the first unit for Friday's game. Across 10 starts this season, Missi has posted averages of 6.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.8 swats per contest.

items.headline: Missi finished with six points (3-7 FG), 10 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal in 24 minutes during Saturday's 111-106 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Missi paced the Pelicans in boards Saturday. The second-year center has hauled in double-digit rebounds in four of his last six games, during which Missi has averaged 6.0 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.5 blocks in 23.8 minutes per tilt while shooting 53.6 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Missi won't start Saturday versus Cleveland.
items.story: Missi started in two of the Pels' previous three contests, most recently amassing an 11-point, 11-rebound double-double in Thursday's win over the Los Angeles Clippers. However, with Dejounte Murray (Achilles) back in the equation, Missi will move to a reserve role versus a Cavs team that is still without Jarrett Allen (knee).

items.headline: Missi posted 11 points (5-5 FG, 1-2 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists and one block in 27 minutes during Thursday's 105-99 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Missi got the start Thursday due to the absence of Dejounte Murray (Achilles) during the second leg of this back-to-back set. He made the most of his minutes with his first double-double since Jan. 25. Missi has been relegated to a secondary role in the rotation. As a backup center who rarely sees over 25 minutes per game, his fantasy potential is limited, but he's been a strong source of blocks lately. He's averaging 5.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.3 assists on 18.5 minutes per game in 11 outings (three starts) since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Missi will start Thursday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: With Dejounte Murray (Achilles) sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set, Missi will rejoin the first unit. As a starter this season (nine games), the big man has averaged 5.9 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.9 blocks in 22.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Missi won't start Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Dejounte Murray (illness) back in the lineup, Missi will slide to the second unit. The big man has averaged 3.8 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 16.2 minutes per contest over his last five outings off the bench.

items.headline: Missi recorded four points (1-4 FG, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists and five blocks across 28 minutes during Monday's 129-111 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Missi moved into the starting lineup, with Dejounte Murray ruled out due to illness. Rather than replace Murray, the coaching staff decided to shuffle the rotation, allowing Missi to slide into the starting center role. Rewarding anyone who took a chance on him, Missi turned in a solid performance, including a season-high five blocks. While Missi is a name to monitor, recent games would suggest that he is nothing more than a streaming consideration on most nights.

items.headline: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Chicago, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Harris still sidelined, San Antonio will rely more on Julian Champagnie. Harris has yet to make his Spurs debut this season, so his absence continues to leave minutes available on the wing until he is cleared to return.

items.headline: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Monday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Harris is making progress toward his season debut but continues to be ruled out 24 hours in advance. His next chance to make his 2026-27 campaign debut will come Wednesday in Chicago.

items.headline: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Harris suffered a strained left calf ahead of the 2026-27 campaign and has yet to make his debut with the Spurs. The veteran is slowly making progress toward a return, though he should be considered week-to-week until more information is released. The 34-year-old, who signed with San Antonio during the offseason, averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 27.7 minutes per contest in 63 regular-season appearances with the Pistons in 2025-26.

items.headline: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Utah, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: This will be Harris' fifth straight game on the shelf as the Spurs continue to wait for his official debut. Harris is progressing and is said to be close to day-to-day.

items.headline: Harris (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Harris is still ramping up from a left calf strain and will miss a fourth consecutive contest to begin the regular season. His next opportunity to make his season debut will come Wednesday at Utah in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson will likely continue seeing increased playing time while Harris is sidelined. "He's progressing on the court, and it's going well," Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said about Harris' return timeline. "We're excited to have him back very soon."

items.headline: Harris (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Harris has yet to play for the Spurs this season, and this will be a third consecutive absence for the veteran forward. With Harris on the sidelines, Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie should be in line for more playing time Saturday and beyond.

items.headline: Harris (calf) is out for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: The veteran forward still isn't ready to make his Spurs debut due to a left calf strain. Harris is up against a quick turnaround if he wants to suit up in time for Saturday's matchup with the Mavericks. Both Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie stand out as worthy streaming candidates until Harris is cleared to play.

items.headline: Harris (calf) will not be ready for the regular-season opener Tuesday against the Thunder, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: "He's ramping up. He's progressing," coach Mitch Johnson said. "He still needs some more progressing on the court." With Harris still not ready to return, the Spurs will likely utilize their three-guard lineup quite a bit, and guys like Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson and Harrison Barnes could find more minutes.

items.headline: Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said the team will not rush Harris (calf) back to the court, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: "It's a calf strain, the seriousness is what it is," said Johnson. "We won't rush him at all. I guess the question will be is he ready for the season opener? Totally questionable and we will not push that at all. So, we'll take it slow. There is no concern of this level of seriousness, and at the same time, we will not rush him at all." It sounds like Harris, who has already been ruled out for the preseason, is in danger of missing the start of the regular season. His absence, for however long it persists, will open up minutes for Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson and Harrison Barnes.

items.headline: Harris will not play in the preseason due to a left calf strain, Michael C. Wright of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Harris sustained the injury to his calf during training camp and will be reevaluated after the preseason. The 34-year-old pro signed a two-year contract with the Spurs this offseason. He should be considered questionable for the regular-season opener against the Thunder on Oct. 20.

items.headline: Harris agreed to a two-year, $31 million deal with the Spurs on Wednesday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Harris was a key component of Detroit's turnaround in recent years, and he's now heading to San Antonio to provide veteran leadership for a young Spurs squad. The 33-year-old forward should play significant minutes for his new team and could push Julian Champagnie for a starting spot, but Harris' usage is likely to take a big hit in a first unit loaded with playmakers. Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 0.9 steals per tilt in 63 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: Harris recorded five points (0-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 23 minutes during Sunday's 125-94 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Harris turned in his worst performance of the postseason, scoring under seven points for the second straight game. While it was certainly not the way he wanted the season to end, his production for the majority of the playoffs was exemplary. Through 14 appearances, he averaged 18.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, 1.4 three-pointers and 2.3 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Harris closed with 16 points (6-17 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block over 36 minutes during Monday's 112-103 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Harris saw a heavy workload on the offensive end once again, though he struggled with efficiency in this one. The veteran forward scored fewer than 20 points after eight straight games reaching that mark, but he still finished as Detroit's third-leading scorer. He also led the team in rebounds and chipped in at least three combined steals-plus-blocks for the fifth time this postseason.

items.headline: Harris recorded 21 points (7-14 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT) and five rebounds across 38 minutes during Saturday's 116-109 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Harris tallied eight points in both the first and third quarters of Saturday's game and finished as the Pistons' second-leading scorer behind Cade Cunningham (27 points). Harris averaged 13.3 points per game during the regular season but has been more active offensively during the playoffs. He has scored 20-plus points in eight consecutive games, and over that span he has averaged 22.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 1.9 threes and 1.5 steals over 36.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Harris totaled 21 points (9-16 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, two blocks and two steals in 37 minutes during Thursday's 107-97 win over the Cavaliers in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Harris has been on a tear throughout the playoffs, scoring at least 20 points in seven straight games. During that span, he has averaged 22.7 points, 7.9 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.9 three-pointers, a huge improvement on what he was able to do during the regular season. Now leading the series 2-0, Detroit will head into Cleveland full of confidence, with Harris looking to continue his postseason resurgence.

items.headline: Harris racked up 20 points (6-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 7-8 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two steals across 39 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 victory over Cleveland in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: After averaging just 13.3 points per game during the regular season, his lowest output since 2012-13, Harris continues to come up big for the Pistons this postseason. The veteran forward has dropped at least 20 points in six consecutive games, averaging 21.4 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.6 steals and 1.3 assists in 35.9 minutes per game over eight appearances in the 2026 playoffs.

items.headline: Harris provided 30 points (11-18 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals across 36 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 victory over the Magic in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Harris continued on his merry way Sunday, playing arguably his best basketball of the past few years. He has now scored at least 20 points in five straight games while also contributing across multiple categories. The Pistons will now face the Cavaliers in the second round of the playoffs, with Game 1 slated for Tuesday in Detroit. On paper, Cleveland poses a much bigger threat to the Pistons, meaning Harris will need to remain a focal point moving forward.

items.headline: Harris (ankle) is available for Friday's Game 6 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Magic.
items.story: Harris will shed his questionable tag due to a left ankle sprain and suit up for this win-or-go-home matchup. The veteran forward has reached the 20-point threshold in three straight games, and across five first-round outings, he has averaged 19.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.6 steals, 1.4 assists and 1.0 blocks in 34.6 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Harris (ankle) participated in Friday's morning shootaround, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Harris remains questionable for Game 6 against the Magic on Friday, but he's trending in the right direction. The veteran forward produced 23 points (9-18 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-7 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two steals across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 116-109 victory.

items.headline: Harris is questionable for Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs Friday against the Magic due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Harris must have picked up the injury during Detroit's Game 5 win over Orlando on Wednesday. Javonte Green would likely be the direct beneficiary if Harris is unable to suit up for Friday's must-win contest, and Daniss Jenkins could also see more playing time in that case.

items.headline: Harris chipped in 23 points (9-18 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-7 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two steals across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 116-109 victory over Orlando in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Harris scored at least 20 points for the third straight game, continuing an excellent playoff series for the veteran. In five appearances, he has averaged 19.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 0.8 steals, and 2.6 combined steals and blocks, a significant improvement over his season-long averages.

items.headline: Harris notched 23 points (8-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Saturday's 113-105 loss to the Magic in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: It was the veteran forward's best scoring performance yet in the series. Harris is averaging 18.7 points, 8.0 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.7 steals, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 threes in 35.7 minutes to begin the Pistons' playoff run, and he should remain a high-floor DFS option in Game 4 on Monday.

items.headline: Harris supplied 16 points (7-17 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, two blocks, two steals and one assist over 33 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 win over the Magic in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Harris contributed as both a scorer and rebounder, recording his first double-double of the postseason after logging three during the regular season. After shooting 36.8 percent from beyond the arc in 63 regular-season contests, the power forward has struggled from deep through two playoff games, going just 1-for-10 after coming up empty Wednesday.

items.headline: Harris (knee) will play Wednesday against the Bucks.
items.story: Harris is set to return from a one-game absence and is no longer on the injury report. Over his last five games, he's averaging 12.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 4.0 assists.

items.headline: Harris (knee) is out for Monday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Harris was downgraded to doubtful earlier in the day Monday, and he's now been officially ruled out due to a bruised left knee and left hip injury management. Ronald Holland, Javonte Green and Kevin Huerter should be in the mix for more looks with Harris sidelined.

items.headline: Harris (knee) is doubtful for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Despite going through shootaround, Harris was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. Duncan Robinson (hip) is also doubtful, meaning the Pistons may need to rely on guys such as Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser and Javonte Green.

items.headline: Harris (knee) is questionable for Monday's game in Orlando.
items.story: Harris played through the knee issue Saturday and looked good across 27 minutes, but he'll likely again need to test his knee at shootaround before an official decision is made on his status. If Harris can't give it a go, that would open up minutes for Ronald Holland and Caris LeVert.

items.headline: Harris (knee) is available for Saturday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Harris was initially given a questionable tag, but the veteran forward will suit up and should handle his regular workload in the Pistons' frontcourt next to Jalen Duren. Harris, who was limited to just six minutes in the win over the Timberwolves on Thursday, is averaging 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.0 blocks per game over his last 10 appearances.

items.headline: Harris is questionable for Saturday's game versus Philadelphia due to a bruised left knee.
items.story: The 33-year-old forward is in jeopardy of sitting out after sustaining the injury during Thursday's win over Minnesota. Should Harris need to miss Saturday's contest, Kevin Huerter, Ronald Holland and Javonte Green would all have an opportunity to step up on the wing.

items.headline: Harris won't return to Thursday's game against the Timberwolves due to a left knee contusion. He'll finish with two points (1-1 FG) and one assist in six minutes.
items.story: The veteran forward collided with Rudy Gobert and limped to the locker room in the opening quarter. Harris was initially deemed questionable to return but was ruled out for the remainder of the game shortly thereafter. His next opportunity to play will come Saturday in Philadelphia. Ronald Holland and Javonte Green will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way Thursday.

items.headline: Harris is questionable to return to Thursday's game against the Timberwolves due to a left knee contusion, Vincent Goodwill of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: After colliding with Rudy Gobert in the first quarter, Harris limped to the locker room. If he's unable to return, Ronald Holland and Javonte Green will likely help pick up the slack.

items.headline: Harris exited to the locker room during the first quarter of Thursday's game against the Timberwolves due to an apparent left knee injury, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Harris looked to bump knees with an opposing player on a drive to the basket and was in obvious pain before the Pistons called a timeout. The veteran forward was spotted walking to the locker room to be examined immediately after the collision. Harris can be considered questionable to return until the team has an update on the extent of his injury.

items.headline: Harris (hip) has been cleared to play Tuesday against the Raptors.
items.story: Harris was tagged as probable leading up to tipoff, so his availability isn't much of a surprise. He'll return to the court following a one-game absence due to a hip issue.

items.headline: Harris (hip) is probable for Tuesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: After sitting out Monday, Harris is expected to be available for the second half of this back-to-back set. The veteran forward has averaged 14.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.4 blocks in 28.0 minutes per tilt in his last seven games, shooting 47.5 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Harris (hip) is out for Monday's game with the Thunder.
items.story: Harris is joining most of Detroit's starting lineup in street clothes Monday, which is the first half of a back-to-back set. Javonte Green and Ronald Holland are both firmly on the streaming map in most fantasy leagues versus Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Johnson will start Friday's game against Detroit.
items.story: With Egor Demin (leg) unavailable, Johnson will get the starting nod for just the second time in his career. He's averaging 7.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.8 steals in 20.8 minutes per contest across four regular-season outings.

items.headline: Johnson ended with 15 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across 29 minutes before fouling out of Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Johnson delivered an efficient performance off the bench, connecting on three triples while playing 29 minutes. The rookie forward also contributed a steal but fouled out of the contest. His playing time and willingness to shoot from beyond the arc make him an intriguing player to monitor in deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and two steals across 27 minutes off the bench in Saturday's 125-121 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Johnson was one of four Brooklyn players -- and the only one who came off the bench -- to score in double digits in Saturday's loss. The former Auburn standout saw an expanded role off the bench after playing just five minutes in the regular-season opener against Charlotte on Wednesday, but he's unlikely to hover around the 20-minute mark consistently. He should be a depth option in the frontcourt and not much more, which limits his fantasy appeal considerably.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is getting ready to reprise his role as a two-way player for Brooklyn in 2026-27.
items.story: Johnson signed a two-way contract with the Nets in June after occupying a two-way roster spot with the club a year ago. Such a role leaves Johnson more likely to begin the new season as a featured part of the G League's Long Island Nets as opposed to the NBA squad, unless injuries strike the parent team at some point between training camp and the regular season.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game versus Oklahoma City, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Johnson will take a seat for the Nets' Summer League finale. The two-way player was productive in four Las Vegas Summer League appearances, averaging 13.0 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.2 steals and 1.8 assists in 26.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Johnson totaled 20 points (9-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds and five steals over 32 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Johnson was dominant despite the loss, matching teammate Danny Wolf with a game-high 20 points as part of a double-double effort. Of Johnson's 10 rebounds, five came on the offensive glass. He also made his presence felt defensively with five steals, while no other player recorded more than three swipes. The Auburn product saw significant run down the stretch of the 2025-26 regular season with the Nets, averaging 8.2 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 20.5 minutes per contest across 17 appearances.

items.headline: Johnson registered 19 points (7-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block in 32 minutes during Monday's 100-79 California Classic Summer League win over Warriors Blue.
items.story: Johnson turned in an extremely efficient performance and finished as Brooklyn's second-leading scorer behind Egor Demin (23 points). Johnson also tied for second on the team in rebounds while tying for the team lead in steals. He scored in double figures and grabbed at least seven boards in both of his California Classic appearances this summer.

items.headline: Johnson (undisclosed) is available for Monday's California Classic Summer League game against Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Johnson was held out of Sunday's win over the Bucks -- the second leg of a back-to-back-to-back set -- though he'll return to action in Brooklyn's final California Classic contest. The two-way player started at center and logged 25 minutes in Saturday's loss to the Kings, during which he supplied 10 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block.

items.headline: Johnson (undisclosed) won't play in Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: After posting a double-double Saturday, Johnson will be held out of the second leg of a back-to-back-to-back set, and for now, he can be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Warriors Blue. Aaron Scott will have a chance to get into the rotation Sunday with Johnson inactive.

items.headline: Johnson signed a two-way contract with Brooklyn on Monday.
items.story: Johnson split time between the G League and the Nets in 2025-26. In 17 regular-season contests with the parent club last season, the 24-year-old averaged 8.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.9 steals across 20.5 minutes. He'll likely spend most of his time with the G League's Long Island Nets in 2026-27.

items.headline: Johnson provided 16 points (6-14 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds, two assists and one steal in 36 minutes during Sunday's 136-101 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Johnson got a chance to show his stuff in the final weeks of the season. He logged the first double-double of his career in the final game of the season, filling in for Nic Claxton (finger). If the Nets shake things up and move Claxton in the offseason, the Auburn product could find himself in a favorable position on the depth chart.

items.headline: Johnson won't start Tuesday's game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Johnson got the starting nod in Sunday's win over Washington but will slide to the second unit Tuesday. As a reserve this season (14 games), he has averaged 7.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 20.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Johnson will start Sunday versus the Wizards, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Nic Claxton (hand) is out, so Johnson will earn his first start of the season. Johnson owns per-36 averages of 13.9 points, 7.5 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.7 steals per game.

items.headline: Johnson registered 11 points (4-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal across 27 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Johnson exceeded 20 minutes for the first time in the past four games, scoring in double digits for the fifth time in his young career. With Brooklyn manipulating its rotation on a nightly basis, it's hard to be too excited by this performance. Generally speaking, fantasy managers are better off focusing on other teams when it comes to streaming candidates.

items.headline: Johnson provided 12 points (5-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and three assists over 26 minutes during Monday's 134-99 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: With the Nets riding out the final stretch of a losing season, Johnson is beginning to make his way onto the streaming radar in deep fantasy leagues. Across his last six contests, Johnson has averaged 9.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.7 blocks in 23.9 minutes per game while shooting 48.6 percent from the field.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 12 points (5-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and one steal over 27 minutes during the Nets' 121-92 loss to the Thunder on Wednesday.
items.story: The Thunder led by as many as 42 points during Wednesday's game, which prompted both teams to empty the bench in the fourth quarter. That gave Johnson the opportunity for an extended run, and the undrafted rookie out of Auburn capitalized by scoring 10 points in the second half while connecting on all four of his field-goal attempts. He has scored in double digits in back-to-back games and could see more playing time moving forward if Noah Clowney were to miss time, as the latter left in the first quarter of Wednesday's game due to a right wrist sprain.

items.headline: Johnson amassed 17 points (6-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-6 FT), nine rebounds and one assist in 25 minutes during Monday's 114-95 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Johnson made a strong impact off the bench, leading the Nets in scoring while finishing one rebound shy of a double-double. The undrafted rookie out of Auburn made his NBA debut March 9 and entered Monday's contest averaging 4.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 17.8 minutes across four appearances.

items.headline: Johnson (not injury related) is not available for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Johnson signed a two-way pact with Brooklyn on Friday and has yet to join the team. His next opportunity to make his NBA debut will come Monday against the Warriors, though it wouldn't be surprising to see him head straight to the club's G League affiliate, the Long Island Nets. The undrafted rookie out of Auburn appeared in 16 G League games for the Cleveland Charge before latching on with Brooklyn, during which he averaged 12.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks in 25.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Nets signed Johnson to a two-way contract Friday.
items.story: Johnson joined the Cavaliers for Summer League and training camp but was eventually waived in mid-October. The Auburn product appeared in 16 G League games for the Cleveland Charge before latching on with Brooklyn, during which he averaged 12.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks in 25.5 minutes per contest. The undrafted rookie will provide frontcourt depth for the Nets, though he'll likely spend the majority of his time with their G League affiliate, the Long Island Nets.

items.headline: Melton totaled two points (0-7 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 27 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 victory over Boston.
items.story: Melton continues to see increased opportunities with Stephen Curry (oblique) sidelined. Although his scoring remains inconsistent, Melton's playmaking and defensive contributions provide fantasy value. He's averaging 24.0 minutes and 2.3 steals over his last three appearances.

items.headline: Melton notched nine points (3-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, five assists, two blocks and two steals over 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Melton bounced back from Wednesday's scoreless outing, but his shooting struggles persisted. He's converted just 31.6 percent of his attempts over five games, limiting his scoring upside despite Stephen Curry's absence. Melton's defensive versatility remains useful in deeper category leagues.

items.headline: Melton is starting Thursday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Melton will enter the starting five after being deployed off the bench in his previous two showings. LJ Cryer will rotate to the bench as a result. Melton finished with eight points, four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 18 minutes during his last start Friday against San Antonio.

items.headline: Melton is not listed in the starting lineup for Monday's game against New Orleans, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Melton got the start for Friday's 123-85 loss to San Antonio, but two-way guard LJ Cryer, who netted a team-high 20 points and six triples in the loss, will get the starting nod Monday. Melton figures to stay involved as a reserve with Stephen Curry (oblique) still sidelined.

items.headline: Melton will start Friday's game against the Spurs, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Melton will make his third start of the season Friday after scoring at least 11 points off the bench in each of Golden State's last two games. Yaxel Lendeborg will start at the four, and Draymond Green will start at center while Al Horford moves to the bench.

items.headline: Melton registered 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one block over 25 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 115-108 loss to Houston.
items.story: The 28-year-old guard scored in double digits for the fourth time in the last seven games (one start), a stretch in which he's averaged 10.7 points, 4.7 boards, 2.6 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.4 steals in 23.1 minutes while shooting 43.9 percent from beyond the arc. Stephen Curry (abdomen) is expected to miss at least two weeks after leaving Wednesday's game early, so Melton could shift into the starting five and take on a bigger workload.

items.headline: Melton finished Monday's 138-87 victory over New Orleans with 16 points (5-11 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 26 minutes.
items.story: Melton continued his hot shooting from beyond the arc, connecting on four of eight attempts. With Will Richard (thumb) and Gary Payton (knee) sidelined, Melton saw plenty of backcourt minutes in the blowout. His threes and steals make him a solid streaming option while Golden State's guard rotation is thin.

items.headline: Melton contributed five points (1-5 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, two assists and three steals over 17 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 victory over Miami.
items.story: Melton struggled offensively for the second consecutive game, shooting a combined 2-for-14 from the field and missing all nine of his three-point attempts over that span. However, the veteran guard remained active defensively, recording at least two steals for the fourth straight contest. Melton's defensive production provides some fantasy appeal in category leagues, though his inconsistent shooting and fluctuating minutes limit his reliability.

items.headline: Melton had 21 points (6-9 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals across 28 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The six made three-pointers represented Melton's best performance from beyond the arc since the 2022-23 season, when he was with the Sixers. The 28-year-old guard was making his second start of the season, this one coming while Stephen Curry got the night off for the front half of a back-to-back. Through seven games this season, Melton is averaging 11.9 points, 4.1 boards, 2.7 threes, 2.3 assists and 1.4 steals in 22.3 minutes while shooting a sizzling 49.1 percent from the floor and 52.8 percent from long range.

items.headline: Melton will start in Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: With Stephen Curry (rest) taking the first night of Golden State's back-to-back off, Melton will enter the starting lineup alongside Brandin Podziemski in the backcourt.

items.headline: Melton logged 16 points (5-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and two steals across 21 minutes during Friday's 112-95 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Melton provided a spark off the bench, scoring 16 points and hitting four three-pointers in 21 minutes. The veteran guard's shooting and defense have made him a valuable part of the rotation, especially with Golden State shorthanded.

items.headline: Melton notched 25 points (8-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, five assists and three steals over 27 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Suns.
items.story: After two poor performances to open the season, Melton finally turned things around, rewarding those who managed to hold onto him. While it did take a number of injuries for him to get there, this was definitely an encouraging effort by the veteran. Based on this performance, he is probably worth holding for at least a few more games, just in case this spurs him into action.

items.headline: Melton will come off the bench in Friday's matchup with Memphis, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Brandin Podziemski (back) is active and starting, so Melton will retreat to the second unit. As a reserve last season, Melton averaged 11.8 points, 2.3 assists, 1.4 triples and 1.5 steals per game.

items.headline: Melton will start Wednesday's game against the Lakers, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Brandin Podziemski won't suit up due to lower-back soreness, opening the door for Melton to enter the starting five. The 28-year-old guard started 24 games in the 2025-26 regular season, averaging 12.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.7 steals across 24.5 minutes per game in those outings.

items.headline: Melton finished Saturday's 111-106 preseason win over the Kings with zero points (0-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal in 18 minutes.
items.story: Melton was on the court for Saturday's exhibition game after not playing against Portland on Wednesday. It wasn't exactly a great showing from the veteran guard, who failed to score a point while finishing with a minus-13 point differential. Melton is expected to serve as the top rotational guard off the bench for the Warriors this season, operating behind starters Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski.

items.headline: Melton (rest) won't travel with the Warriors for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Melton is among several rotation players Golden State is holding out for the second half of a preseason back-to-back. The veteran guard has been working with the Warriors' second unit during training camp and should have another opportunity to suit up Saturday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Melton revealed this offseason that he underwent surgery on each of his thumbs, per Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com.
items.story: Melton is fully recovered now, but playing through the discomfort resulted in him shooting just 29.4 percent from deep during the regular season, his lowest mark since 2019-20 with Memphis. The swingman is competing at training camp with Gui Santos and Yaxel Lendeborg for a starting role, and Melton has shown he is capable of being an effective nine-category fantasy player when healthy after averaging at least 10.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.5 three-pointers in five straight seasons.

items.headline: Melton will sign a two-year, $11 million deal with the Warriors, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
items.story: Melton previously declined his $3.45 million player option after rebuilding his market value with a strong 2025-26 campaign. He averaged a career-high 12.3 points along with 3.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 23.0 minutes per contest across 49 regular-season games (24 starts). Look for him to play a similar role moving forward, though the Warriors are expected to be very busy this offseason.

items.headline: Melton declined his $3.45 million player option for 2026-27 on Monday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: Melton underwent surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee in December 2024 and returned to the Warriors for the 2025-26 campaign, during which he averaged a career-high 12.3 points along with 3.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 23.0 minutes per contest across 49 regular-season games (24 starts). He's now set to explore his options in unrestricted free agency.

items.headline: Melton tallied 16 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds and three assists over 28 minutes during the Warriors' 111-96 loss to the Suns in Friday's Western Conference Play-In Tournament game.
items.story: Melton ended the 2025-26 season with a productive showing off the bench, finishing second on the Warriors in both points and rebounds behind Brandin Podziemski. Melton spent most of the season on the bench but was a regular member of the Warriors' starting five across 23 games from Feb. 5 to April 9. Over that span, he averaged 13.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.7 threes, and 1.7 steals over 24.7 minutes per game. Melton has a $3.45 million player option for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Melton won't start Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Gui Santos will enter the starting five Wednesday, pushing Melton to the second unit. He averaged 11.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals in 21.6 minutes per showing over 25 appearances off the bench during the regular season.

items.headline: Melton will start Sunday's game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Melton came off the bench during Friday's game against the Kings, but he will return to a starting role Sunday. Across his last five starts, Melton holds averages of 6.8 points, 3.4 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 23.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Melton won't start Friday's game against the Kings, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: The Warriors will go with Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis in the starting five, pushing Melton to the second unit for the first time since Feb. 3. He has averaged 11.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals in 21.3 minutes per game across 24 appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Melton supplied 21 points (7-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 29 minutes during Tuesday's 110-105 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: The 21 points led all scorers on the night and represented Melton's best scoring effort since he delivered 27 points against the Wizards on March 16. The 27-year-old guard remained in the starting five Tuesday while Stephen Curry came off the bench for a second straight game, but the two could swap places once Curry is cleared for a full workload. Melton has started 22 straight games since Curry was originally shut down in early February with a knee injury, averaging 13.7 points, 3.5 boards, 2.9 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.7 threes in 25.2 minutes over that span.
