Gillespie is set for unrestricted free agency this summer, and he certainly appears to be in line for a multi-year contract, whether it be with Phoenix or elsewhere.

items.headline: Gillespie will start Game 2 against the Thunder on Wednesday, Shane Young of the Suns' official site reports.
items.story: With Jordan Goodwin (calf) out, Gillespie will step into the starting five. As a starter during the regular season (58 games), the 26-year-old guard averaged 13.3 points, 4.7 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 29.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gillespie ended with five points (1-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 114-110 Play-In Game loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Gillespie continues to put up underwhelming production, scoring in single digits for the fifth time in his past six appearances. While it has been a breakout season for Gillespie, much of his success came when other players were sidelined. With the team now mostly healthy, he has shifted back to a modest role. During his past six games, Gillespie has barely been a top-300 player, averaging 6.3 points, 1.8 assists and 1.3 three-pointers in just 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Gillespie (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Tuesday's Play-In Game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Gillespie took a seat for the final game of the regular season with a shoulder issue, but he'll be ready to roll for Tuesday's matchup. He didn't have much of an impact down the stretch of the regular season, as he averaged 6.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists in his last five showings.

items.headline: Gillespie (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Gillespie will be held out of Sunday's regular-season finale due to a right shoulder contusion. The 26-year-old guard delivered career highs in several categories and will finish the regular season with averages of 12.7 points, 4.6 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 28.5 minutes per game across 80 outings (58 starts). Jamaree Bouyea and Koby Brea will likely see increased playing time for the shorthanded Suns on Sunday.

items.headline: Gillespie is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder due to a right shoulder contusion.
items.story: The shoulder injury is a new concern for Gillespie, who hasn't missed a game since Jan. 27. If he's unable to play in the Suns' regular-season finale, Jamaree Bouyea, Amir Coffey and Koby Brea would be candidates to see increased playing time, as the team could be very thin in the backcourt.

items.headline: Gillespie will start in Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Gillespie is back in the starting lineup after operating from off the bench in the Suns' last three contests. In 57 starts throughout the 2025-26 campaign, the 26-year-old has averaged 13.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 0.1 blocks and 1.3 steals across 29.9 minutes.

items.headline: Gillespie registered nine points (3-11 FG, 3-8 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 24 minutes during Sunday's 120-110 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: After starting in 55 straight appearances, Gillespie was demoted to a bench role Sunday with Jordan Goodwin getting the starting nod. The two players ended up logging 24 minutes apiece, suggesting that this could potentially become a timeshare. This will be a position battle to monitor closely.

items.headline: Gillespie won't start Sunday's game against the Bulls, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: The Suns are switching up the starting lineup, with Jordan Goodwin replacing Gillespie and Mark Williams taking his spot back from Oso Ighodaro. Gillespie has started 55 straight appearances and should still be a major part of the rotation, despite shifting to a bench role. As a reserve (19 games), Gillespie has averaged 11.6 points, 4.8 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 25.5 minutes a night.

items.headline: Gillespie racked up 11 points (4-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 115-111 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Even though he remains a player with decent fantasy upside due to the tight grip he has on a starting role, it's worth noting he's been trending in the wrong direction for a while now. Gillespie might have scored in double digits in seven of his last eight games, but over that stretch, he's averaging 12.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 5.4 assists per contest while shooting 38.5 percent from the floor and 34.8 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Gillespie amassed 11 points (4-16 FG, 3-11 3Pt), five rebounds and 10 assists across 32 minutes during Monday's 131-105 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Gillespie once again struggled to find his rhythm on the offensive end, as he's now 4-for-24 from the field over his last two games. However, he managed to make up for his shooting woes by dishing out double-digit assists for the third time in 74 appearances this season. Gillespie has scored in double figures in six of his last seven showings, and he should continue to receive plenty of chances to turn things around amidst this brief offensive skid.

items.headline: Gillespie finished Tuesday's 125-123 loss to Denver with 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 27 minutes.
items.story: Gillespie has now scored in double figures in five consecutive contests, which comes on the heels of a three-game cold spell where he was held to single digits. Over these past five outings, the sharpshooter has averaged 16.2 points, 4.6 assists, 3.4 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 3.8 three-pointers in 30.6 minutes per game while shooting 43.2 percent from deep.

items.headline: Gillespie finished Thursday's 101-100 loss to the Spurs with 24 points (7-13 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, six assists and two steals in 34 minutes.
items.story: Gillespie led the way for the Suns in this matchup and drained at least six three-pointers for the fifth time this season. The floor general had 17 points in the first half and matched his best scoring mark since the All-Star break. Gillespie has scored in double digits in 10 of his 15 appearances, averaging 12.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game while shooting 40.5 percent from deep in that span.

items.headline: Gillespie posted three points (1-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 23 minutes during Monday's 120-112 loss to Boston.
items.story: With Devin Booker and Jalen Green combining for 61 points, Gillespie took a backseat on offense. His fantasy appeal hasn't been great lately, as he's shooting 37.7 percent from the field over his last eight games with 9.6 points, 5.1 assists, 5.0 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 2.5 three-pointers.

items.headline: Gillespie chipped in 12 points (4-9 FG, 4-9 3Pt), nine rebounds, nine assists and two steals in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 129-114 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Gillespie made his mark in several key categories Tuesday, and he fell just one rebound and one assist shy of his first triple-double of the season. The Villanova product has now scored in double figures in three straight games and has drilled four or more treys in each matchup during this impressive stretch.

items.headline: Gillespie ended with 24 points (8-15 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and four assists over 36 minutes during Sunday's 111-99 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Gillespie drilled five three-pointers to boost his total in the decisive win, and it's apparent that Jalen Green's return to prominence has had zero effect on Gillespie's production. Although he had a down game against Chicago four days ago, the rest of Gillespie's totals in March have been steady and consistent. The third-year pro is on track for a career year, averaging 13.6 points, 4.7 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals over 63 games.

items.headline: Gillespie supplied 17 points (6-10 FG, 5-8 3Pt), five rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 31 minutes during Tuesday's 114-103 win over the Kings.
items.story: Gillespie's breakout campaign continues, and there's no reason to believe he'll be unseated from the first unit anytime soon. Grayson Allen was moved to the bench, with Gillespie starting alongside Devin Booker and Jalen Green on Tuesday. Gillespie has scored at least 15 points in five consecutive games, averaging 18.0 points, 4.8 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 4.2 three-pointers in 33.6 minutes per tilt while shooting 48.8 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Gillespie closed with 18 points (7-14 FG, 4-8 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Sunday's 92-77 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Gillespie led the Suns with 18 points, but he didn't get much help from his teammates, as Jalen Green was the only other player to score in double figures. Gillespie continues to see steady playing time due to Devin Booker (hip) being sidelined. Gillespie has knocked down seven triples over his last two appearances.

items.headline: Gillespie racked up 19 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one steal in 45 minutes during Saturday's 113-110 double-overtime victory over the Magic.
items.story: The third-year guard had failed to score in double digits in any of his prior four games, but Gillespie got his offense going as he played more than 40 minutes in a contest for the first time. Devin Booker (hip) still lacks a clear timeline for his return, while Cole Anthony has yet to make his Suns debut after being acquired from the Bucks at the trade deadline. For now, that leaves Gillespie as the only quality point guard on the Phoenix roster.

items.headline: Jackson underwent a procedure Tuesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
items.story: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

items.headline: Jackson will undergo surgery to repair the broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot and is set to miss significant time.
items.story: The Grizzlies will release a timeline for Jackson's return to basketball activities after he undergoes surgery, though he's facing a lengthy absence. With the 22-year-old forward on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Jackson (foot) is out for Monday's game against Washington.
items.story: The Grizzlies reported Saturday that Jackson suffered a "relatively serious" injury, so it's not a shock that he won't be on the floor for Monday's matchup. However, the team has yet to provide additional clarification on the injury. Jackson can be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game in Cleveland until more information surfaces.

items.headline: According to Grizzlies head coach Tuomas Iisalo, Jackson suffered a "relatively serious" foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over Brooklyn, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Jackson logged only three minutes versus the Nets before exiting the contest and eventually being ruled out. While "the team will continue to evaluate" his status, it doesn't sound like he will be on the floor Monday in Washington. The 21-year-old has appeared in 12 regular-season games during the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 6.7 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists across 15.0 minutes per outing. Assuming Jackson misses time, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Taylor Hendricks could see more minutes.

items.headline: Jackson (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Jackson scored three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt) in three minutes off the bench prior to exiting Saturday's game due to a left foot injury. Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper should get a slight bump in minutes with Jackson out.

items.headline: Jackson finished with 14 points (4-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 22 minutes during Friday's 142-111 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: Jackson had his best all-around performance of the season, logging at least 20 minutes for just the third time in 11 regular-season appearances. Memphis dominated New Orleans, allowing the bench unit to play additional minutes. While this was certainly a 12-team caliber line, managers shouldn't be too quick to overreact, given he had scored a total of just 11 points in his previous four games.

items.headline: Jackson logged 21 points (7-10 FG, 5-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 win over the Kings.
items.story: Jackson scored 12 of his 21 points in the second quarter to extend Memphis' halftime lead to 11, and he finished as the Grizzlies' third-leading scorer behind Cameron Boozer (27 points) and Isaiah Stewart (24 points). It was the first time since April 3 that Jackson scored 20-plus points in a regular-season game, and he'll finish the month of October having averaged 8.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.5 threes over 16.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jackson will come off the bench during Sunday's game against the Kings, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Jackson got the start Friday due to Cedric Coward (wrist) being out, but the former will return to a reserve role Sunday, with the latter back in action. In two appearances, Jackson is averaging 7.0 points, 6.0 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 17.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jackson will start Friday against the Warriors, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Jackson is getting the start with Cedric Coward (wrist) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey. As a starter last season, Jackson averaged 16.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.6 triples and 1.0 blocks per game on 50/39/77 shooting splits.

items.headline: Jackson logged 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and two blocks across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Jackson's fantasy arrow appears to be pointing up following Opening Night. The forward seems to have beaten out Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper for a reserve role in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Jackson (ankle) is off the injury report for Wednesday's season opener against the Jazz.
items.story: Jackson is good to go for the start of the season after dealing with a tweaked ankle. He's battling with Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper for playing time in the frontcourt in the early going.

items.headline: Jackson has been ruled out for Friday's exhibition against the Hornets due to an ankle injury, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Head coach Tuomas Iisalo said that Jackson tweaked his ankle during Friday's preseason win over the Bulls, so he'll miss Friday's preseason finale and will be listed as "day-to-day." For now, he should be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular season opener against the Jazz.

items.headline: Jackson finished Friday's 104-100 preseason win over the Bulls with 14 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one block over 17 minutes.
items.story: Jackson ended up leading the Grizzlies in field-goal attempts and finished Friday's exhibition contest as the team's second-leading scorer behind Ty Jerome (16 points). Jackson has enjoyed some success in Memphis since being selected by the franchise in the second round of the 2023 NBA Draft, though he figures to be limited to a bench role this coming season given the offseason additions of Cameron Boozer (2026 Draft) and Jerami Grant (trade).

items.headline: Jackson posted 15 points (5-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and a steal across 14 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason loss to the Magic.
items.story: Jackson followed up a strong preseason debut with another strong scoring night and contributed on the glass. He's in the final year of his contract and fighting for minutes in a crowded wing rotation that added Jerami Grant in the offseason, so continuing his steady preseason work is his best chance to move up the depth chart.

items.headline: Jackson recorded 14 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 16 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over Atlanta.
items.story: Jackson provided instant offense and didn't commit a turnover during his limited action. He's not considered a favorite for a starting spot, but performances like Monday's could help him earn minutes in a crowded wing and forward rotation.

items.headline: With Cameron Boozer, Karim Lopez (undisclosed) and Jerami Grant now in the mix, Jackson faces increased competition for playing time in the 2026-27 campaign.
items.story: The Grizzlies are expected to focus on developing their young talent this season, though Jackson still faces plenty of competition for minutes. Memphis drafted Boozer and Lopez in June before acquiring Grant in the Ja Morant deal later that month. Jackson has flashed potential throughout his time in the NBA, which the Grizzlies rewarded this summer by exercising his $2.4 million team option. The 21-year-old's long-term upside could help him retain a meaningful role, but he isn't guaranteed steady minutes when the team is at full strength. Jackson is coming off a solid season for an injury-riddled Grizzlies squad in 2025-26, averaging 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.4 combined steals-plus-blocks while shooting 49.6 percent from the field across 21.4 minutes per game in 55 regular-season appearances (28 starts).

items.headline: The Grizzlies exercised Jackson's (knee) $2.4 million team option Monday, Jake Fischer of BleacherReport.com reports.
items.story: Jackson has shown flashes offensively but struggled to stay healthy and put everything together in his first three seasons. However, the Grizzlies are still believers in his long-term upside. Across 55 regular-season contests in 2025-26, he averaged 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists on 49.6 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) is out for Sunday's season finale against the Rockets.
items.story: Jackson will be sidelined for a third consecutive game to end his 2025-26 campaign. Jackson started the year slowly but picked things up once the Grizzlies committed to a rebuild. Over his final 27 appearances, he averaged 17.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 blocks in 25.8 minutes.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Jackson will miss a second consecutive contest due to left knee soreness. His next opportunity to suit up will come in Sunday'regular-season finale against Houston. In the meantime, Toby Okani and Dariq Whitehead are candidates for increased playing time in the injury-riddled Memphis frontcourt.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) is out for Wednesday's game versus Denver.
items.story: Jackson continues to move in and out of the lineup due to nagging left knee soreness. With the forward sidelined Wednesday, fantasy managers should expect Taylor Hendricks, Toby Okani and Dariq Whitehead to each take on meaningful playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) is available for Monday's game versus Cleveland.
items.story: After missing Sunday's loss to Milwaukee with left knee soreness, Jackson has been removed from the injury report. He's looking to extend a streak of double-digit scoring games to 23 straight Monday, with Jackson averaging 18.2 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 blocks in 26.0 minutes per game during this streak.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: As expected, Jackson has been downgraded from doubtful to out and will miss his first matchup since March 20 while tending to left knee soreness. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Monday against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Jackson is doubtful to play Sunday in Milwaukee due to left knee soreness.
items.story: Taylor Hendricks will likely be starting and getting all the run he can handle Sunday evening with Jackson out. There should also be more minutes available for Taj Gibson.

items.headline: Jackson finished with 30 points (10-16 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 7-9 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block in 30 minutes during Friday's 128-96 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: The third-year forward led all scorers on the night, but only two other Grizzlies even scored in double digits in the rout. Jackson is having an impressive surge to close out the campaign, scoring 10-plus points in 21 straight appearances since the All-Star break while averaging 18.0 points, 5.3 boards, 1.8 assists, 1.4 threes and 1.0 blocks in only 25.6 minutes a contest and shooting 51.3 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Jackson racked up 20 points (7-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 123-98 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: The Grizzlies looked completely overmatched against the Spurs, but Jackson was Memphis' best fantasy producer by a wide margin, ending just three boards shy of a double-double while contributing in each of the five major categories. Jackson has been one of Memphis' most reliable fantasy options since the All-Star break, averaging 18.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.1 blocks per game in his last 16 appearances. He's also scored at least 20 points in three of his last five appearances.

items.headline: Jackson closed with 26 points (9-14 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT) and three rebounds across 30 minutes during Monday's 146-107 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Jackson was coming off a 19-point output in the loss to Charlotte on Saturday, and the third-year veteran delivered an even better performance in this 39-point defeat. Jackson surpassed the 25-point mark just for the second time this season -- and first since Feb. 21. Jackson has scored in double digits in his 10 appearances in March, averaging 17.1 points per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Jackson ended Saturday's 124-101 loss to the Hornets with 19 points (7-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 24 minutes.
items.story: Jackson was one of the few standout performers for the Grizzlies in this blowout loss, and while he posted a decent scoring line, his struggles from three-point range are worrisome. The Grizzlies don't have much to play for in the final stages of the season, so Jackson is one of several young players who should continue to see steady minutes. That said, his recent injury history might lead the Grizzlies to rest him at times. He's been productive when available, as this was his fifth straight game with at least 15 points.

items.headline: Jackson (knee) has been cleared to play in Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Jackson is available to return for the second leg of Memphis' back-to-back set after sitting out Friday's loss to Boston due to left knee soreness. His return likely shifts Taylor Hendricks back to a reserve role, though the Grizzlies may still look to monitor Jackson's workload given the quick turnaround and his recent history with lower-body ailments.

items.headline: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Krejci suffered an ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

items.headline: Head coach Micah Nori said that Krejci suffered a left leg fracture during Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Nori did not provide a timetable for Krejci, but it's safe to say that he won't be back soon. His minutes figure to be divvied up amongst Chris Youngblood and Sidy Cissoko.

items.headline: Krejci won't return to Wednesday's game against the Suns due to a left ankle injury.
items.story: The extent of Krejci's ankle injury isn't yet clear, but for now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers. If Krejci needs to miss time, Sidy Cissoko could pick up some extra minutes.

items.headline: Krejci finished with five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over Utah.
items.story: Krejci saw a surge in playing time due to Ja Morant (hamstring) being sidelined, a trend that could continue over the next month with the latter expected to miss at least four weeks due to injury. Although the stats weren't necessarily noteworthy, Krejci still did a little bit of everything in the win, something that could help him earn the trust of first-year head coach Micah Nori as the season progresses.

items.headline: Krejci finished with 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five assists, two rebounds and three steals across 21 minutes in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: Krejci is looking to stave off Sidy Cissoko and Jeremy Sochan for an Opening Night role this preseason. He's unlikely to carry much fantasy appeal while Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday are all healthy for Portland.

items.headline: Krejci provided two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), one rebound and two assists over 13 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Krejci, who joined the Trail Blazers in a midseason trade with the Hawks, appeared in 19 regular-season contests with his new team. He saw 19.2 minutes per contest, posting averages of 7.2 points, 2.7 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.4 three-pointers on 40.5 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) tallied two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) in five minutes off the bench in Sunday's 122-110 win over the Kings.
items.story: Cleared to play for the first time since March 15 after missing the Trail Blazers' previous 13 games due to a left calf contusion, Krejci was barely part of interim head coach Tiago Splitter's rotation. Krejci didn't check into the game until the 3:04 mark of the third quarter, playing the rest of the period before heading to the bench for good with 10:08 remaining in the game. Portland is likely to trim down its rotation in Tuesday's matchup with the Suns in the Play-In Tournament, so Krejci could be at risk of seeing his minutes disappear entirely.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is listed as available for Sunday's game against Sacramento, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portlandreports.
items.story: Krejci has missed Portland's last 13 games. While he'll avoid another absence, he will operate under a minutes limit.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Krejci is in danger of missing a 14th consecutive contest due to a left calf contusion. If he's unable to suit up for Portland's regular-season finale, Kris Murray will likely continue seeing a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers, per Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland.
items.story: Despite being upgraded to questionable and considered a game-time call heading into the contest, Krejci will ultimately sit out his 13th consecutive game due to a lingering left calf contusion. With Krejci remaining on the sidelines, he will have just one final opportunity to suit up in Sunday's regular-season finale before the start of the Play-In Tournament.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is questionable for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Krejci is in danger of missing a 13th straight game, though the fact that he's been upgraded to questionable is a sign he's trending in the right direction. Portland should have another update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs, Casey Holdahl of the Trail Blazers' official site reports.
items.story: Krejci will miss a 12th consecutive contest due to a left calf contusion and remains without a clear timetable for a return. His next chance to play will come Friday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Krejci has missed the Trail Blazers' last 11 games. With another absence potentially on the horizon Wednesday, the 25-year-old will have two more chances to suit up before the Play-In Tournament commences. In 18 appearances with Portland this season, Krejci has averaged 7.4 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.6 steals across 19.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game in Denver.
items.story: Krejci continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close to returning. He should be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game in San Antonio.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Krejci will miss a 10th straight game due to a left calf contusion and is without a clear timetable for a return. His next opportunity to suit up will come Monday   against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Krejci will miss a ninth straight game due to a left calf contusion and is without a clear timetable for a return. His next opportunity to play will come Thursday against the Pelicans. With Krejci out, Matisse Thybulle, Kris Murray and Blake Wesley are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Krejci will miss an eighth consecutive contest due to a left calf contusion. His next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday against the Clippers. With Krejci sidelined, Matisse Thybulle, Kris Murray and Scoot Henderson are candidates to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Dallas.
items.story: After initially being listed as doubtful, Krejci will miss a seventh consecutive contest due to a left calf contusion. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Wizards. With Krejci out, Matisse Thybulle, Kris Murray and Scoot Henderson are candidates to see an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is listed doubtful for Friday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Krejci hasn't appeared in a game since March 15, and that appears unlikely to change while he takes a doubtful designation into Friday's contest. With Krejci trending toward another absence, the Trail Blazers should have spots on the second unit available for all of Matisse Thybulle, Kris Murray and Sidy Cissoko.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Krejci will miss a sixth straight game due to a left calf contusion. The 25-year-old's next chance to play will come Friday against Dallas.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Krejci hasn't taken the court since March 15 after suffering a left calf injury, but he appears to be approaching a return. The team may elect to see how he fares in shootaround or pregame warmups before providing another update on his availability for Wednesday.

items.headline: Krejci (calf) is out for Monday's game against the Nets.

Krejci's absence could lead to a slight uptick in minutes for Sidy Cissoko or other reserves such as Kris Murray and Blake Wesley.

items.headline: Krejci is listed doubtful for Monday's game against the Nets due to a left calf contusion.

If Krejci ends up sitting out, a spot in the rotation could reopen for Kris Murray, who didn't play in a coach's decision in Sunday's 109-103 loss to the 76ers.

items.headline: Krejci posted three points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and one steal across 21 minutes during Wednesday's 122-114 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Krejci scored single digits for the fourth time in the past six games, continuing to play a modest role for his new team. Although it appears as though he has at least carved out a regular spot in the rotation, fantasy managers should look at him for streaming purposes only at this point.

items.headline: Krejci notched 14 points (5-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 19 minutes during Thursday's 121-112 victory over Chicago.
items.story: Even though Shaedon Sharpe (calf) is sidelined, the recent return of Scoot Henderson is cutting into Krejci's opportunities. Although he's scored in double figures in two of his past four games, Krejci's minutes haven't reached the 20s in any of these contests.

items.headline: Krejci chipped in 11 points (4-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 25 minutes during Thursday's 135-119 victory over Utah.
items.story: Krejci appears to be finding his form with his new team, and he took advantage of some injuries once again. Over his last two outings, Krejci has averaged 14.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 three-pointers.

items.headline: Krejci registered 17 points (7-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound and one assist in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 133-109 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Krejci put in his best scoring effort since joining Portland, scoring 17 points off the bench. It's his most points scored in a game dating back to Dec. 29th, when he scored 18 as a member of the Hawks. He's seeing 21.2 minutes per game with the Trail Blazers and has one more chance to make an impression before the All-Star break.

items.headline: Krejci (ankle) recorded five points (2-7 FG, 1-6 3Pt), two steals and one assist across 14 minutes in Tuesday's 130-125 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Krejci had been tending to an ankle sprain before the Hawks traded him to the Trail Blazers on Sunday, but the 25-year-old was quickly able to move past the injury to make his Portland debut Tuesday. He ended up claiming a rotational role right off the bat, and while he struggled to connect from downtown, Krejci made an impact on the defensive side with a pair of steals. The Trail Blazers could get Deni Avdija (back) and Scoot Henderson (hamstring) back from injuries as soon as this weekend, so Krejci may be at risk of losing his spot in the rotation when the team is at full strength.

items.headline: Krejci (ankle) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Tuesday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Krejci suffered a left ankle sprain shortly before being dealt from the Hawks to the Blazers, but he's evidently put the injury behind him. He'll presumably see playing time off the bench behind Shaedon Sharpe and Toumani Camara, though it remains to be seen how involved Krejci will be in his first appearance with Portland.

items.headline: The Hawks traded Krejci (ankle) to the Trail Blazers on Sunday in exchange for Duop Reath (foot) and two future second-round picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Krejci started against the Rockets on Thursday, posting nine points (4-7 FG), four rebounds, one assist and a steal in 27 minutes, but he was in street clothes due to an ankle injury during Saturday's loss in Indiana. Like the last few days, his role has been inconsistent all season, and with Zaccharie Risacher (knee) healthy again and Corey Kispert coming over in a trade, Krejci was going to be blocked for playing time in Atlanta. While Portland has a ton of wing depth, the Trail Blazers don't have many knockdown shooters, so Krejci, who's shot at least 40 percent from deep in three straight seasons, could carve out a role as a specialist once he moves past his ankle issue.

items.headline: Krejci (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Pacers.

items.headline: Krejci is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Pacers due to a left ankle sprain.

items.story: Krejci has been trending in the wrong direction for several weeks, so the Hawks will shake things up Monday. Corey Kispert is getting the starting nod with the team looking to deploy more shooting. However, as long as Kristaps Porzingis (Achilles) and Zaccharie Risacher (knee) remain sidelined, Krejci should have a role in Atlanta's rotation.

items.headline: Krejci produced three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one steal in 19 minutes during Saturday's 132-106 loss to the Celtics.

Outside of a handful of promising performances, Krejci has been mostly underwhelming thus far this season, averaging 9.8 points and 2.5 three-pointers in 23.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Krejci provided eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one block across 21 minutes during Thursday's 117-101 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Although Krejci drew the start, the Hawks utilized a lot of smaller lineups with CJ McCollum playing 29 minutes off the bench with 20 points to his name. Krejci's fantasy appeal remains limited to deeper formats with averages of 7.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.6 three-pointers over his last eight games.

items.headline: Krejci notched zero points (0-8 FG, 0-7 3Pt), one assist, two blocks and two steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 110-87 win over Denver.
items.story: Despite shifting into the starting lineup, Krejci failed to score, missing all eight of his shot attempts. With Zaccharie Risacher sidelined due to a knee issue, Krejci was given an opportunity to play starter-level minutes. His four defensive stats did somewhat salvage what was otherwise a disappointing night. Assuming Atlanta starts to get healthy bodies back on the floor in the coming games, Krejci should be viewed as nothing more than a potential three-point streaming option.

items.headline: Krejci will start against Denver on Friday, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The fifth-year pro will join the first unit due to Zaccharie Risacher (knee) being sidelined. Krejci has started just two games so far this season, during which he has averaged 13.5 points, 2.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 35.0 minutes per tilt. He has been extremely efficient from three-point range of late, shooting 49.2 percent from downtown on 6.5 attempts per game over his last 10 outings.

items.headline: Krejci recorded five points (2-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 117-100 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: The Hawks traded away Trae Young (quadriceps) on Wednesday, but they added CJ McCollum and Corey Kispert which could crowd things for Krejci. Krejci has had some solid outings in recent weeks, so it will be interesting to see what kind of role he carves out for the new-look Hawks.

items.headline: Krejci is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against Minnesota, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

While the fifth-year pro is outside the realm of fantasy relevance, Krejci has come in handy during Atlanta's smattering of absences and should be considered a viable option when the injury tags pile up.

Mavericks president Masai Ujiri said Lively has progressed to shooting and is working toward running on the court, while head coach Dusty May said the center is moving well but has a unique return-to-play protocol given all of his missed time in recent years.

items.headline: Lively (foot) won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Rockets.
items.story: Mavericks president Masai Ujiri said that Lively has progressed to shooting and is working toward running on the court, though Dallas intends to remain patient with the 22-year-old. Lively underwent right foot surgery in December after appearing in just seven regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 4.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 blocks in 16.4 minutes per game. He has yet to be cleared for training camp, and his status for the regular season remains uncertain.

items.headline: Mavericks president Masai Ujiri said Friday that Lively (foot) is "making good progress" in his recovery, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Ujiri noted that Lively has progressed to shooting and is working toward running on the court, though Dallas intends to remain patient with the 22-year-old. Lively underwent right foot surgery in December after appearing in just seven regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 4.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 blocks in 16.4 minutes per game. He has yet to be cleared for training camp, and his status for the beginning of the regular season remains uncertain.

items.headline: Lively (foot) has not been cleared to participate in training camp yet and is slowly ramping up to begin basketball activity, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Lively underwent right foot surgery in December after appearing in just seven regular-season games (four starts), during which he averaged 4.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.6 blocks and 0.6 steals across 16.4 minutes per contest. MacMahon notes that Lively has not suffered a setback. However, the big man is still in jeopardy of missing time to begin the 2026-27 regular season, and it wouldn't be surprising if he operates under a heavy minutes restriction upon his return. If the 22-year-old misses an extended period, Daniel Gafford, Santi Aldama (knee) and Morez Johnson would be candidates for increased burn.

items.headline: Lively (foot) still hasn't progressed to running yet, per Christian Clark of The Athletic.
items.story: Lively is walking and lifting weights, though he's not quite ready to enter the next phase of his rehab. The 22-year-old big man is recovering from right foot surgery, which cut his season short in December of last year, and it remains uncertain if he'll be a full participant in training camp this fall. The Mavericks did take Morez Johnson with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft to improve their frontcourt, but Lively remains the most likely candidate to open next season as Dallas' starting center.

items.headline: Lively (foot) faces increased competition for minutes heading into the 2026-27 campaign, especially with the Mavericks selecting Morez Johnson with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Lively hasn't lived up to expectations through his first three seasons in the NBA. Although the 22-year-old is a talented player, the real concern is his durability. After appearing in 55 games as a rookie, Lively played in 36 contests in his second year. However, things were worse in the 2025-26 campaign, with the 2023 No. 12 overall pick suiting up for only seven games before eventually undergoing season-ending foot surgery. Dallas has plenty of big bodies entering the season, though it's unknown how head coach Dusty May will divide the workload. One thing is clear; time is running out for Lively to prove he can stay healthy. In fact, it may already be too late. With that in mind, Johnson isn't a true center, but even if the former Wolverine plays the position in a limited capacity for the Mavericks in 2026-27, he might surpass Lively on the depth chart sooner rather than later.

items.headline: Lively successfully underwent surgery on his right foot Sunday.
items.story: Lively sought out multiple opinions on his right foot, but it was ultimately determined that season-ending surgery was the best course of action for the third-year center, and he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2026-27 season. Daniel Gafford and Dwight Powell will continue to serve as the main big men for Dallas behind Anthony Davis in Lively's absence.

items.headline: Lively is slated to undergo season-ending surgery in the coming days to address lingering discomfort in his right foot, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Lively sought multiple opinions on his foot since suffering a setback in his last appearance Nov. 21, but doctors determined that surgery was the best course of action. The 21-year-old is expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2026-27 season. He made just seven appearances during his third NBA season, posting averages of 4.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 blocks in 16.4 minutes per contest. Daniel Gafford is likely to have a higher minutes floor for the rest of the season with Lively out of the mix, and Moussa Cisse and Dwight Powell could continue to see more opportunities in backup roles.

items.story: Lively is getting multiple opinions regarding the swelling and discomfort in his right foot. It sounds like the third-year center can be labeled as week-to-week until the next steps in his recovery are determined. Dallas should continue to lean on Anthony Davis and Daniel Gafford (ankle) for the center minutes.

items.headline: Lively (foot) will miss the next three games and will be re-evaluated in seven-to-ten days, the Mavericks announced Tuesday.
items.story: This follows up a previous report from NBA reporter Marc Stein that indicated the Mavericks were fearful of the center missing extended time. Lively is currently being evaluated for swelling and discomfort in his right foot, and that's notable since it's the same foot he had offseason surgery on. This means Lively will be sidelined through Dec. 1, with an earliest possible return date of Dec. 3 against the Heat. Fantasy managers should brace for a longer absence, however. In the meantime, Daniel Gafford is likely to see a bump in fantasy appeal.

items.headline: According to NBA reporter Marc Stein, it is feared that the Mavericks could face an extended injury absence for Lively (foot).

items.headline: Head coach Jason Kidd said Wednesday that Lively (knee) is doing on-court work and will hopefully be back by next week, Christian Clark of the Athletic reports.
items.story: Lively has already missed five straight games with a sprained right knee, and he'll miss at least two more due to the issue. Kidd's comments indicate he'll be sidelined for both legs of Dallas's back-to-back that begins Friday. After that, Lively's next chance to play will come Monday against Milwaukee.

items.headline: Lively (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the  Pelicans.
items.story: Lively is slated to miss a fifth straight game and will be joined on the sidelines by Anthony Davis (calf) once again. That leaves Daniel Gafford as the Mavericks' starting center, with Dwight Powell as his primary backup. Lively's next chance to suit up will come Friday in Memphis, but at this point, he can be considered doubtful for that contest.

items.headline: Lively (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Lively will miss his fourth straight game due to a right knee sprain, with his next opportunity to return coming Wednesday against the Pelicans. With both him and Anthony Davis (calf) sidelined, Daniel Gafford is likely to remain in the starting lineup, while Dwight Powell could see increased opportunities.

items.headline: Lively (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Lively will miss his third consecutive game due to a right knee sprain, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against the Rockets. Dwight Powell is likely to see an uptick in playing time, especially if Daniel Gafford (ankle) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Lively (knee) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Pacers, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Lively will miss his second consecutive contest due to a sprained right knee. His next opportunity to play will come Saturday against Detroit. Anthony Davis will likely shoulder the responsibilities at center Wednesday, with Naji Marshall being in line for more playing time at power forward.

items.headline: Lively (knee) is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Pacers,
items.story: Lively is expected to miss his second consecutive contest due to a sprained right knee. If the big man is ultimately ruled out, his next opportunity to play will come Saturday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Lively (knee) won't play Monday against the Thunder, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: With Lively hitting the sidelines, Anthony Davis will likely slide over to center, which could allow D'Angelo Russell to finally move into the first unit. The Mavs play again Wednesday against the Pacers, and for now, Lively should be considered questionable for that one.

items.headline: Lively (knee) is doubtful for Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Monday's game is the second leg of a back-to-back set, and it sounds like Lively is going to be held out. His injury is being described as a left knee contusion, so it sounds relatively minor. With Daniel Gafford (ankle) considered doubtful, the Mavericks could slide Anthony Davis to center and utilize some smaller lineup combos.

items.headline: Dunn racked up three points (1-5 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four rebounds, five assists and three steals in 19 minutes during Saturday's 110-100 loss to Dallas.
items.story: Dunn recorded three steals for the second time in the past three games, although his peripheral contributions continue to be well below average. In four appearances over the past week, Dunn has barely been a top 200 player, averaging 4.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.8 steals in 20.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dunn won't start in Thursday's game against the Spurs, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn has started in all 13 of the Clippers' games during the 2026-27 campaign. However, he has struggled offensively, so he will come off the bench for the first time this season, resulting in Max Strus getting a turn in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Dunn closed with two points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds, five assists, one block and three steals in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Dunn continues to provide strong defensive production, recording multiple steals for the fifth time in his last eight appearances. The veteran guard has struggled offensively, averaging just 3.5 points over his last four games, but his contributions in steals, assists and rebounds help offset his limited scoring. His defensive upside keeps him relevant in deeper category-based fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Dunn had 14 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: The veteran guard has been a fairly pleasant surprise for the Clippers thus far, averaging 9.1 points, 4.4 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 2.6 steals per game. Dunn is likely to sacrifice some usage once Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is cleared to make his return to action.

items.headline: Dunn amassed five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime loss to the Heat.
items.story: Dunn continues to pile up steals for fantasy managers, recording multiple swipes for the sixth time in eight appearances. He's also registered at least three dimes in all but one game, so Dunn does carry plenty of fantasy appeal in category-based leagues while the Clippers' backcourt is shorthanded.

items.headline: Dunn finished Sunday's 124-112 loss to the Warriors with 12 points (5-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists, two rebounds and seven steals over 27 minutes.
items.story: It was only the second time through six regular-season games that Dunn scored in double digits. However, the veteran guard once again made more of an impact defensively and set a new career high in steals, one more than his previous best that he set Feb. 20, 2025, against the Bucks. Dunn is averaging 8.5 points, 5.3 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 3.0 steals over 29.7 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Dunn tallied 15 points (6-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, five steals, two blocks and two turnovers across 33 minutes in Sunday's 108-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Dunn cracked double digits in scoring for the first time this season, and he did so with remarkable efficiency, missing just two shots in 33 minutes of floor time. The scoring will come and go with Dunn, but as long as he's starting in Los Angeles, he should do enough with the assists and defensive stats to warrant a roster spot in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Dunn logged seven points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and three steals over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Getting the start in the backcourt due to Bradley Beal (knee) being on the shelf, Dunn mainly left the scoring to Darius Garland while the former led the Clippers in assists and made a strong impact on defense. Dunn started 68 of 82 regular-season games last season and averaged a modest 7.3 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 boards, 1.6 steals and 1.0 threes in 27.2 minutes, and his role doesn't seem likely to change much once the backcourt gets healthier.

items.headline: Dunn will start in Wednesday's game against Sacramento, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn will get the start against the Kings to begin the 2026-27 campaign. The 32-year-old started 68 regular-season games in 2025-26, averaging 7.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.6 steals over 27.9 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Dunn (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Kings.
items.story: Dunn sat out Los Angeles' preseason finale but should be back in action Wednesday. The veteran guard started 68 of his 82 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, though he isn't guaranteed a starting role to begin the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Dunn (rest) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Nuggets, independent Clippers reporter Joey Linn reports.
items.story: After appearing in each of the Clippers' first two preseason games, Dunn will be sidelined Wednesday for rest purposes. The veteran guard's next chance to suit up will come in the club's regular-season opener Oct. 21 against the Kings, when he could see an elevated role with Bradley Beal (knee) ruled out.

items.headline: Dunn recorded three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound, one steal and one block in six minutes off the bench during Sunday's 104-101 preseason win over Golden State.
items.story: Dunn saw only six minutes while Darius Garland handled the bulk of the point-guard duties with the first unit. However, Max Strus exited with an injury after starting at shooting guard, potentially opening additional opportunities for Dunn as the Clippers work through several early-season injuries.

items.headline: Dunn could be at risk of handling a reserve role in 2026-27 due to the selection of Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Dunn might be a loser from a fantasy perspective after the Clippers added Wagler, who would likely supplant Dunn from the first unit at shooting guard if he plays well during training camp. The defensive-minded Dunn was essentially a full-time starter last regular season, making 68 starts over 82 games, so his status as the incumbent veteran could also work in his favor if Wagler struggles in Summer League or at camp.

items.headline: Dunn contributed seven points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds, 10 assists and three steals across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to the Warriors.
items.story: With Los Angeles' season coming to an end, Dunn will be able to hold his head high. He appeared in all 82 regular-season games with 68 starts, posting averages of 7.3 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 rebounds, 1.6 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 27.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dunn will start in Sunday's game against Sacramento, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn will make his first start since the 105-99 loss to the Pelicans on March 19. In 63 starts throughout the 2025-26 campaign, the 32-year-old has averaged 7.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.1 blocks and 1.6 steals across 28.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dunn produced two points (1-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals across 21 minutes during Friday's 114-113 victory over Indiana.
items.story: Dun continues to produce on the defensive end, having now recorded at least two steals in five straight games. However, the rest of his numbers have been less than ideal, averaging just 4.2 points and 3.2 assists per game during that span. As has been the case for the majority of his career, Dunn should be considered nothing more than a steals specialist.

items.headline: Dunn will come off the bench Monday against the Bucks, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn was initially announced with the starters Monday, but the Clippers have since released an updated lineup, showing Nicolas Batum will draw the start in place of John Collins (ankle). Dunn has seen plenty of run as a reserve lately, as he logged 26 minutes Wednesday against New Orleans and 32 minutes Saturday in Dallas.

items.headline: Dunn will start Monday's game against the Bucks, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn will enter the first unit with John Collins (ankle) sidelined for Monday's clash. Dunn is averaging 6.5 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.2 steals in 13 March appearances (11 starts).

items.headline: Dunn isn't part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against Dallas, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn will come off the bench again Saturday, as the Clippers deploy a first five of Darius Garland, Kawhi Leonard, Derrick Jones, John Collins and Brook Lopez. Dunn is averaging 7.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.6 steals across 23.3 minutes per game as a reserve this season.

items.headline: Dunn will start Thursday versus the Pelicans, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Darius Garland (toe) and Kawhi Leonard (ankle) are taking the night off, so Dunn will return to the first unit, and he'll be joined by Jordan Miller, Derrick Jones, John Collins and Brook Lopez. As a starter this season, Dunn owns averages of 7.8 points, 3.9 assists, 1.0 three-pointers and 1.6 steals per game.

items.headline: Dunn will come off the bench for Wednesday's game in New Orleans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kawhi Leonard (ankle) is back and starting, so Dunn will shift to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Dunn owns averages of 7.3 points and 1.7 steals per game.

items.headline: Dunn contributed five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and three steals in 29 minutes during Monday's 126-118 win over New York.
items.story: This was a modest line for Dunn, but his offense usually comes and goes. Overall this season, Dunn ranks just outside the top-150 players in nine-category formats with 7.8 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Dunn totaled 16 points (7-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 26 minutes during Monday's 114-101 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Dunn's time as a viable fantasy contributor may be running out soon, as Darius Garland returned to action and will be the starter at point guard once he reaches 100 percent. Fantasy managers who depend on Dunn's production will need to pivot quickly, as productive nights from Dunn could be limited to upcoming back-to-backs if Garland rests.

items.headline: Dunn (head) is off the injury report for Monday's game against the Warriors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn departed Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury and did not return, but he's good to go Monday. The veteran guard has tallied at least one steal and four assists in six of his last seven outings and remains a strong streaming option for swipes and dimes.

items.headline: Dunn left Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury and did not return.
items.story: Dunn exited the game for the locker room in the fourth quarter after appearing to get hit in the head by an inadvertent elbow, and he did not return. It should be noted that the game was all but over when Dunn exited and head coach Tyronn Lue stated postgame that Dunn was "good" following the injury, so it does not appear to be a concern going forward.

items.headline: Dunn went back to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn appeared to get hit with an inadvertent elbow from Pelicans player Karlo Matkovic before heading back to the locker room, grabbing at his head and neck area. Considering the injury occurred in the latter portion of a lopsided contest, it would be surprising if Dunn returns to the game, leaving extra minutes for Bennedict Mathurin.

items.headline: Dunn chipped in seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and two steals across 34 minutes during Sunday's 111-109 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Dunn remains a steady source of swipes without a whole lot else to be excited about in the box score. Over his last 12 appearances, the veteran guard has averaged 8.2 points, 5.2 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 29.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dunn had 16 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, six assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 105-102 win over the Rockets.
items.story: The 16 points were Dunn's third-highest total on the year. The veteran guard has averaged 8.3 points, 4.6 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 27.3 minutes per contest in his last 10 games, so Dunn remains a decent fantasy streamer for dimes and swipes.

items.headline: Dunn was ejected from Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn has been ejected from Sunday's game after getting into a scuffle with Julius Randle. He concludes the contest with nine points (3-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six assists, five rebounds and a steal in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Dunn had six points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and six assists across 27 minutes during Monday's 128-113 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: The absence of James Harden (personal) didn't translate into a noticeable boost in usage for Dunn on Monday. Dunn remains strictly a fantasy streamer for swipes, averaging 6.1 points, 3.6 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 26.0 minutes per tilt in his last seven games.

items.headline: Dunn closed Tuesday's 115-103 win over the Jazz with 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and five steals in 31 minutes.
items.story: Dunn was very effective on defense, padding his fantasy totals with five steals. He also produced 14 points, marking his 15th game with 10 or more points. While his scoring average (7.9 points per game) is still low, decent secondary numbers will often offset a cold shooting night.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) will play in Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The veteran guard left Sunday's 126-89 win over the Nets with a right ankle injury, but he's good to go Tuesday. Dunn has averaged 5.7 points, 3.2 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 27.7 minutes per contest in his last 10 games.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Janis Carr of the Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Dunn departed Sunday's game against the Nets after picking up a right ankle injury, and he's now in jeopardy of missing Tuesday's matchup. Jordan Miller and Cam Christie would be in line for more minutes if Dunn is ultimately unable to go.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) didn't return to Sunday's 126-89 win over the Nets after exiting with 2:25 remaining in the second quarter. He finished the game with two points (1-3 FG), three rebounds and one steal in 13 minutes.
items.story: Dunn checked out of the game after he appeared to tweak his right ankle, and though the Clippers never officially ruled him out for the game, he remained on the bench for the entire second half while Kobe Sanders opened the third quarter with the starters. The Clippers took a 31-point lead into halftime, which may have played a part in the decision to hold Dunn out for the rest of the contest. The team should provide an update on Dunn's status when it releases its next injury report prior to Tuesday's game in Utah.

items.headline: Dunn (leg) left Sunday's game against the Nets for the locker room, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn appeared to roll his right ankle before going back to the locker room in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. If he is unable to return, Kobe Sanders figures to see extra minutes.

items.headline: Dunn posted 15 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 121-117 overtime victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Dunn was a strong all-around presence in Friday's win, hitting key threes while also making his impact felt as a facilitator and on the defensive end. While his scoring can fluctuate, the veteran guard's ability to generate turnovers stands out, as he's recorded at least one steal in 33 of 41 games this season and has logged three or more in three of the past four contests.

items.headline: Dunn closed with zero points (0-6 FG, 0-6 3Pt) and two rebounds over 21 minutes during Monday's 117-109 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: Dunn missed all six of his shot attempts, continuing an awful run of production since the beginning of the year. Over the past seven games, Dunn has averaged only 6.6 points, 3.7 assists and 2.4 rebounds, and he logged a double-digit point total only once over that span. Dunn's subpar play may give way to Jordan Miller in the short term, and the eventual return of Bogdan Bogdanovic (hamstring) could give the starting lineup an upgrade.

items.headline: Dunn recorded seven points (2-9 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 123-111 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dunn was unable to follow up his strong performance against the Warriors on Monday, shooting poorly from the field and recording no defensive stats for just the fourth time this season. While Dunn has not been consistent in his shot efficiency, he is averaging 8.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.2 blocks and 1.2 threes across 28.0 minutes in 30 starts and continues to be an integral part of the Clippers' first unit.

items.headline: Dunn provided 16 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Monday's 103-102 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Dunn rarely shows out like this offensively, so this was a nice surprise for his fantasy managers. He continues to be a solid source of assists, defensive stats and three-pointers, posting averages of 8.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.6 three-pointers in 28.3 minutes over his last seven outings.

items.headline: Carr posted no counting stats in one minute during Sunday's 131-125 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: The rookie missed Los Angeles' first six games due to an oblique injury before making a brief appearance Sunday. His return to the floor is a positive development, though Carr remains outside the regular rotation and carries little immediate fantasy value.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Raptors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Carr, the No. 24 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, has been cleared to make his regular-season debut Sunday following his recovery from a right oblique strain that he picked up during the preseason. It's not clear what his role in the rotation will look like, but he could see most of his minutes in the G League.

items.headline: The Lakers assigned Carr (oblique) to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Friday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: The rookie has yet to debut at the NBA level. He remains miles off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Carr has yet to make his NBA debut while tending to a right oblique strain. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Sunday against Toronto.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder will need more time to recover from the oblique injury that's kept him sidelined for what will be his fifth consecutive contest. Carr's next chance to suit up will come against the Warriors on Friday in the first Emirates NBA Cup matchup, and while it's unclear if he'll be ready for that game, he has been ramping up his activity with practices in the G League.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) was assigned Wednesday to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: With the Lakers unlikely to have much practice time over their current back-to-back set, this assignment gives Carr a chance to continue his recovery work from an oblique injury. The rookie guard was recalled Tuesday and could be brought back to the parent club at some point soon.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Carr (oblique) from the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Tuesday, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
items.story: According to Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times, Carr logged a full practice with the G League Lakers on Tuesday. He's working his way back from an oblique strain, and the rookie's next chance to play for the parent club will come Wednesday against the Clippers in the second leg of the Lakers' back-to-back set.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) was assigned to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Monday, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Carr is presumably getting some work in with LA's G League affiliate as he continues to battle his way back from an oblique strain. He's been ruled out for the Lakers' matchup against Portland on Tuesday but could have a chance to make his NBA debut Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Carr will miss a fourth consecutive regular-season contest due to an oblique strain. The rookie's next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Sunday's game in Utah, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: This will be Carr's third straight game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Trail Blazers, the first game of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Carr isn't quite ready to make his NBA debut, but he can continue to be considered day-to-day. His next chance to take the court will arrive Sunday in Utah.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Carr (oblique), who is out for Wednesday's game against Golden State, is "ramping up" and can be considered day-to-day moving forward, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Carr will miss the Lakers' regular-season opener, though he can be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Clippers until further notice. With the rookie sidelined, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams are candidates for a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Carr has been dealing with an oblique injury. Considering the rookie hasn't been practicing, it appears his absence will extend beyond Opening Night. With Carr sidelined, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams are candidates for more playing time behind Quentin Grimes.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Tuesday, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The rookie guard continues to nurse a contusion. His status remains in the dark for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Monday, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: The rookie guard continues to tend to a contusion. His status is unknown for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against Denver, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Carr will miss a third consecutive contest due to a contusion. His next chance to play will come in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Thursday, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: Carr continues to manage a minor contusion. His status is unknown for Friday's preseason finale versus Denver.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason matchup with the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Carr remains day-to-day but will miss a second straight game due to an undisclosed injury. His final chance to play again in the preseason will come Friday against Denver.

items.headline: Carr won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Kings due to a contusion, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Carr and several other players are reportedly dealing with minor injuries, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com, but the Lakers aren't concerned about him missing any regular-season action. His next chance to play will arrive Tuesday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr totaled 19 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Carr led the Lakers' reserves in scoring and continued to make a case for a rotation role after an impressive Summer League. Coach JJ Redick indicated during training camp that the rookie could earn opportunities this season, and Monday's performance was an encouraging first step.

items.headline: Carr could be part of the Lakers' rotation as a rookie, according to head coach JJ Redick, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Redick indicated that Los Angeles plans to utilize a deeper rotation this season, which could create an opportunity for Carr to earn minutes. The rookie will still need to establish himself during training camp and the preseason, but he appears to have a path to a regular role. Keep an eye on him in deeper formats.

items.headline: Carr contributed 17 points (5-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 28 minutes in Saturday's 92-88 loss to the Warriors in the Las Vegas Summer League Semifinals.
items.story: Carr's and the Lakers' Summer League run came to an end Saturday, and the rookie first-rounder struggled mightily with efficiency. Still, he finished as Los Angeles' second-leading scorer, posting at least 14 points for the fourth time in as many Las Vegas Summer League outings. During that span, Carr averaged 18.0 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists per contest. He's in line to compete for meaningful playing time off the bench in his rookie season.

items.headline: Carr registered 14 points (5-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one steal in 22 minutes during Thursday's 105-82 Summer League win over the Bulls.
items.story: Carr put together a decent effort offensively, and while he couldn't get a shot to fall from beyond the arc, his production from the field helped the Lakers to a 4-0 Summer League record. The rookie has been putting together an impressive showing thus far in Summer League play, and assuming the Lakers don't shut him down, he'll have additional opportunities to get run over the weekend.

items.headline: Carr (thumb) tallied 23 points (8-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 3-5 FT), one rebound, two assists and one block over 29 minutes in Tuesday's 99-85 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Clippers.
items.story: Carr sat out Saturday's Summer League win over the Mavs with a minor thumb issue, but he returned Tuesday to pour in a game-high 23 points, suggesting the issue is behind him. The Lakers are 3-0 through their first three games in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Carr won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against Dallas due to a right thumb contusion, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Carr will be held out of Saturday's contest after scoring 18 points across 29 minutes in the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr finished with 18 points (7-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks across 29 minutes in Friday's 96-84 Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: After scoring just five points in Monday's 88-84 California Classic Summer League win over San Antonio, Carr turned it around Friday, finishing only two points behind Adou Thiero, who scored a game-high 20. The 21-year-old may not play in every game for the Lakers throughout the remainder of the team's time in Las Vegas. However, even if Carr suits up only a few more times, he is already in line for an expanded role heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Carr produced five points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, one assist, one steal and one block in 13 minutes of Monday's 88-84 Summer League win over the Spurs.
items.story: The Lakers relied heavily on their second unit in this contest, and Carr wasn't able to make much of an impact. He's been solid through three exhibitions, however, posting averages of 15.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 3.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Carr logged 26 points (7-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds and one assist in 31 minutes during Sunday's 93-91 double-overtime win over the Heat at the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Carr did much of his work from beyond the arc again Sunday, knocking down a game-high four three-pointers en route to a game-high 26 points. The 24th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has averaged 22.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 27.5 minutes per contest through two Summer League appearances. He figures to remain the Lakers' top option at Summer League for as long as he suits up.

items.headline: Carr finished with 19 points (7-15 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block over 24 minutes in Friday's 104-72 California Classic Summer League loss to Golden State.
items.story: Carr led the Lakers in scoring while tying Yaxel Lendeborg for a game-high 19 points. He also made five three-point shots, three more than the rest of the team combined.
