Despite the continued absence of Cade Cunningham (chest), Sasser has been unable to carve out a consistent role, with Daniss Jenkins the clear beneficiary at this point. At best, Sasser can be considered for streaming purposes by anyone desperate for assists and steals.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is available for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.

items.story: Sasser is expected to play through a right hip strain Saturday. The guard has averaged 5.3 points, 3.0 assists and 1.3 rebounds in 16.8 minutes per contest in his last four games.

items.story: In his return from a three-game absence due to a right hip strain, Sasser paced the Pistons with a 33.8 percent usage rate but his inefficient shooting yielded an underwhelming line. Sasser will likely stick in the Detroit rotation for as long as Cade Cunningham (lung) remains sidelined, but he's expected to continue playing second fiddle to Daniss Jenkins, who has thrived since replacing Cunningham as the team's starting point guard.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is available for Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Sasser is overcoming a probable designation due to a hip injury that cost him the past three contests. Sasser has averaged 7.5 points, 2.9 assists, 1.8 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 20.5 minutes per contest in his last eight games.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is probable for Thursday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Sasser is trending towards a return after spending three straight games on the shelf. He may see a modest workload behind Daniss Jenkins if he gets the green light to suit up.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Sasser was unable to shake his doubtful tag for this contest and will sit for a third straight game. His next chance to play comes Thursday against the Pelicans. Daniss Jenkins should continue to be the primary beneficiary of Cade Cunningham's (lung) absence until Sasser is cleared to suit up.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Sasser appears headed for his third straight absence as a result of a right hip strain. Assuming he's downgraded to out before tipoff, expect Caris LeVert and Kevin Huerter to continue to see a slight uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is out for Monday's matchup with the Lakers.
items.story: This will be Sasser's second straight game on the sidelines, and with Wednesday's game versus the Hawks being the first of a back-to-back set, it wouldn't be surprising to see Sasser spend at least one more game beyond Monday sidelined. Caris LeVert and Kevin Huerter will have a chance for some extra minutes with Sasser unavailable.

items.headline: Sasser is out for Friday's game against the Warriors due to right hip soreness.
items.story: Sasser is sitting out the second half of Detroit's back-to-back set Friday. His absence should slightly increase the streaming value of Daniss Jenkins, Caris LeVert and Duncan Robinson versus Golden State, as Cade Cunningham's (chest) injury has left a ton of usage available in Detroit.

items.headline: Sasser will come off the bench for Sunday's game in Toronto.
items.story: Ausar Thompson (ankle) is back and starting Sunday, so Sasser will shift back to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Sasser owns averages of 4.8 points and 1.8 assists per contest.

items.headline: Sasser (lower leg) started the second half of Saturday's game against the Nets, per the broadcast.
items.story: Sasser headed back to the locker room late in the second quarter after grabbing at his lower left leg. However, he has been cleared to check back in and appears to be good to go for the remainder of the game.

items.headline: Sasser exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Saturday's game against the Nets due to an apparent lower left leg issue, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sasser was seen grabbing at his left lower leg before checking out of Saturday's contest with 1:19 remaining in the first half. If he's unable to return in the second half, Caris LeVert and Kevin Huerter will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Sasser is in the Pistons' starting lineup against the Nets on Saturday, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sasser has seen inconsistent playing time off the Pistons' bench all year, but he'll make his first start of the season (and first since April 13, 2025) due to the absences of Cade Cunningham (quadriceps) and Ausar Thompson (ankle). Sasser is averaging 4.8 points, 1.8 assists and 0.8 rebounds over 9.4 minutes per game this season, though he was a healthy scratch in four of Detroit's last six games.

items.headline: Sasser amassed zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two assists in 10 minutes during Friday's 118-80 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Despite the fact that Jaden Ivey is no longer in Detroit, it appears as though Sasser is still buried on the depth chart. Detroit plans to convert the contract for Daniss Jenkins, allowing him to serve as a regular piece of the rotation. Barring injuries to other players, Sasser can be safely overlooked in most formats.

items.headline: Sasser ended Wednesday's 112-104 win over New Orleans with nine points (3-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and four assists over 21 minutes.
items.story: Sasser played at least 20 minutes for just the third time this season, shifting up in the rotation due to the absence of Cade Cunningham (hip). Although Sasser has been able to contribute when afforded meaningful minutes, situations like that are simply too rare at this point, making him a non-factor in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Sasser finished Thursday's 118-112 loss to Miami with 18 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two steals in 24 minutes.
items.story: After having recorded a DNP-CD in four straight games, Sasser has logged 20-plus minutes in back-to-back outings. The 25-year-old guard has made the most of his minutes of late, scoring at least 18 points in each of his last two appearances. He has totaled 37 points, seven assists, six rebounds and four steals across 48 minutes in that two-game stretch.

items.headline: Sasser had 19 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two steals across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 128-106 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Sasser first served as a direct replacement for Cade Cunningham, but the team elected to play him for the entire fourth quarter, where he did most of his damage during a 20-4 run to end the game. The loss of Tobias Harris  (hip) shook up the rotation, and Ausar Thompson's tepid play opened up a nice opportunity for Sasser to produce.

items.headline: Sasser ended Saturday's 112-86 win over the Hornets with one rebound and one assist across two minutes.
items.story: Sasser failed to score for the third time in four games since returning from injury, continuing to serve as nothing more than a depth piece for the Pistons. Even when playing a meaningful role, Sasser has yet to flash any real upside, meaning his value for this season is likely to be nonexistent.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) tallied zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two assists while playing the final 4:13 of Saturday's 124-112 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Cleared to make his season debut after missing the Pistons' first 23 games due to a right hip impingement, Sasser wasn't part of the rotation Saturday but was able to get into the contest in garbage time after Detroit built up a 25-point advantage. Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Caris LeVert and Jaden Ivey appear to be Detroit's top four guards when the team is at full strength, but Sasser could end up getting a look in the rotation if any of those players are out for a given game. Sasser checked into Saturday's contest slightly before second-year guard Daniss Jenkins, who first got off the bench with 3:34 remaining in the fourth quarter.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is available for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Sasser will be available to make his regular-season debut after missing time due to a right hip impingement. The 25-year-old guard will likely face heavy restrictions as he's eased back into action, though he isn't guaranteed to see significant minutes regardless.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is probable for Saturday's game versus the Bucks.
items.story: Sasser is on track to make his regular-season debut, but he'll likely have some restrictions in his first game of the season. Managers can take a wait-and-see approach with Sasser in most formats.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is listed as out for Friday's game against Portland, per the official NBA lineups page.
items.story: Sasser had been upgraded to questionable for the first time all season, but he won't make his season debut. He's been sidelined due to a right hip impingement, and his next chance to play will come Saturday against Milwaukee.

items.headline: Sasser (hip) is questionable to play Friday against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Sasser has yet to suit up for the Pistons this season as he's been recovering from a right hip impingement, but he recently got in a game with Detroit's G League affiliate, so he's clearly on the cusp of making his regular-season debut. Check back for another update closer to Friday's tip.

items.headline: Detroit recalled Sasser (hip) from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Wednesday.
items.story: Sasser made his season debut for the Cruise in Wednesday's 114-112 G League loss to the Wisconsin Herd after recovering from a right hip issue. He finished with 20 points (7-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists and one steal in 23 minutes. It's unclear when he'll be involved with the NBA club.

items.headline: Detroit assigned Sasser (hip) to the G League's Motor City Cruise on Monday.
items.story: This is likely another rehab assignment for Sasser, as he's yet to make his regular-season debut for Detroit. On Monday, head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said that Sasser is trending in the right direction and has progressed to 3-on-3 work.

items.headline: Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Monday that Sasser (hip) is trending in the right direction and has progressed to 3-on-3 work, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Sasser has yet to make his regular-season debut due to a lingering right hip issue, though he's seemingly nearing a return to the court. The 25-year-old guard has been getting practice reps in with the Pistons' G League affiliate, the Motor City Cruise, though he'll need to be cleared for 5-on-5 work before returning to game action with Detroit. He can still be considered week-to-week until the Pistons provide another update on his rehab.

items.headline: The Pistons recalled Sasser from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Saturday and assigned him back to the G League on Sunday.
items.story: Sasser will presumably join Motor City for practice again as he works his way back from a right hip impingement. While it's an encouraging sign that the 25-year-old guard is getting reps in, he still doesn't have a concrete timetable for his return to game action.

items.headline: Dick supplied zero points (0-2 FG) and one assist over 17 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 loss to Utah.
items.story: Dick saw his four-game double-digit scoring streak come to an end Tuesday, going 0-for-2 from the field in 17 minutes. The third-year wing had averaged 12.5 points on 66.7 percent shooting over his previous four appearances, but his limited playing time and minimal contributions outside scoring continue to restrict his fantasy upside. He remains primarily a three-point shooting option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Dick notched 15 points (6-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two steals in 17 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: Dick went for an efficient 15 points off the bench Sunday. However, the swingman is in danger of losing playing time once Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is cleared to make his season debut.

items.headline: Dick won't start in Wednesday's game against Miami, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dick started in Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto, finishing with 12 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. However, with Rui Hachimura (quadriceps) back in the lineup, Dick will return to the bench.

items.headline: Dick racked up 12 points (5-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 29 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
items.story: With Derrick Jones (knee) sidelined, Dick started and contributed across several categories against his former team, though he attempted just one three-pointer and failed to connect from beyond the arc. The 22-year-old's fantasy upside remains tied to his perimeter shooting and offensive involvement. His two steals helped offset a relatively modest scoring performance in a short-term expanded role.

items.headline: Dick will start Monday's game against the Raptors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dick will get the nod at small forward due to Derrick Jones (knee) sitting out Monday. Dick got off to a strong start this season by dropping 12 points in the opener against the Kings, but he's been held to single digits in the scoring column in five games since.

items.headline: Dick closed Wednesday's 121-96 win over Sacramento with 12 points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and one block across 19 minutes.
items.story: With the rebuilding Clippers dealing with several injuries already, Dick stitched up an Opening Night rotation spot. A 2023 first-rounder, Dick remains worth monitoring on waiver wires until his role becomes more solidified.

items.headline: Dick amassed eight points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds, two steals and four assists over 19 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Dick could see extra opportunities to start the season while Brandon Ingram recovers from a partially torn Achilles. His chances of claiming an Opening Night role increased when the Clippers announced Wednesday that Bradley Beal (knee) won't be ready to begin the year.

items.headline: Dick could see increased opportunities to begin the season while Brandon Ingram recovers from a partially torn Achilles and right heel surgery.
items.story: Dick arrived in Los Angeles alongside Ingram in the Kawhi Leonard trade and will compete for minutes on a Clippers team currently thin on the wing. Ingram's absence gives Dick an opportunity to earn a consistent rotation role, though he'll still face competition for playing time.

items.headline: The Clippers and Raptors mutually agreed Monday to complete the trade sending Leonard to Toronto in exchange for Brandon Ingram (heel), Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The trade hit a snag in July when the league investigated Leonard and the Clippers for salary cap circumvention, but the deal is now official ahead of training camp. The 2023 first-rounder is searching for a fresh start in Los Angeles after averaging 6.0 points and 1.9 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per game across 76 regular-season appearances (one start) for the Raptors last year.

items.headline: The NBA has concluded its investigation into salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers, and the trade sending Dick to Los Angeles is expected to be finalized in the coming days, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Among other punishments, the Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks Wednesday. Furthermore, Leonard was fined $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits. With the findings and penalities being announced, Dick is now expected to officially join the Clippers after spending his first three seasons in the Association with Toronto. The 2023 No. 13 overall pick's production took a hit in 2025-26, during which he averaged 6.0 points and 1.9 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per game across 76 regular-season appearances (one start). The Clippers are set to acquire Dick, Brandon Ingram (heel), two first-round picks, two second-round picks and a first-round pick swap in exchange for Leonard. Dick figures to provide wing depth for Los Angeles in 2026-27, though he'll likely have to compete for playing time with Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal (hip) and Max Strus.

items.headline: The Raptors are expected to send Dick, Brandon Ingram, two first-round picks, a first-round pick swap and two second-round picks to the Clippers on Tuesday in exchange for Kawhi Leonard, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After a promising sophomore campaign, Dick took a major step back in Year 3 and will look for a fresh start with a change of scenery. The sharpshooter shot over 35 percent from three in each of his first two seasons but hit rock bottom in 2025-26, shooting 30.3 percent on 2.4 three-point attempts per game while playing only 14 minutes a night over 76 regular-season games. Dick will likely be competing with Kobe Sanders and Jordan Miller for reserve minutes in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Dick did not see the floor during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: With Brandon Ingram (heel) joining the Raptors, Dick took a huge step back in 2025-26. Across 76 regular-season appearances, the third-year sharpshooter averaged a career-low 6.0 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 14.0 minutes per game. Dick is set to return to Toronto in 2026-27, but it's concerning that he wasn't able to move into a more prominent role despite Ingram's absence in Game 7.

items.headline: Dick ended Sunday's 139-87 win over the Magic with 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 23 minutes.
items.story: Dick has been used sparingly in recent weeks, but he took advantage of some extra touches in this 52-point blowout win. Over his last six outings, he's averaging just 13.7 minutes per contest with 6.8 points, 1.5 assists and 1.5 rebounds on 40.0 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick registered 10 points (2-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 15 minutes during Sunday's 120-98 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: The 2023 first-rounder has been part of Toronto's rotation for just two of the team's last five contests, implying he's not a major aspect of the mix for the time being. That said, Dick has an opportunity to remain in the lineup for Monday's matchup with the Jazz due to the absence of Immanuel Quickley (foot).

items.headline: Dick (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Raptors' 122-115 win over the Suns.
items.story: Dick had appeared in each of Toronto's previous five contests while averaging 5.8 points in 6.8 minutes, but he ended up being the odd man out after head coach Darko Rajakovic condensed his rotation to nine Friday. The third-year wing's chances of re-emerging as a regular in the rotation will become even more difficult moving forward, as Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) appears to be closing in on a return, which will bring the Toronto roster back to full strength.

items.headline: Dick finished with zero points (0-1 FG) in one minute during Tuesday's 111-95 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dick moved back into the rotation after sitting out the previous two games, albeit for one minute during garbage time. Outside of a handful of encouraging performances, Dick has been a letdown this season, averaging just 6.2 points in 15.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dick (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Raptors' 110-107 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Dick had appeared in each of the Raptors' first 58 games of the season, but after he was held under 10 minutes in two of the previous three contests, he was dropped from the rotation entirely. Rather than sticking with Dick on the second unit, head coach Darko Rajakovic went with Jamison Battle (six minutes) as the 10th man in the rotation. While Dick's removal from the rotation could prove to be a short-term arrangement, the Raptors still aren't expected to make the third-year wing a major priority when the team is at full strength.

items.headline: Dick will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Dick made his first start of the season Tuesday, logging 10 points and three rebounds across 23 minutes. However, he'll be replaced by Sandro Mamukelashvili in the first unit for Wednesday's matchup.

items.headline: Dick will start Tuesday versus the Warriors.
items.story: Dick will be earning his first start of the season Tuesday evening, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Jamal Shead, Immanuel Quickley, Brandon Ingram and Scottie Barnes. Per 36 minutes this season, Dick owns averages of 14.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.9 triples and 1.4 steals per game.

items.headline: Dick posted 21 points (9-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-101 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Dick came from nowhere, recording the first double-double of his career, taking advantage of a depleted roster. Toronto was without Immanuel Quickley (back), RJ Barrett (ankle), Sandro Mamukelashvili (illness) and Ja'Kobe Walter (hip), as well as Jakob Poeltl, who continues to deal with a back issue. While this was a great performance, there is no need to prioritize Dick as a pickup, unless health continues to be an issue for others around him.

items.headline: Dick produced 11 points (4-4 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and two steals across 18 minutes during Monday's 118-100 win over the Hawks.
items.story: Dick continues to be used sparingly by the Raptors, making him a hit-or-miss fantasy asset in very deep formats. Over his last seven games, he's seen 15.1 minutes per night with 6.3 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 0.7 three-pointers on 43.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick closed Sunday's 141-127 overtime win over the Warriors with four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 15 minutes.
items.story: Dick has mostly been an afterthought in Toronto's rotation lately. Over his last seven games, he's seen a mere 15.6 minutes per contest with 5.0 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 three-pointers on 34.2 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick totaled 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds and two steals in 15 minutes during Monday's 106-96 victory over Miami.
items.story: Dick bounced back from his last two scoreless appearances to reach double digits in points for just the eighth time this season, which included him breaking a three-game dry spell from beyond the arc. On the season, Dick averages 6.4 points, 1.9 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.7 steals, 0.1 blocks and 0.9 threes across 15.8 minutes.

items.headline: Dick posted zero points (0-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound across eight minutes during Tuesday's 117-101 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dick failed to score for the second straight game, another in a string of disappointing performances. After carving out a serviceable role for himself last season, Dick has been a non-factor thus far, averaging 6.3 points and 0.9 three-pointers in 15.8 minutes per game. He can be ignored in all but deeper leagues.

items.headline: Dick notched four points (2-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 21 minutes during Friday's 111-86 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Dick continues to be used sparingly, resulting in poor production across the board. He has scored double digits only six times thus far this season, averaging 6.8 points and 1.0 three-pointers in 16.4 minutes per contest. At this stage, he would need a lot of luck to force his way into a sizable role.

items.headline: Dick (head) is not listed on Friday's injury report and is on track to be available for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Dick sustained a head injury during the Raptors' win over the Pacers on Wednesday. The injury doesn't appear to be a serious issue for the third-year forward, and he should be available to play in the first leg of the Raptors' back-to-back set Saturday. Across 13 games since Nov. 2, Dick has averaged 6.8 points, 1.8 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 1.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 16.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dick (head) has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday's game against the Pacers, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dick hit his head on the hardwood after taking a fall. He took a brief trip to the locker room before being ruled out. His next chance to play will come Saturday at Charlotte. Jamison Battle and Ochai Agbaji should see an uptick in minutes the rest of Wednesday's contest. Dick went scoreless (0-2 3Pt) with three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block over seven minutes before departing.

items.headline: Dick went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against Indiana after a hard fall, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.careports.
items.story: Dick took a hard fall while pursuing an offensive rebound, and according to Tony East of Forbes.com, Dick hit his head on the floor. The young wing stayed in the game briefly before departing and heading back to the locker room. Jamison Battle and Ochai Agbaji could see additional minutes while Dick is sidelined.

items.headline: Dick recorded 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and two assists in 19 minutes during Monday's 110-108 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Dick logged just his fifth appearance of the season with at least 10 points and his sixth time hitting multiple threes. The 2023 first-round pick has not seen enough volume or produced enough in other categories to warrant any value on any fantasy rosters yet. Still, he could be an intriguing add should one of the starters miss any time.

items.headline: Dick closed with six points (3-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 119-109 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Dick has not been as involved in the rotation as he was thought to be entering the season, averaging 7.6 points, 2.2 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.5 steals and 1.2 threes on a 35.1 percent clip in only 15.9 minutes. His role backing up Brandon Ingram is established, and he will likely only see extended playing time in the event of injury or blowout.

items.headline: Dick amassed 14 points (3-4 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT) and one rebound across 22 minutes during Tuesday's 128-100 win over the Bucks.
items.story: The Raptors ran away with this game early on, allowing Dick to see extended run off the bench. This was Dick's second-highest scoring performance of the season, with his best night coming Opening Night with 21 points. Dick remains mostly a deep-league fantasy asset with averages of 8.0 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.1 three-pointers in 16.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dick notched zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) across eight minutes during Monday's 121-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Dick missed both of his shot attempts, continuing what has been a modest start to the season. Coming off a strong 2024-25 season, Dick's role has seemingly taken a sizeable hit. The addition of Brandon Ingram, as well as the arrival of rookie Collin Murray-Boyles, has seen Dick slide into a negotiable role, with his playing time fluctuating from one night to the next.

items.headline: Dick dropped five points (2-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, an assist and a steal across 18 minutes in Friday's 122-116 loss to Milwaukee.
items.story: Dick was unable to follow up his stellar performance Wednesday against the Hawks. However, he led all bench players in minutes played and will continue in his role as the team's sixth man. Dick's next chance to make amends for his quiet showing will be Sunday against the Mavericks.

items.headline: Dick finished Wednesday's 138-118 victory over Atlanta with 21 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 24 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard led the charge for the Raptors' second unit on a night when they out-scored the Hawks' bench 48-34. Dick saw his minutes and shooting volume increase in 2024-25 without it adversely affecting his efficiency, and the 21-year-old could be poised to take another step forward this season.

items.headline: Dick (back) is slated to play Friday in the preseason finale against Brooklyn, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Dick missed Wednesday's preseason game against the Celtics with back spasms. However, the sharpshooter looks to be good to go Friday and will enter the regular season with a bill of health.

items.headline: Dick (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Celtics, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dick will not suit up due to lower back spasms, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports. The next opportunity for the Kansas product to return to the floor will be Friday's preseason finale against the Nets.

items.headline: Dick finished with 22 points (8-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 24 minutes during Friday's 107-105 preseason win over the Celtics.
items.story: Dick had a strong all-around performance, coming four rebounds shy of a double-double in limited minutes on the floor. The Kansas product shot well, making 61.5 percent of his attempts from the field.

items.headline: Dick will start Friday's preseason game against the Celtics.
items.story: A number of the Raptors' usual starters are sitting Friday, giving Dick a shot with the first five. That said, the sharpshooter will likely begin the regular season in a reserve role.

items.headline: Dick racked up 14 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 15 minutes during Wednesday's 130-122 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Dick was incredibly efficient off the bench during his limited time on the floor. He shot 85.7 percent from the floor while showing his knack for scoring when he's the primary option for Toronto.

items.headline: Goodwin closed Wednesday's 128-107 win over the Kings with two points (1-2 FG), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 17 minutes.
items.story: Although the two points were his lowest of the year thus far, Goodwin has been a pleasant surprise off the bench for the Suns for the most part. Over his first 10 appearances, the swingman has averaged 9.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.9 three-pointers in 19.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Goodwin ended Tuesday's 133-110 victory over the Clippers with 18 points (6-7 FG, 6-7 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes.
items.story: Goodwin returned from a four-game absence due to a calf injury and wasted no time getting back into the swing of things, knocking down six of his seven three-point attempts off the bench. While this was certainly an impressive return, it came in just 14 minutes, and that kind of shooting isn't sustainable. With Luke Kennard, Collin Gillespie and Ryan Dunn all competing for backcourt minutes, Goodwin's playing time could fluctuate on a nightly basis. He should be viewed as a deeper-league streaming option for now, particularly for those needing steals.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is off the injury report for Tuesday's game versus the Clippers.
items.story: Goodwin is set to return Tuesday from a four-game absence with a right calf injury. Ryan Dunn's role had grown amid Goodwin's absence, so it remains to be seen how the Suns handle their wing minutes among their reserves going forward.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Spurs, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Goodwin will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a right calf injury. Coach Jordan Ott noted Monday that the team is hopeful Goodwin can take the court Tuesday against the Clippers, per Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com. Luke Kennard and Ryan Dunn are candidates for increased playing time in Goodwin's stead.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Monday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Goodwin could miss a fourth straight game due to a right calf injury. Collin Gillespie and Luke Kennard are likely to retain expanded roles if Goodwin is unable to play.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Goodwin will miss his third consecutive contest due to a left calf injury. Collin Gillespie and Luke Kennard should remain heavily involved off the bench for the Suns.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is doubtful for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Goodwin is on track to miss his third straight game, which should lead to more minutes for Luke Kennard. Check back for official confirmation on Goodwin's status closer to Saturday's tipoff.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is out for Thursday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Goodwin will miss his second game in a row for the Suns. In his absence Wednesday, Ryan Dunn and Luke Kennard saw minutes in the teens off the Phoenix bench.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) won't play in Wednesday's game against Portland.
items.story: Goodwin suffered a calf injury in Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors. His next chance to suit up will come Thursday versus Orlando. In the meantime, Luke Kennard should be on the floor more than usual.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Portland, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin sustained a left calf injury in Monday's 116-113 loss to Golden State, ending his night after just 10 minutes. If Goodwin is sidelined Wednesday, Luke Kennard should see more action.

items.headline: Goodwin won't return to Monday's game against the Warriors due to a left calf injury, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports. He recorded four points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 10 minutes before exiting.
items.story: Rasheer Fleming and Ryan Dunn could see more opportunities in the second half with Goodwin shut down for the evening. The severity of his injury is unclear at this time.

items.headline: Goodwin ended with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four assists, three steals and two rebounds in 20 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 win over Golden State.
items.story: Goodwin logged 20-plus minutes for a second straight game and tied for the game-high mark in steals. He struggled from three-point range but didn't miss a shot from inside the arc. The versatile 28-year-old will likely continue playing a steady role off Phoenix's bench moving forward.

items.headline: Goodwin recorded five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt) while adding six steals, three rebounds and two assists in 16 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The journeyman guard has been a terror on the defensive end during the exhibition schedule, snagging nine steals in two games so far. Goodwin is coming off a career-best season in 2025-26, producing 8.7 points, 4.9 boards, 2.1 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.5 steals in 22.5 minutes over 70 regular-season games for the Suns, and he should be a key part of the second unit once again in 2026-27.

items.headline: Goodwin recorded seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, three steals and one assist in 11 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Goodwin made an immediate impact off the bench, grabbing three offensive rebounds and creating havoc defensively. His rebounding and defensive versatility should help him compete for a regular spot in Phoenix's rotation.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) agreed to a three-year, $19 million deal with the Suns on Sunday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Goodwin was claimed off waivers by Phoenix last July and made the regular-season roster before delivering a career-best year. Across 70 regular-season appearances (10 starts), the 27-year-old guard averaged 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals while shooting 37.0 percent from deep in 22.5 minutes per game. Goodwin missed the team's final three postseason games against Oklahoma City due to a left calf strain, though he'll likely be good to go by the time training camp rolls around. He receives added security with this new contract, which includes a player option for the third year.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) won't play in Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Monday.
items.story: Goodwin will miss his third game of this first-round series while tending to a left calf strain. His next opportunity to take the floor would arrive Wednesday if the Suns are able to extend the series with a win Monday.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is a game-time decision for Monday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Goodwin is on the brink of a return from a left calf injury, but he'll need to prove his health during warmups before receiving the green light from Phoenix's training staff. Expect another update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Monday, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin has missed the Suns' last two games due to a left calf injury that he sustained in Game 1 on April 19. Collin Gillespie would likely remain in the Suns' starting lineup Monday if Goodwin is not cleared to return.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Goodwin will now miss a second consecutive contest, so his next chance to suit up will be Monday for Game 4. With Goodwin ruled out, Collin Gillespie is expected to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) will go through pregame warmups before Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Goodwin remains questionable for Game 3. However, head coach Jordan Ott stated that the 27-year-old will go through warmups before a decision is made regarding his availability. He suffered an ankle injury during the 119-84 loss to the Thunder to begin the series and was ruled out for Game 2. If Goodwin can't suit up, Collin Gillespie is the favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as questionable for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin is in danger of missing a second straight game due to left calf soreness. However, he was a full participant in Friday's practice, which bodes well for his chances of suiting up. If the 27-year-old isn't cleared to play, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Collin Gillespie would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice, per Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic.
items.story: Goodwin missed Game 2 on Wednesday versus the Thunder with left calf soreness, which cropped up during Sunday's Game 1 loss in Oklahoma City. Phoenix's official injury report should shed more light on the swingman's chances of playing in Game 3, but Goodwin appears to be progressing well.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Game 2 against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin exited Sunday's Game 1 loss after logging just five minutes and did not return due to left calf soreness. He will now miss Wednesday's contest with the same issue, and his next chance to play will come in Game 3 on Saturday. With the 27-year-old out, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Collin Gillespie are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as questionable for Game 2 against the Thunder on Wednesday.
items.story: Goodwin exited Sunday's Game 1 loss to the Thunder due to left calf soreness and is in danger of missing Game 2. If the 27-year-old is ultimately ruled out, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Haywood Highsmith would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin has been ruled out for the rest of Game 1 of the Western Conference first-round playoff series against the Thunder on Sunday due to left calf soreness, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin tweaked his left calf in the second quarter, and medical staff determined that the injury was severe enough for the fifth-year forward to not return to Sunday's game. He'll finish with two points (1-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt) over five minutes. Royce O'Neale started in place of Goodwin to open the second half.

items.headline: Goodwin (undisclosed) went to the locker room during the second quarter of Game 1 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Sunday, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: It's not exactly clear what caused Goodwin to exit Sunday's game, but the team should have an update once he is evaluated by medical staff. Grayson Allen and Haywood Highsmith should see more minutes for as long as Goodwin is out of the game.

items.headline: Goodwin posted 19 points (7-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and six steals in 34 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Goodwin played a significant role on both ends of the floor to help vault the Suns into the playoffs, where the Thunder awaits. Although Grayson Allen (hamstring) was cleared to play, the coaching staff opted to keep him on ice, allowing Goodwin to remain in the starting lineup. He finished the night just one rebound short of a double-double while also recording a season-high six steals.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) has been cleared to play in Tuesday's Play-In Game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Goodwin should be fresh for Tuesday's Play-In Game after sitting out the final two games of the regular season while tending to an ankle issue. He averaged 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals over 70 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) won't play in Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Goodwin started in three consecutive games before missing Friday's 101-73 loss to the Lakers. With Goodwin ruled out, Rasheer Fleming and Jamaree Bouyea should be in line for more work.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin is in danger of missing a second consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain. Jalen Green (knee) and Collin Gillespie (shoulder) are also questionable, while Devin Booker (ankle) and Grayson Allen (hamstring) have already been ruled out, so the Suns could be very thin in the backcourt.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Goodwin exited Wednesday's win over the Mavericks early and will now miss Friday's contest due to a sprained left ankle. His next chance to play will come in Sunday's regular-season finale in Oklahoma City. With Goodwin out, Grayson Allen, Ryan Dunn and Collin Gillespie are candidates for increased playing time.

items.story: With Goodwin out for the remainder of the contest, Rasheer Fleming and Ryan Dunn will likely help pick up the slack. The severity of the ankle injury is unclear, but for now, Goodwin can be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.

items.story: Goodwin logged 13 minutes before exiting to the locker room with 4:53 remaining in the second quarter. He didn't start the second half and can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Goodwin supplied 12 points (5-5 FG, 2-2 3Pt), seven rebounds and one assist across 24 minutes during Sunday's 120-110 win over Chicago.
items.story: Goodwin supplanted Collin Gillespie in the first unit, but each player saw 24 minutes and put up respectable fantasy lines. Goodwin is trending up over his last six games with averages of 8.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.8 three-pointers.

items.headline: Goodwin will start Sunday's game against the Bulls, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin will surprisingly take Collin Gillespie's spot in the starting lineup Sunday. It's unclear if this will stick moving forward, but as a starter this season, Goodwin has averaged 9.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.7 steals in 29.1 minutes a night.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is available for Sunday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: After leaving Thursday's game against the Hornets early, Goodwin is not even listed on the injury report. Over his last six games, he's averaging 8.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.3 steals.

items.headline: Goodwin exited Thursday's 127-107 loss to the Hornets in the third quarter and did not return, and head coach Jordan Ott said postgame that he's dealing with a left calf injury, per Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic. Goodwin finished with three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound and one block across 12 minutes.
items.story: Goodwin limped to the locker room late in the third quarter after diving for a loose ball and colliding with Ryan Kalkbrenner. The severity of the issue is unknown, so Goodwin can be considered questionable for Sunday's game in Chicago for the time being.

items.headline: Goodwin (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Thursday's game against the Hornets, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Goodwin collided with Ryan Kalkbrenner while the pair dove for a loose ball. It's unclear exactly why Goodwin limped to the locker room, though he can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Goodwin (hip) isn't listed on the injury report for Thursday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Goodwin was sent for further evaluation after appearing to suffer a hip injury in Tuesday's loss to the Magic, though he's set to play Thursday. The 27-year-old guard has come off the bench in four straight games, during which he has averaged 8.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 3.0 steals across 26.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Goodwin will be sent for further testing after suffering a hip or groin injury during Tuesday's 115-111 loss to the Magic, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports. He ended the game with nine points (2-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three steals in 29 minutes.
items.story: It's not clear when Goodwin suffered the injury, but head coach Jordan Ott noted after the matchup that the guard is being sent for further evaluation. He can be considered day-to-day until the  team has more to share on the severity of the issue.

items.headline: Goodwin notched nine points (3-9 FG, 3-8 3Pt), four rebounds, eight assists, one block and five steals across 28 minutes during Monday's 131-105 victory over Memphis.
items.story: This was a strong showing for Goodwin despite some mediocre shooting, as his playmaking and defensive activity were on full display. His role could take a hit Tuesday against Orlando, however, as Grayson Allen will be back from a maintenance day and Dillon Brooks (hand) is cleared to return from an 18-game absence.

items.headline: Goodwin isn't in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Royce O'Neale is returning from a knee injury Tuesday, which means Goodwin will shift back to a bench role. He hasn't been nearly as effective as a reserve, as he's averaging 5.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.0 steals in his last five outings off the bench, compared to 10.0 points and 7.3 rebounds per game in his previous three appearances with the first unit.

items.headline: Goodwin recorded 14 points (5-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 25 minutes during Sunday's 120-98 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Goodwin has now drawn three consecutive starts for the Suns amid the absence of Royce O'Neale (knee), and the former should continue to do so until O'Neale is healthy. Over his last five appearances, Goodwin has averaged 7.8 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 steals in 26.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Goodwin will start Thursday's game against the Spurs, Shane Young of the Suns' official site reports.
items.story: With Royce O'Neale (knee) unavailable, Goodwin will join Devin Booker, Collin Gillespie, Jalen Green and Oso Ighodaro in the starting five. As a starter this season (four games), Goodwin has averaged 9.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals in 29.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is available for Friday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Goodwin will shake off his questionable tag and suit up for a third straight outing following a seven-game absence due to a left calf strain. The 27-year-old guard has averaged 6.0 points and 2.5 rebounds across 16.0 minutes per contest in his last two appearances.

items.headline: Bitadze totaled zero points (0-1 FG) and one rebound across five minutes during Sunday's 108-97 loss to Boston.
items.story: Bitadze was largely absent from Orlando's rotation, receiving just five minutes and attempting one shot. With his playing time severely restricted, the veteran center offers little fantasy utility outside of situations where injuries create additional opportunities.

items.headline: Bitadze closed Wednesday's 132-125 loss to the Hawks with six points (1-3 FG, 4-5 FT), six rebounds and one assist in 12 minutes.
items.story: Bitadze made the most of his limited playing time, collecting three offensive rebounds and converting four free throws. However, Wendell Carter handled the starting center duties, and Nikola Vucevic also saw action, leaving Bitadze with an uncertain path to consistent minutes.

items.headline: Bitadze finished with seven points (3-4 FG, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one block in 13 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason victory over Memphis.
items.story: Bitadze was efficient around the basket but saw limited playing time behind Orlando's other frontcourt options. With Nikola Vucevic also competing for minutes, Bitadze could face challenges securing a consistent rotation role.

items.headline: Bitadze recorded 23 points (8-18 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks in 30 minutes during Georgia's 101-74 win over Montenegro in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 27-year-old averaged 5.9 points and 5.0 rebounds while shooting 67.6 percent from the field during the 2025-26 regular season, but his path to playing time has become even more crowded following the Magic's offseason addition of Nikola Vucevic. With Vucevic and Wendell Carter both in the mix at center, Bitadze may struggle to see enough minutes to provide consistent fantasy value in 2026-27.

items.headline: Bitadze averaged 5.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 15.2 minutes per game over 64 regular-season appearances during 2025-26.
items.story: Although Bitadze played the backup center role behind Wendell Carter for much of the year, he wasn't part of Orlando's Game 7 rotation versus the Pistons. Moritz Wagner, who served as the No. 2 big man Sunday, is an impending free agent this summer, so Bitadze could end up reprising a similar role in 2026-27.

items.headline: Bitadze finished Friday's 127-103 win over Chicago with 15 points (6-7 FG, 3-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 17 minutes.
items.story: Bitadze recorded his second straight double-double, taking advantage of a shorthanded opponent. Although it has been a nice stretch for Bitadze, there is no reason to suspect his role is likely to change moving forward. He should continue to serve as the primary backup behind Wendell Carter, typically playing no more than about 15 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bitadze registered 14 points (6-11 FG, 2-2 FT), 15 rebounds, six assists and one steal across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 132-120 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Bitadze took advantage of the fact that the Timberwolves were without Julius Randle (hand) and Rudy Gobert (rest) to dominate the paint, and he delivered a strong double-double coming off the bench. Wendell Carter will remain the starter for the Magic, but Bitadze has proven he can deliver solid numbers when needed. He's averaging 10.5 points, 7.9 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game in the 10 outings in which he's logged at least 20 minutes this season.

items.headline: Bitadze posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal in 24 minutes during Monday's 123-107 victory over the Pistons.
items.story: Bitadze logged at least 20 minutes for the first time in his past 17 appearances, shifting up in the rotation after Wendell Carter was forced from the game due to a neck injury. While it has been a disappointing season for Bitadze, the final week of action could end up being his best stretch, should Carter be forced to miss additional time. Assuming that is the case, managers should view Bitadze as a strong stream candidate.

items.headline: Bitadze was ejected after being assessed a Flagrant 2 foul in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's game against the Hawks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. He'll finish with four points (2-3 FG), five rebounds, two blocks and one assist across 15 minutes.
items.story: The big man committed a hard foul on Jock Landale (ankle) with 7:30 remaining in the final quarter and was sent to the locker room early. Bitadze recorded multiple blocks for the first time since Jan. 18 before being ejected.

items.headline: Bitadze will come off the bench for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Bitadze started in place of Wendell Carter on Thursday, but now that Carter is healthy, Bitadze will retreat to a reserve role. Bitadze has played eight or fewer minutes in each of his last five games as a reserve.

items.headline: Bitadze is in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Bitadze is filling in for the injured Wendell Carter (rib) on Thursday. It'll be the third start of the season for Bitadze, who has averaged 11.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 blocks in 26.8 minutes per game with the first unit.

items.headline: Bitadze closed Monday's 124-112 loss to Atlanta with four points (2-3 FG), three rebounds and one assist over five minutes.
items.story: Bitadze continues to serve as the third-string center, having seen the court only six times in the past 12 games. During that time, he has averaged just 4.8 points and 3.7 rebounds, making him a non-factor in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Bitadze (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Magic's 128-122 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Bitadze had seen action in each of the Magic's previous four games, but his most recent two appearances had come in garbage time at the end of blowouts. With Wednesday's contest remaining competitive throughout, Bitadze failed to get off the bench while Moritz Wagner handled all the backup center minutes behind starter Wendell Carter. So long as Carter and Wagner are available, Bitadze is unlikely to be featured in the rotation.

items.headline: Bitadze will come off the bench Thursday against the Mavericks.
items.story: Bitadze drew a spot start Tuesday with Wendell Carter sidelined, but Carter has been given the green light to take the court Thursday. Bitadze has struggled to remain in the rotation over the last few months, but he could see playing time Thursday given that Jonathan Isaac (knee) is out.

items.headline: Bitadze is starting Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Bitadze will make his return to the rotation Tuesday after falling out of favor down the stretch of February. He figures to share time at center with Moritz Wagner after Wendell Carter was a late scratch due to ankle soreness. Bitadze has started one other game this year for Orlando, totaling 14 points, 13 rebounds, one assist, three steals and two blocks in 32 minutes Jan. 11 against New Orleans.

items.headline: Bitadze (coach's decision) didn't play in Monday's 114-98 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Before head coach Jamahl Mosley opted to remove Bitadze from the rotation entirely Monday, the seventh-year center's role already appeared to be trending down over the last handful of games once fellow center Moritz Wagner was cleared to make his season debut. Though Bitadze offers more rim protection than Wagner, the Magic may prefer the stronger offensive skill set Wagner brings to the table when starter Wendell Carter is off the court. Unless Carter ends up missing time at some point, Bitadze looks as though he may face an uphill battle to see enough minutes on a game-by-game basis to provide much of a meaningful fantasy impact.

items.headline: Bitadze is not in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Wendell Carter is returning from a one-game absence with a hip injury, forcing Bitadze to the second unit. Bitadze has averaged 5.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 16.2 minutes per contest over his last seven games off the bench.

items.headline: Bitadze ended Sunday's 128-118 win over the Pelicans with 14 points (7-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt), 13 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and three steals in 32 minutes.
items.story: With Wendell Carter (hip) ruled out, Bitadze made his first start of the season and played a season high in minutes, and he responded with his first double-double. The 26-year-old center hadn't played more than 20 minutes since Oct. 29 however, and unless Carter's injury proved to be more serious than expected, Bitadze will have a hard time following up this performance, especially with Moritz Wagner (knee) also back and looking for minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Bitadze will start against the Pelicans on Sunday.
items.story: The 26-year-old center will enter the starting five for the first time this season due to Wendell Carter (hip) being sidelined. Over five outings this month, Bitadze has averaged 5.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 15.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bitadze contributed two points (1-2 FG) and two rebounds over 16 minutes during Sunday's 135-127 win over Indiana.
items.story: This was a quiet outing for Bitadze, and that's been the case for a while now. Over his last four appearances, the center has seen 16.9 minutes per contest with averages of 5.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.0 blocks.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) is available for Monday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Bitadze is set to return following a three-game absence due to a left knee strain. The big man will operate as Wendell Carter's backup at center, whereas Jonathan Isaac's playing time will be reduced with the return of Bitadze.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Bitadze has already missed three games with a strained left knee, and his availability for Monday's game remains up in the air. While Bitadze has been sidelined, Jonathan Isaac has seen an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) is out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Bitadze will miss a third straight game while dealing with a strained left knee, meaning Jonathan Isaac will continue to see more minutes in the frontcourt. Bitadze's next chance to play will come against the Raptors on Monday.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.

If the big man remains sidelined, Jonathan Isaac will likely continue to see increased playing time. Over his last five appearances, Bitadze has averaged 4.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 1.2 steals across 15.8 minutes per game off the bench.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) will not play Friday against the Hornets.
items.story: Bitadze was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest and will miss his second straight game. For now, he can be considered questionable for the second leg of this back-to-back set Saturday against Denver.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Bitadze was unable to play against the Trail Blazers on Tuesday due to a left knee strain, but the seventh-year center has a chance to return Friday. Jonathan Isaac would likely see a slight downtick in minutes off the bench if Bitadze is given the green light to play.

items.headline: Bitadze (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Bitadze will sit for the second leg of the Magic's back-to-back set Tuesday due to a left knee strain, and his next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Hornets. Orlando Robinson and Jett Howard are in line for more minutes due to Bitadze, Franz Wagner (ankle) and Tristan da Silva (shoulder) all being sidelined.

items.headline: Bitadze is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers with a strained left knee.
items.story: Fantasy managers can expect the Magic to determine Bitadze's status closer to Tuesday's tipoff. Should the big man be unable to suit up, Orlando Robinson would have the backup center job all to himself.

items.headline: Bitadze ended with seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 17 minutes during Tuesday's 117-108 win over the Heat.
items.story: Bitadze extends his block streak to eight games, averaging 6.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.6 steals and 1.5 blocks across 17.4 minutes in that span. He has done a fine job backing up Wendell Carter and continues to be a great source of blocks and rebounds for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Bitadze accumulated eight points (4-4 FG), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 114-112 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Bitadze has been a big part of Orlando's defense, posting a steal and a block in each of his last five games and in seven of his last eight. Bitadze averages 6.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.7 steals and 1.3 blocks across 16.9 minutes this season, making him an elite blocks specialist with potential to contribute in the points and rebounds categories as well.

items.headline: Bitadze logged 10 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 144-103 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Bitadze returned to action after missing Sunday's loss to Boston due to a sore left ankle, falling one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season Tuesday. Firmly established as the backup behind Wendell Carter, Bitadze has provided Orlando with a serviceable rim protector off the bench. Through 18 games, he has averaged 6.4 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 16.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bitadze (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Bitadze was a late addition to the injury report due to left ankle soreness, though he'll shed his questionable tag and suit up after missing Sunday's loss to Boston. Over his last five appearances, the backup center has averaged 6.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks in 16.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bitadze (ankle) is now questionable for Tuesday's game against the 76ers.

Over his last 10 games, Barlow has averaged a modest 7.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.9 blocks in 23.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Barlow exited Saturday's contest early due to a left ankle sprain, and it initially looked unlikely he'd suit up Monday, though the forward has progressed well and has now been cleared to play. The 22-year-old was averaging 10.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals in 28.2 minutes over his previous five contests prior to Saturday's brief appearance. Barlow has started 53 of the 60 games he's played and hasn't come off the bench when healthy since January, so he figures to slot into the starting five as usual against the Thunder.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Barlow was previously listed as doubtful, but he's trending in the right direction. With so many injuries in Philadelphia, Barlow could see a sizable workload if he's given the green light to play.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Barlow exited Saturday's 126-116 win over Utah after only four minutes of work because of a sprained left ankle. If he can't suit up, Trendon Watford would be considered the favorite to start at power forward against one of the top defensive clubs in the Association.

items.headline: Barlow was diagnosed with a left ankle sprain and has been ruled out for the remainder of Saturday's game against the Jazz, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. He finished with one point (1-2 FT) and two rebounds in four minutes.
items.story: Barlow checked out of the game with 8:19 remaining in the first quarter to get his ankle evaluated and was quickly shut down for the rest of the night. The severity of the ankle sprain won't be known until he undergoes further testing, but Barlow would appear to be at risk of missing the 76ers' next game Monday versus the Thunder.

items.headline: Barlow finished with 11 points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals across 21 minutes during Sunday's 109-103 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: With Paul George still suspended until the March 25 matchup versus the Bulls, it looks like Barlow has a clear runway to a starting role for at least Philadelphia's next four games. Barlow has averaged 8.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 26.5 minutes per tilt in his last seven games, shooting 52.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Barlow racked up four points (2-5 FG), one rebound, two assists and one block over 26 minutes during Saturday's 125-116 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Barlow is holding down the fort at power forward for the suspended Paul George, but the former continues to see little usage in the starting lineup. Barlow has averaged 5.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 24.8 minutes per game over his last nine contests, so fantasy managers may be able to find more appealing streaming options.

items.headline: Barlow (undisclosed) has checked back in to Tuesday's game against the Spurs, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow went to the locker room during the first quarter after picking up an undisclosed injury, but he's since been cleared by the medical staff to return. He shouldn't face any limitations the rest of the way.

items.headline: Barlow exited to the locker room during the first quarter of Tuesday's game against the Spurs with an undisclosed injury, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow was spotted walking down the tunnel to the locker room after picking up his second foul. The nature of his injury is unclear at this time. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Barlow finished with 14 points (4-7 FG, 6-8 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and three steals over 28 minutes during Sunday's 114-98 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: As long as Paul George remains suspended, Barlow appears to be locked into the starting position at power forward. However, the fourth-year forward is averaging just 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks in 27.0 minutes per game over his last seven outings, so he's not seeing a lot of usage in the first unit.

items.headline: Barlow chipped in nine points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal across 31 minutes during Thursday's 124-117 win over the Heat.
items.story: This was another quiet showing for Barlow, but the minutes were at least encouraging -- he's been playing more while Paul George is serving his suspension. Over his last five games, Barlow is averaging 5.4 points and 3.2 rebounds in 26.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Barlow finished Thursday's 117-107 loss to the Hawks with one point (0-3 FG, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three blocks and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: Barlow had quite the dud Thursday, but Trendon Watford wasn't much better off the bench for the 76ers. With Joel Embiid (knee, shin) sidelined, it was Kelly Oubre, Andre Drummond and Adem Bona who stepped up the most for Philadelphia.

items.headline: Barlow produced 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 138-89 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With Paul George suspended until late March, Barlow has a clear runway to the starting job at power forward for the next month and a half or so. Barlow has delivered fairly quality numbers when part of the first unit, averaging 11.6 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 26.6 minutes per game while shooting 55.9 percent from the floor over his last eight contests as a starter.

items.headline: Wilson finished Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers with 24 points (9-17 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and four steals across 34 minutes.
items.story: Wilson turned in an efficient effort, particularly from three-point range, finishing as the Bulls' leading scorer. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also tied for the team lead in rebounds and paced all players in steals, supplying multiple swipes for the fourth time in seven regular-season games. The 20-year-old has been impressive on both ends of the floor to begin his NBA career, reaching the 20-point threshold five times while recording at least three combined steals-plus-blocks in all seven outings.

items.headline: Wilson finished Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics with 23 points (7-16 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 3-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal across 31 minutes.
items.story: Wilson impressed in his first NBA Cup game, leading the Bulls in scoring while reaching the 20-point threshold for the fourth time across six regular-season appearances. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also doubled his previous career high in three-pointers made after shooting 22.2 percent from deep in his previous five appearances. He made an impact on the defensive end as well, matching the game-high mark in blocks. Wilson has yet to record fewer than three combined steals-plus-blocks in a game this season.

items.headline: Wilson finished with 20 points (7-18 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block over 38 minutes in Wednesday's 133-127 loss to New York.
items.story: Wilson's solid inaugural campaign continued Wednesday, with the rookie reaching the 20-point mark for the third time in his young career. While the 20-year-old has certainly been a steady offensive contributor, he's also shined defensively and now has nine steals in his first five professional appearances.

items.headline: Wilson closed with 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal across 32 minutes in Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Wilson didn't deliver his most efficient performance, particularly from three-point range, though he still finished as the Bulls' second-leading scorer. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also had a productive outing on the defensive end, racking up at least three combined steals-plus-blocks for the fourth time in as many regular-season appearances thus far. He also has yet to score fewer than 16 points and has reached the 20-point mark twice on the campaign.

items.headline: Wilson tallied 30 points (10-24 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 9-11 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 38 minutes in Saturday's 124-120 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: After dropping 21 points in Friday's win over Milwaukee, Wilson erupted for a game-high 30 points in the second half of this back-to-back set, though he did struggle from beyond the arc. The rookie forward also tied for the game-high mark in rebounds. He's the first player since Terry Cummings in 1982-83 to record at least 30 points and 14 rebounds in one of his first three career games, per the broadcast.

items.headline: Wilson produced 21 points (7-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and three turnovers across 33 minutes in Friday's 132-125 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Wilson did a much better job of picking his spots offensively and limiting his turnovers in his second NBA game, while coming through with some game-saving plays on defense in the closing seconds of regulation. Additionally, after shooting just 33.3 percent from the free-throw line in Summer League, he's converted 75 percent of his freebies through the first two games of the regular season.

items.headline: Wilson recorded 16 points (7-21 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three steals and one block over 32 minutes in Wednesday's 135-92 season-opening loss to the Raptors.
items.story: While the counting stats were nice, the rookie did not score efficiently and also finished with a game-high nine turnovers. Poor shooting and turnover issues tend to come with rookies, but Wilson will need to do a better job of taking care of the rock in Friday's game in Milwaukee.

items.headline: Wilson finished with 16 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and two blocks across 23 minutes in Friday's 133-116 preseason victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Wilson had another strong showing Friday, leading the Bulls in points while picking up his fifth consecutive preseason double-digit scoring performance. The 2026 No. 4 overall pick will be thrust into a meaningful role immediately, so his name could be mentioned often in Rookie of the Year conversations throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Wilson posted 10 points (4-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 24 minutes in Wednesday's 125-104 preseason victory against the Bucks.
items.story: Wilson received another opportunity to work with Chicago's starting unit but struggled with his outside shot, missing four of five attempts from beyond the arc. The rookie forward also committed four turnovers, highlighting some growing pains despite his contributions across several categories. He'll look to build on his preseason experience as he adjusts to the NBA level.

items.headline: Wilson played 25 minutes in Sunday's 133-128 preseason loss to the Nuggets, scoring 17 points (6-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-7 FT) and adding five assists, four rebounds and a block.
items.story: The rookie led Chicago's starting five in minutes and points, although he also committed a game-high five turnovers. Through three exhibition contests, Wilson is averaging 28.7 minutes, 17.7 points, 3.7 boards, 2.3 assists and 2.0 threes while shooting 47.6 percent from the floor and 31.6 percent from beyond the arc, as he prepares for a significant role in the rotation to begin his NBA career.

items.headline: Wilson finished Friday's 104-100 preseason loss to the Grizzlies with 21 points (7-17 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 2-6 FT), four rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
items.story: Wilson struggled to get going in the first half, during which he scored one point while shooting 0-for-2 from the field in 16 minutes. However, he erupted for 20 points and shot 5-for-10 from downtown in the second half, finishing with a game-high 21 points. The rookie No. 4 overall pick has led the Bulls in scoring in both of their preseason games, totaling 36 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two steals over 61 minutes.

items.headline: Wilson scored a team-high 15 points (6-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT) while contributing three rebounds, two assists and a steal over 29 minutes in Wednesday's preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: The Bulls got balanced scoring up and down the lineup, as six different players delivered 13 or more points, but Wilson's 15 led the way. The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is set to be Chicago's starting power forward Opening Night, and while his willingness to chuck it up from long range is encouraging for his long-term fantasy outlook, it's likely to be a drag on his scoring efficiency as a rookie.

items.headline: Wilson is acclimating to NBA practices, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
items.story: "Honestly, my first two days, it seemed like everything was moving so fast because you're going against NBA talent and everybody's athletic, and the gaps close really fast. But now, it's way more chill. [Friday] was a really good day for me," Wilson said. After Wilson was selected by the Bulls with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, the rookie forward is expected to be thrust into a big role immediately and is being treated as a mid-round player in most fantasy drafts.

items.headline: George supplied 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds and seven assists over 26 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 loss to Dallas.
items.story: George provided balanced production despite playing fewer than 27 minutes, and while Utah's remarkable comeback was driven primarily by Svi Mykhailiuk's perimeter shooting, George still made his presence felt -- he was Utah's third-leading scorer and paced the team in assists. His role as a playmaker and scorer gives him a solid fantasy floor even in games in which his shooting volume isn't very high. His nine field-goal attempts Sunday were a season-low mark.

items.headline: George finished Friday's 111-101 loss to the Suns with 14 points (4-17 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes.
items.story: George came crashing back to earth after back-to-back 30-point games against the two Los Angeles teams. He went cold from deep, and his late turnover ended any hope of a comeback. Off nights like this will happen with Lauri Markkanen (hand) out and defenses keying in on George. He is still averaging 21.6 points and 7.1 assists as Utah's go-to floor general.

items.headline: George supplied 30 points (9-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 7-9 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: George was instrumental in Utah's second consecutive upset, scoring nine points in the fourth quarter to help end Los Angeles' nine-game winning streak. His five three-pointers also matched his highest total of the season, and the 10 assists were the fourth time he has dished out double-digit dimes. With the Jazz continuing to lean on their younger players, George has considerable freedom to generate offense. His ability to combine high-volume scoring with double-digit assists gives him a particularly appealing fantasy profile, even if his shooting efficiency remains somewhat inconsistent. He's averaging 21.6 points, 4.2 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game since the beginning of November.
