items.headline: George popped off for 30 points (10-17 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), 11 assists, two rebounds and two blocks over 35 minutes in Tuesday's 132-107 win over the Clippers.
items.story: George was limited to 13 points on 5-for-17 shooting his last time out, but he got things back on track Tuesday, notching his third 30-point performance of the season. He also matched his career high in swats and finished with a plus-10 differential in an impressive two-way performance. He'll look to keep it going Wednesday against the Lakers.

items.headline: George provided 13 points (5-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight assists and four rebounds over 34 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: George struggled with efficiency, especially from beyond the arc. However, he still finished as one of four Jazz players to score in double figures while pacing the team in assists. The 23-year-old has dished out at least seven dimes in six straight games, averaging 21.2 points, 8.0 assists, 4.7 rebounds and 1.2 steals across 35.2 minutes per game over that period.

items.headline: George finished Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets with 27 points (8-17 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven assists, six rebounds and one steal over 37 minutes.
items.story: George had a quiet first half with only four points while missing four of his five field-goal attempts. However, the fourth-year pro found his form in the second half, when he scored 10 and 13 points in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, to help the Jazz stay in the game. Utah's future was shining bright during Friday's loss, with George, 2025 fifth-overall pick Ace Bailey and rookie second overall selection Darryn Peterson each scoring 20-plus points. For the season, George is averaging 20.9 points, 6.5 assists, 4.6 rebounds, 2.0 threes and 0.9 steals over 32.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: George (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: George is back after a one-game absence. His return will likely push Josh Okogie back to the second unit, and Isaiah Collier's minutes will likely dip. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) set to miss at least the next month, George should be operating with a hefty usage rate moving forward.

items.headline: George (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: George has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. If the 23-year-old guard is cleared to play, fewer minutes would be available for the likes of Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk.

items.headline: George (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: George sustained a right ankle sprain in Sunday's loss to Minnesota and will be sidelined for the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Orlando, and the 23-year-old's absence should open up additional minutes for guys like Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk. Moreover, Darryn Peterson figures to take on additional on-ball duties.

items.headline: George will not return to Sunday's game against the Timberwolves due to a right ankle injury.
items.story: George suffered a right ankle injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and will not return. He concluded the contest with 19 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-10 FT), eight assists, five rebounds and two steals in 29 minutes. George should be considered doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Heat, given the amount of pain he was in after sustaining the injury.

items.headline: George (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: George was listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's contest due to an illness, but he will officially be able to suit up. Over his last five appearances, he holds averages of 20.2 points, 5.0 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 32.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: George (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: George presumably woke up under the weather before being a late addition to the injury report. If the star point guard is unable to suit up, Darryn Peterson could see additional on-ball duties. Additionally, Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: George tallied 16 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, nine assists and a block across 32 minutes in Friday's 112-100 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: George narrowly missed a double-double, providing strong playmaking production while contributing six rebounds. George's consistent playmaking supports his fantasy value, but his overall ceiling depends on improving efficiency and limiting mistakes -- he's had at least three turnovers in his last four games. Overall, George is averaging a solid 21.3 points, 4.2 rebounds and 6.2 assists per game this season while shooting 45.5 percent from the floor and 32.1 percent from deep.

items.headline: George registered 39 points (14-26 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 9-13 FT), two rebounds, nine assists, four steals and one block over 44 minutes in Wednesday's 120-113 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: George had been seriously struggling in his previous two outings, combining for 15 points on 5-for-22 shooting, but he busted out of his funk in a big way Wednesday. He nearly delivered a game-winning dagger for Utah, but his stepback jumper left his hand just a second too late, and the team wasn't able to hang on in overtime. The Jazz have opened the season 1-7.

items.headline: George produced seven points (3-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt) and seven rebounds over 22 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: George endured a frustrating performance, shooting just 25 percent from the field while failing to record an assist or defensive statistic. He also finished with a team-worst minus-30 rating as Utah dropped its fifth consecutive game. With rookie Darryn Peterson handling a significant share of the playmaking duties, George's offensive role and playing time warrant monitoring.

items.headline: George finished Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to San Antonio with 31 points (11-27 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 37 minutes.
items.story: George carried a substantial offensive workload, leading Utah in scoring while knocking down five three-pointers. Although he struggled with efficiency inside the arc and committed five turnovers, his willingness to shoulder significant scoring responsibilities remains promising for fantasy managers. His combination of scoring volume and perimeter shooting gives him considerable upside.

items.headline: George totaled 24 points (7-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-10 FT), nine rebounds, 10 assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: George fell just one rebound shy of nabbing his first career triple-double, and he's now dished out 10 assists in back-to-back games. However, he's also committed 12 turnovers over that two-game stretch.

items.headline: George accumulated 19 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Friday's 120-119 win over New Orleans.
items.story: The points and dimes were nice, but George also committed a game-high six turnovers and missed two of his free-throw attempts. Through the first two games of the season, George is shooting 61.5 percent at the charity stripe, but that number will assuredly improve for the 85.4 percent career free-throw shooter.

items.headline: George tallied 22 points (7-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 4-7 FT), five assists, three rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: George delivered an efficient shooting performance from beyond the arc, though it wasn't enough to help the Jazz secure a win in their regular-season opener. The 22-year-old point guard also led Utah in assists, finishing as the only Utah player to dish out more than three dimes. George is coming off a career year in 2025-26, and he should remain one of the team's top offensive options despite the addition of Darryn Peterson.

items.headline: George closed with 13 points (5-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three steals, two rebounds and one assist across 16 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: George fared well in his limited action, finishing as one of seven Jazz players to score in double figures. After failing to record a steal in his first two preseason appearances, the 22-year-old made his presence felt defensively with three swipes Monday. George will look to take another step forward during the 2026-27 campaign after breaking out with averages of 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals across 54 games last season.

items.headline: George produced 15 points (5-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three assists over 21 minutes in Sunday's 109-97 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: George briefly exited the game after taking a blow to the face, but he returned a short while later and didn't seem any worse for the wear. George will look to take another step forward in Year 4 after breaking out with averages of 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 2.5 triples and 1.1 steals per game last season.

items.headline: George and the Jazz agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: The writing was on the wall for this move a long time ago, as there was a lot of mutual interest to get this done quickly. George averaged 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 33.1 minutes per contest during the 2025-26 regular season, and moving forward he'll get to play alongside No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson in a new-look backcourt.

items.headline: The Jazz selected Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, adding another high-level creator to their backcourt that already includes George (hamstring).
items.story: George remains an important piece of Utah's rebuilding effort, but Peterson's arrival could reduce his on-ball responsibilities after he served as one of the team's primary playmakers last season. The additional talent should improve the quality of George's opportunities, though his fantasy value may become more dependent on efficiency than volume. The Jazz are also projected to be much more competitive in 2026-27, bolstering their late-season outlook.

items.headline: White finished Friday's 111-97 loss to Atlanta with 11 points (5-17 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block over 26 minutes.
items.story: It was a tough shooting night for White, who failed to connect on any of his five attempts from beyond the arc. His volume from the field was enough for him to extend his double-digit points streak to five games, and his nine dimes tied a season high that he set against the Cavaliers in Nov. 9. Over his last five outings, White has averaged 16.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.2 threes and 0.8 steals over 22.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: White closed with 19 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, four assists and three steals in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
items.story: White has found his groove since returning from a calf injury that cost him the start of the season, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games. His fadeaway jumper in the final minute of regulation put Charlotte in front, but a missed free throw shortly after left the door open. His minutes are still being managed, but the guard who signed a three-year, $74 million deal this summer is clearly rounding into form.

items.headline: White ended with 21 points (7-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT) and one assist over 20 minutes during Sunday's 113-105 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: White led the Hornets in scoring while logging just 20 minutes, and he's scored 21 points in back-to-back games. The veteran guard remains on a heavy minutes restriction and will likely continue playing limited minutes as he slowly works toward a full workload. Through six regular-season appearances, he's averaging 11.7 points, 3.2 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 18.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: White registered 21 points (8-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 20 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: The Hornets are continuing to ease White back into the mix after he missed the first seven matchups of the season with a calf injury. He's logged 20 minutes in back-to-back appearances, and he managed to lead Charlotte in scoring Thursday despite playing on a restriction. White's 21-point night also marks his best showing of the 2026-27 season to this point, though it wasn't enough to carry his team to a win.

items.headline: White notched 10 points (3-12 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds and nine assists over 20 minutes during Monday's 124-112 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: White's shot was off, but he made an impact as a facilitator with nine assists in just 20 minutes during his second game back from a calf injury. He's still ramping up his workload, which caps his short-term upside. With Charlotte's backcourt this thin, he should be a key piece once he's at full strength.

items.headline: White supplied four points (2-9 FG, 0-5 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and one block over 18 minutes during Wednesday's 114-104 loss to the Nets.
items.story: White delivered another underwhelming performance as he continues to work his way back from a calf injury. In two games since getting back on the floor, he has averaged just 5.5 points and 2.5 assists in 17.0 minutes. His upside is high enough that he should be rostered in all leagues, although it appears as though it is going to be a slow ramp-up.

items.headline: White (eye) returned to Wednesday's game against the Nets, per the television broadcast.
items.story: White was injured midway through the second quarter after appearing to have been poked in the eye. After heading to the locker room to get checked out, he received the green light to return.

items.headline: White (undisclosed) exited Wednesday's game against the Nets, Owen O'Connor of SI.com reports.
items.story: While an official injury designation hasn't been released, it appears White was poked in the eye halfway through the second quarter. He immediately asked to be removed from the contest and made his way to the locker room, so he should be considered questionable to return. Without White, Dennis Schroder will be on the court more than initially anticipated.

items.headline: White (calf) is available for Wednesday's game in Brooklyn.
items.story: White was initially listed as probable due to left calf injury management, but he'll be available for the matchup. The veteran guard should handle his usual offensive responsibilities in Charlotte's backcourt, barring any restrictions related to his calf.

items.headline: White (calf) is probable for Wednesday's game in Brooklyn.
items.story: White came out of his regular-season debut unscathed and should be available for Wednesday's game. White saw 16 minutes of action in Monday's 124-91 loss to the Pistons, but he should be cleared for more playing time in his second game of the season.

items.headline: White finished Monday's 124-91 loss to Detroit with seven points (3-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt) and three assists in 16 minutes.
items.story: White made his season debut, returning from a calf injury suffered during the preseason. While it certainly wasn't his best performance, the simple fact that he was back on the floor should be seen as a huge positive. There is going to be a ramp-up period, which does limit his short-term upside. However, he is a clear must-roster player, given the fact that Charlotte will need him to play a major role following the offseason departure of LaMelo Ball.

items.headline: White will start Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: White is ready to make his season debut after battling a calf strain, and he will step into the starting five immediately. However, the 26-year-old guard is expected to operate under a minutes restriction. With White back in action, Dennis Schroder will come off the bench.

items.headline: White will come off the bench and have his minutes monitored during Monday's game against Detroit, Owen O'Connor of SI.com reports.
items.story: White has been cleared to make his season debut after missing time with a calf injury, but the Hornets will take a cautious approach as he gets back up to speed. Expect Dennis Schroder to remain in the starting five Monday as a result.

items.headline: White (calf) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: White has yet to play this season. While the former Bull will be back on the floor Monday versus Detroit, he could see limited action for at least a game or two. As a result, Dennis Schroder and Sion James could continue to see steady minutes.

items.headline: Head coach Charles Lee said Monday that White (calf) remains without a timeline for a return, though Lee added that he'll have a better idea of where things stand following the Hornets' two-game road trip, Rod Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: White's next opportunity to play will come Saturday at home against the Sixers in the second leg of a back-to-back set. However, he should be considered highly questionable for that contest until the Hornets offer an update on his status. Dennis Schroder and Christian Anderson will likely continue seeing increased burn until White returns.

items.headline: White (calf) is out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: White has yet to play this season due to a left calf strain, and his next chance to suit up will come against the Pistons on Wednesday. Dennis Schroder should continue to handle an expanded role with White sidelined.

items.headline: White (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: White will miss a third straight game due to a left calf strain, though he's been ramping up in practice. His next chance to suit up will come Monday against the Wizards.

items.headline: White (calf) is out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: White can be viewed as day-to-day while on the mend from a calf strain. He'll miss a second straight regular-season game Friday, but the combo guard has been ramping up and taking more contact at recent practices. Until White is cleared for game action, Dennis Schroder should continue to start at point guard for the Hornets and make a viable streaming choice.

items.headline: White (calf) is out for Wednesday's season opener against the Nets.
items.story: White is doing individual work at practice and isn't yet ready to return to game action with a calf strain. Until he's cleared to retake the court, Dennis Schroder figures to start at point guard for the Hornets and offer streaming appeal in most fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Head coach Charles Lee said Sunday that White (calf) is without a definitive timetable for a return, though he's been ramping up and taking more contact in practice, Nick Carboni of WCNC Charlotte reports.
items.story: Lee wouldn't confirm whether White will miss Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Nets, so he can be considered highly questionable for that contest until further notice. If the 26-year-old guard needs to miss time to begin the regular season, Dennis Schroder and Christian Anderson would likely see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: The Hornets announced Monday that White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will not play during the preseason.
items.story: White missed time with a left calf strain last season and is now in jeopardy of starting the regular season on the inactive list. If the 26-year-old guard is forced to miss time beyond the preseason, Christian Anderson and Dennis Schroder would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: White said Monday that he wanted to return to the Hornets to take on the challenge of a new role, and he's "excited" for the road ahead, Owen O'Connor of SI.com reports.
items.story: After trading away LaMelo Ball, the Hornets signed White to a three-year, $74 million deal this offseason. The veteran guard was traded from Chicago to Charlotte last February and provided a spark off the bench for the Hornets in 2025-26, though he's now expected to step into a starting role. In 21 regular-season games with Charlotte last season, he averaged 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists across 19.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: White will sign a three-year, $74 million contract with the Hornets, Shams Charania of ESPN reports on Thursday.
items.story: The Hornets will quickly lock up White after trading away starting point guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota earlier in the day. White becomes the starter by default in Charlotte and is likely to see a big uptick in fantasy appeal. In 21 regular-season appearances for Charlotte in 2025-26, White averaged 17.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 25.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Retaining White will be a priority for the Hornets this offseason, Bobby Marks of ESPN reports.
items.story: White will be free to test the open market in the offseason, although Charlotte will look re-sign him. After trading for White ahead of the deadline, Charlotte inherited his Bird rights, enabling the team to exceed the salary cap to retain him. Considering the club will be operating well below the luxury tax while possessing three trade exceptions valued at a combined $17.5 million, Marks added that the franchise is in a "strong position" to keep the former Bull on the roster. White appeared in 21 regular-season contests for the Hornets after being acquired from Chicago -- all off the bench -- averaging 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists while shooting 39.1 percent from deep in those appearances. It's unknown what his role would be if he remained with the organization. However, his biggest issue in the last few seasons has been his inability to stay healthy.

items.headline: White finished Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to Orlando with four points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) over 17 minutes.
items.story: White had easily his worst game as a Hornet, contributing to what ended up being a blowout loss. Despite averaging 15.3 points, 2.9 assists and 2.1 three-pointers in 23 games after joining Charlotte, it's safe to say that White's overall fantasy appeal took a large hit following the trade. Looking ahead to next season, White could struggle to be more than a stream-level asset, assuming his role remains largely unchanged.

items.headline: White provided 19 points (7-15 FG, 5-8 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game victory over the Heat.
items.story: White closed the game Tuesday, playing over Kon Knueppel, who continues to struggle from the floor. While the production was certainly more than adequate, the highlight was a game-tying three-pointer that ultimately sent the game into overtime. Although he continues to come off the bench, White has proven himself to be a key contributor, providing the team with a viable scoring threat when others are having an off night.

items.headline: White (calf) is available for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: White will shake off his probable tag due to right calf soreness and suit up in Charlotte's regular-season finale. The 26-year-old guard has appeared in four games in April, during which he has averaged 14.5 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 17.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: White is probable for Sunday's game against the Knicks due to right calf soreness.
items.story: White is expected to push through the pain and make himself available for Sunday's game, and managers can expect to get official confirmation on his status closer to tipoff. Through 20 games with the Hornets, White has averaged 15.5 points, 3.1 assists and 2.0 triples per contest.

items.headline: White (groin) is available for Friday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: As expected, White has been upgraded from probable to available and will return to action after resting Tuesday. He's scored in double figures in 12 straight games, averaging 17.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists in 20.3 minutes a night over that stretch.

items.headline: White (groin) is probable for Friday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: White appears poised for a return after missing Tuesday's game against Boston due to a left groin issue. Expect confirmation on his availability closer to Friday's tipoff.

items.headline: White (groin) is out for Tuesday's game in Boston.
items.story: White is dealing with some tightness in his left groin, so he'll be held out of Tuesday's game. His absence will likely open up minutes for Tre Mann and Sion James.

items.headline: White (groin) is questionable for Tuesday's game against Boston.
items.story: It's unclear if White suffered a setback during Tuesday's morning shootaround, as he was initially deemed probable to play with left groin soreness. If the combo guard cannot suit up, Sion James and Josh Green should help pick up the slack in the backcourt.

items.headline: White (groin) is probable for Tuesday's game against Boston.
items.story: White is nursing left groin soreness, but the issue isn't expected to stop him from playing Tuesday. The combo guard has scored in double figures in 12 consecutive appearances, during which White has averaged 17.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 20.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: White contributed 19 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 20 minutes during Thursday's 127-107 win over the Suns.
items.story: White continues to put up solid numbers off the bench for the Hornets, and this was his 10th consecutive game in which he scored in double digits. Over that 10-game stretch, White is averaging 18.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. White remains a valuable fantasy contributor in most formats due to his scoring prowess, and his involvement on offense is more important than how many minutes he plays.

items.headline: White supplied 16 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and five assists in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 win over the Nets.
items.story: Despite some inconsistent shooting, White continues to provide Charlotte with valuable production off the bench. He has scored in double digits in nine straight games while also chipping in across other categories, most notably assists and threes. While he isn't a must-roster player, he certainly isn't out of place on a standard-league roster.

items.headline: White logged 17 points (6-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 23 minutes during the Hornets' 114-103 win over the Knicks on Thursday.
items.story: White helped the Hornets establish a double-digit lead going into halftime by scoring 12 of his 17 points through the first two quarters of Thursday's game. The veteran guard has been a key contributor off the bench for Charlotte and has scored at least 17 points in five of his last six outings. Over that six-game span, White has averaged 20.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 3.0 threes over 21.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: White collected 27 points (9-12 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and one assist in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 134-90 victory over the Kings.
items.story: White scored 16 of his 27 points in the first half, which included four treys. He provided an undeniable spark off the bench on the way to a blowout win, leading the Hornets in scoring despite being held under 20 minutes. The 26-year-old is averaging 21.6 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 3.4 made triples per game over his last five appearances.

items.headline: George provided 24 points (9-17 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one block over 36 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 victory over the Magic.
items.story: George has averaged 16.8 points, 4.0 assists and 35.8 minutes over his last five games. His six triples Sunday highlighted his scoring upside, while consistent playing time and defensive contributions support his fantasy floor despite occasional shooting struggles.

items.headline: George posted 11 points (5-17 FG, 1-8 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal across 35 minutes during Friday's 98-94 victory over Chicago.
items.story: George endured a difficult shooting performance, connecting on just one of eight attempts from beyond the arc, but his contributions elsewhere helped salvage his fantasy line. The third-year forward has now scored in double digits in each of his 11 appearances this month while also putting up solid numbers in other categories. George is averaging 18.6 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game over that span while shooting an impressive 45.1 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: George contributed 20 points (7-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 40 minutes during Wednesday's 103-99 win over the Raptors.
items.story: George reached the 20-point mark for the first time in his last four appearances and extended his streak of games with double-digit points to 11 contests. His four three-pointers were particularly important, including one during Washington's decisive 11-0 fourth-quarter run, and he's drained multiple threes in all but one of those 11 double-digit-scoring games. With 18.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 4.4 assists and a combined 1.8 steals-plus-blocks per game over that 11-game stretch, George has been a productive piece in the Wizards' backcourt. His contributions in three-pointers, assists and defensive categories give him several ways to remain productive even when his scoring fluctuates.

items.headline: George ended with 25 points (9-20 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and three assists over 39 minutes in Wednesday's 114-101 loss to Indiana.
items.story: George had another quality game Wednesday, leading his team in scoring. However, despite his efforts, Washington couldn't pull off the win, with the Wizards now having lost five straight games. The 22-year-old is averaging 18.5 points, 4.8 assists and 1.3 blocks, all career highs, along with 4.8 rebounds over 33.7 minutes per contest in 12 regular-season appearances. Turnovers have been an issue at times, though he's made up for it by shooting 39.7 percent from behind the arc.

items.headline: George finished with 14 points (5-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and three blocks across 30 minutes in Saturday's 114-75 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: George cooled off Saturday after scoring 33 points in Friday's 139-132 loss to Atlanta. Despite his inefficient shooting night, the 22-year-old shined defensively and has now combined for five blocks in the Wizards' last two games. Overall, George has played well throughout the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 18.5 points, 5.2 assists and 1.4 blocks, all career highs, along with 4.5 rebounds over 33.0 minutes per contest in 10 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: George tallied 33 points (10-19 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 8-10 FT), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal and two blocks over 39 minutes in Friday's 139-132 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: This was George's third consecutive 20-plus-point performance and his fourth straight game with three-plus triples, both career-long streaks. He scored 18 of his 33 points in the final frame while trying to deliver the win for Washington, but his club ultimately fell short in a tough loss to Atlanta. They'll look to avoid a three-game skid Saturday in Oklahoma City.

items.headline: George registered 25 points (10-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds and seven assists in 35 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: George was one of Washington's most effective offensive players, shooting 71.4 percent from the field while finishing one point shy of Anthony Davis for the team lead. The young forward also paced the Wizards with seven assists, though he committed four turnovers and failed to record a defensive statistic. His substantial playing time and expanding offensive responsibilities remain encouraging for his fantasy outlook.

items.headline: George ended Monday's 103-94 victory over the Magic with 22 points (9-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 0-1 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 37 minutes.
items.story: George delivered an efficient all-around performance, finishing second on Washington in scoring while leading the team with four three-pointers. His five assists and contributions in both defensive categories further enhanced his fantasy output. George's ability to produce alongside Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa is particularly encouraging, though the Wizards' crowded offensive hierarchy could lead to fluctuations in his scoring opportunities.

items.headline: The Wizards exercised the fourth-year team option on George on Sunday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Washington selected George 24th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft. Since then, the 22-year-old has appeared in 122 regular-season games, averaging 11.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks in 27.7 minutes per contest. Even with the Wizards' selection of AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick in 2026, George continues to start and remains a key piece of the organization's future.

items.headline: George racked up eight points (4-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, 11 assists and one block in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: George handed out a season-high 11 assists, making amends for what was a passive offensive night. Despite the debut of AJ Dybantsa, George logged a whopping 38 minutes, an encouraging sign for anyone rostering him. It appears as though Washington is fully invested in him moving forward, with foul issues seemingly his only stumbling block when it comes to playing time.

items.headline: George finished with 22 points (8-17 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 6-8 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and four blocks over 36 minutes in Saturday's 124-120 win over the Bulls.
items.story: After committing a career-high eight turnovers in Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors, George did a much better job of taking care of the rock Saturday, limiting his giveaways to three. He's gotten off to a solid start with averages of 17.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.7 blocks per game, although those numbers could dip once AJ Dybantsa (ankle) gets into the mix.

items.headline: George finished with 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: George couldn't take care of the basketball Friday, with the third-year pro responsible for eight of the Wizards' 20 turnovers. He also had a poor shooting night, although his work at the charity stripe was enough for him to finish in a tie with Bilal Coulibaly for the third-most points on Washington behind Trae Young (22) and Tre Johnson (20). George will have his off nights as the third option on the Wizards behind Young and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: George had 18 points (8-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: George was aggressive on offense, finishing second on the team in shot attempts behind Anthony Davis in the win. He also committed a team-high four turnovers, but overall, it was a solid debut for the third-year swingman. This was Washington's first season-opening win since 2022.

items.headline: George logged 14 points (5-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks over 27 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: George put together another efficient night, making five of his seven shots while chipping in on the defensive end. His preseason numbers make a strong case for a full-time starting role for him when the regular season begins.

items.headline: George produced 21 points (6-7 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), one rebound, four assists and three steals over 25 minutes in Monday's 131-119 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: George was dialed in, missing only one shot while he was out there, and he was one of the few Washington players to finish with a positive plus-minus rating. George showed some impressive flashes last season, but he may struggle to assert himself in the offense when working alongside Trae Young, Anthony Davis, AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.

items.headline: George registered 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists and a block across 22 minutes in Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: George contributed across multiple categories, finishing tied for second on the team in rebounds and leading Washington in assists. George also showed his well-known ability to stretch the floor, and he was one of four Wizards who drained multiple threes in this win. The third-year guard looks penciled in to open the 2026-27 regular season as the Wizards' starting shooting guard, and his combination of playmaking, rebounding and perimeter shooting makes him an intriguing fantasy contributor.

items.headline: George (elbow) finished with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 21 minutes for Canada in Friday's 110-84 World Cup Qualifiers win over Puerto Rico.
items.story: George missed the end of the 2025-26 regular season with a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, but he's since been deemed 100 percent. The Wizards are noticeably deeper heading into 2026-27, as Anthony Davis (finger) is expected to be healthy, and the team drafted AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

items.headline: George's (elbow) role becomes less certain after Washington added another high-upside wing prospect in AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: George displayed intriguing playmaking ability and positional versatility during his sophomore campaign. However, the Wizards now possess considerable depth on the wing, including fellow talented youngsters Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly. George is currently penciled into the starting lineup, but his offensive opportunities may fluctuate depending on lineup combinations. The Wizards also just re-signed Trae Young (quadriceps) and will be welcoming Anthony Davis (finger) to the mix.

items.headline: George (elbow) will miss the rest of the 2025-26 season, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports.
items.story: George has been sidelined since March 2 due to a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, and the Wizards had no incentive to rush him back to the court for the last couple of weeks. The forward appeared in 48 regular-season contests with averages of 14.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.1 three-pointers on 43.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: George (elbow) is out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: George has been sidelined since March 2 due to a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow. The team has yet to provide much of an update on his timeline for a return, and there doesn't seem to be much sense in rushing him back for the final few games of the regular season. George can be considered doubtful for Saturday's game in Miami until further notice.

items.headline: The Wizards said Wednesday that George (elbow) will be re-evaluated in one week, at which point an update for his rest-of-season status will be provided, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: George is dealing with a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, an issue that has kept him sidelined since March 3.  The Wizards are planning to take a conservative approach with George, so it wouldn't be surprising for next week's update to rule George out for the season. While George has been out, Will Riley and Jamir Watkins have taken on larger roles. The Wizards have six regular-season games after George's set re-evaluation date of April 1.

items.headline: The Wizards announced Wednesday that George has been diagnosed with a partial tear of the UCL in his left elbow and will be re-evaluated in three weeks.
items.story: George sustained the injury in Monday's loss to Houston and won't return until late March at the very earliest. With the Wizards sitting at 16-45 on the season, it wouldn't be surprising to see the club exercise extreme caution with the second-year wing for the remainder of the season. With George sidelined, Will Riley, Jamir Watkins (ankle) and Justin Champagnie are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: George (elbow) is out for Thursday's game against Utah.
items.story: A sprained left elbow is resulting in a second consecutive absence for George. Will Riley should draw his fifth career start at small forward Thursday, making him a worthwhile streaming option in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: George (elbow) is listed out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: George sprained his left elbow in the third quarter of Monday's loss to the Rockets and will need at least one game off to recover from the injury. With Jamir Watkins (ankle/foot) also sidelined for the second leg of the back-to-back, the Wizards are likely to lean on Will Riley, Tre Johnson, Jaden Hardy and Bilal Coulibaly as their primary options on the wing.

items.headline: George didn't return to Monday's 123-118 loss to the Rockets after exiting with 6:13 left in the third quarter due to a left elbow sprain. He finished with 16 points (5-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: George had been listed as questionable heading into Monday's contest due to a left knee contusion, but it was a new injury that knocked him out of the game early. The second-year wing was later spotted sitting on the bench following a trip to the locker room, but the Wizards didn't clear him to return to the contest. George can be considered questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic until the team provides another update.

items.headline: George is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left elbow sprain.
items.story: George was dealing with a knee injury leading up to tipoff, but he's now dealing with an elbow injury picked up at some point during Monday's clash. Will Riley would see more minutes down the stretch if George is unable to return.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is active for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Awaka was probable to suit up versus Philadelphia with a sprained left ankle, but he's going to play through it for the second straight contest. He'll provide center depth on the bench behind starter Jalen Smith (finger), although Awaka isn't expected to see much playing time.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Awaka played 12 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics after missing one game with the ankle issue. The rookie big man will continue to provide depth off the bench for the Bulls behind Jalen Smith.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is available for Friday's game in Boston.
items.story: The rookie big man is available off the bench for the Bulls on Friday. Awaka may not see significant playing time, though.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game in Boston.
items.story: Awaka continues to battle a left ankle sprain. The rookie big man could go through morning shootaround and pregame warmups before the Bulls update his status.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Awaka will hit the sidelines after tweaking his ankle during Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics. For now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting in Boston.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: The rookie big man is battling an ankle sprain. Zach Collins could pick up a few extra minutes off the bench if Awaka is out Wednesday.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) is available for Friday's game versus the Bucks.
items.story: The rookie big man is good to go for the front end of this back-to-back set. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) still sidelined, Awaka should share the backup center minutes with Zach Collins.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) is probable for Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Awaka is likely to be available off the bench for the first leg of this back-to-back set. The rookie big man played 14 minutes in Wednesday's blowout loss to Toronto, so it remains to be seen if he'll handle a similar workload in more competitive games.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) is available to play Wednesday against the Raptors.
items.story: Awaka was listed as probable, and now we have official confirmation that he'll be out there. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) out to begin the year, Awaka will have a chance to get into the rotation for Chicago.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Awaka remains day-to-day with his knee sprain. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) sidelined to open the season, Awaka could be in the mix at the edge of the rotation.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) is out for Friday's preseason finale versus Minnesota, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Awaka will miss Chicago's final two preseason games due to the knee injury, but for what it's worth, head coach Tiago Splitter said he's "close" to a return. The Bulls open their season Tuesday in Toronto, and for now, Awaka should be considered questionable for that game.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) was unavailable for Wednesday's 125-104 preseason win over Milwaukee, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Awaka missed practice Tuesday and was ultimately sidelined Wednesday while managing a knee injury he sustained Friday against Memphis. The rookie's next chance to suit up will come Friday against Minnesota.

items.headline: Awaka (knee) didn't practice Tuesday, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
items.story: Awaka banged his knee in Friday's preseason game against Memphis. The undrafted rookie can be deemed questionable for Wednesday's exhibition versus the Bucks.

items.headline: Awaka will come off the bench during Sunday's preseason game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Awaka will shift back to a reserve role due to Jalen Smith (foot) returning to the lineup. The Arizona product was held scoreless for 24 minutes during Friday's preseason game against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Awaka will start Friday's preseason game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Nic Claxton (hamstring), Zach Collins (toe) and Jalen Smith (foot) are all unavailable, opening the door for Awaka to enter the starting five. The 22-year-old was highly productive in Wednesday's preseason-opening win over the Suns, recording 14 points, 11 rebounds, a steal and a block in 21 minutes.

items.headline: Awaka produced 14 points (6-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-3 FT), 11 rebounds, one steal and one block over 21 minutes in Wednesday's 124-117 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: With Nic Claxton (hamstring) and Zach Collins (toe) already banged up, Awaka is an intriguing player to monitor this preseason. Though undersized, he's a superb rebounder, so he could earn minutes in the rotation if the Bulls' bigs aren't healthy to start the year.

items.headline: Awaka finished with 12 points (5-5 FG, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and one block over 19 minutes in Thursday's 105-82 Summer League loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Awaka had a double-double in Tuesday's 99-87 Summer League victory over Washington. He wasn't as productive Thursday, but he still managed to record his second consecutive double-digit scoring performance in Las Vegas. The 22-year-old is currently signed to a two-way deal with the Bulls. Although Awaka could see some action with the parent club during the 2026-27 campaign, he is expected to spend most of his time in the G League.

items.headline: Gill (back) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
items.story: Gill's availability is uncertain as Washington deals with multiple injuries in its frontcourt. Gill's status should become clearer closer to tipoff, though he remains a limited fantasy option even if cleared to play.

items.headline: Gill (back) is out for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Gill was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. His absence is not expected to make any waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Gill (back) is questionable to suit up in Monday's contest against Orlando.
items.story: Gill is dealing with back spasms that will leave his status questionable versus the Magic. He's played a total of just one minute in 2026-27, so even if he's sidelined Monday, it won't have any impact on the rotation.

items.headline: Gill agreed to a one-year deal with the Wizards on Tuesday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: Gill is set to play for the Wizards for a seventh straight season. The 33-year-old will offer the club frontcourt depth and a veteran presence in the locker room, but he isn't guaranteed a steady role. Over 55 regular-season appearances (eight starts) last season, he averaged 5.8 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists while shooting a career-best 62.8 percent from the field in 17.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Gill logged 14 points (6-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt), six rebounds and one steal over 30 minutes during Sunday's 130-117 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: After barely seeing the floor to open the season, Gill later became a key role player for the Wizards once the team started to dial back its regulars. Over his last 27 games of the campaign, Gill emerged as a deep-league fantasy asset with averages of 9.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 0.7 steals, 0.6 blocks and 0.5 three-pointers in 26.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gill (back/head) is available for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Gill was initially listed as questionable due to a back contusion and headache, but he has been given the green light to play in Sunday's regular-season finale. He has started in each of the Wizards' last five games, and over that span he has averaged 11.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists over 30.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gill (back) is questionable to face the Cavaliers on Sunday.
items.story: If Gill can't give it a go Sunday, Julian Reese would likely earn the start and log significant minutes as the only true center available. Check back for official word on Gill's status closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Gill (back) will play Friday against the Heat.
items.story: Gill will play through his injury for the second leg of this back-to-back set. On Thursday against the Bulls, he produced 14 points, three rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 39 minutes.

items.headline: Gill (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Heat.
items.story: A maintenance day is on the table for Gill after he played through his questionable tag Thursday. Gill produced 14 points, three rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 39 minutes against the Bulls on Thursday.

items.headline: Gill (neck/back) is available for Thursday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Gill will clear his questionable tag for this contest despite dealing with two injuries. He may be a candidate for maintenance Friday against the Heat, however.

items.headline: Gill (neck/back) is questionable for Thursday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Gill has started each of the Wizards' last three contests. However, he might not play in the rematch with Chicago on Thursday after popping up on the injury report due to lumbar and cervical contusions. If Gill doesn't suit up, Leaky Black might remain in the starting lineup for a third consecutive game.

items.headline: Gill closed Sunday's 121-115 loss to the Nets with 17 points (8-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block in 41 minutes.
items.story: Gill put together a solid showing for the Wizards with several key players sidelined. He's trending up over his last seven games with 12.1 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 0.6 steals in 30.2 minutes per contest while shooting 73.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Gill will start in Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: With Tristan Vukcevic (knee) ruled out, Gill will make his first start since the 130-117 loss to the Pistons on March 17. In two starts this season, the 33-year-old has averaged 5.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.5 blocks and 1.0 steals in 23.5 minutes of action.

items.headline: Gill provided 21 points (8-9 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and six assists over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 153-131 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Gill got a bit of an extended run in the second half of Wednesday's blowout game. He took advantage of the extra playing time to finish as the Wizards' leading scorer with a career-high 21 points and was also second in both assists and rebounds. Gill has scored in double digits in five of his last seven outings, and over that span he has averaged 13.3 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals over 28.7 minutes per game. He'll continue to see more run in games when Alex Sarr (toe) does not play.

items.headline: Gill (ankle) will play Monday against the Lakers.
items.story: Gill will suit up Monday after initially being added to the injury report as questionable with right ankle soreness. He's averaging 12.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.6 steals over his last five showings.

items.headline: Gill is questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers with right ankle soreness.
items.story: Gill is a candidate for a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set. On Sunday against Portland, Gill logged eight points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds and one steal in 31 minutes.

items.headline: Gill amassed eight points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds and one steal in 31 minutes during Sunday's 123-88 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Gill continues to play solid workloads for the Wizards, making him an option for deep-league fantasy managers. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 8.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 0.6 blocks on 63.3 percent shooting in 25.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gill posted 13 points (6-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, one assist and two steals in 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-111 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: The 13 points tied his season high, a mark he reached Feb. 19 against the Pacers. Gill hadn't topped six points in any of his prior six games, however, and the 33-year-old forward's role and usage in the Wizards' rotation isn't likely to become more consistent any time soon. Through nine games (one start) in March, Gill is averaging just 5.6 points, 3.4 boards, 1.6 assists and 1.3 combined steals and blocks in 22.3 minutes.

items.headline: Gill is coming off the bench Thursday against the Pistons.
items.story: Alex Sarr is returning to the starting lineup, forcing Gill to the bench. He should split the backup center minutes with Tristan Vukcevic on Thursday, hurting Gill's fantasy value.

items.headline: Gill closed with two points (1-2 FG), one rebound, one assist, one block and one steal in 16 minutes before fouling out of Tuesday's 130-117 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Gill missed out on a great opportunity, picking up three fouls in the first seven minutes, basically putting an end to any chance he had of delivering meaningful production. With Alex Sarr sidelined due to injury maintenance, it was Gill who was inserted into the starting lineup. Assuming Sarr returns for Thursday's game against the Pistons, Gill will likely return to some sort of a bench role.

items.headline: Gill will start Tuesday's game against Detroit.
items.story: With Alex Sarr (toe) and Julian Reese (two-way) unavailable, Gill will get the starting nod Tuesday. During his lone start this season in a loss to Charlotte on Feb. 22, the 33-year-old posted eight points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 31 minutes.

items.headline: Gill closed Monday's 125-117 loss to the Warriors with four points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and two steals across 32 minutes.
items.story: With Alex Sarr (toe) out Monday, Sarr saw a major workload in the loss. Gill's upside remains very low, however, making him a lukewarm streaming option Tuesday against Detroit, even with several players sitting out for Washington.

items.headline: Gill (illness) is available for Thursday's game against Utah.
items.story: Gill missed the Wizards' last two games while battling through an illness, but he has progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thursday's contest. He has averaged 9.3 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 0.8 blocks over 28.0 minutes per game in six outings (one start) since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Gill (illness) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Gill remains day-to-day after missing the past two games for Washington. The Wizards will be very shorthanded yet again, so Gill could soak up a sizable amount of minutes if he's cleared.

items.headline: Gill (illness) will not play Tuesday against the Magic.
items.story: Gill will be sidelined for a second straight contest Tuesday. The Wizards are going to be very thin up front, so the team could rely more on Julian Reese and Will Riley.

items.headline: Gill (illness) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Gill remains day-to-day after missing Monday's game against the Rockets. The Wizards are going to be very thin up front Tuesday, so Gill could see a sizable workload if he's feeling up to it.

items.headline: Gill (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Gill will be inactive Monday while battling an illness, paving the way for Julian Reese to join the starting five for his team debut. Gill's next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Magic.

items.headline: Gill (illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Gill is in danger of missing Monday's contest due to an illness. The 33-year-old forward has been a key depth piece in Washington's frontcourt of late, even drawing a spot start Feb. 22 when the team was shorthanded at center. However, he recently shifted back to the second unit following the return of Tristan Vukcevic, who is listed as questionable for Monday's contest due to a thigh contusion.

items.headline: Gill will come off the bench Tuesday against the Hawks.
items.story: This is an expected move with Tristan Vukcevic back in the lineup. Gill's usage rate is typically too low to consider in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Gill will start Sunday versus the Hornets.
items.story: This will be Gill's first start of the season and he'll be joined in the first unit by Bub Carrington, Tre Johnson, Bilal Coulibaly and Kyshawn George. Gill could be looking at major minutes Sunday as the tallest player available to man the five-spot, so he's on the radar in daily fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Gill (hand) will play Wednesday against the Cavaliers.
items.story: The Wizards do have a cleaner injury report than usual, so Gill is likely to be deployed as an emergency depth option Wednesday.

items.headline: Gill (hand) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Gill has been dealing with a bruised right hand in February, and the injury caused him to miss the closing end of a back-to-back set Monday. His availability remains up in the air for Wednesday's contest.

items.headline: Gill (hand) will not play Sunday against Miami.
items.story: Gill was unable to shake his questionable tag for the second leg of this back-to-back set. The Wizards could be very thin up front Sunday and may use a committee approach to soak up the minutes.

items.headline: Gill (hand) is questionable for Sunday's game against Miami.
items.story: Gill remains day-to-day with his hand injury. He managed to play through it Saturday against the Nets, finishing with nine points, five rebounds and two assists in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Gill (hand) is available to play Tuesday against the Knicks.
items.story: Gill was able to shake off his questionable tag for this contest. He saw a big workload in his most recent outing, but he finished scoreless in 27 minutes against the Kings on Sunday.

items.headline: Gill is questionable for Tuesday's game against New York with a right hand contusion.
items.story: With Washington shorthanded, Gill saw extended run Sunday against the Kings, but he finished scoreless in 27 minutes. He remains miles off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Gill accumulated no counting statistics across three minutes of court time in Friday's 128-107 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Gill made an appearance for the second game in a row, but he was essentially out of the rotation Friday with Washington welcoming Kyshawn George (hip) back from a seven-game absence and with Khris Middleton (knee) returning from a one-game rest. The Wizards had Gill play the final 5.8 seconds of the third quarter before he was back on the bench to begin the fourth quarter, and he then checked back into the game for the final 2:44, when Washington had fallen behind by 20 points.

items.headline: Gill provided two points (1-1 FG), one rebound and one block across eight minutes during Tuesday's 121-102 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Gill suited up for just the seventh time this season and for the first time in the past five games. He has been a non-factor thus far, averaging 2.1 points in 3.7 minutes across his seven appearances. He can be safely left on all waiver wires.

items.headline: The Wizards are signing Gill to a one-year contract, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: After waiving Gill earlier in the offseason, the Wizards have elected to bring the 32-year-old forward back to the team. Gill didn't have much of a role in Washington's rotation a year ago, having averaged 2.5 points, 1.3 rebounds and 0.3 assists in 7.8 minutes per game over 51 regular-season contests in 2024-25, so he'll likely serve as frontcourt depth behind the likes of Alex Sarr, Bilal Coulibaly and Kyshawn George while the roster is healthy.

items.headline: Gill (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami.
items.story: Gill will end up missing the final three games of the regular season due to a right hamstring strain. JT Thor (knee) and Tristan Vukcevic will likely see increased playing time in Sunday's regular-season finale in Gill's absence. Gill will finish his fifth regular-season with the Wizards averaging 2.6 points and 1.3 rebounds over 7.9 minutes per game across 50 outings.

items.headline: Gill (hamstring) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Gill will miss his second consecutive game due to a strained right hamstring. His last chance to suit up this season will come Sunday against the Heat. JT Thor (knee) and Tristan Vukcevic are candidates for an uptick in minutes due to Gill being sidelined.

items.headline: Gill (hamstring) will not play Wednesday against the 76ers.
items.story: Gill left Tuesday's game against the Pacers after aggravating his hamstring issue, and he was unable to return. Fortunately for Washington, Tristan Vukcevic is no longer on the injury report.

items.headline: Gill won't return to Tuesday's game against the Pacers due to right hamstring soreness.
items.story: Gill was initially listed as questionable due to the hamstring injury before being cleared to play, though he exited the game with 5:13 remaining in the second quarter. He'll finish Tuesday's contest with four rebounds across seven minutes. JT Thor will likely see a slight uptick in playing time the rest of the way due to Gill being sidelined.

items.headline: Johnson registered 10 points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and two steals across 27 minutes during Thursday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Johnson has recorded multiple steals in three of his last five appearances, adding defensive value to his reserve role. However, fluctuating minutes and limited shot volume restrict his scoring upside, keeping him primarily a deeper-league option.

items.headline: Johnson produced four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist across 15 minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Johnson saw his playing time drop to just 15 minutes Tuesday after logging at least 25 minutes in each of his previous five appearances. The veteran forward had scored in double figures in three straight games before Tuesday's setback, but his inconsistent offensive involvement and crowded San Antonio rotation limit his fantasy reliability. He remains a matchup-dependent option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Johnson supplied 18 points (6-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 123-85 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Johnson brought his usual energy off the bench for San Antonio, scoring 18 points in 25 minutes. The veteran has been a steady scorer for the second unit, and nights like Friday show why the Spurs keep him in that role instead of the starting lineup. With so much depth on the wing, his minutes will depend on matchups, but his scoring makes him hard to bench.

items.headline: Johnson chipped in 10 points (4-6 FG, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists and two steals across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 124-119 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Johnson chipped in across the board, turning in one of his better all-around performances of the season. It has been a difficult start for the veteran forward, whose scoring average has dipped from 13.2 points per game last season to under 8.0 this year despite seeing more minutes. While this was an encouraging effort, one game isn't enough to put him back on the standard-league radar. For now, he remains a deep-league option.

items.headline: Johnson closed Monday's 122-96 victory over the Suns with four points (2-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five rebounds and three assists in 26 minutes.
items.story: Johnson has been largely a non-factor in fantasy leagues thus far, despite averaging more minutes per game than last season. His scoring has fallen from 13.2 points per game during the 2025-26 campaign to just 7.8 this season, leaving him well outside the top 250 in standard leagues.

items.headline: Johnson finished with 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), seven rebounds and one assist over 26 minutes during Monday's 119-97 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Johnson set a season high in scoring Monday. Over his first seven appearances, the reigning Sixth Man of the Year has averaged 9.3 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game and hasn't seen much of a usage increase in Tobias Harris' (calf) absence.

items.headline: Johnson closed Tuesday's 130-103 win over Sacramento with 14 points (5-11 FG, 4-5 FT) and four rebounds over 22 minutes.
items.story: Johnson established a season high in scoring, reaching double figures for the second time in four games. The veteran forward attempted a season-high 11 shots but failed to contribute any assists or defensive statistics. Johnson has averaged 9.8 points and 5.0 rebounds through four appearances, leaving him with limited fantasy appeal outside deeper leagues.

items.headline: Johnson (mouth) is available for Friday's game against the Rockets, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Johnson participated in shootaround Friday, and he's received the green light to play in Friday's intrastate matchup. Johnson contributed 10 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes in the season opener against the Thunder on Tuesday. He required three stitches after that game, but he's been cleared to play Friday.

items.headline: Johnson (mouth) participated in shooting drills after Friday's morning shootaround, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News.
items.story: Johnson is trying to play through a mouth laceration for the first half of this back-to-back set. With Tobias Harris (calf) already sidelined, Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant could step into larger roles in the frontcourt if Johnson also cannot play.

items.headline: Johnson is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Rockets due to a mouth laceration.
items.story: Johnson required three stitches after Tuesday's season-opening loss to the Thunder and could miss the front end of this back-to-back set. If the 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year is ruled out, Carter Bryant and Harrison Barnes could see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Johnson contributed 10 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Johnson provided some scoring off the bench, reaching double figures in 20 minutes and adding two steals. Tobias Harris (calf) will limit Johnson's involvement when he returns to action, but the latter, last season's Sixth Man of the Year, will still be good for 15 to 20 minutes nightly. Johnson needed three stitches after Tuesday's game to close a "really deep" cut on the inside of his right cheek following a collision with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News. Johnson also needed stitches in the preseason for a cut on his chin.

items.headline: Johnson posted 15 points (4-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-9 FT), five rebounds and two assists over 20 minutes during Friday's 126-97 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Johnson returned from a night's rest to deliver his usual scoring punch off the bench, posting 15 points for the second time in three games. The reigning Sixth Man of the Year should again anchor San Antonio's second unit this season.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) will play in Friday's preseason game against the Kings, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Johnson was among several players who rested Wednesday against the Suns. However, it appears the Spurs want to get some more reps for their regulars Friday for the finale.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against Phoenix, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Johnson will get a rest day after playing in each of San Antonio's first three preseason games. His next chance to suit up will come Friday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Johnson totaled 15 points (4-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 7-9 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 24 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason loss to Utah.
items.story: With several San Antonio regulars sidelined, Johnson made his first start of the preseason and used a strong effort at the charity stripe to reach the 15-point mark. The reigning Sixth Man of the Year averaged 13.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 23.3 minutes across 82 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Johnson is in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against Utah, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: With several San Antonio regulars inactive, Johnson will enter the starting five. Through two preseason games as a reserve, he's averaging 4.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 17.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Johnson appears to have lost weight ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, with Michael C. Wright of ESPN.com noting that he looks "quicker with a little more bounce than last season."
items.story: Johnson earned Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2025-26, averaging 13.2 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.6 steals across 23.3 minutes per game in 82 regular-season appearances off the bench. He is expected to continue providing a spark with the second unit in 2026-27, though he'll face added competition for touches on a talented San Antonio team that added Tobias Harris (calf) this offseason.

items.headline: Johnson ended with seven points (2-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and five rebounds in 16 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to New York in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Johnson concluded a highly disappointing postseason run with a slightly improved but ultimately quiet performance off the bench as San Antonio was eliminated in five games. Despite earning the 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year award after averaging 13.2 points per game during the regular season, the seventh-year swingman was never able to find his rhythm in the playoffs, frequently taking a back seat in the rotation. His struggles reached a low point in the championship series against New York, where he averaged just 4.4 points and 3.0 rebounds across 15.0 minutes per game while shooting a meager 34.8 percent from the field. Johnson has one year remaining on his four-year, $74 million rookie extension before hitting unrestricted free agency in the summer of 2027. Owed an average annual salary of $18.5 million on a fully guaranteed deal, he will head into the offseason looking to regroup and solidify his standing as a vital, high-priced reserve weapon for a young Spurs core built around Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper.

items.headline: Johnson posted seven points (3-5 FG, 1-4 FT), two rebounds and one steal in 17 minutes during Monday's 115-111 win over New York in Game 3 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Johnson continues to be mostly a non-factor, scoring single digits for the fourth time in the past five games. Despite being named the Sixth Man of the Year, Johnson has been unable to carry his form from the regular season into the playoffs. In 13 appearances over the past month, he has averaged just 8.2 points and 3.4 rebounds in 17.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Johnson registered 11 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 16 minutes during the Spurs' 111-103 win over the Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday.
items.story: Johnson was limited to just two points in the first half, but the 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year came up big for the Spurs in the second half, when he scored nine of his 11 points to help push San Antonio to the NBA Finals. He'll finish the Western Conference Finals having averaged 9.9 points, 2.9 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 1.4 threes over 18.7 minutes per game. The Spurs will welcome in the Knicks on Wednesday for Game 1 of the NBA Finals.

items.headline: Johnson finished with five points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds in 12 minutes during Friday's 123-108 loss to the Thunder in Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Johnson has been mostly underwhelming throughout the playoffs, having scored more than 11 points only twice in 14 appearances. After averaging 12.5 points per game across the regular season, things have gone south for Johnson, as he's put up just 8.8 points per game over his past 12 appearances. The Spurs now trail the series 2-1, with Game 4 slated for Sunday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Johnson posted 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 0-1 FT), five rebounds and one assist in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 122-113 loss to the Thunder in Game 2 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: The 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year, Johnson has seen his minutes go down in the postseason. Through 13 playoff games, he's averaging 19.4 minutes per game with 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 0.7 steals on 41.5 percent shooting from the field. De'Aaron Fox (ankle) and Dylan Harper (adductor) are questionable for Game 3, so Johnson could potentially be more involved.

items.headline: Johnson logged 21 points (8-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, two steals and one block in 22 minutes during Tuesday's 126-97 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 5 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Johnson turned in his best offensive performance of the postseason, delivering an efficient showing from inside the arc while leading the San Antonio bench in scoring. The 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year had averaged just 8.8 points on 41.4 percent shooting in the series entering Tuesday's contest, making his efficiency in this one extremely encouraging. He'll aim to remain productive in Game 6 on Friday, when the Spurs try to close out the series.

items.headline: Johnson produced nine points (2-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-8 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and one block in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 133-95 win over the Timberwolves in Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Johnson struggled with efficiency from the field but did solid work getting to the free-throw line and on the glass, ultimately finishing one point shy of a double-double. Wednesday marked the wing's first double-digit rebounding effort since Feb. 1 and just the seventh such performance of the year between the regular season and playoffs. Through seven postseason games in 2026, Johnson is averaging 7.3 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 19.6 minutes per contest off the bench.

items.headline: Johnson accumulated 11 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 24 minutes during Monday's 104-102 loss to Minnesota in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: The 11 points and 24 minutes were both postseason highs for Johnson. Overall, the 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year has averaged only 7.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 19.7 minutes per game over six outings in the 2026 playoffs, taking a back seat to Dylan Harper as San Antonio's sixth man.

items.headline: Johnson supplied nine points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 17 minutes during Sunday's 114-93 victory over the Trail Blazers in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson continues to put up modest numbers, having failed to score double digits thus far in the playoffs. It's been a rough series for the newly crowned Sixth Man of the Year, with him averaging just 6.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals. With San Antonio now leading the series 3-1, look for Johnson to try to up his efforts in Game 5.

items.headline: Johnson provided seven points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 loss to the Trail Blazers in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Though he's considered one of the favorites for the 2025-26 Sixth Man of the Year award, Johnson hasn't made a big impact so far this postseason. After scoring in double figures in each of his final 12 regular-season contests, the seventh-year swingman has scored in single digits through two playoff games.

items.headline: Johnson registered 20 points (8-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 112-101 win over the Trail Blazers.
