items.story: Johnson posted his 13th game of the campaign with at least 20 points. He took advantage of some extra usage due to Victor Wembanyama (ribs) and Stephon Castle (knee) being sidelined, though the Spurs are hopeful to have both back in the lineup Sunday.

items.headline: Johnson logged 13 points (4-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 25 minutes off the bench during Monday's 115-102 win over the 76ers.
items.story: The 26-year-old wing came up one board short of his sixth double-double of the season, while three combined stocks tied his season high. Johnson has scored in double digits in nine straight games, averaging 15.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 threes in 23.9 minutes over that span.

items.headline: Smith (illness) will play Monday against the Cavaliers, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Smith isn't feeling 100 percent healthy ahead of Monday's matchup, but he's been cleared to suit up. Coach Tiago Splitter stated in his pre-game presser that he expects to be cautious with Smith's playing time, especially after the big man logged 34 minutes Sunday against Denver.

items.headline: Smith (illness) is probable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: With Nic Claxton's (illness) status up in the air, Smith could be a high-end fantasy play Monday. Over his last six appearances, Smith has averaged 18.7 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 blocks, 1.3 steals and 3.2 three-pointers per game while shooting a sizzling 55.9 percent from deep.

items.headline: Smith amassed 26 points (10-14 FG, 6-7 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 34 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 151-145 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Smith has averaged 19.0 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.6 steals, 0.8 blocks and 29.0 minutes over his last five appearances. His expanding perimeter production and defensive contributions provide strong fantasy value despite inconsistent rebounding.

items.headline: Smith (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Nic Claxton has been ruled out due to an illness, so Smith will reprise his role as the Bulls' starting center and could see increased burn. Zach Collins and Noa Essengue should also see more playing time with Claxton sidelined.

items.headline: Smith (illness) has been upgraded to probable for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Smith was initially listed as questionable but is now expected to return from a one-game absence due to an illness. Over his last five appearances, the big man has averaged 17.2 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks across 28.2 minutes per showing. He could also see a slight bump in minutes if Nic Claxton (illness) is ruled out.

items.headline: Smith (illness) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Smith unavailable after being downgraded to questionable earlier Friday, Chicago will need to cover his center minutes elsewhere. His absence opens up added frontcourt work most prominently for Zach Collins and Nic Claxton, the latter of whom is the likelier candidate to start at center.

items.headline: Smith (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Smith was a late addition to the injury report due to a gastrointestinal illness. His absence would leave additional playing time available for Zach Collins and Nic Claxton, though Claxton still appears to be on a minutes restriction.

items.headline: Smith recorded 14 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and one steal in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 137-107 win over the Nets.
items.story: Smith grabbed five offensive rebounds Wednesday, continuing his strong interior activity despite reduced minutes in the blowout. He's scored at least 14 points in five straight games while providing valuable three-point production from the center position. His combination of perimeter shooting, rebounding and defensive upside warrants attention across fantasy formats.

items.headline: Smith (head) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Smith exited Monday's loss to the Cavaliers in the fourth quarter due to an apparent head injury and did not return. However, the big man is set to play Wednesday. Over his last four appearances, Smith has averaged 18.0 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.5 blocks and 1.3 steals in 30.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Smith (head) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 126-115 loss to the Cavaliers and did not return.
items.story: Smith collided with Peyton Watson at the rim, and both players stayed down for several minutes before eventually leaving the contest. Smith did return to the bench after initially going back to the locker room, but Chicago opted to keep him out for good with the tilt in its final stages. He had a stellar outing prior to his exit, finishing with 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks in 28 minutes. Smith noted after the game that he was fine despite taking a blow to the chin, resulting in him hitting the back of his head, per Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic. The 26-year-old can be considered day-to-day leading up to Wednesday's matchup in Brooklyn.

items.headline: Smith (undisclosed) went to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Monday's game against Cleveland, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Smith took a hard fall after colliding with Peyton Watson at the 5:26 mark of the fourth quarter and headed to the locker room for further evaluation. With the contest nearing its conclusion, Smith is unlikely to return. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday in Brooklyn. Should the 26-year-old miss additional time, Nic Claxton and Zach Collins are in line for expanded roles at center.

items.headline: Smith (finger) will play in Monday's game against the Cavaliers, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Smith is back from a one-game absence due to a sprained finger, which is likely to result in Zach Collins shifting back to the bench. Smith and Nic Claxton should receive a fairly even split of the center minutes for the Bulls on Monday.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Smith didn't play in Saturday's 117-106 win over Minnesota. Nic Claxton (hamstring) also didn't suit up in that one, resulting in Zach Collins getting the start. Claxton is good to go for Monday's meeting with the Cavaliers, so he will likely start if Smith is ultimately sidelined again.

items.headline: Smith (finger) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Minnesota, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Smith will miss his first game of the season after being listed as questionable earlier Saturday due to a sprained left finger. Nic Claxton (hamstring) has also been ruled out, leaving Zach Collins and Orlando Robinson as the two healthy bigs remaining for Chicago.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game at Minnesota.
items.story: Smith is in jeopardy of missing Saturday's contest after aggravating his sprained left finger in Friday's overtime win over Atlanta. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) also questionable, the Bulls could be shorthanded in the frontcourt. If either of those guys is ruled out, Zach Collins would likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Smith (hand) exited Friday's 125-117 win over the Hawks in overtime and did not return, finishing with 15 points (6-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals across 32 minutes.
items.story: Smith secured his third double-double of the season while tying his season-high mark in steals. However, the big man came down on his left hand in overtime and exited to the locker room. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's game at Minnesota.

items.headline: Smith exited to the locker room in overtime during Friday's game against the Hawks due to an apparent left hand injury, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Smith went back to the locker room holding his left hand. The big man can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Smith totaled 23 points (8-9 FG, 5-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 124-119 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Smith was nearly flawless on the offensive end, knocking down all five of his three-point attempts en route to a team-high 23 points. However, he failed to record a steal or block against a San Antonio frontcourt led by Victor Wembanyama, and Smith's rebounding was down. Smith continues to start ahead of Nic Claxton, making the former a viable option in most formats, particularly for those needing threes from the center position.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is available for Sunday's game versus Philadelphia.
items.story: The finger injury isn't new, so barring a setback, Smith was expected to suit up all along. The 26-year-old has averaged 11.0 points, 7.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists over 22.5 minutes per contest in eight regular-season appearances in 2026-27. While Smith has had one of the best seasons of his career, the return of Nic Claxton (hamstring) will likely result in a decline in production moving ahead, especially once the latter is cleared for a full workload.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is probable for Sunday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Smith left Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks after just seven minutes of play due to a left finger sprain and was initially deemed questionable for Sunday. His upgraded status is a good sign for Smith, who's been the starting center with Nic Claxton (hamstring) yet to play this season.

items.headline: Smith (hand) won't return to Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Smith has been starting for Nic Claxton (hamstring), who hasn't played this season. However, the Bulls will be down another big, at least for the remainder of Wednesday's contest. As a result, Zach Collins should handle most of the minutes in the middle the rest of the way.

items.headline: Smith went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against the Knicks after suffering an apparent finger injury, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Smith appeared to hurt his finger contesting a shot from OG Anunoby, and for now, he should be considered questionable to return. If he needs to miss time, Zach Collins, Leonard Miller and Noa Essengue would help pick up the slack.

items.headline: Smith is available for Wednesday's game against the Knicks despite a left finger sprain.
items.story: Smith will shed a probable tag for this contest. He's averaging 12.1 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game this season, and the bulk of the center minutes should remain in Smith's hands until Nic Claxton (hamstring) is cleared to make his season debut.

items.headline: Smith is probable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks with a left finger sprain.
items.story: Smith is expected to play through the injury Wednesday, but his time as Chicago's starting center could be coming to an end. Nic Claxton (hamstring) is questionable to make his season debut, and his return would send Smith into a bench role.

items.headline: Smith registered 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 0-1 FT), seven rebounds and four assists across 28 minutes in Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Smith provided efficient interior scoring and useful contributions on the glass while coming close to matching his season-high assist total. This was Smith's fifth double-digit scoring performance this season, and he has recorded at least seven rebounds five times. His scoring and rebounding will drive his fantasy appeal on a young Chicago roster.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is active for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: As expected, Smith will suit up versus the 76ers. He's averaging 12.0 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.0 blocks in 24.2 minutes across six outings so far this season. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) still sidelined, Smith is likely to continue starting for the Bulls.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Smith is battling a finger injury but is expected to suit up versus the 76ers. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Smith will presumably remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Smith ended Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics with five points (2-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 27 minutes.
items.story: Smith was the only player who finished Friday's game with double-digit rebounds, although it was the second time in three games that he failed to score in double digits. The seventh-year center is averaging 12.0 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.0 blocks over 24.2 minutes per game to open the regular season. He'll continue to operate in a starting role for as long as Nic Claxton (hamstring) is out of action.

items.headline: Smith (finger) is available for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Smith popped up on the injury report due to a left finger sprain, though it won't keep him off the floor versus Boston. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) sidelined, Smith has started in all five of the Bulls' regular-season games in 2026-27, averaging 13.4 points, 8.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists over 23.4 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Smith is questionable for Friday's game against Boston with a left finger sprain.
items.story: This is a new injury for Chicago's starting center, but he's considered day-to-day. If Smith is held out against Boston, the Bulls could lean more on Zach Collins.

items.headline: Smith racked up 17 points (7-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt), 11 rebounds, five assists and three blocks over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 133-127 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Smith continues to hold down the fort at center while Nic Claxton tends to a hamstring injury. Over his first five appearances, Smith has averaged 13.4 points, 8.2 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 23.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Smith chipped in seven points (2-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and one assist over 20 minutes during Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Smith struggled to find his rhythm offensively, converting just two of his eight field-goal attempts while failing to record a defensive statistic. The starting center also saw his playing time limited as Chicago fell behind by a substantial margin. Smith's ability to contribute rebounds and three-pointers gives him some fantasy appeal, but inconsistent minutes and scoring could limit his reliability.

items.headline: Ayton (illness) is available for Sunday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Ayton will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up for the 18th consecutive game to begin the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Ayton (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Ayton played 11 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago, but he appears to have picked up some sort of illness over the weekend. If he can't play Sunday, expect Khris Middleton and Bilal Coulibaly to see increased burn off the Wizards' bench.

items.headline: Ayton had two points (1-1 FG), four rebounds and one block in nine minutes during Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Ayton has now logged fewer than 15 minutes in five of his past six games, continuing what has been a rapid decline. During that six-game period, he has averaged just 3.7 points and 5.0 rebounds per game, making him a non-factor in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Ayton (leg) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Ayton left Saturday's game against the Thunder early due to a lower-leg injury, but he will be available Monday. Over his last five completed games, Ayton holds averages of 6.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 17.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Ayton won't return to Saturday's game against the Thunder due to a lower leg injury.
items.story: Ayton will end his evening with two points (1-2 FG), one rebound and one turnover in seven minutes. For now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.

items.headline: Ayton will come off the bench in Saturday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Bilal Coulibaly will replace Ayton in the first unit for Saturday's game. As a reserve this season, Ayton is averaging 5.6 points and 4.3 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Ayton chipped in eight points (4-5 FG), 11 rebounds, three assists and one steal over 23 minutes during Friday's 139-132 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Ayton moved into the starting lineup, replacing Anthony Davis, who was sidelined due to an ankle injury. He managed to pull down a season-high 11 rebounds, although nothing else he did jumped off the page. Washington will face Oklahoma City on Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back. If Davis remains out, Ayton could be a viable streaming consideration for fantasy managers needing boards.

items.headline: Ayton will start Friday against the Hawks.
items.story: Ayton is getting the start with Anthony Davis (ankle) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr. In Ayton's previous start this season, he finished with four points, six rebounds and two assists over 25 minutes.

items.headline: Ayton won't start Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: With Alex Sarr (knee) back in the lineup, Ayton will retreat to the second unit. The veteran center has averaged 5.7 points and 4.3 rebounds in 14.3 minutes per game across six outings off the bench this season.

items.headline: Ayton racked up four points (2-4 FG), six rebounds and two assists in 24 minutes during Monday's 103-94 victory over Orlando.
items.story: Ayton drew the start with Alex Sarr (knee) sidelined but remained a secondary offensive option, attempting just four shots while Anthony Davis dominated the scoring opportunities in Washington's frontcourt. Ayton's limited involvement is concerning for his short-term fantasy value, particularly with Sarr eventually expected to return. Ayton's rebounding offers some utility, but his upside appears restricted in the current rotation.

items.headline: Ayton will start in Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: With Alex Sarr (knee) sidelined, Ayton will slide into the starting center role. Bilal Coulibaly and Khris Middleton could see a bump in minutes off the Wizards' bench.

items.headline: Ayton finished with 10 points (5-5 FG) and three rebounds across 12 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Ayton played no more than 12 minutes for the second straight game, continuing what has been an underwhelming season thus far. Having been acquired by the Wizards during the offseason, Ayton finds himself firmly tethered to the second unit, playing as a backup option behind Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis. At this point, he holds little fantasy value outside of deeper formats.

items.headline: Ayton racked up zero points (0-1 FG), four rebounds and two assists over 12 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Ayton struggled to make an impact offensively while playing a limited role behind Washington's starting frontcourt of Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr. The veteran center has seen inconsistent playing time to begin the season, significantly restricting his fantasy upside. Unless his role expands, Ayton will have difficulty providing reliable production even in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Ayton accumulated 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two blocks over 15 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Ayton was solid in his debut for Washington as the backup center behind Alex Sarr, who finished with six points, nine rebounds and two assists in the season-opening victory. Ayton tied Bilal Coulibaly (11/2/1/2/4) for the team lead in blocks and did not commit any personal fouls or turnovers. Ayton should typically see 15-18 minutes a night as the first big off the bench.

items.headline: Ayton is starting Monday's preseason game against the Nets.
items.story: The Wizards are resting Anthony Davis on Monday, opening a spot in the first unit. Ayton is positioned to play the backup center role for Washington in 2026-27.

items.headline: Ayton is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Pistons, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Wizards will tweak their frontcourt and will have Alex Sarr next to Anthony Davis, meaning Ayton will move to the bench. Ayton is likely to see most of his regular-season minutes off the bench, with Sarr and Davis expected to start when healthy.

items.headline: Ayton will start Thursday's preseason game against the Knicks, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Ayton will get a look with the first unit while Alex Sarr continues to recover from offseason foot surgery. He'll start alongside Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: Ayton won't play for the Bahamas during upcoming FIBA action, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
items.story: There's no report of an injury to Ayton, who appears to be sitting out for maintenance purposes. After being shipped to the Wizards this offseason, the 28-year-old big man is lined up as the primary backup big behind Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis ahead of training camp.

items.headline: The Lakers are trading Ayton to the Wizards in exchange for Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Ayton's departure was imminent following the addition of Walker Kessler. In Washington, Ayton figures to be the primary backup to Alex Sarr, filling the void left by the departure of Marvin Bagley. Ayton doesn't seem like an appealing fantasy option on his new team, as he needs a lot of volume and minutes to be worthwhile in standard formats.

items.headline: Ayton exercised his $8.1 million player option Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: This isn't a huge surprise, but it doesn't mean the Lakers won't try to flip him later on. During his debut season with the Lakers, he made 72 regular-season appearances with averages of 12.5 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.0 blocks on 67.1 percent shooting from the field. As things stand heading into free agency, Ayton is penciled in as the starting center.

items.headline: Ayton logged six points (3-3 FG), three rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes during Monday's 115-110 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: This was a disappointing end to Ayton's first season in Los Angeles. As for the regular season, Ayton logged 72 appearances as the starting center, posting averages of 12.5 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.0 blocks and 0.6 steals on 67.1 percent shooting from the field. The big man will be heading into the final year of his contract in 2026-27.

items.headline: Ayton ended Tuesday's 108-90 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 10 points (5-12 FG), 12 rebounds, two assists and one block over 27 minutes.
items.story: The double-double was his fourth of the postseason in seven games. Ayton has been making an impact on the glass for the Lakers, averaging 11.6 points, 11.0 boards, 1.1 assists and 1.0 blocks during the playoffs while shooting 56.9 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Ayton supplied seven points (2-6 FG, 3-7 FT), 16 rebounds, one assist and one block across 28 minutes during Friday's 98-78 victory over Houston in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Only three Lakers players -- LeBron James, Rui Hachimura and Austin Reaves -- scored in double digits during Friday's victory, but Ayton produced in his own way by grabbing a game-high 16 rebounds, one less than his playoff high in Game 5 on Wednesday. Ayton has logged at least 10 rebounds in each of his last three games and will finish the first round of the Western Conference Playoffs having averaged 11.8 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 blocks over 31.0 minutes. Next up for the Lakers is a conference semifinal matchup against the top-seeded Thunder, and Ayton will have his hands full guarding Chet Holmgren.

items.headline: Ayton registered 18 points (9-14 FG), 17 rebounds and two blocks in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 99-93 loss to Houston in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The 17 boards were a series and season high for Ayton, and represented his best performance on the glass since Feb. 3 of last season, when he ripped down 20 rebounds for Portland in a win over Phoenix. Ayton has three double-doubles in five first-round games, averaging 12.8 points, 9.8 boards, 1.0 assists and 1.0 blocks for the series while shooting 63.8 percent from the floor, and he'll look to come up big again in Game 6 on Friday.

items.headline: Ayton has been ejected from Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Rockets, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Ayton was assessed a Flagrant 2 foul for a hit to the head while guarding Alperen Sengun. He concludes the contest with 19 points (9-12 FG, 1-1 FT) and 10 rebounds in 25 minutes. Jaxson Hayes figures to see more time with Ayton out.

items.headline: Ayton ended with two points (1-3 FG), six rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 33 minutes during Friday's 112-108 overtime win over the Rockets in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Ayton failed to have a meaningful impact for a second straight game, recording just two points despite playing heavy minutes. Although the Lakers now lead the series 3-0, Ayton's questionable defensive efforts cannot be unseen. While advancing to the next round feels like a very real possibility for Los Angeles, a potential matchup with the Thunder is cause for concern given Oklahoma City's sizable interior.

items.headline: Ayton contributed 19 points (8-10 FG, 3-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one block over 35 minutes during Saturday's 107-98 win over the Rockets in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Ayton's scoring total was engineered in part by LeBron James, who found his big man often and generated a few assists by connecting with him. Ayton has had his share of inconsistencies this season, but he went toe-to-toe with Alperen Sengun and finished with the better rebound result. It's all hands on deck for the Lakers, who need balanced output from everyone with Luka Doncic (hamstring) and Austin Reaves (oblique) sidelined. Ayton needs to keep the volume up and assume additional responsibility as a scoring threat to keep ahead of the Rockets in the first-round series.

items.headline: Ayton provided 22 points (10-14 FG, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and three blocks in 26 minutes during Sunday's 131-107 victory over Utah.
items.story: Ayton co-led the Lakers in scoring alongside Rui Hachimura, and the big man will need to provide this kind of output on offense in a difficult first-round series against the Rockets due to the likely absences of Luka Doncic (hamstring) and Austin Reaves (oblique) for much of the series. Ayton averaged 12.5 points and 8.0 rebounds per game across 72 starts in the regular season.

items.headline: Ayton provided 21 points (9-11 FG, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block over 31 minutes during Thursday's 119-103 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: It's the first time since March 12 that Ayton has delivered 20-plus points. All five Laker starters scored in double digits Thursday as the team tries to compensate for the absence of Luka Doncic (hamstring) and Austin Reaves (oblique), and in three games since the two stars went down, Ayton is averaging 12.3 points, 4.0 boards, 1.0 blocks and 0.7 assists in 24.3 minutes.

items.headline: Ayton had 18 points (8-13 FG, 2-3 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 28 minutes during Tuesday's 127-113 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: It was Ayton's best scoring effort since March 12 as he moves past a back issue that sidelined him last Wednesday and limited him to 22 minutes in each of his prior two games. The 27-year-old center's production was inconsistent in March, even when healthy, as he averaged 11.1 points, 7.8 boards, 1.1 blocks and 0.9 assists in 25.5 minutes over 15 appearances, but he did shoot 73.3 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
items.story: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss time. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams (thumb) are all candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Powell is questionable for Sunday's game against the Nuggets due to a right hamstring strain.
items.story: Powell has been one of the few bright spots for the Bulls this season, averaging 20.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game in 13 starts. If he's ruled out, it'd be a huge blow for an anemic Bulls offense. Buddy Hield and Tre Jones could see more playing time if Powell has to miss time.

items.headline: Powell tallied 16 points (7-18 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Friday's 98-84 loss to Washington.
items.story: Powell and the rest of Chicago's offense struggled Friday, as the team finished 36-for-88 (40.9 percent) from the field and 9-for-33 (27.3 percent) on three-pointers. Powell couldn't quite find the range from behind the arc for the second time in three outings, but he should be given plenty of opportunities to keep working as the Bulls' primary scoring threat.

items.headline: Powell accumulated 17 points (6-16 FG, 5-9 3Pt), two rebounds, five assists and one steal across 26 minutes during Wednesday's 137-107 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Powell has averaged 22.6 points, 3.4 assists and 2.4 three-pointers over his last five appearances, attempting 16.8 shots per game. Wednesday marked his third straight outing with at least five assists or three triples. His consistent offensive volume supports strong fantasy value despite limited rebounding contributions.

items.headline: Powell tallied 27 points (10-18 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 7-11 FT), two rebounds, six assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Monday's 126-115 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Powell led Chicago in scoring for the third straight game despite exiting briefly with what appeared to be a lower-body injury. He checked back in with 8:44 remaining in the fourth quarter and nearly brought the Bulls all the way back from a 17-point second-half deficit. However, he was unable to find the range from downtown and left points at the free-throw line. Over his last three outings, Powell is averaging 28.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.3 triples in 31.3 minutes a night.

items.headline: Powell (undisclosed) has been cleared to return to Monday's game against the Cavaliers, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Powell went to the locker room during the fourth quarter for a brief stint after appearing to suffer a lower-body injury, but he was spotted back on the bench shortly after. He was cleared to check back in with 8:44 remaining in the final period.

items.headline: Powell went to the locker room during Monday's game against Cleveland with an undisclosed injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: The nature of Powell's injury is unclear at this time, though he appeared to be limping on his way to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Powell finished with 23 points (10-19 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, a steal and two blocks across 30 minutes in Saturday's 117-106 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Powell followed Friday's 33-point performance against Atlanta with another productive outing, giving him 56 points across two games since returning from a two-game absence due to a back injury. His scoring has been particularly important for a Chicago team that entered Saturday with just two wins in 11 games. The veteran's ability to generate offense remains one of his strongest fantasy attributes, and his return to a substantial workload is encouraging after the recent injury issues. Having scored at least 20 points in five of his 10 appearances this season, Powell should remain a key offensive weapon for the Bulls as long as he stays healthy.

items.headline: Powell (back) is available for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Powell was questionable to play Saturday due to lower-back injury management, but he'll fight through it and suit up for the second leg of Chicago's back-to-back set. Powell dropped a game-high 33 points during Friday's 125-117 win over Atlanta after missing the previous two contests.

items.headline: Powell (back) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: After erupting for 33 points in 31 minutes during Friday's overtime win over the Hawks, Powell is in danger of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set due to lower-back injury management. If the veteran guard is ruled out, Buddy Hield and Tre Jones could see increased burn.

items.headline: Powell finished with 33 points (12-19 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 31 minutes in Friday's 125-117 overtime win over the Hawks.
items.story: Powell led all scorers with 33 points in his return to action, showing no signs of limitations after being cleared to play without a minutes restriction. The veteran guard shot 63.2 percent from the field and knocked down four triples, helping Chicago secure the overtime victory. His immediate return to a prominent offensive role is encouraging for fantasy managers, particularly those relying on his scoring and three-point production.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) is available for Friday's game against the Hawks and will not face a minutes restriction, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Powell's clearance to play without restrictions is encouraging for his fantasy outlook, as he should be able to handle his usual workload. The veteran guard figures to provide Chicago with a significant scoring boost, particularly from beyond the arc, as he returns from a two-game absence.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) is questionable for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Powell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence due to a shoulder injury. With rookie standout Caleb Wilson (hand) going on the shelf for multiple weeks, Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro should both have a chance to step up for the Bulls.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Spurs,Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Powell will miss his second consecutive contest due to a shoulder injury. Head coach Tiago Splitter stated that the 33-year-old veteran is "probably at 70 percent," so there's a chance he won't play Friday against Atlanta. In the meantime, Isaac Okoro is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with significant usage bumps going to Josh Giddey and Caleb Wilson (hip), assuming the latter is cleared to play.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Spurs.
items.story: Powell didn't suit up for Sunday's 127-121 loss to Philadelphia, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. Isaac Okoro took his place in the starting lineup, and that will likely remain the case if Powell misses a second consecutive game Wednesday.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Powell was a late addition to the injury report Sunday morning due to right shoulder inflammation and soreness, and he'll miss his first game of the season. The veteran swingman's next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Spurs. Isaac Okoro will get the starting nod in Powell's stead. Additionally, Buddy Hield and Tre Jones could also see increased minutes.

items.headline: Powell (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Powell wasn't included on Chicago's initial injury report but is now in jeopardy of missing his first game of the season due to right shoulder inflammation and soreness. If the veteran swingman is unable to play, Buddy Hield and Isaac Okoro would be candidates to see increased burn.

items.headline: Powell posted 18 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-11 FT), three rebounds and two steals across 29 minutes in Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Powell struggled with his shooting efficiency, and his lack of assists also limited his fantasy production. However, despite the inconsistency in his scoring numbers, there's a solid floor since Powell has scored at least 15 points in every game so far. He's reached the 20-point threshold twice. He should remain one of Chicago's go-to players on offense alongside young starlets Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson.

items.headline: Powell finished with 30 points (10-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 6-9 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 37 minutes in Wednesday's 133-127 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Powell ended with his highest-scoring game of the 2026-27 campaign Wednesday. He is still a threat from deep. However, Powell has shown growth as a defender and is now averaging a career-best 2.2 steals in his first five games as a Bull.

items.headline: Powell contributed 18 points (4-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds, three assists and four steals across 33 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: The veteran wing led all players in steals on the night, and only Trae Young drained more three-pointers. Powell is looking exactly as advertised to begin his tenure with the Wizards, averaging 19.3 points, 3.7 boards, 2.3 threes, 2.0 steals and 1.7 assists through three games, and his 8.3 three-point attempts a contest would actually be a career high if he can maintain that volume.

items.headline: Powell ended with 15 points (3-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 7-11 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 22 minutes during Wednesday's 135-92 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Powell didn't have the most efficient night from the field, but he finished tied for the third-most points on the Bulls thanks to his seven made free throws, though he connected on only 63.6 percent of his attempts from the charity stripe. Powell averaged over 21.0 points per game in each of the last two seasons, but his offensive output may be limited while playing alongside the young core of Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and rookie fourth-overall pick Caleb Wilson.

items.headline: Powell totaled 16 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-10 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 125-104 preseason win over Milwaukee.
items.story: After not seeing the court in Sunday's contest, Powell returned to the starting lineup Wednesday and did much of his damage at the charity stripe. The shooting guard has scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances. After averaging 21.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 58 regular-season appearances with Miami last season, Powell should have ample scoring opportunities as a veteran presence on a young Chicago team during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Powell is not in the starting lineup for Sunday's preseason game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Powell started each of the previous two preseason games, but he is not starting Sunday. Isaac Okoro will enter the starting five in his place.

items.headline: Powell registered 17 points (3-6 FG, 1-2 FT, 10-12 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal over 19 minutes during the Bulls' 104-100 preseason loss to the Grizzlies on Friday.
items.story: Powell attempted only six field goals during Friday's exhibition game, but thanks to his work at the charity stripe, he finished as the Bulls' second-leading scorer behind rookie Caleb Wilson (21 points). Powell inked a two-year contract with the Bulls in July following his 2025-26 All-Star campaign with the Heat and will form a starting backcourt with Josh Giddey for the upcoming season. Matas Buzelis left Friday's game early due to an ankle injury, and although it was likely a precautionary move to leave him off the court the rest of the way, it's an injury that could positively impact Powell's usage early on in the season.

items.headline: Powell recorded 14 points (3-4 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one assist and one steal in 14 minutes during Wednesday's 124-117 preseason victory over Phoenix.
items.story: Powell made an immediate impact in his first preseason appearance with Chicago, connecting on three triples. The veteran wing appears poised to provide the Bulls with an established perimeter scoring threat alongside Josh Giddey, though his offensive role will become clearer as the preseason progresses.

items.headline: Powell agreed to a two-year, $45 million contract with the Bulls on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Powell has averaged at least 21 points per game in each of the past two seasons, including his first All-Star appearance during his age-32 campaign with the Heat in 2025-26. However, the veteran will now join his third team in as many years, likely serving as the starting shooting guard next to Josh Giddey in Chicago's backcourt.

items.headline: Powell is unlikely to re-sign with the Heat this offseason, Shams Charania reported Tuesday on The Pat McAfee Show.
items.story: Powell is an unrestricted free agent this summer, and it sounds like Miami is preparing to go in a different direction as it tries to manage its payroll following Monday's acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo (calf). The All-Star guard averaged 21.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 3.0 three-pointers in 32.6 minutes per contest through 60 regular-season games last year, so his market value could be higher than the Heat are willing or even able to meet.

items.headline: Powell recorded 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 19 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Tournament loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Powell was limited to just 19 minutes, ending what was otherwise a positive season for the veteran. He finished with averages of 21.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.7 three-pointers, doing enough to earn his first All-Star nod. Assuming he returns to Miami next season, expect to see Powell playing as the second or third option on offense, flirting with 20 points per game on most nights.

items.headline: Powell (groin) is listed as available for Sunday's game versus Atlanta.
items.story: Powell has appeared in only two of Miami's last seven games, most recently missing Friday's 140-117 win over Washington. Despite his availability, he might come off the bench. However, with Pelle Larsson (leg) ruled out, Powell could find himself back in the starting lineup for the first time since the 149-128 loss to Cleveland on March 27.

items.headline: Dybantsa amassed 16 points (4-10 FG, 8-11 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Dybantsa has averaged 19 points, eight rebounds and four assists over his last five games while logging 34 minutes. His six assists matched Friday's output, suggesting growing playmaking responsibilities. Consistent minutes and versatile production strengthen his fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Dybantsa posted 20 points (9-18 FG, 2-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals in 37 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago.
items.story: Dybantsa has now poured in 20 or more points in three straight outings, pushing his season averages to 16.3 points to go along with 6.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals over 33.8 minutes across 13 games. Over this three-game span, the first overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has generated averages of 21.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 2.0 steals in 35.7 minutes.

items.headline: Dybantsa ended Wednesday's 103-99 victory over Toronto with 23 points (9-17 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 38 minutes.
items.story: Dybantsa established new career highs in points and rebounds while recording his first NBA double-double, helping Washington snap an eight-game losing streak. The rookie has now scored 16, 21 and 23 points in his last three appearances, a welcome development and a sign of some much-needed consistency. The Wizards' commitment to giving him substantial opportunities, even with several established veterans in the rotation, is encouraging as well. The offensive consistency is still developing, but performances like Wednesday's demonstrate his considerable upside.

items.headline: Dybantsa contributed 16 points (6-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal in 30 minutes during Sunday's 147-119 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Dybantsa struggled with his efficiency, making just six of his 18 field-goal attempts as Washington suffered its seventh straight defeat. The rookie continues to receive substantial offensive opportunities despite his inconsistency, which is encouraging for his long-term development. However, his fantasy production still depends heavily on scoring volume. He's averaging 15.1 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game in his first 10 appearances while shooting just 40 percent from the field and 24.3 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Dybantsa posted 21 points (8-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 37 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Dybantsa was Washington's second-leading scorer, and his rebounding and shot-blocking added to a solid line. However, his five turnovers were the downside. The rookie is seeing a heavy workload, and his scoring volume gives him plenty of fantasy appeal as he adjusts to the NBA.

items.headline: Dybantsa posted 19 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), six rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes in Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Dybantsa led Washington in scoring despite the lopsided result and reached double-digit scoring numbers for the fifth time in his first six NBA contests. The rookie's workload remains encouraging, though efficiency and secondary contributions will determine his consistency. He's scoring 16.0 points per game but shooting just 42.5 percent from the field, including 27.8 percent from three.

items.headline: Dybantsa amassed 11 points (3-13 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and four steals across 36 minutes during Friday's 139-132 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Dybantsa flirted with his first career double-double, while also adding a career-high four steals. After a delayed start to the campaign, Dybantsa has started his career by producing modest numbers on both ends of the floor. In five appearances, he has averaged 15.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 31.7 minutes per game. However, efficiency remains an issue, as he's currently shooting 41.5 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Head coach Brian Keefe said Wednesday that Dybantsa (ankle) is no longer on a minutes restriction, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dybantsa missed Washington's first four regular-season games due to a sprained left ankle, though he's appeared in each of the team's last three outings while operating under a minutes restriction. The rookie No. 1 overall pick has yet to score fewer than 17 points in a game and is averaging 19.0 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.3 steals across 30.0 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Dybantsa logged 21 points (7-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three steals in 33 minutes during Monday's 103-94 victory over the Magic.
items.story: The rookie was aggressive offensively, attempting 17 shots and converting all six of his free throws. Dybantsa also made his presence felt defensively with three steals, giving him a well-rounded fantasy performance despite his inefficient perimeter shooting. His substantial workload and involvement alongside Washington's established veterans are encouraging signs for his early-season fantasy value.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) will remain on a minutes restriction in Friday's game against the Hornets, Greg Finberg of The Wizards Podcast reports.
items.story: The rookie No. 1 overall pick missed the Wizards' first four regular-season games due to a left ankle sprain. He made his NBA regular-season debut in Wednesday's loss to Cleveland, posting 19 points, two rebounds and two assists in 27 minutes, and it appears likely he'll hover around that mark again Friday.

items.headline: Dybantsa recorded 19 points (8-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and two assists across 27 minutes in Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Dybantsa missed Washington's first four regular-season games due to a left ankle sprain but made his NBA regular-season debut Wednesday. The rookie first overall pick was under a minutes restriction, though he still finished as the Wizards' leading scorer in an efficient performance from two-point range. He should operate as one of the Wizards' top scoring options, though it wouldn't be surprising to see him remain on a minutes restriction in the short term.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) will be on a minutes restriction in Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dybantsa will appear in his first regular-season game Wednesday after missing time due to an ankle injury. However, head coach Brian Keefe indicated the rookie will be on a minutes restriction, which could considerably lower his statistical ceiling.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) will make his NBA debut Wednesday against the Cavaliers, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Washington will finally unveil the No. 1 overall pick Wednesday. With this being his debut, Dybantsa may face restrictions in his first game back. Bilal Coulibaly may see reduced minutes with this news.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) was present at Wednesday's morning shootaround, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The rookie forward remains questionable on the latest injury report. However, he's trending in the right direction and could be cleared to make his NBA debut against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game versus Cleveland.
items.story: The rookie No. 1 overall pick has a chance to make his highly anticipated NBA debut Wednesday. His eventual return from an ankle sprain will likely push Bilal Coulibaly into a reserve role, though it wouldn't be surprising to see Dybantsa operate under a minutes restriction when he returns.

items.headline: Dybantsa, who has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hornets, is progressing well from a left ankle sprain and will take part in on-court activities Tuesday, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dybantsa hasn't been cleared to make his NBA debut after picking up a left ankle sprain in the team's preseason finale. However, he's trending in the right direction according to coach Brian Keefe, hinting that a return either Wednesday against Cleveland or Friday against Charlotte could be on the table. Washington should have another update on the rookie's status after he goes through practice Tuesday.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Dybantsa will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against Cleveland. With the rookie No. 1 overall pick sidelined, Bilal Coulibaly and Tre Johnson will likely continue seeing increased playing time.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Dybantsa will miss a third straight game due to a left ankle sprain, with his next chance to make his regular-season debut coming Monday at Charlotte. Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Khris Middleton are candidates to see an uptick in minutes in Dybantsa's stead.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Raptors, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The rookie No. 1 pick remains day-to-day, according to coach Brian Keefe. Friday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, and considering the day-to-day designation, a return against the Bulls on Saturday could be on the table. In the meantime, the Wizards will likely continue to lean on Bilal Coulibaly.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) will not debut Wednesday against the Bucks, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dybantsa remained limited at Tuesday's practice and is still considered day-to-day after picking up the sprain during the final preseason game Friday. It sounds like the Wizards are being extra cautious with the No. 1 overall pick. In the meantime, Tre Johnson, Bilal Coulibaly and Will Riley could see additional minutes.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) participated in shooting drills during Monday's practice but remains day-to-day, Ben Strober of 106.7 The Fan Washington reports.
items.story: Coach Brian Keefe confirmed the rookie was able to get some shooting work in, though it's unclear whether he's ready to resume full-contact activities. Dybantsa's availability for Washington's regular-season opener remains uncertain, and his participation in upcoming practices should provide a better indication of his readiness.

items.headline: Head coach Brian Keefe said Sunday that Dybantsa is day-to-day with an ankle sprain, Kyle Williams of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
items.story: Dybantsa exited Friday's preseason finale with the ankle injury and did not return. The rookie No. 1 overall pick can be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bucks until the Wizards provide an update on his status. If he's forced to miss time, Tre Johnson, Bilal Coulibaly and Will Riley would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Dybantsa (ankle) won't return to Friday's preseason game against the Pelicans, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports. He'll finish with 12 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and one block in 15 minutes.
items.story: Dybantsa rolled his ankle before walking to the locker room in the second quarter of the Wizards' preseason finale, and he won't return for precautionary reasons. The rookie No. 1 overall pick's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bucks.

items.headline: Dybantsa exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's preseason game against the Pelicans due to an apparent ankle injury, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dybantsa appeared to roll his ankle before walking to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light, though it wouldn't be surprising to see the Wizards exercise caution ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: Dybantsa recorded 14 points (5-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists, a steal and a block across 25 minutes in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Dybantsa overcame a slow start to deliver an encouraging performance, becoming more involved offensively during the second half. His shooting efficiency remained inconsistent, but he contributed in several categories while grabbing four offensive rebounds. The rookie is slated to open the 2026-27 season as the Wizards' starting small forward and should see consistent playing time right out of the gate in his first year in the league.

items.headline: Dybantsa recorded 14 points (4-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 6-10 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one steal across 23 minutes in Saturday's 114-108 preseason win over Detroit in overtime.
items.story: Dybantsa got to the charity stripe often but wasn't very efficient. Still, the rookie first overall pick tied for second on the team in scoring and finished second in rebounds behind Anthony Davis. Dybantsa has scored in double figures in back-to-back games to begin the preseason, totaling 25 points, nine rebounds, five steals and four assists in 46 minutes.

items.headline: Dybantsa recorded 11 points (5-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-3 FT), two rebounds, two assists and four steals across 23 minutes in Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Dybantsa made an impact on the defensive end, leading both teams with four steals while committing no turnovers. The young forward was less effective offensively, missing all three of his attempts from beyond the arc and needing 11 shots to score 11 points. Mistakes are bound to happen for rookie players, and Dybantsa will be allowed to play through his.

items.headline: Dybantsa (rest) will be competing for a starting role during training camp this fall.
items.story: After Dybantsa went first overall in the 2026 NBA Draft, there's a good chance the Wizards will want to showcase him in the first unit immediately. That said, Bilal Coulibaly was a full-time starter a year ago, and Washington also has incumbent veteran Khris Middleton on the roster. Regardless, Dybantsa finds himself in a rather favorable situation playing alongside veteran stars Trae Young (quad) and Anthony Davis (finger).

items.headline: The Wizards are shutting down Dybantsa (rest) for the team's final three Summer League games, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
items.story: Dybantsa was able to make a pair of Las Vegas Summer League appearances before being shut down. The 2026 No. 1 overall pick will now set his sights toward training camp in the fall ahead of his highly anticipated rookie campaign in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Jazz will decline Collier's $4.99 million team option for the 2027-28 season, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: The decision puts Collier on track to become an unrestricted free agent next summer rather than remain under contract with Utah for a fourth season. The young guard has averaged 9.9 points, 6.6 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals across his first three NBA campaigns, establishing himself as a capable playmaker. His impending free agency creates some uncertainty about his long-term destination, though it shouldn't immediately affect his fantasy outlook for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Collier recorded six points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and six assists in 13 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Collier finished second on the team in assists despite his limited playing time, and he now has 13 dimes over his last two outings. With Darryn Peterson and Keyonte George commanding most of the minutes in Utah's backcourt, Collier is averaging just 15.7 minutes per game, which would be a career low in his third NBA season.

items.headline: Collier contributed 11 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five assists, five steals and three rebounds across 22 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Collier was one of seven Jazz players to score in double figures but made his presence felt in other facets of the game. The USC product tallied a game-high five steals while matching Darryn Peterson with a team-high five assists. Keyonte George is penciled in as the starting point guard, but Collier should maintain a notable role off the bench, coming off a 2025-26 season in which he averaged 11.7 points, 7.2 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 25.7 minutes across 59 appearances (19 starts).

items.headline: Collier's ballhandling and playmaking stand out among Utah's current personnel, president of basketball operations Austin Ainge said Monday, Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City reports.
items.story: Collier established himself as a high-level distributor in his second season, averaging 8.7 assists across 78 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. Utah added several new pieces during the offseason, but Collier's ability to create for others gives him a distinct skill set that could help him remain involved in the Jazz's backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) faces increased competition for backcourt minutes after Utah drafted Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The second-year guard flashed strong playmaking ability during his sophomore campaign with 7.2 assists across 59 regular-season appearances, but Peterson is expected to assume a significant offensive role immediately. Collier could still maintain value as a secondary ballhandler, although his ceiling may depend on how the Jazz distribute minutes among their young guards.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Collier will miss a 13th straight game due to a left hamstring strain. The 21-year-old point guard will finish the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 11.7 points, 7.2 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.1 steals across 25.7 minutes per tilt over 59 regular-season outings (19 starts).

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is listed as out for Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Collier has missed Utah's last 11 contests. With only one game left this season for the Jazz after Friday's clash with the Grizzlies, it appears there's a good chance he won't be back on the floor until the 2026-27 campaign. Keyonte George (hamstring) is also still out, so Ace Bailey (knee), who is off the injury report, might find himself back at the point guard spot.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is out for Tuesday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: It's not clear if Collier will be able to get healthy in time to appear in one of Utah's final regular-season contests, but he's quickly running out of time. His next chance to return from a hamstring strain will arrive Friday against Memphis.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: At this point, it's hard to tell if Collier will be back in the lineup before the end of the 2025-26 campaign. However, with Elijah Harkless (hamstring) and Keyonte George (hamstring) also sidelined Sunday, Kennedy Chandler, Bez Mbeng and Cody Williams will likely absorb most of the minutes in the backcourt versus Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is out for Friday's game versus Houston.
items.story: A left hamstring injury is costing Collier a ninth consecutive contest Friday. Fresh off inking a two-year contract with the Jazz, Bez Mbeng should see the bulk of the minutes at point guard.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Collier continues to miss game action while rehabbing from a left hamstring injury. The Jazz have yet to provide an update on his recovery, so it's unclear if he'll return to play this season. The second-year point guard can be considered doubtful for Friday's game in Houston.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers, Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City reports.
items.story: Collier will miss a seventh straight game due to a left hamstring injury. His next chance to suit up comes Wednesday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Collier will miss a sixth straight game due to a left hamstring injury. His next chance to play is Monday against the Cavaliers, but the Jazz have not provided a medical update for the second-year point guard in quite some time.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) has been ruled out for Friday's game in Denver, Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City reports.
items.story: Collier will miss a fifth consecutive game due to left hamstring injury management, and the Jazz haven't provided a clear update regarding where the second-year point guard stands in his recovery. Given that Friday's contest is the front end of a back-to-back set for the Jazz, fantasy managers should prepare for Collier to remain out for Saturday's game in Phoenix.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Collier will remain sidelined while on the mend from a left hamstring injury. His next chance to return will arrive Friday in Denver.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) won't play Monday versus the Raptors.
items.story: This will be Collier's third consecutive game on the inactive list, and with Keyonte George (hamstring) also out, it'll be Elijah Harkless, Kennedy Chandler and Bez Mbeng holding down the fort in the backcourt. Collier's next chance to play will come Wednesday versus Washington.

items.headline: Collier (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: The second-year point guard will join Keyonte George (hamstring) on the inactive list for a second consecutive contest, and the former's next opportunity to play will come Monday against Toronto. With Collier out, Elijah Harkless, Bez Mbeng and Kennedy Chandler are candidates for expanded roles.

items.headline: Collier is out for Thursday's game against the Bucks with left hamstring soreness.
items.story: Collier is sitting out the second leg of Utah's back-to-back and can be considered day-to-day ahead of Saturday's matchup with the 76ers. Elijah Harkless and Bez Mbeng will likely form a timeshare for minutes at point guard Thursday.

items.headline: Collier (knee) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Collier left Sunday's loss to the Kings due to a right knee contusion, but he's good to go for Wednesday. Over his last seven appearances, Collier has averaged 17.6 points, 6.6 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 25.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Collier won't return to Sunday's game against the Kings due to a right knee contusion.
items.story: Collier exited partway through the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest and will not be able to return. He concludes the contest with 21 points (9-21 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and a block in 24 minutes. Bez Mbeng figures to get extra minutes down the stretch with Collier out.

items.headline: Collier ended with 17 points (6-15 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, nine assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Friday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Back in the starting five for the second time in five March appearances, Collier came up just shy of his 11th double-double of the season, which would have tied the total from his rookie campaign. The second-year guard missed a couple games last week due to an illness, but in nine games (five starts) since the All-Star break he's averaging 17.1 points, 6.4 assists, 1.9 boards and 1.6 steals in 26.6 minutes.

items.headline: Collier will start Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The second-year point guard will step into the first unit due to the absence of Keyonte George, who is expected to miss at least two weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain. As a starter this season (16 games), Collier has averaged 15.3 points, 8.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 31.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Collier (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Collier was unable to play against the Warriors on Monday due to an illness, and he missed the Jazz's prior game against the Bucks on Saturday while attending to a personal matter. The 2024 first-rounder is on track to return Wednesday, and he could start against New York if Keyonte George (illness) is unable to play.

items.headline: Collier (illness) is out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Collier was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. Meanwhile, Keyonte George (illness) remains questionable. With this news, Elijah Harkless, Cody Williams and Svi Mykhailiuk could step into larger roles.

items.headline: Collier (illness) is questionable for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Both Collier and Keyonte George were late additions to the injury report due to illness. The Jazz could be very shorthanded, meaning players like Elijah Harkless, Cody Williams and Svi Mykhailiuk could step into larger roles.

items.headline: Collier (personal) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Collier missed Saturday's loss to Milwaukee due to personal reasons, though he's set to return to action Monday. Over his last five games (two starts), the second-year point guard has averaged 17.4 points, 7.2 assists, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 27.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Collier (personal) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Collier will miss his first game since Nov. 5 for personal reasons, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against Golden State. Elijah Harkless, Brice Sensabaugh and Svi Mykhailiuk are candidates for increased minutes due to Collier being sidelined.

items.headline: Collier had 27 points (11-18 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds and 11 assists across 29 minutes during Thursday's 122-112 victory over Washington.
items.story: Collier moved to the starting lineup due to the absence of Keyonte George (right ankle management), and he made the most of the opportunity. Three of Collier's games with at least 20 points have come off the bench this season, but he stood out in more areas than just scoring. This was also his 10th game with double-digit assists in 2025-26.

items.headline: Collier is in the Jazz's starting lineup against the Wizards on Thursday.
items.story: Keyonte George has been ruled out for Thursday's game due to right ankle injury management, so Collier will enter the starting lineup for the 16th time this season. Collier started in nine of the Jazz's first 10 games of February, and over that span he averaged 17.3 points, 9.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 steals over 33.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Collier provided 18 points (5-10 FG, 8-8 FT), five assists, one block and three steals in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 106-102 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Collier gave the Jazz the spark off the bench that they needed during Wednesday's close loss, with the second-year pro leading the team with five dimes while finishing as Utah's second-leading scorer behind Keyonte George (30 points). Collier has taken on a larger role as the season has progressed, and since Feb. 1 he has averaged 17.1 points, 8.8 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 2.2 steals over 32.0 minutes per game in 13 outings (nine starts).

items.headline: Collier won't start Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: With Keyonte George (ankle) back in action, Collier will slide to the second unit. The second-year point guard has averaged 9.3 points, 6.7 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 23.3 minutes per game across 36 outings off the bench so far this season.

items.headline: Collier finished with 11 points (5-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, seven assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Thursday's 129-118 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: It doesn't sound like the Jazz are in a rush to bring Keyonte George (ankle) back, extending Collier's runway in the first unit. Collier has started nine of his last 10 outings, averaging 17.3 points, 9.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 steals in 33.7 minutes per game during this stretch.

items.headline: Collier recorded 24 points (9-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two blocks and four steals across 25 minutes during Friday's 123-114 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Collier wreaked havoc on the defensive end, tying career highs in steals and blocks, and this was the fourth game of his career with at least four steals. Collier has been flirting with top-40 value over the past eight games with averages of 18.1 points, 10.9 dimes and 2.5 swipes per contest.

items.headline: Collier contributed 15 points (3-8 FG, 9-12 FT), two rebounds, nine assists and three steals in 36 minutes before fouling out of Thursday's 135-119 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Making his third straight start and sixth in seven February games while Keyonte George (ankle) remains sidelined, Collier just missed picking up his 10th double-double of the season. Four of those nine double-doubles have come this month, and he's averaging 17.3 points, 11.7 assists, 3.4 boards and 2.3 steals in February. The Jazz haven't been rushing George back into the lineup as they try to stay near the bottom of the standings, and the top of the lottery, so Collier's role won't necessarily shrink on the other side of the All-Star break.

items.headline: Collier provided 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), one rebound, 14 assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-93 win over the Kings.
items.story: Collier turned in an efficient shooting performance, resulting in his 10th straight game in double figures. He's also been distributing the ball at a high level lately and has tallied a double-double in four of his last five matchups. Collier will continue to run the Utah offense until Keyonte George (ankle) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Collier is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Collier came off the bench in Saturday's contest but will return to the starting lineup Monday with Keyonte George (ankle) inactive. Collier has started four of the Jazz's past 10 games, averaging 15.6 points, 9.5 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.8 minutes per contest during that stretch.

items.headline: Collier is not in the Jazz's starting lineup against the Magic on Saturday, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Collier was the starting point guard in the Jazz's last three games and put together some strong performances, including a 22-assist game against the Pacers on Tuesday and a 25-point double-double Thursday against the Hawks. Keyonte George (ankle) was cleared to return from a three-game absence but will be restricted to approximately 24 minutes, so Collier should continue to operate in an expanded role despite his demotion to the bench.

items.headline: Collier produced 25 points (11-22 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and three steals in 48 minutes during Thursday's 121-119 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Collier continues to see elite usage with Keyonte George (ankle) sidelined. The 22-year-old didn't miss a second of game action for a second straight appearance, and he piled on the production across the board yet again. He's now recorded a double-double in back-to-back games and set a new season high in rebounds Thursday.

items.headline: Peterson posted six points (3-9 FG, 0-5 3Pt), three rebounds and five assists over 25 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Peterson's scoring has cooled considerably after four consecutive 20-point performances earlier this month. He's averaged 13.4 points in 28.2 minutes over his last five games, but Lauri Markkanen's (hand) absence should continue providing opportunities for the rookie.

items.headline: Peterson produced 20 points (7-20 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block over 32 minutes in Friday's 111-101 loss to the Suns.
items.story: This was an excellent bounce-back performance from Peterson, who was limited to just 11 points over 19 foul-plagued minutes in Wednesday's win over the Lakers. He recorded the first double-double of his career, and to put a bow on the sterling outing, the rookie finished the game with just one turnover.

items.headline: Peterson ended Wednesday's 109-97 win over the Lakers with 11 points (3-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), one rebound and three assists over 19 minutes.
items.story: Peterson made an efficient contribution in limited playing time, although his 19-minute workload was considerably smaller than those of Keyonte George and Ace Bailey. The rookie continues to compete for opportunities in Utah's crowded backcourt, and his ability to generate offense remains encouraging. While this game was a step in the wrong direction, Peterson had played at least 30 minutes in each of his previous 10 appearances, so fantasy managers shouldn't be overly concerned about the sudden drop in playing time unless it becomes a trend in the following weeks.

items.headline: Peterson logged 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Peterson never found his shooting touch, but he still finished with a decent total as the Jazz snapped their long losing streak. The No. 2 overall pick has been one of the few bright spots in a rough start for the club, averaging 17.1 points as a rookie. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jaren Jackson (knee) sidelined, Peterson should continue to get a heavy share of the offense.

items.headline: Peterson recorded 17 points (7-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal over 34 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Peterson didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance in Sunday's loss. However, the rookie guard still finished as Utah's second-leading scorer while chipping in multiple combined steals-plus-blocks for a third straight game. He's scored at least 17 points in six straight games, during which he's averaged 23.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks in 32.8 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Peterson finished with 28 points (9-20 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 6-7 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Peterson led Utah in scoring while knocking down four triples and contributing across multiple categories. The rookie guard attempted a team-high 20 shots, highlighting his prominent offensive role despite the defeat. Although his efficiency from beyond the arc left room for improvement, Peterson's combination of scoring volume, rebounding and defensive production makes him an intriguing fantasy option as he continues to develop.

items.headline: Peterson finished with 22 points (7-19 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 123-108 loss to the Magic.
items.story: This was Peterson's fourth straight 20-plus-point performance, and he again led his team in shot attempts. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) set to miss at least the next month, there's a massive hole to fill in Utah's offense, but Peterson looks ready to step into a larger role offensively.
