items.headline: Peterson fouled out of Tuesday's 115-109 loss to the Heat after recording 25 points (10-19 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 31 minutes.
items.story: Peterson came close to posting a new career high yet again after scoring his season-high 26 Tuesday, and the rookie is starting to look comfortable as Utah's go-to scorer. The turnovers and fouls are still part of the learning curve, but with three starters out, the Jazz are giving him all the touches he can handle. Utah hosts Orlando on Wednesday to finish a back-to-back.

items.headline: Peterson delivered 26 points (11-21 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists and a steal across 35 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Peterson carried a substantial offensive workload, attempting a team-high 21 shots, and he seems to be finding his footing offensively while scoring at least 20 points in back-to-back games for the first time in his career. The rookie's current playing time and newfound prominent scoring role remain encouraging indicators for his fantasy outlook. He's also surpassed the 15-point mark in four of his last six outings, averaging 17.0 points per game in that stretch.

items.headline: Peterson delivered 21 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two steals and three blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 112-100 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Peterson produced an impressive two-way performance, supplementing efficient scoring with five combined defensive stats. His five assists also highlighted his growing contributions as a playmaker. The rookie's ability to contribute in several categories gives him intriguing fantasy upside, particularly if he maintains a consistent workload near 30 minutes. He's scored at least 14 points in four of his last six games, averaging 15.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Peterson amassed 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, three blocks and three steals across 33 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Peterson struggled with his overall efficiency but delivered an impressive defensive performance, combining for six steals and blocks while leading Utah with six assists. The rookie also logged a team-high 33 minutes and committed just one turnover despite handling substantial playmaking responsibilities. His ability to contribute across the board gives him considerable fantasy upside even when his shot isn't falling.

items.headline: Peterson amassed 16 points (6-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 36 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The 16 points led the Jazz on the afternoon, as only two of his teammates even scored in double digits. Peterson is quickly getting the hang of this NBA thing after being the second overall pick in the 2026 Draft, scoring at least 14 points in four of the last five games while averaging 14.2 points, 4.4 boards, 2.8 assists, 2.0 threes and 1.2 steals, but his 35.2 percent shooting during that stretch indicates he still has plenty to work on.

items.headline: Peterson provided 18 points (4-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Peterson struggled to find his rhythm from the field but compensated with three triples and a perfect showing at the charity stripe. The rookie displayed his scoring potential despite playing considerably fewer minutes than fellow starters Keyonte George and Ace Bailey. Peterson's perimeter shooting and ability to draw fouls should help support his fantasy value as he develops.

items.headline: Peterson (nose) started the second quarter of Wednesday's game against the Spurs, per the broadcast.
items.story: Peterson took a shot to the head and exited to the locker room with a bloody nose in the first quarter. However, he returned to the bench shortly thereafter and started the second quarter.

items.headline: Peterson exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to an apparent head injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: The rookie guard took a shot to the head on a dunk attempt and appeared to have a bloody nose. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Peterson finished with eight points (4-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 30 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Peterson was the only Jazz starter to have a positive plus-minus, despite his shot not falling. The second overall pick in the 2026 draft added four combined steals and blocks, representing his first tallies in each statistical category to begin his career. Through three outings, Peterson is averaging 10.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.3 minutes.

items.headline: Peterson amassed nine points (3-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 loss to Memphis.
items.story: The No. 2 overall pick started at shooting guard in his first regular-season appearance, receiving the third-most minutes among Utah's starters. Peterson attempted just seven shots and struggled to establish himself offensively, but his substantial workload suggests the Jazz intend to give him considerable opportunities to develop. His scoring volume should increase as he becomes more comfortable alongside Keyonte George, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson.

items.headline: Peterson recorded 13 points (4-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, six assists and a steal across 29 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Peterson struggled with his shooting efficiency but made meaningful contributions elsewhere. The young guard finished tied for the team lead with six assists while collecting six rebounds, the second-best mark on the team, showcasing his versatility despite an inconsistent offensive performance. He also committed just one turnover in a team-high 29 minutes, an encouraging sign for his decision-making. Peterson's ability to contribute across multiple categories could help him earn a significant role in Utah's backcourt as the regular season approaches, and as a rookie on a rebuilding team, he'll be given every opportunity to log heavy minutes. He's expected to be the Jazz's starting shooting guard come Opening Night against the Grizzlies on Wednesday.

items.headline: Peterson produced 14 points (5-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal across 24 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over San Antonio.
items.story: Peterson put together a solid offensive effort, finishing as Utah's leading scorer in a well-rounded team victory. After a quiet three-point performance in his preseason debut Oct. 4, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has fared much better in his two most recent appearances. The Kansas product is penciled in as the Jazz's starting shooting guard for the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Peterson tallied 23 points (10-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes in Tuesday's 93-79 preseason loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: With Lauri Markkanen (neck) out and Keyonte George and Jaren Jackson having their minutes monitored, Peterson got some time to shine as the main man on offense for the Jazz. Despite going 1-for-6 from three-point range, he still converted over 50 percent of his shot attempts, and it was nice to see him take 18 shots after attempting just five field goals in the preseason opener.

items.headline: Peterson accumulated three points (1-5 FG, 1-2 FT, 0-2 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and one steal in 22 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason victory over Denver.
items.story: Petersen made his NBA debut, sliding straight into the starting lineup, as expected. Although he struggled with his efficiency, the fact that he played a team-high 22 minutes is an encouraging sign. He should open the regular season as a key piece in the rotation, putting him firmly on the fantasy radar. As a rookie point guard, managers should expect some ups and downs when it comes to his shooting splits. However, his role alone should lend itself to plenty of opportunities, making him a viable target in the 100 range of drafts.

items.headline: Peterson has impressed veteran teammate Jusuf Nurkic with his maturity and work ethic during training camp, according to Jazz reporter Chandler Holt.
items.story: Nurkic said that in 13 NBA seasons he hasn't seen a player enter the league with Peterson's level of maturity, adding that the rookie spends so much time working that Utah has nearly had to tell him to stay out of the gym. Peterson is preparing for his first NBA season after being selected No. 2 overall in the 2026 NBA Draft and should have an opportunity to take on a substantial role immediately.

items.headline: Peterson (rest) is set to compete for a starting role during training camp in the fall.
items.story: The rookie No. 2 overall pick has Ace Bailey to overcome for the top spot at shooting guard with the Jazz. Whether he starts or comes off the bench right off the bat, Peterson is certainly primed for a significant role for Utah in 2026-27. Over five Summer League appearances, the 19-year-old stood out with averages of 23.0 points, 5.2 assists, 3.2 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals per game.

items.headline: Diabate finished with 21 points (9-12 FG, 3-5 FT), 15 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 30 minutes during Friday's 111-97 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: This was Diabate's fourth double-double of the year, and his fourth straight game pulling down double-digit rebounds. He's been providing mid-round value on the season with averages of 9.6 points, 10.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks per game on 63.4 percent shooting from the field and 70.0 percent at the line.

items.headline: Diabate had five points (2-2 FG, 1-2 FT), 16 rebounds, two assists and one block over 38 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Diabate dominated the glass for a game-high rebound total and didn't miss from the field. He also found Naz Reid for the overtime three-pointer that briefly put the Hornets ahead. The energetic big man has been a fixture in Charlotte's frontcourt since returning from a short absence earlier this month, averaging 9.7 rebounds this season.

items.headline: Diabate recorded 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, two assists and three blocks in 26 minutes during Sunday's 113-105 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Diabate turned in an efficient scoring line and was one of three Charlotte starters to finish in double figures. He also contributed in a big way on the boards, leading his team in rebounds on the way to his third double-double of the 2026-27 season. It was nice to see Diabate more involved as a rim protector, as he tied his season high in swats after registering one total block in his previous two appearances entering Sunday.

items.headline: Diabate provided seven points (3-7 FG, 1-2 FT), 13 rebounds, two assists and one block across 32 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Scoring has never been the main attraction with Diabate, and that hasn't changed this season. Instead, he's developed into a useful specialist by averaging 9.5 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 0.9 blocks while shooting 61.0 percent from the field. Those numbers give him legitimate value in category leagues, particularly for managers who can afford to sacrifice some offensive production in exchange for rebounding and defensive consistency.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) is listed as available for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Diabate is returning from a two-game absence Thursday due to a quadriceps injury. Ryan Kalkbrenner is likely heading to the bench, which causes a major hit to his streaming value. Over nine games, Diabate has averaged 8.9 points, 9.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.9 blocks in 28.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) is listed as probable for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Diabate is expected to return from a two-game absence Thursday, which would leave fewer minutes available for Ryan Kalkbrenner. Through nine regular-season games, Diabate has averaged 8.9 points, 9.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.9 blocks in 28.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) has been downgraded to out for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The Hornets initially appeared optimistic about the big man's status for Monday, as he was added to the injury report as questionable Sunday. However, he was downgraded to doubtful earlier in the day Monday and has since been ruled out. The Michigan product will miss his second straight matchup due to right quadriceps tendinopathy.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) has been downgraded to doubtful for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Diabate has been downgraded from questionable to doubtful and will likely miss a second straight game, opening the door for Ryan Kalkbrenner to draw another start. In the likely event that he's ultimately ruled out, Diabate's next chance to suit up will come Thursday in Phoenix.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) is questionable for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Diabate could miss a second straight game due to a right quad injury. If he is unavailable, Ryan Kalkbrenner could see extra minutes.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Boston, according to the Hornets' official injury report.
items.story: Diabate's absence will leave Charlotte shorthanded in the frontcourt against the Celtics. Ryan Kalkbrenner could see additional opportunities at center, while other available big men may also absorb minutes. Diabate's next opportunity to play will come Monday against Cleveland.

items.headline: Diabate (quadriceps) is questionable for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Diabate is in danger of missing his first game of the season. Ryan Kalkbrenner would likely be called upon to make a spot start at center for the Hornets if Diabate is sidelined, with Royce O'Neale likely mixing in as a small-ball center in this case.

items.headline: Diabate closed with seven points (3-6 FG, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals in 24 minutes during Monday's 124-91 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: With a strong start to the year, Diabate seems to have pulled way ahead of Ryan Kalkbrenner for Charlotte's starting job at center. Diabate has come down with at least eight boards in seven of his first eight games, posting at least one steal or block each time out so far.

items.headline: Diabate contributed 10 points (5-11 FG), 12 rebounds, one assist and two steals in 31 minutes during Friday's 95-79 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Diabate continued his strong start to the season, recording his second double-double in the past three games. He appears to be firmly locked in as the starting center, averaging 9.3 points. 9.8 rebounds and 2.6 combined steals and blocks in 29.6 minutes per game over the first six contests of the season. Although his ceiling is somewhat limited, he remains a clear must-roster player, particularly for those needing steals from the center position.

items.headline: Diabate contributed 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 FT), 17 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal over 35 minutes during Monday's 110-103 win over Washington.
items.story: Diabate delivered his strongest rebounding performance of the young season while recording his first double-double of the campaign. The center also made a significant defensive impact with three blocks, providing valuable production across multiple categories. His limited offensive involvement caps his scoring upside, but his rebounding and defensive contributions give him considerable appeal in category-based fantasy formats.

items.headline: Diabate registered five points (2-2 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 21 minutes in Friday's 128-81 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Diabate saw his playing time drop from 34 minutes in the season opener against the Nets on Wednesday to just 21 here, largely because of the lopsided score. He remained productive on the glass, but his scoring and defensive numbers weren't as notable as in the previous game. His rebounding and defensive contributions provide a useful fantasy foundation, although his limited offensive involvement makes consistent minutes particularly important to his value.

items.headline: Diabate registered 17 points (7-11 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and five steals across 34 minutes in Wednesday's 110-103 win over the Nets.
items.story: Diabate opened the regular season with an impressive two-way performance, with his five steals providing a significant fantasy boost while ending just two boards shy of a double-double. The 34-minute workload was particularly encouraging, suggesting he could maintain a substantial role in Charlotte's frontcourt. He can be even better defensively because of his blocking ability, but if Diabate gets enough playing time, he can be a double-double threat every time he steps on the court.

items.headline: Diabate (elbow) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Diabate missed the preseason finale due to a right elbow injury but is good to go for Opening Night. The 2022 second-round pick is expected to start at center but will face competition from second-year big man Ryan Kalkbrenner and rookie Hannes Steinbach.

items.headline: Diabate has been ruled out for Friday's preseason finale against the Grizzlies due to a right elbow injury.
items.story: Diabate can be considered day-to-day moving forward, and his status for Wednesday's regular-season opener in Brooklyn remains unclear. If he's sidelined, Ryan Kalkbrenner and rookie Hannes Steinbach would be candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Diabate closed with four points (1-1 FG, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, three steals, two blocks and one assist in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Diabate assumed the starting center role ahead of both Ryan Kalkbrenner and Hannes Steinbach. Despite scoring only four points, Diabate did what he does best, providing the team with energy and effort on both ends of the floor. He finished with five combined steals and blocks, an element of his game that will need to stabilize should he hope to hold onto the starting role. Assuming that is the case, Diabate is worth a look late in fantasy drafts for those needing to add some center depth.

items.headline: Diabate was spotted working with the first unit in Friday's practice.
items.story: Although he began the 2025-26 season in a reserve role, Diabate started 47 of his 73 regular-season appearances, averaging 7.9 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.8 steals across 26.0 minutes per contest. He faces added competition for playing time this year with Hannes Steinbach and Naz Reid now in the mix. However, it appears likely Reid will start at power forward, while Diabate battles for center minutes with Steinbach and Ryan Kalkbrenner.

items.headline: Diabate could face a more crowded path to playing time after Charlotte acquired additional frontcourt talent in the LaMelo Ball trade, Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports reports.
items.story: The young big man showed flashes as an energy player and rebounder last season, but the additions of Naz Reid and Hannes Steinbach, plus internal improvement of second-year center Ryan Kalkbrenner may create increased competition for minutes. Diabate's defensive activity and athleticism should still give him an opportunity to earn a role, though his playing time may be less secure entering 2026-27.

items.headline: Diabate had two points (1-4 FG), eight rebounds, two assists and three blocks across 18 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Diabate tallied at least three blocks for the seventh time this season, closing out what could be considered a breakout campaign. However, although he was able to establish himself as the starting center in Charlotte, there are certainly some questions when it comes to his overall impact, especially for a team with lofty ambitions. In 75 appearances, Diabate averaged 7.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.7 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Diabate (hip) is available for Friday's Play-In Tournament game versus the Magic.
items.story: Diabate should continue to start Friday, and with him active, there will be fewer minutes available for Ryan Kalkbrenner and Xavier Tillman. In Tuesday's Play-In Tournament win over Miami, Diabate finished with eight points, 14 rebounds, one assist and one block over 36 minutes.

items.headline: Diabate is questionable for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Magic due to left hip soreness.
items.story: It's not clear as to when Diabate picked up this injury, as he logged 36 minutes during Tuesday's overtime win over the Heat. The team will presumably monitor the injury closely leading up to tipoff and should have more information to share on his availability closer to game time.

items.headline: Diabate posted eight points (4-5 FG), 14 rebounds, one assist and one block in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game victory over Miami.
items.story: Despite scoring in single digits for the sixth straight game, Diabate found other ways to impact the game, most notably on the boards, where he grabbed a team-high 14 rebounds. Charlotte will now face either Philadelphia or Orlando, with the winner going on to face the Pistons in the opening round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Diabate notched two points (1-3 FG), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 113-102 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Diabate underwhelmed again, continuing a rough couple of weeks. In seven appearances during that time, he has averaged just 5.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.1 steals. While his role as the starting center is safe, his lack of offensive upside could be an issue during the playoffs.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) will play Sunday in Minnesota.
items.story: Diabate is back after a one-game stint on the sidelines, which could push Ryan Kalkbrenner back to the second unit, while Xavier Tillman might drop from the rotation entirely. Since the All-Star break, Diabate is averaging 7.5 points, 9.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.9 swats per contest.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) is listed as probable for Sunday's game in Minnesota.
items.story: Diabate didn't suit up for Friday's 129-108 win over the Indiana Pacers. However, it appears he will miss only one contest. If that's the case, Ryan Kalkbrenner will likely head back to the bench.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) won't play in Friday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Diabate was listed as questionable heading into this contest because of left-ankle soreness. However, he has since been downgraded to out, meaning his next chance to play will be Sunday in Minnesota. With Diabate unavailable, Ryan Kalkbrenner is considered the favorite to replace him in the rotation, which would mark his first start in over a month.

items.headline: Diabate has left ankle soreness and is questionable for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: It sounds like the Hornets are contemplating a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set, and the inferior opponent may be factored into the decision. If Diabate is held out, Ryan Kalkbrenner could step into a larger role for Charlotte.

items.headline: Davis finished Sunday's 116-96 victory over the Magic with 22 points (8-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 33 minutes.
items.story: Davis has averaged 27.7 points, 10.7 rebounds and 33.7 minutes during Washington's three-game winning streak. His efficient scoring and continued defensive production reinforce his elite fantasy value, though Sunday's seven rebounds snapped his consecutive double-double streak.

items.headline: Davis totaled 36 points (16-26 FG, 4-9 FT), 11 rebounds and three assists in 34 minutes during Friday's 98-94 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Davis delivered his second-highest-scoring performance of the season, overwhelming Chicago's interior defense while securing his fifth double-double in his last seven appearances. His five missed free throws were a significant drawback for category managers, but the veteran's scoring efficiency and rebounding remain major strengths. Davis continues to anchor Washington's frontcourt, and his consistent workload should keep him among the team's most reliable fantasy contributors.

items.headline: Davis ended with 25 points (9-16 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 14 rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks across 34 minutes in Wednesday's 103-99 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Davis finished the night with his eighth double-double of the 2026-27 campaign. He also recorded two blocks for the fourth time in his last five appearances. As expected, the multi-time All-Star is having a productive year, averaging 24.6 points, 10.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.2 steals while shooting a career-best 34.4 percent from deep over 33.9 minutes per outing in 14 regular-season games. Davis has missed only two games, though durability is still a prominent concern moving forward.

items.headline: Davis had 14 points (4-11 FG, 6-6 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal over 31 minutes during Sunday's 147-119 loss to Houston.
items.story: Davis endured a relatively quiet offensive night after scoring 30 points against Detroit on Thursday, but he still contributed in several categories. The veteran had recorded four consecutive games with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds before Sunday's outing, making the reduced production an exception to his recent form. This was just his second game with fewer than 15 points, so fantasy shouldn't be overly concerned by one bad scoring outing, especially given his contributions in other areas.

items.headline: Davis contributed 30 points (13-21 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 15 rebounds, four assists and one steal over 44 minutes before fouling out of Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Davis put together another strong performance despite ultimately fouling out, recording his fourth straight 20-and-10 game. Although the Washington win/loss record is not ideal, Davis appears motivated and, to this point, has been a first-round player in standard leagues. Through 11 games, he has averaged 25.6 points, 10.5 rebounds and 2.3 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Davis registered 44 points (16-21 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 10-11 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist and one steal in 34 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Davis, who missed his team's previous two matchups due to an ankle injury, wasted no time in proving his health Monday. He pieced together an incredibly efficient 40-plus point performance, needing only 21 attempts from the field to set his best scoring mark of the young season. Davis also crashed the boards to secure a double-double for the third time in his last four appearances.

items.headline: Davis (ankle) will play Monday against the Pistons.
items.story: The Wizards considered Davis a true game-time decision after missing two straight games with an ankle injury, but he's managed to prove his health prior to tipoff. He's looked sharp in his last five matchups, averaging 25.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks in 33.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Davis (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.
items.story: Davis has missed the last two games. It appears he has a chance to return Monday against the Pistons. However, if Davis isn't cleared to suit up for that contest, Bilal Coulibaly could remain in the starting lineup. Deandre Ayton (leg), who is not listed on the injury report, is also a candidate to start.

items.headline: Davis (ankle) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
items.story: This will be Davis' second straight game on the sidelines, which could result in another start for Deandre Ayton and extended minutes for Bilal Coulibaly. Davis' next chance to play will come Monday in Detroit.

items.headline: Davis (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: After missing Friday's 139-132 loss to Atlanta, Davis is questionable to suit up on the second night of Washington's back-to-back due to a sprained right ankle. Deandre Ayton started in his place, so if Davis is sidelined again, the former will earn a second consecutive starting nod, while Will Riley, Bilal Coulibaly and Khris Middleton could also see additional minutes.

items.headline: Davis (ankle) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Atlanta is shorthanded, but Washington will also be without one of its top players, with Davis missing his first game of the 2026-27 campaign due to an ankle injury that he picked up when these clubs met Wednesday. As a result, the Wizards may look to Will Riley and Khris Middleton to fill most of the void at the four spot.

items.headline: Davis is questionable for Friday's game against the Hawks due to a right ankle sprain, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Davis picked up the ankle injury during Wednesday's matchup against Atlanta but managed to stay in the game and finish with 26 points in 30 minutes. The Wizards will likely monitor him closely in shootaround and pregame warmups to determine if he suits up Friday evening.

items.headline: Davis finished with 26 points (12-19 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks over 30 minutes in Wednesday's 120-105 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Davis got off to a hot start Wednesday night. He kept it going through most of the contest, though he cooled off in the fourth quarter. Still, it was a quality showing for the multi-time All-Star, who is now averaging 23.4 points, 9.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.1 blocks across 33.0 minutes per outing in eight regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Davis contributed 27 points (12-17 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, three steals and one assist across 34 minutes in Monday's 103-94 win over the Magic.
items.story: Davis turned in an efficient performance en route to a game-high scoring total Monday. The veteran big man also tied for the game-best mark in rebounds while finishing with a season high in steals. Davis has reached the 25-point mark while grabbing at least nine boards in three of his last four outings.

items.headline: Davis finished with 25 points (8-18 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 9-10 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 95-79 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Davis had a quality game Friday to begin NBA Cup group play. He surpassed the 20-point mark for the third time this season, and he's also had at least one steal in each of the Wizards' six regular-season games of the 2026-27 campaign. Davis has shot a career-low 44.1 percent from the field this season, though he is still averaging a productive 22.3 points, 9.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks over 33.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Davis logged 18 points (8-18 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Davis contributed across the board despite an uneven shooting performance, finishing with three combined steals and blocks while committing no turnovers. The veteran big man also connected on two three-pointers, adding another dimension to his offensive production. Although his rebounding total was modest, his ability to contribute in multiple categories continues to make him a valuable fantasy asset.

items.headline: Davis finished with 29 points (11-22 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 10 rebounds and one steal in 36 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Davis put together a strong all-around showing, resulting in his second double-double through four matchups this season. He was spotted grabbing his right hand during the final 30 seconds of Monday's game after getting bumped on a screen, but he joked after the matchup that his hand was simply hot from making too many shots, per Greg Finberg of Wizards Central, so fantasy managers can breathe a sigh of relief.

items.headline: Davis supplied 19 points (8-21 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-5 FT), six rebounds, four assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 win over Chicago.
items.story: The veteran forward bounced back from a nine-point effort against the Raptors on Friday, but Davis' six boards were still his lowest mark on the young season. Through his first three games for the Wizards, Davis is averaging 20.7 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks, and he hasn't even found his rhythm on offense yet -- he's shooting just 41.5 percent from the floor on 17.7 FG attempts a contest.

items.headline: Davis finished with nine points (3-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 32 minutes during Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Davis had a big performance in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bucks, but the veteran big man was held in check Friday by a Raptors team with tough defenders in Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. Even in an off night, Davis was sniffing at a second consecutive double-double and figures to have more productive nights than duds. He could see a dip in minutes on the second leg of the Wizards' back-to-back set Saturday against the Bulls in Chicago.

items.headline: Davis finished Wednesday's 128-116 win over Milwaukee with 34 points (11-20 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 11-14 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 34 minutes.
items.story: Davis dominated in his Wizards' regular-season debut, leading his team in rebounding, shot attempts and scoring. At times, he brought the ball up the floor and operated in a point-center role when Trae Young was off the court, so he should see significant usage in head coach Brian Keefe's system. When healthy, Davis is a league-winning fantasy asset.

items.headline: Davis generated 14 points (6-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks over 27 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Davis notched his second straight double-double, led Washington in rebounds and tied for the team lead in blocks. Washington acquired the veteran big man from Dallas in an eight-player trade in February. The All-Star's health will again be the key variable when Washington opens the regular season Wednesday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Young accumulated 11 points (3-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 win over Orlando.
items.story: Young has shot just 26 percent over his last five games, averaging 31 minutes. However, he's recorded at least eight assists in four of those contests, maintaining fantasy value through playmaking. His shooting struggles remain concerning, but his established offensive role provides upside.

items.headline: Young provided 16 points (4-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, five assists and three steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago.
items.story: Young struggled inside the arc but compensated by connecting on four three-pointers and recording three steals, helping Washington secure its second consecutive win. His scoring has been inconsistent recently, as he has failed to reach the 20-point mark in his last four games since recording a season-high 37 points against Detroit on Nov. 12. Young remains a high-usage offensive option, but his fantasy ceiling depends on both his scoring and playmaking. He's averaging 15.6 points, 7.8 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game since the beginning of November.

items.headline: Young ended with 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), one rebound, eight assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 103-99 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Young endured his third straight game with fewer than 15 points, and it's becoming increasingly clear that performances like his 37-point outburst against the Pistons on Nov. 12 will be outliers. Young remains Washington's primary playmaker, as his eight assists helped compensate for the poor shooting, but sharing offensive responsibilities with Anthony Davis and the team's developing young players means he doesn't need to carry the scoring burden every night. He's averaging 15.6 points and 8.1 assists per game since November, although he's shooting just 33.3 percent from deep in that stretch.

items.headline: Young tallied 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 assists, two rebounds and two steals over 33 minutes in Monday's 136-120 loss to Memphis.
items.story: After going scoreless in Sunday's loss, Young reached double figures but continued to struggle with his efficiency as a shooter. The veteran guard made a greater impact as a facilitator, dishing out at least 10 assists for the sixth time this season. On the year, Young is averaging 17.9 points, 8.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals through 15 appearances.

items.headline: Young finished Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons with 37 points (8-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 17-17 FT), 14 assists and two rebounds across 45 minutes.
items.story: Young struggled from two-point range, but he was productive from downtown and didn't miss a shot at the charity stripe, finishing with a team- and season-high scoring total. The star floor general also dished out a game- and season-best 14 assists, securing his fifth double-double of the campaign. The 28-year-old has reached the 20-point mark in three of his last five outings and has knocked down at least three triples in four of them.

items.headline: Young ended with 20 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-9 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

items.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Young registered 18 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Young delivered a respectable offensive performance against his former team, shooting 50 percent from the field while contributing six assists. However, he committed four turnovers and couldn't prevent Washington from suffering a 15-point defeat. The veteran point guard continues to serve as a primary offensive facilitator for the Wizards, providing a reliable source of points and assists for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Young provided 15 points (5-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 34 minutes during Monday's 103-94 win over Orlando.
items.story: Young took a backseat offensively to Anthony Davis, Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa, who combined for 70 points, but he remained Washington's primary facilitator. His nine assists helped offset a modest scoring total, and his established playmaking role should continue to provide a reliable fantasy floor even when his shot volume fluctuates.

items.headline: Young recorded 22 points (10-20 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and 10 assists in 38 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Young put together another strong final line Monday, though it resulted in a loss. He's been facilitating at an elite level to kick off the 2026-27 campaign, registering three double-doubles in four appearances, and he's been almost as impressive as a scorer, putting up 20 or more points in all four games.

items.headline: Young totaled 25 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 9-9 FT), four rebounds and nine assists in 34 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 win over Chicago.
items.story: The 25 points led the Wizards on the night, as Young just missed extending his double-double streak to three games to begin the season. He's looking as productive as ever in his first full campaign for Washington, averaging 22.3 points, 11.3 assists, 2.7 threes, 1.7 boards and 1.0 steals so far in 2026-27 while launching 8.7 three-point attempts a game, volume comparable to his last couple years in Atlanta.

items.headline: Young posted 22 points (5-15 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 8-10 FT), one rebound, 12 assists and a steal across 37 minutes in Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Even though the Wizards suffered their first loss of the season, Young posted an impressive stat line and excelled as a playmaker. Young has posted at least 20 points and 12 assists in each of his first two games of the season, although it remains to be seen if he can keep it up for an extended stretch and remain healthy.

items.headline: Young closed with 20 points (4-13 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 12-16 FT), 13 assists and two steals over 38 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 victory over Milwaukee.
items.story: Young had a tough time getting his shot to drop and missed all six of his three-point attempts, but he did a nice job of creating contact and getting to the line for easy buckets. He also finished with just one turnover in 38 minutes of floor time, an impressive feat given his game-high 13 dimes.

items.headline: Young finished with 11 points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, 11 assists and a steal across 28 minutes in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: On one hand, Young struggled to find his shooting rhythm, making just one field goal and relying heavily on free throws for his scoring. However, the veteran point guard dazzled as a playmaker with 11 assists, even if the eight turnovers were concerning. Still, the fact that Young posted a double-double despite his offensive inefficiency is a great sign of him being ready for the start of the 2026-27 regular season. Young's passing volume remains an important fantasy asset, but his ball security and shooting efficiency will be worth monitoring. If he stays healthy, he should have a sizable role as the team's primary floor general in a dynamic lineup alongside AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: Young finished with 15 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four assists and two steals across 17 minutes in Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Young made the most of his abbreviated playing time and looked good orchestrating the offense alongside several projected starters in Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Anthony Davis. The veteran guard's combination of perimeter scoring and elite playmaking should remain central to Washington's offensive approach once the regular season begins.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been cleared for training camp and was spotted participating in on-court work during Wednesday's practice, according to Wizards reporter Greg Finberg.
items.story: Young's 2025-26 campaign ended with him sidelined by a right quadriceps contusion and lower-back irritation after appearing in just five games for Washington following his midseason arrival. His participation during the second day of camp indicates he's moved past those issues and enters the preseason healthy.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been doing sand-dune workouts during the offseason, and his trainer discussed the guard's outlook Monday, Mark Medina of RG reports.
items.story: With Young limited to 15 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 due to injuries, any sign of offseason rehab progress is notable. This report points to active conditioning work after his quadriceps issue, though it does not provide a return timeline or formal clearance update ahead of Washington's training camp. However, a previous report from ESPN indicated that he would be ready to roll.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) plans to sign a four-year, $212 million deal with the Wizards, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Young declined his $49 million player option and was initially going to test the waters in free agency. The Wizards were always viewed as the favorites to sign him, however, and it's clear that they value him extremely highly based on this offer. Young was limited to 15 appearances during the 2025-26 regular season due to injuries, posting averages of 17.9 points and 8.0 assists on 45.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Fox is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings due to a right shin contusion, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Fox could miss Monday's game due to a shin injury he likely picked up during Saturday's game against the Pelicans. With Dylan Harper (hip) out and Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) questionable, the Spurs could be thin at the lead guard position, leaving more ball-handling responsibilities for Stephon Castle.

items.headline: Fox racked up five points (1-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds and 10 assists across 26 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: The veteran floor general took a backseat offensively as Victor Wembanyama dominated the scoring with a 50-point performance, but Fox was excellent as a playmaker en route to delivering a season-high mark in assists. His playmaking responsibilities provide a valuable secondary source of production when his shot volume drops, but he needs to be better offensively to remain a consistent starter in fantasy. This was his fourth consecutive game scoring 10 points or fewer, averaging just 7.0 points, 2.8 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game while shooting 28.0 percent from the field in that stretch.

items.headline: Fox ended Thursday's 124-112 win over the Clippers with 10 points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
items.story: Fox put up fewer than six shots for just the second time this season but still nailed all six of his free throws and scored in double figures after totaling 13 points across his last two appearances. The veteran floor general hasn't been very productive through nine games this month, during which he's averaged 10.4 points, 4.4 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.2 steals across 27.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fox contributed six points (3-10 FG, 0-5 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Fox has been held in check in back-to-back appearances, and he never found a rhythm against Detroit's physical perimeter defense. The veteran point guard has been a steadying presence for a 12-3 Spurs team, but he's averaged just 13.1 points in 14 games, which is on pace to be the second-worst scoring average of his career.

items.headline: Fox (hip) is not listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Fox sat out Sunday's 110-102 win over Utah due to left hip tightness, but it appears he'll be back in the lineup Tuesday for a home tilt versus Detroit. Julian Champagnie, who started in place of Fox on Sunday, will likely head back to the bench.

items.headline: Fox (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Fox has been dealing with left hip tightness recently, and it will finally force him to miss his first game of the season. He's playing 28.6 minutes a night, the lowest since his 27.8 mark during his rookie campaign in 2017, en route to averages of 13.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 three-pointers across 13 games in 2026-27. Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper will likely handle the majority of ball-handling duties, while Julian Champagnie would be the top candidate to start in place of Fox.

items.headline: Fox (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Utah.
items.story: Fox has been bothered by left hip tightness. While the injury hasn't cost him any games this season, it wouldn't be surprising if he got the night off to rest against the one-win Jazz. If that happens, Julian Champagnie should be considered the favorite to enter the starting lineup, with Stephon Castle in line for more ball-handling duties.

items.headline: Fox (hip) is listed as available for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Fox was at risk of missing his first game of the season due to a hip injury he picked up sometime after Wednesday's win over Chicago, but he's been cleared to play following his latest evaluation. The 28-year-old guard has averaged 11.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 1.2 steals in 28.2 minutes over the Spurs' last five games.

items.headline: Fox is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left hip soreness.
items.story: Fox is in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 season after picking up a hip injury. He'll presumably be re-evaluated again at some point before tipoff to determine his availability for Friday. Jordan McLaughlin and Julian Champagnie could see more minutes if Fox is unable to suit up.

items.headline: Fox closed Wednesday's 124-119 win over the Bulls with 17 points (7-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, nine assists and three steals over 31 minutes.
items.story: Fox fell one assist short of a double-double while adding a season-high-tying three steals. Although the efficiency wasn't quite there, he has now scored at least 15 points in back-to-back games and continues to look more comfortable after a slow start to the campaign. Sharing ball-handling duties with Dylan Harper caps his assist upside somewhat, but Fox remains a reliable source of points, assists and steals in all formats.

items.headline: Fox ended with 15 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), nine rebounds and six assists over 29 minutes during Monday's 122-96 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Fox flirted with a double-double, turning in his highest-scoring total since the Oct. 31 win over Minnesota. The star guard is bouncing back nicely from a nightmarish NBA Finals run, averaging 13.9 points, 5.9 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 1.2 steals per contest while shooting 53.2 percent from the field in 11 games this season.

items.headline: Fox totaled 12 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 22 minutes during Monday's 119-97 win over Utah.
items.story: Fox converted five of his eight field-goal attempts but wasn't required to shoulder a heavy offensive workload as San Antonio cruised to its fifth consecutive victory. The veteran guard committed five fouls and played just 22 minutes, while rookie Dylan Harper paced the Spurs with 17 points and eight assists. Fox's efficiency was encouraging, but his limited playing time and modest playmaking numbers resulted in a relatively quiet fantasy outing.

items.headline: Fox accumulated 11 points (3-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and six assists over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 win over Sacramento.
items.story: The 26 minutes were a season low for Fox, but that can primarily be attributed to the Spurs nursing a large lead for most of the contest. He's dished out at least six dimes in all four outings and has seven combined steals-plus-blocks, and that trend should continue as long as he remains healthy.

items.headline: Fox recorded 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, nine assists, three steals and one block over 28 minutes in Saturday's 122-106 win over the Mavs.
items.story: Fox has hit the ground running this season, pumping out top-30 value with averages of 17.3 points, 8.3 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 1.3 triples and 2.0 steals per game on 58.1 percent shooting from the field and 80.0 percent at the line. He'll look to maintain his strong play Tuesday against the Kings.

items.headline: Fox chipped in 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, nine assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Friday's 114-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Fox played through a wrist injury, falling one assist short of a double-double. Despite the apparent issue, Fox doesn't seem too bothered, chalking up meaningful stats on both ends of the floor. The injury is something for fantasy managers to monitor, though the fact that he has played in excess of 30 minutes in each of the first two games is a positive.

items.headline: Fox closed with seven points (3-15 FG, 1-8 3Pt), five assists and two steals in 37 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to the Knicks in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Fox wrapped up a brutal championship series with another dreadful shooting display, failing to crack 37.5 percent shooting from the field for a third straight game as San Antonio was eliminated. The 28-year-old guard was never able to recapture his pre-injury form after returning from a Western Conference Finals high-ankle sprain, averaging a meager 12.8 points while shooting 34.4 percent from the field and 25.0 percent from deep across the five Finals contests. Beyond the efficiency woes, Fox's decision-making plagued the Spurs at the worst possible moments and most notably in Game 4, when he inexplicably drove into a contested layup attempt instead of running out the clock and forcing New York to foul while up one with 12 seconds remaining. With San Antonio heading into the offseason, management will have to weigh whether Fox can adjust his game alongside rising stars Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper, or if his maximum contract will continue to clog the team's flexibility.

items.headline: Swain was selected by the Bulls with the No. 15 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Swain lands in Chicago after putting together a dominant junior season at Texas. The athletic forward was the engine of the Longhorns' offense, putting up a stellar line of 17.3 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game while displaying tremendous efficiency inside the arc with a 54.2 percent shooting mark from the field. Swain possesses a versatile, modern skill set, offering the size to impact the game on the glass alongside the playmaking chops to generate looks for others out of the frontcourt. A significant driver behind that high field-goal percentage is Swain's elite ability as a finisher at the rim. He excels at using his length and explosive athleticism to play through contact in the paint, frequently converting tough, contested looks and generating second-chance opportunities. While his perimeter shooting consistency remains a development point as he transitions to the NBA, his interior scoring prowess, defensive motor and elite athletic traits give him dynamic upside. He joins a Bulls squad looking to inject youthful length and playmaking into its core, positioning Swain to compete for immediate minutes during his rookie campaign.

The second-year center has continued to expand his offensive repertoire, and Sunday's three made triples demonstrated his ability to stretch the floor. His three blocks also reinforced the defensive upside that makes him an intriguing fantasy asset, although his inconsistent free-throw shooting remains an area of concern. After failing to reach the 20-point threshold in his first 11 appearances this season, the last two games are a clear step in the right direction for Sarr.

items.headline: Sarr (illness) is available to play in Sunday's game against Houston.
items.story: Sarr was in danger of missing his second game of the 2026-27 campaign due to an illness. However, he will be on the floor Sunday, likely resulting in fewer minutes for Deandre Ayton and Anthony Gill.

items.headline: Sarr (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
items.story: Sarr is under the weather and could miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's absence would open up additional minutes for guys like Deandre Ayton, Anthony Gill and Will Riley.

items.headline: Sarr provided 30 points (12-14 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 44 minutes during Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Although his workload was inflated by a double-overtime affair, Sarr still went off for a highly efficient 30 points Thursday. The third-year big man is still adjusting to life alongside Anthony Davis in the frontcourt, with Sarr averaging 13.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals in 29.1 minutes per game over his last six contests.

items.headline: Sarr tallied 15 points (7-17 FG, 1-9 3Pt), 14 rebounds and an assist across 28 minutes in Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Sarr has endured a slow start to the season, but at least he recorded his first double-double of the season in this matchup. His scoring has been trending in the right direction as well with six double-digit efforts in his last seven appearances, but overall, Sarr is averaging just 10.6 points and 7.1 boards per game, a notable downgrade in scoring compared to the 16.3 points per game he averaged in 2025-26. His perimeter shooting was a major weakness as well -- he missed eight of nine three-point attempts and is shooting just 20.7 percent from beyond the arc this season.

items.headline: Sarr notched 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Sarr returned to action after missing Monday's game against Orlando due to left knee soreness and came within one rebound of a double-double. The young center made his presence felt defensively with three combined steals and blocks despite playing just 23 minutes. His relatively modest workload is worth monitoring, but his ability to contribute defensive statistics continues to bolster his fantasy value.

items.headline: Sarr (knee) is available for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Sarr is returning Wednesday from a one-game absence due to a knee injury and should have no restrictions. His presence will send Deandre Ayton back to the bench in all likelihood.

items.headline: Sarr (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Sarr is dealing with left knee soreness that could force him to miss another contest after sitting out Monday's win over Orlando. If the big man remains sidelined, Deandre Ayton could continue to handle an increased workload in Washington's frontcourt. Sarr's availability should become clearer closer to Wednesday's tipoff.

items.headline: Sarr (knee) is out for Monday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Sarr was previously listed as questionable after picking up the knock Friday against the Hornets. With Sarr out of commission, the Wizards could lean more on backup center Deandre Ayton and may slide him into the first unit.

items.headline: Sarr (knee) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Sarr seems to have picked up the knee issue after logging a season-high 29 minutes during Friday's 95-79 win over Charlotte. If he's unable to suit up in Orlando, Deandre Ayton would likely earn his first start of the season.

items.headline: The Wizards exercised the fourth-year team option on Sarr on Sunday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sarr was the No. 2 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 121 regular-season games, averaging 14.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.7 blocks over 27.0 minutes per contest. Sarr seemingly has All-Star upside, though injuries have certainly slowed down his progression.

items.headline: Sarr ended with three points (1-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and eight rebounds across 29 minutes during Friday's 95-79 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: Sarr saw his playing time elevate to 29 minutes, although that's where the positives end. He turned in his worst performance of the season, despite the increased playing time, a worrying sign for fantasy managers. While he does remain a clear must-hold player, expectations for Sarr should likely be tempered, assuming Washington can maintain a relatively injury-free roster.

items.headline: Sarr finished with 18 points (7-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, two assists, one block and four steals across 26 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Sarr made an impact on both ends of the floor, shooting efficiently while complementing his scoring output with five combined steals and blocks. The third-year center was particularly active defensively, leading all players with four steals despite playing fewer than 30 minutes. His combination of defensive production and developing perimeter game gives him considerable upside in category-based fantasy formats.

items.headline: Sarr amassed 10 points (5-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and three blocks over 23 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: After failing to record a block in the first two games of the season, Sarr opened his account with a big night at the rim in Chicago. The third-year center's 10 points were also his best effort yet in 2026-27, as he attempts to find his place in an offense that's set to be dominated by Trae Young and Anthony Davis as long as both veterans stay healthy, and which will need to accommodate first overall pick AJ Dybantsa (ankle) in the near future as well.

items.headline: Sarr totaled seven points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and two steals over 25 minutes during Friday's 112-102 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Sarr has opened the season with back-to-back games of less than 10 points, and he attempted only four shots during Friday's loss. The 2024 first overall pick has seen steady usage in his first two years in the NBA, but there will be major adjustments for him in 2026-27 in his first full season of playing with both Trae Young and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: Sarr contributed six points (3-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt), nine rebounds and two assists across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Sarr's 2026-27 debut alongside Anthony Davis (34/12/4/1/2) left a lot to be desired. The first overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft was unable to make an impact on the defensive end after averaging 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals across 48 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. Sarr should get on track soon, though the presence of Davis and Deandre Ayton may eat into his bottom line.

items.headline: Sarr tallied 12 points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, one steal and one block in 26 minutes in Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Sarr grabbed nine rebounds for the second straight game and scored a preseason-high 12 points. The third-year big man has shared frontcourt minutes with Anthony Davis this preseason. His rebounding and rim protection should give Washington an imposing pairing up front.

items.headline: Sarr finished with six points (3-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and nine rebounds across 23 minutes in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Without Anthony Davis (rest) drawing attention, Sarr struggled to score Monday. The third-year big man is set to play for the most talented Wizards team of his young career in 2026-27, which also features Trae Young at point guard.

items.headline: Sarr is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Pistons, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Joining Sarr in the first unit for Saturday's exhibition will be Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Anthony Davis. Deandre Ayton will work in the second unit with Sarr active.

items.headline: Sarr (right foot) will play in Saturday's preseason game against the Pistons, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sarr underwent a procedure in mid-June to repair a fracture in his right foot, and he's progressed enough in his recovery to make his preseason debut Saturday. He'll likely operate under a heavy minutes restriction, but it's a positive sign to see the third-year big man on the floor before the 2026-27 regular season commences.

items.headline: Wizards head coach Brian Keefe said Friday that Sarr (foot) is trending in a positive direction regarding his availability, though his status for Saturday's preseason game remains uncertain, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Keefe indicated that a decision on Sarr's availability will be made Saturday, suggesting the big man could be nearing a return to game action. Even if Sarr is cleared to play, Washington could manage his workload during the preseason.

items.headline: Sarr (foot) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Knicks, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Head coach Brian Keefe believes Sarr is close to returning from offseason foot surgery. Saturday's game against the Pistons marks his next chance to make his 2026 preseason debut.

items.headline: Sarr said he took part in the Wizards' 5-on-5 full-contact work during Monday's practice, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sarr is ramping up after undergoing right foot surgery in June. He appears likely to be ready for the start of the regular season, though it's unclear how much action he'll see during the preseason. Across 48 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, he averaged 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 27.2 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Sarr (foot) is expected to begin contact work soon after undergoing surgery this offseason, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sarr is nearing the next step in his recovery from surgery he underwent in mid-June to repair a fractured right foot. The Wizards planned to hold the big man out of contact drills during the first week of training camp, but he's expected to begin full-contact work soon. Sarr remains on track to be ready for the start of the regular season, though his availability for preseason action remains unclear.

items.headline: Sarr (foot) didn't participate in Saturday's scrimmage but is expected to ramp up to full contact in the coming days, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sarr has been limited in training camp thus far while working his way back from surgery he underwent in mid-June to repair a fractured right foot. The big man is expected to be ready for the start of the regular season, though it's unclear how active he'll be during the preseason. Over 48 regular-season games in 2025-26, he averaged 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 27.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sarr will be a partial participant when training camp begins as he continues his recovery from surgery to repair a fractured right foot, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: General manager Will Dawkins said Thursday that Sarr is expected to be ready for the start of the regular season, so the limited workload to begin camp appears precautionary. Sarr underwent surgery in mid-June, and his progress during the preseason will be worth monitoring, but there currently doesn't appear to be significant concern about his availability for Opening Night.

items.headline: Washington's selection of AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft likely won't significantly alter Sarr's (foot) role heading into his third NBA season.
items.story: The 21-year-old big man is currently recovering from foot surgery but is expected to be ready for training camp after averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.0 blocks in 48 regular-season appearances last year. Sarr remains a major part of the franchise's long-term plans, although the additions of established veterans could reduce some offensive responsibilities. His defensive upside should continue to provide substantial fantasy value if he can stay healthy.

items.headline: Sarr underwent surgery to repair a fractured right foot Monday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Despite the procedure, Sarr is expected to be ready for the start of the 2026-27 season. The 2024 No. 2 overall pick was limited to 48 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.0 blocks in 27.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Markkanen supplied 22 points (8-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Markkanen bounced back from a dreadful shooting night in Saturday's 112-90 loss to Portland. His performance marked the first of the season in which he shot better than 47 percent from the field. He finished with game-high figures in scoring and three-pointers while tying Mo Bamba for the team lead in rebounds. Markkanen and the Jazz have struggled out of the gate to begin 2026-27, but there's still plenty of time for him to turn things around from a fantasy perspective.

items.story: Markkanen didn't play in Wednesday's 117-111 loss to San Antonio. He was back on the floor Saturday, though it wasn't his most efficient shooting performance. The 2017 No. 7 overall pick hasn't played the best in his five regular-season appearances in 2026-27, averaging just 15.4 points. However, Markkanen has proven he can be one of the most productive players in the league, so there's reason to believe he will get on track at some point.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is available for Saturday's game against Portland.
items.story: Markkanen missed Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a wrist injury, but the veteran forward has been cleared to return for Saturday's contest. His return means Josh Green will likely revert to a rotational role off the bench.

items.story: Markkanen was forced out of Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies after spraining his wrist, but there's a chance he won't miss any additional game time. Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is also questionable for Wednesday's game, and if they both get cleared, Mo Bamba will lose some of his streaming appeal.

items.story: Markkanen left Monday's loss to Memphis with the injury, and it doesn't sound initially that he's dealing with a significant setback. The star forward can be tentatively deemed questionable for Wednesday's tilt versus the Spurs.

The Jazz noted after the game that Markkanen will be sent for imaging Tuesday, per Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune. If the veteran forward is forced to miss time, Kyle Filipowski, Ace Bailey and Brice Sensabaugh would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Markkanen is questionable to return to Monday's game against Memphis due to a right wrist injury.
items.story: Markkanen exited to the locker room in the opening quarter and is questionable to check back in. If the veteran forward doesn't return, Ace Bailey and Kyle Filipowski will likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Markkanen went to the locker room during the first quarter of Monday's game against the Grizzlies due to an apparent hand injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Markkanen checked out of the game with 5:58 remaining in the first quarter and was spotted walking to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Markkanen ended Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers with 28 points (9-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds and one assist in 38 minutes.
items.story: Markkanen had failed to crack the 20-point plateau through his first two games of the season, but he got hot Sunday and finished as Utah's leading scorer. The 29-year-old forward scored efficiently and committed just one turnover in 38 minutes of floor time, but the Jazz couldn't capitalize on his effort, falling victim to a 52-point barrage from Luka Doncic.

items.headline: Markkanen ended Friday's 120-119 victory over the Pelicans with 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-9 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
items.story: With the Jazz roster rapidly getting stronger around him, Markkanen's usage could be set to decline. The 29-year-old forward averaged 19.2 FG attempts over 42 regular-season games in 2025-26, but through two games to begin the current campaign he's attempted exactly 13 shots in each, with Jaren Jackson, Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson all seeing similar volume in Friday's win. Markkanen still figures to be busy from beyond the arc and grab his share of boards, but his overall scoring could dip well below the 23-25 PPG his fantasy investors have been used to getting from him since he arrived in Utah.

items.headline: Markkanen chipped in 18 points (4-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one block across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Markkanen struggled to find his shooting touch, particularly from beyond the arc, but his aggressiveness at the free-throw line helped salvage his scoring output. The veteran forward played a team-high 36 minutes and finished one rebound shy of a double-double. Despite sharing the frontcourt with Jaren Jackson, Markkanen should remain a prominent offensive option for Utah, and his substantial workload is a positive indicator for his early-season fantasy value.

items.headline: Markkanen ended with 19 points (5-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 27 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Markkanen ended the 2025-26 campaign averaging 26.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steals over 34.4 minutes per contest. Without question, he's an All-Star-caliber player. However, the veteran forward hasn't appeared in more than 68 regular-season games since entering the league in 2017.

items.headline: Markkanen contributed 11 points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two assists, two steals and one rebound across 19 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Markkanen, who's set to be a primary scoring option for Utah this year, overcame a neck injury to suit up for this exhibition. Fantasy managers should feel more comfortable drafting the star forward at his ADP this fall now that he's healthy.

items.headline: Markkanen (neck) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's preseason meeting with the Spurs.
items.story: It looks like Markkanen will be back after a one-game absence, which should shift Jaxson Hayes or Ace Bailey back to the second unit. If Markkanen can manage to stay healthy this season, he could be in for a career year as an integral component of the Jazz's attack.

items.headline: Markkanen won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Nuggets due to neck soreness.
items.story: Markkanen is sitting out the exhibition game with some minor neck soreness, but he should be able to get back out there for Monday's preseason game against the Spurs. Ace Bailey will have a chance to start sans Markkanen, and there will be more minutes available for Svi Mykhailiuk.

items.headline: Markkanen finished with 17 points (5-12 FG, 4-4 FT, 3-7 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal in 16 minutes during Sunday's preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Markkanen hit the ground running, fresh off an impressive performance in the recent World Cup qualifier. Despite another strong campaign during the 2025-26 season, Markkanen's overall fantasy value continues to be somewhat underrated, largely due to the fact that he has missed multiple stretches of games due to both injury and rest in each of the last three seasons. However, with Utah likely to prioritize winning this season, Markkanen is poised for what could be his best season in recent memory, at least from a totals perspective. Landing him in the third or fourth round of drafts feels like a relatively risk-free move.

items.headline: Markkanen registered 21 points (6-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 25 minutes during Finland's 96-67 win over Estonia in Sunday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Markkanen looked sharp in Sunday's exhibition, recording a big double-double. The star forward delivered early-round fantasy value when healthy last year, having averaged 26.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steals in 34.4 minutes per game across 42 regular-season appearances. His pathway to usage has a few more hurdles this time around, however, as Utah will be integrating Jaren Jackson and Darryn Peterson into the lineup.

items.headline: Markkanen (hip) amassed 23 points (7-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes during Finland's 85-77 win over Hungary on Friday.
items.story: Markkanen was out for roughly the final two months of the NBA regular season with a hip injury, but he looks to be entering the new year with a clean bill of health following a FIBA appearance. The star forward was excellent when healthy last year, having averaged 26.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steals in 34.4 minutes across 42 games in 2025-26. However, it'll be interesting to see how Darryn Peterson's presence influences Markkanen's usage moving forward.

items.headline: Utah's selection of Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft should help ease some offensive pressure on Markkanen (hip).
items.story: The veteran forward has often carried a significant scoring burden during the rebuilding process, and the arrival of an elite shot creator could create more favorable opportunities. Markkanen remains the focal point of Utah's frontcourt, although trade speculation and the team's long-term direction could still influence his outlook.

items.headline: Markkanen (hip) will not play in Sunday's season finale against the Lakers.
items.story: As expected, Markkanen will sit out the final game of the season. He ended the campaign having last played Feb. 23. Despite playing just 42 games, Markkanen had what could be considered a bounceback season -- at least in the box score. In his 34.4 minutes per game, he averaged 26.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steals.
