items.story: Markkanen is still recovering from a right hip impingement and hasn't played since Feb. 23. His last chance to suit up this season will come in Sunday's regular-season finale against the Lakers, though he can be considered doubtful for that contest until the Jazz offer an update on his status.

items.headline: The Jazz announced Thursday that Markkanen (hip) will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Sarah Todd of The Deseret News reports.
items.story: Markkanen has dealt with both a right hip impingement and a sprained ankle since he last played Feb. 23, though the hip injury is the main concern at this juncture. Though Markkanen will be re-evaluated in early April, the Jazz will have just five games remaining once he gets examined, so there's a real chance that he won't play again in 2025-26. While Markkanen has been sidelined, the Jazz have been leaning more heavily on Cody Williams, Brice Sensabaugh (illness), Andersson Garcia and Blake Hinson to fill out minutes at forward.

items.headline: Markkanen is out for Thursday's game against the Bucks with a right hip impingement.
items.story: The All-Star forward hasn't appeared since the Feb. 23 loss to Houston, and the Jazz haven't provided an update on his health since Feb. 26. Until he's re-evaluated, Markkanen can be labeled as week-to-week moving forward.

items.headline: Markkanen (hip) won't play Friday versus the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Markkanen is expected to be re-evaluated soon, but the fact that he's still getting ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Until the Jazz provide a meaningful update on where Markkanen is in his recovery, he should be viewed as week-to-week.

Markkanen's minutes could be erratic the rest of the season as a tanking Utah team pushes the envelope on what the league considers acceptable load management, and Monday's showing from three-point range suggests the 28-year-old forward may not be quite 100 percent yet.

items.headline: Markkannen (illness) is available for Monday's game against the Rockets.

items.headline: Markkanen (illness) is probable for Monday's game against the Rockets.

items.headline: Markkanen (illness) is questionable for Friday's game versus Memphis.

items.headline: Buzelis notched nine points (4-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 98-94 loss to the Wizards.

Although Buzelis has shown considerable upside as a scorer, three-point shooter and shot-blocker, this was a step in the wrong direction. The combination of inconsistent minutes and fluctuating production make him a volatile fantasy option. Buzelis is averaging 14.9 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 blocks per game in November.

items.headline: Buzelis ended Wednesday's 137-107 victory over the Nets with 25 points (9-16 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 30 minutes.
items.story: Buzelis posted at least 23 points for the second straight game, scoring a season-high 25 points, including five three-pointers. With Caleb Wilson (hand) sidelined, Buzelis has started to turn things around after a poor start to the season. In six appearances over the past two weeks, he has been a top-40 player in standard leagues, averaging 18.2 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.0 blocks and 3.2 three-pointers.

items.headline: Buzelis registered 23 points (8-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal in 31 minutes during Monday's 126-115 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Buzelis put up a season-high 14 shots en route to a season-best scoring total, and he finished as Chicago's second-leading scorer Monday. The third-year forward didn't offer much outside the scoring column, though he did knock down three triples for the fourth time in his last five outings. During that span, Buzelis has averaged 16.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 blocks while shooting 45.2 percent from beyond the arc in 30.4 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Buzelis recorded 18 points (5-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), nine rebounds and two assists across 30 minutes in Saturday's 117-106 victory over Minnesota.
items.story: Buzelis bounced back from Friday's 11-point performance and came within a rebound of his first double-double of the season. The second-year forward has scored 29 points across Chicago's back-to-back victories while connecting on five three-pointers, a welcome development after entering Saturday averaging 13.3 points per game. His scoring has regressed from the 16.3 points he averaged last season, but his ability to contribute across the board, including some defensive stats here and there, provides additional fantasy value.

items.headline: Buzelis recorded 11 points (3-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Friday's 125-117 overtime win over Atlanta.
items.story: Buzelis offers an unusual mix of three-point shooting and rim protection, making him a valuable fantasy asset even when his scoring remains modest. All three of his made field goals Friday came from beyond the arc, while his three blocks illustrated the defensive upside that separates him from many perimeter-oriented forwards. His offensive consistency is still developing, but the versatility makes him an intriguing option in category leagues. Still, his 13.3 points per game represent a regression from his 16.3 points per contest in 2025-26.

items.headline: Buzelis contributed 13 points (5-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 124-119 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Buzelis knocked down three triples but committed a team-high six turnovers and failed to record a steal or block. Chicago's crowded frontcourt, with Caleb Wilson (hand) and Jalen Smith also looking for shots, continues to make Buzelis' night-to-night production difficult to project. He remains worth holding in most formats thanks to his three-point and defensive upside, but this was a performance to forget.

items.headline: Buzelis recorded 19 points (6-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block in 31 minutes during Sunday's 127-121 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Buzelis submitted his best scoring performance since the Oct. 24 loss to the Wizards. The third-year forward is looking to gain some momentum going forward amid a slow start to the season, having averaged 13.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game in nine appearances so far.

items.headline: Buzelis contributed four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one block across 23 minutes during Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Buzelis endured a frustrating performance, committing five turnovers while attempting just five shots. The young forward has now scored 14 or fewer points in three consecutive appearances, and his limited offensive involvement Monday was particularly concerning. His ability to contribute across multiple categories offers fantasy upside, but inconsistent production remains an issue.

items.headline: Buzelis finished with 17 points (5-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 133-127 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Buzelis had just 11 points in Monday's 133-99 loss to Boston. He got it together Wednesday, ending the night by tying for his second-highest points total of the season thus far. Buzelis is beginning to find his rhythm after a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign, with the 22-year-old shooting 50.0 percent from deep in his last two appearances while amassing one steal in each of his previous three games.

items.headline: Buzelis logged 21 points (7-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal over 35 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 loss to Washington.
items.story: The third-year forward played second fiddle on offense to Caleb Wilson, who erupted for a game-high 30 points, but the 21 points were still Buzelis's best showing yet on the young season as he sank his first three-pointers of 2026-27. Through three games, Buzelis is averaging 15.0 points, 5.3 boards, 1.7 assists and 1.0 blocks, and his scoring should pick up once his 13.3 percent shooting from beyond the arc normalizes.

items.headline: Buzelis racked up 17 points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 13-16 FT), six rebounds and two blocks in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 135-92 loss to Toronto.
items.story: The Bulls shot only 31.8 percent from the field (including 4-for-36 from three-point range) during Wednesday's regular-season opener. Buzelis ended up leading the Bulls in scoring thanks to a career-high 13 made free throws in the loss. Chicago has a young core of Buzelis, Josh Giddey and rookie fourth-overall pick Caleb Wilson, so it might take a few games for the team to mesh together. Chicago will stay on the road for its next game against Milwaukee on Friday.

items.headline: The Bulls picked up Buzelis' team option Tuesday.
items.story: This is a procedural move as the 2024 first-rounder rides out his rookie contract. Expectations are high for Buzelis as he enters his third NBA season, and the forward is primed for a key role with the rebuilding Bulls this year.

items.headline: Buzelis ended with 14 points (5-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block across 19 minutes in Friday's 133-116 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: Buzelis tied Jordan Hawkins to finish second on the team in points behind Caleb Wilson, who had 16. The 22-year-old finished the preseason by averaging 13.2 points, 3.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.2 blocks. However, he logged just 20.8 minutes per contest, so his contributions during the preseason shouldn't reflect what he is expected to do throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Buzelis totaled 19 points (6-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 125-104 preseason win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Buzelis was on fire from beyond the arc, knocking down a game-high five three-pointers en route to a team-high 19 points in a winning effort. The young forward has also made his presence felt defensively, recording at least one block in all four preseason appearances. Buzelis averaged 16.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 blocks across 77 regular-season contests last season and will look to take another leap in his third NBA campaign.

items.headline: Buzelis (ankle) will start Sunday's preseason game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Buzelis left Friday's preseason game against the Grizzlies early due to a right ankle injury, but he will return to the lineup Sunday. Buzelis recorded six points and a block in 12 minutes before exiting Friday's game.

items.headline: Buzelis exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's preseason game against the Grizzlies and will not return due to a right ankle injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports. He'll finish with six points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one block in 12 minutes.
items.story: Buzelis appeared to twist his ankle earlier in the game but initially played through the injury. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's exhibition against Denver. With the 2024 first-rounder out for the remainder of the game, Dailyn Swain and Leonard Miller could see increased playing time.

items.headline: Buzelis produced 14 points (6-15 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT) while adding three rebounds, two steals, two blocks and one assist over 26 minutes during Wednesday's preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: The third-year forward couldn't find his shot from beyond the arc, but Buzelis made up for it with a strong defensive effort. Buzelis took a big step forward in his second NBA campaign, nearly doubling his scoring average to 16.3 points and delivering 5.8 boards, 2.2 threes, 2.1 assists, 1.5 blocks and 0.7 steals over 77 regular-season contests, and further improvement seems likely for the 21-year-old as the Chicago roster gets better around him.

items.headline: Buzelis expects to have more offensive freedom this season and said he focused on becoming more physical and attacking the rim during the offseason, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The 21-year-old felt he attempted too many three-pointers last season, when 51.4 percent of his field-goal attempts came from beyond the arc, and he wants to incorporate more mid-range opportunities into his game. Buzelis also prioritized adding weight and strength, which could help him play through contact as he looks to build upon his 16.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 blocks per game from the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Buzelis (ankle) notched 12 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt), two assists, two rebounds and two blocks for Lithuania in Friday's 105-85 win over Great Britain in the World Cup Qualifiers.
items.story: Buzelis missed Chicago's regular-season finale with an ankle issue, but he's since fully recovered. He will have more competition for usage in the frontcourt following the selections of Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain as well as Chicago's acquisition of Nic Claxton (finger) ahead of the 2026-27 season, but Buzelis will likely maintain a sizable role for the Bulls.

items.headline: Buzelis (ankle) will have more competition for usage in the frontcourt following the selections of Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain as well as Chicago's acquisition of Nic Claxton (finger).
items.story: After trading away Nikola Vucevic at the deadline last year, the Bulls addressed a thin center position by acquiring Claxton ahead of Tuesday's draft. Wilson and Swain, however, pose even more significant threats to Buzelis' role at the forward spots. Buzelis could see less action as a small-ball center in 2026-27, but he certainly appears to be locked into a starting role to open the new year.

items.headline: Buzelis (ankle) won't play Sunday in Dallas.
items.story: With the Bulls playing for Ping Pong balls, Buzelis will hit the sidelines for their regular-season finale. His absence should open up minutes for Patrick Williams and Leonard Miller.

items.headline: Buzelis won't return to Friday's game against the Magic due to a sprained right ankle. He'll finish with 14 points (6-17 FG, 0-9 3Pt, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal in 27 minutes.
items.story: Buzelis was cleared to return from a three-game absence due to an illness but picked up an ankle injury and exited to the locker room with 10:10 remaining in the fourth quarter. The second-year forward should be considered questionable for Sunday's regular-season finale in Dallas until the Bulls offer an update on his status.

items.headline: Claxton (illness) is available for Monday's matchup with the Cavs, Bulls' reporter Will Gottlieb reports.
items.story: Claxton will be back in action following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which may result in fewer minutes for Jalen Smith. Claxton is averaging 9.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.0 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Claxton (illness) is questionable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Claxton is looking to suit up for the second half of this back-to-back after sitting out Sunday against Denver. Jalen Smith is likely to play through an illness of his own and would be a strong fantasy option in all formats if Claxton isn't feeling well enough to play.

items.headline: Claxton (illness) won't play in Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Claxton will miss Sunday's contest due to an illness. He started Friday's 98-94 loss to the Wizards with Jalen Smith (illness) sidelined, but the latter is expected to return versus Denver. Zach Collins and Noa Essengue should get a bump in opportunities with Claxton out.

items.headline: Claxton (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: After missing the first eight outings of the 2026-27 campaign due to a hamstring injury, Claxton has suited up in six of the last seven games for Chicago. However, he's now dealing with an illness that will leave his status for Sunday up in the air. If Claxton doesn't play, expect Zach Collins and Noa Essengue to earn more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Claxton ended with 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 29 minutes during Friday's 98-94 loss to Washington.
items.story: Claxton provided Chicago with a solid interior presence, but he had a tough matchup against Anthony Davis, who finished with 36 points and 11 rebounds. His fantasy appeal remains rooted in rebounding, field-goal percentage and defensive production, but his limited offensive involvement restricts his scoring ceiling. That said, he has scored in double digits in three of his last five appearances, so he's trending in the right direction.

items.headline: Claxton will start Friday's game against Washington, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: With Jalen Smith (illness) sidelined, Claxton will make his first start with the Bulls. The 27-year-old started 68 of his 69 regular-season appearances with the Nets in 2025-26, averaging 11.8 points, 6.9 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.1 blocks over 27.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Claxton finished Wednesday's 137-107 win over Brooklyn with 14 points (6-7 FG, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: Claxton scored double digits for just the second time this season, taking advantage of what ended up being a blowout win over his former team. Claxton continues to come off the bench behind Jalen Smith, having yet to play more than 22 minutes in a game this season. Those in standard leagues are likely facing a dilemma when it comes to his position on the roster. While he should be able to increase his production moving forward, his upside appears to be relatively limited.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Claxton missed the second night of Chicago's back-to-back against the Timberwolves on Saturday due to hamstring injury management. He missed the first eight outings of the season with the issue, but he's now set to suit up for the fourth time in the last five games. Claxton is averaging 7.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 blocks in 18.3 minutes across three regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Claxton was carrying a questionable tag ahead of Saturday's contest, and the big man will miss the game -- his first absence since his season debut Nov. 8 against the 76ers. Claxton will aim to return to action against the Cavaliers on Monday. With Claxton and Jalen Smith (finger) out, Zach Collins and Orlando Robinson are expected to see most of the minutes at center.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Claxton has averaged 7.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 blocks in 18.7 minutes across three games since making his season debut Sunday, but the Bulls may hold him out of Saturday's contest as he continues to manage the hamstring injury that forced him to miss Chicago's first eight games. Zach Collins could work in an expanded role if Claxton doesn't play.

items.headline: Claxton finished with 17 points (5-6 FG, 7-9 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block in 16 minutes during Wednesday's 124-119 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Claxton showed some nice hustle, running the floor and making his presence felt at the rim,  and led the second unit in scoring. It should only be a matter of time before he works his way into the starting unit, and the 27-year-old center looks primed for a bounce-back year with Chicago.

items.headline: Claxton provided four points (2-3 FG), four rebounds, four assists and two blocks across 18 minutes during Sunday's 127-121 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Claxton made his return from a multi-week absence with a preseason calf strain, as well as his Bulls and season debut. The big man is working under a minutes restriction, so fantasy managers will have to temper expectations initially.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is available for Sunday's game against Philadelphia and will be limited to 16-20 minutes off the bench, Will Gotlieb of CHGO reports.
items.story: Claxton will suit up for the first time this season after missing time due to a hamstring injury. The 27-year-old has spent the entirety of his career with the Nets to this point, averaging 10.6 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.6 blocks over 26.2 minutes per outing in 380 regular-season appearances. It's unclear how long Claxton will come off the bench in his first year in Chicago, though he should supplant Jalen Smith (finger) for the top center spot on the depth chart at some point.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Collins was originally marked as probable for Sunday's contest, but he appears to be trending in the wrong direction as game day approaches. If Claxton needs to sit out another game, Jalen Smith (hand) would presumably continue to operate as the Bulls' starting center.

items.headline: Head coach Tiago Splittler said Friday that Claxton (hamstring) is expected to make his season debut Sunday against the 76ers, per Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic.
items.story: Splitter stopped short of confirming Claxton's availability, but the big man is certainly trending in the right direction. Once Claxton is cleared to make his Bulls debut, Jalen Smith (hand) is likely to fall into a reserve role.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Windy City Bulls on Thursday.
items.story: Claxton was assigned to the G League earlier in the day to log a practice as part of his rehab. He'll rejoin the NBA squad following his workout and could make his 2026-27 debut as early as Sunday against the 76ers.

items.headline: The Bulls assigned Claxton (hamstring) to the G League's Windy City Bulls on Thursday.
items.story: This is the next stage of Claxton's rehab, and he'll be recalled shortly after practicing Thursday. Claxton drew a questionable tag prior to Wednesday against the Knicks and is closing in on his season debut.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against New York.
items.story: Claxton was listed as questionable, suggesting he might make his 2026-27 campaign debut Wednesday versus the Knicks. However, that won't happen, meaning his next opportunity to suit up will come Sunday against Philadelphia. With Claxton on the shelf again, Jalen Smith (finger) will likely remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is questionable for Wednesday against the Knicks.
items.story: Claxton has now drawn his first questionable tag of the young season as he closes in on his debut. If he does get the green light, he may face restrictions early on. Jalen Smith (finger) and Zach Collins could lose some steam upon Claxton's return.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Claxton appears to be trending in the right direction after practicing Sunday, but he's not yet ready to make his 2026-27 debut. His next chance to play will arrive Wednesday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Claxton hasn't played this season. The former Net recently logged a full practice Sunday, and while he's moving in the right direction, he likely won't make his debut with Chicago on Monday. Assuming Claxton doesn't play against the 76ers, Jalen Smith (finger), who is probable, will presumably remain in the starting lineup at the five.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
items.story: With Claxton progressing from individual drills Monday to full practice participation Sunday, he appears to be moving in the right direction in his recovery from a hamstring injury that's cost him the start of the regular season. More clarity on Claxton's potential regular-season debut should surface Sunday night, when the Bulls release their injury report for Monday's game in Philadelphia.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) participated in individual drills Monday morning and hopes to join the team for practice next week, Joe Cowley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
items.story: The Bulls reported one week ago that the big man would be re-evaluated in two weeks, so he appears to be right on track with his recovery from a hamstring injury. He'll presumably need to take part in 5-on-5 drills before getting the green light to return to game action.

items.headline: Claxton (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in two weeks, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: This is a tough blow for the Bulls, as they will be without their starting center for at least the first seven regular-season games. Meanwhile, Zach Collins' (toe) status remains in the air. This could set up Jalen Smith for a solid workload to open the season.

items.headline: Claxton tweaked his hamstring and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network of the Bulls Radio Network reports.
items.story: This is a huge blow for Claxton, and it rules him out for the entire preseason. For now, fantasy managers can consider him questionable for Opening Night on Oct. 21 against the Raptors. Jalen Smith is the next man up on the depth chart for Chicago, followed by Zach Collins (toe).

items.headline: Claxton is projected to start at center for the Bulls in the 2026-27 campaign, according to Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The Bulls were left with a big void at the center position after dealing Nikola Vucevic to the Celtics for Anfernee Simons at last year's trade deadline, and they're looking for Claxton to help plug the hole in 2026-27 after coming over from Brooklyn. Claxton, who was a full-time starter with the Nets for the better part of the last four seasons, has generally been a strong source of boards and swats for fantasy managers, though his rebound and block rates as well as his shooting efficiency all essentially declined each year over that time. That said, the 27-year-old big man has an opportunity for a fresh start in Chicago, and he did take a step forward as a playmaker in 2025-26 in the form of a career-high 3.7 assists per game.

items.headline: The Nets traded Claxton (finger) and the No. 33 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft to the Bulls and Timberwolves, respectively, in exchange for Julius Randle and the No. 28 overall pick in this year's draft, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Monday.
items.story: Claxton will head to Chicago after spending the first seven years of his career with the Nets. The big man appeared in 69 regular-season games (68 starts) in 2025-26, averaging 11.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.7 steals in 27.8 minutes per contest. He missed the team's final five games with a sprained finger, though he's expected to be ready for training camp. Claxton is under contract through the 2027-28 campaign.

items.headline: Claxton (finger) is out for Sunday's game in Toronto, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: E.J. Liddell and Trevon Scott could again see significant minutes Sunday as the last men standing in Brooklyn's frontcourt. Claxton will end the season with averages of 11.7 points, 6.9 rebounds, 3.7 assists (career-high figure) and 1.1 blocks per game.

items.headline: Claxton (finger) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Claxton will miss a fourth straight game, and it's unlikely he'll suit up during Sunday's regular-season finale in Toronto. E.J. Liddell should draw another start at center in Claxton's absence.

items.headline: Claxton (finger) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Claxton will miss a third consecutive contest due to a sprained finger, and his penultimate chance to suit up this season will come Friday in Milwaukee. The Nets will be shorthanded in the frontcourt Thursday, leaving plenty of minutes available for the likes of E.J. Liddell, Trevon Scott and Chaney Johnson.

items.headline: Claxton (finger) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Claxton will miss a second consecutive game Tuesday. However, with only three more contests left after the matchup against the Bucks, there's a chance the 26-year-old won't be back on the floor until the start of the 2026-27 campaign. With Claxton sidelined again, E.J. Liddell is the favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Claxton (hand) is out for Sunday's meeting with the Wizards.
items.story: Claxton's absence will open up minutes for Josh Minott and E.J. Liddell. Claxton should be considered questionable for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.

items.headline: Claxton (hand) is available for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Claxton was previously carrying a probable tag for the Nets, but he will power through issues with his wrist on top of an illness. Based on previous outings, the Nets will likely be cautious with his workload.

items.headline: Claxton (hand/illness) is listed as probable for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Claxton is dealing with an illness and right hand soreness, though he's still likely to suit up Friday. The big man has averaged 9.6 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 22.0 minutes per game over his last five appearances. He's been seeing limited playing time of late and hasn't logged more than 23 minutes since March 7.

items.headline: Claxton had four points (1-3 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 22 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Claxton's turned in another underwhelming performance. Despite being a regular fixture in the starting lineup, he has been outside the top 250 in 14 games over the past month. During that time, he has averaged just 8.1 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.0 blocks. At this point, he is nowhere near being a must-roster player.

items.headline: Claxton (rest) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Portland, per C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News.
items.story: After missing Sunday's loss to the Kings, Claxton is set to return to the court Monday. The rebuilding Nets are beginning to dial back Claxton's workload, with the big man averaging 7.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 0.8 blocks in 21.2 minutes per tilt over his last six games.

items.headline: Claxton (rest) won't play in Sunday's game in Sacramento, according to Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: Claxton won't suit up for the first of back-to-back contests to rest. He'll likely be back Monday in Portland. With Day'Ron Sharpe (thumb) done for the remainder of the campaign, the Nets will need to go small Sunday, and Danny Wolf should absorb most of the minutes underneath the basket.

items.headline: Okogie closed with nine points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 19 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Although Okogie is seeing fairly decent burn for the Jazz early on, he's not been productive enough to warrant much fantasy consideration. The veteran forward has averaged 3.0 rebounds, 2.7 points and 1.2 assists per game across six appearances this season.

items.headline: Okogie amassed zero points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two rebounds and one block over 21 minutes during Monday's 110-105 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Okogie received additional playing time after Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson (knee) exited early, but he failed to capitalize offensively. The veteran wing missed all four of his field-goal attempts and offered minimal production elsewhere. His defensive contributions could help him maintain a role in Utah's rotation, though his fantasy appeal remains limited.

items.headline: Okogie finished with eight points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Tuesday's 117-106 preseason loss to Denver.
items.story: Okogie led the second unit in minutes Tuesday. The veteran swingman appears to be competing with Brice Sensabaugh for an Opening Night reserve role, so Okogie's fantasy appeal looks to be limited.

items.headline: Okogie registered 15 points (5-12 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds, 11 assists, one block and four steals in 30 minutes during Nigeria's 100-84 win over Cape Verde in Sunday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Okogie set the pace in assists for Nigeria on Sunday, flirting with a triple-double as well. The swingman agreed to a two-year deal with the Jazz this offseason, and he'll offer the club's young core a veteran presence on the wing. Okogie drew 32 regular-season starts for Houston in 2025-26, his most since 2020-21 with Minnesota, and will battle for an Opening Night rotation spot at training camp.

items.headline: Okogie agreed to a two-year, $12 million deal with the Jazz on Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Okogie played in a career-high 78 regular-season games for the Rockets during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 4.5 points and 2.6 rebounds in 17.4 minutes per game. He'll provide depth on the wing for Utah and should serve as a veteran presence in a young locker room.

items.headline: Okogie registered three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 13 minutes during Friday's 98-78 loss to the Lakers in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Okogie was used sparingly in the postseason, with the Rockets relying heavily on the starting group. He was a key reserve for Houston during the regular season, making 78 appearances (32 starts) with averages of 4.5 points, 2.6 rebounds, 0.9 assists and 0.8 three-pointers in 17.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Okogie won't start Friday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Lakers, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: With Kevin Durant (ankle) sidelined, the Rockets are switching things up. Reed Sheppard and Tari Eason will slide back into the starting lineup, while Okogie heads to the bench. As a reserve this season (46 games), Okogie has averaged 12.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Okogie closed Thursday's 113-102 win over the 76ers with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal over 21 minutes.
items.story: Making his first start since Feb. 5, Okogie just missed recording his second double-double of the season, and the sixth of his career. The 27-year-old wing has filled a more consistent role in the Rockets' rotation in April, averaging 13.6 minutes over the last five games while supplying 4.4 points, 3.4 boards, 1.0 assists and 0.6 steals.

items.headline: Okogie is starting Thursday's game against the 76ers, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Okogie will draw a rare start Thursday with the Rockets electing to shake up the first unit. Reed Sheppard will shift to a bench role as a result of the lineup change.

items.headline: Okogie (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Rockets' 119-109 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: After playing single-digit minutes in four of the Rockets' previous five contests, Okogie finally dropped out of the rotation entirely along with Dorian Finney-Smith while head coach Ime Udoka went with Tari Eason and Jae'Sean Tate as the team's reserve options at forward. Okogie's declining role has come while the 27-year-old has shot just 40 percent from the field since the calendar flipped to 2026.

items.headline: Okogie racked up zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound in two minutes during Monday's 132-124 loss to Chicago.
items.story: Okogie has been mostly a non-factor this season, despite the fact that, for a period of time, he was inserted into the starting lineup. He has now appeared in 16 straight games, averaging 3.3 points and 0.8 three-pointers in 12.6 minutes per contest. While the Rockets seem destined to make the playoffs, depth could certainly be an issue when it matters most.

items.headline: Okogie recorded 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 129-93 loss to Denver.
items.story: Wednesday's game got out of hand during the second half, allowing Okogie to see more playing time off the bench. The 24 minutes were his most since Feb. 25, and considering Okogie got single-digit minutes in four of his prior six games to Wednesday, his fantasy appeal remains muted overall.

items.headline: Okogie provided 14 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals across 24 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 128-97 win over the Kings.
items.story: The 27-year-old wing saw his biggest workload in February during the rout and scored in double digits for the first time this month as a result. Okogie has been struggling to hang onto a spot in the Rockets' rotation, but with Jae'Sean Tate (knee) sidelined into March and Amen Thompson (quadriceps) banged up as well, minutes should be a little easier to come by in the short term.

items.headline: Okogie (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Thursday in the Rockets' 105-101 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: For the second time in three games, head coach Ime Udoka dropped the struggling Okogie from his nine-man rotation and instead opted to go with Jae'Sean Tate for the final spot. The two DNPs were the first of the season for Okogie, who has fallen out of favor after shooting just 39.7 percent from the field and 31.8 percent from three-point range since the calendar flipped to 2026.

items.headline: Okogie recorded no counting stats in 10 minutes during Wednesday's 105-102 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Okogie did his best Tony Snell impersonation, failing to record a stat despite playing 10 minutes. While he has been able to remain in the rotation, Okogie rarely contributes in the box score. In 52 games this season, he has averaged just 5.2 points and 0.9 steals in 19.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Okogie is not in the Rockets' starting lineup against the Thunder on Saturday, Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.story: Okogie started Thursday's loss to the Hornets but will revert to a reserve role Saturday after Tari Eason (lower leg) was cleared to return. Okogie has started eight of the Rockets' last 14 games, and over that span he has averaged 4.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.9 threes and 0.9 steals over 21.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Okogie is in the Rockets' starting lineup against the Hornets on Thursday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie has come off the bench in the Rockets' last three games, but he'll make his 29th start of the season Thursday due to the uncertainty over whether Tari Eason (lower leg) will play. Okogie has averaged 3.8 points, 3.1 rebounds and 0.9 assists over 18.6 minutes per game since Jan. 1.

items.headline: Okogie won't start Saturday's game against the Mavericks, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: With Tari Eason (leg) back in the lineup, Okogie will retreat to the bench. Over his last five appearances with the second unit, the 27-year-old wing has averaged 2.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 15.6 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Okogie is in the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup with the Hawks, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie will return to the starting unit with Tari Eason (rest) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith and Alperen Sengun. In 27 starts this season, Okogie has posted averages of 6.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.1 triples and 1.5 steals per game.

items.headline: Okogie isn't in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Grizzlies, Jackson Gatlin of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Okogie will retreat to a bench role Monday with Tari Eason set to return from a right ankle injury. Okogie hasn't impressed as a reserve recently, as he's been held to zero points in three of his last five bench appearances.

items.headline: Okogie racked up five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-3 FT), one rebound and one steal across 17 minutes during Tuesday's 111-106 victory over San Antonio.
items.story: Okogie remained in the starting lineup but logged fewer than 20 minutes for the second straight game. With head coach Ime Udoka seemingly against starting Reed Sheppard, Okogie has been able to stick as a meaningful part of the rotation despite his lack of production. As a player who is averaging 5.5 points and 1.0 steals in 19.5 minutes per game this season, Okogie warrants no real fantasy attention.

items.headline: Okogie is in the Rockets' starting lineup against the Spurs on Tuesday, Will Guillory of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Okogie was moved to the bench for Sunday's loss to the Pelicans after starting in the three prior games. However, he'll return to the starting lineup Tuesday in the absence of Steven Adams, who is out indefinitely due to a Grade 3 left ankle sprain that he suffered against New Orleans on Sunday. As a starter this season, Okogie is averaging 6.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.1 threes and 1.5 steals over 23.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Okogie is not in the Rockets' starting lineup against the Pelicans on Sunday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie started in each of the Rockets' last three games, though he accumulated just 10 points over that span. He'll revert to a reserve role Sunday while Steven Adams enters Houston's starting lineup.

items.headline: Okogie contributed one point (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one steal over 33 minutes during Friday's 110-105 victory over Minnesota.
items.story: Okogie remained in the starting lineup, logging a season-high 33 minutes in the process. While the playing time was certainly encouraging, the same can't be said for his production. With Tari Eason on the verge of returning from an ankle injury, Okogie will likely shift back to a bench role in the near future. Even as a starter, he holds no value in fantasy, outside of the deepest formats.

items.headline: Okogie is in the Rockets' starting lineup against the Bulls on Tuesday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie has averaged just 9.8 minutes off the bench over the Rockets' last five games, but he'll enter the starting lineup for the first time since Dec. 23 while Aaron Holiday comes off the bench. Over his last nine starts, Okogie averaged 6.9 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.1 threes and 1.0 steals over 24.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Okogie amassed zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) across nine minutes during Monday's 100-97 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Okogie failed to record a single stat, logging no more than 13 minutes for the sixth time in the past seven games. Head coach Ime Udoka continues to throw out some confusing lineups, with Okogie typically starting or barely seeing the floor. Even when he has been afforded starter-level minutes, Okogie is nowhere near being a viable fantasy asset. He can be safely ignored in all standard formats.

items.headline: Okogie amassed zero points (0-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over 10 minutes during Thursday's 119-96 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Okogie was limited to a minor role as he moved out of the starting lineup for the first time since Dec. 1. The disappointing performance lowered his 2025-26 season averages to 6.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He's unlikely to regain significant playing time for now while both Kevin Durant and Tari Eason are fit.

items.headline: Okogie finished with 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 30 minutes during Thursday's 133-128 overtime loss to New Orleans.
items.story: The Rockets continue to trust Okogie with stable workloads, as his versatility on both ends of the court has made him an invaluable part of the rotation. Over his last five games, he's averaging 9.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 23.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Okogie posted eight points (3-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 21 minutes during Thursday's 115-113 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Okogie continues to play a key role for Houston, though his fantasy impact isn't as good as his real-life impact. Across 22 appearances, Okogie holds averages of 6.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Okogie will return to the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Kings, Michael C. Wright of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Okogie will replace Reed Sheppard in the starting unit in a matchup-based decision by coach Ime Udoka, so Okogie should be looking at minutes in the mid-20s Wednesday evening. Through 12 games as a starter this season, Okogie owns averages of 7.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 triples and 1.9 steals per game.

items.headline: Okogie will come off the bench in Sunday's game against the Jazz, Vanessa Richardson of Space City Home Network reports.
items.story: With Kevin Durant (personal) back in action, Okogie will retreat to the second unit. Over four outings off the bench this season, the 27-year-old swingman has averaged 6.0 points and 2.3 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Okogie is starting Monday's game against the Suns, Matt Young of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.story: Okogie and Reed Sheppard will join the first unit with Steven Adams coming off the bench and Kevin Durant (personal) out. Okogie has had plenty of run as a starter this season, averaging 7.8 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.9 steals in 10 chances with the starting five.

items.headline: Okogie will come off the bench for Wednesday's game in Cleveland, Vanessa Richardson of Space City Home Network reports.
items.story: Rockets head coach Ime Udoka is going big, starting Steven Adams and Alperen Sengun to match the Cavaliers' more traditional frontcourt, so Okogie will head back to the second unit. As a member of the reserves this season, Okogie owns averages of 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers per contest.

items.headline: Okogie finished with 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and four steals over 21 minutes during Friday's 140-116 win over Portland.
items.story: Okogie remained in the starting lineup, tallying at least four steals for the second time this season. While he has been a key piece for the Rockets, especially on the defensive end, his playing time typically restricts him from being a suitable fantasy asset. Tari Eason was forced to leave the game due to a hip injury, potentially opening up a few extra minutes for Okogie. However, this is unlikely to change the fact that he can be treated as nothing more than a potential streaming candidate.

items.headline: Okogie ended Wednesday's 124-109 victory over Memphis with 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-5 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and two steals in 24 minutes.
items.story: Okogie has worked wonders for the Rockets since joining the starting lineup, averaging 9.4 points, 1.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.4 steals and 2.0 threes made in five games (Houston is 5-0 in that stretch). In a lineup headlined by Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson, Okogie is not needed to score as much offensively but is capable of hitting open shots if necessary, shooting 51.7 percent from the field and 55.6 percent from three in those five starts.

items.headline: Okogie provided 10 points (4-5 FG), one rebound, two assists, two triples and one turnover through 24 minutes as a starter during Wednesday's 139-121 win over the Raptors.
items.story: "[Okogie] knows his role," Rockets head coach Ime Udoka stated during a recent interview, explaining his decision to move Okogie into the first unit. "He's keeping it simple. He brings the physicality and aggressiveness on the defensive side of the ball. Knows how to play off other guys and then fits in with the areas we like: Crashing the glass, slashing, making plays, second opportunities." Since being inserted into the first unit, the Rockets have rattled off two straight wins, so for now, he looks to be locked in as a starter.

items.headline: Okogie is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Nets, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie will move into the starting lineup after coming off the bench in the first two games, during which he averaged 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 18.5 minutes. He'll replace big man Steven Adams, giving the Rockets a smaller and quicker starting unit.

items.headline: Okogie racked up eight points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block over 20 minutes during Tuesday's 125-124 double-overtime loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Okogie saw a decent role during his Houston debut, though that could change when the Rockets get some reinforcements back -- Jae'Sean Tate (ankle) and Dorian Finney-Smith (ankle) are currently still sidelined. Okogie is more of a defensive specialist with a low usage rate, limiting his overall upside in fantasy formats.

items.headline: Okogie will come off the bench in Tuesday's game against the Thunder, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Okogie will return to the second unit after getting the starting nod in Thursday's preseason win over the Hawks. The 27-year-old swingman will provide depth for the Rockets this season and isn't guaranteed to receive significant minutes on a nightly basis.

items.headline: Okogie compiled 28 points (8-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 10-12 FT), three rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two steals in 32 minutes during Thursday's preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Okogie had his best game of the preseason, thrust into a starting role after it was announced Houston would be resting the majority of its starting five. Okogie signed a one-year deal with the Rockets during the offseason, providing the team with a proven defensive asset. While he is unlikely to play consistent minutes, he will be ready to go whenever his name is called.

items.headline: Bamba is not listed in the starting lineup for Friday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Jaxson Hayes will start Friday, so Bamba will head back to the bench after starting in Utah's last three contests. The 28-year-old has appeared in 12 regular-season games in 2026-27, averaging 9.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.8 blocks over 20.7 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Bamba had 15 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and one block across 31 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Bamba has strung together two strong outings in a row, following up a 26-point effort against the Spurs. His minutes have jumped in that stretch, with Jusuf Nurkic (foot), Jaxson Hayes (knee) and Jaren Jackson (knee) all sidelined. The veteran big man has been one of the league's most efficient big men this season and should hold onto the starting job for now.

items.headline: Bamba recorded 26 points (10-13 FG, 6-6 3Pt, 0-3 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block in 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Bamba was hoisted into a larger role Sunday due to Jaxson Hayes (knee), Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) being out. Bamba did not disappoint, posting a team-high 26 points. The big man did most of his damage from distance, connecting on all six three-point attempts, his most in a game since 2022. Bamba figures to retain a sizable role for as long as Utah's frontcourt battles injuries.

items.headline: Bamba will start in Sunday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: With Jaxson Hayes (knee) ruled out, Bamba will get the start Sunday night, his first since the 2024-25 campaign. In 101 career regular-season starts, the 28-year-old has averaged 10.0 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.5 blocks over 24.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bamba recorded nine points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 20 minutes during Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Friday was the first time since Oct. 26 that Bamba played 20-plus minutes, and that was largely due to Jaxson Hayes leaving the game in the second quarter and not returning due to a left knee injury. Bamba made the most of his extended playing time, with four of his team-high eight rebounds coming on the offensive glass, although he ended up fouling out late in the fourth quarter. The Jazz's next game takes place Sunday against the Spurs, and Bamba could be Utah's starting center in that contest if Hayes is unable to play.

items.headline: Bamba supplied seven points (2-3 FG, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds and three blocks in 17 minutes during Tuesday's 115-109 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Bamba was active on the glass and protected the rim in his bench minutes, giving Utah some energy inside. With Jaren Jackson (knee) and Jusuf Nurkic (foot) both out, the veteran center has a chance to carve out a bigger role in the frontcourt rotation. He'll continue to split those minutes with Jaxson Hayes, Kyle Filipowski and Tony Bradley until the Jazz get healthy.

items.headline: Bamba (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game in New Orleans.
items.story: Bamba will push through an ankle issue and make himself available for Wednesday's game. He's averaging 9.0 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per contest this season.

items.headline: Bamba (ankle) participated in Wednesday's morning shootaround, per Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune.
items.story: Bamba is trending in a positive direction ahead of Wednesday's game in New Orleans. He can be tentatively placed on the right side of his questionable designation.

items.headline: Bamba is questionable for Wednesday's game in New Orleans due to a sprained right ankle.
items.story: Bamba must have tweaked his ankle during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs, and now he's in danger of sitting out Wednesday's game. If Bamba is forced to the sidelines, Kyle Filipowski would likely pick up most of his minutes.

items.headline: Bamba amassed eight points (3-5 FG, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds and two blocks over 18 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Bamba made the most of his limited opportunities, collecting four offensive rebounds and tying for the team lead with eight boards. He also registered multiple blocks despite playing fewer minutes than starting center Jaxson Hayes. Bamba's rebounding and rim protection give him some appeal in deeper formats, but Utah's crowded frontcourt rotation limits his consistency.

items.headline: Bamba totaled 14 points (7-8 FG), seven rebounds, one assist and four blocks across 29 minutes during Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Bamba made his first appearance of the season, delivering arguably his best performance in a number of years. Utah is quickly running out of frontcourt options, with Jusuf Nurkic (toe), Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Jaren Jackson (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) all sidelined. Other than Nurkic, we don't really have a timeline on when any of the other players will return to the court. However, viewing Bamba as a speculative short-term add isn't the worst idea.

items.headline: Bamba (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 123-103 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Utah leaned on Jaxson Hayes and Jaren Jackson in the frontcourt, leaving Bamba without an opportunity in the season opener. The veteran center appears to be a depth option and could struggle to find consistent minutes without injuries ahead of him.

items.headline: Bamba finished with eight points (4-6 FG) and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 117-106 preseason loss to Denver.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Bamba flirted with a double-double Tuesday. The journeyman big man is contending for the backup center role behind Jusuf Nurkic, but Bamba looks to be trailing Jaxson Hayes for playing time.

items.headline: Bamba agreed to a two-year contract with the Jazz on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bamba spent the first four-plus seasons of his career in Orlando before suiting up for the Lakers, 76ers, Clippers, Pelicans, Jazz and Raptors. The 2018 No. 6 overall pick has appeared in 368 regular-season contests, averaging 6.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.4 steals over 16.7 minutes. Bamba isn't the most talented scorer in the NBA, but his defensive acumen gives him value for a Utah squad that's looking to improve in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Jazz waived Bamba on Thursday, Kevin Reynolds of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Bamba went down with an illness and wasn't able to travel with the team on its upcoming three-game road trip, and Utah cut him. In two games with the Jazz, Bamba accounted for a total of 10 points, 20 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two turnovers across 38 minutes.

items.headline: The Jazz signed Bamba to a 10-day contract Sunday.
items.story: Bamba will get another crack with the Jazz after his first 10-day contract was set to expire Sunday. He appeared in two games for Utah on March 4 and 5 and averaged 5.0 points, 10.0 rebounds and 1.0 blocks over 19.0 minutes per game. Bamba gives the Jazz additional frontcourt depth behind Kyle Filipowski and Kevin Love.

items.headline: Bamba ended with four points (2-3 FG), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 106-102 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: This was Bamba's first taste of action since he signed a 10-day contract Feb. 26. He made a strong impression, and with his shot-blocking upside, he's worth monitoring in case he sticks around.

items.headline: Bamba signed a 10-day contract with the Jazz on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bamba has been a standout at the G League level and is being added to provide some depth in Utah. The Jazz have several injuries up front, so there is a path to minutes for Bamba. The big man averaged 17.0 points, 11.5 rebounds and 2.5 blocks at the G League level.

items.headline: Bamba agreed to a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the Raptors on Sunday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Bamba will likely provide Toronto with some added depth at center while Jakob Poeltl battles a back injury. Sandro Mamukelashvili should continue to start at center in Poeltl's absence, though Bamba could end up emerging as Mamukelashvili's top backup in the short term. The 27-year-old Bamba had gotten off to a strong start to the season in the G League with the Salt Lake City Stars, averaging 16.5 points, 11.9 rebounds and 2.7 blocks in 29.3 minutes per contest over 15 appearances.

items.headline: Bamba and the Jazz agreed to a contract Thursday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: The terms of the deal have yet to be reported, but this may be a training camp deal. Bamba has bounced around the league quite a bit with stints in Orlando, both teams in Los Angeles, Philadelphia and New Orleans. He holds career regular-season averages of 6.8 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.3 blocks.

items.headline: Bamba contributed two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist and one block across 26 minutes during Thursday's 113-93 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Bamba, who is on a 10-day deal with the Pelicans, now has two games under his belt. His production has left a lot to be desired, however. In 20.5 minutes, he's averaging 1.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, 0.5 assists and 1.0 blocks on 20.0 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Bamba and the Pelicans agreed to a 10-day contract Monday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: After a brief stint with the Clippers to begin the 2024-25 season, Bamba has since been feasting in the G League for the Birmingham Squadron, posting averages of 21.0 points, 14.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.8 blocks. The Pelicans don't have much to play for at this point in the season, so it would make sense for them to give Bamba an opportunity to impress in the frontcourt.

items.headline: The Jazz acquired Bamba, P.J. Tucker, a 2030 second-round pick and cash from the Clippers on Saturday in exchange for Drew Eubanks and Patty Mills, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After missing most of the first month of the season while recovering from a knee issue, Bamba debuted Nov. 17 for the Clippers and had regularly been serving as the top backup to starting center Ivica Zubac. However, the 26-year-old recently fell out of favor, appearing in just one of the team's last three games before the Clippers shipped him out and brought back Eubanks, who should settle in as LA's new backup center. Eubanks had been filling a regular spot in Utah's rotation, but Bamba may not be guaranteed regular playing time with the Jazz while both Walker Kessler and Kyle Filipowski are healthy and likely to be prioritized ahead of Bamba, who is on an expiring contract. If Bamba does find himself getting meaningful playing time at any point, he could be an appealing fantasy option; he turned in strong per-minute averages of 4.6 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 12.6 minutes over his 28 appearances with the Clippers.

items.headline: Bamba is not in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Bamba started in the Clippers' last two games, but he'll return to his regular second-unit role here since Ivica Zubac (eye) is back in action. Bamba has played off the bench in 24 of his 26 appearances this season, averaging 4.2 points and 4.3 rebounds across 12.5 minutes per game in those instances.

items.headline: Bamba amassed 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt) and seven rebounds across 15 minutes during Monday's 112-99 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Making a spot start at the five for the Clippers on Monday, Bamba was serviceable during his 15 minutes of action in what was his first appearance with the first unit this year. The veteran big man did lose considerable center minutes to Nicolas Batum and Kobe Brown from Los Angeles' second unit, though. If Ivica Zubac is able to return from an eye injury in time for Wednesday's showdown with the Celtics, Bamba would certainly be slated to revert back to the bench.

items.headline: Bamba is starting Monday's game against the Bulls, independent NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Bamba will get a look as the starting center after news broke earlier in the day that Ivica Zubac (eye) would be held out Monday. Bamba has been held to single-digit minutes in two of his last four appearances but should be in line for a longer look versus Chicago.

items.headline: Bamba ended with 12 points (5-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and eight rebounds in 16 minutes during Thursday's 116-98 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Bamba posted a season-high 12 points while hitting a couple of three-pointers during an efficient outing. The 26-year-old also tied his season-best mark in rebounds. The big man has seen little playing time of late, as he has to compete with Nicolas Batum and Kai Jones for minutes behind Ivica Zubac. Over his last five outings, Bamba has averaged 3.2 points and 3.2 rebounds across 9.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bamba finished with two rebounds and one block across 12 minutes during Friday's 102-92 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Bamba continues to put together the worst season of his career, as he is averaging 3.8 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 12.8 minutes per game. Playing behind one of the most consistent centers in the league (Ivica Zubac), Bamba's opportunities have been few and far between. Should a meaningful role ever present itself, Bamba would then become a factor, at least on the defensive end of the floor.

items.headline: Bamba contributed zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and three blocks in six minutes during Monday's 114-110 victory over Memphis.
items.story: Ivica Zubac was considered questionable to play with a calf issue but ended up producing a monster performance in 40 minutes. Bamba has shot-blocking upside, obviously, but the minutes just won't be there when Zubac is healthy.

items.headline: Bamba (knee) is available for Friday's game against Denver, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Bamba sat out Sunday's loss to the Rockets due to left knee injury management, though he'll suit up Friday after nearly a week of rest. The big man has averaged 3.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.8 blocks across 13.2 minutes per contest over his last five outings.

items.headline: Coach Tyronn Lue said Bamba (knee) was a full participant during Tuesday's practice, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Bamba didn't play Sunday against the Rockets due to left knee injury management, but he's on track to suit up Friday in Denver. He's logged double-digit minutes in eight of his last 10 appearances, averaging 13.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
items.story: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Beekman had his Exhibit 10 contract converted to a two-way deal by the Wizards on Saturday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: Beekman signed with the Wizards for training camp and has done enough to earn himself a two-way contract. He last played in the NBA in the 2024-25 season and will likely spend most of his time with the G League's Capital City Go-Go in 2026-27.

items.headline: Beekman agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the Wizards on Sunday.
items.story: Beekman went undrafted in 2024. Since then, he has spent the bulk of his career in the G League, appearing in 62 games between the Santa Cruz Warriors, Long Island Nets and Osceola Magic, averaging 11.7 points, 4.2 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.1 steals over 30.3 minutes per contest. He also logged 36 regular-season games between Brooklyn and Golden State in 2024-25.

items.headline: Beekman registered 13 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, 14 assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Saturday's 91-83 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Hawks.
items.story: Beekman finished his Summer League run strong, recording his first double-double in Las Vegas while leading the Wizards to a victory. His performance helped strengthen his case for a training camp invite with Washington.

items.headline: Beekman logged 11 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 FT) and two assists in eight minutes during Saturday's 126-118 preseason win over the Heat.
items.story: Beekman finished Saturday's exhibition contest as one of six Magic players to score in double digits, and he finished third on the team in the scoring category behind Jase Richardson (13) and Tristan da Silva (12). Beekman inked an Exhibit 10 contract with the Magic in early September after competing with the Nuggets in the Summer League, and he is competing for a permanent spot on Orlando's roster for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Beekman agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with Orlando on Tuesday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Beekman will compete for a spot on Orlando's regular-season roster during training camp. The 23-year-old point guard joined the Warriors on a two-way contract before the 2024-25 season, though he was eventually traded to the Nets in December. He appeared in 36 regular-season games (four starts) between Golden State and Brooklyn, averaging 2.6 points and 1.8 assists across 13.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) is listed in the starting lineup for Thursday's Summer League game against Milwaukee, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Beekman battled a calf injury at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, but he's back at full strength for the start of Summer League play. He'll draw the start alongside Spencer Jones, Hunter Tyson, DaRon Holmes and Tyrell Harrison.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Nuggets on Saturday, Bennett Durando of The Denver Post reports.
items.story: Beekman will join Denver on a non-guaranteed contract and compete for a roster spot. The 23-year-old guard signed a two-way contract with the Warriors last season before being traded to the Nets in December. He averaged 2.6 points, 1.8 assists and 1.1 rebounds across 13.0 minutes per game in 36 regular-season appearances (four starts) between Golden State and Brooklyn.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Beekman popped up on Saturday's injury report due to right calf soreness, and the injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for Sunday's regular-season finale. With Beekman and D'Angelo Russell (ankle) both sidelined, Tyson Etienne could be in line to make his first career NBA start. Over his last five outings (four starts), Beekman averaged 5.4 points, 4.8 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 2.6 steals over 26.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Beekman is listed as questionable for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Knicks due to right calf soreness, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Beekman has started in the Nets' last four games, but he could miss Sunday's contest while working through a right calf issue. With D'Angelo Russell (ankle) already ruled out, Beekman's absence would open the door for Tyson Etienne to see more playing time, potentially in a starting role.

items.headline: Beekman racked up 11 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and three steals over 32 minutes during Friday's 117-91 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Making his fourth straight start for the Nets, the undrafted rookie once again made his presence felt at the defensive end of the court. Beekman has recorded three steals in four of the last five games, and during his run in the starting five he's averaging 6.3 points, 5.5 assists, 2.8 boards and 2.5 steals in 28.0 minutes.

items.headline: Beekman ended with zero points (0-3 FG), four rebounds, 10 assists and three steals over 31 minutes during Tuesday's 119-114 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Although Beekman was held scoreless Tuesday, he was able to dish out a game-high 10 assists while playing a passive role on offense. With the Nets missing several key contributors, it wouldn't be surprising to see Beekman remain in the starting lineup during the final week of the season. Beekman has registered at least five assists, four rebounds and three steals in both of his starting appearances thus far.

items.headline: Beekman contributed 14 points (6-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and three steals over 36 minutes during Sunday's 120-109 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Beekman got his first career start Sunday with D'Angelo Russell (ankle) out and Brooklyn shorthanded, lifting the Nets on both ends of the floor while leading all players in scoring, assists and steals in a losing effort. Beekman's points were a season-high figure, and he also matched season-best marks in rebounds, assists and steals.

items.headline: Beekman will start Sunday's game against the Raptors, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Beekman has been a consistent part of Brooklyn's rotation but played 18 minutes against the Timberwolves on Thursday, posting two points, two rebounds, two assists and three steals. With the Nets shorthanded once again, including an absence to D'Angelo Russell (ankle), Beekman will draw his first career start and should handle a sizable role against the Raptors, who'll also be without multiple starters.

items.headline: Beekman logged three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one rebound over nine minutes during Monday's 111-108 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Beekman was back in the rotation, albeit for just nine minutes. After playing a somewhat consistent role through the months of January and February, this was just the second time Beekman has suited up since the calendar flipped to March. In 28 games played this season, Beekman is averaging just 2.0 points and 1.2 assists.

items.headline: Beekman registered three points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and three steals in 27 minutes during Saturday's 115-94 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Beekman played a career-high 27 minutes, although his numbers tell a different story. Despite the increased playing time, Beekman had no real impact, a worrying trend given he has failed to score double-digits all season. He does provide the Nets with a defensive presence, something that could at least keep him on the floor down the stretch of the season.

items.headline: Beekman amassed two points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 99-97 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Beekman played at least 20 minutes for the second time in his past four games. However, he has also been a DNP-CD in two of the past five games, as the Nets continue to shuffle their rotation on a nightly basis. While he could step into a consistent role at some point, Beekman is likely to remain on the fringe of the rotation, at least for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Beekman finished Monday's 110-96 loss to the Kings with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and two assists across 12 minutes.
items.story: Beekman was back in the rotation, continuing a recent pattern not dissimilar to his teammates. The Nets are chopping and changing their rotation on a nightly basis, making it hard to know who will be playing and how much they will be playing. Unless we see a change in their mentality, Beekman is likely to remain on the fringes of the rotation until further notice.

items.headline: Beekman finished with one point (1-2 FT) and one assist across four minutes during Wednesday's 130-113 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Beekman moved back into the rotation, logging fewer than five minutes for the fourth time in six games since joining the Nets. Moved as part of the Dennis Schroder deal, Beekman has remained on the fringe of the rotation despite the change of location. At this point, there is no reason to think that his role will increase any time soon.

items.headline: The Warriors traded Beekman to the Nets on Sunday, along with De'Anthony Melton (knee) and three second-round picks, in exchange for Dennis Schroder and a second-round pick.
items.story: Beekman wasn't mentioned in the initial trade reports but will ultimately take Yongxi Cui's (knee) spot on the roster. Beekman has made two NBA appearances during his rookie season, totaling only four minutes. However, there may be more playing time available in Brooklyn, especially if the Nets remain active in the trade market. Beekman (trade pending) won't play in Monday's game against the Cavaliers, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.

items.headline: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Allen is set to miss a third consecutive contest due to a concussion. Sion James will continue to start while Royce O'Neale should get more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Allen is currently dealing with concussion-like symptoms and is in line for a second straight absence. Sion James and Royce O'Neale should continue to see an uptick in playing time until Allen is cleared to return.

items.headline: Allen (concussion-like symptoms) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: With Allen on the shelf, Royce O'Neale and Christian Anderson should see a boost in minutes off the Hornets' bench. Allen's next chance to suit up will come Friday versus the Hawks.

items.headline: Allen is not listed in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Allen will shift back to the bench after starting the previous three contests with Brandon Miller (groin) returning from a two-game absence. Allen should remain a vital part of the Hornets' rotation, as he's averaging 15.2 points, 2.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 3.5 three-pointers in 27.3 minutes across 12 outings this season.

items.headline: Allen logged 14 points (5-11 FG, 4-8 3Pt), four rebounds, six assists and one steal over 34 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Few players have benefited more from Charlotte's backcourt injuries than Allen, whose expanded responsibilities have helped him average 15.2 points and 3.5 three-pointers per game. His 46.9 percent shooting from deep has been a major asset, and the additional playmaking opportunities are a welcome bonus. The bigger question is whether he'll maintain this level of involvement once the Hornets return to full strength, as he's likely to move to a bench role when Brandon Miller (groin) and Kon Knueppel (hamstring) are back in the mix.

items.headline: Allen finished with 27 points (8-14 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals across 34 minutes during Monday's 124-112 win over Cleveland.
items.story: Allen erupted for a game-high 27 points after going scoreless in Friday's 119-80 loss to the Celtics. Monday's outing marked the second straight start for the former Sun, and he's now eclipsed the 20-point threshold in three of his last five games. Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is sidelined for at least another four weeks, so Allen is likely to continue seeing a heavy workload, with Brandon Miller (groin) also out.

items.headline: Allen will start in Friday's game against the Celtics
items.story: With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Dennis Schroder (thigh) ruled out, Allen will make his first start of the 2026-27 campaign. In 27 regular-season starts with the Suns in 2025-26, the 31-year-old averaged 17.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.4 steals over 31.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Allen ended Wednesday's 114-104 loss to the Nets with 22 points (6-11 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 27 minutes.
items.story: Allen scored at least 22 points for the second time in the past three games, providing Charlotte with a nice scoring punch off the bench. Although his arrow is likely headed in the wrong direction, another leg injury to Kon Knueppel could ensure Allen remains a viable asset in most fantasy formats, at least for the time being. If he was dropped in your league, adding him might be the way to go.

items.headline: Allen ended Monday's 124-91 loss to Detroit with 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound over 19 minutes.
