items.story: The 76ers declined Watford's team option in June, but he's found a new home ahead of training camp. In New Orleans, Watford will likely provide some emergency depth in the frontcourt, and he may have a tough time carving out a consistent role.

items.headline: The 76ers declined Watford's team option for 2026-27 on Monday, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Watford is now set to become an unrestricted free agent. He's coming off a down campaign in 2025-26, as he posted regular-season averages of 6.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 16.3 minutes per tilt over 53 games.

items.headline: Watford had two points (1-1 FG), one assist and two steals across nine minutes during Sunday's 144-114 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: An adductor strain early in the season more or less derailed Watford's campaign, as he averaged a career-low 6.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 16.3 minutes per tilt over 53 regular-season games. His contract includes a $2.8 million team option for 2026-27, and it's still plausible Philadelphia will pick it up to reinforce its frontcourt depth.

items.headline: Watford (illness) is available for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Magic, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Watford will shake off his probable tag due to an illness and suit up Wednesday. He logged 15 minutes over only three regular-season appearances in April and isn't likely to see significant burn against Orlando.

items.headline: Watford (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Magic.
items.story: Watford is under the weather but appears likely to suit up for Wednesday's contest. However, he totaled just 15 minutes over three regular-season appearances in April, so he isn't guaranteed to see significant playing time.

items.headline: Watford (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the 76ers' 119-109 loss to the Heat.
items.story: With all of Tyrese Maxey, Paul George, Kelly Oubre and Joel Embiid returning to action for Philadelphia within the past three games following extended absences, Watford is one of several 76ers supporting players who has fallen out of the rotation. Before failing to receive any minutes in Philadelphia's last two contests, Watford had appeared in each of the previous 17 games and averaged 7.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 17.9 minutes.

items.headline: Watford contributed 15 points (6-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds and four assists over 22 minutes during Monday's 123-103 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Watford scored in double figures off the bench, though a lack of production for the 76ers other than that of VJ Edgecombe resulted in a lopsided defeat. Over Watford's past six games, all of which have come in a reserve role, the LSU product has reached the 10-point mark in four contests. The three-point shot remains absent from his game, as Watford entered Monday shooting 21.3 percent from beyond the arc and hasn't converted a triple since Feb. 3.

items.headline: Watford closed with 20 points (7-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-6 FT), nine rebounds and four assists over 24 minutes during Saturday's 126-116 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Watford made the most of his 24 minutes off the bench in this win, hitting the 20-point threshold with an efficient effort and also ending just one rebound shy of a double-double. Watford has reached the 20-point mark just twice this season, and his recent performances haven't exactly been eye-popping, so he's not expected to carry much fantasy upside going forward, especially once the 76ers start to get healthier. Right now they're playing without Tyrese Maxey (finger), Joel Embiid (oblique) and Paul George (suspension).

items.headline: Watford totaled 12 points (3-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, six assists, three blocks and one steal in 22 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's 124-96 loss to Denver.
items.story: The three blocks were a season high for Watford, as the 25-year-old forward took advantage of the Sixers' injury-depleted frontcourt rotation. Watford has scored in double digits in four of the last seven games (one start), averaging 8.6 points, 3.3 boards, 2.7 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.7 steals in 20.1 minutes.

items.headline: Watford won't start Saturday's game against the Nets, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: With Adem Bona (back) returning to action, Watford will slide to the bench after a spot start Thursday against Detroit. Despite moving to a reserve role, Watford should still see plenty of minutes given all the absences in the 76ers' frontcourt, including Kelly Oubre (elbow), Paul George (suspension), Joel Embiid (oblique), Jabari Walker (illness) and Andre Drummond (back).

items.headline: Watford is starting Thursday's game against the Pistons, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: With Kelly Oubre out multiple weeks with an elbow sprain, Watford has a chance to carve out a steady role in the first unit. Watford has averaged 9.7 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists in 24.0 minutes per game over six contests as a starter this season, shooting 52.2 percent from the field.

items.headline: Watford is not in the 76ers' starting lineup against the Hawks on Saturday.
items.story: Watford made his sixth start of the season in Wednesday's 106-102 win over the Jazz, when he finished with seven points (3-6 FG, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and one block over 22 minutes. He'll revert to a bench role for Saturday's contest due to the return of Kelly Oubre (illness).

items.headline: Watford will start Wednesday versus Utah, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Kelly Oubre (illness), VJ Edgecombe (back) and Joel Embiid (oblique) are all unavailable for Wednesday's game, so head coach Nick Nurse will trot out a starting lineup featuring Watford, Tyrese Maxey, Quentin Grimes, Dominick Barlow and Adem Bona. Across five starts this season, Watford has produced averages of 10.2 points, 5.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists per contest.

items.headline: Watford (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Saturday's 126-111 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Watford exited the rotation for the first time since Jan. 29, ending a stretch of eight consecutive appearances during which he averaged 7.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 20.5 minutes per contest and shot 48 percent from the field. Rather than turning to Watford to fill minutes on the second unit, head coach Nick Nurse gave more extended playing time to backup forwards Jabari Walker (16 minutes) and Justin Edwards (six minutes).

items.headline: Watford won't start Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Dominick Barlow is back in action following a one-game absence due to an illness, pushing Watford to the second unit. Over his last five appearances off the bench, the 25-year-old power forward has averaged 7.2 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 19.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Watford is starting Monday's game against Portland.
items.story: Watford will presumably be asked to shoulder a sizable workload Monday with both Dominick Barlow (illness) and Joel Embiid (knee) sidelined. This marks Watford's first start since Nov. 14 against the Pistons.

items.headline: Watford finished with 16 points (7-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 113-94 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Paul George's (suspension) extended absence will reveal some new wrinkles in the rotation, and it seems like Watford could make a more significant impact. The fifth-year pro has been hampered by injuries this season, but he appears to be past any limitations. It's too early to give Watford serious fantasy consideration, but his place in the rotation is worth monitoring.

items.headline: Watford (adductor) played the final 4:45 of Wednesday's 131-110 win over the Wizards, finishing with three assists and no other statistics during his time on the court.
items.story: Available to play for the first time since Nov. 25 after a lengthy absence due to a left adductor strain, Watford wasn't included in head coach Nick Nurse's main rotation, as he didn't enter the contest until the 76ers had already built a 17-point lead in the waning minutes of the game. The 25-year-old forward could eventually emerge as a rotation option once he's further removed from the adductor strain, but he may need the 76ers to be without one or more key contributors in order to see meaningful minutes.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) is available to play Wednesday versus Washington.
items.story: Head coach Nick Nurse hinted during his pregame media availability Wednesday that while Watford may be available, he might not see the floor in his first game back from a lengthy layoff. With Kelly Oubre (knee) also set to return Wednesday, Watford might not be a consistent part of the rotation moving forward.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) will have a heavy minutes restriction if he plays in Wednesday's game against Washington, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: Watford is labeled as probable for Wednesday's game, but it's unclear what role he'll play if active. He's been unavailable since Nov. 25 due to a thigh strain.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Watford, who has been sidelined since picking up his thigh strain Nov. 25, is now expected to return from a lengthy absence. The 76ers are pretty healthy these days, so it will be interesting to see what type of role Watford is able to carve out.

items.headline: Watford is questionable for Wednesday's game against Washington due to a left adductor strain.
items.story: Watford sustained the strain during the Nov. 25 loss to the Magic and hasn't appeared since, though it sounds like he's on the verge of returning to action. It's unclear what kind of role he may have upon his eventual return, as it's likely Watford will face a minutes restriction right off the bat. His potential return could be bad news for the playing time of Dominick Barlow in the frontcourt, though.

items.headline: Watford (adductor) will remain on the inactive list for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Watford appears to be on the cusp of a return, as he was recently cleared for full-contact, 5-on-5 work. However, Monday will mark his 17th straight game on the sidelines. Watford's next chance to play will come Wednesday versus the Wizards.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) will be cleared for 5-on-5 practice Sunday, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Watford hasn't played since Nov. 25 due to a left adductor strain, but the forward is set to return in the near future. Across 14 appearances this season, Watford has produced averages of 8.9 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists in 20.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The 76ers announced Monday that Watford (adductor) is "continuing to progress" and is "being reintegrated into team activities," Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Watford was able to take part in Monday's practice in some capacity, but the 76ers aren't yet willing to issue a target date for his potential return to the court. The 25-year-old forward hasn't played since Nov. 25 due to a left adductor strain and appears destined to miss the final two contests of the 76ers' five-game road trip, at a minimum.

items.headline: Watford (adductor) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Watford is still nursing a strained left adductor and remains without a clear timetable for a return. He should be considered week-to-week until the 76ers provide an update on his progress.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) is out for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Watford, who hasn't played since Nov. 25 due to a strained left adductor, can be considered week-to-week until the 76ers update his timeline for a return. Dominick Barlow (illness) should continue to benefit from a fantasy perspective.

items.headline: Watford (thigh) won't play in Friday's game against the Knicks, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: It was reported at the end of November that Watford would be re-evaluated in two weeks, but the team has yet to provide another update on the timetable for his return. At this point in time, the LSU product can be considered week-to-week until Philly has more news to share on the status of Watford's rehab.

items.headline: Watford (adductor) will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.story: Watford went down during Tuesday's blowout loss to the Magic, and he's since been diagnosed with a left adductor strain. The injury is likely to keep the forward sidelined until the middle of December. With Watford out of action, the 76ers are likely to turn to Dominick Barlow and Justin Edwards to help pick up the slack in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Watford has ruled out for the rest of Tuesday's game against Orlando due to a left adductor strain, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports. He recorded eight points (2-2 FG, 4-4 FT), one rebound and one assist in 11 minutes before exiting.
items.story: Watford has been shut down for the rest of the night, but he'll have a few days to recover before his team's next matchup Friday against Brooklyn. Jabari Walker and Johni Broome could pick up a few additional minutes in the second half Tuesday in Watford's absence.

items.headline: Watford went to the locker room during the second quarter of Tuesday's game against the Magic due to an apparent groin injury, Keith Pompey of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: Watford departed with 4:07 remaining in the half after looking to suffer the injury while bringing the ball up the court. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Watford logged 19 points (7-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 127-117 loss to the Heat.
items.story: The fifth-year forward already has one triple-double this season in a start against the Raptors on Nov. 8, and Watford came within sniffing distance of another as he led the Sixers in assists on the afternoon while finishing second in points and boards. His court time and usage remain inconsistent, however, even with Joel Embiid (knee) and Kelly Oubre (knee) on the shelf. Watford had failed to score in double digits in six straight games coming into Sunday, and he'd posted a goose egg in 14 minutes against the Bucks on Thursday. Until he begins to string solid performances together, Watford will be little more than a cheap DFS option for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Watford is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Clippers, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Watford started the 76ers' past four games, even posting a triple-double in his first outing of that stretch. However, he will move back to the bench with Paul George (knee) entering the starting lineup in his season debut. George will be on a minutes restriction early, so Watford should still have a meaningful role, though the LSU product will need to maintain a high level of play to keep earning consistent minutes as George ramps up.

items.headline: Watford finished Saturday's 130-120 win over the Raptors with 20 points (8-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-5 FT), 17 rebounds, 10 assists and one block over 37 minutes.
items.story: Watford was inserted into the 76ers' starting lineup for the first time this season, and he took full advantage of the opportunity. He led all players with career highs in both rebounds and assists en route to the first triple-double of his five-year NBA career, and he finished third on the team in points behind Tyrese Maxey (31) and Joel Embiid (29). Watford's breakout performance Saturday should keep him in the 76ers' starting lineup, at least until Paul George (knee) is cleared to make his 2025-26 debut.

items.headline: Watford will start in Saturday's game against the Raptors, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.story: The fifth-year forward will get the starting nod against Toronto, pushing Jabari Walker to the bench. Over five regular-season appearances off the bench thus far, Watford has averaged 8.4 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists in 19.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Watford contributed eight points (2-4 FG, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 19 minutes during Tuesday's 113-111 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Watford was unable to follow up on his 16/9/7 game Sunday in Brooklyn, but he was still a solid contributor off the bench. With Paul George (knee) and Dominick Barlow (elbow) nursing injuries, Watford may see himself in a prominent bench role again Wednesday against Cleveland.

items.headline: Watford (hamstring) logged two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists across 18 minutes in Tuesday's 139-134 overtime win over the Wizards.
items.story: Sidelined for Philadelphia's first three games due to a tight left hamstring, Watford was cleared to make his season debut Tuesday and provided the 76ers with some reinforcement at forward while Paul George (knee) and Dominick Barlow (elbow) were both out. Watford handled a meager 8.9 percent usage rate in the contest and came up empty in the defensive categories, but he finished second to only sixth man Quentin Grimes (39 minutes) in playing time among bench players. Even so, Watford is still likely to see his minutes get cut once the likes of George, Barlow and Jared McCain (thumb) return, and it wouldn't be surprising if Watford was dropped from head coach Nick Nurse's rotation entirely.

items.headline: Watford (hamstring) will play Tuesday against the Wizards, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Watford is all set to make his season debut after a hamstring issue delayed him to open the campaign. He's likely to be eased back into the mix, but there is a path to minutes for him with so many injuries in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Cooper finished with three points (0-1 FG, 3-6 FT), four rebounds and two assists across 18 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets.
items.story: Cooper made an encouraging first impression in his Lakers debut after signing a two-way contract Nov. 10. The rookie center played a meaningful reserve role despite limited offensive opportunities, providing rebounding and defensive energy in his first extended NBA action. His playing time is worth monitoring, though he remains a speculative fantasy option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Cooper signed a two-way contract with the Lakers on Tuesday, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Cooper will provide the Lakers with some emergency depth at the center position, but he's not expected to be in the rotation. In his final season at Michigan State, Cooper averaged 11.1 points, 7.1 rebounds and 1.0 blocks per game.

items.headline: The Grizzlies waived Cooper on Saturday.
items.story: The move will make room on the roster for Richie Saunders, who signed a two-way contract with Memphis on Saturday. Cooper appeared in one game for the Grizzlies, scoring one point while tallying two rebounds and an assist in three minutes.

items.headline: Murray will start Monday against the Hornets, Hornets reporter Rod Boone reports.
items.story: Murray will replace Jahmai Mashack in the first unit for Monday's game, earning his first start of the season. Per 36 minutes this year, Murray is averaging 6.5 points, 2.2 assists, 1.1 three-pointers, 2.2 steals and 1.3 blocks.

items.headline: Murray produced seven points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one steal across 12 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Murray saw double-digit minutes for just the second time over Memphis' last seven games. He turned in an efficient performance en route to a season-high seven points and could see a bump in minutes for as long as Jerami Grant (calf) and Cameron Boozer (ankle) are sidelined.

items.headline: Murray amassed no counting stats in one minute during Monday's 118-102 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Murray barely saw the floor Monday, the latest installment of what has been a non-descript season so far. He has played in seven games thus far, averaging 1.3 points and 1.7 rebounds in 12.1 minutes per contest. Outside of very deep leagues, he holds no fantasy value.

items.headline: Murray won't start Wednesday's game against Utah.
items.story: Jaylen Wells will return to the starting five in Memphis' regular-season opener, pushing Murray to the second unit. He's expected to provide frontcourt depth for the Grizzlies and isn't guaranteed to see the floor Wednesday.

items.headline: Murray is in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Murray will enter the starting unit for the preseason finale. The No. 23 pick in the 2023 NBA Draft isn't expected to have a major role in his first campaign with the Grizzlies in 2026-27, so he'll likely be a bench option in the regular season.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers traded Murray and Jerami Grant to the Grizzlies on Monday in exchange for Ja Morant, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Murray was the No. 23 pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, but unlike his brother, Keegan Murray, in Sacramento, Kris has failed to break out at the NBA level. He's been a solid role player for Portland, averaging a career-high 23.4 minutes per game across 57 regular-season appearances (15 starts) last season. However, he posted only 5.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.9 steals a night.

items.headline: Murray finished with no counting stats in one minute during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: While he closed the season in a muted role, Murray was serviceable for Portland in 2025-26. The third-year swingman made 15 starts during the regular season, averaging 5.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.9 steals in a career-high 23.4 minutes per tilt covering 57 regular-season games. Murray figures to play a similar role for the Trail Blazers next year.

items.headline: Murray ended with 16 points (6-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and five assists across 30 minutes during Monday's 134-99 victory over the Nets.
items.story: The absence of Jerami Grant (foot) opened the door to more playing time for Murray, who took advantage of the opportunity by tying a season best in points and setting a season high in dimes. However, Murray is likely to revert to a lesser role once Grant is healthy, which could drop Murray's minutes back under the 20s.

items.headline: Murray totaled 14 points (6-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 25 minutes during Monday's 114-95 victory over the Nets.
items.story: After going unused off the bench Sunday, Murray saw extended run Monday and made the most of it, contributing an ultra-efficient 14 points in a winning effort. This marked the Iowa product's second-highest scoring output of the season, with his top mark being a 16-point performance against the Timberwolves on Feb. 24, and his ninth double-digit scoring effort of the campaign. The availability of Vit Krejci (calf) moving forward will likely factor into Murray's role, though Monday's showing bodes well for him to remain in the rotation.

items.headline: Murray (illness) registered three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and four rebounds over 16 minutes during Sunday's 131-111 victory over Indiana.
items.story: Murray returned from a two-game absence Sunday after battling an illness. With Deni Avdija (back) also returning to action in the 20-point win, the Trail Blazers are now close to full health at forward and on the wing. Murray is unlikely to see his playing time pick up dramatically moving forward, making it difficult to depend on him for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Pacers, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Murray will shed his questionable tag and return from a two-game absence due to an illness. He has appeared in just six games (four starts) since Jan. 7, averaging 5.8 points and 2.8 rebounds across 18.2 minutes per tilt during that span.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Murray is in danger of missing a third straight game due to an illness. If he's ultimately ruled out, Sidy Cissoko, Scoot Henderson and Matisse Thybulle could see an uptick in minutes, especially if Deni Avdija (back) is also downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Murray (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Rockets, Casey Holdahl of the Trail Blazers' official site reports.
items.story: Murray initially drew a questionable tag, but the third-year pro will miss a second consecutive game while battling through an illness, so Scoot Henderson should remain in the starting lineup for Friday's contest. Murray's next chance to play is Sunday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Murray was limited to just four minutes of playing time during Sunday's loss against the Hawks due to an illness, which prevented him from playing in Wednesday's win against the Grizzlies. Scoot Henderson figures to remain in Portland's starting lineup if Murray is unable to play Friday.

items.headline: Murray (illness) won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murray attempted to play through the illness during Sunday's loss to the Hawks, but he exited the game after just four minutes and will now miss Wednesday's contest. Murray's next chance to play will come Friday in Houston.

items.headline: Murray (illness) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murray departed Sunday's matchup early due to an illness, and he's now in danger of missing additional game action. The team will presumably re-evaluate the Iowa product leading up to Wednesday's tipoff before providing another update on his status.

items.headline: Murray (illness) will not return to Sunday's game against the Hawks. He'll finish with no counting stats across four minutes.
items.story: Murray got the starting nod Sunday but logged just over four minutes before exiting the contest due to an illness. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday in Memphis.

items.headline: Murray will start Tuesday's game against Minnesota, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back) sidelined, Murray will enter the starting five in his third outing back from a 19-game absence due to a lumbar strain. As a starter this season (11 games), the 25-year-old has averaged 7.4 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.4 steals in 29.2 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Murray (back) is available for Friday's game against the Nuggets, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Murray will return from a 19-game absence due to a lumbar strain. Through 34 regular-season outings (11 starts), he has averaged 6.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals in 25.7 minutes per game. However, the team is mostly healthy Friday, so he isn't likely to reach the 25-minute mark.

items.headline: Murray (back) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Murray hasn't played since Jan. 5 due to a lumbar strain, though he appears to be nearing a return to action and was a full participant in Thursday's practice, per Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland. Through 34 regular-season outings (11 starts), he has averaged 6.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals in 25.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Murray (back) is out for Thursday's game against Utah.
items.story: A lumbar strain has left Murray with no timetable for a return. Portland will presumably re-evaluate the forward when it returns from the All-Star break.

items.headline: Murray (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Murray has been sidelined since Jan. 5 due to a back strain, and he'll remain out Wednesday. It's unclear when he'll be back in action or if he's nearing a return. His next chance to play will come Thursday at Utah.

items.headline: Murray (back) is out for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Murray will miss a 17th straight game due to a back injury. He remains without a timetable for return, but his next chance to suit up comes Wednesday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Murray (back) will not play Saturday against Memphis.
items.story: Murray will miss a 16th straight game and remains without a timetable to return. He's questionable at best for Monday's game against the 76ers.

items.headline: Murray (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murray will miss a 15th consecutive game due to a lumbar strain. His next opportunity to play is Saturday in a rematch against Memphis, though the third-year pro doesn't appear to have a clear timeline for a return.

items.headline: Murray (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Murray is set to miss his 14th straight game due to a lumbar strain. In his absence, Sidy Cissoko and Rayan Rupert should continue to see elevated opportunities against the Suns. The Iowa product's next chance to suit up will come Friday versus the Grizzlies, though a clear timetable for Murray's return remains absent.

items.headline: Murray (back) won't play Friday in New York.
items.story: There have been no reports of Murray making positive progress in his recovery, so he should be viewed as week-to-week moving forward. Murray's minutes will continue to be divvied up amongst Sidy Cissoko and Rayan Rupert.

items.headline: Murray (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Murray will miss his 10th consecutive contest due to a back strain and remains without a clear timetable for a return. He can be considered week-to-week until Portland provides an update on his progress.

items.headline: Murray is out for Friday's game against Toronto due to a lumbar strain.
items.story: Friday marks a ninth consecutive absence for Murray, The forward carries no timetable for a return and should be considered doubtful for Monday's matchup in Boston until Portland offers an update.

items.headline: Murray (back) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Miami.
items.story: Murray will miss an eighth straight game due to a lumbar strain. The third-year forward doesn't have an established timetable for return, and he can likely be viewed as doubtful for Friday's matchup with Toronto.

items.headline: Murray (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Murray's absence will extend to seven games due to a lumbar strain. His next chance to play is Thursday against the Heat, though the third-year pro lacks a clear timeline for a return. Murray stepped into a more prominent role in the nine games (eight starts) prior to his injury and averaged 7.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 steals over 28.7 minutes per game over that span.

items.headline: Murray has been diagnosed with a lumbar strain in his lower back and is currently without an official timetable to return.
items.story: Murray will miss his third consecutive game Sunday with a lumbar strain, and with no firm return date, it seems unlikely he'll play at all during Week 13. Until we receive a positive update on Murray's rehab process, he should be considered week-to-week.

items.headline: Murray (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Murray will miss a third straight game since he's dealing with a lumbar strain, but his absence won't cause a lot of issues in most fantasy formats. His next chance to play will come against the Warriors on Tuesday.

items.headline: Murray (back) is out for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Murray is in line for a second straight absence due to back soreness. He'll have another chance to return Sunday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Murray (back) will not play Wednesday against the Rockets.
items.story: Murray was previously listed as doubtful, so this is an expected update. With Jerami Grant (Achilles) out as well, the Trail Blazers could give utility man Sidy Cissoko some extra minutes against Houston.

items.headline: Murray (back) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Murray is unlikely to suit up Wednesday due to lower back soreness. In the likely event that the 25-year-old forward joins Jerami Grant (Achilles) on the sidelines, Sidy Cissoko is expected to step into the starting five.

items.headline: Murray finished with 10 points (3-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals in 27 minutes during Monday's 137-117 win over Utah.
items.story: Murray has started three consecutive games and eight of his last nine appearances amid the ongoing absence of Jerami Grant (Achilles). During that latter period, Murray has struggled to muster much fantasy relevance with averages of 7.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 steals in 28.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Murray is in Portland's starting lineup against New Orleans on Friday.
items.story: Murray came off the bench during Wednesday's loss to the Thunder but will return to the Trail Blazers' starting lineup Friday while Sidy Cissoko reverts to a bench role. Murray has started eight games this season, and as a starter he is averaging 7.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 steals over 30.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Murray won't start against the Thunder on Wednesday.
items.story: The 25-year-old forward had started each of his last five appearances before missing Monday's win over Dallas due to a right quadriceps contusion. However, he'll slide to the second unit in favor of Sidy Cissoko on Wednesday. In 22 games off the bench this season, Murray has averaged 5.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 steals in 24.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Murray (quadriceps) is available for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Murray missed Monday's win over Dallas due to a right quadriceps contusion but will shed his questionable tag and suit up Wednesday. With Jerami Grant (Achilles) sidelined, Murray has started each of his last five appearances, during which he has averaged 7.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.2 steals in 30.4 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Murray (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Murray is in danger of missing a second straight game due to a right quadriceps contusion. If the 25-year-old forward joins Jerami Grant (Achilles) on the sidelines once again, Sidy Cissoko and Rayan Rupert are candidates for increased minutes. Murray has started each of his last five appearances, during which he has averaged 7.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.2 steals in 30.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Murray (quadriceps) is out for Monday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Murray will miss his first action since Dec. 3 after picking up a right quad contusion. Rayan Rupert and Sidy Cissoko could see a few additional minutes with Murray sidelined.

items.headline: Murray is questionable for Monday's game against Dallas with a right quad contusion.
items.story: Murray is at risk of sitting out the second part of Portland's back-to-back set. Sidy Cissoko and Caleb Love would both have a clearer path to minutes if Murray is out of action Monday.

items.headline: Murray (neck) is available for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Murray was initially deemed questionable for Friday's game due to a neck injury, but he has been cleared to play after going through morning shootaround and pregame warmups. He has started each of the Trail Blazers' last three games, averaging 9.0 points and 4.0 rebounds across 30.7 minutes per game over that span.

items.headline: Murray (neck) is probable for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: A neck injury shouldn't prevent Murray from playing Friday. He's started three consecutive games amid the absence of Jerami Grant (Achilles), logging at least 28 minutes in each contest.

items.headline: Murray is questionable for Friday's game against the Celtics due to neck soreness.
items.story: Murray has started the past three games and will likely get the nod again Friday if available since Jerami Grant (Achilles) is still sidelined. In six starts, Murray is averaging 8.3 points and 5.2 rebounds in 30.2 minutes.

items.headline: Fall chipped in one rebound across three minutes during Friday's 119-95 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Fall was sidelined at the start of the regular season with a quadriceps injury but has since recovered and finally made his season debut in garbage time Friday. However, even when he's healthy, the backup big man isn't expected to be part of the regular rotation.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) is available for Saturday's game against the Hornets, Chris Hine of The Philly Inquirer reports.
items.story: Fall is available to make his 76ers' debut Saturday, and with Joel Embiid (rest) out, he might be able to get into the rotation. That said, Fall may have his minutes monitored in his first game of the season, so he's not a great target in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Fall (quad) is questionable to face the Hornets on Saturday.
items.story: Fall has yet to debut for the 76ers this season, but he might be able to get out there Saturday. With Joel Embiid (foot) out, Fall could be in the rotation if cleared to play.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) is out for Wednesday's game in Indiana.
items.story: Fall was able to get through Tuesday's practice, but he'll remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game. He should continue to be viewed as week-to-week.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) was able to practice on Tuesday, Keith Pompey of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: Fall, who is on a two-way contract, is nearing a return to the floor for Philadelphia. He projects as an emergency depth option when the 76ers are shorthanded.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Fall will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left quadriceps strain. However, the big man's absence shouldn't cause any waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) is out for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Fall still isn't ready for his 76ers debut due to a quadriceps strain. Once cleared to make his season debut, the two-way player could see most of his action come with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats.

items.headline: Fall (quadriceps) is out for Thursday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Fall remains sidelined with a left quadriceps strain. Once cleared to make his season debut, the two-way player could see most of his action come with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats.

items.headline: Fall (hip) is out for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Fall will sit out the 76ers' first regular-season game with the same injury that sidelined him for the preseason. For now, he should be viewed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Cavs.

items.headline: Fall (hip) was limited to individual work during Sunday's practice, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Fall is still dealing with a left hip strain that kept him out of action during the preseason. The two-way player is in jeopardy of missing Tuesday's regular-season opener against New York, though his absence wouldn't significantly impact the rotation.

items.headline: Fall had his Exhibit 10 deal converted to a two-way contract by the 76ers on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Fall joined the 76ers for training camp but didn't play in the preseason due to a left hip strain. The big man last played in the NBA in 2021-22 and is set to provide center depth for the Sixers in 2026-27.

items.headline: Fall (hip) didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason loss to the Celtics in overtime.
items.story: Fall remained on the inactive list due to a left hip strain. He's signed to an Exhibit 10 contract and is in jeopardy of being waived before the team's regular-season opener versus New York on Tuesday.

items.headline: Fall was diagnosed with a left hip strain Thursday and will miss at least two weeks, Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: This is a tough blow for Fall, as he's already facing an uphill battle to make the final roster. A return Oct. 16 for Philadelphia's final preseason game isn't out of the question based on this timetable.

items.headline: Fall signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the 76ers on Tuesday, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Fall has played overseas in recent years and hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season. The 76ers will bring him in for camp, presumably to sign him to their G League affiliate.

items.headline: Fall will sign a one-year contract with Xinjiang to play in the Chinese Basketball Association for 2022-23, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Fall will head abroad after spending three seasons between Boston and Cleveland since he joined the NBA in 2019. The 7-foot-6 center spent most of the 2021-22 season with the G League's Cleveland Charge, where he averaged 14.8 points, 10.4 rebounds and 2.7 blocks in 26 appearances.

items.headline: Fall logged 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-2 FT), 11 rebounds, five blocks and one assist across 32 minutes during Saturday's 118-106 loss to the Motor City Cruise.
items.story: Despite the Cleveland Charge's bad record this G League season, Fall averaged a double-double (14.8 points and 10.4 rebounds) and 2.7 blocks across 26 games as their primary center.

items.headline: Fall logged 25 points (12-13 FG, 1-2 FT), 16 rebounds, three blocks, one assist and one steal across 36 minutes during Tuesday's 116-100 loss to the Westchester Knicks.
items.story: Charge players Brandon Goodwin and Cameron Young were unavailable Tuesday. Fall took advantage of their absences by logging his fifth consecutive double-double since March 20.

items.headline: Fall logged 12 points (6-6 FG, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds, four blocks and one assist across 24 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 win over the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.
items.story: By logging a double-double during each of the Charge's last four games, Fall has been able to average 17.8 points (on a 76.2 field goal percentage) and 13.3 rebounds across that span.

items.headline: Fall logged 20 points (9-11 FG, 2-4 FT), 17 rebounds, three blocks and one assist across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 117-99 loss to the Windy City Bulls.
items.story: Fall has three double-doubles across the Charge's last four games. Following his recent statistical output, he is averaging 14.3 points and 10.0 rebounds across 22 G League matchups this year.

items.headline: Fall logged 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-4 FT), 12 rebounds, three blocks and one assist across 29 minutes during Sunday's 118-108 loss to the College Park Skyhawks.
items.story: Fall has averaged 14.0 points and 9.8 rebounds across 21 G League games this year. Fortunately for him, there are sufficient future matchups he could utilize to average a double-double again.

items.headline: Fall logged 14 points (7-8 FG, 0-3 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 147-137 win over the Delaware Blue Coats.
items.story: Fall has averaged 13.9 points and 9.5 rebounds across 19 G League games this year. Despite no longer averaging a double-double, he remains an adequately reliable source for it.

items.headline: Fall logged 10 points (5-11 FG, 0-2 FT), 17 rebounds and one block across 30 minutes during Friday's loss to the Capital City Go-Go.
items.story: Despite the Charge's problems logging wins, Fall has been one of their best contributors during matchups. He is averaging 13.5 points and 10.3 rebounds across 12 G League games this season.

items.headline: Fall logged 19 points (6-8 FG, 7-11 FT), 12 rebounds and six blocks across 33 minutes during Friday's 118-113 loss to the Long Island Nets.
items.story: Fall was one of the Charge's four players who scored at least 15 points. Despite not standing out scoring-wise, he logged more rebounds and blocks than any other Charge player did Friday.

items.headline: Fall logged 24 points (10-12 FG, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds and two blocks across 27 minutes during Tuesday's 105-96 win over the Greensboro Swarm.
items.story: Fall was the Charge's primary scoring option during their first win since Jan. 11. He has averaged 10.5 points across his last six G League games, though he could receive increased scoring opportunities if the Charge believe their success relies on a key part of the offense running through the big man.

items.headline: Fall logged nine points (4-7 FG, 1-1 FT), 11 rebounds, one steal and one block across 25 minutes during a 98-86 loss Saturday against the Maine Celtics.
items.story: Fall logged his G League return Saturday. He was one point away from a double-double and could consistently record double digits across two statistical categories while being the Charge's starting center.

items.headline: Fall signed with the G League's Canton Charge on Wednesday, Sam Amico of FortyEightMinutes.com reports.
items.story: Fall was waived by the Cavaliers on Sunday, but he'll return to the club's G League affiliate after going unclaimed on waivers. He made four appearances during the G League showcase this year and averaged 23.3 points and 13.3 rebounds in 28.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: The Cavaliers waived Fall on Sunday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With the likes of Jarrett Allen, Evan Mobley and Ed Davis all representing more traditional centers and Kevin Love and Lauri Markkanen on hand as floor-stretching options at the five, the Cavaliers didn't have much of a need to keep the 7-foot-6 Fall around as a depth piece. He appeared in just 11 games for the NBA team this season, averaging 1.1 points and 2.1 rebounds in 5.4 minutes. With the losses of Collin Sexton (knee) and Ricky Rubio (knee) testing its depth in the backcourt, Cleveland will cut Fall loose and hand his two-way spot to a guard (Brandon Goodwin).

items.headline: Fall isn't starting Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Fall joined the starting lineup for Wednesday's loss to the Cavaliers and totaled four points, 10 rebounds and two blocks in 19 minutes. Kevin Love will make his first start of the season Sunday.

items.headline: Fall amassed four points (2-5 FG), 10 rebounds and two blocks over 19 minutes during Wednesday's 111-101 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Fall logged double-digit minutes for the first time this season, recording a plus-minus of minus-6 during his time on the floor. Fall had been working with trainer Drew Hanlen on his offensive game, but it hasn't translated onto the NBA court yet. The fan-favorite won't play again until Sunday -- when the Cavaliers might regain Evan Mobley or Jarrett Allen (COVID-19 protocols).

items.headline: Fall will make his first career start Wednesday against the Celtics, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: The shorthanded Cavaliers will turn to Fall -- one of the few true centers available. His career high for minutes played is 19, so fantasy managers shouldn't expect a full workload from Fall. Still, he can fill up the stat sheet. Per 36 minutes for his career, he's averaged 13.9 points, 13.4 rebounds and 4.8 blocks.

items.headline: Fall posted 26 points (11-16 FG, 2-5 FT), 10 rebounds, five blocks and two assists in 29 minutes during Friday's G League loss to Motor City.
items.story: Fall made his first G League appearance since Nov. 28 during Friday's defeat, but he was quite productive as a member of the starting five. He finished second on the team in scoring and has now logged double-doubles in each of his first four G League appearances of the season.

items.headline: Fall generated 22 points (7-11 FG, 5-5 FT), 17 rebounds and three blocks in Sunday's double-overtime G League win over the Skyforce.
items.story: Fall has been a consistent contributor for the Charge during his time in the G League, and he's scored at least 22 points in each of his three appearances while posting three consecutive double-doubles. He's now averaging 22.3 points and 13.3 rebounds in 28.1 points per game with the G League club.

items.headline: Fall posted 22 points (10-10 FG, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, a steal and a block in 29 minutes during Saturday's G League win over the Skyforce.
items.story: Fall made just his second G League appearance of the season Saturday, and he was perfect from the floor in the narrow win. The center averaged just 2.7 minutes per game with the parent club early in the year, but he should see more playing time in the G League.

items.headline: Fall posted 23 points (10-13 FG, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds and three blocks in 29 minutes during Thursday's G League win over Windy City.
items.story: Fall had minimal playing time with the Cavaliers to begin the 2021-22 campaign, but he made a significant impact during his season debut with the Charge. The 7-5 center will likely be shuffled between the G League and the parent club this year as one of the franchise's two-way players.

items.headline: Fall signed a two-way contract with the Cavaliers on Saturday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Fall signed with Cleveland in late August and spent some time away from the team in early October due to a visa issue. The 25-year-old should be shuffled between the Cleveland Charge and the parent club during the 2021-22 campaign.

items.headline: Fall has rejoined the Cavaliers following an issue with his visa, Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com reports.
items.story: Fall was unable to travel with the team for Tuesday's game at Chicago, but he's back with the Cavs in Atlanta and figures to make his preseason debut within the next several days.

items.headline: Fall did not travel with the Cavaliers for Tuesday's preseason game against Chicago, Evan Dammarell of Locked On Cavs reports.
items.story: The reason for Fall's absence is unclear, but he will not play Tuesday and will likely miss Wednesday's preseason game at Atlanta, as well. The big man signed a non-guaranteed deal with the Cavs in August, so missing the first two preseason games won't help his chances to make the final roster.

items.headline: Fall signed a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the Cavaliers on Tuesday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The 7-foot-5 center has played just 169 NBA minutes in his first two seasons, totaling 47 points, 52 rebounds, 20 blocks, three assists and one steal. If he manages to make the Cavs' roster, he won't be an every-game player.

items.headline: Fall tallied two points (1-1 FG), four blocks and three rebounds in five minutes off the bench Wednesday in the Celtics' 132-96 win over the Magic.
items.story: Fall has shown the ability to consistently put up numbers when he takes the court, but his limited mobility makes it difficult for head coach Brad Stevens to trust him for extended stretches. The 7-foot-5 center was summoned from the bench until garbage time, and so long as the Celtics have at least two of Robert Williams, Tristan Thompson and Luke Kornet available in a given game, Fall is unlikely to be included in the rotation.

items.headline: Fall is averaging 6.0 minutes, 1.7 points, 2.7 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in three games played in the month of April.
items.story: Fall has only played in three games and attempted two shots since March 27. The Celtics acquired two centers -- Luke Kornet and Moritz Wagner -- at the trade deadline and both appear to be firmly ahead of Fall on the depth chart. The Celtics' starting center, Robert Williams, missed Thursday's game with a knee injury, and Fall still recorded his fifth straight DNP.

items.headline: Fall is averaging 6.8 minutes, 3.0 points, 1.0 rebounds, 0.5 assists and 0.5 blocks in four games played since the All-Star break.
items.story: Fall has only eclipsed double-digit minutes in one game this year (Jan. 15 vs. Magic). However, the 25-year-old has at least gotten more run during the few times he's seen the court, as he's averaged almost double the amount of minutes in his sophomore season (7.6) than he did during his rookie year (4.7). The seven-footer has shot 70 percent from the field during his career, but his abysmal free-throw shooting (30 percent) makes him an offensive liability.

items.headline: Fall didn't take the court in Tuesday's win over Denver.
items.story: The center was a DNP-coach's decision for a 10th time over the past 12 games. His two appearances during that span came Feb. 11 versus Toronto and Feb. 14 against the Wizards. Fall recorded a total of seven points and six rebounds across seven minutes in those two outings.

items.headline: Fall (ankle) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game at Philadelphia.
items.story: The 25-year-old is available for Wednesday's contest after the one-game absence due to a left ankle sprain. Tristan Thompson and Robert Williams have both cleared the COVID-19 protocols, so Fall should revert to his reserve role at center for the Celtics.

items.headline: Fall (ankle) won't play Sunday against the Knicks.
items.story: The 25-year-old was listed as questionable with a left ankle sprain and won't be active for Sunday's contest. Fall likely would have filled a reserve role off the bench, and his next chance to take the court will be Wednesday at Philadelphia.

items.headline: Fall is questionable for Sunday's game against the Knicks due to a sprained left ankle.
items.story: With the Celtics' extensive injury report in addition to decisive victories, Fall has seen some action lately. Across the past two games, he's totaled 27 minutes, registering 10 points, 13 rebounds and four blocks. If Daniel Theis (finger) -- also questionable -- ends up sidelined while Fall is available, there's a greater chance the latter would see minutes.

items.headline: Prosper registered 16 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Prosper matched his season high in scoring while collecting four offensive rebounds, demonstrating increased aggressiveness around the basket. He's reached double figures in three of his last four appearances, but his playing time remains inconsistent. Thursday's blowout provided additional opportunities, making sustained fantasy relevance unlikely without a larger rotation role.

items.headline: Prosper recorded five points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and two rebounds over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 win over Cleveland.
items.story: Prosper cooled off after scoring in double figures in consecutive appearances, during which he combined for 23 points on 8-for-11 shooting. The 24-year-old forward has logged at least 16 minutes in three straight games after seeing limited opportunities earlier in November. His increased involvement is encouraging, but inconsistent playing time and modest peripheral production leave him with limited fantasy appeal outside deeper leagues.

items.headline: Prosper registered no counting stats in one minute during Monday's 118-102 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Prosper cracked the rotation for just the fifth time this season, albeit for a brief appearance during garbage time. He has now played a total of 33 minutes, scoring 12 points. Simple math tells you that he has no value outside of the deepest leagues.

items.headline: Prosper (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 123-103 win over Utah.
items.story: The forward remained on Memphis' bench throughout the comfortable victory. Prosper appears to be outside the Grizzlies' preferred rotation and will likely need additional opportunities to become relevant in deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Prosper recorded nine points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one assist and one block in 12 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason loss to Orlando.
items.story: Prosper provided efficient scoring inside the arc while contributing a blocked shot in limited action. The former Mavericks forward will look to build on the performance as he competes for a consistent role in Memphis' frontcourt rotation ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: Prosper (rest) is out for Tuesday's Summer League game against the Hawks, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Prosper is getting Tuesday night off as part of a management plan this summer. He's expected to play Friday in Las Vegas against the Bulls.

items.headline: Prosper produced 17 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and two turnovers in 23 minutes of Sunday's 111-74 Salt Lake City Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Prosper has three years of NBA experience, and it showed Sunday. He's coming off a really solid campaign for Memphis, as he shot 54.9 percent from the field during the regular season. With the Grizzlies in the early stages of a rebuild, Prosper could carve out a sizable role.

items.headline: The Grizzlies picked up Prosper's team option for 2026-27 on Monday, Jake Fischer of BleacherReport.com reports.
items.story: The option was worth $2.4 million. Prosper made 53 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, posting averages of 10.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 18.6 minutes while shooting 54.9 percent from the field.

items.headline: Prosper won't start Sunday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Prosper is available after missing the past two games due to an ankle injury, but he'll operate off the bench for the first time since Feb. 20, while Toby Okani and Taj Gibson start in the frontcourt. Since the All-Star break, Prosper has averaged 14.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 24.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Houston.
items.story: Prosper missed the last two contests because of a sprained right ankle. However, he will be back on the court for the final game of the season for Memphis. Prosper is also expected to return to the starting lineup, likely sending Toby Okani back to the bench.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Rockets.
items.story: Prosper has missed two straight games but could return for the finale. He's scored double-digit points in six straight games, averaging 19.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 21.2 minutes during this stretch.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: As expected, Prosper will miss a second consecutive contest due to right ankle soreness. His final chance to play this season will come Sunday in Houston. Toby Okani, Dariq Whitehead and Taj Gibson are candidates for increased run in Prosper's stead.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) is listed as doubtful ahead of Friday's game against Utah.
items.story: Prosper didn't play in Wednesday's 136-119 loss to Denver. It appears that trend will continue against Utah, so he'll have one more opportunity to suit up after Friday's contest before the Grizzlies call it a season. If Prosper is ruled out, Taj Gibson may find himself in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Prosper's absence comes as no surprise given that he was tagged as doubtful on Tuesday's injury report due to right ankle soreness. He's been in the Grizzlies' starting lineup since the All-Star break, so Taylor Hendricks and Taj Gibson should both see more run time against the Nuggets. Prosper's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Jazz.

items.headline: Prosper (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Prosper is expected to miss Wednesday's contest due to right ankle soreness. If the 23-year-old forward is ultimately ruled out, Taylor Hendricks, Taj Gibson and Toby Okani would be candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Prosper registered a team-high 24 points (10-12 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 142-126 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: The third-year big has become a fairly reliable source of offense in an injury-ravaged Memphis frontcourt. Prosper has scored in double digits in 11 of his last 12 games, averaging 16.3 points, 4.0 boards, 1.9 threes, 1.3 steals and 0.9 assists in 23.3 minutes while shooting 59.0 percent from the floor and 43.4 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Prosper (back) is available for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Propser is set to return from a one-game absence and will likely start. He's been terrific over his last five games with averages of 17.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.8 steals and 1.8 three-pointers in 23.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Prosper (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Toronto, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: As expected, Prosper will miss Friday's contest due to lower-back soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday in Milwaukee. In the meantime, Taylor Hendricks and Rayan Rupert are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Prosper (back) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Prosper is likely to miss Friday's contest due to lower-back soreness, which would mark his second absence in a three-game span. Taylor Hendricks and Rayan Rupert would be candidates to see increased playing time if Prosper is unable to suit up.

items.headline: Prosper (wrist) is not listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game versus the Knicks.
items.story: Prosper is set to return from a one-game absence due to a right wrist injury. The third-year big man has been impressive for the Grizzlies of late, averaging 15.7 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 1.9 three-pointers across 24.6 minutes per game in his last nine appearances, shooting 43.6 percent from beyond the arc over this span.

items.headline: Prosper (wrist) is out for Monday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Prosper has been officially downgraded to out due to a right wrist injury. Taylor Hendricks and Tyler Burton should be in for plenty of minutes with the Grizzlies battling a plethora of injuries in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Prosper (wrist) is doubtful for Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Prosper is dealing with right wrist soreness and is expected to miss his first game since Feb. 9. If the 23-year-old is ultimately ruled out, Taylor Hendricks and Tyler Burton would likely see increased playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Prosper closed with 31 points (12-15 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals across 29 minutes during Friday's 119-109 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Prosper got into some early foul trouble and was limited to just five points through the first half of play, but he caught fire after halftime and finished with a new career high in points. Prosper has been on a heater over the past two games, scoring a total of 48 points on 18-for-25 shooting over that stretch.

items.headline: Prosper produced 17 points (6-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT) and five rebounds over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 123-98 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Prosper has been enjoying additional minutes due to the lack of frontcourt options available on the Memphis roster, and for the most part, the big man has been getting the job done. He's scored in double digits in 13 of his 18 consecutive starts dating back to Feb. 21, averaging 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.3 steals per game. He's a decent option to target if you need frontcourt depth late in the fantasy playoffs, given his steady playing time, as he's averaging 25.4 minutes per game since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Prosper racked up 14 points (4-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-7 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Friday's 117-112 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Prosper continues to thrive in a starting role and has been extremely consistent both as a scorer and as a rebounding asset. Over his last nine starts, Prosper has scored in double digits eight times while averaging a solid line of 14.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.2 steals per contest. Look for Prosper to remain in the starting lineup as long as he stays healthy, as he figures to continue handling a big role following all the movements the Grizzlies made after the trade deadline back in early February.

It's unclear whether Plumlee will be cleared to suit up immediately, though he can be considered questionable for Thursday's game against the Suns.
