items.headline: Plumlee underwent surgery to address his right groin injury and will be reevaluated in six weeks, the Hornets announced Wednesday.
items.story: Plumlee had missed four consecutive games with a strained right groin before going under the knife. The veteran center will be sidelined until at least mid-February. While he's sidelined, PJ Hall will likely step into the third-string center role behind Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow) and Moussa Diabate.

items.headline: Plumlee (groin) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Plumlee is set to miss his fourth consecutive contest due to a right groin strain, and his next chance to play will come Friday against the Bucks. With Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow) also remaining on the shelf, Moussa Diabate and PJ Hall are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Plumlee (groin) is out for Monday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Plumlee will miss a third straight game due to a right groin strain. With Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow) also sidelined, Moussa Diabate figures to see a larger role.

items.headline: Plumlee (groin) will not play in Friday's matchup against the Magic.
items.story: With Plumlee and Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow) sidelined, Moussa Diabate should continue starting and seeing an expanded role.

items.headline: Plumlee is out for Tuesday's game against the Wizards with a strained right groin.
items.story: The veteran big man left Monday's game against the Cavaliers due to right groin soreness, though he's since been diagnosed with a strain. Considering Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow) is questionable, Charlotte could have to lean heavily on Moussa Diabate for the center minutes.

items.headline: Plumlee has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against the Cavaliers due to right groin soreness. He'll finish the night with five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 FT) and five rebounds in 10 minutes.
items.story: It's unclear as to when Plumlee suffered the injury, but the team has elected to shut him down for the night. He can be considered questionable for Tuesday's game against Washington until further notice.

items.headline: Plumlee is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: The veteran center is getting the start in place of the injured Ryan Kalkbrenner (elbow). Plumlee logged 23 minutes in his lone start of the season during the Nov. 23 loss in Atlanta, so a rise in streaming appeal should be expected Monday.

items.headline: Plumlee contributed one rebound, one assist and one steal in seven minutes during Saturday's 112-86 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Plumless continues to play a non-existent role, serving as the third-string center behind Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate. In 13 appearances this season, the veteran is averaging just 1.6 points and 2.7 rebounds in 8.8 minutes per game, making him a non-factor in all fantasy formats.

items.headline: Plumlee provided four points (1-2 FG, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal in 22 minutes during Sunday's 115-106 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Plumlee saw extended minutes Sunday due to the absence of Moussa Diabate (knee) and did a fine job backing up rookie Ryan Kalkbrenner. If Diabate returns for the Hornets' next game Friday against Chicago, Plumlee will revert to the third-string center and may not even see the court.

items.headline: Plumlee is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: No surprise here, given that rookie standout Ryan Kalkbrenner is back in the lineup for the Hornets.  Plumlee has averaged 1.7 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 9.6 minutes per contest over six games this month, leaving him with little to no fantasy appeal Wednesday.

items.headline: Plumlee will start Sunday's game against Atlanta, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: With Ryan Kalkbrenner (ankle) sidelined, Plumlee will get the starting nod for the first time this season. The veteran big man has played a limited role thus far, and he has averaged just 7.0 minutes per contest over his last five appearances dating back to Nov. 2.

items.headline: Charlotte recalled Plumlee from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Tuesday.
items.story: Plumlee is back with Charlotte after spending the afternoon with the Swarm to get some practice reps alongside LaMelo Ball (ankle). Plumlee has been unable to crack the rotation in Charlotte outside of a few brief appearances.

items.headline: Plumlee was assigned to the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Tuesday, Roderick Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Plumlee has been out of Charlotte's rotation for the most part, with an average of 3.8 minutes across three appearances. Plumlee is likely just getting some practice reps along with LaMelo Ball (ankle) and will be recalled after the practice.

items.headline: Plumlee didn't see the floor during Wednesday's 136-117 win over the Nets.
items.story: Plumlee was one of three players for his squad who sat out due to a coach's decision. Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate shouldered the load in the frontcourt, leaving questions as to whether Plumlee will have any fantasy value moving forward.

items.headline: Plumlee failed to score (0-2 FG), adding four rebounds in 11 minutes during Saturday's preseason win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Plumlee went scoreless off the bench, having very little impact on the game. The Hornets are yet to finalize things when it comes to the starting center position. The fact that Plumlee is even in the discussion says a lot about the team's current mindset. Ryan Kalkbrenner recorded a double-double as the starter, his best performance of the preseason. Even if Plumlee is given meaningful minutes, there is almost no chance he moves the needle when it comes to fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Plumlee (coach's decision) did not play in Sunday's preseason loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Plumlee missed a chunk of training camp with an excused absence due to personal reasons. He was initially considered the favorite to start the 2025-26 season at center, but Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate are expected to challenge the veteran.

items.headline: Plumlee won't start Sunday's preseason game against the Thunder, James Plowright of CLTure.org reports.
items.story: Plumlee was absent from practice this week due to an excused absence, but he didn't have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's preseason game against the Thunder and isn't on the inactive list. While he may suit up, it's unclear if Plumlee will actually see any minutes during the preseason opener. Moussa Diabate is starting at center Sunday.

items.headline: Plumlee has remained absent from practice this week due to an excused absence, though he doesn't have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's preseason game against the Thunder, Roderick Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Plumlee was also excused from Monday's media day and may miss the Hornets' preseason opener. The 35-year-old big man signed a veteran's minimum deal with the club this offseason after averaging 4.5 points and 6.1 rebounds across 17.6 minutes per game in 74 regular-season appearances (21 starts) with the Suns last season.

items.headline: Plumlee agreed to a one-year, $3.6 million deal with the Hornets on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The veteran big man will return to the Hornets and compete for playing time with Moussa Diabate and Ryan Kalkbrenner. Plumlee appeared in 74 regular-season games (21 starts) with the Suns in 2024-25, averaging 4.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Plumlee is in Phoenix's starting lineup against Sacramento on Sunday.
items.story: Plumlee will make his 21st start of the season while Oso Ighodaro retreats to the bench. Plumlee has averaged 5.0 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.7 assists across 17.0 minutes per game over his last three outings.

items.headline: Plumlee totaled five points (1-1 FG, 3-6 FT), five rebounds and two assists across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 125-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Plumlee logged over 20 minutes Wednesday for the first time since March 10. The veteran big man has been third on the Suns' depth chart of late, but with Nick Richards (elbow) sidelined, Plumlee served as Oso Ighodaro's backup against the Thunder. Plumlee is likely to maintain the backup center role for the team's final two regular-season games.

items.headline: Plumlee (quadriceps) is available for Monday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Plumlee was held out of his club's previous two matchups while dealing with a left quad strain, but he'll be available off the bench for Monday's clash. He's averaging 7.2 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.0 assists in nine March appearances.

items.headline: Plumlee (quadriceps) is probable for Monday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Plumlee has missed the last two games due to a left quad strain, but he is likely to return to play Monday. Plumlee saw a minimal role in his last four games, averaging just 1.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in 9.8 minutes per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Plumlee (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The big man will miss his second consecutive contest due to a left quadricep strain. His next chance to suit up will come Monday against Milwaukee. Oso Ighodaro could see a slight uptick in playing time due to Plumlee being sidelined.

items.headline: Plumlee is out for Wednesday's game versus the Bulls due to a left quadriceps strain.
items.story: Plumlee will miss his first game since Nov. 15 due to a quadriceps injury. In the veteran big man's absence, Nick Richards and Oso Ighodaro could receive increased playing time. Plumlee's next chance to suit up is Friday's matchup with Cleveland.

items.headline: Plumlee won't start Sunday's game against the Lakers, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Plumlee drew two straight starts in place of Nick Richards (ankle), who's returning to action Sunday. Plumlee was actually more productive coming off the bench before moving into the starting lineup, averaging 13.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 24.5 minutes per game over his past four reserve appearances.

items.headline: Plumlee has been ejected from Friday's game against the Kings after being assessed a Flagrant 2 foul, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: It's the second game in a row that Plumlee has been ejected, this time for receiving a Flagrant 2 foul after elbowing Domantas Sabonis in the head and neck area while boxing out for a rebound. Plumlee will end the night with two points (1-3 FG), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 16 minutes. Oso Ighodaro will likely see more minutes at center for the rest of Friday's game.

items.headline: Ware will start in Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: With Myles Turner (rest) ruled out, Ware will make his first start as a member of the Bucks. In 34 regular-season starts with the Heat in 2025-26, the 22-year-old averaged 12.8 points, 10.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks over 26.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Ware (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game versus the Knicks.
items.story: Ware was a late addition to the injury report with an ankle sprain, and he should be able to handle a normal workload if all goes well Tuesday. The third-year big man is struggling over his last four appearances, posting four points or fewer in each game during that span.

items.headline: Ware is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Ware was a late addition to the injury report, which is never a good sign, but the severity of the issue remains unclear. If the backup big man is unable to suit up, Jericho Sims, Nate Ament and Ousmane Dieng would be candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: The Bucks exercised their fourth-year team option on Ware's contract Monday.
items.story: Ware is now officially under contract for the 2027-28 campaign after being traded to Milwaukee this past offseason. The big man has played a relatively steady role off the Bucks' bench to begin the 2026-27 season, averaging 13.0 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.4 combined steals-plus-blocks and 0.8 assists in 19.7 minutes per game across six appearances.

items.headline: Ware finished Saturday's 136-111 loss to the Cavaliers with 19 points (6-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 24 minutes.
items.story: Most of Ware's production came in the fourth quarter, when the game was already well out of reach for the Bucks. Still, the third-year big man made the most of his opportunity and ended up leading Milwaukee in both points and rebounds en route to his third double-double of the season. All three of those double-doubles have come over his last four outings, and in that span, Ware has averaged 15.0 points, 11.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.3 threes and 1.0 blocks over 22.2 minutes per game while connecting on 42.9 percent of his field-goal attempts. Even with his strong output as of late, Ware's production ceiling will continue to be limited while coming off the bench and working behind starters Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma.

items.headline: Ware provided 16 points (7-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 14 rebounds and one steal across 19 minutes during Monday's 110-102 win over Indiana.
items.story: Ware recorded his second consecutive double-double, providing Milwaukee with a significant boost on the glass. The young center continues to make an impact despite coming off the bench, and his rebounding production gives him a solid fantasy foundation. Ware's ability to consistently produce double-doubles makes him an intriguing option even while sharing frontcourt minutes with Myles Turner.

items.headline: Ware registered 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 13 rebounds, an assist, a steal and two blocks across 29 minutes in Saturday's 127-116 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Ware made the most of his extended opportunity, producing a double-double while also leaving his mark on the defensive end of the court. His 29 minutes were particularly notable compared with Myles Turner's 20, suggesting Ware could push for a larger role in Milwaukee's frontcourt as the season progresses. However, his playing time remains worth monitoring, as his current bench role could limit his chances to produce at this rate on a consistent basis.

items.headline: Ware ended Friday's 132-125 loss to the Bulls with 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT) and four rebounds in 15 minutes.
items.story: Ware logged just 15 minutes, this time without getting into foul trouble. Through two games, fantasy managers have every right to be underwhelmed, with Ware looking as though he is slated for a backup role as opposed to what was seen as a potential breakout opportunity. At this point, it's hard to justify dropping him, given we are still only two games into the season. However, should his role remain the same as the first month of the season unfolds, fantasy managers may want to begin contemplating a move.

items.headline: Ware ended with seven points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 14 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 128-116 loss to Washington.
items.story: Ware struggled with foul trouble in his Milwaukee debut, picking up six personal fouls while serving as a reserve behind Myles Turner. The young center showed some offensive activity but missed both three-point attempts and two free throws. His fantasy upside remains intriguing, though his production could be inconsistent while operating in a limited role.

items.headline: Ware finished with 13 points (6-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block in 25 minutes during Friday's 128-127 preseason win over the Pacers.
items.story: Ware cobbled together another serviceable performance, rounding out what has been a relatively encouraging preseason. While there has been a lot of hype around Ware and what his role might look like in Milwaukee, fantasy managers are no clearer when it comes to his projected playing time. With that said, he will almost certainly see more of the floor than he did last season, making him an acceptable target in middle-to-late rounds.

items.headline: Ware is not listed in the starting lineup for Sunday's preseason game against the Hornets, Sam Perley of the Hornets' official site reports.
items.story: Ware started in Wednesday's 128-126 preseason win over the Thunder, finishing with an 18-point, 12-rebound double-double. He will come off the bench Sunday, with Kyle Kuzma moving into the starting lineup for Milwaukee's preseason meeting with Charlotte.

items.headline: Ware recorded 18 points (7-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and one block across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 128-126 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: After posting 14 points and 12 rebounds over 24 minutes off the bench in Monday's preseason-opening loss to Minnesota, Ware got the starting nod Wednesday. The big man struggled from beyond the arc but still finished as Milwaukee's second-leading scorer behind Myles Turner (19 points). Ware also led all players in rebounds, securing his second double-double in as many preseason games thus far.

items.headline: Ware will start Wednesday's preseason game against the Thunder.
items.story: Ware came off the bench and posted a double-double during his Bucks debut, and he'll now supplant Kyle Kuzma in the starting lineup for Milwaukee's second exhibition game. Ware started 35 regular-season games for the Heat last year, averaging 12.8 points, 11.0 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.8 steals per game.

items.headline: Ware produced 14 points (5-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, one assist and one block across 24 minutes off the bench in Monday's 116-97 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Ware didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance in Milwaukee's preseason opener. However, the big man finished as the club's second-leading scorer and led all players in rebounds. Ware nearly averaged a double-double with Miami in 2025-26 and shot 39.5 percent from beyond the arc on 3.0 three-point attempts per contest. Entering his third year in the league, the 22-year-old is in a much more favorable situation and has an opportunity to take on a more sizable and consistent role than he had with the Heat.

items.headline: Ware has a clearer path to playing time on the Bucks and should have a better opportunity to find firmer footing than he had with Miami, per Zach Kram of ESPN.
items.story: Ware flashed potential in his first two years in the Association with Miami, and he averaged 11.1 points, 9.0 rebounds, 1.9 combined steals-plus-blocks and 0.7 assists in 22.1 minutes per game across 77 regular-season appearances (34 starts) in 2025-26. The big man also shot an impressive 39.5 percent from downtown on 3.0 three-point tries per contest last season. He was dealt to Milwaukee as part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade in June, and Ware now has the chance to start fresh and become a building block for the Bucks in their rebuild. Myles Turner is coming off a down year, and his long-term future in Milwaukee is unclear. Ware could carve out a starting role with the Bucks regardless of Turner's presence, and it wouldn't be surprising to see the former take another step forward in a more favorable situation.

items.headline: The Heat traded Ware, Tyler Herro (foot), Jaime Jaquez, Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, one pick swap and one second-round pick to the Bucks on Monday in exchange for Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Bobby Portis (wrist), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After spending the first two seasons of his career in Miami, Ware will get a fresh start in Milwaukee. The 22-year-old center saw similar playing time in his second season compared to his first, though he still took a step forward in 2025-26. Over 77 regular-season appearances (34 starts) last season, the big man averaged 11.1 points, 9.0 rebounds, 1.1 blocks, 0.8 steals and 0.7 assists in 22.1 minutes per contest. With Antetokounmpo no longer in Milwaukee, the future of Myles Turner (ankle) is up in the air. Ware could see a larger role in Milwaukee than he did in Miami, especially if Turner is traded.

items.headline: Ware chipped in 12 points (5-12 FG, 2-8 3Pt), 19 rebounds, four assists and five blocks over 42 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Tournament loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Ware did everything he could to get Miami over the line, leading the game with 19 rebounds and five blocks. With Bam Adebayo leaving early due to a back injury, Ware was forced into a sizeable role, serving as the primary big man. While it was a solid season for Ware, his ongoing role will no doubt be a contentious topic, as he switched between starting and coming off the bench for much of the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Ware is in the starting lineup for Friday's game versus Washington, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: The Heat are without several key contributors in the penultimate game of the regular season, allowing Ware to draw his 33rd start of the year. The second-year big man has averaged 10.0 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 25.0 minutes per contest across his previous five appearances as a starter.

items.headline: Ware supplied 24 points (10-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 19 rebounds, two assists and seven blocks in 36 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 152-136 win over the Wizards.
items.story: The double-double was the 24th of the season for the second-year center, and the points and boards were his best performances in those categories since a 28-19 effort against the Knicks on Dec. 21. The seven rejections also tied his career high, a mark he first set March 5 against the Nets. Ware has been locked in from long range over the last couple weeks, averaging 10.9 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.9 threes and 1.4 blocks in 20.0 minutes a contest while shooting 48.1 percent (13-for-27) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Ware logged five points (2-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), six rebounds and two assists over 13 minutes during Monday's 119-109 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Ware logged no more than 15 minutes for the second straight game, continuing what has been a wildly unpredictable season. Despite being a top-70 player through 71 games, Ware has struggled to carve out a consistent spot in the rotation. For example, in eight games over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 8.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in 18.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Ware totaled 13 points (5-5 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists and one block in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 120-103 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Ware continues to trend in the right direction for Miami. Over his last eight games, he's nearly averaging a double-double in 21.5 minutes per contest with 8.6 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 blocks on 47.2 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Ware registered one rebound across five minutes during Saturday's 123-122 loss to Houston.
items.story: Ware barely saw the court, logging just five minutes Saturday. For those still holding Ware, this could be the final nail in the coffin when it comes to his fantasy value. Despite the clear upside, his role is seemingly impossible to predict at this point. Even with multiple injuries to other players, Ware hasn't been able to solidify a consistent spot in the rotation. With that said, he should be better than this on most nights, at least keeping him on the radar in standard leagues.

items.headline: Ware will come off the bench in Thursday's game versus the Lakers, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Bam Adebayo (calf) is back and starting, so Ware will shift back to the second unit. As a reserve this season, the second-year center has posted averages of 9.8 points and 7.8 rebounds per contest.

items.headline: Ware ended with 13 points (5-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal in 27 minutes during Saturday's 121-117 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Ware was efficient from the floor and showed impressive energy on the glass en route to posting his first double-double since March 5. He has four double-doubles over his last seven games and has grabbed double-digit boards five times during that stretch. The second-year big man is an excellent option in both point-based and category-based formats due to his ability to fill the stat sheet with ease.

items.headline: Ware is in the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup with the Bucks, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Ware is back and starting after a one-game absence, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Davion Mitchell, Pelle Larsson, Kasparas Jakucionis and Bam Adebayo. As a starter this season, Ware owns averages of 13.1 points, 11.0 rebounds, 1.3 triples and 1.3 swats per contest.

items.headline: Ware (shoulder) is good to go for Thursday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Ware is all set to return from a one-game absence. With this news, Simone Fontecchio could lose some playing time, with Ware likely to reprise his spot in the rotation. Over his past five appearances (all off bench), Ware has averaged 12.4 points, 9.8 rebounds, 2.8 blocks and 2.6 steals in 29.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Ware is questionable for Thursday's game against the Bucks due to right shoulder strain.
items.story: Ware is trying to keep his absence to a one-game minimum Thursday. Simone Fontecchio would likely see a bump in playing time in the event that Ware isn't cleared for action.

items.headline: Ware (shoulder) is out for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Ware was unable to shake his questionable tag and will miss his first game since Jan. 25. Presumably, he'll be listed as day-to-day ahead of Thursday's game against the Bucks. Myron Gardner and Jaime Jaquez are candidates for more minutes with this news.

items.headline: Ware is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Wizards due to a right shoulder strain.
items.story: It's a new injury for Ware, who hasn't missed a game since Jan. 25. If the second-year big man cannot suit up Tuesday, more playing time would be available for Myron Gardner and Jaime Jaquez.

items.headline: Rollins provided eight points (4-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist and one block in 28 minutes during Saturday's 132-129 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Moving into the starting lineup for the first time since Nov. 10, Rollins didn't make much of a contribution, while rookie Brayden Burries delivered 26 points in 26 minutes off the bench. Rollins has scored in double digits in just five of nine November contests (two starts), averaging 10.3 points, 5.3 boards, 3.2 assists, 1.4 threes and 1.2 steals in 22.3 minutes on the month. His spot in the starting five likely won't be very secure unless the fifth-year guard begins to show something closer to his 2025-26 form.

items.headline: Rollins is in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Rollins is moving to the starting lineup after notching 15 points, three rebounds, six assists and four steals in 21 minutes off the bench Thursday against the Trail Blazers. He's averaging 11.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game as a starter this season.

items.headline: Rollins ended Thursday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers with 15 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, six assists and four steals in 21 minutes.
items.story: Rollins matched his season high in assists while establishing a new season high in steals, compensating for another inefficient perimeter performance. His minutes have fluctuated considerably, and Thursday's defensive outburst is unlikely to become routine. However, his ability to contribute across categories provides upside in deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Rollins (illness) is available for Thursday's game against Portland.
items.story: Rollins is off the injury report after missing back-to-back contests with an illness. His return should leave fewer minutes open for Brayden Burries and Kasparas Jakucionis in the Bucks' backcourt.

items.headline: Rollins (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game at Miami.
items.story: Rollins wasn't included on the initial injury report, though he's since been ruled out for a second straight game due to an illness. His next chance to play will come Thursday versus Portland. With the 24-year-old combo guard sidelined, Kasparas Jakucionis and Gary Trent will likely continue seeing increased minutes.

items.headline: Rollins (illness) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Rollins was out sick for Sunday's contest versus Atlanta, but he's feeling well enough to return Wednesday. His presence should most noticeably cut into the workload of Kasparas Jakucionis, who went off for a season-high 25 points his last time out.

items.headline: Rollins (illness) is out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Rollins will miss his first game of the season due to an illness. Gary Trent, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis are candidates for increased roles with Rollins sidelined.

items.headline: Rollins (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Rollins played 30 minutes off Milwaukee's bench during Friday's 107-99 loss to Orlando, but an illness has put his status for Sunday up in the air. If he can't play, expect Gary Trent Jr., AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis to see additional minutes.

items.headline: Rollins (head) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Rollins exited Wednesday's loss to the Lakers early after bumping heads with an opposing player, though he's not on the injury report for Friday's contest. The 24-year-old guard has come off the bench in five of Milwaukee's last six games, averaging 10.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 20.5 minutes per showing during that span.

items.headline: Rollins (head) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 123-112 loss to the Lakers and did not return, finishing with eight points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
items.story: Rollins bumped heads with Collin Sexton with 6:51 remaining in the contest, and both players exited to the locker room. Rollins' status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game at Orlando. If he needs to miss time, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis could see increased playing time.

items.headline: Rollins exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's game against the Lakers due to an apparent head injury, per the broadcast.
items.story: Rollins bumped heads with Collin Sexton, and both players left for the locker room. Rollins can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Rollins will come off the bench in Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Tyler Herro (knee) is back after a one-game absence, so Rollins will return to a reserve role. As a member of the second unit this season, Rollins is averaging 10.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.5 triples and 1.0 steals in 18.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Rollins posted 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and a steal across 24 minutes in Tuesday's 117-85 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Rollins delivered efficient perimeter scoring, making four of six three-point attempts while finishing as Milwaukee's second-leading scorer. Rollins has been trending in the right direction lately, scoring in double digits in four of his last five appearances while averaging 10.8 points and shooting 55.6 percent from three over that span. That said, he's yet to log more than 24 minutes in any of those contests, so his limited workload and inconsistent role could conspire against his fantasy upside.

items.headline: Rollins will start in Tuesday's game against New York.
items.story: With Tyler Herro (knee) sidelined for the first time this season, Rollins will start in Tuesday's meeting with the Knicks. In six starts during the 2026-27 campaign, the 24-year-old has averaged 11.2 points, 4.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists over 26.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Rollins tallied 13 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: With rookie Brayden Burries starting a second straight game, Rollins delivered productive all-around numbers in a reserve role, narrowly missing a double-double while contributing five assists and two defensive stats. His ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him upside whenever Milwaukee provides sufficient opportunities, but the fact that he's played off the bench in his last two games is a bit concerning.

items.headline: Rollins isn't in the starting lineup for Monday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Rollins has struggled mightily to open the campaign, resulting in a change to the starting lineup. Brayden Burries, who's scored in double figures in each of his last two showings off the bench, will draw the start at point guard.

items.headline: Rollins chipped in nine points (4-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds and seven assists over 26 minutes during Saturday's 136-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Although it has only been six games, fantasy managers are right to be concerned when it comes to Rollins' projected fantasy value. In his six appearances, he has averaged just 11.2 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.5 three-pointers in 26.3 minutes per game, leaving him well outside the top 200 in nine-category leagues. His playing time has ranged from 17 to 34 minutes, obviously impacting his on-court production. Those who drafted him are just going to have to sit tight and hope that things turn around at some point in the near future.

items.headline: Rollins closed Monday's 110-102 win over Indiana with 19 points (7-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds and four assists over 32 minutes.
items.story: Rollins delivered his highest-scoring performance through Milwaukee's first four games, connecting on three triples while committing just one turnover. The guard has reached double figures in three consecutive contests and continues to see substantial playing time alongside Tyler Herro. Rollins' combination of scoring and playmaking gives him some solid fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Rollins notched 11 points (3-9 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal in 34 minutes during Friday's 132-125 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Rollins got back on track despite the loss, chipping in across the board in 34 minutes. Although the scoring remains somewhat underwhelming, the fact that he played starter-level minutes should put fantasy managers' minds at ease, at least for the time being. He should continue to play a sizeable role as the lead facilitator, while an uptick in his scoring is almost inevitable.

items.headline: Rollins totaled nine points (4-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt), six rebounds and three assists across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 loss to Washington.
items.story: Rollins had a tough time getting his shot to drop, and he seemed to struggle asserting himself in the offense alongside Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez. However, it probably isn't wise to overreact to one game given that Rollins was a top-50 player last season. He may just need some time to gel with his new teammates.

items.headline: Rollins (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Pacers.
items.story: Rollins will return from a one-game absence due to rest purposes. The 24-year-old guard is coming off a career year in 2025-26 and is expected to remain a key piece for the Bucks as they navigate life without Giannis Antetokounmpo (rest).

items.headline: Rollins (rest) won't play in Wednesday's preseason game against Chicago, Cameron Ezeir of CBS58 reports.
items.story: Rollins will take the night off before possibly suiting up for Friday's preseason meeting with the Pacers. The 24-year-old has played relatively well during the preseason (three games), averaging 13.0 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.3 steals over 19.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Rollins logged 12 points (5-15 FG, 2-8 3Pt), four rebounds, three steals, two assists and two blocks in 23 minutes during Sunday's 105-90 preseason loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Rollins was one of four Bucks players to score in double figures despite struggling from the floor. He excelled defensively, collecting a game-high three steals and adding two blocks. While he was highly productive defensively, Rollins still had the worst plus-minus among Bucks starters at minus eight.

items.headline: Rollins supplied 12 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, seven assists, a steal and a block across 21 minutes in Wednesday's 128-126 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Rollins followed his 15-point performance against Minnesota in the preseason opener with another encouraging outing, this time making a greater impact as a facilitator. He tied Ousmane Dieng for the team lead with seven assists while committing just one turnover and shooting efficiently from the field. Rollins has started both preseason contests alongside Tyler Herro, establishing himself as a reliable backcourt contributor heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Rollins supplied 15 points (6-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 14 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Rollins was Milwaukee's most productive scorer despite lasting only 14 minutes before fouling out, leading the Bucks with 15 points while shooting 50.0 percent from the field. The six fouls stand out, but Rollins' aggressive offensive performance was one of the brighter developments from Milwaukee's preseason opener. Fantasy managers would be wise not to overreact to just one game in preseason, and Rollins figures to have a sizable role once the regular season begins.

items.headline: Rollins (eye) returned to Monday's preseason game against the Timberwolves with 1:37 remaining in the first quarter, per the broadcast.
items.story: Rollins exited the Bucks' preseason opener in the opening quarter due to a right eye laceration. The 24-year-old was deemed likely to return shortly after leaving the court and has since checked back in.

items.headline: Rollins (right eye laceration) is expected to return to Monday's exhibition versus Minnesota.
items.story: Rollins is dealing with a minor cut on his right eye, but he's expected to power through it. He should open the year as Milwaukee's starting point guard and could be headed for a productive season in that role.

items.headline: Rollins (thumb) appears poised for an expanded role after Milwaukee traded Giannis Antetokounmpo and entered a youth movement by drafting Brayden Burries and Nate Ament, Amir Motameni of SI.com reports.
items.story: The 24-year-old is one of the few returning young players expected to receive consistent opportunities as the Bucks evaluate their long-term core. Rollins should compete for a starting backcourt role entering training camp, though his usage could fluctuate depending on Tyler Herro's status. Rollins' fantasy outlook is trending up following Milwaukee's organizational reset.

items.headline: Rollins has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers due to a right thumb sprain.
items.story: Rollins had been ruled out for Friday's win over the Nets due to a hip strain, but it's a different injury that will keep him sidelined for the finale. Kevin Porter (knee) and Gary Trent (oblique) will also be unavailable Sunday, so AJ Green and Cormac Ryan should again start in the backcourt and get all the run they can handle. Rollins will finish the season with averages of 17.3 points, 4.6 rebounds, 5.6 assists, 2.5 triples and 1.5 steals per game.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Nets.
items.story: After being downgraded to questionable earlier in the day, Rollins will ultimately take a seat on Friday due to a lingering right hip strain. The 23-year-old was highly productive during Wednesday's loss to Detroit, racking up 23 points and six assists across 33 minutes, but the Bucks have opted to exercise caution with his injury. With Rollins unavailable for a depleted Milwaukee squad, AJ Green is expected to take on primary playmaking duties, while Taurean Prince should remain in the starting five for a third consecutive contest.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is listed as questionable ahead of Friday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Rollins has been sidelined intermittently of late due to a right hip strain. He recently logged 33 minutes in Wednesday's 137-111 loss to Detroit, finishing with 23 points, two rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block. However, despite appearing to be on track to suit up Friday versus Brooklyn, the 23-year-old is now in danger of missing this contest. If that happens, AJ Green will presumably slide over to point guard, while Taurean Prince would also be in line to make his third consecutive appearance with the first five.

items.headline: Rollins provided 23 points (8-19 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 137-111 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Rollins continues to serve as the Bucks' primary ball-handler while shouldering the bulk of the scoring load. Despite missing a handful of games over the past few weeks, Rollins has certainly proven himself this season, flirting with top-50 value through 74 appearances. All signs point to him being a must-draft player next season, although managers will want to be cautious, given the fact that everything that could have gone right for him this season has.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is available for Wednesday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Rollins missed the front end of this back-to-back set, likely due to maintenance-related rest. The Bucks are missing a ton of players for this matchup, meaning Rollins is likely to see heavy usage. It will be interesting to see how many minutes he's allotted, however.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is out for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Rollins is unavailable for the first half of this back-to-back set. AJ Green should see more action in the backcourt for the depleted Bucks on Tuesday.

items.headline: Rollins chipped in 24 points (10-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 131-115 win over Memphis.
items.story: Rollins returned from a two-game absence related to a hip strain, and he saw a major role for a Milwaukee team hammered by injuries. It's no surprise that he soaked up a ton of usage Sunday, but it will be interesting to see how involved he is for the final four games of the campaign.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is available for Sunday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Rollins will shake off a questionable tag and is one of Milwaukee's few regulars who'll suit up, so he should handle a major role against Memphis. However, he's appeared in just one of the Bucks' past four games, so he may experience some rust. Before the recent injury, Rollins averaged 17.1 points, 6.4 assists, 4.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 31.7 minutes over 16 March appearances.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is questionable for Sunday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Rollins missed the Bucks' last two games because of a strained right hip. If Rollins remains on the shelf Sunday, AJ Green might find himself staying in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Rollins was recently downgraded from probable to questionable, and he has now officially been ruled out for Friday's contest due to a right hip strain. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Memphis. With the 23-year-old point guard sidelined, AJ Green, Cormac Ryan and Gary Harris are candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is now listed as questionable for Friday's game against Boston.
items.story: Rollins didn't suit up for Wednesday's 119-113 loss to Houston. While the 23-year-old was listed as probable heading into Friday's meeting with the Celtics, he has since been downgraded to questionable. If Rollins doesn't suit up, AJ Green would be considered the favorite to draw another start at point guard.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is probable for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: This is a promising development for Rollins, who was held out Wednesday against the Rockets due to a right hip injury. Assuming he doesn't suffer any type of setback leading up to tipoff, all indications point to the 23-year-old suiting up Friday.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) won't play in Wednesday's game in Houston.
items.story: Rollins didn't suit up for Sunday's 127-113 loss to the Clippers before returning for Tuesday's win over the Mavericks. He logged 36 minutes, finishing with 24 points, seven rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 36 minutes. However, the 23-year-old won't play in the second half of this back-to-back. With Kevin Porter (knee) out as well, the Bucks will likely lean on Andre Jackson, AJ Green, and Gary Trent to handle most of the work in the backcourt.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Houston.
items.story: A right hip strain may keep Rollins out for the second leg of this back-to-back set, though it could be maintenance-related. Gary Trent and AJ Green could be very involved in the backcourt if Rollins is unavailable

items.headline: Rollins produced 24 points (8-14 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, nine assists and one steal in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 123-99 win over Dallas.
items.story: Rollins posted a strong all-around line and led the Bucks in points and assists in the blowout victory. The 23-year-old didn't appear to be slowed down at all by the hip injury that kept him from taking the floor Sunday. Rollins has put up 20-plus points in three of his last five matchups and should continue to see opportunities with the first unit as Milwaukee wraps up the regular season with little to play for.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is available for Tuesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Rollins was added to the injury report as probable due to a hip injury after sitting out Sunday, and he's since been given the green light to take the court. He's averaging 20.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 1.6 steals over his last five appearances.

items.headline: Rollins (hip) is probable for Tuesday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Rollins is expected to return from a hip injury, which cost him Sunday's game against the Clippers. The guard is enjoying a breakout year, averaging 20.4 points, 5.8 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 30.2 minutes per contest in his last eight games (all starts).

items.headline: Rollins (hip) won't play in Sunday's game against the Clippers, according to Eric Nehm of The Athletic.
items.story: Rollins will join Kyle Kuzma (Achilles), Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee), Myles Turner (knee) and Kevin Porter (knee) on the shelf, so the Bucks will be desperate for scoring options versus Los Angeles. Without those players, Gary Trent, Ousmane Dieng, and AJ Green are the favorites to handle most of the work on the offensive end Sunday.

items.headline: Thompson contributed 11 points (3-13 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 30 minutes during Tuesday's 115-109 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Thompson struggled to shoot from deep, and the cold streak has followed him from Dallas to his first season in Miami. He made up for it on defense with a key block in the closing minutes. The Heat need his production if he remains a starter, and the hope is that the shot comes around during the upcoming homestand.

items.headline: Thompson supplied 23 points (8-15 FG, 7-13 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and two blocks in 32 minutes during Sunday's 114-108 win over the Kings.
items.story: The veteran wing is re-discovering the long-range shooting form that previously seemed to be left behind in Golden State. Thompson's drained multiple three-points in five straight games and poured in at least seven in three of those contests, averaging 21.6 points, 5.6 treys, 2.8 assists, 1.6 boards and 1.0 blocks over that span while shooting a blistering 50.0 percent from beyond the arc, and 52.8 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Thompson closed with 11 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three assists and two blocks over 23 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Thompson received a warm reception in his return to Golden State but struggled to find his shooting rhythm, connecting on just two of seven attempts from beyond the arc. The veteran guard was coming off a game-winning three-pointer against the Clippers on Wednesday but couldn't sustain that momentum. His two blocks provided an unexpected fantasy boost, though his value remains heavily dependent on perimeter shooting.

items.headline: Thompson notched 30 points (11-22 FG, 8-17 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and one block across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 117-116 overtime win over the Clippers.
items.story: Thompson has made at least four three-pointers in three straight games. After an ice-cold preseason, the veteran sharpshooter has turned things around and is giving Miami valuable spacing around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. Thompson is a strong streaming option for threes while he's this hot, though his lack of peripheral production limits his ceiling.

items.headline: Thompson amassed 19 points (7-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and one assist in 27 minutes during Monday's 138-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Thompson stayed hot Monday, sinking at least four triples for a second consecutive game. The veteran sharpshooter should continue spacing the floor for Miami's star-studded frontcourt, averaging 11.9 points, 1.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 3.3 three-pointers in 21.9 minutes per game so far this season.

items.headline: Thompson supplied 25 points (9-14 FG, 7-12 3Pt) and three assists across 26 minutes during Friday's 145-125 win over the Pacers.
items.story: The 36-year-old turned back the clock to his peak Splash Brothers days in Golden State, with the seven made threes equaling his total from the prior three games combined. Thompson's 25 points were also a season high, but he's reached double digits in scoring in only three of six contests so far in 2026-27 as he adjusts to his new role with Miami. Thompson is averaging 10.7 points, 3.2 treys, 1.3 boards and 1.3 assists in 21.0 minutes to begin his tenure with the Heat.

items.headline: Thompson contributed six points (2-8 FG, 2-7 3Pt), one rebound and one assist across 15 minutes during Monday's 113-109 loss to Dallas.
items.story: Thompson struggled from the field and played a season-low 15 minutes as Miami dropped its fourth consecutive game. The veteran sharpshooter has scored six points or fewer in two of his last three appearances, shooting just 29.0 percent (9-for-31) from the field during that stretch. His limited playing time and inconsistent shooting make him difficult to trust in standard fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Thompson tallied 10 points (3-6 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and a rebound across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Thompson made three triples but offered virtually nothing outside the scoring column, highlighting his increasingly specialized fantasy profile. His 16-minute workload was particularly concerning, as limited playing time can make it hard to generate consistent three-point production, especially since three bench players (Bobby Portis, Nikola Jovic and Pelle Larsson) played 20-plus minutes. Unless his minutes increase considerably, Thompson could struggle to provide reliable fantasy value beyond occasional perimeter shooting.

items.headline: Thompson finished with zero points (0-7 FG, 0-6 3Pt), three assists and one rebound in 15 minutes during Friday's 136-115 preseason loss to the Magic.
items.story: Thompson rounded out what has been a poor preseason, missing all seven of his shot attempts. While he will almost certainly be better than this most nights, Thompson's days of being a viable fantasy asset may be behind him. Thompson is still being drafted in standard leagues, but he might be better left on the waiver wire in most formats.

items.headline: Thompson finished with 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt), one rebound and one block across 23 minutes in Wednesday's 144-128 preseason win over the Nets.
items.story: Thompson started alongside Davion Mitchell in Miami's backcourt but struggled to find his rhythm from deep, missing five of seven three-point attempts. He still reached double figures by converting three shots inside the arc. The veteran's perimeter shooting remains his primary fantasy appeal, though his contributions outside the scoring column were minimal Wednesday.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) is in line to play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Nets, Will Manso of Local 10 Miami reports.
items.story: Miami intends to deploy most of its starters for this exhibition. The veteran sharpshooter should receive some playing time in the first half.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) is out for Saturday's preseason game against the Timberwolves, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The 36-year-old vet will receive a maintenance day Saturday, but he should be back in action for Wednesday's preseason meeting with the Nets. Tim Hardaway should be more involved in the rotation Saturday with Thompson unavailable.

items.headline: Thompson recorded zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two rebounds across 13 minutes in Saturday's 129-105 preseason win over the Raptors.
items.story: Thompson only played in the first half of Saturday's contest and didn't offer much in his preseason debut for the Heat. He started Miami's preseason opener and is the favorite to get the starting nod at shooting guard when the regular season begins.

items.headline: Thompson is the clear front-runner to open the season as Miami's starting shooting guard, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: While the Heat are expected to hold a competition for the job during the preseason, Thompson's floor-spacing ability makes him a natural fit alongside Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo. The veteran sharpshooter made 38.3 percent on 7.6 three-point attempts per game with Dallas last regular season and has converted 38.7 percent from deep over the past three regular seasons.

items.headline: Thompson cleared waivers and officially agreed to a two-year, $11.5 million contract with the Heat on Sunday, Sam Amick and Darnell Mayberry of The Athletic report.
items.story: Miami acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo this offseason, but the Heat are now adding Thompson in hopes of bolstering the team's chances of winning another championship. The 2011 No. 11 overall pick is coming off his worst season, averaging 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists across 21.7 minutes, all career lows, in 69 regular-season games with the Mavericks. It's unlikely that Thompson will return to All-Star form with the Heat, considering he will turn 37 during the 2026-27 campaign. Regardless of his role, Thompson should have an opportunity to be much more productive than he was in Dallas, especially since his shooting acumen will provide spacing for Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

items.headline: The Mavericks announced Friday they have reached a buyout agreement with Thompson, who's expected to sign with the Heat after he clears waivers, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Thompson's status had been in limbo this offseason, so it's not overly surprising to see him and Dallas part ways. The veteran sharpshooter is coming off perhaps the worst season of his career, ending with career-low averages of 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.9 three-pointers in 21.7 minutes per game through 69 regular-season appearances (eight starts). Despite that, Miami appears to have quickly swooped in to secure Thompson's services as a three-and-D presence with championship experience.

items.headline: Thompson amassed 12 points (4-10 FG, 4-9 3Pt), one assist and one steal across 10 minutes during Sunday's 149-128 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Thompson produced a career-worst campaign in 2025-26, drawing a career-low eight starts. The veteran sharpshooter averaged a career-low 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.9 three-pointers in 21.7 minutes per tilt through 69 games this season, shooting 38.3 percent from deep. Thompson is set for his third season with Dallas in 2026-27, barring a trade or contract buyout.

items.headline: Thompson (illness) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Sunday's regular-season finale against the Bulls.
items.story: Thompson missed the past two games for the Mavericks due to an illness, but it appears he'll be available for the last game of the regular season. His return may result in fewer minutes for AJ Johnson and John Poulakidas.

items.headline: Thompson (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Thompson was a late addition to the injury report and will miss Dallas' penultimate game of the season. With the veteran wing sidelined, John Poulakidas, Khris Middleton and AJ Johnson are candidates to see increased minutes. Thompson's final chance to suit up this season will come Sunday against the Bulls.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) will play Friday against the Spurs.
items.story: Thompson received a rest day Wednesday against the Suns, but he'll be back on the court Friday after being omitted from the team's injury report. The veteran forward is averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.2 assists over his last five appearances, all off the bench.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Thompson will get a maintenance day for the second leg of the Mavericks' back-to-back set, so AJ Johnson and John Poulakidas are both poised to see more minutes in Wednesday's contest. Thompson should return for Friday's contest against the Spurs.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Thompson is expected to receive a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set. AJ Johnson has a chance to step into a sizable role with so many Mavericks expected to sit.

items.headline: Thompson provided 18 points (7-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt), one rebound and two assists across 22 minutes during Friday's 138-127 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Cooper Flagg stole the show with his 51-point performance, but Thompson, who returned from a one-game absence due to rest, made his presence felt with his shooting off the bench. Thompson has drained multiple three-pointers in six of his last seven appearances dating back to March 18, and he's shooting 22-for-49 (44.8 percent) from beyond the arc over that stretch.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Thompson received a night off during Tuesday's loss to the Bucks but will be available for Friday's tilt. He's averaging 10.7 points and 1.5 assists in 21.3 minutes over his previous six appearances.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) won't play Tuesday against the Bucks.
items.story: This looks to be a scheduled off day for the veteran forward with the regular season nearing an end. Look for Khris Middleton and  John Poulakidas to pick up minutes in the frontcourt with Naji Marshall (illness), Caleb Martin (heel) and Thompson all sidelined.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: The Mavericks are planning a rest day for the veteran for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Thompson had just five points in 22 minutes against Minnesota on Monday.

items.headline: Thompson chipped in 15 points (5-10 FG, 5-9 3Pt), one rebound, one assist, one block and one steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 137-131 overtime loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Thompson put together a solid line against his former team. He's in the midst of a decent stretch for the Mavericks, posting averages of 14.2 points, 1.2 assists and 3.6 three-pointers on 47.3 percent shooting over his last five games.

items.headline: Thompson (rest) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Thompson is set to return to action Wednesday after receiving two straight games off for rest purposes. He's averaging 13.7 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 20.7 minutes over six March appearances.

items.headline: Turner ended with five points (1-8 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists, four blocks and one steal over 26 minutes before fouling out of Saturday's 132-129 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: The four blocks were his best total since Nov. 2, when he rejected five shots by the Timberwolves. Turner was back at center Saturday with Jericho Sims (coach's decision) not getting onto the court at all, as coach Taylor Jenkins scrambles to generate a spark for his 1-16 club. Over nine starts in November, Turner is averaging 6.9 points, 6.6 boards, 3.3 assists, 2.1 blocks and 1.6 threes in 27.0 minutes.

items.headline: Turner (shoulder) is off the injury report for Saturday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: The veteran big man is set to return after sitting out Thursday's game against Portland due to a left shoulder contusion. After logging a season-high 27 minutes in a spot start his last time out, Pete Nance could be removed from the rotation entirely Saturday.

items.headline: Turner has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Portland due to a left shoulder contusion.
items.story: Turner will miss Thursday's contest after playing 21 minutes against Miami on Wednesday. His next opportunity to return will come Saturday against Philadelphia, pending further injury updates. In Turner's absence, Jericho Sims, Kel'el Ware and Nate Ament are candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Turner posted four points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and three blocks in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 loss to Miami.
items.story: Turner continues to struggle offensively, averaging just 7.1 points per game this season despite maintaining a starting role in Milwaukee's frontcourt. The veteran center remains a valuable source of blocked shots, but his inconsistent scoring and reduced playing time have limited his overall fantasy production. His defensive contributions provide some value in category leagues, though his offensive struggles make him difficult to trust in standard formats.

items.headline: Turner recorded 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), 11 rebounds, three assists and two steals across 31 minutes during Friday's 107-99 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Turner returned from a one-game absence Friday and turned in one of his best performance of the season. After shooting an abysmal 9.1 percent from the field in his previous three appearances, the big man delivered an efficient effort en route to a season-high scoring total. He also grabbed a game- and season-high 11 rebounds, securing his first double-double of the campaign.

items.headline: Turner (rest) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Turner received his first breather of the season Wednesday against the Lakers, but he'll be back in the mix for Friday's game. He's struggled to contribute of late, averaging 2.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 blocks over his last three appearances.

items.headline: Turner has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers due to rest.
items.story: Turner will miss his first game of the season after totaling only three points in 27 minutes during Tuesday's blowout loss in New York. In Turner's absence, Kel'el Ware and Jericho Sims are candidates for increased roles. Turner should return to action Friday in Orlando.

items.headline: Turner registered 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, six assists, two steals and two blocks across 36 minutes in Wednesday's 109-102 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Turner delivered a solid fantasy performance despite attempting just six shots. His six assists were particularly valuable, while four three-pointers and four combined defensive stats significantly boosted his production. He finished with at least two tallies in each of the six major categories. His multi-category production provides a modest fantasy foundation even when his scoring volume remains limited.

items.headline: Turner finished Monday's 112-100 loss to the Timberwolves with 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and five blocks over 31 minutes.
items.story: Turner delivered an impressive defensive performance, matching his season high with five blocks while connecting on three triples. The veteran center has now recorded multiple blocks in four consecutive appearances, reinforcing his value as an elite rim protector. Although his scoring and rebounding numbers have fluctuated, his combination of shot-blocking and perimeter shooting continues to provide considerable fantasy upside.

items.headline: Turner racked up six points (2-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, four blocks and one steal across 28 minutes during Monday's 110-102 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Turner set a season high in rebounds Monday. The veteran big man, a rumored trade candidate, should continue to handle a big role at center as long as he's with the rebuilding Bucks, averaging 7.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.8 blocks and 2.3 assists in 27.8 minutes per game over four contests this season.

items.headline: Turner notched 11 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Turner knocked down two triples and contributed a block in his first regular-season appearance of the campaign, but his overall production was modest despite a substantial workload. The veteran center committed three turnovers and struggled to make a significant defensive impact as Anthony Davis erupted for 34 points and 12 rebounds. Turner should continue to provide value through his combination of three-point shooting and shot-blocking, though fantasy managers will hope for stronger defensive numbers moving forward.

items.headline: Turner (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game versus the Pacers.
items.story: Turner was one of several key Bucks players who sat out Wednesday's loss to the Bulls, but he's been given the green light to return in Milwaukee's preseason finale. The veteran center will look to bounce back in 2026-27 following a lackluster first year with the Bucks, during which he averaged 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.6 blocks, 1.5 assists and 0.7 steals in 26.9 minutes per game across 71 regular-season starts.

items.headline: Turner (rest) won't play in Wednesday's preseason game against Chicago, Cameron Ezeir of CBS58 reports.
items.story: Turner started in all three of Milwaukee's preseason games thus far, averaging 10.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 2.7 blocks over 21.7 minutes per contest. It's unknown if he will suit up for Friday's preseason meeting with the Pacers, Milwaukee's final exhibition before the start of the regular season on Oct. 21 in Washington.

items.headline: Turner recorded five points (2-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt), five blocks, two rebounds and one assist in 24 minutes during Sunday's 105-90 preseason loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Turner provided ample production on the defensive end, racking up a game-high five blocks. However, that's where the good news ends. Coming off a terrible season last year, Turner is looking to reinvigorate his career. He warrants attention in the later rounds of drafts, based on his blocks upside alone. With that said, his peripheral numbers are typically less than ideal, which limits his overall upside.

items.headline: Turner recorded 19 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, two blocks and one steal in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 128-126 preseason win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Turner delivered an efficient offensive performance while providing his usual rim protection. The veteran center's combination of perimeter shooting and shot-blocking should continue to make him a valuable fantasy option heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Turner recorded seven points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 19 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Turner provided a full stat line in Milwaukee's preseason opener Monday. The veteran center is a rumored trade candidate but has two years left of team control on his contract, including 2026-27, so the rebuilding Bucks might want to see Turner revert to his form from his time with the Pacers before considering swinging a deal.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) remains one of Milwaukee's top trade candidates after the organization shifted into rebuilding mode following the Giannis Antetokounmpo deal, Amir Motameni of SI.com reports.
items.story: While the veteran center would likely open the season as the Bucks' starting center, the team's focus on developing younger talent could eventually lead to a move if the right offer emerges. Until then, Turner should continue to serve as a stabilizing presence on a roster headlined by inexperienced players.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the 76ers.
items.story: Turner will sit out Milwaukee's regular-season finale, which should result in a start for Jericho Sims. Turner put up eighth-round value in his first season with the Bucks, posting averages of 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.1 triples and 1.6 blocks per game.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) is off the injury report for Friday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: After sitting out Wednesday's loss to the Pistons, Turner is available for Milwaukee's last home game of the regular season. The star big man has averaged 9.3 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.9 blocks and 1.0 steals in 22.1 minutes per contest over his last seven games.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Turner will be sidelined for a second straight contest. The Bucks are likely to proceed with caution given where they are in the standings. Jericho Sims and Pete Nance are likely to see sizable workloads with this news.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) is out for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Turner is out with a left ankle sprain for the first half of this back-to-back set. Pete Nance and Jericho Sims should see more playing time at center in Turner's absence Tuesday.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) is off the injury report for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Turner is set to return from a one-game absence with an ankle injury. The veteran big man has averaged 9.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.2 blocks in 24.5 minutes per tilt in his last 10 games.

items.headline: Turner (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Turner will get a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set. The Bucks are extremely thin up front, and that could result in more minutes for Jericho Sims and Pete Nance.

items.story: Turner delivered a loaded stat line with at least two tallies in four of the five major categories, but overall, this has been a disappointing season for the former Pacers big man. He's had issues adjusting to the offense, and his numbers have taken a drastic hit as a result. Turner has averaged 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game in 2025-26, and he's experiencing a marked decrease in each of those categories compared to the previous seasons.

items.headline: Turner (knee) is off the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Turner missed Sunday's loss to the Clippers with a knee issue but is set to return Tuesday, and he'll likely push either Jericho Sims or Pete Nance to the bench. Turner has averaged 10.3 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.9 blocks in 24.3 minutes per contest in his last eight games.

items.headline: Turner (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Clippers, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Turner will hit the sidelines for the second leg of this back-to-back set, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Tuesday's meeting with the Mavericks. Jericho Sims, Ousmane Dieng and Pete Nance will help fill the void with Turner unavailable.

items.headline: Turner is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Clippers due to right patella tendonopathy.
items.story: Turner has been playing through a right calf injury as of late but also popped up on the injury report earlier in March due to a knee issue. Sunday's game is the second leg of a back-to-back set for the Bucks, and if Turner is unable to play, then Jericho Sims would be the top candidate to enter Milwaukee's starting lineup. Turner played 28 minutes in Saturday's 127-95 loss to the Spurs and finished with 15 points, six rebounds, one assist, two blocks, one steal and four three-pointers.

items.headline: Turner (calf) is available for Saturday's game against San Antonio.

With Bobby Portis (wrist), Kyle Kuzma (Achilles) and Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) unavailable, Jericho Sims and Pete Nance may both continue to see meaningful minutes even with Turner's return bolstering depth.

items.headline: Turner (calf) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Turner is in danger of missing a second straight game due to right calf soreness. With Bobby Portis (wrist) also listed as questionable, Jericho Sims and Pete Nance could both see a sizable bump in minutes Saturday. Over 12 appearances in March, Turner has averaged 8.3 points and 3.8 rebounds across 22.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Turner (calf) is out for Wednesday's game in Portland.
items.story: Bobby Portis (wrist) and Kyle Kuzma (Achilles) will join Turner on the inactive list for Wednesday's game, leaving Milwaukee very thin up front. Jericho Sims will get a chance to start with Turner out, and there will be more minutes available for Ousmane Dieng. Turner's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Turner is questionable for Wednesday's game against Portland with right calf soreness.
items.story: Turner is a late addition to the injury report, and he's been nursing calf issues for the past week or so. With Bobby Portis' (wrist) status also up in the air Wednesday, the Bucks may need to turn to Jericho Sims and Pete Nance to both take on a featured role in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Turner (calf) will play in Thursday's game against Utah.

items.headline: Turner is questionable for Thursday's game against the Jazz due to a right calf strain.
items.story: After missing Tuesday's loss to the Cavaliers, Turner is in jeopardy of being out once again Thursday. Jericho Sims would likely start at center if Turner cannot play, while Pete Nance would likely find himself more involved in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Turner (calf) won't play Tuesday against Cleveland, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Turner was added to Milwaukee's injury report Monday with a right calf strain, and the team has since downgraded him to out. This will open up opportunities at center for Jericho Sims and Pete Nance.

items.headline: Turner is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers due to a right calf strain.
items.story: Turner has recently been dealing with right patella tendinitis, though it now seems he's picked up a calf injury. His status for Tuesday will presumably depend on how he fares during shootaround and warmups ahead of tipoff.

items.headline: Turner (knee) is available for Sunday's game against the Pacers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Turner drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game due to right patella tendinitis, but the veteran center has been given the green light to play in the second leg of the Bucks' back-to-back set. He's failed to score in double digits in seven of his last eight outings, and over that span he has connected on just 37.1 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: Turner is questionable for Sunday's game against the Pacers due to right patella tendonitis.
items.story: Turner posted eight points, six rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes during Saturday's loss to the Hawks and is in danger of missing the second night of Milwaukee's back-to-back set, which would be his first absence since Feb. 20. With Giannis Antetokounmpo (calf), Bobby Portis (back) and Ousmane Dieng (illness) also questionable, Jericho Sims, Pete Nance and Kyle Kuzma could be candidates for heavy workloads Sunday.

items.headline: Turner accumulated 22 points (7-13 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 129-114 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Turner added 15 of his 22 points from beyond the arc and combined with teammate Kyle Kuzma to drill 11 total threes. Turner had been riding a five-game skid in which he'd failed to score in double figures heading into Tuesday's clash, so this strong all-around showing is a clear step in the right direction for the 29-year-old.

items.headline: Bryant provided eight points (3-8 FG, 2-7 3Pt) and three rebounds in 20 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 win over New Orleans.
items.story: Bryant saw 20 minutes of action for the first time this season in this blowout victory. However, the second-year forward didn't deliver his most efficient effort. He's logged double-digit minutes in three of his last five appearances, averaging 3.8 points and 1.6 rebounds in 11.8 minutes per tilt over that stretch.

items.headline: Bryant recorded zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) across two minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Bryant has gone scoreless in consecutive appearances, playing just seven combined minutes after averaging 9.0 points across his previous two outings. The second-year forward has seen his playing time decline sharply from 19 to five to two minutes over his last three games. His inconsistent role in San Antonio's rotation leaves him with minimal fantasy value outside deeper dynasty leagues.

items.headline: Bryant provided eight points (2-4 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist over 14 minutes during Monday's 122-96 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Bryant played 14 minutes off the bench, maintaining a limited role despite the blowout victory. It's been an underwhelming campaign thus far for Bryant, who has exceeded 15 minutes only twice in 10 appearances.
