He has barely been a top-400 player to this point, averaging 3.1 points in 10.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bryant totaled four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one rebound over 10 minutes during Saturday's 122-106 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Bryant logged double-digit minutes for the first time this season, scoring his first points of the 2026-27 campaign. The second-year forward faces an uphill climb for a steady role, especially once Tobias Harris (calf) returns.

items.headline: The Spurs exercised the team option on Bryant for the 2027-28 season, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Bryant, the 2025 No. 14 overall pick, appeared in 71 regular-season games as a rookie in 2025-26. He got off to a slow start but demonstrated signs of growth by ending the year averaging 7.0 points and 1.9 assists in seven regular-season appearances in April. Bryant should be more productive in 2026-27, though the verdict is still out regarding just how high his ceiling can be at the professional level. The Spurs are willing to be patient and find out, so the team picked up his option for the 2027-28 season.

items.headline: Bryant tallied 16 points (4-7 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and two blocks over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Bryant appeared to have the green light to fire away from deep, connecting on a team-high four triples. The second-year forward is an option for a larger role off the bench while Tobias Harris (calf) is on the shelf.

items.headline: Carter (ankle) is available for Wednesday's preseason game against Phoenix, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: Bryant didn't play in Monday's preseason meeting with the Jazz. However, he is cleared to return Wednesday versus the Suns.

items.headline: Bryant (ankle) won't play in Monday's preseason game against Utah, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News.
items.story: Bryant exited Saturday's preseason loss to Phoenix after rolling his right ankle in the first half and did not return, so the Spurs are giving him a day to recover Monday. His next chance to play comes Wednesday against the Suns.

items.headline: Bryant exited Saturday's 102-98 preseason loss to Phoenix after rolling his right ankle in the first half and did not return, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Bryant suffered the injury after stepping on teammate Devin Vassell's foot and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the contest. However, McDonald suggested the decision was precautionary rather than indicative of a serious injury, while coach Mitch Johnson also characterized the early exit as precautionary. The second-year forward's status for Monday's preseason matchup against Utah remains uncertain, though there is currently no indication of a prolonged absence.

items.headline: Bryant finished with 11 points (3-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, one steal and one block in 23 minutes during Thursday's 123-116 preseason loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Bryant showed encouraging offensive development, knocking down two three-pointers while contributing on the glass and defensively. The second-year forward committed four turnovers but appeared more comfortable making decisions with the ball compared to his rookie campaign. Bryant will look to build on the performance as he competes for a larger role in San Antonio's forward rotation.

items.headline: Bryant (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Bucks, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Bryant will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set, and it's possible the Spurs have seen enough from him this summer after he appeared in the team's first two Las Vegas Summer League games. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against the Jazz.

items.headline: Bryant tallied 19 points (7-10 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two blocks and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 70-49 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: After scoring 12 points on 4-of-13 shooting from the field in Thursday's loss to the Hawks, Bryant bounced back with an extremely efficient performance Saturday. The 20-year-old forward posted a game-high 19 points in this low-scoring affair. He also led the Spurs in blocks, matching the game-high mark.

items.headline: Bryant totaled 12 points (4-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 25 minutes during Thursday's 93-66 Summer League loss to the Hawks.
items.story: The 2025 lottery pick shook off a scoreless first half to reach double figures, though he'll look to improve his efficiency after committing four turnovers. The Spurs used him at shooting guard Thursday, which put him out of his comfort zone, so that's something to watch going forward.

items.headline: Bryant (rest) is starting Thursday's Summer League game against Atlanta.
items.story: The Spurs kept the 2025 first-rounder out of the California Classic portion of Summer League to manage his reps. Bryant should play a featured role for the Spurs this summer as he looks to take a step forward in his second season.

items.headline: Bryant will only play during the Las Vegas Summer League, NBA reporter Matthew Tynan reports.
items.story: The Spurs will play a few games at the California Classic prior to their Vegas trip, and Bryant will be held out of those games. Bryant, who is entering his second campaign, averaged 4.2 points and 2.5 rebounds across 71 regular-season games as a rookie.

items.headline: Bryant chipped in two rebounds in six minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to the Knicks in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Bryant logged single-digit minutes for a ninth consecutive contest, going scoreless for the third time during that span. The rookie first-rounder took on an increased role in the latter half of the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 6.1 points and 3.4 rebounds while shooting 37.3 percent from downtown in 15.3 minutes per game across the final 34 games of the regular season. He finished the regular season with averages of 4.2 points and 2.5 rebounds in 11.5 minutes per contest over 71 outings.

items.headline: Bryant (foot) is available for Game 2 versus the Timberwolves on Wednesday, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: Bryant will be available to play limited minutes off the bench Wednesday. In San Antonio's first-round series with Portland, Bryant averaged 3.2 points and 2.2 rebounds in 9.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bryant (foot) is "trending well" ahead of Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals versus Minnesota, Raul Dominguez Jr. of the Associated Press reports.
items.story: Bryant appears to have a good chance of playing in Game 2, and head coach Mitch Johnson indicated Bryant should suit up for Game 3 if he's not available Wednesday. The 20-year-old averaged 3.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.6  blocks across 9.2 minutes in the Spurs' first-round series against Portland. However, he wasn't on the court for the series opener versus the Timberwolves on Monday night. If Bryant is available, he might see only limited action.

items.headline: Bryant (foot) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Bryant missed Monday's Game 1 loss due to a right foot sprain he sustained in a recent practice, though head coach Mitch Johnson said he's optimistic it won't be a long-term issue. The rookie first-rounder averaged 3.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists across 9.2 minutes per game in five first-round outings. If he remains out, Keldon Johnson could continue seeing a slight bump in minutes.

items.headline: Bryant (foot) is out for Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against Minnesota on Monday, NBA reporter Matthew Tynan reports.
items.story: Head coach Mitch Johnson said Bryant sustained the injury in a recent practice, though Johnson added that he's optimistic it won't be a long-term issue, according to Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News. Bryant didn't make much of an impact in the previous round against Portland, averaging 3.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 9.2 minutes (five games). Keldon Johnson and Harrison Barnes could pick up a few extra minutes in Bryant's place Monday night.

items.headline: Bryant (foot) is listed as questionable for Monday's Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Bryant is dealing with a sprained right foot and could miss Monday's contest. If the rookie first-rounder is ruled out, Keldon Johnson could see a slight uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Bryant closed Sunday's 128-118 loss to the Nuggets with 13 points (6-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), five rebounds, five assists and three blocks over 30 minutes.
items.story: The rookie took advantage of the expanded playing time and posted a solid line despite struggling massively with his three-point shooting. Don't expect Bryant to be much of a factor in the playoffs, though. He averaged 4.2 points, 2.5 rebounds and 0.7 assists per game in 71 appearances during the regular season while logging 11.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bryant chipped in 17 points (6-9 FG, 5-6 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Wednesday's 112-101 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Victor Wembanyama (ribs) and Stephon Castle (knee) were both sidelined, allowing the rookie to step into a larger role off the bench. The Spurs are hopeful to have both players back for Friday, however. Across 69 appearances this season, Bryant has averaged a mere 11.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bryant supplied 10 points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), five rebounds and one assist in 21 minutes during Monday's 119-115 win over the Clippers.
items.story: The one-and-done freshman from Arizona hasn't consistently contributed as a rookie, but he's appeared in 57 games with the parent club and shown flashes of elite defense. Monday marked his seventh game with a double-digit scoring total, but his role will likely decrease when Luke Kornet (knee) and Dylan Harper (calf) are cleared to return.

items.headline: Bryant provided 10 points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and one assist across nine minutes during Thursday's 136-131 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Bryant scored in double figures for the second time this month and needed only nine minutes to do it. He continues to hang on at the back end of the rotation, and while he can occasionally provide a small boost in the scoring or rebounding category, he's not someone you can rely on at this time.

items.headline: Bryant finished Tuesday's 131-91 victory over the 76ers with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), nine rebounds and three assists across 26 minutes.
items.story: Harrison Barnes (ankle) missed his first game of the season, allowing Bryant to see extended run off the bench. He hasn't made much of an impact in fantasy leagues this season with a low usage rate combined with sparse minutes, but he made the most of his opportunity Tuesday.

items.headline: Bryant had 16 points (6-12 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 27 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's 136-108 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: The 14th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft set new career highs in minutes and points in the rout as he led the Spurs' second unit in scoring. Bryant has seen his role increase in February, and through the first five games this month, he's averaging 9.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.0 threes, 1.2 assists, and 1.2 combined steals and blocks in 18.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mathurin has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets due to a right thumb sprain.
items.story: Mathurin wasn't listed on the initial injury report, and the extent of the issue remains unclear. While he's not a major part of the regular rotation, Mathurin, Trey Murphy and Trendon Watford are all expected to be unavailable Wednesday, opening the door for Saddiq Bey, Herbert Jones and potentially Jordan Poole to play more minutes.

items.headline: Mathurin notched 11 points (3-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across 18 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Making his Pelicans debut, Mathurin had a solid showing off the bench Wednesday. The swingman worked as the Clippers' sixth man following a deadline trade from the Pacers last season, and it appears Mathurin will handle a similar role in his new digs.

items.headline: Mathurin is not listed in the starting lineup for Friday's preseason game against the Wizards.
items.story: Mathurin will come off the bench for the last exhibition before the start of the 2026-27 campaign. The 2022 No. 6 overall pick, who is competing for a spot in the starting lineup, has averaged 9.0 points, 2.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists over 16.7 minutes per contest in three preseason appearances.

items.headline: Mathurin chipped in six points (2-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one block across 19 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Preparing for his debut season with the Pelicans, Mathurin is vying for a starting role over Herbert Jones. This will remain a battle for fantasy managers to monitor up until the start of the regular season.

items.headline: Mathurin is listed in the starting lineup for Thursday's preseason game against Miami.
items.story: Mathurin impressed during the preseason opener, finishing with 13 points in just 17 minutes of action off the bench. He'll have a chance to show what he can do with the first unit Thursday while Dejounte Murray (toe) sits and Herbert Jones rotates to the bench.

items.headline: Mathurin scored a team-high 13 points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT) while chipping in five assists and two rebounds in 17 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: The 24-year-old wing signed a two-year deal with New Orleans in August, and he demonstrated his ability to provide offense from the second unit in Tuesday's win. Mathurin is coming off a 2025-26 campaign that saw him average a career-high 17.6 points, 5.4 boards, 2.4 assists and 0.8 steals while also adding 1.4 threes in 30.0 minutes a game between the Pacers and Clippers, but he's unlikely to see that large a workload with the Pelicans.

items.headline: Mathurin signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the Pelicans on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The deal includes a player option for the second season. Mathurin was previously a restricted free agent, but the Pelicans approached the Clippers about withdrawing the qualifying offer prior to this deal. In New Orleans, Mathurin is expected to be a key part of the second unit behind Trey Murphy and Saddiq Bey.

items.headline: The Clippers' acquisition of Max Strus adds another established wing while Mathurin's future with the club remains unresolved as a restricted free agent.
items.story: Strus can absorb minutes at both wing spots and brings shooting and playoff experience, potentially making the Clippers less dependent on retaining Mathurin. However, Los Angeles remained below the first apron following the trade, so the addition of Strus doesn't necessarily prevent Mathurin from returning. His fantasy outlook will depend heavily on where he ultimately signs and what role is available there.

items.headline: The Clippers tendered Mathurin a qualifying offer Monday, per Michael Scotto of USA Today.
items.story: The move will make Mathurin a restricted free agent. The Clippers can match any offer sheet he receives from other teams, and they'll likely make every effort to retain him following last season's Ivica Zubac trade.

items.headline: Mathurin could be set for a reserve role if he remains with the Clippers in 2026-27 due to the selection of Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Mathurin operated almost exclusively off the bench for Los Angeles in 2025-26, making just one start after being traded away from the Pacers. The 2022 first-rounder is slated to become a restricted free agent, so the Clippers do have the ability to match any offer sheet he receives from other teams. If Mathurin sticks around, he'll likely be competing with Wagler and Kris Dunn for the starting spot at shooting guard during training camp in the fall.

items.headline: Mathurin ended with 23 points (7-11 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Following his trade from the Pacers, Mathurin found some success in a bench role with the Clippers. He made 26 appearances (one start) and posted averages of 17.4 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.7 three-pointers in 28.0 minutes per contest. However, he struggled from the perimeter, hitting 20.7 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Mathurin recorded 20 points (7-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), nine rebounds, eight assists and one block across 32 minutes during Sunday's 115-110 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Mathurin stepped up amid Kawhi Leonard's (wrist/knee) absence and produced a solid line. Mathurin came two assists and one rebound shy of a triple-double. Mathurin's numbers have tapered off a bit in recent weeks, but his success against the Warriors should result in another good outing, given the upcoming rematch against Golden State in the Play-In Tournament.

items.headline: Mathurin closed Thursday's 118-99 loss to San Antonio with 18 points (5-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 8-8 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals in 27 minutes off the bench.
items.story: After scoring just four points on 2-for-7 shooting in the Clippers' loss to the Trail Blazers on Tuesday, Mathurin bounced back to his usual level of production. The fourth-year wing has scored at least 16 points in 10 of his last 11 games, averaging 20.6 points, 5.4 boards, 1.9 assists and 0.8 steals over that stretch as a key part of the second unit.

items.headline: Mathurin produced four points (2-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 114-104 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Mathurin surged with three solid games following a four-game absence, but he crashed back to earth Tuesday night. He logged his second-lowest shot volume of the season in the loss, and although Mathurin usually comes off the bench, his low total illustrates how the team depends on the sixth man for production. The team is 1-3 when Mathurin scores less than 10 points.

items.headline: Mathurin closed Sunday's 127-113 victory over Milwaukee with 28 points (7-10 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 13-14 FT), six rebounds and one assist across 27 minutes.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Mathurin led the team in scoring Sunday and got to the free-throw line with ease. The swingman is thriving as the Clippers' sixth man, averaging 23.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 0.8 steals in 30.3 minutes per game across his last eight appearances.

items.headline: Mathurin (toe) chipped in 23 points (7-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 8-11 FT), six assists, four rebounds and one block in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 119-94 win over the Raptors.
items.story: After four straight absences due to the right toe injury, Mathurin returned to action in his usual sixth-man role and delivered a strong performance to help the Clippers improve to 37-36 on the season. Since joining L.A. at the trade deadline, Mathurin has averaged 20.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 three-pointers in 29.8 minutes.

items.headline: Mathurin (toe) has been cleared to play Wednesday against the Raptors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Mathurin is ready to return to the court following a four-game absence due to a right toe injury. He was enjoying a strong March before going down with the injury, averaging 19.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.7 assists over 10 appearances.

items.headline: Mathurin (toe) will remain on the inactive list for Monday's meeting with Milwaukee, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: This will be Mathurin's fourth consecutive game on the sidelines, and it's not a great sign that he continues to get ruled out a day in advance of tipoff. For now, he should be considered highly questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Raptors.

items.headline: Mathurin (toe) will miss the Clippers' upcoming three-game road trip, which wraps up Saturday in Dallas, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: The team initially listed Mathurin as out for Wednesday's matchup, but further clarification was provided shortly after that revealed he would miss LA's next three games to undergo treatment. If all goes according to plan, Mathurin could return to the court as early as Monday against Milwaukee.

items.headline: Mathurin has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans due to right toe injury recovery.
items.story: Mathurin hasn't missed a game since Feb. 8 and has seen an uptick in playing time of late, so his absence Wednesday seems to be a scheduled rest day. If all goes according to plan, expect the Arizona product to be available for the second half of the Clippers' back-to-back Thursday, also against New Orleans.

items.headline: Mathurin amassed 16 points (5-12 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals across 34 minutes during Monday's 119-115 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Mathurin was expected to see increased usage during Kawhi Leonard's (ankle) absence, but the former's total wasn't enough to overcome a productive night from the Spurs. Mathurin snapped an impressive five-game streak of 20-plus point performances. He'll try to renew that streak on the road for a two-game set against the Pelicans.

items.headline: Mathurin totaled 24 points (7-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 10-11 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block across 35 minutes during Saturday's 118-109 loss to Sacramento.
items.story: The severity of Kawhi Leonard's (ankle) injury is unclear, but it's reasonable to assume that Mathurin would get a significant usage boost if the All-Star was unavailable for Monday's game against the Spurs. At present, Mathurin is distinguishing himself as a premier sixth man for the Clippers, averaging 20.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.1 steals since joining the team.

items.headline: Mathurin recorded 26 points (10-19 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 28 minutes during Friday's 119-108 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Mathurin scored at least 20 points for the fourth straight game, providing the Clippers with a reliable scoring punch off the bench. In typical fashion, Mathurin's peripheral contributions have left a little to be desired, dragging down his overall fantasy value. If you need points and out-of-position rebounds, make sure Mathurin isn't somehow available in your league.

items.headline: Mathurin supplied 22 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 10-12 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 153-128 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Even though Kawhi Leonard and Darius Garland carried the team offensively, the Clippers wouldn't have won this game as comfortably as they did without Mathurin's contributions. The forward, who joined the Clippers on the deal that sent Ivica Zubac to the Pacers, was the team's second-highest scorer and has been a regular scoring weapon off the bench for Los Angeles. Mathurin has scored 20-plus points in four of his last five outings off the bench, averaging 20.4 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game in that span.

items.headline: Mathurin logged 28 points (9-20 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 8-9 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal in 36 minutes during Monday's 126-118 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Mathurin's acquisition has played a big role in the Clippers' resurgence, and they have a legitimate chance to escape the Play-In bracket if they can string together more victories. Although the team looked like a squad in tank mode after dealing away James Harden and Ivica Zubac, the Clippers have thrived with the addition of Mathurin and Darius Garland. The team is 7-3 over the past 10 games, and Mathurin's continued work with the second unit will remain a critical part of the game plan.

items.headline: Mathurin posted 21 points (6-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-9 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 35 minutes during the Clippers' 123-120 win over the Grizzlies on Saturday.
items.story: Mathurin's struggles from beyond the arc continued Saturday, and he's now gone 1-for-18 from three-point range over his last six outings. However, the fourth-year pro more than made up for it at the charity stripe and also finished as the Clippers' second-leading rebounder en route to his second double-double of the season. Since being acquired by the Clippers from the Pacers in early February, Mathurin has averaged 18.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.2 steals over 29.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mathurin recorded 23 points (8-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-7 FT), eight rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 130-107 win over the Pacers.
items.story: It seemed Mathurin was extra motivated against his former team. He ended just two boards shy of recording a double-double and has scored at least 20 points in four of his seven appearances with the Clippers after the All-Star break, averaging 21.1 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 0.7 threes made per game in that stretch. Mathurin is doing enough to warrant even more minutes, but as good as he's been off the bench, he's likely to remain in that role for the time being.

items.headline: Mathurin won't start against the Pelicans on Sunday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Kawhi Leonard (ankle) back in the lineup, Mathurin will slide to the second unit. Over six outings (one start) with the Clippers, the 23-year-old swingman has averaged 20.7 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 steals in 31.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mathurin closed with 14 points (4-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal across 34 minutes during Thursday's 94-88 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Mathurin's nightly totals have softened the impact of departures from James Harden and Ivica Zubac, but he didn't provide enough pop to get the Clippers past the Timberwolves. Mathurin has been an essential part of the offense, averaging 20.7 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 blocks since joining the team.

items.headline: Mathurin will start Thursday's game against the Timberwolves, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Mathurin will make his first start since Jan. 2, as he'll be asked to fill in for Kawhi Leonard (ankle). Mathurin has been on a tear off the bench since joining the Clippers, averaging 22.0 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.8 steals across 30.6 minutes (five games).

items.headline: Mathurin closed Sunday's 111-109 loss to the Magic with 21 points (7-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 6-7 FT), nine rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes off the bench.
items.story: The former Pacer scored more than 20 points for a third straight game coming out of the All-Star break, as Mathurin gets comfortable playing a sixth man role on his new squad. During that three-game stretch, the fourth-year wing is averaging 28.3 points, 7.0 boards, 3.7 assists, 1.3 threes and 1.0 steals in 32.0 minutes.

items.headline: Brown has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans due to an illness, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Brown had been sidelined for Sunday's 130-93 loss to the Mavericks due to back injury management and was slated to return to action Wednesday. However, he appears to have fallen ill overnight, as the Nets added him to the injury report as questionable earlier Wednesday before downgrading him to out. Though Brown will be in street clothes, the Nets should get some reinforcement to the backcourt in the form of Egor Demin (leg), who is listed as probable after missing the team's previous six games.

items.headline: Brown (rest) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's meeting in New Orleans.
items.story: Brown rested on the second leg of a back-to-back set Sunday, but he'll be back in action for Wednesday's game. The rookie is averaging 12.9 points, 3.9 assists and 2.0 triples per game this season on 34.6 percent shooting.

items.headline: Brown, who finished with 18 points (5-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal over 25 minutes in Saturday's 124-121 loss to Atlanta, won't play in Sunday's game against Dallas, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Brown logged his fifth consecutive double-digit scoring performance Saturday. However, his efforts weren't enough to help the Nets hold off a late Hawks comeback and earn their third win of the 2026-27 campaign. Head coach Jordi Fernandez mentioned after the game that the rookie won't suit up Sunday versus the Mavericks, the second game of a back-to-back. Without Brown in the lineup, Terance Mann should see more minutes off the bench. Keon Ellis, who didn't get on the floor versus Atlanta, might also get involved.

items.headline: Brown ended with 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 114-104 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Brown provided an offensive spark off the bench, knocking down three triples while finishing as Brooklyn's third-leading scorer. The rookie also contributed four assists and two defensive stats, though he committed four turnovers. His scoring upside is intriguing, but he'll need more consistent playing time to become a dependable fantasy option.

items.headline: Brown tallied 13 points (5-13 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and three assists across 27 minutes in Monday's 103-90 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Brown struggled with his shot once again, and while he scored in double digits for the third game in a row, his efficiency issues are becoming impossible to overlook. Brown remains an intriguing developmental fantasy option, although inconsistent perimeter shooting and modest defensive contributions limit his reliability in standard formats. In five outings, he's shooting just 29.8 percent from the floor and 25 percent from deep, but he's scored in double digits in three games in a row.

items.headline: Brown (rest) is available for Monday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: This is an expected update after Brown was rested Sunday for the first leg of the back-to-back set. There's been no indication of when the Nets will lift Brown's restrictions.

items.headline: Brown (rest) is out for Sunday's game in Indiana, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown will skip the first leg of this upcoming back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game in New York. With Brown inactive, there will be more minutes available for Nolan Traore, Terance Mann and Keon Ellis.

items.headline: Brown finished with 10 points (2-9 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), four assists and one steal across 23 minutes in Friday's 110-94 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Brown was the star for the Nets in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to the Celtics, ending with a career-high 17 points. While the rookie posted another double-digit scoring effort Friday, he didn't have an efficient night shooting the ball. In five professional appearances since entering the league as the 2026 No. 6 overall pick, Brown is averaging 10.3 points and 4.3 assists over 22.5 minutes per contest. He should continue to get opportunities to play, potentially even cracking the starting lineup at some point, though he may have trouble staying consistent throughout his inaugural campaign.

items.headline: Brown tallied 17 points (5-17 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and five assists across 28 minutes in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Brown reached double figures for the first time this season, though that was more based on pure volume than efficiency. His 17 field-goal attempts highlighted an aggressive offensive approach, although he converted just 29.4 percent of his shots. Brown's 28-minute workload and contributions across multiple categories were encouraging, but his efficiency and role within Brooklyn's crowded backcourt could remain inconsistent, ultimately limiting his fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Brown (rest) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Tuesday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Brown was held out of Sunday's matchup against Indiana for rest, but he's expected back in action Tuesday night. He's come off the bench in each of his first two appearances in the NBA, logging six points against Charlotte on Wednesday followed by eight points Saturday in Cleveland.

items.headline: Head coach Jordi Fernandez said Brown (rest) will be held out of Sunday's game against the Pacers, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown missed time in the preseason with an ankle injury and will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after posting eight points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), five assists, two rebounds and two steals across 20 minutes in Saturday's 125-121 loss to Cleveland. The rookie guard's next chance to play will come Tuesday at Boston, though he's expected to continue facing restrictions for the time being.

items.headline: Nets coach Jordi Fernandez said Brown will continue to have restrictions going forward, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: "At some point he'll be able to play more minutes, he'll be able to play back-to-backs, but it's not right now," Fernandez said. Brown had six points (2-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte, but his fantasy managers will need to exercise a lot of patience in the early going.

items.headline: Brown registered six points (2-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Making his much-awaited league debut, Brown wasn't particularly impressive in his first taste of NBA action. The rookie first-rounder dealt with an ankle injury to begin the preseason, and he'll likely remain a work in progress while working under a minutes restriction in the early stages of the season.

items.headline: Brown will remain on a minutes restriction for Wednesday's regular-season opener against Charlotte, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Coach Jordi Fernandez indicated that he wouldn't be comfortable starting a player until cleared to exceed 24 minutes, a threshold Brown has yet to reach. The rookie guard made his preseason debut Wednesday against Miami after missing Brooklyn's first three exhibition games with an ankle injury, recording 15 points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals in 18 minutes. Brown is expected to begin the season in a reserve role while gradually increasing his workload.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) recorded 15 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals across 18 minutes in Wednesday's 144-128 preseason loss to the Heat.
items.story: After missing Brooklyn's first three preseason games due to an ankle injury, Brown made an immediate impact off the bench. The rookie guard connected on two three-pointers, converted all five free-throw attempts and contributed defensively despite a limited workload. His performance provided an early glimpse of his scoring potential as he competes for backcourt minutes alongside Egor Demin and Nolan Traore.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) is available for Wednesday's preseason game against the Heat, per Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: This was the expectation after Brown missed the start of the preseason with an ankle injury. The rookie first-rounder is set to make his first appearance at the professional level Thursday as he aims to begin the year as a starter for the Nets.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Wizards, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown has yet to suit up during the preseason as he continues to work his way back from a left ankle issue. His final chance to get in an exhibition is Wednesday against the Heat, a game he's targeting for his return after going through a scrimmage Monday morning.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) will miss Thursday's preseason game against Philadelphia, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown also missed Tuesday's preseason opener against Charlotte and has been working his way back into basketball activities after suffering the injury during training camp. Brooklyn has been cautious with the rookie guard's recovery, and he remains without a firm timetable for his preseason debut.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) will miss Tuesday's preseason game against the Hornets, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown recently began taking contact in practices and continues to trend in the right direction. The rookie is expected to play at some point during the preseason, but it's unclear when. His next chance to play comes Thursday against the 76ers in another exhibition.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) has progressed to taking some contact in practice and said Sunday that he's "starting to get to full speed," Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown rolled his ankle a couple of weeks ago but is ramping up ahead of the preseason. It wouldn't be surprising if the Nets proceed with caution ahead of the regular season, though the rookie guard's first opportunity to suit up in the preseason will come Tuesday against Charlotte.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) hasn't been cleared to practice with contact and remains without a timetable for a return, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Brown suffered an ankle injury before the start of training camp, and while he's been able to get back on the court in a limited capacity, the team is taking a cautious approach to his rehab. "Yeah, as of right now they're just telling me you could get back to moving a little bit, really just trying to get the strengthening it back up," said Brown on Thursday. "I mean, I am back on the court moving. That's all I'm really worried about right now. I'm just taking it one step at a time." It remains to be seen whether Brown will be cleared in time to play in the preseason.

items.headline: General manager Sean Marks said Monday that Brown rolled his ankle last week and will ramp up at the start of training camp, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: The team "doesn't expect him to miss considerable time," though Brown's status will be worth monitoring heading into the Nets' preseason opener against the Hornets on Tuesday, Oct. 6. The rookie guard was selected with the sixth overall pick this summer and is expected to take on a sizable role early in his career. Over 21 appearances (19 starts) at Louisville in 2025-26, he averaged 18.2 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 41.0 percent from the field in 29.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Brown (rest) is primed for a significant role ahead of his rookie season in 2026-27.
items.story: The Nets chose Brown with the No. 6 overall pick in this year's draft, so they likely have big plans in mind for the 20-year-old guard right away in 2026-27. Brown, who averaged 15.0 points, 4.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.2 three-pointers per game over four Summer League appearances, is lined up to share Brooklyn's starting backcourt with Egor Demin.

items.headline: Brown (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Brown will take a seat for Brooklyn's Summer League finale. The rookie No. 6 overall pick appeared in three Las Vegas Summer League games, averaging 16.7 points, 4.0 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 22.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Brown finished with 14 points (3-15 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Thursday's 100-83 Summer League loss to Houston.
items.story: Brown recorded his lowest-scoring total in three Las Vegas Summer League appearances. He also shot less than 50.0 percent from the field and 40.0 percent from deep for the first time during that stretch. Still, it's been a mostly positive summer for the 20-year-old rookie. Although Brown is expected to have his share of struggles during his inaugural campaign, he should still receive more than enough opportunities to produce right away.

items.headline: Brown (rest) logged 16 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five assists, two rebounds, two steals and one block over 19 minutes in Tuesday's 115-83 Summer League win over the Kings.
items.story: Brown was held out of Saturday's game against the Hawks due to rest purposes but was back in action Tuesday, when he finished second on the Nets in assists and as the team's third-leading scorer behind Egor Demin (22 points) and Drake Powell (18 points). Brown was the sixth-overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, but his playing time could be inconsistent in his rookie season given the number of young guards on the Nets' roster such as Demin, Powell, Ben Saraf and Nolan Traore, as well as fifth-year pro Keon Ellis.

items.headline: Brown (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against Atlanta, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Brown impressed with a 20-point performance in his Las Vegas Summer League debut Friday, though he'll sit out the second half of the back-to-back set. The rookie's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Brown recorded 20 points (6-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, three assists, two steals and one block over 22 minutes during Friday's 91-65 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: Brown was locked in on both ends, getting whatever he wanted offensively while wreaking havoc on defense. He likely would have posted an even bigger stat line, but with the Nets comfortably ahead, he spent most of the fourth quarter on the bench.

items.headline: Brown (undisclosed) will play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Brown will make his Summer League debut after missing Brooklyn's first two games for undisclosed reasons. The 20-year-old guard is coming off an impressive season at Louisville and figures to play a sizable role for the rebuilding Nets in 2026-27. Over 21 outings last season, he averaged 18.2 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 41.0 percent from the field in 29.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Brown (undisclosed) is expected to play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against Warriors Blue, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: It's unknown why Brown won't see action in Brooklyn's first two California Classic Summer League contests, though it appears he is set to play Monday. The 2026 No. 6 overall pick appeared in 21 games for Louisville during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 18.2 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 0.1 blocks and 1.2 steals across 29.2 minutes per showing. Brown is in line for a prominent role with the Nets right out of the gate regardless of his spot on the depth chart.

items.headline: Graves recorded 13 points (5-8 FG, 3-4 3Pt) and five rebounds over 18 minutes during the Raptors' 98-93 loss to the Celtics on Wednesday.
items.story: Graves' 18 minutes were his most in a game since Oct. 28 against the Magic, and the rookie first-rounder made the most of his extended playing time in the absences of both Scottie Barnes (groin) and Kawhi Leonard (knee). Graves helped keep the Raptors in the game with four offensive rebounds in the second half, and his three three-pointers were a season high. His playing time could take a hit if Barnes is cleared to return for the second game of the Raptors' back-to-back set Thursday against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Graves contributed 11 points (5-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal over 20 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Graves delivered an efficient performance off Toronto's bench, contributing across several statistical categories despite playing just 20 minutes. The rookie's six rebounds and four assists were particularly encouraging, while his defensive contributions added to his well-rounded showing. Graves could earn additional opportunities if he continues producing at this level, making him a player to monitor in deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Graves finished Wednesday's 135-92 victory over the Bulls with five points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, three blocks and one steal in 19 minutes.
items.story: Graves scored only five points in his NBA regular-season debut, but the rookie first-rounder showed plenty of effort on both ends of the floor. He was responsible for three of the Raptors' six blocks, and four of his five rebounds came on the offensive glass. Even with Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett in the lineup, Graves should carve out a consistent role in the rotation as long as he continues to bring energy off the bench.

items.headline: Graves won't start Wednesday's matchup with Chicago.
items.story: Graves got the starting nod in Toronto's preseason finale, though he'll return to the second unit Wednesday. The rookie forward isn't guaranteed significant playing time to begin the regular season but will look to carve out a steady role as the campaign progresses.

items.headline: Graves registered nine points (4-13 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block over 23 minutes during Friday's 129-125 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Graves got the starting nod Friday due to the Raptors sitting several prominent players. The rookie first-rounder struggled from the field but showed plenty of effort by hauling in seven of his eight rebounds off the offensive glass. Graves projects to be the ninth or 10th man in Toronto's rotation this season, but he'll likely get an extended run on nights when Kawhi Leonard (rest) sits, particularly during back-to-back sets.

items.headline: Graves will start in Friday's preseason finale against the Pistons, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: The Raptors are sitting their regulars for the preseason finale, giving the rookie an opportunity to start before the season opener Wednesday against the Bulls.

items.headline: Graves totaled five points (1-7 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes during Tuesday's 148-98 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Graves made his preseason debut, having missed the opening games due to a minor groin concern. Although his production was nothing to write home about, he looked relatively confident for a rookie who had yet to see the floor. It would appear as though Graves will open the season as the ninth or tenth man in the rotation, making him a fantasy non-factor outside of dynasty formats.

items.headline: Graves (groin) is available for Tuesday's preseason game against the Knicks, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder is expected to make his first appearance at the professional level Tuesday. Graves appears primed to be part of Toronto's second unit to open the season.

items.headline: Graves (groin) practiced Monday, per Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.
items.story: Graves has yet to make his preseason debut while recovering from a groin injury, but he's making gradual progress. His status remains unknown for Tuesday's preseason game against the Knicks.

items.headline: Graves (groin) has been ruled for Saturday's preseason game against the Clippers, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Graves continues to be sidelined by a groin injury that he picked up early in training camp. His next chance to play is Tuesday against the Knicks, but the Raptors could hold the rookie first-rounder out until the team's regular-season opener against the Bulls on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Graves (groin) was limited during Sunday's practice, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Graves tweaked his groin earlier in training camp and was held out of Saturday's preseason opener against Miami. The rookie remains day-to-day, with Toronto's next preseason game coming Saturday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Graves (groin) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the Heat, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Graves didn't participate in Thursday's scrimmage due to a groin injury, and he'll also be held out of the team's preseason opener. His next chance to suit up will come in next Saturday's preseason game against the Clippers.

items.headline: Graves did not participate in the Raptors' scrimmage Thursday after tweaking his groin in practice, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Graves is competing for a reserve role entering his rookie season, and even though the injury is thought to be minor, it's currently costing him time on the court. He can be considered day-to-day for the time being.

items.headline: Graves has an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during his rookie year with the Raptors.
items.story: Provided the league eventually makes the Kawhi Leonard trade official, Graves appears set to contend primarily with Jamison Battle for the backup role at small forward in 2026-27. The rookie first-rounder showed plenty of promise on both sides of the floor over four Summer League appearances, having averaged 16.8 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 2.2 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.8 three-pointers per game while shooting 50.0 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Graves is out for Sunday's Summer League finale for rest purposes, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet reports.
items.story: Graves will get the night off to close out Summer League after a productive four appearances. Across those four games, he averaged 16.8 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.0 blocks in 27.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Graves finished with 23 points (8-16 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and two blocks over 27 minutes in Thursday's 99-90 Summer League win over Miami.
items.story: Graves has played well throughout four appearances in the Las Vegas Summer League. However, he had his best game Thursday, recording 23 points, his highest-scoring performance during his time in Las Vegas, while shooting an efficient 4-for-6 from deep. The 19-year-old has shown he can be a difference-maker on both ends of the floor. While that doesn't necessarily mean Graves will see consistent playing time with the Raptors to begin his career, it certainly doesn't hurt his chances either.

items.headline: Graves posted 13 points (5-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, six assists and four steals in 26 minutes during Monday's 94-93 Summer League win over Indiana.
items.story: Graves set the pace in steals and dimes for the Raptors on Monday. The rookie first-rounder is trying to make a case for a reserve role with Toronto ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Graves logged 22 points (9-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 13 rebounds, three steals and two blocks across 29 minutes in Friday's 83-80 Summer League overtime loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Graves delivered a well-rounded performance on both ends of the floor Friday, finishing as Toronto's leading scorer while tying the game-high mark in rebounds in his Summer League debut. The 19-year-old forward also stuffed the stat sheet on the defensive end, tying the game high in steals, and he was also one of three Raptors players to record multiple blocks.

items.headline: Graves was selected by the Raptors with the No. 19 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Graves averaged 11.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.9 blocks and 1.9 steals while shooting 41.3 percent from deep across 22.6 minutes in 35 regular-season contests with Santa Clara in 2025-26. He started four games in his only year at the collegiate level. Still, Graves did enough to be named the WCC Freshman of the Year and WCC Sixth Man of the Year. With that in mind, the 19-year-old will presumably come off the bench for a Toronto team that will be looking to contend in 2026-27, though he should hold a stable role at both forward positions.

items.headline: Anderson won't start Wednesday's game versus Boston, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: With Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) back from a one-game absence, Anderson will slide to the second unit. The veteran forward has averaged 6.2 minutes per game in six appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Anderson is starting Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Anderson will join the starting five for the first time this season due to Scottie Barnes (groin) and Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) sitting Monday. Jamison Battle and Allen Graves could also be in line for more minutes with the Raptors sporting a depleted frontcourt.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) is available for Friday's game against the Bucks, Vivek Jacob of the Raptors' official site reports.
items.story: Anderson is available off the bench for the Raptors on Friday. The veteran forward has a chance to play a larger role in the absence of Scottie Barnes (groin).

items.headline: Anderson is questionable for Friday against the Bucks due to illness.
items.story: Anderson is averaging 6.1 minutes across six appearances so far. His status won't carry much weight in fantasy hoops.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) was a full participant in Monday's practice, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Anderson missed Saturday's preseason opener against Miami due to a right knee contusion, but his return to full practice suggests the issue was minor. The veteran forward's next opportunity to play will come Saturday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the Heat, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Anderson will miss the Raptors' preseason opener after sitting out Thursday's scrimmage with a right knee contusion. His next opportunity to suit up in the preseason will come next Saturday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Anderson sat out of Thursday's scrimmage due to a bruised right knee, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Anderson's knee injury is considered to be minor, but his availability will be worth monitoring heading into Toronto's first preseason matchup against Miami on Saturday. The 33-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Raptors in July and is competing for a spot in the frontcourt rotation heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Anderson agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Anderson will join Toronto with the hope of providing depth in the frontcourt. He's bounced around to five different teams over his last two seasons, most recently suiting up for Memphis, Minnesota and Utah a year ago. Anderson averaged 6.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 steals in 43 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Anderson contributed two points (1-3 FG) and three assists across eight minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to the Spurs in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Anderson averaged 19.1 minutes per game across 19 regular-season outings with the Timberwolves. However, the veteran forward was a healthy DNP in four of Minnesota's last seven postseason games, and his eight minutes of playing time Friday all took place during the fourth quarter in garbage time. Anderson suited up for the Grizzlies, Jazz and Timberwolves during the 2025-26 season and enters the offseason as an unrestricted free agent.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) isn't listed on the Timberwolves' injury report for Monday's Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs.
items.story: Anderson missed Thursday's Game 6 win over the Nuggets in the first round due to an illness, though he's set to return to action Monday. Over five first-round appearances, he averaged 0.8 points and 1.6 rebounds in 7.0 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) is out for Thursday's Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs against Denver, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
items.story: Anderson was added to the injury report a few hours before tipoff due to an illness, and the team has since reported that he won't be able to suit up. Terrence Shannon and Naz Reid could pick up a few extra minutes in Anderson's absence.

items.headline: Anderson is questionable for Thursday's Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs against the Nuggets due to illness.
items.story: Anderson will presumably be a true game-time call after being added to the Minnesota injury report a few hours before tipoff. The team should have a better idea of his availability after he goes through warmups.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Saturday's Game 1 against the Nuggets.
items.story: Anderson sat out the Timberwolves' final regular-season game for right knee injury maintenance, but he'll get back out there Saturday. In 19 games with Minnesota this season, Anderson averaged 4.6 points, 3.3 assists and 3.7 rebounds.

items.headline: Anderson won't play Sunday against the Pelicans due to right knee injury maintenance.
items.story: Anderson is one of nine players who won't suit up for Minnesota in the final game of the regular season. The veteran forward averaged 6.2 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game in 43 regular-season contests for the Grizzlies, Jazz and Timberwolves throughout the campaign.

items.headline: Anderson posted 17 points (7-12 FG, 3-5 FT), six rebounds, nine assists and two steals across 33 minutes during Friday's 136-132 win over Houston.
items.story: Anderson filled in with a solid line in place of Julius Randle (hand), who will likely remain out for the team's regular-season finale against the Pelicans. Anderson's participation since joining the Timberwolves has been limited, but he provides critical minutes with the second unit and can help boost the team's rebounding when Randle or Rudy Gobert sits.

items.headline: Anderson is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: The Timberwolves will rest the majority of their regular starters for this game against Orlando, meaning Anderson will be in line for an expanded role in the frontcourt. Anderson is averaging 9.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game through three starts this season.

items.headline: Anderson closed Friday's 115-103 loss to the 76ers with six points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and five assists in 14 minutes.
items.story: Anderson saw just 14 minutes in the loss and was unable to repeat his defensive heroics from the night before. As expected, his recent uptick in production was nothing more than an outlier. Other than being a potential streaming consideration, Anderson holds no real fantasy value.

items.headline: Anderson had three points (1-6 FG, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 110-108 overtime victory over the Rockets.
items.story: Although Anderson saw a considerable workload, he wasn't able to translate it to much fantasy appeal. He's been more involved over his last three games with 21.3 minutes per contest, but he's averaging just 4.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists.

items.headline: Anderson amassed seven points (3-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one block across 25 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Anderson logged 25 minutes off the bench, the most he has played since rejoining the Timberwolves. With Naz Reid forced to the locker room due to an ankle injury, albeit temporarily, Anderson was afforded a few extra minutes. If Reid is to miss any amount of time moving forward, Anderson could be on the radar as a potential streaming candidate given his ability to chip in across multiple categories.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is available for Tuesday's game against the Lakers, per Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast'.
items.story: Anderson is ready to return from a one-game absence with a right knee injury. The veteran forward has made two appearances during his second stint with the Timberwolves, and he should help fill out some reserve minutes in the frontcourt Tuesday.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Anderson is in danger of missing a second straight game while dealing with a right knee issue. He'll presumably be re-evaluated Tuesday morning at which point the team could have a better idea of his availability in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Anderson drew the questionable tag due to right knee soreness. The veteran forward will sit out Saturday's home game and aim to return for Tuesday's road tilt against the Lakers. Jaylen Clark and Terrence Shannon are in line for more minutes off the bench in Anderson's absence.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Anderson is in jeopardy of missing Saturday's contest due to right knee soreness. The veteran forward has logged 14 and 15 minutes through two games with Minnesota, and his absence would free up minutes for the likes of Terrence Shannon and Jaylen Clark.

items.headline: Anderson recorded two points (2-2 FT) and one rebound across 14 minutes Tuesday in the Timberwolves' 117-110 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: After finalizing a one-year deal with the Timberwolves on Monday upon receiving a buyout from the Grizzlies, Anderson entered the rotation Tuesday to kick off his second stint with Minnesota. So long as the Timberwolves have all of Rudy Gobert, Julius Randle and Naz Reid available, the 32-year-old forward isn't expected to see his role expand dramatically and will likely struggle to attain fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Anderson signed a contract with Minnesota on Monday, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
items.story: Anderson recently secured a buyout with the Grizzlies and will join the Timberwolves ahead of their game Tuesday against Memphis. Anderson will be eligible for the postseason as well. The veteran will likely carve out a decent role with the second unit in Minnesota.

items.headline: Anderson has been ruled out for Friday's game in Dallas due to personal reasons.
items.story: The Grizzlies are no longer listing Anderson's right knee tendinitis on the injury report, so it seems like his absence from Friday's game will be strictly due to personal reasons. It's unclear exactly what Anderson is dealing with, but for now, he should be considered questionable for Sunday's game in Indiana.  Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson will continue to pick up the slack in Anderson's absence.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Anderson will miss a third straight game due to tendinitis in his right knee. With several other key frontcourt players sidelined, Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson will likely handle most of the frontcourt minutes Wednesday night. Anderson's next chance to play will come Friday at Dallas.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Anderson is in danger of missing a third straight game due to right knee patellar tendinitis. If the veteran forward is ultimately ruled out, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Taylor Hendricks would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Anderson missed Saturday's contest and had been listed as doubtful due to right knee soreness, so his absence doesn't come as much of a surprise. With the veteran forward inactive, Taylor Hendricks is likely to draw the start at center, while Olivier-Maxence Prosper and GG Jackson could see increased minutes off the bench. Anderson's next chance to play will come Wednesday against Golden State.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) is doubtful to play Monday against the Kings.
items.story: Anderson is on track to miss his second straight game Monday, which will open up minutes for Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Taylor Hendricks. Check back closer to Monday's tip for official word on Anderson's status.

items.headline: Anderson (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Anderson will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to right knee soreness, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against the Kings. With the veteran forward sidelined, Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Anderson is questionable for Saturday's game against the Heat due to right knee soreness.
items.story: After posting 10 points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound and one steal across 18 minutes in Friday's win over Utah, Anderson is in danger of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set. If the veteran forward is ultimately ruled out, Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Anderson finished Friday's 123-114 victory over Utah with 10 points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound and one steal across 18 minutes.
items.story: Anderson was a negligible part of the rotation in Utah, but he's been much more involved in Memphis, averaging 22.3 minutes per game to go with 9.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks per contest. If Anderson is able to flirt with 20 minutes a night with the Grizzlies, he might be able to churn out some low-end value in deep leagues.

items.headline: Anderson won't start against the Jazz on Friday.
items.story: Lawson Lovering will get the starting nod Friday, pushing Anderson to the second unit. Over three appearances (all starts) with the Grizzlies this season, the veteran forward has averaged 9.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.0 combined steals-plus-blocks and 1.0 assists in 23.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Anderson registered 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals in 27 minutes during Saturday's 122-115 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The Grizzlies will try to see what sticks in the frontcourt as they move forward without Jaren Jackson's services. Santi Aldama's (knee) eventual return will likely shift the narrative, but Anderson is one of a few options that the team is utilizing under the basket. Anderson was somewhat effective, but he ceded several minutes to Olivier-Maxence Prosper, who is making his presence known in his third pro season.

items.headline: Anderson is starting against the Trail Blazers on Saturday.
items.story: The Grizzlies don't have a lot of frontcourt players available, so Anderson will be their nominal center. The veteran will make his Memphis debut Saturday after not playing in Friday's loss to the Trail Blazers. Anderson averaged 7.1 points, 3.3 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game in 20 contests off the bench with the Jazz before the trade to Memphis.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) is available for Saturday's game against Portland.
items.story: Anderson is all set to make his Memphis debut after missing the front end of this back-to-back set. The Grizzlies are very thin in the frontcourt, and Anderson has a chance to carve out a sizable role.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Anderson was initially slated to play in Friday's contest, but he has since gone under the weather and will have to wait at least one more game to make his Grizzlies debut. That opportunity will come in Saturday's rematch against Portland.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) is questionable for Friday's game versus Portland.
items.story: Anderson wasn't on the morning injury report, but the Grizzlies have since added him, which doesn't bode well for his status. If Anderson is unable to debut Friday, that could open things up for Taylor Hendricks.

items.headline: Anderson is good to go for Friday's game versus Portland.
items.story: Anderson was traded from the Jazz to the Grizzlies on Tuesday and has the green light to suit up. Anderson will have a lot of familiarity with his former team, and it will be interesting to see what type of role he will play.

items.headline: Anderson (illness/recently traded) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Anderson was traded by the Jazz on Tuesday to the Grizzlies for a return that centered around Jaren Jackson. Anderson spent four years of his NBA career in Memphis, and assuming he isn't shipped again ahead of Thursday's deadline, his next chance to play for the Grizzlies would be Friday against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: The Jazz traded Anderson (illness), Walter Clayton, Taylor Hendricks, Georges Niang (foot) and three first-round picks to the Grizzlies on Tuesday in exchange for Jaren Jackson, John Konchar (neck), Jock Landale and Vince Williams, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Provided the veteran forward stays put, it's set to be his second stint with the Grizzlies. Anderson offers some depth to a Memphis frontcourt that's now thinned out, though his role going forward remains unclear. Over his last 11 outings, Anderson has averaged 7.5 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 0.9 steals in 21.8 minutes per game. He can be considered questionable for Wednesday's game in Sacramento while the trade finalizes.

items.headline: Anderson (illness) is questionable for Tuesday's game versus Indiana, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Anderson was a late addition to the injury report, presumably after waking up under the weather. Additionally, Kevin Love (illness) is now doubtful for this contest. With this news, more minutes could be open for Kyle Filipowski and Taylor Hendricks.

items.headline: Anderson totaled 12 points (4-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Tuesday's 115-103 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Anderson continues to occupy a plug-and-play role of sorts, as he's seen at least 20 minutes in half of his 18 appearances in 2025-26 while sitting out Utah's other 29 games altogether. Although his availability is unreliable, the veteran forward has averaged an efficient 8.2 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 22.0 minutes per game over his last nine appearances.

items.headline: Anderson supplied 12 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-6 FT), six rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 26 minutes during Thursday's 144-122 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Anderson has been in and out of the rotation recently, but with Lauri Markkanen (illness) sidelined and Utah getting blown out Thursday night, the veteran handled more usage than usual. Anderson has played at least 24 minutes six times this season, averaging 10.5 minutes, 5.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.5 steals and 0.8 blocks in 26.3 minutes per game. However, it's been impossible to nail down what Utah's rotation will look like on a given night, with Anderson drawing dozens of healthy DNPs.

items.headline: Anderson logged two points (1-5 FG), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Thursday's 116-114 victory over Dallas.
items.story: With Ace Bailey and Jusuf Nurkic getting the night off for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Anderson made a rare appearance off the bench for Utah. He usually doesn't see the floor when the team is at full strength, however, so he can be ignored in standard formats for the time being.

items.headline: Anderson produced 22 points (8-10 FG, 6-7 FT), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals over 32 minutes during Thursday's 118-101 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: With the Jazz's top two scorers, Keyonte George (illness) and Lauri Markkanen (knee), both sidelined, Anderson took on a larger scoring role and led the team with 22 points in Thursday's loss to the Clippers. The 32-year-old forward hasn't been a consistent piece of Utah's rotation, but he played his most minutes all season and was impactful on both ends of the court. He's averaging 8.2 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.5 steals in 19.3 minutes per game across 10 contests.

items.headline: Whitmore was assigned to the Grand Rapids Gold on Thursday.
items.story: With Whitmore on a two-way contract and not locked into Denver's rotation, this assignment sends him to the Nuggets' G League affiliate for additional playing time. His NBA opportunities should remain sporadic unless injuries or roster needs create a clearer path to minutes.

items.headline: Whitmore provided four points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal over 11 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime win over New Orleans.
items.story: Whitmore made his debut for the Nuggets, logging 11 minutes off the bench. Despite some upside, particularly on the offensive end, Whitmore's career has been a struggle so far. Don't expect him to play a consistent role for his new team.

items.headline: Whitmore posted 17 points (7-13 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-5 FT), four rebounds and a steal over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 122-110 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Whitmore made the most of an extended run off the bench. The 22-year-old signed a two-way deal with Denver in September after Cleveland waived him following a five-team trade. With DeMar DeRozan ahead of him on the depth chart, Whitmore faces a fight for minutes, and his deal limits him to 50 regular-season games.

items.headline: Whitmore logged 14 points (4-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 6-7 FT) and one rebound over 15 minutes in Tuesday's 117-106 preseason win over the Jazz.
items.story: Whitmore begins the 2026-27 season vying for a rotation spot with his third team in four years after beginning his NBA tenure as a first-round pick by the Rockets in 2023. Consistent usage is far from certain, with Cameron Johnson, DeMar DeRozan and Julian Strawther all vying for time at the wing, but an encouraging training camp points to a chance to move up the depth chart.

items.headline: Whitmore made a strong impression on head coach David Adelman during the Nuggets' first day of training camp, standing out alongside Aaron Gordon, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: The 22-year-old has received plenty of praise since joining Denver on a two-way contract, and a strong camp could help him push for a spot in the rotation. Whitmore averaged 9.2 points and 2.8 rebounds in 16.9 minutes across 21 regular-season appearances for Washington last season and is looking to take advantage of a fresh start in Denver.

items.headline: Whitmore agreed to a two-way contract with the Nuggets on Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Whitmore, who is entering his fourth NBA season, holds career averages of 10.5 points and 3.3 rebounds across 119 games. He figures to spend a lot of team with Denver's G League affiliate, but the 2023 first-round pick does have the talent to break into the Nuggets' rotation if he finds his footing.

items.headline: Whitmore (shoulder) was waived by the Cavaliers on Friday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: Whitmore was traded to Cleveland on Aug. 19 as part of the multi-team deal that sent Peyton Watson (hamstring) to the Cavaliers. However, Whitmore will now have to explore other opportunities if he clears waivers. The 22-year-old forward's 2025-26 campaign with the Wizards was cut short due to deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder, and he finished the season with averages of 9.2 points and 2.8 rebounds in 16.9 minutes per tilt across 21 regular-season outings.

items.headline: Whitmore (shoulder) was dealt to Cleveland on Wednesday as a part of a multi-team trade between the Cavaliers, Wizards, Nuggets and Clippers involving Peyton Watson (hamstring), Max Strus, Tre Mann and picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After being drafted by the Rockets in the first round of the 2023 NBA Draft, Whitmore will now suit up for his third NBA team. The 22-year-old had his best campaign as a rookie, when he averaged a career-high 12.3 points and 3.8 rebounds across 18.7 minutes in 47 regular-season games. Since then, his production has decreased. Whitmore will have a fresh start in Cleveland, though he is likely not close to securing a consistent spot in the rotation.

items.headline: Whitmore has begun the recovery process for a diagnosed venous condition, and he will miss the remainder of the 2025-26 season.
items.story: A venous condition is any disorder that affects the veins, but we'll likely have more clarity on precisely what Whitmore is dealing with at a later date. Whitmore will end his 2025-26 season with averages of 9.2 points and 2.8 rebounds per game on 45.6/28.6/74.2 shooting splits.

items.headline: Whitmore is out indefinitely due to deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Tuesday.
items.story: Whitmore has been dealing with right shoulder soreness, but he's since been diagnosed with a more significant issue. It's too early to gauge how long he might be sidelined, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him back anytime soon. Whitmore's minutes should be picked up by the likes of Corey Kispert, Justin Champagnie and Will Riley.

items.headline: Whitmore (shoulder) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Whitmore will be unavailable for a third straight game due to right shoulder soreness, though he hasn't been a part of the rotation of late anyway. His next chance to suit up will come Friday against Toronto.

items.headline: Whitmore (shoulder) is out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Whitmore is set to be out for consecutive outings due to right shoulder soreness. With the 2023 first-rounder sidelined, Will Riley could see just enough playing time to warrant streaming consideration in deep fantasy leagues. Whitmore can be considered day-to-day ahead of Tuesday's matchup with the Hornets.

items.headline: Whitmore (shoulder) will not play Saturday against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Whitmore wasn't able to shake his questionable tag for this contest. His next chance to play comes Sunday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Whitmore is questionable for Saturday's game against Memphis due to right shoulder soreness.
items.story: Whitmore is at risk of missing Saturday's contest due to a shoulder injury. If available, Whitmore could see an expanded role because of the absences of Bilal Coulibaly (ankle) and Corey Kispert (thumb).
