items.story: Harkless, who is in the final year of his two-way contract with the Jazz, figures to be a key role player for the Salt Lake City Stars in 2025-26. During the 2024-25 G League regular season, Harkless averaged 26.9 points, 5.3 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.3 steals per game while being awarded the G League's Most Improved Player Award.

items.headline: Harkless (groin) is out for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Harkless is one of several Utah players who will end the 2024-25 season on the sidelines. He didn't have a big role in the rotation throughout the campaign, though, averaging just 3.2 points and 2.1 boards per game in 10 appearances off the bench. Harkless also spent time with the Salt Lake City Stars of the G League, though the last time he suited up for a game, either in the NBA or the G League, was on March 1.

items.headline: Harkless (groin) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Harkless hasn't played in a game at the G League or NBA level since March 14 due to a left groin strain. His last chance to suit up this season will come Sunday against Minnesota.

items.headline: Harkless (groin) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Portland.
items.story: Harkless hasn't suited up at the G League or NBA level since March 14 due to the left groin strain. The two-way player's next chance to feature will come Friday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Harkless (groin) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Memphis, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Harkless hasn't played in a game at the G League or NBA level since March 14 due to the groin strain. The two-way combo guard's next chance to suit up with the Jazz will come Thursday against the Rockets, though he'll likely make his return with the G League's Salt Lake City Stars, as he hasn't played for the Jazz since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Harkless (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: A two-way player, Harkless hasn't seen action for the Jazz or the G League's Salt Lake City Stars since March 14 due to a groin strain.

items.headline: The Jazz are recalling Harkless from the G League's Salt Lake City Stars on Wednesday, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: With Lauri Markkanen out with a back issue, Utah has called up Harkless as a reserve option ahead of Wednesday's game against the Warriors. The 25-year-old has logged 15.0 minutes per game over nine appearances with the Jazz this year, so he may get some court time against Golden State in his first game back with the parent club.

items.headline: Harkless racked up 11 points (4-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds, three steals, two assists and one block in 22 minutes during Saturday's 125-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Harkless recorded career highs in both points and steals Saturday, leading both teams with a game-high three swipes. The 24-year-old latched on with the Jazz via a two-way contract in late December and has played in seven consecutive outings, during which he has averaged 4.3 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 16.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Harkless agreed to a two-way contract with the Jazz on Tuesday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Harkless' play with San Diego Clippers attracted the attention of the Jazz, who will award him their final two-way slot after he averaged 16.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.4 steals and 1.9 triples in 27.1 minutes per game over his 18 G League appearances. Though the 6-foot-3 guard will be eligible to move between the Jazz and their affiliate -- the Salt Lake City Stars -- going forward, the bulk of his playing time will likely continue to come in the G League.

items.headline: Cenac supplied six points (2-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and one block over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 105-101 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Cenac has earned increasingly meaningful minutes, progressing from seven against Dallas to 12 against Orlando before Wednesday's career-high workload. Coach Joe Mazzulla praised his defensive versatility against Denver's stars, suggesting growing trust in the rookie. However, Boston's crowded frontcourt still makes consistent fantasy production unlikely.

items.headline: Boston recalled Cenac from the G League's Maine Celtics on Saturday.
items.story: Cenac has been gaining experience at the G League level during his rookie season and is expected to remain a depth option for Boston at least in the next few games. The center, who has made three NBA regular-season appearances off the bench, might eventually be sent to Maine once again, where he could continue to rack up minutes while producing via points and rebounds.

items.headline: Boston recalled Cenac from the G League's Maine Celtics on Monday.
items.story: Cenac has rejoined the NBA Celtics ahead of Tuesday's meeting with the 76ers, in which he's expected to serve as a bench option and is not guaranteed to see minutes of play. The young center is coming off a pair of appearances at the G League level, averaging 12.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.0 blocks per contest in that span.

items.headline: The Celtics assigned Cenac to the G League's Maine Celtics before recalling him Wednesday.
items.story: Cenac joined the G League Celtics for practice Wednesday but will be available for the parent club's game against the Bucks. However, the rookie big man isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

items.headline: Cenac is not in the starting lineup for Tuesday's season opener against Detroit, per Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston.
items.story: This is an expected shift in role after Cenac started Boston's preseason finale. With the Celtics' frontcourt healthy, the rookie big man is not likely to see meaningful playing time.

items.headline: Cenac will start Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: With all of Boston's regulars resting, the rookie will make his first career NBA start, albeit in preseason action. He's been off to a slow start during the preseason, but Cenac will have a major opportunity during the final exhibition.

items.headline: Cenac received high praise from teammate Neemias Queta on Monday, with the veteran center saying the rookie has the potential to become a "juggernaut" in the NBA, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Queta highlighted Cenac's combination of size, mobility and ability to defend multiple positions, adding that "the sky is the limit" for the 19-year-old. Cenac showed flashes of that defensive versatility during Summer League, but with Queta, Mitchell Robinson and Luka Garza among the experienced options in Boston's frontcourt, the No. 27 overall pick may have to earn his opportunities during his rookie campaign.

items.headline: Cenac appears to be buried on the Celtics' depth chart ahead of his rookie season.
items.story: Boston signed Mitchell Robinson in free agency and still has Neemias Queta in the fold at center as well, likely leaving Cenac to fight for scraps with Luka Garza off the bench in 2026-27. Much like two-way player Amari Williams, Cenac's clearest path to steady action appears to be with the G League's Maine Celtics while the parent club is healthy.

items.headline: Cenac (rest) has been ruled out for Saturday's Summer League game against the Magic, John Karalis of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Cenac is healthy, but he'll sit out the Celtics' final Summer League tilt for rest purposes. The 2026 first-rounder averaged 10.5 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.8 blocks and 1.0 assists in 23.3 minutes per contest across four appearances in Las Vegas. Cenac may struggle to carve out consistent playing time during the regular season due to Neemias Queta still being in the fold and Boston adding Mitchell Robinson in free agency.

items.headline: Cenac contributed 10 points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, two blocks and one assist across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 82-76 Summer League win over the Kings.
items.story: Cenac came off the bench and dominated the glass, pulling down a game-high 12 rebounds as part of a double-double effort. The rookie big man has scored in double figures in three of his four Summer League appearances, with Wednesday marking his second double-double. Playing time could be difficult to come by during the 2026-27 campaign with Mitchell Robinson and Neemias Queta anchoring the center rotation, but Cenac is viewed as a promising long-term prospect.

items.headline: Cenac contributed 16 points (6-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, four blocks and two assists across 20 minutes in Monday's 102-90 Summer League loss to the Hawks.
items.story: After scoring two points off the bench on 1-of-7 shooting from the field in Sunday's win over the Hornets, Cenac bounced back Monday. The big man entered the first unit in the second half of this back-to-back set and led the Celtics in scoring, finishing in double figures for the second time across three Summer League outings. He also led Boston in blocks, swatting four shots for the second time this summer.

items.headline: Sensabaugh recorded 18 points (6-13 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 26 minutes during Friday's 111-101 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Sensabaugh bounced back from a quiet night against the Lakers and gave Utah another scoring punch off the bench, finishing tied for second on the team in points. His outside stroke was on again after Tuesday's 40-point eruption. He's hitting better than 40 percent from deep on the season

items.headline: Sensabaugh provided 40 points (16-21 FG, 8-11 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds, five assists and one block over 35 minutes during Tuesday's 132-107 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Sensabaugh exploded off the bench for a season high, more than doubling his previous best of the campaign and torching the Clippers from beyond the arc. His minutes were sporadic early in the season, but his role has grown over the past week with Lauri Markkanen (hand) out.

items.headline: Sensabaugh provided 14 points (7-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 30 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Sensabaugh logged a season-high 30 minutes and provided a spark off the bench, leading the second unit in scoring. The 23-year-old has played at least 23 minutes in three straight games, averaging 13.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.7 blocks in 26.7 minutes per tilt over that span. He'll likely see increased burn for as long as Jaren Jackson (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (hand) are sidelined.

items.headline: Sensabaugh produced 19 points (6-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 23 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 123-108 loss to Orlando.
items.story: The fourth-year wing finished second on the Jazz in scoring behind Darryn Peterson's 22 points, and Sensabaugh's 19 points were a season high. The performance ended a streak of five straight games in which he'd scored in single digits, and he's struggling to earn the same kind of court time he did during a breakout 2025-26. Sensabaugh's 23 minutes Wednesday were also a season high, but still less than the 23.5 minutes he averaged over 75 contests last season.

items.headline: Sensabaugh recorded 16 points (5-9 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 18 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Sensabaugh helped pick up the slack left behind by Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Wednesday. Sensabaugh should continue playing the backup role at shooting guard, provided rookie first-rounder Darryn Peterson hangs onto a starting job.

items.headline: Sensabaugh closed with seven points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist across 17 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The 22-year-old grabbed a season-high six rebounds during Utah's second loss of the 2026-27 campaign. Sensabaugh will continue operating in a reserve role behind Ace Bailey and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Sensabaugh closed with 11 points (3-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one steal, two rebounds and two assists across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Sensabaugh was solid off the bench Monday. He's ticketed for a reserve role to begin this year after spending some time as a starter for an injury-plagued Jazz team late last season.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (hip) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's preseason game against San Antonio.
items.story: Sensabaugh sat out Utah's first two preseason games due to a left hip injury, but his omission from the injury report paves the way for the Ohio State product to return to action Monday. In 75 games (22 starts) last season, he averaged 14.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 23.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (hip) won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Nuggets.
items.story: A left hip injury will keep Sensabaugh off the floor for the rematch with Denver. The Jazz will likely be cautious with the 22-year-old, so it's reasonable to believe he could also miss Monday's exhibition versus the Spurs.

items.headline: Sensabaugh won't play in Sunday's preseason opener against the Nuggets due to a left hip injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Sensabaugh's absence from Sunday's exhibition seems largely precautionary. His next chance to play will come Tuesday in a rematch with the Nuggets.

items.headline: Sensabaugh closed with 15 points (4-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 13 minutes during Sunday's 131-107 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sensabaugh started 12 of his last 14 games to close out a losing season for the Jazz, and he'll likely be battling for reserve minutes during training camp next fall. The third-year forward performed fairly well as a scorer, averaging 14.9 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 2.2 three-pointers in 23.5 minutes per tilt through 75 games this season.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (rest) isn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Sensabaugh took a seat for Friday's win over Memphis but will return to action in Utah's regular-season finale. He has started each of his last seven appearances, during which he has averaged 22.4 points, 4.4 assists and 3.7 rebounds in 31.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sensabaugh has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies for rest purposes.
items.story: Sensabaugh will get the night off after appearing in seven straight matchups for the Jazz. John Konchar figures to be the favorite to start in Sensabaugh's place Friday evening.

items.headline: Sensabaugh amassed 34 points (11-19 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 43 minutes during Sunday's 146-111 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Sensabaugh has been outstanding for the Jazz in the second half of the season, and he has taken advantage of the bigger role he's had since the All-Star break to post impressive numbers across the board. This was the fourth time he reached the 20-point mark in his last five appearances, and he's averaging an impressive line of 25.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game in his 11 starts since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Sensabaugh had 20 points (7-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one block across 33 minutes during Friday's 140-106 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: The Jazz might be struggling collectively, but Sensabaugh is one of several young players who have been putting up strong numbers to end the season. The third-year forward has started all but one of his last 11 appearances dating back to March 9, and he's reached the 20-point threshold nine times over that stretch. Sensabaugh has seen his numbers progress with each passing season, and he's on pace to post career-best numbers in points, assists and steals per game.

items.headline: Sensabaugh contributed 28 points (11-18 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 130-117 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: The 28 points led the Jazz on the night. Sensabaugh has scored more than 20 points in eight of 10 games since moving back into the starting five March 9, averaging 25.3 points, 3.8 boards, 3.6 threes, 3.0 assists and 1.0 steals over that span while shooting 53.7 percent from the floor and 47.4 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Sensabaugh ended with 26 points (11-21 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 33 minutes during Saturday's 134-109 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Sensabaugh has made the most of his opportunities during Utah's rash of injuries despite missing a few games over the past couple of weeks. The Ohio State product has logged seven starts this month despite spending most of the season stuck on the depth chart behind Lauri Markkanen (hip) and Ace Bailey. The short-handed situation has significantly heightened Sensabaugh's profile, and he'll likely keep up the production as the season comes to a close.

items.headline: Sensabaugh will start in Friday's game versus Denver.
items.story: Sensabaugh didn't start in his previous appearance before he got the night off for Wednesday's 133-110 loss to the Wizards. However, he will be back with the first five, sending John Konchar to the bench. Sensabaugh has started 15 times during the campaign, averaging 19.0 points, 3.7 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.7 steals in those appearances.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (rest) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Friday's game in Denver, Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City reports.
items.story: Sensabaugh is set to return from a rest day, which could translate to fewer minutes for John Konchar and Bez Mbeng. Through 10 games in March, Sensabaugh has averaged 21.4 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 2.9 triples and 1.0 steals per game on 47/37/85 shooting splits.

items.headline: Sensabaugh will sit out Wednesday's game against the Wizards for rest purposes.
items.story: This looks to be a scheduled night off for Sensabaugh, who is averaging 21.4 points on 46.7 percent shooting from the field over his last 10 appearances. Expect John Konchar, Bez Mbeng and Blake Hinson to see more run in Sensabaugh's absence.

items.headline: Sensabaugh accumulated 24 points (9-19 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 31 minutes off the bench during Monday's 143-127 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Back on the second unit after missing the prior two games with an illness, Sensabaugh couldn't find his rhythm from long distance but otherwise delivered his usual production. The third-year wing has scored more than 20 points in six straight appearances, averaging 28.0 points, 3.7 boards, 3.7 threes, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals in 29.8 minutes over that stretch while shooting 53.4 percent from the floor and 43.1 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (illness) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Monday's meeting with the Raptors.
items.story: Sensabaugh will be back in action following a two-game layoff, which could shift Elijah Harkless back to the second unit, while Cody Williams' usage could dip a bit. Through nine games in March, Sensabaugh has put up averages of 21.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 3.1 triples and 1.0 steals per contest.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: This will be Sensabaugh's second straight game on the sidelines, and six other Utah players will join him on the inactive list Saturday. Ace Bailey and Cody Williams will get all the shots they can handle with Sensabaugh, Lauri Markkanen (hip) and Keyonte George (hamstring) all out.

items.headline: Sensabaugh (illness) is out for Thursday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Sensabaugh will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set after erupting for 41 points (17-31 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 37 minutes in Wednesday's 147-111 loss to Minnesota. Ace Bailey and Elijah Harkless could see larger roles due to Sensabaugh's absence.

items.headline: Sensabaugh generated 41 points (17-31 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 37 minutes of Wednesday's 147-111 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: The blowout loss didn't prevent Sensabaugh from a big points total, as the score-first wing hit the 40-point milestone for the second time in his career (both this season). Sensabaugh accounted for nearly 37 percent of Utah's points and exactly one-third of the team's shot attempts. With several key contributors sidelined due to injury, Sensabaugh looks to have the ultimate green light. In his last 14 games, Sensabaugh is averaging 20.2 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.1 assists over 26.5 minutes.

items.headline: Sensabaugh contributed 22 points (9-17 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and one steal in 23 minutes during Sunday's 116-111 loss to the Kings.
items.story: The third-year wing has started four straight games and scored more than 20 points in all of them, averaging 25.8 points, 4.3 threes, 3.3 boards, 2.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks during that stretch in just 27.8 minutes a contest. Sensabaugh figures to continue handling a bigger role as long as Lauri Markkanen (hip), Ace Bailey (concussion) and other key members of the Jazz rotation remain sidelined.

items.headline: Sensabaugh recorded 31 points (12-19 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 29 minutes during Friday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Making his third straight start, Sensabaugh produced his best offensive performance since he erupted for 43 points against the Bulls on Jan. 14. The third-year wing has been very impressive at times this season when he's gotten a look with the first unit, and in 13 starts he's averaged 17.1 points, 3.7 boards, 2.5 threes and 2.4 assists in 30.1 minutes.

items.headline: Sensabaugh notched 29 points (9-19 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 134-117 loss to New York.
items.story: Sensabaugh started for a second straight game and surpassed the 20-point mark again, as he was coming off a 21-point effort in the win over the Warriors on Monday. Sensabaugh's role often defines his numbers, but he's showcased his scoring ability coming off the bench. The former Florida standout has scored in double digits in all but two of his last nine outings while starting just twice in that span. During that eight-game stretch, Sensabaugh is averaging 16.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists per contest.

items.headline: Sensabaugh finished Monday's 119-116 victory over the Warriors with 21 points (7-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 29 minutes.
items.story: Sensabaugh has turned in some massive totals this season, and his extra usage Monday earned him his third-highest total of the season while playing with the first unit. Ace Bailey and Isaiah Collier were sidelined for this contest due to illness, and Lauri Markkanen (hip) remains out indefinitely, so Sensabaugh's short-term upside is peaking.

items.headline: Sensabaugh will start Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: With Ace Bailey (illness) sidelined and Oscar Tshiebwe moving to the second unit, John Konchar and Sensabaugh will enter the starting five. As a starter this season (10 games), the 22-year-old forward has averaged 14.1 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 30.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sensabaugh finished Thursday's 129-118 loss to New Orleans with 20 points (7-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 25 minutes.
items.story: With several absences throughout the Jazz's roster, Sensabaugh was able to put in 25 minutes of work with the second unit. The third-year pro kept the good vibes going after posting 26 points in the loss against Houston, and his recent results have been equally impressive. He's averaged 17.6 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.9 assists over the past nine games.

items.headline: Sensabaugh logged 26 points (10-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block in 32 minutes off the bench during Monday's 125-105 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: The third-year wing played only 19 minutes Friday in Memphis and managed just nine points, but when he isn't subjected to load management by a tanking Utah squad, Sensabaugh has been one of the team's most consistent offensive producers. He's scored in double digits in 10 of the last 13 games (one start), averaging 16.8 points, 2.8 boards, 2.6 threes and 1.7 assists in 25.8 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Sensabaugh will not start against the Grizzlies on Friday.
items.story: Sensabaugh got the starting nod in Utah's final outing before the All-Star break but will slide to the second unit in favor of John Konchar on Friday. Over six outings off the bench this month, Sensabaugh has averaged 13.2 points and 2.7 rebounds in 24.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Champagnie closed with 20 points (8-14 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 0-2 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes during Thursday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Champagnie provided San Antonio with a much-needed perimeter threat, scoring 20 points while connecting on four three-pointers in his fourth start of the season due to the absence of Dylan Harper (groin). The 29-minute workload was encouraging, but Champagnie's fantasy production still depends heavily on his shooting efficiency. Champagnie has managed to produce regardless of whether he starts or not, scoring in double digits in five of his last seven appearances while shooting 41.7 percent from deep in that span.

items.headline: Champagnie will start in Thursday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: With Dylan Harper (groin) sidelined, Champagnie will return to the starting lineup for Thursday's meeting with the Clippers. The 25-year-old has started three games during the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 9.0 points, 2.7 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.3 steals over 28.7 minutes per outing in those appearances.

items.headline: Champagnie totaled 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-9 3Pt), six rebounds and one block in 30 minutes during Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Champagne provided a scoring punch off the bench, bouncing back from a quiet outing in Utah over the weekend. He has been one of San Antonio's most reliable backups all season, connecting on nearly 42 percent of his three-point attempts. His shooting gives the Spurs a valuable weapon in the second unit, and he could slide into the starting lineup again if Dylan Harper (groin) misses extended time.

items.headline: Champagnie will return to the second unit for Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: De'Aaron Fox (hip) is back after a one-game absence, so Champagnie will return to a reserve role. In 11 games off the bench this season, Champagnie is averaging 9.7 points and 2.6 triples per contest.

items.headline: Champagnie is listed in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Champagnie will earn his third start of the season after De'Aaron Fox was ruled out due to a hip injury. Champagnie averaged 11.5 points, 1.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 3.0 three-pointers in his previous two starts.

items.headline: Champagnie won't start Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Devin Vassell (adductor) is back from a two-game absence, pushing Champagnie to the second unit Friday. Over four appearances off the bench in November, the 25-year-old wing has averaged 7.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.0 triples across 21.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Champagnie will start Monday's game against the Suns, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: With Devin Vassell (groin) unavailable, Champagnie will get the starting nod for the first time this season. He's averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.6 blocks while shooting 44.4 percent from deep in 25.3 minutes per contest across 10 regular-season games.

items.headline: Champagnie had 26 points (9-14 FG, 8-13 3Pt), three rebounds and three assists across 25 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Champagnie was red hot during the first half of Tuesday's win, connecting on eight triples en route to a season-high 26 points. While this was a fantastic night for anyone rostering him, it could certainly have been a lot better had the game been even remotely close. He remains an elite source of three-pointers, although he doesn't offer a lot outside of that category. Given that he had made seven three-pointers in his previous three games, managers shouldn't expect a performance like this very often.

items.headline: Champagnie finished Saturday's 122-106 win over the Mavericks with 12 points (4-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal over 28 minutes.
items.story: Champagnie was one of six Spurs players to score in double digits Saturday, and he was the only member of the team's bench to reach that threshold. He also contributed defensively with three blocks, which was second-most on San Antonio behind Victor Wembanyama (four). Champagnie has gone 7-for-18 (38.9 percent) from three-point range through the first three games of the regular season, and that continued form would help him maintain his role in the rotation once Tobias Harris (calf) is cleared to play.

items.headline: Champagnie finished with six points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt) and three steals in 25 minutes during Friday's 114-110 loss to Houston.
items.story: Champagnie finished with a pair of three-pointers, although that's really where the good news ends. While it does appear as though he is going to play a meaningful role for the Spurs, his ceiling is relatively limited. Coming off his best season in the NBA, the opportunities that he had last year simply aren't going to be available to him, assuming the stacked roster remains largely healthy. Fantasy managers should view him as a viable three-point streaming option.

items.headline: Champagnie notched eight points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two steals over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Although it was Devin Vassell who drew the Opening Night start, Champagnie also appears to be a direct fantasy beneficiary of Tobias Harris' (calf) absence. Champagnie should be worth streaming in most leagues until Harris is cleared to make his season debut.

items.headline: Champagnie (rest) will suit up for Friday's preseason finale against the Kings, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: After taking a day off Wednesday against the Suns, Champagnie is one of several Spurs set to return. Friday's game has the look of a potential dress rehearsal for the regular season.

items.headline: Champagnie (rest) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against Phoenix, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Champagnie started San Antonio's first three preseason games but will get Wednesday off for rest purposes. His next chance to suit up will come Friday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Champagnie supplied 14 points (5-13 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one steal and one block over 26 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason loss to Utah.
items.story: The sharpshooter appears to be competing with Dylan Harper for the Spurs' final starting spot to begin the season. That said, Tobias Harris (calf) should pose another threat to playing time for Champagnie once he's healthy.

items.headline: Champagnie will start Thursday's preseason game against Atlanta, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: The Spurs initially released a starting lineup that didn't include Champagnie, but the team has since reported that De'Aaron Fox has been downgraded to out due to soreness. This opens up a slot in the starting five for Champagnie, who is expected to play a key role this season for San Antonio after averaging 11.1 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 82 regular-season appearances a year ago.

items.headline: Champagnie is not starting Thursday's preseason game against the Hawks, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Dylan Harper is getting the nod over Champagnie in the first unit. The two are battling for San Antonio's final starting position while Tobias Harris (calf) is sidelined.

items.headline: Champagnie said Monday that he's not really "paying attention" to whether he starts or not, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Champagnie is instead focused on helping the Spurs win a title following their NBA Finals loss to the Knicks. The 25-year-old swingman is coming off a career year in which he started 68 of his 82 regular-season appearances, averaging 11.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.4 triples, 1.5 assists and 0.8 steals while shooting 38.1 percent from deep in 27.6 minutes per contest. However, Tobias Harris is now in the mix, making it uncertain whether Champagnie will begin the regular season in the starting five. Still, he's fresh off signing a three-year, $45 million contract and figures to remain an important piece for San Antonio for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Champagnie agreed to a three-year, $45 million contract with the Spurs on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Champagnie is set to remain with the Spurs after spending the past three-plus seasons with the club. The 25-year-old forward is fresh off a career-best year in 2025-26, averaging 11.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 0.8 steals across 27.6 minutes per game in 82 regular-season games (68 starts). He figures to continue playing a significant role for the team for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Champagnie ended Saturday's 94-90 loss to the Knicks in Game 5 of the NBA Finals with 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal over 31 minutes.
items.story: Champagnie delivered a bounce-back performance Saturday after scoring just five points on 2-of-9 shooting in Game 4. The 24-year-old forward was a valuable contributor for the Spurs in their run to the Finals, averaging 11.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 39.6 percent from deep across 30.6 minutes per tilt in 23 playoff appearances. Champagnie is fresh off a career-best year, and the Spurs hold a team option on his contract for 2026-27. Across 82 regular-season appearances (68 starts) in 2025-26, he averaged 11.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 0.8 steals while shooting 38.1 percent from downtown in 27.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Champagnie chipped in five points (2-9 FG, 1-7 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and four steals across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 107-106 loss to New York in Game 4 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Champagnie was mostly a non-factor, tallying just five points. While he was able to contribute four steals on the defensive end, his production on the offensive end remains sketchy, at best. Through four games in the NBA Finals, he has averaged just 10.3 points and 2.8 three-pointers per contest.

items.headline: Champagnie recorded 20 points (6-11 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 37 minutes during the Spurs' 111-103 win over the Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday.
items.story: Champagnie entered Saturday's game having shot 6-for-14 from three-point range over the last two games of the series. He brought the hot hand to Game 7 to lead both teams in three-point makes, finishing as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama (22 points). Champagnie has scored 20-plus points in two of his last three games and will end the Western Conference Finals having averaged 11.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 2.6 threes, 1.1 steals and 0.9 blocks over 33.9 minutes per game. Game 1 of the NBA Finals takes place Wednesday in San Antonio, where the Spurs welcome in the Knicks.

items.headline: Champagnie finished with 22 points (8-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and three steals across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 127-114 loss to the Thunder in Game 5 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: The 22 points were a series high for Champagnie. In fact, he hadn't scored more than 11 in the prior four games. The four made three-pointers and three steals were also series highs, and through five contests against OKC, he's averaging 10.6 points, 6.2 boards, 2.0 threes, 1.6 assists and 2.0 combined steals and blocks in 34.8 minutes. Champagnie will look to stay locked in for Game 6 on Thursday.

items.headline: Champagnie supplied 10 points (4-10 FG, 2-8 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 35 minutes during Friday's 123-108 loss to the Thunder in Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Champagnie scored in double digits for the third time in the past four games, albeit by the thinnest of margins. Over his past six appearances, Champagnie has averaged 10.5 points, 1.5 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 33.3 minutes per contest. Now behind 2-1 in the series, San Antonio will be looking to get things back on track when the two teams meet again Sunday.

items.headline: Champagnie supplied 18 points (5-10 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Friday's 139-109 win over Minnesota in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: After scoring in single digits in three consecutive contests, Champagnie posted an efficient 18 points in Friday's series-ending victory. He knocked down at least four triples for the first time since Game 2 of the second-round series and for the third time this postseason. The 24-year-old forward also chipped in two steals for a fifth straight game and will aim to extend that streak against the Thunder in the Western Conference Finals.

items.headline: Champagnie finished Monday's 104-102 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 17 points (7-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt) and seven rebounds across 32 minutes.
items.story: After erupting for 19 points in the Spurs' series-clinching win over Portland last Tuesday, Champagnie was productive again to begin the second round, albeit in a losing effort. The fourth-year forward has drained multiple three-pointers in all six of San Antonio's playoff games so far, averaging 11.3 points, 5.3 boards, 2.7 threes, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 29.0 minutes over that span while shooting 58.5 percent from the floor and 57.1 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Mavericks, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Hayes will not return Sunday due to a left knee injury. Mo Bamba will soak up most of Hayes' vacated minutes, while Brice Sensabaugh and Tony Bradley could see additional opportunities.

items.headline: Hayes is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Mavericks due to a left knee injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Hayes was a perfect 3-for-3 from the field for eight points and added three rebounds and one assist in 12 minutes prior to exiting Sunday's contest. Mo Bamba should see the majority of the center minutes in Hayes' stead, while Tony Bradley could get some run as the third big.

items.headline: Hayes produced 18 points (7-8 FG, 4-8 FT) and 14 rebounds in 28 minutes during Friday's 111-101 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Hayes set a season high on the glass and tied his best scoring output of the year, giving Utah a strong presence inside in just his second game back from a knee issue. He didn't miss much from the field, though he struggled at the free-throw line. With Jusuf Nurkic (foot) still out, Hayes has moved back into the starting lineup, pushing Mo Bamba to the bench.

items.headline: Hayes is listed in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Hayes will replace Mo Bamba in the first unit for Friday's game. As a starter this season, Hayes is averaging 8.0 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.5 blocks per game.

items.headline: Hayes will come off the bench during Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Hayes missed the last two games due to a knee injury, but he will return to action Wednesday in a reserve role. Mo Bamba will start at the five. Hayes holds averages of 11.0 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 23.4 minutes per contest over his last five appearances.

items.headline: Hayes (knee) is listed as available for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Hayes missed the last two games but will return for Wednesday's meeting with the Lakers. With Hayes back on the floor, Mo Bamba is expected to return to the bench.

items.headline: Hayes (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Hayes is aiming to end a two-game absence Wednesday due to a knee strain. If the big man is unable to play, Mo Bamba would remain worth streaming in the majority of fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Hayes will miss a second consecutive game due to a left knee strain, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday in the second half of the Jazz's back-to-back set. Mo Bamba is likely to remain in the starting lineup after faring well in his first start Sunday. On the year, Hayes is averaging 8.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 blocks across 12 appearances (10 starts).

items.headline: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Hayes left Friday's game against the Rockets with the knee issue, and it will now sideline him for Sunday's tilt versus San Antonio. Mo Bamba will likely join the starting unit while Tony Bradley and Kyle Filipowski should earn more playing time off the bench.

items.headline: Hayes won't return to Friday's game against the Rockets due to a left knee issue.
items.story: Hayes will end up missing the entire second half. He was playing well prior to the injury, finishing with 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting with five rebounds and one assist in 13 minutes. Mo Bamba could be in line for more run with this news.

items.headline: Hayes posted 18 points (6-6 FG, 6-7 FT), six rebounds, an assist and a block across 29 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Hayes capitalized on his opportunities around the basket, converting all six field-goal attempts while delivering solid rebounding production. Hayes offers useful fantasy potential through field-goal percentage, rebounds and blocks, although his value depends on consistent playing time. On that note, he's played at least 28 minutes in back-to-back games, so his playing time seems to be trending up. He'll remain a valuable low-end fantasy option as long as he continues as Utah's starting center.

items.headline: Hayes closed with two points (1-2 FG), seven rebounds, one assist and one block in 21 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 120-113 overtime loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Hayes struggled to stay on the floor against his former team, committing six fouls and four turnovers before exiting. Although he contributed seven rebounds, the center attempted just two shots and offered minimal offensive production. Mo Bamba's 10 rebounds in 14 minutes further highlighted Utah's available frontcourt alternatives, leaving Hayes with an uncertain fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Hayes notched two points (0-2 FG, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Hayes struggled to contribute offensively but made an impact on the glass and defensively, collecting three offensive rebounds while registering multiple blocks. The 37-minute workload was particularly encouraging, though limited scoring opportunities could make consistent fantasy production difficult. His rebounding and shot-blocking provide some value in deeper formats.

items.headline: Hayes is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Spurs.
items.story: Jaren Jackson (knee) is set to sit out at least the next six weeks, and with Jusuf Nurkic (foot) still not close, Hayes appears to be locked in as Utah's starting center. He's gotten off to a hot start this season with averages of 10.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 2.3 swats per contest, so make sure Hayes isn't floating around on your waiver wire.

items.headline: Hayes (shoulder) is available for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Hayes will shake off his questionable tag due to right shoulder soreness and return from a one-game absence. The big man should see significant burn Wednesday due to the absences of Jaren Jackson (knee) and Jusuf Nurkic (foot).

items.headline: Hayes (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: With Jusuf Nurkic (toe) and Jaren Jackson (knee) both sidelined, the Jazz are thin at the center position. If Hayes is available versus the Spurs, he'll presumably start. If not, Kyle Filipowski would likely move into the starting lineup, with Mo Bamba getting more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Hayes (shoulder) is out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hayes will miss the second leg of this back-to-back due to right shoulder soreness after posting nine points, five rebounds, a steal and an assist in 19 minutes during Sunday's loss to the Lakers. That means Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba are likely to handle a bigger role off the bench. Hayes' next chance to play will come against the Spurs on Wednesday.

items.headline: Hayes is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies due to right shoulder soreness, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Hayes could be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set after posting nine points, five rebounds, a steal and an assist in 19 minutes during Sunday's loss to the Lakers. If the big man joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) on the inactive list, Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba would be candidates to see increased minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Hayes supplied 17 points (7-8 FG, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block across 26 minutes off the bench during Friday's 120-119 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: After getting the start in the season opener, Hayes swapped places with Ace Bailey as Utah went with a smaller lineup against New Orleans. Hayes was more productive off the bench, leading the second unit in scoring and boards, and he ended up playing more minutes than Bailey on the night. The duo might continue to switch in and out of the starting five depending on matchups, but Hayes' workload figures to be steady in either role while Jusuf Nurkic (foot) remains sidelined.

items.headline: Hayes won't start Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Hayes got the starting nod in Wednesday's season-opening loss to Memphis, posting five points, six blocks, five rebounds, three assists and two steals in 26 minutes of action. However, the big man will come off the bench behind Jaren Jackson on Friday, with Ace Bailey entering the first unit.

items.headline: Hayes closed Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies with five points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists, six blocks and two steals across 26 minutes.
items.story: Hayes made an immediate defensive impact in his Jazz debut, accounting for half of Utah's 12 blocked shots while adding two steals. The center started alongside Jaren Jackson and Lauri Markkanen, indicating a potentially meaningful role in Utah's frontcourt rotation. Although his offensive production and free-throw shooting were underwhelming, Hayes' defensive upside could make him a useful specialist in deeper fantasy leagues if he maintains substantial playing time.

items.headline: Hayes contributed 11 points (4-5 FG, 3-4 FT) and two rebounds across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Hayes appears to be the favorite to start for the Jazz this season while Jusuf Nurkic (foot) is sidelined. That said, Utah could mix and match based on matchups and deploy Ace Bailey in the first unit at times, with Jaren Jackson serving as the starting center.

items.headline: Hayes will start in Tuesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Jusuf Nurkic (foot) is sidelined, so Hayes will start in the rematch with the Nuggets. The 26-year-old started nine times with the Lakers in 2025-26, averaging 12.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals over 27.4 minutes in those appearances.

items.headline: The Jazz are signing Hayes to a two-year, $12 million deal Wednesday, per Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com.
items.story: The second season on the contract has a team option as well. Hayes spent his last three years with the Lakers, but now he's lined up to compete for the backup center role behind Jusuf Nurkic with Kyle Filipowski next year. Hayes averaged 7.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, 0.9 assists and 0.8 blocks in 18.3 minutes over 66 regular-season contests in 2025-26.

items.headline: Hayes logged 18 points (6-8 FG, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block in 27 minutes off the bench during Monday's 115-110 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: The 25-year-old center was the only member of the Lakers' second unit to score in double digits in the season-ending loss -- the rest of the team's bench managed just five points combined. It was Hayes's best scoring effort of the playoffs, and he heads into free agency this offseason having averaged 7.5 points, 4.1 boards, 0.9 assists and 0.8 blocks in 18.3 minutes over 66 regular-season contests.

items.headline: Hayes accumulated six points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 101-94 win over the Rockets in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hayes had missed the Lakers' final four contests of the regular season due to left foot soreness, but he's back to handling his typical role as the top backup center behind Deandre Ayton this postseason. As long as Ayton stays healthy, however, Hayes could have a hard time cracking the 20-minute plateau on a consistent basis.

items.headline: Hayes (foot) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Saturday's Game 1 matchup with the Rockets.
items.story: Hayes missed L.A.'s final four regular-season games, but he'll return to the floor Saturday. With Hayes back in the mix, Maxi Kleber could drop from the rotation entirely.

items.headline: Hayes (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Hayes will end the regular season with a fourth straight game on the inactive list due to a left foot issue. Maxi Kleber and Jarred Vanderbilt could see increased playing time in Hayes' stead. The big man will finish the regular season with averages of 7.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, 0.9 assists and 0.8 blocks across 18.3 minutes per game in 66 outings (nine starts).

items.headline: Hayes (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Hayes is in danger of missing a fourth straight game due to a left foot issue. If the big man is ruled out, Maxi Kleber and Jarred Vanderbilt would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week.
items.story: Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

items.headline: Nurkic (toe) is listed as out for Friday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Nurkic has yet to play this season due to a toe injury. It's unclear where he is in the recovery process, though he should be considered week-to-week until the team provides an update. While Nurkic remains on the shelf, Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba are expected to continue holding things down in the middle.

items.headline: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
items.story: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

items.headline: Nurkic (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Nurkic has been a spectator to begin the season, and he's still not ready for game action due to a foot injury. The veteran big man should be considered week-to-week until the Jazz update his recovery, so Jaxson Hayes is expected to remain the team's primary center going forward.

items.headline: Nurkic will miss at least the next four weeks due to a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: Nurkic will begin the 2026-27 season on the sidelines, and given the tricky nature of foot injuries for big men, it wouldn't be shocking to see his absence extend beyond this initial four-week window. Jaren Jackson will likely spend more time at center while Nurkic is out, and there will be more minutes available for Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba.

items.headline: Nurkic (foot) is listed as out for Tuesday's preseason game against Denver.
items.story: Nurkic is dealing with a foot issue, so he will miss Utah's second preseason game on the schedule. With Kyle Filipowski (back) also sidelined, Jaxson Hayes, Mo Bamba and Jonas Aidoo should handle the bulk of the minutes at the center position.

items.headline: Nurkic didn't participate in Monday's practice due to a right foot injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Nurkic logged 11 minutes in Sunday's preseason-opening win over Denver, posting four points (1-5 FG, 2-2 FT, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. The big man can be considered questionable for Tuesday's preseason rematch against Denver until the Jazz offer an update on his status.

items.headline: Nurkic totaled four points (1-5 FG, 2-2 FT, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 11 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Nurkic was given the starting nod Sunday and yet played fewer minutes than newly acquired Jaxson Hayes, who ended with 19 minutes off the bench. All signs point to Nurkic being the starting center come Opening Night, putting him on the radar as a potential top-100 candidate. Although his role may not be reflective of what might be considered that of a typical starter, his ability to put up numbers across the board should lend itself to multiple builds. Considering him as a third center in standard leagues feels relatively safe.

items.headline: Nurkic recorded 25 points (11-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-5 FT), 14 rebounds and two assists in 23 minutes during Bosnia and Herzegovina's 78-76 win over Italy in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 32-year-old re-signed with Utah on a two-year deal this offseason after averaging 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.3 steals in 26.4 minutes across 41 regular-season appearances last season. With Walker Kessler now with the Lakers, Nurkic enters 2026-27 with a clearer path to the starting center job and could be a useful source of rebounds and assists in fantasy despite his limited scoring upside.

items.headline: Nurkic (nose) is projected as Utah's top starting center for the 2026-27 season after the Jazz lost Walker Kessler to the Lakers this offseason, Jared Koch of SI.com reports.
items.story: Nurkic was highly productive when available for the Jazz, averaging 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.3 steals in 26.4 minutes per game across 41 regular-season games (36 starts) last year. The veteran big man will have a new partner in the frontcourt with Jaren Jackson now in the fold, so it'll be interesting to see how the two big men mesh in 2026-27. Nurkic should be ready for the start of training camp after undergoing season-ending nose surgery in February.

items.headline: Nurkic (nose) intends to sign a two-year, $22 million contract to return to the Jazz, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Nurkic was a full-time starter for the Jazz since November of the 2025-26 campaign due to the absence of Walker Kessler (shoulder). The former averaged 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.3 steals over 26.4 minutes per game across 41 regular-season games (36 starts) last year, but Nurkic missed the last two months of the season after undergoing surgery on his nose in mid-February. He should be 100 percent for the start of training camp and will likely serve as the Jazz's backup big man behind Kessler for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Nurkic is scheduled to undergo season-ending nose surgery Wednesday, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: Nurkic came back from the All-Star break with a nose injury, and he's opting for a procedure to repair the issue. The 31-year-old big man is set to be an unrestricted free agent ahead of 2026-27, and he should receive plenty of interest on the open market this summer after averaging 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.3 steals in 26.4 minutes per contest through  41 games this season. With Nurkic's campaign over, the runway is clear at center for Kyle Filipowski to handle a starting role the rest of the way.

items.headline: Nurkic (nose) has been ruled out for Monday's game in Houston.
items.story: Monday will mark Nurkic's third consecutive game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Thursday's game against the Pelicans. Kyle Filipowski will continue to get the bulk of the five-man minutes with Nurkic sidelined.

items.headline: Nurkic is out  for Friday's game against Memphis due to nose injury management.
items.story: Nurkic went unused during last Thursday's loss to Portland, and fantasy managers should expect his availability to remain sporadic throughout the course of the stretch run. Kyle Filipowski should handle the bulk of the center minutes Friday, with Kevin Love filling in the No. 2 center spot behind him.

items.headline: Nurkic isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Nurkic will be available for Thursday's matchup, but the fact that he's not listed in the starting lineup is likely a sign that he won't see much if any playing time. Instead, it'll be up to Kyle Filipowski and Kevin Love to eat up minutes at center.

items.headline: Nurkic finished with eight points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), nine rebounds, four assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 121-93 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Utah's intentions when it comes to how much Nurkic will play down the stretch remain unclear, but what's certain is that the veteran center is producing at a high level when available. Nurkic has averaged 14.7 points, 11.8 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.1 three-pointers in 29.4 minutes per contest in his last 16 games, shooting 47.2 percent from long range during this period.

items.headline: Nurkic contributed three points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 14 rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal in 24 minutes during Saturday's 120-117 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Nurkic returned from a two-game absence due to illness/rest, moving straight into the starting lineup alongside the newly acquired Jaren Jackson. Utah opted to run with a sizeable lineup, an encouraging sign for anyone rostering Nurkic. With that said, we have already started to see some questionable absences, a situation that could get worse as the season progresses. For now, managers will have to hold Nurkic or try to pass him off while he is still relatively active.

items.headline: Nurkic is part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Magic, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Nurkic, surprisingly, will be part of a jumbo lineup that includes Keyonte George, Ace Bailey, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson. Nurkic had been a DNP-CD in back-to-back games, and the expectation was that Utah would opt for Nurkic to come off the bench while Jackson manned the center spot. However, it looks like Nurkic could remain in a significant role even with Jackson on the roster. In 38 regular-season appearances thus far, Nurkic is averaging 11.2 points, 10.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists across 26.6 minutes.

items.headline: Jazz head coach Will Hardy said that Nurkic won't start Thursday's game against the Hawks, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Though Nurkic will technically be available Thursday, his presence on the bench likely indicates that the Jazz plan to stay away from using him. The Jazz took that approach in their most recent game Tuesday against the Pacers; Nurkic was initially ruled out in advance of the game for rest purposes, then was upgraded to available before he ultimately went unused off the bench. Kyle Filipowski started at center in that game and played 36 minutes, and he'll likely be in line for another hefty workload Thursday while the Jazz are short on available bodies in the aftermath of the trade deadline.

items.headline: Nurkic will come off the bench Tuesday against the Pacers.
items.story: Nurkic was initially ruled out due to rest purposes, but the team later thought better of this decision after a trade depleted the Utah frontcourt. It remains to be seen how much playing time he'll shoulder Tuesday, as it's obvious the club wanted to give him a night off.
