items.story: Mykhailiuk missed all seven of his shot attempts, adding very little in terms of peripheral numbers. All-in-all, it's been a disappointing season for Mykhailiuk, playing in just 32 games thus far. In 19.3 minutes per game, he is averaging just 8.4 points and 1.8 three-pointers.

items.headline: Hield finished Sunday's 151-145 overtime loss to Denver with 33 points (13-19 FG, 7-13 3Pt), seven rebounds, six assists and one steal in 40 minutes.
items.story: Hield has averaged 16.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 4.0 triples and 24.2 minutes over his last five games. Sunday's offensive explosion highlights his shooting upside, though inconsistent playing time limits his reliability in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Hield will start Sunday's game against Denver.
items.story: Norman Powell (hamstring) is sidelined, so Hield will make his first start of the 2026-27 campaign. The 2016 No. 6 overall pick started three games for the Warriors in 2025-26, averaging 9.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.0 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep in 22.7 minutes per outing in those games.

items.headline: Hield accumulated 15 points (5-10 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and four rebounds across 23 minutes during Friday's 98-94 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Hield provided Chicago with valuable perimeter shooting despite playing just 23 minutes. His offensive role remains heavily concentrated on outside shooting, as nine of his 10 field-goal attempts came from beyond the arc. That specialization gives him value for fantasy managers seeking three-pointers, but the limited playing time and lack of assists or defensive production make his overall contributions difficult to predict. Hield remains a streaming consideration in deeper leagues rather than a dependable option across multiple categories.

items.headline: Hield recorded 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one steal over 19 minutes during Wednesday's 137-107 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Hield has connected on multiple three-pointers in four consecutive appearances, providing dependable perimeter production despite fluctuating scoring totals. However, he's logged fewer than 20 minutes in consecutive games, and his limited contributions outside scoring restrict his fantasy ceiling. He remains primarily a three-point specialist in deeper category leagues

items.headline: Hield amassed 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block over 25 minutes during Friday's 125-117 overtime win over the Hawks.
items.story: Hield rejoined the rotation, scoring in double figures for just the second time this season. The veteran wing has a chance to carve out a more meaningful role moving forward, as Caleb Wilson (hand) is set to miss an extended period.

items.headline: Hield had nine points (4-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists in 16 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: After scoring 13 points on 5-of-6 shooting in Friday's win over Milwaukee, Hield once again provided a spark off the bench Saturday. The veteran shooting guard is averaging 7.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 15.0 minutes per contest across three regular-season games.

items.headline: Hield produced 15 points (4-7 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, two steals and an assist in 19 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 133-128 preseason loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: The veteran wing was picked up from the Hornets at the end of September to provide some experience and a moveable contract to the Bulls' second unit, but while he's with Chicago, Hield's long-range shooting will help spread the floor for young building blocks like Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson. Hield's coming off a disappointing 2025-26 campaign split between Atlanta and Golden State, but prior to last season he hadn't shot below 36.6 percent from three-point range or averaged fewer than 2.2 threes in any of the prior eight seasons.

items.headline: The Bulls acquired Hield and cash from the Hornets on Saturday in exchange for Rob Dillingham (wrist), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Hield was traded to Charlotte on Tuesday but is on the move again to Chicago. The 33-year-old has spent time with the Pelicans, Kings, Pacers, 76ers, Warriors and Hawks throughout his career. In 765 regular-season appearances, Hield has averaged 14.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.4 assists over 27.5 minutes per contest. He's also a career 39.5 percent shooter from deep. However, Hield could have a tough time earning consistent minutes with the Bulls, so his fantasy ceiling isn't very high. While he may only be used situationally, the veteran guard could be a viable pickup when injuries arise.

items.headline: The Hawks are trading Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash to the Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith on Tuesday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Hield struggled to carve out a meaningful role for Atlanta, making just seven regular-season appearances with the Hawks last year, so the move to Charlotte gives him a chance for a fresh start. The veteran sharpshooter gives the Hornets wing depth but still doesn't appear likely to have an Opening Night role.

items.headline: Hield recorded 19 points (7-18 FG, 5-13 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists and two steals in 33 minutes during the Bahamas' 100-82 win over Panama in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The veteran sharpshooter's $9.7 million salary for 2026-27 was fully guaranteed by Atlanta this offseason, but his role remains uncertain on an extremely crowded Hawks roster. Hield averaged 7.6 points while making 1.0 three-pointers per game during the regular season in 2025-26, but Atlanta's collection of perimeter options could make consistent minutes difficult to come by.

items.headline: Hield had his $9.66 million salary for the 2026-27 season fully guaranteed by the Hawks on Sunday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Hield began the 2025-26 campaign in Golden State before being traded to Atlanta ahead of the deadline. In seven regular-season games with the Hawks, he averaged a career-low 5.1 points, 1.1 rebounds and 0.7 assists across 7.3 minutes while shooting 41.2 percent from deep. It's unknown what the future holds for Hield, but he will remain in Atlanta for now. However, there is always a chance other teams in need of a reliable shooter will come calling at some point moving ahead.

items.headline: Hield supplied five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and two rebounds over nine minutes during Thursday's 140-89 loss to the Knicks in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: With the Hawks getting blown out of this contest, Hield was able to make his second appearance of the postseason. Following his move from Golden State, Hield wasn't able to carve out a role in Atlanta. He appeared in just seven regular-season contests for an average of 7.3 minutes per game. The veteran is under contract for two more seasons, though the second year is a player option.

items.headline: Hield provided 31 points (12-18 FG, 7-11 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 21 minutes during Sunday's 143-117 loss to Miami.
items.story: With Atlanta resting most of its starters, Hield saw a massive spike in usage and took advantage of the increased opportunity. He set season highs in points and three-pointers made, and he finished with a pristine effective-field-goal percentage of 86.1.

items.headline: Hield had zero points (0-2 FG) over four minutes during Friday's 141-107 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Hield was back in the rotation, albeit during garbage time. Since arriving in Atlanta, Hield's role has been basically non-existent, suiting up on just six occasions. During his time on the floor, he has averaged 0.9 points and 0.9 rebounds. He can be safely ignored in all formats.

items.headline: Hield (recently traded) is available for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Hield and Jonathan Kuminga (knee) were traded by the Warriors on Wednesday in exchange for Kristaps Porzingis (Achilles). With the trade finalized, Hield is ready to make his debut for the Hawks, though he'll be competing with fellow veterans CJ McCollum and Gabe Vincent for minutes off the bench behind backcourt starters Dyson Daniels and Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Hield averaged 11.3 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.1 threes and 1.0 steals over 20.3 minutes per game over his last nine games with Golden State.

items.headline: Hield (recently traded) is questionable  for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: With Wednesday's trade still pending, Hield is uncertain for his Hawks debut Saturday. If the veteran sharpshooter is out, Zaccharie Risacher and Corey Kispert should both see a considerable workload.

items.headline: The Warriors traded Hield and Jonathan Kuminga (knee) to the Hawks on Wednesday in exchange for Kristaps Porzingis (illness), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Hield joins the Hawks after two seasons in Golden State. The 33-year-old is averaging 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists across 17.5 minutes per game this season while shooting what would be a career-low 34.2 percent from three-point land. He'll have to compete with Corey Kispert and Luke Kennard for minutes off the bench in Atlanta. Hield likely won't be ready in time to face the Jazz on Thursday, making Saturday against Charlotte his next chance to make his Hawks debut.

items.headline: Hield produced 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Monday's 135-112 victory over the Heat.
items.story: It's unclear how Steve Kerr will proceed without Jimmy Butler (knee), but Hield's minutes will probably jump somewhat. He's often served as a backcourt replacement, but his sharpshooting skills can also come in handy at the wing. He'll likely be a prime pivot along with De'Anthony Melton (knee) as the Warriors try to stay relevant in the Western Conference.

items.headline: Hield finished with 14 points (5-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two steals in 18 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 136-116 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: The 14 points were his best scoring effort since Dec. 4, while the five combined steals and blocks were a season high. Hield is still struggling to maintain a consistent spot in the rotation, but performances like this will bolster his case for regular minutes.

items.headline: Hield had six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), three rebounds, one block and two steals in 11 minutes during Monday's 120-107 win over the Nets.
items.story: Hield continues to play a muted role, having now logged no more than 15 minutes in six straight games, two of which he failed to see the court. While expectations were relatively low coming into the season, Hield has been even worse, averaging just 7.5 points and 1.4 three-pointers in 17.6 minutes per game through 31 appearances. Sitting well outside the top 250 in standard leagues, it appears as though Hield's days of being a fantasy asset are now well behind him.

items.headline: Hield supplied three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist over 14 minutes during Sunday's 141-127 overtime loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Hield's role continues to trend in the wrong direction as the Warriors look to give other rotation players a fair shot. Over his last five appearances, Hield has seen 12.6 minutes per contest with 5.0 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.4 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Hield (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Saturday's 119-116 win over the Suns.
items.story: Though Golden State ran with the same starting five for the third game in a row, head coach Steve Kerr continued to tinker with the back end of his rotation. For the first time all season, Hield found himself as the odd man out, even on a night Golden State used 12 players. Kerr elected to reopen a spot in the rotation Will Richard, who hadn't appeared in any of the past three games but responded with a 20-point, five-rebound effort off the bench. Richard's performance could earn him more opportunities on the second unit at the expense of Hield, who had seen his playing time drop in each ensuing game since he made a 26-minute start Dec. 6 in Cleveland.

items.headline: Hield will come off the bench Sunday against Portland, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Golden State's lineups continue to be fluid, and this time it's Hield and Pat Spencer who will move to the second unit. Hield is coming off a pair of duds with an average of 7.5 points over his last two outings.

items.headline: Hield will start Saturday's game against the Cavaliers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The Warriors will shake things up with several lineup changes Saturday. With so much offensive firepower on the sidelines with injuries, Hield will have a big opportunity to get up plenty of shots Saturday.

items.headline: Hield closed Thursday's 99-98 loss to the 76ers with 14 points (6-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 26 minutes.
items.story: Hield received plenty of looks from beyond the arc Thursday night, but he was unable to capitalize. He's struggled to find his groove over his last three matchups, sinking only six of 23 attempts (26.1 percent). Even so, Hield could continue to see key minutes off the bench if Jimmy Butler (knee) misses more time.

items.headline: Hield recorded 13 points (4-15 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, four assists and two steals over 28 minutes during Tuesday's 124-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Hield had quite a green light to shoot Tuesday, which makes sense given the early departure of Jimmy Butler (knee) and absence of Stephen Curry (quadriceps). Even so, the veteran sharpshooter remains a hit-or-miss fantasy option, having averaged 8.7 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 20.7 minutes per game over his last seven outings.

items.headline: Hield supplied 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 23 minutes off the bench during Monday's 134-117 win over the Jazz.
items.story: The 20 points were a season high for Hield, who continues to struggle with his consistency. He's drained at least three three-pointers in three of the last five games, but he managed a total of just two points in the other two contests combined. The veteran guard is averaging a career-worst 7.6 points and 1.4 threes in 17.7 minutes a game as part of the Warriors' second unit, but his recent ceiling performances suggest Hield might be finding a groove.

items.headline: Hield ended Friday's 127-123 loss to the Trail Blazers with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one steal in 16 minutes.
items.story: Hield failed to score for the second time this season, another in a long line of underwhelming performances. He has tallied double digits only five times thus far, averaging 6.9 points through his first 18 games. He holds little to no value in fantasy, outside of limited streaming appeal.

items.headline: Hield (illness) is available for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Hield will power through his illness, but with Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler and Draymond Green all back in action Friday night, Hield's upside will be limited. Hield is averaging 7.3 points and 1.3 triples per game on the year.

items.headline: Hield is listed as probable for Friday's game against Portland due to illness.
items.story: Hield appears to have come down with an illness over the last day or so, but he should still be able to take the floor Friday evening. The team will likely have an update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Hield totaled 18 points (7-20 FG, 4-15 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and two steals in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 110-96 loss to Miami.
items.story: The Warriors struggled to get their offense going to begin this game, as they missed their first 11 shot attempts, but Hield quickly cracked the seal on the rim once he checked into the game and secured Golden State's first bucket. He saw a season high in minutes with Stephen Curry (ankle), Jimmy Butler (back) and Draymond Green (illness) all sitting out the second leg of a back-to-back, but Hield's playing time will likely dip back to the teens Friday with the main guys expected back for that one.

items.headline: Hield (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against Miami.
items.story: The veteran sharpshooter has been battling an illness for the past few days, but he's good to go and should handle a larger role in the absences of Stephen Curry (ankle) and Jimmy Butler (back). For the campaign, Hield has averaged 6.6 points, 1.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 0.8 steals in 16.7 minutes per contest over 16 games.

items.headline: Hield (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Hield was able to play through this illness Tuesday against Miami, finishing with two points on 1-for-3 shooting in 15 minutes. Stephen Curry (ankle) and Jonathan Kuminga (knees) have already been ruled out, while Jimmy Butler (back) and Draymond Green (illness) are questionable, so there will be a ton of touches up for grabs if Hield can give it a go once again.

items.headline: Hield (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Hield is ready to play through an illness Tuesday. On the campaign as a whole, the veteran sharpshooter has averaged 6.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 16.8 minutes per contest across 15 games.

items.headline: Hield (illness) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Hield is listed on the injury report with an illness but is likely to play Tuesday. The veteran has settled into a steady bench role this season, averaging 16.8 minutes per contest across 15 appearances, though his 6.9 points per game and 32.1 percent three-point shooting both represent significant career lows.

items.headline: Hield totaled 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 20 minutes during Sunday's 124-106 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: In addition to the three steals, Hield made three three-pointers, just his third instance of doing so this season. The veteran sharpshooter is averaging 6.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.2 threes made on an underwhelming 32.1 percent clip over 16.9 minutes so far.

items.headline: Hield accumulated eight points (3-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 20 minutes during Sunday's 114-83 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Hield was unable to take advantage of Stephen Curry (illness) missing time, as he logged his fourth game this season without making a three-pointer. Hield is averaging 7.7 points, 1.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.6 steals and 1.4 threes so far, shooting 43.7 percent from the field and 32.6 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hield logged 12 points (4-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 20 minutes during Tuesday's 118-107 win over the Suns.
items.story: Tuesday marked the first time since the second game of the season that Hield finished with double-digit points. During that gap, he was shooting a mere 33.3 percent from the field and playing 14.4 minutes per game. However, with Jimmy Butler (back) missing the second half of Tuesday's win, Hield got some extra minutes and shot attempts.

items.headline: Hield ended with two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and three rebounds in 10 minutes during Tuesday's 98-79 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Hield is seemingly at the edge of Golden State's rotation to open the season. Through five regular-season contests, Hield is seeing 17.1 minutes per game with 7.4 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.6 steals and 1.2 three-pointers on 40.0 percent shooting from the field. His fantasy appeal is limited to deeper formats unless his minutes trend up.

items.headline: Steinbach was recalled from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Thursday.
items.story: Steinbach was assigned to the G League on Nov. 10 and dominated during his time with the Swarm. He averaged 26.0 points, 18.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 3.0 blocks in four appearances and will provide Charlotte with additional depth in the frontcourt after being recalled.

items.headline: Charlotte assigned Steinbach to the G League on Tuesday.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder is coming off back-to-back appearances for the Hornets amid Moussa Diabate's (quadriceps) absence. Steinbach still has a clearer path to action with the Greensboro Swarm.

items.headline: Steinbach notched four points (2-5 FG), 11 rebounds, an assist and three blocks across 27 minutes in Friday's 119-80 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Steinbach made a significant impact on the glass and defensively, leading Charlotte with 11 rebounds while recording a game-high three blocks. His offensive involvement remained minimal, but his 27-minute workload provided ample opportunities to accumulate valuable defensive stats. Steinbach's rebounding and rim protection offer intriguing fantasy potential, particularly in category formats, although his limited scoring remains a concern.

items.headline: The Hornets recalled Steinbach from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Friday.
items.story: Additionally, the Hornets listed the rookie center as available to play Friday against Boston. He will continue to provide depth at center, and he may be more involved if Moussa Diabate (quadriceps) can't play.

items.headline: The Hornets assigned Steinbach to the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Thursday.
items.story: Steinbach will spend time with Greensboro as Charlotte looks to provide the young forward with additional developmental opportunities. The assignment shouldn't significantly affect the Hornets' NBA rotation, and Steinbach remains off the fantasy radar in most redraft formats.

items.headline: Steinbach ended Friday's 95-79 loss to Washington with zero points (0-1 FG) in two minutes.
items.story: Steinbach appeared for just the second time this season, albeit for two minutes during garbage time. Despite some fanfare leading into the season, it appears as though he is going to have to bide his time on the bench, at least for the foreseeable future. Given his current role, there is no reason to be rostering Steinbach outside of dynasty formats.

items.headline: Steinbach (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 110-103 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: The rookie big man remained on Charlotte's bench throughout the Opening Night victory. With the Hornets having other frontcourt options available, Steinbach may face an uphill battle for consistent playing time early in the season.

items.headline: Steinbach logged 19 points (7-9 FG, 5-5 FT), 10 rebounds and three steals over 28 minutes during Friday's 117-98 preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Steinbach exploded off the bench for a double-double, leading Charlotte in scoring and rebounding after totaling just 17 points across his previous three preseason appearances. The rookie checked in early for Ryan Kalkbrenner and played a team-high 28 minutes. With Moussa Diabate (elbow) sidelined, the No. 14 overall pick could be working his way up to quality minutes once the season begins.

items.headline: Steinbach finished with seven points (2-4 FG, 3-4 FT) and four rebounds in 14 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason loss to Brooklyn.
items.story: Steinbach grabbed one offensive rebound and didn't commit a turnover during his limited action. The young big will look to make the most of his preseason opportunities as he competes for frontcourt minutes. He's currently projected to win the backup center job.

items.headline: Steinbach supplied 22 points (7-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), 11 rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes in Friday's 92-90 Summer League loss to the Kings.
items.story: Steinbach turned in an efficient performance from the field in Charlotte's Summer League finale, leading all players in scoring. The big man also grabbed a game-high-tying 11 rebounds. He finished Summer League action with back-to-back 20-point double-doubles and will now look toward his rookie campaign with the Hornets. The Washington product could see meaningful run early in his career but will have to compete for minutes with Moussa Diabate and Ryan Kalkbrenner.

items.headline: Steinbach totaled 27 points (13-22 FG, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists and one steal over 27 minutes in Wednesday's 110-91 Summer League loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Steinbach dominated despite the loss, leading all players in points and rebounds. Seven of the big man's 15 rebounds came on the offensive glass. The No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has shown some flashes through four Summer League appearances and figures to compete with Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate for minutes at center during the regular season.

items.headline: Steinbach totaled seven points (2-5 FG, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and one block across 22 minutes in Saturday's 95-91 Summer League loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: After posting a double-double with a full stat line in his Summer League debut Thursday, Steinbach had a quieter outing Saturday while once again coming off the bench. The No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft figures to compete for minutes at center with Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate.

items.headline: Steinbach registered 15 points (4-7 FG, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal across 22 minutes in Thursday's 86-74 Summer League win over the Magic.
items.story: Coming off the bench, Steinbach delivered a full stat line, highlighted by a game-high 11 rebounds as part of a double-double effort. The Hornets have some intriguing young frontcourt pieces, with Ryan Kalkbrenner and Moussa Diabate both flashing potential at center last season, but given his pedigree as the No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Steinbach figures to compete for minutes early in the regular season.

items.headline: Steinbach was selected by the Hornets with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Steinbach played professionally in Germany before heading to Washington for his lone college season. Over 30 appearances for the Huskies, the 20-year-old big man averaged 18.5 points, 11.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals while shooting 57.7 percent from the field and 34.0 percent from downtown in 34.6 minutes per contest. Steinbach will now join a team that has the potential to make waves in the Eastern Conference in 2026-27. With that in mind, the 20-year-old may not have an opportunity to start for the Hornets initially, as Moussa Diabate and Ryan Kalkbrenner return after showing flashes last season. However, Steinbach could earn meaningful minutes immediately, considering the club doesn't have many reliable options off the bench.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) won't play in Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Williams will miss a second consecutive game due to right hamstring injury management. Royce O'Neale and Tidjane Salaun should continue to see more minutes off the bench for Charlotte.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Hawks.
items.story: Williams started in Tuesday's 118-114 loss to the Lakers, but he will sit out Friday to rest. With Grayson Allen (concussion) also sidelined, Royce O'Neale could find his way into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Williams will start in Tuesday's game against the Lakers, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Williams will earn his first start of the season due to Grayson Allen (concussion-like symptoms) being out and Sion James reverting to a bench role.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) amassed 11 points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block in 16 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Williams made his season debut Thursday, playing limited minutes off the bench. However, the veteran made his presence felt and should see his role grow as he gets further removed from the hamstring injury that's sidelined him since training camp, especially if Brandon Miller (groin) joins Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Dennis Schroder (hamstring) on the long-term injury list.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is listed as available for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: After nursing a hamstring injury since the preseason, Williams is finally ready to make his season debut Thursday. The 28-year-old is likely to face a minutes restriction, but Williams could eventually cut into Royce O'Neale's playing time.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is listed as probable for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams is trending toward making his season debut Thursday after battling a right hamstring strain. However, the veteran forward isn't guaranteed to see meaningful playing time once he returns.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Williams has yet to appear in a game this season due to a right hamstring strain. His next opportunity to suit up comes Thursday against the Suns.

items.headline: The Hornets recalled Williams (hamstring) from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Wednesday.
items.story: Williams has yet to make his season debut due to a right hamstring strain. However, he appears to be making progress after joining the Swarm for practice Wednesday.

items.headline: Charlotte assigned Williams (hamstring) to the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Wednesday.
items.story: Williams will practice with the Swarm and will be recalled directly after. This is the next stage of his rehab as the veteran gets closer to a return for Charlotte.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Williams has yet to suit up during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been much revealed about his health. However, until he is cleared to play, he should be considered week-to-week, meaning Royce O'Neale should see more minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) will be re-evaluated following Charlotte's upcoming two-game road trip, Rod Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Williams' earliest possible return date now looks to be Saturday at home against the 76ers. Royce O'Neale should continue to play meaningful minutes off the bench for the Hornets in the interim.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Williams will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right hamstring strain that popped up during training camp in late September. Sion James will likely continue to operate in an elevated role in the absence of Williams, who can be considered week-to-week until the Hornets provide an update on his progress.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: A hamstring strain continues to leave Williams on the shelf. Sion James played 27 minutes during an Opening Night start in Brooklyn and carries some deep-league streaming appeal.

items.headline: Williams (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's season opener versus the Nets.
items.story: Williams is not yet able to practice fully as he works back from a hamstring injury. The Hornets should turn to Royce O'Neale for some extra playing time until Williams is ready to suit up.

items.headline: Williams will miss the preseason after suffering a right hamstring injury, the Hornets announced Friday.
items.story: Williams will be re-evaluated the first week of the regular season, putting his status for Opening Night in the air. Williams will have a difficult path to minutes this season as he competes with the likes of Naz Reid, Royce O'Neale and Tidjane Salaun.

items.headline: Williams finished with one point (0-4 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one steal across 15 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Williams turned in a lackluster performance in Friday's season-ending loss, scoring in single digits for a sixth straight game. The 27-year-old forward didn't make his season debut until Jan. 10 after rehabbing from right knee surgery he underwent in December 2024. Williams appeared in 36 regular-season games (three starts), averaging 7.0 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 0.5 steals and 0.5 blocks in 19.8 minutes per contest. items.headline: Essengue was selected by the Bulls with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft.

items.story: Barnes was barely visible in the loss, an indication of what is likely to come this season. Although he does provide the team with a valid floor-spacing option, a lack of peripheral stats severely limits his overall upside. At best, he could be streamed in for threes, although only when desperate.

items.headline: Barnes finished with seven points (2-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block in 17 minutes during Thursday's 123-116 preseason loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Barnes delivered a modest but well-rounded performance in limited action, contributing defensively while connecting on one three-pointer. The veteran forward should continue providing San Antonio with experience and perimeter shooting, though his offensive opportunities could be limited within a rotation featuring several emerging young players.

items.headline: Barnes will sign a one-year, $8 million contract to return to the Spurs for the 2026-27 season, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Monday.
items.story: Barnes started for San Antonio for the majority of the 2025-26 regular season before being moved to a bench role in early February. He saw his playing time decline in the playoffs and was a healthy scratch in each of San Antonio's last three games against New York in the NBA Finals. However, Barnes will return to the Spurs for the upcoming season and will provide the team with veteran depth in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Barnes finished the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 10.0 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 25.8 minute per game across 77 regular-season appearances (52 starts).
items.story: Barnes didn't see the floor in any of the final three games of the Finals after logging 17 total minutes in the first two outings of the series. The veteran forward was a regular in the starting lineup to begin the regular season but started only three games after the All-Star break. The 34-year-old is set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason.

items.headline: Barnes finished with five points (0-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and one steal across 16 minutes during Sunday's 103-82 win over the Thunder in Game 4 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Barnes logged at least 15 minutes for just the second time in the postseason, providing San Antonio with some additional size, particularly on the defensive end. In six postseason games over the past two weeks, Barnes has averaged just 2.2 points in 8.0 minutes. Given the fact that Sunday's result was a favorable one for the Spurs, it will be interesting to see whether Barnes once again plays meaningful minutes off the bench in Game 5 on Tuesday.

items.headline: Barnes finished Wednesday's 133-95 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals with 12 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across 15 minutes.
items.story: Barnes scored in double digits for the first time in the postseason, playing a handful of additional minutes as the game descended into garbage time. Prior to Wednesday, Barnes had scored a total of 13 points in six appearances, playing a muted role off the bench. Assuming Game 3 is a little more competitive, expect to see Barnes' playing time back in single digits.

items.story: Mashack, who has been sparsely deployed this season, will get the start with Cameron Boozer (ankle) unavailable. Joining Mashack in the first unit for Saturday's game will be Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells and Zach Edey.

items.headline: Mashack recorded two points (1-1 FG), one rebound and one assist in eight minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over Atlanta.
items.story: Mashack didn't enter until later in the contest and saw significantly fewer minutes than Memphis' primary backcourt options. The second-year guard faces an uphill battle for consistent playing time in a crowded rotation.

items.headline: Mashack logged 12 points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four assists, two rebounds, one steal and two blocks in 22 minutes of Sunday's 111-74 Salt Lake City Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Mashack is hoping to carve out a role in Memphis after playing on a two-way contract in 2025-26. Across 31 regular-season appearances, he averaged 6.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.2 assists while shooting 39.5 percent from the field.

items.headline: Mashack finished with 11 points (4-12 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, 11 assists and two blocks over 38 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 132-101 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: With so many injuries in Memphis, Mashack emerged as a key contributor down the stretch. In 31 total appearances, Mashack averaged 6.2 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.6 three-pointers in 21.7 minutes per contest, shooting 39.5 percent from the field.

items.headline: Mashack finished with 13 points (6-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds, 14 assists and two steals over 48 minutes during Friday's 147-101 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Mashack finished with a triple-double, logging big minutes among Memphis' slim six-player rotation. The 2025 second-round pick should serve as part of a youth-based rebuild in Memphis, as the Tennessee product has posted decent numbers since rejoining the parent club two months ago.

items.headline: Mashack (concussion) ended Wednesday's 136-119 loss to Denver with nine points (4-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 0-2 FT), seven assists and three rebounds across 33 minutes.
items.story: Mashack missed the Grizzlies' previous two games while in concussion protocol, but after gaining clearance for Wednesday's contest, he moved into the starting five and saw heavy minutes while Memphis listed 13 players out. Over his last seven appearances, Mashack is averaging 7.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.6 three-pointers in 27.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mashack will start Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Mashack will return from a two-game absence due to a concussion and step into the starting five. As a starter this season (four games), the rookie second-rounder has averaged 10.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.0 steals and 1.8 assists in 30.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mashack (concussion) is available for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder missed the Grizzlies' last two games due to a concussion, but he has cleared the league's protocol and will return for Wednesday's contest. In 16 games since the All-Star break, Mashack has averaged 7.0 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.1 steals over 25.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mashack (concussion) is questionable for Wednesday's game in Denver.
items.story: Mashack has missed the past two games while in the league's concussion protocol, but this is the first time he's received the questionable tag since going down, which indicates progress. If Mashack is cleared for Wednesday's game, he could see increased playing time for the shorthanded Grizzlies.

items.headline: Mashack is listed out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers with a concussion.
items.story: Mashack is sidelined for a second consecutive contest while in the league's concussion protocol. With Memphis' injury report a mile long, extra ball-handling duties are open to Cam Spencer at point guard Monday.

items.headline: Mashack is listed out for Sunday's game against the Bucks after being placed in concussion protocol.
items.story: Mashack was diagnosed with the concussion after exiting Friday's 128-96 loss to the Raptors due to what the Grizzlies initially labeled as neck soreness. Sunday's contest marks the first of a back-to-back set, so the rookie second-round pick could have a tough time clearing the protocol ahead of Monday's game against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Mashack didn't return during the second half of Friday's 128-96 loss to the Raptors due to neck soreness, finishing with two points (0-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-6 FT), one rebound and one assist across 14 minutes.
items.story: Mashack finished the first half of Friday's loss but never checked back in during the second after being deemed doubtful to return. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game in Milwaukee.

items.headline: Mashack is doubtful to return to Friday's game against the Raptors due to neck soreness.
items.story: Mashack finished the second quarter but is unlikely to return during the second half. Adama Bal and Dariq Whitehead are candidates to pick up the slack while Mashack is sidelined.

items.headline: Mashack is not in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Knicks on Wednesday.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder made his fifth start of the season against the Suns on Monday, when he played 37 minutes and finished with 14 points, three rebounds, two assists, two steals and one three-pointer in a 131-105 loss. He'll revert to a bench role for Wednesday's contest while Memphis rolls with a starting five of Cedric Coward, Javon Small, GG Jackson, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Cam Spencer.

items.headline: Mashack will start Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: The Grizzlies will be extremely shorthanded Monday, opening the door for Mashack to join the starting five. As a starter this season (three games), the rookie second-rounder has averaged 9.3 points, 3.3 steals, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 27.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) finished Saturday's 125-124 win over the Bulls with 17 points (8-12 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 30 minutes.
items.story: Maschack returned Saturday from a six-game absence due to a left ankle sprain and gave the Grizzlies a much-needed boost off the bench. He finished as the team's third-leading scorer behind Cedric Coward (24 points) and Tyler Burton (18). The two-way guard has averaged 25.1 minutes per game since early February and will continue to operate in an elevated role down the stretch, as the Grizzlies are dealing with a plethora of injuries in addition to being eliminated from playoff contention.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle/nose) is available for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Mashack will shed his questionable tag due to a left ankle sprain and a nasal fracture and return from a six-game absence. Over eight appearances in March, the rookie second-rounder has averaged 6.1 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.9 combined steals-plus-blocks in 25.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle/nose) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Mashack has a legitimate chance at returning from a six-game absence due to a left ankle sprain and, more recently, a nasal fracture. With several of the Grizzlies' guards also on the injury report, Mashack would have plenty of opportunities to capitalize on Saturday if he's upgraded to available.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle/nose) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Mashack will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain, and he's also being listed on the injury report with a nasal fracture. The rookie second-rounder's next opportunity to play will come Saturday against the Bulls.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) is doubtful for Friday's game against Houston.
items.story: Mashack appears headed for another absence while on the mend from a left ankle sprain. Expect confirmation on his availability closer to game time.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle/two-way) is out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs, the Grizzlies announced.
items.story: Mashack had been listed as doubtful for Wednesday's contest due to a left ankle sprain, but Memphis is officially listing his absence as due to his two-way status. It'll be Mashack's fifth consecutive absence. His next chance to play will come Friday against Houston.

items.headline: Mashack is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Mashack appears to be set for a fifth consecutive absence Wednesday. With Javon Small (back) in danger of sitting out, the injury-riddled Grizzlies should turn to Walter Clayton, Cam Spencer and DeJon Jarreau to shoulder the load in the backcourt versus San Antonio.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) won't play Monday in Atlanta.
items.story: This will be Mashack's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's not encouraging that he continues to get ruled out a day in advance of tipoff. For now, he should be considered highly questionable for Wednesday's meeting with the Spurs.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Maschack is set to miss a third consecutive game while recovering from a left ankle sprain, and his next chance to return is Monday against the Hawks. Cam Spencer and Rayan Rupert should continue to operate in expanded roles for as long as Maschack is out of action.

items.headline: Mashack is out for Friday's game against the Celtics due to a sprained left ankle.
items.story: Friday is set to be a second consecutive absence for Mashack, whose next chance to play comes Saturday versus the Hornets. His absence should keep each of Cam Spencer, Rayan Rupert and Javon Small in significant roles against Boston.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Mashack has been downgraded from questionable to out for Wednesday's contest. The rookie guard's absence leaves Javon Small, Walter Clayton and Cam Spencer as the Grizzlies' top bench guards. Mashack's next chance to play will come Friday against Boston in what will be the opening leg of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Mashack (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Mashack is dealing with an ankle sprain, which he could test out during Wednesday's pregame warmups before the Grizzlies reach a decision on his status. The likes of Javon Small, Walter Clayton and Cam Spencer could all have an opportunity to be more involved in the backcourt if Mashack cannot play.

items.headline: Mashack provided three points (1-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 26 minutes during Monday's 132-107 loss to Chicago.
items.story: Despite being one of the more consistent members of the Memphis backcourt, at least in terms of playing time, Mashack continues to offer very little in the way of fantasy upside. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 6.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 26.4 minutes per game. At this point, there are likely more enticing options available on your waiver wire.

items.headline: Mashack notched seven points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three blocks, two assists and two steals over 31 minutes during Monday's 126-115 loss to Brooklyn.
items.story: With the Grizzlies having just eight players available Monday, Mashack was given a considerable workload and put together a solid fantasy line. Memphis should get multiple players back for Tuesday's contest in Philadelphia, but the team's rotations are still likely going to be difficult to project on a game-by-game basis. As a result, Mashack's playing time could be volatile the rest of the way, especially while he faces limitations with his availability. While he remains signed to a two-way contract, Mashack is eligible to play in 13 of the Grizzlies' final 19 contests of the season.

items.headline: Mashack (two-way) will be inactive for Tuesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: With Cedric Coward (knee) and Ty Jerome (thigh) returning Tuesday following multi-game absences, Memphis will opt to hold out Mashack and fellow two-way player Javon Small in an effort to preserve their availability. Mashack is inactive for the second time in 12 games, after he appeared in each of the other 10 contests while averaging 6.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.0 steals, 1.6 assists, 0.8 blocks and 0.7 three-pointers in 23.8 minutes. After Tuesday's contest, the defensive-minded guard will be eligible to suit up for 16 of the Grizzlies' remaining 22 games.

items.headline: Mashack (two-way) was inactive Wednesday in the Grizzlies' 133-112 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Mashack had been a staple in the rotation lately for the injury-plagued Grizzlies, but with Ty Jerome (illness) returning from a one-game absence Wednesday and with 10-day signee Rayan Rupert entering the rotation, Memphis opted to keep the rookie second-round pick in street clothes. The 23-year-old had appeared in each of the Grizzlies' last eight games, averaging 7.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.4 steals, 1.8 assists and 0.9 three-pointers in 24.0 minutes per contest. While he remains signed to a two-way contract, Mashack is eligible to play in 18 of the Grizzlies' final 25 games, so expect Memphis to make him inactive on at least a few more occasions when the team has enough bodies at guard and on the wing.

items.headline: Mashack closed Monday's 123-114 loss to the Kings with four points (2-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 22 minutes.
items.story: The Grizzlies have a ton of injuries right now, and Mashack has seen an uptick in minutes as a result. Over his last four outings, he's seen 24.4 minutes per contest with averages of 6.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks on 31.3 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Mashack is part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against Denver.
items.story: Mashack has played 20 or more minutes in four straight games for the short-handed Grizzlies, and Wednesday's game will mark his second start during that span. He's been stellar on the defensive end, totaling 14 steals in those four games, and he's fresh off a career-high 17 points Monday against Golden State.

items.headline: Mashack tallied 17 points (8-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, two steals and one assist across 22 minutes Monday in the Grizzlies' 114-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: With the Grizzlies being hit by injuries and the availability of multiple players in flux in recent days after Memphis overhauled its roster ahead of last week's trade deadline, Mashack has been able to get a foothold in the rotation of late. Listed at just 6-foot-3 and 197 pounds, Mashack's 6-foot-9 wingspan has allowed him to play on the wing, where he's quickly established a reputation as a disruptive defender. While playing at least 20 minutes in each of the past four games, Mashack has averaged an impressive 3.5 steals per contest. The rookie second-round pick typically isn't as involved on the offensive end, but thanks to some red-hot shooting Monday, he was able to establish a new career-high mark in scoring. Mashack's recent production puts him on the radar as a streaming option for steals, though he could see his minutes get cut significantly if Memphis gets at least one or two of Cedric Coward -- who left Monday's game early with a knee injury -- Santi Aldama (knee) or Walter Clayton (knee) back in action for Wednesday's tilt with the Nuggets.

items.headline: Mashack will be deployed off the bench Monday night against Golden State, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Mashack drew his first start of the season Saturday while the Grizzlies were severely shorthanded, but he'll bump back to a bench role Monday. The Tennessee product hasn't had much involvement when Memphis is healthy, as he's averaging 2.1 points, 1.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 9.8 minutes per game across 10 outings this season.

items.headline: Mashack will start against Portland on Saturday.
items.story: With the Grizzlies extremely shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set, the two-way player will make his first career NBA start. Mashack has logged 20-plus minutes in back-to-back games, averaging 3.5 points, 3.0 assists, 3.0 steals and 2.5 rebounds in 21.5 minutes per tilt during that span.

items.headline: Mashack closed Wednesday's 129-125 win over the Kings with two points (1-2 FG), four rebounds, five assists and three steals across 23 minutes.
items.story: Mashack appeared for the first time in the past 12 games, logging a career-high 23 minutes in the process. Memphis appears to be headed for a rebuild, potentially opening up playing time for a multitude of young pieces. While we aren't running to add Maskack, he is someone to keep an eye on moving forward.

items.headline: Mashack agreed to a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Sunday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The No. 59 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Mashack began the season with the Grizzlies' G League affiliate, the Memphis Hustle. Over five appearances with the Hustle, he has averaged 7.6 points, 5.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 3.2 steals in 31.3 minutes per contest. The 23-year-old will give the Grizzlies some much-needed depth in the backcourt with Javon Small (toe) and Scotty Pippen (toe) facing long-term absences and with Ja Morant (calf) and Ty Jerome (calf) uncertain to be available for the team's next game Tuesday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Mashack (hamstring) is not on the Grizzlies' injury report for Memphis' season opener against the Pelicans on Wednesday.
items.story: Mashack had nursed a hamstring injury during the Las Vegas Summer League, but it appears that he's returned to health. The Grizzlies acquired his draft rights back in July but never signed the second-rounder to a deal during training camp, so the expectation is that he'll begin the campaign with the G League's Memphis Hustle.

items.headline: Mashack (hamstring) is out for Friday's Summer League game against the Celtics, Drew Hill of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Mashack is dealing with hamstring soreness and can be deemed day-to-day. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Trail Blazers. Cam Spencer and Zyon Pullin should take on additional playmaking duties in Mashack's absence.

items.headline: Mashack finished with five points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block across 23 minutes in Monday's 112-111 Summer League loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Mashack displayed his defensive abilities while also tying the game-high mark in assists during his Summer League debut. The Tennessee product averaged 6.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.5 assists in 28.2 minutes per game over 38 appearances during his final collegiate season. The 22-year-old isn't expected to take on a meaningful role for the Grizzlies in 2025-26, but he'll aim to make an impression on the organization during Summer League play.

items.headline: Updating a previous report, the Grizzlies announced Sunday that they have acquired the draft rights to Mashack from the Warriors.
items.story: Mashack was part of a historic seven-team trade, and his draft rights were initially sent from Houston to Golden State. However, the Warriors later traded those rights to the Grizzlies. The Tennessee product averaged 6.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.5 assists in 28.2 minutes per game over 38 appearances during his final collegiate season.

items.headline: The Grizzlies traded Mashack to the Warriors, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Sunday.
items.story: Mashack was selected No. 59 overall by the Grizzlies in the 2025 NBA Draft but will now join the Warriors. The Tennessee product averaged 6.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.5 assists in 28.2 minutes per game over 38 appearances during his final collegiate season.

items.headline: Mashack was selected by the Grizzlies with the No. 59 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft.
items.story: Mashack isn't a player who will impress in the scoring column, but he's a notable defender who should fit in well with the Grizzlies. He averaged 6.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.7 steals in 28.2 minutes over 38 appearances with Tennessee during the 2024-25 campaign.

items.headline: Robinson has been waived by the Chicago Bulls following Monday's 122-108 win over Cleveland.
items.story: The Bulls announced late Monday night that they have waived Robinson. He spent time in the G League with the Windy City Bulls but did not make a regular-season appearance at the NBA level. Robinson will have to clear waivers before becoming a free agent.

items.headline: The Bulls recalled Robinson from the G League's Windy City Bulls on Sunday.
items.story: Robinson is back from the G League ahead of Sunday's game against Denver. He has yet to make his season debut but could see the floor Sunday if Nic Claxton (illness) is ruled out.

items.headline: Robinson signed a training camp contract with the Bulls on Friday.
items.story: After appearing in four regular-season games while on a two-way deal with Orlando in 2025-26, Robinson will compete for a spot on Chicago's regular-season roster for the 2026-27 campaign. He averaged 22.6 points, 10.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.3 steals across 31.9 minutes per game in 20 G League outings between the Osceola Magic and Memphis Hustle last season.

items.headline: Robinson recorded 12 points (6-16 FG, 0-5 3Pt), nine rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 29 minutes in Friday's 83-79 Summer League win over Portland.
items.story: Robinson wasn't very efficient, especially from downtown, though he still finished as Utah's second-leading scorer. Additionally, the big man tied the team high in rebounds while matching the game high in blocks. He scored in double figures in all five of his Las Vegas Summer League appearances, blocking multiple shots in two of them.

items.headline: Robinson finished with 14 points (3-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 18 minutes in Monday's 80-63 Summer League win over Chicago.
items.story: Robinson has bounced around the league since going undrafted in 2022, spending time with Miami, Sacramento and Toronto before most recently suiting up for Orlando during the 2025-26 campaign. In 115 career regular-season appearances, the 26-year-old has averaged 4.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.3 steals over 13.3 minutes. Robinson could find more work in the G League during the 2026-27 campaign. He may also see some minutes with an NBA club, though his opportunities at that level will likely be limited.

items.headline: The Magic waived Robinson on Tuesday.
items.story: Orlando has instead decided to replace Robinson's two-way roster spot with Alex Morales to reinforce its backcourt depth. With Moritz Wagner now healthy, it's likely Robinson, who hasn't appeared in a game since Dec. 26, became more expendable. For the time being, Robinson's next step could entail reporting back to the G League's Osceola Magic for the first time since mid-December to maintain his stock.

items.headline: Robinson posted one rebound and one assist in three minutes during Friday's 120-105 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Robinson appeared for just the fourth time this season, logging three minutes during garbage time. Even with Goga Bitadze (knee) sidelined, Robinson was barely used, indicating how low he is on the depth chart. There is no reason to pay attention to him outside of the deepest fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Robinson will be deployed off the bench Tuesday against the 76ers.
items.story: Robinson drew a rare start Sunday with both Wendell Carter (ankle) and Goga Bitadze (ankle) sidelined. However, Robinson will retreat to his usual bench role now that Orlando's center group has returned to health.

items.headline: Robinson will start Sunday's game against the Celtics, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Robinson enters the starting lineup due to Wendell Carter (ankle) and Goga Bitadze (ankle) being out of the lineup. This will be his first start and just his second appearance at the NBA level this season, having logged just two minutes in his previous appearance.

items.headline: The Magic signed Robinson to a two-way contract Monday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Robinson spent the 2024-25 campaign with the Kings and Raptors, playing in 44 regular-season games. He averaged 6.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.8 assists across 17.5 minutes per game, shooting 44.4 percent from the field. Toronto waived the Fresno State product April 10. He'll have a chance at a fresh start with his new squad.

items.headline: Robinson is in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Hornets on Wednesday, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Robinson will make his eighth start of the season (and sixth since the beginning of March) due to the absence of Jakob Poeltl (hand). Robinson has averaged 10.3 points, 6.5 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 21.8 minutes per game over his last 10 outings.

items.headline: Robinson is not in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Pistons, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl will return to his regular role as the starting center for the Raptors, meaning Robinson will return to the second unit. Robinson has logged 21 appearances since the All-Star break, averaging 10.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and a combined 1.1 steals-plus-blocks per game in that span.

items.headline: Robinson is starting Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Robinson will make his second start in three games, while Jakob Poeltl gets the night off to rest. Robinson has fared well in his previous two starts, scoring in double figures in each showing while totaling 16 rebounds across the two appearances.

items.headline: Robinson isn't in the starting five for Tuesday's game versus the Bulls.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl will reclaim his starting spot from Robinson after sitting out Toronto's previous contest due to rest purposes. Robinson has averaged 8.8 points, 7.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 25.0 minutes across his last 10 appearances coming off the bench.

items.headline: Robinson posted 13 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal over 23 minutes during Sunday's 127-109 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl has been resting every other game for Toronto, and Robinson was able to make the most of his minutes Sunday. In six starts this season, Robinson has shown he can be a serviceable streamer with averages of 12.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 0.7 blocks and 0.5 steals.

items.headline: Robinson is not in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Hornets on Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Robinson started in Wednesday's blowout win over the Nets and finished with 23 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one block in 24 minutes. He'll revert to a bench role Friday due to the return of Jakob Poeltl (rest).

items.headline: Robinson closed with a game-high 23 points (10-14 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and one block in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 116-86 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: The 24-year-old center continues to take advantage of his opportunities with the Raptors. Getting the start with Jakob Poeltl (rest) in street clothes once again, Robinson recorded his fourth double-double of the season, all of which have come in his last eight appearances. During that stretch, he's averaging 13.0 points, 8.8 boards and 3.0 assists in 26.1 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Robinson is part of the first unit for Wednesday's game against the Nets, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl (rest) is out, and Colin Castleton wasn't brought back after his 10-day contract expired, so it'll be Robinson manning the center position Wednesday. In four starts with the Raptors, Robinson is averaging 9.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.0 assists across 25.5 minutes.

items.headline: Robinson contributed two points (1-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), seven rebounds and one assist over 19 minutes before fouling out of Monday's 112-104 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Robinson played fewer than 25 minutes for the fourth straight game, following a stretch in which he saw at least 30 minutes in three consecutive appearances. The Raptors continue to shuffle their rotation on a nightly basis, resulting in unpredictability when it comes to playing time. Colin Castleton is nearing the end of his short-term deal, and should Toronto opt to move on from him, Robinson could benefit. It's all speculation at the moment, but it is a situation worth monitoring given Robinson's per-minute upside.

items.headline: Robinson posted 14 points (4-10 FG, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists and two blocks across 34 minutes off the bench during Friday's 126-118 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: The 24-year-old center has been taking full advantage of his opportunity in the Toronto frontcourt with Jonathan Mogbo (nose) sidelined and Jakob Poeltl (rest) having his workload managed. While Colin Castleton got the start in the middle Friday, Robinson was the more productive player as he delivered his third career double-double, all of which have come in the last three games. Robinson's played more than 20 minutes in eight straight contests (two starts), averaging 10.8 points, 8.4 boards, 2.9 assists and 1.1 blocks over that span while also flashing some potential as a stretch big -- he's gone 5-for-12 from three-point range as well.

items.headline: Robinson finished with 25 points (9-19 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 rebounds and six assists over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 118-105 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Robinson shifted to the bench Wednesday due to the return of Jakob Poeltl. That didn't limit Robinson's impact on the floor, as he played more minutes than Poeltl (17) while finishing second on the team in both rebounding and points. Robinson has registered a double-double in two consecutive games and will look to extend that streak to three against the Pacers on Friday.

items.headline: Robinson will come off the bench during Wednesday's game against the 76ers, Aaron Rose of SI.com reports.
items.story: Robinson started two of the last three games for the Raptors but will resume his reserve role Wednesday against Philadelphia. The 23-year-old big man is averaging 4.0 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game off the bench this season for Toronto.

items.headline: Robinson logged 13 points (5-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists and one block across 26 minutes during Monday's 119-104 victory over Washington.
items.story: Robinson got the start Monday due to the absence of Jakob Poeltl (rest), and he made the most of the opportunity. This was his first double-double of the season, and he also notched season-high marks in both points and rebounds. Robinson might see more time in the starting unit in the coming weeks, but until Poeltl is shut down for the rest of the season, Robinson's inconsistent role prevents him from having a bigger role in most fantasy formats. He's averaging 7.0 points and 7.4 rebounds per game in five outings this month.

items.headline: Robinson will start in Monday's game against Washington, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The big man will receive the starting nod due to Jakob Poeltl (rest) being sidelined. Robinson has started in three outings this season, during which he has averaged 8.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 0.7 steals across 25.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Robinson is not in Toronto's starting lineup against Washington on Saturday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Robinson started against the Jazz on Friday and logged seven points, seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block over 25 minutes. He'll return to a reserve role Saturday due to the return of Jakob Poeltl (rest).

items.headline: Robinson recorded seven points (3-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 25 minutes during Friday's 118-109 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Robinson got the start at center due to the absences of Jakob Poeltl (rest) and Jonathan Mogbo (nose), and while he didn't shoot the ball particularly well, he salvaged his fantasy line by posting solid contributions in other categories. Don't expect Robinson to have a ton of upside going forward, however, as Poeltl should return to the starting lineup when Toronto takes on the Wizards on Saturday.

items.headline: Robinson will be in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Jazz, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Robinson will replace Jakob Poeltl (rest) in the starting lineup during Friday's game against Utah. The 23-year-old big man is averaging 9.5 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game as a starter this season.

items.headline: The Raptors converted Robinson from a two-way contract to a standard one-year deal.
items.story: Toronto will bring Jared Rhoden aboard to fill Robinson's vacated two-way slot. Since he initially joined Toronto on a 10-day contract in January, Robinson has appeared in 17 games while averaging 5.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 15.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Robinson put up 12 points (4-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight boards, three assists and one block in 24 minutes during Friday's 125-115 overtime loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The third-year big man had a solid night with the second unit, stringing together a season high in points with his second-best rebounding game of the year. Although his efficiency from the field left plenty to be desired, it was encouraging to see Robinson take as many shots as he did considering it was his highest mark of the season by a good margin. With the Raptors fairly thin at the center position, Robinson has an opportunity to carve out a real role in head coach Darko Rajakovic's rotation going forward.

items.headline: Robinson is not in the starting lineup in Tuesday's game against Boston, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Jonathan Mogbo will draw his 11th start of the season Tuesday, pushing Robinson to the second unit. Over his last 10 appearances off the bench, Robinson has averaged 4.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 0.4 steals and 0.3 blocks in 14.4 minutes.

items.headline: Robinson will be in the starting lineup for the Raptors in Friday's game against the Heat, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Robinson will be a starter for Toronto on Friday when he takes on the team that gave him his first opportunity at the NBA level, the first time he's been in the starting lineup since Dec. 16, 2023. In 20 games this season, the 23-year-old big man has averaged 3.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.0 per game across 10.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Raptors signed Robinson to a two-way contract Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: After previously signing two 10-day deals with the Raptors, Robinson is now set to split time between Toronto and its G League affiliate for the remainder of the season. Robinson will likely compete for depth minutes in the Raptors' frontcourt when he's with the parent club.

items.headline: Robinson closed Wednesday's 138-107 loss to the Grizzlies with one point (1-2 FT) across three minutes.
items.story: Robinson continues to be used sparingly by the Raptors, having played fewer than 15 minutes in four of the past five games. While it has been slow going for Robinson, there is a chance he could step into a meaningful role in the near future. Jakob Poeltl is sidelined due to a hip injury, while Kelly Olynyk was traded to the Pelicans on Wednesday. Depending on what happens at the trade deadline, Robinson could be the next man up in the middle.

items.headline: Robinson scored 10 points (3-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT) and grabbed six boards in 21 minutes during the 106-82 win over the Wizards on Wednesday.
items.story: The backup big man saw his biggest opportunity amidst his second 10-day contract and put together the best performance of his year. Although he struggled to score efficiently, Robinson still managed to log a season high in points and match his best rebounding performance of the year while he was at it. Despite that, with Kelly Olynyk (calf) listed as day-to-day, Robinson could struggle to even see the court once the former returns, let alone deliver meaningful fantasy performances.

items.headline: The Raptors re-signed Robinson to a second 10-day contract Tuesday, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Robinson's first 10-day contract expired earlier Tuesday, but Toronto will bring him back in advance of their next game Wednesday versus the Wizards. He played in three games during his first 10-day deal, averaging 2.7 points, 2.3 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 11.0 minutes. Robinson will likely serve as the top backup to starting center Jakob Poeltl on Wednesday if Kelly Olynyk (calf) is forced to miss a third straight game.

items.headline: Robinson agreed to a 10-day contract with the Raptors on Saturday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: After being waived by the Kings on Jan. 7, Robinson was quickly able to find a new home with the Raptors, albeit on a short-term deal. In nine games with the Kings, the 24-year-old center averaged 2.1 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 6.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: The Kings recalled Robinson from the G League's Stockton Kings on Friday, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Robinson will rejoin the Kings ahead of Friday's game against the Grizzlies but is unlikely to be featured in the rotation. He made his fourth G League appearance of the season in Stockton's 118-94 win over the Memphis Hustle on Thursday, finishing with 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-3 FT), 10 rebounds and two assists in 27 minutes before fouling out.

items.headline: Sacramento recalled Robinson from the G League's Stockton Kings on Sunday.
items.story: Robinson hasn't played much at the NBA level this season, appearing in just eight games for Sacramento while averaging 6.3 minutes per contest. He's unlikely to be part of the rotation in Monday's game against the Mavericks.

items.headline: Sacramento recalled Robinson from the G League's Stockton Kings on Thursday.
items.story: The third-year center hasn't been a regular part of the rotation at the NBA level this season, so he could make frequent trips to Stockton to pick up playing time in the G League.

items.headline: Robinson was assigned to the G League Stockton Kings on Wednesday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Robinson signed a one-year deal with Sacramento during the offseason but didn't make his NBA debut until Saturday. He's played in two NBA games and is averaging 3.0 points and 3.0 rebounds across 9.5 minutes.

items.headline: The Kings recalled Robinson from the Stockton Kings of the G League on Saturday, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Robinson made his G League debut Friday and recorded 26 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks in 29 minutes of action. However, with Sacramento, Robinson is expected to compete for depth minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Robinson is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Timberwolves due to being on a G League assignment with the Stockton Kings.
items.story: Robinson was previously left off of Sacramento's injury report but has now been added back, indicating he is still with the Kings' G League affiliate. However, it appears that Robinson is no longer plagued by his knee injury, which caused him to miss the beginning of the season.

items.headline: Robinson (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Robinson was assigned to the G League on Thursday, but if he's still with Stockton, he would be marked as such on the NBA's official injury report, which isn't the case. It's unclear if Robinson will actually be available to make his season debut Friday, but it appears that could be a possibility.

items.headline: Robinson (knee) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Robinson has yet to suit up this season while recovering from a left MCL sprain. Even though he's been assigned to the Stockton Kings of the G League to resume his rehab process, he doesn't have a clear timetable to play for Sacramento at the NBA level. His next chance to play would come on Saturday against the Jazz.

items.headline: The Kings assigned Robinson (knee) to the Stockton Kings of the G League on Thursday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Robinson has yet to suit up this season while recovering from a left MCL sprain. However, he has been cleared for contact and is set to continue his rehab process in the G League.

items.headline: Robinson (knee) was cleared to participate in contract drills and scrimmages Monday, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Robinson continues to progress through a left MCL sprain that he suffered during training camp in early October. He'll be re-evaluated in a few days, and barring any setbacks, he could make his 2024-25 regular-season debut in November.

items.headline: Robinson (knee) will not play Monday against the Spurs.
items.story: Robinson has yet to make his 2024-25 debut due to a left MCL sprain he suffered in early October. Consider him doubtful at best for Wednesday's game against the Suns.

items.headline: Robinson (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Robinson hasn't made his 2024-25 regular-season debut due to a left MCL sprain he suffered in early October. His next chance at suiting up will be Monday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Watson ended with eight points (3-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and six blocks over 29 minutes during Monday's 122-108 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Watson is averaging 10.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 0.7 steals and 1.8 blocks in 27.8 minutes this season. His defensive production provides fantasy value despite inconsistent scoring, particularly with Evan Mobley (toe) sidelined.

items.headline: Watson amassed 15 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals in 29 minutes during Friday's 128-119 victory over Indiana.
items.story: After missing the previous game due to a minor back concern, Watson delivered arguably his best performance in eight games over the past three weeks. It's been a somewhat underwhelming start to his career in Cleveland, with Watson struggling to find consistency on either end of the floor. Through 13 games, he has averaged 11.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.2 three-pointers and 2.3 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Watson (back) is available for Friday's game against Indiana, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
