items.story: Watson suffered a back contusion in Monday's win over the Bulls and didn't suit up Wednesday against the Grizzlies. He is cleared to return Friday, meaning Mario Hezonja will revert to a reserve role.

items.headline: Watson (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Watson is looking to fight off a bruised back and suit up Friday. If the swingman is unable to give it a go, his absence could result in a second straight start for Mario Hezonja as well as an expanded role for Meleek Thomas.

items.headline: Watson (back) is out for Wednesday's game versus Memphis.
items.story: Watson's next chance to play comes Friday against Indiana. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) also ruled out, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas should each play significant minutes for Cleveland on Wednesday.

items.headline: Watson (back) is doubtful for Wednesday's game versus Memphis.
items.story: It now sounds like Watson is a long shot to play Wednesday after the Cavaliers initially deemed him questionable. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) ruled out, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas should each play meaningful minutes for Cleveland.

items.headline: Watson (back) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Watson is listed on the injury report with a low back contusion after taking a hard fall in Monday's win over the Bulls. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) doubtful to play Wednesday, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas could all see increased playing time if Watson is ruled out.

items.headline: Watson left Monday's 126-115 win over Chicago due to a head injury and did not return.
items.story: As expected, Watson missed the remainder of Cleveland's victory after taking a nasty fall on a drive to the basket with a little more than five minutes left in the game. He recorded 14 points (5-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and one block across 22 minutes. We'll know more once the Cavs provide an update on Watson's status moving forward.

items.headline: Watson is questionable to return to Monday's game against Chicago after taking a hard fall, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Watson landed awkwardly after driving to the basket and colliding with Jalen Smith, who also left the game on the same play. Watson fell hard on his head/shoulder area and was down for several minutes before being helped back to the locker room.

items.headline: Watson (abdomen) will play in Monday's game against the Bulls, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: The defensive-minded forward is returning Monday from a one-game respite due to abdominal soreness. Watson's return likely takes away a starting spot from either Mario Hezonja or Meleek Thomas.

items.headline: Watson (abdominal soreness) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Watson missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas due to a hamstring injury, but he's now dealing with right abdominal soreness. Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas will see an uptick in minutes if Watson remains sidelined Monday.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Watson will join the rest of Cleveland's regular starters on the inactive list. The 24-year-old's next chance to play will come Monday against Chicago. With Watson sidelined, Jaylon Tyson and Mario Hezonja will likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Watson missed a pair of games at the beginning of November due to a sore right hamstring, and he appears to still be battling problems in that same hamstring. Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja may step into larger roles if Watson is ruled out.

items.headline: Watson supplied seven points (2-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and four blocks over 30 minutes in Wednesday's 115-107 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Despite a shaky shooting performance, Watson made a huge impact defensively with a season-high-tying four swats. The forward has particularly been a strong defensive presence for the Cavaliers, averaging 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.7 blocks per contest in 10 games this season.

items.headline: Watson provided 12 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during Saturday's 109-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Watson racked up three stocks after failing to record any defensive statistics his last time out, and this was his second straight game without committing a single turnover. He's been a steady late-round producer on the season with averages of 11.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.6 blocks per game.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is available for Friday's meeting with the 76ers.
items.story: Watson is back after a two-game absence, and his return will likely shift Tyrese Proctor back to the second unit. Watson is averaging 10.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Friday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Watson has missed his team's last two matchups due to a hamstring issue, and he's in danger of missing a third Friday. More information on his availability should come to light as tipoff nears.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game in Oklahoma City.
items.story: This will be Watson's second straight game on the sidelines, and with Friday's game being the first of a back-to-back set, he may need to spend an additional game on the inactive list. Meleek Thomas, Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja will help pick up the slack in Watson's absence.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is out for Monday's game against the Thunder, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Watson was initially listed as questionable due to right hamstring soreness and will be held out of Monday's contest. His next chance to play will come in Wednesday's rematch against Oklahoma City. In the meantime, Meleek Thomas, Mario Hezonja and Sam Merrill are candidates to see increased burn.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Monday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Watson is battling soreness in his right hamstring, an issue that has put his status for Monday's contest in jeopardy. With Jaylon Tyson (ankle) already ruled out, the Cavs could be thin on the wings, while Sam Merrill, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas would all stand to see increased playing time if Watson is forced to miss his first outing of the season.

items.headline: Watson recorded 22 points (9-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Watson continues to find his way in Cleveland, scoring a season-high 22 points while adding another blocked shot. Through four games, he has averaged 14.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 0.8 three-pointers and 3.3 combined steals and blocks. Assuming anyone who drafted him did so in the later rounds, his production thus far has been more than adequate. Despite a somewhat limited ceiling, Watson should be able to do more than enough on most nights to be rostered in the majority of leagues.

items.headline: Watson ended Monday's 127-125 overtime victory over the Timberwolves with 15 points (5-13 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds, one assist, four blocks and three steals in 37 minutes.
items.story: Watson struggled from beyond the arc but compensated with an outstanding defensive performance, recording seven combined steals and blocks. He also established season highs in scoring, rebounds and blocks while playing a substantial role in Cleveland's overtime victory. His defensive production gives him considerable upside in category-based fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Watson amassed eight points (2-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, two assists, one block and two steals over 30 minutes during Thursday's 114-106 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Watson struggled offensively in his first regular-season appearance with Cleveland, missing all three attempts from beyond the arc while committing five turnovers. His defensive contributions provided some fantasy value, but he'll need to improve his efficiency and rebounding to capitalize on his substantial playing time.

items.headline: Watson recorded six points (3-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 22 minutes as a starter during Sunday's 119-105 preseason win over Orlando.
items.story: Watson struggled with his shot, particularly from beyond the arc, but contributed defensively with a pair of steals. His defensive contributions offer fantasy appeal, though inconsistent offensive production could limit his overall upside.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) will start Thursday's preseason game against the Celtics, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Watson is likely to begin the regular season in a starting role, and he will get the starting nod in Cleveland's preseason opener. He'll be joined in the first unit by Donovan Mitchell, Jaylon Tyson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.

items.headline: Although head coach Kenny Atkinson said Friday that the starting lineup for the beginning of the 2026-27 season is not yet set, he praised Watson's (hamstring) fit in Cleveland and added that "there's a lot of room for growth in his offensive game," Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com reports.
items.story: Watson isn't guaranteed a spot in the starting five immediately but will have the chance to compete for it during training camp. The 24-year-old forward figures to play a sizable role for Cleveland after being acquired from the Nuggets in August in a multi-team deal. Watson was limited to just 54 regular-season appearances (40 starts) in 2025-26 due in large part to a strained hamstring, though he impressed when healthy, averaging career highs in points (14.6), rebounds (4.9), assists (2.1) and steals (0.9) while chipping in 1.1 blocks per game and shooting 41.1 percent from beyond the arc. His length and defensive versatility will be key for a Cleveland team trying to reach the Finals for the first time since the 2017-18 campaign. However, his growth on the offensive end will also be crucial to achieving that objective. Watson is one of the top candidates to join James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen in the starting lineup, but Atkinson isn't ready to commit to that idea just yet, as the Cavaliers have other options like Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson.

items.headline: Watson (hamstring) was traded to Cleveland on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. As parts of the deal, the Clippers will receive Max Strus, and the Nuggets will receive an unprotected first-round pick in 2031 and a second-round pick in 2032.
items.story: The Nuggets extended a qualifying offer at the end of July, but the team will now move on from Watson, who averaged a career-high 14.6 points, 2.1 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks across 29.6 minutes in 54 regular-season games in 2026.  The 23-year-old, who also agreed to a four-year, $88 million contract with Cleveland, could make an immediate impact for a team looking to compete in a loaded Eastern Conference. While it's unknown if Watson will start at the three spot, he will presumably have a prominent role regardless.

items.headline: The Nuggets offered Watson (hamstring) $70 million over five seasons, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: This offer comes in well below the $25 million annually that Watson was seeking. Christian Braun previously received a five-year, $125 million deal from the Nuggets and was clearly outplayed by Watson in 2025-26, but Denver holds the leverage. Watson is a restricted free agent, and his top suitors currently don't have the cap space to sign him.

items.headline: The Nuggets tendered a qualifying offer to Watson (hamstring) on Monday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: With tons of injuries in Denver last season, Watson broke out, averaging 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.9 steals per game on 49/41/73 shooting splits. However, the injury bug also hit Watson, who missed 31 of the Nuggets' final 36 games, including every postseason contest. Given his strong performance, Watson is set for a major raise, assuming he's fully healthy during free agency.

items.headline: Dieng (finger) is available for Monday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Dieng underwent a procedure last Monday to repair a fractured left finger, though he will shed his questionable tag and return from a four-game absence to face Toronto. Through 10 regular-season appearances (one start), he's averaging 3.9 points in 12.2 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Dieng (finger) is questionable for Monday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Dieng has missed the last four games while recovering from a procedure to repair a fractured left finger. He reportedly underwent surgery Nov. 16, so his questionable status is somewhat shocking considering it's only been one week. Still, Milwaukee will provide another update prior to tip.

items.headline: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
items.story: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

items.headline: Dieng (finger) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Hawks.
items.story: Dieng was initially listed on the injury report with what was classified as a sprain. Since then, the diagnosis was changed to a fractured left finger. Dieng has appeared in 10 games for the Bucks during the 2026-27 campaign, including one start, averaging 3.9 points, 1.2 rebounds and 1.0 assists across 12.2 minutes per outing. While a sprain could have kept the 23-year-old off the floor for a stretch, there's a chance he will be out even longer, though the team will presumably provide more clarity on his health at some point. Until that happens, Dieng should be considered at least day-to-day.

items.headline: Dieng (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Dieng is dealing with a left finger sprain and will miss Sunday's contest after logging just five minutes while starting Friday's loss to the Magic. Nate Ament could see a slight bump in minutes in Dieng's stead.

items.headline: Dieng finished with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over five minutes during Friday's 107-99 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Dieng moved into the starting lineup Friday, although he saw just five minutes of playing time. Milwaukee continues to toy with its rotation, having won just one of its first 13 games. Dieng had some intriguing performances down the stretch during the 2025-26 season but has been unable to produce anything of note so far this season. He is currently well outside the top 300 in standard leagues, averaging 3.9 points and 1.2 rebounds in 12.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dieng is in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Magic.
items.story: The Bucks continue to mix and match their options in the first unit, replacing Nate Ament with Dieng on Friday. Dieng made 20 regular-season starts for Milwaukee a year ago, averaging 12.5 points, 5.1 rebounds and 4.7 assists in 30.6 minutes per game during that stretch.

items.headline: Dieng accumulated 10 points (3-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound in 15 minutes during Sunday's 117-97 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Dieng popped for a season-high 10 points in Sunday's rout. He's likely to need the rebuilding Bucks to pull the trigger on a trade involving veteran center Myles Turner in order to muster consistent fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Dieng recorded four points (2-9 FG, 0-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 24 minutes off the bench during Friday's 128-127 preseason win over the Pacers in overtime.
items.story: Dieng moved to the bench Friday after starting Wednesday's loss to Chicago. He struggled mightily with efficiency in Milwaukee's preseason finale, missing all six of his three-point tries. The 23-year-old forward is expected to compete with Gary Trent and Nate Ament (ankle) for minutes to begin the regular season.

items.headline: Dieng registered 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt), 11 rebounds, four assists and one block across 27 minutes in Wednesday's 125-104 preseason loss to Chicago.
items.story: Dieng led Milwaukee with 11 rebounds and added four assists, showcasing his versatility despite an inefficient shooting performance. He also committed four turnovers, but his activity on the glass and ability to contribute as a passer stood out. The 23-year-old forward will aim to translate that all-around production into a consistent role once the regular season begins.

items.headline: Dieng is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Chicago.
items.story: With several Milwaukee regulars resting, Dieng will move into the starting lineup Wednesday. In 30 regular-season appearances (20 starts) with the Bucks last season, the young forward averaged 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists in 26.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dieng was a DNP-CD during Monday's 116-97 preseason loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Dieng was available but didn't see the floor in Milwaukee's first preseason contest. The 23-year-old will look to earn a role in a crowded Bucks frontcourt during the remainder of the preseason.

items.headline: Dieng signed a three-year, $17.5 million contract with the Bucks on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After landing with the Bucks ahead of last season's trade deadline, Dieng will return to Milwaukee on a multi-year pact. The versatile forward averaged 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.5 triples and 0.8 steals in 26.9 minutes per contest across 30 regular-season games (20 starts) with the Bucks last season, and he should continue seeing significant playing time with the rebuilding club.

items.headline: The Bucks declined to extend a qualifying offer to Dieng, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports Monday.
items.story: Dieng will enter unrestricted free agency, though Scotto added that the Bucks still have significant interest in re-signing the versatile forward. After spending three-plus seasons with the Thunder to begin his career, the 23-year-old was traded multiple times ahead of last season's deadline. He ended up on the Bucks, with whom he averaged 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 0.8 steals in 26.9 minutes per contest across 30 regular-season games (20 starts).

items.headline: Dieng should receive every opportunity to earn consistent rotation minutes now that Milwaukee has fully embraced a rebuilding direction, Amir Motameni of SI.com reports.
items.story: The former lottery pick flashed intriguing upside after arriving late last season, and the Bucks can afford to prioritize his development alongside fellow youngsters Brayden Burries, Nate Ament, Kel'el Ware and Jaime Jaquez. Increased competition at forward exists, but Milwaukee's emphasis on evaluating its young core should work in Dieng's favor with Giannis Antetokounmpo out of the picture.

items.headline: Dieng supplied 11 points (4-12 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 41 minutes during Sunday's 126-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Following his trade from the Thunder, Dieng immediately became more involved for the rebuilding Bucks. Across 30 games with his new team, Dieng played 26.8 minutes per contest with 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 0.8 steals and 1.5 three-pointers on 42.3 percent shooting from the field. He could have a sizable role next season depending on what happens with Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee).

items.headline: Dieng ended with 12 points (5-12 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds and 12 assists over 37 minutes during Friday's 125-108 win over the Nets.
items.story: Dieng came away with his fifth double-double of the campaign Friday. After getting lost in the shuffle with the defending-champion Thunder earlier in the season, the fourth-year forward carved out a solid role following a trade to the Bucks. Over his last six contests, Dieng has averaged 16.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 6.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dieng closed with 17 points (6-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-7 FT), nine rebounds and six assists in 31 minutes during Sunday's 131-115 victory over Memphis.
items.story: Dieng's shooting comes and goes, but he's making a strong impression on the coaching staff. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 14.4 points, 5.8 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.0 three-pointers on 39.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dieng finished Wednesday's 119-113 loss to the Rockets with 36 points (15-31 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 10 assists, seven rebounds and one steal across 45 minutes.
items.story: Dieng struggled from three-point range but made the most of his increased opportunities with Milwaukee shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set. The 22-year-old forward returned to the first unit after coming off the bench in Tuesday's win over Dallas, and he dropped a game- and career-high 36 points. The fourth-year pro also dished out a game- and career-best 10 dimes, marking his sixth consecutive contest with at least four assists. Dieng should continue to see significant burn for the Bucks, who have already been eliminated from playoff contention and will likely want an extended look at him before he enters restricted free agency this summer.

items.headline: Dieng will start Wednesday's game against the Rockets, per Lachard Binkley of SI.com.
items.story: After shifting to the bench for Tuesday's win over the Mavericks upon Kyle Kuzma's (Achilles) return, Dieng will immediately rejoin the first unit for the second leg of Milwaukee's back-to-back set. The 22-year-old forward remained highly productive despite his brief reserve role Tuesday, posting an 11-point, 10-rebound double-double across 29 minutes. With Kuzma officially sidelined again, Dieng is primed for a heavy workload.

items.headline: Dieng finished with 11 points (4-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Tuesday's 123-99 victory over Dallas.
items.story: Dieng moved to the bench due to the return of Kyle Kuzma (Achilles), but the former still posted an impressive double-double. Dieng is finally getting consistent minutes at the NBA level, and he's proving he can perform at a decent level. Over his last eight games (six starts), Dieng is averaging 12.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals across 29.4 minutes per game while posting double-digit scoring numbers in six of those outings. Even if he ends the regular season coming off the bench, he's an option worth keeping close tabs on as a potential streamer.

items.headline: Dieng won't start Tuesday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Dieng started Milwaukee's last six games. However, with Kyle Kuzma (Achilles) back in the lineup, the 22-year-old will head back to the bench. With that said, Dieng was still productive in his last appearance as a reserve, finishing with 19 points, five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 30 minutes in the 123-116 loss to the Cavaliers on March 17.

items.headline: Dieng logged 12 points (5-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, five assists and four steals across 36 minutes during Saturday's 127-95 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Making his fifth straight start, Dieng set a new career high in steals while scoring in double digits for the ninth time in his last 12 contests (11 starts). Over that latter stretch, the fourth-year forward is averaging 10.8 points, 4.2 boards, 3.3 assists, 1.9 threes and 0.8 steals as he takes on a much bigger role in the Bucks' injury-depleted rotation.

items.headline: Dieng closed with 16 points (7-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists and one block over 33 minutes during Wednesday's 130-99 loss to Portland.
items.story: While Dieng had trouble finding his way with Oklahoma City, he's moved into a significant role since joining the Bucks. He's now started 11 games for Milwaukee, averaging 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 28.9 minutes per contest while shooting 40.8 percent from deep as a member of the first unit.

items.headline: Dieng supplied 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), one rebound, one assist, one block and two steals across 25 minutes during Thursday's 128-96 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Returning to the starting five after he came off the bench Tuesday in his return from a two-game absence due to an illness, Dieng made a minor splash at both ends of the court, and his 25 minutes actually led the Bucks. Dieng has drained multiple threes in six of his eight appearances in March (seven starts), averaging 10.5 points, 4.1 boards, 2.8 assists and 2.3 threes in 27.6 minutes while shooting 47.4 percent from long distance.

items.headline: Dieng is in the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup with the Jazz.
items.story: Joining Dieng in the first unit for Thursday's game will be Ryan Rollins, AJ Green, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. As a starter this season (seven games), Dieng owns averages of 10.1 points, 5.4 boards, 3.7 assists, 1.9 triples and 0.7 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Dieng notched 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 0-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 123-116 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: This was a terrific showing for Dieng, and he's absolutely trending up in fantasy hoops with the Bucks' playoff hopes fading. Plus, there's been reports that the team is considering shutting down Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) for the remainder of the season.

items.headline: Dieng (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against Cleveland, per Eric Nehm of The Athletic.
items.story: Dieng has missed the last two games because of an illness. Fortunately, he'll return on a night when the Bucks will be without Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Myles Turner (calf). To make matters worse, Ryan Rollins (illness) remains questionable. Dieng has averaged 8.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 0.7 steals over seven March appearances. However, the 22-year-old could be more productive with Antetokounmpo, Turner and possibly Rollins sidelined.

items.headline: Dieng (illness) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Dieng is at risk of missing a third consecutive contest due to an illness. Either Ryan Rollins or AJ Green would start in the backcourt if Dieng isn't feeling well enough to give it a go Tuesday, while Kyle Kuzma would also see a boost in streaming appeal in this scenario.

items.headline: Dieng (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pacers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Dieng will end up missing both ends of the Bucks' back-to-back set while battling through an illness, and his next chance to play is Tuesday against the Cavaliers. With Kevin Porter (knee) also sidelined, the Bucks will turn to Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Taurean Prince to each take on elevated roles against Indiana.

items.headline: Dieng (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Dieng sat out Saturday's 122-99 loss against the Hawks, but there is a chance that he could return for the back leg of the Bucks' back-to-back set Sunday. Kevin Porter (knee) has already been ruled out, so Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Taurean Prince would be in line for even more minutes if Dieng is also unavailable.

items.headline: Dieng is out for Saturday's game against the Hawks due to an illness, per Eric Nehm of The Athletic.
items.story: After leaving Thursday's loss to the Heat with the ailment, Dieng isn't feeling well enough to play Saturday and faces a short turnaround for Sunday's matchup with Indiana. His absence vacates a spot in the Bucks' starting lineup at shooting guard, which is likely to be filled by either AJ Green or Ryan Rollins.

items.headline: Dieng (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: An illness caused Dieng to depart during the first half of Thursday's loss to the Heat, when he played 14 minutes and finished with zero points. He's started each of the Bucks' last six games, and if he's unable to play in Saturday's matinee, then Taurean Prince, AJ Green and Gary Trent would be the top candidates to enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Dieng has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game against the Heat due to an illness. He'll end the night with zero points (0-2 FG) in 14 minutes.
items.story: It was clear from the beginning of the game that Dieng wasn't feeling like himself, as he was shut down after failing to record a stat outside of two missed field-goal attempts. This doesn't appear to be a long-term concern for the 2022 first-round pick, who can be considered day-to-day leading up to Saturday's matchup with Atlanta.

items.headline: Dieng contributed 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds, four assists and one steal in 37 minutes during Tuesday's 129-114 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Dieng made the most of his limited opportunities on the offensive end and bounced back from a sluggish two-point showing Sunday against Orlando. He also recorded his second double-double of the season by securing double-digit boards. Dieng should continue to see opportunities with the first unit as long as he keeps up this recent stretch of solid play.

items.headline: Dieng amassed 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt), eight rebounds and nine assists across 32 minutes during Saturday's 113-99 win over Utah.
items.story: Dieng has been a standout performer for the Bucks of late, and the versatile forward was just two rebounds and one assist away from recording a triple-double. Dieng has scored in double digits in each of his past three starts, and displays such as Saturday's will only strengthen his case to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Dieng totaled 14 points (6-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt) and four rebounds over 28 minutes during Wednesday's 131-113 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Dieng has started in the last two games for the Bucks, scoring in double digits both times while shooting a combined 11-for-24 from the field. Dieng was recently praised by head coach Doc Rivers, and while he might continue to see minutes in a starting role, his fantasy upside will be modest.

items.headline: Dieng is starting Monday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Dieng will start Monday as the the Bucks have elected to shake up the first five with Giannis Antetokounmpo back on the floor. Dieng's last start dates back to Feb. 12 against the Thunder, when he finished with 11 points, six rebounds, one steal and four blocks in 36 minutes.

items.headline: Dieng will come off the bench for Friday's game in New Orleans.
items.story: With Ryan Rollins back in action, Dieng will shift to the second unit, and it'll be interesting to see what his minutes look like in the reserve role. If Dieng isn't able to earn 20-plus minutes as a member of the second unit, it'll be difficult for him to offer fantasy-worthy production.

items.headline: Dieng totaled 19 points (7-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, one steal and four blocks in 36 minutes during Thursday's 110-93 victory over the Thunder.
items.story: Dieng stepped into the starting lineup for the first time this season while the Bucks were forced to navigate without Ryan Rollins (foot) and Myles Turner (calf). Dieng came through in a big way, as he led Milwaukee in scoring and posted his first double-double of the 2025-26 campaign. The 22-year-old got off to a slow start with his new club, finishing with two points, one rebound and one steal across five minutes in his Bucks debut, but he's played well in two games since.

items.headline: Dieng is starting Thursday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Dieng will draw his first opportunity to start Thursday with both Ryan Rollins (foot) and Myles Turner (calf) out of action. Dieng performed well in his last game Wednesday against the Magic, finishing with 17 points in 23 minutes.

items.headline: Dieng recorded 17 points (6-10 FG, 5-8 3Pt) and three rebounds across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 116-108 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Making his second appearance with the Bucks, Dieng made a strong impression on the coaching staff. Player development could be a focus for the Bucks after the All-Star break barring a sudden turnaround, making Dieng a player to monitor in deeper formats.

items.headline: Dieng (recently traded) is available for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: The Bucks were sending mixed signals regarding Dieng's availability, but it seems he'll be in uniform Friday after all. It's not a lock he'll enter the game in a significant capacity, though.

items.headline: Dieng (recently traded) is out for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: After not including Dieng on their initial game-day injury report, the Bucks have added the 22-year-old forward and listed him as out for Friday. His next chance to make his Milwaukee debut comes during Monday's meeting in Orlando against the Magic.

items.headline: Dieng (recently traded) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: After being acquired from the Bulls on Thursday, Dieng's absence from Friday's injury report points to him being ready for his Bucks debut. Although he may be available off the bench, it's not yet clear if Dieng will immediately mix into the Milwaukee frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Green racked up nine points (3-3 FG, 3-3 3Pt) in 12 minutes during Saturday's 132-129 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Green was perfect from the field in his 12 minutes off the bench, as he's now 6-for-8 (75 percent) on three-pointers over his last two outings. Despite the efficiency from behind the arc, Green's playing time was less than 15 minutes for the sixth straight contest. Milwaukee has lost 13 consecutive games, so the sharpshooter's minutes are likely to continue fluctuating.

items.headline: Green racked up zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two assists in eight minutes during Friday's 107-99 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Green logged just eight minutes for a third consecutive contest as head coach Taylor Jenkins continues to focus on finding minutes for the team's younger guys. The sharpshooter could be a viable streaming option for triples if he regains a consistent role, though it's concerning to see his playing time dip.

items.headline: Green closed with 12 points (4-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound and one block over 24 minutes off the bench during Friday's 121-107 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: The fifth-year guard has been locked in from downtown to begin November. Green has his two best scoring performances on the young season in the first three games of the month, averaging 10.0 points, 3.0 threes, 2.0 boards and 2.0 assists in 22.7 minutes while shooting an impressive 45.0 percent (9-for-20) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Green posted 13 points (4-8 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 24 minutes during Monday's 112-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Green provided an efficient perimeter scoring boost, accounting for four of Milwaukee's 15 made three-pointers while finishing with a team-best plus-12 rating. He played more minutes than starting forward Kyle Kuzma, who struggled throughout the contest. Green remains a useful specialist for managers seeking three-pointers, though his limited contributions outside scoring and long-range shooting cap his overall fantasy upside.

items.headline: Green finished Saturday's 127-116 loss to the 76ers with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt) and three rebounds across 19 minutes.
items.story: Green provided a spark off the bench once again, scoring 11 points and shooting 3-for-6 from downtown for a second consecutive contest. He's offered a scoring punch for the Bucks through three regular-season games, averaging 9.3 points, 2.7 triples and 1.3 rebounds in 17.0 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Green finished with nine points (3-5 FG, 3-5 3Pt) and two rebounds across 19 minutes in Friday's 128-127 preseason overtime win over Indiana.
items.story: Green didn't play against the Bulls on Wednesday, but he was on the court to finish the preseason. He shot the ball well, though he didn't add much beyond his contributions from behind the three-point line. The 27-year-old is coming off his most productive season in 2025-26, averaging 10.4 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists, all career highs, over 29.1 minutes per contest in 78 regular-season games. He also shot over 40.0 percent from deep for the fourth consecutive season.

items.headline: Green (rest) won't play in Wednesday's preseason game against Chicago, Cameron Ezeir of CBS58 reports.
items.story: Green has played in two of Milwaukee's preseason contests. His final opportunity to get on the floor before the start of the 2026-27 campaign will come Friday in Indiana.

items.headline: Green (coach's decision) was inactive for Wednesday's 128-126 preseason victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Green joined several Milwaukee rotation players on the inactive list Wednesday. His absence was not attributed to an injury, and his next opportunity to take the floor will come Sunday against Charlotte.

items.headline: Green should continue playing a significant role despite Milwaukee's influx of young wings, Amir Motameni of SI.com reports.
items.story: The sharpshooter established himself as one of the league's better perimeter specialists last season, and his floor spacing should remain valuable as the Bucks integrate Brayden Burries and Nate Ament into the rotation. While the rookies could eventually eat into his minutes, Green projects to remain one of Milwaukee's most reliable veterans on the wing following the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.

items.headline: Green notched 19 points (7-16 FG, 5-14 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 36 minutes during Sunday's 126-106 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Green sank five shots beyond the arc and overtook Bucks Hall-of-Famer Ray Allen with 232 career three-pointers, setting a team record in the category. The Bucks locked in the fourth-year pro to a four-year, $45M deal back in October, and the Northern Iowa product is expected to helm Milwaukee's backcourt for the foreseeable future. Green played 78 games this season, averaging 10.4 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists. The sharpshooter also averaged 7.1 three-point attempts per game with a conversion rate of 41.9 percent.

items.headline: Green finished with 35 points (11-18 FG, 11-16 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals across 41 minutes in Friday's 125-108 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Green drained 10 three-point shots combined in his last two appearances heading into Friday night. However, the 26-year-old had 11 in the win over the Nets, setting a new franchise record, surpassing Ray Allen and Damian Lillard (10). With the Bucks down several of their top offensive contributors of late, Green has taken advantage by posting double-digit scoring performances in five of his last six games while shooting 48.6 percent from deep during that span.

items.headline: Green posted 20 points (6-13 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 39 minutes during Tuesday's 96-90 loss to Brooklyn.
items.story: Green continues to deliver elite three-point shooting numbers for an underwhelming Bucks squad that has nothing to play for in the final days of the regular season. Green has drained five or more threes in three of his last four games, and he should continue to benefit from an expanded role on offense. He's scored at least 15 points in five of his last six appearances, averaging 14.7 points per game and shooting 46.2 percent from deep over that stretch.

items.headline: Green posted 15 points (5-15 FG, 5-13 3Pt), eight rebounds and two assists in 46 minutes during Wednesday's 119-113 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Green remains a reliable outside threat, and while he doesn't score enough to lead the Bucks offensively on a game-to-game basis, it's worth noting that he's outstanding in category-based leagues due to his three-point shooting numbers. Green has drained multiple threes in nine of his last 11 games, a stretch in which he's averaging 9.9 points per game but shooting an impressive 41.2 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Green is in the Bucks' starting lineup against the Rockets on Wednesday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: Green has started for the majority of the 2025-26 regular season, though he's come off the bench in 10 of the Bucks' last 14 games. He's played well of late, accumulating 32 points while shooting 50.0 percent from the field over his last two games. With the club shorthanded in the second half of this back-to-back set, he'll make his way back into Milwaukee's starting lineup Wednesday, joining Ousmane Dieng, Pete Nance, Jericho Sims and Gary Trent.

items.headline: Green is not in the Bucks' starting lineup against the Spurs on Saturday.
items.story: Green will shift to the bench for Saturday's game while Gary Trent enters the starting five. Green has come off the bench in seven of his last 11 outings, and over that span, he has averaged 6.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.8 threes over 21.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green will start Wednesday against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Ryan Rollins, Ousmane Dieng, Jericho Sims and Pete Nance will join Green in the first unit for Wednesday's game. As a starter this season, Green owns averages of 9.9 points, 1.9 assists and 2.9 triples per contest.

items.headline: Green racked up 15 points (4-5 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one rebound and two assists in 21 minutes off the bench during Monday's 129-96 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: It was Green's best scoring effort since Feb. 25, as the fourth-year guard had another big night from beyond the arc. He's hit multiple three-pointers in five of the last six games, but Green offers little else from a fantasy perspective, averaging 8.3 points, 2.8 boards, 2.3 threes and 1.0 assists in 20.2 minutes over that stretch.

items.headline: Green will come off the bench Saturday against the Suns.
items.story: The Bucks will mix things up Saturday and move Taurean Prince into the first unit. Green is likely to maintain a sizable role despite this news.

items.headline: Green will start Thursday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: With Kevin Porter (knee) unavailable, Green will rejoin the first unit against Utah. As a starter this season (59 games), the sharpshooter has averaged 10.0 points, 2.9 triples, 2.5 rebounds and 1.9 assists while shooting 41.2 percent from beyond the arc in 29.8 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Green isn't in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Green ran with the first unit Sunday against Indiana, but he'll retreat to a bench role Tuesday as the Bucks elect to roll with Kevin Porter and Ryan Rollins in the backcourt. Green is averaging 5.0 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in his last three appearances as a reserve.

items.headline: Green will start Sunday against the Pacers.
items.story: Joining Green on the first unit for Sunday's game will be Ryan Rollins, Kyle Kuzma, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Myles Turner. As a starter this season, Green owns averages of 10.0 points, 1.9 assists and 2.9 triples per contest on 42/41/82 shooting splits.

items.headline: Green will not start Tuesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: With Kyle Kuzma (back) returning to the lineup after a one-game absence, Green will revert to a bench role. During his lone appearance off the bench this season in Saturday's win over Utah, the sharpshooter posted seven points, one rebound and one assist across 21 minutes.

items.headline: Green will start Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Green came off the bench for the first time this season during Saturday's win over the Jazz, though he'll return to the first unit Sunday with Giannis Antetokounmpo (calf), Kevin Porter (knee) and Kyle Kuzma (back) all sidelined. Over his last 10 starts, Green has averaged 7.6 points, 2.2 triples, 2.0 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 29.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green will come off the bench for Saturday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: With the Bucks struggling, the team will insert Kyle Kuzma into the first unit. Despite this move, Green figures to maintain a sizable role for the Bucks as their top perimeter shooter.

items.headline: Green racked up 13 points (4-11 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds and two assists across 30 minutes during Sunday's 120-97 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The fourth-year wing led all Milwaukee starters in scoring during the rout. Green has drained multiple three-pointers in four straight games and 10 of the last 12, but he doesn't offer much else but long-range shooting -- over that latter stretch, he's averaging just 11.3 points, 3.3 threes, 2.7 boards and 2.1 assists.

items.headline: Green ended Sunday's 122-94 loss to the Raptors with three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 26 minutes.
items.story: Despite considerable workloads, Green can't seem to generate much fantasy appeal. Over his last five games, he's seeing 31.2 minutes per contest with 8.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.4 three-pointers on 34.2 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Green recorded 17 points (6-14 FG, 5-11 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one steal over 38 minutes during Thursday's 110-93 victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Green tallied 15 of his 17 points from beyond the arc and finished second on his team in scoring behind Ousmane Dieng's 19-point night. Green has now scored in double figures in five of his last six matchups and is averaging 14.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists during this stretch.

items.headline: Green recorded 15 points (4-8 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds and one assist over 32 minutes during Monday's 118-99 loss to the Magic.
items.story: The recent scoring surge for Green continues as he scored in double figures for a fourth straight game. Over that stretch, Green is averaging 16.5 points and 5.3 made threes per game. His usage wasn't impacted by the newly-signed Cam Thomas making his Bucks debut. It's hard to imagine Green taking a backseat in the rotation while shooting this well from the field.

items.headline: Green amassed 17 points (6-11 FG, 5-9 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 131-115 win over the Bulls.
items.story: After a quiet three-game stretch in which Green had scored just 13 combined points, the fourth-year guard found his rhythm again from long distance. Green has supplied multiple three-pointers in nine of his last 11 games, averaging 10.4 points, 3.0 threes, 2.3 boards and 2.0 assists over that span while shooting 44.6 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Green closed with three points (1-5 FG, 1-5 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 29 minutes during Sunday's 107-79 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Green had another lackluster performance, scoring in single digits for a third straight game. The fourth-year wing has struggled of late, shooting just 29.4 percent from the field while averaging 4.3 points, 2.3 assists and 2.0 rebounds in 31.7 minutes per tilt over that three-game span. If Green's struggles persist, a move to the second unit is not out of the question once Kevin Porter (oblique) returns.

items.headline: Green (illness) isn't listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Green is set to return Tuesday from a one-game absence due to an illness. The 26-year-old sharpshooter has averaged 10.8 points, 3.1 three-pointers, 2.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists across 32.2 minutes per tilt over nine January appearances thus far.

items.headline: Green (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Green missed Friday's game due to illness, and he's still not recovered from the sickness. The 26-year-old guard's absence allowed for Gary Harris to draw a start, and Harris would likely remain in the first unit if Green can't play Sunday.

items.headline: Green (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Nuggets, Eric Nehm of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Green was a late addition to the injury report Friday and won't suit up due to an illness. The sharpshooter's next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Mavericks. With Gary Trent (illness) and Kevin Porter (oblique) also unavailable, Gary Harris, Kyle Kuzma and Cole Anthony are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Green (illness) is questionable  for Friday's game against Denver.
items.story: It appears that Green woke up under the weather Friday morning, jeopardizing his status. With Gary Trent managing an illness of his own, Cole Anthony and Gary Harris could be thrust into a big role in the Milwaukee backcourt Friday.

items.headline: Green produced 18 points (6-12 FG, 6-12 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 42 minutes during Monday's 112-110 victory over the Hawks.
items.story: The six made three-pointers tied his season high, a mark he'd most recently reached Dec. 26 against the Grizzlies. Green's drained multiple treys in seven of eight January games, averaging 10.3 points, 3.0 threes, 2.1 boards and 2.0 assists on the month.

items.headline: Green contributed 14 points (5-8 FG, 4-7 3Pt), five rebounds and four assists over 37 minutes during Sunday's 108-104 loss to Denver.
items.story: After a tough December, Green is beginning to turn the corner for Milwaukee. Over his last three outings, the sharpshooter is hitting 56.5 percent from the field for averages of 12.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 3.3 three-pointers in 33.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green logged one point (0-6 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 32 minutes during Sunday's 115-98 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Green is stuck in a shooting slump and is going to be hard to trust in most fantasy formats until he finds his rhythm. Over his last seven games, he's shooting 31.1 percent from the field with averages of 8.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 31.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green finished Friday's 125-104 loss to the Grizzlies with 20 points (7-13 FG, 6-11 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: As has been the trend all season long, Green made most of his damage from three-point range, and he tied his previous season-best scoring mark, which was established on Oct. 26 in a loss to the Cavaliers. Green is an outstanding three-point shooter, and he excels in that category for fantasy purposes. He's drained five or more threes in six different games this season.

items.headline: Green (shoulder) tallied five points (2-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 24 minutes in Thursday's 111-105 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Green slotted back into a starting role on the wing Thursday after he had missed the Bucks' previous three games while recovering from an AC joint sprain in his left shoulder. After knocking down at least four three-pointers in each of his previous five non-injury-shortened starts, Green didn't see many spot-up opportunities from the perimeter during his time on the court, but both his scoring output and minutes could pick up a bit during the Bucks' upcoming five-game road trip. Milwaukee is expected to remain without Giannis Antetokounmpo (calf) for all of those contests and will need several supporting players like Green to increase their production in his absence.

items.headline: Tyson (ankle) is available and will come off the bench Monday against the Bulls, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
