Vincent will likely revert to a bench role Sunday against the 76ers if one or both of Doncic and James are cleared to return.

items.headline: Vincent is in the starting lineup for Thursday's game in Toronto, Ryan Ward of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Vincent is back in the starting lineup with Luka Doncic (personal) taking the night off, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Austin Reaves, LeBron James, Rui Hachimura and Deandre Ayton. Over four starts this season, Vincent has posted averages of 4.3 points and 2.8 assists per game.

items.headline: Vincent won't start Monday against the Suns, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: With LeBron James (foot) back in action, Vincent will retreat to the second unit. Over four outings off the bench this season, the 29-year-old guard has averaged 3.8 points while shooting 55.6 percent from the field in 19.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Vincent will start Sunday's game against the Pelicans, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Vincent gets the start due to LeBron James (foot) being out of the lineup. In three starts this season, Vincent holds averages of 3.7 points, 2.3 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 24.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) finished with six points (2-3 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and one assist in 16 minutes Tuesday in the Lakers' 140-126 win over the Jazz.
items.story: While LeBron James' (sciatica) season debut captured most of the headlines, Vincent's return from an extended absence of his own helped bring the Los Angeles rotation back to full strength for the first time in 2025-26. Vincent had started in the Lakers' first three games before going down with a slight ligament tear and sprain of his left ankle, but James' return relegated the veteran guard to the bench. Vincent knocked down a couple of outside shots and was a plus-15 during his time on the court, but he's unlikely to be in line for much more than the 16 minutes he received Tuesday while the Lakers have all of their key guards and wings available.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Tuesday is set to be Vincent's first appearance since Oct. 26 in Sacramento. The veteran guard is in line to play a reserve role in the Lakers' backcourt, likely leaving him with minimal fantasy appeal. For the year, Vincent has averaged 3.7 points, 2.3 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 24.0 minutes per game over three outings.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Vincent hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left ankle sprain, though he appears to be nearing a return to game action. While the 29-year-old guard will likely face restrictions whenever he is cleared to play, his return could mean fewer minutes for Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) has been ramping up his on-court work, but he still hasn't been cleared for one-on-one work or contact drills, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Vincent is traveling with the Lakers on their current five-game road trip, which shows progress, but until he's going through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we can assume he's still not close to returning. While head coach JJ Redick said he hoped to have Vincent back closer to the three-week mark of his initial 2-4 week timetable, which would hint at a potential Nov. 18 return date, that seems unlikely given there won't be much practice time while the team is traveling for the next week.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) is expected to miss two to four weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Vincent suffered a left ankle sprain Sunday against the Kings and is expected to miss multiple weeks while recovering. With both him and Luka Doncic (finger) sidelined for multiple games and Marcus Smart (quadriceps) also banged up, the depleted Lakers backcourt could give playing time to Bronny James, along with increased wing minutes for Jake LaRavia and Dalton Knecht.

items.headline: Vincent (ankle) will not play Monday against Portland, Khobi Price of The Orange County Registerreports.
items.story: This is an expected update after Vincent suffered a left ankle sprain Sunday against the Kings. Look for the Lakers to use a committee approach to absorb Vincent's minutes, as Marcus Smart (leg) is out as well.

items.headline: Vincent will not return to Sunday's game against the Kings due to a left ankle sprain, Dan Woike of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Vincent suffered the injury in the third quarter and exited for the locker room, where he reportedly underwent X-rays, which came back clean. He concludes the game with three points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, one assist and a steal in 18 minutes. If he is forced to miss time, Jake LaRavia and Dalton Knecht could see expanded roles.

items.headline: Vincent left Sunday's game against the Kings due to an apparent ankle injury, Dan Woike of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Vincent appeared to roll his ankle in the third quarter before quickly being subbed out and limping back to the locker room. If he is unable to return, Jake LaRavia and Dalton Knecht could see extra time.

items.headline: Vincent amassed three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one assist and one steal in 29 minutes during Tuesday's 119-109 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Vincent drew the start Tuesday, but his impact on this game was quite limited. The offense in Los Angeles will run through Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves while LeBron James (sciatica) is sidelined, and if Tuesday was any indication, Vincent will struggle to hold much fantasy appeal despite his role as a starter.

items.headline: Vincent logged 22 points (6-15 FG, 4-4 FT, 6-11 3Pt) and three assists over 25 minutes in Wednesday's 121-94 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: The Lakers weren't expected to win this match due to the conservative approach they are taking with their starters. With Luka Doncic (rest) riding the pine, Vincent assumed the point guard role and found great success beyond the arc, draining six three-pointers in the loss. It's an encouraging line for Vincent, who will be quite useful as a second-unit replacement.

items.headline: Vincent will be in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against the Mavericks, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: After missing Tuesday's preseason matchup against the Suns for rest purposes, Vincent will be in the first five for his squad. He'll be joined by Dalton Knecht, Jarred Vanderbilt, Rui Hachimura and Jaxson Hayes.

items.headline: Vincent (rest) will play in Wednesday's preseason game against Dallas, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports.
items.story: After sitting out the front end of the team's back-to-back set in Tuesday's loss to Phoenix, Vincent will return to game action against the Mavericks. The 29-year-old guard appeared in a career-high 72 regular-season games (11 starts) in 2024-25, during which he averaged 6.4 points and 1.4 assists across 21.2 minutes per game. He's expected to back up Luka Doncic in the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Vincent (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Suns, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: With the start of the regular season approaching, head coach JJ Redick has been resting starters and veteran players. Vincent joins Jarred Vanderbilt, Rui Hachimura and Jaxson Hayes, who will be watching from the sideline Tuesday for rest purposes.

items.headline: Vincent isn't part of the starting lineup for Sunday's preseason game against Golden State, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports.
items.story: Vincent started the Lakers' previous exhibition contest, but with Austin Reaves back in action, Vincent will return to the second unit. Reaves, Dalton Knecht, Rui Hachimura, Jarred Vanderbilt and Deandre Ayton make up the starting five Sunday.

items.headline: Flemings closed with 10 points (3-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one steal across 26 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 victory over the Pistons.
items.story: Returning from a back injury, Flemings played 27 minutes after missing three games. His six assists matched his highest total over his last five appearances, offering encouraging playmaking upside. However, inconsistent scoring and a 24-minute average during that span limit his fantasy reliability.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is available to play Sunday's game against the Pistons, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: Flemings will shed the questionable tag in order to suit up versus Detroit. The rookie first-round pick will make his return from a three-game absence due to a back injury, but Atlanta has yet to confirm whether or not he'll be in the starting lineup. CJ McCollum (calf) is out until mid-December due to a calf injury, and thus far, Aaron Wiggins has filled in as the starter in the backcourt alongside Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Across 12 outings (five starts) in 2026-27, Flemings is averaging 7.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 0.7 steals in 21.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is questionable to play Sunday against the Pistons.
items.story: Flemings has missed the past three games, but it looks like there's a chance he could return Sunday. If he's cleared to play, Aaron Wiggins would likely head back to the second unit.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is out for Friday's game against the Hornets, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Friday will mark Flemings' third straight game on the inactive list, which should result in another start for Aaron Wiggins, and Luguentz Dort will have the chance for some extended minutes. For now, Flemings should be considered questionable for Sunday's meeting with the Pistons.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Hornets, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The rookie guard is looking to end a two-game absence with a back injury. Aaron Wiggins would likely draw a second straight start for the Hawks on Friday if Flemings is ultimately ruled out.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Flemings is progressing well, having practiced Tuesday, but the Hawks are taking a cautious approach with the rookie first-round pick. With CJ McCollum on the shelf with a calf strain, Luguentz Dort is likely to enter the first unit while Aaron Wiggins takes on a larger role off the bench.

items.headline: Flemings (back) practiced Tuesday, per Lauren L. Williams of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder missed Sunday's win in Milwaukee with a back injury, but he's making progress toward his return. Flemings can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable tag for Wednesday's game in Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Flemings (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Flemings left Friday's 125-117 loss to Chicago with back tightness after playing 17 minutes. The ailment will keep the rookie first-rounder on the sidelines Sunday, with veteran CJ McCollum the likely candidate to join the starting lineup. Flemings' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Flemings (back tightness) will not return to Friday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Flemings carried a questionable tag into this game, and it appears as though he irritated his injury again. He ended up finishing scoreless with one rebound and one assist in 17 minutes. Consider him questionable for Sunday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is available for Friday's game against Chicago, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Flemings will shed his questionable tag due to a back issue and suit up for a fifth consecutive contest. The rookie floor general has started each of his last four appearances, averaging 10.8 points, 3.8 assists and 2.3 rebounds across 24.8 minutes per tilt during that span.

items.headline: Flemings (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Flemings is in danger of missing his second contest of the year due to a lumbar spasm. The rookie first-rounder recently leapfrogged CJ McCollum for a starting spot, but the latter would likely rejoin the first unit if the former sits out Friday.

items.headline: Flemings will start Wednesday's game against the Wizards, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The rookie floor general will get the starting nod for the first time in his young career, pushing CJ McCollum to the bench. With Jalen Johnson (ankle) sidelined, Flemings will likely see increased on-ball duties. He's averaging 7.1 points, 4.7 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 20.3 minutes per contest across seven regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Flemings (suspension) won't play in Monday's game against Indiana, Andrew Schlecht of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Flemings was assessed a technical foul and ejected late in the Hawks' 121-99 loss to New Orleans on Saturday for intentionally elbowing Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head. Without the rookie on the floor, head coach Quin Snyder will presumably divide the minutes between Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Aaron Wiggins and CJ McCollum.

items.headline: Flemings logged 23 points (9-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Flemings had scored just 13 total points on 33.3 percent shooting through the first four games of the season, but he caught fire Wednesday, finishing with a career high while missing just three shot attempts. He was one of the few Atlanta players to find success offensively in Wednesday's loss, so it'll be interesting to see if that translates to more minutes in Thursday's meeting with the Cavs.

items.headline: Flemings ended with six points (3-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-1 FT), one rebound and four assists over 18 minutes during Monday's 120-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Although Flemings hasn't yet locked down a major role for the Hawks, it's encouraging to see the rookie first-rounder on the floor on a steady basis to begin his career. Over four appearances thus far, Flemings has averaged 4.0 assists, 3.3 points and 3.0 rebounds in 18.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Flemings totaled zero points (0-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one block over 15 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 victory over the Magic.
items.story: The rookie guard couldn't get a shot to fall in his first regular-season appearance, but he contributed as a rebounder and facilitator off Atlanta's bench. Flemings will likely face competition for minutes in a backcourt featuring CJ McCollum, Dyson Daniels and Nickeil Alexander-Walker, limiting his immediate fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Flemings won't start Friday's preseason finale against the Mavericks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: With most of Atlanta's regulars resting, Flemings started and had seven points (3-11 FG, 1-2 FT), seven assists, two rebounds and one steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 113-110 preseason win over Oklahoma City. However, the Hawks are back to full strength for the final exhibition, so the rookie will slide to a reserve role.

items.headline: Flemings had seven points (3-11 FG, 1-2 FT), seven assists, two rebounds and one steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 113-110 preseason win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Flemings made his second start of the preseason, with Atlanta giving the majority of its key players the night off. It's been a steady preseason for the rookie, flashing some upside on both ends of the floor. While he isn't slated to play a major role for the Hawks in his first season, there is a chance he touches the floor on most nights, serving as a third or fourth option behind the likes of Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels and CJ McCollum.

items.headline: Flemings is in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against Oklahoma City, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: With CJ McCollum resting, Flemings will make his second start of the preseason. Through three preseason appearances, the rookie guard is averaging 11.3 points, 2.7 assists, 1.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 20.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Flemings finished Thursday's 123-116 preseason win over the Spurs with 15 points (6-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five assists, three rebounds and three steals in 20 minutes.
items.story: The rookie point guard got the starting nod in Monday's preseason-opening loss to the Grizzlies, though he retreated to the bench Thursday with CJ McCollum back in action. Flemings turned in a much better performance in his second preseason appearance, closing as the Hawks' second-leading scorer while tying for the game-high marks in assists and steals. He was also far more efficient after shooting just 4-for-11 from the field Monday.

items.headline: Flemings isn't starting in Thursday's preseason game against the Spurs, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The rookie started Monday against the Grizzlies and notched 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-4 FT) and two assists across 25 minutes. However, he'll head to the bench for this one, with Aaron Wiggins starting instead. Flemings is likely to see minutes off the bench anyway, as the preseason is the perfect time to see how he'll fare against NBA-caliber opponents with the regular season right around the corner.

items.headline: Flemings registered 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-4 FT) and two assists across 25 minutes in Monday's 132-123 preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Flemings drew the start Monday due to the absence of CJ McCollum (nose) and logged the most minutes among Atlanta's starters, giving the rookie an extended opportunity in his preseason debut. He struggled with efficiency, committing three turnovers and recording just two assists, and his free-throw shooting was also subpar. However, Flemings is a candidate to see steady minutes off the bench in the Hawks' backcourt despite his rookie status, though his role throughout the remainder of the preseason will be worth monitoring.

items.headline: Flemings will start Monday's preseason game against the Grizzlies, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: With CJ McCollum (nose) unavailable, Flemings will draw the start in his preseason debut. The rookie will be joined in the first unit by Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu.

items.headline: Flemings enters his rookie season after Atlanta selected him with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Hawks president of basketball operations Onsi Saleh praised Flemings' competitiveness on both ends of the floor following the draft, and the young guard should have an opportunity to earn minutes despite Atlanta's considerable perimeter depth. Flemings' immediate fantasy value will depend on how quickly he can carve out a role, but his draft capital makes him one of the organization's most important developmental pieces.

items.headline: Flemings (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Wizards, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Flemings will sit out the Hawks' Summer League finale, marking his third consecutive contest on the inactive list. In two Las Vegas Summer League outings, he averaged 7.0 points, 6.5 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 combined steals-plus-blocks in 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Flemings (rest) won't play in Thursday's game against the Grizzlies, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Flemings played two games during the Salt Lake City Summer League before making two appearances in Las Vegas. The 2026 No. 8 overall pick wasn't consistently productive during those four contests, though it's evident the team is still comfortable keeping him off the floor.

items.headline: Flemings (rest) is out for Monday's Summer League game against Boston, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The Hawks are sitting multiple players for this exhibition. Flemings produced nine points (4-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists and one block across 25 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League win over the Nets.

items.headline: Flemings tallied nine points (4-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists and one block across 25 minutes in Saturday's 83-76 Summer League win over the Nets.
items.story: Flemings didn't stand out as a scorer, but he impacted the game in other ways, finishing with a team-high five assists while matching Kobe Johnson for the team lead with seven rebounds. Flemings has recorded at least five assists in each of his four Summer League appearances, showcasing some of the playmaking ability that helped make him the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. The 19-year-old figures to be a key reserve behind starting guards CJ McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker during his rookie campaign.

items.headline: Flemings produced five points (2-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight assists, one rebound, one steal and one block in 24 minutes of Thursday's 93-66 Summer League win over the Spurs.
items.story: Flemings continues to struggle with his shot during the Summer League. In his previous two outings, he shot a combined 30.8 percent from the field. His statistical output apart from shooting has been solid, however.

items.headline: Flemings (rest) is starting Thursday's Summer League game against the Spurs, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: This is an expected update after Flemings was rested Tuesday. The No. 8 overall pick in this year's NBA Draft, Flemings is averaging 11.0 points, 7.0 assists and 2.5 steals through two exhibitions this summer.

items.headline: Flemings (rest) won't play in Tuesday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Grizzlies, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Flemings will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Thursday in the Hawks' Las Vegas Summer League opener against the Spurs.

items.headline: Daniels finished Sunday's 107-97 win over the Pistons with five points (2-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 14 rebounds, eight assists, five steals and two blocks in 39 minutes.
items.story: Daniels struggled with efficiency and scored single-digit points for the third time in the last five games. However, the 23-year-old stuffed the stat sheet outside the scoring column, leading all players in rebounds and steals while adding team highs in blocks and assists. He set a season-high mark in blocks while supplying multiple steals for an eighth straight game.

items.headline: Daniels posted 11 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 10 assists, eight rebounds and four steals over 35 minutes during the Hawks' 111-97 win over the Hornets on Friday.
items.story: It was another strong, all-around performance for Daniels, with the fifth-year pro logging at least four steals for the fifth time this season. He led the Hawks in assists en route to his third double-double of the season, and he was two boards shy from logging the first triple-double of the year and third of his NBA career. Daniels is averaging 9.1 points, 9.7 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.8 steals over 32.9 minutes per game in November.

items.headline: Daniels produced 10 points (5-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt), 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 117-112 victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Daniels recorded his second consecutive double-double and third straight game with at least nine rebounds, continuing to make an impact despite limited scoring opportunities. The defensive-minded guard has collected two steals in each of his last three appearances while averaging 8.3 points, 9.7 rebounds and 4.3 assists during that stretch. Daniels has attempted just 23 shots across those three games, but his contributions in rebounds, assists and steals continue to provide substantial fantasy value, particularly in category leagues.

items.headline: Daniels provided 10 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and four steals in 31 minutes during Monday's 124-114 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Daniels didn't miss a shot from the field and filled the stat sheet again, extending his league lead in steals per game. His rebounding and playmaking keep growing, which makes him far more than a steals specialist in fantasy. His limited shot volume is the only thing holding back his ceiling.

items.headline: Daniels accumulated nine points (4-9 FG, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one block and six steals over 31 minutes during Saturday's 124-121 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Daniels was a beast on both ends of the floor, nudging a rare quadruple-double despite scoring just nine points. Although his offensive output has been somewhat underwhelming, Daniels' contributions across the board have been ultra effective. Look for him to continue racking up the stats when Atlanta hosts the Lakers on Monday.

items.headline: Daniels finished Friday's 139-132 victory over Washington with 13 points (6-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, 12 assists and two steals across 34 minutes.
items.story: Daniels fell one rebound short of a triple-double, including a season-high 12 assists. While the steals have been relatively consistent, Daniels has been a beast on the glass over the past three games, averaging 11.3 rebounds during that span. He has been a top-50 player thus far this season, averaging 9.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 2.6 steals in 30.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Daniels contributed eight points (4-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt), 16 rebounds and eight assists in 34 minutes during Wednesday's 120-105 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Daniels struggled to find his shooting touch but compensated with a dominant effort on the glass, grabbing seven offensive rebounds. The versatile wing also paced Atlanta with eight assists while committing just two turnovers. Although he failed to register a steal or block, his ability to contribute heavily in rebounds and assists helped salvage a productive fantasy outing.

items.headline: Daniels provided eight points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, three assists and three steals in 27 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: It was the fourth time in seven games that Daniels recorded at least three steals, and his 3.0 steals per game average is tied with Collin Gillespie for second-most in the Association behind Zion Williamson (3.2). Daniels has failed to score in double digits in each of his last four outings after doing so in each of the first three games of the regular season. However, the fifth-year pro may be forced to take on a larger role offensively if Jalen Johnson were to be sidelined due to a left ankle injury that he picked up during Saturday's loss.

items.headline: Daniels accumulated seven points (3-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three steals across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 loss to Miami.
items.story: Daniels was limited to just four points, four assists and one steal his last time out, and while the scoring was still low, it was a positive to see him come through with the dimes and defensive stats. He's been a top-50 option through the first five games of the season with averages of 12.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 3.4 steals and just 0.8 turnovers per contest.

items.headline: Daniels ended with 18 points (8-11 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal over 29 minutes before fouling out of Saturday's 121-114 loss to Houston.
items.story: The fifth-year wing wasn't able to keep up his blistering defensive start to the season, but Daniels still put together a productive night. Through three games, Daniels is averaging 16.3 points, 7.0 boards, 4.3 steals and 3.3 assists over 29.0 minutes while shooting a scalding 61.8 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Daniels delivered 11 points (5-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-3 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, seven steals and a block across 23 minutes in Friday's 128-81 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Daniels needed just 23 minutes to produce an outstanding defensive performance, with his seven steals providing an enormous fantasy boost, and a double-digit steals outing would've been within reach had he played more. His rebounding was equally encouraging, falling one board short of a double-double despite the reduced workload. While that level of steals production is unsustainable, Daniels' ability to generate defensive stats gives him considerable fantasy upside even when his scoring remains modest.

items.headline: Daniels closed with 20 points (8-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, three assists and five steals in 35 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Daniels was in his bag to begin the season, getting it done on both ends of the floor. Coming off a strong showing during the 2025-26 season, Daniels will look to advance his game this year, particularly on the offensive end. Although he missed both of his three-point attempts, the fact that he attempted 13 shots was encouraging. He has a chance to lead the league in steals, which provides fantasy managers with a sense of reassurance when it comes to his overall value.

items.headline: Daniels (rest) will play in Friday's preseason finale against the Mavericks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Daniels and most of Atlanta's regulars rested Monday against the Thunder but will return to action for the final exhibition. It's unclear how many minutes Daniels will play Friday, but he should be a full go for the regular-season opener.

items.headline: Daniels (rest) has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Daniels and most of Atlanta's regulars will rest during the Hawks' penultimate preseason contest. Daniels tallied 13 points (6-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 11 rebounds, an assist and a steal across 21 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason win over the Spurs but struggled with his shot against the Pacers on Saturday.

items.headline: Daniels tallied 13 points (6-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 11 rebounds, an assist and a steal across 21 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Daniels was particularly active on the glass, collecting a game-high 11 rebounds, including six offensive boards, to secure a double-double despite an inefficient shooting performance. However, his ability to contribute without relying exclusively on scoring remains a significant part of his fantasy appeal. Daniels will open the season in a starting role in the Hawks' backcourt, where his defensive contributions make him a valuable asset across most formats. If his three-point percentage reverts to at least a respectable margin after shooting 18.8 percent from deep last year, Daniels could be a fantasy darling.

items.headline: Daniels finished with six points (2-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-5 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 18 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Daniels struggled from three-point range and the charity stripe before sitting out the second half along with most of Atlanta's starters. Despite the quiet opener, Daniels should continue filling a prominent two-way role for the Hawks this season.

items.headline: Hawks president of basketball operations Onsi Saleh called Daniels "one of the most impactful players in the NBA" and an "all-world defender" while expressing confidence that his shooting will improve, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Daniels remained highly productive across the board in 2025-26, averaging 11.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 2.0 steals in 33.2 minutes across 76 regular-season appearances, but he connected on just 18.8 percent of his 1.5 three-point attempts per game. Despite the lack of perimeter shooting, Daniels shot 51.7 percent overall and earned a spot on the All-Defensive Second Team. Atlanta's continued confidence in his offensive development is encouraging heading into 2026-27.

items.headline: Daniels may face increased competition for minutes in Atlanta's backcourt after the Hawks drafted Kingston Flemings with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

items.story: The Hawks are resting all of their normal starters for Sunday's regular-season finale, so Kispert will enter Atlanta's starting five for the eighth time this season. His last start took place March 12 against the Nets, when he played 20 minutes and finished with seven points, four assists and three rebounds.

items.headline: Kispert closed Friday's 124-102 win over Cleveland with eight points (2-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-5 FT) and one assist in nine minutes.
items.story: Kispert continues to play limited minutes off the bench, resulting in modest production. While he does provide the Hawks with a floor-spacing option off the bench, his lack of defensive versatility makes him more of a depth piece than a consistent part of the rotation.

items.headline: Kispert (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Hawks' 112-102 win over the Celtics.
items.story: For the first time since being acquired from the Wizards in early January, Kispert was left out of the rotation. The Hawks opted to remove Kispert from the mix after he had struggled to live up to his billing as a perimeter threat over his first 35 appearances with the club, during which he shot just 32.6 percent from downtown on 4.1 attempts per game. Kispert doesn't offer much impact as a creator and isn't a standout defender, so his opportunities could be limited while he continues to struggle with his three-point shot.

items.headline: Kispert had 11 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound and one assist in 16 minutes during Monday's 146-107 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Kispert remains a difficult fantasy player to roster due to his lack of contributions elsewhere in the box score. The swingman has averaged only 7.8 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.8 three-pointers in 14.0 minutes per contest over his last six games, shooting a poor 25.0 percent from downtown during this span.

items.headline: Kispert is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's game versus the Bucks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
items.story: Dyson Daniels (toe) is back from a one-game absence, pushing Kispert back to the second unit. Across his last six outings as a reserve, Kispert has averaged 11.5 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 2.0 three-pointers in 18.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Kispert will start Thursday's game against the Nets, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: Dyson Daniels (toe) was downgraded to out a few hours before tipoff, opening up a spot in the starting five for Kispert. The Gonzaga product started six straight games from Jan. 19 to Jan. 29 and averaged 9.2 points, 1.5 rebounds and 1.7 assists during that span.

items.headline: Kispert supplied two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over 15 minutes during Tuesday's 124-112 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Kispert scored just two points, failing to reach double digits for the ninth time in the past 11 games. While he does provide the Hawks with another floor-spacing option, Kispert offers very little upside across the board. In 25 appearances since joining Atlanta, he has averaged just 10.0 points and 1.6 three-pointers, barely putting up top-300 value.

items.headline: Kispert closed with 33 points (11-19 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block across 28 minutes during Thursday's 126-96 win over Washington.
items.story: Kispert led Washington with 33 points despite being deployed off the bench. This offensive outburst marks his best of the season through 40 games. Unfortunately for Kispert, these opportunities on the offensive end are likely to dwindle once Nickeil Alexander-Walker (foot) and Jalen Johnson (hip) return to play.

items.headline: Kispert supplied 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and two assists across 21 minutes during Tuesday's 119-98 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Kispert snapped a four-game, single-digit scoring streak during Tuesday's win over the Wizards, and this was his first game with multiple triples since Feb. 7. Across 20 games with the Hawks, Kispert has recorded averages of 9.7 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.5 triples per contest, but he could see an uptick in usage if Jalen Johnson (hip) misses extended time.

items.headline: Kispert racked up 12 points (4-12 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one block across 31 minutes during Monday's 138-116 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Kispert saw a boost in playing time with Dyson Daniels (ankle) and Jalen Johnson (knee) both out. However, Kispert's fantasy value remains limited outside of points, as he's averaged 12.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 25.8 minutes per game across his last five outings (no starts).

items.headline: Kispert registered 20 points (7-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and two rebounds across 25 minutes during Thursday's 121-119 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Kispert is carving out a solid role for himself since landing in Atlanta. The 26-year-old sharpshooter remains worth keeping an eye on, but he'll likely need to do more outside the scoring department in order to command more attention in fantasy circles. Over his last five appearances, Kispert has averaged 14.8 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 2.2 three-pointers in 25.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Kispert will come off the bench in Saturday's game against Indiana, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: This is an expected move with Jalen Johnson (calf) returning from a one-game absence. Kispert is likely to maintain a sizable role with Vit Krejci (ankle) sidelined Saturday.

items.headline: Kispert supplied 17 points (7-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes during Thursday's 104-86 loss to Houston.
items.story: Kispert got some extended minutes with Jalen Johnson (calf) taking the night off, and he took advantage of the increased opportunity. This was Kispert's second straight game with multiple triples and double-digit points, and this was his second game of the season with at least one steal and one block. It'll be interesting to see if he can keep the hot streak going Saturday with a favorable matchup against the Pacers.

items.headline: Kispert recorded seven points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and three assists in 17 minutes during Monday's 132-116 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: This was a disappointing effort from Kispert, and the timing isn't great for him either -- Zaccharie Risacher is nearing a return from his knee injury. For the time being, Kispert's fantasy value remains limited to very deep formats for managers in need of a three-point specialist.

items.headline: Kispert will start Monday's game against the Bucks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: The Hawks are going to opt for more shooting Monday with Kispert replacing Vit Krejci in the first unit. Kispert had a strong showing Saturday against the Celtics, scoring 16 points with a pair of three-pointers across 23 minutes.

items.headline: Kispert ended with 16 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal across 23 minutes during Saturday's 132-106 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Kispert scored at least 16 points for the second time in the past three games, albeit as a result of multiple injuries. While he does have the ability to score in bunches, this doesn't feel like a situation where fantasy managers need to overreact. At this stage, he is simply a wait-and-watch player, outside of deeper formats.

items.headline: Kispert registered 19 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT) and one assist in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 141-116 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Kispert saw more opportunities with Zaccharie Risacher (knee) sidelined, but the impact of Kispert's acquisition is an open question. A hamstring injury held him back for much of the season with the Wizards, and while Tuesday's line is encouraging, it's unlikely that he'll secure a role that warrants fantasy attention given the current rotation.

items.headline: Kispert (hamstring) registered two points (0-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal over 14 minutes during Sunday's 124-111 win over Golden State.
items.story: Kispert made his team debut Sunday, coming off the bench alongside fellow Hawks newcomer CJ McCollum. The 26-year-old forward has made just three appearances since the start of December due to a hamstring strain, so it could be difficult to gauge how his role will look with his new squad until his restrictions are loosened.

items.headline: Kispert (not with team) is not on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Kispert's trade to Atlanta was finalized Friday, and the sharpshooting veteran will be available to make his Hawks debut Sunday. Kispert averaged 9.2 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game while shooting 39.5 percent from three-point range in 19 regular-season games (two starts) with the Wizards before the trade.

items.headline: Kispert (not with team) will not play Friday against the Nuggets.
items.story: Kispert's trade to Atlanta was finalized Friday morning, but he and CJ McCollum haven't joined the team yet. Presumably, both players will be ready to make their debuts Sunday against the Warriors.

items.headline: The Wizards traded Kispert (hamstring) and CJ McCollum (quadriceps) to the Hawks in exchange for Trae Young (quadriceps) on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Kispert will join the Hawks after four-plus seasons with Washington. The forward, whose inclusion in the trade likely was due in part to the need to match salaries, is averaging 9.2 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists across 19.5 minutes per game this season. He'll likely battle with Vit Krejci, Zaccharie Risacher and Luke Kennard for minutes on the wing

items.headline: Kispert has been ruled out for Wednesday's game due to left hamstring injury management.
items.story: Kispert got the night off Tuesday for the same injury and was initially cleared for Wednesday's game. However, he's been flipped back to out. Justin Champagnie and Tre Johnson should see an increase in minutes. Kispert's next chance to play for the Wizards will be Friday.

items.headline: Kispert (hamstring) will play Wednesday against the 76ers.
items.story: After getting a maintenance day Tuesday for the front end of this back-to-back set, Kispert is expectedly back in action. The Wizards are sitting CJ McCollum (quadriceps) and Khris Middleton (rest) Wednesday, so Kispert could be more involved than usual.

items.headline: Kispert has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic due to left hamstring injury management.
items.story: Kispert had missed 10 consecutive games earlier this season due to a fractured right thumb, only to strain his left hamstring in his return to action in a Dec. 23 loss to the Hornets. He proceeded to miss the Wizards' next five games before he was cleared to play in the team's 141-115 loss to the Timberwolves on Sunday, when he posted 13 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and one rebound in 18 minutes. Kispert appears to have avoided any setbacks coming out of that contest, but the Wizards will nonetheless exercise some caution with him coming off the injury and will hold him out Tuesday for the front end of a back-to-back set. Kispert will likely be available to play Wednesday in Philadelphia, however.

items.headline: Kispert (hamstring) will be available for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Kispert is set to return after five games on the shelf, so he could face some restrictions. The veteran guard holds averages of 8.9 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 19.5 minutes per contest this season.

items.headline: Dort registered 16 points (4-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and three steals across 31 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Dort has scored 16 points in two of his last three games, but his production remains volatile. He's averaging 25 minutes over his last five appearances, making Sunday's seven rebounds and three steals particularly valuable. Inconsistent minutes and scoring limit his fantasy reliability.

items.headline: Dort posted 16 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and two steals over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 117-112 victory over the Thunder.
items.story: Dort scored 16 points against his former team after totaling just 17 across his previous three games. He connected on three triples and matched his season high with two steals. Despite the improved performance, his inconsistent scoring and limited contributions outside of three-pointers and steals restrict his fantasy appeal to deeper leagues.

items.headline: Dort is not listed in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against Brooklyn, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Jalen Johnson (ankle) missed the last three games, so Dort started during his absence. However, with Johnson back in the equation for the meeting with the Nets, Dort will return to the bench.

items.headline: Dort racked up 25 points (9-15 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and two steals in 32 minutes during Friday's 139-132 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Dort remained in the starting lineup, turning in easily his best performance since arriving in Atlanta. He finished with season-high numbers across the board, rewarding anyone lucky enough to stream him. As long as Jalen Johnson (ankle) is out, Dort is at least on the streaming radar, specifically for anyone needing threes and steals.

items.headline: Dort is starting Monday's game against the Pacers, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Jalen Johnson (ankle) is out Monday, opening up a spot for Dort in the starting five. This marks the first start of the 2026-27 campaign for Dort, who is averaging 8.6 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.6 assists over seven appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Dort closed with 11 points (4-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes during Monday's 120-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Dort is handling a relatively significant role off the bench in his debut season with the Hawks. Over his first four contests, the veteran swingman has averaged 8.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 22.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dort notched eight points (2-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one steal in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 win over the Magic.
items.story: Dort played a substantial role in Atlanta's second unit but struggled to find his offensive rhythm, making just two field goals. He remains capable of contributing three-pointers and defensive statistics, although the Hawks' collection of perimeter scorers could limit his offensive opportunities.

items.headline: Dort (rest) will play in Friday's preseason finale against the Mavericks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Dort and most of Atlanta's regulars rested Monday against the Thunder but will return to action for the final exhibition. It'd be surprising if the veteran played major minutes Friday.

items.headline: Dort (rest) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
items.story: Dort is sitting out Monday for maintenance purposes, along with most of the Hawks' regulars. The veteran swingman's next chance to play is Friday against Dallas.

items.headline: Dort is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason contest against the Pacers, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: The Hawks are tweaking their lineup for this preseason contest, and Dort will get the nod in the starting lineup due to the absence of Nickeil Alexander-Walker (rest). Dort averaged 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.9 three-pointers per contest with the Thunder in 69 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Dort (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Saturday's preseason game in Indiana, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: It appears Dort will make his Hawks preseason debut Saturday, but the 27-year-old veteran will likely have his minutes monitored. Over 69 games with the Thunder last season, Dort averaged 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.9 triples per contest.

items.headline: Dort (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason matchup with San Antonio, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Dort will remain on the shelf for a second straight preseason game due to a right knee contusion. His next opportunity to suit up in the preseason will come against the Pacers on Saturday.

items.headline: Dort won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Grizzlies due to a right knee contusion, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: The veteran swingman will be held out of Atlanta's preseason opener, leaving more minutes available for the likes of Corey Kispert, Aaron Wiggins and Jalen Wilson. Dort's next chance to play in the preseason will come Thursday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Dort recorded 25 points (8-13 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Canada's 97-92 win over Argentina in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 27-year-old will begin a new chapter in 2026-27 after being traded from Oklahoma City to Atlanta during the offseason. Dort averaged just 8.3 points per game last season, and he'll join a deep Hawks perimeter rotation that also features Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, CJ McCollum and Buddy Hield. Dort's defense should earn him consistent playing time, but the competition for shots is expected to limit his fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: The Thunder traded Dort to the Hawks on Sunday in exchange for three second-round picks as part of a three-team deal with the Mavericks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Thunder picked up the defensive-minded swingman's $17.7 million team option in June but are now flipping him for draft capital. The Hawks will receive Dort and Ryan Nembhard (illness), while the Mavericks acquire 2024 No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher. Dort's production took a fairly significant hit in 2025-26, during which he averaged 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals while shooting just 38.5 percent from the field in 26.8 minutes per game across 69 regular-season appearances. He figures to play significant minutes thanks to his defensive prowess, though he could come off the bench behind Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels.

items.headline: The Thunder picked up Dort's $17.7 million team option Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Thunder are already heavily into the tax, but the franchise has every intention of getting back to the NBA Finals, and this was a priority for the team. Dort averaged 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals while shooting a career-low 38.5 percent from the field in 26.8 minutes per game across 69 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, but his defense is invaluable.

items.headline: Dort ended with three points (1-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two assists and one rebound over 16 minutes during Saturday's 111-103 loss to San Antonio in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Dort logged fewer than 20 minutes for the third time over the final four games of the Western Conference Finals and failed to make a positive impact on the offensive end in his limited run Saturday. The 27-year-old swingman remained a mainstay in the Thunder's starting five in 2025-26, though his production took a significant step back. Dort averaged 8.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals while shooting a career-low 38.5 percent from the field in 26.8 minutes per game across 69 regular-season appearances. The Thunder hold a $17.7 million team option on Dort's contract for 2026-27, creating some uncertainty around his future in Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Dort logged zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five rebounds and three assists in 23 minutes during Friday's 123-108 win over San Antonio in Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: While Dort has had a muted impact on the offensive end throughout the postseason, he failed to score for the first time in the 2026 playoffs. The defensive-minded swingman logged a series-high 23 minutes Friday, but given the strong play of Jared McCain and Cason Wallace, Dort could continue seeing a reduced role, especially if Jalen Williams (hamstring) and Ajay Mitchell (undisclosed) are both available for Game 4.

items.headline: Dort recorded six points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt), three rebounds and four assists across 28 minutes during Tuesday's 108-90 win over the Lakers in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Dort's usage was very low in Game 1, but that's to be expected in the postseason. Through five playoff games, Dort has been very quiet with averages of 6.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists on 36.7 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dort posted nine points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt), one rebound and one steal over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 120-107 victory over the Suns in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Ajay Mitchell had the hot hand off the bench, and Alex Caruso was everywhere defensively, so Dort played a modest role Thursday. Through two postseason games, he's averaging 8.5 points, 1.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals.

items.headline: Dort (undisclosed) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Utah.
items.story: Dort suffered an undisclosed injury during Thursday's 139-96 win over the Lakers. However, it must not have been that big of an issue, considering he's not listed on the official injury report. With Dort in the rotation, Ajay Mitchell, who would have been in line to start, will continue to see work from off the bench.

items.headline: Dort (undisclosed) didn't return to Thursday's game against the Lakers. He finished with 14 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt), one assist and two steals in 21 minutes.
items.story: Dort suffered an undisclosed injury during the third quarter, and the team neglected to provide an update after he was seen walking to the locker room. He can be considered day-to-day until Oklahoma City has more news to share on the nature of his injury.

items.headline: Dort went to the locker room during the third quarter of Thursday's game against the Lakers, Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman reports.
items.story: Dort was fouled on an attempt near the rim and was shaken up the play. He was spotted walking to the locker room to get evaluated during the next timeout. Dort can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Dort racked up 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), five rebounds and one block in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 119-109 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Dort didn't stand out for the Thunder, but his three-point shooting was worth highlighting. Even though he's going to take on a secondary role offensively every night, Dort could still generate value as a spot-up shooter from three-point range. Dort has drained two or more threes in five of his last eight games, although he's been far from efficient with a 29.8 percent mark in that span.

items.headline: Dort (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Dort missed the last two games because of a knee issue. He'll likely take back his spot in the starting lineup Monday, meaning Cason Wallace would head back to the bench.

items.headline: Dort has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Wizards due to a left knee contusion.
items.story: Dort was originally slated to play Saturday after being held out of Wednesday's win against the Nets due to rest purposes. It's unclear when the seventh-year pro sustained his left knee injury, but his absence means Cason Wallace will likely start in a second straight game. Dort's next chance to play is Monday against the 76ers.

items.headline: Dort (rest) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Saturday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Dort skipped Wednesday's win over Brooklyn for rest purposes, but he'll be back in action Saturday, which will likely result in Ajay Mitchell or Cason Wallace heading back to the second unit. Dort is averaging 8.5 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.8 triples per game this season.

items.headline: The Thunder list Dort out for Wednesday's game against the Nets for rest purposes.
items.story: Dort will get a night off after logging 19 minutes Tuesday in the Thunder's 113-108 win over the Magic. Alex Caruso, Cason Wallace, Isaiah Joe and Jared McCain could all absorb some of Dort's vacated minutes.

items.headline: Dort racked up six points (2-8 FG, 2-8 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 29 minutes during Thursday's 104-102 victory over Boston.
items.story: Dort struggled with his shot, missing six of his eight attempts from deep, but he managed to contribute as a rebounder to help the Thunder secure a narrow win over the Celtics. While his offensive consistency remains a major question mark, Dort has been a permanent fixture in the starting five, averaging 30.0 minutes per game over his last 10 appearances. During this recent stretch, his scoring has been modest, averaging 8.3 points per game on just 31.5 percent shooting. Despite the lack of high-volume scoring, Dort's primary value to the Thunder lies in his perimeter defense, which keeps his minutes floor secure.

items.headline: Dort ended with 16 points (4-9 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and one assist over 33 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 103-100 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Dort had a strong offensive showing Wednesday, but lines like these have been few and far between. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 9.1 points on 34.7 percent shooting from the field with 4.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 29.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dort was assessed a Flagrant 2 foul and ejected in the fourth quarter of Friday's game against the Nuggets, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. He'll finish with eight points (3-7 FG, 2-6 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes.
items.story: The swingman was ejected after making unnecessary and excessive contact with Nikola Jokic, as Dort tripped the three-time MVP. With Dort unavailable, Alex Caruso and Jared McCain will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Johnson closed with 12 points (4-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds and one steal across 30 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 victory over the Pistons.
items.story: Johnson has averaged 19.0 points, 10.2 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 35.0 minutes over his last five games. Despite Sunday's scoreless assist column, his playmaking remains elite for a forward, though inconsistent perimeter shooting has limited his scoring efficiency.

items.headline: Johnson tallied 26 points (10-15 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, six assists, four steals and one block across 36 minutes during Friday's 111-97 win over Charlotte.
items.story: Johnson delivered a stellar performance to help Atlanta win a third consecutive game. He led all players in scoring while racking up five defensive stats, the latter of which equals his total in that category over the last five contests. Johnson was highly efficient from everywhere Friday, an especially positive note after he went a combined 10-for-28 (35.7 percent) in his previous two outings.

items.headline: Johnson racked up 16 points (5-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 12 rebounds, 11 assists and one block over 34 minutes in Wednesday's 117-112 win over the Thunder.
items.story: This was Johnson's second triple-double of the season and the 17th of his career. However, he continued to struggle with his three-point shot, and he's opened the 2026-27 season converting just 18.0 percent of his long balls. Before this season, he was a career 33.5 percent three-point shooter, so it should only be a matter of time until he finds his footing from long-range.

items.headline: Johnson logged 14 points (5-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-8 FT), 11 rebounds and five assists in 35 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: After delivering his first triple-double of the season Friday against the Bulls, Johnson followed it up with his fifth double-double Sunday. The 24-year-old forward has looked good in four contests since returning from a sprained ankle, averaging 21.5 points, 9.0 boards, 6.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 37.3 minutes.

items.headline: Johnson produced 27 points (11-26 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal across 40 minutes in Friday's 125-117 overtime loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Johnson didn't deliver his most efficient performance, though he did lead the Hawks in points, rebounds and assists en route to his first triple-double of the season. The star forward has reached the 20-point threshold in two of his last three games, though he's missed all 11 of his three-point attempts during that stretch. Through 10 regular-season games, Johnson has posted a triple-double and three double-doubles.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 30 points (11-17 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 8-10 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and one steal in 36 minutes during Saturday's 124-121 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Johnson returned to action after missing the previous three games due to an ankle injury. He showed no signs of rust, leading all scorers with 30 points, powering Atlanta to a come-from-behind victory. It appears to be all systems go for Johnson, especially given he played 36 minutes in his return. Barring any setbacks, expect to see him leading from the front again when the Lakers come to town Monday.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is active for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Johnson has missed Atlanta's last three contests due to a sprained left ankle, but the 24-year-old is ready to roll at home versus Brooklyn. His return will likely push Luguentz Dort back to the bench, while Corey Kispert could see his minutes diminish slightly.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is probable for Saturday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Johnson has missed each of Atlanta's last three games due to a sprained left ankle, though it seems likely that his string of absences will end Saturday. The 24-year-old has gotten off to another strong start this season, averaging 18.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.9 assists in 32.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: This will be Johnson's third straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Nets. Luguentz Dort should continue to start in his absence, while Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Onyeka Okongwu will see a larger role on offense.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against Washington.
items.story: Johnson hasn't played since spraining his left ankle during Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans, and he's now questionable to suit up for Friday's matchup. The Hawks have won two straight in his absence, so there's at least some good news for Atlanta. If Johnson is forced to miss a third consecutive contest, the 2025-26 All-Star forward's next opportunity to play will come at home against the Nets on Saturday.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as out for Wednesday's game in Washington.
items.story: Johnson sustained a sprained left ankle in Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans and wasn't available for Monday's meeting with Indiana. Now that the 24-year-old is ruled out for a second consecutive game, his next opportunity to get back on the floor will come Friday for the rematch with the Wizards. Without Johnson, Luguentz Dort is expected to stay in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game in Washington, Kevin Chouinard of the Hawks' official site reports.
items.story: Johnson suffered a sprained left ankle in Saturday's 121-99 loss to New Orleans and was ruled out ahead of Monday's meeting with the Pacers. If Johnson can't get back on the floor Wednesday versus the Wizards, Luguentz Dort might make his second consecutive start.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game versus Indiana.
items.story: Johnson exited Saturday's loss to the Pelicans with a left ankle sprain and will sit out Monday's contest. The star forward's next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Wizards. In the meantime, Aaron Wiggins, Luguentz Dort and Asa Newell are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is questionable to play Monday against the Pacers.
items.story: Johnson did not return to Saturday's 121-99 loss to New Orleans after suffering a left ankle sprain in the third quarter. He's now been tagged as questionable, and if he is in fact out versus Indiana, Aaron Wiggins and Luguentz Dort are the top candidates to join Atlanta's starting five.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) did not return to Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans. He finished with 13 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one block over 28 minutes.
items.story: Johnson was on the court for the final seconds of the third quarter but didn't see the floor for the entire fourth. The Hawks were facing a large deficit, so the decision to keep him sidelined for the final quarter may have been a precautionary measure. Nevertheless, Johnson's injury status is worth monitoring heading into the Hawks' next game, which takes place Monday against the Pacers. If he were to miss time, then Aaron Wiggins and Luguentz Dort would likely be the top candidates to enter Atlanta's starting lineup.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is questionable to return to Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Johnson may have tweaked his ankle toward the tail end of the third quarter, as he was subbed out for Dyson Daniels for the start of the fourth. Aaron Wiggins and Luguentz Dort are both in line for more minutes while Johnson is out of the game.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 17 points (7-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and seven assists across 34 minutes in Thursday's 114-111 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Johnson delivered another well-rounded performance, contributing as both a rebounder and facilitator despite failing to reach the 20-point mark for the third time in six appearances this season. His seven assists highlighted his importance to Atlanta's offensive scheme, but he lost the ball four times, his third straight game with at least three turnovers. Johnson's substantial playing time and versatility across points, rebounds and assists give him a strong fantasy foundation, but his early-season numbers are slightly down in most categories compared to his career-best season in 2025-26.

items.headline: Johnson finished Wednesday's 129-117 loss to the Heat with 12 points (4-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), nine rebounds, 11 assists and two blocks in 36 minutes.
items.story: Johnson has been struggling mightily from three-point range to start the season, going 5-for-23 from beyond the arc. However, there's no way he'll shoot this poorly all season given that he converted 35.2 percent of his three-point attempts last year, so fantasy managers should stay patient through this slow start.

items.headline: Johnson finished with 21 points (5-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 10-12 FT), nine rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 36 minutes during Monday's 120-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Johnson continues to roll as a first-round fantasy player in the early stages of the campaign. Over four appearances to this point, the star forward has averaged 21.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, 8.5 assists and 1.8 steals in 32.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Johnson contributed 26 points (8-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 8-10 FT), 16 assists, nine rebounds and two steals across 38 minutes in Saturday's 121-114 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: After providing a full stat line in Friday's win over Charlotte, Johnson stuffed the stat sheet once again in the second half of this back-to-back set. The star forward recorded game highs in scoring and assists, dishing out a career-high-tying 16 dimes. The 24-year-old also led the Hawks in rebounds. He's posted at least 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists in all three of his regular-season appearances to begin the campaign.

items.headline: Johnson posted 19 points (9-16 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and a block across 29 minutes in Friday's 128-81 win over the Hornets.
items.story: The Hawks looked dominant on both ends of the court and cruised to a 47-point victory -- and Johnson finished just two dimes and three boards shy of a triple-double despite playing under 30 minutes. Johnson also made his presence felt defensively with four steals-plus-blocks combined. It's only been two games, but Johnson is off to an excellent start in 2026-27 with 39 points, 21 rebounds and 14 assists in his first two contests.

items.headline: Johnson ended Wednesday's 132-125 victory over Orlando with 20 points (7-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 14 rebounds and six assists over 28 minutes.
items.story: Johnson recorded his first double-double of the season, albeit on an inefficient 7-of-19 from the field. Along with the majority of the starting lineup, Johnson's playing time was limited, with head coach Quin Snyder opting to ease his players into the season. All things considered, this was a strong outing for Johnson, although fantasy managers would love to see a little more from him on the defensive end moving forward.

items.headline: Johnson tallied 20 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 9-11 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block over 25 minutes in Friday's 135-111 preseason win over the Mavericks.
items.story: This was Johnson's second double-double of the preseason, and he appears primed for another big year as the main man in Atlanta. The 24-year-old forward earned his first All-Star selection last season with averages of 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, 7.9 assists, 1.7 triples and 1.2 steals during the regular season on 49/35/79 shooting splits.

items.headline: Jovic closed Sunday's 123-113 victory over the Thunder with 15 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 19 minutes.
items.story: Jovic delivered efficient scoring and strong rebounding despite playing fewer than 19 minutes. His three triples and contributions across five categories demonstrate his fantasy potential, but Miami's crowded frontcourt continues to limit his opportunities and consistency.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Jovic's availability gives Miami additional frontcourt depth for Wednesday's contest. The forward has struggled to establish a consistent role in the rotation, limiting his fantasy appeal despite his ability to contribute scoring, rebounding and three-point shooting.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Jovic is trending in the right direction following a one-game absence due to an illness. However, his return wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) is out for Monday's game against Houston.
items.story: Jovic was added to the injury report as questionable due to an illness earlier in the day Monday, and the club has since determined that he won't be able to give it a go. Klay Thompson and Bobby Portis could pick up a few additional minutes in Jovic's absence, though the impact to Miami's rotation should be minimal.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
items.story: Jovic was a late addition to the injury report due to an illness. However, his potential absence wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Jovic closed with one point (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one assist and one block in 12 minutes during Thursday's 120-100 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Jovic struggled to make an impact during his brief stint off the bench, failing to convert either of his three-point attempts and going without a rebound. The 23-year-old saw considerably less playing time than fellow reserves Pelle Larsson and Ryan Conwell, highlighting Jovic's uncertain place in Miami's rotation. With Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and Bobby Portis occupying frontcourt minutes, Jovic remains difficult to trust in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Jovic will come off the bench in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Timberwolves, Zachary Weinberger of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Jovic started in Miami's preseason finale with Giannis Antetokounmpo (rest) taking a night off, but Antetokounmpo is back and starting on Opening Night. As a reserve last season, Jovic averaged 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.

items.headline: Jovic will start in Friday's preseason finale in Orlando, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Bam Adebayo (rest) and Giannis Antetokounmpo (rest) are sitting out the preseason finale, so Jovic will draw the start and he'll be joined in the first unit by Davion Mitchell, Klay Thompson, Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis. In his previous start this preseason, Jovic finished with 14 points, six rebounds, three assists, two triples, two steals and one turnover across 21 minutes.

items.headline: Jovic played 23 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 144-128 preseason win over the Nets, scoring five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and adding seven assists and five rebounds.
items.story: While he left the scoring to others, Jovic still made a strong contribution from the second unit. The 23-year-old big has struggled to stay healthy and establish himself as a regular part of the Heat rotation in his first four NBA seasons, never playing more than 47 regular-season games, and the offseason additions of Bobby Portis and Nick Richards will make bench minutes in the frontcourt even harder to come by.

items.headline: Jovic is not listed in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against the Nets.
items.story: Jovic got the start in Saturday's preseason loss to Minnesota, finishing with 16 points, six rebounds, three assists and three steals over 25 minutes. He will come off the bench once again Wednesday, though it's not known what his role will be versus Orlando on Friday.

items.headline: Jovic managed 16 points (7-11 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, three assists and three steals in 25 minutes during Saturday's 125-124 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Miami held out several key contributors Saturday, opening the door for Jovic to step into the starting five. The 23-year-old turned in an efficient shooting performance, closing the game as Miami's third-leading scorer. He also tied for the game-high mark in steals while finishing as one of five Heat players to grab at least six rebounds.

items.headline: Jovic is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Timberwolves, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Simone Fontecchio, Tre Donaldson, Nikola Jovic, Pelle Larsson and Nick Richards will join Jovic in the first unit for Saturday's exhibition with the regular starters all resting. In Jovic's lone start last season, he produced nine points, three rebounds, two triples, one steal and three turnovers in 23 minutes.

items.headline: Jovic finished with eight points (3-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks in 21 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Jovic struggled with his overall shooting efficiency but made an impact defensively, recording two steals and two blocks while avoiding turnovers. His ability to contribute across multiple categories could help him maintain a meaningful rotation role, although Miami's frontcourt depth may create competition for consistent minutes.

items.headline: Jovic recorded 21 points (9-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 23 minutes during Serbia's 102-73 win over Iceland in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Jovic continued his impressive qualifying run, as he's now averaging 25.0 points while shooting 65.1 percent from the field through three appearances. The 23-year-old is coming off a disappointing 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists while shooting just 36.6 percent from the field across 47 regular-season games. His path to a larger role became more difficult after Miami acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis this offseason, but Jovic is entering the first season of his four-year extension and remains an intriguing developmental piece for the Heat.

items.headline: Jovic (ankle) recorded 22 points (8-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five assists, two rebounds, two blocks and one steal in 27 minutes during Serbia's 97-73 win over Switzerland on Thursday.
items.story: Jovic is healthy for FIBA action after missing the end of the regular season with the Heat due to an ankle injury. He averaged 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 17.2 minutes over 47 regular-season games in 2025-26, and Jovic's role remains uncertain after Miami added Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to its frontcourt this offseason.

items.headline: Jovic (ankle) is out for Tuesday's Play-In Game against the Hornets.
items.story: Jovic was sidelined for Miami's last four games of the regular season due to a left ankle sprain, and his absence will extend at least one additional matchup. If the Heat are able to fend off the Hornets on Tuesday, Jovic would have a chance to return for Friday's game, which will determine the No. 8 seed in the Eastern Conference.

items.headline: Jovic (ankle) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Jovic has played only twice in Miami's last 24 games. At this point, it's unknown if he will be available for the Play-In Tournament. However, while Jovic is ruled out, Simone Fontecchio (ankle), who is probable versus Atlanta, will likely continue to see more action.
