items.headline: Jovic (ankle) will miss the next three games for Miami, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports Tuesday.
items.story: Jovic is not traveling with the Heat on their current road trip. A return against the Hawks on Sunday for the final regular-season game could be on the table depending on how he progresses.

items.headline: Jovic (ankle) is out for Tuesday's game against Toronto, per Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald.
items.story: It's a new injury for Jovic, who's battling a sprained left ankle. His next chance to return comes during Thursday's rematch with the Raptors.

items.headline: Jovic recorded zero points (0-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound over four minutes during the Heat's 123-122 loss to the Rockets on Saturday.
items.story: Saturday's appearance was Jovic's first since Feb. 20. He missed 11 straight games due to a back injury but was a healthy DNP for the Heat's two games prior to Saturday's contest. All of Jovic's runtime against Houston came in the second quarter, and it appears the fourth-year pro doesn't have a clear path to consistent playing time, even when Miami is dealing with multiple injuries.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is available for Tuesday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: After nearly a month on the shelf, Jovic is set to return to the lineup. Bam Adebayo (calf) is doubtful for Tuesday, so there are some minutes up for grabs in Miami.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Jovic is on the verge of ending nearly a month-long absence due to lower-back injury management. With Andrew Wiggins (toe) sidelined, Jovic could play a minor role off the bench in his expected return.

items.headline: Jovic (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Jovic hasn't played since Feb. 20 due to low back injury management. The Heat haven't provided many details regarding where exactly Jovic stands in the recovery process, but the Serbian big man seems unlikely to reclaim a rotation spot once he's finally cleared to play.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is out for Thursday's game versus the Bucks.
items.story: Jovic continues to get ruled out a day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close to returning. With no timetable or updates on his progress from the Heat, Jovic should be considered week-to-week.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is out for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: The Heat continue to keep Jovic from playing due to lower-back injury management. The fourth-year forward holds no definitive timetable for a return to the floor and can be considered doubtful for Thursday's game against the Bucks until Miami offers an update.

items.headline: Jovic (back) will not play Sunday against the Pistons.
items.story: Jovic will be held out for an eighth straight game and remains without a clear timetable to return. His next chance to play comes Tuesday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is out for Friday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Jovic will be sidelined for a seventh straight game and remains without a timetable to return. His next chance to play comes Sunday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Jovic will be sidelined for a sixth straight game Thursday and remains without a timetable for a return. Pelle Larsson and Kel'el Ware could be more involved with this news.

items.headline: Jovic (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Jovic will miss a fifth consecutive game due to a lower-back injury. Pelle Larsson and Simone Fontecchio should continue to see a slight uptick in opportunities in his absence. Jovic's next chance to return will come Thursday in a rematch against the Nets.

items.headline: Jovic (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: The fourth-year pro's absence will extend to four games as he continues to recover from a lower-back injury, and his next chance to play is Tuesday against the Nets. Pelle Larsson and Simone Fontecchio should continue to see more opportunities for playing time for as long as Jovic is out of action.

items.headline: Jovic (back) won't play Thursday in Philadelphia.
items.story: Jovic is set to miss his third straight game Thursday, and for now, he should be considered highly questionable for Saturday's matchup with the Rockets. Pelle Larsson will continue to pick up the slack in Jovic's absence.

items.headline: Jovic (back) will not play Tuesday against the Bucks.
items.story: No surprise here, as Jovic was previously considered doubtful. With Jovic out for a second straight game, Pelle Larsson could see a small uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Jovic (back) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Lower-back tightness is likely to prevent Jovic from playing a second consecutive game Tuesday. Pelle Larsson should see enough playing time to warrant streaming consideration in all fantasy formats.

items.headline: Jovic (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Memphis, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Jovic is dealing with lower-back tightness and will miss just his second outing since Dec. 26. With the 22-year-old big man unavailable, Kel'el Ware and Simone Fontecchio are candidates see a slight bump in playing time.

items.headline: Jovic is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Grizzlies due to lower-back tightness.
items.story: Jovic played just three minutes during the Heat's blowout win over the Hawks on Friday but may have tweaked his back in the process. He's failed to play more than 10 minutes in four of his last six outings, and his absence would lead to slightly more playing time being available for Simone Fontecchio and Jaime Jaquez.

items.headline: Jovic (hip) is available for Tuesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Jovic will be returning from a one-game absence. With Kel'el Ware coming off a strong showing, it will be interesting to see how the frontcourt rotation shapes up Tuesday.

items.headline: Jovic (hip) is questionable for Tuesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Jovic is in jeopardy of missing his second straight game. Kel'el Ware put up a solid showing Sunday against Chicago, and he could get another extended look if the Heat end up being shorthanded again.

items.headline: Jovic (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bulls, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Jovic will be sidelined while dealing with a right hip impingement. In his absence, Simone Fontecchio and Kel'el Ware could see a bump in minutes off the bench, while Jaime Jaquez is likely to continue handling a sizable reserve role. Jovic's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against the Hawks.

items.headline: Jovic is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bulls due to a right hip impingement.
items.story: Jovic likely picked up the injury during Saturday's 125-118 loss to Chicago, when he played 15 minutes and logged two points (1-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal. Simone Fontecchio, Jaime Jaquez and Kel'el Ware should see a bump in playing time Sunday, assuming Jovic is ruled out.

items.headline: Jovic contributed 23 points (6-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-11 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 25 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 147-116 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: The fourth-year big hadn't scored more than eight points in any of the prior six games, but Jovic got some extra run in the rout and took advantage. He's finding a bit of a rhythm from long distance, going 6-for-18 on three-point attempts over the last three contests, but Jovic will need to show more overall consistency to get onto the fantasy radar in most formats.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) is available for Saturday's game against Oklahoma City, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Jovic was a late addition to the injury report Saturday due to an illness, though he'll shed his questionable tag and face the Thunder. Over eight appearances so far this month, the 22-year-old forward has averaged 8.5 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 steals across 20.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jovic (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Jovic is battling through an illness that puts him in jeopardy of missing Saturday's contest. If he's unable to play, then Simone Fontecchio and Pelle Larsson would be in line for more minutes off the bench. In eight games since Jan. 1, Jovic has averaged 8.5 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.0 threes, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks over 20.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jovic (knee) is available for Thursday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: The Heat are giving Jovic the green light to play through right knee soreness Thursday. The forward played just six minutes in Tuesday's win over the Suns, though the absence of Jaime Jaquez (elbow) does free up some playing time in the Miami frontcourt.

items.headline: Jovic is probable for Thursday's game against the Celtics with right knee soreness.
items.story: Confirmation on Jovic's status should arrive closer to Thursday's tipoff. The forward played six minutes, his second-fewest of the season, in Tuesday's win over the Suns, so it appears Jovic could be starting to fall out of favor with head coach Erik Spoelstra.

items.headline: Okongwu recorded six points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block across 29 minutes during Sunday's 107-97 victory over Detroit.
items.story: Despite the quiet scoring performance, Okongwu remains a reliable fantasy center thanks to his rebounding, expanded perimeter shooting and steady starting role. His recent offensive inconsistency shouldn't significantly affect his workload.

items.headline: Okongwu finished Friday's 111-97 win over the Hornets with 16 points (6-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal over 34 minutes.
items.story: Okongwu finished fourth on the Hawks in points and second in rebounds behind Dyson Daniels (eight). After a slow start to the regular season, Okongwu has averaged 18.1 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 2.5 threes, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks over 33.1 minutes over his last eight games while connecting on 55.1 percent of his field-goal attempts. The Hawks will remain at home Sunday to host the Pistons, who will likely be without starting center Jalen Duren (hamstring).

items.headline: Okongwu supplied 28 points (11-21 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 1-3 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 117-112 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Okongwu established season highs in points, three-pointers made and attempted, while leading Atlanta in scoring. The 25-year-old center has scored at least 16 points in four straight games, averaging 19.3 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.0 triples during that span. His increased perimeter volume and consistent playing time continue to strengthen his fantasy value across formats.

items.headline: Okongwu accumulated 16 points (6-12 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 11 rebounds, one block and two steals in 36 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: The 25-year-old center saw his biggest workload of the season as the Hawks navigate multiple injuries to the frontcourt. Okongwu has played at least 30 minutes in every November game so far, averaging 16.3 points, 9.1 boards, 2.4 assists, 2.1 threes, 1.6 steals and 1.0 blocks while shooting 53.8 percent from the floor, and four of his five double-doubles this season have come during that stretch.

items.headline: Okongwu posted 17 points (7-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 125-117 overtime loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Okongwu is one of the best all-around centers in the league, and his newfound ability to hit threes, even though he went 2-for-7 on Friday, is encouraging for his fantasy profile. He's averaging 16.3 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.5 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.0 three-pointers made per game since the beginning of November.

items.headline: Okongwu (throat) returned to Saturday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Okongwu took an inadvertent shot to the throat from Julius Randle early in the first quarter. He was deemed questionable to return, though he is back on the floor after getting checked out in the locker room.

items.headline: Okongwu went back to the locker room after getting elbowed in the face during Saturday's game against the Nets, Lauren L. Williams of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
items.story: Okongwu took an elbow to the face on the first play of the game, and he was down on the ground for a bit before making his way back to the locker room. For now, he should be considered questionable to return.

items.headline: Okongwu registered 22 points (8-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and four steals across 33 minutes during Friday's 139-132 victory over Washington.
items.story: Okongwu recorded his fourth double-double in the past five games, providing fantasy managers with a sense of reassurance. After a slow start to the season, he is now a top-50 player in standard leagues, averaging 13.2 points, 8.6 rebounds, 1.4 three-pointers and 1.6 combined steals and blocks. While the absence of Jalen Johnson (ankle) has certainly helped boost the big man's production, the hope is Okongwu will be able to maintain his current form even when Johnson returns.

items.headline: Okongwu closed Wednesday's 120-105 win over Washington with 14 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 16 rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 31 minutes.
items.story: Okongwu delivered an impressive all-around performance, collecting 13 defensive rebounds while contributing across five fantasy categories. The big man also knocked down two three-pointers, adding another dimension to his offensive production. His combination of rebounding, defensive contributions and improving perimeter range continues to make him a valuable fantasy center.

items.headline: Okongwu posted six points (3-12 FG, 0-5 3Pt), 10 rebounds, one assist and one block over 28 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Okongwu didn't have a great shooting night, especially from beyond the arc. However, he was active on the boards, with five of his 10 rebounds coming on the offensive side of the floor. He's recorded at least nine rebounds in three of his last four outings, and he'll finish the month of October having averaged 11.9 points, 7.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.1 threes and 0.7 blocks over 28.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Okongwu finished with 29 points (11-17 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 12 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block in 32 minutes during Thursday's 114-111 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Okongwu led the charge in the scoring column for Atlanta, and his performance was good enough for his best showing of the young season. He also excelled on the glass, snagging double-digit rebounds on the way to a double-double. Okongwu is averaging 15.4 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.8 assists over six games this year.

items.headline: Okongwu notched 11 points (5-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 29 minutes during Monday's 120-110 loss to Houston.
items.story: Okongwu finally showed signs of life after a disappointing start to the season, providing fantasy managers with a sense of relief. Through four games, Okongwu has averaged 9.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.3 combined steals and blocks in 26.5 minutes per contest. Monday's game saw him record season-high marks in points, rebounds, steals and blocks. He will look to continue his turnaround when Atlanta hosts Miami on Wednesday.

items.headline: Okongwu contributed eight points (3-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and seven assists in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 win over Orlando.
items.story: Okongwu struggled with his perimeter shot but made up for his modest scoring output by leading Atlanta in assists. The starting center's playmaking was encouraging, though he failed to record a defensive statistic. His ability to contribute across multiple categories should keep him valuable despite occasional scoring fluctuations.

items.headline: Okongwu (rest) will play in Friday's preseason finale against the Mavericks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Okongwu and most of Atlanta's regulars rested Monday against the Thunder but will return to action for the final exhibition. It's unclear how many minutes Okongwu will play Friday, but he should be a full go for the regular-season opener.

items.headline: Okongwu (rest) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
items.story: Okongwu is getting the night off Monday, with Atlanta resting a number of starters. His next chance to play arrives Friday against Dallas.

items.headline: Okongwu recorded 18 points (5-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 23 minutes in Saturday's 119-117 preseason win over the Pacers.
items.story: Okongwu delivered a productive offensive performance, making all six of his free-throw attempts while committing just one turnover. The center attempted seven three-pointers, and although he connected on only two, his tendency to stretch the floor has been noticeable in the preseason. That could add another wrinkle to his expanding offensive game. Okongwu, who averaged 15.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks per game across 74 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, will be one of the Hawks' go-to players on both ends of the floor once the regular season starts Oct. 21 at Orlando.

items.headline: Okongwu recorded 13 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and five assists across 22 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: Okongwu showed his versatility as a playmaking big man, leading Atlanta's starters with five assists while connecting on two three-pointers. His willingness to shoot from beyond the arc remains an intriguing element of his offensive development, and if this translates to the regular season, it could unlock a whole new level of upside for Okongwu, who's already an excellent finisher near the rim and an above-average rebounder.

items.headline: Okongwu finished with eight points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one block in 14 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason loss to Memphis.
items.story: Okongwu started at center and knocked down one of his two attempts from beyond the arc. He should remain Atlanta's starting center this season and could provide a boost to his fantasy value if his expanded perimeter shooting carries into the regular season.

items.headline: Okongwu's status as the top center is solidified after Atlanta selected Kingston Flemings with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The Hawks passed up on names like Morez Johnson, Yaxel Lendeborg, Aday Mara and Nate Ament, instead focusing on building their backcourt for the future with the pick of Flemings. Atlanta did nab Zuby Ejiofor later in the first round and also exercised the team option on Mouhamed Gueye's contract to fortify its frontcourt this offseason, but Jock Landale (ankle) is set to enter unrestricted free agency. Neither Ejiofor nor Gueye project as more than reserve players, so Okongwu should have a good chance of building upon a career 2025-26 campaign across the board while effectively functioning as the team's full-time starting center.

items.headline: Okongwu amassed four points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Thursday's 140-89 loss to the Knicks in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Okongwu saved his worst for last, scoring just four points as Atlanta was embarrassed by New York in Game 6. The loss brings to an end what was a breakout season for Okongwu, as he established himself as the starting center for the Hawks. He ended the season as a top-40 fantasy asset, averaging 15.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.9 three-pointers and 2.2 combined steals and blocks over 80 games (including playoffs).

items.headline: Okongwu chipped in 12 points (4-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, one assist and four steals in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-98 loss to New York in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Okongwu turned in an improved performance, albeit still somewhat underwhelming. In his four playoff appearances, Okongwu has averaged 13.8 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.8 three-pointers and 1.9 combined steals and blocks, all down on his season numbers. With the two teams now locked at 2-2, Atlanta will head to New York looking for another road victory.

items.headline: Okongwu (knee) is available for Monday's Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Knicks.
items.story: Okongwu was listed on the injury report with right knee inflammation but will push through and play as the Hawks look to even the series in Game 2. In the Game 1 loss Saturday, the big man totaled 19 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 37 minutes. If Okongwu faces any minutes restriction or a lighter workload, Mouhamed Gueye and Tony Bradley would be in line to pick up the slack.

items.headline: Okongwu is questionable for Monday's Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Knicks due to right knee inflammation.
items.story: Okongwu put together a solid performance in Game 1, logging 19 points and seven rebounds, but he appears to have picked up a right knee injury during the game, putting his status in question for Monday. If he is unable to go, Mouhamed Gueye and Tony Bradley would be candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Okongwu finished Saturday's 113-102 loss to the Knicks in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 19 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block over 37 minutes.
items.story: Okongwu scored 12 of his 19 points in the first half of Saturday's game and finished as the Hawks' third-leading scorer behind CJ McCollum (26 points) and Jalen Johnson (23 points). Okongwu enjoyed a career year in his sixth NBA regular season, though he saw his production dip over his last 19 games from March 1, when he averaged 13.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals, 1.2 blocks and 1.8 threes over 29.8 minutes. The Hawks will need more output from the 2020 first-rounder to help alleviate the pressure for Johnson, McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker.

items.headline: Okongwu (finger) is off the injury report for Game 1 on Saturday versus the Knicks.
items.story: After sitting out Atlanta's regular-season finale, Okongwu is good to go for the beginning of the postseason Saturday. The sixth-year big man enjoyed perhaps his finest season in 2025-26, averaging 15.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.1 steals in 31.0 minutes per contest across 74 contests.

items.headline: Okongwu (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Okongwu will be held out of Atlanta's regular-season finale due to a left index finger sprain. With the Hawks holding multiple key contributors out, Mouhamed Gueye, Asa Newell and Tony Bradley should all see significant run in the frontcourt. Okongwu has taken a significant step forward in 2025-26 and will finish the regular season with averages of 15.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.1 steals in 31.0 minutes per contest across 74 outings (63 starts).

items.headline: Okongwu is questionable to play Sunday against the Heat due to a sprained left index finger.
items.story: Okongwu's left index finger has been bothering him since the end of March, so Atlanta may opt to hold him out of their regular-season finale with Miami. If Okongwu can't play, Mouhamed Gueye would have a chance to start, and there would be more minutes available for Asa Newell and Christian Koloko.

items.headline: Okongwu finished Monday's 108-105 loss to the Knicks with 12 points (4-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and one block over 37 minutes.
items.story: This was a modest line by Okongwu's standards in what has been a terrific campaign for the center. Across 72 appearances, he holds averages of 15.3 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.1 steals, 1.1 blocks and 2.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Okongwu posted 20 points (7-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block over 36 minutes during the Hawks' 112-102 win over the Celtics on Monday.
items.story: Okongwu entered Monday's game having scored 11 points or less in four of his last five outings. It looked like it was going to be another low-scoring affair for the sixth-year big man, but he came out of halftime hot with 11 points in the third quarter and finished as the Hawks' co-leader in scoring with Jalen Johnson. It was Okongwu's 10th game of the season with four-plus three-pointers, and it was his first double-double since March 1. It was an encouraging performance out of the USC product, and that kind of production will help the Hawks as the team looks to improve its standing heading into the postseason.

items.headline: Okongwu (finger) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against Boston.
items.story: Okongwu had only eight points in Friday's 109-102 loss to the Celtics. He didn't suit up Saturday for the 123-113 win over Sacramento. However, Okongwu's absence won't extend beyond one game, meaning Jock Landale will presumably head back to the bench for the rematch with Boston.

items.headline: Okongwu (finger) won't play in Saturday's game against Sacramento, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Jock Landale (shoulder) is questionable. If Landale is upgraded to available, he would likely take over Okongwu's spot in the starting lineup. However, if Landale is also ruled out, Mouhamed Gueye would presumably roll with the first five.

items.headline: Okongwu had 16 points (5-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals over 20 minutes during Monday's 146-107 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Okongwu was one of eight Atlanta players who scored in double digits in this win, and aside from filling the stat sheet, Okongwu was very efficient with his touches near the rim. The big man has scored at least 15 points in just two of his last five appearances, however, and with three single-digit scoring efforts in that span, the center's numbers are trending in the wrong direction.

items.headline: Okongwu had six points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 24 minutes during Friday's 117-95 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: This was the second time over the past four games that Okongwu was held to single digits in scoring, but at least he was able to salvage his stat line with some rebounds and defensive stats. Managers can anticipate a more robust offensive outing Saturday, with a favorable matchup against the Warriors.

items.headline: Okongwu totaled 13 points (4-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-7 FT), nine rebounds, four blocks and two steals in 30 minutes during Thursday's 108-97 victory over the Nets.
items.story: This was Okongwu's second straight game with four swats and nine boards, and he finished with a plus-six differential in the 11-point win. Okongwu is on pace to hit career highs in points (16.1), assists (3.3), triples (2.1) and steals (1.2) this season, and he's flirting with top-30 value on the year.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is available for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Williams will play despite a sprained left thumb. The seventh-year pro has seen a reduced role of late, averaging 2.7 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 16.3 minutes per contest over his last three appearances.

items.headline: Williams is probable for Sunday's game against the Nuggets due to a left thumb sprain.
items.story: Williams is dealing with a sprained thumb on his non-shooting hand, but he's expected to play through it. Williams is averaging 6.9 points and 1.9 assists per game this season.

items.headline: Williams chipped in two points (1-2 FG), one rebound, two assists and one block across 13 minutes during Wednesday's 137-107 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Williams was mostly a non-factor, turning in his second straight dud. After briefly showing out in back-to-back games against Atlanta and Minnesota, Williams has since fallen short of being a fantasy asset, scoring a total of two points in his past two games. Managers are now safe to move on in most formats.

items.headline: Williams (finger) is available for Wednesday's game in Brooklyn.
items.story: Williams was out of the rotation to start the season, but he's been more involved over the past six games, averaging 7.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.2 triples in 22.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Williams (finger) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: After suffering a dislocated right pinky finger in Monday's loss to the Cavaliers, Williams is expected to play Wednesday. The 25-year-old forward is averaging 7.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 steals across 22.7 minutes per contest in six regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Williams (finger) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Williams suffered an injury to his right pinky finger that will end his night prematurely in Cleveland. The forward will finish with no points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) across 13 minutes of action. Noa Essengue figures to see an uptick in playing time should Williams miss extended time. Williams' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday at Brooklyn.

items.headline: Williams ended with 13 points (4-7 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two steals in 24 minutes during Friday's 125-117 overtime victory over the Hawks.
items.story: Williams turned in an efficient performance en route to a season-high 13 points, and he's shot 8-for-11 from the field over his last two games. The veteran forward began the season outside the rotation, but he's logged 20-plus minutes in four straight games and could continue seeing meaningful burn in Caleb Wilson's (hand) stead.

items.headline: Williams accumulated four points (1-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists and one block in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Williams failed to make much of an impact despite receiving 20 minutes off the bench, missing all three of his attempts from beyond the arc and failing to grab a rebound. The 25-year-old forward has struggled to establish a consistent offensive role in Chicago's rotation, leaving him with limited fantasy appeal outside of deeper leagues.

items.headline: Williams (groin) said he will play Friday against Boston, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Williams was listed as questionable on the official injury report, but he went through shootaround with no setbacks and has the green light to suit up. He's yet to see the floor this season and is not guaranteed minutes, to be clear.

items.headline: Williams (adductor) is questionable for Friday's game in Boston.
items.story: Williams is looking to be available for his season debut Friday. The forward could test out the issue prior to Friday's contest before Chicago clarifies his status.

items.headline: Williams (adductor) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Williams continues to battle left adductor soreness. His next opportunity to make his season debut arrives Friday, when the Bulls square off with the Celtics in Boston.

items.headline: Williams (groin) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Williams is in danger of missing his third straight game Wednesday. However, even when healthy, he was not in the rotation.

items.headline: Williams (groin) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Williams is in line for a second straight absence due to right groin/adductor soreness. He's yet to appear in a game this season for Chicago even when healthy.

items.headline: Williams (groin) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Boston.
items.story: Williams is in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest due to right groin/adductor soreness. However, his potential absence wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Williams (groin) is out for Saturday's game versus the Wizards, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: This will be Williams' first missed game this season due to injury. However, he hasn't been in the rotation, so Williams' absence from the active roster won't impact fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Williams (groin) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Williams is a late addition to the injury report due to right groin soreness, so his status will be worth monitoring leading up to the 8:00 p.m. ET tipoff. He has yet to appear in a regular-season game, so his absence wouldn't have much of an impact on the Bulls' bench rotation.

items.headline: Williams (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 135-92 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Williams remained on Chicago's bench despite the Bulls suffering a 43-point defeat. His absence from the rotation is a concerning development for his early-season fantasy value, and he'll need to regain the coaching staff's trust to secure meaningful minutes.

items.headline: Williams produced three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and three rebounds in 10 minutes during Friday's 104-100 preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: The 2020 No. 4 overall pick continues to fall out of favor in Chicago despite being in the middle of a four-year, $72 million contract. The Bulls drafted Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain this offseason to pair with Matas Buzelis, plus 2025 lottery pick Noa Essengue figures to be ahead of Williams on the developmental priority list as well.

items.headline: Williams totaled 13 points (5-15 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one block and three steals over 36 minutes during Sunday's 149-128 loss to Dallas.
items.story: The 2020 first-rounder finished up another pretty disappointing campaign for the Bulls. Williams averaged 7.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 72 games (six starts) this season, shooting a career-low 37.2 percent from the field. Williams is under contract for 2026-27 and appears ticketed for a reserve role on the wing once more.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) will start in Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Williams is in the starting lineup for the second time in the last three games. In five starts this season, the 24-year-old has averaged 11.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 0.4 blocks and 0.8 steals across 32.2 minutes.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) will play in Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.story: The thumb sprain isn't anything new, although it hasn't kept Williams off the floor. He got the start in Thursday's 119-108 win over Washington before moving back to the bench in Friday's 127-103 loss to Orlando. With one more game left on the schedule before Chicago calls it a season, Williams has the chance to put together a strong scoring effort versus a Mavericks squad that hasn't shined defensively throughout the campaign.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is probable for Sunday's game in Dallas.
items.story: Williams has been playing through a sprained thumb on his non-shooting hand the past few games, and it looks like he'll continue to do so in Chicago's regular-season finale. Matas Buzelis (ankle) has already been ruled out, so Williams could be looking at another start Sunday.

items.headline: Williams closed with eight points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds and one steal in 27 minutes during Friday's 127-103 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Williams was unable to keep up his recent production, instead delivering a more 'typical' performance, despite continuing to play meaningful minutes. It is unclear whether Chicago is going to stay the course when it comes to Williams next season, given his inability to add tangible value to the team. As for fantasy, there is no reason to think he will have any appeal moving forward.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) won't start in Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Williams finished with 15 points, eight rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 39 minutes as a starter in Thursday's 119-108 win over Washington. However, with Matas Buzelis (illness) back on the floor after missing the last three games, Williams will move back to the bench.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is listed as available for Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Williams appeared on the injury report because of a thumb injury. However, he is cleared to suit up for Friday's clash with Orlando. The 24-year-old has played well in the last two games, most recently finishing with 15 points, eight rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 39 minutes in Thursday's 119-108 win over Washington.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is probable for Friday's matchup against the Magic.
items.story: Williams joined the first unit during Thursday's game against the Wizards, making it the second consecutive game he played 30-plus minutes. Chicago has an extensive injury report again, so don't be surprised if Williams' role remains bigger than usual.

items.headline: Williams is starting Thursday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Matas Buzelis (illness) and Isaac Okoro (quadriceps) are sidelined Thursday, opening up a spot in the starting lineup for Williams. His last start dates back to Feb. 24 against Charlotte, when he finished with 11 points, two rebounds and one assist in 26 minutes of action.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is available for Thursday's game versus Washington.
items.story: No surprise here, as Williams is overcoming a probable tag with a sprained left thumb. The sixth-year forward put up a season-high 20 points in Tuesday's win over the Wizards, so he'll be looking to build on that success in Thursday's rematch.

items.headline: Williams is probable for Thursday's game against the Wizards due to a left thumb sprain.
items.story: Williams is expected to suit up and handle steady minutes off the bench to bolster the Bulls' frontcourt. He's averaging 6.0 points per game over his last 10 outings, although he scored 20 points in a win over the Wizards on Tuesday.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is available for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Williams is shedding a probable designation with a thumb injury. He's scored in single digits is six consecutive games, which makes him a mostly unappealing fantasy option Tuesday.

items.headline: Williams (thumb) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Williams was a late addition to the injury report with a left thumb sprain, but he intends to play through it. He's been ice cold lately, shooting 27.1 percent from the field over his last eight games.

items.headline: Williams ended with five points (2-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, three assists, one block and one steal in 24 minutes during Sunday's 120-110 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Williams continues to be used sparingly by the Bulls, and he remains ice-cold shooting the ball. Over his last eight games, he's shooting 27.1 percent from the field for 4.3 points per contest.

items.headline: Williams finished with two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound across 19 minutes during Monday's 132-124 win over Houston.
items.story: Williams continues to do very little with his time on the floor, sitting well outside the top 300 in five games over the past two weeks, despite averaging 21.5 minutes per contest. As has been the story for much of his career, Williams can't seem to find any sort of rhythm on either end of the court. For fantasy purposes, he holds little to no value, no matter the format.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) is available for Friday's game against the Clippers, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Williams will shake off his questionable tag and return from a two-game absence due to a left ankle sprain. The 24-year-old forward has averaged 7.6 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 22.8 minutes per game across five appearances (one start) since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Williams remains day-to-day for the Bulls ahead of the second leg of this back-to-back set. Leonard Miller is likely to shoulder a heavy workload if Williams is unable to play.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) won't play Thursday against the Lakers, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Williams was added to Chicago's injury report a day earlier as questionable due to an ankle injury, and after being downgraded to doubtful earlier Thursday, he's now officially been ruled out. Leonard Miller should be in store for more minutes with Williams out of commission.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) is doubtful for Thursday's game versus the Lakers.
items.story: Williams appears likely to miss his second straight contest Thursday. With this news, the Bulls may lean more on Leonard Miller at the forward spots.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) is questionable for Thursday's game versus the Lakers.
items.story: Williams missed Tuesday's win over the Warriors with the ankle issue, and with Thursday's game coming as the first in a back-to-back set, it wouldn't be surprising to see Williams spend at least one more game on the sidelines. Managers can expect to get official confirmation on his status closer to Thursday's tip.

items.headline: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Warriors, Will Gottlieb of AllCHGO.com reports.
items.story: Williams is working through a left ankle sprain that he may have picked up during the Bulls' 126-110 loss against the Kings on Sunday, when he played 17 minutes and finished with five points, one rebound and one block. Tuesday will mark the fifth time in six games that Williams will sit out, as he previously missed time due to a right quad strain. In his absence, the Bulls will rely more heavily on Guerschon Yabusele and Nick Richards off the bench behind Matas Buzelis and Jalen Smith (calf). Williams' next opportunity to play is Thursday against the Lakers.

items.headline: Williams is listed as questionable for Tuesday's game against the Warriors due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: The ankle injury is a new concern for Williams, who recently missed four straight games due to a right quadriceps strain. If the 24-year-old forward is ultimately ruled out, Leonard Miller and Guerschon Yabusele would be candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) provided five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one block in 17 minutes during Sunday's 126-110 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Williams returned from a four-game absence due to a right quad strain and made a limited impact off the bench. As long as the Bulls are at close to full health, Williams may have difficulty pushing past 20 minutes with much regularity.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) is available for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Williams missed the last four games due to a right quadriceps strain, but he will return to the lineup Sunday. Over his last four appearances, Williams has averaged 8.3 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Williams is officially day-to-day after missing the past four games for Chicago. The Bulls could be very shorthanded once again Sunday, so the team may continue to rely on Guerschon Yabusele and Leonard Miller.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Williams appears to be moving in the right direction, as he was upgraded to doubtful before officially being ruled out ahead of Thursday's clash, but he's not yet ready for a return. His next chance to do so will arrive Sunday against the Kings.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) is doubtful for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams' right quadriceps strain is expected to sideline him once again. With the forward likely out of commission and Matas Buzelis (ankle) questionable, the Bulls could turn to Leonard Miller.

items.headline: Bulls head coach Billy Donovan said that Williams will likely be out "at least a week" due to his strained right quad, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: It sounds like Williams will miss at least the next three games for Chicago, with his earliest possible return coming next Thursday in Phoenix. Guerschon Yabusele, Nick Richards and Leonard Miller will likely divvy up Williams' minutes while he's sidelined.

items.headline: McLaughlin (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Kings.
items.story: McLaughlin may miss his seventh game of the year. With De'Aaron Fox (shin) also questionable and Dylan Harper (hip) already sidelined, McLaughlin would be in line to receive extra minutes if he manages to suit up. However, if he's not available versus Sacramento, David Jones Garcia could see significantly more work than usual.

items.headline: McLaughlin produced zero points (0-1 FG), five assists, three steals and one rebound over 11 minutes during Thursday's 124-112 win over the Clippers.
items.story: McLaughlin was held scoreless but still racked up season highs in assists and steals. He has averaged 4.2 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.2 steals across 11.5 minutes per game over his last six appearances, and the 30-year-old could continue to see meaningful playing time in Dylan Harper's (hip) absence.

items.headline: McLaughlin provided 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two assists, one rebound and one steal in 19 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 win over the Jazz.
items.story: The veteran guard delivered an efficient performance and provided a spark off the bench in De'Aaron Fox's (hip) absence. McLaughlin logged a season high in minutes en route to a season-best scoring total. He's logged double-digit minutes in four of his last five appearances, averaging 5.0 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.8 steals in 11.6 minutes per contest during that span.

items.headline: McLaughlin logged zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two assists and one steal in seven minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 win over Sacramento.
items.story: McLaughlin appeared for just the second time this season, with all of his minutes thus far coming during garbage time. McLaughlin has barely been in the rotation throughout his career, a trend that seems likely to continue moving forward. For fantasy leagues, he holds no value.

items.headline: McLaughlin will start in Monday's preseason matchup with the Jazz, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: The Spurs are resting their usual starters for Monday's exhibition, so it'll be McLaughlin starting alongside Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson, Harrison Barnes and Luke Kornet. McLaughlin and Ja'Kobi Gillespie figure to handle the point-guard duties for San Antonio on Monday.

items.headline: McLaughlin agreed to a one-year, $3.3 million deal to return to the Spurs on Monday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: The 30-year-old guard is back with San Antonio for 2026-27 after originally coming from the Kings as part of the De'Aaron Fox trade back in 2024-25. McLaughlin played a career-low 6.4 minutes per game over 44 regular-season appearances last year, so he's likely to serve as emergency depth at point guard and provide a veteran presence for the Spurs' young guards.

items.headline: McLaughlin averaged 2.0 points, 0.9 assists and 0.7 rebounds across 6.4 minutes per tilt in 44 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 season.
items.story: McLaughlin averaged several career lows in his first full season with San Antonio. The 30-year-old point guard logged double-digit minutes in just 12 of his regular-season outings and is now set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason.

items.headline: McLaughlin (ankle) is available for Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Trail Blazers, NBA reporter Matthew Tynan reports.
items.story: McLaughlin missed each of the first three games of the series due to a left ankle sprain. He has progressed enough in his recovery to suit up for Game 4, though he's unlikely to crack the Spurs' playoff rotation, given that he averaged just 6.4 minutes per game off the bench across 44 regular-season contests.

items.story: McLaughlin will return from a 10-game absence due to a strained left hamstring. Although his return will provide San Antonio with additional guard depth, he likely won't crack the Spurs' rotation Wednesday night.

items.story: McLaughlin does not appear to have a prominent role within San Antonio's rotation, as the minutes at backup point guard have gone to rookie Dylan Harper, even with De'Aaron Fox (hamstring) out to start the season. items.story: McLaughlin returned from a three-game absence, so he should be fine for Opening Night. The 29-year-old veteran will battle Dylan Harper for the reserve minutes behind De'Aaron Fox (hamstring) this season.

items.headline: McLaughlin (undisclosed) could return to the lineup for Friday's preseason finale against the Pacers, Dan Weiss of FanDuel Sports Network Southwest reports.
items.story: It doesn't sound like McLaughlin will be available for Monday's exhibition meeting with Indiana. The veteran guard is expected to handle a reserve role in the Spurs' backcourt this season, and he could see an uptick in playing time while De'Aaron Fox (hamstring) is out.

items.headline: McLaughlin (undisclosed) will not play in Friday's preseason game against the Jazz, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.

items.story: McLaughlin spent the last few months of the 2024-25 season with the Spurs after being traded to San Antonio from Sacramento in February. In 18 games with the Spurs, McLaughlin averaged 2.5 points and 1.5 assists over 6.9 minutes. With De'Aaron Fox (finger), Dylan Harper (groin) and Stephon Castle all capable of playing the point guard spot, there likely won't be many minutes available for McLaughlin in 2025-26.

items.headline: McLaughlin ended with two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) across three minutes during Sunday's 125-118 victory over the Raptors.

items.headline: McLaughlin recorded five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal over 10 minutes during Sunday's 120-109 loss to Portland.
items.story: McLaughlin has now played in five straight games, albeit in a limited role. It's been a disappointing season for McLaughlin, logging double-digit minutes only four times since arriving in San Antonio on Feb. 12. In his past 15 games, McLaughlin has averaged just 2.5 points and 1.4 assists in 6.1 minutes per contest.

items.story: McLaughlin has received a DNP via coach's decision in three of the club's last four outings, and his absence shouldn't cause any waves in the club's rotation. His next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Knicks.

items.story: McLaughlin has not had much opportunity to play since joining the Spurs on Feb. 2, and he is now dealing with Achilles soreness, which could cause him to miss time. His availability or lack thereof doesn't figure to have any fantasy implications.

items.headline: McLaughlin (recently traded) is listed as available for Wednesday's game versus the Hawks.
items.story: McLaughlin and De'Aaron Fox are both available to make their Spurs debuts Wednesday after being traded from Sacramento. McLaughlin is expected to compete for depth minutes in San Antonio's backcourt rotation.

items.headline: McLaughlin (recently traded) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Hawks, Michael C. Wright of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The Spurs hope to have McLaughlin available Wednesday after acquiring him in a trade Sunday, but the guard remains iffy to make his team debut. With Chris Paul (finger) also uncertain to play, San Antonio could lean on Stephon Castle and Jeremy Sochan if McLaughlin and De'Aaron Fox (recently traded) aren't ready to suit up.

It's unclear what his role will be in San Antonio's new-look backcourt once he's ready to play, but McLaughlin's next opportunity to take the floor for his new club arrives Wednesday against the Hawks.

items.story: The Kings receive guard Zach LaVine (personal), forward Sidy Cissoko, first-round picks in 2025, 2027, 2031 and three second-round picks (one in 2025, two in 2028), while the Bulls will acquire center Zach Collins, guards Tre Jones and Kevin Huerter and their own 2025 first-round pick back from San Antonio. McLaughlin, who had averaged just 6.8 minutes per game in 28 appearances this season, will face an uphill battle for any sort of consistent role with the Spurs, who have Fox and Chris Paul on hand to cover nearly all of the available minutes at point guard.

items.headline: McLaughlin (personal) is available for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: McLaughlin has averaged 7.0 minutes across 25 appearances for the Kings this season. He's an emergency depth option for the team.

items.headline: McLaughlin (personal) is out for Thursday's game against the Rockets.

items.story: With Duren still out for Detroit but now progressing to a G League practice assignment, this marks a tangible step forward in his recovery from the right hamstring strain that has kept him sidelined since Oct. 23. The Pistons haven't provided a return timeline, but his return appears to be drawing closer as he increases his activity.

items.headline: Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Duren hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right hamstring strain, though he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Until the Pistons offer an update on the 23-year-old big man's progress, he can be considered week-to-week. Paul Reed will likely continue seeing increased minutes for as long as Duren is sidelined.

items.headline: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

items.headline: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Duren suffered the hamstring injury in Friday's win over Miami and is set to miss an extended period. Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

items.headline: Duren has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Duren exited Friday's win over Miami early and did not return, and he's since been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. With the star big man sidelined, Paul Reed is expected to start and figures to see a significant increase in minutes.

items.headline: Duren (thigh) exited Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat in the second quarter and did not return, finishing with four points (2-4 FG), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 10 minutes.
items.story: Duren was deemed questionable to return with a right thigh injury after exiting to the locker room, and he never checked back in. If the big man is forced to miss additional time, Paul Reed would likely step into the starting five. Duren's next chance to play will come Sunday at Philadelphia.

items.headline: Duren is questionable to return to Friday's game in Miami due to a right thigh injury.
items.story: Duren tweaked his thigh and immediately departed to the locker room. If he's not able to get back out there, John Collins and Paul Reed will benefit.

items.headline: Duren exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Heat due to an apparent right knee injury, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Duren appeared to tweak his knee before walking back to the locker room. The big man can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Duren provided 22 points (8-13 FG, 6-7 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 28 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Duren narrowly missed a double-double while matching Cade Cunningham for Detroit's scoring lead. The former also converted a pivotal three-point play during the Pistons' fourth-quarter comeback and committed just one turnover. His efficient finishing and strong free-throw shooting were notable, particularly after he connected on six of seven attempts from the charity stripe. Duren remains a reliable source of points, rebounds and field-goal percentage in fantasy formats.

items.headline: Duren finished Friday's 129-125 preseason win over the Raptors with 14 points (6-9 FG, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block over 20 minutes.
items.story: Most of Duren's work came in the first half, with the fifth-year big man playing sparingly in the third quarter before sitting out for the entire fourth. Duren will be one of the players to watch during the 2026-27 season, given the long contract extension standoff between his camp and the Pistons before the two sides agreed on a five-year, $200 million extension Oct. 1. The Memphis product is coming off a career year in 2025-26 during the regular season but didn't match that production during the playoffs, when he averaged just 10.2 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.2 blocks over 30.1 minutes across 14 postseason contests.

items.headline: Duren finished with 24 points (8-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block across 15 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason victory over Minnesota.
items.story: Duren appeared in his first preseason game, and while he wasn't on the floor long, he still ended with the game high in points. The 2022 No. 13 overall pick, who just agreed to a five-year extension with Detroit, finished the 2025-26 campaign by averaging a career-high 19.5 points along with 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists over 28.2 minutes per contest. Duren also appeared in at least 70 games for the second consecutive season.

items.headline: Duren (reconditioning) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Minnesota, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Duren has completed his reconditioning process and is ready to make his preseason debut. The young center inked a five-year, $200 million extension at the beginning of October after averaging 19.5 points, 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists across 70 regular-season appearances last season.

items.headline: Duren (reconditioning) won't suit up for Saturday's preseason game against the Wizards, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Duren is still working himself into game shape after sitting out training camp while his contract negotiation played out, but he is hopeful to suit up at some point during the preseason. His next chance to get on the court will come Wednesday in Minnesota.

items.headline: Duren (rest) is expected to play at some point this preseason, per Hunter Patterson of The Athletic.
items.story: After Duren engaged in a long standoff regarding contract negotiations with Detroit, the Pistons are monitoring the big man's reps as he ramps up his activity at training camp. His next chance to see exhibition action comes Saturday in Washington.

items.headline: Duren (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Suns, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Duren returned to practice Monday for the first time since signing a five-year, $200 million extension. However, it's unclear when the big man will see live game reps. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said they have a "plan" to ramp Duren up, and the goal is to have their All-Star center available for the regular-season opener against Boston on Oct. 20.

items.headline: Duren was spotted back at practice Monday, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Duren was back in the building for the first time since signing a five-year, $200 million extension. However, it remains to be seen if the Pistons will immediately give him some live-game reps during Monday's exhibition against the Suns.

items.headline: Duren (undisclosed) is not present for the Pistons' open practice Saturday, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Duren signed a five-year, $200 million contract with the Pistons on Thursday after an offseason of negotiating. It's unclear exactly why the big man isn't at Saturday's practice, though he can be considered questionable for Detroit's preseason opener against the Suns on Monday.

items.headline: Duren agreed to a five-year, $200 million contract extension with the Pistons on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The two sides had been at a standstill since it was reported Monday that Duren wasn't showing up to media day or for the start of training camp, but a fully guaranteed deal has since been reached. Now that the big man's contract has been resolved, he'll presumably have plenty of time to join the team and ramp up his basketball activities to appear in a preseason game or two before the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Duren won't attend the Pistons' media day Monday and isn't planning to show up for the start of training camp, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Pistons have reportedly offered Duren a fully guaranteed five-year, $200 million deal in restricted free agency, but the two sides remain at a stalemate. Duren is coming off a breakout 2025-26 regular season in which he earned his first All-Star and All-NBA selections while averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds on 65.0 percent shooting. The 22-year-old big man has until Thursday's deadline to accept the extension or his $9.6 million qualifying offer, unless Detroit extends the deadline.

items.headline: Duren and the Pistons remain in a standoff over contract negotiations, per Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press.
items.story: The gap in negotiations between the two sides has been well-documented this offseason. With the preseason looming, the two parties are running out of time to reach a compromise at this point. As it stands, Duren is a restricted free agent but would be primed for a big role at center if he accepts the qualifying offer or lands an extension and stays with a Pistons team that shipped out Isaiah Stewart over the summer.

items.headline: Duren and the Pistons remain apart in contract negotiations, with Detroit offering approximately $35 million annually while Duren is seeking more than $40 million per year, according to Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com.
items.story: The two sides have been unable to reach an agreement throughout the summer, leaving Duren as one of the NBA's most prominent remaining restricted free agents. The 22-year-old could accept his $9.6 million qualifying offer and become an unrestricted free agent next summer, but Detroit has maintained that it wants to retain him long-term, making an eventual agreement the more likely outcome. Duren is coming off a breakout 2025-26 regular season in which he earned his first All-Star and All-NBA selections while averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds on 65.0 percent shooting.

items.headline: Duren and the Pistons have seemingly not made any progress on a long-term extension, with Tim MacMahon of ESPN reporting that negotiations have been "nasty."
items.story: MacMahon didn't elaborate on just how bad things have been between the two sides and isn't sure if Duren plans to sign an extension. The 2022 No. 13 overall pick spent his first four years with Detroit, though he is coming off his most productive campaign to date, averaging a career-high 19.5 points along with 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 28.2 minutes per showing across 70 regular-season games in 2025-26. Additionally, he earned his first All-Star nod. However, it was a different story during the postseason, with the 22-year-old averaging 10.2 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.2 blocks over 30.1 minutes per game in 14 playoff appearances. There are several directions this situation can go, including Duren agreeing to the proposed contract of roughly $35-$38 million annually. He can also accept a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer and become an unrestricted free agent next summer. While there is still time for progress to be made, both sides are likely running out of patience, which won't improve the chances of Duren remaining in Detroit beyond the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Strawther (knee) is not listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Strawther has yet to make an appearance in 2026-27 due to a left knee sprain he suffered during preseason. However, it appears as if the fourth-year forward could be available to make his season debut at home versus Dallas.

items.headline: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
items.story: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

items.headline: Strawther (knee) will undergo an MRI on Thursday morning, Katy Winge of Altitude Sports reports.
items.story: Strawther exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Wednesday's preseason loss to the Clippers after his left knee bent awkwardly following contact while handling the ball. "All you can do is hope for the best," said Nuggets head coach David Adelman. An extended absence for Strawther would test Denver's depth on the wing, with Spencer Jones (hamstring) not yet cleared for contact. Strawther finished Wednesday's game with 11 points (4-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt) and two rebounds in 18 minutes.

items.headline: Strawther (knee) exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers and will not return, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Strawther's left knee bent awkwardly, leaving him in considerable pain and forcing an early exit to the locker room. An update on the 24-year-old's status could come after the game or in the coming days, but an extended absence would test the Nuggets' depth on the wing with Spencer Jones (hamstring) not yet cleared for contact.

items.headline: Strawther registered 15 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and a steal across 18 minutes in Tuesday's 117-106 preseason win over the Jazz.
items.story: Strawther had a solid night beyond the arc in Denver's first preseason victory. The Gonzaga product enters his fourth season with the Nuggets in a crowded situation at his position following the addition of DeMar DeRozan. While youth is certainly on Strawther's side, a breakout campaign where he finally averages 10 or more points per game seems less likely.

items.headline: Strawther recorded 14 points (6-13 FG, 1-2 FT, 1-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 20 minutes during Sunday's preseason loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Despite coming off the bench, Strawther led the Nuggets with 14 points, while also logging a team-high 20 minutes. With Jamal Murray unavailable, Strawther made the most of his opportunity, as he pushed for more playing time on a team that needs offensive production. Although he has flashed some scoring upside throughout his career, Strawther has been mostly disappointing to this point. There is no indication he will see increased minutes this season, which makes him nothing more than a deeper-league target. However, if he is put in a position where he is tasked with more offensive responsibility, he could be worth consideration as a short-term flier.

items.headline: Strawther could play an expanded role for the Nuggets in 2026-27 after Peyton Watson was traded to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Strawther is still ticketed for a bench role this season, even with Watson now out of the picture, but his playing time could be more consistent after finishing last postseason outside the rotation. The sharpshooter averaged 7.2 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.0 three-pointers in 15.1 minutes per game over 57 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Strawther (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Nuggets' 119-114 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 2 of a first-round playoff series.
items.story: Strawther appeared in each of the Nuggets' final 11 regular-season games and averaged 8.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers and 1.3 assists in 15.5 minutes per contest over that stretch. However, head coach David Adelman has dropped the third-year wing from Denver's rotation for both of the team's first two postseason contests. Unless Denver loses one of its key players to injury at some point during its playoff run, Strawther's opportunities could be largely limited to garbage-time scenarios.

items.headline: Strawther is not in Denver's starting lineup against Minnesota for Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs Saturday.

items.headline: Proctor posted 24 points (10-19 FG, 4-13 3Pt), 11 rebounds and 10 assists across 34 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas.
items.story: Proctor earned his second start of the season and more than delivered for a short-handed Cavs team, as the 2025 second-round pick recorded the first triple-double of his career. The performance is even more impressive when considering Cleveland was without all of James Harden (calf), Donovan Mitchell (knee), Jarrett Allen (knee), Evan Mobley (toe), Sam Merrill (elbow) and Peyton Watson (hamstring). Prior to Saturday's victory, Proctor averaged 8.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 17.9 minutes over 12 outings. He's proven himself as an important role player for a Cavaliers team with championship aspirations, and he should continue providing a spark as their sixth man off the bench.

items.headline: Proctor will start in Saturday's game versus the Mavericks.

items.headline: Proctor recorded 22 points (7-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes during Friday's 133-121 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Proctor made the most of his minutes and matched his previous career-high mark in scoring, but five three-pointers on seven attempts isn't a realistic nightly expectation. Proctor's role remains relatively modest behind Cleveland's established guards, making consistent fantasy production difficult to project. However, performances like Friday's could strengthen his case for additional minutes as the season progresses.

items.headline: Proctor posted 22 points (9-16 FG, 4-8 3Pt), 11 rebounds, eight assists and one steal across 35 minutes off the bench in Sunday's 130-117 win over the Wizards.

items.headline: Coulibaly recorded 19 points (7-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, an assist, three steals and a block across 24 minutes off the bench in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.

This is a make-or-break year for Coulibaly, who's expected to open the season as a bench alternative after the Wizards drafted AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Coulibaly can be an intriguing fantasy option as long as he logs enough playing time, but his role remains uncertain this season after posting down numbers in the 2025-26 campaign, when he averaged 11.7 points, 4.3 boards and 2.6 assists per game -- all downgrades compared to 2024-25.

items.story: Coulibaly is expected to be one of the top players in the future of the franchise, and the young Frenchman has shown promise at times throughout the season. This was the first time he reached the 20-point mark since March 27, and he's scored 20-plus points seven times this season. He's struggled to stand out individually at times due to the Wizards' struggles this season, but the talent and upside are clearly there. Coulibaly is certainly worth holding on to in dynasty formats.
