items.headline: Coulibaly amassed 19 points (7-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-6 FT), three rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 129-98 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Coulibaly was one of the few Wizards to score efficiently during Tuesday's blowout loss, and this was his second straight game with multiple swats. The 21-year-old swingman has been playing well since the All-Star break with averages of 14.1 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.5 triples, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks per game on 45/38/70 shooting splits.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) will play Tuesday against the Bulls.
items.story: Coulibaly will shake off a questionable tag to return from a one-game absence. He'll likely play a modest role as the Wizards continue to monitor him closely.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Coulibaly is at risk of sitting out Tuesday due to right retrocalcaneal bursitis. If the swingman cannot play, his absence would translate to an expanded role for Will Riley.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Coulibaly will miss the second half of Washington's back-to-back set after posting 12 points (5-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, three blocks, two assists and two steals across 25 minutes during Saturday's 152-136 loss to Miami. His next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against the Bulls. Given the Wizards' lengthy injury report, Leaky Black and Jamir Watkins are candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Coulibaly was also listed as questionable with a heel issue leading up to Saturday's matchup, so this designation isn't much of a surprise. The Wizards should have more information on his status for Sunday closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Coulibaly registered 12 points (5-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, three blocks, two assists and two steals across 25 minutes during Saturday's 152-136 loss to Miami.
items.story: The Wizards have been limiting the third-year forward's minutes lately, but that hasn't stopped him from producing for fantasy managers. He's scored in double digits in 10 of his last 11 appearances, averaging 15.1 points, 4.5 boards, 2.9 assists, 1.5 three-pointers, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks over that span.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is listed as available for Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: Coulibaly didn't play in the 120-101 loss to the Lakers on Monday before subsequently returning for the 153-131 loss to Philadelphia on Wednesday. However, despite making another appearance on the injury report, the 21-year-old has the green light to suit up for his second consecutive contest. Coulibaly is coming off a productive month, averaging 14.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.8 blocks and 1.2 steals across 27.8 minutes in March.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: The third-year forward continues to nurse soreness in his right heel. If Coulibaly is unable to push through this issue, the Wizards will likely lean more on Will Riley.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) will play Wednesday against the 76ers.
items.story: Coulibaly is set to return from a one-game absence. The second-year forward is averaging 14.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 25.0 minutes over his last five contests.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Coulibaly is in danger of missing a second consecutive game with a lingering heel injury. If the swingman cannot play Wednesday, more playing time would be available to Justin Champagnie, Leaky Black and Jamir Watkins.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Coulibaly will miss Monday's contest due to a heel issue, and his next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Philadelphia. With the 21-year-old forward sidelined, Jamir Watkins, Will Riley and Justin Champagnie are candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: A questionable tag for the second leg of this back-to-back set has been a common theme for Coulibaly this season. If he's held out for maintenance, the Wizards may lean more on Will Riley.

items.headline: Coulibaly (knee) is available for Sunday's game in Portland.
items.story: Coulibaly will push through the pain and make himself available for Sunday's game. The third-year swingman is averaging 11.5 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.2 triples and 1.4 steals per game this season.

items.headline: Coulibaly is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Portland due to right retrocalcaneal bursitis.
items.story: Coulibaly has been tending to a heel injury recently, and he's likely set to miss at least one end of the Wizards' upcoming back-to-back set. If he can't go Sunday, Leaky Black (hip), Justin Champagnie and Jamir Watkins would likely see more action.

items.headline: Coulibaly posted 21 points (8-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block across 19 minutes during Friday's 131-126 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Coulibaly was limited to 19 minutes for a second consecutive game, but that didn't stop him from being a productive fantasy option. He has scored at least 21 points in four of his last seven games despite averaging just 27.9 minutes per game over that stretch. The numbers are there for the Frenchman, but it's worth keeping a close eye on his playing time, as his fantasy upside won't be very high -- despite how talented he is -- if he continues to log fewer than 20 minutes per game.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) will play Friday against the Warriors.
items.story: The second-year forward will continue to push through his heel issue for now, but he may receive some maintenance days down the stretch. Over his last three games, he's averaging 15.0 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists.

items.headline: Coulibaly (heel) is questionable for Friday's matchup with the Warriors.
items.story: Coulibaly has been playing through the heel issue the past few games, but we'll have a better idea on his status based on his activity level at shootaround. If Coulibaly is out, more minutes will fall to Jamir Watkins and Leaky Black.

items.headline: Thomas recorded 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal across 21 minutes during Monday's 122-108 loss to Chicago.
items.story: Thomas has averaged 10.3 points, 2.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.0 steals in 21.0 minutes over his last three appearances. The rookie's defensive activity is encouraging, though inconsistent shooting and a limited workload restrict his fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Thomas contributed 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 22 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Thomas has scored in double figures in five consecutive games, averaging 14.0 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.4 three-pointers during that stretch. The rookie's perimeter shooting provides fantasy appeal, but fluctuating playing time (18-34 minutes) and modest contributions outside scoring limit his reliability in standard leagues.

items.headline: Thomas will come off the bench Monday against the Bulls, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Thomas drew a start Saturday against Dallas and took advantage of the chance, finishing with 20 points, three triples, four rebounds and two assists in 34 minutes. However, he'll return to a bench role now that Peyton Watson, Donovan Mitchell and James Harden are back in action.

items.headline: Thomas will start in Saturday's game against Dallas.
items.story: With all the Cavaliers' starters unavailable, Thomas will move into the starting lineup for Saturday's meeting with the Mavericks. In two starts during the 2026-27 campaign, the rookie has averaged 13.0 points and 4.5 rebounds over 25.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Thomas tallied 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks across 27 minutes in Monday's 124-112 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Thomas moved to the bench Monday but made the most of his season-high-tying 27 minutes. The rookie second-rounder turned in an efficient performance from downtown, posting a team- and career-best 18 points, 12 of which came in the final quarter. Thomas also tied his career high in steals and swatted a career-best two shots. He has yet to log fewer than 18 minutes in a game since being left out of the rotation in Cleveland's first two regular-season outings, and he should continue providing a spark off the bench when the first unit is at full strength.

items.headline: Thomas won't start Monday's game against the Hornets, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: With Jarrett Allen (knee) back in the lineup, Thomas will retreat to the second unit. The rookie swingman has averaged 12.0 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals in 21.4 minutes per contest across five appearances off the bench so far this season.

items.headline: Thomas will start in Saturday's game against the Knicks, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: With Cleveland missing Jaylon Tyson (ankle), Jarrett Allen (knee) and now Sam Merrill (right elbow management), Thomas will earn the second start of his young NBA career. He posted 17 points (7-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes in his first career start against the Thunder on Nov. 2.

items.headline: Thomas won't start Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Tyrese Proctor will enter the starting five in Peyton Watson's (hamstring) absence, pushing Thomas to the second unit. The rookie second-rounder has averaged 13.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 20.7 minutes per game across three appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Thomas finished with 17 points (7-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 117-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Thomas got the first start of his NBA career due to Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jaylon Tyson (ankle) both being sidelined, and he did not disappoint. The rookie second-round pick was second behind only Donovan Mitchell in shot attempts (16 for Thomas and 17 for Mitchell), and they tied for the team lead in scoring with 17 points each. Thomas was one of seven Cavaliers to score 10 or more points, and despite his low assist numbers (four assists in four games), he's not making too many unnecessary mistakes, averaging 0.75 turnovers a night. The 20-year-old has certainly earned the trust of the coaching staff and his teammates, and his confidence and energy should keep him in the regular rotation throughout the regular season.

items.headline: Thomas will start Monday's game against Oklahoma City, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Thomas will enter the starting five with Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jaylon Tyson (ankle) sidelined. Thomas has offered a spark off the bench in three appearances this season, as he's managed to put up 10 or more points in each of those games.

items.headline: Thomas contributed 13 points (5-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound, two assists, one block and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 136-111 win over the Bucks.
items.story: After missing the previous game due to a foot injury, Thomas returned to action, continuing his strong start to the season. In three appearances, he has averaged 13.0 points, 1.0 steals and 2.3 three-pointers in 20.8 minutes per game. While he isn't doing quite enough to be considered a 12-team asset, he should certainly be on the radar.

items.headline: Thomas (foot) is listed as available for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: After missing Thursday's 114-111 loss to the Hawks, Thomas will be back on the floor Saturday. The rookie has appeared in two regular-season games thus far, averaging 13.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals over 20.0 minutes per contest. He has also shot an efficient 66.7 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Thomas (foot) has been upgraded to probable ahead of Saturday's meeting in Milwaukee.
items.story: Thomas missed Thursday's 114-111 loss to the Hawks due to a foot injury, but he'll be back in action Saturday evening. In two games, Thomas is averaging 13.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.0 three-pointers per contest.

items.headline: Thomas (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: A foot injury could cost Thomas a second straight contest Saturday. Sam Merrill could pick up a few extra minutes off the bench if Thomas is unable to suit up.

items.headline: Thomas (foot) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Hawks, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Thomas will be sidelined for the second leg of the Cavaliers' back-to-back set while nursing a foot injury, and his next opportunity to play is Saturday against the Bucks. The rookie second-rounder averaged 19.5 minutes per game over his last two outings, and that playing time should be absorbed by Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja.

items.headline: Thomas (foot) is questionable for Thursday's game in Atlanta.
items.story: Thomas is at risk of sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set. Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja could get on the streaming radar Thursday, especially if Jaylon Tyson (neck) is sidelined.

items.headline: Thomas posted 10 points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Thomas logged at least 19 minutes for the second straight game, continuing to prove his worth on the biggest stage. After missing the first two games of the season, Thomas has seemingly moved ahead of Craig Porter in the rotation. Thomas, Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson all played roughly 20 minutes Wednesday. Thomas isn't doing quite enough to be rostered in standard leagues, but he should certainly be on the radar moving forward, just in case his role continues to develop.

items.headline: Thomas contributed 16 points (6-10 FG, 4-5 3Pt), two rebounds and a steal across 19 minutes off the bench in Monday's 127-125 overtime win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Thomas made an immediate impact from beyond the arc, connecting on four of five three-point attempts while producing 16 points in just 19 minutes. His efficiency was impressive, but the limited workload and minimal contributions outside scoring suggest his fantasy value remains uncertain. Thomas will likely need more consistent playing time to become a dependable option, particularly with Cleveland featuring several established offensive contributors in the backcourt. He has some upside in dynasty and deep leagues.

items.headline: Thomas (coach's decision) did not play in Thursday's 114-106 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: The rookie guard was left out of Cleveland's initial rotation, with Craig Porter and Tyrese Proctor both receiving playing time off the bench. Thomas showed scoring potential during the preseason, but he'll need to work his way into coach Kenny Atkinson's rotation before becoming a viable fantasy option.

items.headline: Thomas registered 16 points (6-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one steal across 13 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason loss to Orlando.
items.story: Thomas provided a late offensive spark for Cleveland, scoring 14 of his 16 points in the fourth quarter. The rookie showed off his scoring ability with an efficient shooting performance, making a strong impression in limited playing time as he looks to establish himself in the Cavaliers' backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Thomas recorded 11 points (5-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and three steals in 23 minutes during Thursday's 124-113 preseason loss to Boston.
items.story: Thomas struggled from beyond the arc but displayed encouraging defensive activity, leading Cleveland with three steals. The rookie second-round pick received significant playing time in his first preseason appearance, providing an opportunity to showcase his scoring instincts and defensive potential. However, his regular-season role will likely be limited as he adjusts to the NBA level.

items.headline: Thomas recorded 24 points (10-20 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two assists, two rebounds and one steal over 25 minutes in Friday's 100-91 Summer League win over the Bulls.
items.story: Thomas helped keep the Cavaliers afloat in the second half, with 15 of his game-high 24 points coming over the final two quarters of Friday's game. The rookie second-rounder has put together some strong performances in the Summer League, but unless he dominates in training camp and the preseason, he'll likely spend most of the 2026-27 season in the G League.

items.headline: Thomas (rest) won't play in Wednesday's Summer League game against the Pelicans, per Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland.
items.story: The Cavaliers are monitoring the rookie second-rounder's reps Wednesday after he exploded for 35 points (14-23 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT) during Monday's 90-73 Summer League win over the Heat. His next chance to play comes during Friday's matchup with the Bulls.

items.headline: Thomas tallied 35 points (14-23 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 30 minutes in Monday's 90-73 Summer League win over the Heat.
items.story: Thomas put on a show Monday, delivering an extremely efficient performance and knocking down a game-high five triples en route to a game-best 35 points. The rookie second-rounder also tied for the game high in steals and was one of three Cavaliers players to record at least three combined steals-plus-blocks. Thomas has reached the 20-point mark in all three of his Las Vegas Summer League games thus far, and he has dropped 30-plus points in back-to-back outings.

items.headline: Thomas tallied 30 points (10-24 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven assists, four rebounds and four steals across 34 minutes in Sunday's 103-94 Summer League loss to the Pistons.
items.story: After dropping 20 points in Friday's loss to the Pacers, Thomas erupted for a game-high 30 points Sunday. The rookie guard also dished out a game-high seven assists while leading the Cavaliers in steals. Through two Summer League outings, he's averaging 25.0 points, 5.0 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 2.5 steals in 30.5 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Thomas tallied 20 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Friday's 99-93 Summer League loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Thomas scored six points on 1-of-3 shooting from the floor in the first half before erupting for 14 points during the second, including 12 in the fourth quarter alone. The 34th overall pick in this year's draft tied for the game high in scoring in his Summer League debut, and he also tied for second on the Cavaliers in rebounds. The 19-year-old guard out of Arkansas isn't guaranteed a consistent role in the Cleveland rotation as a rookie, as he's buried behind guys like Sam Merrill, Max Strus and Craig Porter.

items.headline: The Kings selected Thomas with the No. 34 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded him to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Thomas represents excellent value for the Cavaliers, who received a future second-round pick to move back from No. 29 and still got a first-round talent. The 19-year-old guard put together a highly productive freshman season under John Calipari at Arkansas, starting 21 of 37 games and establishing himself as a premier perimeter weapon. Thomas averaged 15.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals per contest while serving as the focal point of the Razorbacks' floor spacing. He proved to be a lethal threat from beyond the arc, knocking down an impressive 41.6 percent of his three-point attempts on substantial volume. His 43.5 percent mark from the field reflects some struggles finishing inside against elite collegiate size, so he may struggle in the NBA. Defensively, he uses his quick hands and active anticipation to disrupt passing lanes, pacing Arkansas in total steals. He lands with a Cleveland squad that can afford to bring him along slowly in a deep backcourt, offering him an ideal environment to refine his frame and physical tools while providing the bench with elite, ready-made shot-making depth.

items.headline: Mitchell registered 28 points (8-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 11-12 FT), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and two blocks over 37 minutes in Monday's 122-108 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Mitchell has struggled from beyond the arc over the past three games, shooting 5-for-22 from three-point range, and he could have a tough time snapping out of his slump Wednesday with a difficult matchup against the Knicks. Despite leading his team in scoring Monday evening, Mitchell finished with a minus-13 point differential.

items.headline: Mitchell produced 34 points (14-27 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: This was Mitchell's second straight 30-plus point performance and his fourth of the season. He's flirting with top-25 value on the year with averages of 24.8 points, 4.7 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 2.7 triples and 1.3 steals per game on 49.8 percent shooting from the field and 80.2 percent at the stripe.

items.headline: Mitchell posted 39 points (16-25 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, four assists and three steals across 36 minutes during Monday's 126-115 win over Chicago.
items.story: Mitchell established new season highs in scoring, shooting efficiency and steals to help Cleveland win a second consecutive game. The seven-time All-Star was aggressive in getting to his spots on the floor, as 20 of his 25 shot attempts came inside the three-point line. Mitchell will continue to provide multi-category fantasy production for the 8-7 Cavaliers.

items.headline: Mitchell (knee) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Mitchell sat out Saturday's 127-117 victory over Dallas due to a left knee contusion. Mitchell and the rest of the Cavs' starting five missed the win against the Mavericks after the team dealt with flight issues following Friday's loss in Miami. However, the superstar guard will be back as Cleveland's offensive engine Monday. He's averaging 23.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 5.6 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.8 three-pointers in 33.0 minutes across 13 outings in 2026-27.

items.headline: Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Mitchell will miss his first game of the season due to a left knee contusion. The Cavaliers will be without all of their usual starters, meaning Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Craig Porter should all see significant minutes in the backcourt.

items.headline: Mitchell (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Mitchell is dealing with a left knee contusion and could sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. The star guard's absence would open up more minutes for guys like Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor. James Harden (lower leg/calf), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) are all also in danger of joining Evan Mobley (toe) and Sam Merrill (elbow) on the shelf, so Cleveland could be shorthanded against Dallas.

items.headline: Mitchell closed Friday's 133-121 loss to the Heat with 25 points (9-21 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and seven assists in 33 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell remains Cleveland's primary scoring threat, although the presence of James Harden gives the Cavaliers another established playmaker capable of handling significant offensive responsibilities. That arrangement could occasionally reduce Mitchell's assist opportunities without affecting his scoring ceiling, and he has been thriving of late, scoring 23 or more points in five of his last six appearances. As long as Mitchell remains the Cavaliers' go-to scorer, he should stay in the upper tier of fantasy guards.

items.headline: Mitchell provided 37 points (13-22 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 6-11 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 37 minutes during Saturday's 109-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: The counting stats were nice, but Mitchell was responsible for nearly half of his team's turnovers and uncharacteristically bricked five of his freebies. He also didn't get much help from his co-star, James Harden, who finished with seven points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two blocks and two turnovers in 34 minutes. This was Cleveland's third loss over the past four games, but they'll look to get things back on track with a favorable matchup with the Hornets on Monday.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 23 points (7-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 8-10 FT), seven rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block across 33 minutes in Friday's 119-95 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Mitchell ended with a game-high figure in scoring. It wasn't his most efficient night shooting the ball, and he also committed four turnovers. Still, the 30-year-old did enough to help the Cavaliers snap a two-game skid and earn the win over a Philadelphia team that had just one loss entering Friday's NBA Cup matchup. Mitchell has averaged just 22.6 points in his first nine appearances of the 2026-27 campaign, his lowest since his rookie season. However, he's been more productive in most of the other statistical categories, and there's a good chance he will increase his scoring contributions sooner rather than later.

items.headline: Mitchell ended Wednesday's 124-116 loss to Oklahoma City with 27 points (10-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal across 33 minutes.
items.story: Mitchell led Cleveland in scoring, shooting 58.8 percent from the field while knocking down five three-pointers. The star guard also distributed six assists and committed just two turnovers, providing efficient offensive production against the 2024-25 champions. He remains one of Cleveland's primary scoring options alongside James Harden.

items.headline: Mitchell totaled 17 points (6-17 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-4 FT), five rebounds and 11 assists in 36 minutes during Monday's 117-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Mitchell found the majority of his success from beyond the arc, which was a welcome sight after watching him go 3-for-13 from deep over his previous two matchups. He also made an impact as a facilitator, setting a new season high in assists on the way to his first double-double of the season. Despite a strong final line from the star guard, it was Shai Gilgeous-Alexander who played spoiler with a 43-point night to lead Oklahoma City to victory.

items.headline: Mitchell tallied 22 points (7-19 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 7-8 FT), three rebounds, three assists and a steal across 33 minutes in Thursday's 114-111 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Mitchell struggled from beyond the arc and missed two potential game-tying shots on Cleveland's final possession. His seven made free throws helped salvage his scoring output, but overall, this was a subpar stat line. Mitchell's substantial offensive responsibilities maintain his scoring upside. However, sharing playmaking duties with James Harden could lead to a few games where Mitchell will cede the primary scoring and playmaking role to Harden's hot hand.

items.headline: Mitchell registered 26 points (10-21 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block in 38 minutes during Monday's 127-125 overtime win over Minnesota.
items.story: Mitchell continued his hot start to the 2026-27 campaign by leading Cleveland to a second consecutive win. He's put up 20-plus points in all three of his appearances so far this year, and he was more involved as a facilitator Monday, recording seven dimes after totaling seven total assists through his first two matchups entering the day.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 22 points (7-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block across 35 minutes in Saturday's 125-121 win over the Nets.
items.story: Mitchell followed his 32-point season opener with another productive scoring performance, and he's led the Cavaliers in scoring in both games thus far. Although sharing offensive responsibilities with James Harden and Evan Mobley could cause occasional fluctuations in his usage and assist totals, his role as the team's No. 1 scorer and primary playmaker looks set in stone, and he's one of the shooting guards with the highest fantasy floor across all formats.

items.headline: Mitchell finished with 32 points (11-19 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-11 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in 35 minutes during Thursday's 114-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Mitchell helped his team get out to an impressive 24-point lead at the half, but Philly emerged a different team out of the locker room to begin the third quarter. Despite a tough second half, the star guard managed to stuff the stat sheet. Mitchell led the Cavs in scoring and rebounding, resulting in a double-double in his first action of the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Mitchell recorded 15 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight assists and two rebounds across 25 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason loss to Orlando.
items.story: Mitchell struggled from beyond the arc but made up for his shooting woes with a strong playmaking performance, leading Cleveland with eight assists while committing just two turnovers. The veteran guard also paced the Cavaliers in scoring and should remain the focal point of Cleveland's offense heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Mitchell ended with 11 points (3-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one steal across 26 minutes in Sunday's 119-105 preseason win over Orlando.
items.story: As was the case in Thursday's preseason loss to the Celtics, Mitchell finished with a modest 11 points Sunday. However, he was inefficient when shooting the ball and has now shot a combined 1-for-6 from deep in his first two preseason appearances of the year. Mitchell, who agreed to a four-year, $273 million contract extension in July, is coming off a solid 2025-26 campaign, averaging 27.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, 5.7 assists and 1.5 steals over 33.5 minutes per contest in 70 regular-season games. The 2017 No. 13 overall pick does a lot of things well, and assuming he continues to stay healthy, he should be a top-15 fantasy producer in any format.

items.headline: Mitchell recorded 11 points (4-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and three assists across 17 minutes in Thursday's 124-113 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Mitchell played exclusively in the first half as Cleveland distributed minutes evenly among its starters, with all five logging exactly 17 minutes. With Cleveland prioritizing rotation evaluation during the preseason, Mitchell's modest workload shouldn't raise concerns about his regular-season offensive role. He should remain one of the team's go-to options ahead of the regular-season opener against the 76ers on Thursday, Oct. 22.

items.headline: DiVincenzo (Achilles) has been cleared for team basketball activities, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
items.story: DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. According to Shams Charania of ESPN, the veteran guard has completed five-on-five scrimmages in recent weeks and is targeting a return "shortly before or after the New Year." With DiVincenzo and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.

items.headline: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
items.story: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

items.headline: Team president Tim Connelly believes DiVincenzo (Achilles) will return at some point this season, Jack Borman of the Locked On Wolves Podcast reports.
items.story: DiVincenzo underwent surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles in late April, but there's optimism he'll be able to contribute for the Timberwolves later this year. Although the door is open for the sharpshooter to make a late-season return, he's highly unlikely to be a factor in fantasy leagues in 2026-27.

items.headline: DiVincenzo will undergo surgery Sunday to repair a ruptured right Achilles tendon that he suffered during the Timberwolves' Game 4 win over the Nuggets on Saturday.
items.story: DiVincenzo will have his surgery done by Dr. Martin O'Malley, the same surgeon who repaired the torn right Achilles of Jayson Tatum in May 2025. The fact that the procedure is taking place within 24 hours of DiVincenzo's injury should help with the recovery, though it would be unfair to expect the veteran guard to return as quickly as Tatum did, which was in essentially 10 months. It seems more likely that DiVincenzo will miss the entire 2026-27 season, though if he does progress enough to return, it wouldn't be until late in the regular season. The Timberwolves will also be without Anthony Edwards (knee) for multiple weeks, so the team will turn to Ayo Dosunmu, Mike Conley and Bones Hyland to carry more of the load for the rest of the postseason.

items.headline: DiVincenzo has been diagnosed with a torn right Achilles tendon, and he will miss the remainder of the postseason, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: An Achilles tear comes with a lengthy rehab period, so it wouldn't be shocking to see DiVincenzo wind up missing the entire 2026-27 season, but we'll have a better idea of his potential timetable after he undergoes surgery. Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland will help absorb DiVincenzo's minutes in Minnesota.

items.headline: DiVincenzo (leg) won't return to Saturday's Game 4 matchup with the Nuggets.
items.story: DiVincenzo suffered a non-contact lower right leg injury, and his diagnosis should become clearer after further testing. His absence will open up minutes for Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland.

items.headline: DiVincenzo exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Saturday's Game 4 against the Nuggets due to an apparent right lower leg injury, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: DiVincenzo limped off the floor under his own power after suffering a non-contact injury just over one minute into Saturday's contest. If he's unable to return, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland will likely help pick up the slack.

items.headline: DiVincenzo amassed 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Monday's 119-114 victory over the Nuggets in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The 29-year-old guard drained four treys for the second straight game to begin the Timberwolves' playoff run. With Anthony Edwards leading the charge for Minnesota once again, DiVincenzo is back to being a steady source of secondary offense, and he's sunk at least one three-pointer in 15 straight games dating back to March 18, averaging 11.9 points, 3.2 threes, 2.8 boards, 2.7 assists and 0.9 steals during that stretch.

items.headline: DiVincenzo notched 12 points (4-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and two steals in 31 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 loss to Denver in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: DiVincenzo was the lowest-scoring Minnesota starter in Game 1. Still, he was the team's best shooter from downtown by sinking four of his seven attempts while leading the team in steals. With the Timberwolves falling short of a win to open the series, Minnesota will try to knot things up Monday night in Game 2.

items.headline: DiVincenzo totaled 11 points (4-12 FG, 3-10 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists and one steal across 31 minutes during Tuesday's 124-104 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: DiVincenzo left his mark in this comfortable win over the Pacers, but he had a rough shooting performance. The veteran guard has been trending in the wrong direction despite having a starting role all but secured in the Timberwolves' backcourt. He has failed to clear the 15-point plateau in five straight games, a stretch in which he's averaging 9.6 points, 2.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game while shooting just 32.6 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: DiVincenzo ended with 15 points (5-11 FG, 5-9 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 30 minutes during Monday's 124-94 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: DiVincenzo has drained exactly five three-pointers in three straight games. He has drained multiple threes in six games in a row, although he's failed to hit double-digit scoring twice in that stretch. DiVincenzo's ability as a reliable three-point shooter is huge for the Timberwolves, and his ability to stretch the floor is quite an asset while playing alongside players who command a ton of attention from opposing defenses, such as Anthony Edwards and Julius Randle.

items.headline: DiVincenzo finished Wednesday's 110-108 overtime victory over the Rockets with 17 points (6-15 FG, 5-12 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and two steals in 36 minutes.
items.story: While this was a step in the right direction, DiVincenzo has been far from reliable in fantasy hoops. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 30.4 minutes per contest with 10.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.6 three-pointers on 35.6 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: DiVincenzo ended with nine points (3-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 26 minutes during Wednesday's 147-111 win over Utah.
items.story: DiVincenzo delivered an improved performance, albeit only just. Coming off a scoreless effort only 24 hours earlier, DiVincenzo at least provided managers with upside in the assists column. Despite his slump, DiVincenzo remains a must-roster player, at least until Anthony Edwards (knee) is cleared to return.

items.headline: DiVincenzo supplied 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt), nine rebounds and one assist across 30 minutes during Sunday's 116-103 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: This was a strong showing for DiVincenzo in what's been a volatile couple of weeks for the guard. Over his last seven games, he's shooting just 40.4 percent from the field for averages of 8.6 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.9 three-pointers in 28.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: DiVincenzo contributed six points (2-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 153-128 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: A quiet stretch continued for DiVincenzo, who has scored in single digits in four of his last five games. During this stretch, the combo guard has averaged 7.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.6 three-pointers in 28.3 minutes per game while shooting only 35.3 percent from the field.

items.headline: DiVincenzo logged 16 points (4-7 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals over 27 minutes during the Timberwolves' 115-107 win over the Raptors on Thursday.
items.story: DiVincenzo did most of his damage from beyond the arc during Thursday's win. It was the 26th time this season that he connected on at least four threes, and he has made at least three triples in six of seven games since the All-Star break. Over that seven-game span, DiVincenzo has averaged 13.9 points, 4.7 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.6 threes and 1.4 steals over 30.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: DiVincenzo finished Thursday's 94-88 win over the Clippers with 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four assists and two steals over 31 minutes.
items.story: DiVincenzo logged a solid total, drilling four three-pointers alongside decent secondary numbers. He's enjoyed a productive four-game run since the All-Star break, averaging 14.3 points, 5.0 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists over the span.

items.headline: DiVincenzo produced 19 points (7-13 FG, 5-10 3Pt), one rebound, four assists and two steals across 33 minutes during Tuesday's 124-121 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The 29-year-old guard continues to fill up the bucket from long range. DiVincenzo has sunk at least three three-pointers in three straight games and 12 of the last 17 dating back to Jan. 17, averaging 11.7 points, 4.4 assists, 4.2 boards, 3.2 threes and 1.6 steals over that latter stretch while shooting 41.9 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: DiVincenzo logged nine points (3-5 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Friday's 122-111 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: DiVincenzo fell agonizingly short of a double-double, albeit a very unassuming one. It's been a tough stretch for DiVincenzo, sitting well outside the top 150 in four games over the past two weeks. During that time, he has averaged 5.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 5.5 assists, 1.8 steals and 1.5 three-pointers. While his starting role appears to be safe, the recent addition of Ayo Dosunmu at least gives Minnesota another option, if and when DiVincenzo is struggling.

items.headline: DiVincenzo contributed three points (1-5 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four rebounds, five assists and three steals in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 133-109 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: This was a tough showing for DiVincenzo, and consistency continues to be a concern for the veteran guard. Ayo Dosunmu had a much better night off the bench, and it will be interesting to see how this position battle unfolds after the All-Star break.

items.headline: DiVincenzo supplied six points (2-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal over 26 minutes during Friday's 119-115 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: DiVincenzo scored in single digits for the first time in his past five games, struggling to get anything going on the offensive end. While there is no reason for fantasy managers to panic, the situation in Minnesota is worth monitoring. With Ayo Dosunmu (quadriceps/recently traded) about to enter the rotation, it will be interesting to see what the playing time looks like for DiVincenzo. For reference, in eight games over the past two weeks, he has averaged 13.6 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.6 steals and 3.9 three-pointers in 28.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: DiVincenzo logged 21 points (7-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four assists, three rebounds and two steals over 34 minutes during Minnesota's 137-128 loss to Memphis on Monday.
items.story: DiVincenzo and Jaden McDaniels combined to go 10-for-14 from beyond the arc during Monday's loss while the rest of the Timberwolves went 6-for-27 (22.2 percent) from downtown. It was DiVincenzo's 11th game of the season with five-plus threes, and the veteran guard's 36 games of at least three three-pointers leads the Association. He has averaged 13.9 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 3.7 threes and 2.0 steals over 31.0 minutes per game over his last nine outings.

items.headline: DiVincenzo produced eight points (3-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and five steals in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 118-105 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: The 28-year-old guard set a new season high in steals while tying his career high, a mark he last reached April 27, 2025, against the Lakers. DiVincenzo has recorded at least one pilfer in seven straight games and has drained multiple three-pointers in 12 straight, averaging 14.1 points, 4.9 boards, 4.5 assists, 3.8 threes and 1.7 steals over that latter stretch while shooting 42.9 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: DiVincenzo logged 22 points (7-19 FG, 6-15 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 111-85 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Facing the team he spent the 2022-23 campaign with, DiVincenzo produced his best scoring effort since Jan. 8 while tying his season high in made three-pointers. The 28-year-old guard has scored in double digits in nine of the last 10 games, averaging 14.6 points, 5.0 boards, 4.5 assists, 3.8 threes and 1.4 steals over that stretch.

items.headline: Harden registered 21 points (5-14 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 8-8 FT), six rebounds and five assists across 37 minutes during Monday's 122-108 loss to Chicago.
items.story: Harden cooled off following Friday's 51-point explosion against Indiana. He's averaging 18.5 points, 4.9 rebounds and 6.2 assists in 33.8 minutes this season, maintaining solid fantasy value through his playmaking and substantial workload despite inconsistent shooting.

items.headline: Harden erupted for 51 points (15-for-26 FG, 7-11 3Pt, 14-14 FT), six rebounds, six assists and one steal across 40 minutes during Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana.
items.story: Harden couldn't be stopped Friday, as he scored a game- and season-high 51 points to lead Cleveland to a 14-point comeback win. The scoring marks Harden's highest effort since November 2025, giving him 21 outings with 50-plus to go along with four 60-point performances. Per NBA.com, the 37-year-old passed Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games on the NBA's all-time list.

items.headline: Harden posted 14 points (4-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, nine assists and one block across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Harden has been struggling with his shot in his age-37 season, shooting a career-low 38.5 percent from the field. He's making just 40.3 percent of his two-point attempts, which is a significant drop-off from his 50.6 percent career average from inside the arc. Additionally, Harden's usage rate has dropped to 22.2, which would be his lowest mark since the 2023-24 season. It's been a less-than-ideal start for the 17-year veteran.

items.headline: Harden notched nine points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 assists, four rebounds and one steal across 34 minutes during Monday's 126-115 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Harden returned from a one-game absence due to a calf issue and struggled with efficiency. However, the veteran guard still led all players in assists, dishing out a season-high 10 dimes. The 37-year-old has shot 40.0 percent from the floor over his last five appearances, averaging 15.8 points, 6.4 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals across 32.2 minutes per game during that time.

items.headline: Harden (calf) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's tilt against the Bulls.
items.story: Harden is expected to make his return from a one-game absence due to left calf tightness. He missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas, and he had a front-row seat to watch Tyrese Proctor record his first career triple-double. However, Harden will reprise his starting role in Cleveland's backcourt alongside Donovan Mitchell (knee), who is also expected to play.

items.headline: Harden (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Harden will miss his first game of the season due to a calf issue he picked up sometime after Friday's loss to Miami. Fellow guard Donovan Mitchell (knee) will also be inactive Saturday, leaving Tyrese Proctor, Craig Porter and Meleek Thomas as Cleveland's top backcourt options.

items.headline: Harden (left lower leg/calf tightness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Harden could be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set. If the veteran guard is ruled out, Tyrese Proctor and Craig Porter would likely see increased playing time. Donovan Mitchell (knee), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) are all also in jeopardy of joining Evan Mobley (toe) and Sam Merrill (elbow) on the inactive list, so the Cavaliers could be shorthanded Saturday.

items.headline: Harden finished with 20 points (5-13 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 8-8 FT), six rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block across 35 minutes in Friday's 133-121 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Harden struggled with his perimeter shot, connecting on just two of eight attempts from beyond the arc. However, he made up for it with a perfect showing at the free-throw line. The veteran guard also contributed across the board, leading Cleveland in assists while recording three steals. Despite the loss and inefficient shooting, Harden delivered a well-rounded fantasy performance, continuing to provide value through his playmaking and defensive contributions.

items.headline: Harden produced 32 points (9-14 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 9-11 FT), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 115-107 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Harden had combined for 18 points on 5-for-18 shooting in his previous two outings, but he busted out of his slump in a big way Wednesday, notching new season highs in scoring and three-pointers made. It's been a bumpy start to the season for Harden, but maybe this is a sign that he's ready to start rolling.

items.headline: Harden recorded 11 points (3-9 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Monday's 124-112 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Harden's shot wasn't falling, and he turned the ball over four times in a limited 25-minute workload. His playmaking keeps him fantasy-relevant on off nights, but his efficiency has been inconsistent. He's shooting only 36.4 percent from the field this season.

items.headline: Harden contributed seven points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five assists, two rebounds and two blocks across 34 minutes during Saturday's 109-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Harden couldn't get his shot to fall in this one, recording fewer than eight points in a regular-season game for the first time since Feb. 4, 2025. However, the veteran guard still tied for the team lead in assists and matched his season-high mark in blocks. Over his last five games, Harden has averaged 14.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 0.8 blocks in 31.6 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Harden supplied 19 points (5-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), nine rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 124-116 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Harden struggled with his shot but compensated with strong production on the glass and as a facilitator, finishing one rebound shy of a double-double. The veteran guard also matched his season high with two blocks and knocked down three triples. Despite shooting just 31.3 percent from the field, Harden's ability to contribute across multiple categories helped salvage a productive fantasy outing.

items.headline: Harden closed with 14 points (5-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-3 FT), four rebounds, six assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Monday's 117-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Harden connected on three shots from beyond the arc but attempted only 10 field goals as Cleveland spread its offensive opportunities across the starting lineup. He remained involved as a facilitator, though his modest scoring and unusual struggles at the free-throw line kept him from producing a more impactful fantasy performance.

items.headline: Harden recorded 24 points (7-14 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-9 FT), five rebounds and four assists across 36 minutes in Thursday's 114-111 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Harden scored 20 points through the first three quarters, though he provided a muted impact in the fourth. The veteran guard still delivered an efficient shooting performance and finished as the Cavaliers' leading scorer, reaching the 20-point mark for the first time this season. He's averaging 17.4 points, 6.2 assists and 4.6 rebounds per tilt through five regular-season games.

items.headline: Harden tallied 19 points (7-17 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, nine assists and two steals across 39 minutes in Monday's 127-125 overtime win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Harden delivered his strongest performance of the young season, finishing one assist shy of a double-double while posting season-high marks in points and dimes. His nine three-point attempts also highlighted his offensive involvement despite modest shooting efficiency, and although he seems to have lost a bit of a step offensively, Harden should remain valuable in Cleveland's offensive scheme. He's averaging 15.6 points, 5.3 rebounds and 7.0 assists per game to open the season.

items.headline: Harden contributed 16 points (5-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, five assists and a steal across 33 minutes in Thursday's 114-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Harden had a decent stat line in a game where Donovan Mitchell was the only Cavaliers player to cross the 20-point threshold. Harden led the team in assists and finished third in scoring, so he certainly made his presence felt. However, that stat line is a step in the wrong direction compared to the 2025-26 season, in which Harden averaged 23.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 8.0 assists over 34.8 minutes per contest in 70 regular-season games combined for the Cavaliers and Clippers. This was a slow start for Harden, but he should recover his go-to playmaking and scoring role sooner rather than later.

items.headline: Harden recorded 13 points (3-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT), two assists and a steal across 27 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason loss to the Magic.
items.story: Harden endured a difficult shooting performance. The veteran guard compensated somewhat by going perfect from the charity stripe, but his two assists and three turnovers were also disappointing. Harden's limited playmaking production was particularly notable, with Donovan Mitchell leading Cleveland with eight assists. Despite the underwhelming outing, Harden remains positioned to play a prominent offensive role during the regular season.

items.headline: Harden finished with 24 points (7-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 7-9 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 26 minutes in Sunday's 119-105 preseason victory over Orlando.
items.story: Harden wasn't available for Thursday's 124-113 preseason loss to Boston due to an ankle injury, but he was cleared to suit up Sunday. He played exceptionally well, already appearing in mid-season form in his first exhibition of the 2026-27 campaign. The 2018 Most Valuable Player, who signed a three-year deal with Cleveland in August, averaged 23.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 8.0 assists over 34.8 minutes per contest in 70 games combined for the Cavaliers and Clippers in 2025-26. While Harden is entering his age-37 season, he is still an All-Star-caliber player despite his most productive days likely being a thing of the past.

items.headline: Harden (ankle) will play and start Sunday's preseason game against the Magic, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Harden missed Cleveland's preseason opener due to right ankle soreness, but he will play Sunday. He will likely see fairly limited action in his return, given that it is the preseason.

items.headline: Harden (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against the Celtics, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Harden is dealing with right ankle soreness and will be held out of Cleveland's preseason opener. With the veteran guard sidelined, Jaylon Tyson will join Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen in the starting five.

items.headline: Allen racked up 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and one block in 29 minutes during Monday's 122-108 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Allen has averaged 13.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.0 blocks in 30.0 minutes over his last three appearances. His rebounding has fluctuated, but efficient interior scoring and steady minutes sustain his fantasy value.

items.headline: Allen totaled 19 points (7-15 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-5 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 124-121 loss to Memphis.
items.story: While the points and rebounds were nice, Allen failed to record a single swat and also committed a team-high four turnovers. This was his second straight game with four giveaways, a notable departure from the nine he had committed through his first 11 games of the season. Managers can expect him to bounce back Friday with a favorable matchup against the Pacers.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Allen missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas to manage a right knee injury, but he'll be back in Cleveland's starting five versus Chicago on Monday. Allen is averaging 12.5 points, 8.3 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.4 blocks in 26.0 minutes across 11 outings.

items.headline: Allen (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Allen will get a break to rest his injured right knee after playing in each of Cleveland's last three games. With Evan Mobley (toe) also out, Thomas Bryant can be expected to take on a larger role Saturday.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Allen has played in each of Cleveland's last three games after sitting out two contests with a right knee injury, but lingering issues have now put his availability for Saturday's game in jeopardy. Thomas Bryant and Mario Hezonja could take on increased playing time if Allen ends up sitting.

items.headline: Allen notched 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-3 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block over 32 minutes in Wednesday's 115-107 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Allen collected a game-high 14 boards Wednesday, posting his second double-double of the season in the process. The 28-year-old big man is hovering around his career norms so far, averaging 12.9 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per contest in 10 games this season while shooting 64.1 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Allen (knee) will play Monday night against the Hornets, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Allen will make his return following a two-game absence due to a bruised right knee suffered during Wednesday's tilt against the Thunder. Excluding the game he exited early due to injury, the big man is averaging 15.1 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.7 blocks in 27.7 minutes (seven appearances) so far this year.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Allen has missed the last two contests due to a bruised right knee. Sam Merrill (elbow) is also sidelined, so Meleek Thomas may remain in the starting lineup, with Peyton Watson sliding over to the four and Evan Mobley handling things at the five.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is out for Saturday's game against the Knicks
items.story: Allen missed Friday's game against the 76ers and will also miss the second leg of the back-to-back set against the reigning champions. That means Evan Mobley will continue to start at center, with Mario Hezonja probably entering the lineup at one of the two forward spots. Allen's next chance to play will come against the Hornets on Monday.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is out for Friday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Allen will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set after tweaking his knee in Wednesday's 124-116 loss to the Thunder, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Saturday's matchup with the Knicks. Evan Mobley will spend more time at center with Allen unavailable, and Thomas Bryant could see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is questionable for Friday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Allen picked up a right knee injury during Wednesday's clash against the Thunder and failed to return. He'll presumably be monitored closely leading up to tipoff to determine if he can take the court Friday night.

items.headline: Allen (knee) exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's 124-116 loss to the Thunder and did not return, finishing with zero points (0-1 FG) and one rebound in seven minutes.
items.story: Allen exited to the locker room with a right knee injury. The big man was deemed doubtful to return and did not check back in. If he needs to miss time, Thomas Bryant would likely see increased playing time behind Evan Mobley. Mario Hezonja could also see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is doubtful to return to Wednesday's game against the Thunder, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Allen suffered a right knee injury late in the first quarter and is not expected to check back in. Thomas Bryant figures to see increased burn while Allen is sidelined.

items.headline: Allen exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to an apparent right knee injury, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Allen went down and grabbed at his knee after setting a screen. The big man was able to walk off the floor under his own power and can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Allen accumulated 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 28 minutes during Monday's 117-112 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Allen cooled off after posting 25 points and 11 rebounds against Milwaukee on Saturday, managing just six boards despite collecting three on the offensive glass. He continues to offer reliable interior scoring and defensive contributions, though his rebounding production was modest in Monday's contest.

items.headline: Allen finished with 25 points (12-16 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-4 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal across 24 minutes in Saturday's 136-111 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Allen had his most productive game of the 2026-27 campaign Saturday, ending with a season high in scoring while picking up his second double-double in his last three appearances. The 28-year-old is now averaging 15.3 points, 9.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.8 blocks over 27.8 minutes per contest in five regular-season games. Allen has also displayed improved range, considering he has missed just one of his three attempts from deep this season.

items.headline: Allen posted 14 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, an assist and two blocks across 30 minutes in Thursday's 114-111 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Allen remained efficient offensively while providing his usual rebounding and rim protection. His two blocks boosted his fantasy output, though he finished two rebounds shy of a double-double. Allen has shot at least 50 percent from the field in all but one of his first five appearances of this season, and he continues to form a strong partnership with Evan Mobley in the Cavaliers' frontcourt. Allen's strong field-goal percentage and defensive contributions continue to support his value in category-based formats.

items.headline: Allen produced 21 points (7-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-8 FT), eight rebounds, two steals and a block across 27 minutes in Saturday's 125-121 win over the Nets.
items.story: Allen improved upon his 14-point season opener with an efficient scoring performance, making seven of eight field-goal attempts en route to finishing as the Cavaliers' second-highest scorer. He also finished second on the team in rebounds and added three stocks, making his presence felt on both ends of the court. Allen's rebounding and blocks should provide a reliable fantasy foundation, although his scoring output will likely fluctuate depending on Cleveland's offensive distribution. He's scored at least 14 points in his first two outings this season, so he's enjoying a strong start to the campaign.

items.headline: Allen finished with 14 points (6-10 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds and two blocks across 28 minutes in Thursday's 114-106 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Allen scored all 14 of his points before halftime but failed to maintain that offensive involvement as Cleveland squandered a 29-point lead. His seven rebounds were relatively modest, although his two blocks helped preserve some fantasy value. With James Harden and Donovan Mitchell in the backcourt, Allen should continue benefiting from opportunities around the rim, but his fantasy ceiling remains heavily dependent on rebounding, blocks and efficient finishing.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is active for Thursday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Despite carrying a questionable tag leading up to Cleveland's regular-season opener in Philadelphia, Allen was always expected to suit up. The Cavaliers' starting center could be on a soft minutes restriction given his history with the lingering knee issue. Evan Mobley, Thomas Bryant, Peyton Watson and Jaylon Tyson would likely benefit from any vacated minutes.

items.headline: Allen (knee) said he expects to play Thursday against the 76ers, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Allen is listed as questionable on the latest injury report. He was able to get some shots up Thursday morning, however, and it sounds like he intends to push through the minor injury. The Cavaliers may keep a close eye on his minutes if he's cleared to suit up.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is questionable for Thursday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Allen is in danger of missing the Cavaliers' first game of the 2026-27 campaign. If Allen can't suit up, Evan Mobley would presumably slide to the five, with Jaylon Tyson the favorite to move into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Allen registered six points (3-5 FG), four rebounds and two steals across 17 minutes in Thursday's 124-113 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Allen made the most of his limited touches before the Cavaliers turned to their reserves. The center collected all four rebounds on the defensive glass and finished with a neutral plus-minus rating, which was the best mark among Cleveland's starters. His limited offensive involvement wasn't surprising given the Cavaliers' abbreviated rotation, and Allen should continue serving as a reliable source of rebounds, efficient interior scoring and defensive production during the regular season. His role ahead of the start of the campaign isn't at risk, with the Cavaliers simply limiting the playing time of their projected starters in the preseason games.

items.headline: Allen closed with six points (3-5 FG), three rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 26 minutes during Monday's 130-93 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Finals.
items.story: Allen salvaged what was an otherwise underwhelming night, tallying four defensive stats to go along with just six points. While it certainly wasn't the way he would've wanted the season to end, Allen was able to turn in a number of strong performances down the stretch. In 15 postseason appearances over the past month, he averaged 13.1 points, 7.7 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 29.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Allen racked up 10 points (3-6 FG, 4-8 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 35 minutes during Tuesday's 115-104 overtime loss to the Knicks in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals.
items.story: Allen finished with a serviceable line, although he was well below his best. He continues to alternate good and bad games, adding to Cleveland's mixed fortunes thus far. With that said, he has scored double digits in six of the past seven games, blocking at least one shot in 14 straight contests. Look for Allen to try to play a more decisive role when the two teams clash again in Game 2 on Thursday.

items.headline: Mann recorded two points (2-2 FT), one assist and one steal over two minutes during Monday's 136-120 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Mann continues to operate primarily during garbage time, having appeared in just seven games thus far. At this point, he should not be on anyone's radar, even those in deeper leagues. He has barely been a top-400 player this season, averaging just 1.4 points in 5.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mann registered zero points (0-1 FG) in one minute during Friday's 95-79 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Mann made a rare appearance during garbage time, touching the floor for just the second time this season. At this point, it appears as though he is not going to be an every-night part of the rotation, making him a non-factor in all fantasy formats.

items.headline: Mann finished with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one assist over 12 minutes in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Mann skipped Saturday's exhibition due to general soreness, but he was back in action Monday evening. Mann will battle Bub Carrington for the reserve minutes behind Trae Young, but he's not expected to have a significant role in the rotation.

items.headline: Mann is out for Saturday's game against the Pistons due to general soreness, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Mann is a bit sore after logging 16 minutes in Thursday's preseason opening win over the Knicks, so he'll sit out Saturday's exhibition. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Nets.

items.headline: Mann finished with six points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 16 minutes during Thursday's 111-109 preseason victory over New York.
items.story: Mann struggled with his shot but provided solid rebounding and playmaking off the bench. The veteran guard also committed three turnovers, and his role in Washington's backcourt remains uncertain with Trae Young and several younger guards competing for opportunities. Mann could provide scoring and assists when given sufficient playing time, though consistent fantasy production may be difficult to achieve.

items.headline: The Cavs traded Mann and a 2027 second-round pick to the Wizards on Wednesday in exchange for Cam Whitmore, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Mann will add some depth to the Wizards backcourt, where he'll compete for minutes with Bub Carrington and Tre Johnson. Mann averaged 5.5 points and 1.6 assists on 36/32/85 shooting splits with the Hornets last regular season.

items.headline: The Hornets traded Mann to the Cavaliers on Friday in exchange for Dennis Schroder and cash considerations, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Mann was expected to serve as backcourt depth for Charlotte before the move, and now he'll assume a similar role with his new team. He'll likely be competing in training camp with Craig Porter and Tyrese Proctor for the backup role at point guard behind James Harden, and Mann has an opportunity for a fresh start after playing a career-low 12.6 minutes per game for the Hornets last regular season.

items.headline: Mann supplied two points (0-3 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one assist in seven minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Mann didn't see the floor in Tuesday's Play-In Game win over the Heat but logged seven minutes during Friday's blowout loss. The 25-year-old guard posted several career lows while playing a limited role in 2025-26, averaging 5.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.5 steals in 12.6 minutes per game across 53 regular-season appearances (one start). He's under contract for the 2026-27 season, and the Hornets hold a team option for 2027-28.

items.headline: Mann registered zero points (0-1 FG) across four minutes during Sunday's 110-96 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Mann continues to play a minimal role, typically appearing during garbage time only. In 10 appearances over the past month, he has averaged 2.3 points in 4.5 minutes.

items.headline: Mann recorded two points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in six minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: Mann has failed to play more than 10 minutes in 16 straight games, and in six of those he has failed to see the floor at all. With Charlotte firing on all cylinders at the moment, Mann's role is basically non-existent, eliminating any chance he has at putting up fantasy value. He can be ignored in just about every format.

items.headline: Mann chipped in three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one block across 10 minutes during Saturday's 126-119 win over the Hawks.
items.story: Mann remained in the rotation, albeit playing a minor role. With Collin Sexton having departed, and newly acquired Coby White sidelined with an ongoing calf issue, Mann could certainly remain in the rotation, at least for the short term. With that said, it doesn't appear as though he is going to see enough court time to warrant any serious attention outside of deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Mann (illness) is off the injury report for Saturday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Mann's absence from the Hornets' injury report signals that he's recovered from an illness that cost him Thursday's win in Orlando. It's worth mentioning that Mann was available to play in Wednesday's loss to Cleveland but ultimately didn't see any action, so the guard may not see meaningful minutes Saturday.

items.story: Mann hasn't been a regular rotation player for Charlotte in recent weeks when the team has been at or near full strength, so his potential absence Wednesday won't necessarily open up minutes for other players.

items.headline: Mann had 20 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 12 minutes during Saturday's 150-95 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Mann hadn't seen the hardwood in five of Charlotte's last six outings due to a coach's decision, though he received extended burn in this blowout win. The 24-year-old guard led Charlotte with 20 points in just 12 minutes, matching his season-best mark in points. He also knocked down a season-high four triples. Still, with the team near full strength, Mann isn't guaranteed to play meaningful minutes moving forward.

items.headline: Mann (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Hornets' 132-125 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Since returning to action Dec. 20 following a seven-game absence due to a knee contusion, Mann had shot just 26.9 percent from the field over the Hornets' ensuing five contests and had seen his minutes drop in each successive game. Even though the Hornets were without Miles Bridges (ankle) on Wednesday, it didn't open up any extra playing time for Mann, who dropped out of the rotation while Liam McNeeley (10 minutes) ended up serving as the 10th man for Charlotte. Along with Bridges, the Hornets may need to be down at least one more key guard or forward before Mann regains notable minutes.

items.headline: Mann closed with 13 points (5-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and one block across 17 minutes during Monday's 139-132 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Mann dropped 13 points, a much-improved performance when compared to his previous outing. Despite his offensive upside, Mann has failed to carve out a sizable role in Charlotte, even with others around him missing time due to injuries. At best, Mann can be streamed in if and when the schedule is in his favor.

items.story: Mann returned from a seven-game absence due to a right knee bone bruise. If and when LaMelo Ball misses time, Mann can be considered for streaming purposes.

items.story: Mann played through a recent ankle concern, although perhaps his time would have been better spent sitting on the bench. The 24-year-old has appeared in each of the Hornets' last three games, averaging 7.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 17.3 minutes per contest during that span.

items.headline: Mann (ankle) recorded three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one assist across 17 minutes in Sunday's 113-110 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Mann made his return to action after missing the Hornets' previous two contests due to a sore left ankle. Though the Hornets had plenty of playing time up for grabs at point guard and on the wing while LaMelo Ball (ankle) and Brandon Miller (shoulder) being rested for the second leg of a back-to-back set, Mann actually finished below his season-long average in minutes (21.9 per game) and submitted an ugly 1:3 assist-to-turnover ratio in addition to shooting poorly from the field during his time on the court. With both Ball and Miller expected back for Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Mann is unlikely to see his role grow even though he's healthy again.

items.headline: Mann (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against the Hawks.

The guard can provide scoring pop off the bench, though his efficiency has lagged, shooting 36.5 percent from the field and 30.6 percent from deep across 14 appearances this season.

Mann is capable of racking up the stats when given the minutes, so if Ball and Sexton are out again Monday, Mann would make for a quality streaming option.

items.headline: Mann provided 18 points (8-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and two steals across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 116-112 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Mann scored at least 13 points for the third straight game, continuing to benefit as those around him fall. After a slow start to the season, Mann has stepped things up, averaging 14.0 points and 2.0 three-pointers in 21.2 minutes per game over the past four contests. While his offensive output has been encouraging, he offers very little else, making him nothing more than a streaming candidate on low-volume nights.

items.headline: Mann finished with 16 points (6-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, five assists and one steal across 23 minutes during Saturday's 122-105 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Mann gave the Hornets a lift off the bench, recording a season-high 16 points. Charlotte has yet to settle on a consistent starting shooting guard alongside LaMelo Ball, perhaps keeping Mann in the conversation as a candidate for that spot. That said, Mann may need find a groove before he's seriously considered for the role -- he's averaged 8.2 points, 3.0 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 0.8 steals per contest while shooting just 31.6 percent from the field over his first six games.
